@lActionDescriptor::ActionDescriptor@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lActionDescriptor::ActionDescriptor@k_Z.body: Creates an ActionDescriptor by delegating the supplied TransformAction to its base Action constructor, performing no additional initialization.

@lActionDescriptor::ActionDescriptor@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lActionDescriptor::ActionDescriptor@k_Z.body: Initialises a descriptor that encapsulates a transform action, stores its name and arity, and keeps the supplied transform implementation under a unique pointer.

@lActionDescriptor::operator cmList::Tra.author: AI Short Overview
@lActionDescriptor::operator cmList::Tra.body: This const member simply returns the object’s `Action` field.

@lAddAutogenExecutableToDependencies@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddAutogenExecutableToDependencies@k_Z.body: The helper pulls the executable identifier from a `GenVarsT` instance and records it in a list of dependency names – taking the `Target` name when an object is present, otherwise falling back to the raw string value.

@lAddBacktrace@k_ZL12AddBacktraceR13Back.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddBacktrace@k_ZL12AddBacktraceR13Back.body: The function adds a backtrace entry to the provided graph and, if the addition succeeds, records the new index in the JSON object under the key `"backtrace"`. It returns immediately after the update.

@lAddBundleExecutable@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddBundleExecutable@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The template function tries to add the provided executable to a runtime dependency set. If the underlying `AddBundleExecutable` call fails, it registers an error via the helper and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lAddCustomCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116A.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddCustomCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116A.body: Adds a custom command to the build system: it selects or creates a source file (using the main dependency if present, otherwise generating a rule file), checks for an existing command to avoid duplicates, and finally attaches the command to that file along with its outputs and by‑products, marking it with the “__CMAKE_RULE” flag.

@lAddEvaluationFile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddEvaluationFile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function gathers the input and target names, parses the supplied output and condition strings into compiled generator expressions, and then injects a new evaluation entry into the current makefile via its `AddEvaluationFile` helper, passing along the new line character and permissions flag, while updating the status object with the resulting back‑trace context.

@lAddFileSetEntries@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddFileSetEntries@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function walks through a target’s header‑ and C++‑module file‑set entries, retrieving each named set via `GetFileSet` and delegating each set’s creation to `addFileSetEntry`.

@lAddInlineVisibilityCompileOption@k_ZL3.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddInlineVisibilityCompileOption@k_ZL3.body: The routine examines the target’s visibility setting. It first pulls a definition named CMAKE_<lang>_COMPILE_OPTIONS_VISIBILITY_INLINES_HIDDEN from the makefile; if that definition is missing it returns immediately. If the target’s VISIBILITY_INLINES_HIDDEN property is false it also exits. When a warning flag is supplied it records the “VISIBILITY_INLINES_HIDDEN” string and returns; otherwise it appends the retrieved flag string to the output flag buffer.

@lAddInstallRuntimeDependenciesGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddInstallRuntimeDependenciesGenerator.body: The routine registers three install generators for runtime dependencies: first a “get‑runtime‑dependencies” generator that produces the necessary lists; then a library‑dependency set generator that handles DLLs on non‑Apple platforms or normal libraries on others; finally, on macOS, a framework‑dependency generator. As it creates each generator it updates the corresponding boolean flag to indicate which kind of dependency was added.

@lAddInterfaceEntries@k_Z19AddInterfaceE.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddInterfaceEntries@k_Z19AddInterfaceE.body:
The function `AddInterfaceEntries` populates a collection of interface definitions for a target by querying the target’s link‑implementation objects for the requested language.  
It first checks whether runtime libraries should be included.  
If so, it fetches a `cmLinkImplementation` instance for the given config, and for the specified language retrieves the matching library from its internal map, adding that library to the result set via `addInterfaceEntry`.  
Afterwards it always appends the generic library list of that implementation.  
If runtime‑only mode is off, it falls back to a `cmLinkImplementationLibraries` object and processes only its library list.  
During all steps the function copies the `HadContextSensitiveCondition` flag into the supplied `entries` structure so callers know whether any of those libraries required runtime‑context‑sensitive handling.

@lAddLangSpecificImplicitIncludeDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddLangSpecificImplicitIncludeDirector.body: The function scans a target’s linked libraries, picks those whose compile language matches the requested language, retrieves each library’s include path (either from a specified property or a binary‑/object‑directory fallback depending on the mode flag), and appends these directories to the supplied entries list.

@lAddLangSpecificInterfaceIncludeDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddLangSpecificInterfaceIncludeDirecto.body: It walks the linked‑interface dependency chain for a given language, collects each dependency’s include directory (using either the stored property or, if missing, the target’s binary or object path per the specified fallback), and concatenates those paths into a semicolon‑separated string that it returns.

@lAddLinkDir@k_ZL10AddLinkDirR10cmMakefi.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddLinkDir@k_ZL10AddLinkDirR10cmMakefi.body: The `AddLinkDir` helper simply registers a directory that should be searched for libraries when the build system resolves link paths. It receives a reference to the current `cmMakefile` instance and a directory string, then pushes that path into the makefile’s internal list of link search directories. Internally it normalises the path format (slashes, trailing slashes) and guards against duplicate entries before appending the entry to the makefile’s vector of link directories. This registration is later consulted when the CMake compiler resolves library references during makefile generation.

@lAddLinkDir@k_ZL10AddLinkDirR10cmMakefi.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddLinkDir@k_ZL10AddLinkDirR10cmMakefi.body: The function normalizes a directory path to Unix style, determines whether it is a relative path or a generator expression, and according to the CMP0015 policy either emits a warning, an error, or (under NEW) converts the relative path to an absolute one by prefixing the current source directory. The resulting path is then appended to the supplied vector of directories.

@lAddObjectEntries@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116A.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddObjectEntries@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116A.body: The routine walks through the libraries recorded in the given target’s link‑implementation list. For each library whose target type is `OBJECT_LIBRARY` it builds an expression that represents that library, evaluates it in the current build context, and places the produced values into the supplied `entries` list. It flags any result that was found to be context‑dependent.

@lAddTrailingSlash@k_ZL16AddTrailingSlas.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddTrailingSlash@k_ZL16AddTrailingSlas.body: It appends a “/” to the string if it isn’t already terminated by one.

@lAddVisibilityCompileOption@k_ZL26AddVi.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddVisibilityCompileOption@k_ZL26AddVi.body: The function examines a target’s visibility property for a specific language, fetches the corresponding compile‑time flag from the target’s makefile, and, if the property is set to one of the supported values (hidden, default, protected, internal), appends that flag to the list of flags to be passed to the compiler. If the property is undefined, or set to an unsupported value, the function silently exits; if a warning flag is supplied, the message is appended to that string. The function does not perform any error‑handling beyond the error call, so any failure after a warning is returned directly.

@lAdjustRPathELF@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Adj.author: AI Short Overview
@lAdjustRPathELF@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Adj.body: AdjustRPathELF parses an ELF file, optionally rewrites its RPATH/RUNPATH string entries using a supplied callback, and writes the updated strings back to the file. It returns a success flag while indicating whether the file was altered.

@lAdjust_Cursor_Position@p@l./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lAdjust_Cursor_Position@p@l./Source/Cur.body: The routine takes a pointer to the current field’s buffer and an offset pointer to that same buffer, computes the linear distance between them, and then uses that distance to update the form’s current row and column. Depending on whether the `USE_DIV_T` macro is enabled, the row is calculated either via a custom division routine or via a plain integer division, and the column is set to the remainder. After updating, it clamps the row back to zero if the new row would exceed the field’s declared row limit.

@lAfter_End_Of_Data@p@l./Source/CursesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lAfter_End_Of_Data@p@l./Source/CursesDi.body: The function receives a buffer pointer and its length, then steps backward from the buffer’s end until it encounters a non‑blank character and returns a pointer to that position. It essentially trims trailing whitespace by pointing to the last meaningful byte in the buffer.

@lAfter_Last_Non_Pad_Position@p@l./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lAfter_Last_Non_Pad_Position@p@l./Sourc.body: The function returns a pointer just after the last padding byte at the end of the buffer—it trims trailing pad bytes by moving back until a non‑pad byte is found.

@lAfter_Last_Whitespace_Character@p@l./S.author: AI Short Overview
@lAfter_Last_Whitespace_Character@p@l./S.body: This routine walks backward from the buffer’s end until it finds a whitespace character, then returns a pointer to that position. It assumes the supplied length correctly indexes into the buffer and that `is_blank` correctly identifies whitespace; otherwise it may over‑run or return an invalid address.

@lAnyOutputMatches::[lambda_0]@kAnyOutpu.author: AI Short Overview
@lAnyOutputMatches::[lambda_0]@kAnyOutpu.body: Checks whether the given string ends with the specified `name`, optionally preceded by a slash.

@lAnyOutputMatches@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116A.author: AI Short Overview
@lAnyOutputMatches@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116A.body: The function scans a collection of strings and returns `true` if any string ends with the supplied name, provided that the matched part is either at the very start of the string or is preceded by a slash (`/`). If no string satisfies this condition, the function returns `false`.

@lAnyTargetCommandOutputMatches::[lambda.author: AI Short Overview
@lAnyTargetCommandOutputMatches::[lambda.body: The lambda is a short predicate: it captures an outer `name` and, given a `cmCustomCommand` reference, invokes `AnyOutputMatches(name, command.GetByproducts())` to determine if that command’s output products match the stored name, returning the Boolean result.

@lAnyTargetCommandOutputMatches@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lAnyTargetCommandOutputMatches@k_ZN12_G.body: The function scans the supplied list of custom commands and returns true if at least one of those commands contains an output that matches the supplied target name, delegating that comparison to `AnyOutputMatches`.

@lAppendAttribute@k_ZL15AppendAttributeR.author: AI Short Overview
@lAppendAttribute@k_ZL15AppendAttributeR.body: The function writes an XML “attribute” element where both the `key` and `value` attributes are set to the supplied string. It calls the writer’s `StartElement`, `Attribute`, and `EndElement` methods in that order.

@lAppendDictionary@k_Z16AppendDictionary.author: AI Short Overview
@lAppendDictionary@k_Z16AppendDictionary.body: The template accepts an XML writer, a key string, and a value of any type. It writes a `<dictionary>` element containing the key and value sub‑elements, then closes the element.

@lArchToolsetHelper::[lambda_0]@kArchToo.author: AI Short Overview
@lArchToolsetHelper::[lambda_0]@kArchToo.body: The lambda examines a JSON value: if it’s null it clears the output fields and sets the strategy to nullopt, then returns true; if it’s a string it copies that string into the output and again returns true; if it’s an object it forwards the work to a helper routine; otherwise it emits a pre‑set error and returns false.

@lArchToolsetHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lArchToolsetHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body:
The function creates a helper that validates and populates a `ConfigurePreset` instance from a JSON value.  
* It receives pointers to two members (`valueField` and `strategyField`) of the target object.  
* It builds a `JSONHelperBuilder` bound to the fields `"value"` and `"strategy"` using `PresetStringHelper` and `ArchToolsetStrategyHelper`.  
* The returned lambda:  
  * If the JSON value is `nullptr`, it clears both fields and reports success.  
  * If the value is a string, it assigns that string to the `value` field and clears the strategy field.  
  * If the value is an object, it delegates parsing to the prepared helper.  
  * On any other type, it reports an `INVALID_PRESET` error and returns failure.

@lArchToolsetStrategyHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lArchToolsetStrategyHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: Parses a JSON string into an `ArchToolsetStrategy` enum, returning success or failure while populating an optional output and reporting invalid values.

@lArchiveError@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Archi.author: AI Short Overview
@lArchiveError@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Archi.body: ArchiveError builds a message from the supplied string, appends an archive‑specific error string if available, then forwards the combined message to cmSystemTools::Error for handling.

@lArgs::Args@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14ArgsC1EO.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgs::Args@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14ArgsC1EO.body: `Args` is a simple wrapper around a pair of iterators that represent a contiguous subsequence of a `std::vector<std::string>`; it inherits from `cmRange`, storing `begin_` and `end_`. The constructor `Args(Args&& other)` performs a *move* operation: it copies the `begin_` and `end_` members from `other` into the new instance, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state. The type is typically used to pass around string ranges without copying the underlying data.

@lArgs::Args@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14ArgsC1ER.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgs::Args@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14ArgsC1ER.body: Constructing an Args object from an existing one is a trivial copy: the constructor simply copies the underlying iterator state (the begin and end positions) into the new instance, preserving the range semantics inherited from cmRange. This allows callers to pass an Args by value or to re‑wrap an existing range without altering its contents.

@lArgs::Args@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14ArgsC1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgs::Args@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14ArgsC1Ev.body: Args is a small wrapper that represents a sequence of string arguments. It derives from cmRange, so it behaves like a container range whose elements are string references from a std::vector<std::string>. In practice this means an Args instance can be iterated over with normal begin()/end() semantics, yielding each string argument supplied to a command.

@lArgs::PopBack@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14Args7.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgs::PopBack@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14Args7.body: The function removes and returns the last element of the container: it first checks for emptiness and throws an error if none, then takes the element just before the end iterator, decrements the container’s size, and finally returns that element. It relies on the container’s `retreat(1)` method to actually drop the element.

@lArgs::PopFront@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14Args.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgs::PopFront@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14Args.body: The method removes and returns the element at the front of the underlying container. It first checks whether the collection is empty; if it is, it throws a json_error initialized with the supplied error message. Otherwise it obtains a reference to the element at the container’s beginning, calls advance(1) to move the internal cursor forward, and then returns the reference to the removed element.

@lArgs::~Args@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14ArgsD1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgs::~Args@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_14ArgsD1E.body:
The `~Args()` member is the destructor for the `Args` type.  
When a `Args` instance goes out of scope, this destructor is invoked automatically and releases any resources or cleanup that the `Args` class may have accumulated during its lifetime.

@lArgumentParser::Base::BindKeywordMissi.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Base::BindKeywordMissi.body: The `BindKeywordMissingValue` method stores a supplied `KeywordNameAction` into the `KeywordMissingValue` binding slot, first ensuring that this slot hasn’t already been set. It moves the action into the internal structure, guaranteeing that the binding is now owned by the instance.

@lArgumentParser::ExpectAtLeast::ExpectA.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ExpectAtLeast::ExpectA.body: This public constructor simply stores the supplied `count` in the member `Count`. When invoked, it assigns the argument to the member variable, effectively setting up the object with the required count value.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: The operator() function is a const member that accepts a cm::string_view argument and returns an instance of Continue.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: Continuing operator()(cm::string_view) processes the supplied `string_view` and returns the resulting value (or status) without mutating the object.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: Creates a Continue instance from the supplied string_view, serving as a lightweight constructor for an operator object.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: This function produces a lightweight, read‑only string view by assembling the current object's data into a cm::string_view without copying the underlying characters. It allows callers to inspect the object’s textual representation in a non‑mutating fashion.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: Captures a reference to `val`. When invoked with a `cm::string_view` argument, it casts `val` to a `std::string&` and assigns the view’s content to it. Finally, it returns `Continue::No`.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: Checks if the input string is empty – if so and parsing is in progress it records an error – then assigns the string value to the provided variable and returns “No” to indicate the operation succeeded.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: This lambda assigns the given string_view to a `std::string` variable and returns `Continue::No`.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: The lambda captures `val` by reference, accepts a `string_view` argument, pushes that argument to the back of `val`, and then returns `Continue::Yes`.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: Captures a reference to a container `val` and, when called with a `string_view`, pushes that view into the container via `emplace_back`. Afterwards it signals success by returning the enum value `Continue::Yes`.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind::[lambd.body: This lambda inserts the provided `cm::string_view` into `val` and returns `Continue::Yes`.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.body: The `Bind` function stores a callback that will be invoked once the parser has read the required number of keyword values (`ExpectAtLeast` indicates the minimal count). The stored callback (`KeywordValueFunc`) is later called with the string fragment that was just read. The function also records how many keyword values the parser should expect in `KeywordValuesExpected`. This pairing of function and expected count is what drives the keyword‑value extraction logic downstream.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.body: The `Bind` overload takes a `Maybe<std::string>` reference and registers a callback that, when invoked with a `cm::string_view`, copies the view into the referenced string and returns `Continue::No`. It effectively wires the input string into the `Maybe` so that the value is set once the bound function runs.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.body: The routine registers a callback that captures a string argument, rejects an empty value by flagging a keyword‑error, stores the argument in the supplied `NonEmpty<std::string>` holder, and signals completion via a `Continue::No` return.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.body: The method registers a callback that, when invoked, copies the incoming string‑view argument into the supplied `std::string` reference and returns a `Continue::No` value. It also enforces that at least one argument is supplied via the `ExpectAtLeast{1}` clause.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.body: The template ensures the supplied optional contains a value – creating one with the default constructor if it’s empty – and then forwards the dereferenced value to a concrete overload of `Bind`.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.body: The function guarantees that the optional argument contains a valid value before delegating to an overload: if the optional is empty it is default‑constructed, then the dereferenced value is passed along with the context to the actual Bind implementation.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.body: The function simply sets the passed‐in reference to `true` and then forwards control to another `Bind` overload, passing a null pointer and a minimal‑argument constraint (`ExpectAtLeast{0}`). It essentially acts as a thin wrapper that performs the assignment before delegating to the more detailed binding routine.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Bind@k_ZN14A.body: The function creates a new inner vector in `multiVal`, captures a reference to it, and then registers a callback that appends any string it receives to that inner vector. Each invocation of the callback returns a `Continue::Yes` value.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::Consume@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::Consume@k_ZN.body: The routine first looks for the supplied argument in the keyword map; on a hit it records the keyword, resets the value‑counter, flags the keyword as seen, and invokes any registered callbacks. If no keyword is matched and a keyword‑value handler is present, it runs that handler (updating the value‑counter or resetting the handler as required). Failing that, it falls back to a positional lookup and, if found, calls the corresponding positional handler. Any argument that survives all checks is appended to the unparsed list. The function thus orchestrates the state transitions that drive the parser.

@lArgumentParser::Instance::FinishKeywor.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Instance::FinishKeywor.body: If a keyword has been parsed but not enough values were supplied, the method registers an error with the parser’s results and, if a custom handler has been bound, invokes that handler with the missing‑value notification.

@lArgumentParser::KeywordActionMap::Empl.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::KeywordActionMap::Empl.body: Returns whether `elem.first` is strictly less than `k`.

@lArgumentParser::KeywordActionMap::Empl.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::KeywordActionMap::Empl.body: The `Emplace` member inserts a key/value pair into the underlying associative container. It performs a lower‑bound search using a custom comparator, then returns the iterator to the element that would occupy that position. If an element with the same key already exists, it returns that iterator with a `false` flag; otherwise it inserts the new pair and returns the iterator to the newly‑inserted element with a `true` flag. The returned pair thus indicates whether an insertion occurred and gives a handle to the stored element.

@lArgumentParser::KeywordActionMap::Find.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::KeywordActionMap::Find.body: Returns true when the first component of `elem` is less than the supplied key `k`, acting as a comparison predicate.

@lArgumentParser::KeywordActionMap::Find.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::KeywordActionMap::Find.body: The `Find` member performs a binary search in the underlying container: it creates a `std::lower_bound` iterator using the map’s internal key ordering (`elem.first < k`), then checks if the found element matches the key. If it matches, the iterator is returned; otherwise the function returns the end iterator. This guarantees that an already‑sorted container delivers logarithmic lookup time while preserving const‑ness of the map.

@lArgumentParser::ParseResult::AddKeywor.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ParseResult::AddKeywor.body: AddKeywordError records a parsing error when a keyword appears again during argument processing. It takes the keyword name and an error‑description string, then appends this information to the parser’s internal error list so that duplicate or unexpected keyword usage can later be reported to the caller.

@lArgumentParser::ParseResult::MaybeRepo.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ParseResult::MaybeRepo.body: The function checks whether any keyword‑related errors were recorded. If so, it concatenates those messages into a single string and issues a fatal error via the supplied `cmMakefile`. It then returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lArgumentParser::ParseResult::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ParseResult::operator.body: It evaluates the state of the `KeywordErrors` collection and returns `true` when that collection is empty; otherwise it returns `false`. This conversion operator is marked `explicit`, so it will only be invoked in contexts that expect an explicit boolean value, and it guarantees it does not alter any internal state.

@lArgumentParser::PositionActionMap::Emp.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::PositionActionMap::Emp.body: The lambda takes a pair‑like object and an integer. It returns true when the first element of the pair is strictly less than the supplied integer.

@lArgumentParser::PositionActionMap::Emp.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::PositionActionMap::Emp.body: Emplace locates the place where a key `pos` would fit using `lower_bound`. If the key already exists, it returns that iterator with `false`; otherwise it inserts a new `value_type` at that position and returns the new iterator with `true`.

@lArgumentParser::PositionActionMap::Fin.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::PositionActionMap::Fin.body: Returns `true` when the element’s `first` field is strictly smaller than the supplied `k`; otherwise `false`.

@lArgumentParser::PositionActionMap::Fin.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::PositionActionMap::Fin.body: The function performs a binary search over the sorted container for the given key and returns an iterator pointing to the matching element if it exists, otherwise the end iterator.

@lArgumentParserWithOutputVariable::Argu.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParserWithOutputVariable::Argu.body: It initializes a parser that maps a command‑line argument named “OUTPUT_VARIABLE” to the `Output` member of the `Result` type. The base class `CMakePathArgumentParser` supplies the underlying path‑parsing logic, while this constructor simply establishes that binding.

@lArgumentParserWithOutputVariable::Bind.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParserWithOutputVariable::Bind.body: Binds a named argument to the specified member of the result type and returns the current parser instance for fluent chaining.

@lArgumentParserWithOutputVariable::Pars.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParserWithOutputVariable::Pars.body: It forwards the supplied vector of strings to a helper parser, passing the compile‑time `Advance` value along. The helper’s `Parse` method performs the actual argument‑processing, and the result is returned to the caller.

@lBT::BT@k_ZN2BTC1ET_19cmListFileBacktra.author: AI Short Overview
@lBT::BT@k_ZN2BTC1ET_19cmListFileBacktra.body: It constructs a `BT` instance by moving a supplied value of type `T` and a supplied `cmListFileBacktrace` into its internal members.

@lBTs::BTs@k_ZN3BTsC1ET_19cmListFileBack.author: AI Short Overview
@lBTs::BTs@k_ZN3BTsC1ET_19cmListFileBack.body:
This constructor initializes a `BTs` object with a value and a back‑trace entry.  
- The template parameter `T` is moved into `Value` via `std::move`.  
- It then appends the supplied `cmListFileBacktrace` to the `Backtraces` container using `emplace_back`.

@lBacktraceData::Add@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::Add@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The method inserts a back‑trace node into the internal map and JSON array, deduplicating identical entries and recursively linking any parent node, then returns the newly assigned index.

@lBacktraceData::Add@k_ZN13BacktraceData.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::Add@k_ZN13BacktraceData.body: The `Add` method processes a back‑trace entry. It first returns `false` if the supplied list is empty. It looks up the top item in an internal mapping; if that node already exists, it outputs its stored index and returns `true`. If it’s a new node, the function builds a JSON object containing the file path, optional line number, and optional command name. It then recurses on the popped parent list to wire in any parent reference, stores the new node in the internal vector, records its index in the map, and finally returns `true`.

@lBacktraceData::AddCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::AddCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: Adds the supplied command string to the internal list if it isn’t already present, maps the string to its position index in that list, and returns that index. If the command was already stored, it simply returns the existing index without modifying the list.

@lBacktraceData::AddCommand@k_ZN13Backtr.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::AddCommand@k_ZN13Backtr.body: The routine checks if the supplied command string already has an index stored in the internal map; if it’s absent it inserts a new entry assigning an index equal to the current size of the command list, pushes the string into the list, and finally returns that index.

@lBacktraceData::AddFile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::AddFile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: Searches a file in `FileMap`; if absent it inserts a new entry, appends the file path to `Files`, and returns the index of that file in the array.

@lBacktraceData::AddFile@k_ZN13Backtrace.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::AddFile@k_ZN13Backtrace.body: The function looks up the given filename in a map that records each file’s position. If the file isn’t already mapped, it inserts a new entry keyed by the name, assigns it the next free index (the current count of stored files), and appends the name to a list. Finally it returns that index.

@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN12_GL.body: Moves the supplied string into the internal `TopSource` member, leaving the object otherwise uninitialized.

@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN12_GL.body: BacktraceData(BacktraceData&& other) is a move‑constructor that efficiently transfers the internal state of an existing BacktraceData instance into a new one, avoiding deep copies of the contained data structures.

@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN12_GL.body: The copy constructor creates a new BacktraceData instance by duplicating the data from an existing instance. It performs a shallow copy of the member fields, allocating any required resources only when necessary. This is the standard way the class is initialized from a source object.

@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN13Bac.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN13Bac.body: The constructor creates a new `BacktraceData` instance by taking ownership of the contents from an existing object (`std::move`). It transfers the internal state (typically a collection of back‑trace frames or other diagnostic data) from the source to the new instance, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state.

@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN13Bac.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN13Bac.body: BacktraceData is a copy constructor that initializes a new instance with the contents of an existing BacktraceData object. It copies internal state, enabling callers to duplicate and pass backtrace information between components such as the multi‑process test harness.

@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN13Bac.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::BacktraceData@k_ZN13Bac.body: The function initializes a `BacktraceData` object from a stack trace, collects and organizes call‑stack frames into a structured format (e.g., a vector of frame descriptors), and then returns this populated data structure for later consumption.

@lBacktraceData::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The method clears the internal maps and then moves the stored Commands, Files, and Nodes into a JSON object before returning it.

@lBacktraceData::Dump@k_ZN13BacktraceDat.author: AI Short Overview
@lBacktraceData::Dump@k_ZN13BacktraceDat.body: The method clears the internal command, file, and node maps and returns a JSON object containing the moved `Commands`, `Files`, and `Nodes` collections.

@lBase32Encode5@k_ZL13Base32Encode5PKhPc.author: AI Short Overview
@lBase32Encode5@k_ZL13Base32Encode5PKhPc.body: The function turns five input bytes into an eight‑character Base‑32 string. It extracts 5‑bit groups in the precise order defined by the bit‑shifts, merges adjacent bits from neighboring bytes where necessary, and passes each 5‑bit value to `Base32EncodeChar` to obtain the corresponding character in the output buffer.

@lBase32EncodeChar@k_Z16Base32EncodeChar.author: AI Short Overview
@lBase32EncodeChar@k_Z16Base32EncodeChar.body: The function simply performs a lookup in the `Base32EncodeTable` array, returning the byte at the index supplied by the argument. It relies on the caller to guarantee that the supplied `int` falls within the table’s valid range, as there are no bounds checks performed. The `inline` qualifier hints at a trivial in‑place expansion for speed, and the use of `unsigned char` ensures the result is a byte value rather than a signed value.

@lBlockScopePushPop::BlockScopePushPop@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lBlockScopePushPop::BlockScopePushPop@k.body: The constructor inspects the supplied `ScopeSet`; for each requested scope type it creates a helper object that temporarily pushes that scope onto the current context and will pop it on destruction. If the set contains a `POLICIES` flag, a `PolicyPushPop` is instantiated; if it contains a `VARIABLES` flag, a `VariablePushPop` is instantiated, both stored as unique pointers.

@lBlockScopePushPop::BlockScopePushPop@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lBlockScopePushPop::BlockScopePushPop@k.body: The `BlockScopePushPop` helper encapsulates the RAII pattern for block-scoping: it takes an instance of a `BlockScope`, pushes it onto a global or context‑wide stack when constructed, and guarantees that the corresponding `pop` is performed when the object goes out of scope. It’s a thin wrapper that relies on the destructor to automatically unwind the stack, ensuring that each block push is matched by a pop even in the presence of early exits or exceptions.

@lBlockScopePushPop::operator=@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lBlockScopePushPop::operator=@k_ZN12_GL.body: Deletes the copy‑assignment operator, so an instance of the class cannot be assigned from another – effectively preventing copying after construction.

@lBlockScopePushPop::~BlockScopePushPop@.author: AI Short Overview
@lBlockScopePushPop::~BlockScopePushPop@.body: The ~BlockScopePushPop() routine is the helper that the command processing code uses to keep track of nested “block” contexts. When a new block is entered, the routine pushes a scope marker onto an internal stack; when the block is exited, it pops that marker. This ensures that any state changes (such as local variable bindings or resource handles) that belong to the block are automatically restored when the block finishes.

@lBoolNode::BoolNode@k_ZN8BoolNodeC1EOS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lBoolNode::BoolNode@k_ZN8BoolNodeC1EOS_.body: BoolNode is a move‑constructor that takes an rvalue reference of the same type and initializes a new BoolNode. It is used whenever a boolean expression node needs to be copied or transferred in the AST, allowing efficient construction from an existing BoolNode instance.

@lBoolNode::BoolNode@k_ZN8BoolNodeC1ERKS.author: AI Short Overview
@lBoolNode::BoolNode@k_ZN8BoolNodeC1ERKS.body: The constructor simply creates a new BoolNode instance by copying the internal state from the supplied source instance. It performs a shallow copy of the node’s member variables (e.g., flags, operands) without any additional side‑effects, ensuring that the new node is an exact replica of the original.

@lBoolNode::BoolNode@k_ZN8BoolNodeC1Ev@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lBoolNode::BoolNode@k_ZN8BoolNodeC1Ev@f.body: It creates a BoolNode instance, setting its internal boolean flag to a default state (typically false) and initializing any inherited members so the node is ready for use.

@lBoolNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK8BoolNode8Eval.author: AI Short Overview
@lBoolNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK8BoolNode8Eval.body: Returns the string `"1"` when the first element of `parameters` is not considered “off”; otherwise it returns `"0"`.

@lBoolNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_ZNK8.author: AI Short Overview
@lBoolNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_ZNK8.body: The `NumExpectedParameters()` method simply reports that each instance of this class expects a single argument. It is a `const` virtual override that returns the literal value `1` to indicate that only one parameter is required for any processing that relies on it.

@lBoolNode::operator=@k_ZN8BoolNodeaSEOS.author: AI Short Overview
@lBoolNode::operator=@k_ZN8BoolNodeaSEOS.body: This operator overload performs a move‑assignment for a `BoolNode`. It takes an rvalue reference to another `BoolNode`, transfers its internal state to the current object, and returns a reference to the updated node so that further operations can be chained.

@lBoolNode::operator=@k_ZN8BoolNodeaSERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lBoolNode::operator=@k_ZN8BoolNodeaSERK.body: The operator overload assigns the internal state of the right‑hand `BoolNode` to the left‑hand object, returning a reference to the updated object.

@lBoolNode::~BoolNode@k_ZN8BoolNodeD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lBoolNode::~BoolNode@k_ZN8BoolNodeD1Ev.body: The `~BoolNode()` function is the destructor of the `BoolNode` struct. It runs automatically when a `BoolNode` instance goes out of scope, performing any necessary cleanup (such as releasing owned resources or resetting internal state). It ensures that the node’s resources are properly released before the object is destroyed, preventing leaks and maintaining correctness in the expression‑generation workflow.

@lBooleanOpNode::BooleanOpNode@k_ZN13Boo.author: AI Short Overview
@lBooleanOpNode::BooleanOpNode@k_ZN13Boo.body: The constructor creates a new `BooleanOpNode` by moving the contents of an existing node into the new instance, transferring ownership of all internal data members while leaving the source node in a valid but unspecified state.

@lBooleanOpNode::BooleanOpNode@k_ZN13Boo.author: AI Short Overview
@lBooleanOpNode::BooleanOpNode@k_ZN13Boo.body: The constructor simply stores the supplied operator and value strings in the node’s members, so the object has the operator and the corresponding success and failure return values ready for later evaluation.

@lBooleanOpNode::BooleanOpNode@k_ZN13Boo.author: AI Short Overview
@lBooleanOpNode::BooleanOpNode@k_ZN13Boo.body: This constructor initializes a new `BooleanOpNode` by copying the internal state (expression tree, operator type, and any child nodes) from an existing node instance, ensuring the new node behaves identically to the source.

@lBooleanOpNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13Boolean.author: AI Short Overview
@lBooleanOpNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13Boolean.body: The routine checks each supplied parameter. When it encounters the value designated as a failure flag it immediately returns that flag. For any other value it verifies that the string equals the expected success marker; if it does not, it logs an error and yields an empty result. If all parameters satisfy the success condition, the function returns the success value.

@lBooleanOpNode::NumExpectedParameters@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lBooleanOpNode::NumExpectedParameters@k.body: Returns a constant indicating that the implementing object expects **one or more parameters**. The override simply reports that fact to callers that query parameter requirements.

@lBooleanOpNode::ShouldEvaluateNextParam.author: AI Short Overview
@lBooleanOpNode::ShouldEvaluateNextParam.body: The function checks whether the last supplied parameter equals a special failure token. If that token appears, it assigns that token to the output string and signals that no further evaluation should occur by returning false; otherwise it returns true, indicating the next parameter can be processed.

@lBooleanOpNode::~BooleanOpNode@k_ZN13Bo.author: AI Short Overview
@lBooleanOpNode::~BooleanOpNode@k_ZN13Bo.body: The virtual destructor `~BooleanOpNode()` guarantees proper polymorphic cleanup when an instance of `BooleanOpNode` (or any class derived from it) is destroyed, freeing any owned resources before the base `cmGeneratorExpressionNode` destructor runs.

@lBuffer_To_Window@p@l./Source/CursesDia.author: AI Short Overview
@lBuffer_To_Window@p@l./Source/CursesDia.body: The routine copies a field’s internal buffer into a curses window. It walks the buffer row‑by‑row, truncating each line to the window’s width before calling waddnstr to render the characters in place.

@lBuildLabelRE@k_ZL12BuildLabelRERKiRi@p.author: AI Short Overview
@lBuildLabelRE@k_ZL12BuildLabelRERKiRi@p.body: BuildLabelRE clears the supplied output vector, iterates through each string in the input vector, and appends those strings that are not empty to the output vector. It then returns *true* if at least one string was added; otherwise it returns *false*.

@lCLCompileAndDependencies::[lambda_0]@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLCompileAndDependencies::[lambda_0]@k.body: It captures a `std::string` by const‑reference and yields its underlying C string through `c_str()`.

@lCLCompileAndDependencies@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLCompileAndDependencies@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function parses its argument vector looking for three options – “--dep‑file=…”, “--working‑dir=…”, and “--filter‑prefix=…”. After collecting those values it builds a command list from the remaining arguments (everything after the “--” separator). It then creates a process object, sets the command and working directory, and runs the process. While the process runs it streams its output through a custom include‑parser that writes dependency entries into the specified file. After the process exits it checks the exit state: normal exit, exception, or error. If the exit was non‑zero, the created dependency file is deleted as it is considered invalid. Finally the function returns the exit status as its own return value.

@lCLIncludeParser::CLIncludeParser@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLIncludeParser::CLIncludeParser@k_ZN1.body: The constructor stores the prefix string, the dependency file stream, and the output stream in member variables so the parser can later write matched include lines to the dependency file and write parsed results to the output stream.

@lCLIncludeParser::ProcessLine@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLIncludeParser::ProcessLine@k_ZN12_GL.body: The routine scans the current line: if it begins with the configured prefix, it extracts the following path string, normalises it into a long‑form absolute path, and appends that path (in string form) to the dependency output stream. If the line lacks the prefix, it simply forwards the line unchanged to the general output stream. The method always returns success.

@lCLIncludeParser::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLIncludeParser::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The move‑assignment operator (`operator=`) for `CLIncludeParser` accepts an rvalue reference to another `CLIncludeParser` instance and efficiently transfers its internal state into the current object, returning a reference to the moved‑into object.

@lCLIncludeParser::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLIncludeParser::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The operator= function copies the configuration and internal state of another CLIncludeParser instance into the current one, updating any parsing flags, buffers, and any internal structures accordingly, and finally returns a reference to the modified object.

@lCLIncludeParser::~CLIncludeParser@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLIncludeParser::~CLIncludeParser@k_ZN.body: The function implements the cleanup logic for the include‑directive parser. It traverses the input stream, tokenises include statements, resolves quoted or angle‑bracket paths, and builds the corresponding internal representation while ensuring proper error handling and resource deallocation.

@lCLOutputLogger::CLOutputLogger@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLOutputLogger::CLOutputLogger@k_ZN12_.body: CLOutputLogger is a move constructor that takes an rvalue‑reference of an existing logger instance. It transfers the internal state (e.g. log buffers, file handles, configuration flags) from the source object to the new one, ensuring no deep copy of data occurs. The constructor is used to instantiate a new logger by “moving” the resources of an already‑constructed temporary, thereby avoiding expensive re‑initialisation or allocation overhead.

@lCLOutputLogger::CLOutputLogger@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLOutputLogger::CLOutputLogger@k_ZN12_.body: The constructor initializes a new `CLOutputLogger` by copying the state of an existing instance. It copies configuration options, log destinations, and any in‑memory buffers that the base `cmProcessTools::OutputLogger` uses, ensuring the new object is ready to emit log entries in the same way the original would. This pattern is employed in `cmcmd.cxx` (around line 262) when a logger instance needs to be duplicated or transferred across module boundaries without re‑creating the underlying logging infrastructure.

@lCLOutputLogger::CLOutputLogger@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLOutputLogger::CLOutputLogger@k_ZN12_.body: CLOutputLogger passes the provided std::ostream reference to its base class, initializing the logger with that stream.

@lCLOutputLogger::ProcessLine@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLOutputLogger::ProcessLine@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The overridden `ProcessLine` simply flushes the log stream (`*this->Log << std::flush;`) and then returns `true`.

@lCLOutputLogger::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLOutputLogger::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The assignment operator provides a move‑style assignment for `CLOutputLogger`. It accepts an rvalue reference of the same type, transfers ownership of the underlying logger state into the target object, and returns a reference to that object for chaining.

@lCLOutputLogger::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLOutputLogger::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of a source logger into the current instance, preserving its configuration flags and buffer contents. It performs a self‑assignment guard, copies each relevant member, and returns a reference to *this so callers can chain assignments or use the returned object in further statements.

@lCLOutputLogger::~CLOutputLogger@k_ZN12.author: AI Short Overview
@lCLOutputLogger::~CLOutputLogger@k_ZN12.body:
Handles output dispatch for the `CLOutputLogger` type.  
When invoked, it captures the supplied log record, formats it according to the internal configuration (e.g., timestamps, severity), and writes the formatted string to the attached sink (file, console, or network).  
The implementation ensures thread‑safety by serializing access through an internal mutex and performs a non‑blocking flush to avoid stalling the main execution path.

@lCMakeCommandUsage@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeCommandUsage@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function builds a single text string that lists all “cmake” sub‑commands (copy, remove, rename, tar, etc.), prefixed by a header that shows the program name and, depending on the `CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP` macro, either a full “cmake bootstrap” message or a brief “cmake version …” line. Finally, it calls `cmSystemTools::Error` to emit that help text to the console.

@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: Creates file‑management objects, taking ownership of resources from a temporary CMakeFiles instance. The routine moves data from a source object into the newly‑constructed instance, ensuring proper ownership transfer and registration of the created files.

@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The constructor sets up internal state: it stores a reference to a file‑API object, records the version number, builds paths for the CMake modules directory and the top‑level source and build directories, and sets a flag indicating whether the build directory is outside the source tree. The `static_cast<void>(Version)` line simply suppresses an “unused value” warning and performs no runtime action.

@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: CMakeFiles is a copy‑constructor that receives a const reference to another CMakeFiles instance and duplicates its internal file‑map state to initialise a new object.

@lCMakeFiles::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110C.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110C.body: The `Dump` method serializes the `CMakeFiles` instance into a JSON object: it creates an empty JSON object, populates the `"paths"` field with the result of `DumpPaths()` and the `"inputs"` field with the result of `DumpInputs()`, and returns the constructed JSON value.

@lCMakeFiles::DumpInput@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::DumpInput@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body:
The function receives a file path and produces a JSON object describing where the file belongs.  
It marks the file as `isCMake`, `isExternal`, or `isGenerated` depending on whether the path falls under the CMake modules directory, the top‑source or top‑build directories, or the generated‑out‑of‑source directory.  
After determining those flags, it returns the file’s relative path (relative to the source root if applicable) and the flag values in a `Json::Value` map.

@lCMakeFiles::DumpInputs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::DumpInputs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: Iterates over the local generators supplied by the global CMake generator, retrieves each generator’s makefile, enumerates the files listed in that makefile, appends each file (via `DumpInput`) to a JSON array, and returns that array.

@lCMakeFiles::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: This function returns a JSON object containing two keys—`source` and `build`. The values are pulled directly from the class’s member pointers (`TopSource` and `TopBuild`). It simply creates an object, assigns those two entries, and returns the object.

@lCMakePathArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakePathArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN12_G.body: The `Bind` template registers a member of the target type (`Result`) as a named argument in the underlying argument‑parser infrastructure. It forwards the name and member pointer to the base parser (`cmArgumentParser<Result>`) and returns the current parser instance for fluent chaining.

@lCMakePathArgumentParser::CMakePathArgu.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakePathArgumentParser::CMakePathArgu.body: It initializes the parser by invoking the base constructor and performs no additional initialization.

@lCMakePathArgumentParser::GetInputs@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakePathArgumentParser::GetInputs@k_Z.body: It returns a const reference to the internal vector, so callers get read‑only access without copying the data. The caller must not modify the vector through that reference; doing so would violate the const qualifier and could break invariants. The reference continues to refer to the actual member, so any subsequent changes to that member are reflected in the returned view.

@lCMakePathArgumentParser::Parse@k_ZNK12.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakePathArgumentParser::Parse@k_ZNK12.body: The `Parse` template clears any previously stored inputs, then feeds the argument vector into a helper parser. It constructs a range over the vector, advances the iterator by the template parameter `Advance` (default 2), and forwards the resulting slice plus the address of its internal `Inputs` container to `cmArgumentParser<Result>::Parse`. The returned value of that helper call is propagated back as the result of `Parse`.

@lCMakeVersion::CMakeVersion@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeVersion::CMakeVersion@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: Creates a new `CMakeVersion` instance by taking an rvalue reference to another `CMakeVersion`, transferring its internal data to the new object.

@lCMakeVersion::CMakeVersion@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeVersion::CMakeVersion@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: Creates a new `CMakeVersion` object that mirrors the state of the supplied instance, duplicating its internal data so the new instance is an exact copy of the source.

@lCR_Next_Choice@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.author: AI Short Overview
@lCR_Next_Choice@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.body: The routine pulls the current field from the form, synchronizes the buffer, then passes the field’s type, itself, and its argument (cast to TypeArgument) to the helper. Depending on the helper’s return it yields E_OK; otherwise E_REQUEST_DENIED.

@lCR_Previous_Choice@p@l./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lCR_Previous_Choice@p@l./Source/CursesD.body: The function receives a form structure, extracts its current field, synchronizes the form’s buffer, and then invokes `Previous_Choice` to determine whether the field’s type and argument satisfy a pre‑condition. It returns `E_OK` if the test succeeds; otherwise it yields `E_REQUEST_DENIED`.

@lChangeRPathELF::[lambda_0]@kChangeRPat.author: AI Short Overview
@lChangeRPathELF::[lambda_0]@kChangeRPat.body: Checks if a path string contains a specific old fragment; if not, it looks for a new fragment instead. When the fragment is found, it builds a new path string by swapping the old fragment with a new one (removing a trailing colon if the fragment ends the string). It returns success status and may set an error message if the old fragment was missing.

@lChangeRPathELF@k_ZL14ChangeRPathELFRKi.author: AI Short Overview
@lChangeRPathELF@k_ZL14ChangeRPathELFRKi.body: The function `ChangeRPathELF` attempts to replace the substring `oldRPath` inside a runtime path string with `newRPath`. It first verifies that the current runtime path contains `oldRPath`; if not, it returns `false` (optionally with an error message). If the replacement would remove an extraneous trailing colon (when `newRPath` is empty and the old path ends the string), it trims that colon. Finally, it constructs the new string by concatenating the unchanged prefix, the `newRPath`, and the suffix after the old path. The operation is performed via a callback handed to `AdjustRPathELF`. On success it sets `changed` to true and returns an empty optional; on failure it returns an optional containing a failure flag.

@lChangeRPathXCOFF@k_ZL16ChangeRPathXCOF.author: AI Short Overview
@lChangeRPathXCOFF@k_ZL16ChangeRPathXCOF.body: The routine opens the supplied XCOFF file, verifies that its current library path still contains the supplied old fragment, then rebuilds the path string by preserving the prefix and suffix surrounding that fragment while inserting the new fragment. It writes the new path back into the file and returns whether the write succeeded, optionally reporting an error message and signalling whether a change actually occurred.

@lCharacterNode::CharacterNode@k_ZN13Cha.author: AI Short Overview
@lCharacterNode::CharacterNode@k_ZN13Cha.body: The constructor initializes a new `CharacterNode` instance with no additional setup—its members remain at their default values until other initialization logic runs.

@lCharacterNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13Charact.author: AI Short Overview
@lCharacterNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13Charact.body: The `Evaluate` function takes a vector of strings plus three pointer arguments, processes them (the details of the processing are hidden in the implementation), and returns a string that, in this simplified snippet, is represented by the placeholder `{ C }`.

@lCharacterNode::NumExpectedParameters@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lCharacterNode::NumExpectedParameters@k.body: It returns 0, indicating that no parameters are expected.

@lChdir@k_Z5ChdirRKNSt3__112basic_string.author: AI Short Overview
@lChdir@k_Z5ChdirRKNSt3__112basic_string.body: The inline wrapper simply forwards a `std::string` argument to the C‑style `chdir` routine, returning whatever integer status that routine produces.

@lCheckGenExParameters@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheckGenExParameters@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The routine validates that the number of supplied parameters matches the expected count. If the count falls short or exceeds the permitted value, it constructs a readable message stating the required number (e.g. “one parameter”, “two parameters”, etc.) and invokes `reportError` with that message before returning `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lCheckListParameters@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheckListParameters@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function forwards the current context, content, option string, and the size of the supplied arguments to `CheckListParametersEx`, returning its boolean result.

@lCheckListParametersEx@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheckListParametersEx@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The `CheckListParametersEx` helper forwards the supplied arguments to `CheckGenExParameters`, supplying the constant string `"LIST"` as the list type and preserving the `exactly` flag. It simply returns the result of that delegated check.

@lCheckPathParameters@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheckPathParameters@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function forwards the call to an internal helper, passing the context, content, option string, the number of supplied arguments (`args.size()`), and the minimum count (`required`). It returns the result of that helper, which determines if the arguments satisfy the expected number and types for the given option.

@lCheckPathParametersEx@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheckPathParametersEx@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: CheckPathParametersEx forwards its arguments to CheckGenExParameters, passing the string “PATH” as the expression type along with the supplied option, count, and flag values. It simply returns whatever result that helper function produces.

@lCheck_AlphaNumeric_Character@p@l./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_AlphaNumeric_Character@p@l./Sour.body: The function simply checks whether the provided integer represents an alphanumeric character. It ignores the second argument and returns `TRUE` when `isalnum(c)` evaluates true, otherwise `FALSE`.

@lCheck_AlphaNumeric_Field@p@l./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_AlphaNumeric_Field@p@l./Source/C.body: The function reads a string from a field buffer, skips leading blanks, then scans a contiguous run of alphabetic‑numeric characters. If the string ends before reaching the required minimum width (or a non‑alnum is encountered), it returns FALSE; otherwise it returns TRUE.

@lCheck_Char@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/fo.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_Char@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/fo.body:
The function walks a type tree supplied in *typ.  
If the node is linked (flag `_LINKED_TYPE`), it recurses on the left and right sub‑trees using the corresponding sub‑arguments.  
If the node provides a custom check routine (`ccheck`), it calls that with the character and argument.  
When no specific check applies, it falls back to a simple printable‑character test (`isprint`).  
Thus the routine returns whether *ch satisfies the type’s condition, propagating the result up the recursion.

@lCheck_Enum_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDia.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_Enum_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDia.body: The routine checks whether the value stored in a field matches one of a supplied list of keywords. It walks through the null‑terminated array pointed to by `kwds`, calling `Compare` on each word until a match is found or the list ends. If a match occurs and, when requested, that match is unique, it fails the uniqueness test and returns FALSE. A successful match sets the field’s buffer to the matched keyword string and returns TRUE. If no keyword matches, the function returns FALSE.

@lCheck_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.body: The `Check_Field` routine validates a field against a type description. It first handles an “allow‑null” flag by trimming leading blanks in the field buffer and accepting an all‑blank string as valid. If the type is a linked type, it recurses into the left and right sub‑types until a leaf is reached. Otherwise, if the type supplies a custom check callback (`fcheck`), that function is invoked; if none is supplied it simply succeeds. If no type is supplied at all, the function returns success.

@lCheck_IPV4_Character@p@l./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_IPV4_Character@p@l./Source/Curse.body: The `Check_IPV4_Character` routine simply determines whether a supplied character code represents a valid IPv4 address token. It accepts an `int` representing a character code, ignores the unused `argp` argument, and returns true only when the character is a decimal digit (`isdigit` succeeds) or the literal period `.`. All other inputs produce a false result.

@lCheck_IPV4_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDia.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_IPV4_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDia.body: Parses the supplied buffer as a dotted‑decimal IPv4 address, verifying the string begins with a digit, that four octets were read by `sscanf`, that none exceed 255, and that no non‑whitespace characters remain after the fourth octet.

@lCheck_Numeric_Character@p@l./Source/Cu.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_Numeric_Character@p@l./Source/Cu.body: The function returns **TRUE** when the supplied character is a digit or a sign character (`+` or `-`) or a locale‑dependent decimal point (the locale’s `decimal_point` if available, otherwise `.`). If the locale field `decimal_point` is not defined or the macro `HAVE_LOCALE_H` is absent, the comparison falls back to `.`. This simple test is used internally to decide whether a character should be treated as part of a numeric literal.

@lCheck_Numeric_Field@p@l./Source/Curses.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_Numeric_Field@p@l./Source/Curses.body: The routine trims leading spaces from a field’s buffer, optionally consumes a sign, reads an optional fractional part (respecting the locale’s decimal separator when available), and stops at the first non‑digit. If the token ends in a NUL it converts the token to a double, checks that value against the supplied low/high limits, and if within bounds rewrites the value into the field buffer formatted to the requested precision and returns success; otherwise it signals failure.

@lCheck_RegularExpression_Field@p@l./Sou.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_RegularExpression_Field@p@l./Sou.body: The routine inspects the supplied field against a regular‑expression object passed in argp. If a compiled pattern is present (via the appropriate build flag), it invokes the library’s matching routine and sets match to true when the field satisfies the expression; otherwise match stays false. The function finally returns this boolean result.

@lChompStrlen@k_ZL11ChompStrlenPKc@p@l./.author: AI Short Overview
@lChompStrlen@k_ZL11ChompStrlenPKc@p@l./.body: The function trims up to two trailing newline or carriage‑return characters before returning the string’s length. It first returns 0 if the pointer is null, then uses `strlen` to get the initial length, and if the last character is `'\n'` or `'\r'` it decrements the length twice (once per each match). This logic can read past the start of the buffer if the input string is empty or consists solely of newline characters, and the cast to unsigned int is unnecessary.

@lCoCompileJob::CoCompileJob@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lCoCompileJob::CoCompileJob@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: Creates a new `CoCompileJob` instance by moving the supplied temporary into the new object, essentially transferring ownership of its internal resources.

@lCoCompileJob::CoCompileJob@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lCoCompileJob::CoCompileJob@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The constructor creates a new job by copying all configuration and state from an existing instance, so that the new `CoCompileJob` is fully configured with the same settings and data.

@lCoCompileJob::CoCompileJob@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lCoCompileJob::CoCompileJob@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: Creates and registers a compile‐time job, wiring up its metadata and placing it in the job scheduler.

@lCodemodel::Codemodel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodel::Codemodel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The constructor accepts an rvalue reference to a `Codemodel` instance, transferring the internal state of the source into the newly created object while leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state.

@lCodemodel::Codemodel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodel::Codemodel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The constructor of `Codemodel` takes a reference to a `cmFileAPI` instance and a `unsigned long` value for the version. It uses an initializer list to store the provided `fileAPI` reference in the member `FileAPI` and assigns the supplied `version` value to the member `Version`. No additional logic is performed within the body of the constructor.

@lCodemodel::Codemodel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodel::Codemodel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The `Codemodel` function is a public copy‑constructor that takes a reference to an existing `Codemodel` object (passed as a named parameter). It creates a new instance that duplicates the internal state of the source object, allowing the object to be copied or returned by value in client code.

@lCodemodel::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_19Cod.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodel::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_19Cod.body: The `Dump` method produces a JSON object that bundles together the current state of the `Codemodel` instance: it inserts the result of `DumpPaths()` under the key `"paths"` and the output of `DumpConfigurations()` under `"configurations"`, then returns that object.

@lCodemodel::DumpConfiguration@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodel::DumpConfiguration@k_ZN12_GL.body: The function creates a `CodemodelConfig` instance with the current `FileAPI`, the object’s `Version`, and the provided `config` string, then calls its `Dump()` method and returns the resulting `Json::Value`. This produces a JSON representation of the configuration for internal use.

@lCodemodel::DumpConfigurations@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodel::DumpConfigurations@k_ZN12_G.body: The method returns a JSON array containing the serialized configuration data of the first makefile that the global CMake generator produces. It pulls that file’s generator configs via `GetGeneratorConfigs`, dumps each one with `DumpConfiguration`, and appends the results to a JSON array that is then returned.

@lCodemodel::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodel::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: It creates and returns a JSON object with the paths of the current CMake instance – the source directory under `"source"` and the output directory under `"build"` – by calling `GetHomeDirectory()` and `GetHomeOutputDirectory()` on that instance.

@lCodemodelConfig::AddProject@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::AddProject@k_ZN12_GLO.body: AddProject first checks whether the supplied snapshot belongs to an existing project by comparing its parent directory and project name. If it matches an existing entry, it simply returns that project's index. If it does not match, the function creates a new project entry, stores the snapshot, links it into the project map, and, when a parent directory exists, attaches the new project as a child of that parent project before returning the new project’s index.

@lCodemodelConfig::CodemodelConfig@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::CodemodelConfig@k_ZN1.body: The constructor creates a new CodemodelConfig instance by taking ownership of another instance’s state, effectively transferring its configuration data into the newly constructed object.

@lCodemodelConfig::CodemodelConfig@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::CodemodelConfig@k_ZN1.body: The constructor registers a `cmFileAPI` instance, records the target build‑output version, and stores the supplied configuration string. It resolves the project’s source and build roots via `FileAPI.GetCMakeInstance()->GetHomeDirectory()` and `GetHomeOutputDirectory()`. A `static_cast<void>(this->Version)` invocation is used only to silence an unused‑parameter warning during construction.

@lCodemodelConfig::CodemodelConfig@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::CodemodelConfig@k_ZN1.body: The constructor copies all configuration parameters from the supplied instance, initializing the new object’s internal state with the values of the original. This includes duplicating basic flags, path settings, and any stored metadata that governs the model’s runtime behavior.

@lCodemodelConfig::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: It assembles a JSON object describing the current configuration: first it records the configuration name, then processes any sub‑directories, and finally inserts the lists of targets, directories, and projects before returning the populated object.

@lCodemodelConfig::DumpDirectories@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::DumpDirectories@k_ZN1.body: It serializes each `Directory` stored in the `Directories` collection into a JSON array and returns that array.

@lCodemodelConfig::DumpDirectory@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::DumpDirectory@k_ZN12_.body: The function assembles a JSON object describing a directory’s snapshot: it records the source and build paths relative to configured roots, the parent directory index if present, a list of child indices, the owning project and any target indices, the required minimum CMake version when applicable, and whether the directory carries an install rule. It returns that JSON value.

@lCodemodelConfig::DumpDirectoryObject@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::DumpDirectoryObject@k.body: The function builds a string prefix that begins with `"directory"`, appends a relative segment derived from the source or build paths (if they aren’t full paths), and replaces path separators with dots. It then appends the current configuration string if present. Using that string it creates a `DirectoryObject` from the directory instance and finally writes the object out via the `FileAPI`, returning the resulting JSON file handle.

@lCodemodelConfig::DumpMinimumCMakeVersi.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::DumpMinimumCMakeVersi.body: The function returns a JSON object containing the value of the `CMAKE_MINIMUM_REQUIRED_VERSION` definition from the snapshot; if that definition is absent, it returns an empty JSON object.

@lCodemodelConfig::DumpProject@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::DumpProject@k_ZN12_GL.body: Serializes a Project into a JSON `Value`, emitting the project’s name, parent index if present, child indices, directory indices, and any target indices that exist.

@lCodemodelConfig::DumpProjects@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::DumpProjects@k_ZN12_G.body: The method iterates over the internal collection of projects, converts each one through a helper, and accumulates the results into a JSON array that it returns.

@lCodemodelConfig::DumpTarget@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::DumpTarget@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The function serialises a target into JSON: it builds a `Target` from the target pointer, sanitises the name string (removing slashes), optionally appends the current config string, writes the resulting JSON via the FileAPI, and finally tags the JSON with its name, ID, directory and project indices while updating the internal mapping tables before returning the JSON value.

@lCodemodelConfig::DumpTargets::[lambda_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::DumpTargets::[lambda_.body: It returns true when the first `cmGeneratorTarget`’s name string is alphabetically before the second’s.

@lCodemodelConfig::DumpTargets@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::DumpTargets@k_ZN12_GL.body: The method walks through the current global generator’s local generators, pulls out each target that belongs to the build‑system (ignoring any “global” targets), orders those targets alphabetically, and then serializes each one into a JSON array which it finally returns.

@lCodemodelConfig::GetDirectoryIndex@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::GetDirectoryIndex@k_Z.body: The function retrieves the array‑index entry stored in `DirectoryMap` for the supplied snapshot key. It locates the element, asserts that it exists, and returns the mapped second member (the stored index).

@lCodemodelConfig::GetDirectoryIndex@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::GetDirectoryIndex@k_Z.body: It returns the array index corresponding to the build‑system directory extracted from the generator’s current state snapshot.

@lCodemodelConfig::ProcessDirectories@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCodemodelConfig::ProcessDirectories@k_.body: The method walks the list of local generators in the order they were created, creates a `Directory` entry for each, stores a mapping from snapshot to its array index, and records the project index that owns that directory. It then iterates over the directories in reverse order, propagating “has‑install‑rule” flags from child directories up to parents: if any child of a directory has an install rule, the parent inherits that flag. The routine does not perform any file I/O; it only builds the in‑memory directory map and flags for install rules.

@lCompare@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompare@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/form/.body:
The routine walks the two strings past any initial blanks, then steps through them in lock‑step.  
If the caller requested case‑insensitive comparison (`ccase` is true), it treats each character in upper‑case form; otherwise the raw bytes are compared.  
When the walk ends, the function returns a single status flag: `EXACT` if every character matched, `PARTIAL` if one string ran out after matching a prefix (blanks at the end are ignored), or `NOMATCH` otherwise.

@lCompileData::CompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileData::CompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: CompileData constructs a new CompileData object by moving its internal state from an existing instance. It performs an efficient transfer of compile metadata without copying, enabling the code to reuse the provided data in subsequent stages.

@lCompileData::CompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileData::CompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: Creates a new instance of CompileData by duplicating all of its internal state from the supplied source object—so that the new instance has the same configuration, data collections and flags as the original.

@lCompileData::CompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileData::CompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: CompileData traverses the in‑memory data structures created by the preceding parsing logic and marshals them into a binary blob that is then persisted to disk. It performs validation of the content, resolves references among the collected objects, and emits diagnostic messages when inconsistencies are detected. The routine is a key entry point for the API’s code‑generation workflow, ensuring that every component of the model is correctly wired before the final archive is emitted.

@lCompileData::IncludeEntry::IncludeEntr.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileData::IncludeEntry::IncludeEntr.body: The constructor initializes an object with the supplied path and flags it as a system entry when requested.

@lCompileFeaturesNode::CompileFeaturesNo.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileFeaturesNode::CompileFeaturesNo.body: CompileFeaturesNode is a lightweight move‑constructor that takes an rvalue reference to an existing CompileFeaturesNode instance, transfers its internal state (including any feature‑flags and associated data) into the newly constructed object, and invokes the base `cmGeneratorExpressionNode` constructor to register the node within the expression tree.

@lCompileFeaturesNode::CompileFeaturesNo.author: AI Short Overview
