@lCompileFeaturesNode::CompileFeaturesNo.body: The `CompileFeaturesNode` constructor creates a new instance by copying the internal state of an existing `CompileFeaturesNode` object. It performs a shallow copy of all member data and re‑initializes any dynamically allocated resources in the new instance, ensuring that the new object is an independent yet equivalent representation of the original. This copy constructor is used throughout the generator to preserve node state when cloning or re‑applying features during expression tree transformations.

@lCompileFeaturesNode::CompileFeaturesNo.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileFeaturesNode::CompileFeaturesNo.body: This constructor initializes a node that represents a feature in the compiler’s feature‑graph. It sets up the node’s internal state (e.g., ID, type, and any semantic flags) so that subsequent passes can query and manipulate the feature graph during code generation.

@lCompileFeaturesNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK19C.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileFeaturesNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK19C.body: The `Evaluate` method validates that a target is present and that each supplied language‑specific feature is supported by the current compiler. It first resolves every feature string with `CompileFeatureKnown`; if any cannot be compiled it reports an error and aborts. It collects all supported features per language, caching them in `availableFeatures` for reuse. For every language it compares the supplied features against the language’s supported list. If a feature is missing, or the compiler cannot provide the required standard level, the function returns `"0"`, signaling failure. If all checks pass, the method returns `"1"`, indicating success.

@lCompileFeaturesNode::NumExpectedParame.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileFeaturesNode::NumExpectedParame.body: The override simply returns the enum value `OneOrMoreParameters`, signalling that the caller must supply at least one argument for the operation.

@lCompileFeaturesNode::operator=@k_ZN19C.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileFeaturesNode::operator=@k_ZN19C.body: The `operator=` function implements a move assignment for `CompileFeaturesNode`. It accepts an rvalue reference to another `CompileFeaturesNode`, efficiently transfers the internal state from the source node to the current instance, and returns a reference to the updated object for fluent chaining.

@lCompileFeaturesNode::operator=@k_ZN19C.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileFeaturesNode::operator=@k_ZN19C.body: The operator= overload copies the contents of a source CompileFeaturesNode into the current instance, performing a member‑wise assignment and returning a reference to the left‑hand side for chaining.

@lCompileFeaturesNode::~CompileFeaturesN.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileFeaturesNode::~CompileFeaturesN.body: The `~CompileFeaturesNode()` function is the class destructor that guarantees any resources acquired by a `CompileFeaturesNode` instance are released correctly when the object is destroyed. It implicitly calls the base‐class destructor of `cmGeneratorExpressionNode` and performs any node‑specific cleanup such as freeing internal data structures or deregistering itself from global registries before the instance is reclaimed.

@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::CompileLangu.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::CompileLangu.body: CompileLanguageAndIdNode creates a node instance that couples a language identifier with an ID token, used during expression generation to represent the language‑specific identifier in the generated code.

@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::CompileLangu.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::CompileLangu.body: The constructor copies the language identifier and any associated metadata from the supplied instance into a new `CompileLanguageAndIdNode` object, then registers this new node in the node‑registry so that it participates correctly in the later code‑generation phases.

@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::CompileLangu.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::CompileLangu.body: The function processes a language descriptor and produces a structured ID node that encapsulates compiled metadata for subsequent use.

@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::Evaluate@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::Evaluate@k_Z.body: The function verifies that the current generator supports a compile‑language construct. It ensures the generator is not one of the unsupported ones (Makefiles, Ninja, Visual Studio, Xcode, Watcom, Green Hills). If the first language argument matches the requested language, it forwards the remaining parameters to a compiler‑specific node via `CompilerIdNode::EvaluateWithLanguage`. Otherwise, it falls back to a generic “0” return.

@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::NumExpectedP.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::NumExpectedP.body: The override signals that this concrete class expects at least two arguments. When invoked, the method returns the `TwoOrMoreParameters` indicator, allowing callers to treat the instance as one that requires a minimum of two inputs and to branch logic accordingly.

@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::operator=@k_.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to another `CompileLanguageAndIdNode`, moves its internal data into the current instance, and then returns a reference to the updated object.

@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::operator=@k_.body: The assignment operator takes a `CompileLanguageAndIdNode` instance and copies its internal state into the target object, updating member fields (e.g., language ID, node type, and any context pointers) while ensuring proper ownership semantics. It returns a reference to the left‑hand side to allow chaining of assignments.

@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::~CompileLang.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageAndIdNode::~CompileLang.body: The `~CompileLanguageAndIdNode` function is a helper that glues together a language identifier node with its associated language context during the AST generation phase. It essentially takes an `IdNode` and a language tag, validates that the identifier matches the current language configuration, and then produces a `CompileLanguageAndIdNode` instance that is subsequently used by the code generator to emit the correct language‑specific code paths. This helper keeps the language‑specific handling separate from the generic node creation logic, ensuring that any node that needs language awareness goes through a single, well‑defined entry point.

@lCompileLanguageNode::CompileLanguageNo.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageNode::CompileLanguageNo.body: The `CompileLanguageNode` function takes an rvalue reference (likely to a temporary node object) and constructs a new `CompileLanguageNode` instance. It initializes that instance with the supplied data and returns the freshly‑created node for insertion into the expression‑generation hierarchy.

@lCompileLanguageNode::CompileLanguageNo.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageNode::CompileLanguageNo.body: The `CompileLanguageNode` constructor takes a reference to an existing `CompileLanguageNode` (typically a temporary copy) and initializes a new instance that inherits from `cmGeneratorExpressionNode`. It is typically used when the compiler emits a language‑specific node into the AST during the code‑generation phase, ensuring that the new node carries over any state required by the parent expression‑generator base class.

@lCompileLanguageNode::CompileLanguageNo.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageNode::CompileLanguageNo.body: The function takes a language‑node structure, applies the language‑specific compilation steps (parsing, normalising, type‑checking, and code‑generation), and emits the resulting bytecode or intermediate form. It also contains a lint suppression comment that prevents a modern‑C++ default‑equals linting warning.

@lCompileLanguageNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK19C.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK19C.body: Checks the supplied language against the current generator and returns a status string. It first ensures the language is explicitly set and that the generator can be evaluated. If the generator is unsupported it emits an error and exits. When no parameters are given it simply echoes the current language. For each provided parameter it returns `"1"` if it matches the current language; otherwise it falls back to `"0"`.

@lCompileLanguageNode::NumExpectedParame.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageNode::NumExpectedParame.body: This member simply returns the constant `ZeroOrMoreParameters`, indicating the call‑site accepts any number of parameters (including zero) without imposing a fixed requirement.

@lCompileLanguageNode::operator=@k_ZN19C.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageNode::operator=@k_ZN19C.body: The `operator=` overload takes an rvalue reference to a `CompileLanguageNode`, moves its contents into the current instance and returns a reference to `*this`. It performs an in‑place copy/move of the node data, ensuring the left‑hand side holds the new node after the call.

@lCompileLanguageNode::operator=@k_ZN19C.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageNode::operator=@k_ZN19C.body: The overloaded assignment operator copies the contents of the source node into the current object and returns a reference to that object, enabling chainable assignments in the node‑generation logic.

@lCompileLanguageNode::~CompileLanguageN.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileLanguageNode::~CompileLanguageN.body: The `~CompileLanguageNode()` method is invoked during the code‑generation phase for nodes that represent language‑specific language constructs. It performs the heavy lifting of a semantic node into its concrete output form: it resolves the node’s type, emits the correct syntax fragment for the target language, and attaches any required declarations or helper code. Its job is to bridge the internal node representation to the final textual representation that will be emitted by the generator.

@lCompileOnlyNode::CompileOnlyNode@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileOnlyNode::CompileOnlyNode@k_ZN1.body: The `CompileOnlyNode` constructor takes an rvalue reference to another `CompileOnlyNode` and initializes the new instance by stealing the underlying data from the source. This pattern guarantees efficient construction—no deep copies are performed, and the temporary object can be safely discarded after the move.

@lCompileOnlyNode::CompileOnlyNode@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileOnlyNode::CompileOnlyNode@k_ZN1.body: The constructor creates a new `CompileOnlyNode` by copying the internal state of an existing instance—primarily duplicating the node’s expression data and any associated flags so the new node behaves exactly like the original when used in expression generation.

@lCompileOnlyNode::CompileOnlyNode@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileOnlyNode::CompileOnlyNode@k_ZN1.body: The constructor creates a new CompileOnlyNode instance without initializing any members, relying on the default construction state. It uses the `NOLINT(modernize-use-equals-default)` annotation to silence a lint warning about modernizing constructors with default member initializers, ensuring the code passes the linter unchanged.

@lCompileOnlyNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK15Compi.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileOnlyNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK15Compi.body: The function checks whether a D‑AG checker is present. If it isn’t, it reports an error about a “compile‑only” construct and returns an empty string. When the checker indicates that only transitive properties are in play, it returns the first string from the supplied parameters vector; otherwise it also returns an empty string.

@lCompileOnlyNode::operator=@k_ZN15Compi.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileOnlyNode::operator=@k_ZN15Compi.body: The assignment operator accepts an rvalue reference to a `CompileOnlyNode` and moves its contents into the current instance, returning a reference to that instance. It is used to chain assignments without copying, enabling efficient construction of “compile‑only” expression nodes that should never be evaluated at runtime.

@lCompileOnlyNode::operator=@k_ZN15Compi.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileOnlyNode::operator=@k_ZN15Compi.body: The `operator=` function takes a `CompileOnlyNode` instance and copies its internal state into the current object, returning a reference to the modified instance. It performs a straightforward assignment (deep or shallow copy, depending on the member fields) and is used throughout the codebase where `CompileOnlyNode` objects are reassigned.

@lCompileOnlyNode::~CompileOnlyNode@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lCompileOnlyNode::~CompileOnlyNode@k_ZN.body: ~CompileOnlyNode() is the destructor for the CompileOnlyNode struct. It runs automatically when an instance is destroyed, ensuring its members and any allocated resources are cleaned up—typically delegating to the base destructor chain.

@lCompilerIdNode::CompilerIdNode@k_ZN14C.author: AI Short Overview

If the field is finished and not growable it will try to auto‑skip to the next field; otherwise it advances to the next character. The function returns E_OK on success, E_REQUEST_DENIED if the field cannot accept the character, or E_SYSTEM_ERROR if field growth fails.

@lDebGenerator::DebGenerator@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: DebGenerator implements a move‑constructor that takes an rvalue reference to another DebGenerator instance. It simply transfers internal state (buffers, handles, etc.) from the temporary object to the newly created one, allowing efficient in‑place construction without deep copying. The constructor should guard against self‑move and ensure any resources are correctly reset in the source after the transfer.

@lDebGenerator::DebGenerator@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::DebGenerator@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: DebGenerator initializes its internal state from the supplied arguments. It maps the specified compression type to an appropriate suffix and tar‑archive enum, and defaults to “gzip” if none is provided. It then parses the thread count string, falling back to a single thread on parsing failure. The constructor also stores all control values and flags for later processing.

@lDebGenerator::DebGenerator@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::DebGenerator@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: DebGenerator(const DebGenerator& other) constructs a new DebGenerator instance by copying the configuration and state from the provided instance.

@lDebGenerator::DebGenerator@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::DebGenerator@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: DebGenerator initializes a Deb object, configures its internal state from supplied parameters, and returns the ready‑to‑use instance.

@lDebGenerator::generate@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::generate@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL_.body: Invokes a chain of helper methods in order: first it creates a binary and a control file, then attempts to build a data‑tar; any failure in that step aborts early and returns false. Afterward it produces an md5 file, uses that name to create a second control tar, and, if all steps succeed, finally delegates to generateDeb() returning its boolean result.

@lDebGenerator::generateControlFile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::generateControlFile@k_ZN.body: The method writes a `control` file in the instance’s working directory, serialising each entry from the `ControlValues` map as “key: value” lines. After dumping those pairs, it totals the byte sizes of all files listed in `PackageFiles`, converts that sum into kilobytes (by adding 1023 and dividing by 1024 to round up), and appends the resulting value as an “Installed‑Size” line before closing the file.

@lDebGenerator::generateControlTar@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::generateControlTar@k_ZNK.body: The function opens a temporary “control.tar.gz” file in the working directory and creates a Debian‑style control archive. It sets ownership to root, establishes the standard 644 (or 755 for executable scripts) permissions, and populates the archive with the mandatory control files (“control”, “md5sum”) and any optional add‑ons (shlibs, post‑install, post‑remove, and user‑specified extras). Each addition is verified, and any failure is logged; otherwise the routine returns success.

@lDebGenerator::generateDataTar@k_ZNK12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::generateDataTar@k_ZNK12_.body: The routine opens a file stream for “data.tar”, creates a `cmArchiveWrite` instance, sets the archive’s UID/GID to root, and then walks through every file in `PackageFiles`. For each file it derives the relative path, applies any stored permissions (or a default 0755 for directories), and adds the file to the archive. If any step fails, it logs an error and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lDebGenerator::generateDeb@k_ZNK12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::generateDeb@k_ZNK12_GLOB.body: The function builds a Debian .deb file by creating an ar‑style archive. It opens the destination file, writes the three archive entries (the binary package, the control archive, and the data archive), and then records the root ownership attributes. If any file‑write or archive‑open step fails, an error is logged and the function returns false; otherwise it finishes successfully and returns true.

@lDebGenerator::generateDebianBinaryFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::generateDebianBinaryFile.body: Creates a file called debian‑binary inside the current work directory, opens it for writing, and writes the line “2.0\n” to the file. The function is declared const, so it does not modify any member data, and it does not perform error checking or verify the stream state after writing.

@lDebGenerator::generateMD5File@k_ZNK12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::generateMD5File@k_ZNK12_.body:
The function writes a “md5sums” file in the build directory.  
It iterates over `PackageFiles`, skips directories and symlinks, computes an MD5 hash for each regular file, strips the temporary‑directory prefix from the path, writes a line in the format “\<hash>  <relative‑path>”, and finally returns the full path to the created file.

@lDebGenerator::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference of `DebGenerator`, copies or moves its internal state into the current object, and returns a reference to that object, enabling chainable assignments and efficient ownership transfer.

@lDebGenerator::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lDebGenerator::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state from the supplied `DebGenerator` argument into the current object and returns `*this`. It performs a deep copy of any owned resources (e.g., vectors, pointers, or handles) and guards against self‑assignment, ensuring that the object remains in a valid state after the operation.

@lDefer::Defer@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_15DeferC.author: AI Short Overview
@lDefer::Defer@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_15DeferC.body: Defer constructs a lightweight “deferred‑action” object that stores a callable and invokes it automatically when the object goes out of scope, enabling a clean “execute‑on‑destruct” pattern for one‑shot cleanup logic.

@lDefer::Defer@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_15DeferC.author: AI Short Overview
@lDefer::Defer@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_15DeferC.body: `Defer` is a small RAII‑style helper that accepts a callable and stores it until the object’s destructor runs. When the surrounding scope ends, the stored callable is invoked, allowing code to attach a deferred action (like a cleanup or reset) without scattering explicit cleanup logic throughout the code. It is typically used in places such as the `cmCMakeLanguageCommand.cxx` line 57 context to guarantee that temporary changes (e.g., of state or resources) are automatically undone when the function returns.

@lDefer::Defer@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_15DeferC.author: AI Short Overview
@lDefer::Defer@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_15DeferC.body: Defer registers a cleanup action that is automatically executed when the guard object goes out of scope. It typically stores a callback inside a helper struct and invokes it in the struct’s destructor, allowing deferred cleanup in a RAII‑style manner.

@lDeviceLinkNode::DeviceLinkNode@k_ZN14D.author: AI Short Overview
@lDeviceLinkNode::DeviceLinkNode@k_ZN14D.body: The constructor for `DeviceLinkNode` takes an rvalue reference to another `DeviceLinkNode` and performs a move‑semantics transfer of its internal state. It copies over the constituent members (e.g. device identifiers, linkage flags, and any shared‑resource handles) from the source object into the new instance, leaving the source in a safe‑to‑destroy state. No deep copying is performed; the move simply swaps pointers or references so that the new node owns the resources that were originally owned by the source. This facilitates efficient re‑use of already‑parsed linkage information when building or transforming the syntax tree.

@lDeviceLinkNode::DeviceLinkNode@k_ZN14D.author: AI Short Overview
@lDeviceLinkNode::DeviceLinkNode@k_ZN14D.body: DeviceLinkNode is a copy constructor that creates a new `DeviceLinkNode` instance by copying the state of an existing one. It’s used when an existing node needs to be duplicated during expression tree manipulation.

@lDeviceLinkNode::DeviceLinkNode@k_ZN14D.author: AI Short Overview
@lDeviceLinkNode::DeviceLinkNode@k_ZN14D.body: Creates a new `DeviceLinkNode` instance, setting up its internal state (including default flags and pointers) so the node is ready to participate in a device‑linking relationship.

@lDeviceLinkNode::Evaluate::[lambda_0]@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lDeviceLinkNode::Evaluate::[lambda_0]@k.body: The lambda simply checks whether an element equals `DL_BEGIN` or `DL_END`; if so, it returns `true`, causing `cm::erase_if` to remove that element from `list`.

@lDeviceLinkNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK14Device.author: AI Short Overview
@lDeviceLinkNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK14Device.body: The routine first verifies that the current target can accept link options; if the pre‑conditions fail it reports an error and returns an empty string. When the target is a device link it strips any existing `<DEVICE_LINK>` markers from the supplied list of parameters, re‑inserts those markers at the start and end of the list, and returns the concatenated string.

@lDeviceLinkNode::NumExpectedParameters@.author: AI Short Overview
@lDeviceLinkNode::NumExpectedParameters@.body: The function simply returns the constant ZeroOrMoreParameters, indicating that the caller accepts any number (including zero) of parameters and that the result is unaffected by mutation.

@lDeviceLinkNode::operator=@k_ZN14Device.author: AI Short Overview
@lDeviceLinkNode::operator=@k_ZN14Device.body: The assignment operator for `DeviceLinkNode` moves the contents of a temporary rvalue into the target node, efficiently transferring ownership of the underlying resources without copying. This enables a fluent interface where a `DeviceLinkNode` can be constructed or reassigned from a move‑only temporary, maintaining move‑semantic semantics while preserving the internal state of the node.

@lDeviceLinkNode::operator=@k_ZN14Device.author: AI Short Overview
@lDeviceLinkNode::operator=@k_ZN14Device.body: The `operator=` overload copies the internal state of the right‑hand `DeviceLinkNode` into the left‑hand object and returns a reference to the updated object. It performs a shallow field‑by‑field copy (including any nested pointers or handles), guarding against self‑assignment, and ensures that the source node’s ownership semantics are respected before returning the lvalue reference.

@lDeviceLinkNode::~DeviceLinkNode@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lDeviceLinkNode::~DeviceLinkNode@k_ZN14.body: The destructor for `DeviceLinkNode` releases any owned resources (e.g. pointers to linked nodes or allocated buffers) and then invokes the base‑class cleanup. It guarantees that when a `DeviceLinkNode` instance goes out of scope, its internal connections are cleanly severed and no stray pointers remain.

@lDiagnoseAncientPolicies@k_ZL23Diagnose.author: AI Short Overview
@lDiagnoseAncientPolicies@k_ZL23Diagnose.body: The function scans the list of legacy‑style policies required by the current project and builds a single diagnostic string that explains why each policy is incompatible with the active CMake version. It then emits a fatal‑level message telling the user that the project must either be updated to the newer policy API or run with an older CMake that still supports the old behavior.

@lDirectoryObject::AddBacktrace@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::AddBacktrace@k_ZN12_G.body: The method appends a new back‑trace record to the object’s internal list, then captures that record’s assigned index and writes it into the supplied JSON value under the key “backtrace”.

@lDirectoryObject::DirectoryObject@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::DirectoryObject@k_ZN1.body: DirectoryObject is a public constructor that initializes a directory‑level object from a temporary or move‑constructed instance, essentially transferring ownership of any internal resources without altering the object's state. It typically accepts a reference to an unnamed temporary of the same type and copies or moves its internal data structures into the new instance, ensuring that the original is left in a valid but unspecified state.

@lDirectoryObject::DirectoryObject@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::DirectoryObject@k_ZN1.body: Stores the supplied arguments in member variables and initializes the internal paths: it sets TopSource and TopBuild from the generator’s home directories, then creates the Backtraces helper using TopSource.

@lDirectoryObject::DirectoryObject@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::DirectoryObject@k_ZN1.body: The constructor duplicates the internal state of the supplied `DirectoryObject` instance—copying its directory path, any stored entries, and associated metadata while preserving ownership semantics.

@lDirectoryObject::DirectoryObject@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::DirectoryObject@k_ZN1.body: Creates an in‑memory representation of a directory tree, wiring up internal structures such as the root path, the entry list and lookup maps. It validates incoming parameters, allocates the necessary buffers, and registers the object with the global registry so that other subsystems can enumerate, read or modify the directory contents through the standard interface.

@lDirectoryObject::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: Creates a JSON object containing the directory’s paths, installers, and backtrace graph.

@lDirectoryObject::DumpInstaller@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::DumpInstaller@k_ZN12_.body: The function serializes an install generator into a JSON object. It first checks the generator type via `dynamic_cast` and, depending on the specific subclass (e.g. target, file, directory, export, script, runtime dependency set, file‑set, or C++ module B‑MI), it populates a set of fields describing that installer: type, destination, optional flag, and the list of paths (sometimes with renames). It skips installers that are sub‑directories or runtime‑dependent artifacts. Finally it tags common metadata such as component and exclusion flags before returning the built JSON object.

@lDirectoryObject::DumpInstallerExportTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::DumpInstallerExportTa.body: The method walks through each target in the supplied export set, builds a JSON object containing that target’s id and its assigned index, and returns a JSON array of those objects.

@lDirectoryObject::DumpInstallerPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::DumpInstallerPath@k_Z.body: It computes the relative path from a given top directory to a source path. If the destination path is identical to the source, it returns that single path; otherwise it returns a JSON object mapping `"from"` to the relative path and `"to"` to the target path.

@lDirectoryObject::DumpInstallers@k_ZN12.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::DumpInstallers@k_ZN12.body: This method assembles a JSON array of installer objects. It iterates over every install‑generator returned by the makefile, calls `DumpInstaller` on each, and if the resulting JSON value is non‑empty it appends it to a `Json::arrayValue`. Finally it returns the populated array.

@lDirectoryObject::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lDirectoryObject::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: This method builds and returns a JSON object containing two relative paths: the current source directory under the top‑source prefix and the current binary directory under the top‑build prefix.

@lDisplay_Or_Erase_Field@p@l./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lDisplay_Or_Erase_Field@p@l./Source/Cur.body:
The routine receives a pointer to a field structure and a flag that indicates whether the field should be cleared.  
It first verifies the argument, obtains the form’s underlying window, and creates a derived window positioned at the field’s row/column coordinates.  
If the field is marked visible, the function applies the pre‑set attributes; otherwise it copies the form window’s current attributes onto the new window.  
After that, it erases the window to hide the field.  
When the erase flag is not set, the function repopulates the window with the field’s value—either re‑justifying text that fits the field width or, if justification is not permitted, writing the buffer content directly into the window.  
Finally, the window is synchronized and then destroyed, returning success or a system error code.

@lDown_Neighbour_Field@p@l./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lDown_Neighbour_Field@p@l./Source/Curse.body: The routine returns the field that comes immediately below the supplied one in the page layout, advancing to the first field on the next line (or, if the field is already at the line’s end, to the first field of that line).

@lDumpCTestInfo@k_ZL13DumpCTestInfoR14cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpCTestInfo@k_ZL13DumpCTestInfoR14cm.body: The function serialises a test run into a JSON value: it first sets the test name, conditionally adds the config and full command array when present, then embeds the exported property values, and finally attaches any back‑trace data. The result is a flat JSON object ready for downstream use.

@lDumpCTestProperties@k_ZL19DumpCTestPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpCTestProperties@k_ZL19DumpCTestPro.body: It walks through each field of `testProperties` and appends any non‑empty or otherwise relevant values into a JSON array, using helper utilities to format the individual entries.

@lDumpCTestProperty@k_ZL17DumpCTestPrope.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpCTestProperty@k_ZL17DumpCTestPrope.body: The function packages a given name and value into a JSON‐style object, moving the value into the resulting structure so that no copy of the payload is performed.

@lDumpFile@k_ZL8DumpFileRKNSt3__112basic.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpFile@k_ZL8DumpFileRKNSt3__112basic.body: The routine opens a file by name, checks whether it is an executable (by inspecting the DOS header). If it is a raw COFF/LLVM object it runs a helper object‑dump routine that walks the file’s symbol table and inserts any found symbols into the supplied sets. It returns false when the file is an executable, when a mapping fails, or the header is unrecognised; otherwise it succeeds and returns true.

@lDumpFileWithLlvmNm@k_ZL18DumpFileWithL.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpFileWithLlvmNm@k_ZL18DumpFileWithL.body: The routine builds a command vector, invokes llvm‑nm, and parses its output line‑by‑line, inserting each symbol into either the data or normal symbol set according to the leading type indicator.

@lDumpMeasurementToJsonArray@k_ZL26DumpM.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpMeasurementToJsonArray@k_ZL26DumpM.body: The function walks through the supplied map, creates a JSON object for each entry with the keys “measurement” and “value”, and appends each object to a JSON array that is finally returned.

@lDumpRegExToJsonArray@k_ZL20DumpRegExTo.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpRegExToJsonArray@k_ZL20DumpRegExTo.body: The function creates a JSON array containing only the string parts of each pair in the input vector, returning that array.

@lDumpResourceGroupsToJsonArray@k_ZL29Du.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpResourceGroupsToJsonArray@k_ZL29Du.body: The function walks a two‑level vector of `cmCTestTestResourceRequirement`s, builds a JSON array where each group is an object that contains a “requirements” array. Each requirement object records its type and the number of slots needed, dropping any unit information that was commented out. The result is returned as a `Json::Value` representing the full list of resource groups.

@lDumpTimeoutAfterMatch@k_ZL21DumpTimeou.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpTimeoutAfterMatch@k_ZL21DumpTimeou.body: The function builds a JSON object that contains two fields: `timeout`, populated with the count of `AlternateTimeout` entries in the supplied properties, and `regex`, populated by converting the regular‑expression list to a JSON array. It returns this JSON value.

@lDumpToJsonArray@k_ZL15DumpToJsonArrayR.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpToJsonArray@k_ZL15DumpToJsonArrayR.body: Creates a JSON array by iterating through each string in the supplied vector and appending the value to a Json::Value array, then returns that array.

@lDumpVersion@k_ZL11DumpVersionii@p@l./S.author: AI Short Overview
@lDumpVersion@k_ZL11DumpVersionii@p@l./S.body: The function builds and returns a JSON object containing the supplied `major` and `minor` fields.

@lEM_Insert_Mode@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.author: AI Short Overview
@lEM_Insert_Mode@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.body: The routine clears the “over‑limit” flag in the supplied form structure and then signals success.

@lEM_Overlay_Mode@p@l./Source/CursesDial.author: AI Short Overview
@lEM_Overlay_Mode@p@l./Source/CursesDial.body: It sets the overlay‑mode bit in the form’s status field and returns success.

@lEnforceUnknownArguments@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lEnforceUnknownArguments@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function checks whether an unknown argument can be tolerated for the current CMake installation. It first verifies that a list of unknown arguments is non‑empty, then parses a supplied maximum version string into four components (major, minor, patch, tweak). If the current CMake version is at least equal to or newer than that maximum, it accepts the unknown argument; otherwise it records an error in the status object and returns false.

@lEnsureStdPipe@k_ZL13EnsureStdPipei@p@l.author: AI Short Overview
@lEnsureStdPipe@k_ZL13EnsureStdPipei@p@l.body: The routine checks whether the given descriptor is still open; if it isn’t, it opens `/dev/null` in the matching direction (read for stdin, write for stdout/stderr) and then replaces the original descriptor with that new one.

@lEnsureTrailingSlash@k_ZL19EnsureTraili.author: AI Short Overview
@lEnsureTrailingSlash@k_ZL19EnsureTraili.body: The function appends a slash to `path` only when the string is non‑empty and already lacks a trailing slash. It uses the preprocessor macro `_WIN32` to decide whether to add a back‑slash (Windows) or a forward‑slash (Unix‑like). It does not handle or normalise existing slashes; it simply checks the last character and appends a slash if different.

@lEntryIsContextSensitive@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lEntryIsContextSensitive@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: It returns whether the supplied `cmCompiledGeneratorExpression` instance reports that it contains a context‑sensitive condition flag.

@lEnvironmentHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lEnvironmentHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function returns whether a JSON value is null or a string and sets an optional string accordingly; if the value is neither, it reports an error and returns false.

@lEqualNode::EqualNode@k_ZN9EqualNodeC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lEqualNode::EqualNode@k_ZN9EqualNodeC1E.body: The constructor creates a new `EqualNode` by moving the contents of an existing one—copying its internal state (like member pointers and flags) into the new object while leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state.

@lEqualNode::EqualNode@k_ZN9EqualNodeC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lEqualNode::EqualNode@k_ZN9EqualNodeC1E.body: EqualNode compares two expression nodes to determine if they represent the same logical value or structure, returning true when the nodes are identical in content and structure.

@lEqualNode::EqualNode@k_ZN9EqualNodeC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lEqualNode::EqualNode@k_ZN9EqualNodeC1E.body: The `EqualNode` routine is a public member that receives two tree node objects and returns a boolean indicating whether the two nodes contain identical data (e.g., same value, same children). It performs a shallow comparison (typically just member‑wise equality) and is deliberately kept simple so the function can be inlined or inlined in test harnesses. The comment `// NOLINT(modernize-use-equals-default)` is a lin‑t suppression that tells the static analysis tool to ignore the rule that would normally recommend using a default‑argument form for `operator==`. In short: the function just compares two nodes for equality.

@lEqualNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK9EqualNode8Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lEqualNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK9EqualNode8Ev.body: The function parses two string parameters into integers, checks for parsing errors, and returns `"1"` when the parsed values are equal, otherwise it returns `"0"`.

@lEqualNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lEqualNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_ZNK.body: Returns the numeric count of parameters this type expects—hard‑coded to **2**. The method is `const` and `override`, signalling that it implements an interface contract without modifying state.

@lEqualNode::ParameterToLong@k_ZN9EqualN.author: AI Short Overview
@lEqualNode::ParameterToLong@k_ZN9EqualN.body: The function checks whether the input string begins with a binary prefix (0b or 0B, optionally preceded by a sign). It determines the numeric base accordingly, then calls strtol to convert the remaining string to a long. If the conversion fails, overflowed, or the string contains trailing junk, the function returns false. Otherwise it stores the parsed value in *outResult and returns true, adjusting the sign if necessary.

@lEqualNode::operator=@k_ZN9EqualNodeaSE.author: AI Short Overview
@lEqualNode::operator=@k_ZN9EqualNodeaSE.body: The function overloads the assignment operator for `EqualNode`. It accepts an rvalue reference to another `EqualNode`, moves its internal state into the target object, and returns a reference to the modified instance. This enables efficient assignment without deep copies, preserving the node’s semantics while ensuring the object remains in a valid state after the move.

@lEqualNode::operator=@k_ZN9EqualNodeaSE.author: AI Short Overview
@lEqualNode::operator=@k_ZN9EqualNodeaSE.body: The assignment operator copies the state of another `EqualNode` into the current instance – copying each member (likely the underlying expression components) – and then returns a reference to the object itself. It performs a safe self‑assignment check and ensures that all fields are correctly replicated.

@lEqualNode::~EqualNode@k_ZN9EqualNodeD1.author: AI Short Overview
@lEqualNode::~EqualNode@k_ZN9EqualNodeD1.body: When an `EqualNode` instance goes out of scope, its destructor (`~EqualNode()`) is invoked. It takes care of any dynamically allocated resources tied to the node, clears internal state (e.g., resetting pointers or reference counters), and guarantees that the base class destructor (`cmGeneratorExpressionNode`) runs. In short, it performs the standard cleanup needed when a node object is destroyed.

@lEscapeArg@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_19EscapeArg.author: AI Short Overview
@lEscapeArg@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_19EscapeArg.body: The routine walks through the supplied string and builds a new string in which every semicolon is prefixed with a back‑slash, yielding a version of the text that can be safely used in contexts where a plain semicolon would otherwise terminate a list.

@lEvaluateComment@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluateComment@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ev.body: The function `EvaluateComment` takes a C‑style string containing a comment, a generator expression object, a local generator pointer, and a configuration string. It parses the comment via the generator expression’s `Parse` method to obtain a compiled generator expression and immediately invokes that expression’s `Evaluate` method with the local generator and configuration. The returned string is the result of that evaluation.

@lEvaluateDepends@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluateDepends@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ev.body: The routine collects all dependency paths generated by **EvaluateSplitConfigGenex** for each supplied path, normalises them to a canonical path format (full‑path collapse or Unix‑style slash normalisation), and returns the resulting list.

@lEvaluateDepfile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluateDepfile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ev.body: The function parses a generator expression from the supplied path and immediately evaluates it against the provided local generator and configuration, returning the textual result of that evaluation.

@lEvaluateOutputs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluateOutputs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ev.body: The routine walks the supplied path list, parses each entry into a compiled generator expression via the provided expression parser, then hands that result to the supplied local‑generator instance to expand any custom‑output directives using the supplied config string; the resulting string paths are accumulated into and returned as a vector.

@lEvaluateSplitConfigGenex@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluateSplitConfigGenex@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function walks through an input string, detecting markers of the form $<…>, handling nested markers by counting levels, and for each found expression it selects the correct configuration string (command or output) based on a COMMAND_CONFIG or OUTPUT_CONFIG prefix, if present). It parses the expression into a compiled generator expression, evaluates it with the chosen configuration, and, when requested, records the generator targets that were referenced during that evaluation. The output is the concatenated result of all evaluated sub‑expressions.

@lEvaluateTargetPropertyEntries@k_Z29Eva.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluateTargetPropertyEntries@k_Z29Eva.body: It iterates over the supplied vector of property entries, invoking EvaluateTargetPropertyEntry on each one and collecting the resulting evaluated entries in a newly‑created EvaluatedTargetPropertyEntries object, which is then returned.

@lEvaluateTargetPropertyEntry@k_Z27Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluateTargetPropertyEntry@k_Z27Evalu.body: The function builds an `EvaluatedTargetPropertyEntry` from the supplied `TargetPropertyEntry`. It calls `entry.Evaluate` (via `cmExpandList`) to fill `ee.Values`, then marks `ee.ContextDependent` if the entry has a context‑sensitive condition, and finally returns that populated entry.

@lEvaluatedTargetPropertyEntries::Evalua.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluatedTargetPropertyEntries::Evalua.body: The `EvaluatedTargetPropertyEntries` helper is a thin wrapper that takes an `EvaluatedTargetPropertyEntries` value (or rvalue) and materialises the internal container of property entries for a target property instance. It simply extracts the underlying list of entries from the passed object and returns that list, enabling callers to enumerate or manipulate the target property’s entries without exposing the internal storage directly.

@lEvaluatedTargetPropertyEntries::Evalua.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluatedTargetPropertyEntries::Evalua.body: The function iterates over a set of target property entries, applies the relevant evaluation logic, and returns a structured collection of the evaluated results. It’s used to transform raw entry data into a canonical form for downstream use.

@lEvaluatedTargetPropertyEntry::Evaluate.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluatedTargetPropertyEntry::Evaluate.body:
The move constructor automatically transfers ownership of all internal members to a new instance without copying, allowing the object to be relocated efficiently.  
It simply performs a shallow copy of the member fields, leaving the moved‑from object in a valid but unspecified state.  
No extra logic or resource cleanup is performed beyond what the compiler generates by defaulting the move constructor.

@lEvaluatedTargetPropertyEntry::Evaluate.author: AI Short Overview
@lEvaluatedTargetPropertyEntry::Evaluate.body: The constructor takes a `cmLinkImplItem` reference and a back‑trace list, forwards the item to its base class (`LinkImplItem`) and stores the back‑trace in the member `Backtrace` via `std::move`.

@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.body: The function recursively expands macro placeholders in a preset into the graph’s environment. It first maps each environment entry to an unvisited cycle state, prepares a default and an environment‑specific macro expander, then iterates over each environment variable: if it matches the “env” namespace it evaluates the corresponding value (including environment variables or preset‑specific data) using the expander chain; if any macro fails it aborts with an error or condition failure. After all variables are resolved, any preset condition is evaluated; if true the expanded preset is attached to the graph, otherwise the result is discarded. The function returns `true` on success or `false` on failure.

@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.body: The routine walks through the optional output configuration, invoking the CHECK_EXPAND helper on each field that may contain macro expressions. It resolves those expressions with the supplied macro expander list, supplying the current graph version when needed. If every required expansion succeeds, it returns true; otherwise the routine halts and returns false.

@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.body: The routine walks through the preset’s targets and native‑tool options, invoking the macro expansion logic supplied in the `macroExpanders` vector and applying the graph‑derived version information. On completing both passes it simply returns `true`.

@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.body: The `ExpandMacros` routine walks through every variable in the preset it is given, applying each registered macro expander to replace placeholders with concrete values derived from the graph’s version data. It also applies the same logic to the preset’s own configuration fields (config file name, package name, version, directory, vendor name). If every expansion succeeds, it returns `true`; otherwise it aborts early by returning `false`.

@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.body: The routine walks through a preset’s macro list, uses each supplied `MacroExpander` to resolve the macro into concrete workflow steps, and writes the expanded form into the `out` optional reference; it returns `true` to indicate success (no failure paths are coded).

@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpandMacros@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Expan.body: The function resolves relative directories in a preset (binary, install, and tool‑chain paths), normalises path separators, and then walks each preset variable, applying any supplied macro‑expander to produce expanded values that are stored in the output preset.

@lExpressionParser::ExpressionParser@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpressionParser::ExpressionParser@k_Z.body: The constructor stores the input string as the expression to be parsed, sets the separator token to a semicolon and builds a regular‑expression object that recognizes Windows‑registry path patterns (HKCU, HKLM, HKCR, HKCLASSES_, HKCC, HKU, HKROOT etc.) so the parser can split an input string into registry tokens.

@lExpressionParser::ExpressionParser@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpressionParser::ExpressionParser@k_Z.body: The constructor accepts an rvalue reference to another `ExpressionParser` instance, performing a move of its internal state (likely its token buffer, parse tree, and any associated resources) into the newly created object. This enables efficient transfer of ownership without deep copying of parsed expression data.

@lExpressionParser::ExpressionParser@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpressionParser::ExpressionParser@k_Z.body: ExpressionParser is a copy constructor that creates a new instance by duplicating an existing parser’s internal state. It performs a deep copy of tokens, grammar rules, and any allocated resources so the new object has the same parsing context. The function is invoked whenever a parser must be cloned—e.g., to preserve state before a recursive parse or when a component requests a fresh parser with the same configuration.

@lExpressionParser::Find@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpressionParser::Find@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: Find parses the expression against a pre‑configured registry format, extracting the root key, sub‑key, and an optional value name. It uses zero‑copy string_views and treats the string “(default)” as a special marker that clears the value name. The routine verifies the presence of a separator before performing any slice operations and signals success by returning a bool.

@lExpressionParser::operator=@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpressionParser::operator=@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The move‑assignment operator takes an rvalue of type ExpressionParser, transfers its internal state into *this, and returns a reference to the modified object, enabling chaining of assignments.

@lExpressionParser::operator=@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lExpressionParser::operator=@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The `operator=` function is the copy‑assignment operator for `ExpressionParser`. It copies all internal state from the right‑hand side object into the left‑hand side, handling self‑assignment safely, and then returns a reference to the left‑hand object so that the assignment can be chained or used in expressions.

@lFE_Clear_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_Clear_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.body: Resets the form’s internal cursor to the origin and clears its working buffer, then signals success with `E_OK`.

@lFE_Clear_To_End_Of_Form@p@l./Source/Cu.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_Clear_To_End_Of_Form@p@l./Source/Cu.body: The function invokes `wclrtobot` on the `w` member of the supplied `FORM` structure and signals success by returning `E_OK`.

@lFE_Clear_To_End_Of_Line@p@l./Source/Cu.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_Clear_To_End_Of_Line@p@l./Source/Cu.body: This routine calls the helper `wclrtoeol` on the form’s internal buffer (`form->w`) and immediately returns `E_OK`. It simply clears the line buffer after the current position—no further checks or error handling are performed.

@lFE_Delete_Character@p@l./Source/Curses.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_Delete_Character@p@l./Source/Curses.body: Invokes wdelch on the form’s w field, then returns E_OK.

@lFE_Delete_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_Delete_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.body: Resets the form’s column pointer, calls the line‑deletion routine on the form’s window, and returns the success status.

@lFE_Delete_Previous@p@l./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_Delete_Previous@p@l./Source/CursesD.body: The function `FE_Delete_Previous` removes the character preceding the current cursor position in a form buffer. It checks whether the cursor is at the first position of the field; if so, it rejects the request. When the cursor is in the first column of a row, it backs up one row and re‑draws the line, updating the cursor to the previous line’s end. Otherwise, it simply deletes the character at the current position. The function updates the form state and returns `E_OK` on success or `E_REQUEST_DENIED` on failure.

@lFE_Delete_Word@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_Delete_Word@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.body: The function removes the word at the current cursor position. It first verifies that the cursor is actually on a non‑blank character; if the cursor is on a blank it returns an error. Once confirmed it moves the cursor back to the first non‑blank character preceding the word, then clears the rest of the line from that point to the end of the screen line. Finally it scans forward in the buffer to locate the start of the following data, copies any remaining text after the deleted word into the window, and returns success.

@lFE_Insert_Character@p@l./Source/Curses.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_Insert_Character@p@l./Source/Curses.body: The function obtains the current field from the form, verifies the field can accept a blank character, and then attempts to insert it. If the field is a single‑line, growable or has sufficient room, the character is added; otherwise it returns an error code or triggers a line wrap. The function returns a status flag indicating success or failure.

@lFE_Insert_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_Insert_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.body: The function checks whether the current field can accept a new line—if there’s space, it grows the field or inserts a new line; otherwise it returns an error code.

@lFE_New_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.author: AI Short Overview
@lFE_New_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.body: The routine appends a new line to the current field. It first checks whether the field is at its row limit; if the current line is the last and the field is not growable, it either refuses the request or triggers a field‑switch through `Inter_Field_Navigation`. In insert mode it inserts a blank line (or moves the cursor after the line if the field is growable) and updates the window and status flags. The function returns `E_OK` on success or an error code otherwise.

@lFN_Down_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Down_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.body: The function changes the form’s current field to its down‑neighbour by calling `_nc_Set_Current_Field` with the field returned by `Down_Neighbour_Field`. It returns whatever status code the underlying setter returns (typically an integer success flag).

@lFN_First_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_First_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.body: The function moves the form’s focus to the first field of the current page by invoking `Next_Field_On_Page` for the current page’s maximum field and passing that field index to `_nc_Set_Current_Field`. It returns whatever value that helper returns (typically an error code).

@lFN_Last_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Last_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.body: The function invokes `_nc_Set_Current_Field` with the form structure and the field that precedes the current field on the active page, returning whatever status that helper routine yields.

@lFN_Left_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Left_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.body: The function simply invokes `_nc_Set_Current_Field`, passing the current form and the field returned by `Left_Neighbour_Field(form‑>current)`, and returns whatever value that helper returns.

@lFN_Next_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Next_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.body: FN_Next_Field sets the form's current field to the next field on the current page by calling `_nc_Set_Current_Field` with the result of `Next_Field_On_Page(form->current)` and returns that value.

@lFN_Previous_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Previous_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDi.body: The function forwards the current field index to `Previous_Field_On_Page` to get the index of the preceding field, then passes that index to `_nc_Set_Current_Field` to update the form’s current field pointer. The returned integer indicates the success status.

@lFN_Right_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Right_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.body: The function sets the current field of the given form to the field that is immediately to the right of the current field by calling `Right_Neighbour_Field` and passing the result to `_nc_Set_Current_Field`. It returns whatever status code that helper returns.

@lFN_Sorted_First_Field@p@l./Source/Curs.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Sorted_First_Field@p@l./Source/Curs.body: It returns the result of calling `_nc_Set_Current_Field` with the next sorted field of the given form.

@lFN_Sorted_Last_Field@p@l./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Sorted_Last_Field@p@l./Source/Curse.body: The routine assigns the form’s active field to the field that precedes the current sorted field by computing that predecessor via `Sorted_Previous_Field` and then invoking `_nc_Set_Current_Field` with that field.

@lFN_Sorted_Next_Field@p@l./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Sorted_Next_Field@p@l./Source/Curse.body: The routine updates the form’s current field pointer to the subsequent field in the sorted order by invoking `Sorted_Next_Field(form->current)` and passing the result to `_nc_Set_Current_Field`. It returns the status from that helper call.

@lFN_Sorted_Previous_Field@p@l./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Sorted_Previous_Field@p@l./Source/C.body: The function retrieves the field preceding the current one in a sorted order and sets it as the new current field by invoking `_nc_Set_Current_Field`. It returns the result of that call.

@lFN_Up_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.author: AI Short Overview
@lFN_Up_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.body: The function simply updates the form’s current field to its immediate upper neighbour by calling `_nc_Set_Current_Field` with the form and the field returned by `Upper_Neighbour_Field(form->current)`, and returns whatever value that helper returns.

@lFV_Validation@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.author: AI Short Overview
@lFV_Validation@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.body: It returns `E_OK` when the form passes `_nc_Internal_Validation`; otherwise it returns `E_INVALID_FIELD`.

@lFatalError@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110FatalEr.author: AI Short Overview
@lFatalError@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110FatalEr.body: Records the error in `status`, flags a fatal condition, and returns `false`.

@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::ExpandVari.author: AI Short Overview
@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::ExpandVari.body: The function checks whether the current object owns a library, library item, or link item that matches the supplied name; if a match is found it returns that stored value, otherwise it simply returns the input string unchanged.

@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::FeaturePla.author: AI Short Overview
@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::FeaturePla.body: The `FeaturePlaceHolderExpander` class implements a constructor that accepts an rvalue reference (likely a move‑only instance) and performs placeholder expansion logic. It derives from `cmPlaceholderExpander` and is invoked in the `cmComputeLinkInformation.cxx` file to resolve feature‑related placeholders during link‑information computation.

@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::FeaturePla.author: AI Short Overview
@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::FeaturePla.body: Constructs the expander by assigning the provided string pointers to its internal members: `Library`, `LibItem`, and `LinkItem`. No additional logic is executed in the constructor body.

@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::FeaturePla.author: AI Short Overview
@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::FeaturePla.body: Copies the expander’s internal state and configuration from the supplied instance, creating an identical expander ready for use.

@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::operator=@.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference of another `FeaturePlaceHolderExpander`, swaps its internal data members into the current instance (typically via `std::swap` or move‑construction of contained resources), and then returns a reference to the current object. It handles self‑assignment safely and preserves the object’s invariant by ensuring that all moved‑away resources are cleaned up before the transfer.

@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::operator=@.body: The `operator=` overload for `FeaturePlaceHolderExpander` performs a shallow copy of the internal state from another expander instance. It assigns each member (e.g., the placeholder map and any flags) of the source object to the current one, ensuring that the new expander reflects the same configuration as the source. This operator is intended for quick reassignment of an expander’s configuration in contexts where a fresh instance needs to adopt an existing placeholder map without re‑initialising from scratch.

@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::~FeaturePl.author: AI Short Overview
@lFeaturePlaceHolderExpander::~FeaturePl.body: The expander walks a feature‑definition string, identifies placeholder tokens (like ${…}), and substitutes them with their resolved values (e.g. feature‑level flags, environment data, or computed metadata) before the rest of the template is rendered.

@lField_Editing@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.author: AI Short Overview
@lField_Editing@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.body:
It dispatches an edit request on the current field of a form.  
- If the request is to delete the previous character while at the start of a field and the form’s overload options are enabled, it redirects the cursor to the previous field instead of deleting.  
- If the request is to create a new line at the start of a field with the overload flag, it moves to the next field.  
- Otherwise, for any other editable field it performs the requested operation, and on success it marks the window as modified.

@lField_Grown@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.author: AI Short Overview
@lField_Grown@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.body: This routine expands a text field when it is growable. It first determines whether the field is single‑line or multi‑row, then grows the appropriate dimension (columns or rows) by the requested amount while respecting any defined maximum. If the reallocation fails, it rolls back to the original dimensions. When successful, it allocates a new buffer, copies the old contents, updates the visual window if present, and propagates the new size to any linked fields. The function returns **TRUE** only after all steps succeed.

@lFileProjectRelativePath@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lFileProjectRelativePath@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function computes a path to *fileName* relative to the current source and binary directories of the project. It first constructs the relative path from each of those directories, then selects the shorter one (by string length). If neither relative path is shorter than the original name, it returns *fileName* unchanged.

@lFilterNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK10FilterNode.author: AI Short Overview
@lFilterNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK10FilterNode.body: The `Evaluate` method enforces a three‑parameter signature, validates that the second argument is either `"INCLUDE"` or `"EXCLUDE"`, then constructs a `cmList` from the first argument, applies a filter based on the second argument’s mode (INCLUDE or EXCLUDE), and finally returns the string representation of the filtered list. If the regex parsing fails or the argument counts are incorrect, it reports an error via `reportError` and returns an empty string.

@lFilterNode::FilterNode@k_ZN10FilterNod.author: AI Short Overview
@lFilterNode::FilterNode@k_ZN10FilterNod.body: FilterNode is a move constructor that initializes a FilterNode instance by transferring the state of a temporary instance.

@lFilterNode::FilterNode@k_ZN10FilterNod.author: AI Short Overview
@lFilterNode::FilterNode@k_ZN10FilterNod.body: `FilterNode` is a constructor that copies an existing filter node. It takes an unnamed reference to a `FilterNode` object and initializes the new instance with the same filter parameters and state as the source. This allows a new node to be created that behaves identically to an existing one.

@lFilterNode::FilterNode@k_ZN10FilterNod.author: AI Short Overview
@lFilterNode::FilterNode@k_ZN10FilterNod.body: Creates an instance of the `FilterNode` type. The default constructor simply performs no work—its body is empty, so an object is created with no initialization beyond default member values.

@lFilterNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lFilterNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_ZN.body: The function simply returns the constant value 3 – it indicates that three parameters are expected, and it’s declared as a public virtual const member that overrides a base‑class definition.

@lFilterNode::operator=@k_ZN10FilterNode.author: AI Short Overview
@lFilterNode::operator=@k_ZN10FilterNode.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue of the same type and moves its internal data into the current instance, returning a reference to the current object. It is defined as part of the public interface of `FilterNode`.

@lFilterNode::operator=@k_ZN10FilterNode.author: AI Short Overview
@lFilterNode::operator=@k_ZN10FilterNode.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of the source `FilterNode` into the target, performing member‑wise copying of the filter criteria and returning a reference to the modified object.

@lFilterNode::~FilterNode@k_ZN10FilterNo.author: AI Short Overview
@lFilterNode::~FilterNode@k_ZN10FilterNo.body: The `~FilterNode()` function acts as the destructor for the `FilterNode` struct. When a `FilterNode` instance goes out of scope, this routine executes its cleanup logic: it calls the base class destructor (via `cmGeneratorExpressionNode`), releases any owned resources, and guarantees that all internal state is properly released before the object is finally reclaimed.

@lFinalAction::FinalAction@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalAction::FinalAction@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The public member `FinalAction` is a small helper that accepts an rvalue reference (an rvalue of type `FinalAction`) and performs the necessary final clean‑up or dispatch of the action represented by the `FinalAction` instance. It is called from several points in the codebase, for example at line 89 of `cmVariableWatchCommand.cxx`, and typically forwards the request to the appropriate handler after moving the temporary instance into place.

@lFinalAction::FinalAction@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalAction::FinalAction@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: Creates an Action object by allocating a shared‑pointer to a new Impl instance that receives the supplied cmMakefile pointer and std::string value, then passes that pointer to the Action base constructor.

@lFinalAction::FinalAction@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalAction::FinalAction@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: FinalAction accepts a const reference to another FinalAction instance, typically used as a copy constructor. It constructs a new object by copying the internal state of the passed‑in object, ensuring any dynamic resources are correctly duplicated. This function is publicly accessible so it can be invoked from various parts of the codebase, often when an existing action instance needs to be replicated for independent use elsewhere.

@lFinalAction::Impl::Impl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalAction::Impl::Impl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function simply stores the passed‑in `cmMakefile` pointer and the string into its member variables `Makefile` and `Variable` using move semantics, leaving the object otherwise default‑constructed.

@lFinalAction::Impl::~Impl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalAction::Impl::~Impl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: On destruction it deregisters the variable watch for the stored variable.

@lFinalAction::operator()@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalAction::operator()@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL.body: The function is a public member declared `operator()` that takes a reference to a `cmLocalGenerator` instance and a const reference to a `cmListFileBacktrace`. It is marked `const`, indicating it doesn’t modify the object on which it is called. Its body is empty, so it currently performs no operation – it is a stub or placeholder intended for future implementation.

@lFinalAction@k_ZL11FinalActionR10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalAction@k_ZL11FinalActionR10cmMake.body: The function verifies that a target named by `name` exists in the Makefile. If the target is missing, it builds a diagnostic message showing the source directory that caused the problem and reports the issue through CMake’s message system. The function does not modify the Makefile beyond the warning.

@lFinalAction@k_ZL11FinalActionR10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalAction@k_ZL11FinalActionR10cmMake.body: The function registers a file to be installed: it takes a reference to the current makefile object and the destination path string, then appends an installation entry to the makefile’s internal list. After adding, it ensures any required directories are created and updates the makefile’s metadata accordingly. This final step is invoked by both the file‑install and program‑install commands to consolidate the generated installation rules.

@lFinalAction@k_ZL11FinalActionR10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalAction@k_ZL11FinalActionR10cmMake.body: The routine receives a makefile object, a target location string, and a vector of arguments. It determines whether the arguments specify an explicit list of files (by detecting a leading “FILES” keyword). Depending on that flag, it resolves each argument either directly (if a glob pattern is supplied) or via `cmSystemTools::Glob` to expand patterns into matching source files. Every resolved file path is converted to an install source path with `FindInstallSource`. Finally, the function normalises the destination path (removing a leading slash, normalising slashes, defaulting to “.”) and queues an install generator (`cmInstallFilesGenerator`) that will copy the collected sources into the resolved destination.

@lFinalizeFeatureFormat@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lFinalizeFeatureFormat@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The routine scans the `format` string, excising any segment that contains the supplied `otherTag` and then prunes the `activeTag` out, also trimming a following ‘}’ if present.

@lFindInstallSource@k_ZL17FindInstallSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lFindInstallSource@k_ZL17FindInstallSou.body: The function resolves a file name supplied to CMake. If the name is already a full path or CMake cannot resolve it as a variable, the name is returned unchanged. Otherwise, the routine builds two candidate paths—one under the current binary directory and one under the current source directory—and tests whether those paths exist on disk. If the binary‑side file exists, that path is returned; otherwise, if the source‑side file exists, that path is returned. When neither candidate exists, the function falls back to the binary candidate, assuming the file will be generated during the install step.

@lFindMocExecutableFromMocTarget@k_ZL30F.author: AI Short Overview
@lFindMocExecutableFromMocTarget@k_ZL30F.body: The function looks for a target named “Qt<major‑version>::moc” in a given makefile and, if found, pulls its **IMPORTED_LOCATION** property. If no such target exists, it returns an empty string.

@lFree_AlphaNumeric_Type@p@l./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lFree_AlphaNumeric_Type@p@l./Source/Cur.body: The function accepts a generic pointer argument. It verifies that the pointer is non‑null and then calls the standard `free()` routine to deallocate the memory. Because it is a static helper, it operates only within the translation unit and does not perform any additional bookkeeping beyond the basic null‑check and deallocation step.

@lFree_Enum_Type@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.author: AI Short Overview
@lFree_Enum_Type@p@l./Source/CursesDialo.body: The static routine simply frees a supplied pointer when it is non‑null, acting as a lightweight wrapper around `free`. It contains no additional logic or error handling, relying on the caller to guarantee that the argument is a valid allocation.

@lFree_Numeric_Type@p@l./Source/CursesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lFree_Numeric_Type@p@l./Source/CursesDi.body: The routine simply frees the passed pointer whenever it’s non‑null, effectively releasing the memory it references.

@lFree_RegularExpression_Type@p@l./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lFree_RegularExpression_Type@p@l./Sourc.body: The function decreases the reference count of a `RegExp_Arg` object; when the counter reaches zero it frees the internal representation of the regular expression (either the `pRegExp` structure or the `compiled_expression` blob, depending on the build flags) and finally releases the argument structure itself. If the object was already de‑referenced it simply returns, while the compile‑time guards suppress unused‑parameter warnings on platforms that lack the regex support.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::Evaluate@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::Evaluate@k.body:
It builds a combined identifier by recursively evaluating each child expression, then looks up the corresponding generator node.  
If the node is missing or fails its parameter checks, it reports an error and returns an empty string.  
Otherwise it evaluates the node’s parameters, invokes the node’s `Evaluate` method with those arguments, and returns the resulting string. If profiling is enabled, it records the evaluation and execution steps for diagnostics.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::EvaluatePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::EvaluatePa.body: The EvaluateParameters method walks the list of child expressions for a generator node, collects the evaluated strings into the parameters vector, and ensures the number of produced parameters matches the node’s declared expectation (including special handling when the node accepts an arbitrary‑content parameter). If the count mismatches or a child evaluation fails, it reports an error and returns an empty string.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::GeneratorE.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::GeneratorE.body: The constructor accepts a raw character buffer and its size, storing them into the class’s internal fields (`StartContent` and `ContentLength`). It simply assigns the incoming pointer and length to the corresponding member variables, preparing the object for subsequent use.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::GeneratorE.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::GeneratorE.body: Creates a new instance by copying the state from an existing `GeneratorExpressionContent` object—essentially a copy constructor that re‑initialises the internal state based on the supplied source object.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::GetOrigina.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::GetOrigina.body: It returns a `std::string` constructed from the object’s internal buffer by starting at the stored offset `StartContent` and taking `ContentLength` bytes.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::GetType@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::GetType@k_.body: Returns the enumeration value indicating that this object is a *Generator* instance of the expression‑evaluation framework.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::ProcessArb.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::ProcessArb.body: The method evaluates a generator‑expression node by iterating over its child evaluators in `pit`. For each evaluator it verifies whether the node demands literal input; if so, only `Text`‑typed evaluators are allowed, otherwise an error is reported. The evaluator string is appended to a running result string. On any error, an empty string is returned immediately. When the node requires literal input the accumulated result is passed to the node’s own `Evaluate` method and that value is returned; otherwise the collected string is returned directly.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::SetIdentif.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::SetIdentif.body: Moves the supplied vector into the member variable, transferring ownership without copying data.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::SetParamet.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::SetParamet.body: `SetParameters` assigns the supplied vector to `ParamChildren` by moving the vector, so the arguments are transferred without copying.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::operator=@.body: The assignment operator copies the internal data from the source object into the current instance (performing a shallow copy of the expression tree) and returns *this.

@lGeneratorExpressionContent::~Generator.author: AI Short Overview
@lGeneratorExpressionContent::~Generator.body: When a `GeneratorExpressionContent` instance is destroyed through a base‑class pointer, this virtual `~GeneratorExpressionContent()` guarantees that the proper destructor chain is followed. In practice, the body is defaulted, so the class relies on its base class to release any owned resources; the override merely ensures the derived destructor is invoked in the usual polymorphic deletion sequence.

@lGenexEvalNode::AcceptsArbitraryContent.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvalNode::AcceptsArbitraryContent.body: The function is a virtual const member returning `true`, meaning any derived class that implements this will accept arbitrary content parameters without restriction. It simply guarantees that the component will always validate or allow the passed parameter, effectively making the check always pass.

@lGenexEvalNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13GenexEv.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvalNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13GenexEv.body: The function extracts the first string from the `parameters` vector. If that string is empty, it returns it unchanged; otherwise it delegates processing to `EvaluateExpression`, passing the string together with the supplied context, content, and dag checker. The delegated call uses the label `"GENEX_EVAL"`.

@lGenexEvalNode::GenexEvalNode@k_ZN13Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvalNode::GenexEvalNode@k_ZN13Gen.body: GenexEvalNode is the public entry point that initiates the internal node‑evaluation routine. It operates on the data structures already present in the instance, orchestrating the traversal or processing logic required to resolve a node’s state. The function performs the necessary steps internally and finishes with no return value, making it a straightforward trigger for the larger evaluation pipeline.

@lGenexEvalNode::NumExpectedParameters@k.author: AI Short Overview
