@lGenexEvalNode::NumExpectedParameters@k.body: This function signals that the concrete subclass expects exactly one argument in its interface. It’s a virtual const override that returns the constant value 1, indicating the sole required parameter for the derived implementation.

@lGenexEvalNode::operator=@k_ZN13GenexEv.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvalNode::operator=@k_ZN13GenexEv.body: The overloaded assignment operator lets you assign a temporary or existing `GenexEvalNode` to an existing instance. It takes an r‑value reference (`GenexEvalNode&&`), moves the internal state (e.g., pointers, flags, sub‑nodes) into `*this`, and then returns a reference to the updated object. This enables fluent chaining and efficient in‑place updates of the node hierarchy.

@lGenexEvalNode::operator=@k_ZN13GenexEv.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvalNode::operator=@k_ZN13GenexEv.body: The operator= overload copies all internal state from the source GenexEvalNode into the target, returning a reference to the target node so that assignments can be chained.

@lGenexEvalNode::~GenexEvalNode@k_ZN13Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvalNode::~GenexEvalNode@k_ZN13Ge.body: `~GenexEvalNode()` implements the node‑specific evaluation logic for the Genex system; it walks a node tree and applies the appropriate logic for each node type.

@lGenexEvaluator::EvaluateExpression@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvaluator::EvaluateExpression@k_Z.body: The routine checks whether the current context has a head target, and if so it spins up a DAG‑checker for that target. The checker scans the expression; if a self‑ or cycle‑reference is detected it emits an error and returns an empty string. If the check passes, the routine hands the expression and context over to `EvaluateDependentExpression`, which performs the actual evaluation using the supplied DAG checker and context objects. If there is no head target, it skips the DAG check and calls `EvaluateDependentExpression` directly.

@lGenexEvaluator::GenexEvaluator@k_ZN14G.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvaluator::GenexEvaluator@k_ZN14G.body: GenexEvaluator is a helper that owns and evaluates Genex expressions during generation. The constructor shown accepts an rvalue of itself (essentially a move‑constructor) and simply forwards the supplied Genex expression node to the base cmGeneratorExpressionNode class to construct the node’s internal state.

@lGenexEvaluator::GenexEvaluator@k_ZN14G.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvaluator::GenexEvaluator@k_ZN14G.body: GenexEvaluator is a public constructor that accepts a reference to another GenexEvaluator instance for initialization. It initializes a new object by copying the state of the provided instance, setting up any internal state required for evaluating expressions within the generator. The constructor is defined in cmGeneratorExpressionNode and is used throughout the code base to create evaluator objects that perform expression evaluation tasks.

@lGenexEvaluator::GenexEvaluator@k_ZN14G.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvaluator::GenexEvaluator@k_ZN14G.body: Creates an evaluator object, wiring up any default options and preparing internal state for later evaluation runs.

@lGenexEvaluator::operator=@k_ZN14GenexE.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvaluator::operator=@k_ZN14GenexE.body: This overload implements move‑assignment for `GenexEvaluator`. It accepts an rvalue reference to another `GenexEvaluator`, transfers its internal state (typically members such as expression tree nodes) into the current object, and then returns a reference to that object so the assignment can be chained.

@lGenexEvaluator::operator=@k_ZN14GenexE.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvaluator::operator=@k_ZN14GenexE.body: Assigns a copy of another GenexEvaluator into the current object, performing the usual copy‑assignment logic and returning *this so that the operation can be chained.

@lGenexEvaluator::~GenexEvaluator@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lGenexEvaluator::~GenexEvaluator@k_ZN14.body: The `~GenexEvaluator()` is the virtual destructor for the `GenexEvaluator` class. When an object of this type is destroyed, the destructor runs to release any owned resources (e.g., delete allocated memory, close file handles, or unregister callbacks). Because it is declared virtual, the appropriate derived‑class destructor will be invoked, ensuring that all resources specific to the derived class are cleaned up before the base destructor runs.

@lGetDirectoryValueFromFileExtension@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetDirectoryValueFromFileExtension@k_Z.body: The function normalises the supplied file‑extension string to lower‑case and returns a specific directory string depending on that value. If the extension is “framework”, “xcframework” or “xcassets”, it returns a predefined directory name (“wrapper.framework”, “wrapper.xcframework” or “folder.assetcatalog”). For any other extension it falls back to a generic “folder”.

@lGetDistribValue@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetDistribValue@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ge.body:
The function reads a key prefixed by “DISTRIB_”, looks up the remaining part in a static map loaded once from `GetOSReleaseVariables`.  
If the key ends with “INFO”, it concatenates all values, registers them in the makefile, and returns the joined string.  
Otherwise it returns the single value that matches the sub‑key, or an empty string if none exists.

@lGetGroupMapKeyFromPath@k_ZL22GetGroupM.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetGroupMapKeyFromPath@k_ZL22GetGroupM.body: The function builds a key string by concatenating the target’s name with a hyphen‑separated version of the supplied path, returning that string.

@lGetIncludes@k_ZL11GetIncludesR10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetIncludes@k_ZL11GetIncludesR10cmMake.body: GetIncludes parses the supplied argument string for include‑directory tokens (handling quotes and escaped spaces) and appends the resolved paths to the current makefile’s include list.

@lGetIncludes@k_ZL11GetIncludesR10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetIncludes@k_ZL11GetIncludesR10cmMake.body: The routine tokenises a newline‑separated list of include directives, normalises each entry, and appends every non‑empty result to the supplied vector.

@lGetIndexArg@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111GetInd.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetIndexArg@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111GetInd.body: The `GetIndexArg` routine parses a string argument into a numeric index and reports whether the operation succeeds. It first attempts to convert the string to a long; if that fails it consults the current policy status (`CMP0121`) and emits a warning or fatal error message according to the policy level. On success it casts the parsed value to an `int` and assigns it to the supplied `idx` pointer before returning `true`. If the string cannot be parsed, it returns `false` (or triggers a fatal error depending on the policy).

@lGetList@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17GetListERKN.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetList@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17GetListERKN.body:
A single‑line summary:  
It returns a `cmList` containing the passed string when non‑empty, otherwise an empty `cmList`; when non‑empty the `EmptyElements::Yes` flag is set.

@lGetList@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17GetListERKN.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetList@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17GetListERKN.body: The function resolves a variable into a list of strings: it first attempts to obtain the string value via `GetListString`; if that fails it returns an empty optional. When the string is empty it returns an empty list. Otherwise it expands the string into a list and, based on the makefile’s policy for CMP0007, either issues a warning, silently ignores empty items, or produces a fatal error, before finally returning the list.

@lGetListString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113GetL.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetListString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113GetL.body: GetListString looks up a variable in a `cmMakefile` object. It retrieves the definition via `GetDefinition`, checks whether the value exists, copies the result into the supplied `listString` reference, and returns `true` when a value was found or `false` when the variable is missing.

@lGetMocVersion@k_ZL13GetMocVersionRKNSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetMocVersion@k_ZL13GetMocVersionRKNSt.body: The function runs the specified moc executable with the `--version` flag, captures the resulting output, and if the command completes successfully, it parses that output into an `IntegerVersion`; otherwise it returns an empty result.

@lGetNextNumber@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113GetN.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetNextNumber@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113GetN.body: The routine scans a comma‑separated string for the next token, converts that token to an integer, moves a cursor past the comma, and signals whether another token follows.

@lGetNextRealNumber@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetNextRealNumber@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: Parses a comma‑separated token from the input string. It sets `val` to the parsed number (or `-1` for an empty token) and advances `pos` to the next field, returning `1` if more tokens follow or `0` at the end.

@lGetNumericArgument@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetNumericArgument@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: Parses the supplied string into an integer of the appropriate size; if the conversion succeeds and the whole string is consumed it writes the result into the output reference and returns true, otherwise it returns false. It uses `std::stol` or `std::stoll` depending on the size of the target type and traps `std::invalid_argument` to signal parse failure.

@lGetNumericArguments@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetNumericArguments@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine iterates over the supplied arguments (expanding them into a list when the *ExpandElements* flag is enabled), calls **GetNumericArgument** on each value, reports a parsing error for any non‑numeric token, pushes successful indices into the output vector, and returns *true* only when every argument passes validation.

@lGetOSReleaseVariables::[lambda_0]@kGet.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetOSReleaseVariables::[lambda_0]@kGet.body: The lambda receives a file path, pulls the base filename via `cmSystemTools::GetFilenameName`, and then checks that the name is at least 11 characters long and begins with three digits followed by a dash. It returns `true` when any of those conditions fail (i.e., the string is too short, the first three characters are non‑digits, or the fourth character isn’t `‐`). It uses `std::isdigit` without casting to `unsigned char`, which can trigger undefined behaviour for signed‐char values, and it accesses `filename[3]` without guarding against very short strings—though the preceding length check normally prevents out‑of‑bounds access.

@lGetOSReleaseVariables::[lambda_1]::ope.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetOSReleaseVariables::[lambda_1]::ope.body: The `operator()` function is a public const method that accepts two string references and returns a Boolean value, typically used to compare the supplied arguments according to the particular business logic in the surrounding codebase. In practice, callers rely on it to perform a quick, read‑only check between two textual values—often for equality, ordering, or membership determination—without modifying any internal state.

@lGetOSReleaseVariables::[lambda_1]@kGet.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetOSReleaseVariables::[lambda_1]@kGet.body: It extracts the first three characters from each string, converts them to numbers using `cmStrToLong`, and returns whether the first number is smaller than the second.

@lGetOSReleaseVariables@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetOSReleaseVariables@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The function scans standard OS‑release locations and, if nothing is found, falls back to a set of CMake‑provided scripts. It parses the first key/value pair it encounters from each file, filters unknown variables, and returns a map of the discovered OS identifiers (e.g. `NAME`, `VERSION`, `RELEASE`, plus a record of which fallback script supplied the data).

@lGetParallelCPUCount@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetParallelCPUCount@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine lazily computes and caches the number of CPUs usable for parallel work. On the first call it queries the system, clamps the result between 1 and a predefined maximum, and on subsequent calls simply returns the stored value.

@lGetPolicyDefault@k_ZL16GetPolicyDefaul.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetPolicyDefault@k_ZL16GetPolicyDefaul.body: The function resolves the policy’s default by looking up the variable “CMAKE_POLICY_DEFAULT_<policy>” in the given makefile. It then maps the retrieved string to the corresponding enum value (NEW, OLD, or WARN when the string is empty). If the string is unrecognized, it emits a fatal error and returns false; otherwise it returns true with the enum set.

@lGetProjectCommands@k_Z18GetProjectComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetProjectCommands@k_Z18GetProjectComm.body:
`GetProjectCommands` registers a wide set of built‑in CMake commands with a command state object. It calls `AddBuiltinCommand` for each supported command string, passing the identifier and the callback that implements the command.  
When “boot‑strap” code is compiled in, it adds a handful of extra commands that were historically optional.  
The function also registers several disallowed commands linked to policy numbers that should not be invoked directly; it records the policy ID, the corresponding handler, and a message warning developers of their misuse.

@lGetProjectCommandsInScriptMode@k_Z30Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetProjectCommandsInScriptMode@k_Z30Ge.body: The routine simply marks a predefined list of project‑level commands as “unexpected” when invoked in script mode, using the macro helper to register each name with the state object. This prevents those commands from being processed by the script‑based builder.

@lGetScriptingCommands@k_Z20GetScripting.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetScriptingCommands@k_Z20GetScripting.body:
The routine registers the built‑in command handlers into the script‑state.  
It first attaches all flow‑control commands (break, continue, foreach, function, if, macro, return, while, block).  
Then it loads the core CMake commands such as cmake_* variants, file utilities, and property helpers.  
Afterwards it adds the “unexpected” handlers that emit error messages when a flow command appears outside its expected block.  
Finally it marks a handful of legacy or disallowed commands as forbidden under specific policy checks.

@lGetSourcecodeValueFromFileExtension@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetSourcecodeValueFromFileExtension@k_.body: The routine normalises the supplied extension and then traverses a chain of specific string checks; for each recognised case it returns a descriptor string that tags the file as a particular source‑code type (e.g. “compiled.mach‑o.objfile”, “image”, “text”, etc.). When the extension matches a known‑type pattern it also flips the supplied reference flag so callers can remember that the file is a last‑known type.

@lGetTargetDependsClosure@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetTargetDependsClosure@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body:
The function walks the dependency graph of a target, caching the result in a map.  
When called for a target, it first ensures the target has an entry in the map.  
If the target was not already visited, it collects its direct dependencies that are linkable and non‑cross, inserts any that are executable/shared/module libraries, and then recurses into each of those dependencies to accumulate their transitive closures.  
Finally it returns the accumulated set of all reachable targets that satisfy those filters.

@lGetTargetObjectDirArch@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetTargetObjectDirArch@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body:
It pulls the OS‑architecture list stored in the target object.  
If more than one entry is present, it falls back to the compile‑time constant `"$(CURRENT_ARCH)"`.  
If exactly one entry exists, that single value is returned.  
Otherwise (no entry) it returns the supplied `defaultVal`.

@lGetTransitiveUsages@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetTransitiveUsages@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function walks through a list of requested module names, adds each found module’s location and method to the result list, and records the module’s name. While doing so, it also registers any transitive dependencies found in the usage map. After finishing the primary pass, it iterates over those transitive dependency names. For each that isn’t already a direct usage, it looks up the reference information and, if present, appends that module’s location and method to the list. The function finally returns the assembled list of all modules (both direct and indirect) that must be used.

@lGetValue@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_18GetValueER.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetValue@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_18GetValueER.body: GetValue examines a key string against a fixed list of recognised identifiers and returns a stringified value for that property by calling the appropriate accessor on the supplied SystemInformation object. If the key does not match any supported entry, it returns an empty optional.

@lGetValueChained@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetValueChained@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ge.body: It recursively invokes a sequence of functions that each may return an optional string. Starting with the first function, it returns that value if present; otherwise it falls back to the next function in the chain, continuing until one succeeds or the chain is exhausted, yielding an empty optional.

@lGetValueChained@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetValueChained@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ge.body: It simply returns an empty optional<string> value.

@lGet_First_Whitespace_Character@p@l./So.author: AI Short Overview
@lGet_First_Whitespace_Character@p@l./So.body: The function scans the supplied buffer from its start until it encounters a character that `is_blank()` recognizes as whitespace. When it finds such a character it returns a pointer to that location; if the scan reaches the buffer’s end without a match it returns the original buffer pointer. The routine assumes the caller guarantees that `buf` points to at least `blen` bytes of valid storage and that `is_blank()` is defined elsewhere. It asserts non‑null buffer and non‑negative length, and uses a forward loop without bounds checks beyond the provided length. This behaviour makes it suitable for quick look‑ups where callers need a pointer to the first blank or to the buffer start when none exists.

@lGet_Start_Of_Data@p@l./Source/CursesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lGet_Start_Of_Data@p@l./Source/CursesDi.body: The function scans a supplied buffer for the first non‑blank character and returns a pointer to that position; if the entire buffer consists of blanks it returns the original buffer pointer.

@lGetcwd@k_Z6GetcwdPcj@f./Source/kwsys/S.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetcwd@k_Z6GetcwdPcj@f./Source/kwsys/S.body: The `Getcwd` function is a thin inline wrapper that forwards the supplied buffer and length to the underlying `getcwd` routine and returns a pointer into that buffer. It does not perform any safety checks itself, so callers must ensure the buffer has enough space for the current‑working‑directory string and that `getcwd` will not overrun the supplied length.

@lHSC_Generic@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.author: AI Short Overview
@lHSC_Generic@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.body: The `HSC_Generic` routine adjusts the current column position of a form field. It receives a `FORM*` pointer and a column count; a positive value moves the cursor right, a negative one left. The function clamps movements so the cursor never leaves the field’s data width. On success it updates `form->curcol` and `form->begincol`, returning `E_OK`; otherwise it leaves the values unchanged and returns `E_REQUEST_DENIED`.

@lHSC_Horizontal_Half_Line_Backward@p@l..author: AI Short Overview
@lHSC_Horizontal_Half_Line_Backward@p@l..body: The function performs a single operation: it invokes `HSC_Generic` with the supplied form and an integer argument equal to the negative of the form’s current column count divided by two. The function returns whatever `HSC_Generic` returns.

@lHSC_Horizontal_Half_Line_Forward@p@l./.author: AI Short Overview
@lHSC_Horizontal_Half_Line_Forward@p@l./.body: The function computes the midpoint column of the current form—specifically `(form->current->cols + 1)/2`—then passes that value to `HSC_Generic` and returns the result.

@lHSC_Horizontal_Line_Backward@p@l./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lHSC_Horizontal_Line_Backward@p@l./Sour.body: Invokes HSC_Generic with the supplied form and the negative of its current column count.

@lHSC_Horizontal_Line_Forward@p@l./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lHSC_Horizontal_Line_Forward@p@l./Sourc.body: The function simply forwards a form to `HSC_Generic`, passing the current form’s column count, and returns that result.

@lHSC_Scroll_Char_Backward@p@l./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lHSC_Scroll_Char_Backward@p@l./Source/C.body: Internally, it invokes the generic scrolling helper with a negative offset, effecting a single character step backwards and propagating the result.

@lHSC_Scroll_Char_Forward@p@l./Source/Cu.author: AI Short Overview
@lHSC_Scroll_Char_Forward@p@l./Source/Cu.body: Calls HSC_Generic with a step of 1, returning that result.

@lHandleAbsolutePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleAbsolutePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The function simply forwards the arguments to `HandleTransformPathCommand`, supplying a lambda that converts the given `cmCMakePath` to an absolute form using the provided base string. It returns the outcome of that helper call.

@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: Processes a list of arguments by parsing them into an `OutputVariable`, checks for parsing errors, constructs a CMake path from the provided inputs, and finally appends that path as a new definition in the target makefile. It signals failure through the `status` object and returns a success flag.

@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: It simply forwards the arguments to the shared implementation routine, telling it to perform an append operation, and returns whatever that routine reports.

@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function implements the CMakeLists `append` command: it checks that at least three arguments are supplied, expands the named list variable, and then registers an updated definition in the makefile that appends the given values to that list.

@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: Handles the APPEND sub‑command: it takes the variable name from the second argument, concatenates the remaining arguments with the current value of that variable (or an empty string if none exists), and writes the combined string back into the makefile’s definition table. The function returns `true` on success and `false` if the arguments are insufficient.

@lHandleAppendStringCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleAppendStringCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: Parses the argument vector, appends any input paths, registers the resulting path in the makefile as a definition, and returns a success indicator.

@lHandleArchiveCreateCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleArchiveCreateCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: Parses the supplied arguments, validates their consistency (e.g. format‑compression compatibility, compression level ranges, required path list), maps the chosen compression type to an internal enum, and finally invokes `cmSystemTools::CreateTar` with the resolved settings; returns success status while marking fatal errors on any validation failure.

@lHandleArchiveExtractCommand@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleArchiveExtractCommand@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The routine parses a set of command‑line options into a small struct of flags (verb‑osity, list‑only, destination, patterns, touch). It validates that no unknown options remain; on failure it records an error in the status object and aborts. If the user asked only to list matches, it lists the files matching the provided patterns. Otherwise, it creates or switches to the target directory (creating it if needed), changes the working directory to that location, and finally invokes the extraction routine. If the “touch” flag is set the timestamps of the extracted files are preserved. If any step fails, the status is set to fatal and the function returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lHandleAsciiCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleAsciiCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The routine parses a command’s arguments, converts each numeric token into its ASCII character (if in the valid range), concatenates the results, and records the resulting string in the supplied variable within the makefile. If the argument list is too short or contains an out‑of‑range value, it reports an error and aborts.

@lHandleCMakePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCMakePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The function receives a list of arguments and a status reference, then forwards the call to `HandlePathCommand` supplying the `ToCMakePath` conversion callback. This delegates the actual path handling logic while preserving the original status semantics.

@lHandleCacheMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCacheMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.body: The routine checks that a cache name was supplied, then queries the current makefile state for a cached entry. If the entry exists, it extracts the specified property’s value and writes that value back into the running context via `StoreResult`, finally signalling success with a `true` return.

@lHandleChmodCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleChmodCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: Handles a chmod command by forwarding the provided argument list and status reference to the underlying implementation function, passing a flag set to false, and returns that function’s boolean result.

@lHandleChmodCommandImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleChmodCommandImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: Interprets the command line options to determine target files/directories, validates the supplied permission masks, and then applies those masks to the matching paths (recursively expanding directories when requested) while reporting any errors that occur during the operation.

@lHandleChmodRecurseCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleChmodRecurseCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: It forwards the supplied arguments and status to the internal implementation routine, passing a flag that enables recursive handling, and returns the result of that call.

@lHandleCompareCommand::[lambda_0]::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCompareCommand::[lambda_0]::oper.body: The `operator()` function performs a comparison between two `cmCMakePath` objects—likely checking for equality or equivalence of the underlying path strings (normalised to a canonical form) and returning a boolean flag indicating success of the comparison. It’s invoked in various places where code needs to verify whether two path values represent the same physical path.

@lHandleCompareCommand::[lambda_0]@kHand.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCompareCommand::[lambda_0]@kHand.body: Compares two `cmCMakePath` instances and returns `true` only if they are equal.

@lHandleCompareCommand::[lambda_1]::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCompareCommand::[lambda_1]::oper.body: The function takes two path references and returns whether they represent the same filesystem location after normalizing relative components and slashes.

@lHandleCompareCommand::[lambda_1]@kHand.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCompareCommand::[lambda_1]@kHand.body: The lambda compares two `cmCMakePath` objects and returns `true` when they are not equal.

@lHandleCompareCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCompareCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function parses a COMPARE command: it resolves the comparison operator (EQUAL or NOT_EQUAL) from the third argument, applies it to the two path arguments, and records the resulting boolean as a named variable in the makefile.

@lHandleCompareCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCompareCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function parses a COMPARE sub‑command, verifies that the command is well‑formed, extracts the comparison mode and operands, performs the requested comparison (equal, not‑equal, less/≤, greater/≥, etc.), and if the comparison succeeds, records the result (1/0) in the makefile via `AddDefinition`. It returns `true` on success and `false` on error or unsupported mode.

@lHandleConcatCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleConcatCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine verifies that the argument list contains at least two elements; if this requirement isn’t met it records an error via the status object and returns false. When the check succeeds it forwards the arguments to `joinImpl`, passing an empty‑separator string and an offset of 1, and returns the boolean value produced by that helper.

@lHandleConfigureCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleConfigureCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The function parses the CONFIGURE arguments, validates the mandatory OUTPUT and CONTENT options while rejecting any unrecognized parameters, then safely resolves the output file path (creating necessary directories, rejecting illegal characters), and copies the supplied content to that file—expanding variables on the fly—only when changes are detected, and finally records the output file for subsequent cleanup.

@lHandleConfigureCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleConfigureCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The function parses a list of arguments to create a string definition in the makefile. It first verifies that at least two arguments are provided – the source string and the name of the output variable – and then scans remaining arguments for optional flags such as `@ONLY` or `ESCAPE_QUOTES`. After validating the options, it retrieves the configured string via `ConfigureString` and stores the result in the makefile under the given name. If any check fails, it reports an error via the `cmExecutionStatus` object and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true` to indicate success.

@lHandleConvertCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleConvertCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function takes a list of command‑line arguments and validates that the request is either “convert to CMake format” or “convert to native format”. It splits the supplied path string on the platform‑specific separator, normalizes each component (optionally normalizing the paths), and then stores the result back into the supplied variable name in the generated Makefile. If any of the pre‑conditions fail it records an error in the status object and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lHandleCopyCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCopyCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: Creates a `cmFileCopier` with the given status and returns the result of its `Run` call with the supplied arguments.

@lHandleCopyFile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Han.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCopyFile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Han.body: The function validates that at least three arguments are supplied (old path, new path, and optional flags). It normalises both paths to absolute form using the current source directory if necessary. A simple argument parser extracts three optional flags: “INPUT_MAY_BE_RECENT”, “ONLY_IF_DIFFERENT”, and a result variable name. If any unknown arguments remain, an error is returned. The routine then checks whether the source or target paths refer to directories; if the source is a directory the function records an error or definition (depending on whether a result variable was supplied) and returns failure. Similarly, copying into a directory is rejected. It maps the flags to an internal copy‑policy (`OnlyIfDifferent` or `Always`) and to whether to consider the source’s timestamp. Finally it calls `CopySingleFile` with those settings. On success, if a result variable was requested it stores “0”; otherwise it propagates any error through the status object. The function returns a `bool` indicating success (`true`) or failure (`false`).

@lHandleCppCheck@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Han.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCppCheck@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Han.body: The function builds a command line for **cppcheck** by collecting the `‑D`, `‑I` and `‑U` options from the original compiler arguments, adds the source file, runs the tool, prints its diagnostics (warnings, errors, or informational messages) to standard error, and finally returns the tool’s exit status.

@lHandleCppLint@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Hand.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCppLint@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Hand.body: The routine assembles a cpplint command line from the supplied executable and source file, runs it via cmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand, and writes any returned diagnostics to stderr. If the command fails it reports the failure; any produced output is emitted as a warning. Regardless of success or failure, it always returns 0 so the build can continue.

@lHandleCreateLinkCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleCreateLinkCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: Handles parsing of command arguments for creating a link (hard or symbolic), optionally copying the target file on failure, and records the result string in the build‑file if a variable is supplied.

@lHandleDifferentCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleDifferentCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The function parses a command that expects a variable name followed by the keyword “FILES” and two file names. It then uses the helper `cmSystemTools::FilesDiffer` to compare the two files; if they differ it assigns the string `"1"` to the given variable, otherwise `"0"`. The result is stored in the build system’s definition table via `status.GetMakefile().AddDefinition`. If the arguments are malformed, an error is recorded in `status`.

@lHandleDirectoryMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleDirectoryMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function first resolves the requested directory (if a non‑empty name is supplied) and, if that directory exists, switches the current makefile to that directory’s makefile. It then checks whether the property requested is “DEFINITIONS” and applies the appropriate CMP0059 policy branch (issue warnings, use old or new define flags, or fall through). Finally, it stores the retrieved property value via `StoreResult` and returns success/failure.

@lHandleDirectoryMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleDirectoryMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: Parses a list of command‑line options describing a directory‑install operation. It interprets directives such as DESTINATION, TYPE, PATTERN, REGEX, and various permission or optional flags, validates their ordering, and gathers the corresponding settings. It builds the list of target directories, resolves a destination (or default), and finally registers an installation generator with the global generator. If any argument is invalid or out of order, it reports an error and returns false.

@lHandleDownloadCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleDownloadCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The function parses a *DOWNLOAD* invocation, interprets its arguments as options (timeouts, TLS/SSL verification, file‑location, HTTP headers, byte ranges, progress printing and hash verification), then uses libcurl to fetch the URL into an optional file while streaming the response to the makefile’s variable system. It performs pre‑flight checks such as ensuring the file’s directory exists, rejecting unknown options, and aborting if any required argument is missing. After performing the curl operation it optionally verifies a supplied hash against the downloaded file and records download status and any progress data in the current makefile.

@lHandleExportAndroidMKMode@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleExportAndroidMKMode@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The routine parses a set of command‑line options to configure an Android export set, validates that a destination and a proper “.mk” filename were supplied, and then creates an `cmInstallExportGenerator` that installs that export set into the global makefile.

@lHandleExportMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleExportMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: The routine parses export‑mode command line arguments, validates the supplied options (destination, file name, permissions, etc.), checks that the requested export target complies with the required CMP0022 policy, and then registers an export‑install generator with the current makefile so the export set can be installed.

@lHandleExprCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleExprCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The routine checks that the argument list has either three or five items; it extracts the target variable and expression, determines whether the output should be decimal or hexadecimal based on an optional “OUTPUT_FORMAT” flag, parses the expression string into a numeric value, formats that value into a string according to the chosen format, records any parser warning, and finally writes the formatted value into the makefile’s variable table, returning success or failure.

@lHandleFilesMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleFilesMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.body: The routine parses and validates the command‑line options for the “FILES” installation mode. It resolves argument names, checks for conflicts such as both a TYPE and DESTINATION flag, normalises file paths, applies policy rules to exported files, and if all checks pass, it creates and registers the corresponding install generator in the global generator. The function returns true on success or false with an error message set in the supplied status object.

@lHandleFilterCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleFilterCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine parses a FILTER command: it checks that the supplied arguments contain a list name, a filtering operator (INCLUDE or EXCLUDE), and a mode (currently only REGEX). It resolves the named list, applies the requested filter with the given pattern, and registers the result as a definition in the makefile. If any of these steps fails (missing arguments, unknown operator, or list not found), the status is updated with an appropriate error and the function returns false. Otherwise the definition is added successfully and the function returns true.

@lHandleFindCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleFindCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function checks that the command line contains exactly four tokens: the command name, a list name, an item to search for, and a variable name. It pulls the requested list from the current makefile; if the list is absent, it creates a new definition for the variable with the string "-1". If the list exists, it looks for the item; the result—either the position in the list or the sentinel npos—is converted to a string (or "-1" if not found) and stored in the variable. The function returns true on success, and signals an error through the status object when the argument count is wrong.

@lHandleFindCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleFindCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function validates that the supplied argument list contains 4 or 5 elements, uses an optional “REVERSE” flag to decide whether to search forward or backward, ensures that the requested output variable name isn’t “REVERSE”, then searches for the specified character in the given string and writes the resulting position (or –1 if not found) into the makefile definitions. It returns success status based on whether a definition was added.

@lHandleGenerateCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGenerateCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The function parses and validates the arguments for the GENERATE sub‑command, applies any permission flags specified, and finally calls AddEvaluationFile with the resolved parameters; it returns false if any validation fails.

@lHandleGenexStripCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGenexStripCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function validates that the command was invoked with exactly three arguments (the command name, an input string, and a variable name). It then passes the input string through a preprocessing routine that removes any embedded generator expressions, and finally registers the cleaned string under the given variable name in the makefile context, reporting success via a true return value or an error status otherwise.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_0]::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_0]::operator.body: The function `operator()` takes a reference to an existing `cmCMakePath` and a flag. It constructs and returns a new `cmCMakePath` instance—typically by appending or adjusting the internal path string based on the flag. The result is a freshly‑configured path object that can be used further in the build system.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_0]@kHandleGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_0]@kHandleGe.body: Accepts a `cmCMakePath` and a `bool`; returns the path’s root name via `GetRootName()`.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_1]::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_1]::operator.body: The `operator()` function creates a new `cmCMakePath` from the current instance and an additional path passed in, optionally altering the resulting path based on the boolean flag. It performs no state mutation, returns a freshly‑constructed object and therefore has negligible runtime cost.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_1]@kHandleGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_1]@kHandleGe.body: Returns the root directory of the supplied `cmCMakePath` object; the second boolean argument is ignored.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_2]::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_2]::operator.body: The const `operator()` takes an existing `cmCMakePath` and a `bool`. It returns a new `cmCMakePath` instance that may optionally modify its internal representation based on the flag. The source instance is left unchanged, ensuring immutability. This helper is used wherever a path needs to be recomputed without mutating the original object.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_2]@kHandleGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_2]@kHandleGe.body: The lambda simply returns the root part of the supplied `cmCMakePath`, ignoring the second argument. It calls `GetRootPath()` on the incoming path and returns that value.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_3]::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_3]::operator.body: The function `operator()` is a const member that takes a reference to another `cmCMakePath` instance plus a boolean flag, and returns a new `cmCMakePath` object. It effectively performs a transformation on the input path (or combines it with the current instance) and produces a resulting path without modifying the original objects.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_3]@kHandleGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_3]@kHandleGe.body: The lambda accepts a `cmCMakePath` and a boolean flag, but the flag is unused; it simply calls `GetFileName()` on the path and returns the resulting `cmCMakePath`.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_4]::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_4]::operator.body: Creates a new `cmCMakePath` object from the supplied path reference. The `bool` parameter controls whether the returned path is modified (for example, normalized or stripped) before being returned.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_4]@kHandleGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_4]@kHandleGe.body: It accepts a `cmCMakePath` and a flag; if the flag is true, it returns the path’s last‑extension part, otherwise it gives the wide‑extension representation of the same path.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_5]::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_5]::operator.body: The `operator()` function is a const member that takes a reference to a `cmCMakePath` and a `bool`, then returns a new `cmCMakePath` instance – effectively creating a path object based on the supplied path and flag without modifying the original.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_5]@kHandleGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_5]@kHandleGe.body: The lambda returns a `cmCMakePath` object: if `last_only` is true it returns the file name without extension (the stem), otherwise it returns the last component of the path (the narrow stem).

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_6]::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_6]::operator.body: The operator returns a new `cmCMakePath` built by combining the current instance with the supplied `cmCMakePath` argument; the bool flag switches an optional modifier (e.g., whether to normalize or preserve the trailing slash).

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_6]@kHandleGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_6]@kHandleGe.body: The lambda receives a `cmCMakePath` and a boolean flag, then invokes `GetRelativePath()` on the path object and returns that value. It ignores the boolean argument entirely.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_7]::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_7]::operator.body: This operator returns a new cmCMakePath that represents the current path optionally altered according to the supplied flag. It creates a derived path object based on the given cmCMakePath argument and the truth value of the flag.

@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_7]@kHandleGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand::[lambda_7]@kHandleGe.body: The lambda accepts a `cmCMakePath` and a (currently unused) boolean, invokes `GetParentPath()` on the supplied path, and returns the resulting parent path.

@lHandleGetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: HandleGetCommand validates the GET command arguments, extracts the requested action (e.g., ROOT_NAME, ROOT_DIRECTORY, EXTENSION, etc.), and invokes the corresponding lambda stored in a static map. It parses any optional flag (e.g., LAST_ONLY for EXTENSION/ STEM), then computes the requested path component, registers it in the Makefile as a definition, and returns success unless an error occurs (missing arguments, unknown action, or invalid path).

@lHandleGetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: The routine implements the **GET** sub‑command used by the makefile parser. It verifies that at least three indices follow the list name, resolves that list via `GetList`, and stops if the list is missing or empty. It then converts each supplied index string into an integer via `GetIndexArg`, collects them into a vector, and fetches the requested items from the list with `list->get_items`. The retrieved values are stored in the makefile’s context through `AddDefinition`. Errors are returned in `status` with appropriate diagnostic messages, including out‑of‑range exceptions. The function returns `true` on success (including the special “NOTFOUND” fallback) and `false` otherwise.

@lHandleGetRuntimeDependenciesCommand@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetRuntimeDependenciesCommand@k_.body: The routine orchestrates the `GET_RUNTIME_DEPENDENCIES` makefile command: it verifies platform support, parses the supplied options, loads the relevant runtime dependency metadata, resolves the actual dependencies, and then registers the resulting resolved, unresolved, and conflicting dependency lists back into the makefile for downstream use.

@lHandleGlobCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGlobCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: Handles a global command by delegating to the internal implementation (`HandleGlobImpl`) with the supplied arguments, explicitly passing a flag of `false`. It returns the success status from that call.

@lHandleGlobImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Han.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGlobImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Han.body: The function parses a list of glob‑style arguments, applies policy rules for symlink handling (e.g., whether to follow links or not), tracks flags such as “list dirs”, “follow symlinks”, and “relative” mode, and collects the files that match the glob expression. It reports errors for malformed options, warns about cyclic recursion or unexpected behaviors, updates the build system’s glob cache, and finally registers the resulting file list under the given variable name.

@lHandleGlobRecurseCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGlobRecurseCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function forwards a list of arguments to the underlying implementation, explicitly enabling recursion by passing `true`, and returns the status yielded by that call.

@lHandleGlobalMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGlobalMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: Validates the supplied name, fetches a global property from the current CMake instance and attempts to store that value in the supplied variable. It returns true when the property is successfully stored, or false (after recording an error) otherwise.

@lHandleHasExtensionCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHasExtensionCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: Delegates to HandleHasItemCommand, passing it a lambda that returns the result of `path.HasExtension()` for the supplied path.

@lHandleHasFilenameCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHasFilenameCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: This function delegates to the generic `HandleHasItemCommand` logic, invoking a lambda that returns `path.HasFileName()` for each supplied path argument, effectively reporting whether each argument contains a filename.

@lHandleHasItemCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHasItemCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function validates that exactly two arguments were supplied, extracts and verifies the input path, and ensures the output variable name is valid. It then calls the supplied predicate on the resolved path and records the boolean result as a definition in the current makefile before returning success.

@lHandleHasParentPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHasParentPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The function forwards its arguments to a generic handler that checks whether a `cmCMakePath` instance reports having a parent path. It returns the result of that check as a boolean.

@lHandleHasRelativePartCommand@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHasRelativePartCommand@k_ZN12_GL.body: The function wraps a call to `HandleHasItemCommand`, passing the supplied arguments and status along with a predicate that simply forwards to `path.HasRelativePath()`. It returns true if any of the provided paths satisfies that condition.

@lHandleHasRootDirectoryCommand@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHasRootDirectoryCommand@k_ZN12_G.body: This function forwards the input arguments to `HandleHasItemCommand`, supplying a predicate that inspects each `cmCMakePath` and returns `true` only when `path.HasRootDirectory()` evaluates to `true`. It thereby returns the outcome of that delegated call.

@lHandleHasRootNameCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHasRootNameCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: It forwards the supplied arguments to `HandleHasItemCommand`, supplying a predicate that simply calls `path.HasRootName()` on each `cmCMakePath`.

@lHandleHasRootPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHasRootPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: It forwards the arguments to `HandleHasItemCommand`, passing a lambda that simply calls `HasRootPath()` on the `cmCMakePath` instance and returns that result. The function returns the boolean value produced by `HandleHasItemCommand`.

@lHandleHasStemCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHasStemCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: It forwards the supplied arguments to `HandleHasItemCommand`, passing a lambda that calls `path.HasStem()` on the `cmCMakePath` instance. The result is a Boolean indicating whether the path in question contains a stem.

@lHandleHashCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHashCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The `HandleHashCommand` function validates that exactly three arguments were supplied, resolves the input file path, and then verifies that the third argument (the output variable name) is non‑empty. It reads the input file, computes a hash value from the file’s contents, and finally adds a definition for the output variable in the current makefile (the hash value encoded in hexadecimal). If any step fails, it records an error in the supplied `cmExecutionStatus` object and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lHandleHashCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHashCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The routine checks that three arguments were supplied, creates a `cmCryptoHash` instance for the first argument (the input file), hashes that file with the second argument as the output name, and, on success, registers the hash value in the makefile; it reports errors if the argument count or hashing fails.

@lHandleHashCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHashCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function expects three arguments: the hash algorithm name, an output variable name, and a string to hash. It first validates the argument count, reporting an error if the count is incorrect. On success, it creates a hash object, hashes the supplied string, and records the resulting hash value under the specified variable in the generated makefile. The routine reports success with a `true` return value and failure with `false`.

@lHandleHexCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleHexCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: The routine first verifies that three parameters were supplied. If not, it reports an error and aborts. When the argument count is correct, it treats the second string as raw data, converts every byte to a two‑digit hexadecimal representation, concatenates those bytes into a single string, and records that string in the makefile definition map under the name given in the third argument. It returns true on success and false if the argument count check fails.

@lHandleIWYU::[lambda_0]@kHandleIWYU::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleIWYU::[lambda_0]@kHandleIWYU::[l.body: Returns true if the given string starts with the literal prefix `"--error"`.

@lHandleIWYU@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110HandleI.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleIWYU@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110HandleI.body: The function builds an iwyu command by appending all original options except the first, runs the tool while capturing its standard‑error output, prints any diagnostics that advise removing or adding lines, and finally returns the tool’s exit status only if the “‑-error” flag was supplied; otherwise it suppresses a non‑zero exit as a normal, non‑fatal condition.

@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode@k_Z.body: The routine parses a list of target names supplied for an “import‑runtime‑artifacts” request, validates that each target is a local importable executable, library, or module, and then creates the appropriate install generator objects (library, runtime, framework, or bundle) for each target. It attaches any generic flags (permissions, configurations, component, optional, exclude‑from‑all, etc.) to each generator, registers them with the global generator and finally returns true if all generators were successfully created and registered.

@lHandleInsertCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleInsertCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine validates that the INSERT sub‑command receives the required arguments, resolves the target list name and desired insertion index, and then applies the requested elements (expanded from the current makefile) into the list at that position. It updates the internal definition of the list, returns success status, and records any exception or argument errors in the supplied status object.

@lHandleInstallCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleInstallCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function receives a list of command‑line arguments and a reference to a status object, creates a `cmFileInstaller` instance with that status, and delegates the work to the installer’s `Run` method, returning its Boolean result.

@lHandleInstallMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleInstallMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: Checks that a non‑empty name was supplied, retrieves (or creates) the corresponding installed file via the current makefile’s cmake instance, reads the requested property from that file if present, and stores the value (or a null pointer if absent) in the output container; if the file cannot be found, it records an error.

@lHandleIsAbsoluteCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleIsAbsoluteCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function processes the `IS_ABSOLUTE` command: it verifies that three arguments are supplied, extracts the input path, validates the output variable name, determines whether the input path is absolute via `cmCMakePath::IsAbsolute`, and then records the Boolean result in the makefile.

@lHandleIsPrefixCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleIsPrefixCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The routine verifies the expected number of arguments for the IS_PREFIX command, parses and validates the two input paths, then determines whether one path is a prefix of the other. It records the boolean result as a definition in the makefile and returns success or failure.

@lHandleIsRelativeCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleIsRelativeCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function validates that three arguments were supplied, retrieves the first argument as a path, verifies the second argument is a non‑empty variable name, uses `cmCMakePath` to determine whether that path is relative, and stores the resulting boolean in the makefile under the supplied variable name.

@lHandleJSONCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleJSONCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function parses a vector of string arguments to interpret a JSON‑manipulation command. It reads the first argument as a variable name, then examines a mode keyword (GET, SET, EQUAL, etc.) to decide what operation to perform on a JSON document parsed from a subsequent argument. Depending on the mode it may read values, modify members, append to arrays, compare whole JSON objects, or report errors by creating “‑NOTFOUND” definitions. The routine updates the *cmMakefile* with the result (or an error message) and returns a success flag.

@lHandleJoinCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleJoinCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: Handles the JOIN sub‑command by verifying the four‑token syntax, pulling the named list from the current makefile, and storing its joined‑string (separated by the supplied glue) under the specified variable name—falling back to an empty definition when the list is not found.

@lHandleJoinCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleJoinCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function validates that at least three arguments are supplied (the command name, a target, and a file name). It then calls `joinImpl` with the full argument vector, the second element as a target identifier, and a hard‑coded offset of 2, propagating the status object obtained from the current makefile. It returns the result of that call.

@lHandleLWYU@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110HandleL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleLWYU@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110HandleL.body: Creates a command list containing the supplied run command and the source file, executes it while capturing stdout, and if the output includes the phrase “Unused direct dependencies:” it emits a warning to standard error.

@lHandleLengthCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleLengthCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine checks that exactly three arguments were supplied, extracts the list name and target variable name, looks up the list via `GetList`, and if found, records its size (or zero) as a new definition in the current makefile. It returns `true` on success, otherwise signals an error and returns `false`.

@lHandleLengthCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleLengthCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function checks that exactly two arguments were passed, converts the second argument to an integer string, and records that value as a macro definition in the build system. It returns success only if the arguments were correct; otherwise it reports an error.

@lHandleLockCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleLockCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: Parses a LOCK sub‑command: it validates and interprets options (DIRECTORY, RELEASE, GUARD, RESULT_VARIABLE, TIMEOUT), creates the needed directory and file, applies the requested lock scope via the global lock pool, optionally stores the lock result string in a user‑supplied variable, and signals success or failure.

@lHandleMakeCIdentifierCommand@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleMakeCIdentifierCommand@k_ZN12_GL.body: The function first validates that the command received exactly three arguments; if not, it records an error message and aborts. When the arguments are correct, it extracts the input string and the desired variable name, then invokes `cmSystemTools::MakeCidentifier` to convert the input into a compliant C identifier. Finally, it registers that identifier in the current makefile by adding a definition for the given variable name, and returns success.

@lHandleMakeDirectoryCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleMakeDirectoryCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The routine iterates over each supplied path argument after the command token, normalises it to an absolute path (by prefixing the current source directory when necessary), verifies that the file system permits creation at that location, and finally invokes the system‑level make‑directory helper. If any of those checks or the actual creation fails, it records an error through the `status` object and returns `false`; otherwise the directory is created and the function returns `true`.

@lHandleNativePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleNativePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The routine parses the arguments for the NATIVE_PATH command, verifies they match the expected count and format, normalises the supplied path if requested, and records the resulting value as a definition in the current makefile before returning success.

@lHandleNativePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleNativePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: Handles a path‑based request by delegating to the generic `HandlePathCommand` routine, passing along the incoming arguments and the `ToNativePath` conversion indicator, and propagates the resulting status and success flag.

@lHandleNormalPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleNormalPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function parses the supplied arguments, verifies that no unexpected inputs were provided, resolves the input path to a normalized form, and then records that path as a definition in the current makefile, reporting success or failure.

@lHandlePackage@k_ZL13HandlePackageRKiR1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePackage@k_ZL13HandlePackageRKiR1.body: The `HandlePackage` function is a static helper that takes a read‑only `std::vector<std::string>` of arguments and returns a `bool` indicating success or failure. Internally it parses the supplied strings, performs whatever processing is necessary for that package (e.g., validation, registration, or dispatch), and reports whether the operation completed without errors. The function is invoked from various parts of the codebase, notably at line 41 of `cmExportCommand.cxx`, where it is used to process command‑line arguments before further execution.

@lHandlePackage@k_ZL13HandlePackageRKiR1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePackage@k_ZL13HandlePackageRKiR1.body: The routine walks the arguments list, pulls out a single package identifier, validates its format, then applies the current export policy. If the policy dictates no export it exits immediately; otherwise it hashes the current binary directory and records the result in the package registry.

@lHandlePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function validates that a path‑handling command receives exactly three arguments. It splits the second argument on the platform‑specific path separator, applies a supplied string‑transform function to each path component, concatenates the result, and records the transformed path value in the execution status’s makefile under the name given in the third argument.

@lHandlePopBackCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePopBackCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The routine first confirms there are at least two tokens – the sub‑command name and the name of a list variable. It then looks up that list; if it can’t be found it simply removes any following definitions that were supplied and returns success. If the list contains values, the function removes the trailing element (or, if extra variable names are supplied, it assigns successive trailing elements of the list to those variable names, removing each assigned element from the list). After any assignments the list is rewritten in the makefile, and any unused variable names are undef‑defined. The routine always ends by returning `true`.

@lHandlePopFrontCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePopFrontCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The function validates the argument count, fetches a list by name from the current makefile, then either removes the first element or, if variable names follow, copies that element into the supplied variable definitions before removing it. If the list is empty or nonexistent, it simply cleans up any passed variable definitions. If variables were supplied it assigns any remaining elements in the list to those variables, then updates the list definition accordingly.

@lHandlePrependCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePrependCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The routine first verifies that enough arguments were supplied (≥ 3). It fetches the name of the list to modify, expands that list’s current contents, and then inserts the supplied arguments (starting at index 2) at the front of that list definition via `cmMakefile::AddDefinition`. If the operation succeeds it returns true.

@lHandlePrependCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePrependCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function checks that a PREPEND command has at least one argument after the variable name, concatenates any supplied values, appends the existing definition if present, and writes the resulting string back into the makefile’s definitions.

@lHandleRPathChangeCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRPathChangeCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The routine parses a command that specifies a file and its old/new runtime‑path values, validates the inputs, and if all checks pass attempts to replace the old RPATH entry in the file with the new one (optionally clearing any environment‑derived path). On success it writes the updated file time back into the file’s metadata and signals success; otherwise it reports a suitable error via the status object.

@lHandleRPathCheckCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRPathCheckCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function parses the “FILE” and optional “RPATH” arguments, reports any missing or unexpected options, and if the specified file exists but does not contain the expected RPath value, it deletes the file so a reinstall can occur.

@lHandleRPathRemoveCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRPathRemoveCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function parses the command‑line arguments for the `RPATH_REMOVE` command, validates that the supplied file exists, then calls `cmSystemTools::RemoveRPath`. If the removal succeeds it writes a “Removed runtime path from …” status message and records the file’s modified timestamp; otherwise it reports an appropriate error.

@lHandleRPathSetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRPathSetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: Parses the supplied arguments, verifies the target file and desired RPATH value, updates the file’s runtime path if possible, and records the operation’s outcome.

@lHandleRandomCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRandomCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The `HandleRandomCommand` routine processes the `RANDOM` sub‑command found in the makefile. It first validates that the argument list contains the minimum number of required arguments (excluding the optional flags). It then scans any additional keyword arguments (`LENGTH`, `ALPHABET`, `RANDOM_SEED`) to override the default length, alphabet string, or random seed. If no custom alphabet is supplied it falls back to a built‑in pool of alphanumeric characters. After validating the alphabet and length, the routine seeds the random generator (once per program run or when a seed is supplied), builds a string of the requested length by randomly picking characters from the chosen alphabet, and finally registers this string in the current makefile context under the variable name supplied as the last argument. It reports failure via `status.SetError()` when argument validation fails or when the generated string would be empty, and returns `true` on success.

@lHandleReadCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleReadCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The routine parses the command arguments, locates the requested file (appending a relative path if necessary), opens it, optionally seeks to a supplied offset, reads up to an optional limit of bytes (in plain or hex form), and stores the read data as a variable definition in the makefile.

@lHandleReadElfCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleReadElfCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function validates that at least three arguments are supplied, parses optional “RPATH”, “RUNPATH”, and “CAPTURE_ERROR” options, verifies the file exists, then loads the ELF file. If the ELF is invalid it reports an error or logs a definition named by the supplied error name. When valid, it extracts the “RPATH” and “RUNPATH” strings from the ELF and defines them in the Makefile under the names supplied in the options.

@lHandleReadSymlinkCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleReadSymlinkCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function expects three command‑line arguments: the command name, a symlink path, and a variable name. It validates the argument count, reads the target of the specified symlink, and on success stores that target string in the given makefile under the supplied variable name; otherwise it reports an error.

@lHandleRealPathCommand::[lambda_0]@kHan.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRealPathCommand::[lambda_0]@kHan.body: This lambda constructs a `cmMakePath` from the supplied `in`. If that path is relative, it prefixes it with the `BaseDirectory` stored in `arguments`. Finally, it resolves the real, case‑sensitive path with `GetRealPath` and stores the canonical string back into `result`.

@lHandleRealPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRealPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The routine reads the supplied arguments for the `REAL_PATH` command, applies an optional tilde‑expansion flag, and then normalises the path relative to a base directory (defaulting to the current source directory when omitted). Depending on the CMP0152 policy in effect, it either uses the new relative‑path resolution method or the legacy one; when the legacy behaviour differs from the new one, it emits a warning. Finally it stores the resolved path into the variable named in the third argument.

@lHandleRegexCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRegexCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The function examines a command’s arguments, verifies that a mode string such as “MATCH”, “MATCHALL”, or “REPLACE” is present, and that enough additional arguments are supplied for that mode. It then routes the request to the corresponding helper routine—`RegexMatch`, `RegexMatchAll`, or `RegexReplace`—returning a success flag or reporting an error when the mode is unrecognized.

@lHandleRelativePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRelativePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: This function forwards the supplied arguments to `HandleTransformPathCommand`, passing along the current status and a lambda that, for each provided path, invokes `path.Relative(base)` to compute a relative path relative to the given base string. It returns whatever boolean result `HandleTransformPathCommand` produces.

@lHandleRelativePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRelativePathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The function validates that four arguments were supplied, extracts the output variable name, a source directory and a file path, ensures both paths are absolute, then computes the relative path between them and stores that value as a makefile definition. If any check fails, an error status is set and the function returns false.

@lHandleRemove@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Handl.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRemove@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Handl.body: Returns the result of the internal helper `HandleRemoveImpl` by forwarding the supplied argument vector and status reference, passing a `false` flag to indicate that the removal operation should not trigger any special‐case handling.

@lHandleRemoveAtCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRemoveAtCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The routine parses a `REMOVE_AT` command: it first verifies that at least three arguments are supplied, fetches the named list, validates that the requested indices are numeric, accumulates them in a vector, then applies `remove_items` to those indices. If the operation throws `std::out_of_range` it records an error via the status object; otherwise the list definition is rewritten in the makefile and the function returns success.

@lHandleRemoveDuplicatesCommand@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRemoveDuplicatesCommand@k_ZN12_G.body:
The routine parses a *REMOVE_DUPLICATES* sub‑command issued from a `makefile`.  
It verifies that exactly one argument (the list name) is supplied; if more than one it reports an error via `status.SetError`.  
The supplied name is used to look up the corresponding list definition in the current makefile.  
If the list does not exist, the function exits successfully with no side‑effects, signalling that nothing to change.  
Otherwise, the list’s current definition is replaced with a new definition generated by its `remove_duplicates()` method, serialized back to a string and written back into the makefile.

@lHandleRemoveExtensionCommand@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRemoveExtensionCommand@k_ZN12_GL.body:
The routine parses an `args` vector for an optional output variable and a `last‑only` flag.  
If parsing fails, it returns `true` (error already reported).  
On success it verifies no surplus inputs, extracts the input path, and either removes the final extension component or all extension suffixes according to the `last‑only` flag.  
Finally it records the resulting path in the makefile as a definition keyed by the (user‑supplied or fallback) output name, and returns `true` to signal success.

@lHandleRemoveFilenameCommand@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRemoveFilenameCommand@k_ZN12_GLO.body: Handles a `REMOVE_FILENAME` command by validating the supplied arguments, optionally capturing an output variable, stripping the file‑name component from the given path, and adding the resulting path back into the current makefile as a definition.

@lHandleRemoveImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRemoveImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body:
The function walks the argument list (skipping the first token that represents the command), normalises relative paths to the current source directory, and then removes each path:

* If the argument is empty, it logs a warning and skips it.  
* If the name is not an absolute path, it prefixes the current source directory.  
* When the resolved path refers to a directory that is not a symlink and recursion is enabled, it calls `RepeatedRemoveDirectory`; otherwise it calls `RemoveFile`.  

The routine always returns `true`.

@lHandleRemoveItemCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRemoveItemCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function parses a command whose arguments specify a list name followed by item names, retrieves that list, and removes the supplied items from it—then records the change in the makefile definition.

@lHandleRemoveRecurse@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRemoveRecurse@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function simply delegates to `HandleRemoveImpl`, passing the received arguments and the status reference, with the third parameter hard‑coded to `true`. It returns whatever boolean result `HandleRemoveImpl` produces, propagating that result back to the caller.

@lHandleRename@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Handl.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRename@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Handl.body: The function parses the supplied arguments, validates that at least two new path names are provided, constructs full paths (using the current source directory when necessary), interprets optional arguments for a “NO_REPLACE” flag and a RESULT variable, then invokes the system‑level rename routine. Depending on the outcome it may set an error in the status object or, on success, optionally defines the RESULT macro in the makefile.

@lHandleRepeatCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRepeatCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function validates that exactly four arguments are supplied, converts the repeat count from a string to an unsigned long, builds a string consisting of the original string repeated that many times (optimizing the single‑character case), and finally registers the resulting string as a new definition in the current makefile.

@lHandleReplaceCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleReplaceCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: This routine validates the number of arguments, pulls the match string, replacement string, and variable name from the argument list, concatenates the remaining arguments into a single string, performs a string replacement using the system tool, and stores the resulting value as a definition in the makefile. It returns a success flag indicating whether the command was processed correctly.

@lHandleReplaceExtensionCommand@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
