@lHandleReplaceExtensionCommand@k_ZN12_G.body: Parses the command arguments using an argument‑parser, validates the input path, then replaces either the last extension or all extensions of that path (depending on the LAST_ONLY flag) and finally registers the resulting path as a variable in the makefile.

@lHandleReplaceFilenameCommand@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleReplaceFilenameCommand@k_ZN12_GL.body: This function parses a list of arguments, validates the input path, replaces the file name component of that path with an optional new name from the parsed inputs, updates the current makefile definition with the new path string, and reports success or failure via the supplied status object.

@lHandleReverseCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleReverseCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The `HandleReverseCommand` routine checks that the command supplied at least one argument beyond the command name. It retrieves the named list from the current makefile context; if the list is missing it silently succeeds. Otherwise it writes a new makefile definition that holds the stringified reverse of that list’s contents. The function returns success unless the caller supplied an incorrect argument count.

@lHandleRuntimeDependencySetMode@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleRuntimeDependencySetMode@k_ZN12_.body: The routine checks that the host system supports runtime‑dependency installation, then parses the supplied arguments into categories for libraries, runtime components, and frameworks. It builds individual install‑command objects for each category, attaches the shared generic arguments, finalises the arguments, registers any required installation components with the global generator, and returns success status, reporting any errors for unknown or missing arguments.

@lHandleScriptMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleScriptMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: The routine parses the argument list to extract any declared COMPONENT and to detect the mutually exclusive `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` or `ALL_COMPONENTS` flags. It then walks the arguments again, switching into “script” or “code” mode when encountering `SCRIPT` or `CODE` and attaches the following value to a new `cmInstallScriptGenerator`, passing along component and exclusion flags. Finally it records the component name in the global generator and signals success, returning `false` and an error message when misuse is detected.

@lHandleSetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleSetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body:
The routine verifies that the `SET` command has the expected number of arguments, rejects empty variable names, and then uses a `NormalizeParser` to split the argument string into path‑components.  
If the parser reports a single input it normalizes that path (optionally reducing slashes, etc.) and stores the resulting generic string in the makefile as a new definition under the supplied variable name.  On success it returns `true`; on any validation failure it records an error message in `status` and returns `false`.

@lHandleSizeCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleSizeCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function verifies that exactly three arguments were supplied, checks that the named file exists and is readable, and then records the file’s size in the makefile by adding a definition for the output variable with the numeric file length.

@lHandleSortCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleSortCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body:
The routine interprets a list of arguments that describe a `SORT` sub‑command.  
It validates that each option (COMPARE, CASE, ORDER) appears no more than once, builds a `SortConfiguration` object from the specified tokens, and finally applies that configuration to the named list, storing the resulting sorted list as a makefile definition.

@lHandleSourceMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleSourceMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: The routine validates a source name, resolves the file path (optionally forcing it to absolute form), retrieves or creates the source entry in the current makefile, and finally stores its property value for the caller. It returns true only when all these steps succeed; otherwise it records an error and returns false.

@lHandleStringsCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleStringsCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: HandleStringsCommand takes a list of arguments that includes a file name and a target variable name. It parses optional flags that limit how many strings to read, the maximum number of characters per string, and can filter strings by a regular‑expression or a minimum/maximum length. The routine opens the file (converting a hex‑encoded version if requested), reads the contents character by character, breaking lines on newline characters, and groups printable characters into strings. Strings that meet the filter are accumulated into a list; the list is finally written into the specified makefile variable as a semicolon‑separated list.

@lHandleStripCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleStripCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The routine checks that exactly three arguments are supplied. It treats the second token as a string value and the third as a variable name. It scans the string to locate the first non‑space character and the last non‑space character, forming a substring that removes any leading and trailing whitespace. That substring is then stored in the build system as the new value of the named variable.

@lHandleSublistCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleSublistCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function parses a SUBLIST command that expects four arguments: the name of an existing list, a start index, a length, and a variable name. It first validates the argument count, then retrieves the target list. If the list is missing or empty, it creates an empty definition for the variable. Otherwise, it resolves the start and length arguments to integer indices, checks that they fall within bounds, and finally extracts the requested sub‑list using `sublist(start, length)`. The resulting list is stored in the makefile under the supplied variable name, and the function returns `true` on success or `false` if any validation or extraction fails, reporting errors via the `status` object.

@lHandleSubstringCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleSubstringCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The function validates a five‑argument command that extracts a substring from a provided string. It checks that the arguments count is correct, parses the start index and ending position, and verifies that the indices fall within the string bounds (begin must be non‑negative and not exceed the string length; end must be at least ‑1). On success it registers the extracted substring as a new variable definition in the current makefile. If any check fails, it reports a descriptive error through the status object and aborts the operation.

@lHandleTargetMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: The function first checks that a target name is supplied, then looks up that target in the current makefile. If found, it handles alias logic (whether the target is an alias or an alias global), stores the appropriate value (the target’s name or an alias flag), and returns true. If the target isn’t found or a required property is missing, it reports an error and returns false.

@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_0]::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_0]::operato.body: The `operator()` function receives a const reference to a `cmInstallCommandFileSetArguments` object and returns a boolean indicating whether the installation command arguments were successfully processed. It typically performs validation of the arguments and updates internal installation state accordingly.

@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_0]@kHandleT.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_0]@kHandleT.body: The lambda supplies a Boolean flag that reflects whether `fileSetArg` reports its internal “name‑link‑only” state; it’s essentially a short accessor used inside a larger conditional expression.

@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_1]::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_1]::operato.body: The function `operator()` accepts a reference to a `cmInstallCommandFileSetArguments` object, performs validation and registration logic for install‑file set commands, and returns `true` when the command is correctly processed or `false` if any validation fails.

@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_1]@kHandleT.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_1]@kHandleT.body: This lambda simply forwards the result of `fileSetArg.GetNamelinkSkip()` to decide whether name‑linking should be skipped.

@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_2]::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_2]::operato.body: The operator() function evaluates a `cmInstallCommandFileSetArguments` instance and returns `true` if the arguments satisfy all required constraints; otherwise it returns `false`. It performs validation checks (e.g., ensuring non‑null pointers, required flags present, and that all paths/targets are valid) before any installation logic proceeds.

@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_2]@kHandleT.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_2]@kHandleT.body: The lambda captures a `fileSetArg` object and returns `true` if that object reports that a name‑linked component exists; otherwise it returns `false`. It performs this check by invoking `fileSetArg.HasNamelinkComponent()` and using the result directly as the lambda’s boolean return value.

@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_3]@kHandleT.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_3]@kHandleT.body: It evaluates whether `fileSetArg.GetType()` contains any text and returns the corresponding true/false result.

@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_4]@kHandleT.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetsMode::[lambda_4]@kHandleT.body: A concise check that simply returns whether the file set tied to `fileSetArg` contains any elements.

@lHandleTargetsMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTargetsMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function parses a list of target names and their associated options from a set of command‑line arguments, validates the options (enforcing rules such as correct placement of “NAMELINK_ONLY”, “NAMELINK_SKIP”, and “NAMELINK_COMPONENT”), builds a set of install generators for each target type (shared, static, module, framework, etc.), and finally registers those generators with the global generator so the install rules can be emitted. It returns true on success and false on any validation failure.

@lHandleTestMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Han.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTestMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Han.body: The function validates that a test name is supplied, queries the provided makefile for a test matching that name, and if found it stores the requested property in the result buffer; otherwise it flags an error and returns false.

@lHandleTidy@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110HandleT.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTidy@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110HandleT.body: The routine assembles the command line for running the clang‑tidy tool, stripping any `--export‑fixes=` options, and—unless a `-p` flag is supplied—injects a `--` separator followed by the original compiler arguments. It then invokes the tool via the system‑tool wrapper, streams the tool’s standard output to `stderr`, prints any returned error messages, and finally returns the tool’s exit status.

@lHandleTimestampCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTimestampCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The function parses the argument list to extract a file name, an optional format string, and an optional “UTC” flag. It obtains the file’s modification time (formatted optionally) and stores the result as a variable in the makefile.

@lHandleTimestampCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTimestampCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The function validates the number of arguments, pulls an output variable name and optional format string, optionally interprets a “UTC” flag, then creates a timestamp string in the chosen format. It finally writes this value into the makefile definition table and returns success status.

@lHandleToLowerCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleToLowerCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function forwards the argument vector and status reference to the generic handler, passing `false` to indicate that the operation should perform a lower‑case conversion only. It returns whatever the underlying `HandleToUpperLowerCommand` returns.

@lHandleToUpperCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleToUpperCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function forwards its arguments to the shared helper `HandleToUpperLowerCommand`, passing `true` to signal that the operation should be performed in an “upper” mode. It simply returns the helper’s result.

@lHandleToUpperLowerCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleToUpperLowerCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The routine takes a vector of string arguments, verifies that at least three items are present, extracts the target variable name from the third element, and then converts the second argument either to uppercase or lowercase according to the flag. Finally, it records the transformed string in the internal make‑file definition store.

@lHandleTouchCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTouchCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The function simply forwards the provided arguments to `HandleTouchImpl`, passing along a hard‑coded `true` flag and a reference to the `status` object, and returns the boolean result of that call.

@lHandleTouchImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTouchImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.body: The function iterates over the supplied arguments, normalising each argument into an absolute path if it isn’t one already, then verifies that the running user is permitted to write the resulting file. If the permission check fails it records an error in the provided status object and marks the operation as fatal. When writable, it attempts to touch (create or update) the file, propagating any failure as an error. If all touches succeed it returns true, otherwise it propagates the first encountered error and returns false.

@lHandleTouchNocreateCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTouchNocreateCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: This function forwards the supplied argument vector and status reference to `HandleTouchImpl`, passing a `false` flag so the implementation treats the call as a “no‑create” touch operation and returns the result directly.

@lHandleTransformCommand::ActionDescript.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTransformCommand::ActionDescript.body: The constructor creates an `ActionDescriptor` instance by initializing its internal `Name` member with the supplied string, moving the argument into storage to avoid a copy. It essentially assigns the provided name to the object’s name field and performs no other initialization.

@lHandleTransformCommand::ActionDescript.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTransformCommand::ActionDescript.body: Creates an `ActionDescriptor` object that simply stores the supplied name, the callable `TransformAction`, and the expected arity. The constructor moves the string into its `Name` member, assigns the `TransformAction` to `Action`, and records `arity` in `Arity`. No additional logic or validation is performed.

@lHandleTransformCommand::ActionDescript.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTransformCommand::ActionDescript.body: The operator returns a constant reference to the internal `Name` string, enabling read‑only access to the underlying string without copying it. It acts as a conversion operator, letting objects of this type be used wherever a `const std::basic_string<char>&` is expected.

@lHandleTransformCommand::[lambda_0]@kHa.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTransformCommand::[lambda_0]@kHa.body: The lambda takes two string references and returns the result of the less‑than comparison, i.e. `true` when the first string compares lexicographically before the second.

@lHandleTransformCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTransformCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The routine parses the TRANSFORM sub‑command, validates the supplied action name against a small table of supported actions (APPEND, PREPEND, TOUPPER, TOLOWER, STRIP, GENEX_STRIP, REPLACE), checks that the required number of arguments are present, and then consumes optional selectors (REGEX, AT, FOR) or an OUTPUT_VARIABLE specifier. Once all options are consumed it retrieves the target list variable, applies the requested transform (appending, replacing, etc.) to the list’s entries, writes back the updated list value under the (possibly new) output variable name, and returns success or failure with an appropriate error message.

@lHandleTransformPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleTransformPathCommand@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The function parses an argument list expecting an optional base‑directory variable, an optional output‑variable name, and an optional normalize flag. It resolves the source path supplied as the second argument relative to the chosen base directory (or the current source directory if none is supplied). The supplied transformation function is applied to that path, and if requested, the resulting path is normalized. Finally, the resolved path string is stored in the makefile under the specified output variable name (or the input name if none is given).

@lHandleUploadCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleUploadCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine first validates that at least three arguments are supplied (a file, a URL, and optional parameters). It then parses optional flags such as timeouts, TLS verification, headers, netrc settings, and progress display, emitting warnings for unknown arguments. After opening the source file it initializes a libcurl handle, applies the collected options (including timeout limits, SSL verification, custom headers, user credentials, and netrc authentication), then performs the upload via `curl_easy_perform`. On completion it records the result code in the supplied status variable, optionally logs response/debug output, cleans up resources, and returns true on success or false if any step fails.

@lHandleUuidCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleUuidCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: It pulls the first argument as an output variable name and then walks through the remaining tokens, collecting the optional flags “NAMESPACE”, “NAME”, “TYPE”, and an optional “UPPER” switch. After validating that a namespace UUID string and a name are present, it converts the namespace string to binary, produces a version‑5 UUID by hashing the namespace and name with either MD5 or SHA1 as requested, optionally upper‑cases the result, and finally registers the generated UUID in the makefile under the supplied variable name.

@lHandleVariableMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleVariableMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The routine checks that the supplied name is empty; if it isn’t, it records an error via `status.SetError` and returns `false`. Otherwise it delegates to `StoreResult` with the current makefile context and returns that result.

@lHandleWriteCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleWriteCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: Handles write requests by invoking `HandleWriteImpl` with the supplied arguments and a hard‑coded `false` flag, propagating any status updates back to the caller.

@lHandleWriteImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleWriteImpl@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.body: It parses the supplied arguments to find a target file, verifies that the current process is allowed to create or append to that file, creates any missing directories, temporarily gives the file write permission if it lacks it, opens the file (in append or overwrite mode), writes the concatenated arguments string into it, and re‑re‑sets the original permissions before returning a success flag.

@lHasUniqueOutputs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHasUniqueOutputs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: The function iterates over each `cmCustomCommandGenerator`, inserting every output and by‑product string into a set; any duplicate causes an early return of `false`, while a complete pass yields `true`.

@lHelper::CheckCMP0006@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::CheckCMP0006@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL__N.body:
The function inspects the current policy status for CMP0006 in the makefile.  
- If the status is **WARN**, it logs a warning and falls through.  
- If **OLD**, it permits the legacy behavior and returns `true`.  
- If **NEW**, it disallows compatibility (no explicit return; falls through).  
- For **REQUIRED_IF_USED** or **REQUIRED_ALWAYS**, it flags a failure, issues a fatal error, and exits.  
Finally, if none of those cases trigger a return, the function returns `false`.

@lHelper::GetArchiveDestination@k_ZNK12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetArchiveDestination@k_ZNK12_.body: The function simply returns the result of calling `GetDestination` with the supplied arguments, using the “CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR” key and the “lib” default, effectively determining the target installation directory for the library archive.

@lHelper::GetCxxModulesBmiDestination@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetCxxModulesBmiDestination@k_.body: The function checks for a non‑null argument object and returns the destination string stored in it; if the argument pointer is null, it simply returns an empty string.

@lHelper::GetDataDestination@k_ZNK12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetDataDestination@k_ZNK12_GLO.body: The helper returns the fully‑resolved install path for data files by delegating to `GetDestination`, passing the `CMAKE_INSTALL_DATADIR` key and the default data root. This produces the concrete directory string to be used when installing data under the project’s data tree.

@lHelper::GetDataRootDestination@k_ZNK12.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetDataRootDestination@k_ZNK12.body: The helper returns the directory that will be used when installing data files. It passes a specific environment‑variable name and a fallback value to the shared `GetDestination` routine, which resolves the real path. The function itself is just a thin wrapper that forwards the arguments and the hard‑coded “share” suffix to the generic destination resolver.

@lHelper::GetDestination@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetDestination@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL_.body: The function first checks for a non‑empty destination supplied in the `args` object; if that is missing it retrieves a safe definition for `varName` via the `Makefile` helper; and if that also fails, it finally returns the supplied `guess` value.

@lHelper::GetDestinationForType@k_ZNK12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetDestinationForType@k_ZNK12_.body: The `GetDestinationForType` helper checks whether an explicit destination is already supplied in the command arguments; if not, it selects a default destination string by matching the requested `type` against a fixed set of known keys (e.g., “BIN”, “SBIN”, “SYSCONF”, “SHAREDSTATE”, etc.). Each key maps to a specific `Get…Destination` member that returns the corresponding path. If the supplied type does not match any known value, the helper returns an empty string.

@lHelper::GetDocDestination@k_ZNK12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetDocDestination@k_ZNK12_GLOB.body: Returns the path that will be used for installing documentation files. It does so by delegating to the generic `GetDestination` helper, passing the fixed key `"CMAKE_INSTALL_DOCDIR"` and the data‑root path (`GetDataRootDestination(nullptr)`) with `"/doc"` appended. This produces the fully‑qualified destination string used by the install machinery.

@lHelper::GetIncludeDestination@k_ZNK12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetIncludeDestination@k_ZNK12_.body: Returns a path to the include directory by delegating to the underlying GetDestination routine with the predefined CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR key and the “include” flag.

@lHelper::GetInfoDestination@k_ZNK12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetInfoDestination@k_ZNK12_GLO.body: The function builds the full path for “info” files by delegating to `GetDestination`. It supplies the install‑command arguments, the keyword `CMAKE_INSTALL_INFODIR`, and a base path formed by appending “/info” to the data‑root directory returned by `GetDataRootDestination`. The result is returned as a `std::string`.

@lHelper::GetLibraryDestination@k_ZNK12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetLibraryDestination@k_ZNK12_.body: Calls GetDestination with the macro name `CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR` and the default sub‑directory `"lib"` to compute and return the library installation path.

@lHelper::GetLocalStateDestination@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetLocalStateDestination@k_ZNK.body: The `GetLocalStateDestination` helper simply asks its base `GetDestination` routine to resolve the directory that represents the project‑specific “local state” storage. It supplies the constant keys “CMAKE_INSTALL_LOCALSTATEDIR” and “var” so the underlying logic can look up the appropriate value in the supplied `cmInstallCommandArguments` and return that as a string.

@lHelper::GetLocaleDestination@k_ZNK12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetLocaleDestination@k_ZNK12_G.body: The function builds a path string by calling `GetDestination` with the flag `"CMAKE_INSTALL_LOCALEDIR"`, passing the result of `GetDataRootDestination(nullptr)` appended with `"/locale"`. It returns that constructed string.

@lHelper::GetManDestination@k_ZNK12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetManDestination@k_ZNK12_GLOB.body: The function composes a path for the **`man`** directory. It first obtains the root location from `GetDataRootDestination(nullptr)`, appends `"/man"` to that root, and finally resolves the full installation target through `GetDestination`, passing along the specific key `"CMAKE_INSTALL_MANDIR"`. This yields the final path where manual pages should be installed.

@lHelper::GetRunStateDestination@k_ZNK12.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetRunStateDestination@k_ZNK12.body: The method constructs the run‑state directory path by calling the helper routine `GetDestination` with the supplied install‑command arguments, passing the key `"CMAKE_INSTALL_RUNSTATEDIR"`, and appending `"/run"` to the base location returned by `GetLocalStateDestination()`.

@lHelper::GetRuntimeDestination@k_ZNK12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetRuntimeDestination@k_ZNK12_.body: This helper simply forwards the request to the generic `GetDestination` routine, passing the predefined install‑type key `"CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR"` and the fallback subdirectory `"bin"`. The result is the resolved runtime path for installing binaries.

@lHelper::GetSbinDestination@k_ZNK12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetSbinDestination@k_ZNK12_GLO.body: GetSbinDestination returns the path for the sbin directory by calling GetDestination with the macro key "CMAKE_INSTALL_SBINDIR" and the suffix string "sbin".

@lHelper::GetSharedStateDestination@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetSharedStateDestination@k_ZN.body: This function simply returns a path string for shared‑state files by delegating to the helper’s `GetDestination` routine with the key `CMAKE_INSTALL_SHAREDSTATEDIR` and the suffix `"com"`.

@lHelper::GetSysconfDestination@k_ZNK12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::GetSysconfDestination@k_ZNK12_.body: The method simply forwards the call to `GetDestination`, passing the arguments, the configuration key `"CMAKE_INSTALL_SYSCONFDIR"`, and a default of `"etc"`. It returns the resulting string that represents the system‑configuration installation path.

@lHelper::Helper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Help.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::Helper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Help.body: The helper simply consumes an rvalue reference of its own type and performs the internal bookkeeping needed for the surrounding logic.

@lHelper::Helper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Help.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::Helper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Help.body: The constructor stores a reference to the supplied `cmExecutionStatus` instance and a pointer to its associated `Makefile` object. It then queries that `Makefile` for a configuration value named `CMAKE_INSTALL_DEFAULT_COMPONENT_NAME`. If the retrieved string is empty, it falls back to the literal `"Unspecified"`. This establishes the helper’s default component name used during processing.

@lHelper::Helper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Help.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::Helper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Help.body: Helper() takes a const reference to another Helper instance and copies all of its member data into the newly constructed object.

@lHelper::MakeFilesFullPath@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::MakeFilesFullPath@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The function iterates through a list of relative file names, converts each one into an absolute path by prefixing it with a given base directory (unless the file name already contains a full path or appears to be a symlink). It then verifies that the resulting path does not refer to a directory; if it does, the helper reports an error with the mode name and aborts the operation, otherwise the fully‑resolved path is appended to an output vector for further processing.

@lHelper::MakeFilesFullPath@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::MakeFilesFullPath@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The helper method expands each relative file path in `relFiles` into its absolute form by resolving it against the current source directory obtained from the `Makefile`. It forwards the call to a more specific overload, passing that directory, and returns `true` only if every file path could be resolved successfully.

@lHelper::SetError@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16He.author: AI Short Overview
@lHelper::SetError@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16He.body: This method forwards the supplied error string to the `Status` object, updating its error state.

@lHorizontal_Scrolling@p@l./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lHorizontal_Scrolling@p@l./Source/Curse.body: The routine first examines whether the current field within the supplied `FORM` occupies only one line. If that test succeeds it invokes the supplied callback function pointer and returns its result. When the field spans more than one line it short‑circuits the callback and returns the error code `E_REQUEST_DENIED`.

@lHostLinkNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK12HostLink.author: AI Short Overview
@lHostLinkNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK12HostLink.body: Checks whether the provided context and DAG checker are valid and that the current target supports link options. If the conditions fail, it logs an error and returns an empty string; otherwise it returns a string listing the parameters or an empty string when the target is a device link.

@lHostLinkNode::HostLinkNode@k_ZN12HostL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHostLinkNode::HostLinkNode@k_ZN12HostL.body: HostLinkNode accepts an rvalue reference of an already‑constructed `HostLinkNode` instance and efficiently re‑initializes the new object with the same internal state. It essentially performs a move‑construction of the node, ensuring that the target instance holds all of the original’s properties while preserving any parent‑node relationships.

@lHostLinkNode::HostLinkNode@k_ZN12HostL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHostLinkNode::HostLinkNode@k_ZN12HostL.body: The constructor copies an existing `HostLinkNode` instance into a new one. It simply forwards the source instance’s internal data to the new object, ensuring that the new node is initialized with the same state as the original. This is used throughout the code—e.g., at line 2635 of `cmGeneratorExpressionNode.cxx`—whenever a new node must mirror an existing one.

@lHostLinkNode::HostLinkNode@k_ZN12HostL.author: AI Short Overview
@lHostLinkNode::HostLinkNode@k_ZN12HostL.body: This constructor simply performs default initialization—no parameters and no custom setup logic. It leaves all member variables in their default state and performs no side‑effects.

@lHostLinkNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHostLinkNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_.body: The function `NumExpectedParameters()` is a `const` override that declares the number of parameters the virtual function expects. In this declaration it returns the value `ZeroOrMoreParameters`, which is a constant that indicates the function accepts zero or more arguments (i.e. there is no fixed number of parameters required). This value is used by the framework that calls the virtual function to decide how many arguments must be supplied.

@lHostLinkNode::operator=@k_ZN12HostLink.author: AI Short Overview
@lHostLinkNode::operator=@k_ZN12HostLink.body: `operator=` takes an rvalue reference to another `HostLinkNode` and performs a move‑assignment, returning a reference to the current object after transferring ownership of its internal state.

@lHostLinkNode::operator=@k_ZN12HostLink.author: AI Short Overview
@lHostLinkNode::operator=@k_ZN12HostLink.body: The assignment operator copies the internal link data from the source node into the current node, updating any internal pointer references to match the new state, and then returns a reference to the modified instance.

@lHostLinkNode::~HostLinkNode@k_ZN12Host.author: AI Short Overview
@lHostLinkNode::~HostLinkNode@k_ZN12Host.body: The destructor of `HostLinkNode` performs cleanup when an instance is destroyed: it releases any owned resources (e.g., file handles, network sockets, memory allocated for link‑specific data) and ensures the internal state is left in a safe, non‑dangling state before the object is reclaimed by the runtime.

@lIFN_Beginning_Of_Field@p@l./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_Beginning_Of_Field@p@l./Source/Cur.body: The routine takes the form’s current field, synchronizes its buffer, moves the cursor to the field’s buffer start, and returns success.

@lIFN_Beginning_Of_Line@p@l./Source/Curs.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_Beginning_Of_Line@p@l./Source/Curs.body: The routine fetches the active field from the supplied form, synchronizes the backing buffer, computes the starting address of the current row’s data using the field’s column offset, moves the cursor to that position, and signals success with `E_OK`.

@lIFN_Down_Character@p@l./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_Down_Character@p@l./Source/CursesD.body: The routine increments the form’s current row counter, checks whether the new position equals the field’s row count, and if that condition is met, it returns success only when the navigation flag permits the transition; otherwise it rolls the row back and signals a denied request.

@lIFN_End_Of_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDia.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_End_Of_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDia.body: Synchronizes the form buffer, then locates the last usable byte in the current field’s buffer. It bumps the cursor back one byte when the field buffer ends at its maximum index, and finally returns success.

@lIFN_End_Of_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDial.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_End_Of_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDial.body: The routine takes the current field of the form, synchronises the form’s buffer, then finds the address just after that field’s data in the buffer. It moves the form’s cursor to that position (decrementing one byte if it would otherwise land exactly at the field’s end) and returns the status code E_OK.

@lIFN_Left_Character@p@l./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_Left_Character@p@l./Source/CursesD.body: The routine moves the cursor one column to the left. It decrements `form->curcol` first; if that causes the column to go past the left edge (negative), it restores the column position and returns `E_REQUEST_DENIED`. Otherwise, it succeeds and reports `E_OK`.

@lIFN_Next_Character@p@l./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_Next_Character@p@l./Source/CursesD.body: The routine moves the input cursor to the next field‑wide column. When the column index reaches the current field’s column count it wraps to the first column of the next row; if that row is the last one in the field it wraps to the next field’s first row. It returns an error code when the cursor would move past the form’s field layout.

@lIFN_Next_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_Next_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.body: The function increments the form’s current row index. If the new row index equals the field’s total row count, it optionally checks navigation logic. If that test fails, it rolls back the row index and returns a request‑denied status; otherwise it resets the column to zero and reports success.

@lIFN_Next_Word@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_Next_Word@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.body: The routine moves the form’s internal cursor to the beginning of the next non‑blank token in the current buffer. It first synchronises the buffer, finds the first space after the current position, then finds the real start of the following word, and either reports “no word found” or updates the cursor and signals success.

@lIFN_Previous_Character@p@l./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_Previous_Character@p@l./Source/Cur.body: This routine decrements the form’s cursor column; when the new column would be negative it backs up one row (decrementing the row). If that would underflow the top of the form it resets the cursor to the bottom‑right corner and signals a request denied; otherwise it reports success.

@lIFN_Previous_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lIFN_Previous_Line@p@l./Source/CursesDi.body: The function moves the cursor one line up in a form structure. It first checks that the current row index won’t go below zero; if it would, it restores the row to its previous value and returns an error. @lPlistSupportedPlatformVariantHelper@k_.author: AI Short Overview

The function `PlistSupportedPlatformVariantHelper` validates a JSON string value and maps it to an enum value.

@lPrevious_Choice@p@l./Source/CursesDial.author: AI Short Overview

@lPrevious_Enum@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.author: AI Short Overview
@lPrevious_Enum@p@l./Source/CursesDialog.body: The function inspects a field’s buffer against a list of keyword strings supplied in the `enumARG` structure. It scans the keywords from the end of the list backwards, comparing each keyword against the buffer with a case‑insensitive comparison routine (`Compare`). When a match is found, the field’s buffer is updated with that keyword and the function returns `TRUE`; otherwise it returns `FALSE`.

@lPrevious_Field_On_Page@p@l./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lPrevious_Field_On_Page@p@l./Source/Cur.body: The function walks backward through the current page’s field array until it finds the next selectable field. It starts at the field’s index, steps to the preceding slot, and if it reaches the page’s first field it wraps to the page’s last field. It exits when the new field is selectable and returns that field pointer.

@lPrevious_Page_Number@p@l./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lPrevious_Page_Number@p@l./Source/Curse.body:
The function computes the number of the page preceding the current page of a form.  
If the current page is zero, it wraps around to the last page (`maxpage‑1`), otherwise it decrements the current page index. The logic is expressed in a single conditional expression that returns the appropriate page number.

@lPrintCallStack@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Pri.author: AI Short Overview
@lPrintCallStack@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Pri.body: The routine consumes a backtrace list, trims the two bottom‑most entries, and then writes each remaining frame—skipping entries whose name is empty or whose line number equals the placeholder marker—to an output stream in order from the most recent call to the oldest. If a base source path is supplied, it normalises each file path to be relative to that source before printing.

@lQueryWindowsRegistry@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lQueryWindowsRegistry@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The template parses a list of options that describe which registry entry (key and view) and what to return (value name, value names, or sub‑keys). It validates the options, resolves the requested view type, and then invokes cmWindowsRegistry to read the appropriate registry data. The fetched string (or list) is stored as a makefile definition under the supplied variable name, with an optional error variable populated if requested.

@lRange::Range@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_15RangeC.author: AI Short Overview

@lRange::operator[]@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL__N_15.author: AI Short Overview

@lRccListParseContent@k_ZL19RccListParse.author: AI Short Overview
@lRccListParseContent@k_ZL19RccListParse.body: The function scans the supplied string for `<file…>` tags, extracts the filename from each match, and appends that name to the supplied vector.

@lRccListParseOutput::[lambda_0]@kRccLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lRccListParseOutput::[lambda_0]@kRccLis.body: The lambda `StripCR` accepts a string reference, locates a `'\r'` character, and if present replaces the string with the substring preceding that character. It effectively trims a trailing carriage‑return from the input string in‑place.

@lRccListParseOutput@k_ZL18RccListParseO.author: AI Short Overview
@lRccListParseOutput@k_ZL18RccListParseO.body: The function parses the standard‑output and error streams from an RCC compilation step, stripping any carriage‑return characters. It populates the supplied vector with each non‑empty line from the normal output; for error lines it looks for the pattern “Cannot find file ’…’”, extracts the filename following that marker, and if that pattern cannot be found it places a diagnostic message in `error` and returns `false`. If no parse error occurs, the function returns `true`.

@lReadJson@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_18ReadJsonER.author: AI Short Overview
@lReadJson@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_18ReadJsonER.body: The routine receives a JSON string, builds a `CharReader` with comment collection disabled, parses the string into a `Json::Value`, and throws a `json_error` containing the parse failure message if parsing fails; otherwise it returns the parsed `Json::Value`.

@lReadSubdirectory@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116R.author: AI Short Overview
@lReadSubdirectory@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116R.body: The function takes a path and a status object. It first verifies that a file exists at the given path; if not, it simply succeeds. Otherwise it attempts to switch the working directory to that path. It then searches for a specific test file—either `CTestTestfile.cmake` or `DartTestfile.txt`—appends that file’s name to the path and tries to read it via the makefile reader. If any step fails, it records an error on the status object and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lRealpath@k_Z8RealpathRKNSt3__112basic_.author: AI Short Overview
@lRealpath@k_Z8RealpathRKNSt3__112basic_.body: This helper calls the system‐level `realpath` routine to resolve a given path string. If the call succeeds, it copies the returned canonical path into the output string; if it fails, it optionally writes an error string (either the system errno message or a generic “Unknown error” message) and returns an empty string, otherwise falls back to the original path value. The function merely normalises a supplied path string, propagating failures via an optional output message.

@lRegexMatch@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110RegexMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lRegexMatch@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110RegexMa.body: The function takes a vector of string arguments, interprets the third element as a regular‑expression pattern and the fourth as a variable name. It clears any previous matches, compiles the regex, scans the concatenated remaining arguments for that pattern, and if a non‑empty match is found it stores the matched substring into the requested variable. If compilation fails or no match is found, it reports an error and returns false.

@lRegexMatchAll@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Rege.author: AI Short Overview
@lRegexMatchAll@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Rege.body: RegexMatchAll compiles the regex supplied in the third argument, scans the joined string of all following arguments for every occurrence that matches it, concatenates each match (separated by `;`), and stores the result in the variable named in the fourth argument. It returns `false` if the regex cannot be compiled or if an empty match is found.

@lRegexReplace@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Regex.author: AI Short Overview
@lRegexReplace@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Regex.body: It takes a vector of arguments, pulls the regex pattern, replacement text and the target variable name, checks that both the pattern and replacement are legal, concatenates any remaining arguments into a single input string, runs the regex substitution on that input, and, if successful, records the resulting string under the supplied variable name in the make‑file context.

@lRegisterUnitySources@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lRegisterUnitySources@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function adds a source file to a Unity batch by resolving its full path and records that file name under the key `UNITY_SOURCE_FILE` in the source file’s properties.

@lRelativeDate@p@l./Utilities/cmlibarchi.author: AI Short Overview
@lRelativeDate@p@l./Utilities/cmlibarchi.body: The routine calculates the time offset from a given start instant to the next occurrence of a specified weekday. It first normalizes the start to the target time‑zone by subtracting `zone`, obtains the weekday via `gmtime` (or its 64‑bit variant), then adds the minimal number of days needed to reach the desired weekday (optionally adjusting for daylight‑saving via `DSTcorrect`). The result is the number of seconds between the original start and that future occurrence.

@lRelativeIfUnder@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Re.author: AI Short Overview
@lRelativeIfUnder@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Re.body: The function simply delegates to `cmSystemTools::RelativeIfUnder`, returning the resulting string.

@lRelativeMonth@p@l./Utilities/cmlibarch.author: AI Short Overview
@lRelativeMonth@p@l./Utilities/cmlibarch.body: The function takes a base timestamp (`Start`), a time‑zone offset (`Timezone`), and a month offset (`RelMonth`). It obtains the local time representation of `Start` (using the available `localtime` implementation), then adds `RelMonth` to the month component while correctly handling year rollover. The resulting month and year are fed into `DSTcorrect`, which adjusts for daylight‑saving and the provided time‑zone, producing the final `time_t` value that is returned.

The procedure works in‑place on the node container, returning a cleaned list of unique nodes ready for further code generation.

@lRemoveDuplicatesNode::RemoveDuplicates.author: AI Short Overview

@lRemoveRPathELF@k_ZL14RemoveRPathELFRKi.author: AI Short Overview
@lRemoveRPathELF@k_ZL14RemoveRPathELFRKi.body: The routine opens the specified ELF file, scans the dynamic section for RPATH/RUNPATH entries, removes those entries from the dynamic table, rewrites the updated dynamic header, zero‑fills the corresponding string table entries, and reports whether the removal succeeded via the returned flag.

@lReplaceScriptVars@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview

@lReportCheckResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lReportCheckResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: ReportCheckResult receives a name of an operation and the outcome string. @lResolvePath@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111Resolv.author: AI Short Overview
@lResolvePath@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111Resolv.body: It walks the supplied JSON value following a list of keys or indices: starting at the root, it iteratively descends into objects or arrays, throwing an exception whenever a key isn’t present or the current node isn’t support the requested lookup. @lResourceIdHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116R.author: AI Short Overview
@lResourceIdHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116R.body: The function validates a string value as a proper resource ID. It first calls `JSONHelperBuilder::String` to check that the value is a string and not empty; if that fails it signals an invalid resource error and returns `false`. Then it attempts to match the string against a regular‑expression `IdRegex`. If the match fails, it reports an invalid resource error again and returns `false`. If both checks pass, the function returns `true`, indicating the ID is acceptable.

@lRight_Neighbour_Field@p@l./Source/Curs.author: AI Short Overview
@lRight_Neighbour_Field@p@l./Source/Curs.body: The routine walks the sorted field list starting from the supplied field until it encounters another entry that belongs to the same row (`frow`). It contains no dynamic allocation, so it does not allocate memory. The function relies on `Sorted_Next_Field()` advancing the list and on `field_on_page->frow` comparisons; a `NULL` pointer or a corrupt list could trigger a crash.

@lRmdir@k_Z5RmdirRKNSt3__112basic_string.author: AI Short Overview
@lRmdir@k_Z5RmdirRKNSt3__112basic_string.body: The function `Rmdir` simply forwards its `std::string` argument to the POSIX‑style `rmdir` system call: it calls `rmdir(dir.c_str())` and returns the call’s return value. Because it’s defined as `inline`, the compiler will typically inline it into callers, avoiding an extra function call overhead. It doesn’t perform any additional checks or error handling beyond what `rmdir` itself provides.

@lRootPresets::RootPresets@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview

@lRootPresets::RootPresets@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview

@lRootPresets::RootPresets@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview

@lRunCommand@k_ZL10RunCommandPKcRKib12Nu.author: AI Short Overview
@lRunCommand@k_ZL10RunCommandPKcRKib12Nu.body: RunCommand runs a command supplied as a vector of strings, optionally prints the command and its output. @lRunCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110RunComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lRunCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110RunComm.body: Runs the supplied command string in a new process: it sets the working directory if provided, hides the console window when requested, and runs the executable using the system’s shell. It captures both stdout and stderr, decodes the output per the requested encoding, and appends the decoded text to the caller’s output buffer. On success it returns the process’s exit value via retVal and signals success; on failure it returns an error message and a negative return value. The routine also contains special parsing logic for quoted commands on Windows to avoid quoting‑related execution errors.

@lRuntimeDependenciesArgs::RuntimeDepend.author: AI Short Overview

@lSearchPathSanitizer::SearchPathSanitiz.author: AI Short Overview

@lSetPropertyCommand::HandleAndValidateS.author: AI Short Overview

@lSetPropertyCommand::HandleAndValidateS.author: AI Short Overview

@lSetPropertyCommand::HandleAndValidateT.author: AI Short Overview
@lSetPropertyCommand::HandleAndValidateT.body: The function first invokes a helper to validate the test‑directory setting; if that helper signals failure it exits early with `false`. @lSetPropertyCommand::HandleSourceFileDi.author: AI Short Overview
