If so, it normalises the path relative to the current source directory, looks up the corresponding `cmMakefile` via the global generator, and assigns it to `directory_makefile`. If the directory does not exist, it records an error in `status` and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lSetPropertyCommand::MakeSourceFilePath.author: AI Short Overview
@lSetPropertyCommand::MakeSourceFilePath.body: The function returns the original path unchanged when `needed` is false; otherwise it collapses the path against the current source directory to produce an absolute file path.

@lSetPropertyCommand::MakeSourceFilePath.author: AI Short Overview
@lSetPropertyCommand::MakeSourceFilePath.body: When the caller indicates that absolute paths are required, this routine walks the supplied range of file names, calls the helper to turn each relative path into an absolute one, and appends the result to the output vector. If the flag is false, it simply copies the original entries into the destination vector and returns immediately.

@lSetRPathELF::[lambda_0]@kSetRPathELF::.author: AI Short Overview
@lSetRPathELF::[lambda_0]@kSetRPathELF::.body: It compares the two path variables; when they differ it assigns the new one to `outRPath`, then always returns `true`.

@lSetRPathELF@k_ZL11SetRPathELFRKiS0_PiP.author: AI Short Overview
@lSetRPathELF@k_ZL11SetRPathELFRKiS0_PiP.body:
`SetRPathELF` accepts a file name and a target path, along with optional error and change‑flag parameters.  
Internally it constructs a small lambda that, when called, simply assigns the new path to an `optional<std::string>` argument whenever the current value differs from the supplied one.  
The routine then hands that lambda to `AdjustRPathELF`, passing along a placeholder callback from `MakeEmptyCallback`. The result of `AdjustRPathELF`—an `optional<bool>` flag indicating success—is what `SetRPathELF` returns.

@lSetRPathXCOFF@k_ZL13SetRPathXCOFFRKiS0.author: AI Short Overview
@lSetRPathXCOFF@k_ZL13SetRPathXCOFFRKiS0.body: The routine updates the relative‑path value stored in a specified file. It accepts the file name, the new relative path to be written, and optional output slots for a diagnostic message and a flag that reports whether the path actually changed. It returns an optional<bool> indicating whether the operation succeeded.

@lSetupWorkflowConfigurePreset@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lSetupWorkflowConfigurePreset@k_ZN12_GL.body: The function assigns the supplied preset to the output pointer and returns true.

@lSetupWorkflowConfigurePreset@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lSetupWorkflowConfigurePreset@k_ZN12_GL.body: Checks whether the preset’s `ConfigurePreset` field matches the name of the provided `ConfigurePreset` object. If they differ, it logs an error via `cmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_WORKFLOW_STEPS` and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lShellPathNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13ShellPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lShellPathNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13ShellPa.body: The function receives a list of absolute‑path strings, validates each element, and converts path separators to the shell‑specific form. If any path isn’t absolute it reports an error and returns an empty string; otherwise it joins the validated strings with “;” on Windows or “:” on other systems and returns the concatenated result.

@lShellPathNode::ShellPathNode@k_ZN13She.author: AI Short Overview
@lShellPathNode::ShellPathNode@k_ZN13She.body: The constructor creates a new instance of `ShellPathNode`, copying the relevant information from the supplied temporary object (the unnamed parameter). It initializes the node’s internal fields with the values from that source node, so that the new node represents the same shell‑path expression in the parse tree.

@lShellPathNode::ShellPathNode@k_ZN13She.author: AI Short Overview
@lShellPathNode::ShellPathNode@k_ZN13She.body: The constructor copies the internal state from an existing `ShellPathNode`, setting up the new instance’s members to match that source. It is used whenever a node representing a shell‑path expression must be replicated within the generator’s expression‑node hierarchy.

@lShellPathNode::ShellPathNode@k_ZN13She.author: AI Short Overview
@lShellPathNode::ShellPathNode@k_ZN13She.body: This constructor simply constructs a `ShellPathNode` instance; it performs no additional initialization logic beyond the default construction of the object.

@lShellPathNode::operator=@k_ZN13ShellPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lShellPathNode::operator=@k_ZN13ShellPa.body: Assigns another `ShellPathNode` into the current object, effectively moving its internal state (e.g. path string and flags) into the target node while leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state.

@lShellPathNode::operator=@k_ZN13ShellPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lShellPathNode::operator=@k_ZN13ShellPa.body: Assigns another ShellPathNode into the current instance (copying its internal data members) and then returns a reference to the updated object.

@lShellPathNode::~ShellPathNode@k_ZN13Sh.author: AI Short Overview
@lShellPathNode::~ShellPathNode@k_ZN13Sh.body: The destructor `~ShellPathNode()` is responsible for releasing any resources owned by a `ShellPathNode` instance and for invoking cleanup logic defined in the base `cmGeneratorExpressionNode`. It ensures that any internal pointers or buffers are freed and that the node’s life‑cycle is properly terminated before the object is reclaimed by the system.

@lShell_CharIsMakeVariableName@k_ZL28She.author: AI Short Overview
@lShell_CharIsMakeVariableName@k_ZL28She.body: The function returns true when the input character is non‑zero and either an underscore or an alphabetic character.

@lShell_CharIsWhitespace@k_ZL22Shell_Cha.author: AI Short Overview
@lShell_CharIsWhitespace@k_ZL22Shell_Cha.body: The function returns true when the supplied character is a space or a tab character; otherwise it returns false.

@lShell_CharNeedsQuotesOnUnix@k_ZL27Shel.author: AI Short Overview
@lShell_CharNeedsQuotesOnUnix@k_ZL27Shel.body: It checks whether a character is one of the shell’s metacharacters that must be quoted in a Unix command line (for example, `'`, ``, `;`, `#`, `&`, `$`, `(`, `)`, `~`, `<`, `>`, `|`, `*`, `^`, `\`). If the character matches any of those, the function returns true.

@lShell_CharNeedsQuotesOnWindows@k_ZL30S.author: AI Short Overview
@lShell_CharNeedsQuotesOnWindows@k_ZL30S.body: The function returns true when the input character is one of the common shell metacharacters that must be quoted on Windows (`'`, `#`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `|`, `^`). It simply checks each candidate with a logical OR and yields a boolean.

@lSocketHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Socke.author: AI Short Overview
@lSocketHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Socke.body: Parses the JSON value into a map of socket names to resource vectors, checks that there is at most one socket set, clears or assigns the resulting vector to `out.Resources`, and returns true only when the single‑socket list is valid.

@lSorted_Next_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lSorted_Next_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDi.body: The function walks a singly‑linked list of `FIELD` structs, following the `snext` pointers until it encounters a field that satisfies the `Field_Is_Selectable` predicate, then returns that field. It keeps looping until it either returns to the starting field (detecting a cycle) or finds a selectable field, at which point it breaks out of the loop. If the input list contains no selectable elements, the loop will cycle back to the original pointer and the function will return that same pointer.

@lSorted_Previous_Field@p@l./Source/Curs.author: AI Short Overview
@lSorted_Previous_Field@p@l./Source/Curs.body: The routine walks backward through a doubly linked list of `FIELD` nodes, following the `sprev` pointer until it finds a node that satisfies `Field_Is_Selectable`. It stops when the search returns to the starting node, ensuring it never traverses beyond the list’s bounds. If no selectable node is found, the loop terminates only when it circles back to the original node, which can lead to an infinite loop if the list is malformed or no selectable node exists.

@lStaticLibraryCycle@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lStaticLibraryCycle@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The function performs a breadth‑first search over static‑library dependencies starting from the dependent target. It keeps a set of visited libraries and a queue of pending ones; each library’s own dependencies are enqueued only if they are static libraries and have not been visited before. If during traversal the origin target is reached, a cycle is detected and the routine returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lStorePackageRegistry@k_ZL20StorePackag.author: AI Short Overview
@lStorePackageRegistry@k_ZL20StorePackag.body: The function resolves the location where a package‑registry file should live, creates that directory if necessary, and writes the supplied content to a uniquely named file only when a file of the same name is not already present. It distinguishes between a build‑time location for the __HAIKU__ build and a user‑specific cache for other builds, using the appropriate environment variable in each case. If any system call fails, it reports a warning through the makefile instance.

@lStoreResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111StoreR.author: AI Short Overview
@lStoreResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111StoreR.body: The function forwards a value that may be `nullptr` into a generic `StoreResult` overload. It creates a `cmValue` wrapper around the `nullptr` argument and delegates to the underlying implementation, returning that function’s boolean result.

@lStoreResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111StoreR.author: AI Short Overview
@lStoreResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111StoreR.body: The function adds or removes a makefile definition based on the provided value. If the `infoType` is `OutSet`, it writes the variable as “1” or “0” according to the truthiness of the value. Otherwise (for `OutValue`) it writes the actual value when non‑zero, and deletes the definition if the value is zero/false. It always returns `true`.

@lStoreResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111StoreR.author: AI Short Overview
@lStoreResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111StoreR.body: StoreResult simply registers a variable definition in the supplied makefile by invoking its `AddDefinition` method with the given variable name and value.

@lStoreResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111StoreR.author: AI Short Overview
@lStoreResult@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111StoreR.body: It adds a definition to a makefile: if a non‑null property string is provided, that string is stored; otherwise an empty string is used.

@lStrEqualNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK12StrEqual.author: AI Short Overview
@lStrEqualNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK12StrEqual.body: The `Evaluate` member performs a simple equality comparison between the first two elements of the `parameters` vector. If they are equal, it returns the string `"1"`, otherwise it returns `"0"`. The extra parameters (`context`, `content`, `dagChecker`) are unused in this implementation.

@lStrEqualNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lStrEqualNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_.body: It supplies a constant value that the consuming code uses to verify the count of arguments it must pass to the constructor or factory routine for this class. In this case, the function reports exactly two parameters are required.

@lStrEqualNode::StrEqualNode@k_ZN12StrEq.author: AI Short Overview
@lStrEqualNode::StrEqualNode@k_ZN12StrEq.body: The `StrEqualNode` struct is a specialized expression node that represents a string‑comparison operation. It is declared `static const` so it is intended to be a single, reusable instance used during expression generation. When the parser encounters a string‑equality operator, it creates a `StrEqualNode` (normally in `cmGeneratorExpressionNode::Generate`) which is then integrated into the AST. This node inherits from `cmGeneratorExpressionNode` and implements the logic needed to evaluate or emit code that performs the string equality test at runtime.

@lStrEqualNode::StrEqualNode@k_ZN12StrEq.author: AI Short Overview
@lStrEqualNode::StrEqualNode@k_ZN12StrEq.body: Copies an existing **StrEqualNode** instance. The constructor simply duplicates the contents of the supplied node, ensuring the new node has the same internal state (e.g., left‑ and right‑operand references) as the source instance. This is the standard copy‑constructor pattern used when a node needs to be replicated while preserving its configuration.

@lStrEqualNode::StrEqualNode@k_ZN12StrEq.author: AI Short Overview
@lStrEqualNode::StrEqualNode@k_ZN12StrEq.body: The function builds a node that represents a string‑equality check in the AST, using the custom node type rather than the standard `==` operator. The comment suppresses the linter warning about modernizing the comparison to `==`.

@lStrEqualNode::operator=@k_ZN12StrEqual.author: AI Short Overview
@lStrEqualNode::operator=@k_ZN12StrEqual.body: The overload assigns a `StrEqualNode&&` into the current instance, performing a move‑semantics assignment: it copies or moves the internal state from the rvalue into the object, updates its members accordingly, and then returns `*this`.

@lStrEqualNode::operator=@k_ZN12StrEqual.author: AI Short Overview
@lStrEqualNode::operator=@k_ZN12StrEqual.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state from the source node into the current instance and returns a reference to that instance, allowing chained assignment.

@lStrEqualNode::~StrEqualNode@k_ZN12StrE.author: AI Short Overview
@lStrEqualNode::~StrEqualNode@k_ZN12StrE.body: When a `StrEqualNode` instance goes out of scope, its virtual destructor is invoked. It performs necessary cleanup for the node’s internal state—releasing any owned resources and ensuring the base `cmGeneratorExpressionNode` destructor runs to tidy up inherited resources.

@lStringSorter::ApplyFilter@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::ApplyFilter@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The method copies the input string into a local variable and sequentially applies every non‑null filter stored in the `Filters` collection to that string. Each filter receives the current string, produces a new string, and the method replaces the current string with that result. After all filters have run, the final string is returned.

@lStringSorter::GetCaseFilter@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::GetCaseFilter@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The `GetCaseFilter` function returns a `StringFilter` that performs case‑insensitive matching when the caller requests an insensitive comparison; otherwise it returns `nullptr` to signal no filter. It simply checks the `CaseSensitivity` enum value and maps it to the predefined `cmSystemTools::LowerCase` filter. The implementation is compact and avoids any dynamic allocation, ensuring O(1) performance.

@lStringSorter::GetCompareFilter@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::GetCompareFilter@k_ZN12_.body: The function returns the `GetFilenameName` filter when the argument is `FILE_BASENAME`; otherwise it yields `nullptr`.

@lStringSorter::GetComparisonFunction::[.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::GetComparisonFunction::[.body: This method acts as a small utility that inspects the two incoming string arguments—likely checking for equality or another defined relationship—and reports the outcome as a simple boolean flag.

@lStringSorter::GetComparisonFunction::[.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::GetComparisonFunction::[.body: This lambda takes two string references and returns `true` when the first string is lexicographically less than the second.

@lStringSorter::GetComparisonFunction::[.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::GetComparisonFunction::[.body: A short lambda that takes two string references and returns `true` when the first string is lexicographically less than the second.

@lStringSorter::GetComparisonFunction@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::GetComparisonFunction@k_.body: The function produces a callable predicate that reports whether the first string is considered “smaller” than the second one. When the requested comparison style is *natural*, it defers to a helper that performs a locale‑aware, case‑sensitive comparison; otherwise it falls back to a simple lexical comparison that uses the built‑in string operator. The returned lambda can be used wherever a `std::function<bool(const std::string&,const std::string&)>` is expected.

@lStringSorter::StringSorter@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::StringSorter@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The move‑constructor `StringSorter(StringSorter&&)` creates a new `StringSorter` by taking ownership of the internal data of the temporary (or otherwise rvalue) instance passed in, avoiding deep copies. It simply swaps the internal resources (e.g., pointers, buffers) with those of the source object, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state. This allows fast construction when the original is about to be discarded.

@lStringSorter::StringSorter@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::StringSorter@k_ZN12_GLOB.body:
Creates a sorting helper configured from a `SortConfiguration`.  
It builds internal filter objects for comparison and case handling, assigns the chosen comparison function to `SortMethod`, and records whether the requested order is descending.

@lStringSorter::StringSorter@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::StringSorter@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: Creates a new `StringSorter` object by copying the internal state of the supplied instance (used in e.g., line 99 of cmList.cxx).

@lStringSorter::operator()@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lStringSorter::operator()@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: Applies a filter to each input string, then calls the class’s `SortMethod` with the filtered strings swapped when the `Descending` flag is true. The return value of `SortMethod` is forwarded as the function’s boolean result.

@lStrucmp@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17StrucmpENSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lStrucmp@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17StrucmpENSt.body: The function compares two string views in a case‑insensitive way. It first handles the trivial cases of emptiness, otherwise it walks through the strings comparing each character after converting it to lower case, and finally returns the difference in lengths if the compared characters were equal, or the difference of the first differing character codes. This yields a negative, zero, or positive value that indicates lexical order.

@lSubConditionHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lSubConditionHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: SubConditionHelper attempts to parse a JSON node into a condition object. It first creates an empty unique_ptr<Condition>, passes it along with the JSON value and state to ConditionHelper. If ConditionHelper succeeds and the pointer is non‑null but its IsNull() flag is set, it reports an error via cmCMakePresetsErrors and returns false. Otherwise it moves the pointer into the output parameter and returns the helper’s boolean result.

@lSynchronize_Buffer@p@l./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lSynchronize_Buffer@p@l./Source/CursesD.body: When a form has been modified, `Synchronize_Buffer` clears the `_WINDOW_MODIFIED` flag, flags that a full check is required, writes the current buffer to the window with `Window_To_Buffer`, and finally moves the cursor to the new position with `wmove`.

@lSynchronize_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lSynchronize_Field@p@l./Source/CursesDi.body: Synchronize_Field refreshes a form field’s display: it clears the current field, applies justification for public fields, copies the buffer into the window, marks the field as changed, and returns a status code.

@lSynchronize_Linked_Fields@p@l./Source/.author: AI Short Overview
@lSynchronize_Linked_Fields@p@l./Source/.body: The routine walks the linked list that starts at the supplied `field`. For each node it calls `Synchronize_Field`. It stops if a call fails, and the first non‑OK error value is propagated back; otherwise `E_OK` is returned.

@lTLL::AffectsProperty@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTLL::AffectsProperty@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The routine inserts a property name into an internal set; if that name wasn’t already present, it calls the target object to attach that property to the current directory context, supplying the location trace for later resolution.

@lTLL::AppendProperty@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTLL::AppendProperty@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The method records a property change by calling `AffectsProperty`, then passes the property/value pair—together with a back‑trace from `Makefile`—onward to the target object's `AppendProperty` implementation.

@lTLL::HandleLibrary@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_13.author: AI Short Overview
@lTLL::HandleLibrary@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_13.body: This function checks that a library can be linked to a target under the current keyword or policy context, reports fatal or warning errors for signature conflicts or disallowed target types, and finally records the library in the target’s INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES property (optionally in specific configuration variants).

@lTLL::TLL@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_13TLLC1ER10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lTLL::TLL@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_13TLLC1ER10c.body: Constructs a TLL object by wiring together a Makefile instance and a Target. It first verifies that the target’s makefile matches the one supplied; if they differ it consults the CMP0079 policy. Depending on the policy returned value it flips one of three internal flags: WarnRemoteInterface, RejectRemoteLinking, or EncodeRemoteReference. When EncodeRemoteReference is on it builds a directory‑identifier string from the current makefile’s directory id.

@lTLL::TLL@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_13TLLC1ERKS0.author: AI Short Overview
@lTLL::TLL@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_13TLLC1ERKS0.body: Copies the internal state of an existing instance into a new object, preserving the linkage data that the rest of the code expects to be identical to the original.

@lTLL::~TLL@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_13TLLD1Ev@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lTLL::~TLL@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_13TLLD1Ev@f.body:
When an instance of `TLL` is destroyed, its destructor iterates over every string in the member `Props`.  
For each property it calls `Target->AppendProperty`, passing that string, a constant separator (`CMAKE_DIRECTORY_ID_SEP`), and a back‑trace string from `Makefile`.  
No other resource cleanup is performed.

@lTarget::AddBacktrace@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::AddBacktrace@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The method stores the index of a supplied back‑trace instance into a JSON value only when that instance is non‑null—writing the integer value under the key `"backtrace"`.

@lTarget::AddBacktrace@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::AddBacktrace@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The method inserts the supplied `bt` into the internal list `Backtraces`. If the addition succeeds (the list returns a valid index), it writes that index into the supplied JSON object under the key `"backtrace"`.

@lTarget::AddSourceCompileGroup@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::AddSourceCompileGroup@k_ZN12_G.body: The function creates or retrieves a compile‑group for a given source file. It builds a key from the file’s compile data, looks that key up in a map; if not present it allocates a new group entry, storing the group’s index and pushing it into the group container. Finally it records the caller’s source index in the group’s list and returns the group’s index. This way ensures each distinct compile data gets a single group and avoids duplicate entries.

@lTarget::AddSourceGroup@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::AddSourceGroup@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The function checks whether a given source group already exists in `SourceGroupsMap`. If it isn’t present, it records the group in the map, creates a new `SourceGroup` entry with the group’s full name, and appends that entry to the `SourceGroups` vector. Finally it appends the supplied array index (`si`) to the `SourceIndexes` list of that group and returns the new group's array position.

@lTarget::BuildCompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::BuildCompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function gathers compile‑time metadata from the source file, evaluates any generator expressions inside that metadata, and then populates a `CompileData` object with the resulting flags, options, include directories, framework directories, and pre‑defined macros. It handles language detection, optional pre‑compile headers, and collects both file‑level and configuration‑level definitions, ensuring that any user‑supplied expressions are resolved before being used in the final compile command.

@lTarget::CompileGroup::CompileGroup@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::CompileGroup::CompileGroup@k_Z.body: The CompileGroup function accepts a CompileGroup instance by rvalue reference and performs the necessary steps to compile that group of source files, resolving dependencies and producing the corresponding build artifacts.

@lTarget::CompileGroup::CompileGroup@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::CompileGroup::CompileGroup@k_Z.body: The `CompileGroup` constructor creates a new instance by copying all internal data from the supplied object, initializing its own member variables accordingly while ensuring that any allocated resources (e.g., buffers or symbol tables) are correctly cloned and that ownership semantics are preserved. It performs any necessary consistency checks on the input before committing the state.

@lTarget::CompileGroup::CompileGroup@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::CompileGroup::CompileGroup@k_Z.body: The `CompileGroup()` routine orchestrates the compilation of a collection of source files identified by a specific build group. It first resolves each file’s dependency tree, checks for cyclic or missing dependencies, and then schedules the individual files for parallel compilation jobs while keeping track of compilation state across threads. On completion, it aggregates the generated object modules, links them into a single binary, and records build metadata (timestamps, dependency paths, and build flags) in a shared manifest for incremental rebuilds. The routine ensures cache‑hits by consulting a pre‑computed hash map of source hashes; if unchanged, it skips re‑compilation and reuses the cached artefact. When any step fails, it propagates a diagnostic payload so the invoking build system can surface precise failure information.

@lTarget::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Target.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Target.body: The `Dump` method serializes a target’s internal state into a JSON object: it records the target’s name, type, unique ID, relative paths, and any special flags such as generator‑provided or install rules; it attaches back‑trace information, optional artifacts, and links (or archives) for executables or static libraries; it then incorporates dependency lists, source and compile group data, language specifics, and any folder or source group contexts before returning the fully populated `Json::Value` descriptor.

@lTarget::DumpArchive@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpArchive@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: Creates a JSON object that may contain two optional entries: a “commandFragments” array when there are fragments to serialize, and a single‑bit “lto” flag that is true if the current link‑language is in IPO mode.

@lTarget::DumpArtifacts@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpArtifacts@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The function walks through the target’s artifact map and builds a JSON array of file paths. For object libraries it collects the compiled object files; otherwise it emits the runtime binary. On Windows it also adds the import library and optional PDB file. The result is an array of objects each containing a single “path” field.

@lTarget::DumpCommandFragment@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpCommandFragment@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The function serializes the provided fragment into a JSON object, optionally adds a role field when supplied, attaches any back‑trace information via `AddBacktrace`, and then returns that JSON value.

@lTarget::DumpCommandFragments@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpCommandFragments@k_ZN12_GL.body: It turns a vector of fragments into a JSON array, serialising each element with `DumpCommandFragment` before returning the composed array.

@lTarget::DumpCompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpCompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function serialises a `CompileData` instance into a JSON‑compatible object by inspecting each field and adding it to the output only when that field is non‑empty. For each populated section—such as language, sysroot, compile flags, includes, frameworks, defines, pre‑compile headers, and language standard—the method calls the corresponding helper (`DumpSysroot`, `DumpCommandFragments`, `DumpInclude`, `DumpFramework`, `DumpDefine`, `DumpPrecompileHeader`, `DumpLanguageStandard`) to convert the raw data into the appropriate JSON representation. The resulting object contains keys that map directly to the input fields, ensuring a compact, self‑contained output that mirrors the original `CompileData` structure.

@lTarget::DumpCompileGroup@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpCompileGroup@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: It merges the compile data from the group’s first entry into a JSON object, adds the group’s source‑index list to that object, and returns the resulting `Json::Value`.

@lTarget::DumpCompileGroups@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpCompileGroups@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The function walks through the object’s internal `CompileGroups` collection, serializes each group by calling `DumpCompileGroup`, and returns a JSON array containing those serialized representations.

@lTarget::DumpDefine@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpDefine@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16.body: Returns a JSON object that contains the value from the supplied `def` and records the associated back‑trace information for later reference. The code simply sets the `define` field to `def.Value`, registers the back‑trace via `AddBacktrace`, and returns the constructed value.

@lTarget::DumpDependencies@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpDependencies@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: Obtains the target’s global generator, iterates over each direct dependency, serializes it with `DumpDependency`, and appends each serialized form to a JSON array that is returned.

@lTarget::DumpDependency@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpDependency@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The method constructs a JSON object that represents a dependency, inserting its identifier via `TargetId` and then attaching the dependency’s back‑trace information through `AddBacktrace`. It finally returns that populated JSON value.

@lTarget::DumpFileSet@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpFileSet@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: Creates a JSON object that contains the file‑set’s name, type and visibility, and fills an array with each supplied directory path resolved relative to the target’s top source directory. This object is then returned.

@lTarget::DumpFileSets@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpFileSets@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: Creates a JSON array of every file‑set in the current target and returns it together with a map that associates each file path to the index of the file‑set that contains it. The routine walks the target’s registered sets, serialises their file and directory entries, and builds a lookup table for later use.

@lTarget::DumpFolder@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpFolder@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16.body: The `DumpFolder` method queries the `GT` instance for a property named `"FOLDER"`. If that property exists, it creates a JSON object containing the folder’s name under the key `"name"`. The method then returns this JSON object; otherwise it returns an empty value.

@lTarget::DumpFramework@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpFramework@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The method simply forwards an `IncludeEntry` object to the `DumpInclude` routine and returns whatever JSON value that routine produces.

@lTarget::DumpInclude@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpInclude@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The `DumpInclude` helper builds a JSON representation for a single include entry: it constructs a JSON object, records the include’s path, tags it as a system include when appropriate, records the originating backtrace, and finally returns that populated object.

@lTarget::DumpInstall@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpInstall@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The `DumpInstall` method builds a JSON object containing the current install prefix and a list of destination paths. It calls `DumpInstallPrefix()` and `DumpInstallDestinations()` to populate the `prefix` and `destinations` fields respectively, then returns that object.

@lTarget::DumpInstallDestination@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpInstallDestination@k_ZN12_.body: Creates a JSON object that records the installation path for this component. It calls the supplied generator to obtain the destination path (via GetDestination), inserts that value under the key `"path"`, attaches any back‑trace information returned by the generator, and returns the resulting JSON object.

@lTarget::DumpInstallDestinations@k_ZN12.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpInstallDestinations@k_ZN12.body: Creates a JSON array containing the JSON results of each install‑generator. It first obtains the list of install generators via `GetInstallGenerators()`, then iterates through that list, calling `DumpInstallDestination()` for each generator and appending the returned JSON value to the array. Finally the array is returned.

@lTarget::DumpInstallPrefix@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpInstallPrefix@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: It pulls a definition string from the internal Makefile helper, normalises the path separators to Unix‑style slashes, packages that string into a JSON object under the key “path”, and returns that object.

@lTarget::DumpLanguageStandard@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpLanguageStandard@k_ZN12_GL.body: The function builds a JSON object that records the name of a language standard and, if present, a list of its backtrace indices. It populates a “standard” field and, when backtraces exist, adds a “backtraces” array containing each index. The resulting Json::Value is returned.

@lTarget::DumpLink@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Ta.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpLink@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Ta.body: Collects the link‑language via `GT->GetLinkerLanguage`, appends any command‑fragment data if present, then inserts a `sysroot` entry when the appropriate makefile definition is defined, and finally sets the `lto` flag when IPO is enabled.

@lTarget::DumpLinkCommandFragments@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpLinkCommandFragments@k_ZN1.body: Collects all of the flags, library paths and framework paths needed by the current target and turns them into a JSON array of “command‑fragment” objects, one per flag, path or library. The result can be fed straight into the linker command creation code.

@lTarget::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16T.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16T.body: It creates a JSON object that maps two keys—`source` and `build`—to the paths of the current source and build directories. It obtains those directories via the local generator, then normalises them to be relative to the top‑level source and build roots before returning the object.

@lTarget::DumpPrecompileHeader@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpPrecompileHeader@k_ZN12_GL.body:
Creates a JSON‐object that contains the supplied header string.  
It builds a new `Json::Value` called `precompileHeader`, stores the header text in its `"header"` field, attaches any back‑trace information via `AddBacktrace`, and returns this populated JSON value.

@lTarget::DumpSource@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpSource@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16.body: Creates a JSON object for a source file, resolving its full path, marking whether it is a generated file, appending back‑trace info, looking up its file‑set and source‑group indices, and for most kinds adding a compile‑group index before returning the constructed value.

@lTarget::DumpSourceGroup@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpSourceGroup@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The routine takes a `SourceGroup` reference, builds a JSON object containing the group’s name and a list of its source indexes (moving that list into the new value), and returns that object.

@lTarget::DumpSourceGroups@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpSourceGroups@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The method collects every `SourceGroup` in the current object by iterating over `this->SourceGroups`, serializes each group via `DumpSourceGroup`, and appends the resulting JSON value to a JSON array that it returns.

@lTarget::DumpSources@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpSources@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: Creates a JSON array of source descriptions by iterating over the generator target’s stored sources and calling `DumpSource` for each, appending the returned value to the array.

@lTarget::DumpSysroot@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::DumpSysroot@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function creates a JSON object containing the supplied file‑system path. It sets the field `"path"` to the given string and returns this object. No additional processing or validation occurs.

@lTarget::MergeCompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::MergeCompileData@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function constructs a new CompileData object for a given language. It first copies the language, system root, pre‑compile headers, and language standard from the target’s existing entry in CompileDataMap. Then it concatenates the source’s flags, includes, frameworks, and defines, placing the source‑specific items before the target‑wide ones. Finally, it removes duplicate definitions before returning the merged result.

@lTarget::ProcessLanguage@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::ProcessLanguage@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: Obtains per‑language compile parameters – language string, optional system‑root path, compile flags, pre‑defined macros, include directories (distinguishing framework/system paths), pre‑compiled headers, and the language standard.

@lTarget::ProcessLanguages@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::ProcessLanguages@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The routine fetches the set of language identifiers supplied by the generic translator (GT) via the current configuration, then iterates over that collection, invoking `ProcessLanguage` for each individual language string.

@lTarget::SourceGroup::SourceGroup@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::SourceGroup::SourceGroup@k_ZN1.body: This constructor creates a new `SourceGroup` by moving the internal state of an rvalue reference to another `SourceGroup`. It transfers owned resources (e.g., containers or handles) into the newly constructed instance without allocating new memory for those resources, leaving the source in a valid‑but‑unspecified state.

@lTarget::SourceGroup::SourceGroup@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::SourceGroup::SourceGroup@k_ZN1.body: Creates a new `SourceGroup` by copying all of its internal state from the supplied instance.

@lTarget::SourceGroup::SourceGroup@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::SourceGroup::SourceGroup@k_ZN1.body: The function creates and initializes a `SourceGroup` instance, wiring the underlying source objects together for later use.

@lTarget::Target@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::Target@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targ.body: Moves the internal state of an existing `Target` instance into a new instance via an rvalue reference, transferring ownership of any owned resources.

@lTarget::Target@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::Target@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targ.body: Initialises a `Target` object: stores the passed‑in generator (`gt`) and config string; obtains the project’s home directory and output directory from the global generator; pulls the source groups from the target’s makefile; and builds a `Backtraces` helper rooted at the home directory. All member variables are set in the initializer list.

@lTarget::Target@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::Target@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targ.body: The `Target` constructor performs a copy‑construction: it receives a `const Target&` argument and copies that object's internal state into the new instance, initializing all member fields (including any owned resources) accordingly. If any allocation fails, it may throw an exception.

@lTarget::ToJBT@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targe.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::ToJBT@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targe.body: The function constructs a new `JBT<T>` instance by copying the stored value from a `BTree<T>` argument and registering its back‑trace in the current object’s back‑trace collection. It simply forwards the value and appends the supplied trace to the existing history before returning the new `JBT` object.

@lTarget::ToJBTs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lTarget::ToJBTs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_16Targ.body: Creates a JBTs object from a given BTS<T> instance: it walks through the input’s back‑traces, adds each one to a back‑trace container, captures the returned indices in a vector, and finally returns a JBTs constructed with the original value and the gathered indices.

@lTargetArtifactBase::GetTarget@k_ZNK18T.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetArtifactBase::GetTarget@k_ZNK18T.body: The function takes a list of parameters, extracts the first entry as a target name, verifies that the name conforms to a known target format, and then queries the current context for a matching target. If the target does not exist or its type is disallowed (neither a library nor executable), it reports an error. Finally, if the evaluation context forbids certain targets (e.g. when a link‑library is being evaluated), the call fails, otherwise the resolved target object is returned.

@lTargetArtifactBase::TargetArtifactBase.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetArtifactBase::TargetArtifactBase.body: The `TargetArtifactBase` constructor accepts an rvalue reference (moved‑in) and initializes a new object of this type. It forwards that rvalue to its base class (`cmGeneratorExpressionNode`) and then runs any class‑specific initialization logic that follows the move operation. This pattern allows the object to be efficiently constructed from an existing instance without duplicating data.

@lTargetArtifactBase::TargetArtifactBase.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetArtifactBase::TargetArtifactBase.body: The constructor creates a new instance by copying the state of an existing `TargetArtifactBase` object, delegating the copy of member fields to its base class `cmGeneratorExpressionNode`.

@lTargetArtifactBase::TargetArtifactBase.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetArtifactBase::TargetArtifactBase.body: The constructor simply creates a `TargetArtifactBase` object without performing any initialization logic—the body is empty, so it performs no custom setup beyond the default construction of its members.

@lTargetArtifactBase::operator=@k_ZN18Ta.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetArtifactBase::operator=@k_ZN18Ta.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to a `TargetArtifactBase` and assigns its contents to the current object, typically performing a move‑style copy of internal state (e.g., copying member pointers or handles). It is invoked in places where a `TargetArtifactBase` instance is constructed from a temporary or returned from a factory function.

@lTargetArtifactBase::operator=@k_ZN18Ta.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetArtifactBase::operator=@k_ZN18Ta.body: The `operator=` function implements a copy‑assignment for `TargetArtifactBase`. It takes a `const TargetArtifactBase&` source, copies all of the source’s data members into the current object (including any inherited fields such as those from `cmGeneratorExpressionNode`), and returns a reference to the current object (`*this`). This allows chaining assignments and ensures the object’s state matches the source after the operation.

@lTargetArtifactBase::~TargetArtifactBas.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetArtifactBase::~TargetArtifactBas.body: The destructor of `TargetArtifactBase` performs the necessary cleanup for an instance of the class. It deallocates any owned resources, unwinds any child nodes or member objects, and ensures the object is left in a consistent state before it is removed from memory.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::HandleDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::HandleDi.body: The function appends a new property named “COMPILE_DEFINITIONS” to the provided target. It concatenates the supplied vector of strings with a helper join routine, then attaches the back‑trace of the current Makefile instance. Regardless of the `prepend` or `system` flags, it simply performs that append and returns `true` to signal success.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::HandleMi.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::HandleMi.body: If a target name is supplied that the project has not built, this routine triggers a fatal error via the makefile system, halting execution.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::Join@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::Join@k_Z.body: The `Join` function builds a single string from a vector of strings. It walks the vector in order; when an element starts with `‑D`, it drops that prefix and appends the remaining part, otherwise it appends the whole element. Each appended element is separated by a semicolon, so the result is a semicolon‑delimited list of the original strings with any leading `‑D` removed.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::TargetCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::TargetCo.body: Moves the target‑specific compile‑definition data from one instance into another, preserving the internal state while resetting the source to a valid, empty‑state form so that the new instance fully owns the configuration.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::TargetCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::TargetCo.body: This constructor creates a new instance of `TargetCompileDefinitionsImpl` by copying the internal state from an existing instance. It initializes the object’s own configuration of compile‑definitions data, preserving any command‑specific settings that are carried over to the new instance.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::TargetCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::TargetCo.body: The function walks through a target’s definition list, creating and registering each definition entry in the internal property store while honoring the conditions defined in the base class. It returns a success flag indicating that the definition set was populated correctly.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::cmTarget.body: The function cmTargetPropCommandBase is a public entry point that receives a reference to an execution‑status object. It is invoked from TargetCompileDefinitionsCommand to parse and handle command‑line arguments for a target definition. The routine delegates to TargetCompileDefinitionsImpl(status).HandleArguments(...), which performs the actual argument processing and returns the resulting status. The function therefore acts as a thin wrapper that forwards the status and argument parsing to the underlying implementation.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::operator.body: Moves the internal state of the source object into the destination and returns a reference to the destination.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::operator.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of another `TargetCompileDefinitionsImpl` into the current instance, returning a reference to the modified object.

@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::~TargetC.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileDefinitionsImpl::~TargetC.body: The overridden method orchestrates the compile‑time resolution of target‑specific definitions. It delegates the actual compilation to the base implementation, collects the resulting status, and returns it wrapped in the expected result object.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::HandleDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::HandleDirec.body: The function creates a `cmStandardLevelResolver` from the current `Makefile`, iterates over each string in `content`, and for each one calls `AddRequiredTargetFeature`. If that call fails, it stores the returned error message in `error`, invokes `SetError` with it, and returns `false`. If all calls succeed, it returns `true`.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::HandleMissi.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::HandleMissi.body:
The function intercepts a missing‑target situation by throwing a fatal error.  
When a compile feature is requested for a target that the current project does not build, it logs a message that the target “<name>” is unavailable and stops further processing.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::Join@k_ZN12.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::Join@k_ZN12.body: The `Join` method simply returns a string representation of the supplied vector of strings by delegating to `cmList::to_string`. It accepts a `const std::vector<std::string>&` argument and, via an override of a virtual interface, produces a single string containing the formatted list.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::TargetCompi.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::TargetCompi.body: A move‑constructor that initializes a new `TargetCompileFeaturesImpl` instance by transferring (moving) the internal state from the supplied rvalue reference to another `TargetCompileFeaturesImpl`.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::TargetCompi.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::TargetCompi.body: The constructor creates a new target‑features object by copying the compile‑feature settings from an existing instance. It ensures the new object inherits the exact feature set of the source, ready for further configuration or command handling.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::TargetCompi.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::TargetCompi.body: TargetCompileFeaturesImpl is a public member that initializes the command object. When invoked it registers the target‑specific compile‑features with the framework, populates internal data structures, and then triggers the generic compile‑flow that pulls feature flags from its base class. In effect, it wires up the command’s internal state so that later stages can query and apply the enabled features during a target‑specific build.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::cmTargetPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::cmTargetPro.body: The function creates and returns a `cmTargetPropCommandBase` instance that takes a reference to an execution‑status object and wires that status into the command‑handling machinery. It’s the entry point for initializing a command‑base and handing it back to the caller for further argument processing.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::operator=@k.body: The move‑assignment operator for `TargetCompileFeaturesImpl` accepts an rvalue reference of the same type. It copies (actually moves) the internal state from the source object into the target, ensuring that any owned resources are transferred rather than duplicated. It returns a reference to `*this`, enabling chained assignments. The function is intended to be used only when a temporary or already‑destroyed instance is being assigned, and it performs a shallow copy of internal members, preserving invariants of the derived `cmTargetPropCommandBase`.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::operator=@k.body: Copies data from the supplied instance into this object, then returns a reference to the updated object.

@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::~TargetComp.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetCompileFeaturesImpl::~TargetComp.body: The implementation of `~TargetCompileFeaturesImpl()` gathers the target‑specific compile settings (e.g., optimization flags, language dialects, and other compiler options) from the surrounding infrastructure and applies them to the build system so that the generated binaries match the target’s requirements.

@lTargetExistsNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK16Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetExistsNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK16Targ.body: The method validates that exactly one target name is supplied and that the name conforms to the internal target‑name rules. It then queries the current makefile to see whether a target with that name is defined, returning the string `"1"` if found or `"0"` if not.

@lTargetExistsNode::NumExpectedParameter.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetExistsNode::NumExpectedParameter.body: Returns the constant value 1, indicating that the class expects a single parameter when this virtual function is invoked.

@lTargetExistsNode::TargetExistsNode@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetExistsNode::TargetExistsNode@k_Z.body: TargetExistsNode is a public constructor that creates a node representing a target‑existence test. It derives from cmGeneratorExpressionNode so that node can be inserted into an expression tree during code generation.

@lTargetExistsNode::TargetExistsNode@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetExistsNode::TargetExistsNode@k_Z.body: TargetExistsNode is a statically defined node in the generator expression hierarchy that represents a check for the existence of a specific target within the system. It inherits from cmGeneratorExpressionNode and is employed in the generator logic, notably around line 411 of cmGeneratorExpressionNode.cxx, to evaluate whether a target is present.

@lTargetExistsNode::TargetExistsNode@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetExistsNode::TargetExistsNode@k_Z.body: Checks whether a target node exists and returns a Boolean result indicating success.

@lTargetExistsNode::operator=@k_ZN16Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetExistsNode::operator=@k_ZN16Targ.body: The `operator=` overload lets a `TargetExistsNode` be assigned from another instance of the same type. It takes the source as an rvalue reference (`TargetExistsNode &&`), copies all of its data members into the target object, and then returns a reference to the left‑hand side (`*this`). This allows chaining of assignments and efficient move‑style copying without allocating new nodes.

@lTargetExistsNode::operator=@k_ZN16Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetExistsNode::operator=@k_ZN16Targ.body: The assignment operator copies the source node’s internal state into the current object, returning `*this`.

@lTargetExistsNode::~TargetExistsNode@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetExistsNode::~TargetExistsNode@k_.body: ~TargetExistsNode() checks whether a specific target node is present in the current generator expression tree. It returns a boolean result that other parts of the system use to decide whether to continue processing that node or skip it.

@lTargetFileArtifact::Evaluate@k_ZNK18Ta.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifact::Evaluate@k_ZNK18Ta.body: The `Evaluate` method first resolves a `target` through `GetTarget`. If no target is found, it returns an empty string. Otherwise it calls `TargetFileArtifactResultGetter<ArtifactT>::Get` with that target, the current context, and content. If an error was recorded in the context during that call, it again returns an empty string; otherwise the retrieved result string is returned.

@lTargetFileArtifact::NumExpectedParamet.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifact::NumExpectedParamet.body: It returns the single integer 1 that the calling code uses to know how many arguments a concrete class derived from this interface is expected to provide when its abstract operation is invoked.

@lTargetFileArtifact::TargetFileArtifact.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifact::TargetFileArtifact.body:
The `TargetFileArtifact` function is a simple constructor‑style routine that produces a representation of a file artifact in the system.  
Because the body is empty, the implementation is a placeholder that other code will fill in or rely on default construction.  
The comment `// NOLINT(modernize-use-equals-default)` indicates the intent is to avoid the automatic value‑initialization that newer C++ standards encourage, keeping the constructor explicit.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: The static function `Get` accepts a `cmGeneratorTarget*` and returns a string that represents the target’s current state (often used in expression evaluation). It performs a simple lookup and serialization of the target’s data into a standard string format.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: The function simply fetches the file‑prefix string for a given target by asking the target object to provide it using the configuration supplied in the expression context. It returns whatever string the target’s `GetFilePrefix` method yields for that configuration.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: The function simply forwards the current configuration from the supplied `context` to the target, calling `GetFileSuffix` on that target and returning the resulting string.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: The `Get` function checks whether a `cmGeneratorTarget` possesses an import library. If it does, it returns the file‑prefix string for that library; otherwise it yields an empty string.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: Checks if the target’s config includes an import‑library flag; if the flag is present it calls the target’s `GetFileSuffix` for the import‑library artifact and returns that string, otherwise it returns an empty string (the passed `GeneratorExpressionContent*` argument is unused).

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: The function first verifies that the target can be linked; if not, it logs an error and returns an empty string. Then it selects the artifact type (import‑library or runtime binary) based on whether the target has an import library for the given configuration, and finally returns the corresponding file prefix via GetFilePrefix.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: The function checks whether the supplied target is link‑able; if not, it emits an error about the required `ENABLE_EXPORTS` flag and returns an empty string. It then decides whether the target represents an import library or a normal runtime binary, and finally asks the target for the appropriate file‑suffix string based on that artifact type.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: The Get routine first verifies that the supplied target is linkable. If it is not, it reports an error and returns an empty string. When the target declares an import library it immediately returns the corresponding file‑prefix string. If neither condition applies, it returns an empty string.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: The function retrieves a file‑suffix string for a target. It first ensures the target can be linked; if not, it reports an error tied to the specific suffix rule and returns an empty string. When the target is linkable, it checks whether an import library is associated with the current configuration and, if so, returns the suffix provided by that library; otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: Checks whether the given target can be linked, emits an error if it’s a non‑exporting library, and otherwise returns the library’s file prefix for a DLL; if the target isn’t a DLL it returns an empty string.

@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileArtifactResultGetter::Get@k_.body: The `Get` function first validates that the supplied target is linkable and not a static library; if either condition fails it reports an error and returns an empty string. If the target is a DLL‑compatible platform and not a static library, it returns the appropriate file suffix for the requested runtime binary artifact; otherwise it simply returns an empty string.

@lTargetFileBaseNameArtifact::Evaluate@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lTargetFileBaseNameArtifact::Evaluate@k.body: The routine first resolves a target from the supplied inputs; if it cannot be found it returns an empty string. @lTransformActionGenexStrip::~TransformA.body:
`TransformActionGenexStrip` is a concrete implementation of the `TransformAction` interface that performs a “genex‑strip” operation on the graph model.  
In practice it traverses the graph, identifies nodes or edges that match a *Genex* pattern (typically a generic operation that has become redundant after a previous transformation), and removes or replaces them with a simpler construct.  
The implementation usually follows these steps:

1. Scan the graph for *Genex* nodes that satisfy the strip criteria (e.g., a specific opcode or metadata flag).  
2. For each matched node, rewire its incoming and outgoing edges to preserve connectivity while discarding the node itself.  
3. If the node is part of a composite operation, update any surrounding control‑flow or data‑flow edges accordingly.  
4. Finally, emit a concise report of the changes so downstream passes can adjust their state.  

This helper is invoked from several points in the code base, notably at line 504 of `cmList.cxx`, where the system needs to prune the intermediate *Genex* representation after a generic transformation phase.

@lTransformSelectorIndexes::TransformSel.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorIndexes::TransformSel.body: The `TransformSelectorIndexes` routine walks through the stored selector indices in a `TransformSelector` instance and rewrites them into a canonical form suitable for the current transformation pass. It takes the existing map of logical selector IDs to the underlying physical indices, applies any pending translation rules (including aliasing or renaming that might have been added by earlier passes), and writes the updated mapping back into the selector’s internal data structure. The function finally returns a new instance of the transformed selector that can be injected back into the pipeline for subsequent stages.

@lTransformSelectorIndexes::TransformSel.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorIndexes::TransformSel.body: It updates the internal mapping of selector indexes after a transformation operation.

@lTransformSelectorIndexes::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorIndexes::operator=@k_.body: The assignment operator copies another `TransformSelectorIndexes` object into the current instance, updating all of its internal fields (indexes, masks, etc.) and then returns a reference to the modified object.

@lTransformSelectorIndexes::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorIndexes::operator=@k_.body: Copies the contents of the supplied `TransformSelectorIndexes` into the current instance and returns a reference to that instance.

@lTransformSelectorIndexes::~TransformSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorIndexes::~TransformSe.body:
The `~TransformSelectorIndexes()` virtual function is part of the **TransformSelector** hierarchy.  
When an instance of **TransformSelectorIndexes** is instantiated, this override is invoked automatically during the generic transform process to convert the internal representation of selector indexes to the format required by the particular selector type. In practice it receives the current selector index mapping, applies the specific re‑indexing rules for the “Indexes” selector (for example, remapping a flat index sequence into a multi‑dimensional scheme), and returns the transformed index map. This hook is what lets the generic `TransformSelector` framework plug in selector‑specific index logic without duplicating code in every selector implementation.

@lTransformSelectorRegex::InSelection@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorRegex::InSelection@k_.body: The function returns `true` when the supplied string matches the internal regular‑expression (`Regex`) and `false` otherwise—it simply exposes the regex‑matching test for callers.

@lTransformSelectorRegex::TransformSelec.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorRegex::TransformSelec.body: Initializes a `TransformSelector` with the type identifier `"REGEX"` and stores the supplied regex string in a member variable. The constructor consumes the string via move semantics.

@lTransformSelectorRegex::TransformSelec.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorRegex::TransformSelec.body: `TransformSelectorRegex` is a helper that builds a `TransformSelector` instance from a regular‑expression pattern. It parses a string pattern, compiles it into a `std::regex`, and stores the compiled pattern so that subsequent `TransformSelector` calls can match targets against that regex.

@lTransformSelectorRegex::TransformSelec.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorRegex::TransformSelec.body: Initializes the internal `Regex` member with the argument and forwards `"REGEX"` to the base `TransformSelector` constructor.

@lTransformSelectorRegex::TransformSelec.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorRegex::TransformSelec.body: Creates a new `TransformSelectorRegex` instance by copying the source instance’s internal state, thereby setting up the regex‑based selector configuration for subsequent matching operations.

@lTransformSelectorRegex::Validate@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorRegex::Validate@k_ZN1.body: It returns whether the current object’s internal regex object reports itself valid. The function ignores the size_t argument and simply forwards that status.

@lTransformSelectorRegex::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorRegex::operator=@k_ZN.body: The operator= takes a TransformSelectorRegex and returns a reference to it, effectively creating a new TransformSelectorRegex instance that can be used in subsequent transformations.

@lTransformSelectorRegex::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorRegex::operator=@k_ZN.body: The assignment operator copies the internal configuration (including regex pattern and any associated flags) from the provided `rhs` object into the current instance and returns a reference to the current object for chaining.

@lTransformSelectorRegex::~TransformSele.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransformSelectorRegex::~TransformSele.body: The `~TransformSelectorRegex` virtual function generates a regex‑based selector string for the current selection rule. It takes the internal selector representation, composes it into a regex pattern (handling any required escaping or capturing groups), and returns that string for use in filtering or matching operations elsewhere in the code.

@lTransitiveLinkImpl::Compute::[lambda_0.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransitiveLinkImpl::Compute::[lambda_0.body: Checks whether the supplied item is present in the `Excluded` set of the current instance.

@lTransitiveLinkImpl::Compute@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransitiveLinkImpl::Compute@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The `Compute` routine takes the current list of libraries, clears its own list, re‑inserts the original libraries into the emitted set, then processes each original item by first following the target’s direct dependencies and finally appending the item itself. After all items are added, it prunes the list by erasing any entries that match the excluded set.

@lTransitiveLinkImpl::Follow@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransitiveLinkImpl::Follow@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The method walks a target’s link interface, recursing through its HeadInclude items, emitting each library only once, marking any context‑sensitive condition, and recording exclusions from the HeadExclude list.

@lTransitiveLinkImpl::TransitiveLinkImpl.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransitiveLinkImpl::TransitiveLinkImpl.body: The constructor builds a new instance by taking ownership of another one. It accepts an rvalue reference (the unnamed argument) and performs a move‑style transfer of the internal state, avoiding any expensive copying. This allows code such as in `cmGeneratorTarget.cxx` to recycle an existing `TransitiveLinkImpl` object quickly without reallocating resources.

@lTransitiveLinkImpl::TransitiveLinkImpl.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransitiveLinkImpl::TransitiveLinkImpl.body: The constructor of `TransitiveLinkImpl` simply stores the supplied arguments into its member fields (`Self`, `Config`, `ImplFor`, `Impl`). It performs no other initialization logic; its purpose is to make the object ready to be used via those stored references.

@lTransitiveLinkImpl::TransitiveLinkImpl.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransitiveLinkImpl::TransitiveLinkImpl.body: Creates a new `TransitiveLinkImpl` object that replicates the state of the supplied instance. The constructor copies the internal configuration, references, and any flag values so that the new object behaves equivalently to the original.

@lTransitiveUsage::TransitiveUsage@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTransitiveUsage::TransitiveUsage@k_ZN1.body: The constructor initializes a TransitiveUsage instance by storing the supplied `name` in `LogicalName`, the supplied `location` in `Location`, and the supplied `LookupMethod` in `Method`. It uses `std::move` on the string arguments to avoid unnecessary copies. The constructor performs no further logic beyond these member initializations.

@lTree::BuildUnit@k_ZNK4Tree9BuildUnitER.author: AI Short Overview
@lTree::BuildUnit@k_ZNK4Tree9BuildUnitER.body: The function iterates over the `files` vector, emitting a `<Unit>` element with a `filename` attribute composed of the supplied `fsPath` plus the file name. Inside each `<Unit>`, it writes an `<Option>` child carrying a `virtualFolder` attribute pointing to `"CMake Files\\"`. After finishing the file list, it traverses each sub‑`Tree` in `folders` and delegates to a helper that recursively builds the same structure for nested directories.

@lTree::BuildUnitImpl@k_ZNK4Tree13BuildU.author: AI Short Overview
@lTree::BuildUnitImpl@k_ZNK4Tree13BuildU.body: The function traverses the tree in depth‑first order, emitting an `<Unit>` element for every file that records its full path and a nested `<Option>` node containing a path string that maps the file into a virtual folder hierarchy. It then recurses into sub‑directories, appending each child’s relative path to the current virtual and filesystem prefixes before processing the child’s own files.

@lTree::BuildVirtualFolder@k_ZNK4Tree18B.author: AI Short Overview
@lTree::BuildVirtualFolder@k_ZNK4Tree18B.body: The method writes an XML element named “Option”, builds a string of virtual‑folder paths by iterating over its child folders, hands that string to each child via BuildVirtualFolderImpl for further processing, then records the resulting list as a “virtualFolders” attribute before closing the element.

@lTree::BuildVirtualFolderImpl@k_ZNK4Tre.author: AI Short Overview
@lTree::BuildVirtualFolderImpl@k_ZNK4Tre.body: The routine builds a virtual path string by appending a “CMake Files\” prefix, the current node’s path and a trailing backslash, then recurses through each child node appending its own path to the same string. It relies on string concatenation with the `+` operator and expects that all string arguments are correctly escaped for backslashes. The function is a simple depth‑first traversal that progressively constructs a slash‑separated list of virtual folder paths.

@lTree::InsertPath@k_ZN4Tree10InsertPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lTree::InsertPath@k_ZN4Tree10InsertPath.body: The `InsertPath` method walks the vector of path components (`split`), creating or reusing `Tree` nodes as it descends. When the remaining component count is zero, the file name is added to the current node’s `files` set; otherwise it searches `folders` for a matching child and recurses into it. If no child matches, a new `Tree` instance is built for the component and appended to `folders`, with its own subtree built recursively. This design allows a hierarchical file‑tree where each level holds its subfolders and files, and new paths are integrated by creating missing intermediate nodes automatically.

@lTree::Tree@k_ZN4TreeC1EOS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTree::Tree@k_ZN4TreeC1EOS_.body: The public constructor initializes a `Tree` instance by taking ownership of a temporary, typically moving the contents into its internal data structures and setting up any necessary state.

@lTree::Tree@k_ZN4TreeC1ERKS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lTree::Tree@k_ZN4TreeC1ERKS_.body: Creates a new tree object by copying all member data from the provided instance. The constructor performs a member‑wise copy (shallow copy for value members; deep copy for dynamic members) to preserve the original tree’s structure and invariants.

@lTree::Tree@k_ZN4TreeC1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lTree::Tree@k_ZN4TreeC1Ev.body: The **Tree** function initializes and returns an instance of the internal tree structure, wiring its fields (e.g., left/right children, key/value pairs) and exposing standard tree operations such as insertion, traversal, and search.

@lTryCompileCompileDefs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lTryCompileCompileDefs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: Appends the supplied value to the argument set’s `CompileDefs` collection and signals that processing should continue by returning `Continue::Yes`.

@lTryCompileLangProp@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lTryCompileLangProp@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: Stores the provided key/value pair in the `args.LangProps` map (converting both arguments to `std::string` in the process) and returns `Continue::No`.

@lTryReachPresetFromWorkflow@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lTryReachPresetFromWorkflow@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The function looks up a named preset in the supplied map. If the preset is missing or its source file isn’t among the reachable files of the originating workflow, it records the appropriate error and returns false. When the preset is found and reachable, it hands the preset’s expanded form to SetupWorkflowConfigurePreset<T>, which performs the preset’s configuration and then returns true to signal success.

@lTryRunCommandImpl::DoNotRunExecutable@.author: AI Short Overview
@lTryRunCommandImpl::DoNotRunExecutable@.body: The routine performs the plumbing for a cross‑compile “try_run” helper: it copies the built executable to a permanent location, records whether that run succeeded, and emits a small CMake‑style report file with the result and any captured stdout/stderr so the caller can inspect the outcome. If the run failed it flags the cache entry as advanced, writes a minimal error message to the results file, and aborts the build with an explicit error message.

@lTryRunCommandImpl::RunExecutable@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lTryRunCommandImpl::RunExecutable@k_ZN1.body: The function builds a command string that optionally prefixes a defined emulator, appends quoted arguments from that emulator, and finally appends the executable path and any supplied run arguments. It then invokes `RunSingleCommand`, passing pointers for stdout/stderr and an optional working directory. Depending on the success flag, it stores the exit code as a string in `RunResultVariable`; if caching is disabled, it writes that string as a normal definition, otherwise it caches it.

@lTryRunCommandImpl::TryRunCode@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lTryRunCommandImpl::TryRunCode@k_ZN12_G.body: The function parses the supplied command‑line arguments, performs a compile‑try for the command, and if the compilation succeeds (exit code 0) it executes the compiled binary. It captures stdout/stderr according to the supplied output‑variable options, sets the run‑result variables in the Makefile, and finally cleans up any temporary files or directories created during the try‑run.

@lTryRunCommandImpl::TryRunCommandImpl@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lTryRunCommandImpl::TryRunCommandImpl@k.body: The implementation takes an existing command object, transfers its ownership into a fresh context, registers that command with the internal registry, then immediately triggers its execution pipeline and returns the result status.

@lTryRunCommandImpl::TryRunCommandImpl@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lTryRunCommandImpl::TryRunCommandImpl@k.body: This code declares a constructor for `TryRunCommandImpl`. It takes a pointer to a `cmMakefile` and passes that pointer directly to its base class constructor (`cmCoreTryCompile`). No additional logic is executed in the body.

@lTryRunCommandImpl::TryRunCommandImpl@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lTryRunCommandImpl::TryRunCommandImpl@k.body: `TryRunCommandImpl` is the concrete implementation that executes a user‑supplied shell command through the underlying `cmCoreTryCompile` framework. It takes a command string, runs it via the system shell (usually via `system()` or an equivalent API), and captures the exit status and any output streams. The method returns an `CmdResult` object that signals success or failure along with any captured stdout/stderr. The function handles validation of the command path, sets environment variables, and cleans up temporary resources before returning.

@lTwoArgsSignature@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116T.author: AI Short Overview
@lTwoArgsSignature@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116T.body: The function validates that at least two arguments were supplied, retrieves the current makefile from the status object, ensures a configuration type (defaulting to “Release” if none is defined), constructs the command needed to rebuild the project, and either returns success immediately if that definition is already cached or stores the new command in the cache before returning success.

@lUndo_Justification@p@l./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lUndo_Justification@p@l./Source/CursesD.body: Undo_Justification writes the original contents of a field back to a window: it locates the buffer’s start, calculates the length of data that follows that point, and, if any data remains, rewrites that string to the window after moving the cursor to the top‑left position.

@lUpperCaseNode::AcceptsArbitraryContent.author: AI Short Overview
