@lUpperCaseNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13UpperCa.author: AI Short Overview
@lUpperCaseNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK13UpperCa.body: The method is a public, const override that returns the upper‑cased value of the first string supplied in the `parameters` vector.

@lUpperCaseNode::UpperCaseNode@k_ZN13Upp.author: AI Short Overview
@lUpperCaseNode::UpperCaseNode@k_ZN13Upp.body: The constructor of `UpperCaseNode` accepts an rvalue of the same type and forwards its internal contents to initialize a new instance—essentially enabling the node to represent an identifier already transformed to uppercase for later expression‑generation use.

@lUpperCaseNode::UpperCaseNode@k_ZN13Upp.author: AI Short Overview
@lUpperCaseNode::UpperCaseNode@k_ZN13Upp.body: The constructor takes an already‑constructed `UpperCaseNode` instance and creates a new node that behaves exactly like the original—essentially a shallow copy that preserves the internal expression tree while ensuring any new construction follows the same ownership semantics for the node hierarchy.

@lUpperCaseNode::UpperCaseNode@k_ZN13Upp.author: AI Short Overview
@lUpperCaseNode::UpperCaseNode@k_ZN13Upp.body: The function normalizes a node’s string representation, ensuring the node’s identifier or content is converted to upper‑case form before further processing.

@lUpperCaseNode::operator=@k_ZN13UpperCa.author: AI Short Overview
@lUpperCaseNode::operator=@k_ZN13UpperCa.body: The assignment operator for `UpperCaseNode` takes an rvalue reference to another `UpperCaseNode` and copies its internal data into the current instance, returning a reference to the modified object. This allows chaining of assignments while handling self‑assignment safely.

@lUpperCaseNode::operator=@k_ZN13UpperCa.author: AI Short Overview
@lUpperCaseNode::operator=@k_ZN13UpperCa.body: The `operator=` function is a copy‑assignment operator for `UpperCaseNode`. It takes a single parameter by const reference (the source node) and copies all data members into the current object, then returns `*this`. It implements the usual semantics of an assignment operator: it performs a member‑wise copy, handles self‑assignment safely, and returns a reference to the object for chaining. This operator is declared `public` in the `UpperCaseNode` class, enabling external code to assign one node to another with the standard `=` syntax.

@lUpperCaseNode::~UpperCaseNode@k_ZN13Up.author: AI Short Overview
@lUpperCaseNode::~UpperCaseNode@k_ZN13Up.body: The `~UpperCaseNode()` function is a virtual destructor for the `UpperCaseNode` type, ensuring that when an instance of this node is deleted, any resources tied to the `UpperCaseNode` (such as internal expression trees or cached results) are properly released in derived classes.

@lUpper_Neighbour_Field@p@l./Source/Curs.author: AI Short Overview
@lUpper_Neighbour_Field@p@l./Source/Curs.body: This function walks upward in the sorted field list to find the first field that precedes the given field’s row. It moves up to the previous line, then scans leftward until it reaches the right‑most field on that line, returning that field. If no previous line exists, it returns the original field.

@lUserArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lUserArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: Iterates over the supplied names, inserting each into the map with a default‑constructed `T`. @lUserArgumentParser::BindKeywordsMissin.author: AI Short Overview

@lUserArgumentParser::BindKeywordsMissin.author: AI Short Overview
@lUserArgumentParser::BindKeywordsMissin.body: The function registers a callback that captures any keyword arguments lacking an explicit value: each such keyword is appended to the supplied vector for later handling.

@lUserArgumentParser::UserArgumentParser.author: AI Short Overview
@lUserArgumentParser::UserArgumentParser.body: UserArgumentParser is a move constructor that takes an rvalue reference to an existing instance and creates a new object by transferring ownership of its internal state.

@lUserArgumentParser::UserArgumentParser.author: AI Short Overview
@lUserArgumentParser::UserArgumentParser.body: The `UserArgumentParser` constructor creates a new parser instance by copying the state of an existing parser object, preserving any previously‑parsed arguments and configuration so that subsequent argument‑handling code can reuse that state without re‑parsing from scratch.

@lUserArgumentParser::UserArgumentParser.author: AI Short Overview
@lUserArgumentParser::UserArgumentParser.body: `UserArgumentParser` is a utility that, when invoked, walks through a collection of CLI tokens and builds a strongly‑typed representation of the supplied options. It inherits from `cmArgumentParser<void>`, thereby reusing the base parsing logic but adding domain‑specific validation (e.g., required flags, default values, and type conversions). On construction, it immediately registers known options (such as `--help`, `--config`, etc.) and exposes a single entry point—typically a `parse()` method—that returns a populated argument‑object or throws an informative exception if the input is malformed.

@lVSC_Generic@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.author: AI Short Overview
@lVSC_Generic@p@l./Source/CursesDialog/f.body: Moves the current cursor row of a `FORM` by the requested number of lines, constraining the movement to the form’s data‑row limits. It returns `E_OK` on success or `E_REQUEST_DENIED` if the move would exceed the available rows.

@lVSC_Scroll_Half_Page_Backward@p@l./Sou.author: AI Short Overview
@lVSC_Scroll_Half_Page_Backward@p@l./Sou.body: The routine computes a negative offset equal to half the current rows plus one and forwards that to VSC_Generic, yielding the resulting scroll adjustment.

@lVSC_Scroll_Half_Page_Forward@p@l./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lVSC_Scroll_Half_Page_Forward@p@l./Sour.body: The routine calls the generic scrolling helper, passing the form and a delta that equals roughly one‑half‑page of the current form. It returns the helper’s result.

@lVSC_Scroll_Line_Backward@p@l./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lVSC_Scroll_Line_Backward@p@l./Source/C.body: The routine forwards the form object to `VSC_Generic`, passing a fixed negative step (-1) that tells the generic routine to shift the display upward by one line, then returns the result code from that generic call.

@lVSC_Scroll_Line_Forward@p@l./Source/Cu.author: AI Short Overview
@lVSC_Scroll_Line_Forward@p@l./Source/Cu.body: The function simply forwards the current form’s line pointer by one, delegating the actual step‑change logic to `VSC_Generic`. It returns whatever status the generic routine reports (typically an error code or success flag).

@lVSC_Scroll_Page_Backward@p@l./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lVSC_Scroll_Page_Backward@p@l./Source/C.body: The routine invokes `VSC_Generic` with the form and the negative of its current row count, effecting a backward scroll.

@lVSC_Scroll_Page_Forward@p@l./Source/Cu.author: AI Short Overview
@lVSC_Scroll_Page_Forward@p@l./Source/Cu.body: It forwards the current form view by passing the form and its current row count to the generic scrolling routine, returning whatever status that routine emits.

@lValidateAndConvertPermissions@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lValidateAndConvertPermissions@k_ZN12_G.body:
The routine receives an optional list of permission strings.  
If the list is empty it reports success immediately.  
Otherwise it walks the list, converting each string into a `mode_t`.  
When a string cannot be parsed it records an error message, flags a fatal condition and returns failure; only when every entry converts cleanly does it return success.

@lValueToString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Valu.author: AI Short Overview
@lValueToString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Valu.body: The `ValueToString` function returns a `std::string` representation of a C‑style string: if the passed pointer is non‑null it returns the pointer’s string value; if it’s null it returns an empty string. It’s a tiny wrapper that safely converts a raw C‑string into a `std::string` while guarding against null dereference.

@lValueToString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Valu.author: AI Short Overview
@lValueToString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Valu.body: The function simply returns the provided string unchanged, acting as a pass‑through that accepts a `const` reference and yields the same value.

@lValueToString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Valu.author: AI Short Overview
@lValueToString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113Valu.body: Converts a `std::size_t` value to its decimal string representation, returning a `std::string`.

@lVariableHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Var.author: AI Short Overview
@lVariableHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Var.body: The function converts a JSON value into a `CacheVariable`. It sets the `out` variable to a `CacheVariable` whose `Type` field is either `"BOOL"` (for booleans) or empty (for strings), and whose `Value` field contains the literal `"TRUE"`/`"FALSE"` or the string text. For objects it initializes a temporary variable and forwards the value to `VariableObjectHelper`. If the JSON value is `null`, it assigns `cm::nullopt` to `out`. The function returns `true` on success and `false` after reporting an invalid variable type.

@lVariableValueHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lVariableValueHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The helper examines the incoming JSON value. If it’s null, it clears the output string and succeeds. If the value is a Boolean, it writes the literal “TRUE” or “FALSE” into the output string. For any other kind of value it delegates to `VariableStringHelper` to perform the appropriate conversion.

@lVersion::Version@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17Ve.author: AI Short Overview
@lVersion::Version@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17Ve.body: The function constructs (or re‑initialises) a `Version` instance from an rvalue reference to another `Version` object and an auxiliary placeholder argument. It returns the newly created `Version` object, enabling fluent chaining or assignment scenarios.

@lVersion::Version@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17Ve.author: AI Short Overview

@lVersion::Version@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17Ve.author: AI Short Overview

@lVersionCompare@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114Ver.author: AI Short Overview

@lVersionNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK11VersionNo.author: AI Short Overview
@lVersionNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK11VersionNo.body: The `Evaluate` function compares the first two entries in the supplied `parameters` vector using `cmSystemTools::VersionCompare`. If the comparison succeeds, it returns the string `"1"`; otherwise it returns `"0"`.

@lVersionNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lVersionNode::NumExpectedParameters@k_Z.body: It returns the constant 2, indicating the class expects exactly two parameters.

@lVersionNode::VersionNode@k_ZN11Version.author: AI Short Overview
@lVersionNode::VersionNode@k_ZN11Version.body: The constructor simply creates a new `VersionNode` object. It performs no custom initialization beyond the default construction of its member fields.

@lVertical_Scrolling@p@l./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lVertical_Scrolling@p@l./Source/CursesD.body: The routine only invokes the supplied callback when the current field isn’t a single‑line field. If the callback succeeds (returns E_OK) it sets the _NWTTOP flag on the current field and then returns the callback’s result; otherwise it simply returns E_REQUEST_DENIED.

@lVisitEnv@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_18VisitEnvER.author: AI Short Overview
@lVisitEnv@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_18VisitEnvER.body: The routine sets the cycle state to *InProgress*, expands macros in the supplied string, propagates any macro‑expansion failure, and upon success flags the status as *Verified* before returning `Ok`.

@lVisitPreset@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111VisitP.author: AI Short Overview
@lVisitPreset@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111VisitP.body: The template walks a preset’s inheritance tree. It first marks the preset as “in‑progress” to catch cycles, then validates that the preset’s own data is sane (no empty name, non‑null condition). For each parent in its inheritance list, it locates the parent preset, confirms the parent is reachable from the current file, recurses into that parent, then merges the parent’s environment into the current preset and adopts its condition evaluator if none is already set. After all parents are processed, it performs a post‑inheritance hook on the preset, finally marking the preset as “verified” and returning success.

@lWindow_To_Buffer@p@l./Source/CursesDia.author: AI Short Overview
@lWindow_To_Buffer@p@l./Source/CursesDia.body: It walks through the rows of the given window, copies each line into the field’s buffer, and afterward replaces any padding characters with standard blanks before terminating the buffer with a null byte.

@lWorkflowStepTypeHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lWorkflowStepTypeHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The helper reads a JSON value and maps it to an enum value. It first guards against a null value and ensures the JSON is a string. Then it compares the string against the allowed step names (“configure”, “build”, “test”, “package”). If a match is found it assigns the corresponding enum value and returns success; otherwise it records an invalid‑preset error and returns failure.

@lWrapping_Not_Necessary_Or_Wrapping_Ok@.author: AI Short Overview
@lWrapping_Not_Necessary_Or_Wrapping_Ok@.body: The routine checks whether the current field requires a line wrap. If a wrap is needed, it computes the split point, inserts the wrapped text onto the next line, and updates the cursor position accordingly. If no wrap is needed or the operation fails, it simply returns E_OK (or E_REQUEST_DENIED on failure).

@lWriteDepfile::[lambda_1]@kWriteDepfile.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteDepfile::[lambda_1]@kWriteDepfile.body: It captures a string reference and returns it unchanged, effectively acting as an identity function for `std::string`. This is the minimal, direct logic of the lambda.

@lWriteDepfile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Write.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteDepfile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112Write.body: The routine iterates over the dependency list, normalises each path relative to the project’s top‑binary directory (unless the generator is Xcode, in which case absolute paths are kept), and writes the formatted entries to the supplied stream. For every dependency it writes its rule filenames first, then a colon followed by its path names, each separated by a newline. If the requested format is a “make‑style” depfile, it also emits a phony target entry for each path after the main list. The helper `WriteFilenameGcc` is used to render the individual file names.

@lWriteFilenameGcc@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116W.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteFilenameGcc@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116W.body: Writes the filename to a stream, replacing spaces with “ \\ ” and backslashes with “\\\\”.

@lWriteFilesArgument@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteFilesArgument@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The routine writes a list of file paths to an output stream. It forwards the list of items to `WriteMultiArgument`, supplying an inline formatter that returns each item's path wrapped in quotes. The formatter appends the supplied configuration string to the item’s path before emitting it.

@lWriteGenexEvaluatorArgument@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteGenexEvaluatorArgument@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The function takes a keyword and a list of “genex” strings, runs each through a generator expression evaluator with a supplied config and local generator, and if a non‑empty result is produced, it escapes the string for CMake syntax before writing it out via `WriteMultiArgument`.

@lWriteJson@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_19WriteJson.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteJson@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_19WriteJson.body: This function serializes a `Json::Value` to a string: it creates a `Json::StreamWriterBuilder`, configures it to indent with two spaces and to omit comments, and then calls `Json::writeString` to perform the actual conversion, returning the resulting JSON text.

@lWriteMSBuildAdditionalInputs@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteMSBuildAdditionalInputs@k_ZN12_GL.body: The routine silently skips empty content, prefixes a UTF‑8 BOM to the output stream, then flattens every path in the supplied dependency list. It normalises each path into an absolute form (expanding relative parts against the binary directory when needed), replaces forward slashes with back‑slashes, and streams the paths into the output file separated by semicolons, appending a trailing line‑feed.

@lWriteMessageEvent@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteMessageEvent@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112.body: The routine writes a “message” event to the log only when the configured log version 1 is active. It starts an event with a “message‑v1” tag, emits the supplied text as a literal block, and then closes the event.

@lWriteMultiArgument@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteMultiArgument@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The function iterates over a list of values, applies a user‑supplied transform that may produce an optional string, and writes each returned string to an output stream prefixed by a given indentation and keyword.

@lWriteTryRunEvent@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116W.author: AI Short Overview
@lWriteTryRunEvent@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116W.body: The function emits a “try_run‑v1” event into the supplied log only when the corresponding log level is active. It records the compile‑time state via WriteTryCompileEventFields, then logs the run result’s attributes (variable, caching flag, any captured stdout/stderr, and the exit code if present). It performs safe conversion of the exit code into an integer, falling back to the raw string if parsing fails.

@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::E.author: AI Short Overview
@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::E.body: The overload accepts a C‑string, safeguards against a null pointer by converting it to an empty `std::string` when `expression` is `nullptr`, and then delegates to the string‑based `Evaluate` overload, returning the same reference result.

@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::E.author: AI Short Overview
@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::E.body:
The `Evaluate` method runs the given expression through the internal expression interpreter.  
If the compiled expression reports a context‑sensitive condition, it logs a fatal error that includes the expression, the problematic property, and the source file path.  
Finally, it returns the processed string produced by the interpreter.

@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::X.author: AI Short Overview
@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::X.body: The constructor initializes a `XCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter` object by delegating to its base class `cmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter` with the given target and language strings, and stores the supplied `sourceFile` in the `SourceFile` member for later use during expression interpretation.

@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::X.author: AI Short Overview
@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::X.body: The function `XCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter` is a public entry point used by the code‑generation subsystem to walk an expression AST and produce the corresponding code fragments. When invoked it receives an expression node, examines its kind (literal, binary operation, function call, etc.), and recursively resolves sub‑expressions, emitting the appropriate intermediate representation (e.g., assembly instructions, bytecode or intermediate representation) that will later be stitched into the final generated source. It essentially bridges the syntax tree to the code‑generation logic, ensuring that every expression node is translated correctly into the target language.

@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::o.author: AI Short Overview
@lXCodeGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::o.body: The overload assigns a new interpreter to the current object and returns a reference to that object, enabling fluent chaining of calls. It’s used in the global generator to plug in a new interpreter instance during code‑generation passes.

@lXML_SetUnknownEncodingHandler@kXML_Set.author: AI Short Overview
@lXML_SetUnknownEncodingHandler@kXML_Set.body: Sets a callback that the parser will invoke whenever it comes across an XML character encoding it can’t recognize. The function stores the supplied handler pointer and user‑supplied opaque data in the parser object so that when an “unknown‑encoding” event is detected the parser can forward the callback with the context supplied in the third argument.

@lZeroNode::AcceptsArbitraryContentParam.author: AI Short Overview
@lZeroNode::AcceptsArbitraryContentParam.body: The method simply indicates that any content parameter is considered acceptable by always returning `true`. It is declared `const` and `override`, so it can be overridden by derived classes but inherently performs no validation logic.

@lZeroNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK8ZeroNode8Eval.author: AI Short Overview
@lZeroNode::Evaluate@k_ZNK8ZeroNode8Eval.body: This method consumes a list of string parameters, context objects, and content data, then orchestrates the evaluation logic—typically invoking the `cmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker` to validate the expression graph before producing a stringified result. The returned string is the textual representation of the evaluation outcome.

@lZeroNode::GeneratesContent@k_ZNK8ZeroN.author: AI Short Overview
@lZeroNode::GeneratesContent@k_ZNK8ZeroN.body: The method is a stub that signals “no content is produced.” It returns `false`, effectively marking that the current implementation does not generate any content and is intended to be overridden by derived classes.

@lZeroNode::ZeroNode@k_ZN8ZeroNodeC1EOS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lZeroNode::ZeroNode@k_ZN8ZeroNodeC1EOS_.body: ZeroNode simply creates a constant‑zero expression node within the compiler’s expression tree. It produces a node that represents the literal value 0 (or 0.0 for floating types) and registers it with the surrounding generator infrastructure. The node is plain—no operands, no side‑effects—so it acts as a reusable “zero” placeholder wherever a zero value is required in generated code.

@lZeroNode::ZeroNode@k_ZN8ZeroNodeC1ERKS.author: AI Short Overview
@lZeroNode::ZeroNode@k_ZN8ZeroNodeC1ERKS.body: ZeroNode creates a new ZeroNode instance that contains no value or state – effectively a no‑op copy constructor that leaves the new node empty.

@lZeroNode::ZeroNode@k_ZN8ZeroNodeC1Ev@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lZeroNode::ZeroNode@k_ZN8ZeroNodeC1Ev@f.body: ZeroNode(){} constructs an object with all member variables zero‑initialized, performing no additional logic. It simply returns a freshly‑constructed instance.

@lZeroNode::operator=@k_ZN8ZeroNodeaSEOS.author: AI Short Overview
@lZeroNode::operator=@k_ZN8ZeroNodeaSEOS.body: The `operator=` overload on `ZeroNode` implements a move‑assignment that accepts an rvalue reference to another `ZeroNode` instance, assigns its contents to the current object (typically via member‑wise assignment or member‑wise move operations), and returns a reference to the modified object. It permits expressions like `node1 = std::move(node2);`, ensuring the source object is left in a valid but unspecified state.

@lZeroNode::operator=@k_ZN8ZeroNodeaSERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lZeroNode::operator=@k_ZN8ZeroNodeaSERK.body: The assignment operator copies all of ZeroNode’s data members from the supplied argument into the target instance, then returns a reference to that instance so calls can be chained.

@lZeroNode::~ZeroNode@k_ZN8ZeroNodeD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lZeroNode::~ZeroNode@k_ZN8ZeroNodeD1Ev.body: The destructor for ZeroNode cleans up any resources the node owns. When an instance is destroyed—either automatically at end of scope or explicitly via delete—it releases internal allocations and ensures any virtual cleanup expected by its base class is performed.

@l[lambda_0]::operator()@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@l[lambda_0]::operator()@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL_.body: The function evaluates two `cmList::TransformAction` arguments and returns `true` only when the supplied actions satisfy the specific internal condition (e.g., identical or compatible). It is a lightweight const check used in the surrounding code to decide whether a list transformation should proceed.

@l[lambda_0]@k[lambda_0]#@o1@p@l[unnamed.author: AI Short Overview
@l[lambda_0]@k[lambda_0]#@o1@p@l[unnamed.body: A lambda used as a comparison predicate; it takes two values and returns `true` when the first argument is strictly less than the second.

@l[lambda_0]@k[lambda_0]#@o1@p@l[unnamed.author: AI Short Overview
@l[lambda_0]@k[lambda_0]#@o1@p@l[unnamed.body: Accepts a string and a pointer but always returns true.

@l__archive_get_date@k__archive_get_date.author: AI Short Overview
@l__archive_get_date@k__archive_get_date.body: The function parses a human‑readable date string (p) relative to a given epoch time (now). It tokenises the string, builds a state machine that recognises date/time components, applies defaults (local zone, current date when omitted), handles relative offsets (e.g. “next week”, “+3 days”), computes the resulting absolute epoch value, and returns that value (or 0 if the computed time equals the special error value -1).

@l__builtin___memset_chk@k__builtin___me.author: AI Short Overview
@l__builtin___memset_chk@k__builtin___me.body: The `__builtin___memset_chk` routine implements a bounds‑checked variant of the standard `memset` operation: it copies a specified number of bytes from a source buffer into a destination buffer while verifying that the destination’s size is sufficient for the requested copy. On entry it performs a quick bounds check against the supplied size arguments; if the check passes, the routine performs the raw memory copy (often via a simple `memcpy` or loop) and then returns the destination pointer. This helper is typically used internally by the compiler to replace ordinary `memset` calls with a safer, compiler‑generated implementation that automatically guards against out‑of‑bounds writes.

@l__builtin_object_size@k__builtin_objec.author: AI Short Overview
@l__builtin_object_size@k__builtin_objec.body: The function `__builtin_object_size` calculates the size of an object at runtime. It takes a pointer to an object and an integer flag and returns that size as an `unsigned long`. This result is then used by the compiler to supply the correct size argument to calls such as the `memset` invocations seen in `archive_getdate.c`.

@l_nc_Copy_Argument@k_nc_Copy_Argument@f.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Copy_Argument@k_nc_Copy_Argument@f.body:
The routine creates a copy of a `TypeArgument` instance for the specified type.  
If the type declares it has arguments (`_HAS_ARGS`) it recursively copies the left/right sub‑arguments for linked types.  
When a `copyarg` function is present it delegates copying to that; otherwise it simply returns the original pointer.  
On allocation failure it increments the supplied error counter and returns `NULL`.

@l_nc_Copy_Type@k_nc_Copy_Type@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Copy_Type@k_nc_Copy_Type@f./Source.body: The routine duplicates a FIELD’s type and argument. It copies the type pointer, then deep‑copies the argument via `_nc_Copy_Argument`, propagating any copy error. On failure it frees any partially allocated argument, resets the fields, and returns FALSE; on success it bumps the type’s ref‑count (if present) and returns TRUE.

@l_nc_First_Active_Field@k_nc_First_Acti.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_First_Active_Field@k_nc_First_Acti.body: It returns the first visible field on the current form page. It walks back from the last field on that page, and if no visible field is found it returns the page’s first visible field instead.

@l_nc_Free_Argument@k_nc_Free_Argument@f.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Free_Argument@k_nc_Free_Argument@f.body:
It releases an argument structure according to its type descriptor.  
If the type’s `status` has the `_LINKED_TYPE` bit set, it recursively frees the left‑ and right‑sub‑arguments and then frees the current node.  
Otherwise, if a type‑specific free routine (`freearg`) is supplied, that function is invoked; if none is present the argument is left untouched.

@l_nc_Free_Type@k_nc_Free_Type@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Free_Type@k_nc_Free_Type@f./Source.body: The routine decrements the reference counter of the type stored in the field, then frees the argument structure with `_nc_Free_Argument`.

@l_nc_Internal_Validation@k_nc_Internal_.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Internal_Validation@k_nc_Internal_.body: The routine performs in‑place validation of the current field of a form. It first synchronises the form’s internal buffer, then checks whether the field is either marked as required or flagged as not already OK. If validation fails it clears the “required” flag on the form, marks the field as changed, and synchronises any fields that depend on it. If all checks pass it returns success.

@l_nc_Make_Argument@k_nc_Make_Argument@f.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Make_Argument@k_nc_Make_Argument@f.body: The routine walks a type‑descriptor tree, allocating a new `TypeArgument` node for each linked type. It recurses on the `left` and `right` sub‑nodes, or if the node supplies a `makearg` function it delegates construction to that factory. Any allocation or factory failure bumps the shared error counter.

@l_nc_Position_Form_Cursor@k_nc_Position.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Position_Form_Cursor@k_nc_Position.body: The routine moves the form’s internal cursor to the current field’s screen position. It first validates the passed form, fetches the current field, and the form’s window. It then issues a raw `wmove` to the form window. If the field contains invisible regions, it performs an explicit move on the field’s window with an offset calculation and synchronises the cursor; otherwise it simply synchronises the form window. The function returns success or error codes.

@l_nc_Refresh_Current_Field@k_nc_Refresh.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Refresh_Current_Field@k_nc_Refresh.body: The routine updates the visual representation of the active field. It calculates the appropriate scrolling offsets for public (scrollable) fields—handling both horizontal single‑line and vertical multi‑line cases), copies the affected area of the form window into the field window via `copywin`, and then performs the necessary window synchronisation calls before returning the cursor to its proper screen position.

@l_nc_Set_Current_Field@k_nc_Set_Current.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Set_Current_Field@k_nc_Set_Current.body: The routine switches the form’s active field to *newfield*, reallocating the field’s window if necessary, refreshing the display only when the field actually changes (or when the form isn’t already posted). It performs argument validation, clears the old window when required, adjusts the form’s status bits (_WINDOW_MODIFIED, _NEWTOP), and enforces justification or visibility rules before handing control back to the caller.

@l_nc_Set_Form_Page@k_nc_Set_Form_Page@f.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Set_Form_Page@k_nc_Set_Form_Page@f.body: When invoked, this routine changes the form’s current page when the supplied page number differs from the current page. It redraws all fields marked visible on that page, then sets the current field either to a supplied field or to the first field of the page. The routine reports any error encountered during redraw or field selection.

@l_nc_Synchronize_Attributes@k_nc_Synchr.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Synchronize_Attributes@k_nc_Synchr.body: When called it updates a field’s visual representation in its form. It first makes sure the field exists; if the field belongs to an active form and is actually drawn, it synchronises the field’s buffer with the form’s current window, applies justification rules if necessary, and finally forces a repaint of the field’s area. If the field is not visible, it falls back to a full field display. The routine returns a status code indicating success or the error that occurred.

@l_nc_Synchronize_Options@k_nc_Synchroni.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Synchronize_Options@k_nc_Synchroni.body: The routine updates a field’s option set, first taking a snapshot of the old options and computing the XOR between the new and old values to discover what bits changed. If the field is the active field in its containing form, it rolls back to the original options and reports that the current field cannot be altered. For visibility changes it checks whether the field should now be shown or erased – a visible bit that was added triggers a Display_Field call; a visible bit that was cleared triggers Erase_Field. It also handles the transition to or from the static flag: clearing static removes the “may‑grow” status bit and may force a redraw if justification is in effect. Finally, if any of these redraw operations fail, the function returns the error code; otherwise it returns success (E_OK).

@laddFileSetEntry@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115ad.author: AI Short Overview
@laddFileSetEntry@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115ad.body: The routine compiles directory entries for a file‑set, evaluates them with the current target and configuration, and then iterates through each file entry: it creates a `TargetPropertyEntryFileSet` for that file, adds it to the global entry list, resolves the file’s full path, and if the file is not already in a source group it inserts the file into a “Header Files” group (only when the set is a headers set). It also emits author‑level warnings if path resolution fails and aborts if resolution cannot be performed.

@laddFilesToItsSourceGroups@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@laddFilesToItsSourceGroups@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The routine walks through each path in **sgFilesPaths**, tokenises it (optionally prefixed by *prefix*), finds or creates a source‑group that matches that tokenised path, and registers the file (with its full collapse‑resolved path) inside that group. If any group cannot be obtained, it reports the failure via *errorMsg* and aborts the operation.

@laddInterfaceEntry@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@laddInterfaceEntry@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The routine walks through a list of library links; for each link that owns a target it builds a local evaluation context, invokes the target’s EvaluateInterfaceProperty with the supplied property string and that context, collects the produced values, flags whether the evaluation was context‑sensitive, and appends the resulting EvaluatedTargetPropertyEntry into the supplied collection.

@larchive_entry_gid@karchive_entry_gid.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_gid@karchive_entry_gid.body: Retrieves the 64‑bit identifier stored in an `archive_entry` and returns it as a `la_int64_t`. This value is used elsewhere in the system for lookup, comparison or identification of the entry.

@larchive_entry_gname@karchive_entry_gna.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_gname@karchive_entry_gna.body: The function returns a pointer to the name string stored in the given `archive_entry` structure. It expects a pointer to a `struct archive_entry` and simply yields the internal name field (a `const char *`) for use elsewhere in the code—such as the call in `cmSystemTools.cxx` at line 1929.

@larchive_entry_hardlink@karchive_entry_.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_hardlink@karchive_entry_.body: The function `archive_entry_hardlink` takes an `archive_entry` and returns a C‑string pointer that represents the hard‑linked file name (or its canonical path) associated with that entry. It is used internally to resolve the hard‑link target when reading or writing entries in the archive.

@larchive_entry_nlink@karchive_entry_nli.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_nlink@karchive_entry_nli.body: The routine reads the `nlink` field of an `archive_entry` structure and returns that count (zero if the field is absent or uninitialized). It performs no allocation, merely inspecting the stored value.

@larchive_entry_pathname_w@karchive_entr.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_pathname_w@karchive_entr.body: The function returns a pointer to the archive entry’s path name as a `const wchar_t*`. It guarantees the string is null‑terminated and safe for read‑only use in subsequent string operations.

@larchive_entry_size@karchive_entry_size.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_size@karchive_entry_size.body: `archive_entry_size` computes and returns the exact byte size of an `archive_entry` instance. It performs the necessary calculations to determine the amount of storage occupied by the entry’s data and metadata, then returns that size as a `size_t` value for use in the calling code.

@larchive_entry_strmode@karchive_entry_s.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_strmode@karchive_entry_s.body: The function `archive_entry_strmode` takes a pointer to a `struct archive_entry` and returns a `const char *` that represents the entry’s file‑mode bits in a human‑readable string form (for example, “r‑w‑x” style strings for regular files, “d” for directories, etc.).

@larchive_entry_symlink@karchive_entry_s.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_symlink@karchive_entry_s.body: The function `archive_entry_symlink` takes a pointer to an `archive_entry` structure and returns a C‑string that represents the symbolic link target associated with that entry. This string is used elsewhere in the code to resolve or compare symlink destinations when processing archive entries.

@larchive_entry_uid@karchive_entry_uid.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_uid@karchive_entry_uid.body: The function returns the 64‑bit UID stored in the given `archive_entry`. It reads the `uid` field (a `la_int64_t`) and performs a simple bounds check, returning the value or `0` if the entry is invalid. This provides a quick way to map an entry back to its unique identifier.

@larchive_entry_uname@karchive_entry_una.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_entry_uname@karchive_entry_una.body: The function returns a pointer to the uname string stored in the supplied `archive_entry` structure (or `NULL` if the entry is invalid or its name field is unset).

@larchive_error_string@karchive_error_st.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_error_string@karchive_error_st.body: Returns a pointer to the error message stored inside the given `archive` instance, providing a readable error string for the caller.

@larchive_match_excluded@karchive_match_.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_match_excluded@karchive_match_.body: The function evaluates a given `archive_entry` against the archive’s exclusion rules and returns a status code indicating whether the entry should be ignored.

@larchive_match_free@karchive_match_free.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_match_free@karchive_match_free.body: The `archive_match_free` routine walks through the archive’s match list, deallocates any embedded buffers (e.g., match descriptors or payloads), and finally clears the list pointers so the structure can be safely discarded.

@larchive_match_new@karchive_match_new.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_match_new@karchive_match_new.body: Creates an empty archive structure, allocates the required memory, initializes its fields to default values, and returns a pointer to that freshly‑initialized archive.

@larchive_match_path_unmatched_inclusion.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_match_path_unmatched_inclusion.body: The function walks the archive’s list of “inclusion” entries, finds the first one that hasn’t yet been matched, writes its path string into the supplied `const char **` buffer, and returns 0 if a match was found (or –1 if none remain). It’s the helper that drives the loop in the caller’s search for the next unmatched inclusion.

@larchive_read_close@karchive_read_close.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_read_close@karchive_read_close.body: Closes the archive reader’s underlying file descriptor, releases the read buffer, clears the open flag, and frees any allocated memory so that subsequent read attempts error out immediately.

@larchive_read_data_block@karchive_read_.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_read_data_block@karchive_read_.body: The routine pulls a data block from an archive object into a caller‑supplied buffer. It updates the supplied buffer pointer, size counter and offset pointer to reflect the read amount and new position, then returns 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise.

@larchive_read_free@karchive_read_free.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_read_free@karchive_read_free.body: It traverses the internal archive structure and releases every allocated buffer and sub‑object, zeroing out the pointers so that the structure can be safely discarded. It also guarantees that any dependent resources—such as file descriptors, hash tables, and embedded sub‑archives—are correctly cleaned up before the top‑level pointer is freed.

@larchive_read_new@karchive_read_new.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_read_new@karchive_read_new.body: The function allocates a new archive structure, initializes its fields (including any internal state needed for I/O handling), and returns the pointer so callers can immediately begin populating it.

@larchive_read_next_header@karchive_read.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_read_next_header@karchive_read.body: The function reads the next header entry from a given archive stream. It allocates and fills a `archive_entry` structure with the header data, assigns that structure to the caller‑supplied pointer, and returns a status code indicating success or failure.

@larchive_read_open_filename_w@karchive_.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_read_open_filename_w@karchive_.body: The `archive_read_open_filename_w` routine initializes an `archive` instance by opening a file specified by a wide‑character path. It takes a pointer to the archive structure, a wide‑character string containing the filename, and an optional size argument for any pre‑allocated buffers. On success it returns `0`; on failure it returns a negative error code (e.g., `-1` for file‑open errors or `-2` for invalid arguments).

@larchive_read_support_filter_all@karchi.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_read_support_filter_all@karchi.body: The function scans the entire archive structure, applying the support‑filter logic to each entry. It returns an integer status code and, when needed, populates a result set with entries that satisfy the current filter rules. The routine is used by higher‑level components that need a quick “all‑entries‑in‑archive” view for validation, reporting or export.

@larchive_read_support_format_all@karchi.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_read_support_format_all@karchi.body: The routine walks through the archive’s registered format handlers, verifies each can be read, and returns an integer status (0 on success, a non‑zero error code otherwise). It’s used in various entry points to gate further processing until a supported format is confirmed.

@larchive_write_data_block@karchive_writ.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_write_data_block@karchive_writ.body: The function copies a user‑provided buffer into the archive at a given offset and returns the number of bytes written (or a negative error code). It takes a pointer to the archive object, the source data pointer, the data size, and the offset within the archive to be written. The return value of type `la_ssize_t` is used to confirm the write succeeded, as shown by the assignment to a constant of that type in the surrounding code.

@larchive_write_disk_new@karchive_write_.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_write_disk_new@karchive_write_.body: Creates a fresh archive structure, wiring its internal buffers and file‑handles so it is ready to stream data to the backing disk.

@larchive_write_disk_set_options@karchiv.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_write_disk_set_options@karchiv.body: The function `archive_write_disk_set_options` configures the behaviour of a disk‑write operation for an `archive` instance. It receives a pointer to the archive and an integer flag value that encodes particular write options (for example, the `ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_TIME` flag used in the shown call). The routine applies the flag to the archive’s internal settings and returns an integer status code (zero on success, non‑zero on failure). This helper is invoked before initiating any write operation to ensure the archive knows exactly which options are in effect.

@larchive_write_finish_entry@karchive_wr.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_write_finish_entry@karchive_wr.body: The function finalizes a pending entry in an archive by writing any in‑memory buffers to the underlying file descriptor, marking the entry as complete, and updating internal bookkeeping such as the current offset and entry count. It performs checks for write‑success, propagates error codes back to the caller, and ensures that the archive’s state remains consistent before returning. If any write fails, the function cleans up partially‑written data, logs an error, and returns a negative status code to signal the failure to the calling context.

@larchive_write_free@karchive_write_free.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_write_free@karchive_write_free.body: The `archive_write_free` routine finalizes a write‑phase of an `archive` object: it releases any buffers or structures that were allocated during a write operation, cleans up internal state, and returns an integer status indicating success or failure.

@larchive_write_header@karchive_write_he.author: AI Short Overview
@larchive_write_header@karchive_write_he.body: The function `archive_write_header(struct archive *, struct archive_entry *)` writes the metadata for a new entry into the archive file. It serializes the fields of `archive_entry` (such as name, size, timestamp, and any flags) into the archive‑specific format, writes them to the archive descriptor, and updates the archive’s internal bookkeeping (e.g., entry count and offsets). It returns 0 on success or a non‑zero error code on failure.

@lassert@kassert.author: AI Short Overview
@lassert@kassert.body: `assert` is a lightweight helper that checks a condition at run‑time and aborts the current operation if the condition is false. It is typically invoked with a boolean expression, and if the expression evaluates to false it triggers an error path (logging, breaking into a debugger, or halting the process). The function itself is essentially a guard that ensures invariants before proceeding with the rest of the code.

@latof@katof.author: AI Short Overview
@latof@katof.body: Converts a null‑terminated string into an integer value, returning that integer.

@lbindexplib::AddDefinitionFile@k_ZN10bi.author: AI Short Overview
@lbindexplib::AddDefinitionFile@k_ZN10bi.body: The routine opens a text file, iterates over each line, ignores any that start with “LIBRARY” or “EXPORTS”, trims leading blanks, and then splits the line at a “ DATA” marker. The token before that marker is inserted into a symbol set; if the marker is present it keeps the trailing part in a data‑specific set, otherwise the whole line goes into a general symbol set.

@lbindexplib::AddObjectFile@k_ZN10bindex.author: AI Short Overview
@lbindexplib::AddObjectFile@k_ZN10bindex.body: AddObjectFile simply loads an object file into the index library: it invokes DumpFile with the library’s current path, the supplied filename, and the two internal symbol tables (Symbols and DataSymbols), then returns the success status that DumpFile reports.

@lbindexplib::SetNmPath@k_ZN10bindexplib.author: AI Short Overview
@lbindexplib::SetNmPath@k_ZN10bindexplib.body: The method simply assigns the passed‑in string to the internal member variable that holds the name‑path. It performs no validation or side‑effects beyond the assignment.

@lbindexplib::WriteFile@k_ZN10bindexplib.author: AI Short Overview
@lbindexplib::WriteFile@k_ZN10bindexplib.body: The function writes to the given file stream: it first outputs the line `EXPORTS` followed by a newline, then for each string in `DataSymbols` it prints a tab‑prefixed line containing the symbol name, a tab, and the literal word `DATA`, and finally for every string in `Symbols` it prints a tab‑prefixed line with just the symbol name.

@lbindexplib::bindexplib@k_ZN10bindexpli.author: AI Short Overview
@lbindexplib::bindexplib@k_ZN10bindexpli.body: The function assigns the string literal `"nm"` to the variable `NmPath`, initializing it for subsequent use.

@lbool2string@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111bool2s.author: AI Short Overview
@lbool2string@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111bool2s.body: The function casts the boolean to an integer, adds that value to the character `'0'`, and constructs a `std::string` from the resulting single character. Its design relies on `static_cast` and a one‑character string constructor, which is both unconventional and fragile.

@lcURLEasyGuard::cURLEasyGuard@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLEasyGuard::cURLEasyGuard@k_ZN12_GL.body: The constructor stores the supplied CURL pointer in the `Easy` member so that the guard keeps a reference to the underlying CURL instance for the duration of its lifetime.

@lcURLEasyGuard::cURLEasyGuard@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLEasyGuard::cURLEasyGuard@k_ZN12_GL.body: The guard’s sole purpose is to prevent accidental reuse or copying of a URL instance. When a `cURLEasyGuard` object is constructed it validates the URL string, guarantees the string is properly quoted for system calls, and its copy‑constructor is deleted to enforce move‑only semantics. This ensures that any URL passed to external commands is safe and cannot be inadvertently duplicated.

@lcURLEasyGuard::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLEasyGuard::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The deleted assignment operator in `cURLEasyGuard` forbids any copy or reassignment of guard instances. It prevents code from writing `guard = otherGuard;` or reusing a temporary, ensuring each guard remains uniquely owned and its associated resources are not inadvertently shared or duplicated.

@lcURLEasyGuard::release@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLEasyGuard::release@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: This method simply clears the `Easy` member by assigning it to `nullptr`. No other side‑effects are performed; the function only performs that single assignment.

@lcURLEasyGuard::~cURLEasyGuard@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLEasyGuard::~cURLEasyGuard@k_ZN12_G.body: When an instance of the wrapper is destroyed, it checks whether an underlying CURL easy handle (`Easy`) is non‑null and, if so, calls `::curl_easy_cleanup(this->Easy)` to free that resource.

@lcURLProgressHelper::GetMakefile@k_ZN12.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLProgressHelper::GetMakefile@k_ZN12.body: The function simply returns the internal `Makefile` member pointer.

@lcURLProgressHelper::UpdatePercentage@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLProgressHelper::UpdatePercentage@k.body: The function updates an internal percentage field from a reported value and total, rounds the result to a whole‑number percentage, caps it at 100 %, and, if the percentage changed, it rewrites a human‑readable status message (including the current percentage and a label). It returns a Boolean indicating whether the state actually changed.

@lcURLProgressHelper::cURLProgressHelper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLProgressHelper::cURLProgressHelper.body: The constructor takes an rvalue reference to another `cURLProgressHelper` instance, moving its internal state (progress counters, callbacks, etc.) into the new object without copying data.

@lcURLProgressHelper::cURLProgressHelper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLProgressHelper::cURLProgressHelper.body: Assigns the supplied make‑file pointer and text string to the helper’s internal members so it can report progress during a cURL operation.

@lcURLProgressHelper::cURLProgressHelper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcURLProgressHelper::cURLProgressHelper.body: The constructor creates a new cURLProgressHelper instance by copying the internal state from an existing helper. It clones the configuration used to report download progress, preserving the current progress counters and any settings that control how progress updates are emitted.

@lceil@k_Z4ceilB7v160000T_.author: AI Short Overview

@lceil@k_Z4ceilB7v160000d.author: AI Short Overview
@lceil@k_Z4ceilB7v160000d.body: The `ceil` template rounds a `double` value up to the smallest integer that is not less than the argument, returning that integer as a `double`. It’s useful for quickly clamping a value to an integral boundary without converting types, and is often employed in calculations that require a whole‑number ceiling (e.g. allocating resources or bounding loop indices).

@lceil@k_Z4ceilB7v160000e.author: AI Short Overview
@lceil@k_Z4ceilB7v160000e.body: Computes the next integer above the given value, returning that as a `long double`.

@lceil@k_Z4ceilB7v160000f.author: AI Short Overview
@lceil@k_Z4ceilB7v160000f.body: The `ceil` function returns the smallest integer value that is not less than the argument, effectively rounding a floating‑point value upward to an integer. It’s defined in `<cmath>` and is typically used when you need an integral result from a fractional input.

@lcheckArgumentsPreconditions@k_ZL27chec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcheckArgumentsPreconditions@k_ZL27chec.body: Checks each parsed argument against the required pre‑condition constraints (presence, valid ranges, logical consistency) and returns true only when all arguments satisfy the rules needed for the command to be processed.

@lcheckArgumentsPreconditions@k_ZL27chec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcheckArgumentsPreconditions@k_ZL27chec.body: The function calls checkSingleParameterArgumentPreconditions for three specific options (kPrefixOptionName, kTreeOptionName, kRegexOptionName), propagates the first error encountered into errorMsg, and returns true only if all three checks succeed.

@lcheckInterfacePropertyCompatibility@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcheckInterfacePropertyCompatibility@k_.body: The function `checkInterfacePropertyCompatibility` verifies that a given property `p` on a generator target `tgt` is consistent with the corresponding interface property (`INTERFACE_` + `p`) of all linked dependencies. It first fetches the property value via `getTypedProperty`, then iterates over the targets returned by `GetLinkImplementationClosure`. For each dependency it compares the interface value with the target’s property (explicitly set, implied, or unset), updating the value if needed. Mismatched values trigger an error via `cmSystemTools::Error`. The function returns the resolved property value.

@lcheckPropertyConsistency@k_Z24checkPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcheckPropertyConsistency@k_Z24checkPro.body: The template inspects a target’s property called `propName`. If any value in that property’s list has already been emitted, it registers a link‑interface dependency for that value; otherwise it reports an error. It also verifies that no user‑defined property is listed in the property value.

@lcheckSingleParameterArgumentPreconditi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcheckSingleParameterArgumentPreconditi.body: The function verifies that a single parameter supplied to a command satisfies all required pre‑conditions before the command proceeds. It examines the argument’s type, scope, and any constraint flags, returning `true` when the argument is acceptable and `false` otherwise, thereby short‑circuiting the command path in failure scenarios.

@lcheckSingleParameterArgumentPreconditi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcheckSingleParameterArgumentPreconditi.body: The function validates that a single‑argument flag supplied in a command‑line string actually has exactly one value associated with it. It looks up the flag in a map of parsed arguments, checks that a value was supplied and that only one such value exists, and if either condition fails it returns `false` with an explanatory message. If all checks pass, it returns `true`.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: The function is a compile‑time helper that turns a string literal into a `string_view`. It takes a reference to a `char[N]` array (the literal’s size), and produces a `string_view` that covers the array’s data up to the terminating null (hence the size `N‑1`). This lets you create views of string literals without allocating a new string.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: The function takes a const reference to a `static_string_view` and returns that view unchanged.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: Returns the underlying string_view wrapper for the supplied string by delegating to its view() method.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: Returns a `string_view` that refers to the supplied string.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: The `view` helper simply turns a raw C‑string (`const char*`) into a `string_view` instance and returns that view. Its implementation relies on an implicit conversion from the raw pointer to the `string_view` type, so the function effectively provides a tiny wrapper around that conversion.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: Creates a `string_view` that covers just the single character passed in. The function takes a `const char&`, points the view’s data pointer at that character, and sets the size to one. The result is a view over one byte of the original string.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: The function `view` simply accepts a `string_view` parameter and returns that same view unchanged. Because it is declared `static`, it is a free function and does not depend on any object state. It guarantees no copying or allocation; it just forwards the argument.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: This template turns a compile‑time array of characters into a `std::string`. It takes a reference to a character array of size `N` and constructs a string from the first `N‑1` elements, effectively stripping the terminating `'\0'` that is implicit in a string literal.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: The function is a no‑op helper: given a `std::nullptr_t` value it simply returns an empty `string_view` (i.e., a default‑constructed view representing an empty string).

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: The function extracts the underlying string from a `StringOpPlus` instance, returning it by value. It provides a lightweight, noexcept wrapper that lets callers obtain the plain `std::string` representation without any additional processing.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: It returns the string it receives unchanged.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: The function `into_string` checks for a null pointer and otherwise constructs a `std::string` from the C‑string. It returns a `String` (presumably an alias of `std::string`) constructed with the input `s`. The implementation’s return statement mistakenly uses `std::string`, which should be `std::string`.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: Creates a new `std::string` that contains only the supplied character and returns that string.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ENS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ENS.body: Creates a String from a static_string_view by delegating to the internal constructor that also takes a private‑tag. The private tag distinguishes this overload so that only explicit conversions from a static view are allowed.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EON.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EON.body: The constructor takes an rvalue‑reference of a `std::string` and a marker type `Private`. It allocates a new internal `std::shared_ptr<std::string>` from the moved‑string and stores it in `string_`. Immediately after that, it builds a non‑owning view (`view_`) over the raw buffer of the newly‑created string. In effect, this private constructor is a thin wrapper that just forwards the incoming string into its internal storage and exposes a string‑view of that storage for other members to use.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOS.body: Transfers the internal string and its view into the new instance, then clears the source object’s string and view to leave it in a safe empty state.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOS.body: The constructor forwards an rvalue reference to the main `String` constructor. It accepts a `String&&` and a `Private` tag to mark the call as private, and it is declared `noexcept` to guarantee no exceptions are thrown during the delegation.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOT.body: The constructor builds a `String` from any argument that satisfies the `IntoString` trait. It forwards the argument to `IntoString<T>::into_string`, then forwards the resulting string to a private constructor that performs the actual storage initialization.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EPK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EPK.body: It forwards the raw C‑string and length to the underlying `std::string` constructor, then passes that temporary to the base‑class `String` constructor, effectively building a `String` instance from a C‑string slice.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EPK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EPK.body: Constructs a `String` object by taking a raw C‑style string and a length value. It allocates internal storage large enough for the requested size, copies the supplied characters into that storage (usually via `std::memcpy`), and guarantees the resulting string is null‑terminated. The constructor validates that the source pointer is non‑null and that the supplied length does not exceed the source buffer’s bounds. Once constructed, the resulting `String` instance owns its contents and can safely be used elsewhere in the program.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.body:
The declaration defines the copy constructor for `String`.  
It is `noexcept` and explicitly `= default`, so the compiler will generate the usual copy‑constructor that performs a bit‑wise copy of the internal data without throwing exceptions.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.body: Creates a new `String` that shares the underlying storage of `s`. It copies the backing string reference (`string_`) and then sets `view_` to a slice starting at `s.data() + pos`, limited to `count` characters or the rest of `s` if `count` exceeds the remaining length. The constructor does not perform any further manipulation of the data.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.body: Constructs a new string by copying a segment from an existing one: it takes a source string reference plus a start offset and a length, then creates a new string containing that substring (copying the corresponding characters).

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ESt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ESt.body: This constructor takes an `initializer_list<char>` and forwards it directly to the other `String` constructor that accepts a `std::string`. It relies on delegating‑constructor syntax (the colon‑initialiser) to perform the actual construction.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ET_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ET_.body: This template provides a delegating constructor that accepts any pair of iterators (`first`, `last`) and forwards them to the constructor that takes a `std::string`. In effect, it creates an instance of the custom `String` type from a range of elements that can be interpreted as characters, delegating the heavy lifting to the `std::string` constructor that actually performs the conversion.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Ei@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Ei@.body: The constructor forwards a `std::string` constructed from the incoming `string_view` to the other constructor while also passing a `Private()` tag so that the resulting `String` instance is marked as a “private” instance. This prevents implicit conversions and ensures the internal string data is constructed exactly as intended.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EiN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EiN.body: The constructor merely stores the supplied `string_view` in the member `view_`. The extra `Private` parameter is an intentionally opaque token that blocks ordinary use; it is only meant to be supplied by trusted factory code, preventing external code from invoking the constructor directly.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Eic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Eic.body: Creates a new `String` instance that contains `n` copies of the character `c` by delegating to the `std::string` constructor that takes the repeated‑character string.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Ev.body:
This public function is the default constructor for the `String` class.  
When invoked it initializes the new object’s internal buffer to an empty string (zero length and no characters) and sets any internal bookkeeping fields accordingly, ensuring the instance is in a valid, empty state before any further manipulation.

@lcm::String::at@k_ZNK2cm6String2atEi@f..author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::at@k_ZNK2cm6String2atEi@f..body: The member `at` returns the character at the requested index by delegating to the underlying view’s own `at` routine – a simple read‑only accessor that throws (typically `std::out_of_range`) if the position is out of bounds, and otherwise delivers the stored character in constant‑time.

@lcm::String::back@k_ZNK2cm6String4backE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::back@k_ZNK2cm6String4backE.body: The function simply returns the last element from the internal `view_` member. It’s a `const` member that guarantees not to throw (declared `noexcept`).

@lcm::String::begin@k_ZNK2cm6String5begi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::begin@k_ZNK2cm6String5begi.body: The `begin()` member simply returns the beginning iterator of the underlying `view_`. It’s marked `noexcept` and returns a `const_iterator` to allow read‑only traversal of the container.

@lcm::String::borrow@k_ZN2cm6String6borr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::borrow@k_ZN2cm6String6borr.body: The `borrow` function receives a `string_view` and returns a `String` instance that represents the supplied view without copying the underlying characters. It is used in `cmDefinitions.cxx` to obtain string objects for keys in the internal maps; callers feed a key string view and receive back a `String` that can be used in subsequent map lookup operations.

@lcm::String::borrow@k_ZN2cm6String6borr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::borrow@k_ZN2cm6String6borr.body: Returns a new `String` constructed from the given `string_view`, marking the internal buffer as private (i.e., unshared).

@lcm::String::c_str@k_ZN2cm6String5c_str.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::c_str@k_ZN2cm6String5c_str.body: The function returns a C‑style string representation of the `String` object. It first checks whether the data buffer is null; if it is, it returns that pointer. Then it verifies that the buffer ends in a null byte at the current string size; if it already is null‑terminated it simply returns the buffer. Otherwise it coerces the internal buffer to a `std::string` internally, obtains its `c_str()` pointer, and returns that pointer.

@lcm::String::cbegin@k_ZNK2cm6String6cbe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::cbegin@k_ZNK2cm6String6cbe.body: Returns a const iterator that points to the first element of the container. The call is marked noexcept, indicating it will not throw exceptions, and simply forwards the result of the internal `begin()` implementation.

@lcm::String::cend@k_ZNK2cm6String4cendE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::cend@k_ZNK2cm6String4cendE.body: This member simply gives you a read‑only iterator positioned just past the final element of the underlying collection. Because the function is marked `const` and `noexcept`, it guarantees no modification of the object and no exception is thrown, making it safe to use in constant contexts while traversing the container in a read‑only fashion.

@lcm::String::clear@k_ZN2cm6String5clear.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::clear@k_ZN2cm6String5clear.body: Resets the internal value of the current instance to an empty string.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body: Returns an integer comparison result by forwarding the argument to `AsStringView<T>::view`, then calling the member `compare` of the stored view. The template is SFINX‑enabled via `std::enable_if` so it participates only when the type satisfies the `AsStringView` trait. The call preserves value‑category via `std::forward`.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body: It forwards a comparison request to the internal view object and returns that result.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body: The function simply forwards the comparison request to the underlying `view_` object, passing the requested positions and lengths, and returns the comparison result it produces.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body: It forwards a comparison of a substring of the stored view (starting at `pos1` with length `count1`) against the supplied `string_view` and returns the comparison result.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body: This const member simply forwards the comparison arguments to the internal `view_` object and returns whatever integer result that routine yields.

@lcm::String::copy@k_ZNK2cm6String4copyE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::copy@k_ZNK2cm6String4copyE.body: This member copies up to `count` characters from the internal buffer starting at offset `pos` into the supplied buffer `dest`. It returns the number of bytes actually copied and leaves the source unchanged.

@lcm::String::copy@k_ZNK2cm6String4copyE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::copy@k_ZNK2cm6String4copyE.body: The method forwards a copy operation to its internal view object: it places `count` characters starting at position `pos` into the supplied `dest` buffer and returns the number of bytes actually written.

@lcm::String::operator bool@k_ZNK2cm6Str.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::operator bool@k_ZNK2cm6Str.body: It returns a boolean that indicates whether the internal pointer returned by `data()` is non‑null, and it does so without throwing exceptions (`noexcept`) because the check itself never fails. @lcm::uv_async_ptr::send@k_ZN2cm12uv_asy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_async_ptr::send@k_ZN2cm12uv_asy.body: The `send()` function obtains a deleter for the async handle, acquires the deleter’s mutex, and if the handle is non‑null, forwards the call to `uv_async_send`. @lcm::uv_handle_deleter::operator()@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_handle_deleter::operator()@k_ZN.body: The function receives an async handle, locks the internal mutex to protect the shared state, and then invokes `handle_default_delete` to free the handle’s resources.

@lcm::uv_handle_deleter::operator()@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_handle_deleter::operator()@k_ZN.body: The function checks whether the supplied signal handle is non‑null. If it is, it first stops any pending signal callback via `uv_signal_stop` and then frees the handle with `handle_default_delete`. Because the method is marked `const`, it promises not to modify any member state of the surrounding class; it simply performs this cleanup routine.

@lcm::uv_handle_deleter::operator()@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_handle_deleter::operator()@k_ZN.body: The function is a const member that, when invoked, simply forwards its argument to `handle_default_delete`, effectively freeing the resource associated with `type_handle`. It performs no additional logic beyond that call.

@lcm::uv_handle_deleter::uv_handle_delet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_handle_deleter::uv_handle_delet.body: The constructor creates a shared‑pointer to a `std::mutex`, assigning it to the member `handleMutex`. This ensures the object holds a mutex that can be used for synchronizing access to any handles it manages.

@lcm::uv_handle_ptr_::operator type-para.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_handle_ptr_::operator type-para.body: The function is a const conversion operator that, when invoked, returns the raw pointer stored in the internal `handle` member. It performs a simple `return this->handle.get();` without modifying any state, so it is safe to call on a const-qualified instance. The function is typically used to expose the underlying raw handle to callers that expect a plain pointer type.

@lcm::uv_handle_ptr_base_::allocate@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_handle_ptr_base_::allocate@k_ZN.body: The function clears any previously stored handle, then allocates memory for a new object of type `T` using `calloc`. @lcm::uv_handle_ptr_base_::get@k_ZNK2cm1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_handle_ptr_base_::get@k_ZNK2cm1.body: The `get()` member simply forwards the call to the underlying handle and returns the raw pointer (`T*`) it holds.

@lcm::uv_handle_ptr_base_::operator->@k_.author: AI Short Overview

@lcm::uv_handle_ptr_base_::reset@k_ZN2cm.author: AI Short Overview

@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::operator()@k_ZNK2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::operator()@k_ZNK2.body: Runs the loop, shuts it down, checks that the close succeeded, and finally frees the memory that was allocated for that loop.

@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::uv_loop_deleter@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::uv_loop_deleter@k.body: The `uv_loop_deleter` function is a small, straightforward cleanup helper that accepts a `uv_loop_deleter` instance and a placeholder parameter. It immediately releases any internal loop resources—primarily the underlying event‑loop structure—by invoking the appropriate deallocation routine and then nullifies the pointer. In practice, this helper is invoked during teardown paths (e.g., the `cmUVHandlePtr.cxx` cleanup code at line 17) to guarantee that a running loop is properly destroyed before the surrounding context is discarded.

@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::uv_loop_deleter@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::uv_loop_deleter@k.body: The `uv_loop_deleter` function performs the clean‑up of a libuv event loop instance. When invoked, it safely releases any resources tied to the loop—such as pending handles or I/O channels—and then deallocates the loop object itself, ensuring that no further callbacks or tasks are queued thereafter. This guarantees that the loop’s internal state is reset and its memory freed before the program continues.

@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::uv_loop_deleter@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::uv_loop_deleter@k.body: The function cleans up the event loop, releasing the underlying `uv_loop_t` instance and ensuring its resources are freed safely. It is invoked during the `uv_loop_deleter` struct’s destructor and any helper routines that need to guarantee the loop’s lifetime ends cleanly.

@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::~uv_loop_deleter@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_loop_deleter::~uv_loop_deleter@.body: The function tears down a running uv_loop, freeing its internal structures and detaching any registered callbacks before the loop is discarded.

@lcm::uv_loop_ptr::get@k_ZNK2cm11uv_loop.author: AI Short Overview

@lcm::uv_loop_ptr::operator->@k_ZNK2cm11.body: The function simply returns the `uv_loop_t*` stored in the `uv_loop_ptr` instance. It is declared `const` and `noexcept`, so it guarantees no state mutation and no exceptions, and it calls the internal `loop.get()` accessor to retrieve the pointer.

@lcm::uv_loop_ptr::reset@k_ZN2cm11uv_loo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_loop_ptr::reset@k_ZN2cm11uv_loo.body: The method simply forwards a reset call to the underlying loop instance, clearing its internal state.

@lcm::uv_pipe_ptr::init@k_ZN2cm11uv_pipe.author: AI Short Overview

@lcm::uv_pipe_ptr::uv_pipe_ptr@k_ZN2cm11.author: AI Short Overview

@lcm::uv_signal_ptr::init@k_ZN2cm13uv_si.author: AI Short Overview

@lcm::uv_timer_ptr::init@k_ZN2cm12uv_tim.author: AI Short Overview

@lcm::uv_timer_ptr::uv_timer_ptr@k_ZN2cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::uv_timer_ptr::uv_timer_ptr@k_ZN2cm.body: `uv_timer_ptr()` is a convenience wrapper around the libuv timer structure. It holds a raw `uv_timer_t*` and automatically frees it when the wrapper goes out of scope. - Otherwise it verifies that at least one test name and one executable are supplied.  
- It then looks up the test in the current makefile; if it already exists it forbids a second new‑style definition unless the test was originally created in the old manner.  
- When the test is created, it flags it as an old‑style test, registers a generator for it once, and finally stores the full command vector on the test object.  
- The function reports success via its return value and records any error through the supplied `cmExecutionStatus`.

@lcmAlphaNum::View@k_ZNK10cmAlphaNum4Vie.body: The `View` member returns a string view: it checks whether the optional string (`RValueString_`) is present; if so, it returns that string, otherwise it falls back to the default view (`View_`).

@lcmAlphaNum::cmAlphaNum@k_ZN10cmAlphaNu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmAlphaNum::cmAlphaNum@k_ZN10cmAlphaNu.body: The constructor formats the supplied unsigned integer into a string using a "%u" format specifier and stores the resulting string in the object’s internal view and digit containers.

@lcmArchiveWrite::Add@k_ZN14cmArchiveWri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::Add@k_ZN14cmArchiveWri.body: The function trims a trailing slash from the supplied `path` string, then forwards the trimmed path, `skip`, a `prefix` string, and a `recursive` flag to a member helper `AddPath`. Finally, it returns the success flag from `Okay()`.

@lcmArchiveWrite::AddData@k_ZN14cmArchiv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::AddData@k_ZN14cmArchiv.body: The function opens the given file, reads it in 16‑kB blocks, streams each block into the archive, and records an error if the file cannot be opened, read, or written into the archive.
