@lcmArchiveWrite::AddFile@k_ZN14cmArchiv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::AddFile@k_ZN14cmArchiv.body: The routine copies the given file into the archive: it constructs an `archive_entry` object, fills it with the file’s path, timestamps, user/group IDs, permissions, and clears any ACL/xattr data, then writes the header and the file’s data (or, if it is a symlink, skips content) to the archive stream.

@lcmArchiveWrite::AddPath@k_ZN14cmArchiv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::AddPath@k_ZN14cmArchiv.body:
The routine walks a filesystem path and adds each entry it encounters to the archive. It first tests whether the supplied path refers to the current directory; if not, it delegates to AddFile() to add the file.  
If the path is a directory and the recursive flag is set, it loads that directory, iterates over its entries, and recursively calls itself for every entry that is not “.” or “..”. The function uses the helper helpers cmSystemTools::FileIsDirectory, cmSystemTools::FileIsSymlink and cmsys::Directory to discover the contents and builds the next path string with cmStrCat. It returns true only when every recursive step succeeds; otherwise it aborts and returns false.

@lcmArchiveWrite::ClearPermissions@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::ClearPermissions@k_ZN1.body: Invokes the member `Permissions` object’s `Clear()` method to reset the permission state.

@lcmArchiveWrite::ClearPermissionsMask@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::ClearPermissionsMask@k.body: The routine invokes the internal `PermissionsMask` member’s `Clear()` method, resetting whatever flag or bit‑set the mask holds. No additional logic or state changes occur.

@lcmArchiveWrite::ClearUIDAndGID@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::ClearUIDAndGID@k_ZN14c.body: Resets the stored UID and GID values to an empty or default state, clearing both fields in the current object.

@lcmArchiveWrite::ClearUNAMEAndGNAME@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::ClearUNAMEAndGNAME@k_Z.body: Resets the internal Uname and Gname properties to empty strings, effectively clearing any stored name data.

@lcmArchiveWrite::GetError@k_ZNK14cmArch.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::GetError@k_ZNK14cmArch.body: Returns the current error message stored in the object unchanged.

@lcmArchiveWrite::Okay@k_ZNK14cmArchiveW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::Okay@k_ZNK14cmArchiveW.body: Checks whether the error string is empty, returning true if no error is present.

@lcmArchiveWrite::Open@k_ZN14cmArchiveWr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::Open@k_ZN14cmArchiveWr.body: The `Open` method first verifies that no prior error has been recorded; if `this->Error` is non‑empty it returns `false`. Otherwise it attempts to initialise the archive by calling `archive_write_open` with the stored archive handle, a pointer to this object, and a callback wrapper. If that call does not return `ARCHIVE_OK`, it records the failure message from the underlying library in `this->Error` and returns `false`. If the call succeeds, `Open` returns `true`.

@lcmArchiveWrite::SetMTime@k_ZN14cmArchi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::SetMTime@k_ZN14cmArchi.body: The `SetMTime` function assigns the supplied string `t` to the member variable `MTime`. It accepts the argument as a const reference, preventing copying, and simply stores the value; no validation or checks are performed, so callers must ensure the string meets any required format.

@lcmArchiveWrite::SetPermissions@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::SetPermissions@k_ZN14c.body: The method simply forwards the supplied integer to the underlying `Permissions` helper, which updates the internal permission bits accordingly.

@lcmArchiveWrite::SetPermissionsMask@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::SetPermissionsMask@k_Z.body: The method assigns the supplied integer value to the internal `PermissionsMask` member by calling its `Set` method. This updates the object’s permissions state in a single, straightforward operation.

@lcmArchiveWrite::SetUIDAndGID@k_ZN14cmA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::SetUIDAndGID@k_ZN14cmA.body: Assigns the supplied UID and GID values to the corresponding member wrappers through their `Set` methods. No checks or conversions are performed; it simply forwards the raw integers to the underlying fields. It assumes the callers provide valid values and does not perform bounds checking or error reporting.

@lcmArchiveWrite::SetUNAMEAndGNAME@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::SetUNAMEAndGNAME@k_ZN1.body: The method stores the supplied strings into the object's `Uname` and `Gname` members, updating the instance’s identity data with the new values.

@lcmArchiveWrite::SetVerbose@k_ZN14cmArc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::SetVerbose@k_ZN14cmArc.body: Sets the internal Verbose flag to the supplied boolean value.

@lcmArchiveWrite::cmArchiveWrite@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::cmArchiveWrite@k_ZN14c.body: Handles writing archive entries to persistent storage, serializing in‑memory data structures into a compact binary format while guarding against inadvertent duplication of the writer object by deleting its copy constructor.

@lcmArchiveWrite::cmArchiveWrite@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::cmArchiveWrite@k_ZN14c.body: Constructs an archive‑writer instance. It picks the requested compression filter (None, Compress, Gzip, Bzip2, Lzma, Xz, Zstd), sets thread count limits, applies an optional compression‑level, and selects the desired format. On any library call failure it records the error string for later inspection. It finishes by disabling the final‑block padding.

@lcmArchiveWrite::operator bool@k_ZNK14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::operator bool@k_ZNK14c.body: The conversion operator simply returns the result of calling `this->Okay()`. It’s marked explicit, so it won’t participate in implicit Boolean conversions, and being const guarantees no state changes.

@lcmArchiveWrite::operator!@k_ZNK14cmArc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::operator!@k_ZNK14cmArc.body: Returns the logical negation of the object's internal state by invoking its `Okay()` method; being `const`, it guarantees no side‑effects on the object.

@lcmArchiveWrite::operator=@k_ZN14cmArch.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::operator=@k_ZN14cmArch.body: A deleted copy‑assignment operator that blocks implicit assignment of one `cmArchiveWrite` object to another.

@lcmArchiveWrite::~cmArchiveWrite@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWrite::~cmArchiveWrite@k_ZN14.body: The destructor releases resources: it frees the memory associated with the `Disk` member via `archive_read_free` and frees the archive structure via `archive_write_free`.

@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::Clear@k_ZN22cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::Clear@k_ZN22cm.body: Clear() resets the internal flag `IsValueSet` to false, marking the instance as having no value set.

@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::Get@k_ZNK22cmA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::Get@k_ZNK22cmA.body:
Returns a copy of the stored member `Value` when invoked on a constant instance.  
The function is read‑only—no mutation occurs—and guarantees that callers cannot alter the internal state via the returned result.

@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::IsSet@k_ZNK22c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::IsSet@k_ZNK22c.body: Returns whether the internal flag indicating that a value has been assigned.

@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::Set@k_ZN22cmAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::Set@k_ZN22cmAr.body: The `Set` member simply assigns the supplied argument to the internal `Value` field and flips the `IsValueSet` flag to true. No validation or side‑effects are performed; it merely records that a value has been supplied.

@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::cmArchiveWrite.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::cmArchiveWrite.body: The `cmArchiveWriteOptional` function simply forwards its argument to the internal `Set` method; it is a convenience wrapper that writes the supplied value into the underlying archive object.

@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::cmArchiveWrite.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArchiveWriteOptional::cmArchiveWrite.body: The function is a convenience wrapper that resets the internal state of the archive writer, clearing buffers and restoring the object to a pristine start‑up condition.

@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.body: The `Bind` overload registers a named argument‑parsing rule that captures a supplied callback. When the parser encounters an argument matching the name, it forwards that string view to the stored lambda. That lambda invokes the provided `std::function`, wraps its `Continue` result, and forwards it back to the parser’s continuation mechanism. The optional `ExpectAtLeast` argument specifies how many occurrences of that argument must appear before parsing continues. The method returns a reference to the parser itself, allowing fluent chaining of further bindings.

@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.body: The method registers a parsing callback that extracts the current keyword from the instance and invokes the supplied function `f` with that keyword and the argument string, returning a `Continue` value. It returns the parser object to allow chaining of additional bindings.

@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.body: This function registers a handler that extracts a string argument from the command line and invokes the supplied callback with that string, returning a reference to the parser to allow fluent chaining. It also ensures the argument is present by using the ExpectAtLeast parameter.

@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.body: The `Bind` function attaches a continuation callback to a `cmArgumentParser`. When invoked, it registers a handler that will be called after the parser has matched at least the specified number of arguments (`ExpectAtLeast`). The callback receives two string views: the matched argument and its remaining portion, and performs the continuation logic defined by the caller.

@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.body: Binds the provided reference `ref` to a named entry in the parser by registering a callback that invokes `instance.Bind(ref)` when the relevant argument is parsed. It forwards to `Base::Bind` with a lambda capturing `ref` and returns the parser for fluent chaining.

@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.body: This template captures a reference to an object and registers a lambda that, when invoked on an `Instance`, will call `instance.Bind(ref)`. The function delegates to `MaybeBind`, returning `true` if the binding succeeds and `false` otherwise.

@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.body: This template implements a `Bind` helper that returns a `bool` indicating success, accepting a `cm::string_view` for the target name and a reference to an object (`T&`) that will be bound. The implementation uses the provided string_view to look up a matching entry in a registry or map, then assigns the found object to the supplied reference, returning `true` if the lookup succeeded and `false` otherwise.

@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::Bind@k_ZN16cmArgumen.body: The method registers a callback that stores the parsed argument into the supplied `optional<std::string>` reference. It then returns the parser instance, enabling fluent chaining.

@lcmArgumentParser::Parse@k_ZNK16cmArgum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::Parse@k_ZNK16cmArgum.body: The template creates a `ParseResult` instance, passes it (along with the `Bindings` and an optional `unparsedArguments` vector) to an `Instance` helper, then invokes that helper’s `Parse` routine with the supplied argument range and starting index. Finally it returns the populated `ParseResult`.

@lcmArgumentParser::cmArgumentParser@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmArgumentParser::cmArgumentParser@k_Z.body: The `cmArgumentParser` function scans a command‑line argument vector, extracts key/value pairs (typically `--option=value` or `--flag`), validates them against the expected schema, and produces a typed struct or map that callers can query for specific options. It handles defaults, type‑coercions, and reports errors for missing or malformed arguments, making it a reusable entry point for any component that needs robust CLI parsing.

@lcmAuxSourceDirectoryCommand@k_Z27cmAux.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmAuxSourceDirectoryCommand@k_Z27cmAux.body: The routine validates that exactly two arguments are supplied, resolves the first argument to a full path relative to the current source directory if needed, scans that directory for files, filters those whose extensions match the tool’s recognised source patterns, registers each matching file as a source entry, and finally registers the collected file list under the supplied definition name.

@lcmBZRXMLParserUnknownEncodingHandler@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBZRXMLParserUnknownEncodingHandler@k.body: When the XML parser sees the encoding names “ascii”, “cp1252” or “ANSI_X3.4‑1968”, this routine loads a 256‑entry Latin‑1 translation table into the supplied map and signals success (return 1); otherwise it returns 0.

@lcmBase32Encoder::cmBase32Encoder@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBase32Encoder::cmBase32Encoder@k_ZN1.body: Creates a new instance that duplicates the internal state of the supplied `cmBase32Encoder` object—copying its configuration data and any internal buffers so that the new encoder starts with the same settings as the original.

@lcmBase32Encoder::cmBase32Encoder@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBase32Encoder::cmBase32Encoder@k_ZN1.body:
A default constructor that relies on the compiler to generate the boiler‑plate initialization.  
The class likely holds internal state (buffers, state flags, etc.) that the default constructor zero‑initializes or sets sane defaults, ensuring an object is ready for subsequent `encode()` calls without any further explicit setup.

@lcmBase32Encoder::encodeString@k_ZN15cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBase32Encoder::encodeString@k_ZN15cm.body: The routine takes a raw byte buffer and returns its Base‑32 representation. It walks the input in 5‑byte blocks, each producing 8 encoded characters, and for any trailing bytes it pads with zeros before encoding and optionally appends pad‑characters to the final output. The result is returned as a std::string.

@lcmBase32Encoder::~cmBase32Encoder@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBase32Encoder::~cmBase32Encoder@k_ZN.body: The function `~cmBase32Encoder()` is the class destructor. It is marked as `= default;` which tells the compiler to generate the default destructor that simply performs the usual cleanup of member objects. In other words, when an instance of `cmBase32Encoder` goes out of scope or is deleted, this destructor runs automatically and releases any resources owned by the object.

@lcmBasicUVIStream::close@k_ZN16cmBasicU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVIStream::close@k_ZN16cmBasicU.body: Invokes the `close()` method of the embedded `Buffer` object, which performs the actual resource release/cleanup for the stream.

@lcmBasicUVIStream::cmBasicUVIStream@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVIStream::cmBasicUVIStream@k_Z.body: The constructor invokes the base class’s default constructor and then calls `open(stream)` to attach the provided `uv_stream_t*` to the new stream object, thereby initializing the stream for subsequent I/O operations.

@lcmBasicUVIStream::cmBasicUVIStream@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVIStream::cmBasicUVIStream@k_Z.body: Constructs an instance of `cmBasicUVIStream` by invoking the `std::basic_istream` constructor with a pointer to the stream’s own buffer (`&this->Buffer`). No additional actions are performed in the constructor body.

@lcmBasicUVIStream::is_open@k_ZNK16cmBas.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVIStream::is_open@k_ZNK16cmBas.body: This member simply forwards the open status of its underlying buffer. When called, it returns the value obtained from `Buffer.is_open()`, indicating whether the stream currently has an active buffer that can be used for I/O operations. The function itself is marked `const`, ensuring it does not modify any internal state.

@lcmBasicUVIStream::open@k_ZN16cmBasicUV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVIStream::open@k_ZN16cmBasicUV.body: The function simply forwards the provided `uv_stream_t*` to its internal buffer by calling `this->Buffer.open(stream)`. This delegates stream initialization to the `Buffer` instance, which is expected to perform the actual setup work.

@lcmBasicUVPipeIStream::close@k_ZN20cmBa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVPipeIStream::close@k_ZN20cmBa.body: The `close()` routine calls its base class implementation to close the underlying stream and then clears the internal pipe buffer by invoking `reset()` on the `Pipe` member.

@lcmBasicUVPipeIStream::cmBasicUVPipeISt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVPipeIStream::cmBasicUVPipeISt.body: The constructor registers the stream with the supplied event loop and immediately calls `open()` on the provided file descriptor, so the instance is ready for asynchronous I/O.

@lcmBasicUVPipeIStream::cmBasicUVPipeISt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVPipeIStream::cmBasicUVPipeISt.body: Creates a UV‑pipe input stream instance, binding it to its underlying source with the default streaming traits so that the stream is ready to read UV‑encoded data.

@lcmBasicUVPipeIStream::open@k_ZN20cmBas.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVPipeIStream::open@k_ZN20cmBas.body: The function initializes the internal pipe with the supplied event‑loop, opens that file descriptor via the libuv `uv_pipe_open` call, and then hands control off to the base class’s `open` implementation for further setup.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::HandleAlloc@k_ZN18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::HandleAlloc@k_ZN18.body: The function computes the amount of data still in the stream buffer, copies that data into the internal `InputBuffer`, updates the internal get/put pointers to point at the newly copied data, and then fills a `uv_buf_t` structure that represents the available memory region: `buf->base` points at the buffer’s current end, and `buf->len` is set to the remaining capacity expressed in bytes (adjusted for the character type size).

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::StreamRead@k_ZN18c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::StreamRead@k_ZN18c.body: The routine repositions the internal get area based on the requested read length. When a positive count is supplied, it extends the read window by the requested amount (converted to characters via the element size) and signals the stream to cease further reads. If the count is zero or negative, the function flags the end‑of‑file condition and similarly invokes the stop routine.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::StreamReadStartSto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::StreamReadStartSto.body: This lambda fetches the stream buffer stored in the handle’s data field and passes the incoming buffer to that buffer’s `HandleAlloc` method.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::StreamReadStartSto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::StreamReadStartSto.body: The lambda casts `stream2->data` to a `cmBasicUVStreambuf<CharT, Traits>*` and then forwards the read byte count (`nread`) to that buffer’s `StreamRead` method, effectively reporting how many bytes were read. It ignores the third parameter.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::StreamReadStartSto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::StreamReadStartSto.body: The function first halts any pending read on the underlying libuv stream handle; once the buffer has no more data left to read it re‑initiates the read loop by registering two callbacks: one that allocates a fresh buffer into the stream buffer when libuv asks for memory, and another that passes any incoming data to the stream‑buffer’s read handler. In short: it stops an ongoing read, clears the current buffer, and immediately restarts the read pipeline with fresh allocation and consumption callbacks.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::close@k_ZN18cmBasi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::close@k_ZN18cmBasi.body: It halts the read loop on the current stream, restores the stream’s data pointer to its original value, clears the stored stream pointer, resets the internal buffer positions to empty, and then returns the buffer object itself.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::cmBasicUVStreambuf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::cmBasicUVStreambuf.body: Initialises the internal buffers—setting PutBack to at least 1, allocating InputBuffer with a size of max(putBack,bufSize)+PutBack—and then forces a fresh, closed state by invoking close() on the instance.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::is_open@k_ZNK18cmB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::is_open@k_ZNK18cmB.body: The method simply reports whether the internal stream pointer is set – it returns true when the stream is non‑null and false otherwise. This check is performed without modifying any state, guaranteeing const‑correctness.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::open@k_ZN18cmBasic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::open@k_ZN18cmBasic.body: The method first aborts any prior stream by calling `close()`, assigns the supplied `uv_stream_t` to its internal `Stream` member, clears the EOF flag, and if the stream is valid it stores its previous data and installs this object as the new stream data. Finally it calls `StreamReadStartStop()` to initialise reading state and returns `this`.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::showmanyc@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::showmanyc@k_ZN18cm.body: The protected member simply verifies the underlying stream is available: if the stream is either closed or already at EOF, it returns –1; otherwise it reports success by returning 0.

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::underflow@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::underflow@k_ZN18cm.body: The method first verifies that the underlying stream is open; if it is closed it returns the end‑of‑file marker. If there is a byte already in the buffer, it returns that byte immediately. Otherwise it invokes the internal read routine, spinning until input becomes available or the read fails, and finally yields the next byte (or EOF if no more data).

@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::~cmBasicUVStreambu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBasicUVStreambuf::~cmBasicUVStreambu.body: The destructor for `cmBasicUVStreambuf` calls its `close()` method to release any underlying resources (e.g., buffers or file handles) before the object is destroyed.

@lcmBinUtilsLinker::Prepare@k_ZN16cmBinU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsLinker::Prepare@k_ZN16cmBinU.body: This member simply signals a successful preparation step—by defaulting to `true`, it offers a hook that subclasses can override to execute custom initialization logic.

@lcmBinUtilsLinker::ScanDependencies@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsLinker::ScanDependencies@k_Z.body:
The pure virtual ScanDependencies member is intended to be implemented by concrete classes.  
It receives a file path, parses that file for dependency declarations, and returns true only if the scan succeeds (i.e., no parsing errors were encountered).

@lcmBinUtilsLinker::SetError@k_ZN16cmBin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsLinker::SetError@k_ZN16cmBin.body: Accepts the error string and passes it straight to the internal Archive object’s SetError routine.

@lcmBinUtilsLinker::cmBinUtilsLinker@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsLinker::cmBinUtilsLinker@k_Z.body: The constructor simply stores the supplied `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive*` in the `Archive` member, establishing the context needed for later linking of binary utilities.

@lcmBinUtilsLinker::~cmBinUtilsLinker@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsLinker::~cmBinUtilsLinker@k_.body: The virtual destructor is defined as `default`, which means the compiler generates the usual destruction logic automatically. When an object of this type or any subclass is deleted, this destructor guarantees that all resources owned by that object (including base‑class sub‑objects) are released in the correct order. This default form also supports polymorphic cleanup because the destructor is virtual, allowing derived classes to add any additional cleanup code while still invoking the base destructor automatically.

@lcmBinUtilsLinuxELFGetRuntimeDependenci.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsLinuxELFGetRuntimeDependenci.body: The method simply forwards the supplied error string to the `Archive` member by calling its `SetError` routine, passing along the `error` argument unchanged.

@lcmBinUtilsLinuxELFGetRuntimeDependenci.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsLinuxELFGetRuntimeDependenci.body: The constructor simply stores the supplied `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive*` in its `Archive` member, setting up the tool for later use. No other state changes occur during construction.

@lcmBinUtilsLinuxELFObjdumpGetRuntimeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsLinuxELFObjdumpGetRuntimeDep.body: Runs `objdump` on the supplied file, parses its output for the three types of entries it emits, and fills the supplied vectors with those strings. It returns `true` only if the external tool ran cleanly and produced no errors; otherwise it records an error string via `SetError` and returns `false`.

@lcmBinUtilsLinuxELFObjdumpGetRuntimeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsLinuxELFObjdumpGetRuntimeDep.body: The constructor creates a Linux‑ELF‑dependency‑tool instance by forwarding the supplied `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` to its base class and performing any necessary initialisation.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.body: The `GetFileInfo` function is a pure virtual interface that must be implemented by derived classes to gather metadata about a file identified by its path. It receives the file path as a `const std::string&` argument and returns a `bool` indicating success or failure. In practice, implementations typically open the file, read its attributes (size, timestamps, permissions, etc.), and then signal whether the information extraction succeeded.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.body: The method simply forwards the supplied error string to the underlying `Archive` instance, delegating the error handling to that object.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.body: The constructor simply retains the supplied `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` pointer so that subsequent dependency‑resolution logic can query the archive for the Mach‑O runtime dependencies.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.body: Parses a Mach‑O binary and returns the list of dynamic libraries it depends on at load time.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state from the right‑hand operand into the current instance. It performs a shallow copy of the class’s data members, preserving value semantics while guarding against self‑assignment. Because the source object is passed by const reference, the function assumes that all referenced resources can be safely duplicated without modification of the source. It returns a reference to the left‑hand object so that chained assignments remain idiomatic.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOGetRuntimeDependen.body: The destructor finalizes the tool’s internal state, releasing any resources that were allocated while parsing a Mach‑O binary to extract its runtime‑dependency list.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::FileInfo::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::FileInfo::.body:
The constructor `FileInfo(FileInfo&& other)` is a move‑constructor.  
It creates a new `FileInfo` object by taking ownership of the internals of `other` (shallow copying of trivial members, or moving pointers/handles where appropriate) so that the source instance is left in a valid but unspecified state. This pattern avoids needless deep copies and allows efficient transfer of file metadata across the code that relies on `FileInfo`.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::FileInfo::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::FileInfo::.body: This constructor creates a new `FileInfo` instance by copying the contents of the supplied reference. It simply assigns each member of the source object to the new one, ensuring the new instance is an exact duplicate. The constructor is publicly exposed and is referenced in several parts of the codebase, most notably at line 28 of *cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker.h*.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::FileInfo::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::FileInfo::.body: FileInfo retrieves file metadata for the Mach‑O linker and returns a `FileInfo` struct populated with fields such as file name, type, and permissions. It’s invoked during linking to supply the necessary file attributes to subsequent stages.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::GetFileDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::GetFileDep.body: Iterates over each name in the supplied list, skipping those that the archive marks as pre‑excluded. For each remaining entry it attempts to resolve the dependency against the current executable and loader paths. Resolved paths are added to the archive; if the resolution yields a unique file that has not yet been processed, the routine recurses into that file’s own libraries and rpaths to scan further transitive dependencies. Any failure to resolve or scan causes the function to short‑circuit and return false; otherwise, after all names have been processed, it returns true.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::GetFileInf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::GetFileInf.body: Checks a cache; if the file hasn’t been processed, it calls Tool‑>GetFileInfo to fill a FileInfo structure, stores that structure in a map, and returns a pointer to the cached entry (or nullptr if the call fails).

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::Prepare@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::Prepare@k_.body:
Retrieves the name of the runtime‑dependencies tool from the linked archive.  
If the returned string is empty it defaults to “otool”.  
Only when that value matches exactly “otool” does it instantiate the corresponding helper (`cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDependenciesTool`) and store it in `this->Tool`.  
If any other value is supplied, it logs an error message and returns false.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveDep.body: The function dispatches dependency resolution to helper routines based on special prefixes (`@rpath/`, `@loader_path/`, `@executable_path/`). If none match, it treats the input as a concrete path, marks it resolved, and finally verifies the result is an absolute path before returning success.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveExe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveExe.body: The function takes a name and an optional executable path. If the supplied path is empty, the function marks the dependency unresolved and returns success. Otherwise it substitutes the leading “@executable_path” placeholder in the name with the provided path, then verifies the resulting path exists. Depending on that check it sets the resolved flag accordingly and returns true.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveLoa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveLoa.body: The function substitutes the first twelve‑character segment of the supplied name with the loader path, then checks whether that resulting path actually exists on disk. It sets `resolved` to true only if the file can be located; otherwise it leaves `resolved` false. The return value is always true, signalling the resolution routine completed (successfully or not).

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveRPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveRPa.body: The function walks through the provided rpath list, replacing the initial “@loader_path/” or “@executable_path/” prefix of the target name with each rpath in turn. For each candidate it first attempts to resolve via loader or executable‑path helpers; if neither matches, it falls back to a simple filesystem existence check. If a match is found, the search file is returned in path and the resolved flag set true. If no match occurs after exhausting the list, resolved remains false.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ScanDepend.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ScanDepend.body: ScanDependencies() resolves the executable path (either from the supplied file or the bundle’s default), fetches the file’s metadata, and—if that metadata is present—passes the gathered libraries and rpaths to the internal scan routine, returning the outcome of that scan.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ScanDepend.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ScanDepend.body: The function extracts the directory component of the supplied file path using `cmSystemTools::GetFilenamePath`, then forwards that directory together with the provided library list, runtime path list, and executable path to `GetFileDependencies`. The return value is whatever `GetFileDependencies` reports, indicating whether the dependency scan succeeded.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::cmBinUtils.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::cmBinUtils.body: The constructor initializes a new `cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker` instance by taking ownership of the contents from an rvalue reference of the same type, ensuring the internal state (including any resources needed for Mach‑O linking on macOS) is correctly set up before use.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::cmBinUtils.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::cmBinUtils.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` to its base class `cmBinUtilsLinker`. No further state‑management or resource allocation is performed beyond whatever base‑class construction already handles.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::cmBinUtils.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::cmBinUtils.body: The function initializes a new `cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker` object by copying the configuration and state from another instance. It performs a shallow copy of all internal members, ensuring that the new instance shares the same settings but remains independent of the original, without altering any of its owned resources.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::operator=@.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference of the same type, copies the internal state from the source object into the current instance, and returns a reference to the modified instance. The parameter is unnamed in the declaration, and the implementation follows move‑assignment semantics to avoid unnecessary copies.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::operator=@.body: The assignment operator copies all member data from the supplied `cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker` instance into the current object, returning a reference to `*this`. It performs a shallow copy of the base class and any internal members, with a self‑assignment guard to avoid unnecessary work.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::~cmBinUtil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::~cmBinUtil.body: The `~cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker` destructor tidily frees any resources (file handles, memory buffers, or temporary files) that the Mach‑O linking helper has allocated during its lifetime, guaranteeing a clean teardown before the object is discarded.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.body: Runs `otool` on a Mach‑O file, parses its output for LC_RPATH and LC_LOAD directives, and fills the supplied vectors with extracted paths and library names. Any command‑or‑parse failure sets an error and returns false.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.body: The function consumes an instance of its own type (by rvalue reference) and produces a list of runtime dependency identifiers that the Mach‑O tool requires, typically collected by inspecting the Mach‑O binary and resolving linked libraries.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.body: The constructor simply passes the supplied `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` instance to the base class constructor, enabling the tool to access the archive’s information for retrieving runtime dependencies from a Mach‑O binary.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.body: Constructs a new cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDependenciesTool instance by copying the internal state from an existing object—effectively duplicating the tool’s dependency data for further use.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to another instance of the same type and moves its internal state into the current object, returning a reference to `*this` so that the operation can be chained.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.body: This operator overload copies every member of the given instance into the current object and then returns a reference to the current object, enabling chained assignments.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDep.body: The public virtual function `~cmBinUtilsMacOSMachOOToolGetRuntimeDependenciesTool()` returns a list of runtime dependencies needed for the Mac OS Mach‑O tool. It is designed to be overridden by derived classes so that the dependency list can be customized for different build scenarios.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEDumpbinGetRuntimeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEDumpbinGetRuntimeDe.body: GetFileInfo builds a command line that invokes the external dumpbin utility with the `‑dependents` flag for the supplied file. It launches this process, parses its standard‑output for lines that match the pattern for DLL names, and appends each discovered dependency to the supplied vector. On any failure (spawn, non‑zero exit, or parse error) it records the error message and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEDumpbinGetRuntimeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEDumpbinGetRuntimeDe.body: This constructor simply forwards the `archive` pointer to its base class `cmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenciesTool` without performing any additional initialization.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.body: The `GetFileInfo` method is an interface that derived classes must implement: it accepts a file path (by `const std::string&`) and returns a `bool` flag indicating whether the file‑information retrieval succeeded.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.body: The method passes the supplied error string to the internal `Archive` object, invoking its `SetError` routine so that the error propagates to any component observing the archive.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.body: The constructor simply stores the provided dependency archive in the `Archive` member for later use.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.body: The routine scans a Windows PE executable, extracts every imported DLL (including its import‑time resolution), and builds a list of absolute paths that the runtime will need. It validates each found library against the system’s search path, and returns a vector of `cmfntDependentFileInfo` structures – one per dependency – indicating the file’s location and whether it is a system‑DLL or a third‑party module.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of the supplied `cmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenciesTool` instance into the current object, then returns `*this`.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEGetRuntimeDependenc.body: The destructor automatically deallocates any internal buffers or handles that were allocated during the runtime‑dependency discovery process, guaranteeing that no file handles, memory blobs or intermediate data structures linger after the object is destroyed.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.body: The function constructs and runs an `objdump` command for the given file, parsing its output line‑by‑line with a regex that matches `"DLL Name: <name>"`. Each matched name is appended to the `needed` vector. It reports errors if the process fails to start, if the output stream cannot be read, or if the program exits with a non‑zero status.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.body: The `cmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDependenciesTool` function drives the objdump utility on a given PE file, parses its output, and stores the discovered runtime dependency links in the tool’s internal dependency representation.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.body: The constructor forwards the supplied archive to the base class that gathers runtime dependency data. It relies on the base to perform the actual scanning of PE files and populate the dependency list. The body itself remains empty because initialization is handled entirely in the base class.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.body: The function creates a tool object that analyzes a Windows PE file by invoking the `objdump` utility. It parses the import table of the binary, collecting the names of DLLs and exports that the executable requires at runtime. The resulting set of dependencies can be queried later to resolve missing libraries or validate linkage.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.body: The assignment‑operator overload takes an rvalue reference to another `cmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDependenciesTool` object, copies its internal state into the current instance, and returns `*this`. It implements the usual move‑assignment semantics for the helper class.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.body: The assignment operator copies all internal members from the right‑hand operand into the current instance and returns a reference to *this so the call can be chained.

@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsWindowsPEObjdumpGetRuntimeDe.body: The function initializes a process that opens a given Windows PE file, runs the `objdump` tool to analyze the binary, parses the resulting dump output to extract a list of runtime dependencies (imports, libraries, and symbols), and then stores this list for later use by the framework.

@lcmBlockCommand@k_Z14cmBlockCommandRKiR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockCommand@k_Z14cmBlockCommandRKiR.body: The function receives a vector of strings and a reference to a status object. It parses the arguments with a custom parser that extracts an optional list of scopes and a list of propagation items. It validates that only the scopes `"VARIABLES"` and `"POLICIES"` are allowed; any other scope or an unsupported propagation without a variable scope causes an error and aborts the call. When the arguments are valid it creates a `cmBlockFunctionBlocker` with the gathered scopes and propagation list, adds that blocker to the makefile, and returns `true`. If any parsing or validation step fails, it sets an error in the status, flags a fatal error, and returns `false`.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch.body: The function `ArgumentsMatch` verifies that the function definition supplied (`lff`) contains **no** arguments. It returns `true` only when `lff.Arguments()` reports an empty collection; otherwise it returns `false`. This check guards against invoking the block handler in contexts where arguments are present.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName.body: It returns a cm::string_view containing the literal `"endblock"`—used as the identifier for the command that marks the end of a block.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::EndCommandSupp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::EndCommandSupp.body: This method signals that the end‑command variant does not accept any arguments; it simply reports that argument support is disabled by returning `false`.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN12_.body: The `Replay` routine walks through the stored commands in a block, executing each via the active Makefile context. Whenever a command returns a return, break or continue flag, it propagates that back into the overall execution state and exits the loop immediately, halting further processing. The method finally reports success by returning `true`.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::StartCommandNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::StartCommandNa.body: The `StartCommandName` method simply returns a constant string literal that identifies the command type. In this example it supplies the literal `"block"`, which the rest of the codebase uses to look up or dispatch the corresponding command implementation. The method is `const` and `override`, ensuring it can be called polymorphically without altering object state.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::cmBlockFunctio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::cmBlockFunctio.body: The constructor stores the supplied make‑file pointer, the scope set, and the list of variable names into the corresponding member members (`Makefile`, `Scopes`, `BlockScope`, and `VariableNames`), using the member‑initialisation list; no additional logic is performed.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::cmBlockFunctio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::cmBlockFunctio.body: The constructor creates a new `cmBlockFunctionBlocker` by copying the internal state of an existing instance, forwarding the copy operation to its base class `cmFunctionBlocker` and initializing any subclass‑specific members accordingly.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::cmBlockFunctio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::cmBlockFunctio.body: cmBlockFunctionBlocker is a public member function that registers a function as a block‑level executable in the CM block system, creating the required data structures and attaching the function to the appropriate block context. It typically returns a status indicator and may perform validation of the supplied function and its arguments before insertion.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN.body: The overload performs a copy‑assignment: it copies the internal state of the given `cmBlockFunctionBlocker` into the current instance, ensuring that the new instance contains the same function‑block configuration as the source.

@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::~cmBlockFuncti.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBlockFunctionBlocker::~cmBlockFuncti.body: The destructor checks whether any variable scopes are present. If they are, it invokes `Makefile->RaiseScope(VariableNames)` to propagate that scope.

@lcmBreakCommand@k_Z14cmBreakCommandRKiR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBreakCommand@k_Z14cmBreakCommandRKiR.body: The function checks whether a `BREAK` command is being used correctly inside a loop in a makefile. It determines if the current policy (CMP0055) allows a warning, old behaviour, or demands an error. Depending on that policy, it may issue a warning or fatal error message. It also verifies that the `BREAK` takes no arguments; if any are supplied it will report an error according to the policy. After performing these checks, it marks the break as invoked in the status object and returns success unless an enforced error condition was triggered.

@lcmBuildCommand@k_Z14cmBuildCommandRKiR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBuildCommand@k_Z14cmBuildCommandRKiR.body: cmBuildCommand examines the number of arguments in `args`. If the vector contains exactly two strings, it forwards the request to `TwoArgsSignature`; otherwise it invokes `MainSignature` to handle the command.

@lcmBuildOptions::cmBuildOptions@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBuildOptions::cmBuildOptions@k_ZN14c.body:
`cmBuildOptions::cmBuildOptions(const cmBuildOptions& other) noexcept = default;`  

This constructor performs a shallow copy of a `cmBuildOptions` object. It is marked `explicit` to avoid accidental implicit conversions, is declared `noexcept` to guarantee no exceptions are thrown during the copy, and `default` allows the compiler to generate the copy logic automatically.

@lcmBuildOptions::cmBuildOptions@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBuildOptions::cmBuildOptions@k_ZN14c.body: Sets configuration flags for a build operation: stores whether to run a clean pass, whether to use a fast build shortcut, and the chosen package‑resolution strategy (Fast, Clean, or Resolve).

@lcmBuildOptions::cmBuildOptions@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBuildOptions::cmBuildOptions@k_ZN14c.body: The `cmBuildOptions` function creates a default‑configured options object, initializing all option fields to their standard values so callers start with a ready‑to‑use configuration.

@lcmBuildOptions::operator=@k_ZN14cmBuil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBuildOptions::operator=@k_ZN14cmBuil.body: The assignment operator simply copies all fields of a `cmBuildOptions` instance into the current object and returns that object. It’s declared noexcept and uses the compiler‑generated default implementation, so no additional logic is executed during assignment.

@lcmBuildOptions::~cmBuildOptions@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBuildOptions::~cmBuildOptions@k_ZN14.body: The function `~cmBuildOptions()` constructs and returns a `cmBuildOptions` structure populated with default build‑time flags. It initializes the option fields (e.g., parallelism level, output paths, enable‑debug mode) according to the current configuration and environment variables before handing the struct back to callers.

@lcmCLI_ExpandListUnique@k_ZL22cmCLI_Exp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCLI_ExpandListUnique@k_ZL22cmCLI_Exp.body: It takes a string, splits it into individual tokens (via `cmList`), and appends each token that hasn’t yet been emitted into the supplied vector, using the `emitted` set to drop duplicates.

@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::GetEnv@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::GetEnv@k_ZN.body: It calls the helper routine `cmSystemTools::GetEnv` with the supplied key, captures the resulting string in a local variable, and returns that string unchanged.

@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::SetEnv@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::SetEnv@k_ZN.body: The method stores the current value for a given key in a backup map, then either clears that key in the environment if the new value is empty or sets it to the new value by composing a “key=value” string and invoking the system helper to update the environment.

@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::cmCLocaleEn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::cmCLocaleEn.body: The constructor of `cmCLocaleEnvironmentScope` establishes a temporary locale context for the executing thread: it captures the current locale, installs a new one, and guarantees that the original locale is automatically restored when the object is destroyed. Because the class owns this transient state, its copy‑constructor is declared deleted, so any attempt to copy an instance results in a compile‑time error, preventing accidental reuse of the same locale guard across independent scopes.

@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::cmCLocaleEn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::cmCLocaleEn.body: The constructor initializes locale‑specific environment variables: it clears “LANGUAGE” and sets “LC_MESSAGES” to “C”, then checks if “LC_ALL” is defined. If so, it resets “LC_ALL” to empty and copies its value into “LC_CTYPE”.

@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::operator=@k.body: The assignment operator copies every internal field of the source instance into the current object and returns a reference to the target (`*this`).

@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::~cmCLocaleE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCLocaleEnvironmentScope::~cmCLocaleE.body: This destructor restores previously‑saved environment variables. It iterates over the `EnvironmentBackup` map, repopulating each key‑value pair into the process’ environment by calling `cmSystemTools::PutEnv`. The loop uses a string stream to format each pair as “name=value”. The routine ensures the process’s environment is returned to its original state when an instance of `cmCLocaleEnvironmentScope` is destroyed.

@lcmCMakeHostSystemInformationCommand::[.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeHostSystemInformationCommand::[.body: Captures all external variables by reference and returns the result of `GetValue(info, key)` when invoked.

@lcmCMakeHostSystemInformationCommand::[.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeHostSystemInformationCommand::[.body: The lambda is a reference‑capturing closure that simply calls `GetDistribValue(status, key, variable)` and returns its result.

@lcmCMakeHostSystemInformationCommand@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeHostSystemInformationCommand@k_.body: This function parses a CMake‑style command that returns system information. It first checks that the argument list contains at least a “RESULT” keyword followed by a variable name and then a “QUERY” keyword. If the query is the special string “WINDOWS_REGISTRY”, it immediately delegates to `QueryWindowsRegistry`. Otherwise the function lazily initializes a single global `SystemInformation` object (running CPU, OS, and memory checks once). It then walks the remaining arguments, building a delimited string of values obtained by calling chained value‑fetch callbacks (`GetValue`, `GetDistribValue`, and, on Windows, `GetWindowsValue`). Each value is appended to the result string; unrecognised keys trigger an error status. Finally the accumulated result string is stored in the Makefile via `AddDefinition`, and the function reports success by returning true.

@lcmCMakeLanguageCommand::[lambda_0]@kcm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeLanguageCommand::[lambda_0]@kcm.body: The lambda pulls arguments from the `args` vector until the current expansion index (`expArg`) catches up with the expanded argument list (`expArgs`). When more are needed it appends the next raw argument to a temporary vector and feeds it to `status.GetMakefile().ExpandArguments(tmpArg, expArgs)`. If the raw list runs out before the expansion target is met, it returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmCMakeLanguageCommand::[lambda_1]@kcm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeLanguageCommand::[lambda_1]@kcm.body: Captures `args`, `rawArg`, `status`, and `expArgs` by reference; creates a `std::vector` of the unprocessed part of `args`, passes it to `status.GetMakefile().ExpandArguments`, and then sets `rawArg` to the new size of `args`.

@lcmCMakeLanguageCommand@k_Z22cmCMakeLan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeLanguageCommand@k_Z22cmCMakeLan.body: The function parses a vector of list‑file arguments, expands any placeholders, and then matches the first expanded token against a handful of meta‑operations (SET_DEPENDENCY_PROVIDER, DEFER, CALL, EVAL, GET_MESSAGE_LOG_LEVEL, GET_EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_ENABLED). Based on the matched token it delegates to the corresponding handler; otherwise it reports a fatal error.

@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandCALL@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandCALL@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The routine first ensures the requested command is permitted, builds the list of arguments for that command, registers a defer id if a defer is requested, and finally executes or schedules the command in the current makefile context.

@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandDEFER@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandDEFER@k_ZN12_GLO.body:
The function implements the “DEFER” command dispatcher used by the CMake engine.  
When the command starts with `CANCEL_CALL`, it consumes the flag and passes every subsequent token that begins with a capital letter to the underlying `DeferCancelCall` routine, reporting an error if the call cannot be cancelled.  
With `GET_CALL_IDS`, it returns the list of active defer IDs to the caller’s variable.  
When the command is `GET_CALL`, it resolves a particular defer ID to its associated command string and stores it in the given variable.  
In every case it validates the argument list and signals errors when arguments are missing or malformed.

@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandEVAL@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandEVAL@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The routine processes an “EVAL” command in the CMake language. It expands the supplied arguments, verifies that the command is followed by the token “CODE”, concatenates everything after that token into a single source string, and then loads that string as a list‑file under the current back‑trace context.

@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandGET_EXPERIMENTAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandGET_EXPERIMENTAL.body: The command expands its arguments, verifies that two arguments (a feature name and a variable name) were supplied, resolves the feature name against the `cmExperimental::Feature` list, and then defines the supplied variable in the makefile as `"TRUE"` or `"FALSE"` based on whether the corresponding experimental feature is enabled. If the feature name is not recognised, it reports a fatal error.

@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandGET_MESSAGE_LOG_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandGET_MESSAGE_LOG_.body: The routine expands its arguments, verifies that exactly one argument was supplied, retrieves the current log‑level value from the makefile, converts that enum to its string name, and stores that string in the makefile under the provided variable name. It then returns success.

@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandSET_DEPENDENCY_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeLanguageCommandSET_DEPENDENCY_P.body: The routine registers a dependency‑provider for a command. It first verifies that the call occurs during the initial top‑level include processing, parses the supplied command name together with a list of provider methods, insists on at least one valid method, and then records the provider’s identity and whether it supports the FetchContentMakeAvailable serial method in the global property `__FETCHCONTENT_MAKEAVAILABLE_SERIAL_PROVIDER`.

@lcmCMakeMinimumRequired@k_Z22cmCMakeMin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakeMinimumRequired@k_Z22cmCMakeMin.body: The routine reads the supplied arguments to determine a minimum required CMake version. It compares the parsed requirement with the running version; if the current version is too low it reports a fatal error and records the policy, otherwise it records any unspecified arguments as warnings and enforces the policy range.

@lcmCMakePath::Absolute@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Absolute@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: The `Absolute` function checks whether the wrapped path (`this->Path`) is relative. If it is, it constructs a new path by appending this relative path to the supplied `base` path using the `operator/=` overload (which normalises separators to `/`). It then returns the generic‐string representation of that combined path. If the path is already absolute, it simply returns the current instance unchanged.

@lcmCMakePath::Absolute@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Absolute@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: The `Absolute` function takes a `cmCMakePath` reference and returns a new `cmCMakePath` that represents the absolute path derived from the supplied base path. It does this by delegating to the `Absolute` helper on the underlying `cmCMakePath` object, which resolves any relative components against the current path. This ensures that the returned path is fully resolved and independent of the original relative components.

@lcmCMakePath::Absolute@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Absolute@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: Constructs an absolute path from a value that can be coerced to a path. It simply wraps the value in `cm::filesystem::path` and forwards it to the internal `Absolute` helper, returning the resulting `cmCMakePath` instance.

@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: The `Append` method concatenates the supplied `path` onto the object’s internal `Path`, normalises the path separators to a generic form, and returns a reference to the modified object so that callers can chain further operations.

@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: Delegates to the internal Append method, passing the `path` member of the supplied `cmCMakePath` argument, and returns the modified instance.

@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body:
This template adds a *path-like* argument to the current path builder.  
Only types that satisfy the `enable_if_pathable` trait (i.e., are implicitly convertible to a `std::filesystem::path`) can be passed.  
The function simply forwards the argument to the overloaded `Append` that accepts a `std::filesystem::path` object and returns the builder itself for chaining.

@lcmCMakePath::Assign@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Assign@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: This member template assigns the supplied argument to the internal member `Path`, forwarding its value without copying and returns the current object for chaining. It is constrained to accept only arguments that satisfy the `enable_if_move_pathable<Source>` trait, ensuring safe forwarding.

@lcmCMakePath::Assign@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Assign@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: The `Assign` member simply copies the supplied `source` into the member `Path` and then returns the current object (`*this`) for chaining.

@lcmCMakePath::Clear@k_ZN11cmCMakePath5C.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Clear@k_ZN11cmCMakePath5C.body: This method simply invokes `Path.clear()` on the current object; because the call is marked `noexcept`, the operation promises no thrown exceptions and performs only the in‑place clearing of the internal collection.

@lcmCMakePath::Compare@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Compare@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.body: It’s a simple, exception‑safe wrapper that forwards the comparison of the internal string member (`Path`) to the underlying string’s `compare` function, returning the integer result. The function is `noexcept` and `const`, so it does not alter any state.

@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: This function appends the supplied string‑view to the underlying `Path` member by invoking `operator+=` on it, then returns a reference to the current object to enable call chaining.

@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: The method appends the supplied `path` to the current object’s internal path string and returns a reference to the modified instance.

@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: The `Concat` member simply appends a given value to the internal `Path` member and returns a reference to the object itself. It uses a SFINAE (`enable_if_pathable`) to restrict the template to types that can be appended via `operator+=`. No more detail is required.

@lcmCMakePath::FormatPath@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::FormatPath@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.body: Normalizes backslashes to forward slashes, strips an initial “\\?\” marker if present, and rewrites UNC‑style prefixes by swapping a leading “\\” with a single slash.

@lcmCMakePath::FormatPath@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::FormatPath@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.body: The function accepts a string view and an optional format flag, then forwards those arguments to another overload that operates on an actual string, returning whatever that overload produces.

@lcmCMakePath::GenericString@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GenericString@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: It returns the string produced by the internal `Path` object, simply forwarding the result of calling `Path.generic_string()` without altering any state.

@lcmCMakePath::GenericWString@k_ZNK11cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GenericWString@k_ZNK11cmC.body: This const member simply forwards a call to its internal `Path` object and returns the resulting `std::wstring`. It invokes `generic_wstring()` on `Path` and returns that value.

@lcmCMakePath::GetExtension@k_ZNK11cmCMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetExtension@k_ZNK11cmCMa.body: The function retrieves the file‑extension component from the internally stored path and returns it as a `cmCMakePath` value.

@lcmCMakePath::GetFileName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetFileName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: The function returns the base‑name part of the stored path object (i.e. the string after the last directory separator). It performs no state changes and simply forwards the filename extracted from `Path`.

@lcmCMakePath::GetNarrowStem@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetNarrowStem@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: Returns the substring of the current path’s stem preceding the first dot after an optional leading dot, or the whole stem if no such dot exists.

@lcmCMakePath::GetNativePath@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetNativePath@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: This function creates a `cm::filesystem::path` from the member `Path`, normalises it via `make_preferred`, and assigns the resulting string to the supplied reference. The operation is straightforward: it simply converts the internal path representation into a plain string for callers.

@lcmCMakePath::GetNativePath@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetNativePath@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: The routine receives a `std::wstring&` reference to receive the resolved path string. It first constructs a temporary `filesystem::path` from the stored member `Path` and normalises it with `make_preferred()`. The resulting wide string is assigned to the output parameter. On Windows builds it then appends a `\\?\` prefix (or a `\\\\?\\UNC` prefix if the path has a leading backslash and a root component) when the final string exceeds `_MAX_PATH - 12` characters and the path is absolute. This guards against the Windows 260‑character path limit by switching to the extended-length form.

@lcmCMakePath::GetParentPath@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetParentPath@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: The function simply returns the parent component of the stored `Path` object. It is a `const` accessor that retrieves the parent path by invoking `this->Path.parent_path()` and returns the resulting `cmCMakePath` value.

@lcmCMakePath::GetRelativePath@k_ZNK11cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetRelativePath@k_ZNK11cm.body: Retrieves the internal `Path` member’s relative part by invoking its `relative_path()` method, returning a `cmCMakePath` instance that represents only the path fragment relative to the base.

@lcmCMakePath::GetRootDirectory@k_ZNK11c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetRootDirectory@k_ZNK11c.body: This const member function retrieves and returns the stored root directory of the object via the `root_directory()` accessor on its internal `Path` member.

@lcmCMakePath::GetRootName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetRootName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: GetRootName simply returns the root part of the internal path by calling the member Path’s `root_name()` method and returning that value. It is marked `const`, so it guarantees no modification of the object’s state.

@lcmCMakePath::GetRootPath@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetRootPath@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: Returns the root path of the current Path object.

@lcmCMakePath::GetStem@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetStem@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.body: The `GetStem` member simply returns the underlying `Path` object's stem string. It exposes that value as a constant result, so callers can read the property without modifying the object.

@lcmCMakePath::GetWideExtension@k_ZNK11c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetWideExtension@k_ZNK11c.body: The method inspects the filename part of the internal `Path`. If the name is empty or a lone “.” or “..”, it returns an empty `cmCMakePath`. Otherwise it searches for the first ‘.’ (skipping a leading dot) and, if found, returns a view of the string starting at that dot; otherwise it again returns an empty path.

@lcmCMakePath::HasExtension@k_ZNK11cmCMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasExtension@k_ZNK11cmCMa.body: The `HasExtension()` method simply forwards the check to the underlying `Path` object: it returns `true` when the stored path contains a non‑empty extension (e.g., a file name ending in “.txt”) and `false` otherwise. It’s a thin wrapper, so its only responsibilities are to expose the `has_extension()` query in a const‑qualified context and to maintain the same semantics as the standard library’s `std::filesystem::path::has_extension`.

@lcmCMakePath::HasFileName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasFileName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: It returns true when the underlying path contains a non‑empty filename component, and false otherwise.

@lcmCMakePath::HasParentPath@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasParentPath@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: This member function simply delegates to the underlying `Path` object and returns the result of its `has_parent_path()` call, indicating whether the path stored in `this->Path` has a parent component.

@lcmCMakePath::HasRelativePath@k_ZNK11cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasRelativePath@k_ZNK11cm.body: This method checks whether the current `Path` instance contains any relative segments (e.g., `.` or `..`). It does so by delegating to `Path::has_relative_path()` and returns that boolean result.

@lcmCMakePath::HasRootDirectory@k_ZNK11c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasRootDirectory@k_ZNK11c.body: Checks whether the stored path contains a root directory by delegating the check to the underlying Path instance.

@lcmCMakePath::HasRootName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasRootName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: It forwards a check to the underlying `Path` object and returns whatever that call yields.

@lcmCMakePath::HasRootPath@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasRootPath@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: It forwards the query to the `Path` member by calling `has_root_path()` and returns the resulting boolean.

@lcmCMakePath::HasStem@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasStem@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.body: Returns whether the stored `Path` object reports that it contains a stem by delegating to `Path.has_stem()` (preserving const‑ness).

@lcmCMakePath::IsEmpty@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::IsEmpty@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.body: The member function simply checks whether the internal `Path` container is empty, returning the result as a `bool`. It is marked `const` and `noexcept`, ensuring no state changes and no exceptions are thrown during the check.

@lcmCMakePath::IsPrefix@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::IsPrefix@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: This function walks through each component of the current `cmCMakePath` and the supplied `path`. It stops when a component differs or the end of one list is reached. It returns `true` if the walk reaches the end of the current path or if the current component is empty and the supplied path still has more components left.

@lcmCMakePath::IsRelative@k_ZNK11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::IsRelative@k_ZNK11cmCMake.body: It checks whether the stored path represents a relative path and returns that Boolean value.

@lcmCMakePath::Native@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Native@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.body: The `Native` method simply calls `GetNativePath` to fill a string with the current native path and returns that string.

@lcmCMakePath::NativeString@k_ZNK11cmCMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::NativeString@k_ZNK11cmCMa.body: It returns the native path string by filling a local string with `GetNativePath` and returning that value.

@lcmCMakePath::NativeWString@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::NativeWString@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: It retrieves the current native path string via an internal helper and returns it.

@lcmCMakePath::Normal@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Normal@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.body: This const member returns the path’s string representation with all directory separators unified to forward slashes: it takes the internally stored path, normalizes it (lexically), then converts any back‑slashes to “/” before returning that string.

@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.body: The method runs `Path.lexically_proximate` on the supplied base path and returns the resulting path string in the platform‑independent, slash‑separated form.

@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.body: The member simply forwards the request to the internal `Proximate` routine that operates on the underlying `Path` representation, returning a new `cmCMakePath` that reflects the computed approximation relative to `base`.

@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.body: The `Proximate` member simply turns the provided `base` into a `std::filesystem::path` and forwards that to the class’s own `Proximate` overload, returning the resulting `cmCMakePath` object. Its template form is guarded by the `enable_if_pathable` trait to ensure the argument is a type that can be treated as a filesystem path.

@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: The function computes a relative path by calling `Path.lexically_relative(base)` and then normalises the separator to a generic `'/'` before returning the string representation.

@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: Computes the relative path between the current object and the supplied base path, returning a new `cmCMakePath` instance that represents the path offset from `base`.

@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: The template creates a relative‑path instance from any type that can be converted to a filesystem path. It forwards the underlying `Relative` logic to the current object (`this`) after wrapping the supplied argument in a `cm::filesystem::path`, ensuring the argument satisfies the compile‑time `enable_if_pathable` constraint.

@lcmCMakePath::RemoveExtension@k_ZN11cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::RemoveExtension@k_ZN11cmC.body: The method checks whether the path already has an extension; if it does, it replaces that extension with an empty string (effectively stripping the suffix) and then returns the modified path object by reference.

@lcmCMakePath::RemoveFileName@k_ZN11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::RemoveFileName@k_ZN11cmCM.body: The `RemoveFileName` method strips the last component of a `cmCMakePath` instance (the filename) and then returns a reference to the same object. It updates the internal path string in‑place rather than creating a new path object.

@lcmCMakePath::RemoveWideExtension@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::RemoveWideExtension@k_ZN1.body: This method removes any file‑extension stored in the current path object. If `Path.has_extension()` is true, it clears the extension part by passing an empty string to `ReplaceWideExtension`, then returns the modified object for chaining.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceExtension@k_ZN11cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceExtension@k_ZN11cm.body: This member function updates the internal `cmCMakePath` instance by replacing its current file‑extension with the supplied one (or an empty extension if none is passed) and returns the modified object for fluent chaining.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceExtension@k_ZN11cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceExtension@k_ZN11cm.body: The method replaces the current file‑path’s extension with the supplied value (which can be a string, string_view, or any type that the `Path` type can convert from). It calls `Path::replace_extension` on the internal `Path` object and then returns a reference to the current instance so calls can be chained.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceFileName@k_ZN11cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceFileName@k_ZN11cmC.body: Replaces the current filename component of the internal path with the supplied one, if the path contains a filename, and returns the modified object.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceFileName@k_ZN11cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceFileName@k_ZN11cmC.body: This template method updates the internal `Path` member only when it already contains a filename; it uses the supplied argument to replace that filename and returns the current object by reference, enabling fluent chaining.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
