@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.body: The `ReplaceWideExtension` member removes an existing extension from the current filename (if present), then attaches the supplied `extension`—adding a leading dot when necessary—and finally updates the internal `Path` member, returning the modified object.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.body: The function simply forwards the supplied extension to a string‑view overload: it converts the `cm::filesystem::path` to a `cm::string_view` of its string representation and returns the result of `this->ReplaceWideExtension(...)`.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.body: Replaces the current path’s file extension with the provided extension string and returns the modified `cmCMakePath` reference.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.body: The function forwards a supplied extension source to an underlying ReplaceWideExtension implementation and returns a reference to the resulting cmCMakePath object. It is constrained with enable_if_pathable so that only types that satisfy that trait can instantiate this overload.

@lcmCMakePath::String@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::String@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.body: It returns a copy of the string representation stored in the object’s internal `Path` member—effectively forwarding whatever string representation `Path.string()` supplies.

@lcmCMakePath::WString@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::WString@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.body: It returns a wide‑character string representation of the object’s internal Path by calling that member’s wstring() routine.

@lcmCMakePath::begin@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::begin@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath5.body: Returns an iterator that points at the first element in the internal path container. It constructs that iterator with the current instance and the underlying container’s begin iterator, giving callers a handle to the start of the path sequence.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: Creates a `Path` instance from the supplied string view by formatting the input with the specified format, then initializing the base `Path` via the `FormatPath` helper—all in a noexcept context.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: `cmCMakePath` is a noexcept constructor that forwards a `cm::filesystem::path` argument to its base class `Path` using a move‑construct. It performs no other work.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: The constructor performs a move‐style copy: it takes an rvalue reference to another `cmCMakePath` and forwards its stored path to the base `Path` class via perfect forwarding, guaranteeing noexcept safety.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: cmCMakePath constructs a Path object by formatting the supplied C‑string source with the requested format. It creates a cm::string_view from the raw pointer and forwards it, along with the format, to the base Path constructor via FormatPath.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: The `cmCMakePath` copy‑constructor is explicitly declared as `= default`, meaning the compiler generates a shallow copy that duplicates the internal state of the object (member variables) without custom logic. It simply creates a new `cmCMakePath` instance with the same configuration as the source.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: Creates a `Path` instance by forwarding the supplied `source` into `FormatPath` with the specified format. It’s enabled only when the source type satisfies the `enable_if_move_pathable` constraint, ensuring the constructor works only for types that can be moved into a `Path`.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: cmCMakePath takes a string_view and a format description, interpolates any supplied format tokens into the view, normalizes separators (e.g., converting forward/backward slashes) and returns a ready‑to‑use path string that other components can safely join to file system paths.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: The function `cmCMakePath()` is a defaulted, noexcept constructor that simply creates and returns an instance of the `cmCMakePath` type.

@lcmCMakePath::end@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath3en.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::end@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath3en.body: The `end()` member returns an iterator that refers to the sentinel position after the last element in the internal path sequence; it constructs that iterator with `this` and the end iterator of the underlying container (`this->Path.end()`).

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::iterator@k_ZN11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::iterator@k_ZN11.body:
It’s a constructor that ties a particular file‑system element to the internal iterator state.  
The ctor stores a pointer to the original `cmCMakePath`, holds a reference to the current iterator position, and captures the path element represented by that iterator in `PathElement`. This wiring lets the object expose the current directory or file node when later methods query `Path` or `PathElement`.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::iterator@k_ZN11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::iterator@k_ZN11.body: Creates a new iterator instance that duplicates the underlying iterator, path, and path element from the supplied instance.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::iterator@k_ZN11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::iterator@k_ZN11.body: The `iterator()` member produces an iterator for the internal container, exposing a forward traversal interface. It’s marked default, so the compiler supplies the implicitly generated copy‑constructible instance without extra boilerplate. The iterator type implements standard range‑based for‑loop support and guarantees noexcept traversal semantics.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator*@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator*@k_ZNK.body: Provides read‑only dereference of the underlying `PathElement` member, exposing it as a reference without copying.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator++@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator++@k_ZN.body: The postfix increment operator copies the current iterator state, increments the underlying iterator, and then returns the copy representing the state before the increment.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator++@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator++@k_ZN.body: It increments the internal iterator, stores the dereferenced element in `PathElement`, and returns the updated object.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator--@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator--@k_ZN.body: The operator decrements the iterator and returns the original position: it makes a copy of the current iterator, calls the decrement implementation on the current object, and returns the copied iterator that represents the state before the decrement.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator--@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator--@k_ZN.body: The method decrements the internal iterator, assigns the dereferenced element to `PathElement`, and then returns the current object.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator->@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator->@k_ZN.body: The overload returns a pointer to the member `PathElement` so that code using `obj->member` can transparently access `PathElement`’s members while preserving const‑read‑only access.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator=@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::operator=@k_ZN1.body: The operator= copies the iterator and path from the argument, assigns the internal path element to the dereferenced value of that iterator, and returns the current instance.

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::~iterator@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::iterator::~iterator@k_ZN1.body: The `~iterator()` function is a destructor for an `iterator` class. It is implicitly declared as defaulted, meaning the compiler will generate the default destructor unless explicitly overridden. When an `iterator` instance is destroyed, this destructor will be invoked to release any owned resources (e.g., memory or file handles) and perform any necessary cleanup before the object is de‑allocated. It plays the usual role of a C++ destructor: ensuring the internal state is left in a clean, deterministic state and that no dangling resources remain after the object’s lifetime ends.

@lcmCMakePath::operator+=@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::operator+=@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.body: The `operator+=` overload appends the supplied `cmCMakePath` to the current instance by delegating to `Concat`, returning a reference to the updated path.

@lcmCMakePath::operator+=@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::operator+=@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.body: The template overloads `operator+=` to append a `Source` argument to the internal path buffer. It forwards the call to `Concat`, constrained by `enable_if_pathable`, and returns a reference to the current instance (`cmCMakePath&`).

@lcmCMakePath::operator/=@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::operator/=@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.body: The operator appends the supplied `cmCMakePath` to the current instance by delegating to `Append`, then returns a reference to the updated object.

@lcmCMakePath::operator/=@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::operator/=@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.body: This overload allows a `cmCMakePath` object to absorb a value that satisfies the `pathable` trait. It forwards the incoming value to the internal `Append` routine and returns a reference to the current object, enabling fluent chaining of multiple appends.

@lcmCMakePath::operator=@k_ZN11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::operator=@k_ZN11cmCMakePa.body: This overload swaps the internal `Path` member with the incoming `cmCMakePath` instance by moving its `Path` value when the source differs from the target, and then returns a reference to the current object.

@lcmCMakePath::operator=@k_ZN11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::operator=@k_ZN11cmCMakePa.body: The template provides an assignment operator that forwards the incoming `source` to `Assign`, returning a reference to the current object. It is enabled only when the source type satisfies the `enable_if_move_pathable` condition, ensuring safe move‑assignment.

@lcmCMakePath::operator=@k_ZN11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::operator=@k_ZN11cmCMakePa.body: The function overloads the assignment operator for the `cmCMakePath` class. It first checks for self‑assignment (`this != &path`) and, if different, copies the `Path` member from the RHS `path` into the current object. Finally, it returns a reference to `*this` so that the assignment can be used in chained expressions.

@lcmCMakePath::operator=@k_ZN11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::operator=@k_ZN11cmCMakePa.body: This overload of `operator=` accepts any type that satisfies the `enable_if_pathable` constraint. It forwards the source to the `Assign` member to perform the actual assignment and then returns a reference to the current instance, allowing callers to chain further operations in a fluent‑style API.

@lcmCMakePath::swap@k_ZN11cmCMakePath4sw.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::swap@k_ZN11cmCMakePath4sw.body: Swaps the internal `Path` string with that of another `cmCMakePath` instance. The operation is marked `noexcept`, guaranteeing no exception is thrown during the swap.

@lcmCMakePath::~cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::~cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMak.body: The `~cmCMakePath` function is the destructor for the `cmCMakePath` class, handling cleanup of any resources allocated during the lifetime of a `cmCMakePath` instance.

@lcmCMakePathCommand@k_Z18cmCMakePathCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePathCommand@k_Z18cmCMakePathCom.body: Checks that at least two arguments are provided; if not, it sets an error in the status and fails. Otherwise it looks up the first argument in a static lookup table of sub‑commands and forwards the full argument list to the corresponding handler, returning that handler’s result.

@lcmCMakePolicyCommand@k_Z20cmCMakePolic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePolicyCommand@k_Z20cmCMakePolic.body: The function takes a list of arguments for a CMake policy command and dispatches the command based on the first word. It validates the argument list, invokes the specific handler for SET, GET, PUSH, POP, VERSION, or GET_WARNING, and reports an error through the status object when the command name is unknown or arguments are malformed.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::BUILD_TEST_PRESE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::BUILD_TEST_PRESE.body: This routine reports an unsupported build‑preset scenario by injecting a specific error message into the supplied `state` instance, indicating that the current JSON file version is below the required threshold (≥ 2).

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CONDITION_UNSUPP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CONDITION_UNSUPP.body: The function checks whether the current JSON file version supports condition features. If the file version is less than 3, it logs an error via the state object: “File version must be 3 or higher for condition support.”

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CONFIGURE_PRESET.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CONFIGURE_PRESET.body: If invoked during preset resolution, the routine simply flags that the preset identified by `presetName` cannot be reached from its originating file. It builds a diagnostic string—including the name—and forwards it to the supplied `cmJSONState` via `AddError`.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CONFIGURE_WORKFL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CONFIGURE_WORKFL.body: The function logs an error indicating that the supplied step name cannot be used because it is not the first step. It simply calls `state->AddError` with a message built from `stepName`.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CTEST_JUNIT_UNSU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CTEST_JUNIT_UNSU.body: The function registers an error message on the supplied state object. It records that the current file version is insufficient—an error is logged indicating the version must be 6 or newer to support CTest JUnit output.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CYCLIC_INCLUDE@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CYCLIC_INCLUDE@k.body: The helper records a cyclic‑include error by calling `state->AddError` with a message that prefixes the offending file name.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CYCLIC_PRESET_IN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::CYCLIC_PRESET_IN.body: The function records a cyclic inheritance error for a preset named *presetName* by adding an error entry into the supplied *state* object.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::DUPLICATE_PRESET.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::DUPLICATE_PRESET.body: Adds an error message to the given `cmJSONState` object indicating that a preset with the supplied name already exists, preventing a duplicate entry.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::FILE_NOT_FOUND@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::FILE_NOT_FOUND@k.body: The routine appends a formatted error string to the supplied state object. It builds the message by prefixing `"File not found: "` to the filename argument via `cmStrCat` and pushes the result into the state’s error list through `AddError`.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::FIRST_WORKFLOW_S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::FIRST_WORKFLOW_S.body: It verifies that the initial workflow step must be a “configure” step; if it isn’t, the routine registers an error in the state.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INCLUDE_UNSUPPOR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INCLUDE_UNSUPPOR.body: The routine simply records a validation failure for an include that cannot be processed because the JSON file’s version is below the minimum supported value (4). When invoked it injects an error message into the supplied state object—no further action is taken.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INHERITED_PRESET.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INHERITED_PRESET.body: This routine registers an error indicating that a preset referenced via inheritance cannot be reached in the current preset’s file, attaching a diagnostic message to the state object.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INSTALL_PREFIX_U.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INSTALL_PREFIX_U.body: The function simply records a validation failure when the JSON document’s declared file‑version is below 3, by calling `state->AddErrorAtValue` with a message that the install‑directory preset requires a minimum version of 3.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_CONDITIO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_CONDITIO.body: The function registers an error message stating that the condition for a preset is invalid, using the preset’s name obtained via `getPresetName` to format the message.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_CONDITIO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_CONDITIO.body: It builds a string that embeds the preset name obtained from the state object.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_CONDITIO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_CONDITIO.body: The function is a small helper that constructs a specific error object. It packages an error of type `INVALID_NAMED_OBJECT` with a message built by a lambda; the message interpolates the preset name via `getPresetName(state)`. The result is an `ErrorGenerator` that, when invoked, produces the string “condition for preset “<name>””. This helper is used to surface a contextual error during JSON validation.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_CONFIGUR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_CONFIGUR.body: The function simply reports an “invalid configurePreset” error: it appends a message that says “Invalid “configurePreset” : {presetName}” to the supplied JSON state.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_INCLUDE@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_INCLUDE@.body: When an “include” field is malformed, the helper simply records the problem in the parser’s state: it passes the offending value to `state->AddErrorAtValue`, tagging it as an “Invalid include” error.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_MACRO_EX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_MACRO_EX.body: Adds an error entry to the supplied state. The message is built by concatenating “Invalid macro expansion in ” with the given preset name and a closing quote. The function simply calls state‑>AddError() with that string.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET@k.body: The function is a small helper that, when called with a JSON value and a state object, tells the state to register an error message (“Invalid preset”) tied to that specific value. This usually means the parsing logic has encountered a preset that does not meet the expected format or constraints, and the helper records the error so that calling code can react accordingly.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESETS@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESETS@.body: When invoked the routine records an error for the JSON field named “configurePresets”. It tags that specific value in the state’s error list so the caller knows the field contains invalid data.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET_N.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET_N.body: The function creates an error message “Invalid Preset Name”, appends the offending string if supplied, and records the error in the supplied state.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET_N.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET_N.body: The routine records an error for an invalid preset name by invoking `AddError` with a message that embeds the supplied `presetName`.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET_O.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET_O.body: A function object that takes two pointers— a `const Json::Value*` and a `cmJSONState*`—ignores them and simply returns the string literal `"Preset"`.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET_O.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESET_O.body: The function creates a specific error for a JSON object that is not a preset. It forwards the given error type and any extra fields to `JsonErrors::INVALID_NAMED_OBJECT`, supplying a lambda that always returns the string “Preset” to be used as the object name in the error message. The result is an instance of `JsonErrors::ErrorGenerator` that can be used elsewhere to report the issue.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_ROOT@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_ROOT@k_Z.body: The routine registers an error in the supplied state for an invalid root object.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_ROOT_OBJ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_ROOT_OBJ.body: The lambda accepts a JSON value pointer and a state pointer, then immediately returns the literal string `"root object"`.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_ROOT_OBJ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_ROOT_OBJ.body: The function produces a named‑object validation error for the JSON root element. It wraps a lambda that, when invoked, returns the identifier string `"root object"`. The returned error object is created with the supplied error type and any additional fields.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_VARIABLE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_VARIABLE.body: The routine pulls the current variable name via `cmCMakePresetsErrors::getVariableName`, then signals an “Invalid CMake” error on the supplied JSON value by invoking `state->AddErrorAtValue`.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_VARIABLE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_VARIABLE.body: The lambda simply returns a string by invoking getVariableName on the supplied cmJSONState pointer—effectively extracting the variable name encoded in that state.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_VARIABLE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_VARIABLE.body: Creates a named object error instance for the supplied error type and fields, using an inline lambda that fetches the variable name from the provided state.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_VERSION@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_VERSION@.body: The `INVALID_VERSION` function registers a validation failure when the JSON contains a “version” field that is missing or malformed. It pushes an error message into the state context so that caller logic can report the problem to callers or callers’ callers.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_WORKFLOW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_WORKFLOW.body: The function appends a descriptive error message to the state object by formatting the supplied workflow step name and invoking the state’s `AddError` method.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::NO_VERSION@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::NO_VERSION@k_ZN2.body: The `NO_VERSION` routine is a minimal error‑handler used during JSON schema validation: when the parser encounters a value that lacks a required `"version"` field, it records the problem in the provided `cmJSONState` instance by invoking `AddErrorAtValue` with a concise message. This helper keeps the error‑reporting logic isolated from higher‑level parsing code.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::NO_WORKFLOW_STEP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::NO_WORKFLOW_STEP.body: The routine simply records a missing‑step condition by appending a message that no workflow steps were supplied for the supplied preset name. It uses the state helper’s `AddError` to surface the notification.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::PACKAGE_PRESETS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::PACKAGE_PRESETS_.body: The routine simply registers a hard‑coded error in the state object, stating that the current file version is below the required minimum (6) for preset support. It contains no further checks or logic beyond that call.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::PRESET_MISSING_F.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::PRESET_MISSING_F.body: Adds an error entry noting that a preset is missing a required field.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::SCHEMA_UNSUPPORT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::SCHEMA_UNSUPPORT.body: The `SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` routine simply records an error in the JSON parsing context when a file’s version number is below the minimum required (8). It does this by calling `AddError` on the supplied `cmJSONState` object with a fixed message indicating that the schema is only supported from version 8 onward.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::TEST_OUTPUT_TRUN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::TEST_OUTPUT_TRUN.body: The function `TEST_OUTPUT_TRUNCATION_UNSUPPORTED` is a small helper that rejects legacy output‑format versions. When invoked, it checks the numeric *FileVersion* stored in the supplied `cmJSONState` object and, if that value is lower than 5, records an error via the `AddError` method. This signals to the caller that the current JSON configuration cannot be processed with the older output‑truncation preset.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::TOOLCHAIN_FILE_U.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::TOOLCHAIN_FILE_U.body: The function records an error in the state that a toolchain file with a version less than 3 is unsupported.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::TRACE_UNSUPPORTE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::TRACE_UNSUPPORTE.body: When trace preset support is requested on a file whose version number is below 7, the routine simply records an error in the supplied JSON state by calling `AddError` with the message that the file version must be at least 7.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::UNRECOGNIZED_CMA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::UNRECOGNIZED_CMA.body: The function builds a closure that, when executed, records an error in the state indicating that the supplied CMake version string is insufficient because the required minimum is greater than the current value, formatting the message with the provided version and numeric values.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::UNRECOGNIZED_VER.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::UNRECOGNIZED_VER.body: The function simply flags a missing or invalid “version” field by adding an error entry into the parser state object, which records that the encountered JSON value didn’t contain the expected version string.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::WORKFLOW_PRESETS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::WORKFLOW_PRESETS.body: The routine flags a workflow‑preset incompatibility by registering an error in the given state object—specifically noting that the file’s version must be at least 6 for preset support.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::WORKFLOW_STEP_UN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::WORKFLOW_STEP_UN.body: The function logs an error when a requested workflow step cannot be reached from a preset file. It simply records that the step name is unreachable by adding an error message to the provided state object.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::getPreset@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::getPreset@k_ZN20.body: The function examines the current parsing context; if there are at least two items in the parsing stack, it checks whether the top‑level key corresponds to one of the preset namespaces (“configurePresets”, “packagePresets”, “buildPresets”, “testPresets”). When a match occurs, it returns the value stored in the second stack entry; otherwise it yields a null pointer.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::getPresetName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::getPresetName@k_.body: The function calls `getPreset()` to fetch the preset object. If that object exists and contains a `"name"` field, it returns that string; otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::getVariableName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsErrors::getVariableName@.body: The routine fetches the value that follows the key `"cacheVariables"` in the JSON state, then formats that name into a human‑readable phrase that reads `“variable "<name>" for preset "<preset>"`. It simply stitches together a few strings and returns the resulting string.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::BuildPreset::Visi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::BuildPreset::Visi.body: The method checks whether a preset instance is marked as non‑hidden and has no configuration stored in its `ConfigurePreset` collection. If that condition holds, it returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::BuildPreset::Visi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::BuildPreset::Visi.body: The function propagates configuration from a supplied parent preset into the current preset by calling a set of helper routines (`Inherit*`). It copies scalar values, optional values, and vectors for configuration, environment, jobs, targets, etc., then falls back to a direct assignment for `ResolvePackageReferences` if the child preset doesn’t already override it. Finally it returns `true`, signalling that the inheritance step succeeded.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ClearPresets@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ClearPresets@k_ZN.body: This routine wipes every internal preset container and the associated ordering maps, then removes all file entries, effectively resetting the object’s preset state to empty.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::Condit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::Condit.body: The constructor builds a new `Condition` object by copying the state of an existing instance—ensuring that all internal members are properly duplicated so the new object is ready for use within the graph context.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::Evalua.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::Evalua.body: The pure virtual `Evaluate()` function is an abstract contract that derived classes must fulfill. It performs a domain‑specific assessment and returns `true` only when the internal state satisfies the caller’s criteria, otherwise `false`. Its implementation is expected to be provided by concrete subclasses that perform the actual evaluation logic.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::IsNull.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::IsNull.body: This member simply reports that the object is never considered null, returning `false`. It’s declared virtual so derived types can override it to provide custom null‑checking logic, and the const qualifier guarantees that the call does not modify the object state.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::operat.body: Assigns the contents of one Condition instance to another, performing a member‑wise copy of all of the condition’s internal state and returning a reference to the target object.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::~Condi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition::~Condi.body: The virtual destructor `~Condition()` is declared `= default;`. It tells the compiler to generate the usual destructor that automatically destroys all data members and invokes the base‑class destructors. Because it’s marked `virtual`, any subclass that derives from this class can override it to add its own cleanup logic, but if it’s left default the compiler will provide the standard behaviour.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ConfigurePreset::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ConfigurePreset::.body: The method verifies a preset’s configuration after it has been created. It first skips validation if the preset is flagged as hidden. For versions below 3 it ensures the mandatory fields `generator` and `binaryDir` are present; missing ones trigger an error and return false. It then rejects any preset that would emit a warning but is marked as an error for either deprecation or dev‑use. Finally, it flags an error if any cache variable has an empty key. If none of these checks fail, it returns true.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ConfigurePreset::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ConfigurePreset::.body:
The method simply verifies that the preset’s environment map does not already contain a key of an empty string.  
If such a key is present it returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ConfigurePreset::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ConfigurePreset::.body: The method copies each configuration field from a supplied parent preset into the current instance—overwriting strings, optionals, and booleans only when unset, then merges the parent’s cache variable set into the current preset’s collection.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::GetFilename@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::GetFilename@k_ZN1.body: The function returns the full path of the file `CMakePresets.json` by appending the constant suffix `"/CMakePresets.json"` to the supplied `sourceDir`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::GetUserFilename@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::GetUserFilename@k.body: The function simply builds and returns the path string by appending “/CMakeUserPresets.json” to the supplied directory string, using the helper `cmStrCat` to perform the concatenation.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::GetVersion@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::GetVersion@k_ZNK1.body: Returns the integer `Version` stored in the preset’s `OriginFile`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PackagePreset::Vi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PackagePreset::Vi.body: The function checks whether a preset is hidden or has no configuration data. If the preset is visible and its configuration data is non‑empty, it returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PackagePreset::Vi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PackagePreset::Vi.body: The `VisitPresetInherit` method copies configuration data from a parent preset into the current instance. It assigns scalar strings, optional values, and vector collections—merging lists and inserting any new variables into the current preset’s set—before returning `true` to signal success.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Preset::VisitPres.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Preset::VisitPres.body: The `VisitPresetAfterInherit` virtual function acts as a hook that can be overridden in derived classes. It accepts a version identifier and a `cmJSONState*` pointer, and by default always returns `true`. This signals that the caller should continue processing unless a derived override chooses to return `false`. The function itself contains no real logic; its sole effect is to signal success with the returned boolean.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Preset::VisitPres.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Preset::VisitPres.body: The `VisitPresetBeforeInherit` method acts as a no‑op hook in the visitor chain: it simply returns `true`, signalling that the default handling is successful and allowing the caller to continue without interruption. Override this method to inject custom pre‑inheritance logic when needed.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Preset::VisitPres.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::Preset::VisitPres.body: This pure virtual function is an interface contract that concrete subclasses must implement. When called, it receives a reference to a preset object and is expected to perform whatever processing is appropriate for that preset. It must return `true` or `false` to indicate whether the visit succeeded.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintAllPresets@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintAllPresets@k.body: The function collects and prints all preset categories. It creates a `PrintPrecedingNewline` flag set to `False`, then sequentially calls `PrintConfigurePresetList`, `PrintBuildPresetList`, `PrintTestPresetList`, `PrintPackagePresetList`, and `PrintWorkflowPresetList`, passing the flag reference each time so that a consistent newline formatting is applied to every output.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintBuildPresetL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintBuildPresetL.body: The routine gathers the list of build‑presets that are marked as expanded and whose condition flag is set. For each such preset it stores the corresponding `Preset` object in a local vector. If that vector is non‑empty, it writes a newline marker and then prints a banner followed by the list of these presets.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintConfigurePre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintConfigurePre.body: The lambda passed to `PrintConfigurePresetList` simply takes a `ConfigurePreset` reference and unconditionally returns `true`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintConfigurePre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintConfigurePre.body: The function forwards the request to the internal `PrintConfigurePresetList` routine, supplying a simple filter that accepts every preset. It then invokes the provided `newline` printer for each entry, effectively printing the full list of preset configurations.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintConfigurePre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintConfigurePre.body: This routine scans the graph’s preset collection, keeping only those that are visible (not hidden) and have a satisfied expansion status, then emits the qualifying presets in a formatted list.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPackagePrese.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPackagePrese.body: The lambda is a predicate that always returns `true` for each `PackagePreset` argument, effectively meaning all presets in the list will be processed/printed.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPackagePrese.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPackagePrese.body: Delegates its work to the overload that accepts a filter lambda—providing a predicate that always returns `true`, so every `PackagePreset` in the internal collection is printed using the supplied `PrintPrecedingNewline` instance.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPackagePrese.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPackagePrese.body: Collects all presets that are not hidden, whose expansion succeeded, satisfy the supplied filter, and then prints the resulting list after a header line. It uses the helper routines to emit a newline and the “Available package presets:” message before delegating the actual list output to PrintPresets.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPresets::[la.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPresets::[la.body: It compares two `Preset` pointers and returns `true` when the first preset’s `Name` string is shorter than the second’s.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPresets@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintPresets@k_ZN.body: The function iterates through a list of preset objects, printing each preset’s name padded to the width of the longest name in the list. If a preset has a non‑empty `DisplayName`, it appends “ ‑ ” followed by that description. The output is left‑aligned, with each line terminated by a newline.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintTestPresetLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintTestPresetLi.body: It iterates over the stored test‑preset IDs, retrieves each preset, and for those that are visible (not hidden) and whose Expanded flag is set and whose condition succeeded, it adds them to a list. If any such presets exist, it prints a header line followed by the list of those presets via `PrintPresets`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintWorkflowPres.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::PrintWorkflowPres.body: The function gathers presets that are not hidden, are expanded, and whose expansion condition passed, then writes them after a header line if any such presets exist.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadJSONFile::[la.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadJSONFile::[la.body: This operator() receives a key string, a root type and a read reason, and fills an output string reference; it returns true when the lookup succeeds and false otherwise.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadJSONFile::[la.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadJSONFile::[la.body: The lambda reads a JSON file into an internal representation; if the read fails it propagates the failure message and returns `false`. On success it merges the `ReachableFiles` list from the included file into the current file’s set and returns `true`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadJSONFile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadJSONFile@k_ZN.body: The `ReadJSONFile` routine opens a JSON preset file, validates its schema according to the current software version, and populates internal data structures with the parsed preset objects. It checks for circular includes, enforces minimum CMake version requirements, processes macro expansion in include paths, and organizes the presets into the various preset maps (build, test, workflow, etc.) while tracking file reachability for later use.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadProjectPreset.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadProjectPreset.body: The method sets the internal source path, clears any existing presets, then invokes the internal reader. If that reader returns false it wipes the presets again and returns false; otherwise it reports success.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadProjectPreset.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::ReadProjectPreset.body: The function opens a preset file in the project directory (using either the user‑specified file or a default fallback), parses it into preset maps, validates that each preset refers to existing presets and that its origin files can reach the referenced preset, then expands all macros in the preset contents; if any step fails it records an error and returns false. If all checks succeed, it returns true.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::TestPreset::Visit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::TestPreset::Visit.body: The function verifies whether a preset is usable after inheritance: if the preset is not hidden and its `ConfigurePreset` list is empty, it returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::TestPreset::Visit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::TestPreset::Visit.body: The method takes a parent preset and copies each field that is present in that preset into the current instance. It walks through simple values, optional members, strings, vectors, and nested optional structs (like Output, Filter, Execution), updating the current preset’s members only when the parent contains a value. After merging all relevant fields it returns true.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::WorkflowPreset::V.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::WorkflowPreset::V.body: The function `VisitPresetAfterInherit` is a virtual hook meant to be overridden by derived classes. In its base implementation it simply returns `true` without inspecting its arguments, effectively signalling that the visit succeeded by default. It takes an integer `version` and a `cmJSONState*` pointer but doesn’t use them; subclasses can implement custom logic that runs after a preset is inherited.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::WorkflowPreset::V.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::WorkflowPreset::V.body: The method serves as a virtual hook for handling preset inheritance; in its current form it performs no work and simply returns `true`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::cmCMakePresetsGra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::cmCMakePresetsGra.body: The routine constructs a dependency graph of CMake presets, mapping how each preset depends on the others so the build system can resolve and apply the preset chain.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::printPrecedingNew.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraph::printPrecedingNew.body:
The function receives a pointer to a `PrintPrecedingNewline` flag.  
If the pointer isn’t null and its value equals `True`, it emits a newline (`std::endl`).  
Afterwards it writes `True` into the pointed‑to location.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.body: The `AnyAllOfCondition` node encapsulates a collection of sub‑conditions and evaluates to true only when **every** of those sub‑conditions is satisfied; otherwise it evaluates to false. It is used in the graph to represent a logical AND across multiple condition checks.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.body: The `AnyAllOfCondition` class wraps a collection of subordinate conditions. When its `evaluate` method runs, it returns success only if at least one of those child conditions is satisfied, otherwise it fails. This allows a CMake preset graph to express “if any of these checks pass, the overall condition is true.”

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.body:
The function iterates through the stored `Conditions`. For each condition it evaluates it; if the evaluation fails, it clears `out` and returns `false`.  
If any evaluation yields `false`, it clears `out` and returns `true`.  
If an evaluation matches `StopValue`, it assigns that value to `out` and returns `true`.  
When all conditions succeed without triggering the stop value, it assigns `!StopValue` to `out` and returns `true`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.body: The operator=` assigns a supplied `AnyAllOfCondition` instance to the current object, replacing its internal condition representation with the new condition.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.body: The assignment operator copies the internal condition lists of the source `AnyAllOfCondition` into the target object, updating all associated predicates and flags. It returns a reference to the current instance, enabling method chaining while carefully guarding against self‑assignment to avoid corrupting internal state.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::AnyAllOfC.body: The function implements a node in the CMake preset‑graph that evaluates whether a set of subordinate conditions collectively hold. When invoked it returns **true** only if *every* of the child conditions succeeds; otherwise it reports failure. This logic allows callers to treat the node as a single “all‑of” check that can be embedded in larger, possibly nested, condition graphs.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::BuildPres.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::BuildPres.body: BuildPresetsHelper initializes a static JSON helper that, given a JSON array, parses each element into a BuildPreset instance (using BuildPresetHelper) and records any parsing errors via cmCMakePresetsErrors::INVALID_PRESETS). It then returns the helper’s boolean success flag.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::Configure.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::Configure.body: Parses a JSON array into a vector of ConfigurePreset instances, using a static JSONHelperBuilder instance to validate and convert the data; returns true if the operation succeeds, otherwise false.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.body: The constructor simply moves an existing `ConstCondition` instance into a new one, transferring all of its internal state (including any ownership markers) without copying, so that callers can efficiently reuse a temporary condition object.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.body: The constructor duplicates an existing condition object, creating a new instance that mirrors the original state without modifying it. It ensures the new instance is independent and maintains internal consistency.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.body: The method stores the stored value into the supplied optional reference and then returns true to indicate success.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.body: The assignment operator takes a `ConstCondition` (by rvalue reference) and moves its internal representation into the target object, then returns the object itself.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.body: The assignment operator copies the state of a given `ConstCondition` into the current object and returns a reference to that object.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ConstCond.body: The function is the virtual destructor of `ConstCondition`. It guarantees that any resources owned by a `ConstCondition` instance are released when the object is deleted, ensuring derived classes in the `cmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition` hierarchy execute their cleanup logic before the base destructor runs.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::Environme.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::Environme.body: The function registers a JSON helper that knows how to serialize/deserialize an optional string wrapped in the `Environment` type. When invoked it delegates the work to that helper, returning true if the mapping succeeds and false otherwise.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.body: EqualsCondition checks whether two condition objects represent the same logical test, returning true when their internal states match.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.body: This function creates an instance of the `EqualsCondition` class (or copies an existing one). It takes a reference to a `EqualsCondition` object and uses it to initialize the new instance, typically copying internal state such as comparison operators or values that represent an equality test. The resulting object can then be used wherever a condition is required—such as in the condition‑checking logic of the `cmCMakePresetsGraph` machinery.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.body: The routine expands the stored left‑hand‑side and right‑hand‑side strings with the supplied macro expander set, assigns the boolean result of their string comparison to the optional output parameter, and unconditionally reports success (true).

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.body: The `operator=` overload accepts an `EqualsCondition` instance and assigns it to the current object, returning the modified instance so that the condition can be used fluently in the preset graph logic.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.body: The `operator=` overload performs a shallow copy of an `EqualsCondition` instance, copying its internal data members and returning a reference to the current object so the assignment can be chained.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::EqualsCon.body: The `~EqualsCondition()` function is a virtual destructor that implements the comparison logic for `EqualsCondition` objects. In the library it is invoked whenever a `Condition` instance needs to be compared for equality—typically during graph construction or cleanup passes where the framework must decide whether two condition objects represent the same logical constraint. The implementation simply checks whether the underlying condition data match (often by comparing internal IDs or hash values) and returns that Boolean result. This function is crucial for deduplicating conditions in the graph and for ensuring consistent behavior in condition‑based comparisons.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ExpandMac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ExpandMac.body: The function iterates through each `MacroExpander` supplied in `macroExpanders`. For each, it invokes the expander with the supplied namespace and macro name; if any expander returns a result other than `Ignore`, that result is returned immediately. If all expanders return `Ignore` and the namespace equals `"vendor"`, the function returns `Ignore`; otherwise it falls through to return `Error`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ExpandMac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::ExpandMac.body: The routine walks through the input string character‑by‑character, looking for a dollar sign followed by a namespace in braces. When it finds a valid namespace and a macro name inside the braces, it calls ExpandMacro to substitute the macro expansion into the result string; if the namespace is invalid or expansion fails it returns an error. When parsing ends, any trailing incomplete macro is added verbatim or triggers an error. The function returns an `ExpandMacroResult` indicating success or failure.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.body: The routine expands the stored string via the supplied macro expanders and version, then scans a list of strings; if the expanded string matches any list entry it assigns the optional flag to true and returns true, otherwise it assigns false and still returns true.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.body: Creates an instance of the `InListCondition` class that checks whether a given value is present in a specified list, and returns the resulting condition object.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.body: InListCondition is a lightweight predicate object that encapsulates a check for the presence of a particular node or value in a predefined list of identifiers.  It inherits from cmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition and implements a single‑method interface that, when invoked, simply returns true if the supplied value appears in the internal list and false otherwise.  The constructor takes an rvalue reference (or an unnamed argument) that represents the list to be queried; the implementation assumes that reference is valid and non‑null.  It is typically instantiated inside other parts of the graph‑presets logic to filter nodes or edges during a traversal or search pass.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.body: `operator=` implements a move‑assignment for an `InListCondition`. It takes an rvalue reference, transfers the internal condition data from the argument into the current instance, and returns a reference to `*this`. The implementation simply swaps or copies the relevant members (e.g., the list of conditions) so that after the call the new object contains the state of the source object.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.body: InListCondition::operator= copies all of the source object's fields into the current instance, then returns a reference to the object itself.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::InListCon.body: `~InListCondition()` is a virtual destructor that cleans up a condition node used in the graph of CMake preset checks. It ensures that any resources (e.g., allocated memory or registered callbacks) tied to an instance of `InListCondition` are released when the node is removed from the graph during cleanup or when the application terminates. The function is part of the `cmCMakePresetsGraph` condition hierarchy, and its implementation typically frees internal lists, unregisters listeners, and invokes the base class destructor to maintain correct reference counting and avoid leaks.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.body: The `Evaluate` method checks whether a given string contains a substring that matches a regular expression. It first prepares a string and a regex pattern by expanding any macros in the supplied `expanders` vector using a macro‑expander helper (`CHECK_EXPAND`). It then compiles the pattern with `cmsys::RegularExpression`. If compilation fails the method returns `false`; otherwise it performs a regex match against the string and writes the result into the `out` optional flag. The method finally returns `true` to signal that the evaluation succeeded (either the match succeeded or failed but the operation itself completed).

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.body: The function takes another `MatchesCondition` instance (via move semantics) and compares it against the current instance, returning a boolean that indicates whether the two conditions are considered equivalent for the purposes of the surrounding code.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.body: The `MatchesCondition` public function is essentially a constructor that creates a new condition object from an existing instance (passed by const reference). In the context of `cmCMakePresetsGraph`, this object is used to represent a specific matching rule that can be queried against graph nodes or other conditions to decide whether a particular match succeeds. The implementation handles copying the underlying condition data and ensuring the new instance is ready for evaluation in the graph traversal logic.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.body: The operator assigns a new `MatchesCondition` to the current instance by copying the passed condition and returning a reference to the object, allowing chainable assignments. It effectively updates the internal state to reflect the new condition.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.body: Copies the state of another `MatchesCondition` into the current instance, returning the instance by reference so the assignment can be chained.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::MatchesCo.body: The function evaluates whether a condition instance satisfies the current matching criteria, returning true only when the internal state fulfills the necessary predicates.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.body:
The method runs the wrapped `SubCondition` first.  
If that call fails, it clears the output flag and returns `false`.  
Otherwise, if the wrapped condition produced a value in `out`, the method flips that boolean value (`!value`) before returning `true`. The `out` parameter is left untouched if the wrapped condition never set it.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.body: The *NotCondition* function constructs a new instance by taking an existing `NotCondition` instance (by rvalue reference) and re‑using or moving its internal state to the new object.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.body: Creates a new `NotCondition` instance by copying the condition state from the supplied reference.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to another `NotCondition` instance, copies or moves its internal state into `*this`, and then returns a reference to the left‑hand instance. It’s used wherever a temporary `NotCondition` must be assigned to an existing object.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.body: When called, it copies the internal state of the source `NotCondition` into the target object and returns the target instance. This allows chaining of assignments while maintaining the condition’s current state.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NotCondit.body: ~NotCondition() is the virtual destructor of `NotCondition`, ensuring that any resources allocated by a `Condition` instance are properly released when the object is destroyed.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.body: The `Evaluate` method simply marks the operation as successful by assigning `true` to the optional output reference (`out`) and then returns `true`. It ignores both the vector of `MacroExpander` objects and the `version` parameter, performing no further checks or logic.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.body: This private virtual member simply reports that the object is in a null state by always returning `true`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.body: NullCondition is a move constructor that takes an rvalue reference to another NullCondition instance, allowing the object to be efficiently constructed from an existing one.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.body: NullCondition is a lightweight condition type that represents an empty or no‑op constraint. Its constructor simply forwards to the base `cmCMakePresetsGraph::Condition` without adding any extra state.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.body: The assignment operator accepts an rvalue reference to a `NullCondition`, copies its internal state (e.g., the Boolean flag and any associated data), assigns that to the current instance, and returns a reference to the instance for chaining.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state from another `NullCondition` into the current instance and returns a reference to that instance, enabling chained assignments.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::NullCondi.body: ~NullCondition() simply signals that no condition applies – it evaluates to a neutral/false result.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PackagePr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PackagePr.body: The helper builds a vector of `PackagePreset` objects from a JSON value using a predefined helper and records errors if parsing fails.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetBoo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetBoo.body: The function creates a single, lazily‑initialized helper that knows how to parse a JSON boolean. It simply forwards the supplied output reference, the JSON value pointer, and state pointer to that helper, returning the helper’s success flag.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetCon.body: The helper constructs a new `Condition` instance by calling `ConditionHelper`, assigns that instance to the `out` parameter by moving the unique‑pointer into a shared pointer, and returns the Boolean result produced by `ConditionHelper`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetInt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetInt.body: It creates a helper instance once, then applies it to extract an integer from a JSON value into the supplied reference, returning true when the conversion succeeds and false otherwise.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetNam.body: The function validates that a JSON value is a non‑empty string; if the value is missing, not a string, or empty it records an “INVALID_PRESET_NAME” error in the supplied state and returns false, otherwise it copies the string to the output reference and returns true.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetOpt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetOpt.body:
The function is a thin wrapper that forwards an optional‑bool value to the generic JSON helper system.  
It accepts a destination `cm::optional<bool>&`, a JSON node pointer, and a parsing state pointer. Internally it lazily creates a static helper built with `PresetBoolHelper` and simply delegates the work of converting the JSON value into the optional container, returning `true` on success and `false` otherwise. The helper handles presence/absence cases and the appropriate conversion logic.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetOpt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetOpt.body: It simply attempts to read an integer from the JSON tree into an `cm::optional<int>` using a pre‑built helper; if parsing succeeds it returns `true`, otherwise `false`.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetStr.body: The function creates a single static helper via `JSONHelperBuilder::String` and then hands off the provided string reference, JSON value pointer, and state pointer to that helper, returning the helper’s boolean result.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetVec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetVec.body: Creates a static helper that parses a JSON array into a std::vector<int> and returns the helper’s boolean result.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetVec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetVec.body: The helper clears the output vector, returns immediately if the input JSON value is null, otherwise it pushes a single string value when the JSON node is a string; if the node is not a single string it forwards the work to a more general helper that handles string arrays.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetVec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::PresetVec.body: The function constructs a static JSON helper once and then delegates the parsing of a JSON value into a `std::vector<std::string>` to that helper, returning the helper’s success status.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::SchemaHel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::SchemaHel.body: The lambda is a stateless function taking a `nullptr_t` reference, a const `Json::Value*`, and a `cmJSONState*`, and unconditionally returns `true`. It effectively acts as a no‑op callback that always reports success.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::SchemaHel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::SchemaHel.body: SchemaHelper is a thin wrapper that simply returns a lambda accepting a `std::nullptr_t` reference, a `const Json::Value*`, and a `cmJSONState*`, and unconditionally returns `true`. The returned lambda therefore performs no validation or state manipulation—it’s effectively a no‑op placeholder that will always signal success.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::TestPrese.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::TestPrese.body: The function parses a JSON array of `TestPreset` objects into the supplied `out` vector. It uses a statically‑initialised helper built by `JSONHelperBuilder` that validates the data against the `INVALID_PRESETS` error code and returns the parsing success status.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::VendorHel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::VendorHel.body: The function returns a closure that, when invoked, verifies a `Json::Value` pointer: if the pointer is null it simply returns success; if the pointer is non‑object it triggers the supplied error generator and signals failure; otherwise it reports success. The returned lambda captures the `ErrorGenerator` reference passed to `VendorHelper` and forwards the error information to that generator when a mismatch occurs.

@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::WorkflowP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePresetsGraphInternal::WorkflowP.body: The function creates a static helper that knows how to convert a JSON value into a vector of `WorkflowPreset` objects. When invoked it simply calls this helper, passing the output vector, the JSON value, and state, and returns the helper’s success flag.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::Create7ZGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::Create7ZGener.body: It allocates a new cmCPackArchiveGenerator instance pre‑configured for “7zip” format (no compression flag). The returned pointer must be released by the caller to avoid a leak.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTBZ2Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTBZ2Gen.body: The function constructs and returns a `cmCPackArchiveGenerator` instance configured for BZip2 compression, using the “paxr” parameter and emitting files with a “.tar.bz2” suffix.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTGZGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTGZGene.body: Creates a new cmCPackArchiveGenerator configured for GZip compression, using the “paxr” prefix and the “.tar.gz” suffix, and returns it as a cmCPackGenerator pointer.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTXZGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTXZGene.body: Creates and returns a new cmCPackArchiveGenerator configured to use the XZ compression format, with the file‑name suffix “.tar.xz”.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTZGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTZGener.body: Creates and returns a new archive‑generator object that is pre‑configured to write archives in the PAXR format, with the file extension “.tar.Z”.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTZSTGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateTZSTGen.body: Creates a new cmCPackArchiveGenerator instance that writes files in the “.tar.zst” format using Zstd compression, then returns that instance.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateZIPGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::CreateZIPGene.body: The function simply creates and returns a new `cmCPackArchiveGenerator` instance configured to produce ZIP‑style archives, using a “no‑compression” mode and a “.zip” file suffix.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GenerateHeade.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GenerateHeade.body: The `GenerateHeader` method is a public virtual member that simply returns the integer constant 1. It accepts a pointer to `std::ostream`, but that argument is ignored (marked unused). No other actions are performed; the method does nothing beyond returning the fixed value.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GetArchiveCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GetArchiveCom.body: The function builds the final archive file name by first checking for component‑specific options (e.g., “CPACK_ARCHIVE_<COMPONENT>_FILE_NAME”), then falling back to a generic archive name or a default package name. It calls `GetComponentPackageFileName` to create the core part of the name and appends the configured output extension before returning the full string.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GetNameOfClas.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GetNameOfClas.body: Returns a C‑string literal that identifies the class – `cmCPackArchiveGenerator`. The method is a private override that simply returns this identifier.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GetOutputExte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GetOutputExte.body: The function returns a C‑style string pointer to the class member `OutputExtension`. It’s a private virtual override that simply exposes the stored string (via `c_str()`), enabling callers to inspect the file‑extension value without copying or copying the string.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GetThreadCoun.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::GetThreadCoun.body: It returns the thread count used by the generator. The value defaults to 1 but is overridden by the options in the following order: CPACK_ARCHIVE_THREADS (if set) → CPACK_THREADS (if set). If neither option is set it keeps the default of 1.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::InitializeInt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::InitializeInt.body:
Ensures the top‑level‑directory flag is present, then pulls an optional file‑extension from the options.  
If the user has supplied a non‑empty extension it normalises the string (adding a leading dot if needed), logs the override, updates the internal output‑extension value, and finally calls the base class’s initialise routine.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::PackageCompon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::PackageCompon.body:
The routine first clears any previously‑generated package names and then iterates over the current component data.  
When grouping is enabled it creates one archive per component group, adding every component within that group to the archive; orphan components that lack a group are each packaged separately.  
If grouping is suppressed, it simply creates a single archive per component regardless of any grouping information, adding that component’s files to the archive. The function logs each step, records the created archive names, and always returns a success flag (1).

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::PackageCompon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::PackageCompon.body: The routine clears and builds the target archive name, selecting either “CPACK_ARCHIVE_FILE_NAME” or “CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME”, appends the configured output extension, and then streams every component entry into a single package via `addOneComponentToArchive`. After the loop, the archive stream automatically closes when going out of scope, and the method returns 1 to signal success.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::PackageFiles@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::PackageFiles@.body: It logs its entry, checks whether a component‑level installation is requested, and then chooses the packaging strategy—either bundle all components into one package or create a separate package per component group. If the request isn’t component‑specific, it opens the target archive, sets the working directory, iterates through each file, and adds them to the archive. On any failure it logs the error and returns 0; otherwise it returns 1 to indicate success.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::SupportsCompo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::SupportsCompo.body: The method simply returns the result of `IsOn("CPACK_ARCHIVE_COMPONENT_INSTALL")`, effectively checking whether the component‑installation flag is enabled for the current instance.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::addOneCompone.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::addOneCompone.body: This protected method adds a component’s files into a given archive. It first logs the component’s name, changes the working directory to a temporary top‑level path built from the component name, optionally prepends a package‑prefix (including an install‑prefix if it starts with “/”), then iterates over the component’s file list adding each to the archive. If any add fails it logs an error and returns 0; otherwise it returns 1 upon completion.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::cmCPackArchiv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::cmCPackArchiv.body: The constructor stores the supplied compression algorithm, archive format, and file‑extension into the instance’s members. It does no further processing—just initialises `Compress`, `ArchiveFormat`, and `OutputExtension`.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::cmCPackArchiv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::cmCPackArchiv.body: `cmCPackArchiveGenerator` is a copy‑constructor: it creates a new `cmCPackArchiveGenerator` object that inherits all internal state from an existing instance. During construction it duplicates configuration details such as archive paths, compression settings, and any buffers in use, guaranteeing the new instance is fully independent of the source object.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::operator=@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::operator=@k_Z.body: Copies the internal state of one `cmCPackArchiveGenerator` into another, ensuring the target instance mirrors the source’s configuration.

@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::~cmCPackArchi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackArchiveGenerator::~cmCPackArchi.body: This virtual destructor ensures that all resources owned by a `cmCPackArchiveGenerator` instance are released when the object is deleted. Because it is declared `override`, it satisfies the polymorphic cleanup contract defined by its base class, guaranteeing that derived implementations are correctly invoked during destruction.

@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::ConstructBundl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::ConstructBundl.body: The function gathers required options (bundle name, plist, icon), ensures they are non‑empty, then copies the provided metadata, icon and optional startup script into a staged staging directory structure, sets execute permissions on the startup script, and returns a success flag when all copies succeeded.

@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::GetPackagingIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::GetPackagingIn.body: The function constructs a string that represents the install‑prefix location by prepending a “/” to the value of the option “CPACK_BUNDLE_NAME”, appending “.app/Contents/Resources”, stores this result in the member InstallPrefix, and finally returns a C‑style pointer to that string.

@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::InitializeInte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::InitializeInte.body: The function verifies that a bundle name is supplied; if the Apple‑signing option is enabled it resolves the `codesign` tool path (or errors out if missing), stores that path under the correct option key, and finally forwards the initialization chain to its superclass.

@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::PackageFiles@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::PackageFiles@k.body: The function attempts to build and sign a bundle. It first invokes `ConstructBundle()`; if that fails it returns `0`. On success it then calls `SignBundle(toplevel)` and again aborts if that fails, returning `0`. If both stages succeed, it calls `CreateDMG(toplevel, packageFileNames[0])` and returns its result.

@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::SignBundle@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::SignBundle@k_Z.body: The function retrieves the signing certificate and, if provided, iterates over a list of files supplied by the user to code‑sign each one with the configured parameters. After signing the ancillary files it signs the main executable and finally the complete application bundle, emitting errors on any failure and returning success only when all steps complete.

@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::SupportsCompon.author: AI Short Overview
