@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::SupportsCompon.body: The `SupportsComponentInstallation` member indicates that the bundle generator does not support installing components—implementations of this virtual function simply return `false`, signalling callers that any component installation attempts should be rejected or treated as unsupported.

@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::cmCPackBundleG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::cmCPackBundleG.body: `cmCPackBundleGenerator` is a constructor that establishes the object’s internal bookkeeping for handling pack drag‑and‑drop scenarios. It performs the minimal initialization required for the generator to work: it registers the new instance with the framework’s macro system and sets up any internal structures needed for later bundle‑generation work.

@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::~cmCPackBundle.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackBundleGenerator::~cmCPackBundle.body: When an object of `cmCPackBundleGenerator` is destroyed, this destructor runs automatically. Because it’s marked `default`, the compiler supplies the standard destruction logic, handling base‑class cleanup and member destructors without any custom code. It merely ensures that all owned resources are released when the object goes out of scope.

@lcmCPackComponent::GetInstalledSize@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackComponent::GetInstalledSize@k_Z.body: The method lazily computes and caches the component’s total size. If the size is already stored in `TotalSize`, that value is returned immediately; otherwise the method iterates over the stored file list, concatenates each file name to the supplied `installDir`, retrieves each file’s length via `cmSystemTools::FileLength`, adds the result to an internal accumulator, stores the final value in `TotalSize`, and returns it.

@lcmCPackComponent::GetInstalledSizeInKb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackComponent::GetInstalledSizeInKb.body: The function returns the installed size in kilobytes by rounding up the byte count to the next full kilobyte: it adds 512 bytes (half‑kilobyte) before dividing by 1024, so any partial kilobyte is counted as a full one. It then guarantees a non‑zero answer by returning 1 when the computed value would be zero.

@lcmCPackComponentGroup::cmCPackComponen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackComponentGroup::cmCPackComponen.body: The constructor initializes a component group instance, setting its `IsBold` flag to `false` and marking that it should not be auto‑expanded (`IsExpandedByDefault` set to `false`). This establishes the default visual and interaction state for the group without performing any additional setup.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::CanGenerate@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::CanGenerate@k_ZN1.body: On macOS, it checks for a `dpkg` binary in two standard installation directories; if the binary is found it returns `true`, otherwise `false`. On all other platforms the function simply returns `true`.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::CreateGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::CreateGenerator@k.body: Creates a new instance of cmCPackDebGenerator (the type defined by the macro) and returns it.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::GetComponentInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::GetComponentInsta.body:
The method produces the suffix used when constructing the install‑directory name for a component.  

* If the global packaging policy is **ONE_PACKAGE_PER_COMPONENT** it simply returns the component’s own name.  
* If the policy is **ONE_PACKAGE** it returns a constant marker (“ALL_COMPONENTS_IN_ONE”).  
* Otherwise the code looks up an optional group name (e.g., “CPACK_COMPONENT_…_GROUP”) via `GetOption`; if that option exists its value is returned, otherwise the component name is returned.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::GetNameOfClass@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::GetNameOfClass@k_.body: The `GetNameOfClass` virtual member retrieves the class’s identifier as a string (typically via a generated macro that expands to a static `const char*` literal or a `std::string` constructed from `typeid`). It is called by code that needs run‑time type information (e.g., factories, serializers, debug logging) and relies on the macro mechanism to provide the actual name at compile time.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::GetOutputExtensio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::GetOutputExtensio.body: A protected override that supplies the literal ".deb" as the default file‑extension string for generated output files.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::InitializeInterna.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::InitializeInterna.body: The routine sets the “CPACK_PACKAGING_INSTALL_PREFIX” option to “/usr” (if it isn’t already set), then checks whether the “CPACK_SET_DESTDIR” option is turned off; if so, it assigns it the value “I_ON”. Finally, it invokes the base‑class `InitializeInternal()` to perform the remaining initialization.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::PackageComponents.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::PackageComponents.body:
The function clears the list of package file names, determines the base directory, and then iterates over the component data.  
If `ignoreGroup` is true, it packages every component individually by calling `PackageOnePack` for each component entry.  
Otherwise it packages each defined component group, and finally any orphan components (those not in a group) are each packaged separately. The return value aggregates the success bits of all those packaging calls.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::PackageComponents.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::PackageComponents.body: The function `PackageComponentsAllInOne` orchestrates packaging of all component groups into a single package. It clears any previous package name list, establishes the temporary base directory, and logs the packaging step. It builds the path for the single package file using the configured temporary directory, output file name, and any component‑specific sub‑directory. It updates the relevant configuration options (`CPACK_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY`, `CPACK_OUTPUT_FILE_NAME`, `CPACK_TEMPORARY_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME`, and optionally `CPACK_DEB_PACKAGE_COMPONENT_PART_PATH`). Finally it invokes the CMake script `CPackDeb.cmake`; on success it triggers creation of the final DEB packages via `createDebPackages()`.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::PackageFiles@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::PackageFiles@k_ZN.body: The function examines whether a component‑level installation is required. If so, it selects the appropriate packaging helper—either a single‑package helper for an “all‑in‑one” strategy or a per‑component helper otherwise—and returns the result. If a component install is not required, it falls back to a generic single‑package helper.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::PackageOnePack@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::PackageOnePack@k_.body: The method assembles a temporary directory and file path for a single Debian package component. It sets several internal options that describe the target component, its output file name, and where the component resides in the build tree. After configuring those values, it loads the specific “CPackDeb.cmake” script for that component and, if successful, hands control to the internal package‑creation routine. If any step fails, it logs an error and exits with a failure code.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::SupportsComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::SupportsComponent.body: The method simply queries an internal flag via `IsOn` and returns that boolean value. It tells whether the “CPACK_DEB_COMPONENT_INSTALL” setting is enabled in the current configuration.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::cmCPackDebGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::cmCPackDebGenerat.body: Creates a new cmCPackDebGenerator instance by copying the internal state from the supplied instance.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::cmCPackDebGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::cmCPackDebGenerat.body: This constructor sets up the internal state and buffers needed for generating packet debuffs.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::createDbgsymDDeb@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::createDbgsymDDeb@.body: The method assembles a map of package‑metadata fields (name, type, version, dependencies, etc.) based on options supplied to the generator, then constructs a DebGenerator instance with those values and the pre‑configured directories and compression settings, and finally calls generate() to create the debug‑symbol `.deb` package.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::createDeb@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::createDeb@k_ZN19c.body: The function assembles a map of Debian‑control fields (name, version, section, priority, architecture, maintainer, description, and any optional fields such as Source, Depends, Recommends, Suggests, Homepage, etc.), optionally writes a shlibs file and post‑install/remove scripts, then hands the values to a DebGenerator to produce the .deb package, returning the generator’s success flag.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::createDebPackages.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::createDebPackages.body: The lambda tries to collect files from a specified directory, logs an error if the lookup fails, and, on success, appends the new package name to the internal list before reporting success.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::createDebPackages.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::createDebPackages.body: The function orchestrates the building of Deb‑style packages from configured directories. It first defines a helper lambda that, given a source path, a logical name key, and a member‑function pointer, attempts to locate files in that path. If files are found, it invokes the supplied member function; when that function succeeds, the resulting package name is appended to a list of generated files. The routine then invokes this helper twice: once for the main package using the standard output file name, and again—conditionally based on a configuration flag and an existing directory— for a debug‑symbol package. Finally, the outcome of these two creation attempts is returned as an integer status flag.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::operator=@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::operator=@k_ZN19c.body: The assignment operator performs a deep copy of another `cmCPackDebGenerator` instance into the current object. It copies the internal state maintained by the base `cmCPackGenerator` along with any additional buffers or flags specific to the derived class. The function returns a reference to the target object to allow chaining, and it guards against self‑assignment by checking object identity before copying. The implementation also ensures that any internal resources (e.g., file handles, caches) are properly released or re‑initialised to avoid leaks or stale references.

@lcmCPackDebGenerator::~cmCPackDebGenera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDebGenerator::~cmCPackDebGenera.body: The destructor is defaulted, meaning it performs no explicit cleanup beyond the automatic destruction of its member objects and base‑class sub‑objects. It simply allows the runtime to free resources that the class’s members already manage.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::BreakLongLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::BreakLongLi.body: It walks the input string, cutting it into pieces of at most 255 characters by pulling back to the nearest preceding space; if it can’t find a space before that limit, it flags an error that a word exceeds the allowed length.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::CopyFile@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::CopyFile@k_.body: The `CopyFile` method extracts the file path strings from the provided `ostringstream` references, calls `cmSystemTools::CopyFileIfDifferent` with those paths, logs an error via `cmCPackLogger` on failure, and returns a boolean flag indicating whether the copy succeeded.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::CreateDMG@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::CreateDMG@k.body: It retrieves configuration options for the source directory and output name, prepares a staging area, optionally copies custom icons, background, and .DS_Store files, creates a temporary disk image, optionally attaches it to apply custom icon/DS_Store setups, detaches it, then converts the temporary image to the requested format with the given license information embedded, and finally writes the resulting compressed DMG file.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::CreateEmpty.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::CreateEmpty.body: The function opens a file for binary output, seeks to one byte before the requested size, writes a single zero byte, and returns whether the write succeeded (true on success, false if the stream couldn’t open). It’s a minimal‑size placeholder that makes the file as large as requested.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::CreateGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::CreateGener.body: The function produces a new instance of the drag‑and‑drop generator type, wiring its internal state for immediate use.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::EncodeLicen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::EncodeLicen.body: Iterates over the supplied strings, appending each line’s raw characters into the `dict.Data` buffer and inserts a carriage‑return character after each line and once more at the end.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::EncodeMenu@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::EncodeMenu@.body: The function serializes a list of strings into a binary dictionary format: it writes a 16‑bit count of lines (respecting the build‑time endianness flag) followed by each string prefixed with its 8‑bit length. Once serialized, the resulting data is appended to the dictionary’s internal buffer.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::GetComponen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::GetComponen.body:
The function resolves the suffix to append to a component’s installation directory name.  
If the global component‑packaging flag is set to “one package,” it simply returns the constant string “ALL_IN_ONE.”  
When the flag indicates “one package per group,” it looks up the group name from the options map for that component, concatenates it with the base package file name (using GetComponentPackageFileName), and returns that string.  
If neither of those modes applies, it checks for a component‑specific file‑name option; if present it returns that, otherwise it falls back to constructing a default suffix via GetComponentPackageFileName.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::GetNameOfCl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::GetNameOfCl.body: The function returns the name of the class this instance belongs to, typically as a string (or `const char*`) obtained via a static lookup or hard‑coded literal.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::GetOutputEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::GetOutputEx.body: It returns the literal string “.dmg”, the file‑extension tag used for the generator’s output files.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::InitializeI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::InitializeI.body:
The routine walks through a sequence of preparation steps:  

1. Collects candidate paths for helper utilities.  
2. Attempts to locate the `hdiutil`, `SetFile`, and `Rez` programs; if any are missing, logs an error and aborts.  
3. If a “SLA” directory is configured, it validates that the directory exists, that a language list is supplied, and that each language either shares a common license file or has its own license/RTF files, and that a corresponding menu file exists.  
4. On any missing file or mis‑configuration, it reports the problem and returns failure.  
5. When everything checks out, it delegates to the base class for the remainder of initialization.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::PackageFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::PackageFile.body: The function gathers all component installation directories, removes duplicates, sorts them, and then iteratively creates dmg archives for each unique directory. It returns success only after all archives have been successfully created.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::ReadFile@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::ReadFile@k_.body: It opens the requested file, iteratively reads each line, and for each line it calls `BreakLongLine` to append the split pieces into the supplied vector. If any call fails, the function returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true` after exhausting the file.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::RezDoc::Rez.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::RezDoc::Rez.body: The public `RezDoc` function takes a temporary `RezDoc` instance by rvalue reference (`RezDoc&&`) and returns a reference to that instance, facilitating efficient move‑semantics and easy chaining.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::RezDoc::Rez.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::RezDoc::Rez.body: Creates a new `RezDoc` object by copying the data from the supplied source instance.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::RezDoc::Rez.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::RezDoc::Rez.body: RezDoc() constructs and populates a RezDoc struct with the necessary metadata (e.g., id, name, type) for the subsequent drag‑and‑drop packing logic. The function typically returns a ready‑to‑use instance that other modules consume for serialisation or UI rendering.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::RunCommand@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::RunCommand@.body: Runs a system command via `cmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand`, returns `true` on success or logs an error and returns `false` when the command fails or exits non‑zero.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::SupportsCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::SupportsCom.body: This method simply returns `true`, indicating that the drag‑and‑drop generator always supports component installation.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::WriteLicens.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::WriteLicens.body:
The routine configures a license entry in the supplied `RezDoc`.  
It picks a license file – either a specified one or a default in the s‑license directory – and reads its text.  
The file’s contents are encoded into a `RezDict` and appended to the document’s license array.  
A menu entry for the same language is similarly built, either from a supplied menu file or from a default.  
If any read fails, the function reports an error and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::WriteRezArr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::WriteRezArr.body: The routine serialises a RezArray into XML: it emits a single `<key>` element containing the array’s key, then writes each `RezDict` entry inside an `<array>` container by delegating to `WriteRezDict`. It exits immediately if the array has no entries.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::WriteRezDic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::WriteRezDic.body: The routine serialises a `RezDict` into an XML fragment. It first base‑64‑encodes the dictionary’s raw data, then emits an XML `<dict>` element whose children are a sequence of `<key>`‑`<string>` or `<data>` pairs for the attributes “Attributes”, “Data”, “ID”, and “Name”.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::WriteRezXML.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::WriteRezXML.body: The method serializes a `RezDoc` instance into an XML file. It opens the target file, writes a `<plist>` root node with a `version` attribute, then creates a nested `<dict>` element populated by four arrays (`LPic`, `Menu`, `Text`, `RTF`) via `WriteRezArray`. Finally, it closes all elements and flushes the stream.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::cmCPackDrag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::cmCPackDrag.body: The constructor creates a new `cmCPackDragNDropGenerator` instance by copying the state of an existing one. It simply copies all relevant internal data from the source object into the new instance.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::cmCPackDrag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::cmCPackDrag.body: The constructor initializes a cmCPackDragNDropGenerator object with a single‑package drag‑and‑drop strategy. It sets `singleLicense` to `false` and assigns the internal `componentPackageMethod` flag to the constant `ONE_PACKAGE`. No further logic is executed at construction time.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::operator=@k.body: The assignment operator performs a deep copy of a source `cmCPackDragNDropGenerator` instance into the target object. It copies all member variables—including the internal generator state, drop‑zone configuration, and any cached drag‑drop handlers—ensuring that the receiving object is an exact replica of the source at the time of assignment. The operator returns a reference to the newly assigned object, enabling fluent chaining if desired.

@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::~cmCPackDra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackDragNDropGenerator::~cmCPackDra.body: The destructor `~cmCPackDragNDropGenerator()` is a virtual override that cleans up any resources owned by the `cmCPackDragNDropGenerator` object when it is destroyed. It guarantees that all internal data structures (e.g., drag‑and‑drop buffers, event handlers, or associated UI components) are released in a deterministic order before the object is removed from memory.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::CreateGenera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::CreateGenera.body: CreateGenerator constructs and returns a new instance of the cmCPackGenerator type. It performs the necessary setup and registration steps defined in the macro-generated code, ensuring the returned object is ready to be used immediately for packing operations.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::GetNameOfCla.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::GetNameOfCla.body: `GetNameOfClass` is a virtual member that returns the fully‑qualified name of the class instance. When called it queries the current object’s type information (via RTTI or a stored string) and emits it as a `std::string` or C‑style string. The routine is meant to be overridden by derived types so they can expose a custom identifier, especially useful when the macro `cmCPackTypeMacro(cmCPackExternalGenerator, cmCPackGenerator)` expands to a type registration routine.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::GetOutputExt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::GetOutputExt.body: Returns the literal string ".json" to indicate the file extension used for output.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InitializeIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InitializeIn.body:
It sets the internal “known‑versions” option, then loads a configuration file.  
On failure it logs an error and returns 0; otherwise it creates the appropriate generator object (based on the requested major version) and finally defers to its base class to finish the initialization.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InstallCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InstallCMake.body: The function `InstallCMakeProject` delegates to the base `cmCPackGenerator::InstallCMakeProject` when staging is enabled; otherwise it returns `1` immediately. It receives configuration parameters like destination directories, component flags, and a string reference to collect the absolute destination files.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InstallProje.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InstallProje.body: The function short‑circuits its own logic when staging is disabled: it checks `StagingEnabled()`; if true it forwards the call to the base implementation (`cmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaInstallCommands`); otherwise it simply returns `1`.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InstallProje.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InstallProje.body: Checks whether the object’s staging flag is active. If it is, it forwards the install call to the base class’s implementation; otherwise it simply returns 1 as the success code.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InstallProje.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::InstallProje.body: The function checks whether staging is enabled. If it is, it forwards the call to its base implementation (`cmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaInstalledDirectories`) passing along the destination flag, temporary directory, and default mode. If staging is not enabled, it simply returns the constant `1`, effectively signalling that no installation took place.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::PackageFiles.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::PackageFiles.body: The function builds a JSON representation of the package’s contents and writes it to a file. It first creates a JSON stream writer, then creates the root object. It calls `Generator->WriteToJSON` to populate that object. The resulting JSON is written to the file specified by `packageFileNames[0]` (or `package.json` if none is set). If an external script option (`CPACK_EXTERNAL_PACKAGE_SCRIPT`) is supplied and refers to a full path, the function reads that script’s list file to potentially add a “built packages” list to the output. The function returns `1` on success, `0` on any failure.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::RunPreinstal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::RunPreinstal.body: When staging is enabled the function forwards the call to the base class’s implementation; otherwise it simply returns the constant value 1.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::StagingEnabl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::StagingEnabl.body: The method checks the “CPACK_EXTERNAL_ENABLE_STAGING” option; if that option is not disabled (i.e., not off), it returns `true`, otherwise `false`.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::SupportsComp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::SupportsComp.body: The `SupportsComponentInstallation` method is a simple constant member that unconditionally signals that the component can be installed; its body merely returns `true`.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The `cmCPackExternalGenerator` function acts as the public constructor for the external pack generator class, accepting an rvalue reference parameter and initializing the new instance—typically setting up its internal state and any required configuration data before the object is used elsewhere in the system.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The `cmCPackExternalGenerator` constructor takes a reference to another `cmCPackExternalGenerator` instance and copies its internal data into the new object. It is a copy constructor that initializes the new instance with the state of the supplied one.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: This function constructs a new external generator object, wiring it to the base packing system so that any subsequent packing logic can invoke its specialized behaviour.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: This protected virtual method simply returns the hard‑coded major version number (currently 1). It serves as the default implementation that derived classes can override to expose their own version info.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The protected virtual member supplies the minor part of a version string. Sub‑classes override it to expose a value that matches the contract of the base class. In this concrete implementation the method returns the constant 0, signalling that no specific minor version is defined in this branch of the hierarchy.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: Accepts an rvalue reference of the same type and uses it to move‑initialize the new instance with the internal state of the supplied object.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: Creates a new instance of cmCPackExternalVersion1Generator by copying all of the internal state from the supplied object—deep‑copying the owned resources so that the new instance is an independent copy.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of the source generator into the target, correctly handling resources and ensuring a clean state after the copy.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: Assigns the contents of the right‑hand side instance to the current object, returning a reference to the object for fluent chaining.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The `~cmCPackExternalVersion1Generator` function is a public virtual entry point that the framework calls when a new external‑byte‑stream needs to be built for version 1 of the CPack format. It takes the current state objects (e.g., file descriptor, buffer, and context flags) and serialises the payload into the required header‑payload format, producing a `cmCStream` instance that downstream code can consume. The implementation is usually a thin wrapper that delegates to a protected helper which actually writes the binary stream to the output buffer.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: Retrieves an integer representing the major part of a version number; must be overridden in concrete subclasses to supply the appropriate value.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: Returns an integer that represents the minor part of the version number. The function is protected and pure virtual, so any concrete subclass must provide its own implementation that supplies the proper minor‑version value.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The `WriteToJSON` method serializes the current generator’s configuration into a JSON tree. It writes version information, various package options (name, version, description files, build config, permissions), and flags controlling install behavior. Then it populates arrays of projects, components, and groups, each with their metadata (names, directories, installation types, dependencies, and grouping relations). Finally it sets a success flag and returns `1`.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The function writes the current major and minor version numbers into the supplied JSON object and returns 1.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The constructor stores a pointer to its parent `cmCPackExternalGenerator` in the `Parent` member; no further initialization logic is performed.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: This function initializes an external‑version generator object. It accepts the necessary configuration parameters (typically a version string, a source path, and optional flags) and validates them before constructing the internal generator that will emit version identifiers for the packing process. Once constructed, the returned instance is ready to be queried or invoked by other components that need the externally‑derived version for packaging or deployment decisions.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of a `cmCPackExternalVersionGenerator` instance into the current one, performing a member‑wise copy and returning a reference to `*this`. It handles self‑assignment safely and preserves exception safety by ensuring all members are copy‑assignable.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::cmCPackExter.body: The destructor for cmCPackExternalVersionGenerator is implicitly declared as a virtual destructor with `= default`, meaning the compiler will generate a trivial body that simply destroys the member data members in the usual order. No special cleanup logic is needed.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::operator=@k_.body: The move‑assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to a `cmCPackExternalGenerator`, transfers its resources into the current instance, and returns a reference to that instance.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::operator=@k_.body: The `operator=` copies the internal state of a source `cmCPackExternalGenerator` into the target object, replacing any existing resources and returning a reference to the current instance after the assignment is complete.

@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::~cmCPackExte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackExternalGenerator::~cmCPackExte.body: The ~cmCPackExternalGenerator function is a virtual override in cmCPackExternalGenerator that builds and returns an “external‑packaging” object (typically a cmPacker instance or similar). It receives contextual input (configuration data, resource descriptors, etc.) and assembles the necessary data structures so that downstream components can consume the packaged output.

@lcmCPackGenerator::CanGenerate@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::CanGenerate@k_ZN16cm.body: A simple static bool that always returns true.

@lcmCPackGenerator::CleanTemporaryDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::CleanTemporaryDirect.body: The function first retrieves the temporary installation directory path via `GetOption`. It verifies the directory exists; if so, logs the attempt to remove it, then calls `RepeatedRemoveDirectory`. If removal fails, it logs an error and returns `0` (failure). On success or if the directory doesn't exist, it returns `1` (success).

@lcmCPackGenerator::ConfigureFile@k_ZN16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::ConfigureFile@k_ZN16.body: The function delegates the configuration task to the underlying `MakefileMap` object, passing along the source and target names and a `copyOnly` flag. It then interprets the result as a boolean success indicator: it returns `true` only when the call to `ConfigureFile` yields exactly one successful record (i.e., the returned integer equals 1).

@lcmCPackGenerator::ConfigureString@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::ConfigureString@k_ZN.body: The function simply forwards the input string and a reference to the output string to the underlying `MakefileMap::ConfigureString` method, passing two boolean flags (`true` and `false`). It then returns `true`, acting as a thin wrapper around the underlying logic.

@lcmCPackGenerator::DisplayVerboseOutput.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::DisplayVerboseOutput.body: It logs the supplied string as a verbose‑level entry using `cmCPackLogger`. The `progress` argument is unused, so the call simply forwards the message to the logger without any progress handling.

@lcmCPackGenerator::DoPackage@k_ZN16cmCP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::DoPackage@k_ZN16cmCP.body: The `DoPackage` routine orchestrates a full packaging cycle: it logs the initiation, prepares internal names and grouping rules, optionally removes an existing top‑level directory, installs the project files, discovers all files under a temporary directory, builds the package archive, optionally runs post‑build scripts, computes a checksum for the final archive(s), copies the resulting package(s) to their final destination, and finally writes a checksum file for each produced package.

@lcmCPackGenerator::FindTemplate@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::FindTemplate@k_ZN16c.body: The method logs the lookup, attempts to fetch a module file from an internal map, falls back to a default internal location if the map lookup fails, normalises slashes and verifies the file exists, and finally returns either the resolved path or an empty string if none is found.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetComponent@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetComponent@k_ZN16c.body: The routine fetches a component identified by `name`. If the component hasn’t been defined yet, it builds a new entry: it pulls configuration options prefixed with `CPACK_COMPONENT_…`, fills the component’s metadata (display name, visibility flags, archive/plist files, description, etc.), attaches it to its group, and records any declared dependencies and supported installation types. Finally it returns a pointer to that component.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetComponentGroup@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetComponentGroup@k_.body: The function retrieves or creates a component‑group for a given project. It first normalises the group name via a macro‑prefixed key, then checks the internal map; if the group does not exist it builds a new instance, fills its properties from the system options (display name, description, bold/expanded flags), and, if a parent is specified, attaches the new group to that parent’s sub‑group list. Finally it returns the constructed or existing group pointer.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetComponentInstallD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetComponentInstallD.body: The method simply returns the supplied component name unchanged, serving as the suffix appended to the base installation path for that component.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetComponentPackageF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetComponentPackageF.body: Builds the final filename by appending a suffix that can come from a plain group or component name or, if an option is set, from a corresponding display name. The function returns that combined string.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetInstallPath@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetInstallPath@k_ZN1.body:
The function lazily computes a cached installation path.  
If `InstallPath` is already non‑empty it is returned unchanged.  
Otherwise, on Windows it probes the `ProgramFiles` or `SystemDrive` environment variable, falling back to `"c:/Program Files"`. It then appends a trailing slash, the configured package name and version (separated by a hyphen).  
On a Haiku build it resolves the standard system directory via `find_directory`, defaulting to `"/boot/system"`.  
On other builds it simply returns the constant `"/usr/local/"`.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetInstallationType@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetInstallationType@.body: The function looks up an entry in an internal map keyed by the requested name. If the map already holds a `cmCPackInstallationType` for that name, it simply returns it. When no entry exists, it constructs a new `cmCPackInstallationType`: it builds a macro name prefix (“CPACK_INSTALL_TYPE_” + uppercase of the supplied name), pulls an optional display‑name string via `GetOption`, uses that if present (otherwise falling back to the name itself), assigns the new object a numeric index equal to the current size of the map, and finally returns the pointer to the freshly created type.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetInstalledFile@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetInstalledFile@k_Z.body: Retrieves a pointer to a const cmake instance that corresponds to the supplied name by consulting the internal Makefile mapping, and forwards the call to that instance’s GetInstalledFile method.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetNameOfClass@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetNameOfClass@k_ZN1.body: GetNameOfClass is a pure virtual method that returns a C‑style string identifying the class type; any concrete subclass must implement it.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetOption@k_ZNK16cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetOption@k_ZNK16cmC.body: The function queries the internal `MakefileMap` for a definition matching the supplied key and returns the resulting `cmValue`. If no entry exists, it records a debug‑level warning before returning an empty value.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetOptions@k_ZNK16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetOptions@k_ZNK16cm.body: It returns the vector of strings produced by `MakefileMap::GetDefinitions()` for the current instance.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetOutputExtension@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetOutputExtension@k.body: This protected virtual method supplies the default file‑extension string that derived classes can override. It simply returns the literal `".cpack"` and is intended to be called by code that needs the appropriate suffix when writing an output file.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetOutputPostfix@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetOutputPostfix@k_Z.body: The protected virtual method `GetOutputPostfix()` is a hook that derived classes can override to supply a string suffix (or postfix) to be appended to output when rendering a message. By defaulting to `nullptr`, the base implementation signals that no postfix is to be applied.

@lcmCPackGenerator::GetPackagingInstallP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::GetPackagingInstallP.body: The routine retrieves the current value of the `CPACK_PACKAGING_INSTALL_PREFIX` option, logs that value for debugging, and returns it as a C‑style string.

@lcmCPackGenerator::Initialize@k_ZN16cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::Initialize@k_ZN16cmC.body: Sets the makefile map and name, records them as options, optionally loads a project‑specific config file, runs an internal initialization routine, and if the packaging prefix option is still unset, assigns it a default value before returning the result (or zero if an error flag is set).

@lcmCPackGenerator::InitializeInternal@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::InitializeInternal@k.body: The `InitializeInternal()` routine is a protected virtual entry point that is intended to be overridden by derived pack‑generator classes. It performs any subclass‑specific setup that must run before the public `Initialize()` method returns success, and it reports success via its `int` return value (here hard‑coded to 1).

@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallCMakeProject:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallCMakeProject:.body: The lambda captures the current object (`this`) and forwards the supplied message and progress value to `DisplayVerboseOutput`. It is registered as the progress callback for the component `cm`.

@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallCMakeProject@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallCMakeProject@.body: The routine builds the destination path hierarchy, injects all required installation variables into a generated makefile, and finally runs the `cmake_install.cmake` script to copy files into that tree. It handles both top‑level and component‑specific installs, tracks absolute‑destination files that may be declared by downstream generators, and updates the component file lists after the copy succeeds. If any step fails, it returns 0; otherwise it returns 1.

@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProject@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProject@k_ZN1.body: The routine orchestrates the installation of a project: it clears a temporary staging area, determines the final installation prefix (appending a predefined prefix if a destination isn’t already set), creates the target directory and sets the DESTDIR environment variable, applies any default directory permissions, and then sequentially executes the install commands, scripts, and installed‑directories entries specified in the configuration. It also handles CMake‑based projects and any pre‑build scripts before returning the operation status.

@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaIns.body: The function reads the CPACK INSTALL_CMAKE_PROJECTS option, validates that a CMake generator is also defined, and then iterates over each 4‑field project entry (directory, name, component, sub‑directory). For each project it collects the relevant installation types and components (if any are defined), ensures at least one build configuration is available, and finally triggers the internal InstallCMakeProject routine for each component under each configuration. If any check fails (missing generator, insufficient list entries, etc.) the routine exits with 0; otherwise it records the successfully installed projects and returns 1.

@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaIns.body: The function sets the installation prefix environment variable, then iterates over the list of install commands specified in the configuration. For each command it runs the command, logs the command and its output, and if any command fails it records the error into a temporary log file and returns 0; if all commands succeed it returns 1.

@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaIns.body: The function reads the list of install‑scripts from the “CPACK_INSTALL_SCRIPTS” option (falling back to the single “CPACK_INSTALL_SCRIPT” value if present). For each script it logs the entry, determines whether a DESTDIR‑based prefix is required, sets the corresponding “CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX” option accordingly, updates the current binary and source directories, and finally invokes the MakefileMap reader for that script. It returns success (1) only if all scripts are processed without error.

@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::InstallProjectViaIns.body: The routine walks the list of directory/sub‑directory pairs supplied in the `CPACK_INSTALLED_DIRECTORIES` option. For each pair it recurses into the source directory tree, skips files matching any ignore patterns, and copies the remaining files into the temporary installation path. If a source file is a symlink, the target is remembered and later a new link is created in the destination tree. Any failure in copying or symlink recreation causes the function to log an error and return 0; otherwise the function returns 1 on success.

@lcmCPackGenerator::IsOn@k_ZNK16cmCPackG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::IsOn@k_ZNK16cmCPackG.body: The method accepts an option name, retrieves the corresponding option object via `GetOption(name)`, and returns the result of `cmIsOn` applied to that option—effectively reporting whether the named option is enabled.

@lcmCPackGenerator::IsSet@k_ZNK16cmCPack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::IsSet@k_ZNK16cmCPack.body: The method simply forwards the query to its `MakefileMap` member, returning `true` if the given `name` exists in that map. As a `const` function it guarantees no mutation of the instance.

@lcmCPackGenerator::IsSetToEmpty@k_ZNK16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::IsSetToEmpty@k_ZNK16.body: Queries the map for the given key and returns whether the fetched entry is empty—otherwise returns false.

@lcmCPackGenerator::IsSetToOff@k_ZNK16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::IsSetToOff@k_ZNK16cm.body: The method looks up the key in the internal map. If an entry exists, it hands the stored value to `cmIsOff` to decide if that value represents an “off” state. If the lookup yields nothing, the result defaults to `false`.

@lcmCPackGenerator::PackageFiles@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::PackageFiles@k_ZN16c.body: The `PackageFiles` function currently serves as a stub: it returns 0 immediately and performs no additional work. It is intended as a placeholder where the actual file‑packaging logic will eventually be inserted.

@lcmCPackGenerator::PrepareGroupingKind@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::PrepareGroupingKind@.body:
It examines the user‑supplied options and, based on their values, decides which component‑packaging strategy to employ.  
It first checks the legacy flags (`ALL_IN_ONE`, `IGNORE_GROUPS`, `ONE_PER_GROUP`) to pick a corresponding method; then parses the string value of `CPACK_COMPONENTS_GROUPING` to override that choice if provided.  
If the chosen method requires grouping but no groups are defined, it falls back to a component‑per‑package strategy and logs a warning. Finally, it stores the resolved strategy in `componentPackageMethod` and returns a success indicator.

@lcmCPackGenerator::PrepareNames@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::PrepareNames@k_ZN16c.body: The function builds all required path strings and option values for a package generator instance. It first verifies whether the generator supports the “CPACK_SET_DESTDIR” flag and logs a warning or error if it does not. Then it constructs the temporary directory name from the configured package directory, top‑level tag (if any), and generator name. Next, it validates mandatory options such as the package file name, output extension, and output directory, emitting errors if any are missing. It proceeds to resolve and store options for various path prefixes: output‑file prefix, top‑level directory, temporary directory, and install paths. If a package‑description file is supplied, the function reads and stores its contents. Finally, it checks the supplied checksum algorithm and sets the default flag to remove top‑level directories before finishing, returning success when all steps pass.

@lcmCPackGenerator::ReadListFile@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::ReadListFile@k_ZN16c.body: The function resolves a module’s list‑file path via `MakefileMap`, invokes `ReadListFile` on that object, and returns `true` only when the read succeeds and no global error flag has been raised during the operation.

@lcmCPackGenerator::RunPreinstallTarget@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::RunPreinstallTarget@.body: The function checks if the global generator declares a pre‑install target. If so, it builds the corresponding CMake command, runs it in the target’s directory, and streams any output to a temporary log file. On failure it records the error and exits with zero; otherwise it reports success.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetLogger@k_ZN16cmCP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetLogger@k_ZN16cmCP.body: The method assigns the supplied `cmCPackLog` pointer to the class’s internal `Logger` member. It performs a direct pointer assignment with no copying or allocation. No null‑check is performed, so callers must ensure `log` is valid. No ownership transfer semantics are declared— the object merely holds the pointer.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOption@k_ZN16cmCP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOption@k_ZN16cmCP.body: The `SetOption` method passes the supplied option name and value directly to the internal `StoreOption` routine, delegating the actual storage logic to that helper.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOption@k_ZN16cmCP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOption@k_ZN16cmCP.body: The method forwards the supplied option name and value to an internal storage routine, effectively recording the configuration for later use.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOption@k_ZN16cmCP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOption@k_ZN16cmCP.body: The method simply forwards a string‑encoded value into a `cmValue` wrapper and delegates to the underlying `SetOption` overload that expects a typed value.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOptionIfNotSet@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOptionIfNotSet@k_.body: This public method simply forwards its arguments to the internal helper `StoreOptionIfNotSet`, ensuring the option is only stored when it hasn’t already been set.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOptionIfNotSet@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOptionIfNotSet@k_.body: The method simply passes the supplied key/value pair to `StoreOptionIfNotSet`, delegating the actual check and storage logic to that internal routine.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOptionIfNotSet@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetOptionIfNotSet@k_.body: The function forwards its arguments to the overloaded `SetOptionIfNotSet` that expects a `cmValue` object; it essentially wraps the raw string value into a `cmValue` before delegating the call.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetTrace@k_ZN16cmCPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetTrace@k_ZN16cmCPa.body: The method simply updates the internal flag that governs whether tracing output is emitted during execution.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetTraceExpand@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetTraceExpand@k_ZN1.body: The method simply assigns the supplied boolean value to the internal `TraceExpand` member, toggling the trace expansion state.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SetVerbose@k_ZN16cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SetVerbose@k_ZN16cmC.body: When called, the function switches an internal flag to enable or disable verbose output. A `true` value assigns `cmSystemTools::OUTPUT_MERGE` to `GeneratorVerbose`, otherwise it assigns `cmSystemTools::OUTPUT_NONE`. This toggles the verbosity mode used by the generator.

@lcmCPackGenerator::StoreOption@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::StoreOption@k_ZN16cm.body:
This template inserts or removes a named option in an internal map.  
If `value` evaluates to *false* (zero, null, or equivalent for its type), it deletes the entry for `op` and exits; otherwise it logs the change and writes the value into the map.

@lcmCPackGenerator::StoreOptionIfNotSet@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::StoreOptionIfNotSet@.body: The template checks whether an option named `op` has already been defined in the makefile map; if it is non‑empty it simply returns, otherwise it stores the supplied value via `StoreOption`. The function thus guarantees that an option is only initialized once.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SupportsAbsoluteDest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SupportsAbsoluteDest.body: The method simply indicates that this pack‑generator implementation supports absolute destination addresses; it returns `true` and can be overridden in derived classes by marking the function virtual.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SupportsComponentIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SupportsComponentIns.body: This function is a protected virtual const member that simply returns `false`, indicating that the component does not support component installation.

@lcmCPackGenerator::SupportsSetDestdir@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::SupportsSetDestdir@k.body: The function simply reports whether the packer supports specifying a destination directory, returning the predefined constant `cmCPackGenerator::SETDESTDIR_SUPPORTED`.

@lcmCPackGenerator::WantsComponentInstal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::WantsComponentInstal.body: The function returns true when the pack is not in monolithic‑install mode, component installation is supported, and there is at least one component or component group to install.

@lcmCPackGenerator::cmCPackGenerator@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::cmCPackGenerator@k_Z.body: This constructor creates a new `cmCPackGenerator` instance by copying the internal state of another instance. It duplicates all internal resources, ensuring that the new object has its own independent state while preserving any configuration parameters from the source object.

@lcmCPackGenerator::cmCPackGenerator@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::cmCPackGenerator@k_Z.body: The constructor initializes the pack‑generator’s internal state: it clears any existing make‑file map pointer, sets the verbosity flag to “none”, initializes the logger handle to nullptr, and configures the component‑packaging rule to the default “one package per group” mode.

@lcmCPackGenerator::operator=@k_ZN16cmCP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::operator=@k_ZN16cmCP.body: The `operator=` function is the copy‑assignment operator for `cmCPackGenerator`. When invoked it copies the internal state of the source object into the current instance and returns a reference to the current object (`*this`). It performs a shallow copy of the member data that represents the packed data contents.

@lcmCPackGenerator::~cmCPackGenerator@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGenerator::~cmCPackGenerator@k_.body: The destructor simply assigns `nullptr` to the `MakefileMap` member, effectively clearing that pointer when an object of `cmCPackGenerator` is destroyed.

@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::GetGenerators.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::GetGenerators.body: GetGeneratorsList returns a const reference to the internal map of generator descriptions, providing read‑only access to that collection.

@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::NewGenerator@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::NewGenerator@.body: The function retrieves a generator factory from a map keyed by name; if found it constructs a `cmCPackGenerator`, attaches the shared logger to it, and returns the instance; otherwise it returns a null pointer.

@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::RegisterGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::RegisterGener.body: The method attaches a creation callback to a name and records its description, after guarding against a null pointer and emitting a diagnostic if registration is impossible.

@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::SetLogger@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::SetLogger@k_Z.body: This method simply stores the supplied logger pointer in the instance’s internal `Logger` member. It performs a direct assignment (`this->Logger = logger;`) without any validation or error handling. As a result, the caller must ensure that the passed pointer is valid and that the object’s state remains consistent (e.g., guarding against concurrent writes or accidental null assignments).

@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::cmCPackGenera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::cmCPackGenera.body: The function is a move‑style constructor for the `cmCPackGeneratorFactory` class. It consumes an unnamed rvalue reference to another factory object, transferring the internal state (such as configuration or context) into the new instance. The constructor then returns a fully initialized factory capable of producing individual `cmCPackGenerator` objects on demand.

@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::cmCPackGenera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::cmCPackGenera.body: The constructor copies an existing factory, cloning its internal generator registry so a new instance starts with the same set‑up of available pack generators.

@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::cmCPackGenera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackGeneratorFactory::cmCPackGenera.body: The constructor introspects each concrete generator type’s static `CanGenerate()` flag. For every generator whose condition passes, it calls `RegisterGenerator` with a string key, a human‑readable description, and the generator’s factory method. The registrations cover standard archive formats (7‑Z, ZIP, etc.), platform‑specific installers (Cygwin, Drag‑N‑Drop), and optional packaging back‑ends (RPM, FreeBSD). The factory ends once all eligible generators have been registered.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::ExpandListArgument@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::ExpandListArgument@k.body:
The routine takes a space‑separated string, turns it into a list, and then iterates over that list.  
If the count of tokens is odd, the lone token is stored with an empty value.  
Otherwise it groups every pair of tokens (key, value) and inserts them into the supplied multimap.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::GetOption@k_ZNK16cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::GetOption@k_ZNK16cmC.body: The function `GetOption` receives a `std::string` key `op`. It checks whether the internal `Generator` member is set; if so, it forwards the request to that generator’s `GetOption` method and returns the resulting value. If `Generator` is null, the function simply returns `nullptr`. The method itself is `const`, so it does not modify internal state.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsOn@k_ZNK16cmCPackI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsOn@k_ZNK16cmCPackI.body: The member returns the result of the underlying generator’s IsOn call—only if the internal `Generator` pointer is non‑null; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsSetToEmpty@k_ZNK16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsSetToEmpty@k_ZNK16.body: The function simply checks whether an internal `Generator` object is present and, if so, forwards the request to its own `IsSetToEmpty` implementation, returning that result. If `Generator` is null it safely returns `false`.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsSetToOff@k_ZNK16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsSetToOff@k_ZNK16cm.body: The method simply asks the embedded generator whether the requested operation is disabled. It returns the result of that query, or false if there is no generator attached.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsVersionEqual@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsVersionEqual@k_ZNK.body: The method verifies that the internal generator object is available; if not, it immediately returns false. When the generator exists, it delegates the actual comparison to `cmSystemTools::VersionCompare`, passing the stored framework version and the supplied version string, and returns the result of that comparison.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsVersionGreater@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsVersionGreater@k_Z.body: The function returns true only when the current framework’s version (held in `this->Generator->FrameworkVersion`) is considered greater than the supplied `version` string according to `cmSystemTools::VersionCompare` using the `OP_GREATER` comparison flag; if no generator object exists it simply returns false.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsVersionLess@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::IsVersionLess@k_ZNK1.body: It returns `true` only when the stored framework version precedes the supplied one; if the generator is missing, it immediately returns `false`. It relies on `cmSystemTools::VersionCompare` to perform the semantic comparison.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::WriteGeneratedByToSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::WriteGeneratedByToSt.body: The `WriteGeneratedByToStrim` helper builds a comment line summarizing the tool that produced the XML. If a `Generator` object is set, it writes a string such as “Generated by CPack <version> IFW generator for QtIFW <framework> tools at <timestamp>”. If the instance’s `IsVersionEqual("1.9.9")` returns true, the framework is reported as “less 2.0”; otherwise the actual framework version is used. The comment string is finally passed to the writer via `xout.Comment`.

@lcmCPackIFWCommon::cmCPackIFWCommon@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWCommon::cmCPackIFWCommon@k_Z.body: The constructor simply forwards a null pointer to its base `Generator` and performs no further initialization, leaving the object in a default‑constructed state.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::BuildBinaryCreato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::BuildBinaryCreato.body: The method constructs a list of command‑line arguments for a binary‑creation tool. It starts with the binary‑creator program name and then adds options conditioned on the object’s state—such as archive format, compression, macOS signing, top‑level resources and package directories. It also handles repository directories, online‑only mode, and package dependencies by forming comma‑separated lists. Finally it appends the target installer file (either a supplied name or a default “installer” name with a configured extension) and returns the vector of arguments.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::BuildRepogenComma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::BuildRepogenComma.body: It assembles a list of command‑line tokens for running the *repogen* tool. It starts with the tool name, then appends options conditionally: archive format and compression when the tool version is ≥ 4.2; a legacy “‑c” flag for older builds; a top‑level package and repository path; optional extra package and repo directories if specified; and an “‑i” list of downloaded packages when required. Finally it adds the target repository directory before returning the vector.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponent@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponent@k_ZN.body: The method first looks up the component in an internal map; if it isn’t found it calls the base generator to create one. Once the component is obtained it resolves the package name, checks whether a package for that name already exists, and if not it creates and configures a new package object, wiring it into the installer’s registry and marking it as downloaded or binary accordingly.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponentGroup.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponentGroup.body: This protected virtual method fetches a component group for a given project and group name. It first delegates to the base implementation; if the group is missing it returns immediately. If the group exists, the method checks whether an associated package is already in the internal map. When absent, it constructs a new package wrapper, populates its fields, configures it with the group, and records it in the internal maps and installer list. If the configuration step fails, the package entry is removed and an error is logged. The method finally returns the package‑linked component group.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponentInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponentInsta.body: The routine builds the relative path fragment used when staging a component’s package. It prefixes the “packages/” string, appends either the root package name or a component‑specific package name (determined by the class’s package‑method flag), and finally appends “/data”. It returns this composed string.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponentPacka.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponentPacka.body: When invoked, `GetComponentPackage` performs a constant‑time lookup in the `ComponentPackages` map: it searches for the supplied component key, and if found returns the corresponding package pointer; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponentPacka.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetComponentPacka.body: The routine supplies the logical name that will be used for a component’s package. It first guards against a null component and, if the component already has an explicit package via `GetComponentPackage`, returns that package’s name. Otherwise it builds a candidate name by prefixing the component’s own name in upper‑case form (“CPACK_IFW_COMPONENT_…_”). It then checks whether a custom option overrides the default; if so, that value is used; otherwise the component’s original name is kept. When the component belongs to a group, the routine may return the group’s package name directly, or, if the group rule permits sharing, it may prepend the group name to avoid duplicate names (optionally adding a dot separator). Finally the constructed string is returned as the component‑package identifier.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetGroupPackage@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetGroupPackage@k.body: The function performs a lookup in the `GroupPackages` map using the supplied `group` key. If an entry exists, it returns the corresponding `cmCPackIFWPackage` pointer; otherwise it yields `nullptr`.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetGroupPackageNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetGroupPackageNa.body: The function builds a package name for a component group: it first looks for a custom option string; if not present it uses the group’s own name. If the group belongs to a parent group, it optionally prefixes the parent’s package name (unless that prefix already appears or duplicate names are disabled).

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetOutputExtensio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetOutputExtensio.body:
Returns a pointer to the internal string storing the output file extension.  
The method simply returns `OutputExtension.c_str()` – a `const char*` that points into the existing `std::string`.  
Derived classes can override this virtual getter to supply a different extension string.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetPackagingInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetPackagingInsta.body: This protected virtual function first fetches the default install‑prefix from its base class, then—if the current instance has no components—appends a “packages/<root‑name>/data” sub‑folder to that prefix. It stores the final string under the option key `CPACK_IFW_PACKAGING_INSTALL_PREFIX` and returns the stored value.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetRepository@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetRepository@k_Z.body: The function retrieves a repository by name: it first checks the internal map; if present, returns it. If missing, it constructs a new repository entry, sets its name and generator pointer, and attempts configuration. On success, it adds the repository either to the list of remote repositories or the update queue depending on the repository’s update flag. If configuration fails, it removes the entry and logs a warning, returning a null pointer.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetRootPackageNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::GetRootPackageNam.body:
It examines the options in priority order:  
1. If the option **CPACK_IFW_PACKAGE_GROUP** is present, it instantiates a `cmCPackIFWPackage` from that group and returns the group’s name.  
2. If only **CPACK_IFW_PACKAGE_NAME** is present, it returns that value.  
3. Otherwise, it falls back to **CPACK_PACKAGE_NAME**.  
If none of those options exist, it simply returns the default string `"root"`.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::InitializeInterna.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::InitializeInterna.body: The function loads and validates the build‑time options, resolving the paths to the binary‑creator and repository‑generator tools and clearing any stale data. It then populates internal state objects with the parsed options: framework version, duplicate‑name resolution flag, additional package directories, archive format and compression level, and the installer and repository objects. Finally, it establishes the executable and output file extensions based on the target system and forwards to the base implementation to complete the initialization.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::IsOnePackage@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::IsOnePackage@k_ZN.body: Returns true when the instance’s current package configuration flag equals the ONE_PACKAGE constant; otherwise returns false.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::PackageFiles@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::PackageFiles@k_ZN.body: The function logs the start of the packaging phase, drives the installer to generate its output file and the package files, retrieves the configured top‑level directory to form a temporary output path, then invokes the internal “RunRepogen” and “RunBinaryCreator” steps. If either of those steps fails it exits early with a zero return; otherwise it reports success by returning one.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::RunBinaryCreator@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::RunBinaryCreator@.body: The method assembles a command vector from `BuildBinaryCreatorCommmand`, logs the command string, executes it through `RunSingleCommand`, and on failure writes diagnostic details into a temporary file before signaling an error. If execution succeeds, it reports success via a return value of 1; otherwise it returns 0 after logging the failure.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::RunRepogen@k_ZN19.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::RunRepogen@k_ZN19.body: The function verifies that remote repositories exist, constructs the command to invoke the *Repogen* tool, runs it while capturing stdout/stderr, logs the execution result, writes a temporary output file in case of failure, and finally reports whether the repository update succeeded.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::SupportsAbsoluteD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::SupportsAbsoluteD.body: The method signals that the generator does **not** support absolute‑destination addressing – it always returns `false`, and as a `protected virtual const` function can be overridden by subclasses to modify that behaviour.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::SupportsComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::SupportsComponent.body: The function is a protected virtual const member that simply signals the class declares that component installation is supported.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::SupportsSetDestdi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::SupportsSetDestdi.body: The `SupportsSetDestdir()` function is a protected, virtual member that simply returns the enum value `cmCPackGenerator::SETDESTDIR_SHOULD_NOT_BE_USED`. It signals that the current pack generator implementation does not permit changing the destination directory after construction. It’s a constant‑returned flag used by callers to decide whether the `setDestdir()` operation should be enabled.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::cmCPackIFWGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::cmCPackIFWGenerat.body: The constructor of `cmCPackIFWGenerator` simply sets the member `Generator` to refer to the current instance (`this`). This ensures that the `Generator` member points to the same object that owns it, allowing the class to expose its own generator functionality through that reference.

@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::~cmCPackIFWGenera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWGenerator::~cmCPackIFWGenera.body: When an object of `cmCPackIFWGenerator` is discarded, this virtual destructor automatically invokes the cleanup logic defined in the base class hierarchy. It guarantees that all owned resources—whether raw pointers, containers, or other RAII objects—are freed in the correct order without requiring any manual intervention.

@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::ConfigureFromOpti.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::ConfigureFromOpti.body: The method walks through a predefined set of option keys, retrieves any supplied value, and applies it to the installer’s configuration fields, falling back to hard‑coded defaults when a value is missing. It verifies that referenced files exist before assigning them, emits warnings for missing files, and handles version‑specific logic (e.g., wizard page list flag only for QtIFW ≥ 4.0). All other settings (icons, logos, wizard style, command‑line interface, etc.) are populated in the same manner, ensuring the installer is prepared with the appropriate defaults.

@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::GenerateInstaller.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::GenerateInstaller.body: The method builds the installer’s configuration XML and copies all referenced assets into the output directory. It first resolves any missing directory path, creates a stream to a *config.xml* file, then writes the installer’s core attributes (name, version, title, optional publisher, URLs, icons, and various UI options). Depending on the QtIFW version it emits additional elements such as wizard dimensions, menu path, maintenance tool details, and script references. Image files (logo, banner, water‑mark, background, product images) and other resources are copied to the *config/* or *resources/* sub‑folders and referenced by name only. When no resources are available the method simply skips copying them. Finally, the generated XML document is closed.

@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::GeneratePackageFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::GeneratePackageFi.body: The routine first checks whether any packages are queued. If none exist or only a single package is present, it constructs a default package, attaching the current generator and installer. It then consults a package‑group option: if a group is supplied, it configures the package from that group and sets a flag for forced installation unless an explicit override option is present; otherwise it configures from standard options. Finally, it writes out the generated package file. If multiple packages exist, the function simply iterates over the collection and calls each package’s own generation routine.

@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::cmCPackIFWInstall.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::cmCPackIFWInstall.body: The `cmCPackIFWInstaller` constructor simply creates an instance of the installer helper class. It initializes internal state, sets up required resources, and registers itself with the framework’s installation routine, leaving the rest of the installation logic to the class’s member functions.

@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::printSkippedOptio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWInstaller::printSkippedOptio.body: This protected method logs a warning indicating that a configuration option named `optionName` with the value `optionValue` will be ignored because the file it refers to does not exist, using the class’s logger at the WARNING level.

@lcmCPackIFWPackage::CompareStruct::Comp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWPackage::CompareStruct::Comp.body: The function `CompareStruct` takes two `CompareStruct` objects (via rvalue references) and returns a boolean indicating whether the two instances are equivalent in all of their member values.

@lcmCPackIFWPackage::CompareStruct::Comp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWPackage::CompareStruct::Comp.body: The function is a constructor that takes a reference to an existing `CompareStruct` object and initializes the new instance by copying the data from that source.

@lcmCPackIFWPackage::CompareStruct::Comp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWPackage::CompareStruct::Comp.body: The constructor initializes a `CompareStruct` instance by assigning the member variable `Type` the value `cmCPackIFWPackage::CompareNone`, which denotes that no comparison operation has been performed yet.

@lcmCPackIFWPackage::ConfigureFromCompon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWPackage::ConfigureFromCompon.body: The routine reads a component’s metadata and populates the package object. It restores defaults, builds a key prefix from the component name, then pulls configuration values such as version, script, user‑interface list, dependencies, licenses, and sorting priority. Flags like essential, virtual, and forced‑install are set based on component flags. Finally it invokes a prefix‑based configuration routine and returns its result.

@lcmCPackIFWPackage::ConfigureFromGroup@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCPackIFWPackage::ConfigureFromGroup@.body: The routine first resets its own configuration to defaults, then pulls the group’s name, display name, and description to populate its internal fields. It builds a prefix string for lookup options and attempts to pull a VERSION value from that prefix; failing that it falls back to a package‑wide version or a hard‑coded default. Next it pulls optional SCRIPT, USER_INTERFACES, and LICENSES values, performing a sanity check on the license list (expecting even pair count) and clearing it if malformed. It logs a warning if a deprecated PRIORITY option is found, advising use of the newer SORTING_PRIORITY. Finally, it hands off the constructed prefix to a helper that completes the full configuration from that prefix.

@lcmCPackIFWPackage::ConfigureFromGroup@.author: AI Short Overview
