@lcmCTestHandlerCommand::operator=@k_ZN2.body: The `operator=` in `cmCTestHandlerCommand` performs an in‑place copy assignment: it copies the internal command data from the right‑hand operand into the current instance, updating any relevant state members, and finally returns a reference to the object itself so that chained assignments can be performed.

@lcmCTestHandlerCommand::~cmCTestHandler.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestHandlerCommand::~cmCTestHandler.body:
`~cmCTestHandlerCommand()` is a public virtual entry point in the `cmCTestHandlerCommand` class that subclasses may override to translate incoming test‑commands into concrete handler invocations. It typically:

1. receives a parsed command object (or raw payload),
2. performs basic validity checks,
3. delegates to the appropriate internal command handler,
4. returns a status code or result object reflecting success/failure.

Because it’s virtual, concrete handlers can swap in new logic without changing the base class.

@lcmCTestLaunch::CheckResults@k_ZN13cmCT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::CheckResults@k_ZN13cmCT.body: The function first bypasses all checks if passthru mode is enabled, then immediately treats any reported error as a failure. Finally, it scans the error and output logs; if any problematic content is found it flags a failure, otherwise it deems the run successful.

@lcmCTestLaunch::HandleRealArg@k_ZN13cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::HandleRealArg@k_ZN13cmC.body: When an argument starts with ‘@’, the routine treats the rest of the string as a path to a response‑file. On Windows it opens that file, reads it line by line, parses each line as a command‑line argument, and appends each parsed token to the RealArgs vector; otherwise it just adds the original argument to RealArgs.

@lcmCTestLaunch::LoadConfig@k_ZN13cmCTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::LoadConfig@k_ZN13cmCTes.body: The function creates a `cmake` instance for the test role, clears home‑output directories, and establishes default definitions from the current snapshot. It then invokes a global generator to read the file *CTestLaunchConfig.cmake* located in the reporter’s log directory. If that file exists, the function reads it and extracts the `CTEST_SOURCE_DIRECTORY` definition, normalizing the path’s slashes before storing it in `Reporter.SourceDir`.

@lcmCTestLaunch::LoadScrapeRules@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::LoadScrapeRules@k_ZN13c.body: The method prevents re‑loading by checking a flag, sets that flag to true, and then invokes the private helper to add the two specific match rule sets (“Warning” and “WarningSuppress”) to the internal rule collection.

@lcmCTestLaunch::LoadScrapeRules@k_ZNK13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::LoadScrapeRules@k_ZNK13.body: The routine assembles a file path from the reporter’s log directory and a supplied purpose suffix, opens that file, parses each line as a regular‑expression definition, and, on successful compilation, appends the resulting expression object to the supplied vector of rules.

@lcmCTestLaunch::Main@k_ZN13cmCTestLaunc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::Main@k_ZN13cmCTestLaunc.body: The function checks whether it was invoked with exactly two command‑line arguments; if so, it prints a usage note to standard error and exits with code 1. Otherwise it creates a `cmCTestLaunch` instance with the given arguments and delegates execution to that instance’s `Run()` method, returning whatever value that method produces.

@lcmCTestLaunch::ParseArguments@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::ParseArguments@k_ZN13cm.body: The function walks through the argument list, alternately setting a flag for each recognised option (`--output`, `--source`, `--language`, `--target-name`, `--target-type`, `--build-dir`, `--filter-prefix`) and consuming the next token as the value for that option. When it encounters the separator token `--`, it records the index following it and then copies the remaining tokens into the `RealArg*` members, calling `HandleRealArg` on each. If the separator is missing, it reports an error and returns false.

@lcmCTestLaunch::Run@k_ZN13cmCTestLaunch.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::Run@k_ZN13cmCTestLaunch.body: The function first verifies that a valid `Process` object exists, then calls `RunChild()` to launch a child process. Afterward, it checks whether the child succeeded via `CheckResults()`; if not, it returns the reporter’s exit status. Finally, it loads configuration, associates the reporter’s `Process` member, writes the result to an XML file, and returns the final exit code.

@lcmCTestLaunch::RunChild@k_ZN13cmCTestL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::RunChild@k_ZN13cmCTestL.body:
The `RunChild` function orchestrates the execution of a child process.  

1. It first checks whether any real command arguments exist; if not, it exits immediately with a success exit code.  
2. If a command is present, it configures a `cmsysProcess` instance with the command string.  
3. Depending on whether passthru mode is enabled, it either attaches the child’s standard output streams to the parent’s streams or redirects them to log files opened for binary output.  
4. The function then invokes `cmsysProcess_Execute` to start the child process.  
5. While the child runs, it continuously polls for data on stdout and stderr pipes. For each piece of output received it decodes the raw bytes to text, writes the decoded data to the appropriate log file, and echoes it back to `std::cout` or `std::cerr`.  
6. Once the child terminates, the code retrieves and records the exit status in the reporter’s exit code field.

@lcmCTestLaunch::ScrapeLog@k_ZN13cmCTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::ScrapeLog@k_ZN13cmCTest.body: The function loads scrape rules, then scans a log file line by line. For each line it first skips those beginning with any configured filter prefixes; if a line matches the warning regex but does not match the suppression regex, the function returns true immediately. If no such line is found, it returns false.

@lcmCTestLaunch::cmCTestLaunch@k_ZN13cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::cmCTestLaunch@k_ZN13cmC.body: The `cmCTestLaunch` routine is an entry point for starting a test run – it creates the test harness, parses any command‑line arguments, sets up the test‑data structures, and finally dispatches the registered test cases to the execution engine. Importantly, the copy constructor is deleted (`cmCTestLaunch(const cmCTestLaunch&) = delete;`) so that instances of the launcher cannot be inadvertently duplicated, ensuring that each test run is only driven by a single, authoritative instance.

@lcmCTestLaunch::cmCTestLaunch@k_ZN13cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::cmCTestLaunch@k_ZN13cmC.body: The function `cmCTestLaunch` initializes the test‑execution context: it clears any previous process handle, parses the supplied command‑line arguments, copies the parsed arguments to a reporter object, and computes the expected output file names. It then clears flags indicating whether the rule set has been scrapped and whether any output or error streams have been produced, and finally creates a new process wrapper with `cmsysProcess_New()`.

@lcmCTestLaunch::operator=@k_ZN13cmCTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::operator=@k_ZN13cmCTest.body: When you try to assign one `cmCTestLaunch` object to another, the code will refuse because the assignment operator is declared `= delete`. This means any attempt to copy‑assign the object is a compile‑time error, preventing accidental mutation or unintended sharing of internal state.

@lcmCTestLaunch::~cmCTestLaunch@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunch::~cmCTestLaunch@k_ZN13cm.body: The destructor calls `cmsysProcess_Delete` to free the `Process` member, ensuring the associated process resources are released before the object is destroyed.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::ComputeFileName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::ComputeFileName.body: The method reads the `CTEST_LAUNCH_LOGS` environment variable; if it’s missing, it exits immediately. Otherwise it stores that directory plus a trailing slash, hashes the current working directory together with all command‑line arguments, and uses the resulting hash as a suffix to create two log file names: one ending in `‑out.txt` and the other in `‑err.txt`.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::DumpFileToXML@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::DumpFileToXML@k.body: The function opens a file for binary reading, iterates over each line, skips lines that match a filtering prefix, tags lines that match warning regexes with a prefix marker, and appends each processed line to a new XML element inserted into the provided parent element. When a line matches the warning‑suppress regex it is prefixed with “[CTest: warning suppressed] ”; when it matches the normal warning regex it is prefixed with “[CTest: warning matched] ”. The element is closed after the stream ends.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::IsError@k_ZNK21.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::IsError@k_ZNK21.body: The function simply checks whether the stored exit code is non‑zero; if so, it reports an error condition.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::LoadLabels@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::LoadLabels@k_ZN.body:
The routine first checks that a build‑directory and a target name have been supplied; if either is missing it exits immediately.  
It builds the path to the target‑specific label file (`…/CMakeFiles/<target>.dir/Labels.txt`) and then attempts to read it.  

While reading the file it skips comments and blank lines. Lines that begin with a single space are treated as label entries; the routine only records those that appear after the target’s header and, if a source filename is supplied, that follow a matching source entry. These collected label strings are inserted into the `Labels` member container for later use.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::Match@k_ZN21cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::Match@k_ZN21cmC.body: The function returns `true` as soon as one of the supplied `RegularExpression` objects matches the given line; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::MatchesFilterPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::MatchesFilterPr.body: Checks whether the supplied string starts with the stored `OptionFilterPrefix`. If that prefix is empty, the function returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true` only when the string begins with that prefix.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::SourceMatches@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::SourceMatches@k.body: Returns true when the two passed file‑path strings are identical; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXML@k_ZN21.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXML@k_ZN21.body: The method opens a file named after the current log directory and a hash, prefixes it with “error‑” or “warning‑” depending on the status, and streams a XML document. It writes a top‑level <Failure> element whose type attribute reflects the error type, then appends data about the action, command, result, and any labels.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXMLAction@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXMLAction@.body: The `WriteXMLAction` routine serialises the current action’s metadata into XML. It adds a top‑level “Action” node and, when present, emits child elements for TargetName, Language, SourceFile (with path handling for relative sources), OutputFile, and an appropriate OutputType string derived from the target type or source file status.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXMLCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXMLCommand.body: The method writes an XML fragment: it appends a comment “Details of command”, creates a “Command” node, inserts a WorkingDirectory child when a CWD is present, and then emits each string in RealArgs as an “Argument” child of that node.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXMLLabels@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXMLLabels@.body: It loads the label list, and if any labels are present it writes an XML comment “Interested parties” and then emits a `<Labels>` element containing a `<Label>` entry for each label.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXMLResult@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::WriteXMLResult@.body: The routine writes a structured XML snapshot of a command’s execution result. It attaches a comment, captures standard‑output and -error streams as child elements, and records the process’ exit status (including normal exit, timeout, or exception details).

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::cmCTestLaunchRe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::cmCTestLaunchRe.body: The deleted copy constructor forces instances of `cmCTestLaunchReporter` to be non‑copyable. Any attempt to copy a reporter (e.g., via assignment or passing it by value) triggers a compile‑time error, ensuring that only a single, uniquely‑owned instance can exist at a time.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::cmCTestLaunchRe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::cmCTestLaunchRe.body: The constructor sets initial flags (`Passthru = true`, `ExitCode = 1`), captures the current working directory, calls `ComputeFileNames()`, and registers three regular‑expression patterns in `RegexWarning` used to detect compiler warnings.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::operator=@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::operator=@k_ZN2.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents copying or reassignment of a cmCTestLaunchReporter instance, ensuring the object cannot be overwritten after construction.

@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::~cmCTestLaunchR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLaunchReporter::~cmCTestLaunchR.body: When an instance is destroyed, the code removes its LogOut and LogErr files unless the Passthru flag is set.

@lcmCTestLogWrite::cmCTestLogWrite@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestLogWrite::cmCTestLogWrite@k_ZN1.body: `cmCTestLogWrite` takes a raw data buffer and its length, then stores those values into the member fields `Data` and `Length`. It’s essentially a lightweight setter that preserves the supplied data for later use.

@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::BindArguments@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::BindArguments@.body: It calls the base class’s BindArguments implementation and then registers the DefectCount property under the key “DEFECT_COUNT” using the Bind helper.

@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::Clone@k_ZN22cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::Clone@k_ZN22cm.body: The `Clone` method creates a new `cmCTestMemCheckCommand` instance, copies the current `CTest` and `CTestScriptHandler` members into it, and returns that new command wrapped in a `std::unique_ptr<cmCommand>`.

@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::InitializeActu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::InitializeActu.body: This protected virtual method obtains the test’s memory‑check handler, calls its `Initialize()` routine, and then pulls a series of configuration values from the makefile into the test’s internal settings. It applies the retrieved values to the handler’s quiet mode and finally returns the configured handler instance.

@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::ProcessAdditio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::ProcessAdditio.body: Checks whether the defect counter list is populated and, if so, passes the current defect count from the handler into the makefile as a new definition.

@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::operator=@k_ZN.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state from another `cmCTestMemCheckCommand` instance, updating all relevant members and returning a reference to the current object.

@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::operator=@k_ZN.body: The assignment operator performs a deep copy of all internal fields from the source instance, guarding against self‑assignment, and finally returns a reference to the current object for chaining.

@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::~cmCTestMemChe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckCommand::~cmCTestMemChe.body: The function `~cmCTestMemCheckCommand()` is a virtual command implementation that scans the current process memory state, typically counting allocated blocks and detecting leaks or corruptions. It hooks into the test harness’s command system, performing the check only when invoked, and returns a diagnostic result encapsulating any anomalies discovered.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::AppendMemTeste.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::AppendMemTeste.body: The routine reads a text file containing memory‑test output and appends each line to the test result buffer. If logging is enabled it also deletes/renames the file after the contents have been read, noting the operation in the optional log.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::FindOrAddWarni.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::FindOrAddWarni.body: The function scans the existing result strings; if the supplied warning string already exists, it returns that string’s index. If it doesn’t, the function appends a zero to `GlobalResults`, pushes the warning onto both `ResultStrings` and `ResultStringsLong`, and finally returns the new string’s index.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::GenerateCTestX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::GenerateCTestX.body: The routine writes a structured XML snapshot of a test run. It first verifies that XML output is requested, then initiates the XML block for the current test case, inserting the checker’s identity and timestamps. It iterates over every test result, emitting a short path for each test file, and for each result it writes the defect details (type, count) and the captured log. Defect counts are accumulated globally and listed at the end. If output compression is enabled, the log data is compressed before being written. The XML is closed and the writer finalises the document.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::GenerateTestCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::GenerateTestCo.body: The routine assembles a command string and argument list for a memory‑checking tool. It substitutes a test‑number placeholder in each dynamic option, appends the options to the argument vector, and records any directories that require creation. It also supports passing options via an environment variable when needed and finally logs the complete command for debugging or verbosity.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::GetDefectCount.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::GetDefectCount.body: It returns the current defect count stored in the instance.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::Initialize@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::Initialize@k_Z.body:
The routine first calls the base class’s Initialize, then resets every flag, counter and container to a clean state:  
• LogWithPID → false,  
• CustomMaximumPassedTestOutputSize and CustomMaximumFailedTestOutputSize → 0,  
• MemoryTester, MemoryTesterDynamicOptions and MemoryTesterOptions are cleared,  
• MemoryTesterStyle is set to the UNKNOWN enum value,  
• MemoryTesterOutputFile is cleared, and  
• DefectCount is reset to zero.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::InitializeMemo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::InitializeMemo.body: It parses the test’s configuration to locate and configure a memory‑checker executable. It clears any previous state, determines the checker type (Valgrind, DrMemory, Purify, BoundsChecker, CUDA sanitizer or one of the sanitizer styles), sets up command‑line options and log paths, and finally prepares output vectors for result collection. The function returns false if no suitable checker or required files cannot be found.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::InitializeResu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::InitializeResu.body: The routine clears the existing result vectors, then, unless the current style flag indicates that only a minimal set of checks should be used, it fills three vectors with a predefined list of short error codes, their verbose descriptions, and an initial score of zero. The three vectors—ResultStrings, ResultStringsLong, and GlobalResults—are thus initialized to a known default state that the rest of the class can rely on.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PopulateCustom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PopulateCustom.body: Populates custom vector entries in the CTest system: registers the pre‑, post‑, and ignore‑memcheck handlers in the test runner.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PostProcessBou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PostProcessBou.body: The routine logs its start, collects the names of output files produced by the bounds‑checker, and if any exist it opens the first file, appends a special marker to the test result’s output stream while streaming each line, then pauses for a second before deleting the temporary .dpbd and .xml files that the checker generated. It also logs each removal step for debugging visibility.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PostProcessDrM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PostProcessDrM.body: The routine locates the output sub‑folder, enumerates all files matching the pattern `resfile.*`, reads each one to extract a path line, appends that information to the supplied result structure, and finally removes the temporary file that has just been consumed.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PostProcessHan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PostProcessHan.body: The virtual function triggers the custom post‑memory‑check command. If the command fails, it logs an error and returns 0; on success, it returns 1.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PostProcessTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PostProcessTes.body: The method logs the test’s result and then, based on the configured memory‑check style, either delegates to a bounds‑checker routine, a direct‑memory‑checker routine, or simply appends the resulting file outputs to the test result.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PreProcessHand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::PreProcessHand.body: PreProcessHandler first invokes InitializeMemoryChecking; if it fails the function exits immediately. If memory checking starts successfully, it runs ExecuteCommands on the CustomPreMemCheck routine. Any failure in that step results in an error log and a return of 0; a successful path returns 1.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.body: Parses the bounds‑checker output string, splits it into lines and halts at the first “BOUNDS_CHECKER_MARKER”. It feeds each non‑skipped line into a parser, tallies any parse failures into the `results` vector and tallies the defect count. It updates the internal defect counter, clears the output log only if defects were found, and returns true only when no defects were detected.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.body: The routine scans a multi‑line output string, matches each line against a set of regular‑expression patterns that identify known CUDA‑API, memory‑or‑race‑check errors, and optionally leaks. When a pattern matches it records the defect, increments a defect counter and appends a formatted warning text to the output buffer. All non‑sanitizer lines are appended after the error‑tags, and the buffer is truncated if it exceeds a predefined maximum size. The function finishes by returning **true** when no defects were encountered, otherwise **false**.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.body: The method parses a raw log string into individual lines, scans each line with several regular‑expression patterns to identify specific memory‑diagnostic patterns (e.g., “UNADDRESSABLE ACCESS”, “LEAK”), and tallies counts in a result vector indexed by enum constants. It tallies the total defect count, appends a formatted trace of the processed lines to an output log, and returns true only if no error patterns were matched.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.body: The function dispatches memory‑check output handling by inspecting the current memory‑tester style and delegating to the corresponding implementation. If the style matches one of the defined enum values (VALGRIND, DRMEMORY, PURIFY, etc.), it calls the appropriate specialized `ProcessMemCheck…Output` routine; otherwise it logs an unrecognized style and returns `true`.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.body:
Parses the input string into lines, then for each line checks against a regular‑expression pattern that extracts a code and its description.  
For each match it looks up that code in a stored list; if found it increments the corresponding result counter, appends a formatted marker to the output log, and otherwise logs an error.  
The routine finishes by returning true only when no defects were detected.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.body: The routine scans the raw sanitizer‑output text, detects known warning patterns for the current sanitizer style, and for each match it appends a formatted HTML‑styled snippet to the log string while updating a vector that tracks each warning’s occurrence count. It also increments a defect counter and returns `true` only when no defect‑hits were found (i.e., zero defects).

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::ProcessMemChec.body: It consumes a raw test‑output string, splits it into individual lines, scans each line against a list of regexes that represent different memory‑fault patterns, tallies any matches (incrementing counters for each fault type), builds a formatted log of the findings, and returns true only when no faults were detected.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::TestOutputFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::TestOutputFile.body: The routine substitutes the test number into a pre‑configured file pattern, optionally appends a wildcard if logging with PID is enabled, and then searches for files matching that pattern. If none are found it logs a warning and clears the output string; otherwise it returns the discovered file names via the supplied vector.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::cmCTestMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::cmCTestMemChec.body: The constructor accepts an rvalue reference, moves the internal state into the new instance, and sets up the memory‑check hooks that the test harness uses.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::cmCTestMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::cmCTestMemChec.body: The constructor for `cmCTestMemCheckHandler` simply copies the configuration and callback state from the supplied instance into the new handler, effectively creating a duplicate handler ready to process the same test‑level memory‑check workflow.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::cmCTestMemChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::cmCTestMemChec.body: The constructor initializes the handler with default settings: it turns on memory‑checking, starts the output size counters at zero, and turns off PID‑based logging.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::operator=@k_ZN.body: The operator= overload in cmCTestMemCheckHandler is a move‑assignment operator: it takes an rvalue reference to another cmCTestMemCheckHandler, copies the relevant internal state into the target instance, and returns a reference to the target so that the assignment can be chained.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::operator=@k_ZN.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of the source handler into the target object, returning a reference to the target (`*this`). It performs a shallow copy of the member fields, preserving the object's configuration and ensuring that the returned object can be used in further chained assignments.

@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::~cmCTestMemChe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMemCheckHandler::~cmCTestMemChe.body: The `~cmCTestMemCheckHandler()` destructor finalizes the handler: it tears down any allocated memory‑checking resources, flushes pending logs, and restores any global or per‑test state modified during the test run.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::AllResourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::AllResourc.body: Checks each allocated resource; if any resource has a non‑zero lock count it returns `false`, otherwise returns `true`.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::AllocateRe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::AllocateRe.body: The method first verifies that resource allocation is enabled. It then builds a collection of allocation requests and attempts to allocate them via a helper routine. If any allocation fails it aborts immediately. On success the routine records each allocation in its internal structures, ensuring the allocated resources for the current process are stored for later use before returning success.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckCycle.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckCycle.body: The function walks the test‑dependency graph, performs a depth‑first traversal from every node, and returns `false` if any back‑edge (cycle) is discovered; otherwise it returns `true`. If a cycle is found it emits an error message and aborts the current run.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckGener.body: The function scans all registered tests to locate a single test that declares a GENERATED_RESOURCE_SPEC_FILE. It verifies that only one such test exists, that it declares exactly one fixture, that the specified file path is absolute, and that no other test without that fixture references any resource groups. If a resource‑spec file is supplied via the command‑line option, it forbids using that file for the generator. Finally, it attempts to initialise the resource allocator and returns success only if all those conditions pass.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckResou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckResou.body: The function loops through the sorted test list (when resource specification is active), attempts to allocate resources for each test, and records any allocation‑failure errors.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckResum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckResum.body: The routine opens a temporary checkpoint file found under the test binary directory when a fail‑over flag is still active. It streams each line as an integer index, calling a helper that removes the test case at that position from the current run set. If a fail‑over flag is absent but a residual file exists, the file is deleted. The method also logs a concise header to signal that a previous test run is being resumed.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckStopO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckStopO.body: Returns the current stop‑on‑failure flag stored in the test object.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckStopT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CheckStopT.body: The function checks whether the stop time has already been marked as passed. If not, it retrieves the stop time via `CTest->GetStopTime()`; if that time is set and is not in the future (i.e., <= now), it sets the internal flag via `SetStopTimePassed()`. It then returns the flag value.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CreatePara.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CreatePara.body: The routine builds a sorted run‑queue for the next parallel test pass. It first pushes every test that failed in the previous run straight to the front of the queue. Then it iteratively climbs one dependency level at a time: it picks the current top‑level set, adds all tests that depend on that set into the next level, and removes those dependencies from the current set until no new dependencies remain. Once all levels are populated, it sorts each level in descending order of dependency depth (deepest first) by test cost via a stable sort and appends the results to the final test list, taking care to avoid re‑adding tests already sorted earlier.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CreateSeri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CreateSeri.body: The routine first gathers every test id into a temporary list, stably sorts that list using a custom comparator, and then iterates over the sorted list. For each test, it adds the test and any of its yet‑unsorted dependencies to an output list, using a set to avoid re‑inserting tests that have already been added.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CreateTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::CreateTest.body: The function checks the current parallelism level; if more than one, it delegates to a routine that builds a parallel test‑cost list, otherwise it falls back to the serial variant.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Deallocate.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Deallocate.body: The function removes all resources allocated for a given process index. It iterates through the nested maps stored in `AllocatedResources`, calls the allocator’s `DeallocateResource` for each resource type and ID, asserts the deallocation succeeded, and finally erases the entry for that index from the container.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::EraseTest@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::EraseTest@.body: The method removes an entry with key `test` from two internal containers: the map of tests and the auxiliary sorted sequence, keeping the two structures in sync. It looks up the element in the sorted list via `std::find` and erases it, guarding against a missing key by checking the iterator before calling `erase`.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::FindMaxInd.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::FindMaxInd.body: The function scans the `Tests` collection, tracking the largest value found in the first element of each pair, and returns that maximum value.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::FinishTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::FinishTest.body: The method marks the current test as finished: it stores its outcome (passed or failed), updates the internal maps that track which tests are still running, releases any resources tied to the test (including processor slots and processor affinity), and, if the test completed successfully, triggers the next test in the queue.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::GetAllTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::GetAllTest.body: The routine walks the dependency graph recursively, appending every discovered test index to the supplied list, ultimately returning a flat list of all tests that the given test depends on.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::GetName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::GetName@k_.body: The function `GetName` retrieves the `Name` field from the `Properties` array for the supplied `test` index. It returns that string directly. If `test` is out of bounds, the dereference of `Properties[test]` is undefined behaviour, potentially causing a crash or garbage value.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::GetProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::GetProcess.body:
inline size_t cmCTestMultiProcessHandler::GetProcessorsUsed(int test)  
returns the number of processor slots that the handler should employ for a specific test. It pulls the target count from the Properties array, casts it to size_t, and then limits that value to the handler’s ParallelLevel. If the desired count exceeds the available affinity and the test requires affinity, the value is capped at the available affinity. The function finally returns this clamped count.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::GetTestHan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::GetTestHan.body: Returns the current test‑handler object that the instance holds internally.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::InitResour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::InitResour.body: The function loads the resource specification from a JSON file; on success it marks the specification as usable, seeds the internal allocator with those parameters, and returns `true`; if the file cannot be read or parsed, it populates the supplied string with a descriptive failure message and returns `false`.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::LockResour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::LockResour.body: The routine pulls the range of locked resource identifiers stored in the `Properties[index]` entry and merges that collection into the instance’s `LockedResources` set. If the `RunSerial` flag for that property is set, it flips the `SerialTestRunning` flag to true for the current handler.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::MarkFinish.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::MarkFinish.body: The function deletes the temporary checkpoint file located under the CTest binary directory’s “Testing/Temporary” folder.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::OnTestLoad.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::OnTestLoad.body: OnTestLoadRetryCB is a timer‑callback that retrieves the owning handler from the timer’s data pointer and invokes StartNextTests to kick off the subsequent test sequence.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::PrintLabel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::PrintLabel.body: The `PrintLabels` method gathers every label stored in the `Properties` map into a set to remove duplicates, then emits a single “All Labels:” header if any exist, otherwise a “No Labels Exist” notice. Finally, it iterates over the sorted set and prints each label prefixed by two spaces. This routine is essentially a logging helper that shows the current label set to the console or log output.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::PrintOutpu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::PrintOutpu.body: It walks through the stored test properties, builds a JSON object that records the test set’s kind, version, and a list of individual test records (skipping any marked “NOT_AVAILABLE”), adds the back‑trace graph, and streams the finished JSON to standard output.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::PrintTestL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::PrintTestL.body: The method first checks whether the test should be emitted as JSON; if so, it delegates to `PrintOutputAsJson` and exits. Otherwise it prepares the test list by setting the highest index in the handler. It then iterates over each registered test property, constructs a `cmCTestRunTest` object, configures it with that test’s index and properties, and emits the command line that would execute that test. When a test has labels, those are printed before the test’s name. Depending on the `MemCheck` flag, it tags the test either with “Memory Check” or “Test”. Each test line is prefixed with a formatted index number padded to fit the widest index width for alignment, and any disabled tests are flagged with “(Disabled)”. Finally, after listing all tests, the function prints the total test count.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.body: The constructor creates a new `PropertiesMap` by adopting the internal map from the source instance, avoiding any element‑wise copy. This move‑style operation lets the object take ownership of the source’s property map efficiently, preserving the original state while ensuring the moved‑from instance is left in a valid, empty state for further use.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.body: The `PropertiesMap` constructor takes a reference to another `PropertiesMap` and performs a deep copy of the internal property store. It duplicates all key/value pairs so that the new object contains an identical snapshot of the original’s properties.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.body: The `PropertiesMap` helper collects the current test’s properties into a standard map, mapping each property name to its corresponding value so the test framework can query and compare expected values during test execution.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.body: This operator assigns an rvalue reference of a `PropertiesMap` to an existing map by moving its contents. It swaps the internal data of the source into the target instance, updates any bookkeeping (like size or capacity), and then returns a reference to the modified object for chaining. The move semantics avoid copying and ensure efficient reassignment.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::Properties.body: Copies the incoming map’s entries into the current object—replacing its own key‑value pairs—and then returns a reference to the modified instance.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::ReadCostDa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::ReadCostDa.body: The method opens the file returned by CTest‑>GetCostDataFile, reads it line‑by‑line until it encounters a line containing “---”. For each line it splits the line on spaces, expects at least three fields (name, previous‑run count, cost), converts the numeric parts into the appropriate types, finds the matching property entry, and writes the parsed values into that entry’s PreviousRuns and Cost fields (but only if ParallelLevel >1 and the current Cost is zero). After the first section it continues reading the rest of the file and pushes any non‑empty lines into the LastTestsFailed list. If the file is missing, malformed, or no matching property is found, the function exits early.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::RemoveTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::RemoveTest.body: It clears the test at the given index, flags it as finished, and bumps the completed‑test counter.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::RunTests@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::RunTests@k.body: The method performs a single‑pass test run: it first verifies that the handler can resume and aborts early if circular references or malformed resource specs exist. It then (conditionally) creates a signal‑hacking RAII, configures its own max‑index via `FindMaxIndex`, and uses libuv’s loop API to execute all queued tests. Once all tests finish, it validates that every test was completed, that no pending tests remain, and that all resources are still free. Finally, it marks the handler finished, records the spent cost, and returns control.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SearchByNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SearchByNa.body: SearchByName scans the Properties collection and returns the key of the first property whose Name matches the given string; if no match is found, it returns –1.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetCTest@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetCTest@k.body: Assigns the internal `CTest` member to the pointer passed in as the argument.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetParalle.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetParalle.body: It assigns the supplied level to the internal `ParallelLevel` field, but if the argument is less than 1 it replaces it with 1.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetPassFai.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetPassFai.body: The function simply assigns the provided pointer arguments to internal members, meaning the caller must guarantee the lifetime of the supplied vectors; otherwise the object may later dereference a dangling pointer. No defensive checks are performed, so passing a null pointer will leave the member dangling, and concurrent accesses could race if the vectors are modified elsewhere. To increase safety, consider taking const references, copying the vectors, or using smart pointers (e.g., `std::shared_ptr<std::vector<std::string>>`). This keeps the object decoupled from external memory and protects against inadvertent misuse.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetQuiet@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetQuiet@k.body: Assigns the value of the parameter `b` to the member variable `Quiet`. No additional logic is performed.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetRepeatM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetRepeatM.body: Sets the internal repeat configuration fields to the supplied mode and count.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetResourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetResourc.body: The method assigns the supplied filename to the internal `ResourceSpecFile` member, enabling the object to reference the specified resource‑spec file for subsequent operations.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetStopTim.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetStopTim.body: This method marks that the stop time has been reached: if the internal flag is still unset, it logs the event and switches the flag to true so subsequent executions skip the log.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetTestHan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetTestHan.body: The `SetTestHandler` member assigns the supplied `cmCTestTestHandler` pointer to the instance’s `TestHandler` member variable, essentially replacing any previous handler that was in use. This operation does not perform any validation or copying; it simply stores the pointer reference.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetTestLoa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetTestLoa.body: The `SetTestLoad` routine records a supplied load value in the instance’s `TestLoad` field. It then probes an environment variable named `"__CTEST_FAKE_LOAD_AVERAGE_FOR_TESTING"`. If that variable is present, the routine parses its content into the `FakeLoadForTesting` field; should parsing fail, it logs an error via `cmSystemTools::Error`.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetTestRes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetTestRes.body: Assigns the supplied vector of test‑results to the internal `TestResults` member.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetTests@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::SetTests@k.body: It assigns the supplied test and property maps to the handler, resets the running/finished flags for each test, and then (unless the “show‑only” flag is set) loads test‑cost data, verifies that no cyclic dependencies exist and that generated resources are valid. If either check fails it aborts the setup; otherwise it builds the list of per‑test costs.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::StartNextT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::StartNextT.body:
The routine orchestrates the launching of pending test executions.  
It first clears any pending retry timer (if the routine was re‑invoked) and exits early if there are no tests to run or a stop condition applies.  
A counter is derived from the configured concurrency level; if the current running count is below the limit it determines how many tests can be started in this cycle.  
The routine then iterates over the sorted test list, skipping any that would violate a RUN_SERIAL constraint or would exceed available processor slots.  
For each eligible test it verifies that the current system load does not exceed the configured `TestLoad` threshold; if a limit is hit the loop stops starting new tests.  
If no tests can be started, it schedules a short delay and re‑enters the routine via `TestLoadRetryTimer`.  
The function therefore balances parallelism, system load, and special serial‑only tests to dispatch tests in a controlled fashion.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::StartTest@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::StartTest@.body: The `StartTest` routine checks whether any required resources for the given test are already locked; if any are, it aborts immediately. It then attempts to allocate resources, deallocating them if allocation fails. If the test has no outstanding dependencies it proceeds to run the test; otherwise it cleans up and signals the test cannot be started at this moment.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::StartTestP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::StartTestP.body: The function coordinates the start of a test run: it first checks for processor affinity requirements and reserves the required CPU slots; if insufficient processors are available it exits. It then registers the test as running, removes the test from the pending set, and creates a test‑run object with any repeat‑mode settings and allocated resources. The routine scans for failed dependencies, locks the required resources, reports any allocation errors, and finally attempts to switch to the test’s working directory. If all preliminaries succeed, it hands the test‑run object to the test‑execution engine; otherwise it aborts with a failure notification.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestList::.body: `TestList(TestList&&)` – a move‑constructor that takes an rvalue reference to another `TestList` and initializes the new instance with the data from the source, typically delegating to the base `std::vector<int>` constructor.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestList::.body: TestList is a copy constructor that constructs a new instance by copying the contents of an existing TestList, invoking the base std::vector<int> copy constructor.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestList::.body: The `TestList()` function simply creates a new instance of the `TestList` struct, which inherits the standard `std::vector<int>` interface. It doesn’t add any special initialization logic beyond what the base `std::vector<int>` already provides—so the constructor just forwards to `std::vector<int>`’s default constructor.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::T.body: TestMap is a thin wrapper around the standard map container that maps integer keys to TestSet objects; it is employed in the multi‑process test harness to store and retrieve test configurations keyed by an integer identifier.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::T.body: The `TestMap` constructor simply forwards a source `TestMap` to the base `std::map<int, TestSet>` constructor, enabling a shallow copy of the underlying mapping. This copy constructor is used throughout the code—e.g., in `cmCTestMultiProcessHandler.h`—where `TestMap` instances need to be duplicated without altering the internal test‑set containers.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::T.body: The function `TestMap` is a unit‑test helper that exercises the mapping logic in the code base. When invoked, it runs a series of assertions against the map implementation to confirm that each input key correctly resolves to the intended value and that no unexpected side‑effects occur. In the surrounding code this helper is called from various test harnesses to validate that both the public API and any internal helpers honour the same mapping contract.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::o.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::o.body: The assignment operator overload for `TestMap` accepts an r‑value reference to another `TestMap`. It moves the contents of the right‑hand side into the left‑hand instance, then returns a reference to the current object. This provides an efficient way to transfer a `TestMap` instance without copying the whole container, relying on the underlying `std::map` move semantics.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::o.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestMap::o.body: Assigns the current map’s contents with those from the supplied `TestMap`, iterating through each key‑value pair and copying them into the current instance; it returns a reference to the modified object (i.e. `*this`).

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestSet::T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestSet::T.body: A public move constructor that initializes a new `TestSet` instance from an rvalue reference of an existing `TestSet`, ensuring the underlying `std::set<int>` contents are transferred efficiently.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestSet::T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestSet::T.body: TestSet is a copy constructor that takes an existing `TestSet` instance and creates a new instance containing the same elements. It preserves the ordering and size of the original set.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestSet::T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TestSet::T.body: TestSet initializes a set of test‑ID integers and exposes the set for downstream code. It is a thin wrapper around std::set<int> that helps the rest of the code quickly instantiate and use a collection of test identifiers.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TryAllocat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::TryAllocat.body: The function clears the passed‑in `allocations` map, walks through the `ResourceGroups` of the process at the given index, and pushes an entry for each needed resource unit into the map keyed by the resource type. It then queries the `ResourceAllocator` for each type; if the type is missing it records a `NoResourceType` error, otherwise it attempts a round‑robin allocation. On failure it records an `InsufficientResources` error. If any allocation fails it returns `false` (or sets `result` to `false`), otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::UnlockReso.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::UnlockReso.body:
UnlockResources removes all resources tied to a property at the given index from the internal collection.  
If that property is flagged to run tests serially, it clears the flag that a test is in progress.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::UpdateCost.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::UpdateCost.body: The routine reads the current cost‑data file, rewrites each entry with the in‑memory metrics (removing those that are no longer present), appends any new tests that were not previously recorded, and finally writes the list of failed tests back to the file, effectively synchronising the persistent store with the current state.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::WriteCheck.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::WriteCheck.body: The protected method opens a file named “CTestCheckpoint.txt” in the test‑output directory of the current binary directory, appends the supplied integer index followed by a newline, and then closes the stream. It relies on the custom `cmsys::ofstream` type and does not perform any error handling, locking, or path‑creation checks.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::cmCTestMul.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::cmCTestMul.body: Creates a new `cmCTestMultiProcessHandler` by copying the internal state of an existing instance (i.e., performs a copy‑constructor that duplicates the handler’s data and resource handles).

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::cmCTestMul.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::cmCTestMul.body: This constructor initializes the internal state for a multi‑process test runner: it establishes default counters for test load, completion, and running threads, clears any cycle‑or‑resource‑spec flags, records the number of CPUs available via `cmAffinity::GetProcessorsAvailable()`, and marks the handler as not yet busy. The setup is straightforward—no complex logic, simply priming the object’s fields to known starting values.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::operator=@.body: The assignment operator (`operator=`) in `cmCTestMultiProcessHandler` performs a deep copy of the source object's internal state into the current instance. It first safeguards against self‑assignment, then releases any owned resources (e.g., closing threads, freeing memory) before transferring ownership of the source’s resources. Finally, it copies primitive members and pointers (ensuring correct reference counts for shared resources) and returns a reference to `*this`. This operator allows callers to write `handler1 = handler2;` to duplicate the process‑handler configuration while ensuring proper cleanup of previous state.

@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::~cmCTestMu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestMultiProcessHandler::~cmCTestMu.body: The virtual destructor ensures that any resources held by an instance of `cmCTestMultiProcessHandler` are released properly when an object of that type—or any subclass—is destroyed, enabling subclasses to provide additional cleanup if needed.

@lcmCTestP4::GetUserData@k_ZN9cmCTestP41.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::GetUserData@k_ZN9cmCTestP41.body: Fetches a user record from the internal Users map. If the user is not already in the map, it spawns a helper process that writes the user’s record to a temporary file; after that re‑queries the map and returns either the found User object or an empty User when the lookup still fails.

@lcmCTestP4::GetWorkingRevision@k_ZN9cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::GetWorkingRevision@k_ZN9cmC.body: The GetWorkingRevision method gathers the current Perforce revision for the working copy. It builds a command vector that includes the “changes” flag, options for the local path, and a “#have” suffix to limit output to the current workspace. It runs this command via RunChild, capturing standard output and errors with dedicated parsers. If the child process fails, it returns “<unknown>”; otherwise, if the output parser returns an empty string, it returns “0”. Otherwise the parsed revision string is returned.

@lcmCTestP4::LoadModifications@k_ZN9cmCT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::LoadModifications@k_ZN9cmCT.body: The `LoadModifications` method configures a diff command, pushes its arguments (including a required “‑dn” flag and a source directory path), then spawns a child process that feeds its output to a `DiffParser` and logs errors via an `OutputLogger`. Upon completion it returns `true`.

@lcmCTestP4::LoadRevisions@k_ZN9cmCTestP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::LoadRevisions@k_ZN9cmCTestP.body: The function builds a list of revision ranges, runs the Perforce `p4 changes` command to gather the changes, parses the output into the internal list, then iterates over each change to obtain detailed logs with `p4 describe`, populating `ChangeLists`, and returns `true` if any changes were collected.

@lcmCTestP4::NoteNewRevision@k_ZN9cmCTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::NoteNewRevision@k_ZN9cmCTes.body: Updates the `NewRevision` member with the current working revision and logs the new value, then returns `true`.

@lcmCTestP4::NoteOldRevision@k_ZN9cmCTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::NoteOldRevision@k_ZN9cmCTes.body: The method records the current working revision in `OldRevision`, logs that value, stores it in `PriorRev`, and returns true.

@lcmCTestP4::SetP4Options@k_ZN9cmCTestP4.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::SetP4Options@k_ZN9cmCTestP4.body: The routine gathers the command‑line flags that should prefix a `p4` invocation. It builds a cache of options in the member `P4Options`, adding the executable path, an optional `‑c` flag with a client name if configured, the `‑L en` language switch, and any extra switches stored in the `P4Options` configuration variable. Once cached, it clears the supplied vector and copies the cached options into it, producing a ready‑to‑use vector of C‑style `char const*` arguments.

@lcmCTestP4::UpdateCustom@k_ZN9cmCTestP4.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::UpdateCustom@k_ZN9cmCTestP4.body: Wraps the supplied command string into a null‑terminated list of C‑style strings and hands that list to RunUpdateCommand, feeding it with dedicated output and error loggers while returning the command’s success status.

@lcmCTestP4::UpdateImpl@k_ZN9cmCTestP410.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::UpdateImpl@k_ZN9cmCTestP410.body: The function first attempts to fetch a custom update command string; if supplied it delegates to `UpdateCustom`. Failing that, it checks that the current revision is known – if not, it logs an error and returns false. It then builds a command‑line array populated with the “sync” option and any user‑specified options (from either “UpdateOptions” or “P4UpdateOptions”), parsing them into individual arguments. For nightly tests it appends a timestamp formatted for Perforce. Finally it appends the source path and invokes `RunUpdateCommand`, routing stdout and stderr to logger objects.

@lcmCTestP4::User::User@k_ZN9cmCTestP44U.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::User::User@k_ZN9cmCTestP44U.body: The `User(User&&)` constructor performs a move‑construction: it takes an rvalue reference of a `User` instance and transfers its internal state into the new object (e.g., moving owned resources rather than copying them).

@lcmCTestP4::User::User@k_ZN9cmCTestP44U.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::User::User@k_ZN9cmCTestP44U.body: The constructor creates a new `User` instance by copying the data from an existing `User` object passed by const reference.

@lcmCTestP4::User::User@k_ZN9cmCTestP44U.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::User::User@k_ZN9cmCTestP44U.body: The `User()` function constructs a `User` instance (defined in `cmCTestP4.h`) and returns it to callers; it’s used in the test harness to supply a standard user object for subsequent test logic.

@lcmCTestP4::cmCTestP4@k_ZN9cmCTestP4C1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::cmCTestP4@k_ZN9cmCTestP4C1E.body: The constructor of **cmCTestP4** simply initializes the object by invoking its base class constructor and sets the member `PriorRev` to the value `Unknown`.

@lcmCTestP4::cmCTestP4@k_ZN9cmCTestP4C1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::cmCTestP4@k_ZN9cmCTestP4C1E.body: The constructor copies the state of an existing `cmCTestP4` object into the new instance.

@lcmCTestP4::operator=@k_ZN9cmCTestP4aSE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::operator=@k_ZN9cmCTestP4aSE.body: Copies the data from the right‑hand side into the current object and returns a reference to the updated instance.

@lcmCTestP4::~cmCTestP4@k_ZN9cmCTestP4D1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestP4::~cmCTestP4@k_ZN9cmCTestP4D1.body: The virtual destructor `~cmCTestP4()` is defined as `=default;` in the class, meaning the compiler provides the generated cleanup logic. It is marked `override` so that it satisfies the polymorphic cleanup contract of any base class with a virtual destructor. No custom resource‑release code is needed beyond the standard destruction of members.

@lcmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand::Clone@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand::Clone@k.body: The `Clone` method creates a new instance of `cmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand`, copies the current object's `CTest` member into it, and returns that new instance wrapped in a `std::unique_ptr<cmCommand>`. It effectively performs a shallow copy of the command’s state.

@lcmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand::Initial.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand::Initial.body:
The function first ensures the argument list is non‑empty; if it isn’t, it records an error and returns `false`.  
Otherwise it iterates over each string in the list, passing that string and the internal makefile object to `ReadCustomConfigurationFileTree`.  
On finishing the loop, it returns `true`. The second parameter (`cmExecutionStatus&`) is intentionally ignored.

@lcmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand::cmCTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand::cmCTest.body: This function parses and loads user‑defined test files specified in the command‑line or configuration, registering them with the test runner for later execution.

@lcmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand::~cmCTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand::~cmCTes.body: The virtual member `~cmCTestReadCustomFilesCommand` is invoked to load user‑supplied test files into the test harness. It receives a list of file paths, opens each, parses the contents into the test framework, and stores the resulting test definitions in the internal registry. Errors during opening or parsing are reported via the command’s status flag.

@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::AllocateReso.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::AllocateReso.body: The function first verifies that the requested resource name and id exist in the internal map. It then checks that the requested number of slots does not exceed the available quota, increments the locked count if sufficient, and returns true on success (otherwise false).

@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::DeallocateRe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::DeallocateRe.body: The method looks up a resource identified by name and id in the allocator’s internal map; if it doesn’t exist or if the requested slot count exceeds what’s currently locked, it returns failure. When the conditions pass, it subtracts the requested slot amount from the current locked count and signals success.

@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::GetResources.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::GetResources.body: The function simply returns a reference to the allocator’s internal map of resources. It exposes the full mapping of resource identifiers to their corresponding Resource objects, but guarantees that callers cannot modify the underlying collection.

@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::InitializeFr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::InitializeFr.body: This function clears the current resource map and rebuilds it from a given resource specification, setting each resource’s total capacity to the capacity value in the spec and initializing its lock count to zero.

@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::Resource::Fr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::Resource::Fr.body: The function simply returns the current available amount by subtracting the locked counter from the total counter. It is a const member, so it has no side‑effects, and it returns an unsigned int value.

@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::Resource::op.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::Resource::op.body: The overload simply returns the logical negation of the equality operator, delegating to the existing `operator==` implementation and keeping the operation read‑only.

@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::Resource::op.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceAllocator::Resource::op.body: The `operator==` simply returns whether the two `Resource` objects have equal `Total` and `Locked` values.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::Pars.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::Pars.body: Parses the supplied string using a generated lexer: it allocates a scanner context, invokes the lexer to process the string, then frees the intermediate buffer and destroys the scanner before returning `true` if parsing succeeded (the lexer returned 0) or `false` otherwise.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::SetN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::SetN.body: Sets the internal `NeededSlots` field to the supplied `count` value.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::SetP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::SetP.body: The function receives an unsigned integer and simply assigns that value to the member variable `ProcessCount`. It performs no validation or side‑effects—its sole job is to update the internal counter to the supplied value. If the surrounding code runs in a multi‑threaded environment, callers must ensure that the write is safely synchronized.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::SetR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::SetR.body: Assigns the supplied string to the class’s internal `ResourceType` field.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::Writ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::Writ.body: The method iterates over the current `ProcessCount`, appends each element from the `Process` collection to the `Output` container, clears the `Process` list, and finally resets `ProcessCount` to 1.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::Writ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::Writ.body: The function appends a new entry to the `Process` container, using the current `ResourceType`, `NeededSlots`, and a fixed value of `1`.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::cmCT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::cmCT.body: This constructor creates a `cmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper` object by copying the internal data from an existing helper instance. It tokenizes the supplied resource‑group string, building a ready‑to‑use representation for later test‑configuration parsing.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::cmCT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::cmCT.body: The constructor receives a collection of requirement groups and stores them in the member variable `Output`, ready for later processing.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::cmCT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::cmCT.body: The function `cmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper()` serves as a utility that assists in parsing and organizing resource group definitions during the test configuration phase. It processes input streams (typically CMake files or test scripts), extracts and normalises group identifiers, and populates internal data structures that later drive test‑selection logic.

@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::~cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper::~cmC.body: The destructor `~cmCTestResourceGroupsLexerHelper()` simply performs the default destruction of the helper object. It performs no custom logic—just releases any owned resources following the standard RAII pattern.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_create_buffer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_create_buffer.body: The routine builds a new buffer object: it allocates a `yy_buffer_state` structure, assigns the requested size, allocates an internal character buffer (size + 2 to hold the trailing end‑markers), tags the buffer as owned (`yy_is_our_buffer = 1`), runs the generic initialization via `yy_init_buffer`, and finally returns the ready‑to‑use handle.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_delete_buffer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_delete_buffer.body: The routine releases a buffer structure: it first checks that the supplied pointer is valid, then clears the global current‑buffer reference if the buffer being freed is that current buffer, and finally frees the buffer’s internal data buffer and the buffer structure itself.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_flush_buffer@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_flush_buffer@.body: Resets the lexer’s input buffer: it zeroes out the char count, writes two sentinel end‑of‑buffer markers, and re‑initialises state flags (pos, at‑BOF, status). If the buffer is the active one, it triggers a buffer‑load routine to refill the scanner.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_init_buffer@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_init_buffer@k.body: The routine prepares a new buffer instance for a scanner run: it allocates the buffer structure, stores the given `FILE*` handle, and assigns the scanner context. It also zero‑initialises internal state flags so that subsequent parsing logic can read from a clean slate.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_init_buffer@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_init_buffer@k.body: The function clears any previously buffered input, attaches the supplied file handle to the buffer structure, and marks that a new read should begin from the start of the file. It resets the line‑and‑column counters only when switching to a different buffer, preserves the interactive flag by checking whether the file descriptor is a terminal, and finally restores the original errno value before returning.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_load_buffer_s.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_load_buffer_s.body: The function takes a scanner handle, casts it to the internal structure, and updates that structure with the current buffer’s information: it sets the character count, the buffer pointer (assigning it to both `yy_c_buf_p` and `yytext_ptr`), records the current input file in the global `yyin`, and stores the current buffer character in `yy_hold_char`.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_scan_buffer@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_scan_buffer@k.body: The routine prepares a new buffer for a scanner: it validates that the supplied data block ends with two special end‑of‑buffer markers, allocates a private state structure, copies the base pointer into its fields, and then hands that structure over to the scanner’s buffer manager so it will read from that buffer.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_scan_buffer@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_scan_buffer@k.body: Sets up the internal scanner state with the supplied buffer and length, returning a YY_BUFFER_STATE value that indicates whether the buffer was accepted for processing or rejected.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_scan_bytes@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_scan_bytes@k_.body: The function allocates a temporary buffer that is two bytes larger than the incoming byte array, copies the supplied bytes into it, appends two sentinel bytes (EOB markers), then hands the buffer over to the low‑level scan routine (`yy_scan_buffer`). If either the allocation or scan fails, a fatal error is raised. Once the scan completes, the buffer is flagged as “our” so the caller knows it must free the memory. This helper centralises the boilerplate of copying and sentinel‑terminating for any scan that expects a null‑terminated buffer, avoiding repeated allocation logic elsewhere.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_scan_string@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_scan_string@k.body: The routine forwards a C‑string and its length to the core byte‑scanning routine; it simply invokes `yy_scan_bytes` with the string’s actual size (calculated via `strlen`) and the supplied scanner.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_switch_to_buf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yy_switch_to_buf.body: The routine swaps the active buffer in a scanner context: it pushes the new buffer onto the stack, flushes any pending data from the previous buffer, updates the buffer pointers in the scanner’s state, and marks that a buffer switch has occurred so that EOF handling can proceed safely.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyalloc@k_Z29cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyalloc@k_Z29cmC.body: The function simply forwards a size request to `malloc`, casting the supplied scanner pointer to an internal structure without using it. It returns the raw pointer from `malloc` as the requested allocation.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyalloc@k_Z29cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyalloc@k_Z29cmC.body: The function allocates a memory block based on a requested size and an active scanner context, returning a pointer that callers can use for subsequent storage.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyensure_buffer_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyensure_buffer_.body: The routine guarantees that the scanner’s internal buffer‑stack exists and is big enough for the next push. On first entry it lazily allocates space for two slots (to avoid an immediate re‑allocation), zeroes the newly‑allocated array, and sets the top index to zero. When the current top index reaches the maximum size, the routine expands the allocation in blocks of eight elements, zero‑initialises the fresh slots, and updates the maximum counter. In short, it lazily allocates and grows the buffer stack on demand.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyfree@k_Z28cmCT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyfree@k_Z28cmCT.body: The routine simply frees the memory passed in `ptr`. It casts the second argument `yyscanner` to a private `struct yyguts_t*` only to satisfy the compiler’s type‑checking, then discards the value. The pointer is cast to `char*` before calling `free`, matching the signature used elsewhere in the package (e.g. in `yyrealloc`). Essentially it is a thin wrapper around `free()` that discards the auxiliary context argument.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_column@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_column@k_Z.body: The function returns the current column index if a buffer is present; otherwise it returns zero. It simply checks the `YY_CURRENT_BUFFER` macro and returns the `yycolumn` field (which should be a member of the `yguts_t` structure).

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_debug@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_debug@k_Z3.body: The function simply casts the supplied scanner pointer to its internal `struct yyguts_t` type and returns the value of the `yy_flex_debug` field from that structure.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_extra@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_extra@k_Z3.body: The function merely casts the generic `yyscan_t` argument to the internal `struct yyguts_t` used by the framework and returns the `yyextra` member that holds the caller‑supplied data stored in that structure.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_in@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_in@k_Z30cm.body: The routine interprets a scanner handle as a pointer to its private “y‑guts” structure, pulls out the embedded `FILE *` member and returns that pointer.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_leng@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_leng@k_Z32.body: The routine merely casts the supplied scanner object to a `yfguts_t` pointer and returns the field `yyleng`. It does **not** perform any validation or error handling – if `yyscanner` is `NULL` or not truly a `yfguts_t` instance the cast is undefined behaviour. Also, `yyleng` isn’t declared in the shown snippet, so in practice the function would either rely on a global of that name or compile‑time error. The function is essentially a thin wrapper around accessing a member of the internal structure.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_lineno@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_lineno@k_Z.body: It casts the supplied scanner pointer to its internal struct, checks that a buffer is present, and then returns the stored line‑number value.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_out@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_out@k_Z31c.body: The routine extracts the output buffer that is stored in the scanner’s context. It casts the passed `yyscanner` to the internal `yyguts_t` structure and returns the `yyout` field of that structure.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_text@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yyget_text@k_Z32.body: The function casts the supplied `yyscanner` handle to an internal `struct yyguts_t` pointer and returns the `yytext` member from that struct, effectively exposing the text buffer associated with the given scanner.

@lcmCTestResourceGroups_yylex@k_Z27cmCTe.author: AI Short Overview
