@lcmCommandLineArgument::ArgumentLambdaH.body: It returns a callable that, when invoked, writes the supplied string into the `value1` reference and signals success with `true`.

@lcmCommandLineArgument::cmCommandLineAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommandLineArgument::cmCommandLineAr.body: Creates a lightweight object that represents a CLI argument: it stores the argument’s name, the type of value it expects, whether a separator is required, and a callable that will be invoked with the parsed value.

@lcmCommandLineArgument::cmCommandLineAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommandLineArgument::cmCommandLineAr.body:
The template constructor creates an argument object for a command‑line parser.  
It records the argument’s name (`Name`), type (`Type`), and whether a separator is required (`SeparatorNeeded`).  
Two message objects (`InvalidSyntaxMessage` and `InvalidValueMessage`) are prepared for error reporting.  
Finally, the supplied callable (`func`) is stored in `StoreCall` for later invocation when the argument is parsed.

@lcmCommandLineArgument::cmCommandLineAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommandLineArgument::cmCommandLineAr.body: A constructor that wires up the argument’s metadata and the callback used to persist a parsed value. It stores the argument name, its type, whether a separator is required, and a function that records the value once it has been parsed. The helper messages are pre‑built for reporting syntax and value‑validation errors.

@lcmCommandLineArgument::cmCommandLineAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommandLineArgument::cmCommandLineAr.body:
The constructor takes a name, a failure‑message string, a value type, and a callable.  
It forwards the callable to the member `StoreCall`, and stores error‑messages in `InvalidSyntaxMessage` and `InvalidValueMessage`.  
The member `SeparatorNeeded` is set to `RequiresSeparator::Yes` to indicate that the argument requires a separator.

@lcmCommandLineArgument::extract_single_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommandLineArgument::extract_single_.body: The function `extract_single_value` scans a string for a value following the object’s name. It strips a leading “=” and any leading space, then returns the remaining substring. If no content follows the name it flags an error by setting `parseState` to `ValueError`; otherwise it returns the parsed value unchanged.

@lcmCommandLineArgument::matches@k_ZNK21.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommandLineArgument::matches@k_ZNK21.body: The method checks whether a supplied string matches an internally stored name. If the type flag is Zero it requires an exact equality; otherwise it first checks that the input begins with the stored name prefix. When a prefix is present it confirms that the next character is either '=' or a space before reporting a match.

@lcmCommandLineArgument::parse@k_ZNK21cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommandLineArgument::parse@k_ZNK21cm.body: The function implements a command‑argument parsing routine that validates an input string against a declared command name and argument type. It walks through the command’s argument definition (Zero, One, OneOrMore, Two, etc.), checks the incoming argument list for the expected number and format of values (including optional hyphen‑prefixed tokens for “zero or one” cases), and invokes `StoreCall` to record the parsed value(s). It tracks success via a `parseState` enum, emits syntax or value errors through `cmSystemTools::Error`, and finally returns `true` only when all required arguments were correctly extracted and stored.

@lcmCommandLineArgument::setToTrue@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommandLineArgument::setToTrue@k_ZN2.body: The function creates and returns a callable object (a `std::function`) that, when invoked, will assign the values supplied to each of the supplied arguments, effectively turning them to `true`. It forwards its parameters with perfect forwarding and relies on `ArgumentLambdaHelper` to build the lambda that performs the assignments.

@lcmCommandLineArgument::setToValue@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommandLineArgument::setToValue@k_ZN.body: The function constructs and returns a callable that, when invoked, will assign the supplied arguments to a target via the helper `ArgumentLambdaHelper`. It forwards each value using perfect forwarding and defers the actual set‑to‑value logic to the helper, keeping the implementation generic over any function signature.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::AddIncludeFla.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::AddIncludeFla.body: The `AddIncludeFlags` member is a protected pure virtual hook that concrete target‑generator implementations must supply. Its job is simply to append the appropriate `‑I`‑style include‑path flags (and any associated language‑specific switches) into the supplied `flags` string, using the `lang` argument to tailor the flag set for the current language. The base class provides no implementation; subclasses generate the specific flags for a given language and platform and push them onto the flag buffer before the final command string is built.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::AppendFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::AppendFortran.body: The routine extracts the Fortran format setting from the supplied source file, falls back to the target generator’s default if none is defined, selects the corresponding flag name according to the resolved format (fixed or free), and appends that flag definition into the supplied flag string through the local generator.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::AppendFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::AppendFortran.body: The function merges Fortran pre‑processing flags into the compilation options string. It reads the Fortran_PREPROCESS property of the source file; if the source does not specify it, it falls back to the target property. Based on the retrieved value it selects either the “PREPROCESS_ON” or “PREPROCESS_OFF” flag string. If a flag is chosen, it appends that flag’s value (from the makefile definition) to the provided flags string.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::AppendOSXVerF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::AppendOSXVerF.body: The method builds a version‑flag string by first looking up a definition named `CMAKE_<lang>_OSX_<name>_VERSION_FLAG`. If that definition is present, it retrieves the target’s major/minor/patch numbers (falling back to a default property if needed). When any component of the version is non‑zero, it formats the flag as `<def>major.minor.patch` and appends that string to the supplied flag list.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::ComputeTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::ComputeTarget.body: The function returns the path to a compiled PDB file for a target. It first aborts if the target type is beyond a simple library; otherwise it asks the target for a pre‑defined compile‑PDB path. If that path is empty, it constructs a default one: it starts with the target’s support directory, appends the configuration name when multi‑config is enabled, and finally appends the target name (plus “.pdb”) when the target is a static library. The resulting string is returned.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GenerateCodeC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GenerateCodeC.body: `GenerateCodeCheckRules` builds a shell command string that runs the C/C++ source file through a series of checks (tidy, iwyu, cpplint, cppcheck). It collects each check’s executable path from the generator’s property store, escapes them for the shell, and then appends them to the base command (`cmakeCmd`). If a custom launcher is present, it is added via `--launcher`. Finally, the composed string is returned.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetAIXExports.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetAIXExports.body: The routine queries whether the current target is an AIX build. If that test succeeds, it inspects the target’s “AIX_EXPORT_ALL_SYMBOLS” property. When that property is explicitly set to *off* (as determined by `cmIsOff`), the function assigns the string “‑n” to the output buffer; otherwise the buffer remains empty. The string is then returned.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetClangTidyR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetClangTidyR.body: The protected, pure‑virtual member `GetClangTidyReplacementsFilePath` returns the filesystem path where clang‑tidy expects to write its temporary replacement‑tracking file. Derived target‑generator classes override this method to compute a concrete location—often derived from the build configuration or target‑specific directories—so the base class can invoke it without knowing the concrete path. The returned string is then used by the implementation of `cmCommonTargetGenerator` when creating the fix‑up file for clang‑tidy processing.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetCompilerLa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetCompilerLa.body: The function checks whether the requested language is one of the supported compilers, looks up the corresponding property that holds the compiler launcher expression, evaluates that expression in the context of the current target, and returns the resolved string. If no valid launcher is found, it returns an empty string.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetConfigName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetConfigName.body: The method gives read‑only access to the stored list of configuration names by returning a const reference to the internal `ConfigNames` vector; callers can read the contents but cannot modify them.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetDefines@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetDefines@k_.body: Retrieves the pre‑built string for the requested language‑config pair, generating and caching it with the local generator only if it does not already exist, and then returns that cached value.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetFeature@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetFeature@k_.body: It forwards the supplied feature and configuration strings to the underlying `GeneratorTarget` instance and returns the value that target produces.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetFlags@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetFlags@k_ZN.body: The function retrieves or lazily builds a compile‑flags string for a requested language. It indexes a per‑config‑arch map; if the flags for the language are missing, it delegates to the local generator to generate them, stores the result in the map, and returns the flags string.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetIncludes@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetIncludes@k.body: The method fetches a cached include string for a given language‑config pair; if none exists it builds the string via `AddIncludeFlags`, stores it in the per‑config map, and returns it.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetLinkedTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetLinkedTarg.body: The routine walks through the link‑information of the current target, adding qualifying linked targets to either a *forward* or *direct* list. It filters out targets that are imported, import‑only, non‑synthetic, or of the wrong language; it also skips INTERFACE_LIBRARY entries that have already been processed. When the build is a multi‑config setup it appends the config name to each directory path. The result is a `LinkedTargetDirs` struct whose `Forward` and `Direct` vectors contain the paths of the linked targets that should be linked forward‑ or directly.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetLinkerLaun.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetLinkerLaun.body: This function retrieves a linker launcher command string from the generator’s configuration, evaluates any expression property that defines it, normalises the resulting argument list into shell‑escaped form, and returns the assembled command line (or an empty string if no launcher is defined).

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetManifests@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetManifests@.body: Collects the list of manifest source files from the generator target, converts each path into the required shell format through the local conversion helper and prefixes them with a language‑specific linker flag obtained from the Makefile definition, and finally concatenates the resulting flags into a single space‑separated string returned to the caller.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::HaveRequiredL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::HaveRequiredL.body: The function scans the supplied list of source files, records every distinct language used by those files, and then ensures each of those languages is enabled in the current build state. If any required language is disabled, it emits a fatal‑error message and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::LinkedTargetD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::LinkedTargetD.body: LinkedTargetDirs is a public move constructor that takes an rvalue reference to a temporary instance and transfers ownership of internal directory data to the new object. It is employed in the code to initialize or reinitialize a target‑directory structure from an existing instance.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::LinkedTargetD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::LinkedTargetD.body: LinkedTargetDirs is a constructor that creates a new instance by copying the contents of an existing LinkedTargetDirs object, initializing the new object with the same linked‑target directory data.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::LinkedTargetD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::LinkedTargetD.body:
LinkedTargetDirs returns a list of directory paths that are linked targets.  
Its primary job is to discover and return directories that match a given target name or pattern, ensuring each returned path actually exists on disk.  
When used in `cmCommonTargetGenerator.h`, it supplies a quick lookup of sub‑directory targets for later build steps.  
Key edge cases:  
* If a target name contains no matching directories, the function returns an empty list.  
* If a directory appears multiple times in the search tree, duplicates will still be returned unless dedup logic is added.  
* Beware circular references: an overly‑deep link chain can cause stack over‑runs or excessive recursion.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::cmCommonTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::cmCommonTarge.body: The constructor initializes a `cmCommonTargetGenerator` by establishing its base `GeneratorTarget`, recording its owning makefile, and storing pointers to the local and global common generators tied to the supplied `cmGeneratorTarget`. It also retrieves the list of configuration names from the local generator for later use.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::cmCommonTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::cmCommonTarge.body: The constructor copies an existing `cmCommonTargetGenerator` instance, cloning its internal state (including any target‑specific data) into the new object so that the new generator is fully initialized without needing separate member‑by‑member assignments.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::operator=@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::operator=@k_Z.body: The `operator=` overload performs a deep copy of another `cmCommonTargetGenerator` instance into the current one. It assigns all internal member values from the source object and returns `*this`, allowing assignment chaining while handling self‑assignment safely.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::~cmCommonTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::~cmCommonTarg.body: The virtual destructor `~cmCommonTargetGenerator` is responsible for cleaning up any resources tied to the class. It is marked `virtual` so that derived classes can override or extend its cleanup logic, while the source file supplies a defaulted destructor (`= default`) that relies on the compiler to generate the standard destruction sequence.

@lcmCompareTargets::cmCompareTargets@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompareTargets::cmCompareTargets@k_Z.body: cmCompareTargets is a public function that takes two cmCompareTargets objects (typically via an rvalue reference) and compares them. It performs the comparison logic required by the surrounding code base and returns a result indicating whether the two targets are equivalent or which one precedes the other.

@lcmCompareTargets::cmCompareTargets@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompareTargets::cmCompareTargets@k_Z.body: `cmCompareTargets` is a public helper that takes two target descriptors and returns whether they represent the same logical target. It does a shallow structural comparison of the identifying fields (e.g., target name, architecture, and any custom flags) and then falls back on a deep comparison of any embedded configuration objects. The routine is used throughout the project wherever a target needs to be checked for equivalence – for instance‑reuse checks in code‑gen or duplicate‑resource avoidance. The implementation is intentionally simple: it returns `true` only when every comparable field is equal, otherwise `false`; this keeps the comparison O(1) in practice and avoids costly re‑parsing of target metadata.

@lcmCompareTargets::cmCompareTargets@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompareTargets::cmCompareTargets@k_Z.body: cmCompareTargets is a public helper that accepts two target identifiers (e.g., target IDs or target descriptors) and determines whether they are considered equivalent for the current code‑generation context. Internally it applies the same comparison logic that is reused in several places in the codebase—for instance, it is invoked around line 1338 of cmGlobalXCodeGenerator.cxx and elsewhere in the generation workflow. The function returns a boolean flag: true when the two targets match under the current rules, false otherwise.

@lcmCompareTargets::operator()@k_ZNK16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompareTargets::operator()@k_ZNK16cm.body: The operator returns `true` if the left operand’s target name is `"ALL_BUILD"`, returns `false` if only the right operand’s target name is `"ALL_BUILD"`, otherwise it performs a lexical comparison of the target names (`a < b`).

@lcmCompareTargets::~cmCompareTargets@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompareTargets::~cmCompareTargets@k_.body: `~cmCompareTargets()` checks whether two target objects are equivalent. It walks through each field defined in `cmCompareTargets`, performing field‑by‑field comparisons (e.g., identifiers, types, flags) and returns a boolean indicating full equality. The routine is used throughout the system wherever target objects must be validated against one another, such as in the global X‑code generator at line 1338.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::Evaluat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::Evaluat.body: The function constructs a context from the supplied arguments and then forwards that context and the DAG checker to `EvaluateWithContext`, returning the string reference produced by that helper.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::Evaluat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::Evaluat.body: If evaluation is required, the method clears any previous output, iterates over each evaluator invoking its Evaluate method (passing the current context and a DAG checker), appending the returned string to the output buffer. It tracks seen target properties, aborts on the first error encountered, and finally updates internal flags for language‑sensitive conditions and dependency lists before returning the built string.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetAllT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetAllT.body: The function simply returns a read‑only reference to the `AllTargetsSeen` member—a `std::set` of pointers to `cmGeneratorTarget` objects. It is a `const` member, so callers cannot alter the set; the returned reference is immutable and does not create a copy.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetBack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetBack.body: It returns the stored back‑trace list so callers can inspect the current sequence of file‑access calls.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadC.body: This method returns the current state of the `HadContextSensitiveCondition` flag, indicating whether a context‑sensitive condition has been set.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadH.body: Returns the `HadHeadSensitiveCondition` flag, indicating whether a head‑sensitive condition has been met.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadL.body: Returns the value stored in the `HadLinkLanguageSensitiveCondition` member.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetInpu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetInpu.body: Returns a const reference to the internally stored string, letting callers read the value without copying or mutating it.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetMaxL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetMaxL.body: The function looks up the provided target in the internal `MaxLanguageStandard` map. If an entry exists, it copies that entry’s value into the supplied `mapping` variable. If the key isn’t found, the mapping stays unchanged.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetSeen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetSeen.body: The method simply returns a read‑only reference to the internal `SeenTargetProperties` set, allowing callers to inspect which property identifiers have been recorded without exposing the set to modification.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetSour.body: It returns the const member `SourceSensitiveTargets`, a `std::set` of pointers to `cmGeneratorTarget`.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetTarg.body: The `GetTargets()` member simply returns the stored `DependTargets` set – a const reference to the `std::set<cmGeneratorTarget*>` that holds the current target collection.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::SetEval.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::SetEval.body: Assigns the internal `EvaluateForBuildsystem` flag to the supplied boolean, potentially affecting subsequent build‑system evaluation decisions.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::SetQuie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::SetQuie.body: Updates the internal quiet flag to the supplied boolean value.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::cmCompi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::cmCompi.body: The constructor records a back‑trace and the raw input string, creates a profiling RAII entry for the “genex_compile” phase, tokenizes the input with a lexer, sets a flag if the lexer detected any generator expressions, and when that flag is true, parses the token stream to build the list of evaluators.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::cmCompi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::cmCompi.body:
The constructor `cmCompiledGeneratorExpression(cmCompiledGeneratorExpression const&) = delete;` disables copying of instances.  
This prevents accidental duplication of the internal state held by a compiled generator expression, ensuring that only explicit construction (e.g., through factory functions or move semantics) can create a new object.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::operato.body: The `operator=` function copies the internal expression tree from another `cmCompiledGeneratorExpression` into the current instance, updating its internal state, and returns a reference to the modified object.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::~cmComp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::~cmComp.body: The destructor `~cmCompiledGeneratorExpression()` is defined as default; it automatically releases all resources owned by the instance, leaving no lingering state.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::Compute@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::Compute@k_ZN2.body: `Compute()` orchestrates the construction of a component graph for the current data structure. It first runs the Tarjan algorithm to discover strongly‑connected components, then resizes the internal vector to match the number of components found, and finally populates that vector by invoking `TransferEdges()` to wire the component graph.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::GetComponentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::GetComponentG.body: Returns a const reference to the internal graph, enabling callers to inspect the component graph without permitting modification.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::Tarjan@k_ZN23.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::Tarjan@k_ZN23.body: It sets up the auxiliary structures and then walks the graph once: it resizes the entry and component arrays to the graph’s size, clears the stack, and performs a depth‑first traversal from each vertex that hasn’t yet been visited, pushing and popping nodes as it recurses.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TarjanVisit@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TarjanVisit@k.body: TarjanVisit performs a depth‑first traversal from node i, marking it visited, pushing it onto an internal stack, and updating the lowest‑indexed ancestor reachable from that node. While recursing over each outgoing edge it propagates the current “root” identifier upward whenever a back‑edge is found, and upon unwinding it flushes the stack to extract a new strongly connected component. After a component is completed it is appended to the component list and sorted for deterministic ordering.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TransferEdges.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TransferEdges.body: The routine scans every adjacency list in the input graph. For each edge it checks the Tarjan component IDs of the incident vertices. If the two vertices belong to different components, it appends a corresponding entry into the component graph’s adjacency list—preserving the edge’s strong, cross, and back‑trace flags. No deduplication logic is performed; every inter‑component edge is simply forwarded to the component graph.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::cmComputeComp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::cmComputeComp.body: Initializes the instance with the provided graph.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::~cmComputeCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::~cmComputeCom.body: The destructor for `cmComputeComponentGraph` is responsible for cleaning up the internal graph data structures created by the component graph builder. It releases any dynamically allocated nodes, edges, or auxiliary data structures and ensures that all internal resources are properly freed before the object is destroyed, preventing memory leaks.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddDirectLinkEnt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddDirectLinkEnt.body: The routine stitches together all the static and language‑specific link libraries that belong to the current target. It first obtains the link implementation structure for this build configuration, then injects the default library list and object files into the dependency graph. Next, for every supported language it pulls in any language‑runtime entries that are present in the implementation’s lookup table, adding them to the graph. Finally, it iterates over any “wrong‑config” libraries and performs a sanity check for each.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddLinkEntries@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddLinkEntries@k.body: It walks through each library entry for a target, parses any feature or group markers that may appear in the entry string, records the features applied to each entry, issues warnings when an undefined feature is referenced, and updates the internal structures that track inferred dependencies and ordering constraints among link items.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddLinkEntry@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddLinkEntry@k_Z.body:
The routine allocates a slot for the supplied link item, skips re‑processing if the item is already present, then stores the item, target and inferred kind (flag, group or normal) in the entry list.  
If the entry has a target it enqueues a `BFSEntry` for later processing; otherwise it looks up an old‑style `…_LIB_DEPENDS` definition and, if found, enqueues that; if not known it marks the dependency set as inferred. The function finally returns the new entry’s index and a flag indicating the entry was freshly added.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddLinkObject@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddLinkObject@k_.body: Confirms the item is not a target, allocates a slot via `AllocateLinkEntry`, and if that slot is new, it populates it with the item’s string, backtrace, kind `Object`, its source, and records the index in `ObjectEntries`.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddLinkObjects@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddLinkObjects@k.body: The function receives a vector of link items and forwards each one to the class’s `AddLinkObject` method, effectively enqueueing them for later processing.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddVarLinkEntrie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AddVarLinkEntrie.body: The function parses a semicolon‑separated list of link items, determines each item's link type (explicit “debug”, “optimized”, or “general”, or via a _LINK_TYPE variable), verifies that the item is allowed for the current link type or configuration, resolves the item to a library reference via ResolveLinkItem, and finally appends it to the target’s link list via AddLinkEntries.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AllocateLinkEntr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::AllocateLinkEntr.body: The function adds a new link item to the internal data structures. It creates an `index_entry` from the given `item` and the current size of `EntryList`, inserts that entry into `LinkEntryIndex`, and if the insertion succeeds (the key was not already present), it appends default‑initialised elements to `EntryList`, `InferredDependSets`, and `EntryConstraintGraph`. It finally returns the iterator to the inserted element and a flag indicating whether a new element was inserted.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::CheckCircularDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::CheckCircularDep.body: The function scans the dependency graph component‑by‑component. For each component that contains at least one group entry, it determines whether that group entry participates in a cycle of dependencies. If any such cycle is found, it constructs a human‑readable description of the involved entries and their inter‑relations and emits a fatal error message, then returns `false`. If no cycles are detected across all components, it returns `true`.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::CheckWrongConfig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::CheckWrongConfig.body: When called during a dependency pass, the routine first checks if the legacy “old‑link‑dir” flag is still active. If it’s disabled it exits immediately. Otherwise it examines the link item in question: if the item’s target exists and is not an imported target, the target is added to a set of “wrong‑config” items. In other words, it flags any non‑import target that would be linked into a configuration that mistakenly uses its output directory as a link directory, marking it for special handling later.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::CleanConstraintG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::CleanConstraintG.body: The function iterates over each edge list in `EntryConstraintGraph`, sorts the list in place to keep the relative order as close to the original insertion order as possible, and then removes consecutive duplicate edges using `std::unique` followed by `erase`.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::Compute@k_ZN20cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::Compute@k_ZN20cm.body: The routine starts by enqueueing direct links and then performs a breadth‑first walk through the dependency graph, filling in any implicit edges. After that, it pulls in shared‑library dependencies, infers missing edges, and prunes raw items into their group wrappers. The routine then prunes the constraint graph, builds the component graph (ensuring no cycles), orders the final link sequence, removes duplicate shared‑library entries, and finally expands group entries before returning the ordered list.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::ComputeComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::ComputeComponent.body: The routine scans the supplied node list, checks each node’s target for a link interface, and keeps the highest multiplicity seen. It starts with a default of 2 and finally returns that maximum value.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::DisplayComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::DisplayComponent.body: The routine walks the component graph, emitting each component’s index, its constituent node IDs, the edges leaving it, and the component’s topological index. It pulls the component list from the graph, iterates over each node in that list printing its value, then lists the outgoing edges to the next component, before printing the stored component‑order index.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::DisplayConstrain.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::DisplayConstrain.body: This routine walks through the stored constraint graph, serialises each node and its outgoing edges into a text buffer, and finally emits that buffer to standard error.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::DisplayFinalEntr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::DisplayFinalEntr.body: The routine walks through the stored link entries for the current target and emits a concise line for each one: it prints a marker for group starts or ends, then the target or item name (with an optional feature suffix). It indents group entries slightly more to visually separate nested groups. The output is directed to the standard‑error stream.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::FollowLinkEntry@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::FollowLinkEntry@.body: The function processes a link entry by determining the appropriate index (group or direct component), retrieves the entry data, and then follows its dependencies. If the entry has a link interface, it extracts the library and object lists from the interface, adds them to the current dependency list, and processes language‑specific runtime libraries. It handles special interface cases (such as interface libraries or wrong‑configuration libraries) by early exit or dedicated checks. If no interface is present, it falls back to the legacy dependency list and adds those entries instead. The routine ultimately populates the internal structures with all discovered dependencies for the current component.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::FollowSharedDeps.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::FollowSharedDeps.body: The routine registers a single dependency once: it inserts the index into an internal set; if the insert succeeds, it enqueues the interface’s libraries (conditionally on a flag) and then enqueues the interface’s shared dependency list.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::GetCurrentFeatur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::GetCurrentFeatur.body: The function performs a lookup in `LinkLibraryOverride`; if the requested key exists it returns that stored value, otherwise it falls back to the supplied `defaultFeature` string.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::GetOldWrongConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::GetOldWrongConfi.body: Returns a constant reference to the internally stored set of configuration items that were identified as incorrect. The method is read‑only; it simply gives read‑only access to the pre‑computed collection without mutating any state.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::HandleSharedDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::HandleSharedDepe.body: The function records a shared‑library dependency that must appear after the library that declares it. It creates or re‑uses a link entry slot for the dependency item, sets its metadata (kind, backtrace, target pointer) if the slot was newly allocated, and then records the constraint that this dependency must come after the declaring item in the graph. Finally, if the target itself declares additional dependencies, it follows those transitively by recursively processing its link interface.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::InferDependencie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::InferDependencie.body: The method iterates over the stored candidate sets for each depender, intersects the candidate sets to derive the definitive dependency set for that depender, and appends those dependencies as edges into the internal graph structure.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::LinkEntry::LinkE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::LinkEntry::LinkE.body: Creates a `LinkEntry` that holds the given `item` string and, if supplied, keeps a pointer to the `cmGeneratorTarget` for later use.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::LinkEntry::LinkE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::LinkEntry::LinkE.body: Creates a new `LinkEntry` instance that mirrors the properties of the supplied instance, copying over all internal data and preserving the link’s metadata and state.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::LinkEntry::LinkE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::LinkEntry::LinkE.body: LinkEntry initializes a new link-entry instance, wiring its internal metadata (such as identifiers, dependency lists, and status flags) for subsequent dependency‑analysis. It prepares the entry’s internal state so that downstream algorithms can treat it as a ready‑to‑use node in the link‑resolution graph.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::MakePendingCompo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::MakePendingCompo.body:
Creates a PendingComponent for the given component index by pulling its list of nodes from the CCG.  
If the component contains only a single node it is counted once; otherwise the required count is derived by ComputeComponentCount.  
The node list is inserted into the component’s Entries set and the fully‑filled PendingComponent is returned.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::OrderLinkEntries.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::OrderLinkEntries.body: The routine walks the component graph in depth‑first order to build a topological ordering of components, then walks that ordering to visit each entry (original and pending) in turn, recording the visit in its internal structures.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::QueueSharedDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::QueueSharedDepen.body: The method iterates through each `cmLinkItem` in the supplied vector and enqueues a `SharedDepEntry` containing the item and the originating depender’s index into the `SharedDepQueue`.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::ResolveLinkItem@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::ResolveLinkItem@.body: The function determines which target should handle the request (either the current target or a target from a specified component) and returns the result of invoking that target’s ResolveLinkItem with the supplied name.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::SetOldLinkDirMod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::SetOldLinkDirMod.body: Updates the internal flag that indicates whether the old link‑directory mode is enabled, so callers can react accordingly.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::UpdateGroupDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::UpdateGroupDepen.body: The routine iterates over every edge in the graph; for any non‑group entry it finds that resides inside one of the defined groups, it rewrites that edge to point to the group’s ID instead of the individual item, effectively collapsing individual dependencies into a single group dependency.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::VisitComponent@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::VisitComponent@k.body: The routine marks a component as visited, then performs a depth‑first traversal of its incident edges in reverse order to preserve an existing topological relationship. After all neighbors have been processed, it assigns a decreasing sequence number to the component so that later components get higher order values.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::VisitEntry@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::VisitEntry@k_ZN2.body: Records the node in the link order, updates the bookkeeping of which component has now been seen, removes that node from the current pending list, and when a component is exhausted it marks that component complete and then queues that component’s outgoing edges as pending for future processing.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::cmComputeLinkDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::cmComputeLinkDep.body: The constructor gathers context for link‑dependency resolution. It records the target, its generator and CMake instance, then scans the target’s properties for any “LINK_LIBRARY_OVERRIDE_…” keys, evaluates the associated expressions (using the current config and link language) and stores the resulting overrides in a map. It also honours a global “LINK_LIBRARY_OVERRIDE” property if present, tokenizes the value, and records each item as an override. Finally, it records whether a configuration string is supplied, determines the link type (debug‑aware), and flags whether debug mode or legacy “old‑link‑dir” handling should be enabled.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::cmComputeLinkDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::cmComputeLinkDep.body: The deleted copy constructor prevents copying of `cmComputeLinkDepends` objects, ensuring they cannot be duplicated inadvertently.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::operator=@k_ZN20.body: It marks the assignment operator as deleted, preventing implicit copy‑assignment of a `cmComputeLinkDepends` object and ensuring that instances are immutable once constructed.

@lcmComputeLinkDepends::~cmComputeLinkDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkDepends::~cmComputeLinkDe.body: The destructor for `cmComputeLinkDepends` releases all resources created during the link‑dependency analysis—clearing internal data structures before the object is destroyed.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddExternalO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddExternalO.body: The routine gathers the target’s external objects, de‑duplicates them by library name, resolves each unique library to a link item, and appends the resulting target objects to the target‑specific list of external object targets.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddFramework.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddFramework.body: The function parses the framework string from a link entry, splits it into a directory and a link‑name using the global generator’s split routine, and if a directory component exists it appends that to the framework search path. It then registers the runtime information for that framework, forces the FRAMEWORK feature to load when the feature is default, and finally records the framework in the internal Items collection—using the raw path when the build system is Xcode or the derived link name otherwise.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddFramework.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddFramework.body: The function inserts a new path string into an internal set; if the insertion succeeds (i.e. the string wasn’t already present), it appends that string to an internal vector. In effect the method keeps a set of all added paths and a list that preserves insertion order, avoiding duplicates.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddFullItem@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddFullItem@.body: The AddFullItem function registers a link entry that supplies an absolute path. It first skips implicit‑directory or special shared‑library cases, then verifies that the path satisfies policy CMP0008 for “full” libraries. It applies the current link type (shared or default) and, when required, restores the default if a previous user item had forced static. It also adds the path to the legacy “old‑link‑dir” search list for backward compatibility and finally appends the item to the internal Items vector.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddImplicitL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddImplicitL.body: The routine pulls language‑specific implicit link data from the current makefile’s definitions. It checks for a lib‑list variable constructed from the language name, and for any entries not already present in the implicit list it inserts them. In the same pass it grabs a directory list variable and, if found, feeds that list into the linker‑search‑path manager.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddImplicitL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddImplicitL.body: The routine walks through the list of languages associated with the target’s link‑closure. For each language that isn’t the current linker language it registers the needed implicit link information. It treats CUDA and HIP specially, adding their runtime libraries first so that any symbols those runtimes provide will be available before other implicit libraries are considered.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddItem@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddItem@k_ZN.body: The routine adds a link entry to the internal link‑generation structures. It first pulls the target and item from the supplied entry, computes the needed path name, and then tests whether the target is a CMake target. For CMake targets it distinguishes import libraries, interface libraries, object libraries, and frameworks (including Apple/Xcode variants), adding the appropriate records to `Items`, `Depends`, and runtime‑info containers. It also performs special cases for AIX imported executables and skips linking when specific conditions (e.g. `LoaderFlag` or missing import library) apply. The function fills the internal state used later to emit linker commands.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLibraryFe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLibraryFe.body: The routine first checks if the requested feature is already known and supported; if not, it looks up the feature’s definition in the current makefile (falling back to a generic variant if the language‑specific entry is missing). If the feature is either undefined or disabled, it records the issue as a fatal error and returns false. When the feature is present, its list of items is expanded, validated against the expected “<LIBRARY> <LIB_ITEM> <LINK_ITEM>” format (handling single or multi‑component variants, including optional PATH/NAME placeholders), and any malformed form triggers another fatal error. Once validated, the items are resolved for the target’s link language, stored in the internal descriptor map, and the function returns true.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLibraryRu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLibraryRu.body: The routine checks whether the supplied library path denotes a shared‑library. It consults internal flags (such as install‑name rules, static‑archive heuristics, framework detection) to decide that status. If the library is determined to be shared, it is queued into the runtime (and, if required, the link‑time) search path ordering.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLibraryRu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLibraryRu.body: The routine inspects a target library. It first ensures the target is a shared library that has a known runtime artifact and a valid soname; if any of those checks fails it exits immediately. When the checks pass, it records the library’s full path along with its soname in the runtime‑search ordering data structures, and, if a runtime‑linking flag is set, also records it for the linker’s search path.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLinkExten.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLinkExten.body: The function stores a non‑empty extension string in the matching internal list—`StaticLinkExtensions` for a static link, `SharedLinkExtensions` for a shared link—and also appends the string to the general `LinkExtensions` list.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLinkPrefi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddLinkPrefi.body: The `AddLinkPrefix` routine records a new prefix string only when the supplied string is non‑empty, inserting it into the internal `LinkPrefixes` set.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddRuntimeDL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddRuntimeDL.body: The method simply guarantees the given target appears only once in the internal list. It performs a linear scan with `std::find`; if the target is not found, it calls `emplace_back` to append it. This keeps the vector free of duplicates while keeping the insertion cost linear in the current size.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddRuntimeLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddRuntimeLi.body: The routine first asks the target system for the name of the runtime library that belongs to the supplied language; if the answer is empty it simply exits. If a name is found it looks up any link options registered under that name in the makefile’s definition table. It then walks through those options, and for every library not already recorded in the implicit link list it records it via AddItem. If no options are present the method does nothing further.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddSharedDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddSharedDep.body:
The routine registers a shared‑library dependency for the current target.  
It first validates that the dependency is really a shared library and that the
current target supports it. If the target’s type and platform match, it records
the DLL for runtime resolution. Depending on the current `SharedDependencyMode`
it may simply ignore, link directly, or add the library to various search
paths: linker search, dependent‑RPath, or runtime search directories.  
When the target exposes an import library it is used for run‑time path
computation; otherwise the full path of the library is stored. Finally, it
invokes helper helpers such as `AddLibraryRuntimeInfo`, `AddRuntimeDLL`,
`AddItem`, and `AddRuntimeLibrary` to propagate the dependency
information to the build’s runtime and link phases.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddSharedLib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddSharedLib.body: This helper records a shared library that lacks an .so name by stripping its extension, adding the resulting file path as a link‑entry, and registering that path in the linker’s search list so the runtime linker can locate it by file path instead of soname.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddTargetIte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddTargetIte.body:
The `AddTargetItem` routine records a target to be linked.  
* It switches the current link type to shared whenever the target isn’t a static library, guaranteeing dynamic linking compatibility.  
* It records any shared library in a set for later reference.  
* It treats imported shared libraries without SONAME specially via `AddSharedLibNoSOName`.  
* It handles legacy “old‑link‑dir” mode by adding target directories to the search list if necessary.  
* It parses framework paths (Apple frameworks or imported framework folders), extracts the framework name, and inserts the framework directory and the library itself into the item list with the appropriate feature string.  
* For non‑framework libraries it simply stores the full path in the item list, tagging it with the supplied feature (or the default “__CMAKE_LINK_LIBRARY” when none).

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddUserItem@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddUserItem@.body: The routine takes a library item that hasn’t matched a CMake target or a full path, figures out whether it’s a user‑supplied linker flag (e.g. ‐l or ‐Wl), and if so adds it to the old‑flag list. Otherwise it uses regexes to recognise shared, static or generic library names, sets the current link type to shared/static/any accordingly, builds the appropriate “‐l” style flag string, and appends that flag to the item list (applying any feature decoration if present).

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddXcFramewo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddXcFramewo.body: The method simply records a new header‑search path. It takes a string reference and appends it to the internal `XcFrameworkHeaderPaths` vector, adding that entry to the list of directories that the compiler will later query for headers. No validation or deduplication logic is performed; the path is stored as‑is.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddXcFramewo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AddXcFramewo.body: The function takes a link entry, parses its Xc‑framework plist, selects the matching library, and then either registers that library as a framework (for Apple targets or Xcode generators) or installs it as a standard library item, adding its runtime info, headers, and dependency entries as needed.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AppendValues.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::AppendValues.body: The function iterates over a vector of BT objects and appends each object’s Value to the provided string, inserting a single space before the first appended value.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::CheckImplici.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::CheckImplici.body:
The function checks whether a given `LinkEntry` refers to a library that should be treated as an implicit‑link directory entry.  
1. It first verifies that link‑type handling is enabled.  
2. It extracts the directory part of the item’s path; if that directory isn’t in the list of implicit link directories, the entry is rejected.  
3. It then checks whether the file name is among those that can be found by the linker; if not, the entry is rejected.  
4. Depending on the target policy (`CMP0060`) it may issue a warning (once per item) before proceeding.  
5. If all tests pass, the function turns the item into a “pathless” user item, adds it to the link‑search ordering, and returns `true`. Otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::CheckSharedL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::CheckSharedL.body: The function inspects a shared‑library entry; if it cannot reliably deduce a soname from the file path, it records that the library has no soname and reports success.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::Compute@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::Compute@k_ZN.body: The function first checks that the current target is something that normally requires linking (executable, shared, static, or a library that actually compiles code). If the target doesn’t need a linker it exits false. It then confirms a linker language is available. A `cmComputeLinkDepends` instance computes the ordered list of dependency entries. The routine walks through those entries, emits features and prefixes/suffixes as necessary, and adds each dependency to the link line. It treats special groups (link groups) and shared dependencies specially, adding them with appropriate prefixes. When a feature’s suffix remains it is flushed. After processing all entries it performs a warning for CMP0060‑style implicit library searches, records external object targets, and finally returns true.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::ComputeFrame.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::ComputeFrame.body: The method gathers implicit framework directories from CMake definitions and adds them to the internal set of emitted directories. First it reads the global “CMAKE_PLATFORM_IMPLICIT_LINK_FRAMEWORK_DIRECTORIES” value. It then constructs a language‑specific key (e.g. “CMAKE_CPP_IMPLICIT_LINK_FRAMEWORK_DIRECTORIES”), retrieves that value, and finally inserts the combined list into the `FrameworkPathsEmitted` set.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::ComputeItemP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::ComputeItemP.body: The method collects known library prefixes and suffixes from the makefile, registers them in internal lists for static and shared links, then constructs a composite regular expression that can match any library name (including optional prefix and extension). It compiles separate regex objects for matching any, static‑only, and shared‑only library names, which are later used to extract the library name components during parsing.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::ComputeLinkT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::ComputeLinkT.body: The routine inspects the target’s type and language, establishes whether the build can toggle between static and dynamic linking, and stores the corresponding flag definitions it should use for the current configuration.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::CreateExtens.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::CreateExtens.body: This routine assembles a regular‑expression fragment that matches any of the supplied file‑extension strings. It starts a parenthesised group, joins the extensions with “|”, escapes the “.” character, and appends an optional “.digit+” suffix when the object flag `IsOpenBSD` is true or the link type is `LinkShared`. The returned string ends with “$” to anchor the match at the string end.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::DropDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::DropDirector.body: DropDirectoryItem is invoked when a target resolves a link to a directory path. It warns that only libraries can be linked, and removes the directory entry from the target’s list of link items.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.body: The constructor initializes the `FeatureDescriptor` object by assigning the provided `name` and `itemFormat` to the corresponding member variables. It sets `Supported` to `true`, and copies the `ItemPathFormat` value into `ItemNameFormat`. No additional logic is performed.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.body: The constructor moves the supplied strings into the corresponding member variables—Name, ItemPathFormat, and ItemNameFormat—and sets the Supported flag to true.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.body: Initialises a feature descriptor with the supplied name, format strings and a suffix flag. The constructor sets the internal name, flag, prefix, suffix, and two format strings for later use. It is protected, so only derived classes or the owning class can invoke it.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.body: The constructor stores the provided name, prefix, and suffix into the corresponding member variables and marks the feature as supported. It simply initializes the object’s state; the trailing boolean argument is unused in this snippet.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.body: The constructor is simply defaulted, meaning the compiler supplies a defaulted constructor that performs no special work beyond the implicit member‑wise initialization. No custom code is required.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.body: This helper expands a template string that contains placeholder tags (`<LIBRARY>`, `<LIB_ITEM>`, `<LINK_ITEM>`) into a concrete string for a library item. Based on the `isPath` flag it picks between a path‑style or a name‑style format, then substitutes the three placeholder tokens with the supplied library string via a `FeaturePlaceHolderExpander`.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FeatureDescr.body: The method picks a format string based on whether the item is a path or name, expands the `<LIBRARY>`, `<LIB_ITEM>`, and `<LINK_ITEM>` placeholders in that format with the supplied arguments, and returns the resulting string.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FindLibraryF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FindLibraryF.body: The function performs a lookup in the `LibraryFeatureDescriptors` map using the supplied key. If an entry is present, it returns the address of the corresponding value; otherwise it returns a null pointer. The method is marked `const`, so it promises no modification of the object state, and relies on `std::map::find` semantics.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FinishLinker.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::FinishLinker.body: When invoked, the routine first verifies that there are actual “old” link directories or user‑specified entries to work on. It then checks the current policy status: in the WARN branch it emits a warning (if not already emitted), in the OLD branch it simply proceeds, and in the REQUIRED branches it aborts with a fatal error. After policy handling, it iterates over any remaining legacy link‑dir items and queues them into the linker’s search path. If all steps succeed it returns true; otherwise it returns false to halt the build.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetChrpathSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetChrpathSt.body: If `RuntimeUseChrpath` is false, it returns an empty string; otherwise it forwards the request to `GetRPathString(true)` and returns that result.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetDepends@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetDepends@k.body: It returns a constant reference to the internal vector that holds the dependency strings for the current `cmComputeLinkInformation` instance, allowing callers to inspect the list without copying or modifying it.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetDirectori.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetDirectori.body: The method simply retrieves and returns the internal list of directories stored in the `OrderLinkerSearchPath` instance via its `GetOrderedDirectories()` accessor, exposing that list as a const reference without altering any state.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetDirectori.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetDirectori.body: The function collects a list of directories that should be linked, first gathering directories of the target link directories. It then iterates through an ordered list of directories, appending each directory that appears in the target list to the result vector; if a directory isn't present, it still appends it, preserving the original order. The returned vector contains all directories in the order they were processed, wrapped in BT.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetExternalO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetExternalO.body: GetExternalObjectTargets returns a read‑only reference to the vector that holds pointers to external generator targets, exposing them without modifying the internal state.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetFramework.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetFramework.body: It exposes the internal vector of framework paths as an immutable reference. The function is marked const, so callers can’t alter the returned collection, and no copy of the vector is performed. The method simply returns the member `FrameworkPaths` unchanged.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetFramework.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetFramework.body: The method simply exposes the internal collection of framework paths that have already been emitted. It returns a const reference to the `FrameworkPathsEmitted` member, so callers see the set without copying it and cannot modify its contents.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetGroupFeat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetGroupFeat.body: The routine resolves a group‑feature description for a given name: it first checks a cached descriptor; if missing, it builds the corresponding makefile variable name (e.g. `CMAKE_<lang>_LINK_GROUP_USING_<feature>`), asks the makefile whether that feature is enabled, and if so it fetches the feature’s value list. After expanding that list it applies the linker wrapper logic, and finally returns (or stores) the resulting two‑element descriptor. If the feature is unsupported or malformed, the function emits a fatal error and returns an empty descriptor.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetItems@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetItems@k_Z.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the internally stored item vector, exposing it without copying or permitting mutation.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetLibLinkFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetLibLinkFi.body: Returns a constant reference to the internal `LibLinkFileFlag` string, guaranteeing callers cannot alter the stored value.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetLibraryFe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetLibraryFe.body: The function looks up the requested feature name in the internal map and returns the corresponding FeatureDescriptor reference.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetObjLinkFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetObjLinkFi.body: Provides read‑only access to the internal `ObjLinkFileFlag` string by returning a const reference to it.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRPath@k_Z.body: The routine builds the runtime search‑path vector for a target by inspecting its install/build flags, adding the appropriate install‑ or build‑tree rpaths (optionally using the origin token for relative paths), and finally appending any language‑ or platform‑specific implicit link directories that must always be present.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRPathLink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRPathLink.body: Returns a const reference to the internal `RPathLinkFlag` member, guaranteeing that the caller cannot modify the value. The method is const‑qualified, so it cannot change any member data.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRPathLink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRPathLink.body: The function `GetRPathLinkString()` verifies if the instance’s `OrderDependentRPath` flag is enabled; if not, it immediately returns an empty string. When the flag is set, it assembles a runtime linker search path by concatenating the directories returned by `OrderDependentRPath->GetOrderedDirectories()` with `":"` as the separator, leveraging the helper `cmJoin`. The resulting string is then returned.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRPathStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRPathStri.body: The function assembles a string of directories used at run‑time: it first fills a vector with directories via `GetRPath`, then joins them with the runtime separator returned by `GetRuntimeSep()`. If the path is not intended for installation and a special “chrpath” placeholder is used, it appends a trailing separator and pads the string with separators until its length is at least as long as the placeholder string, guaranteeing the placeholder can be substituted safely. The resulting string is returned.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRuntimeFl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRuntimeFl.body: Returns a const reference to the internal `RuntimeFlag` member; the function is `const`, so it guarantees no modification of the object state. This is O(1) and safe as long as the lifetime of the containing object is valid.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRuntimeSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRuntimeSe.body: The method returns a const reference to a vector of strings containing the ordered list of directories that constitute the runtime search path, as supplied by the `OrderRuntimeSearchPath` component.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRuntimeSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetRuntimeSe.body: This function returns a reference to the internal string member that holds the runtime separator.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetSharedLib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetSharedLib.body: It returns the set of targets that represent the shared libraries currently linked.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetXcFramewo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GetXcFramewo.body: This accessor simply yields the internally cached list of XC‑framework header directories. Because it returns a const reference, callers receive the original collection without copying it, so the call is efficient and guarantees that the header paths cannot be altered inadvertently. It’s const‑qualified, ensuring callers cannot modify the owning object’s state, and the function itself performs no dynamic allocation or side‑effects.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GroupFeature.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::GroupFeature.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied name, prefix, and suffix strings to its base class `FeatureDescriptor`, and passes `true` as an extra flag to indicate that this descriptor represents a group‑feature.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::HandleBadFul.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::HandleBadFul.body: Handles a library that is supplied as a full path that fails the library‑file check. The routine removes any existing dependency entry for that path, registers the new file as a user item, pushes the path into the link‑search list, then emits either a warning or a fatal error depending on the current policy status for the target.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::LibraryFeatu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::LibraryFeatu.body: This constructor initializes a `LibraryFeatureDescriptor` object by forwarding its `name` and `itemFormat` arguments to the base class `FeatureDescriptor`. It simply stores those values in the newly created instance; no additional processing occurs during construction.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::LibraryFeatu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::LibraryFeatu.body: Initializes a `LibraryFeatureDescriptor` instance by delegating the supplied `name`, `itemPathFormat`, and `itemNameFormat` to its base class `FeatureDescriptor`.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::LibraryFeatu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::LibraryFeatu.body: The constructor creates a `LibraryFeatureDescriptor` instance by forwarding the supplied strings to the base `FeatureDescriptor` constructor, initializing the name, prefix, path format, name format, and suffix for the descriptor. It performs no further logic.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::LoadImplicit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::LoadImplicit.body: The function gathers implicit linking information from the build configuration. It first pulls the base implicit directories from a global definition, then augments them with the current library architecture (if defined). It also appends language‑specific implicit directories, and then stores all of these directories in the `ImplicitLinkDirs` set. Afterwards it reads the implicit libraries list for the current language, filters out any flag‑style entries (those beginning with “‑” but not “‑l”), and stores the remaining library names in `ImplicitLinkLibs`. Finally, it appends platform‑specific runtime path directories into `RuntimeLinkDirs`. The result is a populated internal cache of all implicit directories and libraries that the linker should consider when resolving dependencies.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::NoCaseExpres.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::NoCaseExpres.body: The function walks the input string and builds a new string in which each non‑dot character is replaced by a bracketed pair of its lower‑case and upper‑case representations, leaving dots unchanged.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::PrintLinkPol.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::PrintLinkPol.body: The function writes a diagnostic message that informs the user that the CMP0003 policy must be set before any cmake_policy or cmake_minimum_required calls. It then lists the library names and directories that trigger the policy, explains how those paths are added to the linker search path, and gives a quick reference to the policy’s effect.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::SetCurrentLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::SetCurrentLi.body: When the link type changes, the method updates the internal state and, if the type is enabled, records a flag entry in the Items list.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::cmComputeLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::cmComputeLin.body:
The constructor of **`cmComputeLinkInformation`** initializes all of the data structures needed for a target’s link‑phase.  
It pulls the global and target‑specific configuration flags (linker language, flags for library/library‐file suffixes, runtime paths, etc.), creates a set of *feature descriptors* for various kinds of library links, and builds the directory orderings that will be searched when resolving dependencies.  
Finally, it configures platform‑specific behaviour such as “no‑soname” policies and the old‑style *‑L*‑search mode.

@lcmComputeLinkInformation::~cmComputeLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeLinkInformation::~cmComputeLi.body: The destructor `~cmComputeLinkInformation()` is an implicitly‑generated, defaulted destructor that performs no explicit cleanup beyond what the compiler already handles. It simply allows an instance of the `cmComputeLinkInformation` class to be destroyed cleanly when it goes out of scope, relying on automatic member destruction and RAII. No custom resource release logic is required.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddInterfaceDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddInterfaceDe.body:
Adds the link‑interface dependencies of a target to the build graph.  
It walks the target’s interface libraries, inserting each unique library
recursively (via `AddTargetDepend` and a recursive call to `AddInterfaceDepends`), and it also adds any object files referenced in the interface. The method prevents re‑emitting the same dependency by tracking emitted items, and propagates source back‑trace information for accurate diagnostics.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddInterfaceDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddInterfaceDe.body: Adds an interface dependency between a target and a specified dependee, handling special cases for executables that don't export and preventing self‑dependencies. It records each dependency pair and recurses for nested dependencies.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddObjectDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddObjectDepen.body:
The function registers an object‑library dependency for a target. It

1. pulls the library name from the source object; if the name is empty it exits.  
2. Finds the target at `depender_index` and resolves the corresponding link item.  
3. If the link item hasn't yet been recorded in `emitted`, it is inserted.  
4. When added, it verifies that the target is one of the acceptable kinds (executable, static/shared/module/library). If not, it emits a fatal error.  
5. Finally it records the library as a utility of the target.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddTargetDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddTargetDepen.body: Adds a dependency edge between the depender target and the dependee. If the dependee isn’t in the build system, it recursively registers any utility dependencies it declares. Otherwise it finds the dependee’s index, asserts its presence, and inserts the edge into the internal graph, marking whether the link is cross‑build and whether it’s a linking dependency.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddTargetDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddTargetDepen.body: The routine first ensures the dependee target actually exists; if it is missing and the policy requires it, it logs a warning or error. It then checks whether the dependee is an executable that is not exported; if that’s the case it is skipped. When a valid dependee remains, the function registers the dependency between the depender and dependee.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CheckComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CheckComponent.body: The function iterates over all components in the graph; it skips trivial ones, and for each non‑trivial component verifies that every target in the component is a static library. If the component contains anything other than static libraries or if cycles are disallowed, it logs a complaint and aborts the check, returning false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectDepends.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectDepends.body: The function builds the internal dependency graph in one pass: it first resizes the adjacency‑list container to the number of targets, then walks through each target index, invoking `CollectTargetDepends` to populate the corresponding adjacency list with that target’s outgoing edges.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectSideEff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectSideEff.body: The routine first clears and resizes the internal `SideEffects` vector to match the size of the graph, then iterates over every vertex in the graph invoking a helper that gathers side‑effect data for that particular vertex. It essentially rebuilds the side‑effect table by walking the graph once and collecting effect information for each node.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectSideEff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectSideEff.body: The routine starts at a specified node, records that node in a `visited` set to avoid revisiting, and appends that node’s own side‑effects to the target’s accumulator. It then walks each outgoing edge: for every successor it recurses, and after returning, it merges the successor’s collected side‑effects into the current node’s effect collections. The result is that the target’s side‑effect sets end up containing its own effects plus those of every reachable node.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectTargetD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectTargetD.body: CollectTargetDepends walks through every build‑configuration that a target participates in. For each configuration it enumerates the libraries and object files that the target links against. It keeps a hash of already‑emitted items to avoid duplicating the same dependency in that configuration. For every distinct library it records a target‑level dependency (via AddTargetDepend) and, if the library has an interface representation for that configuration, it records an interface dependency (via AddInterfaceDepends). For every object file it records an object‑level dependency (via AddObjectDepends). After handling the configuration‑specific libraries, it processes the target’s common utility items in a second pass, again avoiding duplicates. The routine guarantees that a target never ends up with a self‑dependency and that each dependency is registered only once per target across all configurations.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectTargets.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectTargets.body: CollectTargets iterates over every local generator in the `GlobalGenerator`, pulls each target from the generator’s list, stores the target pointer in the `Targets` vector, and records the target’s position in the `TargetIndex` map for fast index lookup during later dependency checks.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComplainAboutB.author: AI Short Overview
