@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComplainAboutB.body: The method builds a diagnostic message that lists every target in the offending component, reports which of its dependencies lie inside that same component, and finally triggers an error that halts the current computation. If the flag *strong* is true it adds a note that no such cycle can be broken because it involves only strong dependencies created by add_dependencies. If no‑cycle mode is active it notes that cyclic dependencies are forbidden; otherwise it states that only static libraries may contain cycles. Once assembled, the message is passed to cmSystemTools::Error to abort execution.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::Compute@k_ZN22.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::Compute@k_ZN22.body: The Compute method assembles the target‑dependency graph in a few passes: it first gathers targets and their raw dependencies, optionally dumps the initial graph when debugging is on; then it builds an intermediate graph incorporating side‑effects, verifies its component structure, and finally resolves the final dependency links between those components, returning true only if every validation succeeds.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComputeFinalDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComputeFinalDe.body: The function first obtains the component list and component graph, then allocates a final graph with the same size as the initial graph. It linearizes intra‑component edges by walking each component in reverse order, building a head for each component while detecting cycles; if a cycle is found it reports an error and exits. After that, it rewires all inter‑component edges by connecting the tail node of each component to the head node of its dependents. On success it returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComputeInterme.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComputeInterme.body: The routine clears the intermediate graph, resizes it to match the initial graph, and then iterates over every target. For non‑library targets it simply copies the initial edges. If a target is a static or object library, the routine checks whether dependency optimisation is enabled; if so, and the optimisation flag is on, it calls OptimizeLinkDependencies to prune the edges, otherwise it keeps the original edges unchanged.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplayCompone.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplayCompone.body: The function prints the list of strongly connected components of a component graph. It first writes a header line containing the graph name, then iterates over the vector of node lists returned by `GetComponents()`. For each component, it prints the component index and lists each node in that component, printing the node’s index and its target’s name from the `Targets` array. Finally, it writes a blank line to separate the output.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplayGraph@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplayGraph@k.body: The function prints the structure of a dependency graph to standard‑error: it starts by outputting the graph name, then walks every node in order, writing the target’s name and iterating through its adjacency list. For each outgoing edge it prints the child target’s name and whether the edge is “strong” or “weak”.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplaySideEff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplaySideEff.body: Iterates through a collection of side‑effect descriptors, printing for each target the custom command side effects and language side effects that affect it, along with the originating target indices and names.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::GetTargetDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::GetTargetDirec.body: The routine takes a target pointer and a reference to a target‑dependency set. It first locates the target’s index in the internal map, ensuring the target is known. Using that index it fetches the pre‑computed list of outgoing edges from the final dependency graph. For each edge in that list it looks up the target at the edge’s destination, inserts the corresponding target object into the supplied set and annotates the new element with the edge’s properties: whether it’s a strong link, whether it crosses a build boundary, and any back‑trace flag. This populates the caller‑supplied `deps` container with exactly the direct dependencies of the supplied target.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::GetTargets@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::GetTargets@k_Z.body: The `GetTargets()` member returns a const reference to the internal `Targets` vector, giving read‑only access to the stored target pointers.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::IntraComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::IntraComponent.body: The function traverses a directed graph of components, marking visited nodes to avoid revisiting and detect cycles. It adds edges that belong to the same component (`cmap[j] == c`) into the resulting “final” graph, preserving the order of strong intra‑component edges. When an edge is strong, it performs a recursive call to process the target node. If any recursive call fails, the function returns `false`. Otherwise, it records the edge and, for the first node in the component, sets `ComponentTail`. After all edges of a component are added, the function returns `true`.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::OptimizeLinkDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::OptimizeLinkDe.body: Processes each incoming graph edge: keeps the ones flagged as strong; for others it looks up side‑effect data tied to the edge and emits new edges for each dependent target that appears in the custom‑command or language‑specific side‑effect lists. The emitted set guarantees that a target is only added once per input edge, so no duplicate edges appear in the output list.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::cmComputeTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::cmComputeTarge.body: Initialises the global generator reference and pulls configuration flags for debug and cycle‑checking mode from the cmake instance.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::cmComputeTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::cmComputeTarge.body: It receives a target representation and recursively walks its dependency graph, collecting every reachable prerequisite in a flattened, ordered list that reflects the full transitive dependency chain.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::~cmComputeTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::~cmComputeTarg.body: The ~cmComputeTargetDepends routine walks the dependency graph for a build target, collecting the set of prerequisite targets that must be built before it runs. It gathers the result into an internal list for later use in scheduling the build.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetBooleanValue@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetBooleanValue@.body: This method examines an argument string in three passes: it first matches exact “on/off” tokens, then tries to parse a numeric representation (converting the full string to a double and treating zero as false), and finally falls back to a predefined definition lookup if the string isn’t a literal.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetBooleanValueO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetBooleanValueO.body: The method interprets a single argument as a Boolean: if `one` is true it treats the value as a literal (0 → false, 1 → true) or a previously defined variable; if the value parses as a number it falls back to that numeric value; otherwise it evaluates the definition and returns the inverse of cmIsOff.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetBooleanValueW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetBooleanValueW.body: The method accepts a command argument and decides which policy to apply. It first checks whether the current policy is NEW or OLD and immediately forwards to the corresponding `GetBooleanValue` implementation. If neither policy applies, it invokes both the new and old evaluation functions to compare their results. Should they differ, it issues a warning or error according to the policy level (WARN, OLD, REQUIRED_IF_USED, REQUIRED_ALWAYS, NEW), populates `errorString` and `status`, and finally returns the appropriate boolean value—normally the new result unless the policy mandates the older logic.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetDefinitionIfU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetDefinitionIfU.body: If the argument is quoted and the current policy is neither OLD nor WARN, the function immediately returns `nullptr`. Otherwise it retrieves the variable’s definition; if the variable was quoted under a WARN policy and this hasn’t been reported before, it issues a warning message, then returns the definition.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetVariableOrStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::GetVariableOrStr.body: The function first attempts to resolve the argument to a variable definition. If a definition is found, that value is returned; otherwise it falls back to the argument’s literal string value, which is then returned.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel0@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel0@k_Z.body: The function walks through a list of arguments, looking for opening‑paren markers. When it finds one, it walks forward until it balances that opening with a matching closing paren, extracts that sub‑segment, evaluates it recursively through `IsTrue`, and replaces the whole bracketed fragment in the original list with the resulting boolean value. If it cannot find a matching close, it flags a fatal error.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel1::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel1::[l.body: The lambda examines the current status and the keyword against the current argument; when both conditions are satisfied it constructs a warning message explaining that the keyword will be treated as an operator under the NEW policy, but since the policy isn’t set, the old interpretation is used, and the message is issued through `Makefile.IssueMessage`.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel1@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel1@k_Z.body: Handles the first‑level argument list by iterating over each entry, issuing policy‑warning messages when appropriate, and conditionally reducing or replacing arguments when a keyword is detected (e.g. file existence checks, directory/symlink checks, absolute‑path checks, command availability, policy existence, target resolution, variable definitions, and test conditions). The routine always returns true after performing these reductions.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel2::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel2::[l.body: Parses two strings through `std::sscanf`, returning `true` only when both calls succeed (i.e. both scans yield `1`).

@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel2@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel2@k_Z.body: The function walks through the argument list, applies the various CMake comparison operators (numeric, string, version, file‑time, list, path equality) according to policy state, and collapses arguments that satisfy the operator into a single result.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel3@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel3@k_Z.body: HandleLevel3 iterates through the supplied argument list; whenever it sees an argument marked by the keyword keyNOT, it fetches the Boolean value from the next argument (via GetBooleanValueWithAutoDereference), and then removes that argument from the list. The function always returns true.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel4@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::HandleLevel4@k_Z.body: The routine walks through the supplied argument list, looking for an operand pair tagged with either an AND or OR key. When it finds such a key, it fetches the two neighboring arguments, automatically resolving any indirection, and feeds those values into the selector that applies the corresponding logical operator. The resulting Boolean is then used to collapse the two original arguments into one, effectively shrinking the list in place. After iterating over the list it simply returns true, indicating that the level‑4 handling succeeded.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::IsKeyword@k_ZNK2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::IsKeyword@k_ZNK2.body: The `IsKeyword` member performs a quick policy‑aware check: it first checks whether the current policy allows quoted arguments to be treated as keywords; if the policy is not “WARN” or “OLD” and the argument is quoted, it returns `false`. Otherwise it compares the argument’s value against the supplied keyword. If they match and the argument is quoted while the policy is “WARN”, it logs a warning (to avoid accidental mis‑interpretation in the new policy) and returns `true`. The function finally returns the result of this comparison.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::IsTrue@k_ZN20cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::IsTrue@k_ZN20cmC.body: The routine receives a vector of arguments, clears any pre‑existing error flag, and then iteratively feeds the argument list through a chain of five handler routines (representing parenthesis handling, predicate parsing, binary operations, logical NOT, and AND/OR combination). Each handler attempts to collapse the list; if any handler reports failure it aborts and returns false. When no more reductions are possible the function expects exactly one argument left and, if present, returns its boolean value; otherwise it records an error and returns false.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The function returns an iterator that, when advanced, yields the current element first and then automatically proceeds to the next element of the underlying sequence.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The constructor simply copies an existing iterator so that the new instance points to the same element and has the same “next‑element” reference pre‑computed. This allows code that walks a container to access both the current item and the following one in a single object instead of recomputing the next pointer each time.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The constructor assigns `current` to the container’s beginning and, using `std::next`, assigns `next` to the following iterator if `current` isn’t equal to the end; otherwise `next` is left at the end iterator.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The function supplies a lightweight look‑ahead pair: given a standard iterator, it yields the element that the iterator currently points to and the one that follows. It’s used in the condition‑evaluation phase to test forthcoming values without advancing the underlying sequence, allowing callers to perform two‑step checks in a single call.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The method moves the iterator forward by one element, updates the internal `current` and `next` pointers accordingly, and then returns the iterator instance itself.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: Creates a new iterator by taking ownership of the source instance’s internal state (typically via a move‑constructor), thus efficiently re‑initialising the iterator without copying its underlying data.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The constructor initializes an iterator that yields the current element followed by the next two elements of a sequence, and exposes a `next()`/`hasNext()` interface that returns the next element in that sequence until all three have been consumed. It validates bounds on the underlying container and guards against null pointers, throwing an exception when the iterator runs out of data.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The constructor sets `current` to the container’s beginning, and then initializes `next` and `nextnext` to the successive elements if they exist, otherwise leaving them at the end.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The function walks a sequence, yielding a triplet of items: the element at the current index and the following two elements. It’s employed by the condition‑evaluator to examine short windows of values when testing predicates that depend on a running window of data.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: Advances the iterator by moving the `current` pointer to its next element, then recomputing `next` and `nextnext` based on the updated `current` and whether the iterator has reached the end. Finally, it returns the updated iterator instance.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The template replaces the element pointed to by the iterator with an expanded argument derived from the supplied boolean value, then discards the next element in the sequence, effectively collapsing two consecutive arguments into one.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: The method takes a boolean flag and an iterator bundle that points to the current argument and two following arguments. It replaces the current argument with an expanded command argument representing the flag value, then removes the subsequent two arguments from the container.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: It returns the current iterator instance as a `CurrentAndNextIter`.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmArgumentList::.body: Returns a `CurrentAndTwoMoreIter` that iterates over the current object and its next two elements.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmConditionEvalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmConditionEvalu.body: It moves the internal state from a temporary `cmConditionEvaluator` into a newly constructed instance, effectively transferring ownership of any held resources.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmConditionEvalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmConditionEvalu.body: The constructor simply stores a reference to the supplied cmMakefile, keeps the supplied back‑trace list, and queries the makefile for the current statuses of several policy flags (CMP0012, CMP0054, CMP0057, CMP0064, CMP0139). No evaluation logic is performed during construction; it merely records this information for later use.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmConditionEvalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmConditionEvalu.body: The constructor creates a new evaluator by copying the internal state from an existing instance, preserving its configuration and any pre‑configured evaluation data.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::matchKeys@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::matchKeys@k_ZN20.body: matchKeys is a variadic template that forwards the provided key arguments to matchKeysImpl. It returns the 1‑based index of the key that matched the supplied argument.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::matchKeysImpl@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::matchKeysImpl@k_.body: The `matchKeysImpl` template simply returns `0`, indicating that no matching key was found; the template parameter `N` is unused in the body.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::matchKeysImpl@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::matchKeysImpl@k_.body: The function recursively walks a variadic list of key objects (`key...`). For each `current` key it invokes `IsKeyword` with the command argument; if that returns true it short‑circuits recursion and returns the current index `N`. If not, it recurses with the next key by instantiating `matchKeysImpl<N+1>(arg, key...);` until the end of the pack.

@lcmConfigureFileCommand@k_Z22cmConfigur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureFileCommand@k_Z22cmConfigur.body: The routine takes the arguments for a `configure_file` invocation, resolves the source and target paths (expanding any relative paths), and processes optional flags such as `COPYONLY`, `ESCAPE_QUOTES`, `@ONLY`, and file‑permission modifiers. It validates that the supplied options are consistent (e.g., `FILE_PERMISSIONS` cannot coexist with `USE_SOURCE_PERMISSIONS` or `NO_SOURCE_PERMISSIONS`), and that at least one permission option is supplied when file permissions are requested). After the checks it forwards the parsed parameters to the makefile’s `ConfigureFile` method; any failure along the way results in an error status being set and the call returning `false`.

@lcmConfigureLog::BeginEvent@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::BeginEvent@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The function starts a new log entry: it first confirms the logger is ready, writes a separator line, bumps the indentation level, and then records the event’s kind along with back‑trace and check details for that makefile.

@lcmConfigureLog::BeginLine@k_ZN14cmConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::BeginLine@k_ZN14cmConf.body: It writes a number of two‑space units equal to the current `Indent` value to the internal stream and returns that stream reference for further chained output.

@lcmConfigureLog::BeginObject@k_ZN14cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::BeginObject@k_ZN14cmCo.body: The function `BeginObject(cm::string_view)` registers the start of a JSON‑style object. It takes a view of a string that identifies the object name or key, then writes the opening brace and any required indentation or newline conventions used by the surrounding code. The function is invoked whenever the code needs to emit the beginning of a new object—typically in the serializer routine that writes top‑level objects or nested structures within other JSON payloads.

@lcmConfigureLog::BeginObject@k_ZN14cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::BeginObject@k_ZN14cmCo.body: The method emits a line that starts with the supplied key followed by a colon, then ends the line and increments the internal indentation level so that any subsequent log entries will be rendered as nested under this key.

@lcmConfigureLog::EndEvent@k_ZN14cmConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::EndEvent@k_ZN14cmConfi.body: The routine simply verifies that the current indentation level is non‑zero and then decreases it, marking the end of the active logging block.

@lcmConfigureLog::EndLine@k_ZN14cmConfig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::EndLine@k_ZN14cmConfig.body: Convenient helper used to finish a log entry by pushing a newline into the stream.

@lcmConfigureLog::EndObject@k_ZN14cmConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::EndObject@k_ZN14cmConf.body: The `EndObject` method simply decrements the indentation counter, effectively signaling that the current object block has closed. It verifies that an indentation level is in use before performing the decrement.

@lcmConfigureLog::EnsureInit@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::EnsureInit@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The function checks whether the logging stream is already open; if not, it opens the file in append mode, sets the internal flag, and writes a header and the opening of an events object to the log file.

@lcmConfigureLog::IsAnyLogVersionEnabled.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::IsAnyLogVersionEnabled.body: The routine performs a linear‑time intersection test between two sorted lists: it walks through the input vector `v` and the stored `LogVersions` in tandem, advancing the iterator that points to the smaller value until a match is found. If any element matches, it returns `true`; otherwise it exhausts both lists and returns `false`.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteBacktrace@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteBacktrace@k_ZN14c.body: Extracts the back‑trace entries from a cmMakefile, normalises any file paths that fall inside the project root into relative form, collects each formatted entry into a string vector, and finally stores that vector under the key “backtrace”.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteChecks@k_ZN14cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteChecks@k_ZN14cmCo.body: This routine first verifies that there are any checks still pending (`HasCheckInProgress`). If there are none it exits immediately. Otherwise it opens a “checks” block, then streams each pending check message in reverse order, prefixing each line with “‑ ”. When done, it closes the block.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteEscape@k_ZN14cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteEscape@k_ZN14cmCo.body: This function takes a single byte, formats it as a two‑digit hexadecimal escape (`\xNN`), and writes that string to the instance’s stream. The buffer is sized to hold the maximum 5‑character escape plus a null terminator. If formatting succeeds (non‑negative result from `snprintf`), the escape string is sent out via the stream’s write routine.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.body: The function writes a literal text block, taking a string_view and a string reference to format the output. It writes the provided text directly to the output stream, handling any necessary escaping or formatting steps.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.body: The `WriteLiteralTextBlock` function is a small utility that writes a block of literal text into an output buffer. It takes two string views: one identifying the target location or stream and another containing the text to be emitted. The routine simply writes the provided content verbatim, handling any necessary escaping or formatting inline with the surrounding rendering logic. This helper is invoked from various rendering paths where a consistent, unmodified block of text needs to be emitted.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.body: Accepts a key and a std::string, then forwards the call to the underlying implementation by converting the string to a string_view before delegating.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.body: Writes a key and its value as a literal text block, escaping new‑lines, tabs, backslashes, and non‑printable bytes—including UTF‑8 characters—while handling indentation and line breaks to produce properly formatted output.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteTextBlock@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteTextBlock@k_ZN14c.body: WriteTextBlock accepts a key and a text string view, storing the supplied text under that key in the system’s configuration logging.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: `WriteValue` serializes a `cm::string_view` into an internal storage medium (e.g., a binary log, a JSON blob or a database record) and updates the corresponding in‑memory representation. In the codebase it is invoked during configuration reloads, cache invalidation, and when a new telemetry value must be persisted.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: WriteValue accepts a string view and a string reference, validates the inputs, then persists or forwards the string payload to the target medium (e.g., memory buffer, file, or remote sink), handling any I/O errors before completing the operation.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The `WriteValue` function is a thin wrapper that forwards a string-view value to the underlying storage mechanism. It takes a `cm::string_view`—an immutable view over a string buffer—to avoid unnecessary copies, and a `bool` flag that tells the caller whether the write should be treated as an append (`true`) or a replace‑in‑place (`false`). Internally, the function resolves the correct transport channel (e.g., file, socket, or in‑memory) and performs the actual serialization, handling any error conditions that arise.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The function stores a 32‑bit integer at the location identified by the `string_view` argument, effectively persisting the value into the internal buffer or map that backs the current session.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The method writes the supplied key to the log, appending “: null” and then finalises the line; the second parameter is unused.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The `WriteValue` method emits a single key‑value pair into the internal log stream. It prefixes the key with a colon and a space, passes the raw string value to the configured encoder for serialization, and finishes the record with a newline from `EndLine`. The result is a nicely formatted log entry like `key: value` on its own line.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The function serialises a map of string‑to‑string pairs into an output stream. For each entry it first tests whether the key consists solely of the characters in the static list `rawKeyChars`. If the key contains only those characters, it writes the pair directly via `WriteValue`. If the key contains any other character, it prefixes the key with a newline and encodes the key and value with `Encoder`, inserting a colon separator in the output stream. When all entries are processed it closes the object marker.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The method takes a key string and a boolean flag. It calls the internal stream‑handling helpers `BeginLine()` and `EndLine()` to frame a single log entry: it writes the key, a colon, and the literal “true” or “false” depending on the value. After rendering the line, it flushes the buffer so the entry appears in the output stream.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: Writes a single key‑value entry to the internal log buffer by streaming the key and the integer value between calls to `BeginLine()` and `EndLine()`. The routine assumes the key is non‑null and that the internal stream handles proper formatting; it performs no additional validation or error handling.

@lcmConfigureLog::cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14c.body: The constructor initializes the log directory and version list, guarantees that the latest log‑version entry (1) is present, and creates a new JSON stream writer that the internal encoder uses for output.

@lcmConfigureLog::cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14c.body: The `cmConfigureLog` routine is the single entry point that pulls together all of the project’s log‑output knobs—log‑level thresholds, output targets (file, console, remote collector), and formatting flags. Invoking it once during application start‑up wires the global log subsystem with the supplied `cmConfigureLog` struct instance; every subsequent component that pulls in `cmConfigureLog.h` implicitly uses that shared configuration. No other module has to touch individual loggers; the function simply registers the chosen settings into the framework’s shared state so that all later log calls emit consistently.

@lcmConfigureLog::cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14c.body: The function initializes the logging subsystem: it reads the current configuration, establishes logger instances and handlers, and applies the appropriate log levels and output targets.

@lcmConfigureLog::~cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::~cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14.body: When an instance of `cmConfigureLog` is destroyed, the destructor checks whether the log session is still open. If it is, it calls `EndObject()` to tidy up the logging object and then emits a terminating marker (the literal string `"...\n"`) into the output stream.

@lcmConsoleBuf::SetUTF8Pipes@k_ZN12cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConsoleBuf::SetUTF8Pipes@k_ZN12cmCon.body: The routine simply turns on UTF‑8 pipe handling for the console output and error streams—when the code is built for 32‑bit Windows and the CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP macro is not defined, it forwards the UTF‑8 pipe switch to the internal `m_ConsoleOut` and `m_ConsoleErr` objects.

@lcmConsoleBuf::cmConsoleBuf@k_ZN12cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConsoleBuf::cmConsoleBuf@k_ZN12cmCon.body: The `cmConsoleBuf` constructor initializes the console‑buffer object with its default state, setting up any internal buffer pointers or state variables to their default starting values. It performs no custom logic beyond the compiler‑generated default initialization.

@lcmConsoleBuf::~cmConsoleBuf@k_ZN12cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConsoleBuf::~cmConsoleBuf@k_ZN12cmCo.body: When an instance of **cmConsoleBuf** goes out of scope, the compiler‑generated default destructor automatically tears down its members, ensuring any resources they own are properly released.

@lcmConstStack::Empty@k_ZNK12cmConstStac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::Empty@k_ZNK12cmConstStac.body: The Empty() method simply reports whether the stack contains any elements, returning true only when the internal size counter is zero. Because it is marked const, the call cannot modify the stack, making it safe to invoke in any context that expects a read‑only view. The implementation is typically a one‑line check against an internal counter or an empty container, so its execution is O(1) and incurs no heap allocation. The function is used before pop operations or in decision logic to avoid under‑flow errors, as shown in the example usage in cmConstStack.h.

@lcmConstStack::Pop@k_ZNK12cmConstStack3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::Pop@k_ZNK12cmConstStack3.body: The `Pop` member removes the top element from the stack, returning that element while decrementing the internal counter to reflect the reduced size.

@lcmConstStack::Push@k_ZNK12cmConstStack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::Push@k_ZNK12cmConstStack.body: The `Push` method returns a new stack containing the supplied value at its top, leaving the original unchanged.

@lcmConstStack::Top@k_ZNK12cmConstStack3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::Top@k_ZNK12cmConstStack3.body: Returns the top element of the stack as a read‑only reference (const reference), allowing callers to inspect the element without modifying the stack.

@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.body: The protected constructor receives a `std::shared_ptr` that points to a constant `Entry`. It assigns this pointer to the stack’s internal `top` member, ensuring that the stored entry cannot be modified through the stack interface. If the passed pointer is `nullptr`, the function guards against invalid states, typically by throwing or asserting an error. This guarantees that the stack always exposes only read‑only access to the top element.

@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.body: The protected `cmConstStack` function receives a shared pointer to a constant `Entry` and a value of type `T`. It’s used to push that value onto an internal stack that is kept const‑only for the lifetime of the `Entry` instance.

@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.body: The function `cmConstStack()` constructs and returns a constant‑value stack (a stack that holds a fixed set of values). It is used wherever the code needs a pre‑configured stack, typically by calling it in a header or at a key line such as shown on line 20 of `cmConstStack.h`.

@lcmContinueCommand@k_Z17cmContinueComma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmContinueCommand@k_Z17cmContinueComma.body: The function validates a CONTINUE statement in a makefile. It first verifies that the current execution context is inside a loop block; if not, it emits a fatal error and flags the system. It then marks that a CONTINUE has been invoked in the status object. Finally, it checks that the command receives no arguments, reporting a fatal error if any are supplied, and returns `true` to signal the command was processed (even though it always fails validation).

@lcmCoreTryCompile::Arguments::Arguments.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::Arguments::Arguments.body: The `Arguments` function extracts and validates a set of parameters supplied by the caller, returning an `ArgumentParser::ParseResult` that indicates whether the incoming arguments were parsed successfully. It performs early sanity checks (e.g., required flags present, numeric ranges) and, on success, populates a populated `Arguments` object that other parts of the system consume.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::Arguments::Arguments.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::Arguments::Arguments.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied `cmMakefile` pointer to its base class, establishing the internal `Makefile` reference for the instance.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::Arguments::SetSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::Arguments::SetSource.body: The `SetSourceType` function checks the supplied `sourceType` string against two valid values (“NORMAL” or “CXX_MODULE”). It assigns the corresponding enum value to `SourceTypeContext` and flags the match as true; if the string doesn’t match any known type it records a single error message in `SourceTypeError`.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::CleanupFiles@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::CleanupFiles@k_ZN16c.body: The method removes every file inside a temporary build directory. It first verifies that the supplied path is non‑empty and only contains the “CMakeTmp” or “CMakeScratch” markers; otherwise it aborts and logs an error. It then enumerates the directory’s contents, skips “.” and “..”, and any file whose name starts with “.nfs”, and recursively cleans sub‑directories. For each real file it attempts removal, retrying once on Windows if a virus scanner blocks the delete, and reports any failure via the `Makefile` message system. The routine returns immediately when nothing can be removed.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::FindOutputFile@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::FindOutputFile@k_ZN1.body: The method clears any previous error and output data, builds a path to the expected output file by appending the target name (and optionally the current configuration name when in a multi‑configuration build), and a suffix “_loc”. It then verifies that the file exists; if not, it records an error message. When the file is found, the method reads the first line of that file (which is expected to contain the path to the actual output file) and stores this resolved path in `OutputFile`. If any step fails, the corresponding error message is set in `FindErrorMessage`.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::IsTemporary@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::IsTemporary@k_ZN16cm.body: The function scans a file‑system path for the substrings that identify the engine’s temporary directories (“CMakeTmp” or “CMakeScratch”) and reports whether either marker is found.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::ParseArgs@k_ZN16cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::ParseArgs@k_ZN16cmCo.body: The function creates an `Arguments` object from the current `Makefile`, then calls the supplied `cmArgumentParser` to parse the iterator range into that object while collecting any arguments that cannot be parsed into the `unparsedArguments` vector. If parsing succeeds but some arguments were left over, it emits a warning listing those unknown arguments. Finally, it returns the fully populated `Arguments` instance.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::ParseArgs@k_ZN16cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::ParseArgs@k_ZN16cmCo.body: ParseArgs consumes a range of strings representing command‑line options and produces a populated arguments object. It first inspects the second argument to decide whether the input follows the newer “PROJECT” or “SOURCE” format; if neither, it falls back to the legacy signature. Depending on the detected format it dispatches parsing to the corresponding sub‑parser and then normalises optional fields—e.g. resetting empty strings to an unspecified state—before returning the resulting argument bundle.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::TryCompileCode@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::TryCompileCode@k_ZN1.body: This routine coordinates a “try‑compile” of a CMake target. It parses the supplied arguments, establishes source and binary directories, writes a temporary `CMakeLists.txt` file that sets compiler policies and the test target, then invokes the core `TryCompile` call. The result is captured, cached or stored in the project’s cache, and any requested output file is copied to the user‑specified location. Errors and copy failures are reported through the Makefile’s message system.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::WriteSource@k_ZNK16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::WriteSource@k_ZNK16c.body: The function constructs a path in the binary directory, opens the file for writing, writes the provided content, and reports any failure by issuing fatal‑error messages; if successful it returns the full file path.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::WriteTryCompileEvent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::WriteTryCompileEvent.body: The function records the outcome of a try‑compile step. It serializes the result into a structured log entry: the description (if present), the source and binary directories, any CMake‑specific variables, and a nested block that contains the variable used, whether it was cached, the captured stdout and the process exit code. All data is written through the `cmConfigureLog` interface, with conditional sections guarded by the build‑time macro.

@lcmCoreTryCompile::cmCoreTryCompile@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCoreTryCompile::cmCoreTryCompile@k_Z.body: This function initiates the compilation workflow for a makefile. It assigns the provided makefile to the internal reference and then triggers the core compilation routine, handling any errors or fallbacks without explicit boilerplate.

@lcmCreateTestSourceList@k_Z22cmCreateTe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCreateTestSourceList@k_Z22cmCreateTe.body: Creates a test driver source list from the supplied argument list, extracting any special options (EXTRA_INCLUDE, FUNCTION), generating forward declarations for each test file, and building a mapping table that associates test file names with function names. The function then writes the appropriate definitions into the makefile and returns success status.

@lcmCryptoHash::Append@k_ZN12cmCryptoHas.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::Append@k_ZN12cmCryptoHas.body: Append takes a `cm::string_view` argument and copies that data into the object’s internal buffer, updating any internal state that tracks the accumulated input.

@lcmCryptoHash::Append@k_ZN12cmCryptoHas.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::Append@k_ZN12cmCryptoHas.body: The `Append` method feeds raw data into the hash context by calling `rhash_update`. It copies the provided buffer of length `sz` into the internal state, advancing the digest computation.

@lcmCryptoHash::Append@k_ZN12cmCryptoHas.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::Append@k_ZN12cmCryptoHas.body: The method feeds the supplied string view into the running hash state by calling rhash_update with the view’s data pointer and length.

@lcmCryptoHash::ByteHashFile@k_ZN12cmCry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::ByteHashFile@k_ZN12cmCry.body: The routine opens the requested file; when the stream opens, it calls Initialize, reads the file in 512‑byte blocks, passes each block read (after checking that the read succeeded) to Append, and finally calls Finalize to obtain and return the hash. If the file cannot be opened or an I/O error occurs, the function simply returns an empty vector.

@lcmCryptoHash::ByteHashString@k_ZN12cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::ByteHashString@k_ZN12cmC.body: ByteHashString produces a byte vector that represents the cryptographic hash of the supplied string view. It returns that vector to be used in later cryptographic operations.

@lcmCryptoHash::ByteHashString@k_ZN12cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::ByteHashString@k_ZN12cmC.body: The method initializes a hashing context, feeds the supplied string into the hash engine, and returns the resulting digest vector.

@lcmCryptoHash::ByteHashToString@k_ZN12c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::ByteHashToString@k_ZN12c.body: The routine translates a raw byte vector into its hexadecimal string form. It pre‑allocates twice the byte count to avoid reallocation, then iterates over each byte, appending the high and low nibble hex characters using a fixed 16‑element lookup table. The final string is returned.

@lcmCryptoHash::Finalize@k_ZN12cmCryptoH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::Finalize@k_ZN12cmCryptoH.body: The function finalizes an ongoing hash computation by allocating a vector sized to the digest size, running the library’s final routine to write the digest into that buffer, and returning the vector containing the resulting hash bytes.

@lcmCryptoHash::FinalizeHex@k_ZN12cmCryp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::FinalizeHex@k_ZN12cmCryp.body: This member simply produces a hexadecimal string of the digest by calling `Finalize()` to finish the hashing process and then converting the resulting byte array to a string via `ByteHashToString`.

@lcmCryptoHash::HashFile@k_ZN12cmCryptoH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::HashFile@k_ZN12cmCryptoH.body: The `HashFile` function receives a file path, forwards it to the internal `ByteHashFile` routine that produces a raw byte digest, and finally converts that byte vector to a human‑readable string via `ByteHashToString`. It returns the resulting hash string.

@lcmCryptoHash::HashString@k_ZN12cmCrypt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::HashString@k_ZN12cmCrypt.body: Hashes the supplied string‑view and returns the resulting digest as a standard string (often a hex‑encoded SHA‑256/MD5 value). The routine is used to generate stable, collision‑free identifiers such as include‑guard names.

@lcmCryptoHash::HashString@k_ZN12cmCrypt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::HashString@k_ZN12cmCrypt.body: The method accepts a string view, runs it through the internal Byte‑hash routine, and returns the resulting hash as a string. The conversion from raw bytes to the string is performed by ByteHashToString.

@lcmCryptoHash::Initialize@k_ZN12cmCrypt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::Initialize@k_ZN12cmCrypt.body: The method simply clears the internal hashing context by invoking `rhash_reset(this‑>CTX)`, priming the object for the next hash operation.

@lcmCryptoHash::IntFromHexDigit@k_ZN12cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::IntFromHexDigit@k_ZN12cm.body: Converts a single hex character into its numeric value, returning `true` when the conversion succeeds and `false` otherwise. If successful, the `output` parameter is set to the corresponding integer value for 0‑9, a‑f, or A‑F.

@lcmCryptoHash::New@k_ZN12cmCryptoHash3N.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::New@k_ZN12cmCryptoHash3N.body: The `New` static function creates and returns a `std::unique_ptr` to a freshly‑constructed `cmCryptoHash` object. It receives an `algo` string (typically the name of a hash algorithm), parses that string to identify the appropriate algorithm type, allocates the specific hash implementation, and hands back ownership of the new object via the smart pointer.

@lcmCryptoHash::New@k_ZN12cmCryptoHash3N.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::New@k_ZN12cmCryptoHash3N.body: Creates a new hash‑object by matching the supplied algorithm name to one of the supported constants (MD5, SHA1, SHA224/256/384/512, or SHA3‑224/256/384/512). If a match is found, it constructs a `cmCryptoHash` instance for that algorithm and hands it back wrapped in a `std::unique_ptr`; otherwise it returns a null pointer.

@lcmCryptoHash::cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCry.body: The constructor assigns the algorithm‑specific identifier from a mapping table and immediately invokes the rhash initialization routine to create the internal context object.

@lcmCryptoHash::cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCry.body: The `cmCryptoHash` function is a public entry point that computes a cryptographic hash (e.g., SHA‑256/MD5) over supplied data and returns the resulting digest. It is intended to be invoked directly to obtain a hash value for a given input string or byte buffer.

@lcmCryptoHash::operator=@k_ZN12cmCrypto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::operator=@k_ZN12cmCrypto.body: The deleted assignment operator blocks any copying of a `cmCryptoHash` instance.

@lcmCryptoHash::~cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::~cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCr.body: It calls `rhash_free(this->CTX)` to release the hash context.

@lcmCryptoHash_rhash_init@k_ZL23cmCrypto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash_rhash_init@k_ZL23cmCrypto.body: It guards a one‑time global initialization flag, invokes the underlying `rhash_library_init()` on first entry, and then forwards the supplied identifier to `rhash_init()`—returning the resulting `rhash` handle.

@lcmCurlFixFileURL@k_Z16cmCurlFixFileURL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCurlFixFileURL@k_Z16cmCurlFixFileURL.body: The function returns a normalized URL string. It first checks that the string begins with “file://”; if not, it passes the string unchanged. It replaces literal spaces with “%20” to escape them. On Windows, it further converts the resulting string from Unicode to the ANSI code‑page (ACP) by converting the wide string to an ANSI multi‑byte string before returning the final URL.

@lcmCurlSetCAInfo@k_Z15cmCurlSetCAInfoPi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCurlSetCAInfo@k_Z15cmCurlSetCAInfoPi.body: The function probes the supplied CA‑file and, if it is missing, walks through the environment‑variables SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR and a set of built‑in paths; whenever a valid file or directory is found it calls curl_easy_setopt to bind the CA bundle or search path to the Curl handle, returning an empty string on success or an error message otherwise.

@lcmCurlSetNETRCOption@k_Z20cmCurlSetNET.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCurlSetNETRCOption@k_Z20cmCurlSetNET.body: The function maps a textual net‑rc level (“OPTIONAL”, “REQUIRED”, “IGNORED”) to the corresponding libcurl enum, assigns the option with `curl_easy_setopt`, and if a file path is supplied, it sets that too. It returns an empty string on success or an error message if the level is invalid or a set‑up call fails.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::GetValueAsBool@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::GetValueAsBool@k_Z.body: The method returns `true` when the widget’s internal `Value` equals the string `"ON"`, otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN18.body: When ENTER/SPACE is pressed, the function flips the internal boolean value of the widget, refreshes the associated window, and returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::SetValueAsBool@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::SetValueAsBool@k_Z.body: Sets the widget’s label to “ON” when true and “OFF” when false, then updates its foreground/background to the corresponding color pair (BoolOn or BoolOff) if color support is enabled.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::cmCursesBoolWidget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::cmCursesBoolWidget.body:
cmCursesBoolWidget is a lightweight helper that represents a toggle‑style widget in a terminal UI.  
It initializes the widget’s internal state, renders a simple on/off glyph, and updates that glyph in response to user input or programmatic state changes. The class prevents accidental copying by deleting its copy constructor, ensuring that only freshly constructed instances are used.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::cmCursesBoolWidget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::cmCursesBoolWidget.body: This constructor initializes a Boolean‑field widget: it flags the widget type as BOOL, configures visual attributes (foreground/background) only when curses colors are disabled, turns the field non‑editable by clearing the O_STATIC flag, and finally seeds the field with a default value of `false`.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::operator=@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::operator=@k_ZN18cm.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents any code from assigning one `cmCursesBoolWidget` instance to another; attempting an assignment will trigger a compile‑time error.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::~cmCursesBoolWidge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::~cmCursesBoolWidge.body: ~cmCursesBoolWidget() constructs a Curses‑style widget that displays a Boolean toggle. It inherits from cmCursesWidget, adding a single on/off switch that can be rendered with a Curses UI. The constructor takes a label and initial state, creates a small display area, and handles key events to flip the Boolean value. Its public interface exposes a `value()` accessor and a `setValue(bool)` mutator, and emits a signal whenever the state changes, allowing other parts of the code to react to the user’s toggle.

@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::GetValue@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::GetValue@.body: If `Label` is set, the method simply forwards the call to that object’s own `GetValue()` and returns whatever pointer that method provides; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::cmCursesC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::cmCursesC.body: A defaulted move constructor that automatically transfers ownership of the internal data of a cache entry.  When a `cmCursesCacheEntryComposite` instance is constructed from an rvalue reference, the compiler-generated implementation simply swaps internal state, avoiding any copying of potentially heavy resources. This allows the type to be used in containers and algorithms that rely on efficient move semantics without having to write any custom code.

@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::cmCursesC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::cmCursesC.body: The constructor takes a cache‑key and state, creates a standard label widget for the entry, then uses the entry type returned by the state to instantiate the corresponding widget (bool, path, file‑path, or string/option). It sets the widget’s value from the cached value, stores the created widget in `Entry`, and throws an error if the entry type is undefined.

@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::cmCursesC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::cmCursesC.body: Creates a cache‑entry widget that holds a key string, a label widget sized by `labelwidth`, and a string widget sized by `entrywidth`. In the constructor the label widget is built with the provided key string; a placeholder label widget is created for new‑label cases; and the string widget is instantiated with the given dimensions. This composite object is stored in the cache for later retrieval.

@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::cmCursesC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::cmCursesC.body: The `cmCursesCacheEntryComposite` constructor that takes a const reference to another instance is intentionally deleted, meaning that objects of this type cannot be copied. This forces users to explicitly create new instances (usually via factory or factory‑like helpers) rather than relying on implicitly generated copies. The deletion is a defensive measure that keeps the cache entries in a strict ownership regime, preventing accidental duplication that could corrupt the internal cache state.

@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::operator=.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::operator=.body: The move‑assignment operator (`operator=`) takes an rvalue reference, transfers the internal state of the temporary into the target object, and leaves the source in a valid but unspecified state. It performs a self‑assignment check, then swaps or reassigns all member fields so that the destination ends up with the new data while the source becomes empty. This allows code to safely replace a `cmCursesCacheEntryComposite` instance with another without deep copying, as seen in the two sample calls in the source file.

@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::operator=.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::operator=.body: The operator copies the state from the source object into the current one and returns a reference to the updated object, enabling assignment chaining.

@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::~cmCurses.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesCacheEntryComposite::~cmCurses.body:
The `~cmCursesCacheEntryComposite()` destructor is declared with `= default;`.  
That means the compiler supplies an automatically generated destructor that performs the standard destruction of member objects and resources.  
No custom cleanup logic is executed; any necessary release of resources is handled by the compiler‑generated destructor.

@lcmCursesColor::GetColor@k_ZN13cmCurses.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesColor::GetColor@k_ZN13cmCurses.body: The function lazily initializes a map from a character identifier to a short color code by parsing the environment variable `CCMAKE_COLORS` the first time it is called. On each call it looks up the supplied `id` in that map and returns the mapped value if present; otherwise it returns the supplied `fallback` value.

@lcmCursesColor::HasColors@k_ZN13cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesColor::HasColors@k_ZN13cmCurse.body: It reports whether the system can use curses colors: if the build-time flag is enabled it queries the runtime with has_colors(); otherwise it returns false.

@lcmCursesColor::InitColors@k_ZN13cmCurs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesColor::InitColors@k_ZN13cmCurs.body: The routine queries the terminal’s color capability; if supported, it turns on color mode, loads the system defaults, and registers a handful of color pairs that tie UI symbols (BoolOff, BoolOn, String, Path, Choice) to specific palette entries via GetColor.

@lcmCursesDummyWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesDummyWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN1.body: The function is a stub: it ignores all arguments and simply returns `false`.

@lcmCursesDummyWidget::cmCursesDummyWidg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesDummyWidget::cmCursesDummyWidg.body: The `cmCursesDummyWidget` constructor creates a minimal stub widget that registers with the Curses UI framework; its copy constructor is explicitly deleted to avoid accidental cloning.

@lcmCursesDummyWidget::cmCursesDummyWidg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesDummyWidget::cmCursesDummyWidg.body: The constructor forwards its parameters to the base `cmCursesWidget` constructor, then marks the new instance’s `Type` field as `cmStateEnums::INTERNAL`. This establishes the widget as an internal‑level component within the Curses framework.

@lcmCursesDummyWidget::operator=@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesDummyWidget::operator=@k_ZN19c.body: The `operator=` declaration marks the copy‑assignment operator for the class as deleted, meaning any attempt to copy‑assign a `cmCursesDummyWidget` instance (e.g. `a = b;`) will be a compile‑time error. This prevents accidental or accidental modification of an object that should remain immutable after construction.

@lcmCursesDummyWidget::~cmCursesDummyWid.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesDummyWidget::~cmCursesDummyWid.body: The virtual destructor `~cmCursesDummyWidget()` ensures that any dynamically allocated or Curses‑specific resources associated with a `cmCursesDummyWidget` instance are released when the widget is destroyed. It guarantees proper cleanup while still allowing derived classes to extend the cleanup process through overriding.

@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::cmCursesFilePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::cmCursesFilePa.body: The constructor marked `= delete` prevents copying a `cmCursesFilePathWidget` object. Any attempt to copy‑construct (e.g., `cmCursesFilePathWidget a(b);` or `auto c = b;`) will be rejected at compile time, ensuring each instance manages its own resources without accidental duplication.

@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::cmCursesFilePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::cmCursesFilePa.body: Creates a widget of the given size and position, then tags it as a file‑path widget by storing the `cmStateEnums::FILEPATH` value in `Type`.

@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::operator=@k_ZN.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents copying or reassigning a `cmCursesFilePathWidget` instance from a const reference. Any attempt to do `widget = otherWidget;` will be a compile‑time error.

@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::~cmCursesFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::~cmCursesFileP.body: The destructor `~cmCursesFilePathWidget()` is a public, virtual function that cleans up resources when a `cmCursesFilePathWidget` object is destroyed. It overrides the base class’s virtual destructor and is responsible for releasing any allocated memory or handles associated with the file‑path widget.

@lcmCursesForm::AddError@k_ZN12cmCursesF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::AddError@k_ZN12cmCursesF.body: It receives an error description and a C‑style string (possibly an error code or extra data) and records or forwards that information for later handling.

@lcmCursesForm::DebugEnd@k_ZN12cmCursesF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::DebugEnd@k_ZN12cmCursesF.body: The `DebugEnd` routine finalises debugging for the form: if the global `Debug` flag is already cleared it exits immediately; otherwise it turns the flag off and shuts down the open debug‑log file.

@lcmCursesForm::DebugStart@k_ZN12cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::DebugStart@k_ZN12cmCurse.body: The function turns on debugging for the form and opens a file named **ccmakelog.txt** to receive debug output.

@lcmCursesForm::GetForm@k_ZN12cmCursesFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::GetForm@k_ZN12cmCursesFo.body: The method simply returns the instance’s internal `Form` member, exposing whatever form data the object holds.

@lcmCursesForm::HandleInput@k_ZN12cmCurs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::HandleInput@k_ZN12cmCurs.body: The pure virtual member `HandleInput` is part of an abstract interface that derived form classes must implement. It is invoked whenever the form receives input from the user (keystrokes, mouse clicks, etc.), and the implementation is responsible for translating that input into state changes or actions specific to the concrete form.

@lcmCursesForm::HandleResize@k_ZN12cmCur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::HandleResize@k_ZN12cmCur.body: The HandleResize routine first tears down the current display (`endwin()`), then verifies that the screen was successfully re‑initialized. If the initialization fails it writes a concise error message to the standard error stream and terminates the process. Once the screen is known to be valid it disables input echo, re‑enables line buffering, activates keypad handling, and finally redraws the full interface by calling `Render()` with the new terminal dimensions before updating the status bar.

@lcmCursesForm::LogMessage@k_ZN12cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::LogMessage@k_ZN12cmCurse.body: The `LogMessage` routine checks the global debug flag; if debugging is enabled it appends the supplied string to a global output stream (typically a file). The function performs no allocation or parsing—just a guarded write to the stream.

@lcmCursesForm::Render@k_ZN12cmCursesFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::Render@k_ZN12cmCursesFor.body:
The `Render` method is intended to be overridden by concrete widgets.  
When called, it should paint the widget’s visual representation into the rectangle defined by the four parameters: the left and top coordinates of the upper‑left corner, and the width and height of the area to fill.

@lcmCursesForm::UpdateStatusBar@k_ZN12cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::UpdateStatusBar@k_ZN12cm.body: The `UpdateStatusBar` method is a pure‑virtual member that classes derived from the base form class must implement. It’s purpose is to refresh the textual status bar shown to the user—typically by querying current state (e.g., cursor position, validation messages, or form‑specific flags) and rendering that information to the designated status line in the curses UI. This function is invoked whenever the form’s state changes and ensures the status display stays in sync with the underlying data.

@lcmCursesForm::cmCursesForm@k_ZN12cmCur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::cmCursesForm@k_ZN12cmCur.body: The deleted copy‑constructor `cmCursesForm(cmCursesForm const&) = delete;` blocks copying the object, ensuring instances of `cmCursesForm` can’t be duplicated inadvertently.

@lcmCursesForm::cmCursesForm@k_ZN12cmCur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::cmCursesForm@k_ZN12cmCur.body: It assigns the internal form member to a null state, establishing a clean starting point for any subsequent form operations.

@lcmCursesForm::operator=@k_ZN12cmCurses.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::operator=@k_ZN12cmCurses.body: The deleted copy‑assignment operator (`operator=`) prevents assigning one `cmCursesForm` object to another. When you try `a = b;` for two instances, the compiler rejects it because the operator is marked `delete`. This ensures that `cmCursesForm` objects cannot be inadvertently overwritten after construction.

@lcmCursesForm::~cmCursesForm@k_ZN12cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::~cmCursesForm@k_ZN12cmCu.body: The destructor releases the underlying `ncurses` form object if it was allocated, unposting and freeing the form and clearing the pointer to avoid double‑deallocation.

@lcmCursesLabelWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesLabelWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN1.body: The function simply returns `false`, signaling that it does not process any input. It leaves all arguments unchanged.

@lcmCursesLabelWidget::cmCursesLabelWidg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesLabelWidget::cmCursesLabelWidg.body: The deleted copy constructor prevents accidental copying of the widget, ensuring that only move operations or explicit construction are possible.

@lcmCursesLabelWidget::cmCursesLabelWidg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesLabelWidget::cmCursesLabelWidg.body: The constructor creates a label widget of the specified size and position, turns off its editability, active, and static flags, and finally sets the widget’s displayed text to the supplied name.

@lcmCursesLabelWidget::operator=@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesLabelWidget::operator=@k_ZN19c.body: `operator=` deletes the copy‑assignment operator for `cmCursesLabelWidget`. It prevents accidental assignment of one instance to another, ensuring that the widget’s internal state cannot be inadvertently copied or overwritten. This restriction is part of the class’s copy‑semantics rule‑of‑five implementation.

@lcmCursesLabelWidget::~cmCursesLabelWid.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesLabelWidget::~cmCursesLabelWid.body: The `~cmCursesLabelWidget()` destructor is declared virtual and marked `override`, ensuring that derived classes properly release any resources when destroyed. It is defined as `= default`, so the compiler generates the standard destructor logic to free any owned resources (e.g., dynamic allocations, file handles). No custom cleanup code is executed; any cleanup must be implemented in subclasses that override this function.

@lcmCursesMainForm::AddError@k_ZN16cmCur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::AddError@k_ZN16cmCur.body: The `AddError` method takes a message string, pushes it to the internal `Outputs` collection, marks that a non‑status output was produced, and finally triggers `DisplayOutputs` to present the message. The second parameter is intentionally unused and ignored.

@lcmCursesMainForm::Configure@k_ZN16cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::Configure@k_ZN16cmCu.body: The routine resets the output state, registers a progress‑callback when `noconfigure` is zero, writes the current GUI state to disk, then either runs pre‑configuration checks (if `noconfigure` is non‑zero) or executes the main configuration routine. Afterwards it clears the callback, displays any generated error or status messages in a scrolling dialog, restores the UI, and finally re‑renders the main form before returning.

@lcmCursesMainForm::DisplayOutputs@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::DisplayOutputs@k_ZN1.body: The function first queries the current terminal size, then checks whether the displayed form matches its internal log form. If it’s different, a new `cmCursesLongMessageForm` is instantiated, set as the current form, and rendered. If the same form is already active, it simply pushes the new output string into that form and updates the display.

@lcmCursesMainForm::FillCacheManagerFrom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::FillCacheManagerFrom.body: The routine walks through every UI‑bound cache entry, normalizes its old and current values using `FixValue`, and when a normalized value change is detected it tags that entry as modified and writes the new value back into the cache.

@lcmCursesMainForm::FixValue@k_ZNK16cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::FixValue@k_ZNK16cmCu.body: The function trims trailing spaces from the input string, then—if the value represents a path—converts back‑slashes to forward‑slashes, and—if the value is a boolean flag—converts it to the literal “ON” or “OFF”.

@lcmCursesMainForm::Generate@k_ZN16cmCur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::Generate@k_ZN16cmCur.body: The function clears any previous output, hooks a callback that updates a progress bar, calls the underlying make‑instance to generate, then (depending on the return code and error flags) presents a single‑screen message form with the generated output or an error notice, finally re‑initialises the main UI and renders it again before returning success.

@lcmCursesMainForm::HandleInput@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::HandleInput@k_ZN16cm.body: The routine runs an endless input‑handling loop that refreshes the status bar, prints the key‑display and then interprets the pressed key. It first checks whether the form itself or the currently focused widget wants to consume the key; if not, it dispatches navigation (up/down/page/home/end) and command keys (write, configure, help, search, generate, delete entry, etc.) while updating the UI accordingly.

@lcmCursesMainForm::InitializeUI@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::InitializeUI@k_ZN16c.body: The routine rebuilds the list of cache‑entry composites used by the UI. It first gathers all cache keys, counts the “real” entries, and creates a temporary vector large enough to hold them. It then iterates over the keys twice: first adding composites for any entry that isn’t already present (treating it as “new”), then adding composites for those that already exist. Finally it swaps the new list into place of the old one and triggers a layout refresh with `RePost`.

@lcmCursesMainForm::JumpToCacheEntry@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::JumpToCacheEntry@k_Z.body: It forwards the supplied name to the two‑parameter overload, passing the string unchanged and a hard‑coded `false` flag.

@lcmCursesMainForm::JumpToCacheEntry@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::JumpToCacheEntry@k_Z.body: The function scans the form’s fields starting at the current field, optionally wrapping around, until it finds a field whose value contains the supplied string (case‑insensitive). It stops when the field is found or the search returns to the start position. The `reverse` flag flips the search direction and adjusts the navigation logic that flips pages when the field list is exhausted. The routine relies on `field_userptr` to obtain the widget pointer and uses `cmSystemTools::LowerCase` for case‑insensitive matching.

@lcmCursesMainForm::LoadCache@k_ZN16cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::LoadCache@k_ZN16cmCu.body: The `LoadCache` member performs a shallow initialization of the caching subsystem: it first delegates cache loading to the underlying `CMakeInstance`; if that call succeeds it applies the current arguments to the instance via `SetCacheArgs`, then triggers a pre‑load of any CMake files that may populate the cache before control returns to the caller.

@lcmCursesMainForm::LookForCacheEntry@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::LookForCacheEntry@k_.body: The function scans the internal collection `Entries` and returns `true` if any element’s `Key` equals the supplied `key`, otherwise `false`.

@lcmCursesMainForm::PrintKeys@k_ZN16cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::PrintKeys@k_ZN16cmCu.body: The routine first guards against a terminal that is too small – it exits immediately if the current width or height is below the minimum required sizes. If a form widget is present, it attempts to ask that widget to render its own key hints; if that fails or no widget is active, the routine falls back to a default set of key‑bindings hard‑coded into the function. It lays these hints out in a fixed vertical strip at the bottom of the screen, drawing each line with a small amount of padding so that the three rows of shortcuts align neatly. If the “Advanced mode” toggle is active, a line is printed that indicates whether the mode is on or off. Finally, the routine prints a page counter in the upper‑right corner of the window. Once all lines have been written, the cursor is left in a position ready for normal input.

@lcmCursesMainForm::RePost@k_ZN16cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::RePost@k_ZN16cmCurse.body: The function RePost rebuilds the form’s field list: it frees any existing form, clears the cached field vector, then counts the entries that should appear (honoring the advanced‑mode flag), guaranteeing at least one dummy entry when none are visible. It then populates the field vector with the label, “new” flag and actual entry widgets for each eligible cache entry, appending a trailing null to terminate the list.

@lcmCursesMainForm::RemoveEntry@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::RemoveEntry@k_ZN16cm.body: The routine first guards against a null pointer, then scans the internal collection for an entry whose stored value matches the supplied string. When such an entry is located it invokes a cleanup routine on that value and removes the entry from the container.

@lcmCursesMainForm::Render@k_ZN16cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::Render@k_ZN16cmCurse.body: The Render routine first checks whether the current form is present; if so, it resets the edit flag on any string‐type widget that might be in edit mode, removes the old form and frees its resources. It then validates the supplied dimensions against minimal width/height thresholds, aborting if the space is insufficient. Depending on whether the form is in “advanced” mode, it counts how many entries should be displayed: in normal mode only those entries without the *ADVANCED* flag are shown. It walks through the entry list to compute the number of pages needed to fit the visible rows within the given height, moving each entry’s label, value box and flag widgets into calculated positions. Finally, it constructs a new form object from the prepared field array, posts it, refreshes the status bar and help‑keys, and forces a screen refresh.

@lcmCursesMainForm::ResetOutputs@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::ResetOutputs@k_ZN16c.body: The method clears the internal log view, empties the output collection, and resets the flags and progress indicators back to their default false/empty state.

@lcmCursesMainForm::UpdateProgress@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::UpdateProgress@k_ZN1.body: It takes a message and a progress value, builds a textual progress bar of 40 characters, stores the resulting string in `LastProgress`, and pushes the message to the output queue. It then calls `DisplayOutputs()` to render the current status. If the supplied progress is negative, it simply queues the message instead of rendering a bar.

@lcmCursesMainForm::UpdateStatusBar@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::UpdateStatusBar@k_ZN.body: This public routine refreshes the status bar at the bottom of the curses form: it first verifies that the terminal window is wide and tall enough; if not, it clears the screen and writes a warning. Otherwise it determines which field’s label is active, composes a status line from either the supplied message or the current label’s help text, pads or truncates it to fit the form width, writes it with a highlighted field, then displays the CMake version string on the right‑hand side before restoring the cursor.

@lcmCursesMainForm::UpdateStatusBar@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::UpdateStatusBar@k_ZN.body: The overridden UpdateStatusBar method simply delegates the refresh logic to another helper routine, passing a null‑optional argument so that the underlying status‑bar update routine can determine the current state without any specific payload.

@lcmCursesMainForm::Write@k_ZN16cmCurses.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::Write@k_ZN16cmCurses.body: Populates the cache manager with UI‑derived data, persists that cache to the configured output directory, and then forces a reload to bring the in‑memory view back up to date.

@lcmCursesMainForm::cmCursesMainForm@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::cmCursesMainForm@k_Z.body: The constructor creates a new instance of the main curses‑based form. It is marked `= delete` to forbid copying, ensuring that each form object is created only once and cannot be duplicated.

@lcmCursesMainForm::cmCursesMainForm@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::cmCursesMainForm@k_Z.body:
The constructor prepares the CMake UI by:

- Collecting the command‑line arguments supplied to the tool.  
- Storing a help banner that is shown when the interface starts.  
- Instantiating a single‑threaded `cmake` object (role = Project) and hooking it up with the runtime‑generated CMake command line editor.  
- Re‑constructing the first argument to point at the running `cmake` binary (by appending “/cmake” to the executable’s own path) and forwarding that argument list to the new `cmake` instance.
