@lcmCursesMainForm::operator=@k_ZN16cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::operator=@k_ZN16cmCu.body: `operator=` is declared deleted, so instances of `cmCursesMainForm` cannot be copy‑assigned. This enforces that the object can’t be rebound to another after construction, preventing accidental sharing or resource mismanagement.

@lcmCursesMainForm::~cmCursesMainForm@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::~cmCursesMainForm@k_.body: The destructor cleans up the curses form: it checks if `Form` is non‑null, calls `unpost_form` to detach it from the screen, frees the underlying form structure with `free_form`, and finally sets the pointer to `nullptr`.

@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::AddOption@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::AddOption@k_ZN2.body: Adds the supplied string to the internal `Options` container by invoking `push_back()` on that vector. The method receives the option as a const reference to avoid copying, and simply stores it for later use.

@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::HandleInput@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::HandleInput@k_Z.body: Handles key navigation in the options widget: it first checks for an empty options list, then interprets the pressed key. For an ENTER press it advances to the next option, refreshes the screen; for left‑shift or Ctrl‑b it moves to the previous option; for right‑shift or Ctrl‑f it again moves forward. If the key isn’t one of those it returns false, otherwise it updates the display and reports success.

@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::NextOption@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::NextOption@k_ZN.body: The function increments an option index, wraps to zero when it passes the last entry, and updates the widget’s current value accordingly.

@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::PreviousOption@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::PreviousOption@.body: Moves the current index to the preceding entry in the options array, wrapping back to the last element when at the start, and then applies that value through SetValue.

@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::SetOption@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::SetOption@k_ZN2.body: It assigns the default index, updates internal state, and then scans the stored options to locate the supplied value, setting the internal `CurrentOption` to the matching index.

@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::cmCursesOptions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesOptionsWidget::cmCursesOptions.body: The constructor initializes a Boolean‐style options widget. It hard‑codes the widget type to `cmStateEnums::BOOL` (a quick workaround to avoid string‑type conflicts in the build system). The constructor then checks whether the terminal supports colors; if so, it assigns the widget’s foreground and background to the predefined color pair for the choice state, otherwise it falls back to the normal and standout attributes. Finally, it turns off the static flag on the field.

@lcmCursesPathWidget::OnReturn@k_ZN18cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesPathWidget::OnReturn@k_ZN18cmC.body: The method simply forwards the return event to its base class, delegating the handling to `cmCursesStringWidget::OnReturn` without adding any extra logic.

@lcmCursesPathWidget::OnTab@k_ZN18cmCurs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesPathWidget::OnTab@k_ZN18cmCurs.body:
The function is the tab‑completion handler for a path widget.  
When invoked, it first checks that a non‑empty string is present; if the string is unchanged since the last call it resets its internal cycle state.  
It then fetches a list of matching paths by invoking the global‑search helper, and if the current index is within that list it replaces the widget’s text with the corresponding entry.  
If the returned entry ends with a ‘*’, that trailing symbol is removed; a trailing slash is appended when the entry is a directory.  
Finally the widget’s display is refreshed, and the internal index is advanced (wrapping back to zero when it reaches the end).

@lcmCursesPathWidget::OnType@k_ZN18cmCur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesPathWidget::OnType@k_ZN18cmCur.body: The method clears the widget’s internal status—resetting its cycle flag, index counter, and last‑glob string—before deferring the typing event to the base string widget.

@lcmCursesPathWidget::cmCursesPathWidget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesPathWidget::cmCursesPathWidget.body: The `cmCursesPathWidget` constructor explicitly deletes its copy constructor, ensuring that instances of this widget cannot be duplicated inadvertently—any attempt to copy a `cmCursesPathWidget` object will be rejected at compile‑time.

@lcmCursesPathWidget::cmCursesPathWidget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesPathWidget::cmCursesPathWidget.body: This constructor creates a path‑type widget, disables the cycling flag, initializes the current index to zero, and applies the appropriate foreground/background color pairs depending on whether terminal color support is available.

@lcmCursesPathWidget::operator=@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesPathWidget::operator=@k_ZN18cm.body: `operator=` is a copy‑assignment operator that is explicitly deleted, preventing any assignment of one `cmCursesPathWidget` instance to another. This stops accidental shallow copies of the widget’s internal state, ensuring that instances remain independent and reducing the risk of dangling pointers or duplicated resources.

@lcmCursesPathWidget::~cmCursesPathWidge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesPathWidget::~cmCursesPathWidge.body: ~cmCursesPathWidget() is the key routine that sets up the widget’s internal state—initialising path tracking, binding navigation callbacks, and wiring the UI to respond to user actions so the widget can display and edit filesystem paths.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetInEdit@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetInEdit@k_ZN20.body: Retrieves the internal edit flag to indicate whether the instance is currently in edit mode.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetString@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetString@k_ZN20.body: Returning the widget’s string value, the `GetString` method simply delegates to the internal `GetValue` function and returns its result.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetValue@k_ZN20c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetValue@k_ZN20c.body: The `GetValue` member simply forwards to the internal helper `field_buffer`, requesting the first character (index 0) from the widget’s current field buffer and returning that pointer as a read‑only C‑string.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN.body: The function toggles the widget’s edit state and processes keyboard events. When in edit mode it interprets arrow keys, home/end, tab, escape, and control shortcuts to modify the underlying form buffer. It exits edit on any navigation key unless a special return key or escape, restoring the original text. If the form window shrinks beyond a minimal size it quits on a “q” press. For each input it dispatches the appropriate form_driver request (next/prev field, delete character, etc.) and finally updates the screen before returning.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnReturn@k_ZN20c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnReturn@k_ZN20c.body: The function toggles the widget’s edit state. When already in edit, it ends the edit session, clears the stored original text, forces the form to refresh the next‑field cursor position (a hack to update the UI), logs the transition, and marks the widget as “done”. When not in edit, it starts an edit session by recording the current field buffer and logging the state change.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnTab@k_ZN20cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnTab@k_ZN20cmCu.body: The `OnTab` function is the tab‑key event handler for the string widget. In its current form it simply executes an empty body; the only code line that is present is a commented-out call to retrieve the current form (`fm->GetForm()`), but no further action is performed. Thus, as of now, pressing Tab triggers the function but no functional change occurs.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnType@k_ZN20cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnType@k_ZN20cmC.body: The method captures a key event and forwards it to the helper routine `form_driver`, supplying the form instance retrieved from the supplied `cmCursesMainForm`. It ignores the `WINDOW*` argument.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::PrintKeys@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::PrintKeys@k_ZN20.body: The function verifies terminal dimensions, then, if the widget is in edit mode, it clears the bottom of the screen and prints a three‑line instruction block telling the user how to finish or cancel the edit.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::SetInEdit@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::SetInEdit@k_ZN20.body: Sets the internal `InEdit` flag to the supplied `inedit` value, updating the object’s edit‑state accordingly.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::SetString@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::SetString@k_ZN20.body: The method simply forwards the supplied string to the internal `SetValue` routine, causing the widget to update its displayed value with the new string.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::cmCursesStringWi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::cmCursesStringWi.body: The `cmCursesStringWidget` constructor moves an existing instance into a new `cmCursesStringWidget` object. It takes the contents of the supplied temporary (via a reference‑to‑rvalue) and transfers ownership of the underlying data—such as the string buffer and any internal state—from the source object to the newly constructed widget. This allows efficient re‑use of a fully‑initialised widget without copying its internal state.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::cmCursesStringWi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::cmCursesStringWi.body: The constructor creates a new `cmCursesStringWidget` that copies all of the original widget’s state—including its text buffer, visual attributes, and event‑handling configuration—so that the new instance behaves identically to the source instance.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::cmCursesStringWi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::cmCursesStringWi.body: The constructor creates a string‑widget instance: it sets the widget’s internal `InEdit` flag to false, records its type as `STRING`, and applies an appropriate foreground/background color pair. If the terminal supports colors, it uses the predefined string color pair; otherwise it falls back to the default foreground/background attributes (`A_NORMAL` / `A_STANDOUT`). Finally, it turns off the `O_STATIC` option for the field so the widget can be edited or redrawn dynamically.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::operator=@k_ZN20.body: The `operator=` assignment operator takes an rvalue of `cmCursesStringWidget` and copies its internal string content into the current instance, then returns a reference to the modified object so that calls can be chained. This allows callers to set or replace the widget’s displayed text in a single, fluent statement.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::operator=@k_ZN20.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of the source widget into the target instance – effectively duplicating its string contents and any other member data – and then returns a reference to the left‑hand side object. It performs the usual self‑assignment check to avoid needless work when both operands are the same instance. The operation is exception‑safe (no state changes are made until the copy succeeds) and provides the usual strong guarantee: in the event of an exception the target remains unchanged.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::~cmCursesStringW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::~cmCursesStringW.body: The `~cmCursesStringWidget()` destructor cleans up the resources owned by a `cmCursesStringWidget` instance. It removes any string‑display widgets that were created in the constructor (typically a `cmCursesStringWidget` object is responsible for drawing a piece of text on a curses-based UI). When a `cmCursesStringWidget` is destroyed, it also invalidates any references to its underlying `cmCursesWidget` base class, ensuring that no lingering pointers are left dangling. This cleanup is required to avoid memory leaks in the curses‑based UI loop.

@lcmCursesWidget::GetPage@k_ZN14cmCurses.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::GetPage@k_ZN14cmCurses.body: It returns the value stored in the `Page` field. If that field hasn’t been initialized, or if concurrent code writes to it, callers can see an invalid or stale value.

@lcmCursesWidget::GetType@k_ZN14cmCurses.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::GetType@k_ZN14cmCurses.body: It simply returns the value stored in the `Type` member. The function is a straightforward getter that yields the `cmStateEnums::CacheEntryType` corresponding to the current cache entry.

@lcmCursesWidget::GetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::GetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.body: The `GetValue()` member simply yields a C‑style string view of the widget’s stored `Value`. It returns a pointer to the internal `std::string`’s null‑terminated data via `c_str()`, enabling callers to read the widget’s current value without copying the string.

@lcmCursesWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN14cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN14cmCu.body:
HandleInput receives a key code reference, a pointer to the main form, and a curses window.  
It processes the input and returns true if the input was handled successfully, false otherwise.  
Derived classes provide the concrete handling logic for the specific widget.

@lcmCursesWidget::Move@k_ZN14cmCursesWid.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::Move@k_ZN14cmCursesWid.body: If the widget’s field is present, the method repositions it to the supplied `(x, y)` coordinates and then records whether this move starts a new page by toggling its internal flag accordingly.

@lcmCursesWidget::PrintKeys@k_ZN14cmCurs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::PrintKeys@k_ZN14cmCurs.body: Designed to be overridden by derived types, the base method simply returns false without performing any printing.

@lcmCursesWidget::SetPage@k_ZN14cmCurses.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::SetPage@k_ZN14cmCurses.body: The `SetPage` function simply assigns the supplied `page` value to the instance’s internal `Page` member – it performs no validation, range checks, or other side‑effects.

@lcmCursesWidget::SetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::SetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.body:
The routine stores the supplied string in the widget’s internal `Value` member and immediately pushes that content into the widget’s display buffer by calling `set_field_buffer`.  
The `const_cast<char*>` is used to satisfy the C‑style API that expects a mutable `char*`, discarding the const‑ness of the `std::string` buffer.  
The function makes no defensive checks; it assumes the field pointer is valid and that `set_field_buffer` will correctly interpret the buffer contents.

@lcmCursesWidget::SetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::SetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.body: The `SetValue` function is intended to update an internal string value; it accepts a `const std::string&` and, when called, copies or assigns that value to an internal member (or propagates it to dependent state) and may trigger any necessary state‑change notifications or side‑effects required by the widget’s logic.

@lcmCursesWidget::cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14c.body: Disallowing any copy construction of `cmCursesWidget` instances, this deleted constructor guarantees that objects of this type cannot be duplicated inadvertently.

@lcmCursesWidget::cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14c.body: Creates a Curses field with the supplied width‑height and top‑left offset, stores the widget pointer in that field, turns off automatic scrolling, and initializes the widget’s internal page counter to zero.

@lcmCursesWidget::operator=@k_ZN14cmCurs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::operator=@k_ZN14cmCurs.body: The deleted assignment operator forbids assigning one `cmCursesWidget` to another, ensuring the widget’s internal state can’t be duplicated inadvertently.

@lcmCursesWidget::~cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::~cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14.body: The destructor checks whether the `Field` member is non‑null; if it is, the function releases its memory via `free_field` and then clears the pointer to avoid dangling references.

@lcmCustomCommand::AppendCommands@k_ZN15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::AppendCommands@k_ZN15.body: This method adds the supplied command lines to the command sequence stored in the `cmCustomCommand` instance by delegating to the `cm::append` helper, which simply concatenates the two lists.

@lcmCustomCommand::AppendDepends@k_ZN15c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::AppendDepends@k_ZN15c.body: The method simply takes a read‑only list of dependency strings and appends them to the command’s internal collection via the helper routine `cm::append`. It performs no other logic or validation.

@lcmCustomCommand::AppendImplicitDepends.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::AppendImplicitDepends.body: Takes a constant reference to an implicit‑dependency list and merges it into the object’s own `ImplicitDepends` list via the helper `cm::append`.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK15c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK15c.body: The function simply returns a constant reference to the `Backtrace` member of the `cmCustomCommand` object, allowing callers to read the back‑trace data without modifying the internal state.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetByproducts@k_ZNK15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetByproducts@k_ZNK15.body: This accessor returns a read‑only view of the internal collection of product identifiers. It simply exposes the stored `Byproducts` vector without copying it, letting callers inspect the contents while preserving the class’s encapsulation.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetCMP0116Status@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetCMP0116Status@k_ZN.body: The `GetCMP0116Status` function simply queries the internal state machine for the CMP‑0116 command and returns the current status flag (e.g., enabled, pending, or completed). It performs a read‑only operation with no side‑effects, ensuring any caller sees a snapshot of the flag at the moment of call.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetCMP0147Status@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetCMP0147Status@k_ZN.body: GetCMP0147Status retrieves the current operational state of the CMP0147 component, reading its internal flags and returning an enum (or boolean) that indicates whether the component is active, idle, or fault‑condition.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetCommandExpandLists.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetCommandExpandLists.body: Returns the value of the member `CommandExpandLists`, indicating whether command expansion is enabled.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetCommandLines@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetCommandLines@k_ZNK.body: Returns a const reference to the internal `CommandLines` member, so callers receive the stored data without any copying and cannot modify it.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetComment@k_ZNK15cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetComment@k_ZNK15cmC.body: Returns a pointer to the internal comment string if the object reports that it has a comment; otherwise it returns a null pointer.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetDepends@k_ZNK15cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetDepends@k_ZNK15cmC.body: It returns a const reference to the internal vector of strings that holds the command’s dependency list.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetDependsExplicitOnl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetDependsExplicitOnl.body: This method simply returns the value of the member variable `DependsExplicitOnly`. It returns `true` if the command’s dependencies are flagged to be explicitly declared only; otherwise it returns `false`. The function is read‑only and does not modify any state.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetDepfile@k_ZNK15cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetDepfile@k_ZNK15cmC.body: It returns a reference to the internal `Depfile` member. Because the method is marked `const`, it guarantees that the returned `std::string` reference cannot be used to modify the object’s state. The function simply exposes the value of `Depfile` without copying it, so callers get the exact string stored in the instance.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetEscapeAllowMakeVar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetEscapeAllowMakeVar.body: Returns the value of the `EscapeAllowMakeVars` flag indicating whether escape of make‑variables is permitted.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetEscapeOldStyle@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetEscapeOldStyle@k_Z.body: The function is a simple accessor that returns the stored flag `EscapeOldStyle`. It is marked `const`, guaranteeing that it does not alter the object state and can be called on immutable instances. Since it merely returns the member value, the code is trivial and incurs no side‑effects. The method name follows conventional “Get” naming for read‑only properties, signalling that the value is expected to be read‑only and not written to elsewhere.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetImplicitDepends@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetImplicitDepends@k_.body: The `GetImplicitDepends` member simply returns a const reference to the `ImplicitDepends` list stored inside the object. It provides read‑only access to the implicit dependency list maintained by the command. The function’s body is a single `return` statement, exposing the internal list without copying or modifying it.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetJobPool@k_ZNK15cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetJobPool@k_ZNK15cmC.body: The function is a const member accessor that returns a read‑only reference to the internal `JobPool` string. It simply hands back the stored value without copying or mutating it, and being marked `const` guarantees it cannot modify the object.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetJobserverAware@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetJobserverAware@k_Z.body: This accessor simply returns the value stored in the private `JobserverAware` member. It lets callers query whether the current `cmCustomCommand` instance is marked as aware of the job‑server. No validation or side‑effects occur; the call is read‑only.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetMainDependency@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetMainDependency@k_Z.body: It returns a reference to the first dependency stored in the object, after asserting that the object is marked as having a main dependency.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetOutputs@k_ZNK15cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetOutputs@k_ZNK15cmC.body: Returns a reference to the internal `Outputs` member. The function is `const`, so the returned vector cannot be modified through the reference.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetStdPipesUTF8@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetStdPipesUTF8@k_ZNK.body: This method simply returns the value of the `StdPipesUTF8` member.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetTarget@k_ZNK15cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetTarget@k_ZNK15cmCu.body: The `GetTarget` method is a const accessor that hands back a reference to the internal string member `Target`. It guarantees that no state can be altered, and avoids copying by returning the reference directly.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetUsesTerminal@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetUsesTerminal@k_ZNK.body: Returns the value of the `UsesTerminal` flag stored in the object, exposing whether the command is intended to use a terminal interface. The method is a trivial, read‑only accessor.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetWorkingDirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetWorkingDirectory@k.body: This member function simply exposes the internal path stored in the object. When called, it returns a read‑only reference to the string that holds the current working directory, ensuring the caller cannot modify the underlying value.

@lcmCustomCommand::HasMainDependency@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::HasMainDependency@k_Z.body: It returns the internal flag that indicates whether the current instance is marked as having a main dependency.

@lcmCustomCommand::RecordPolicyValues@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::RecordPolicyValues@k_.body: The routine loops over every policy defined by the macro `CM_FOR_EACH_CUSTOM_COMMAND_POLICY` and assigns each policy’s current status from the given snapshot to the corresponding member in the object (e.g. `this->ReadPolicyStatus = snapshot.GetPolicy(cmPolicies::Read);`). It relies on the helper macro to generate the assignment code for all policy types automatically.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetBacktrace@k_ZN15cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetBacktrace@k_ZN15cm.body: The function assigns the passed‑in `cmListFileBacktrace` instance to the class member `Backtrace` by moving the argument into it. It relies on `std::move` to transfer ownership without copying, so the input object should not be accessed after the call. The operation is O(1) and preserves the original object’s state only if it supports move semantics. No additional validation or safety checks are performed, so callers should guarantee the argument is in a valid state before invoking this setter.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetByproducts@k_ZN15c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetByproducts@k_ZN15c.body: The function assigns the supplied vector of strings to the object’s internal `Byproducts` member by moving the argument into the member variable.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetCommandExpandLists.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetCommandExpandLists.body: The method assigns the supplied Boolean value to the internal flag `CommandExpandLists`, effectively toggling the expansion state used elsewhere in the class.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetCommandLines@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetCommandLines@k_ZN1.body: Moves the supplied `cmCustomCommandLines` instance into the internal member, transferring ownership without copying.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetComment@k_ZN15cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetComment@k_ZN15cmCu.body: Assigns the supplied C‑string to the object’s comment member, using an empty string when the pointer is null, and sets a flag to indicate whether a comment was supplied.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetDepends@k_ZN15cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetDepends@k_ZN15cmCu.body: SetDepends replaces the command’s internal dependency list with the supplied vector. If the command already has a primary dependency (`HasMainDependency_`), it prepends that first dependency to the new list before assigning it to the member.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetDependsExplicitOnl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetDependsExplicitOnl.body: This method assigns the supplied Boolean to the internal flag `DependsExplicitOnly`, toggling whether the object should treat its dependencies as strictly explicit during its internal logic.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetDepfile@k_ZN15cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetDepfile@k_ZN15cmCu.body: The `SetDepfile` method simply assigns the provided string to the `Depfile` member; it accepts a const reference to avoid unnecessary copying and exposes the new value immediately for later use. No additional validation or side‑effects are performed within the method.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetEscapeAllowMakeVar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetEscapeAllowMakeVar.body: This method toggles the internal flag that controls whether escape characters are permitted when constructing Makefile variables.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetEscapeOldStyle@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetEscapeOldStyle@k_Z.body: Sets the internal flag that toggles the legacy “escape‑style” mode. The method simply stores the supplied boolean in the member variable `EscapeOldStyle`.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetImplicitDepends@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetImplicitDepends@k_.body: The method simply assigns the supplied list of implicit dependencies to the member variable `ImplicitDepends`. It performs a shallow copy of the argument (a reference to a const‑qualified list) into the object’s own data member, replacing any previous value. This is a straightforward setter – no validation, no side‑effects, and it assumes the caller has already prepared a valid list.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetJobPool@k_ZN15cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetJobPool@k_ZN15cmCu.body: Assigns the provided string to the object’s internal `JobPool` member, effectively updating the instance’s job‑pool setting.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetJobserverAware@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetJobserverAware@k_Z.body: Sets the internal flag that indicates whether the object should act aware of a job server.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetMainDependency@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetMainDependency@k_Z.body: The method replaces the first element of `Depends` if one already exists; otherwise, if the supplied string is non‑empty, it inserts that string at the front of the `Depends` vector and marks that a main dependency now exists. An empty string when no dependency has been set results in no modification.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetOutputs@k_ZN15cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetOutputs@k_ZN15cmCu.body: Assigns the supplied string to the internal member `Outputs` by moving the argument into it.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetOutputs@k_ZN15cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetOutputs@k_ZN15cmCu.body: The `SetOutputs` method assigns the passed vector of strings to the `Outputs` member using move semantics, thereby transferring ownership of the string data without copying and ensuring the internal state reflects the supplied values.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetStdPipesUTF8@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetStdPipesUTF8@k_ZN1.body: Sets the internal flag that determines if standard pipes should use UTF‑8 encoding.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetTarget@k_ZN15cmCus.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetTarget@k_ZN15cmCus.body: Assigns the supplied string to the `Target` member of the `cmCustomCommand` instance.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetUsesTerminal@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetUsesTerminal@k_ZN1.body: The method assigns the supplied flag to the internal `UsesTerminal` member, toggling the component’s use of terminal‑attached functionality.

@lcmCustomCommand::SetWorkingDirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::SetWorkingDirectory@k.body: The function assigns the supplied path string to the object’s WorkingDirectory member, defaulting to an empty string when the pointer is null.

@lcmCustomCommand::cmCustomCommand@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::cmCustomCommand@k_ZN1.body: cmCustomCommand is a public entry point that accepts a command payload—typically a string or structured request—dispatches it to a dedicated handler, performs validation and any necessary side‑effects, and finally returns a status indicator (often a boolean or error code).

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::AppendArgume.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::AppendArgume.body: The `AppendArguments` routine builds a command string by first adding any cross‑compiler emulation arguments (if present) and then appending the command‑specific arguments that follow that emulator. It escapes each argument according to the current escape strategy (old‑style or the newer `EscapeForShell` routine), taking care to switch back to the normal `MakeVars` logic when appropriate. This produces a ready‑to‑run string that contains all required arguments in the correct order.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::FillEmulator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::FillEmulator.body: The method checks whether cross‑compiling is enabled; if it is, it scans each command, looks up the target that corresponds to the command’s first argument, and if that target has an emulator property, it expands that property’s value into the command’s argument list.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetArgv0Loca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetArgv0Loca.body: The function checks whether the first argument of a command line refers to a target that can be executed (an imported executable or an executable in a cross‑compiling environment). If that target is valid and matches the required type, it returns the target’s location string; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetByproduct.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetByproduct.body: It provides read‑only access to the internal list of product names: the method returns a constant reference to the stored vector, so callers can inspect the collection without any copying or mutation.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetCC@k_ZNK2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetCC@k_ZNK2.body: The function returns a reference to the internal `cmCustomCommand` stored in the object. It simply dereferences the internal pointer `CC` and delivers the referenced command. The method guarantees that the returned reference cannot be modified (`const`), preserving the immutability of the command instance.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetCommand@k.body: The function returns a command string for a given index. It first tries to retrieve an emulator entry via `GetCrossCompilingEmulator`; if that yields a non‑empty vector, it returns the first element. If no emulator is found, it falls back to `GetArgv0Location` and returns that location string if available. Finally, if neither source supplies a string, it returns the pre‑stored command from `CommandLines[c][0]`.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetComment@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetComment@k.body: Retrieves a comment string from the `CC` object. If the pointer is null or points to an empty string it returns an empty optional. Otherwise it builds a `cmGeneratorExpression` using the current CMake instance and the back‑trace from `CC`, then runs the comment through `EvaluateComment` with the current language generator and output configuration, returning the resulting string wrapped in an `optional`.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetCrossComp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetCrossComp.body: This method returns the emulator‑argument list for the requested index; if the index is beyond the stored range, it yields an empty vector.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetDepends@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetDepends@k.body: Returns a const reference to the internal `Depends` vector so callers can inspect the list of dependency strings without modifying it.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetDepfile@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetDepfile@k.body: It pulls the dependency‑file path from its compiler context. If the path is empty, it simply yields an empty string. Otherwise it builds a generator expression from the stored back‑trace and evaluates the dependency path with the current language‑generator and output configuration, returning the resolved value.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetFullDepfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetFullDepfi.body: The function resolves the full path of the dependency file: it first retrieves the relative depfile name, returns an empty string if none, otherwise it prefixes the current binary directory if the file isn’t already an absolute path, and finally normalizes the path before returning it.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetInternalD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetInternalD.body:
Gets the full path of the internal depfile; if that path is empty it returns an empty string.  
Otherwise, if the object’s flag to compute the internal depfile is set, it calculates that path via ComputeInternalDepfile; if not, it falls back to GetInternalDepfileName.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetInternalD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetInternalD.body: The function computes the internal name of a dependency file by hashing the supplied `depfile` name and appending a format‑specific suffix. It picks the suffix (“.d”, “.AdditionalInputs”) according to the current `DepfileFormat` and then concatenates the hash, suffix, and the binary directory to form the final internal dep‑file path.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetNumberOfC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetNumberOfC.body: The method returns the current count of command entries. It casts the size of the internal `CommandLines` container to an `unsigned int` and returns that value.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetOutputs@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetOutputs@k.body: Returns the vector of output strings stored in the object.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetUtilities.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetUtilities.body: The function is a const accessor that returns a read‑only reference to the `Utilities` member of `cmCustomCommandGenerator`. It exposes the internal set of `BT<std::pair<std::string, bool>` objects without allowing modification of that collection.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetWorkingDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetWorkingDi.body: Returns the value stored in the `WorkingDirectory` member – the current working directory for the instance.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::HasOnlyEmpty.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::HasOnlyEmpty.body: It iterates over every string in each custom‑command line stored in `CommandLines`; if it finds any non‑empty string it immediately returns `false`. If no such string is encountered, the function reaches the end of the loops and returns `true`. This means the function simply reports whether all lines are empty.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::cmCustomComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::cmCustomComm.body: This constructor prepares a custom command generator: it stores the command’s configuration, builds the command lines while resolving argument values and optional argument lists, collects any required target dependencies, optionally transforms the depfile when requested, and evaluates the command’s outputs and by‑products.

@lcmCustomCommandLine::cmCustomCommandLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandLine::cmCustomCommandLi.body: It parses the arguments supplied for the custom command line‑style interface, wiring them into the engine’s internal command objects, and dispatches the resulting command flow to the appropriate subsystem.

@lcmCustomCommandLines::cmCustomCommandL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandLines::cmCustomCommandL.body: The constructor creates a new `cmCustomCommandLines` instance by copying the state of the supplied `cmCustomCommandLines` object.

@lcmCustomCommandLines::cmCustomCommandL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandLines::cmCustomCommandL.body: The function gathers the custom command strings that the rest of the code needs and returns them in the form expected by callers.

@lcmCustomCommandLines::~cmCustomCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandLines::~cmCustomCommand.body: The `~cmCustomCommandLines` routine acts as a convenience wrapper that exposes a uniform interface for registering custom command‑line arguments in the CMake infrastructure. When invoked, it takes a specification of the desired command‑line flags, processes any necessary defaults or validation, and then records the mapping in the global command registry so that subsequent command‑line parsing can recognize and properly dispatch those arguments.

@lcmCxxModuleExportInfoDeleter::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCxxModuleExportInfoDeleter::operator.body: The method simply frees the memory owned by the supplied pointer by calling `delete`. It’s a public const member that accepts a `cmCxxModuleExportInfo*` and performs the deallocation.

@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::ApplyToTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::ApplyToTarget.body: It invokes the logic that was built during construction—walking through the stored mapping and applying the recorded effects to the supplied `cmTarget` instance.

@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::GetHash@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::GetHash@k_ZNK.body:
The member `Hash` holds the pre‑computed hash string. The accessor simply returns a reference to that string, guaranteeing callers read the value without copying it. Because the function is marked `const`, it cannot modify `Hash`, and the compiler guarantees the returned reference will not outlive the lifetime of the `cmCxxModuleUsageEffects` instance.

Potential pitfalls to keep in mind:

* **Lifetime** – The reference is only valid while the owning object exists; any attempt to use the reference after the object is destroyed will result in undefined behavior.  
* **Aliasing writes** – Even though the return type is a `const&`, a caller could still cast away the constness and modify the string, corrupting the internal state.  
* **Thread safety** – If multiple threads may access the same instance, the reference itself is read‑only, but external code must ensure no concurrent mutation of `Hash` occurs.  

These considerations make the simple getter robust and easy to use while guarding against accidental misuse.

@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::cmCxxModuleUs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::cmCxxModuleUs.body:
The function is a move‑constructor for the `cmCxxModuleUsageEffects` class.  
It accepts an rvalue reference, transfers internal state to the new instance, and thus avoids expensive copying of the underlying effect data.  
It is invoked in various parts of the code whenever an existing `cmCxxModuleUsageEffects` object needs to be transferred to another object.

@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::cmCxxModuleUs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::cmCxxModuleUs.body: The constructor of `cmCxxModuleUsageEffects` receives a pointer to a `cmGeneratorTarget` and initializes an internal hash with a fixed string. Inside the constructor, the implementation is expected to inspect the supplied generator target to gather whatever information could influence how a C++ module is consumed or generated. The body is currently a placeholder for that logic.

@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::cmCxxModuleUs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCxxModuleUsageEffects::cmCxxModuleUs.body: Constructs a new instance by copying the state from an existing `cmCxxModuleUsageEffects` object. The constructor performs a deep copy of internal data members, ensuring the new object mirrors the original state without sharing mutable resources. It guarantees that any dynamic resources are duplicated, not referenced, preserving encapsulation integrity.

@lcmDebugger::GetStackTraceResponse@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::GetStackTraceResponse@k_ZN.body: The routine acquires the thread’s lock, walks backward through its stored call‑stack frames, and for each frame builds a `StackFrame` object: it records file name, line number, and frame identifier and packages these into the response’s `stackFrames` list, finally setting `totalFrames` to the list’s size before returning the populated `StackTraceResponse`.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::ClearSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::ClearSt.body: It clears any pending stepping state by resetting the next‑step indicator to “none”, turning the step‑in flag off, clearing the depth counter, and disabling any pause request that might still be pending.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnBegin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnBegin.body: Creates a new shared `cmListFileFunction` for the source file and pushes it onto the current thread’s stack so the parsing machinery knows what file and arguments to handle.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnBegin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnBegin.body: When a function call begins, the debugger acquires a mutex, records the call frame, and then checks whether the current line matches any active breakpoints. If a breakpoint or a step request (step‑in, step‑out, or pause) is pending, it clears the step‑requests, signals the session with a stopped event (specifying the reason and any breakpoint IDs hit), and then blocks on a semaphore until the session resumes execution.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnEndFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnEndFi.body: The method finalises the file‑parse context by removing the current stack frame from the default thread’s call stack and resetting the internal pointer that tracks the list of file‑level functions. This ensures the parser’s state is clean before handling the next file or terminating.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnEndFu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnEndFu.body: When a debugging session finishes a function invocation, this routine removes the corresponding stack frame from the current thread’s call stack. It effectively restores the thread’s execution context to the state prior to that function call, ensuring that any nested frames are correctly discarded and that the thread is ready for the next operation.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnFileP.body: When a source file finishes parsing, this routine forwards the file’s path and the list of functions found in it to the breakpoint manager, letting the manager register the file’s functions and set up any breakpoints that should be associated with that source.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnMessa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::OnMessa.body:
When a debugger receives an output message, `OnMessageOutput` asks the `ExceptionManager` whether that message should trigger an exception event.  
If an exception is produced, the function stamps the event with the current thread’s ID, forwards it to the debug session, and then blocks until a resume signal (`ContinueSem`) is received before returning.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::ReportE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::ReportE.body: The function finalizes the current thread by sending an exit‑code event, a termination event, and a thread‑exit event to the debugging session; it then blocks until the session acknowledges the disconnect.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::cmDebug.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::cmDebug.body: The constructor initializes a debugging adapter that ties a CMake‑generated program to a DAP session. It wires a shared `cmDebuggerConnection` into the adapter, installs a logger if supplied, and clears any queued breakpoints. It then creates the session, breakpoint and exception managers, registers all request handlers for initialization, thread enumeration, stack traces, variable evaluation, and control flow operations (pause, continue, step‑in/out, next). As part of its setup it also hooks error callbacks to tear down the session and signals a disconnect event. Finally, it starts listening for a client and spawns a worker thread that consumes payloads from the DAP session until the session terminates.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::cmDebug.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::cmDebug.body: The constructor stores the passed connection and, if a path is supplied, creates an optional `dap::Writer` that writes to that file; otherwise the log writer is left empty. It forwards these values to the base `cmDebuggerAdapter` class that handles the underlying debugger connection.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::cmDebug.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::cmDebug.body: The constructor creates a new adapter by copying the state of an existing one, re‑initializing its internal components (e.g., event sources, debug‑state trackers) so that the new instance operates with the same configuration and lifecycle hooks as the original.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::operato.body: `operator=` implements the copy‑assignment operator for `cmDebuggerAdapter`. It takes a const reference to another adapter instance, copies its internal state into the current object (typically by invoking a helper such as `copyFrom` or assigning member variables directly), then returns `*this` to allow chaining of assignments. No additional side‑effects are performed beyond the usual copy semantics.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::~cmDebu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerAdapter::~cmDebu.body: The destructor ensures a clean shutdown: it blocks until the session thread finishes (joining it if joinable), then clears the current session object and, if a log file is open, flushes and closes that file before the object is reclaimed.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: It scans the list of functions for the requested file, picks the first function whose start line is at or after the supplied line, and returns that line number. If the line falls after the final function’s end, it returns the start of that last function; otherwise, if no such function is found, it returns 0.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The `ClearAll` function acquires the internal mutex with a `unique_lock` and then empties the breakpoints container, ensuring that all breakpoints are removed safely without race conditions.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The routine searches a pre‑built map of function ranges for the requested file; if the supplied line falls within any stored range it returns that range’s start line, otherwise it yields 0.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The function returns the total number of breakpoints by iterating over the `Breakpoints` collection and summing the sizes of each breakpoint set.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The function implements an overload of the arrow‑operator that inspects a `cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint` instance and returns a `bool`. It performs the minimal work necessary to query the breakpoint state and reports success or failure to the caller, enabling callers to use the breakpoint in a boolean context without needing an explicit method call.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The lambda is a predicate that, given a breakpoint, returns `true` only when the breakpoint is marked valid and its line number equals the desired `line`. It is used to locate a breakpoint that matches those criteria in a collection.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The routine locks the global breakpoint container, looks up the list for the requested file, then scans that list with a lambda‑based find‑if loop, pushing each matching breakpoint’s ID into a result vector. The code uses a linear search with `std::find_if` (which isn’t actually in the standard library) and calls `emplace_back` on the vector – both of which will not compile; the intended logic is to push IDs into the vector (e.g., `breakpoints.push_back(it->GetId());`). The function returns the collected IDs; if none exist it simply returns an empty vector.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body:
The function receives a set‑breakpoints request, acquires a lock, and then

1. removes any existing breakpoints for the request’s source file,  
2. stores each requested line as a new breakpoint (assigning a fresh id),  
3. if the file’s source is already loaded, validates the line numbers (adjusting them with CalibrateBreakpointLine) and marks the breakpoint as verified; otherwise it flags the line for later validation;  
4. builds a response list mirroring the input, populating each breakpoint’s id, line, source path, and verified flag, and finally returns that response.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: When a source file is loaded, the manager updates its internal records for that file: it records the function‑line ranges, clears any pending validation flag, then walks through the breakpoints that belong to that file, recalculates each breakpoint’s line number (if the project source differs from the runtime view), marks the breakpoint verified or invalid, and finally emits a breakpoint event for the debugger session.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The operator function receives a SetBreakpointsRequest, validates its fields, updates the internal breakpoint table accordingly, and returns a SetBreakpointsResponse that reports success or any errors that occurred during the update.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: Captures the current context and forwards any incoming `dap::SetBreakpointsRequest` to `HandleSetBreakpointsRequest`, returning that function’s result.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The move constructor of `cmDebuggerBreakpointManager` takes an rvalue reference to another instance and efficiently transfers its internal breakpoint data and auxiliary state to the new object, avoiding expensive copies while preserving correct resource ownership.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The constructor of `cmDebuggerBreakpointManager` takes a `dap::Session*` and stores it in its `DapSession` member. It immediately registers a handler for `dap::SetBreakpointsRequest` that forwards each incoming request to the `HandleSetBreakpointsRequest` method.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The constructor creates a new breakpoint manager by copying the internal breakpoint registry and configuration flags from an existing instance. It performs a shallow copy of the breakpoint map, ensuring that the new instance maintains its own mutable state while preserving the original's breakpoint configurations.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The move‑assignment operator copies the internal state of the right‑hand side object into the left‑hand side object. It swaps the internal breakpoint data, ensuring that after the assignment the left‑hand object holds the new breakpoint configuration while the right‑hand object is left in a valid but unspecified state.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: Assigns all member data from a source instance to the current object, returning a reference to the object for chaining.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerBreakpointManage.body: The destructor `~cmDebuggerBreakpointManager()` cleans up all internal state—clearing its breakpoint list, deallocating any allocated tables, and resetting the internal bookkeeping flags so that no dangling references remain.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::GetR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::GetR.body:
`GetReader` is a pure virtual function that a concrete subclass must override.  
When called, it returns a `std::shared_ptr<dap::Reader>` that the implementation creates or retrieves.  
The function is typically used to provide the caller with a reader instance capable of performing the required read‑operations, often without exposing the concrete reader type.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::GetW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::GetW.body: The function is a pure virtual accessor that derived debugger adapters must implement to supply an instance of `dap::Writer`. It returns a `std::shared_ptr<dap::Writer>`, enabling shared ownership of the writer object so callers can safely use and store the returned pointer without risking premature destruction.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::Star.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::Star.body: The function `StartListening` is a public pure virtual member. Implementations must initiate the listening process for a specific adapter; they return `true` on success or `false` on failure, optionally writing a diagnostic string into `errorMessage`. It is intended to be overridden in concrete adapter classes that perform the actual listening logic.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::Wait.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::Wait.body: The `WaitForConnection()` method is a pure virtual member that obligates every concrete subclass to block until a new communication channel has successfully opened. When called, the implementation typically performs a blocking wait (for example, a `std::condition_variable` wait or an event‑signaled loop) until the underlying socket or IPC socket reports an active connection. No other logic follows – the method simply provides a synchronization point for derived classes to signal that the debugger is ready to receive or send commands.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::oper.body: Copies internal connection data from the source instance into the current instance and returns a reference to that instance for chaining.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::~cmD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerConnection::~cmD.body: The destructor `~cmDebuggerConnection()` is declared virtual so derived debugger adapters can override cleanup behaviour. It ensures that when a `cmDebuggerAdapter` is destroyed via a base‑type pointer, the appropriate derived destructor runs, freeing any resources (e.g., sockets, files, or internal state) that the concrete connection implementation acquires.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The routine acquires the shared mutex, then empties the internal exception list.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The function acquires a lock on `Mutex`, then prepares an `ExceptionInfoResponse`. If `TheException` holds a value, it copies its `Id` and `Description` into the response and sets `breakMode` to `"always"`. Finally it clears `TheException` and returns the populated response.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The function locks the internal mutex, sets the `supportsExceptionInfoRequest` flag to true, then iterates over the global `ExceptionMap` to build a list of `ExceptionBreakpointsFilter` objects (copying each entry’s filter, label, and default exception handler) and finally assigns that list to `response.exceptionBreakpointFilters`.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The routine acquires the global mutex, wipes out any previously‑registered exception flags, then iterates over the supplied filter list and records each one as enabled by inserting a flag into the shared map. It returns an empty success response.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The operator overload hashes the given `MessageType` by converting it to an `int` via `static_cast` and then applying the standard `std::hash<int>` functor. Because the conversion is performed at compile‑time, no runtime checks or exception handling are required, but the caller must guarantee that `MessageType` is implicitly or explicitly convertible to an `int`. The function is `const`, so it does not modify any object state, and the hash calculation is O(1) in time.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The function checks if the current exception type matches a configured filter. If a match is found, it creates a `dap::StoppedEvent` marked as a pause on exception, attaches the provided text, stores the exception details in `TheException`, and returns the event wrapped in an `optional`. If no filter matches, it returns an empty optional.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The function is a move‑constructor that takes an rvalue reference to a `cmDebuggerExceptionManager` instance. It transfers ownership of the internal exception‑handling state—such as registered callbacks, internal buffers, and any pending exception records—into the new object while guaranteeing the source is left in a safe, destructible state. This ensures that exception handlers are correctly transferred during container moves or re‑initializations without leaking resources or duplicating callbacks.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The constructor registers request handlers for the DAP protocol, initializes a mapping of message types to `cmDebuggerExceptionFilter` objects that associate a tag and a display string, and enables automatic exception raising for specific error categories (AUTHOR_ERROR, FATAL_ERROR, INTERNAL_ERROR, and DEPRECATION_ERROR).

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The copy constructor initializes a new `cmDebuggerExceptionManager` instance by duplicating the configuration and handler collections from the supplied source object. It preserves the current exception‑handling settings, ensuring the new instance behaves identically to the original while maintaining its own internal state.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The move‑assignment operator `operator=` takes an rvalue of `cmDebuggerExceptionManager`, transfers its internal state into the current instance and returns `*this`. It efficiently swaps the exception manager’s contents without copying.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: Copies all internal data from the supplied `cmDebuggerExceptionManager` instance into the current object, then returns a reference to the updated instance.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerExceptionManager.body: The function initializes and registers the debugger’s global exception handling routine, wiring the system to intercept and route exception events to the debugging infrastructure during normal operation.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerFunctionLocation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerFunctionLocation.body: This function retrieves the debugger’s internal representation of a function’s source location, typically used by the breakpoint manager to map breakpoints to the correct source file and line number.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.body: Creates a UNIX‑domain socket, stores its descriptor in `rw_pipe`, and then attempts to connect that socket to the address supplied by `PipeName`. If the socket creation fails or the `connect()` call fails, it closes the socket (if already open) and throws a `std::runtime_error` with a message that includes the system error string.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.body: The close method checks whether the pipe is still open; if so, it calls ::close on the descriptor and then sets the member variable to –1 to mark the socket as closed.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.body: The constructor simply moves the supplied string into the member variable `PipeName`. It initializes that member with the provided name, using move semantics to avoid copying.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.body: The constructor creates a new POSIX‑backed debugger client by copying the internal state from the supplied instance. It performs a shallow copy of the member handles that represent the pipe endpoints and any configuration flags, ensuring the new object is immediately ready to send and receive debugger protocol messages over the existing pipe. The copy semantics are defined so that both objects can coexist without interfering with each other’s underlying file descriptors.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.body: The `isOpen()` function simply evaluates whether the underlying POSIX pipe descriptor `rw_pipe` is valid by checking that it is non‑negative; if `rw_pipe` is `>= 0`, the function returns `true`, otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.body: This function implements the copy‑assignment operator for the `cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX` class. When invoked, it copies all of the source object's internal state into the current instance and returns a reference to the receiver so that the assignment can be chained. The implementation is straightforward: it first guards against self‑assignment, then copies each data member in turn, and finally returns `*this`. This operator is used throughout the code whenever a `cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX` instance needs to be replaced with another’s configuration or connection data.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.body: The function reads up to `n` bytes from the internal pipe when it’s open. It casts the result of the POSIX `read()` call to an `int`, stores it in `count`, and if that read yields exactly zero bytes, it shuts the pipe by calling `close()`. Finally the byte count is returned.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.body: Writes up to `n` bytes from `buffer` to the POSIX pipe if the client is open, then returns `true` if any bytes were written. On a negative return value it aborts the connection by invoking `close()`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX.body: The destructor for `cmDebuggerPipeClient_POSIX` simply invokes the cleanup routine for the underlying POSIX pipe—ensuring that the file descriptor is closed and any associated resources are released before the object is reclaimed.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: This `GetReader` simply hands back the current instance as a `dap::Reader` shared pointer. It uses `shared_from_this()` to retrieve the `shared_ptr` that owns this object, then casts that pointer to the base type `dap::Reader` via `static_pointer_cast`. The caller receives a `std::shared_ptr<dap::Reader>` that refers to the same underlying object, enabling read‑only operations on the connection without exposing implementation details.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: The `GetWriter` method returns a `std::shared_ptr<dap::Writer>` that points to the current object. It obtains the `shared_from_this()` pointer (which is a `shared_ptr` to the base type) and then performs a `static_pointer_cast` to the `dap::Writer` type, yielding a pointer of that type that can be returned to callers.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: Creates a UNIX‑domain socket, binds it to the configured pipe path, starts listening, and records the listening state. If any system call fails, it populates `errorMessage` with the failure reason and returns `false`; otherwise it flags the listener as started and returns `true`.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: The function accepts a new TCP connection on the listening socket (`listen_fd`). It stores the resulting socket descriptor in `rw_pipe`. If the `accept` call fails, it calls `close()` and returns immediately. Once a connection is accepted, the listening socket is closed via `close_listen()`, freeing the listening resources.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: The function stops listening on the pipe, closes the underlying file descriptor with the system‑level `close()`, and then marks the connection as closed by setting `rw_pipe` to –1.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: The function removes the Unix‑domain socket file (if its path is non‑empty) by calling `unlink`, then clears the path string and finally closes the listening socket descriptor, resetting it to -1.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: The constructor assigns the supplied name to the member storing the pipe identifier and clears the socket address buffer so that the `sun_path` field starts empty.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: Copies the state of an existing POSIX‑pipe connection into a new instance. It transfers ownership of the underlying file‑descriptor, clones the internal buffers and flags, and re‑initializes any per‑connection bookkeeping to match the supplied source.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: The method merely reports whether the internal descriptor `rw_pipe` is non‑negative, which is the standard flag for an active POSIX pipe.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: Assigns the internal state of a `cmDebuggerPipeConnection_POSIX` instance to the current instance, performing a deep copy of its internal members.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: The `read` function attempts a blocking read on the file descriptor stored in `rw_pipe`. If data is read successfully, it forwards the byte count to the caller. A zero return triggers an automatic `close()` call to terminate the connection. Errors from the underlying `read` call are silently ignored (no explicit error handling or retry logic).

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: The function is a virtual wrapper that forwards a buffer write request to the underlying POSIX pipe file descriptor. It checks that the descriptor is valid (≥ 0); if so, it attempts to write the requested number of bytes. The result of the write system call (≥ 0 means success) is stored in *result*. If that write fails, the function invokes its own *close* routine to tear down the connection. Finally, it returns *result*, indicating success (true) or failure (false).

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerPipeConnection_P.body: The destructor checks whether the pipe remains open; if so, it invokes the internal `close()` routine to release the file descriptor and any associated resources, guaranteeing that no dangling handles survive after the object’s lifetime ends.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: The function simply returns the value of the internal member `IsValid`. Because it only reads an already‑stored boolean and performs no dynamic allocation or exception‑throwing, it’s marked `noexcept`. The method is `const`, so callers are guaranteed it won’t modify the object. It’s a lightweight accessor that callers can use in validation checks, but only after the object’s state has been properly established—otherwise it may expose stale or uninitialized data.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: Returns the stored line identifier in a noexcept, const‑qualified getter.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetId@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetId@k_.body: The member function simply exposes the 64‑bit identifier stored in the object. Because it’s declared const, it guarantees it does not alter any member state, so callers can safely use it in multi‑thread contexts where the object remains immutable. However, callers must still ensure that the underlying `Id` field is initialized; otherwise the function would return an indeterminate value. Since the body performs only a single read, it imposes negligible overhead.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetName@.body: `GetName()` is a simple, read‑only accessor that returns a reference to the internal `Name` member. It is marked `const`, so calling it does not alter object state, and callers receive a read‑only reference that avoids a copy of the string. The function simply returns the stored name value.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetScope.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetScope.body: The method first protects data with a mutex lock, then looks up a pre‑built scope list in `FrameScopes`. If found, it immediately returns that list. Otherwise it falls back to the frame map, and if the frame is missing it returns an empty response. When the frame is present, it creates a new local‑variables helper instance, stores that helper in `FrameVariables`, builds a `dap::Scope` object (setting name, hint, and variable reference), attaches the source information from the frame, pushes the scope into the per‑frame scope list and finally returns a response containing that single scope.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetStack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetStack.body: This function locks the debugger’s internal mutex, looks up the requested frame ID in `FrameMap`, and returns the stored `std::shared_ptr<cmDebuggerStackFrame>` if present; otherwise it returns an empty (null) pointer.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetStack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetStack.body: It returns the current number of frames stored in the object’s internal container, exposing that count to callers without altering any state.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetTopSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetTopSt.body: The function locks the thread’s mutex, checks if the internal `Frames` container has any frames, and if so returns a shared pointer to the most‑recent frame (`Frames.back()`). If the container is empty, it returns an empty `shared_ptr` (i.e. a null pointer).

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetVaria.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::GetVaria.body: The function acquires a mutex lock, delegates the request to the `VariablesManager`, stores the returned variables in a `VariablesResponse` object, and returns that populated response.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::PopStack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::PopStack.body: `PopStackFrame` removes the most recent frame from the debugger’s internal stacks. It locks the mutex to protect the shared maps, deletes the frame’s entries from `FrameMap`, `FrameScopes`, and `FrameVariables`, and finally pops the frame from the `Frames` vector.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::PushStac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::PushStac.body: It acquires the shared mutex, creates a new shared‑pointer to a `cmDebuggerStackFrame` using the supplied parameters, pushes that frame onto the `Frames` vector, and records it in `FrameMap` keyed by the frame’s ID. No additional logic beyond synchronisation and insertion.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::cmDebugg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::cmDebugg.body: The function creates and starts a debugger thread by taking an rvalue reference to a `cmDebuggerThread` instance, initializing the thread context, and executing the debugger loop until termination.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::cmDebugg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::cmDebugg.body: Creates a new `cmDebuggerThread` instance by copying the state from an existing one, initializing the internal debugging context and thread resources for the new debugging session.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::cmDebugg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::cmDebugg.body: The constructor sets the thread’s `Id` and `Name` members, then creates a shared instance of `cmDebuggerVariablesManager` to manage the thread’s variables. The new manager is stored in the `VariablesManager` member.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::operator.body: This `operator=` implements a move‑assignment for `cmDebuggerThread`. It takes an rvalue reference to another `cmDebuggerThread`, transfers ownership of the thread’s internal state (e.g. thread handle, buffers) into the current instance, and returns a reference to `*this`. The implementation must guard against self‑assignment (no‑op when `this == &rhs`), ensure strong exception safety (no partial state left if an internal move throws), and properly reset the source object to a safe state after the move. It also typically clears any pending debug actions in the source before adopting them.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::operator.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of the source instance into the current instance, handling self‑assignment safely and returning a reference to *this.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::~cmDebug.author: AI Short Overview
