@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThread::~cmDebug.body: The `~cmDebuggerThread` destructor cleanly terminates the debugger’s background worker: it signals the running thread to stop, waits for its completion (joining), closes any open sockets or files, and releases all owned resources before the object is destroyed.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThreadManager::E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThreadManager::E.body:
The `EndThread` function simply erases a thread object from the internal thread list.  
- It receives a shared‑pointer to the thread instance.  
- It invokes `Threads.remove(thread)`, which removes that element from the container that holds all active threads.  
- No further cleanup is performed, so any thread‑specific resources (sockets, locks, etc.) must be released elsewhere to avoid leaks.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThreadManager::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThreadManager::G.body: The routine scans the internal thread list for a thread whose `GetId()` matches the supplied identifier. Upon a match it forwards the thread pointer to `GetStackTraceResponse()` and returns the resulting `StackTraceResponse` wrapped in an `optional`; if no matching thread is found, it yields an empty optional.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThreadManager::S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThreadManager::S.body: The `StartThread` routine constructs a fresh `cmDebuggerThread` instance, hands it a freshly‑incremented identifier via `NextThreadId`, registers that instance in the manager’s internal container (`Threads`), and hands back a `std::shared_ptr` that keeps the new thread alive for any callers that hold a reference to it.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThreadManager::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerThreadManager::c.body: This function defines the default constructor for the `cmDebuggerThreadManager` class, automatically initializing the object with default values.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.body:
The constructor initializes a `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` instance:

* `Name` is set to the supplied string (moved for efficiency).  
* `Value` is set to the supplied C‑string or an empty string if the pointer is `nullptr`.  
* `Type` is hard‑coded to `"string"`.

No additional actions are performed in the constructor body.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.body: Constructs a variable entry by storing the supplied name and value in the member fields, setting the Type member to the literal “string”, and performs the moves with std::move to avoid copy overhead.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.body: The constructor creates a `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` instance, storing the supplied name, value, and type in its member fields. It simply forwards these values into the internal strings without any additional processing.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.body: Initialises a debugger‑variable entry by assigning the supplied name to `Name`, converting the Boolean argument to the literal string `"TRUE"` or `"FALSE"` in `Value`, and marking the entry’s type as `"bool"`.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.body: Creates a new debugger‑variable entry by moving the supplied name into the internal `Name` member, converting the supplied integer value to a string for storage in `Value`, and hard‑coding the type string to `"int"`. The constructor therefore simply establishes those three fields via an initializer list, with no additional logic or side‑effects.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.body: Creates a new entry with the supplied name, converts the integer to a string for the Value field, and marks the type as “int”.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.body: The constructor initializes a new `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` by moving the fields of the temporary argument, ensuring the new instance owns all resources without copying. It essentially performs a move‑only assignment so the source instance becomes empty or in a moved‑state.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.body: Creates a new `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` instance by copying the member values from the supplied entry object.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::c.body: This function is a default constructor that forwards empty string arguments to the main constructor, initializing an instance of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` with blank identifiers, values, and types.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::~.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariableEntry::~.body: It creates and registers a single debugger‑friendly variable entry, wiring the variable’s name, type and current value into the debugger’s internal variable table so the UI can query and display its state.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::AddSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::AddSu.body: The function appends a non‑null `cmDebuggerVariables` instance to the internal list `SubVariables`. It checks the pointer is not `nullptr` before inserting, preventing a null dereference.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::Clear.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::Clear.body: When called, the routine discards every element stored in the `SubVariables` collection, effectively resetting that internal container.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::Enume.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::Enume.body: EnumerateSubVariablesIfAny scans a variable’s scope for nested or child variables and, when any are present, iterates over each to expose them in the debugger’s UI. This helper keeps the enumeration logic isolated from the main debugger loop, enabling the UI to lazily fetch only those sub‑variables that actually exist, which keeps the rendering path lean and reduces needless traversal of empty variable trees.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::GetId.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::GetId.body: Retrieves the member `Id` field as a 64‑bit integer. The method is marked `inline`, `const` and `noexcept`, guaranteeing no observable side‑effects and no exceptions during the call.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::GetNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::GetNa.body: The inline getter is marked noexcept and const, returning a copy of the stored string member without modifying any state.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::GetVa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::GetVa.body: Returns the stored string value without modifying state or throwing exceptions.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::Handl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::Handl.body: The function collects runtime variable values by calling a user‑supplied callback, filters out empty‑string entries when `IgnoreEmptyStringEntries` is true, builds `dap::Variable` objects with the provided metadata, and appends them to a list. It then enumerates any nested sub‑variables that may exist and optionally sorts the final list alphabetically by the variable name before returning the array.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetEn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetEn.body: This method assigns the supplied Boolean value to the internal `EnableSorting` flag, toggling whether the object will perform sorting.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetIg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetIg.body: This routine writes the supplied boolean into the internal flag that dictates whether entries with an empty string value are ignored during processing.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetVa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetVa.body: It assigns the supplied string to the member variable, copying the value without throwing any exception. It receives the string by const‑reference, keeps the caller’s data untouched, and guarantees no exceptions are thrown during the assignment.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::cmDeb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::cmDeb.body: The constructor stores the supplied manager, name, and flag, generates a unique Id via `NextId.fetch_add`, and immediately registers a request‑handler callback with the manager. The callback captures `this` and delegates every incoming `VariablesRequest` to the member function `HandleVariablesRequest()`, which supplies the variable data.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::cmDeb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::cmDeb.body: The constructor assigns a unique identifier, stores the supplied name, variable‑type flag, and a callback that returns the current variable set. It then registers this object with the shared manager so that future variable requests are forwarded to its `HandleVariablesRequest` method.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::cmDeb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::cmDeb.body: The constructor initializes a new `cmDebuggerVariables` instance by copying the internal state from an existing instance. It transfers all variable‑level debug information—such as current values, scopes, and any attached metadata—ensuring the new object reflects the exact state of the source object at construction time.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::opera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::opera.body: The operator= overload copies all member values from another cmDebuggerVariables instance into the current object. It performs a deep copy of the internal state (e.g., variable maps, flags, and configuration data) so that after assignment the object reflects exactly the source’s state, including any nested structures such as the internal `variables` map or reference tables. It returns a reference to `*this` to allow chaining.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::~cmDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::~cmDe.body: When an instance of `cmDebuggerVariables` is destroyed, its destructor is invoked. It first calls `ClearSubVariables()` to release any internal sub‑variables, then signals the owning `VariablesManager` to drop the associated handler using `UnregisterHandler(Id)`. This guarantees that no dangling references remain after the object is deallocated.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda builds a vector of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` objects. For each policy ID from 0 to `CMPCOUNT‑1`, it checks whether the ID is defined in the policy map; if so, it fetches the status, formats the ID as `"CMP"` followed by a zero‑padded 4‑digit number, and stores the ID‑string and status‑string pair in the vector, which is returned.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The function builds a `cmDebuggerVariables` instance that reports every policy present in the supplied `policyMap`. It walks the fixed set of policy IDs, and whenever a policy is defined it records a pair consisting of a zero‑padded identifier string (“CMPxxxx”) and the textual label (“OLD”, “WARN”, “NEW”, “REQUIRED_IF_USED”, or “REQUIRED_ALWAYS”) of its status. The resulting collection is passed to the new object via a lambda at construction time.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The static `Create` function builds a nested `cmDebuggerVariables` hierarchy: it starts with a root variable that holds the current source line, then adds sub‑variables for the current closure’s locals, for any closure keys that look like directory paths, for each cache entry in the current makefile state, and finally for the ordered targets and the default configuration tests. Each sub‑variable is populated via a lambda that fetches the relevant value (e.g. line number, variable definition, or cache value). The resulting tree is returned as a shared pointer to be used by the debugger.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda maps each `AppleSDK` enum value to its textual name, returning `"Unknown"` if the value isn’t one of the defined cases.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda `makeFileEncodingString` takes a `codecvt_Encoding` value and returns a string literal describing that encoding, defaulting to `"Unknown"` for unrecognized values.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda gathers three pieces of data from a `test` object – the command‑expansion list, the name string, and the old‑style flag – and returns them as a `std::vector` of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` structs.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda takes a `cmFileSetVisibility` value and returns a string describing that value (e.g., `"Private"`, `"Public"`, or `"Interface"`, defaulting to `"Unknown"` when the value is unexpected).

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: It builds a vector of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` objects by copying each key/value pair from the supplied list. It pre‑allocates the result vector to match the list size, iterates over the list, pushes a new entry for each pair, and returns the populated vector.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda collects each string in `values` into a vector of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` objects, assigning a key of the form “[index]” (where the index is incremented per iteration) for each value, and finally returns that vector.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda creates a vector of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` objects. It first reserves space for the number of incoming values, then walks through that list, appending each value prefixed with an index in brackets (`[0]`, `[1]`, …). Finally it returns the filled vector.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: Creates a `std::vector<cmDebuggerVariableEntry>` containing each element of the input list paired with its zero‑based index encoded as a string (`"[0]"`, `[1]`, …). It reserves space for the list size, iterates over the list, pushes each entry into the vector, and finally returns that vector.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda constructs and returns a `std::vector<cmDebuggerVariableEntry>` populated with key‑value pairs obtained from the `mf` instance: define‑flags, directory identifiers, and platform flags such as 32‑bit/64‑bit, x32, Apple SDK type, and whether the current file is the root makefile.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: A lambda that pulls a set of named settings from a generator object and packs them into a vector of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` pairs – each entry maps a variable name (e.g. “AllTargetName”) to the corresponding value returned by the generator. The function simply returns that collection.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda creates and returns a `std::vector` of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` structs that capture the `Name`, `Type`, and `Visibility` of a `fileSet` instance by calling its accessors and converting the visibility to a string.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: If the supplied `cmMakefile` pointer is non‑null, the function instantiates a `cmDebuggerVariables` object populated with a set of key/value pairs extracted from the makefile (flags, directories, SDK type, platform flags, etc.), then attaches sub‑collections for the file lists returned by `GetListFiles()` and `GetOutputFiles()`. If the pointer is null, it immediately returns an empty `std::shared_ptr` (i.e. `nullptr`).

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The function generates a collection of debugger‑variables by pulling metadata from a supplied generator object. It immediately exits with an empty pointer if the generator is null, otherwise it builds a `cmDebuggerVariables` instance populated with a predefined list of name/value pairs obtained via the generator’s accessor methods. When the generator offers an “InstallComponents” sub‑generator, the function recurses into itself to embed that sub‑generator’s variables as a nested entry. Finally, it disables empty‑string filtering and tags the variable set with the generator’s primary name before returning the shared pointer.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The function returns a new `cmDebuggerVariables` instance populated with the test’s properties; it first checks whether the supplied `cmTest` is null, returning an empty pointer if so. It then constructs a shared object containing the test’s command‑expand lists, name, and old‑style flags, and recursively attaches sub‑variables for the test’s command and properties lists.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body:
Creates a `cmDebuggerVariables` instance that holds information about a `cmFileSet`.  
The routine builds an array of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` objects containing the set’s name, type, and visibility string (derived from `cmFileSetVisibility`).  
It then attaches any sub‑sets as nested variables by recursively calling `CreateIfAny` on the directory and file collections returned by `GetDirectoryEntries()` and `GetFileEntries()`.  
Finally it returns the populated `shared_ptr` to the caller.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: Creates a `cmDebuggerVariables` only when the provided test list isn’t empty. It builds the main variable, adds a sub‑variable for every test recursively, assigns the variable’s value to the count of tests, and finally returns the shared pointer.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The `cmDebuggerVariablesHelper` helper function is used internally to set up and maintain the internal state of debugging‑related variables. It typically pulls current debugger information (such as variable scopes, breakpoints, and thread contexts), normalises that data, and stores the result in a shared structure so that other debugger components can read and modify it in a consistent fashion.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesManager.body: The function looks up a handler keyed by the request’s `variablesReference` and, if found, forwards the request to that handler; otherwise it returns an empty array.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesManager.body: The `RegisterHandler` method associates a function object with a numeric key. It takes an identifier (`id`) and a callable that accepts a `VariablesRequest` and returns a `dap::array<dap::Variable>`. The handler is stored in the `VariablesHandlers` map using `std::move` to transfer ownership, so subsequent lookups can invoke the stored function.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesManager.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesManager.body: The routine invokes the underlying container’s `erase` with the supplied key, discarding the corresponding entry without performing any existence checks or side‑effects.

@lcmDefinePropertyCommand::[lambda_0]@kc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDefinePropertyCommand::[lambda_0]@kc.body: The lambda captures the variable `initializeFromVariable` and, given a C‑style string `prefix`, invokes `cmHasPrefix` to test whether that prefix is present in `initializeFromVariable`. It simply returns the boolean result of that check.

@lcmDefinePropertyCommand@k_Z23cmDefineP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDefinePropertyCommand@k_Z23cmDefineP.body: The function parses a list of arguments to define a new property in a Makefile. It first validates that at least one argument is supplied, then interprets the first argument as the scope (GLOBAL, DIRECTORY, TARGET, SOURCE, TEST, VARIABLE, or CACHED_VARIABLE). Subsequent arguments are parsed into a property name, brief and full documentation strings, an inherited flag, and an optional variable name from which to initialize the property. The code performs a series of checks: ensuring a property name was supplied, confirming that if an “initialize‑from‑variable” is requested the scope is TARGET, verifying that the variable name ends with the property name, contains an underscore, and that it does not start with a reserved prefix. On successful validation it calls `DefineProperty` on the current makefile state with the collected data and returns `true`; otherwise it records an error in the status object and returns `false`.

@lcmDefinitions::ClosureKeys@k_ZN13cmDef.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDependsC::ParseTransform@k_ZN10cmDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsC::ParseTransform@k_ZN10cmDep.body: The function extracts a macro name and its value from a string that follows the pattern `NAME(%)=VALUE`. It finds the delimiter `(%)=`; if absent or at the string’s start, the routine simply returns. When the delimiter is found, the text before it becomes the key and the text after it becomes the value, both trimmed by `substr`. These two strings are stored in the member map `TransformRules`.

@lcmDependsC::ReadCacheFile@k_ZN10cmDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsC::ReadCacheFile@k_ZN10cmDepe.body: The method opens the cache file specified by `CacheFileName`. If the file cannot be opened it returns immediately. It reads the file line‑by‑line, ignoring blank lines that separate entries. For each non‑empty line it treats the first one after a separator as a file name; it then loads that file’s timestamp and compares it with the cache’s timestamp. When the cache entry is newer, the line’s data is used to populate the corresponding entry in `FileCache`. Subsequent non‑empty lines that follow the file name are interpreted as quoted locations and added to the entry’s `UnscannedEntries`. The function also verifies that special marker lines match the expected regex strings (`IncludeRegexLineString`, `IncludeRegexScanString`, etc.), aborting the load if any mismatch occurs.

@lcmDependsC::Scan@k_ZN10cmDependsC4Scan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsC::Scan@k_ZN10cmDependsC4Scan.body: Marks a file as “used”, then walks through its lines: any transform rules are applied, each include directive is parsed by regex, the referenced file’s name is normalised (relative paths resolved to the current directory), and new files that haven’t yet been queued are added to the internal cache and scan‑queue.

@lcmDependsC::SetupTransforms@k_ZN10cmDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsC::SetupTransforms@k_ZN10cmDe.body: The method reads transformation rules from the generator’s makefile, registers each rule by calling `ParseTransform`, and then assembles a single regular‑expression that captures all include/​import lines that match any of those rules; it also records a string representation of the rule set for quick re‑use.

@lcmDependsC::TransformLine@k_ZN10cmDepe.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDependsC::WriteDependencies@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview

It first checks for cached dependencies; if none are found it performs a depth‑first walk over the include graph, using the header‑location cache and include path cache to resolve paths and avoid rescanning already‑visited headers. For every discovered header it records the file, adds it to the dependency list, and writes the list in both the standard make‑file format and a separate internal‑dependency file. If any file cannot be located or an error occurs, the function reports it and returns false.

@lcmDependsC::cmDependsC@k_ZN10cmDepends.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsC::cmDependsC@k_ZN10cmDepends.body: The constructor initializes a dependency‑analysis object for a specific target directory and language. It first asks the associated makefile for any language‑specific include‑regex definitions; if none are defined, it falls back to default patterns. It then compiles those regexes (for a single include line, for scanning matches, and for matching “complain” patterns). With those compiled, it builds string markers to identify such lines in source files. It proceeds to call `SetupTransforms()` to register any language‑specific transformations, and finally reads a cached include list from a language‑specific cache file (e.g. `<lang>.includecache`) to avoid recomputing the same include graph repeatedly.

@lcmDependsCompiler::CheckDependencies@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsCompiler::CheckDependencies@k.body:
The function parses a cached dependency file and updates a map of rules-to‑targets.  
It first reads the file listed in *internalDepFile*, building a map from each rule name to a list of dependent files.  
Then it iterates over every compiler‑generated dependency file in *depFiles*. For each, it verifies the file’s existence, compares modification times against the cached file, and if the cache is stale, it parses the file according to its format (custom, msvc, or gcc).  
During parsing, it removes any entries that fail the supplied *isValidPath* predicate and ensures the source file appears as the first dependency.  
Finally, the parsed list is written back into the supplied *dependencies* map. The function returns *true* only when no newer dependency files were found; otherwise it signals that the cache is out‑of‑date.

@lcmDependsCompiler::WriteDependencies@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsCompiler::WriteDependencies@k.body: The `WriteDependencies` routine serialises the dependency graph into two plain‑text files that a `make`‑driven build system will later read. It walks the supplied dependency map, normalises each target and dependency path to a form that `make` understands (converting relative paths, converting backslashes to slashes, etc.), and emits a “target : dep1 dep2 …” line for each target. If the generator supports long‑line dependencies it emits a line‑continuation directive (`\`) for every subsequent dependency; otherwise each line is terminated with a newline. While emitting these lines it tracks every dependency that is not a concrete file into a set of *phony* targets, which it writes out as empty rules after the normal list. Finally it dumps an “internal” dependency list that records the same graph in a second, more compact format that is used only for internal analysis.

@lcmDependsJavaParserHelper::CurrentClas.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDependsJavaParserHelper::DeallocateP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsJavaParserHelper::DeallocateP.body: The function clears a `char*` pointer by assigning it to `nullptr` after confirming that both the pointer itself and its pointee are non‑null, then decrements a counter (`UnionsAvailable`). It does **not** free the memory; it merely nulls the pointer. As a result, callers must ensure the underlying memory is freed elsewhere, otherwise the allocator will leak. The decrement of `UnionsAvailable` is performed unsafely—if multiple threads invoke the helper concurrently, the counter could be mis‑counted unless protected by a mutex or atomic operation. Renaming the routine to something like `ClearParserPointer` would better convey its intent and avoid confusion that it actually deallocates.

@lcmDependsJava_yyparse@k_Z21cmDependsJa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsJava_yyparse@k_Z21cmDependsJa.body:
**High‑level summary of the code fragment**

*The code is a fully‑generated C parser (likely produced by a tool such as bison or Yacc) for a Java‑like grammar.  
The parser implements a classic table‑driven shift/reduce algorithm:  

| Feature | What it does |
|----------|--------------|
| **Token loop** | The parser repeatedly fetches a token from the lexer (`yylex()`), pushes it onto a parse stack and then consults a look‑ahead table (`yyact`, `yyact2`, `yyact3`). |
| **Shift / Reduce** | When the table entry indicates a shift, the token is pushed onto the stack and the state advances; when the entry indicates a reduce, a production rule is applied and the stack is popped accordingly. |
| **Semantic actions** | The big `switch` that follows the table lookup contains one case per grammar rule. Each case contains the user‑supplied code that implements the semantic action for that rule – e.g. handling of a `castExpression`, building an `arrayAccessExpression`, etc. |
| **Error handling** | The code has a `yyerror()` helper that reports syntax errors and a back‑track routine (`yybacktrack()`) that undoes the partial parse on error. |
| **Data structures** | Two stacks are maintained: `yyval` (holds semantic values) and `yytype` (holds the type of each value). The stacks grow dynamically; the parser checks for overflow. |
| **Primitives** | The parser uses macros like `YYERROR`, `YYABORT`, and helper functions for look‑ahead and stack manipulation (`yyshift()`, `yypop()`). |
| **Grammar rules covered** | The grammar covers expressions such as `argumentList`, `arrayCreationExpression`, `arrayAccessExpression`, `postfixExpression`, `unaryExpression`, `shiftExpression`, `relationalExpression`, `equalityExpression`, and many others that build up Java‑style expressions and statements. |

---

### Key take‑aways

1. **Shift‑Reduce loop** – The core of the parser is the `yyact` table that dictates whether to shift, reduce, or error.  
2. **Semantic code** – Each `case` in the big switch contains the actual code that builds the AST node for that rule.  
3. **Error recovery** – On an error the parser jumps to the `yyerror()` routine, reports the issue and may back‑track (`yybacktrack()`).  
4. **Stack safety** – The parser checks for stack overflow and reports a stack‑overflow error if the stack grows beyond its limit.  
5. **Utility helpers** – There are helper functions to push/pop values, fetch look‑ahead tokens, and report problems (`yyerror`, `yybacktrack`).  

This gives you a quick, high‑level picture of how the generated parser works without diving into every case in the switch.

@lcmDocumentation::PrintHelpOnePolicy@k_.body: The function attempts to display the documentation for a single CMake policy. It builds the policy’s name by appending the current argument to the “policy/” path, calls the internal helper to print the policy’s files, and returns true if successful. If the argument isn’t a policy, it reports an error message and returns false.

@lcmDocumentation::PrintHelpOneProperty@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::PrintHelpOneProperty@.body: The routine attempts to display the help description of a single CMake property. It resolves the help‑file name for the current argument, invokes a helper that emits the file’s contents to the supplied stream, and returns `true` if the file exists. If the property isn’t known, it writes an explanatory message and returns `false`.

@lcmDocumentation::PrintHelpOneVariable@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::PrintHelpOneVariable@.body: This helper reads the help file for a single variable. It first resolves the variable’s name, then tries to print the corresponding help file from the “variable/” sub‑directory. If the file is found and printed successfully, the function returns true; otherwise it prints an explanatory message telling the user that the variable is undefined and suggests using the variable‑list option.

@lcmDocumentation::PrintNames@k_ZN15cmDo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::PrintNames@k_ZN15cmDo.body: It gathers the list of files matching a glob pattern, reads each file until it encounters a non‑empty line beginning with an alphanumeric character or ‘<’, stores that line as a name, then outputs the collected names in sorted order.

@lcmDocumentation::PrintOldCustomModules.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::PrintOldCustomModules.body: The routine generates a brief deprecation notice for the legacy `--help-custom-modules` option. It pulls the current argument as a filename, splits the extension from the basename, and writes either an HTML page, a troff‑style block, or plain text depending on the file’s extension. The message contains a short summary and a fuller explanation, and the function always returns `true`.

@lcmDocumentation::PrintRequestedDocumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::PrintRequestedDocumen.body: This function iterates over a collection of requested help items. For each item it sets a current argument and then decides whether to write the help to a file (if a filename is supplied) or to the supplied output stream. When a file is used, it opens the file, otherwise it may add a newline between multiple items. After choosing the stream, it delegates to `PrintDocumentation` to actually emit the formatted help; any stream error flips the overall return flag to `false`. The function returns a boolean indicating whether all prints succeeded.

@lcmDocumentation::PrintUsage@k_ZN15cmDo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::PrintUsage@k_ZN15cmDo.body: The method looks up a “Usage” entry in the internal map; if found, it forwards that section to the formatter for output, then returns true.

@lcmDocumentation::PrintVersion@k_ZN15cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::PrintVersion@k_ZN15cm.body: PrintVersion writes the document name and the CMake version string to the supplied output stream, appends a newline and the maintenance notice, and signals success.

@lcmDocumentation::SectionAtName@k_ZN15c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::SectionAtName@k_ZN15c.body:
The function performs a **lookup‑and‑insert**: it calls `AllSections.emplace(name, cmDocumentationSection{ name})`.  
If a section with that key already exists, `emplace` leaves the existing entry untouched and returns an iterator pointing to it; otherwise it inserts a new `cmDocumentationSection` constructed with the supplied `name`. The method then returns a reference to the stored section (`.first->second`). Thus, after the call the caller receives a reference that can be used to read or modify the section in the `AllSections` container.

@lcmDocumentation::SetName@k_ZN15cmDocum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::SetName@k_ZN15cmDocum.body: Sets the class’s internal `NameString` member to the value passed in `name`. It performs a simple assignment of the provided string to the object’s internal string storage. No additional logic or side‑effects is performed.

@lcmDocumentation::SetSection@k_ZN15cmDo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::SetSection@k_ZN15cmDo.body: Stores the provided `cmDocumentationSection` in the internal map under the key supplied by `name`. If an entry with the same key already exists, it is overwritten. If `name` is `nullptr`, the function will crash (dereferencing a null pointer). The call uses `std::move` to transfer ownership of the `section` argument, ensuring no copies are made.

@lcmDocumentation::SetSection@k_ZN15cmDo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::SetSection@k_ZN15cmDo.body: The `SetSection` template accepts any iterable collection of documentation items, constructs a `cmDocumentationSection` with the supplied name, appends every element from the iterable into that section, and finally forwards the fully populated section to the internal `SetSection` helper by moving the temporary section object. This pattern allows callers to pass heterogeneous collections (e.g. vectors, lists, or initializer‑lists) of docs without copying the contents into an intermediate structure.

@lcmDocumentation::SetShowGenerators@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::SetShowGenerators@k_Z.body: The `SetShowGenerators` method simply assigns the supplied boolean value to the `ShowGenerators` member flag. This flag controls whether generator components are rendered in the application’s UI.

@lcmDocumentation::WarnFormFromFilename@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::WarnFormFromFilename@.body: The `WarnFormFromFilename` routine examines the file’s extension (upper‑casing it), flags the help type as “None” for any of the legacy extensions (`.htm`, `.html`, `.docbook`, or single‑digit “.1”‑“.9” patterns), sets the result flag to true for those unsupported formats, and emits a warning message via `cmSystemTools::Message`.

@lcmDocumentation::addCMakeStandardDocSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::addCMakeStandardDocSe.body: The function registers a standard “Generators” section in the documentation system. It creates a `cmDocumentationSection` instance named `sec`, feeds it a pre‑built “CMakeGeneratorsHeader” content via `Append`, then stores that section in the `AllSections` map under the key “Generators”. This enables other parts of the application to query and render that particular documentation fragment.

@lcmDocumentation::addCPackStandardDocSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::addCPackStandardDocSe.body: The function creates a new documentation section named “Generators”, attaches the standard header for that section, and inserts the resulting section into the collection of all sections.

@lcmDocumentation::addCTestStandardDocSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::addCTestStandardDocSe.body: The `addCTestStandardDocSections()` method simply delegates to the existing `addCMakeStandardDocSections()` routine. It exists to keep older builds that relied on the previous interface functional while still allowing newer builds to use the same logic without duplication. This method primarily exists to preserve backward‑compatibility and may be omitted in future revisions once the older contracts are retired.

@lcmDocumentation::addCommonStandardDocS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::addCommonStandardDocS.body: The function creates a new documentation section labeled **“Options”**, appends a predefined set of standard options to it, and inserts that section into the internal map of sections for later use.

@lcmDocumentation::cmDocumentation@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::cmDocumentation@k_ZN1.body: The `cmDocumentation` public constructor accepts an rvalue reference to another `cmDocumentation` instance, enabling efficient move‑construction of its internal state (e.g., swapping or reassigning internal members) rather than performing deep copies. This allows callers to initialise a new object from an existing one without unnecessary duplication of data.

@lcmDocumentation::cmDocumentation@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::cmDocumentation@k_ZN1.body: The public function `cmDocumentation(const cmDocumentation & [unnamed])` acts as a copy‑constructor, creating a new `cmDocumentation` instance by copying the state of an existing instance supplied as the unnamed reference. It’s used throughout the code wherever a `cmDocumentation` object needs to be duplicated.

@lcmDocumentation::cmDocumentation@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentation::cmDocumentation@k_ZN1.body: Creates default documentation sections by calling `addCommonStandardDocSections()` and then enables generator output by setting `ShowGenerators` to true.

@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintColumn@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintColumn@.body: PrintColumn prints a given string in a fixed‑width column, wrapping words that would overflow and starting a new line after any newline or when a word would exceed the current line’s remaining space. It indents each new line (except the first) and inserts a single space between words, with an extra space after a period to mark sentence boundaries.

@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintFormatt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintFormatt.body: The routine processes the supplied text, grouping consecutive characters until a space or newline is hit. At that point it writes the accumulated chunk via the appropriate printer (paragraph or pre‑formatted) and then clears the buffer. The process repeats until the entire string is output, taking care to apply the correct indentation and line‑ending rules.

@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintParagra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintParagra.body: The function writes an optional indentation string (if `TextIndent` is non‑empty), then forwards the supplied text to `PrintColumn`, and finally inserts a newline.

@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintPreform.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintPreform.body: Writes the supplied string to the output stream followed by a newline. It simply inserts `text` into the stream and terminates the line.

@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintSection.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationFormatter::PrintSection.body: The function writes a section’s title to the output stream, then iterates over each documentation entry within that section. For entries that have a name, it aligns the name to a fixed column width (calculated from a name‑prefix and a fixed name length), prints the name prefixed by the custom prefix string, and follows it with an “= ” marker and the brief text. If the name exceeds the allotted width it breaks the line before the brief. For entries lacking a name it simply prints the brief on a new line. After finishing the entries, it appends an extra newline and restores the previous indentation state.

@lcmDocumentationFormatter::SetIndent@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationFormatter::SetIndent@k_.body: The function assigns the supplied `indent` value to the `TextIndent` member of the current object. It expects `indent` to be a `std::size_t` and simply stores it; no validation or side‑effects are performed.

@lcmDocumentationFormatter::cmDocumentat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationFormatter::cmDocumentat.body: The constructor takes an rvalue reference to another cmDocumentationFormatter instance and moves its internal resources into the new object, leaving the source in a valid‑but‑unspecified‑state.

@lcmDocumentationFormatter::cmDocumentat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationFormatter::cmDocumentat.body: The copy constructor creates a new formatter that inherits all formatting state from an existing instance. It performs a member‑wise copy of internal configuration (indent levels, flags, style tables, etc.), ensuring the new object starts with the same visual layout settings as the source.

@lcmDocumentationFormatter::cmDocumentat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationFormatter::cmDocumentat.body: cmDocumentationFormatter takes raw documentation strings and produces a clean, consistently indented string suitable for output. It normalizes spacing, trims excess whitespace, and ensures the text is ready for display or further processing.

@lcmDocumentationSection::Append@k_ZN22c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationSection::Append@k_ZN22c.body: The Append function enqueues a new documentation entry into the internal collection.

@lcmDocumentationSection::Append@k_ZN22c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationSection::Append@k_ZN22c.body: The function takes an arbitrary iterable and copies every element it contains into the class’s internal container by calling the container’s `insert` with the iterable’s begin and end iterators.

@lcmDocumentationSection::Prepend@k_ZN22.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationSection::Prepend@k_ZN22.body: The `Prepend` template inserts a range of elements into the container stored in `this->Entries` by calling `insert` with the beginning iterator of `this->Entries` and the range `[begin(entries), end(entries))`. This results in the supplied elements appearing at the front of the underlying container.

@lcmDocumentationSection::cmDocumentatio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationSection::cmDocumentatio.body: The constructor `cmDocumentationSection(const char* name)` initializes the object’s `Name` member with the supplied string. It performs no additional work beyond storing this reference.

@lcmDurationTo@k_Z12cmDurationToRKi@f./S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDurationTo@k_Z12cmDurationToRKi@f./S.body: The template `cmDurationTo` safely converts a custom `cmDuration` into a standard `std::chrono::duration` of any arithmetic type `T`. It first clamps the value between the type’s maximum and minimum allowed values, then casts the duration to a `std::chrono::duration<T, std::ratio<1>>` using `duration_cast`, finally returning the underlying count.

@lcmDynamicLoader::FlushCache@k_ZN15cmDy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDynamicLoader::FlushCache@k_ZN15cmDy.body: The method simply forwards a cache‑flush request to the singleton cache manager by calling its `FlushCache()` method.

@lcmDynamicLoader::OpenLibrary@k_ZN15cmD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDynamicLoader::OpenLibrary@k_ZN15cmD.body: It first queries a cache for an existing handle; if found it returns that handle. If not, it loads the library via DynamicLoader, stores the handle in the cache, and finally returns it.

@lcmDynamicLoader::cmDynamicLoader@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDynamicLoader::cmDynamicLoader@k_ZN1.body: The `cmDynamicLoader` function is a protected routine that prepares the system to load and initialise components dynamically. It orchestrates the registration of modules, resolves dependencies, and ensures that resources are correctly instantiated and cleaned up when no longer needed.

@lcmDynamicLoader::~cmDynamicLoader@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDynamicLoader::~cmDynamicLoader@k_ZN.body: The protected destructor `~cmDynamicLoader()` automatically de‑allocates any internally‑held resources (e.g., handles to loaded modules or reference‑counted objects) when an instance is destroyed, ensuring no dangling pointers remain.

@lcmDyndepCollation::AddCollationInforma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDyndepCollation::AddCollationInforma.body: The routine simply writes four entries into the supplied JSON object: a key holding the list of CXX modules obtained via `CollationInformationCxxModules`, a key with the BMI installation data from `CollationInformationBmiInstallation`, a key containing the export list from `CollationInformationExports`, and a key storing the passed‑in configuration string. The function performs no further logic beyond these assignments.

@lcmDyndepCollation::IsBmiOnly@k_ZN17cmD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDyndepCollation::IsBmiOnly@k_ZN17cmD.body: Checks whether the supplied object name refers to an entry in `exportInfo.ObjectToFileSet` that has its `BmiOnly` flag set. On Windows it first normalizes slashes to Unix form; otherwise it uses the string unchanged. It looks up the key in the map and returns true only if a matching entry exists and its `second.BmiOnly` field is true.

@lcmDyndepCollation::IsObjectPrivate@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDyndepCollation::IsObjectPrivate@k_Z.body: The function maps the supplied object name to an entry in `export_info.ObjectToFileSet`. If that entry exists and the corresponding file set’s visibility flag is not marked as an interface (`cmFileSetVisibilityIsForInterface` returns false), the function reports the object as private (returns `true`). If the object isn’t found in the map or its file set is flagged as an interface, the function returns `false`.

@lcmDyndepCollation::ParseExportInfo@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDyndepCollation::ParseExportInfo@k_Z.body: The function reads a JSON-like value and builds a `cmCxxModuleExportInfo` object. It pulls the `"config"` field (defaulting to `"noconfig"` if empty), then iterates over the `"exports"` array to fill a list of `CxxModuleExport` entries. If a `"bmi-installation"` object is present it fills a `CxxModuleBmiInstall` structure. It finally walks the `"cxx-modules"` mapping, creating file‑set descriptors for each module. The constructed object is returned wrapped in a `unique_ptr`.

@lcmDyndepCollation::WriteDyndepMetadata.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDyndepCollation::WriteDyndepMetadata.body: The function gathers export data, creates property files per export, writes install scripts for BMI files, tracks module visibility, and checks that public sources only require public modules while ensuring that any missing module definitions are reported.

@lcmDyndepMetadataCallbacks::cmDyndepMet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDyndepMetadataCallbacks::cmDyndepMet.body: The function hooks into the system that registers the callbacks used during dynamic dependency resolution—essentially wiring up the logic that reacts when a component’s metadata changes so that the resolver can keep its dependency graph updated.

@lcmELF::EncodeDynamicEntries@k_ZNK5cmEL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::EncodeDynamicEntries@k_ZNK5cmEL.body:
If the instance is valid, the function forwards the given list to an internal helper and returns the helper’s result.  
If the instance is not valid, it simply returns an empty `std::vector<char>`.

@lcmELF::GetDynamicEntries@k_ZNK5cmELF17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::GetDynamicEntries@k_ZNK5cmELF17.body: The method returns a list of dynamic entries when the instance is in a valid state; otherwise it yields an empty list, ensuring callers never see an internal pointer. It defers no side‑effects and keeps const‑ness intact.

@lcmELF::GetDynamicEntryPosition@k_ZNK5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::GetDynamicEntryPosition@k_ZNK5c.body: The `GetDynamicEntryPosition` method retrieves the position of a dynamic entry for a given index. It first verifies that the `cmELF` instance is in a valid state; if so, it delegates the lookup to the `Internal` helper and returns that position. If the instance is invalid, it simply returns zero.

@lcmELF::GetFileType@k_ZNK5cmELF11GetFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::GetFileType@k_ZNK5cmELF11GetFil.body: The method checks the object’s validity; if valid, it forwards the call to the internal implementation and returns that file type. If the object isn’t valid, it falls back to a default sentinel value (`FileTypeInvalid`).

@lcmELF::GetMachine@k_ZNK5cmELF10GetMach.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::GetMachine@k_ZNK5cmELF10GetMach.body: If the object reports valid, the method forwards the request to its internal component; otherwise it simply returns zero.

@lcmELF::GetNumberOfSections@k_ZNK5cmELF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::GetNumberOfSections@k_ZNK5cmELF.body: It returns the number of sections stored in the underlying `Internal` object, but only if the current `cmELF` instance reports itself as valid; otherwise it returns 0.

@lcmELF::GetRPath@k_ZN5cmELF8GetRPathEv@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::GetRPath@k_ZN5cmELF8GetRPathEv@.body: When called, it checks that the current object is in a valid state and that its file type is either executable or a shared library. If those conditions hold, it hands back the internal pointer returned by `GetRPath()`. If either check fails, the function returns a null pointer.

@lcmELF::GetRunPath@k_ZN5cmELF10GetRunPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::GetRunPath@k_ZN5cmELF10GetRunPa.body: The function checks that the current object is valid and that its internal file type is either an executable or a shared library. If both conditions hold, it returns the internal run‑path entry; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmELF::GetSOName@k_ZN5cmELF9GetSONameE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::GetSOName@k_ZN5cmELF9GetSONameE.body: The method calls an internal helper to obtain a string entry; if that entry exists, it copies the entry’s value into the provided string reference and returns true, otherwise it returns false.

@lcmELF::GetSOName@k_ZN5cmELF9GetSONameE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::GetSOName@k_ZN5cmELF9GetSONameE.body: Returns the internal shared‑object name only when the instance is valid and its type is a shared library; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmELF::IsMIPS@k_ZNK5cmELF6IsMIPSEv@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::IsMIPS@k_ZNK5cmELF6IsMIPSEv@f./.body: The method returns a bool. It first verifies the instance is in a valid state; if it is, it forwards the query to the internal object’s `IsMips()` method, otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmELF::PrintInfo@k_ZNK5cmELF9PrintInfo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::PrintInfo@k_ZNK5cmELF9PrintInfo.body: The function writes the object’s state to an output stream. It first verifies the ELF object is valid; if so, it forwards the request to an internal helper, otherwise it writes a simple “Not a valid ELF file.” message.

@lcmELF::Valid@k_ZNK5cmELF5ValidEv@f./So.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::Valid@k_ZNK5cmELF5ValidEv@f./So.body: The `Valid` function returns `true` only when the internal pointer is non‑null and the associated file type is not marked as `FileTypeInvalid`.

@lcmELF::cmELF@k_ZN5cmELFC1EPKc@f./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::cmELF@k_ZN5cmELFC1EPKc@f./Sourc.body: It parses an ELF file: it opens the file, reads the identification bytes to verify the magic and endianness, then creates the appropriate 32‑ or 64‑bit internal implementation, recording any failure in `ErrorMessage`.

@lcmELF::operator bool@k_ZNK5cmELFcvbEv@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::operator bool@k_ZNK5cmELFcvbEv@.body: Returns the result of the internal `Valid()` check, letting an instance be used directly in a Boolean context.

@lcmELF::~cmELF@k_ZN5cmELFD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELF::~cmELF@k_ZN5cmELFD1Ev.body: The `~cmELF` destructor ensures that every resource owned by a `cmELF` instance is properly released—deallocating memory, closing file handles, and performing any necessary finalization logic before the object is discarded.

@lcmELFByteSwap@k_Z13cmELFByteSwapRT_@f..author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFByteSwap@k_Z13cmELFByteSwapRT_@f..body: The `cmELFByteSwap` template casts its argument to a raw byte buffer and forwards it to a size‑specific routine, effectively reversing the byte order of the object in place.

@lcmELFByteSwap@k_ZL13cmELFByteSwapPc17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFByteSwap@k_ZL13cmELFByteSwapPc17c.body: The function performs a simple two‑byte in‑place swap: it copies the first byte into a temporary variable, writes the second byte over the first, and then restores the temporary byte into the second position. The second argument (`cmELFByteSwapSize<2>`) is unused; it merely signals the intended size. The routine assumes the caller supplies a buffer of at least two bytes and does not perform any bounds or null‑check, so passing a too‑small or null pointer will lead to undefined behaviour.

@lcmELFByteSwap@k_ZL13cmELFByteSwapPc17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFByteSwap@k_ZL13cmELFByteSwapPc17c.body: The routine in‑place swaps the first and last bytes, then the middle two, achieving a 4‑byte reversal without allocating new storage. It uses a single temporary byte, but performs no bounds checking or null‑pointer validation.

@lcmELFByteSwap@k_ZL13cmELFByteSwapPc17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFByteSwap@k_ZL13cmELFByteSwapPc17c.body: The routine in‑place reverses the byte order of an 8‑byte buffer: it swaps byte 0 with 7, 1 with 6, 2 with 5, and 3 with 4. The single‑byte temporary variable carries each intermediate value during the swaps, and the unused template argument signals the fixed 8‑byte length.

@lcmELFInternal::EncodeDynamicEntries@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::EncodeDynamicEntries@k_.body: The function walks through the collection of dynamic entries, serialises each into its binary representation (typically a length‑prefixed payload) and stitches them together into a single contiguous buffer. It then hands that buffer back for further processing or storage. The virtual nature allows subclasses to override the exact encoding details while retaining the overall pipeline.

@lcmELFInternal::GetDynamicEntries@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::GetDynamicEntries@k_ZN1.body: GetDynamicEntries() should be overridden to supply a collection of dynamic entries that the system manages. Implementations typically query the relevant sources and return the resulting list.

@lcmELFInternal::GetDynamicEntryPosition.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::GetDynamicEntryPosition.body: GetDynamicEntryPosition is an abstract member that, given an integer index, yields the numeric position within a dynamic data structure – for instance‑specific implementations to supply the actual lookup logic.

@lcmELFInternal::GetDynamicSectionString.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::GetDynamicSectionString.body: The GetDynamicSectionString method is a pure virtual interface that derived classes must implement to translate a numeric tag into the appropriate string entry. Call sites in cmELF.cxx use it to obtain the text representation for tags such as D_T_SONAME, D_T_RPATH, and D_T_RUNPATH, so any subclass can provide its own mapping between tags and string literals while guaranteeing that callers always receive a non‑null pointer to a StringEntry.

@lcmELFInternal::GetFileType@k_ZNK13cmEL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::GetFileType@k_ZNK13cmEL.body:
The `GetFileType` method simply returns the value of the `ELFType` member held by the instance.  
It performs no additional work or side‑effects, leaving the caller with the file‑type information that was previously stored.

@lcmELFInternal::GetMachine@k_ZNK13cmELF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::GetMachine@k_ZNK13cmELF.body: GetMachine is a const member that simply returns the stored 16‑bit unsigned value representing the current machine identifier.

@lcmELFInternal::GetNumberOfSections@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::GetNumberOfSections@k_Z.body: The `GetNumberOfSections` function is a pure virtual entry point that obliges any concrete subclass to supply the current count of logical sections pertinent to the object. When invoked, the implementation simply returns an unsigned integer representing that count. In practice, code paths that rely on this metric typically call the function to decide how many sub‑objects, iterators or resource partitions a given object exposes.

@lcmELFInternal::GetRPath@k_ZN13cmELFInt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::GetRPath@k_ZN13cmELFInt.body: The function forwards a request to the underlying dynamic‑section lookup. It returns a constant pointer to a `StringEntry` that holds the string corresponding to the `D_T_RPATH` identifier, without modifying any internal state.

@lcmELFInternal::GetRunPath@k_ZN13cmELFI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::GetRunPath@k_ZN13cmELFI.body: `GetRunPath` retrieves the current run‑path string by delegating to the infrastructure that stores dynamic‑section strings. It simply forwards the request to `GetDynamicSectionString`, passing the `D2_RUNPATH` key, and returns the resulting pointer to the caller.

@lcmELFInternal::GetSOName@k_ZN13cmELFIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::GetSOName@k_ZN13cmELFIn.body: This method delegates to `GetDynamicSectionString`, passing the `D_T_SONAME` key, and returns the resulting `StringEntry` pointer.

@lcmELFInternal::IsMips@k_ZNK13cmELFInte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::IsMips@k_ZNK13cmELFInte.body: The `IsMips()` member is an abstract, const‑qualified predicate that any concrete subclass must implement. It returns a `bool` without affecting object state, and because it’s declared `=0` it’s a pure virtual function—therefore the base type cannot be instantiated and the method is guaranteed to be overridden in derived types. In practice, callers invoke it polymorphically to query whether the specific runtime object satisfies the “MIPS” condition without needing to know the concrete class, relying on the virtual dispatch to deliver the appropriate true/false result.

@lcmELFInternal::PrintInfo@k_ZNK13cmELFI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::PrintInfo@k_ZNK13cmELFI.body: PrintInfo serialises the object’s state to a provided output stream—each concrete subclass supplies its own formatting logic, ensuring the object’s internal data can be inspected or logged without exposing implementation details.

@lcmELFInternal::SetErrorMessage@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::SetErrorMessage@k_ZN13c.body: Assigns the supplied message to the `External->ErrorMessage` field and marks the current state as an invalid file type.

@lcmELFInternal::cmELFInternal@k_ZN13cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::cmELFInternal@k_ZN13cmE.body: The constructor stores the supplied `cmELF` pointer and the input stream, then determines whether later byte‑swapping is required by comparing the provided byte‑order flag with the build‑time endianness macro. Finally it marks the dynamic‑section index as “not yet loaded”.

@lcmELFInternal::operator=@k_ZN13cmELFIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::operator=@k_ZN13cmELFIn.body: This operator copies all member data from the right‑hand operand into the current instance and returns a reference to `*this` for chaining. It safeguards against self‑assignment and performs a shallow copy of the internal state (without reallocating resources).

@lcmELFInternal::~cmELFInternal@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternal::~cmELFInternal@k_ZN13cm.body: The `~cmELFInternal` destructor is declared `virtual` and uses the compiler’s default implementation (`= default`). This means it participates in polymorphic cleanup: when a derived instance is destroyed through a base‑pointer, the destructor chain will invoke this one automatically. Because no custom destruction logic is supplied, it simply ensures that any resources owned by the base class are released according to the normal destructor semantics—no extra overhead or side‑effects are introduced.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::ByteSwap@k_ZN17cmEL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::ByteSwap@k_ZN17cmEL.body: The routine invokes `cmELFByteSwap` on the two fields (`d_tag` and `d_un.d_val`) of the `ELF_Dyn` argument, effectively flipping the byte ordering of each of those values.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::ByteSwap@k_ZN17cmEL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::ByteSwap@k_ZN17cmEL.body: The private `ByteSwap` routine walks through every field in an `ELF_Ehdr` instance and applies the helper `cmELFByteSwap` to each member. This helper performs the low‑level byte‑swap needed to correct the endianness of the ELF header fields (`e_type`, `e_machine`, `e_version`, `e_entry`, `e_phoff`, `e_shoff`, `e_flags`, `e_ehsize`, `e_phentsize`, `e_phnum`, `e_shentsize`, `e_shnum`, and `e_shstrndx`). In effect, calling `ByteSwap` on an `ELF_Ehdr` guarantees that every header word is in the machine’s native byte order before further processing.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::ByteSwap@k_ZN17cmEL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::ByteSwap@k_ZN17cmEL.body: The `ByteSwap` routine walks the `ELF_Shdr` structure, invoking `cmELFByteSwap` on every member field. It effectively reorders the bytes of the header’s fields to match the required endianness (big‑ or little‑endian). No return value is emitted; the function only mutates the passed‑in structure.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::EncodeDynamicEntrie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::EncodeDynamicEntrie.body: It accepts a list of `(tag, value)` pairs, allocates a buffer of the right size, loops through each pair, packs the data into a native `ELF_Dyn` structure, performs a byte‑order swap when flagged, and appends the raw bytes into a `std::vector<char>` that is returned.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::FileTypeValid@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::FileTypeValid@k_ZN1.body: FileTypeValid maps the supplied enum value to an integer and checks whether that integer matches one of the predefined constants (ET_NONE, ET_REL, ET_EXEC, ET_DYN, ET_CORE) or lies within the ranges defined by ET_LOOS–ET_HIOS or ET_LOPROC–ET_HIPROC. If any of those conditions is met, it returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::GetDynamicEntries@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::GetDynamicEntries@k.body: The function returns a list of dynamic‑section entries. It first calls `LoadDynamicSection`; if that fails it returns an empty list. When the section is available it pre‑allocates the result list to the number of internal entries and copies each entry’s tag/value pair into the result before returning it.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::GetDynamicEntryPosi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::GetDynamicEntryPosi.body: The routine returns the file offset of the *j*‑th entry in the executable’s dynamic section. It first verifies that the dynamic section is loaded; if not, it returns zero. It then checks that *j* is a valid index into the section’s entry array; an out‑of‑range index again yields zero. Otherwise it looks up the relevant section header and computes the entry’s offset by adding the base offset of that section to *j* times the entry size, returning the result as an unsigned long.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::GetDynamicSectionSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::GetDynamicSectionSt.body: The method caches a requested string in a map keyed by its tag, returns a previously‑stored entry if present, otherwise it loads the DYNAMIC section, validates the referenced string table, walks the dynamic entries looking for a match, reads the string from the file (handling trailing nulls) and records its position, length, and index. If any step fails—out‑of‑range indices, missing section or unreadable data—it reports an error and returns nullptr.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::GetNumberOfSections.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::GetNumberOfSections.body: The method simply pulls the section‑count value stored in the ELF header, casts it to an unsigned integer, and returns that value.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::IsMips@k_ZNK17cmELF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::IsMips@k_ZNK17cmELF.body: The method simply tests whether the ELF header’s `e_machine` field equals the MIPS identifier (`EM_MIPS`) and returns that boolean value.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::LoadDynamicSection@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::LoadDynamicSection@.body: The routine verifies that a dynamic section exists and isn’t already populated; if so, it resizes the internal entry vector according to the section’s size and iteratively reads each dynamic entry from the file stream, returning success only after all entries are successfully loaded.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::LoadSectionHeader@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::LoadSectionHeader@k.body: The routine fetches the header at position *i*, stores it in the internal list, marks that index as the dynamic section if the header’s type equals SHT_DYNAMIC, and reports whether the read succeeded.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::PrintInfo@k_ZNK17cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::PrintInfo@k_ZNK17cm.body: PrintInfo serializes the object’s metadata to an output stream: it emits the string “ELF <type‑name>” followed by the byte‑order suffix (“MSB” or “LSB”) and then a human‑readable label that identifies the file as a relocatable object, executable, shared library, core file, or an OS/processor‑specific type, before ending with a newline.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::Read@k_ZN17cmELFInt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::Read@k_ZN17cmELFInt.body: The function attempts to read the raw bytes of a data‑structure into the provided reference, then performs a byte‑swap if the reader’s endianness flag is set. It returns `true` only when the underlying stream reports no failure after the read (i.e. when the `read` call succeeded and no stream‑error flag is set). If the stream fails to provide enough bytes or any other I/O error occurs, the function will return `false`.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::Read@k_ZN17cmELFInt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::Read@k_ZN17cmELFInt.body: The `Read` function reads an ELF header into the supplied `ELF_Ehdr` reference, then checks whether the file’s byte order matches the current system. It first reads the raw bytes; if that fails, it returns false. It inspects the `e_type` field: if a swap is required (indicated by `NeedSwap`) it performs a byte‑swap on the value. If the resulting type still fails validation, it flips the swap flag and retries. Finally, if swapping is still needed, it applies a full byte‑swap on the whole header structure. Upon success it returns true.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::Read@k_ZN17cmELFInt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::Read@k_ZN17cmELFInt.body: Attempts to read a full `ELF_Shdr` structure from the underlying stream into `x`. If the internal flag indicates the need for endianness conversion, it calls `ByteSwap` to correct the order. The function returns `true` only when the read operation succeeded without stream failure.

@lcmELFInternalImpl::cmELFInternalImpl@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFInternalImpl::cmELFInternalImpl@k.body: The constructor loads the ELF file’s main header, classifies the file type (relocatable, executable, shared library, core, or OS‑/proc‑specific types), records the target machine, and then reads all section headers into the internal section list.

@lcmELFTypes32::GetName@k_ZN12cmELFTypes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFTypes32::GetName@k_ZN12cmELFTypes.body: It is a static member that simply returns a constant string literal representing “32‑bit”.

@lcmELFTypes64::GetName@k_ZN12cmELFTypes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmELFTypes64::GetName@k_ZN12cmELFTypes.body: The function simply returns a pointer to the string literal `"64-bit"`, whose storage duration is static. Because the function is declared `static`, it can be invoked without an instance, and the returned `const char*` guarantees the literal cannot be modified.

@lcmEnableLanguageCommand@k_Z23cmEnableL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmEnableLanguageCommand@k_Z23cmEnableL.body: The routine first validates that it received at least one argument; it looks for an explicit “OPTIONAL” token to flag optional behavior, gathers the remaining strings as language names, and then passes that list (together with the optional flag) to the current makefile’s EnableLanguage method. If the argument list is non‑empty, the call succeeds and the function returns true.

@lcmEnableTestingCommand@k_Z22cmEnableTe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmEnableTestingCommand@k_Z22cmEnableTe.body: The helper registers the `CMAKE_TESTING_ENABLED` flag in the current Makefile via the supplied status object and signals success.

@lcmExecProgramCommand@k_Z20cmExecProgra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecProgramCommand@k_Z20cmExecProgra.body: The function parses a list of arguments, building a command string and optionally capturing output into a make‑file variable. It then invokes the command (optionally in a newly‑created directory), captures the exit status and any output, and stores that data into the supplied status object’s makefile definitions before returning success.

@lcmExecuteProcessCommand::[lambda_1]@kc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecuteProcessCommand::[lambda_1]@kc.body: The lambda takes an integer index, queries the process state for that child, and returns a human‑readable string describing the exit code or exception text (or an error message if the state cannot be retrieved).

@lcmExecuteProcessCommand@k_Z23cmExecute.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecuteProcessCommand@k_Z23cmExecute.body: The routine parses its argument list, constructs a child process pipeline, executes the specified commands while directing standard‑output and error streams to files or make‑file variables as requested, captures the command exit codes, and records the results—success, failure messages, and any return codes—back into the makefile before returning success or failure.

@lcmExecuteProcessCommandAppend@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecuteProcessCommandAppend@k_ZN12_G.body:
The routine attaches a raw byte sequence to a `std::vector<char>` that is passed by reference.  
When compiled for Apple, it first protects against a known vector‑emplace bug by inserting the very first byte of the payload into an otherwise‑empty container, then decrements the length count.  
Finally, it forwards the (possibly updated) pointer and adjusted count to `cm::append`, which performs the actual range‑copy into the vector.

@lcmExecuteProcessCommandFixText@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecuteProcessCommandFixText@k_ZN12_.body: The routine cleans a string stored in a `std::vector<char>` by filtering out any null bytes and collapsing any lone carriage‑return followed by a newline into a single line break. It then optionally trims any whitespace at the end of the resulting text and finally null‑terminates the vector so it can be treated as a C‑style string.

@lcmExecuteProcessCommandIsWhitespace@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecuteProcessCommandIsWhitespace@k_.body: The function simply checks whether a character represents whitespace by testing for space‐like characters (`isspace`) and explicit newline or carriage‑return characters. It returns true when any of those conditions holds.

@lcmExecutionStatus::GetMakefile@k_ZN17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::GetMakefile@k_ZN17c.body: The function simply returns a reference to the `Makefile` object stored in the current instance, allowing callers to read or modify the make‑file contents through that reference.

@lcmExecutionStatus::SetBreakInvoked@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::SetBreakInvoked@k_Z.body: This method marks the `BreakInvoked` flag as true—indicating that the break condition has been triggered. It sets the internal state so any subsequent logic can detect that the break has already occurred.

@lcmExecutionStatus::SetError@k_ZN17cmEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::SetError@k_ZN17cmEx.body: It assigns the supplied string to the object’s `Error` member. The parameter is a const reference, so the call‑site’s string isn’t copied. (The code’s use of `std::string` is a typo; it should be `std::string`.)

@lcmExecutionStatus::SetReturnInvoked@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::SetReturnInvoked@k_.body: Clears the `Variables` container and flags `ReturnInvoked` as true.

@lcmExecutionStatus::cmExecutionStatus@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::cmExecutionStatus@k.body: This constructor stores a reference to a `cmMakefile` object and immediately sets an internal error message to “unknown error.” It performs no other logic.

@lcmExpandList@k_Z12cmExpandList7cmValue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandList@k_Z12cmExpandList7cmValue.body: The function `cmExpandList` takes a single value `arg` and adds it to a vector `argsOut`. The call to `cmList::append` handles whether to insert placeholders for empty elements according to the supplied flag `emptyElements`. The function itself is merely a thin wrapper around that append routine, exposing a convenient inline interface for callers that want to expand a list of arguments into an output vector.

@lcmExpandList@k_Z12cmExpandListiRiN6cmL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandList@k_Z12cmExpandListiRiN6cmL.body: The function `cmExpandList` converts a single string into a collection by appending it to the supplied vector. It simply forwards the string (`arg`) to `cmList::append`, which internally parses the string into individual elements and adds them to `argsOut`. The optional `emptyElements` flag dictates whether empty tokens are preserved or omitted during the append operation.

@lcmExpandListWithBacktrace@k_Z25cmExpan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandListWithBacktrace@k_Z25cmExpan.body: The function creates a `cmList` from the input string and empty‑argument marker, reserves enough space in a result vector, and then copies each element of that list into a new `BT<std::string>` instance (moving the string). The returned vector contains a back‑trace‑augmented representation of the original list.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::GetValue@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::GetValue@k_.body: The function simply returns the internal string member `Value`; it’s a `const` member function, so callers can’t modify the underlying object. It’s a read‑only accessor that returns a reference to the stored string.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::WasQuoted@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::WasQuoted@k.body: The method simply returns the stored flag indicating whether the argument was originally quoted – it exposes that internal state without performing any further work.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::cmExpandedC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::cmExpandedC.body: The constructor for cmExpandedCommandArgument initializes its two data members: Value is set by moving the supplied string into the member variable, and Quoted is set to the supplied Boolean. No other logic runs in the body.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::cmExpandedC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::cmExpandedC.body: The cmExpandedCommandArgument constructor prepares an instance for parsing or normalising expanded command‑line arguments. It establishes the internal representation (e.g., populating fields that hold argument lists, flags, or variable bindings) that will later be consumed by the command‑processing logic. It performs any required default initialisation before the instance is used elsewhere in the code.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::empty@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::empty@k_ZNK.body: Returns `true` when the internal container `Value` holds no elements; otherwise returns `false`.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::operator==@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::operator==@.body: The function returns true only when the two pointers refer to the same memory address; it does **not** perform a character‑by‑character comparison of the strings. It also assumes the argument is non‑null, and will silently succeed if either pointer is null. The method is marked `const`, so it promises not to modify the object’s state, but it still compares raw pointers, which can lead to logical errors when the underlying strings are allocated separately but contain identical content.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::operator==@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::operator==@.body: It compares the internal string member to an externally‑supplied string and returns true when the two strings are identical, otherwise false.

@lcmExperimental::DataForFeature@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
