@lcmExperimental::DataForFeature@k_ZN14c.body: The function simply forwards the call to the global `DataForFeature` helper: it accepts a `Feature` enum value and returns a constant reference to the corresponding `FeatureData` instance by delegating the lookup to the top‑level `::DataForFeature` function.

@lcmExperimental::HasSupportEnabled@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExperimental::HasSupportEnabled@k_ZN.body: The function examines a makefile entry to see if the feature’s associated variable equals the expected UID. If it does, it marks the feature as enabled; on the first activation it emits a single warning message and records that the warning has been issued. It finally returns whether the feature was found enabled.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: The method is invoked during the creation of an Android makefile; it writes to the supplied stream the list of target rules that a downstream build system is expected to generate. In practice it interprets the `target` string to enumerate all required artefacts (e.g., binaries, libraries, resource packages) and emits the corresponding make‑rules, ensuring the generated makefile contains the explicit build commands needed to satisfy the target’s dependencies.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: The `GenerateImportFooterCode` method is the point where the generator emits the closing portion of the generated Makefile or build‑script snippet that pulls in the shared‑library or object imports. When invoked, it writes the minimal boiler‑plate lines that declare the final link commands or import directives needed for the Android build, ensuring that the generated build rules are syntactically correct before the file is closed.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: The method appends a makefile line that defines the `LOCAL_PATH` variable as the result of invoking the `my-dir` makefile function, ensuring the build script knows where local sources reside.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: This routine writes the import‑property lines into the generated Android‑makefile. It iterates over the supplied map of properties, emitting each property’s declaration into the provided output stream for the target’s build configuration.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: The protected virtual function `GenerateImportTargetCode` writes a fragment of a Makefile for an Android target. It concatenates the namespace with the target’s export name to form the module name, then outputs the standard headers (`include $(CLEAR_VARS)`), the module name line (`LOCAL_MODULE := <name>`), and finally writes the path to the target’s source file(s) using `cmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputPath`. The function currently leaves the configuration selection unresolved (the `noConfig` placeholder).

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: The function simply forwards the given target and property map to a more detailed overload, passing along a configuration string that comes from the first entry in its internal configuration list (if that list is non‑empty). It chooses the default “BUILD” mode when invoking the helper routine.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: The function examines a CMake target and emits the corresponding build‑script fragments for the Android NDK build system. It first checks whether the old CMP0022 policy is in effect and, if so, logs a warning. Then it writes the interface property entries: it appends compile options, distinguishes between shared and static link libraries and formats the export‑library list appropriately, adds include directories, and dumps link flags. If the target is a prebuilt static library that uses C++ it emits a flag. Finally, depending on the target type (shared, static, or executable) it includes the relevant pre‑built library snippet.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: The protected virtual function `GenerateMissingTargetsCheckCode` is intended to emit diagnostic or guard code into an output stream that verifies that required build targets are present when generating Android Makefiles. Sub‑classes can override it to emit target‑specific validation checks before the normal build commands are written.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: The function writes the standardized footer section of a policy’s generated code into the supplied output stream, ensuring proper termination of the policy definition in the generated source.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::Gener.body: The function writes the policy’s header section to the supplied output stream, assembling the necessary import directives, namespace declarations, and any boiler‑plate comments that accompany the generated code. It runs during the policy‑generation pass, emitting the standard scaffolding required for any generated policy class before the rest of the file is populated.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::cmExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::cmExp.body: The `cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator` function acts as a move constructor: it constructs a new `cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator` instance by taking an rvalue reference of another instance. It simply transfers internal state (such as configuration data and resource handles) from the source object to the new one, avoiding expensive deep copies. This constructor is typically invoked when an existing generator instance needs to be reused or re‑instantiated in other parts of the code that generate Android makefiles.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::cmExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::cmExp.body: The constructor `cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator(const cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator&)` initializes a new instance by copying the internal state from an existing `cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator`. It ensures that all member data (e.g., file paths, build options, generator settings) are duplicated correctly so the new instance can generate the Android Make‑file independently. The class derives from `cmExportBuildFileGenerator`, so it inherits common export‑build logic and specializes it for Android.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::cmExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::cmExp.body: The constructor simply initializes the object’s internal pointers, setting both `LG` and `ExportSet` to `nullptr` so that the instance starts in a clean, non‑null‑reference state before any further configuration is performed.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::opera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::opera.body: Assigns another `cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator` instance into the current one by moving its internal state, then returns the updated instance.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::opera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::opera.body: Copies the contents of another `cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator` instance into the current one, mirroring its internal state and data members.

@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::~cmEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator::~cmEx.body: The function `~cmExportBuildAndroidMKGenerator()` is an entry point for exporting an Android‑specific makefile (.mk) from the project’s configuration data. Internally it marshals build‑time settings—module paths, compiler flags, and dependency lists—into a format that Android’s incremental build system can consume, writing the resulting `.mk` file into the expected output directory. The function is invoked from a variety of build‑export flows; it typically pulls data from a `cmExportBuildFileGenerator` base and materialises that into the canonical Android makefile format expected by downstream tools.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::AppendTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::AppendTarg.body: The `AppendTargets` method copies each element from the supplied `targets` vector into the object’s internal `Targets` collection, extending that collection by the same number of entries.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::ComplainAb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::ComplainAb.body: When an exported target is referenced but its source file is absent from the current export set, the method assembles a diagnostic message that lists the missing target name and enumerates the export sets that should contain it. It then forwards this message as a fatal error to the build system, effectively aborting the build until the exporter is correctly configured.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::Compute@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::Compute@k_.body: The method stores the supplied `cmLocalGenerator` pointer in the object and, when an export set is present, forwards the call to that set’s own `Compute` implementation.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::FindBuildE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::FindBuildE.body: The `FindBuildExportInfo` function walks through the export sets from a `cmGlobalGenerator`. For each set it pulls the list of targets; if the supplied name appears in that list it records the set’s file name and its namespace. Finally it returns a pair consisting of the collected file names and the namespace string that matched.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GenerateCx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GenerateCx.body: The routine writes a list of include‑directives for the module’s configuration files: for every entry in the internal configuration list it emits an `include("…/cxx-modules‑<name>-<config>.cmake")` line, substituting a placeholder `"noconfig"` when the entry is empty. If the module has more than one configuration it appends “OPTIONAL” to each line so that the generated files are treated as optional dependencies.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GenerateIm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GenerateIm.body: Creates a *.cmake* file in the CMake directory, one per exported target that contains C++ module sources. For each such target it writes a line that includes “target‑<name>‑<config>.cmake”, and returns false only if the file cannot be created.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GenerateIm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GenerateIm.body: The routine walks through every exported target, gathers import‑specific properties into a local map, conditionally records the target’s location, detail, and link‑interface information, and finally emits the corresponding import property code into the supplied output stream.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GenerateMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GenerateMa.body: It iterates over the list of targets to populate an export list, ensuring each target appears only once. While doing so it concatenates their export names into a string of expected targets. For each target it gathers interface properties (sources, compile options, headers, link options, etc.), populates the required property map, and writes the interface block for that target. It handles policy differences (e.g., CMP0022), produces the C++‑module data block, and writes the configuration‑specific import sections. At the end it emits a missing‑target check and returns success.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetCxxModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetCxxModu.body: The accessor simply returns the stored path for Cxx modules, exposing it as a read‑only reference so callers cannot alter the internal string.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetCxxModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetCxxModu.body: The method simply returns the value of the `CxxModulesDirectory` member. It’s a read‑only accessor that does not modify the object’s state.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetExportT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetExportT.body: Returns the appropriate export target type. It first pulls the target’s type. If the target is an object library but the generator can’t tell where the object file will be found, it downgrades the type to an interface library. The resulting enum value is returned.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetFileSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetFileSet.body: The routine walks through each configuration for a target, evaluates the directory entries that belong to the given file set, and appends escaped directory strings to an output list. If a configuration‑dependent directory is encountered while the file set type is a C++ module, the routine aborts with a fatal error. Once all directories are processed, it returns a single string containing the escaped paths separated by spaces.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetFileSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetFileSet.body: The function walks through every configuration in a target’s makefile, evaluates which directories and files belong for that configuration, and builds a space‑separated list of those file paths—escaping them for CMake syntax. If any entry is context‑sensitive and the file‑set type is a C++ module, it reports a fatal error because such sets aren’t supported. Once all relevant files are collected, it joins them into a single string to return.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetTargets.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::GetTargets.body:
Collects target names defined in the internal export set.  
If a set of exports exists, the method iterates over each export object, skips those flagged as *Name‑link‑only*, and appends the remaining target names to the supplied vector.  
When no export set is present, the method simply copies the pre‑populated vector of targets into the output vector.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::HandleMiss.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::HandleMiss.body: The function records a missing target by appending its export name to `link_libs`. If `AppendMode` is off it first looks up the export info for the target; if exactly one export file is found it adds that name to the list and records it in `MissingTargets`. Otherwise it logs a complaint about the missing target. If `AppendMode` is on, it simply appends the namespace and the target’s export name to `link_libs`.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::InstallNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::InstallNam.body: It checks whether the current build’s platform has the `CMAKE_PLATFORM_HAS_INSTALLNAME` flag; if so, it queries the target for its install‑name directory for the supplied config and returns that string (empty otherwise).

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetAppendM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetAppendM.body: It assigns the supplied Boolean to the object’s `AppendMode` field, switching the internal flag that governs whether subsequent operations should append data rather than overwrite.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetCxxModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetCxxModu.body: This method assigns the provided string to the internal member `CxxModulesDirectory`, transferring ownership with `std::move`. It expects a valid directory path; passing an empty or non‑existent path may later cause file‑access errors. The call should be followed by any necessary validation (e.g., verifying the directory exists) before using the value.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetExportS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetExportS.body: Sets the class’s internal pointer to the supplied `cmExportSet` instance. The method simply stores the given pointer in the member variable `ExportSet` for later use.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetImportL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetImportL.body: The function assigns import‑location metadata for a target. It first distinguishes whether the target is an object library; if so, it aggregates all its object files and stores them under an “IMPORTED_OBJECTS” property. For normal targets it records the main binary’s full path under “IMPORTED_LOCATION” and, when applicable, attaches the import‑library path under “IMPORTED_IMPLIB”.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetTargets.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::SetTargets.body: The `SetTargets` method simply assigns the provided vector to the `Targets` member of the object, performing a copy of the vector. It takes the argument by const reference to avoid an unnecessary copy of the argument itself, and then relies on the assignment operator of `std::vector` to copy the contents into the member.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::cmExportBu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::cmExportBu.body: The constructor takes an rvalue reference of the same type and performs a move‑style initialization: it adopts the source instance’s internal state (file descriptors, configuration settings, build targets) so the new object assumes ownership of all resources without re‑allocating them.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::cmExportBu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::cmExportBu.body: Creates a new export‑build‑file generator by copying the internal state of an existing instance, ensuring the new object starts with the same configuration and file‑collection information as the source object.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::cmExportBu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::cmExportBu.body: The constructor simply initializes two internal pointers—`LG` and `ExportSet`— to `nullptr`. This guarantees that any later use of those members will start from a known, safe state rather than an indeterminate value.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::operator=@.body: The `operator=` member performs an assignment‑style copy for `cmExportBuildFileGenerator`. When invoked, it takes another `cmExportBuildFileGenerator` instance (or an unnamed temporary) and copies its internal state—namely the output path, file‑generation flags, and any configuration specific to the export build file generator—into the target object. After copying, it returns a reference to the modified instance, allowing chained assignments. The operator is public to permit callers in other parts of the code to replace a generator with a newly constructed or previously created one, ensuring that all internal members are correctly duplicated without leaking or dangling pointers.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::operator=@.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of a `cmExportBuildFileGenerator` instance: it copies member variables, re‑initialises any owned resources, and returns `*this`. It guards against self‑assignment, uses copy‑and‑swap idioms where appropriate, and throws only on failures that would leave the object unchanged.

@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::~cmExportB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportBuildFileGenerator::~cmExportB.body: The routine assembles the necessary data and writes an export‑ready build file into the target location, reporting success or any failure encountered.

@lcmExportCommand@k_Z15cmExportCommandRK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportCommand@k_Z15cmExportCommandRK.body: The function processes a CMake export command. It parses the supplied arguments, resolves target names (or an export set), validates file paths, and creates an appropriate export‑file generator (normal or Android‑specific). It then registers the generator with the global builder to record which targets and configurations should be exported to the chosen file.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::AddConfiguratio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::AddConfiguratio.body: This routine records a new configuration string into an internal list. When called, it simply appends the provided `config` value to the `Configurations` collection, extending the sequence of stored settings.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::AddTargetNamesp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::AddTargetNamesp.body: The function resolves a target reference from the input string, replacing it with a namespaced name when the target is already exported, with the imported name if the target is imported, or with the raw target name otherwise, and returns true only when a namespace was successfully applied.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateCxxModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateCxxModu.body: The function is a pure virtual interface that concrete subclasses must implement. It receives the module name (as a `const std::string&`) and additional arguments required to build the corresponding configuration data structure for the module’s C++ export file. The implementation is expected to assemble and emit the required configuration metadata during the export‑file generation phase, typically invoked from `cmExportFileGenerator` in the code base.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateCxxModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateCxxModu.body: The function checks that the “Cxx‑modules” directory exists; if it’s missing it exits. Otherwise it builds the include path string pointing to the module‑specific CMake file and writes an include directive into the provided output stream. It then opens a new file stream in that directory (creating the file if it doesn’t exist) and delegates writing of configuration‑specific include fragments to the `GenerateCxxModuleConfigInformation` helper.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateExpecte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateExpecte.body: The routine emits a block of CMake‑style code that first guards against duplicate imports, then iterates over a supplied list of expected targets. For each expected target it appends it to a running list and records whether the target already exists in the current target set; those that exist are added to a “defined” list, the rest to a “not‑defined” list. If the collected list of defined targets matches the original expectation list the routine clears all helper variables and exits; otherwise it reports a fatal error listing which targets were already defined and which remain undefined.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportC.body: It builds a suffix string from the supplied config (using an underscore‑prefixed uppercase form or a default “NOCONFIG”) and then forwards that string, together with the original config, to `GenerateImportTargetsConfig`.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportF.body: The function first opens the target import file (appending if `AppendMode` is set). It writes a header block, then writes the main import content generated by `GenerateMainFile`. Finally it appends a footer and returns `true` only if all writes succeeded; otherwise it records an error and returns `false`.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportF.body: The function writes a short footer comment and a version-setting command into the output stream, marking the end of the import section.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportH.body: The function writes a header section to the supplied output stream. It prints a top‑level separator line, the “Generated CMake target import file” notice, and—when a non‑empty configuration string is supplied—adds a line describing that configuration. After that it writes a closing separator line and a blank line, then forwards the stream to GenerateImportVersionCode to finish the header.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportP.body: The function writes to the provided output stream a snippet that declares an imported target for a particular configuration. It builds the target’s exported name by concatenating the instance’s namespace with the target’s export name, then emits a header comment followed by a call to `set_property` that flags the imported configuration (using the uppercase form of the config name or a default “NOCONFIG” when empty). Finally it emits a `set_target_properties` block that lists each property key/value pair from the supplied map, escaping the value string before printing.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportT.body: Writes the script lines that create an imported target in the build file: builds the target name, emits the appropriate add_executable or add_library call for the target type, and sets properties such as enabling exports, marking frameworks or bundles, handling deprecation, and applying special flags for non‑system or system imports.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportT.body: The pure‑virtual `GenerateImportTargetsConfig` is meant to emit a serialized description of all import‑target entries into the supplied output stream (`std::ostream`). When a concrete exporter implements it, it will walk the internal data structures (probably a map of target names → settings) and write out the appropriate configuration lines or JSON/INI snippets that can later be parsed to recreate the import‑target table. The base class declares it pure‑virtual so every derived exporter class is forced to provide its own concrete serialization logic for the specific target format it supports.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportV.body: The function writes a single line to the output stream that sets a CMake variable indicating the format version of the import file; it uses the `clang-format off/on` directives to keep the line intact.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImporte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImporte.body: The function iterates over all targets that have been recorded for an import‑check, and for each target loops through the list of files that should be present. For each file it verifies that the file exists on disk; if it does not exist, an error message is emitted describing the missing file and possible reasons for the failure. The loop then cleans up all temporary variables before returning.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImporte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImporte.body: The routine generates a CMake‑style check list for the target being exported. It writes two list commands—one listing the target itself and another listing each file that the target imports. For each imported path, it looks up the associated property (from the imported‑file map) and emits its escaped value. The list lines are terminated with a closing parenthesis and newline.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateInterfa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateInterfa.body: Generates a block of property assignments for a target by writing a `set_target_properties` header followed by each key/value pair, escaping the value and closing the block when the property map is non‑empty.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateMainFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateMainFil.body: The protected pure virtual function `GenerateMainFile` is intended to be overridden by derived classes to serialize the main file contents into the supplied output stream. Implementations typically write the required data to the stream and return `true` on success or `false` if the write fails, allowing callers to react accordingly.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateMissing.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateMissing.body: This virtual member writes CMake directives that, during a package export, list every imported target that was expected but not found. It first emits the list of those missing targets, then generates a CMake block that sets a failure flag and emits a fatal‑error message containing the target names if any were absent. This logic ensures that an export which relies on other projects fails early with a clear diagnostic.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GeneratePolicyF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GeneratePolicyF.body: The method appends the literal text `cmake_policy(POP)` followed by a newline into the provided output stream.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GeneratePolicyH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GeneratePolicyH.body: The function writes a header that enforces a minimum CMake version of 2.8.3 by printing a version check that aborts if the current `CMAKE_MAJOR_VERSION` and `CMAKE_MINOR_VERSION` are older than the required threshold. It then pushes a policy stack to set the policy level to the oldest supported version for the current CMake release, ensuring that older policy warnings are suppressed while still enabling newer features.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateRequire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateRequire.body: The method writes a CMake block that aborts the build if the detected CMake version is lower than the required one.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateTargetF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateTargetF.body: The routine iterates over the target’s interface file sets, emits a CMake file‑set block for each one (including its type, base directories and file list), and appends directories for header‑only sets. It checks that every referenced file set exists, emitting a fatal error and aborting if not found.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetCxxModulesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetCxxModulesDi.body: The `GetCxxModulesDirectory` function is a pure virtual const member that subclasses must implement. It returns a `std::string` containing the path to the directory where Cxx modules are stored, allowing callers (e.g., `cmExportFileGenerator`) to retrieve the location without knowing concrete details. It is declared in the base interface and overridden in concrete derived classes to provide the appropriate directory name.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetFileSetDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetFileSetDirec.body: The `GetFileSetDirectories` function is an abstract hook that any concrete file‑exporter must implement. It’s job is to inspect the supplied `cmGeneratorTarget` instance and return a string that lists the directories in which the file set’s member files reside. Implementations typically walk the target’s internal data structures, resolve any relative paths, and concatenate the directory paths into a single string (often comma‑separated or newline‑separated). Because the method is pure virtual, each derived generator type provides its own logic for extracting the relevant directory information, making the function a convenient extension point for plug‑in modules that generate code or resources to the filesystem.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetFileSetFiles.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetFileSetFiles.body: The GetFileSetFiles routine accepts a cmGeneratorTarget* to obtain the file‑set string that represents the collection of files the exporter should use. When a subclass implements it, it typically resolves the target’s path information and concatenates the appropriate file names into a single string ready for output.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetMainExportFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetMainExportFi.body: The const member function simply returns a const reference to the member string `MainImportFile`. It returns that reference without copying or modifying any data.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetNamespace@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetNamespace@k_.body: Returns the value of the `Namespace` member (a string). It makes no changes to the object and returns the string by copy.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::HandleMissingTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::HandleMissingTa.body: A protected pure virtual function `HandleMissingTarget` is intended to be overridden by subclasses that know how to recover when a required library cannot be found during the linking phase. The implementation typically performs a diagnostic action—such as logging the missing library, cleaning up any partially‑bound symbols, or throwing a detailed exception—before allowing the program to terminate or retry. The function accepts a reference to a string containing the name of the missing target, so subclasses may use that value to construct a helpful error message or perform a lookup in an auxiliary cache. This contract ensures that any component inheriting from the exporter base class has a concrete, type‑safe path for handling the “missing target” situation.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::InstallNameDir@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::InstallNameDir@.body: The function computes the path string that will be used when a target is installed; it pulls together information from the target object and returns the full directory name that the build system will create in the output tree.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateCompati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateCompati.body: The routine first pulls the interface property identifiers defined for a target (including base, string, and numeric bounds), collates them into a set, and then injects each identifier into the supplied map under a key prefixed with “INTERFACE_”. If the target isn’t an interface library, it extends the set with any configuration‑specific interface names before filling the map.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateCxxModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateCxxModu.body: Populates a map of exported C++‑module properties. It first verifies that the target has CXX module sources; if so, it pulls a fixed set of properties—extensions, include directories, compile definitions, options, features, and link libraries—from the target’s current build context. For each property, it fetches the computed value (or plain property if not computed), preprocesses it through the generator expression system with the current context, and inserts the result into the passed‑in map. When the export is for an install interface it also rewrites any install‑prefixes and appends any destination‑directory includes. Once all properties have been collected and preprocessed, the function returns true.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateExportP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateExportP.body: The function inspects the target’s *EXPORT_PROPERTIES* list and, for each entry, checks that it is not a reserved “IMPORTED_*” or “INTERFACE_*” property. It retrieves the property’s value, verifies that the value is concrete (contains no generator expressions), and if valid, records it in the supplied map. If any property fails the checks, an error message is set and the function returns false. Otherwise the map is populated and the function returns true.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInclude.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInclude.body: The function first clears the current include‑directory list, reads the target’s *INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES* property, and parses the target’s install‑include directories. It evaluates those directories, prefixes them, and then combines the result with any pre‑existing includes. The merged string is re‑preprocessed, targets resolved, and finally the property map is updated. If a context‑sensitive include path is detected, the function aborts with a fatal error.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInterfa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInterfa.body: The function checks whether a target can be linked; if so, it pulls any of the three predefined “INTERFACE_LINK_…” properties from the target, preprocesses them with the current rule, resolves any generator expressions, and stores the resulting strings in the provided property map. It returns true only if at least one of those properties was present and successfully processed.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInterfa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInterfa.body: It forwards the supplied property name twice to a helper overload that populates the target’s property map.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInterfa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInterfa.body: The method pulls a value from the supplied `cmGeneratorTarget` using the property name, and if a value is returned, inserts that value into the provided `ImportPropertyMap` under the same key.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInterfa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateInterfa.body: Retrieves a property from the target, preprocesses it if present, resolves any embedded target references, and stores the final string in the supplied map under the given output name.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateLinkDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateLinkDep.body: The function verifies the preprocessing rule, fetches the “INTERFACE_LINK_DEPENDS” property from the target, skips if it’s missing or empty, then preprocesses the string, resolves any generator‑specific targets, validates the interface directories, and finally stores the cleaned‑up result back into the property map.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateLinkDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateLinkDir.body: The routine reads the `INTERFACE_LINK_DIRECTORIES` property from the target, skips processing if the property is absent or empty, otherwise it preprocesses the property string (applying the given rule), resolves any generator expressions inside, verifies the resulting directories through `checkInterfaceDirs`, and finally writes the validated list back into the provided properties map.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateSources.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::PopulateSources.body: The routine pulls the value of the special property `"INTERFACE_SOURCES"` from the target, skips if nothing is defined, and if the property contains a non‑empty string it runs the standard preprocessing logic. After resolving any internal references it validates that the derived interface directories are legitimate. If all checks pass, the final processed string is stored back in the `properties` map under the same key.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::ReplaceInstallP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::ReplaceInstallP.body: This private virtual method is a hook that derived classes can override to customize how an install‑prefix string is replaced. The base implementation performs no operation—simply returning without touching its argument.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::ResolveTargetsI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::ResolveTargetsI.body: The routine scans a generator‑expression string for three special marker formats – `$<TARGET_PROPERTY:…>`, `*TARGET_NAME:*` and `*LINK_ONLY:*`, `*COMPILE_ONLY:*`. For each marker it locates the token’s bounds, extracts the target name, validates that name (ensuring it’s a literal and reachable target), and if the target is acceptable it swaps the placeholder with the resolved target name in the input string. It tracks errors such as incomplete expressions or invalid target names, reporting them via the target’s local generator. The function also applies any install‑prefix replacement required by the generator.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::ResolveTargetsI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::ResolveTargetsI.body: The routine walks a string of generator expressions, splits it into individual tokens, and for each token decides whether it refers to a known target or namespace. It adds missing namespace bindings for un‑resolvable tokens and recursively resolves nested expressions, rebuilding the string only after all tokens have been processed.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetExportFile@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetExportFile@k.body: The method stores the provided file name, then pulls apart its path components: it records the full path, extracts the directory portion, strips the final extension to obtain the base filename, and captures the last extension separately.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetExportOld@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetExportOld@k_.body: The method assigns the supplied boolean to the internal flag that governs whether export operations use legacy (old) behavior.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetImportDetail.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetImportDetail.body:
The function walks through a target’s configuration and records metadata that the export system needs to know when the target is imported. It

* pulls the target’s shared‑library SONAME if the target is a shared library or module library, and stores that value under a property whose name ends with the supplied suffix.
* records the link‑interface languages and private dependencies that a consuming linker will need to load, emitting them as “IMPORTED_LINK_INTERFACE_LANGUAGES” and “IMPORTED_LINK_DEPENDENT_LIBRARIES”.
* if the target is a managed build (not a native one) it records the runtime language (or “CSharp” for C# only projects) under “IMPORTED_COMMON_LANGUAGE_RUNTIME”.

In short, it populates an import‑property map with SONAME, link‑interface information, and the managed‑runtime flag so that downstream tools know how to load or link the target.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetImportLinkIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetImportLinkIn.body: The function retrieves a link‑interface definition from a target. If the interface is marked as an implementation, it records the associated libraries in the property map and returns. Otherwise it looks up either a suffixed or generic “LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES” property, validates that the target’s CMP0022 policy is still legacy‑compatible, and, if the value is non‑empty, pre‑processes the string (resolving any generator expressions) before storing it in the map under the key “IMPORTED_LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES” + suffix. If any step fails the function simply returns, clearing the property entry.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetImportLinkPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetImportLinkPr.body: The function iterates over a vector of generic entries, concatenating them into a semi‑colon separated string that may include a target namespace when `targetNames==Yes`. It then appends this string into a property map under a key formed from the supplied property name plus suffix, effectively registering the import‑link property for later use.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetNamespace@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::SetNamespace@k_.body: The method simply assigns the provided string to the object’s `Namespace` member, overwriting whatever value was previously stored. It takes a const reference to `std::string` and performs a direct assignment (`this->Namespace = ns;`). No validation or side‑effects are performed.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::cmExportFileGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::cmExportFileGen.body: The `cmExportFileGenerator` constructor initializes a new generator instance by copying the configuration and state from an existing `cmExportFileGenerator` object, ensuring that the new instance starts with identical export‑file parameters and internal state.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::cmExportFileGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::cmExportFileGen.body: The constructor simply initializes two internal flags to `false`: it sets `AppendMode` to `false` (meaning no appending when exporting) and `ExportOld` to `false` (meaning it will not export old versions).

@lcmExportFileGenerator::operator=@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::operator=@k_ZN2.body: The operator= copies the state of another cmExportFileGenerator into the current object and returns a reference to the current instance.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::~cmExportFileGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::~cmExportFileGe.body: When an instance of `cmExportFileGenerator` is destroyed, the compiler‑generated destructor runs automatically, invoking any base‑class cleanup and releasing owned resources without any explicit code.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Cle.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Cle.body: Releases any intermediate data structures that were allocated for the export process, ensuring that all temporary buffers are cleaned and no residual data remains in memory.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The function writes the expected target entries into the provided output stream, emitting the appropriate configuration fragments needed for the Android build system to recognize and process each target during installation.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The `GenerateImportFileConfig` function is a protected virtual method that receives a string reference (likely a file path or identifier) and simply returns `true`. In practice it is a placeholder that probably performs validation or setup of import‑file configuration data before delegating to the real implementation. It currently contains no logic beyond the unconditional return, serving as a stub or default success indicator.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The protected virtual `GenerateImportFooterCode` is an extension point used by concrete `ExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator` implementations to emit any finalization code that should appear after the main import section in the generated Android Make‑file. Sub‑classes override it to inject their own footer logic—such as closing pragmas, adding helper function wrappers, or appending cleanup directives—before the generated file is finalized.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The routine emits a shell‑style import header that defines the installation path and a relative import prefix. It calculates how many “../” segments are needed to reach the root from the current install directory, writes those directives to the output stream, and finally iterates over each export target. For every non‑empty export it assigns a `__dest` property pointing to the target’s destination (obtained from either its library or archive generator).

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The function writes a formatted import‑prefix string into the provided output stream—generally the prefix required to correctly include the generated CMake files during the install phase. It relies on helper utilities to compose the appropriate namespace and file‑path tokens before streaming them.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: Generates the import‐property definitions for an Android export target, writing each entry from the supplied property map into the provided output stream as a CMake macro/variable definition.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The function builds a module name from the namespace and target’s export name, then emits a minimal CMakeMakefile‑style declaration: it adds an “include” line, declares the module variable, and appends a path derived from the target’s destination property, finally writing the full target path (potentially overridden by an explicit configuration string).

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: Iterates over the collection of imported files, executes validation checks on each entry, and streams the diagnostic results to the supplied output stream.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The function iterates over the given set of file identifiers, retrieves the corresponding property information from the supplied `ImportPropertyMap`, and emits to the output stream the CMake expressions required to enforce that each file referenced in the import properties has been correctly installed and satisfies the expected checks (for example existence, permissions, or versioning) before the generated build script proceeds.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: This method extracts the first configuration string (if any) from the instance’s configuration list and then forwards the target, stream and properties along with that configuration string to the base class’s `GenerateInterfaceProperties` implementation for handling the actual generation.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The method writes a runtime check into the build script that verifies whether the expected targets are present; if any are missing it aborts the build with an informative diagnostic.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The function **GeneratePolicyFooterCode** is a protected virtual override that writes the closing portion of a policy definition to the supplied output stream. It handles any necessary formatting tokens—such as closing braces, delimiters, or final comments—so that a generated policy file is syntactically complete and ready for downstream use.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The function is responsible for emitting the boiler‑plate header section of a generated policy file, pulling in the required include directives, namespace wrappers, and any standard licence or author‑information comments that precede the policy implementation. Its protected virtual signature allows subclasses to extend or replace that header logic.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Gen.body: The function writes the required CMake version string into the output stream (typically a build file). It takes a stream and a string identifying the needed version and writes the appropriate “required CMake version” line into that stream.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Loa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::Loa.body: The function reads configuration files from the specified directories and parses them into internal data structures for use during the installer's execution.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::cmE.body:
The `cmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator` function is the entry point for generating an Android‑specific “export‑install” makefile. When invoked it simply constructs an instance of `cmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator`, which inherits the generic file‑generation logic from `cmExportInstallFileGenerator` and augments it with Android‑specific rules (e.g., target paths, Android SDK paths, resource handling). Internally it:

1. Reads the export‑install configuration passed in.  
2. Builds a makefile skeleton that copies files to the appropriate Android install directories.  
3. Emits the final makefile through its `Generate()` routine.  

The function itself is a thin wrapper that orchestrates the above steps, ensuring the Android build system receives a correctly‑formatted installation script.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::cmE.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied generator pointer to its base class (`cmExportInstallFileGenerator`), establishing the instance that will subsequently handle exporting the Android‑specific Make‑file generator.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::cmE.body: The function creates a new export‑install generator instance by copying the configuration from an existing generator object. This new instance is then used to build the Android makefile that drives the installation process.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::ope.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::ope.body: The `operator=` function is an overloaded assignment operator that copies the state from another `cmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator` instance into the current object, returning a reference to `*this`. It ensures any internal resources (e.g., file handles or configuration data) are properly duplicated or released before overwriting, guarding against self‑assignment and resource leaks.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::ope.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::ope.body: The assignment operator takes a const reference to another `cmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator` instance and copies all of its internal state into the current object, returning a reference to `*this`.

@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::~cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator::~cm.body: The function generates the Makefile snippet that drives an Android‑specific export‑install build—collecting the target paths, configuring the install rules, and writing the resulting `Android.mk` into the designated output directory.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::CleanupT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::CleanupT.body: The function emits a comment marker followed by a “set” command that resets the import‑prefix flag, inserting these lines into the output stream when the generator is told to clean up its temporary state.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Complain.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Complain.body: The routine gathers the names of the two targets involved and the list of export‑sets that the second target belongs to. It then constructs a diagnostic string that states that the first target depends on the second one, but that dependent target is not present in the current export set (or is present in several other export sets). Finally, it calls cmSystemTools::Error to emit that message as an error.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::FindName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::FindName.body: The function searches the export sets of a generator for any export that matches the supplied target name. When a match is found, it collects every destination file associated with that export’s installations and records the namespace in which those exports reside. Finally it returns the list of destination files together with the namespace string.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.body: The function writes a snippet of CMake code that, for a given module name, opens the current CMake list directory, reads all matching “cxx‑modules‑<name>‑*.cmake” files, includes each of them, and then clears the temporary variables used. The code is emitted to an output stream.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.body: The routine creates a CMake include file in the C++ modules directory. It first determines the destination path, defaults the config name if empty, and records the generated file in the internal maps. It then iterates over each exported target: if the target contains C++ module sources it appends an include directive for a target‑specific script file and records that file in the target‑file vector. On any stream error it reports an error and returns false; otherwise it returns true after writing all necessary include lines.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.body: The function first checks whether the given configuration should be processed; if it’s not enabled it simply returns true. It builds a file name from the base and extension, opens a stream to that file, writes the import header, the per‑config information, and the footer, records the file name in a map, and returns true when successful or false on failure.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.body:
The routine computes the value for the `_IMPORT_PREFIX` variable used by the CMake import system.  
If the export path is an absolute path it writes the fixed prefix that was configured.  
Otherwise it emits commands that walk up the directory tree from the current list file until it reaches the export location, generating the relative path that will become the import prefix.  It also includes a special branch that keeps the original prefix when the resolved path ends up on a `/usr/lib…` symlink that would otherwise be rewritten by the relative walk.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.body: The function walks through each target export in the current export set. For each target (except those marked as interface libraries) it gathers import‑location data from the various generators (archive, library, runtime, objects, framework, bundle). Once any location is found, it enriches the import map with the target’s details, link interface info, and finally writes the resulting import‑property code and the corresponding file‑check code into the export file stream.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::Generate.body: The function gathers all export targets, deduces the minimum CMake version needed, emits import‑library code, loads configuration files, writes per‑configuration import files, and appends checks for missing targets before returning a success flag.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetConfi.body: Creates a glob string that joins the object’s base file name, a hyphened wildcard segment, and the desired file extension. The resulting pattern—e.g. “Base‑*-ext”—is returned for later use in locating or matching configuration‑import files.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetCxxMo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetCxxMo.body: The method simply forwards a request to the `IEGen` instance: it calls `IEGen->GetCxxModuleDirectory()` and returns that value unchanged. The function is `const` and `virtual`, so callers may override it, but the default implementation is just a thin wrapper that retrieves the current C++‑module directory string.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetExpor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetExpor.body: The function returns the target type of a target export. It first retrieves the type from the target, then, if the target is an object library but has no `ObjectsGenerator`, it treats it as an interface library by changing the type to `INTERFACE_LIBRARY`. Finally it returns the adjusted type.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetFileS.body: It builds a list of destination directories for a file‑set by iterating over the available generator configs, escaping the resulting paths for CMake, and handling special context‑sensitive cases (e.g., C++ module interface files). The resulting vector of paths is then joined into a space‑separated string and returned.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetFileS.body: The routine iterates over each generator configuration for a given file‑set. For every configuration it gathers the corresponding directory and file entries, evaluates the destination path (adding a prefix if the path isn’t absolute), escapes filenames for CMake, and conditionally prefixes configuration tags when the build is context‑sensitive. It collects the resulting escaped names in a vector and finally joins them into a single space‑separated string returned to the caller.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::HandleMi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::HandleMi.body:
The routine looks up the exported target for a dependent target that is missing.  
It pulls that target’s name, fetches the global generator context, and queries the export list for the target’s name.  
If the list contains exactly one file, it builds a missing‑target string (the file name plus the export name), appends it to the supplied `link_libs` string, and records the missing target in the `MissingTargets` collection.  
If more than one file is found, it treats this as a user‑error and triggers the complaint‑handler.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::InstallN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::InstallN.body: The routine checks whether the makefile’s CMAKE_PLATFORM_HAS_INSTALLNAME flag is set; if it is, it asks the target to compute an install‑path string using the given config and a fixed import‑prefix, and returns that string.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::LoadConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::LoadConf.body: The function writes a CMake snippet that iterates over every file matched by the glob returned from `GetConfigImportFileGlob()` and includes each of those files. It emits the foreach‑include‑unset pattern to the supplied stream.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::ReplaceI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::ReplaceI.body: The method delegates string replacement to the base class `cmGeneratorExpression`, passing the input string and the `${_IMPORT_PREFIX}` placeholder, effectively updating the string with the appropriate import prefix.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::SetImpor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::SetImpor.body: The function checks whether an install target is applicable to a given configuration. If so, it builds the path where the target will be installed, and stores this path under a property key in the provided map. Depending on the target’s kind (import library, object library, framework, bundle, etc.) it selects the appropriate property name (e.g., IMPORTED_IMPLIB, IMPORTED_OBJECTS, IMPORTED_LOCATION) and the value contains the relative path plus any required suffix. The function also handles special cases such as relative installation prefixes or Apple‑specific bundle layout. The end result is a populated map of import‑location properties for that target.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::cmExport.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::cmExport.body: The constructor records the supplied `cmInstallExportGenerator*` in the member `IEGen`, establishing the generator that the object will later use to create export‑install files.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::~cmExpor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::~cmExpor.body: The function `~cmExportInstallFileGenerator()` provides a custom implementation of the virtual file‑generation routine defined in the base class `cmExportFileGenerator`. When invoked, it produces a ready‑to‑install bundle based on the current export context, assembling any required metadata, packaging artifacts, and configuring installation hooks. This specialized routine is typically called by callers that need to materialise an installable artifact instead of a standard export.

@lcmExportSet::AddInstallation@k_ZN11cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportSet::AddInstallation@k_ZN11cmE.body: The `AddInstallation` method appends the supplied `cmInstallExportGenerator` instance to the internal `Installations` container, enabling the exporter to track newly created installation data.

@lcmExportSet::AddTargetExport@k_ZN11cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportSet::AddTargetExport@k_ZN11cmE.body: The function `AddTargetExport` accepts a `std::unique_ptr<cmTargetExport>` and appends it to the internal collection (`TargetExports`). It simply moves the pointer into the vector, adding the new export to the set.

@lcmExportSet::Compute@k_ZN11cmExportSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportSet::Compute@k_ZN11cmExportSet.body: Iterates over each entry in `TargetExports`, retrieves the target for that export, and verifies that every interface file set in the target has a corresponding entry in the export’s `FileSetGenerators`. If any file set is missing, it logs a fatal‑error message and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmExportSet::GetName@k_ZNK11cmExportSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportSet::GetName@k_ZNK11cmExportSe.body: The `GetName()` member simply exposes the stored `Name` string as a read‑only reference. Because the function is marked `const`, callers are guaranteed that calling it cannot modify the object, and because it returns a `const&` the returned reference cannot be used to alter the string either. This guarantees that the internal `Name` member remains unchanged while still allowing efficient, read‑only access without copying the whole string.

@lcmExportSet::cmExportSet@k_ZN11cmExpor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportSet::cmExportSet@k_ZN11cmExpor.body: The constructor simply stores the provided string into the `Name` member by moving it into place, leaving the object in a minimal state with no further initialization.

@lcmExportSet::~cmExportSet@k_ZN11cmExpo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportSet::~cmExportSet@k_ZN11cmExpo.body: The destructor `~cmExportSet()` automatically releases any owned resources, such as memory or file handles, when an instance of `cmExportSet` is destroyed. It has a default implementation, so no custom cleanup logic is required unless the class manages external resources.

@lcmExportSetMap::operator[]@k_ZN14cmExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportSetMap::operator[]@k_ZN14cmExp.body: The operator returns a reference to the `ExportSet` associated with the supplied name. If the name is absent from the internal map, a new empty export set is constructed, inserted into the map, and then returned.

@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::FindT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::FindT.body: FindTargets retrieves a target’s property; if it’s missing it returns an empty string. Otherwise it parses the property as a generator expression (creating a special DAG‑checker when the property is “INTERFACE_LINK_OPTIONS”), evaluates that expression in a dummy target context, collects every target referenced by the expression, records any new targets in the exported list, and finally returns the resulting string.

@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::Gener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::Gener.body: Process each target in the export list only once. For each one, it emits the appropriate import code, gathers the interface‑specific properties (by invoking the language‑specific target finder via the macro), stores them in a map, and finally writes out the interface properties.

@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::GetFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::GetFi.body: Converts a cmFileSet’s directory entries into an escaped string via cmOutputConverter::EscapeForCMake.

@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::GetFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::GetFi.body: Retrieves the file names from the supplied `cmFileSet`, converts the list to a CMake‑ready string (escaping any special characters) via `cmOutputConverter::EscapeForCMake`, and returns that string.

@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::Insta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::Insta.body: The method checks whether the current target’s makefile is configured to use an “install name” directory (via the `CMAKE_PLATFORM_HAS_INSTALLNAME` flag). If that flag is present, it pulls the corresponding directory string from the target (via `GetInstallNameDirForBuildTree`) and returns it; otherwise the result remains an empty string.

@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::Popul.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::Popul.body: The routine walks through all property keys of a generator target, filling the supplied property map with those values that exist. For any key that matches one of the special prefixes (“IMPORTED_LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES”, “IMPORTED_LINK_DEPENDENT_LIBRARIES”, or “INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES”), it resolves the referenced targets, adds any newly‑seen target to the exported list, and records the target in the emitted set so it isn’t processed again.

@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::SetCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::SetCo.body: The method assigns the supplied configuration string to the object's `Config` member, copying the value via a const reference to avoid unnecessary copying.

@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::cmExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::cmExp.body: The constructor initializes a **cmExportTryCompileFileGenerator** instance by recording the requested target languages and immediately populating the corresponding exported objects by invoking `gg->CreateImportedGenerationObjects(mf, targets, this->Exports)`.

@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::~cmEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportTryCompileFileGenerator::~cmEx.body: The `~cmExportTryCompileFileGenerator` function orchestrates the generation of an export‑ready file from a source specification. It first validates the target path, then invokes the base `cmExportFileGenerator` machinery to serialize the data object into the appropriate format. If the serialization step fails, it records the error and aborts; otherwise it finalises the file and returns success.

@lcmExprParserHelper::Error@k_ZN18cmExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::Error@k_ZN18cmExpr.body: The function captures the current input buffer position, formats an error message string containing the supplied text and that position, and stores it in the member variable `ErrorString`.

@lcmExprParserHelper::GetError@k_ZN18cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::GetError@k_ZN18cmE.body: GetError returns a pointer to the internal string held in ErrorString. It essentially gives callers C‑style access to the error message that has been recorded in the object. This is a trivial, read‑only accessor; its usefulness and safety depend entirely on the lifetime of the underlying string.

@lcmExprParserHelper::GetResult@k_ZNK18c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::GetResult@k_ZNK18c.body:
The function returns the stored 64‑bit integer `Result`.  
Because it is declared `const`, callers cannot modify any member state.  
The function returns the value by value, not by reference.  
If `Result` is large or expensive to copy, consider returning a reference or move semantics.  
If `Result` is not initialized before use, callers must guard against an uninitialized value.

@lcmExprParserHelper::GetWarning@k_ZNK18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::GetWarning@k_ZNK18.body: The function is a const accessor that returns a read‑only reference to the internal `WarningString` member. It simply returns that reference, allowing callers to read the stored warning without copying the string, and guarantees that the returned reference cannot be used to modify the underlying data.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParseString@k_ZN18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParseString@k_ZN18.body: The function initializes parsing state from the supplied string, runs a generated parser on that buffer, captures any parsing or evaluation exception, records an explanatory error message in its internal error string, and finally returns success (1) or failure (0) according to whether an error was recorded.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::Parser.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::Parser.body: The constructor duplicates an existing ParserType instance, copying every internal field so the new object starts in the same state as the source. It preserves the parser’s configuration and any cached data needed for subsequent parsing operations.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::Parser.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::Parser.body: Parses input data by constructing and returning an appropriate parser object—essentially a convenience wrapper that exposes the parser’s interface to the rest of the system.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::operat.body: This overload takes a const reference to another `ParserType` and copies its state into the current object, then returns a reference to that object so the assignment can be chained.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::~Parse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::~Parse.body: ~ParserType() parses the input data stream, maps it to the appropriate concrete type according to the registered parsers, and then returns an instantiated object. The routine consolidates type‑resolution logic and enforces validation before passing the created instance to the caller.

@lcmExprParserHelper::SetResult@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::SetResult@k_ZN18cm.body: The method assigns the supplied 64‑bit integer to the internal `Result` member, overwriting any previous value.

@lcmExprParserHelper::cmExprParserHelper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::cmExprParserHelper.body: The constructor initializes three members: `FileLine` is set to –1 (indicating no line has been parsed yet), `FileName` is cleared to a null pointer, and `Result` is reset to zero.

@lcmExprParserHelper::~cmExprParserHelpe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::~cmExprParserHelpe.body: The ~cmExprParserHelper destructor simply performs the automatic cleanup that the compiler supplies for a defaulted destructor: it releases any resources owned by a cmExprParserHelper instance (for example, destroying member objects or freeing allocated memory) when an object of that class goes out of scope.

@lcmExpr_yy_create_buffer@k_Z23cmExpr_yy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yy_create_buffer@k_Z23cmExpr_yy.body: The routine builds a new scanning buffer: it allocates a `yy_buffer_state` structure, stores the requested size, allocates a character array that is two bytes larger (to hold two EOF terminators), flags that the buffer belongs to this scanner, and then calls `yy_init_buffer` to set up the buffer’s internal state before returning the handle.

@lcmExpr_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z23cmExpr_yy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z23cmExpr_yy.body: The routine checks whether the supplied buffer pointer is non‑null; if it is the currently‑used buffer it clears that global reference, then releases the buffer’s internal memory via yyfree before freeing the buffer struct itself.

@lcmExpr_yy_flush_buffer@k_Z22cmExpr_yy_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yy_flush_buffer@k_Z22cmExpr_yy_.body: The routine clears a buffer in a scanner: it zeroes the character counter, puts two sentinel end‑of‑buffer markers into the buffer slot, resets the buffer pointer to the start, marks the buffer as “new” and flags that the parser is at a beginning‑of‑line. If the buffer being reset is the one currently in use, it triggers a reload of the buffer state.

@lcmExpr_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z21cmExpr_yy_s.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z21cmExpr_yy_s.body: `yy_scan_buffer` sets up a scanning buffer for the lexer. It receives a base address, the buffer’s size, and the scanner type, then returns a `YY_BUFFER_STATE` indicating whether the buffer was successfully created or an error occurred. This helper is used when initializing or resetting the lexer’s input source.

@lcmExpr_yy_scan_bytes@k_Z20cmExpr_yy_sc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yy_scan_bytes@k_Z20cmExpr_yy_sc.body: Allocates a temporary buffer, copies the given byte sequence into it, appends two end‑of‑buffer markers, hands the buffer to the core scanner routine, and tags the returned buffer object as owned so it can be freed later.

@lcmExpr_yy_scan_string@k_Z21cmExpr_yy_s.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yy_scan_string@k_Z21cmExpr_yy_s.body: Computes the string’s length with `strlen` and forwards the raw buffer and that length to the core byte‑scanning routine, returning its result.

@lcmExpr_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z26cmExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z26cmExpr.body: Switches the lexer’s current buffer to the one specified in new_buffer. It first guarantees the buffer‑stack is valid, returns immediately if the requested buffer is already active, and otherwise flushes the current buffer’s state (position and char count) into its structure. The new buffer is then set as current, the corresponding buffer state is loaded, and a flag marking that a buffer switch occurred during an EOF transition is set.

@lcmExpr_yyalloc@k_Z14cmExpr_yyallocmPv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyalloc@k_Z14cmExpr_yyallocmPv.body: The function `yyalloc` takes a requested byte count (`yy_size_t`) and a scanner context (`yyscan_t`) and returns a pointer to a freshly allocated block. The allocation is performed through the scanner’s internal pool allocator, ensuring the memory is tagged for the lexer’s lifetime and avoiding per‑allocation overhead. The returned pointer is expected to be zero‑initialized and is used by the lexer to store token data or intermediate parsing structures.

@lcmExpr_yyerror@k_ZL14cmExpr_yyerrorPvP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyerror@k_ZL14cmExpr_yyerrorPvP.body: The routine passes the supplied error message straight to the current scanner’s error‑handling callback, retrieving that callback from the scanner’s auxiliary data store.

@lcmExpr_yyfree@k_Z13cmExpr_yyfreePvS_@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyfree@k_Z13cmExpr_yyfreePvS_@f.body: The `cmExpr_yyfree` routine simply deallocates a previously‑allocated chunk. It accepts an opaque scanner handle, immediately casts it to an internal `yguts_t` structure (though the handle is unused), and calls `free()` on the supplied pointer after casting it to `char*` to satisfy the legacy allocator interface. No other bookkeeping is performed.

@lcmExpr_yyget_column@k_Z19cmExpr_yyget_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyget_column@k_Z19cmExpr_yyget_.body: The routine casts the scanner handle to its internal structure, checks whether a current buffer exists, and then returns the stored column value; if no buffer is present it simply returns 0.

@lcmExpr_yyget_debug@k_Z18cmExpr_yyget_d.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyget_debug@k_Z18cmExpr_yyget_d.body: The function casts its argument to the internal scanner‑state structure and simply returns the global flag that controls whether the lexer prints its internal debug traces. It does nothing but expose that flag to callers.

@lcmExpr_yyget_extra@k_Z18cmExpr_yyget_e.author: AI Short Overview
