@lcmExpr_yyget_extra@k_Z18cmExpr_yyget_e.body: The function casts the opaque scanner handle to its internal guts structure and simply returns the `yyextra` field stored therein – the extra data that callers expect to retrieve from the scanner context.

@lcmExpr_yyget_in@k_Z15cmExpr_yyget_inPv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyget_in@k_Z15cmExpr_yyget_inPv.body: The function casts the scanner handle to its internal `yyguts_t` struct and simply returns the `yyin` member, which holds the input stream for the lexer.

@lcmExpr_yyget_leng@k_Z17cmExpr_yyget_le.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyget_leng@k_Z17cmExpr_yyget_le.body: The routine simply returns the internal `yyleng` field from the scanner’s internal `yyguts_t` structure—essentially a tiny accessor that casts the generic scanner handle to the concrete struct and returns that field.

@lcmExpr_yyget_lineno@k_Z19cmExpr_yyget_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyget_lineno@k_Z19cmExpr_yyget_.body: It returns the current line number of the scanner if a buffer is active; otherwise it returns zero.

@lcmExpr_yyget_out@k_Z16cmExpr_yyget_out.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyget_out@k_Z16cmExpr_yyget_out.body: The function simply interprets the scanner handle as a pointer to its internal structure and returns the stored `yyout` file pointer, which represents the output stream that the parser writes to.

@lcmExpr_yyget_text@k_Z17cmExpr_yyget_te.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyget_text@k_Z17cmExpr_yyget_te.body: The function casts the opaque scanner handle to its internal `yyguts_t` structure and returns the pointer to the stored text buffer (`yytext`).

@lcmExpr_yylex@k_Z12cmExpr_yylexPN18cmEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yylex@k_Z12cmExpr_yylexPN18cmEx.body: The routine scans input through a deterministic automaton, matching one of a handful of token types—decimal or hex numbers, the arithmetic operators (+ – * / % | & ^), parentheses, and end‑of‑file markers. Once a pattern is matched it executes the associated action: assigning a value to the token‐value structure and returning the appropriate enum (e.g., exp_NUMBER, exp_PLUS). The function also handles buffer transitions, EOF handling, and reports any unexpected characters that do not fit a defined token.

@lcmExpr_yylex_destroy@k_Z20cmExpr_yylex.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yylex_destroy@k_Z20cmExpr_yylex.body: The routine walks through the internal buffer stack, deallocates each buffer, then frees the stack itself and any start‑state stack that was allocated. It clears all static pointers (including the global context) and finally resets the lexer instance to a clean, NULL‑state so that the object can be safely discarded.

@lcmExpr_yylex_init@k_Z17cmExpr_yylex_in.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yylex_init@k_Z17cmExpr_yylex_in.body: The routine validates the supplied globals pointer, allocates a `yyguts_t` structure via `yyalloc`, zeroes its contents, and then forwards the newly‑allocated handle to `yy_init_globals()`, signalling allocation or initialization failure by setting `errno` and returning `1`.

@lcmExpr_yylex_init_extra@k_Z23cmExpr_yy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yylex_init_extra@k_Z23cmExpr_yy.body: This routine registers a user‑supplied extra type, allocates a `yyguts_t` block, zero‑initialises it, attaches the extra data to the global state, and finally calls `yy_init_globals` to perform the remaining system initialisation.

@lcmExpr_yyparse@k_Z14cmExpr_yyparsePv@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyparse@k_Z14cmExpr_yyparsePv@f.body: The routine implements a hand‑crafted LR parser that reads input tokens via the scanner, maintains a state stack and a value stack, and performs reductions according to the grammar table. It drives the parse by shifting tokens, shifting on table entries, and when a rule’s right‑hand side is matched it applies the corresponding semantic action. The code contains a large switch‑case that sets the semantic value for each rule (rules 2–24) and a sequence of macros that handle error recovery, token discarding, and stack reallocation. The function returns 0 on success, 1 on failure, and 2 on memory exhaustion.

@lcmExpr_yypop_buffer_state@k_Z25cmExpr_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yypop_buffer_state@k_Z25cmExpr_.body: The routine clears the current buffer: it first checks for an active buffer, deletes it, clears the global buffer pointer, reduces the stack depth if any buffers remain, and if a new buffer is still active it reloads that buffer state and flags it as having switched on EOF.

@lcmExpr_yypush_buffer_state@k_Z26cmExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yypush_buffer_state@k_Z26cmExpr.body: Pushes the supplied buffer onto the internal stack, copying its position and character‑count fields into the new current buffer slot and flagging that a buffer switch has just taken place.

@lcmExpr_yyrealloc@k_Z16cmExpr_yyrealloc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyrealloc@k_Z16cmExpr_yyrealloc.body: The function reallocates a memory block supplied via its first argument, using the supplied size and a scanner context, returning the resized pointer that is used throughout the parser to grow internal tables or buffers.

@lcmExpr_yyrestart@k_Z16cmExpr_yyrestart.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyrestart@k_Z16cmExpr_yyrestart.body: Accepts a FILE pointer and a scanner handle, casts the handle to its internal struct, guarantees a buffer stack is present, creates or re‑uses the current buffer when absent, then initializes that buffer with the supplied file and finally restores the buffer state for subsequent scanning.

@lcmExpr_yyset_column@k_Z19cmExpr_yyset_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyset_column@k_Z19cmExpr_yyset_.body: The routine updates the current column index in the scanner’s context, first verifying that a buffer is active; if no buffer is present it aborts with a fatal error.

@lcmExpr_yyset_debug@k_Z18cmExpr_yyset_d.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyset_debug@k_Z18cmExpr_yyset_d.body: The routine applies a new debug flag value to the parsing engine. It casts the supplied scanner handle to the internal `yyguts_t` structure, then writes the flag value into the global `yy_flex_debug` field so subsequent lexer actions respect the requested debug mode.

@lcmExpr_yyset_extra@k_Z18cmExpr_yyset_e.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyset_extra@k_Z18cmExpr_yyset_e.body: The routine stores the supplied user‐defined value into the scanner’s internal “extra” field by first casting the opaque scanner handle to the concrete `yyguts_t` structure and then assigning the value to the `yyextra` member.

@lcmExpr_yyset_in@k_Z15cmExpr_yyset_inPi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyset_in@k_Z15cmExpr_yyset_inPi.body: The function `yyset_in` assigns the supplied `FILE*` to the global variable `yyin` that the scanner uses to read input. It casts the provided scanner handle to its internal type `yyguts_t` to keep the pointer local. The routine performs no validation; it simply performs the assignment, so callers must ensure that the arguments are valid before invoking it.

@lcmExpr_yyset_lineno@k_Z19cmExpr_yyset_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyset_lineno@k_Z19cmExpr_yyset_.body: The routine assigns the new line number to the scanner’s global counter after ensuring a current input buffer is present; if no buffer is active, it aborts with a fatal error.

@lcmExpr_yyset_out@k_Z16cmExpr_yyset_out.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyset_out@k_Z16cmExpr_yyset_out.body: This routine assigns the supplied `FILE*` to the parser’s internal output handle (`yyout`). It performs a simple cast from the generic scanner object to the concrete `yyguts_t` structure and stores the pointer in `yyg`. No additional logic or checks are performed.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Cr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Cr.body: The method returns a string. It checks whether the provided strings are empty; if one is empty it returns the other (or an empty string if both are). When both are non‑empty, it concatenates them with a space‑dash‑space separator, producing `extraGenerator + " - " + globalGenerator`.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::En.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::En.body: This function receives three arguments—though all are unused—but represents the point where the project generator can turn a particular language on or off. When invoked, it would normally validate that the requested language is supported, adjust internal settings accordingly, and trigger any necessary bookkeeping (e.g., updating flags that influence subsequent file‑generation steps). In the supplied code body, no action occurs; the function is currently a no‑op placeholder.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Ge.body: The `Generate` method is an abstract entry point that derived classes must implement; it encapsulates the concrete logic for producing the appropriate output (e.g., a makefile or project file) during the build‑generation phase.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Ge.body: The `GetName()` member simply returns a copy of the object’s internal `Name` field; its `const` qualifier guarantees that it does not modify the object and that the returned string can be safely used without side‑effects.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Ge.body: Returns a reference to the internal `SupportedGlobalGenerators` vector, giving read‑only access to the list of global generators that the instance supports.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Op.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Op.body: The `Open` member performs the (currently unimplemented) logic required to initialise a project generator using a supplied bindir and project name. When called it simply returns `false`, signalling that the operation was not performed—this placeholder represents the point where the real implementation would perform the necessary initialisation steps (e.g., validate paths, parse makefile data, and launch the generator) before marking success.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Se.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Se.body: Assigns the supplied pointer to the instance’s member, storing it for later use.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Se.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Se.body: Assigns the supplied string to the class’s `Name` member. It accepts the argument by constant reference so no copy is performed before the assignment.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::op.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::op.body: Copies the state of the given `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator` instance into the current instance and returns a reference to the current instance.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::~c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::~c.body: The `~cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator()` destructor is declared virtual and defaulted. This means that any derived class will automatically invoke this destructor when destroyed, and that the compiler will generate the destructor body to perform default destruction (i.e., destroying member objects automatically). This ensures proper cleanup of resources when an instance of the class hierarchy is destroyed.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: The `AddSupportedGlobalGenerator` method simply appends the supplied `base` string to the `SupportedGlobalGenerators` collection, enabling the factory to remember that this generator type is now supported.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: The function **CreateExternalMakefileProjectGenerator** constructs and returns an instance of the external‑makefile project generator. In practice it is invoked in various modules to obtain a configured generator that knows how to write the appropriate `Makefile` entries for a project; the returned object is stored in a local variable and used to drive the generation process.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: The method simply returns the value of the `Documentation` member. It does nothing else—no validation, no side‑effects, and guarantees const‑correctness.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: The method returns the stored `Name` member of the `cmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFactory` object. It simply returns that string without performing any logic beyond the return statement.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: This member function simply returns the internally stored list of supported global generators, keeping the original collection intact.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: A constructor for the `cmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFactory` class takes two string arguments—`n` (the name) and `doc` (the documentation). It assigns these values to the `Name` and `Documentation` member variables using move semantics to avoid copying.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: The function is a constructor that creates a factory object for external‑makefile projects. It stores the configuration needed to instantiate a `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator` when requested. It is used in the build‑system code (see line 70 of `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator.h`).

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: The `operator=` assigns a new `cmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFactory` instance to the current object, copying its internal state and returning a reference to the updated instance.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: The virtual destructor for `cmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFactory` simply performs the standard cleanup for the factory object—releasing any owned resources and ensuring derived classes are properly destructed. No custom teardown logic is implemented beyond the default behavior.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorSimp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorSimp.body: The method allocates a `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator`, assigns it the current object's name with `SetName(this->GetName())`, and returns the instance as a `std::unique_ptr`.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorSimp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorSimp.body: Creates an instance of the simple‑makefile generator factory, passing the supplied name and documentation string to the base `cmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFactory` constructor. No additional setup is performed in this constructor.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::AppendTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::AppendTarg.body: The function serialises a build target into XML: it emits options for output directories, compile definitions, include paths, and sets up the compiler and command elements that drive the build command for that target.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::BuildMakeC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::BuildMakeC.body: BuildMakeCommand assembles a command line string for running a build tool. It picks the appropriate syntax for the current generator (NMake, MinGW, Ninja, or generic), escapes spaces in the makefile path where required, appends flags for verbosity and target selection, and returns the fully‑constructed command string.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::CreateDumm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::CreateDumm.body: This function builds a unique temporary file name for an object‑library target, creates that file in the build tree, writes a minimal comment header into it, and returns the full path.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::CreateNewP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::CreateNewP.body: The routine scans the supplied generators, aggregates their source files (excluding system‑included files and optionally external ones), builds a virtual folder hierarchy, and writes a CodeBlocks‑style XML project file that declares project options, the chosen compiler, and all targets—both normal and “fast” variants—along with their source units and any corresponding headers.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::CreateProj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::CreateProj.body: The routine uses the first local generator in the list to determine the binary directory and project name, concatenates the two resulting file names (the main “.cbp” file and a “.layout” file), and then delegates creation of the new project file to the helper function CreateNewProjectFile.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::Generate@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::Generate@k.body: The `Generate` function iterates over each entry in the global project map and delegates the creation of a new project file to the `CreateProjectFile` helper for every sub‑project it encounters.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::GetCBCompi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::GetCBCompi.body: The routine first checks if the user supplied a compiler ID via the `CMAKE_CODEBLOCKS_COMPILER_ID` definition; if present it returns that value. Otherwise it determines which language is enabled (C++, C, or Fortran) and then maps the appropriate CodeBlocks compiler identifier (e.g. `gcc`, `msvc8`, `icc`, etc.) based on the “compiler id” from the makefile, defaulting to `gcc` when no specific case matches.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::GetCBTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::GetCBTarge.body: The routine inspects a `cmGeneratorTarget` and returns a small integer code: 0 for a Win32‑style executable or a Mac OS X bundle, 1 for other executables, 2 for static/ object libraries, 3 for shared/module libraries, and 4 for anything outside those categories.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::GetFactory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::GetFactory.body: The function lazily creates (or re‑uses a singleton) of a `cmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorSimpleFactory` for the `cmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator`. It configures the factory with a name and description, then ensures the set of globally‑supported generators is populated – adding specific makefile backends (e.g. MinGW, NMake, Ninja, Unix) when the list is empty. The function finally returns a pointer to that factory instance.

@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::cmExtraCod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator::cmExtraCod.body: The default constructor for `cmExtraCodeBlocksGenerator` simply initializes the object without performing any custom logic. It guarantees that the generator is in a valid state before any code‑block generation operations are invoked.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CollectSourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CollectSourc.body: The function first determines whether the target is an executable, static library, or dynamic library, setting a string accordingly. It then walks through the target’s source files, routing each one into either the map of known source files or the set of other files based on the file extension, and finally returns the project type string.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateFolder.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateFolder.body: The function collects the keys from the provided file map into a set and then delegates to the other overload of `CreateFoldersAndFiles`, passing that set, the XML writer, and the project path.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateNewPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateNewPro.body: This routine creates a new project file for a CodeLite target. It opens the file, starts an XML document, gathers all source files used by the target, separates them into C/C++ implementation files and other files, and writes a `<CodeLite_Project>` element that lists these files with attributes for the target name and type. If the file cannot be opened, it exits immediately.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateNewPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateNewPro.body: This function creates an XML project file for a set of local generators. It opens the output stream, starts an XML document with a root element “CodeLite_Project”, writes attributes for the project name and type, then walks each generator’s makefile to collect implementation and other source files into two containers. Finally, it writes source entries (via CreateProjectSourceEntries) and finishes the XML document.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateProjec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateProjec.body: Creates a project descriptor file in the first generator’s output directory by concatenating the binary directory with the project name and then calling CreateNewProjectFile with that path.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateProjec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateProjec.body: The function populates a CodeLite‑compatible XML project file: it first partitions source files into “src” and “include” virtual directories, then emits the full project configuration block. It reports CPU count for parallel make options, determines the code‑compiler name from the makefile, and writes compiler/linker/resource compiler options, working‑directory handling, and custom build commands (rebuild, clean, build, single‑file build). All directives are wrapped in the appropriate `<Settings>…</Settings>` element hierarchy used by CodeLite.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateProjec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateProjec.body: Creates a list of project file names. For each project in the workspace map, it pulls the binary directory and project name, writes the project name into the return vector, builds the path for the new project file (making it relative to the workspace), creates the file, and records the name and path in an XML element. The function returns a vector of all created project names.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateProjec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::CreateProjec.body: The routine walks through every local generator in the workspace, and for each declared target produces a lightweight “project” file in the target’s binary directory. While doing so it records the target’s name in a vector and emits a small XML entry describing the project (name, relative path, and whether it is active). The function finally returns the list of target names that were processed.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::FindMatching.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::FindMatching.body: The function iterates over a map of source files, builds a candidate header‑file name by swapping the source file’s extension to each known header extension, and checks if that file exists. When a match is found it adds the header name to a set that tracks headers already processed. If the file already appears in the set it skips further checks, otherwise it inserts the new header into the set.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::Generate@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::Generate@k_Z.body: The function scans the global project map, extracts the root project’s metadata, and generates an XML workspace file that lists all projects in the workspace. It builds a `<BuildMatrix>` section containing a `<WorkspaceConfiguration>` element and individual `<Project>` entries for each target or project based on the current configuration setting.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetBuildComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetBuildComm.body: The function builds a command string that runs the appropriate make program for the current generator. It picks the `make` binary from the makefile and, based on the generator type, appends the `-f` flag plus the project’s path and optional `-j` flag with the configured CPU count. If a target name is supplied, that target is appended at the end of the command.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetCleanComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetCleanComm.body: It builds a clean‑command string: it fetches the base command via GetBuildCommand, then appends either “‑t clean <targetName>” (when a target is supplied and the generator is Ninja) or just “clean”.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetCodeLiteC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetCodeLiteC.body: The `GetCodeLiteCompilerName` member simply selects an identifying string for the compiler used by the CodeLite generator. It first checks whether the C++ language is enabled; if not, it treats the request as plain C. It then fetches the compiler‑ID definition from the makefile data, and based on that ID returns one of three canonical strings: “VC++” for MSVC, “clang++” for Clang, “gnu g++” for GNU, and otherwise defaults to “gnu g++”. This string is used downstream by the generator to locate the proper compiler executable.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetConfigura.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetConfigura.body:
The function pulls the value of the **CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE** definition, removes any leading or trailing whitespace, and returns the cleaned string.  
If the trimmed value is empty, it falls back to the literal `"NoConfig"`.  

**Key points**

- Uses `GetSafeDefinition` to obtain the raw value.  
- Trims spaces by calling `erase` with indices computed from `find_first_not_of`/`find_last_not_of` – note those helpers are non‑standard; they’ll need custom implementations.  
- Declared `const` ensures the caller can’t modify the object state.  
- The fallback value `"NoConfig"` guarantees a non‑empty return even if the definition is missing or blank.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetFactory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetFactory@k.body: The `GetFactory` static function builds (once) and returns a shared factory instance that knows how to generate CodeLite‑style project files. It lazily registers the list of global generators that the factory supports—if that list is still empty, it populates it with the built‑in Makefile back‑ends (e.g. “Ninja”, “Unix Makefiles”, and, on Windows, “MinGW Makefiles”/“NMake Makefiles”). Once inited, it simply returns a pointer to that factory.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetRebuildCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetRebuildCo.body: The method constructs a command string that first invokes the target’s clean command and then, using “&&”, invokes the target’s build command, effectively running a clean‑then‑build sequence.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetSingleFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::GetSingleFil.body: The function builds a command line string to invoke the appropriate make tool for a single‑file build. It pulls the make program name and generator type from the makefile, checks whether the generator is a Unix‑style or MinGW makefile, and then concatenates the make command with the -f flag pointing to the project‑path Makefile and the -B option with the current file’s object target. The resulting string is returned as the build command.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::cmExtraCodeL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::cmExtraCodeL.body: This constructor (or factory‑style helper) creates a “lite” code generator that plugs into the external‑project framework. It wires up the `cmExtraCodeLiteGenerator` class to the `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator` infrastructure, registers the generator with the make‑file builder, and prepares any internal state required for emitting the simplified code snippets used in downstream build steps.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::cmExtraCodeL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::cmExtraCodeL.body: The constructor takes a const reference to another `cmExtraCodeLiteGenerator` instance and performs a shallow copy of its internal state, delegating to the base `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator` constructor where appropriate. It does not reallocate resources, simply replicating member variables so the new object mirrors the source’s configuration.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::cmExtraCodeL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::cmExtraCodeL.body: This constructor simply sets the member `ConfigName` to the default string “NoConfig” during object creation, with no other side effects.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::operator=@k_.body: It moves an rvalue of type `cmExtraCodeLiteGenerator` into the current object and returns a reference to that object.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::operator=@k_.body: `operator=` is a copy‑assignment operator that takes a const reference to another `cmExtraCodeLiteGenerator` and copies its internal state into the current object, then returns `*this`. It performs a shallow copy of the data members (no dynamic allocation is transferred) and ensures that after the call the two instances hold identical state.

@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::~cmExtraCode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraCodeLiteGenerator::~cmExtraCode.body: The `~cmExtraCodeLiteGenerator` function implements the virtual interface for generating lightweight supplemental code blocks in a `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator` context. When invoked it walks the internal AST, emits minimal scaffolding code (e.g., pragma directives, minimal helper stubs) and returns the resulting code snippet. It avoids heavy boilerplate, focuses on correctness, and gracefully handles missing or malformed input by emitting empty results or warning‑level diagnostics.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AddEnvVar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AddEnvVar.body: The helper inspects an environment variable, compares it against a cached entry, and picks the value to write to the output stream. If the variable is unset in the environment but already cached, it uses the cache; if the environment value is present but absent from the cache, it writes that value and records it in the cache. If both exist, it prefers the environment value unless that value is already a substring of the cached one, in which case it keeps the cached value. Finally, if a value is chosen, the function writes “<name>=<value>|” into the output stream.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendInc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendInc.body: The routine walks the supplied include‑directory list, normalises each path (collapsing it to a canonical form), strips any “…/Frameworks/…framework” segment on macOS, and for each path that hasn’t yet been emitted writes a distinct `<pathentry>` element to the XML writer, emitting only unique entries marked as system include paths.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendLin.body: The `AppendLinkedResource` helper takes a resource name, its file‑system path, and a `LinkType` flag, then serializes a single `<link>` element into the supplied `cmXMLWriter`. It selects the appropriate tag name (`location` or `locationURI`) and numeric type code (1 or 2) based on the link kind, and emits the three sub‑elements (`name`, `type`, and the chosen location tag) before closing the element.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendSca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendSca.body: Creates an XML snippet for a scanner profile: sets the profile id, enables optional open‑action and parsing switches, and records the run‑action command/arguments and whether to use a default.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendSto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendSto.body: The routine gathers the compiler name and command‑line switches from the supplied makefile, falls back to a default when missing, and then writes a `<storageModule>` block into the XML writer. Inside that block it writes an `<autodiscovery>` element with fixed attributes and invokes two helper calls to emit scanner profiles that reference the collected compiler information and the prepared compiler‑argument string.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::AppendTar.body: The routine emits a `<target>` element populated with the supplied properties: it writes the target name (prefixed by `prefix`), the path, a fixed targetID, and nested elements for the command name, its arguments, and the target to invoke—defaulting to the target name if `makeTarget` is null—then closes the element.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateCPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateCPr.body: Creates the Eclipse CDT configuration file by gathering the project’s makefile data, serialising the build targets, include paths, and macro definitions, and writing them as XML into a “.cproject” file.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateLin.body:
The method walks the project’s local generators, and for each target it builds a link‑name string that incorporates a prefix (“[exe] ” or “[lib] ”) according to the target type.  
It then records that link in the XML writer and, unless the generator is told to skip linked resources, collects the source files belonging to the target’s makefile, adds them to the proper source groups, and finally emits those groups through WriteGroups.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateLin.body: When linked‑resource generation is enabled, the routine iterates over the global project map and, for each sub‑project whose source directory is neither the base directory nor a sub‑directory of it, appends a virtual “[Subprojects]/…” link to the XML writer. The link is resolved via `GetEclipsePath`, and is written under the “Subprojects” section; it explicitly avoids adding the link to the `srcLinkedResources` list to sidest Eclipse’s index‑conflict (#13596).

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreatePro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreatePro.body: The routine serializes a project description into an XML‐style `.project` file: it writes the build command configuration (including compiler‑specific environment variables, the make command and arguments), configures the error‑parsers for each supported compiler, and finally attaches linked resources (source directories or subproject links) and any virtual‑folder associations that the build requires.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateSet.body: The routine picks the first local generator associated with the current generator, pulls its makefile and writes a file named `.settings/org.eclipse.core.resources.prefs` in the output directory. It records the preferences version and, if present, the project‑specific encoding setting.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::CreateSou.body: Creates a .project file in the home directory by opening the file, writing a minimal XML description that contains the project name, an empty comment, the standard project sections (projects, buildSpec, natures) and the linkedResources element. If virtual‑folder support is enabled, it adds the sub‑project links inside linkedResources and clears the list that holds those links. If the file cannot be opened, the routine exits immediately.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::EnableLan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::EnableLan.body: The routine iterates over the supplied language names, inserting the corresponding Eclipse nature identifiers into its internal `Natures` set and setting the appropriate enable flags (`CXXEnabled`, `CEnabled`). It thereby configures the object to support C++, C, and Java projects based on the requested language strings.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::Generate@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::Generate@.body:
Parses the Eclipse‑makefile to set flags that enable or disable features (virtual folder support, Mach‑O parsing, error parsing) according to the detected Eclipse version.  
Determines source‑vs‑build directories, decides if linked resources and a source‑project file should be emitted, and warns when the build directory is nested under the source tree.  
Finally it writes the standard Eclipse project files (.project, .cproject) and the resource‑settings file.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::GenerateP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::GenerateP.body: The `GenerateProjectName` function concatenates a given base project name with an optional type suffix followed by an “@” and the target path. It returns a string in the format: `baseName[-type]@path`. If the `type` string is empty, the separator “-” is omitted. This simple string composition allows callers to construct a unique identifier that combines name, type, and location in a single token.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::GetEclips.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::GetEclips.body: The routine runs a system command to resolve an Eclipse path on Windows‑specific builds. It builds a command string `cygpath -m <path>`, executes it via `cmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand`, trims any trailing newline from the output, and returns that string; if execution fails or is not on the defined platform, it simply returns the original path.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::GetFactor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::GetFactor.body: The `GetFactory` function creates and returns a static instance of `cmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorSimpleFactory` specialized for the `cmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator`. It registers the generator under the name “Eclipse CDT4”, tags it as deprecated, and conditionally populates the list of global generators that the builder supports (e.g., “NMake Makefiles”, “MinGW Makefiles”, “Ninja”, “Unix Makefiles”). The returned reference is reused across calls.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::GetPathBa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::GetPathBa.body: The function receives a file‑style path string, strips any trailing slashes, then returns the substring after the last slash (handling both '/' and '\\' separators). It simply yields the basename component of the supplied path.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::WriteGrou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::WriteGrou.body: The method walks through each source group, building a forward‑slash separated path for that group, sanitizing any backslashes, and registering the group itself as a linked resource. It then recurses into any child groups before attaching each contained file as a linked resource under the same path hierarchy.

@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::cmExtraEc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraEclipseCDT4Generator::cmExtraEc.body:
The constructor initializes the generator’s feature flags.  
- `IsOutOfSourceBuild` and `GenerateSourceProject` are set to **false** so the generator will not create out‑of‑source builds or generate source‑project projects.  
- `SupportsVirtualFolders`, `GenerateLinkedResources`, `SupportsGmakeErrorParser`, and `SupportsMachO64Parser` are all enabled (`true`), indicating the generator can handle virtual folder mappings, linked‑resource generation, parsing Make‑style error messages, and parsing Mach‑O64 binaries.  
- `CEnabled` and `CXXEnabled` are set to **false**, meaning C/C++ code generation is disabled unless otherwise configured.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::AppendTarget@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::AppendTarget@k_Z.body: The function writes one JSON‑formatted line for each element in `configs`. For every config it emits an entry that contains the target’s name and a command string built from the supplied `make`, `makeArgs`, and the path that depends on whether `UseNinja` is true – in that case it prefixes the path with `homeOutputDir` and appends a `-f` file suffix. It uses a static separator that starts as a space and is replaced by a comma after the first entry. The function itself is const and simply streams these constructed strings into the provided output stream.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::CreateDummyKateP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::CreateDummyKateP.body: The function builds a path by concatenating the binary directory, a slash, the project name, and the extension “.kateproject”. It then opens a file stream to that path. If opening fails it exits early. On success it writes a single line comment indicating the file was generated automatically and should not be edited.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::CreateKateProjec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::CreateKateProjec.body: The routine writes a .kateproject file in the binary directory of the build. It opens the file, writes a JSON‑style header with the project name and source directory, appends a list of generated files, then adds target information before closing the JSON object. If the file cannot be opened, it exits immediately.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::Generate@k_ZN20c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::Generate@k_ZN20c.body: It pulls the first local generator, grabs its makefile, builds the CMake‑style project name from that generator’s name, the build‑type flag and the binary directory name, flips the Ninja flag if the global generator is “Ninja” or “Ninja Multi‑Config”, and finally writes out the main and dummy Kate project files.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::GenerateFilesStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::GenerateFilesStr.body: The function builds a string that first figures out the VCS type (SVN, GIT, HG, FOSSIL) from the given configuration or by looking for hidden markers in the source tree, then gathers all source and list‑files from the current and nested generators, filtering out generated files, and finally formats that collection as a JSON‑style list embedded in a string.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::GenerateProjectN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::GenerateProjectN.body: The `GenerateProjectName` member simply stitches together its three string parameters into a single identifier: it appends a hyphen only when the `type` argument is non‑empty, then appends `type`, a literal “@”, and finally the `path` string. The result is returned as a `std::string`.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::GetFactory@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::GetFactory@k_ZN2.body: The function lazily constructs a static factory instance for “Kate” generators. When the factory’s supported‑generator list is empty, it populates it with a predefined set of global generators (conditionally compiled for certain platforms). Finally it returns a pointer to that singleton factory.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::GetPathBasename@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::GetPathBasename@.body: The routine trims any trailing slashes or backslashes from the given path and then returns the part of the string that follows the last slash/backslash, i.e., the final path component.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::WriteTargets@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::WriteTargets@k_Z.body: The function gathers target information from the current and any nested generators, then writes a JSON‑style block to the output stream. It first emits the standard “build”, “clean” and “quick” targets, then iterates through each local generator’s targets. Depending on the target type (global, utility, executable or library), it applies a few filters—skipping certain utility names and avoiding sub‑directory globals—and appends the appropriate target entries (including optional “fast” variants for non‑Ninja builds). Finally it appends any individual‑file compilation targets before closing the JSON array.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::cmExtraKateGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::cmExtraKateGener.body: When a `cmExtraKateGenerator` object is constructed from an rvalue, this constructor performs a *move construction*: it transfers the internal state (configuration data, file paths, and any cached resources) from the source instance into the new one, avoiding deep copies, then forwards the relevant parameters to the base `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator` constructor to set up the external‑project glue.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::cmExtraKateGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::cmExtraKateGener.body: The function is a copy‑constructor that initializes a new `cmExtraKateGenerator` instance from an existing one. It copies all of the internal state from the source object into the new instance, ensuring that the new instance has the same configuration and data as the original.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::cmExtraKateGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::cmExtraKateGener.body: The constructor initializes the generator’s internal state and sets up its default configuration, preparing it for subsequent use in the system.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::operator=@k_ZN20.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to another `cmExtraKateGenerator` instance and moves its internal data into the current object, effectively transferring ownership of all internal resources without deep copying.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::operator=@k_ZN20.body: The assignment operator copies the complete internal state of a source `cmExtraKateGenerator` into the target, performing a deep copy of all member data (including any owned resources) and returning a reference to the current instance. It guards against self‑assignment by comparing pointers before copying, ensuring the object remains in a consistent state even in edge cases.

@lcmExtraKateGenerator::~cmExtraKateGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraKateGenerator::~cmExtraKateGene.body: The `~cmExtraKateGenerator` member function is implemented in the `cmExtraKateGenerator` class (which inherits from `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator`) to provide the specific logic required for generating extra Kate build artefacts. It is invoked by other parts of the system that need the extended build‑file information produced by this generator.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::AppendAll.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::AppendAll.body: The routine walks through every local generator in the given list, emitting a makefile entry for each target it owns. It branches on the target’s classification: global targets from the top‑level binary directory, utility targets (except nightly/continuous/experimental variants), and all executable/library targets. For the latter it emits both the normal and a “/fast” variant. The function feeds these entries into the output stream, tagging them with the current compiler and make program identifiers and any custom flags supplied.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::AppendTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::AppendTar.body: The `AppendTarget` method adds a target’s build information into the generated file stream. It collects all source files for the target, extracts their compiler flags, defines, and include paths via a regex scan, and emits a JSON‑style entry (or Ninja syntax) with fields such as name, command, working directory, and a file‑matching regex.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::BuildMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::BuildMake.body: It builds a command string that runs the make program with the correct options for each generator. Depending on the generator name, it adds the proper flag (e.g. ‑f or /f), and quotes or escapes the makefile path and target accordingly.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeDe.body: The method builds a comma‑separated list of pre‑processor macros that should be passed to the compiler for the current build. It starts by pulling the makefile’s target‑specific flags, then pulls any compile‑time definitions declared in the source file itself. Both sets of definitions are fed through an expression interpreter that expands any variable references according to the current configuration. The resolved strings are accumulated into a `std::set` and finally flattened into a single string that is returned to the caller.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeFl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeFl.body:
Builds a string of compiler flags for a source file.  
It first pulls the file’s language, applies the target’s explicit language flag, merges target‑specific compile flags, then appends any source‑specific compile‑flags or options evaluated by the generator expression interpreter, and finally returns the assembled flag string.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeIn.body: The function collects include directories defined on the source file (and any additional ones from the target), evaluates them through the generator expression interpreter, merges the resulting include flags into a single string, and returns that string.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::CreateNew.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::CreateNew.body: The routine writes a Sublime configuration file that records folder entries relative to the source and output directories, optionally excludes build directories, writes build system definitions, and includes any environment settings supplied.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::CreatePro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::CreatePro.body: The method takes the first generator in the list, pulls its binary directory and project name, stitches them into a path ending in “.sublime‑project”, and forwards that path and the vector of generators to a helper that actually creates the file.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::Generate@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::Generate@.body: The function pulls two configuration values – a flag that controls whether a build‑tree is excluded and a string of environment settings – from the global generator. It then walks through every project in the internal project map and calls CreateProjectFile for each one.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::GetFactor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::GetFactor.body: Creates a single shared factory that produces *cmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorSimpleFactory* objects for the “Sublime Text 2” generator. It registers a set of supported global generators (e.g., “MinGW Makefiles”, “NMake Makefiles”, “Ninja”, and “Unix Makefiles”) when the factory’s current list is empty, ensuring the generator can be selected from the UI. The returned reference is cached so subsequent calls reuse the same factory instance.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::Open@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::Open@k_ZN.body: The method checks for a required executable and, if found, builds a project‑specific filename. When called in dry‑run mode it merely verifies that the file exists; otherwise it runs the external tool with the constructed arguments.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::cmExtraSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::cmExtraSu.body: The function processes user‑supplied tokens, resolves any format markers, and emits a well‑structured Sublime‑ready text blob that the surrounding project‑generation framework consumes.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::cmExtraSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::cmExtraSu.body: Creates a new instance of **cmExtraSublimeTextGenerator** that adopts the internal configuration of the supplied source object, ensuring all internal fields and resources are duplicated into the new instance.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::cmExtraSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::cmExtraSu.body: The constructor initializes the `ExcludeBuildFolder` flag to **false**, ensuring that, by default, the generator does *not* skip the build folder during its processing.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::operator=.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::operator=.body: Accepts a temporary instance, transfers its internal state into the current object, and returns that object by reference for fluent chaining.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::operator=.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::operator=.body: The operator assigns the contents of the right‑hand object to the left‑hand object, returning a reference to the left‑hand object for chaining. It performs a member‑wise copy, guarding against self‑assignment.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::~cmExtraS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::~cmExtraS.body: The virtual function `~cmExtraSublimeTextGenerator()` implements the public API defined by `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator`. It receives context about a makefile project and emits formatted textual output that is consumed by downstream components. Internally, it orchestrates generation logic—parsing project descriptors, applying rendering rules, and emitting the resulting string (or stream) to the caller.

@lcmFLTKWrapUICommand@k_Z19cmFLTKWrapUIC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFLTKWrapUICommand@k_Z19cmFLTKWrapUIC.body: The routine walks through the supplied GUI‑file names, invokes the Fluid‑Toolkit executable on each to emit a matching .h header and a .cxx C++ source file, and registers both as custom‑command outputs with the required dependencies. It then records the full paths of the generated sources in a makefile variable named for the target (e.g. `<target>_FLTK_UI_SRCS`).

@lcmFSPermissions::stringToModeT@k_ZN15c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFSPermissions::stringToModeT@k_ZN15c.body: The function translates a string name into a set of permission bits: it checks the input string against known identifiers (e.g., “OWNER_READ”, “GROUP_EXECUTE”, “SETUID”) and, when matched, ORs the corresponding flag into the supplied `mode_t` reference; it returns `true` for a successful match and `false` if the string is unrecognized.

@lcmFileAPI::AddProjectQuery@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::AddProjectQuery@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The function verifies that the requested object kind and version fall within the supported ranges, rejects the disallowed kinds, and registers the query in the internal list if it hasn't been recorded already—setting a flag that indicates a query now exists.

@lcmFileAPI::AddReplyIndexObject@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::AddReplyIndexObject@k_ZN9cm.body: This routine looks up an entry in the internal index map; if it’s already present it returns that entry. If the entry is missing, it builds the corresponding reply object, writes it out to a JSON file, stores the path in the map alongside the object’s kind and version, and finally returns the freshly‑created index entry.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildCMake@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildCMake@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: The function builds and returns a JSON object that describes the current CMake installation and its runtime environment. It queries the running `CMakeInstance` for its version string and global generator details, then collects a set of command paths for CMake, CTest, and CPack from the helper utility `cmSystemTools`, and injects these strings into the JSON structure before returning the resulting object.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildCMakeFiles@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildCMakeFiles@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The function constructs a JSON object describing a CMake file for the supplied `object`. It sets the `kind` field from the object’s kind name and, if the object’s version equals 1, injects a `version` entry built by `BuildVersion`; otherwise it returns the constructed object (the non‑1 case is effectively unreachable).

@lcmFileAPI::BuildCache@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildCache@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: BuildCache constructs a JSON value for an object. It calls `cmFileAPICacheDump` with the current instance and the object’s version, then inserts a `"kind"` field using `this->ObjectKindName`. It then checks the object’s `Version`. If it equals 2, it calls `BuildVersion(2, CacheV2Minor)` and stores the result in the `"version"` field; otherwise it returns the cache immediately (the `return cache` inside the `else` block is effectively unreachable). The function ultimately returns the populated JSON value.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReply@k_ZN9cmFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReply@k_ZN9cmFil.body: The function starts by calling `BuildReply` to obtain a base JSON reply. If the incoming query does not carry a JSON payload (`HaveQueryJson` is false), it returns that base reply unchanged. When a JSON payload is present, it populates the `"query.json"` section of the reply with the parsed `ClientQueryJson` data. If an error string is recorded in the parsed data, the function replaces the `"query.json"` field with an error‑formatted object. Otherwise, it adds the `client` value (if present) and the list of `requests` to the JSON. Finally, it appends a `responses` array produced by `BuildClientReplyResponses` and returns the fully built reply object.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReplyResponse@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReplyResponse@k_.body: The function first checks whether the incoming request contains an error string. If it does, it immediately constructs an error‑only reply via `BuildReplyError` and returns that value. If there is no error, it enriches the response with the request‑specific index information through `AddReplyIndexObject` and returns the populated reply.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReplyResponses@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReplyResponses@k.body: It builds a JSON array of reply objects: if any request carries an error, it immediately returns an error JSON; otherwise each request is processed into a reply and appended to the result array.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequest@k_ZN9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequest@k_ZN9cmF.body: The function validates a JSON request: it checks that the payload is an object, extracts the `"kind"` field, matches it against known kinds, and parses the `"version"` array. Depending on the kind it delegates to a specific helper that fills the `ClientRequest` structure. If any step fails, it records an error message and returns that error state.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCMakeFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCMakeFile.body: The function scans the supplied list of `RequestVersion` objects, picks the first one that matches the supported version criteria (major = 1 and minor ≤ `CMakeFilesV1Minor`), assigns that major number to the request, and if no such version is present, records an error in the request.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCache@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCache@k_Z.body: The function walks through the supplied `versions` vector, picks the first entry whose major version is 2 and whose minor version does not exceed the compiler‑defined `CacheV2Minor`, assigns that major number to `r.Version`, and if no match is found it populates the request’s error field with the result of `NoSupportedVersion(versions)`.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCodeModel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCodeModel.body: The routine scans the supplied version list for the first entry whose major version is 2 and whose minor component does not exceed the predefined threshold. When it finds such a version it records the major number in the request’s `Version` field. If the scan finishes without a match, it marks the request with an error indicating that none of the requested versions is supported.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestConfigure.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestConfigure.body: The routine scans the supplied version list for an entry whose major part equals 1 and whose minor part does not exceed ConfigureLogV1Minor; if such a version is found it assigns that major value to the request’s Version field, otherwise it records an error.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestInternalT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestInternalT.body:
Scans the supplied version list for a compatible internal‑test version.  
If a version with major 1 (minor ≤ InternalTestV1Minor) or major 2 (minor ≤ InternalTestV2Minor) is found, the request’s Version field is set to that major and the routine exits.  
When no such version exists, it records a “no‑supported‑version” error.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestToolchain.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestToolchain.body: The function iterates through the supplied version list, assigns the first entry whose major component is 1 and minor component is ≤ ToolchainsV1Minor to the request’s `Version`. If no such entry exists, it assigns the request’s `Error` field to the value returned by `NoSupportedVersion(versions)`.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequests@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequests@k_ZN9cm.body: The function receives a JSON array of request objects, creates a `ClientRequests` container, and returns it. If the array is missing or not an array, it records an error message in the container’s `Error` field. Otherwise, it reserves space for each element and converts each request via `BuildClientRequest`, appending the results before returning the populated container.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildCodeModel@k_ZN9cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildCodeModel@k_ZN9cmFileA.body: BuildCodeModel constructs a JSON representation of an object, assigning its kind and populating a “version” node when the object’s version equals 2. It returns that JSON payload.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildConfigureLog@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildConfigureLog@k_ZN9cmFi.body: The function constructs a JSON log entry for a supplied object: it creates a base log with the object’s version, tags it with the object kind name, and then embeds a version sub‑object according to the object’s version (currently only handling version 1). The function returns the fully populated log value.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildInternalTest@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildInternalTest@k_ZN9cmFi.body: This function builds a JSON object that records the object’s kind name and a version field. It calls one of two helper routines—`BuildVersion(2,InternalTestV2Minor)` or `BuildVersion(1,InternalTestV1Minor)`—depending on whether the input object's version equals 2 or not, and then returns that JSON object.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildObject@k_ZN9cmFileAPI1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildObject@k_ZN9cmFileAPI1.body: The method inspects the `Kind` of the supplied `Object` and delegates to the corresponding helper (`BuildCodeModel`, `BuildConfigureLog`, etc.). Whatever helper returns is stored in `value` and then returned. No other processing occurs inside this dispatcher.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildReply@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildReply@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: BuildReply walks through a Query’s Known and Unknown lists. For each known object it pulls the object’s name and inserts a value returned by AddReplyIndexObject into the JSON reply under that name. For any name that isn’t in the known list it inserts an error value created by BuildReplyError. The function finally returns the constructed JSON reply.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildReplyError@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildReplyError@k_ZN9cmFile.body: Creates a Json::Value containing the supplied error string under the key “error” and returns that object.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildReplyIndex@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildReplyIndex@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The function constructs a JSON object that indexes the reply data: it first records the CMake build info, then serialises the primary query reply and all client‑specific replies, and finally aggregates the list of generated objects into a single array field before returning the completed JSON value.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildToolchains@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildToolchains@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The function creates a JSON object describing a “toolchain” for a given object. It first dumps the base data via `cmFileAPIToolchainsDump`, tags the type with `ObjectKindName`, and then includes a “version” field. If the object’s version is `1`, it populates the version field with `BuildVersion(1, ToolchainsV1Minor)`; otherwise, for any other version, it simply returns the assembled JSON (the code path after the `else` is a guard against unsupported versions).

@lcmFileAPI::BuildVersion@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildVersion@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.body: It creates a JSON value containing the supplied `major` and `minor` numbers in a simple key/value map and returns that value.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.body: The `ClientRequest` public function is a move constructor. It accepts an rvalue reference to another `ClientRequest` instance and initializes the new object by transferring ownership of its internal state. This efficiently reuses the data of the source object without copying, leaving the original in a valid but unspecified state.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.body:
The function in question is the entry point used when a client sends a request to the system. It typically pulls the incoming data, packages it into a **`ClientRequest`** instance (the struct defined in `cmFileAPI.h`), and then delegates to the appropriate subsystem for further handling. In practice, the function usually:

1. parses the request payload,
2. validates the payload format against the expected `ClientRequest` schema,
3. instantiates a `ClientRequest` object,
4. routes that object to the relevant handler chain, and finally,
5. returns a status or result back to the caller.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.body: The constructor takes an rvalue reference, effectively moving the underlying vector of `ClientRequest` objects into the new instance. It relies on the base `std::vector` move semantics to transfer ownership of the contained elements without copying, so the source object is left in a valid but unspecified state. This enables efficient construction when building a new `ClientRequests` from an existing one, such as in factory or move‑oriented patterns.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.body: Constructs a vector of ClientRequest objects, exposing the usual vector operations while ensuring type safety and that each inserted request passes any necessary validation checks.

@lcmFileAPI::ComputeSuffixHash@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ComputeSuffixHash@k_ZN9cmFi.body: The function computes a SHA‑256 hash of the given file and then truncates the resulting 64‑character hexadecimal string down to a 20‑byte string padded with “0” characters.

@lcmFileAPI::ComputeSuffixTime@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ComputeSuffixTime@k_ZN9cmFi.body: The function obtains the current system‑time, casts it to milliseconds, then to whole seconds. It formats the epoch seconds and the sub‑second fraction (millisecond remainder) into a string. The formatted string consists of a timestamp created with `cmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT` followed by a dash and a four‑digit millisecond field padded with zeros. The result is returned as a plain string.

@lcmFileAPI::GetCMakeInstance@k_ZNK9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::GetCMakeInstance@k_ZNK9cmFi.body: Returns a pointer to the internal CMake instance, exposing it for read‑only use.

@lcmFileAPI::GetConfigureLogVersions::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::GetConfigureLogVersions::[l.body: The lambda iterates through a `Query`’s known objects, and whenever an object has `Kind == ObjectKind::ConfigureLog`, it appends that object’s `Version` to the `versions` vector.

@lcmFileAPI::GetConfigureLogVersions@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::GetConfigureLogVersions@k_Z.body: The function walks the object tree in the top‑level query and each client query, collecting the `Version` of every object whose kind is `ConfigureLog`. After gathering all values it sorts them, removes duplicates with `unique`, and returns the sorted list of distinct version numbers.

@lcmFileAPI::LoadDir@k_ZN9cmFileAPI7Load.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::LoadDir@k_ZN9cmFileAPI7Load.body: The function opens the given directory, walks through its entries, pushes each file name (excluding the special “.” and “..” entries) into a vector, sorts that vector alphabetically, and returns the sorted list of file names.

@lcmFileAPI::MaybeJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::MaybeJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAP.body: The function checks whether the supplied JSON value is an object or array. If it is, it calls `WriteJsonFile` to persist the data and wraps the resulting file‑path in a new JSON object; otherwise it passes the value through unchanged.

@lcmFileAPI::NoSupportedVersion@k_ZN9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::NoSupportedVersion@k_ZN9cmF.body: It builds an error string saying that no supported version was supplied. If a list of candidates is given, it appends each major.minor pair to the message so the caller knows which versions were rejected.

@lcmFileAPI::Object::Object@k_ZN9cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Object::Object@k_ZN9cmFileA.body: Creates a default‑valued instance of the `Object` struct and returns it for use in the rest of the API.

@lcmFileAPI::ObjectKindName@k_ZN9cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ObjectKindName@k_ZN9cmFileA.body:
The helper simply indexes a compile‑time string table by the `ObjectKind` value and returns that literal.  
It relies on the enum’s ordering staying in sync with the array; passing a value outside the valid range will index garbage and produce undefined behaviour.  
Because the data is constant, the function is trivially fast and thread‑safe, but callers must validate the enum value or guard against out‑of‑range accesses.

@lcmFileAPI::ObjectName@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ObjectName@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: The function builds a unique string identifier for an object by concatenating its kind name and version, producing a value like “<Kind>-v<Version>”. It simply calls `ObjectKindName` to get the kind’s textual name, appends `‑v` and the numeric version, and returns the result.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadClient@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadClient@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: It walks through the client’s query directory, populates the client‑specific query lists and flags the special “query.json” case to be handled by the dedicated `ReadClientQuery` helper.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadClientQuery@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadClientQuery@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The function loads a client‑specific query file, validates that the top‑level JSON is an object, extracts the optional “client” field into the `ClientValue` member of the result structure, and finally fills the `Requests` vector by parsing the “requests” part of the JSON. If any step fails, it records an error string in the result structure.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.body: The function reads a file into a buffer and invokes the JSON reader to parse that buffer; it returns true on success, otherwise clears the output value, records an error message, and returns false.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadQueries@k_ZN9cmFileAPI1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadQueries@k_ZN9cmFileAPI1.body: The function first verifies that the “query” sub‑folder exists under the API’s base path; if it’s missing it returns immediately. Once the directory is found, it enumerates all filenames in that folder. For each name, it distinguishes client‑prefixed queries from regular ones: client‑style files trigger the dedicated `ReadClient` routine, whereas other queries are parsed via `ReadQuery`. Any query that fails to load gets recorded in a dedicated “unknown” collection for later inspection.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadQuery@k_ZN9cmFileAPI9Re.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadQuery@k_ZN9cmFileAPI9Re.body: ReadQuery parses an input string in the form `"<kind>-<ver>"` and, based on the `<kind>` value, creates an `Object` of the appropriate type with the corresponding version number (e.g., `CodeModel‑v2`, `InternalTest‑v1` or `v2`). It appends the constructed object to the supplied vector and returns `true`; if the format or version is unrecognised it returns `false`.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadRequestVersion@k_ZN9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadRequestVersion@k_ZN9cmF.body: Parses a JSON value into RequestVersion objects, validates the required major (and optional minor) fields, and appends them to a result vector while signalling parsing failures via an error string.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadRequestVersions@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadRequestVersions@k_ZN9cm.body: The function takes a JSON value that may represent one or multiple request‑version objects. It walks through the value: if it’s an array, each element is parsed with ReadRequestVersion, accumulating the results in the supplied vector; otherwise a single element is parsed. On any parsing failure it returns false and populates the error string; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmFileAPI::RemoveOldReplyFiles@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::RemoveOldReplyFiles@k_ZN9cm.body: The routine scans the *reply* folder, lists every file it contains, and for each entry that isn’t recorded in the internal `ReplyFiles` map it deletes the file from disk.

@lcmFileAPI::ReportCapabilities@k_ZN9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReportCapabilities@k_ZN9cmF.body: The function creates and returns a JSON object describing the request kinds the API supports. It builds an array named “requests”, and for each supported request type (CodeModel, ConfigureLog, Cache, CMakeFiles, Toolchains) it inserts an object with a “kind” field (the kind’s string name) and a “version” array containing a single version created via BuildVersion. The resulting object therefore lists five request entries, each with a single version entry.

@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::RequestVers.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::RequestVers.body: The function retrieves the current protocol/file‑format revision and returns it in a `RequestVersion` structure (containing fields such as `major`, `minor`, and optional patch or build tags). It performs any necessary validation of the input parameters before dispatching the request.

@lcmFileAPI::WriteJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::WriteJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAP.body: It serializes the supplied JSON value into a temporary file, then atomically renames that file into the final path built from a prefix and a suffix derived from the temporary file name; the resulting file name is stored for later use.

@lcmFileAPI::WriteReplies@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::WriteReplies@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.body: When invoked, `cmFileAPI::WriteReplies()` first checks if a query exists. If it does, it ensures the `APIv1/reply` directory exists (creating it if necessary) and writes a JSON file named “index” containing the reply index returned by `BuildReplyIndex()`. After that, it calls `RemoveOldReplyFiles()` to prune any stale reply files. The routine silently handles any file‑system errors that might arise during the directory creation or file write steps, so callers need not worry about intermediate cleanup beyond the final purge.

@lcmFileAPI::cmFileAPI@k_ZN9cmFileAPIC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::cmFileAPI@k_ZN9cmFileAPIC1E.body:
Creates an instance linked to a running CMake instance.  
The constructor builds the API root path by concatenating the current CMake “home‑output” directory with “/.cmake/api/v1”, then builds two JSON helpers: a `CharReader` configured with a small set of flags (e.g. no comment collection, strict‑root, etc.) and a `StreamWriter` that pretty‑prints JSON with tab indentation. Both helpers are stored as owning pointers for later use in the API.

@lcmFileAPICMakeFilesDump@k_Z23cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPICMakeFilesDump@k_Z23cmFileAPI.body: Creates a CMakeFiles object with the supplied `fileAPI` and `version`, then calls its `Dump()` method and returns that result.

@lcmFileAPICacheDump@k_Z18cmFileAPICache.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPICacheDump@k_Z18cmFileAPICache.body: Creates a `Cache` object with the supplied `fileAPI` and `version`, then returns the result of `cache.Dump()`.

@lcmFileAPICodemodelDump@k_Z22cmFileAPIC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPICodemodelDump@k_Z22cmFileAPIC.body: Creates a Codemodel instance with the given cmFileAPI and version, then returns the result of calling codemodel.Dump().

@lcmFileAPICommand@k_Z16cmFileAPICommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPICommand@k_Z16cmFileAPICommand.body: The routine verifies that an argument list is supplied, then looks up the first token in a compile‑time‑built dispatch table and invokes the corresponding handler, returning that handler’s success flag.

@lcmFileAPIConfigureLogDump@k_Z25cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPIConfigureLogDump@k_Z25cmFileA.body: The function creates a `ConfigureLog` helper using the supplied `cmFileAPI` instance and a version number, then immediately returns the result of calling `Dump()` on that helper. This returns a JSON value that describes the current log‑dump configuration for the file, typically a list of log messages or a status report.

@lcmFileAPIToolchainsDump@k_Z23cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPIToolchainsDump@k_Z23cmFileAPI.body: Creates a Toolchains instance with the supplied fileAPI and version, then returns the result of its Dump() method.

@lcmFileCommand@k_Z13cmFileCommandRKiR17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCommand@k_Z13cmFileCommandRKiR17.body: cmFileCommand interprets the first element of args as a command keyword and routes the request to a corresponding handler. The command keyword is matched against a static table that maps identifiers such as "WRITE", "READ", "HASH", "COPY", etc. to specific handler functions. If the table lookup succeeds the matching handler is invoked; otherwise the function reports an error via `status`. The routine returns a boolean indicating whether the sub‑command was handled successfully.

@lcmFileCommandCurlDebugCallback@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCommandCurlDebugCallback@k_ZN12_.body:
