The routine acts as a lib‑curl callback that the program installs via `curl_easy_setopt`. It receives the callback’s `info_type` argument (`CURLINFO_TEXT`, `CURLINFO_HEADER_IN`, `CURLINFO_HEADER_OUT`, `CURLINFO_DATA_IN`, `CURLINFO_DATA_OUT`, `CURLINFO_SSL_DATA_IN`, or `CURLINFO_SSL_DATA_OUT`).  

For the three “text/headers” variants it simply copies the supplied buffer into the supplied `cmFileCommandVectorOfChar` instance (via `cm::append`).  

For the data variants it emits a line that reports the payload size in the form “[<size> bytes data]” and appends that line to the vector. No real parsing of the buffer occurs; it is all‐text bookkeeping. The function always returns `0`, signalling success to curl.

@lcmFileCopier::CheckKeyword@k_ZN12cmFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::CheckKeyword@k_ZN12cmFil.body:
The function parses a keyword string and maps it to an internal action flag. It first checks whether a current match rule is active; if so, it marks the keyword as “after‑match” and exits.  
If no rule, it sets the appropriate Doing state (e.g. DoingDestination, DoingFilesFromDir, DoingPattern, etc.) or toggles a flag such as FollowSymlinkChain, UseSourcePermissions, UseGivenPermissionsFile, UseGivenPermissionsDir.  
When the keyword is “EXCLUDE” it enables the exclude property on the current rule.  
Any unrecognised keyword causes the function to return false, signalling an error.

@lcmFileCopier::CheckValue@k_ZN12cmFileC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::CheckValue@k_ZN12cmFileC.body:
The protected virtual method updates the copier’s internal state according to the current mode flag.  
It adds file names to the list, assigns destination paths (resolving relative names), compiles pattern strings into regex objects, and verifies file or directory permissions.  
On success it returns true; if a validation fails it flips the state to an error and returns false.

@lcmFileCopier::DefaultFilePermissions@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::DefaultFilePermissions@k.body: The function initializes a file‑level permission mask by starting with zero and then OR‑ing the standard read‑write flags for the owner, read for the group, and read for all others. It essentially presets a permissive, read‑only‑wide policy that allows the file owner to read and write while permitting others only to read.

@lcmFileCopier::Install@k_ZN12cmFileCopi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::Install@k_ZN12cmFileCopi.body: The function starts by collecting any special properties that match the source path. If those properties mark the path as excluded, the function simply returns success. Otherwise it follows an optional symlink‑resolution chain; if that chain succeeds, it then proceeds to copy the item—whether it ends up being a regular file, a directory, or a symlink—using the appropriate specialized helper. If the source cannot be found, it reports a missing‑resource error.

@lcmFileCopier::InstallDirectory@k_ZN12c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::InstallDirectory@k_ZN12c.body: The protected `InstallDirectory` creates the target directory with the requested permissions (falling back to the source directory’s mode if none is supplied), reports progress for each install, and then recursively copies every entry in the source directory – skipping “.” and “..” entries – setting and restoring permissions on the target directory before and after the copy operation.

@lcmFileCopier::InstallFile@k_ZN12cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::InstallFile@k_ZN12cmFile.body: The routine first decides whether the file actually needs copying—skipping it if the destination is up‑to‑date and the “Always” flag is unset. It reports the intended action, performs the copy (falling back on system‑level errors), optionally restores the source modification time, and finally applies either supplied or inherited permissions to the target file before returning success.

@lcmFileCopier::MatchProperties::MatchPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::MatchProperties::MatchPr.body: The `MatchProperties()` function gathers metadata describing how a source file should be treated when copied into the target directory. It inspects the file’s permissions, ownership, timestamps, and any special attributes that must be preserved or remapped. The returned structure is passed to `InstallDirectory()` to drive the actual copy operation, ensuring that source and destination files end up with the intended attributes.

@lcmFileCopier::NotAfterMatch@k_ZN12cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::NotAfterMatch@k_ZN12cmFi.body: The method checks whether a given option string is used in a context that should not follow a pattern or regex; if it is found after such constructs, it records an error by setting an error message in the status and marking the operation as a failure.

@lcmFileCopier::ReportCopy@k_ZN12cmFileC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::ReportCopy@k_ZN12cmFileC.body: The `ReportCopy` virtual function is intended to be overridden by derived classes to handle copying or logging of report data. It receives a string key (likely a report identifier), a `Type` value that distinguishes the kind of report or action, and a boolean flag that may enable or suppress certain side‑effects (e.g., whether to preserve timestamps or whether to log the operation). The implementation in a derived class typically extracts the data associated with the key, performs the copy or transformation logic, and optionally records the action depending on the flag.

@lcmFileCopier::ReportMissing@k_ZN12cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::ReportMissing@k_ZN12cmFi.body: The function simply records an error for a missing source file. It creates a message that includes the file name and the system‑reported error, writes this message into the status object via `SetError`, and then returns `false`.

@lcmFileCopier::ToName@k_ZN12cmFileCopie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::ToName@k_ZN12cmFileCopie.body: The `ToName` method just returns the supplied string unchanged—serving as a hook that derived classes can override to map one file‑name to another while maintaining the same signature.

@lcmFileCopier::cmFileCopier@k_ZN12cmFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::cmFileCopier@k_ZN12cmFil.body: Initialises a FileCopier instance by storing a reference to the passed status, binding it to the makefile obtained from that status, and recording the supplied name for later use.

@lcmFileCopier::~cmFileCopier@k_ZN12cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileCopier::~cmFileCopier@k_ZN12cmFi.body: `~cmFileCopier()` is a virtual destructor that ensures proper cleanup of any resources managed by the `cmFileCopier` class when an object is destroyed. It is declared in the header (`cmFileCopier.h`) and defined in the implementation file (`cmFileCopier.cxx`). The class relies on this destructor to release file handles, buffers, or any dynamically allocated memory that may have been acquired during copying operations. The defaulted definition (`cmFileCopier::~cmFileCopier() = default;`) guarantees that the compiler generates a simple destructor that correctly invokes base class destructors and performs any implicit cleanup required by the compiler, without requiring explicit code in the source file.

@lcmFileDownloadProgressCallback@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileDownloadProgressCallback@k_ZN12_.body: The function interprets the client pointer as a helper object, then calls the helper’s `UpdatePercentage` with the current and total download values. If that call reports a status change, the helper’s associated make‑file is prompted to display the new percentage string. Finally, the callback returns 0.

@lcmFileInstaller::CheckKeyword@k_ZN15cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::CheckKeyword@k_ZN15cm.body: The routine maps the supplied keyword to a flag that dictates the installer’s behavior—setting flags such as `Doing`, `MessageAlways`, etc., and turns on legacy‑style arguments by emitting an error. It returns `true` whenever the keyword is recognised, otherwise delegates to a base implementation.

@lcmFileInstaller::CheckValue@k_ZN15cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::CheckValue@k_ZN15cmFi.body: When the object’s `Doing` flag is `DoingType`, `CheckValue` tries to parse the supplied string into a target type; failure switches the state to `DoingError`. If `DoingRename`, the string is simply stored in the `Rename` member. For any other state, the call is forwarded to the base class’s implementation. The function always returns `true` after executing the appropriate branch.

@lcmFileInstaller::DefaultFilePermission.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::DefaultFilePermission.body: The method first delegates to the base implementation, then examines the install type. If the target is a shared or module library and the `CMAKE_INSTALL_SO_NO_EXE` flag isn’t present, it falls through; otherwise, for executable or program types, it appends execute bits to the file’s permission mask.

@lcmFileInstaller::GetTargetTypeFromStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::GetTargetTypeFromStri.body: The routine inspects a string descriptor and translates it into the corresponding internal enumeration. It assigns the matching `cmInstallType_*` value to `InstallType` and signals failure when the input doesn’t match any recognized token, in which case it populates an error message and returns `false`.

@lcmFileInstaller::HandleInstallDestinat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::HandleInstallDestinat.body: The function validates and normalises the install destination path. It checks for empty or relative paths, prefixes a DESTDIR value when supplied, and rejects network‐style paths unless they are absolute. It then ensures the target exists (creating it if needed) and confirms it is a directory with the proper permissions before returning success.

@lcmFileInstaller::Install@k_ZN15cmFileI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::Install@k_ZN15cmFileI.body: The `Install` method first checks whether the installer’s type is a directory and the source string is empty. In that special case it calls `InstallDirectory` with the destination path and the current match properties. If that condition isn’t met, it simply forwards the request to the base `cmFileCopier::Install` implementation, which performs a normal file copy.

@lcmFileInstaller::InstallFile@k_ZN15cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::InstallFile@k_ZN15cmF.body:
The routine first checks the configured install mode.  
If the mode is a plain copy it delegates to the base copier.  
For symlink modes it attempts to compute a relative path to the source; if that fails or the symlink already points to the same target it skips copying.  
When creating the link succeeds it removes any old file, ensures the target directory exists, and creates the symlink.  
If link creation fails (or a relative link cannot be formed), it falls back to copying the file.  
On any failure it records an error message and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmFileInstaller::ManifestAppend@k_ZN15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::ManifestAppend@k_ZN15.body: The routine appends the given path (minus the destination‑prefix part) to the internal `Manifest` string, inserting a semicolon separator only if the string already contains entries.

@lcmFileInstaller::Parse@k_ZN15cmFileIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::Parse@k_ZN15cmFileIns.body: The function first delegates to the base parser; if that fails it returns false. It then enforces constraints on a rename option (only single file, correct install type), validates that only one of the mutually‑exclusive message flags is set, and finally reads the CMAKE_INSTALL_MODE environment variable to select the install mode, reporting an error if the value is unknown. On success it returns true.

@lcmFileInstaller::ReportCopy@k_ZN15cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::ReportCopy@k_ZN15cmFi.body: The function logs the installation or update of a file. It first checks the `MessageNever` and `MessageLazy` flags; if neither suppresses a message, it builds a string “Installing: <file>” (or “Up‑to‑date: <file>” when not copying) and sends it to `Makefile->DisplayStatus`. Afterward, if the item isn’t a directory it records the file in the manifest via `ManifestAppend`. The method is `protected` and `virtual`, allowing subclasses to override the reporting behaviour.

@lcmFileInstaller::ReportMissing@k_ZN15c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::ReportMissing@k_ZN15c.body: The function simply checks whether the installer is marked as optional; if not, it forwards the call to the base `cmFileCopier::ReportMissing` implementation. It returns the logical OR of those two results.

@lcmFileInstaller::ToName@k_ZN15cmFileIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::ToName@k_ZN15cmFileIn.body: Determines the final file name to use—falling back to a configured override when one is present.

@lcmFileInstaller::cmFileInstaller@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::cmFileInstaller@k_ZN1.body: The constructor sets up a file‑installing instance: it passes the status reference and the literal “INSTALL” to the base `cmFileCopier`, disables source‑permission checks, optionally forces an “always‑install” mode if the environment variable `CMAKE_INSTALL_ALWAYS` evaluates to “on”, and stores the current manifest definition obtained via `Makefile->GetSafeDefinition`.

@lcmFileInstaller::~cmFileInstaller@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileInstaller::~cmFileInstaller@k_ZN.body: When a cmFileInstaller is destroyed, its destructor records the final install‑manifest by calling the owning Makefile instance’s AddDefinition routine with the key `CMAKE_INSTALL_MANIFEST_FILES` and the stored manifest object. This effectively writes the current state of the installer into the makefile before the object is reclaimed.

@lcmFileLock::IsLocked@k_ZNK10cmFileLock.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::IsLocked@k_ZNK10cmFileLock.body: This method simply checks whether the supplied filename string matches the stored `Filename` member; it returns `true` when they are equal, indicating that the file is considered locked.

@lcmFileLock::Lock@k_ZN10cmFileLock4Lock.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::Lock@k_ZN10cmFileLock4Lock.body: The `Lock` method first validates the supplied path, rejecting empty strings or a lock that is already in use. It records the filename, opens the file, then attempts to acquire the lock. If the caller passed `-1` as the timeout value, it falls back to a no‑timeout (blocking) lock; otherwise it hands the timeout to the helper that blocks until the timeout expires. On failure the method clears the stored filename to keep the object in a clean state and then returns a status code that callers can inspect.

@lcmFileLock::LockWithTimeout@k_ZN10cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::LockWithTimeout@k_ZN10cmFi.body:
Attempts to acquire a write‑lock by repeatedly calling `LockFile`.  
On each failure it examines `errno`; if the error isn’t `EACCES` or `EAGAIN` it fails with a system error, otherwise it retries after a 1‑second pause.  
If the timeout counter reaches zero the routine returns a timeout status; a successful lock returns an OK status.

@lcmFileLock::LockWithoutTimeout@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::LockWithoutTimeout@k_ZN10c.body: The function attempts to acquire a write lock on the target file via `LockFile`. If the system call fails, it returns an error‑indicating `MakeSystem`; otherwise it signals success with `MakeOk`.

@lcmFileLock::OpenFile@k_ZN10cmFileLock8.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::OpenFile@k_ZN10cmFileLock8.body: The function attempts to open a file identified by `Filename` in read‑write mode, stores the resulting file descriptor in `File`, and returns a result object indicating success or a system failure. If the `open` call fails (returns –1), the function returns a failure result via `MakeSystem`; otherwise it signals success via `MakeOk`.

@lcmFileLock::Release@k_ZN10cmFileLock7R.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::Release@k_ZN10cmFileLock7R.body:
If no file is stored, it returns success immediately.  
Otherwise it unlocks the file descriptor via LockFile, clears the stored name, closes the descriptor, and reports success only when the unlock call succeeds; otherwise it reports a system failure.

@lcmFileLock::cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLoc.body: The constructor assigns the owning file descriptor from the source instance to the new object, resets the source’s descriptor to an invalid sentinel, and moves the file‑name string into the new instance.

@lcmFileLock::cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLoc.body: cmFileLock acquires an exclusive lock on a file descriptor, preventing other processes from writing to the file until the lock is released. It returns a status code that indicates success or failure of the lock operation. The function is invoked in various parts of the code—for example, the call in `cmFileLock.h` around line 24 and the default constructor in `cmFileLockUnix.cxx` at line 12. In typical edge cases such as non‑existent files or insufficient permissions, the routine will return an error status to signal the inability to obtain the lock.

@lcmFileLock::operator=@k_ZN10cmFileLock.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::operator=@k_ZN10cmFileLock.body: The operator takes ownership of a temporary `cmFileLock` instance: it copies the `File` handle from `other`, resets that handle to `-1`, moves the `Filename` string into the current object, and finally returns the updated instance via `*this`.

@lcmFileLock::~cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::~cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLo.body: The destructor of `cmFileLock` verifies that a file lock was previously acquired. If the `Filename` member is non‑empty, it calls `Release()` to free the lock, discarding the returned `cmFileLockResult` (by casting to void) and asserts that the operation succeeded. This ensures the lock is cleaned up automatically when the object goes out of scope.

@lcmFileLockPool::IsAlreadyLocked@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::IsAlreadyLocked@k_ZNK1.body: The function scans the registered scopes in order: first all function‑specific scopes, then all file‑specific scopes, and finally the generic process scope. It asks each scope whether the supplied file name is already marked as in use, immediately returning true on the first affirmative answer; if none report a lock, it falls back to the process‑level check and returns that result.

@lcmFileLockPool::LockFileScope@k_ZN14cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::LockFileScope@k_ZN14cm.body: The function first checks whether the requested file is already held by the current locking pool; if so, it immediately returns a result indicating the file is already locked. Otherwise, it guarantees that there is at least one active scope (via the `assert`) and then delegates the actual lock operation to the most recent `FileScope` instance, forwarding the filename and timeout parameters and returning the outcome of that underlying lock attempt.

@lcmFileLockPool::LockFunctionScope@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::LockFunctionScope@k_ZN.body: The `LockFunctionScope` routine first verifies whether the requested file is already locked via `IsAlreadyLocked`; if so it returns an `AlreadyLocked` result. If no scopes are registered it returns a `NoFunction` result. Otherwise it forwards the lock request (along with the provided timeout) to the most recently added `FunctionScope` instance, returning that result.

@lcmFileLockPool::LockProcessScope@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::LockProcessScope@k_ZN1.body: If the file is already locked, the method returns a result indicating that; otherwise it forwards the lock request to the underlying `ProcessScope` component.

@lcmFileLockPool::PopFileScope@k_ZN14cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::PopFileScope@k_ZN14cmF.body: The method removes the most recently added file scope from the internal list, assuming that the list is not empty before the operation.

@lcmFileLockPool::PopFunctionScope@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::PopFunctionScope@k_ZN1.body: The `PopFunctionScope` method removes the most recent function scope from `FunctionScopes`, asserting that the stack is non‑empty before the pop.

@lcmFileLockPool::PushFileScope@k_ZN14cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::PushFileScope@k_ZN14cm.body: Creates a new entry at the end of the internal `FileScopes` container by calling its `emplace_back()` method—effectively appending a fresh scope object to the pool.

@lcmFileLockPool::PushFunctionScope@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::PushFunctionScope@k_ZN.body: The method appends a new scope instance to the internal container that tracks active scopes.

@lcmFileLockPool::Release@k_ZN14cmFileLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::Release@k_ZN14cmFileLo.body: It iterates through the stored scopes in the pool, invoking each scope’s Release method for the specified file; if any invocation reports an error it propagates that error immediately, otherwise it cascades through all scopes and returns the final status from the process‑level release.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.body: The function returns a Boolean indicating whether the supplied `cmFileLock` object represents a valid lock; it performs the necessary checks on that lock reference and reports the result.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.body: The lambda captures a string `filename` and, given a `cmFileLock` instance `lock`, returns `true` if that lock reports the file `filename` is currently locked (`lock.IsLocked(filename)`), otherwise `false`.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.body: The function iterates over the pool’s internal collection of lock objects and returns true if any of them reports that the supplied file name is already locked; if no lock matches the name it returns false.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::Lock@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::Lock@k_ZN14.body: The method attempts to lock the specified file; if successful, the lock is appended to the pool and an OK result is returned, otherwise the failure result is propagated.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::Release@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::Release@k_Z.body: The function iterates over the pool’s stored locks, checks each for a matching filename and, when found, invokes that lock’s `Release()` method, returning its result. If no matching lock is present, it simply returns an “OK” result.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::ScopePool@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::ScopePool@k.body: The move constructor creates a new `ScopePool` instance by transferring the internal state from another `ScopePool` object (passed as an r‑value reference). Because it is declared `noexcept`, it guarantees no exceptions will be thrown during the move. The defaulted implementation simply copies the moved‑from object's members (or swaps them) to initialize the new instance, ensuring efficient and exception‑safe construction.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::ScopePool@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::ScopePool@k.body: The `ScopePool` constructor initializes the lock‑pool object. It sets up internal bookkeeping (e.g., an allocator or a map of active locks) and prepares the pool for use. No additional initialization logic is required beyond the default constructor.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::operator=@k.body: This method moves the internal lock set from a temporary `ScopePool` into the current one—first guarding against self‑assignment, then moving the resource collection, and finally returning the updated object.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::~ScopePool@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::~ScopePool@.body: When the `ScopePool` object is destroyed, its destructor automatically releases any file‑level locks it holds, cleans up internal bookkeeping structures, and propagates the release of associated resources. Because the implementation is marked `= default`, the compiler generates a trivial destructor that performs these standard de‑allocation steps without custom logic.

@lcmFileLockPool::cmFileLockPool@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::cmFileLockPool@k_ZN14c.body: The constructor initializes the internal data structures that manage a pool of file‑level locks – allocating any necessary tables, setting initial flags, and ensuring the pool starts in a clean, ready‑to‑use state.

@lcmFileLockPool::~cmFileLockPool@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::~cmFileLockPool@k_ZN14.body: The `~cmFileLockPool()` destructor simply performs the clean‑up for a `cmFileLockPool` instance: it releases any internal lock handles and releases the underlying memory when the object goes out of scope. No explicit logic is executed beyond that, as the destructor is defaulted and relies on the class’s member destructors to tidy up its internal resources.

@lcmFileLockResult::GetOutputMessage@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::GetOutputMessage@k_Z.body:
This function maps the internal `Type` field of a `cmFileLockResult` instance to a user‑friendly string.  
When the `Type` is `OK`, it simply returns `"0"`.  
If the `Type` is `SYSTEM`, the code relies on the Windows `FormatMessageA` API to translate the stored error code (`ErrorValue`) into a human‑readable message; should that call fail, a fallback error string is returned.  
For the other enum values (`TIMEOUT`, `ALREADY_LOCKED`, `NO_FUNCTION`, `INTERNAL` and the default case) it returns a small, fixed explanatory string.  
In non‑Windows builds the `SYSTEM` branch falls back to `strerror`, providing the standard C library message for the error code.

@lcmFileLockResult::IsOk@k_ZNK16cmFileLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::IsOk@k_ZNK16cmFileLo.body: Returns true when the internal `Type` field holds the value `OK`. The function is a simple constant accessor that merely compares the stored status against the expected success indicator.

@lcmFileLockResult::MakeAlreadyLocked@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::MakeAlreadyLocked@k_.body: It returns a `cmFileLockResult` instance with the status flag set to `ALREADY_LOCKED` and an error code of `0`.

@lcmFileLockResult::MakeInternal@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::MakeInternal@k_ZN16c.body: It creates and returns a `cmFileLockResult` instance marked with `INTERNAL` and a zero error code.

@lcmFileLockResult::MakeNoFunction@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::MakeNoFunction@k_ZN1.body: This static method constructs and returns a `cmFileLockResult` instance signaling that no operation was performed (code `NO_FUNCTION` and no value).

@lcmFileLockResult::MakeOk@k_ZN16cmFileL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::MakeOk@k_ZN16cmFileL.body: Creates and returns a cmFileLockResult object with its status set to OK and an error code of 0, signifying a successful operation.

@lcmFileLockResult::MakeSystem@k_ZN16cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::MakeSystem@k_ZN16cmF.body: It fetches the current OS error code (via GetLastError on Windows or errno otherwise) and returns a `cmFileLockResult` instance that holds that code along with a flag indicating a system‑level failure.

@lcmFileLockResult::MakeTimeout@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::MakeTimeout@k_ZN16cm.body: Creates a `cmFileLockResult` object that signals a timeout condition—no error code other than zero.

@lcmFileLockResult::cmFileLockResult@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::cmFileLockResult@k_Z.body: This constructor captures the supplied error type and error instance into its internal fields. The two arguments are forwarded to the class’s fields (Type and ErrorValue) via an initializer list, leaving the object in a ready‑to‑use state.

@lcmFileLockResult::cmFileLockResult@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::cmFileLockResult@k_Z.body: Moves an existing `cmFileLockResult` into a new instance, copying the internal lock status and any associated state so that the new object correctly reflects the lock result of the source.

@lcmFileLockResult::cmFileLockResult@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::cmFileLockResult@k_Z.body: The constructor simply copies an existing `cmFileLockResult` instance, preserving its lock status and any error‑related data.

@lcmFileLockResult::operator=@k_ZN16cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::operator=@k_ZN16cmFi.body: The overloaded assignment operator takes an rvalue reference of type `cmFileLockResult`, performs an efficient move of the internal data members into the target object, updates its internal state accordingly, and returns a reference to the modified object to allow chaining. It is designed to avoid unnecessary copying, handle self‑assignment safely, and keep the object in a valid state after the move.

@lcmFileLockResult::~cmFileLockResult@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::~cmFileLockResult@k_.body: The `~cmFileLockResult()` function returns a status object that conveys whether a file locking attempt succeeded, failed, or timed‑out. It encapsulates a concise result code (often an enum or integer) together with any pertinent error details, enabling callers to quickly evaluate the outcome and react accordingly.

@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.body: It takes a single r‑value argument of type `cmFilePathChecksum` and produces a new instance that owns the supplied data. The function simply forwards the incoming object’s internal state (file path, checksum, any metadata) to the newly constructed instance, enabling efficient transfer of ownership without copying.

@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.body: The constructor extracts four key directory paths from the provided `cmMakefile` instance and forwards them to `setupParentDirs`. This prepares the internal state needed for subsequent checksum operations.

@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.body: The constructor simply forwards the four directory strings to `setupParentDirs`, initializing the object's internal parent‑directory state.

@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.body: It computes a checksum for a given file‑path string and returns that value (typically used to verify or compare file identities).

@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFilePathChecksum::cmFilePathChecksum.body: cmFilePathChecksum computes a hash of a file path string (typically using a fast checksum algorithm such as CRC32 or a cryptographic hash) so that callers can verify that a path has not been altered. It returns the resulting hash value (often as a 32‑bit integer or hexadecimal string) and can be invoked directly to confirm path integrity in other parts of the system.

@lcmFilePathChecksum::get@k_ZNK18cmFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFilePathChecksum::get@k_ZNK18cmFileP.body: The method resolves a file’s canonical path, locates the nearest registered “project root” from the stored `parentDirs` map (falling back to the system root if none matches), then builds a relative path from that root. It concatenates a seed string with this relative path, hashes the resulting string using SHA‑256, and finally encodes the hash bytes with a Base‑32 encoder to produce the checksum string that is returned.

@lcmFilePathChecksum::getPart@k_ZNK18cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFilePathChecksum::getPart@k_ZNK18cmF.body:
The method `getPart` fetches the value stored for `filePath` via `get(filePath)` and returns a prefix of that value.  
It takes a single argument `length`; if `length` is larger than the string’s size, `substr` will automatically truncate to the string’s end—no exception is thrown. Because the method is marked `const`, it guarantees no mutation of the object’s internal state. The only caveats to watch for are that `get(filePath)` may throw or return an empty string if the file path is unknown, and that callers should guard against unreasonable `length` values that could create zero‑length substrings unintentionally.

@lcmFilePathChecksum::setupParentDirs@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFilePathChecksum::setupParentDirs@k_.body: The function resolves the actual filesystem paths for four directories—current source, current binary, project source, and project binary—using `cmSystemTools::GetRealPath`, and stores each real path together with a descriptive label in the `parentDirs` collection.

@lcmFileSet::AddDirectoryEntry@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmFileSet::AddFileEntry@k_ZN9cmFileSet.body: The function appends the supplied `BTP<std::string>` instance to the internal `FileEntries` container using `std::move` to avoid copying, effectively adding the file path to the file set.

@lcmFileSet::ClearDirectoryEntries@k_ZN9.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::ClearDirectoryEntries@k_ZN9.body: The method simply empties the internal container that holds the file‑system entries. When invoked, it discards all stored directory records, resetting the state to no entries.

@lcmFileSet::ClearFileEntries@k_ZN9cmFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::ClearFileEntries@k_ZN9cmFil.body: The method wipes out the current list of file‑level entries held by the `cmFileSet` instance. It effectively resets the internal collection to an empty state, discarding every previously stored entry.

@lcmFileSet::CompileDirectoryEntries@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmFileSet::CompileFileEntries@k_ZNK9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::CompileFileEntries@k_ZNK9cm.body: The function collects each entry’s expressions, parses them with a generator instance, and returns a vector of the resulting compiled expressions.

@lcmFileSet::CopyEntries@k_ZN9cmFileSet1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::CopyEntries@k_ZN9cmFileSet1.body: This routine simply appends the directory and file entries from the supplied `cmFileSet` into the current instance’s lists using the helper `cm::append`.

@lcmFileSet::EvaluateDirectoryEntries@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::EvaluateDirectoryEntries@k_.body: The function `EvaluateDirectoryEntries` iterates over a list of generator‑expression objects, resolves each entry to a path (normalising relative paths to absolute ones based on the current source directory), and then verifies that the resulting set of directories contains no base‑directory overlaps – i.e. no entry may lie in a sub‑directory of another. If such a conflict is detected, the generator issues a fatal error message and the function returns an empty result; otherwise it returns the list of cleaned directory strings.

@lcmFileSet::EvaluateFileEntry@k_ZNK9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::EvaluateFileEntry@k_ZNK9cmF.body: This method processes a collection of file paths returned by a compiled generator expression. It normalizes each path to an absolute form, prepends the current source directory when needed, collapses redundant components, and determines the directory in which the file resides relative to a supplied list of base directories. If a file does not belong under any of those base directories, it logs a fatal error and aborts processing. Otherwise the file is added to a map keyed by the relative directory path, grouping files per directory for subsequent handling.

@lcmFileSet::GetDirectoryEntries@k_ZNK9c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetDirectoryEntries@k_ZNK9c.body: This member function returns a read‑only reference to the internal container holding the directory’s entries, letting callers inspect the stored items without triggering a copy while preserving the object’s const‑correctness.

@lcmFileSet::GetFileEntries@k_ZNK9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetFileEntries@k_ZNK9cmFile.body: Returns a reference to the internal vector storing the entries. The method is const, so it guarantees no mutation of the object and simply exposes the stored data.

@lcmFileSet::GetName@k_ZNK9cmFileSet7Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetName@k_ZNK9cmFileSet7Get.body: Returns the stored string by reference so callers can read it without copying, and because the method is marked `const` it guarantees no modification of the object’s state.

@lcmFileSet::GetType@k_ZNK9cmFileSet7Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetType@k_ZNK9cmFileSet7Get.body:

@lcmFileSet::GetVisibility@k_ZNK9cmFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetVisibility@k_ZNK9cmFileS.body: The method simply returns the value of the `Visibility` member of the object, allowing read‑only access without modifying any state.

@lcmFileSet::cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetC1E.body: Creates a `cmFileSet` instance that stores the supplied `cmake` instance, the desired set name, type, and the visibility flag, forwarding the `cmake` instance to the base class.

@lcmFileSetVisibilityFromName@k_Z27cmFil.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmFileSetVisibilityIsForSelf@k_Z28cmFi.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmFileSetVisibilityToName@k_Z25cmFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSetVisibilityToName@k_Z25cmFileS.body: This function maps a `cmFileSetVisibility` value to its textual name: it returns a static string view for the `Interface`, `Public`, or `Private` cases, and falls back to an empty string if none of those matches.

@lcmFileTime::Compare@k_ZNK10cmFileTime7.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTime::Compare@k_ZNK10cmFileTime7.body:
This member compares the internal timestamp of the current object with the timestamp of another `cmFileTime`.  
* It computes the signed difference between the two times.  
* If the difference is zero, the function returns `0` to indicate equality.  
* If the difference is negative, it returns `-1`, indicating the current object is earlier.  
* If the difference is positive, it returns `1`, indicating the current object is later.  

Because the method is marked `const`, it guarantees no modification of member data during the comparison.

@lcmFileTime::Load@k_ZN10cmFileTime4Load.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTime::Load@k_ZN10cmFileTime4Load.body:
The Load member reads the last‑modified timestamp of a file and stores it in the object’s Time field.  
If compiled for POSIX it invokes stat to fetch the file’s attributes; on Windows it uses GetFileAttributesEx to obtain the extended file attributes.  
Depending on the platform’s resolution (nanoseconds, microseconds or seconds) it performs the appropriate conversion to the internal representation.  
If the file cannot be accessed or the attribute call fails, the function immediately returns false; otherwise it writes the retrieved value into Time and returns true.

@lcmFileTime::Newer@k_ZNK10cmFileTime5Ne.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTime::Newer@k_ZNK10cmFileTime5Ne.body: The method checks if a supplied `cmFileTime` instance represents a timestamp that is earlier than the time stored in the current object. It simply returns `true` when `ftm.Time` is strictly less than `this‑>Time`; otherwise it yields `false`.

@lcmFileTime::Older@k_ZNK10cmFileTime5Ol.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTime::Older@k_ZNK10cmFileTime5Ol.body: The function returns true when the object’s stored time value precedes the time value supplied in the `cmFileTime` argument – i.e., when the current instance is earlier in time.

@lcmFileTime::cmFileTime@k_ZN10cmFileTim.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmFileTime::cmFileTime@k_ZN10cmFileTim.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTime::cmFileTime@k_ZN10cmFileTim.body: Retrieves the current file’s last‑modified timestamp, normalizing it to a standard `time_t` value that callers can compare against other file timestamps.

@lcmFileTime::~cmFileTime@k_ZN10cmFileTi.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmFileTimeCache::Compare@k_ZN15cmFileT.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmFileTimeCache::Load@k_ZN15cmFileTime.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmFileTimeCache::Remove@k_ZN15cmFileTi.body: Removes the named key from the internal cache map, returning true only when an entry was actually deleted.

@lcmFileTimeCache::cmFileTimeCache@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTimeCache::cmFileTimeCache@k_ZN1.body: The `cmFileTimeCache` constructor establishes an internal cache that stores timestamps of files. It populates a map keyed by file paths with their last‑modified times, so subsequent lookups can be answered in O(1) time rather than re‑querying the file system. The cache is thread‑safe and invalidates entries when the underlying file time changes.

@lcmFileTimeCache::~cmFileTimeCache@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTimeCache::~cmFileTimeCache@k_ZN.body: The `~cmFileTimeCache()` destructor releases any internal resources (such as file‑handles or in‑memory structures) that the cache manager holds. It ensures that the cache’s internal data structures are cleanly deallocated and that any pending cleanup tasks are performed before an instance is destroyed.

@lcmFileTimes::Copy@k_ZN11cmFileTimes4Co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTimes::Copy@k_ZN11cmFileTimes4Co.body: Copies the timestamp metadata from a source file to a target file. The routine constructs a `cmFileTimes` instance, invokes its `Load()` method on the source path, and upon success forwards that data to `Store()` for the destination. The function returns a status object that signals either success or the specific load‑or‑store failure that occurred.

@lcmFileTimes::IsValid@k_ZNK11cmFileTime.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTimes::IsValid@k_ZNK11cmFileTime.body: The method simply checks whether the `times` member is non‑null. If `times` points to an instance, `IsValid()` returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmFileTimes::Load@k_ZN11cmFileTimes4Lo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTimes::Load@k_ZN11cmFileTimes4Lo.body:
The `Load` method obtains the timestamps for a file named `fileName`.  
If the current instance already has valid times, it simply reuses them; otherwise it creates a new `Times` object, queries the operating system for the file’s creation, last‑access, and last‑write times (via Windows’ `CreateFileW` or POSIX `stat`), stores them in the instance’s `Times` member, and returns a `cmsys::Status` reflecting success or the last error encountered.

@lcmFileTimes::Store@k_ZNK11cmFileTimes5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTimes::Store@k_ZNK11cmFileTimes5.body: The `Store` method stores a previously cached set of timestamps on a file. It first checks that the object is in a valid state and returns an error if not. On Windows it opens the file via the Windows API, sets the creation, last‑access and last‑write times with `SetFileTime`, and reports any failure. On other platforms it calls `utime`. On success it returns a success status.

@lcmFileTimes::cmFileTimes@k_ZN11cmFileT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTimes::cmFileTimes@k_ZN11cmFileT.body: The `cmFileTimes` constructor initializes an object by loading the supplied file’s metadata via `Load`. It sets up internal state (file name, timestamps, etc.) to enable subsequent queries or comparisons of the file’s time attributes.

@lcmFileTimes::cmFileTimes@k_ZN11cmFileT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTimes::cmFileTimes@k_ZN11cmFileT.body: cmFileTimes is a class constructor that initializes internal data structures for tracking file timestamps. It sets up any necessary state so the rest of the application can query and manipulate file time information.

@lcmFileTimes::~cmFileTimes@k_ZN11cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileTimes::~cmFileTimes@k_ZN11cmFile.body: The destructor of the `cmFileTimes` class is invoked automatically when an instance goes out of scope. It releases any resources that the object may have acquired during its lifetime—such as file handles, allocated memory, or any other internal state—ensuring that no memory leaks or dangling references remain.

@lcmFileUploadProgressCallback@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileUploadProgressCallback@k_ZN12_GL.body: The function receives a callback context and progress values, casts the context to a `cURLProgressHelper` instance, then calls its `UpdatePercentage` method with the current upload fraction. If that call succeeds, it obtains a status string and tells the associated `cmMakefile` object to display that status. It returns 0 to signal success.

@lcmFindBase::CheckForVariableDefined@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::CheckForVariableDefined@k_.body: The method checks whether a given variable is defined in the current makefile. It first queries the makefile for a definition; if one exists, it retrieves the current state cache entry for that variable. It then determines whether the variable’s type is already known in the cache. If the entry is cached with a non‑uninitialized type, it updates the instance’s VariableType and, if a HELPSTRING property is present, stores that documentation. It also flags the case where the value was supplied on the command line but the cached entry had no meta‑information. If any of these conditions indicates the variable is indeed defined, the function returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmFindBase::ExpandPaths@k_ZN10cmFindBa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::ExpandPaths@k_ZN10cmFindBa.body: The routine orchestrates a series of conditional path‑filling operations: it first applies any default, package‑root, CMake‑var, and CMake‑env paths if the corresponding skip flags are unset, then always injects a user‑hint path. Afterwards, if defaults are still enabled, it appends system‑environment and CMake‑system variable paths where flagged, and finally injects a user‑guess path. This sequence guarantees that the resolved path list contains every applicable source in the correct precedence order.

@lcmFindBase::FillCMakeEnvironmentPath@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::FillCMakeEnvironmentPath@k.body: The function gathers search‑paths for CMake by appending a prefix (“CMAKE_…_PATH”) and an optional suffix list. It then adds a “CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH” to the list, and depending on the value of CMakePathName either appends “CMAKE_APPBUNDLE_PATH” (if the name is “PROGRAM”) or “CMAKE_FRAMEWORK_PATH” (otherwise). Finally it merges any pre‑supplied suffixes. The routine simply assembles a list of environment‑based paths for later lookup.

@lcmFindBase::FillCMakeSystemVariablePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::FillCMakeSystemVariablePat.body: The function decides, based on the current Makefile flags, whether the CMake install prefix should appear in the system‑prefix list. It checks whether the prefix is already in the list, removes it if it is present but should be omitted, or inserts it if it is missing. After that it appends the appropriate CMake variable names (program‑specific or framework‑specific) and the configured suffixes to finish the path list.

@lcmFindBase::FillCMakeVariablePath@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::FillCMakeVariablePath@k_ZN.body: The routine builds the set of CMake‑specific search paths. It first constructs the variable name `CMAKE_<name>_PATH` from the stored `CMakePathName`, pushes the standard `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` into the list, and then inserts that constructed variable. Depending on whether the path label is the special “PROGRAM” case, it appends either the `CMAKE_APPBUNDLE_PATH` or the `CMAKE_FRAMEWORK_PATH` entry. Finally it appends any suffixes stored in `SearchPathSuffixes` to the collection.

@lcmFindBase::FillPackageRootPath@k_ZN10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::FillPackageRootPath@k_ZN10.body: The routine gathers the package‑root locations that were discovered during a preceding `find_package` search. It iterates over the stored stack in reverse order, appending each collected path to the internal path list as a prefix, and finally appends a set of standard suffixes that are common to the search.

@lcmFindBase::FillSystemEnvironmentPath@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::FillSystemEnvironmentPath@.body: It grabs the `SystemEnvironment` entry from the internal map, then injects any configured environment path into that `cmSearchPath` instance (if one was supplied). After that it ensures the standard `PATH` variable is added to the search list, and finally it appends the class‑wide suffixes that should be appended to every entry. The routine therefore guarantees the search paths for the system environment are properly populated before any further lookup logic runs.

@lcmFindBase::FillUserGuessPath@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::FillUserGuessPath@k_ZN10cm.body: It loops over the stored guess arguments, inserting each into the labeled‑path list for the *Guess* label, and then appends the defined suffixes.

@lcmFindBase::FillUserHintsPath@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::FillUserHintsPath@k_ZN10cm.body: The function grabs the hint‑path list, iterates over every string in `UserHintsArgs` adding each one as a user path to that list, and finally appends the configured suffixes to the collection.

@lcmFindBase::NormalizeFindResult@k_ZN10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::NormalizeFindResult@k_ZN10.body: When `NormalizeFindResult()` runs, it first checks whether the `Makefile` policy `CMP0125` is in the *NEW* state. If so, it resolves any relative path returned by the find command into an absolute path relative to the current working directory. It then normalises that path string (normalising slashes, removing redundancies). Next it decides whether the result should be cached: if so, it updates the cache entry for the variable. If a new cache entry is added and the old entry existed, it may also replace the existing cache definition. When caching is not requested, it simply ensures the variable is defined in the Makefile, creating a normal definition if one was absent or replacing an obsolete one. The function also cleans up any previous definition that was found only in the cache, so that the final state contains only the canonical definition.

@lcmFindBase::ParseArguments::[lambda_0].author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::ParseArguments::[lambda_0].body: It captures `validatorName` and compares a supplied string against it with a case‑insensitive comparison, returning true when they match – essentially a predicate used to locate a matching entry.

@lcmFindBase::ParseArguments@k_ZN10cmFin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::ParseArguments@k_ZN10cmFin.body: The function verifies that at least two arguments were supplied, then walks through the input vector once. It strips out special tokens (“DOC”, “NO_CACHE”, “ENV”, “PATH_SUFFIXES”, “NAMES”, “PATHS”, “HINTS”, “NAMES_PER_DIR”, “NO_SYSTEM_PATH”, “REQUIRED”, “REGISTRY_VIEW”, “VALIDATOR”) and any other recognized keywords. Anything that does not match a keyword is collected into one of four buckets: names, paths, hints, or suffixes. When it encounters a “DOC” token it stores the following argument as documentation text. After this first pass the function fills internal structures for variable name, documentation string, and sets the various flags (e.g., cache usage, environment path, required‑ness, registry view, validator command). It then invokes helper routines to determine default search modes, root‑path mode, and registry policy, expands any user‑supplied paths, and finally resolves the effective search paths. The routine finishes by returning true if all arguments were successfully processed, otherwise it signals an error and returns false.

@lcmFindBase::StoreFindResult@k_ZN10cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::StoreFindResult@k_ZN10cmFi.body: When called, the method examines whether the incoming string is non‑empty. If it contains data, it either records the value in a cached definition (and, if appropriate, also records it as a regular definition) or simply writes it as a normal definition, depending on the internal flags `StoreResultInCache` and the policy states for `CMP0125`/`CMP0126`. When the string is empty, it records a special “‑NOTFOUND” marker in the same way. If the operation is marked as required and no value was found, the function emits a fatal‑error message listing the missing item and signals a global fatal‑error flag.

@lcmFindBase::Validate@k_ZNK10cmFindBase.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::Validate@k_ZNK10cmFindBase.body: The function first checks whether a validator is configured; if not, it simply returns true. Otherwise it sets up two scoped policy objects, creates a status flag name, registers a Boolean definition in the makefile, and then constructs a list‑file command for the validator with the flag and path arguments. The command is executed, and the function finally returns the Boolean value of the definition that was set by the validator.

@lcmFindBase::cmFindBase@k_ZN10cmFindBas.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::cmFindBase@k_ZN10cmFindBas.body: This constructor forwards the supplied `status` to `cmFindCommon` and stores the provided `findCommandName` into the member `FindCommandName` using move semantics. It performs no additional work beyond initializing the base class and the member variable.

@lcmFindBase::cmFindBase@k_ZN10cmFindBas.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::cmFindBase@k_ZN10cmFindBas.body: The constructor copies an existing `cmFindBase` instance into a new one, delegating the actual field initialization to the base `cmFindCommon` class while preserving any internal configuration the caller supplies.

@lcmFindBase::operator=@k_ZN10cmFindBase.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::operator=@k_ZN10cmFindBase.body: Assigns the state of the source instance into the current object, returning a reference to `*this`.

@lcmFindBase::~cmFindBase@k_ZN10cmFindBa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBase::~cmFindBase@k_ZN10cmFindBa.body:
The public virtual destructor of `cmFindBase` is defined as `virtual ~cmFindBase() = default;`.  
Because it is declared `virtual`, the compiler will generate a virtual destructor that automatically calls the destructors of any derived classes. The `= default` clause means no custom code is executed; the compiler-generated body simply performs standard object‑destruction. This guarantees that any resources owned by subclasses will be correctly released when an object of the base type is destroyed.

@lcmFindBaseDebugState::DebugLibState::D.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBaseDebugState::DebugLibState::D.body: The constructor copies the first argument into the member `regexName` and moves the second argument into the member `path`. No additional logic is performed.

@lcmFindBaseDebugState::DebugLibState::D.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBaseDebugState::DebugLibState::D.body: DebugLibState is a public routine that re‑initialises the library’s internal debugging flags to the predefined defaults before any diagnostic output is emitted. It guarantees that every component that invokes the debugging subsystem starts with a clean, known‑state configuration, thereby preventing stale or conflicting debug‑session data from leaking into successive runs.

@lcmFindBaseDebugState::FailedAt@k_ZN20c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBaseDebugState::FailedAt@k_ZN20c.body: The `FailedAt` helper records a failed regex‑match attempt: when debug mode is on it pushes a pair of the supplied regex name and search path into the `FailedSearchLocations` container.

@lcmFindBaseDebugState::FoundAt@k_ZN20cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBaseDebugState::FoundAt@k_ZN20cm.body: When called, `FoundAt` checks the object’s `DebugMode` flag. If debugging is enabled, it constructs a `DebugLibState` instance from the supplied `regexName` and `path`, and stores that instance in `FoundSearchLocation`. If debugging is off, the function performs no action.

@lcmFindBaseDebugState::cmFindBaseDebugS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBaseDebugState::cmFindBaseDebugS.body: Initialises the debug‑state finder: it stores the supplied command name and forwards the supplied find‑base pointer to the base class, leaving the object in a ready‑to‑use state.

@lcmFindBaseDebugState::~cmFindBaseDebug.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindBaseDebugState::~cmFindBaseDebug.body: The function is a destructor that, when called in debug mode, constructs a detailed diagnostic string. It concatenates the command name, variable name, list of names (wrapped in quotes), documentation, and flags for search‑only settings. It then appends each path from `FailedSearchLocations`, and finally reports whether a matching path was found. The resulting buffer is supplied to `DebugMessage`.

@lcmFindCommon::AddPathSuffix@k_ZN12cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::AddPathSuffix@k_ZN12cmFi.body: The function trims leading and trailing slashes from the supplied string; if the resulting string is non‑empty, it appends that string to the `SearchPathSuffixes` vector.

@lcmFindCommon::CheckCommonArgument@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::CheckCommonArgument@k_ZN.body: When called, the function matches the supplied string against a set of predefined keys. For a recognised key it flips the corresponding internal flag (or sets an enumeration value) and returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmFindCommon::ComputeFinalPaths@k_ZN12.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::ComputeFinalPaths@k_ZN12.body: Filters out ignored entries, clears the current path list, expands any root‑level directories, and normalises each path by appending a trailing slash.

@lcmFindCommon::ComputeIfDebugModeWanted.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::ComputeIfDebugModeWanted.body: The function checks whether a debug mode is desired by first consulting an internal flag (via ComputeIfDebugModeWanted) and, if that yields false, falling back to the CMake instance’s debug‑find logic for the supplied variable name.

@lcmFindCommon::ComputeIfDebugModeWanted.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::ComputeIfDebugModeWanted.body: The function checks three internal flags that indicate whether debug‑mode should be enabled for the current build: it returns `true` if either the package mode flag (`GetDebugFindPkgMode`) is on, or if the makefile’s `CMAKE_FIND_DEBUG_MODE` switch is set, or if the CMake instance’s debug‑output flag (`GetDebugFindOutput`) is active. It simply aggregates those three conditions with logical OR.

@lcmFindCommon::DebugMessage@k_ZNK12cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::DebugMessage@k_ZNK12cmFi.body: The method simply forwards the supplied string to the `Makefile` instance, invoking `IssueMessage` with a `LOG` type when `Makefile` is non‑null.

@lcmFindCommon::DebugModeEnabled@k_ZNK12.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::DebugModeEnabled@k_ZNK12.body: This getter simply exposes the internal `DebugMode` flag, returning its boolean value. It is a trivial accessor that returns the current debug‑mode status of the object.

@lcmFindCommon::GetIgnoredPaths@k_ZN12cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::GetIgnoredPaths@k_ZN12cm.body: The routine collects the ignored paths into a temporary vector via an internal helper and then inserts every element from that vector into the supplied set.

@lcmFindCommon::GetIgnoredPrefixPaths@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::GetIgnoredPrefixPaths@k_.body: It calls an overload that fills a vector with the ignored prefixes, then copies that vector into the caller‑supplied set.

@lcmFindCommon::InitializeSearchPathGrou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::InitializeSearchPathGrou.body: The routine builds a mapping from each search‑label to a dedicated search path, populates an ordered list of the groups (here only “All”), and records those mappings in the class’s internal containers so the rest of the search system can iterate over the defined groups in the proper sequence.

@lcmFindCommon::PathGroup::PathGroup@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::PathGroup::PathGroup@k_Z.body: The constructor takes a string reference and uses an initializer‑list to copy the value into the member variable `cmPathLabel`. This establishes a new `PathGroup` instance with its label set to the supplied string.

@lcmFindCommon::PathGroup::PathGroup@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::PathGroup::PathGroup@k_Z.body: The `PathGroup` helper collects a set of paths into a single logical group so later parts of the code can treat that collection as one entity—often for lookup, caching, or rendering a composite path. It basically bundles the paths’ metadata and any common flags or optimisations needed before the group is used elsewhere.

@lcmFindCommon::PathLabel::PathLabel@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::PathLabel::PathLabel@k_Z.body: A move constructor that efficiently steals the internal state of a temporary `PathLabel` instance, allowing the object to be copied without re‑allocating resources.

@lcmFindCommon::PathLabel::PathLabel@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::PathLabel::PathLabel@k_Z.body: PathLabel is a constructor that assigns the supplied string to the member variable `cmPathLabel`. It accepts its argument by const reference to avoid unnecessary copying. The body is empty beyond that member‑initialisation.

@lcmFindCommon::PathLabel::PathLabel@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::PathLabel::PathLabel@k_Z.body: Creates a new `PathLabel` by copying the internal state of an existing instance, initializing its label and path data accordingly.

@lcmFindCommon::PathLabel::PathLabel@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::PathLabel::PathLabel@k_Z.body: PathLabel attaches a unique identifier to a path instance, enabling efficient referencing and subsequent processing of that specific path within the program.

@lcmFindCommon::RerootPaths::[lambda_0]@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::RerootPaths::[lambda_0]@.body: This lambda returns true when the two supplied paths represent the same location (after resolving real paths) or when one path is a sub‑directory of the other.

@lcmFindCommon::RerootPaths@k_ZN12cmFind.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::RerootPaths@k_ZN12cmFind.body: The routine normalizes a list of file system paths by prefixing them with a set of candidate “root” directories (sysroot, sysroot‑compile, sysroot‑link, root‑path). It iterates over each root, checks whether a path is already a sub‑directory of that root (or equal to it), and if not, it constructs a new path prefixed with that root. Depending on the mode flag, it may also keep the original paths in the final list.

@lcmFindCommon::SelectDefaultMacMode@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::SelectDefaultMacMode@k_Z.body: The routine reads the two configuration strings “CMAKE_FIND_FRAMEWORK” and “CMAKE_FIND_APPBUNDLE” from the makefile; depending on whether each string equals **NEVER, ONLY, FIRST,** or **LAST** it flips the corresponding `SearchFramework…` and `SearchAppBundle…` flags so that the search logic knows whether to skip, find only, or prioritize the first/last match.

@lcmFindCommon::SelectDefaultRootPathMod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::SelectDefaultRootPathMod.body:
The function reads the value of a policy variable named `CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_<path‑name>` (where `<path‑name>` is the current CMake path name).  
It then compares that value against three literal strings – “NEVER”, “ONLY”, and “BOTH” – and assigns the corresponding enum value (`RootPathModeNever`, `RootPathModeOnly`, or `RootPathModeBoth`) to the `FindRootPathMode` member. If the value is none of those literals, the code simply falls through without modifying the mode.

@lcmFindCommon::SelectDefaultSearchModes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::SelectDefaultSearchModes.body: The routine walks a fixed list of flag–environment‑identifier pairs, queries each identifier from the current make‑file, and assigns the associated member‑flag to the logical negation of the definition’s truth.

@lcmFindCommon::SetError@k_ZN12cmFindCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::SetError@k_ZN12cmFindCom.body: The function forwards an incoming error message to the class’s internal status tracker, invoking the status object’s `SetError` routine so the error string is stored for later reporting.

@lcmFindCommon::cmFindCommon@k_ZN12cmFin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::cmFindCommon@k_ZN12cmFin.body: cmFindCommon is a public method that computes and returns the common elements between two input collections, typically by moving or swapping values as needed.

@lcmFindCommon::cmFindCommon@k_ZN12cmFin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::cmFindCommon@k_ZN12cmFin.body: The constructor configures the search behavior for the tool: it establishes defaults for locating frameworks, bundles, and system paths; it sets flags that govern whether frameworks or bundles are searched first, whether only they should be considered, and whether to search in the last position. It initializes the search‑path groups and activates debug mode conditionally. It also determines which Windows registry view to use (32‑bit or 64‑bit) based on policy and “CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P” definition.

@lcmFindCommon::cmFindCommon@k_ZN12cmFin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::cmFindCommon@k_ZN12cmFin.body: The `cmFindCommon` function is a copy‑constructor. It takes a const reference to an existing `cmFindCommon` instance and creates a new object whose internal state (including any collections or flags that the class manages) is duplicated from the source. In effect it simply replicates the data members of the argument into the newly‑constructed object, leaving the original untouched.

@lcmFindCommon::operator=@k_ZN12cmFindCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::operator=@k_ZN12cmFindCo.body: The assignment operator accepts an rvalue reference to a `cmFindCommon` instance, moves its data into the current object, and returns a reference to `*this`.

@lcmFindCommon::operator=@k_ZN12cmFindCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindCommon::operator=@k_ZN12cmFindCo.body: The assignment operator copies another cmFindCommon’s internal state into the current object and returns a reference to that object for chained assignments.

@lcmFindFile@k_Z10cmFindFileRKiR17cmExec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindFile@k_Z10cmFindFileRKiR17cmExec.body: cmFindFile initializes a cmFindFileCommand using the provided status, then runs its InitialPass on the supplied argument vector, returning that result.

@lcmFindFileCommand::cmFindFileCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindFileCommand::cmFindFileCommand@k.body: The constructor for cmFindFileCommand registers the command under the name “find_file” and flags that the result will be a file‑path value. It also enables inclusion of the file in the search path by setting IncludeFileInPath to true.

@lcmFindFileCommand::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindFileCommand::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference, efficiently transferring the internal state of the source object into the current instance. This enables a compact, move‑style copy while preserving the proper ownership semantics of the command object.

@lcmFindFileCommand::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindFileCommand::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.body: The overloaded assignment operator copies the configuration state from the right‑hand side object into the current instance. It performs a member‑wise copy of the internal data members and then returns a reference to the modified object so that further chaining or assignment can be performed in a single statement.

@lcmFindFileCommand::~cmFindFileCommand@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindFileCommand::~cmFindFileCommand@.body: The overridden function supplies the concrete implementation of the *Find File* command: it parses the supplied search arguments, walks the configured search space looking for a matching file, and returns the first path that satisfies the criteria (or an error if none is found).

@lcmFindLibrary@k_Z13cmFindLibraryRKiR17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibrary@k_Z13cmFindLibraryRKiR17.body: The function simply passes the supplied argument list and status reference to an internal command handler (`cmFindLibraryCommand`) and returns that handler’s boolean result.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::AddArchitectureP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::AddArchitectureP.body: The method builds a list of search‑paths for a given architecture: it first looks for a “lib/” sub‑path, tries the variant suffixed with the requested suffix (or with a trailing “/”), and, if both exist, prefers the suffixed one unless it would duplicate a symlinked directory; finally it adds both directories to the internal list, tagging them for the current architecture.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::AddArchitectureP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::AddArchitectureP.body: The method temporarily stores the current search‑path list, then iterates over each original entry. For each entry it invokes the helper to add a new path built with the supplied suffix (the helper is responsible for the actual path construction). If debug mode is on, it emits a message describing the removal of the original suffix and the addition of the new path.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindFrameworkLib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindFrameworkLib.body: Returns a string that is either the result of `FindFrameworkLibraryNamesPerDir()` or `FindFrameworkLibraryDirsPerName()` depending on the `NamesPerDir` flag.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindFrameworkLib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindFrameworkLib.body: The function iterates over every search path and each library name. It builds a candidate path by appending “.xcframework” or “.framework” to the name, checks whether the path exists as a directory, collapses the absolute path, validates it through a custom rule, and returns the first matching path. If none match, it returns an empty string.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindFrameworkLib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindFrameworkLib.body: The function scans each search‑path and each candidate name, builds a path ending in “.xcframework” then “.framework”, tests whether that path points to a directory that satisfies the class’s Validate rule, and returns the fully‑expanded path of the first such match; if none exists, it returns an empty string.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindLibrary@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindLibrary@k_ZN.body: The function first attempts to locate a library using a framework search when the flags `SearchFrameworkFirst` or `SearchFrameworkOnly` are set. If that search fails and the `SearchFrameworkOnly` flag is not active, it falls back to a normal library search. Finally, if the fallback search still yields nothing and `SearchFrameworkLast` is true, it attempts the framework search one more time before returning the resulting path. The returned string is empty only if none of the searches succeed.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindNormalLibrar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindNormalLibrar.body: The function checks whether a “names‑per‑directory” flag is set; if so, it calls a helper that looks up a library by name‑per‑dir; otherwise it falls back to a directory‑by‑name search.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindNormalLibrar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindNormalLibrar.body: The function iterates over every library name in `Names` and for each one probes each directory listed in `SearchPaths`. It uses `cmFindLibraryHelper` to set the current name and test a directory with `CheckDirectory`. When a match is found, it immediately returns that directory path; if none match is found, it returns an empty string.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindNormalLibrar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::FindNormalLibrar.body: The function iterates over the stored names, registers them with a helper helper, then scans each directory in `SearchPaths` for a file that matches any of those names. As soon as a match is found, it returns that file’s full path; if nothing matches, it returns an empty string.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::InitialPass@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::InitialPass@k_ZN.body:
The function first parses the supplied arguments and configures the debug mode.  
If the library is already known it normalises the result and returns success.  
Otherwise it builds the search path, preferring any custom suffix, then adding architecture‑specific directories (32/64/x32) as requested, and finally performs the actual find operation, storing the result before returning true.

@lcmFindLibraryCommand::cmFindLibraryCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryCommand::cmFindLibraryCom.body: The constructor for `cmFindLibraryCommand` initializes the command’s internal state: it sets the environment variable path to `"LIB"`, enables multiple‑name resolution per directory, records a short documentation string, and marks the variable type as a file path.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::AddName@k_ZN19cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::AddName@k_ZN19cmF.body: Adds a library entry: verifies the name has a valid suffix, stores the raw name, then builds a regex string by concatenating a prefix, the literal name, and a suffix (with an optional version pattern for OpenBSD). The regex is compiled and the resulting `Name` object is appended to the internal list.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::CheckDirectory@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::CheckDirectory@k_.body: Iterates over the stored names in the object; for each name it calls `CheckDirectoryForName` with the supplied path. If any call returns true, the function immediately returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::CheckDirectoryFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::CheckDirectoryFor.body: The function searches a specified directory for a library file that matches the requested library name. It first attempts a straightforward match using the raw name, then enumerates all files in the directory, matching each against a compiled regex that encodes known prefixes, suffixes and version parts. As matches are found it keeps the “best” candidate by preferring earlier‑listed prefixes/suffixes and higher version numbers, storing that path in `BestPath`. When finished, it returns true if a suitable file was found, otherwise it reports failure.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::DebugLibraryFaile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::DebugLibraryFaile.body: The routine records a library‑load failure when debugging is enabled: it picks the single stored prefix/suffix (or a regex fallback), builds a combined name from those parts and the supplied library name, and forwards that composite string to the internal failure reporting mechanism.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::DebugLibraryFound.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::DebugLibraryFound.body:
The routine records when a library is discovered.  
When the internal debug switch is on, it stitches the supplied name into a pre‑built regex pattern (prefix + name + suffix) and hands that pattern along with the actual file location to the internal logger (`DebugSearches.FoundAt`).

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::GetPrefixIndex@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::GetPrefixIndex@k_.body: The function performs a linear search through the stored prefixes vector to locate the supplied string and returns its zero‑based position (or a large value if not found).

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::GetSuffixIndex@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::GetSuffixIndex@k_.body: The routine scans the internal list of suffixes with a linear search (`std::find`) and converts the resulting iterator into a zero‑based offset by subtracting the list’s beginning iterator. If the requested suffix is missing, the iterator will be `end()`, so the returned value equals the list’s size, which callers may interpret as “not found”. The implementation is straightforward but incurs an O(n) lookup; alternatives such as maintaining a hash map or keeping the list sorted for a binary search could lower the average cost.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::HasValidSuffix@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::HasValidSuffix@k_.body: The function scans a pre‑populated list of suffix strings. For each entry it first checks if the supplied name ends exactly with that suffix; if that succeeds it returns true. If no exact match is found it appends a dot to the suffix and then checks whether that dotted string occurs anywhere in the name; a match here also yields true. If none of the suffixes match, the routine returns false.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::Name::Name@k_ZN19.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::Name::Name@k_ZN19.body: It accepts a temporary `Name` instance and performs the necessary initialization or move‑logic for that object.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::Name::Name@k_ZN19.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::Name::Name@k_ZN19.body: The function **Name** accepts a `Name` instance by const reference and performs the core transformation logic required by the surrounding module, returning the resulting value for downstream consumption.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::Name::Name@k_ZN19.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::Name::Name@k_ZN19.body: The Name function is a public entry point that creates and returns an instance of struct Name. It is invoked from several other modules, with its implementation located in the cmFindLibraryCommand.cxx file (around line 215).

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::RegexFromList@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::RegexFromList@k_Z.body: The routine builds a regex pattern that matches any of the supplied strings. It first adds an opening parenthesis, then appends each literal escaped by `RegexFromLiteral`, separating them with a pipe (`|`). Finally, it closes the group with a closing parenthesis.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::RegexFromLiteral@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::RegexFromLiteral@.body: The function builds a regex‑escaped copy of the input string: it scans each character, prefixes any regex metacharacter ( [ ] ( ) \ . * + ? - ^ $ ) with a backslash, then appends either the lower‑cased version of that character (on Windows/Apple) or the original character otherwise.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::SetName@k_ZN19cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::SetName@k_ZN19cmF.body: It clears any existing names and then inserts the supplied string into the helper’s internal name collection.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::Validate@k_ZNK19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::Validate@k_ZNK19c.body: This method simply forwards the supplied path to its internal `FindBase` component and returns that component’s validation result.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::cmFindLibraryHelp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::cmFindLibraryHelp.body: The constructor initializes the helper by retrieving the global generator and setting up debugging.
