It gathers the configured prefix and suffix lists, builds regex strings from those lists, and stores them in member lists. Finally, it checks the project’s global property to decide whether OpenBSD‑style version comparisons are enabled.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::cmFindLibraryHelp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::cmFindLibraryHelp.body: The function creates a `cmFindLibraryHelper` instance from an existing helper passed by rvalue reference, enabling the calling code to reuse the helper’s internal state for subsequent library‑search operations.

@lcmFindLibraryHelper::cmFindLibraryHelp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindLibraryHelper::cmFindLibraryHelp.body: The helper gathers a list of candidate paths for each requested library, normalising names and applying any version or architecture constraints, then probes those paths in search order until a match is found or the search exhausts. If a matching file is located it returns its full path; otherwise it reports failure so the caller can handle the absence.

@lcmFindNot@k_Z9cmFindNotRKT_RKT0_@f./So.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindNot@k_Z9cmFindNotRKT_RKT0_@f./So.body: The function returns an iterator pointing to the first element in the supplied range that is not equal to the value `t`. It works for any range type that offers a `const_iterator`.

@lcmFindPath@k_Z10cmFindPathRKiR17cmExec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPath@k_Z10cmFindPathRKiR17cmExec.body: The function forwards a list of arguments to `cmFindPathCommand` and returns the outcome of its `InitialPass` call, propagating the given execution status object.

@lcmFindPathCommand::FindFrameworkHeader.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::FindFrameworkHeader.body: Iterates over every stored header name and each search path, calling `FindHeaderInFramework`. If that call returns a non‑empty string, the function immediately returns that path; otherwise it continues until all combinations are exhausted, eventually returning an empty string.

@lcmFindPathCommand::FindHeader@k_ZN17cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::FindHeader@k_ZN17cm.body:
This method searches for an appropriate header file:  
• It first tries framework‑only or framework‑first mode by calling `FindFrameworkHeader`.  
• If that fails and normal searching is allowed, it falls back to `FindNormalHeader`.  
• If still none found and a final “last‑framework” flag is set, it attempts `FindFrameworkHeader` again.  
• The resulting string (empty if not found) is returned.

@lcmFindPathCommand::FindHeaderInFramewo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::FindHeaderInFramewo.body: It parses the requested file name to isolate a possible framework component, then probes that framework’s /Headers directory for a matching header file. If found, it returns that path (optionally prefixed with the framework name depending on IncludeFileInPath) and logs the discovery via the supplied debug object; if no match is found it falls back to a glob search across all framework directories under dir, returning the first match or an empty string if none exist.

@lcmFindPathCommand::FindNormalHeader@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::FindNormalHeader@k_.body: The function iterates through each header name in `Names` against every directory in `SearchPaths`, concatenating them with `cmStrCat`. For each candidate path it checks that the file exists and passes a custom `Validate` test; when a match is found it records the success via `debug.FoundAt` and returns either the full file path (if `IncludeFileInPath` is true) or just the directory. If no match succeeds, it returns an empty string.

@lcmFindPathCommand::InitialPass@k_ZN17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::InitialPass@k_ZN17c.body: The function first assigns a default path value, then parses the supplied arguments. If parsing fails it exits early. It determines whether debug mode should be enabled based on a variable name, and if the target has already been defined it normalises and returns success. Otherwise it resolves the header’s location, records that result, and signals success.

@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.body:
The constructor of `cmFindPathCommand` forwards the command name and status to its base class, then initializes a handful of member variables:  
- `EnvironmentPath` is set to the literal `"INCLUDE"`.  
- `IncludeFileInPath` is set to `false`.  
- `VariableDocumentation` records a generic description of the variable.  
- `VariableType` is assigned the enum value `cmStateEnums::PATH`.  

No special logic or side‑effects appear in this constructor.

@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.body: The function performs the actual path lookup: it parses the supplied path specifier, walks the search roots (including environment‑derived directories), resolves any relative fragments, and returns the first matching absolute path (or signals failure if none is found).

@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied status to its base class, initializing the command named “find_path”.

@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.body: The `cmFindPathCommand` constructor initializes a path‑search command in CMake’s command system. It registers the command with the command registry, parses the supplied arguments to determine the target directory and any optional patterns, and creates a `cmFindPath` object that will execute the search when the command is executed.

@lcmFindPathCommand::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.body: The operator= overload copies the contents of another cmFindPathCommand into the current instance, then returns a reference to the modified object. It enables chaining assignments while preserving the internal state of the command.

@lcmFindPathCommand::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.body: The assignment operator copies all member data from a source instance into the current object, returning a reference to the left‑hand side so that chains of assignment remain valid.

@lcmFindPathCommand::~cmFindPathCommand@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::~cmFindPathCommand@.body: The function `~cmFindPathCommand` implements the runtime command that searches for a path between two nodes (or a node and a target) in the graph managed by `cmFindBase`. It parses the supplied arguments, invokes the underlying path‑finding algorithm, and returns the result set to the caller.

@lcmFindProgram@k_Z13cmFindProgramRKiR17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgram@k_Z13cmFindProgramRKiR17.body: It receives a list of argument strings and a status object, then invokes the `InitialPass` routine on the command returned by `cmFindProgramCommand`. The result of that call (a boolean) is returned directly by `cmFindProgram`.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindAppBundle@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindAppBundle@k_.body: The routine loops through each name in its internal list, appends “.app” to form a candidate directory name, and queries the system for that directory under the configured search paths. When such a directory is located, it extracts the executable path inside the bundle and returns that path in a collapsed form. If no matching bundle is discovered in any of the paths, it returns an empty string.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindNormalProgra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindNormalProgra.body:
The method simply returns the result of one of two helper functions.  
If the member flag `NamesPerDir` is set, it delegates to `FindNormalProgramNamesPerDir()`, otherwise it calls `FindNormalProgramDirsPerName()`.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindNormalProgra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindNormalProgra.body: The function iterates through the configured `Names`. For each name it configures a helper object with that name, checks if the name string already contains a directory separator (a “compound” name). If so, it returns the best‑matched path immediately. If not, it walks through every directory listed in `SearchPaths`, calling the helper’s `CheckDirectory` for each. On the first directory that matches, the function returns that directory’s path. If no match is found after all names and directories have been examined, the function returns an empty string to signal failure.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindNormalProgra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindNormalProgra.body: It iterates over each supplied name, registering them with a helper that scans the configured search directories. When a helper finds a directory containing one of the names, the method immediately returns that path; if none match, an empty string is returned.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindProgram@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::FindProgram@k_ZN.body: The function returns a program‑path string. It first attempts to find an app bundle if either the “first” or “only” search flags are set. If that fails and the “only” flag isn’t set, it falls back to a normal search. Finally, if still empty and the “last” flag is on, it retries the bundle search. The resulting string (or an empty string if nothing is found) is returned.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::GetBundleExecuta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::GetBundleExecuta.body: Retrieves the executable’s file URL inside a bundle by creating CF strings, URLs, and a bundle reference from the supplied path, copying the executable URL, converting that URL to a filesystem path string, and releasing all CoreFoundation objects before returning the resulting string (empty if the URL cannot be resolved).

@lcmFindProgramCommand::InitialPass@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::InitialPass@k_ZN.body: It sets the internal path name to “PROGRAM”, parses the supplied arguments, enables debug mode based on the variable name, and if the program was already defined it normalises the stored result; otherwise it performs a fresh FindProgram(), stores that result, and returns true.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::cmFindProgramCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::cmFindProgramCom.body: The function is a move‑constructor that takes an rvalue reference to an existing `cmFindProgramCommand` instance and creates a new command object from it, transferring any internal state (like command arguments, flags, or search paths) without copying heavy resources. This allows callers to efficiently replace or re‑initialize a command object in place while preserving its configuration.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::cmFindProgramCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::cmFindProgramCom.body: Creates a find‑program command that stores whether names can be searched per directory, records the documentation string and type (file path), and then chooses which registry view to probe on Windows: if the CMP0134 policy is still old‑style, the code selects Reg64_32 or Reg32_64 according to the size‑of‑void value; otherwise it uses both views.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::cmFindProgramCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::cmFindProgramCom.body: The function receives a `cmFindProgramCommand` instance, runs the internal lookup logic defined in `cmFindProgramCommand::Find()`, and returns a populated result object containing the resolved program path and any diagnostic information. It orchestrates the lookup by consulting the configured search paths, handling any defaults or fall‑back rules, and surfaces errors only when the lookup fails to satisfy the caller’s request.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::operator=@k_ZN20.body: The assignment‑operator of `cmFindProgramCommand` takes another `cmFindProgramCommand` (or a compatible temporary) and copies its internal state into the current instance, returning a reference to that instance so calls can be chained. It essentially implements a copy‑assignment that preserves the base‑class parts and the command‑specific data needed for executing the `find‑program` operation.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::operator=@k_ZN20.body: The assignment operator performs a deep copy of all internal fields from the source object to the target, including re‑initializing any internal caches or state flags that the base class or derived members depend on, then returns a reference to the updated instance.

@lcmFindProgramCommand::~cmFindProgramCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramCommand::~cmFindProgramCo.body: The function implements the command‑search logic of the framework: it walks the internal program registry, applies any supplied filters, and returns the matching command object. It plugs into the base “find” workflow, handling errors and caching results as appropriate.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::AddName@k_ZN19cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::AddName@k_ZN19cmF.body: Adds the supplied string to the instance’s internal collection of names for later use.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckCompoundName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckCompoundName.body: The lambda checks whether the supplied file name string includes a directory separator; if it does, it delegates to `CheckDirectoryForName` to verify that path is acceptable under the current directory context.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckCompoundName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckCompoundName.body: This function iterates over every entry in the Names collection; for each string it verifies whether the string contains a directory separator (`’/’`). If it does, the function invokes CheckDirectoryForName with that string, and returns true as soon as any such invocation succeeds. If none of the names satisfy these conditions, the function returns false.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectory::[.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectory::[.body: This `operator()` acts as a lightweight validator: it receives a string reference, performs a quick check (e.g., pattern matching, flag verification, or simple rule enforcement), and returns a `bool` indicating success or failure. Its main role is to provide a quick, read‑only gatekeeper for higher‑level logic that consumes the string without mutating any internal state.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectory::[.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectory::[.body: Checks if the name contains a directory separator and, if so, forwards the check to `CheckDirectoryForName` using the current context.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectory@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectory@k_.body: The function iterates over the internal collection `Names` and returns `true` if at least one element satisfies the condition defined in the lambda. The lambda captures the current object (`this`) and the given `path` and invokes `CheckDirectoryForName` for each name. If any invocation returns `true`, the function immediately returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectoryFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectoryFor.body: The lambda concatenates `name` with a suffix (`ext`), collapses the resulting path, checks if the file exists, logs the outcome, stores the found path if present, and returns a boolean indicating success.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectoryFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::CheckDirectoryFor.body: The function iterates over a stored list of extensions, appending each to the supplied base name; for each such name it normalises the path, verifies the file’s existence with `FileIsValid`, logs the outcome through the `DebugSearches` helper, and on success records the first matching path in `BestPath` before returning `true` – otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::FileIsExecutableC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::FileIsExecutableC.body: The function checks whether a given file satisfies the executability conditions defined by the CMP0109 policy. It returns true when the file exists and meets the required executable criteria for the current policy, emitting a warning if the file’s executability status does not match the policy expectations.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::FileIsValid@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::FileIsValid@k_ZNK.body: The `FileIsValid` method verifies a file’s suitability in three steps: first it checks whether the file is executable via an internal helper; if that fails, the method immediately rejects it. On Windows builds it additionally rejects any file that resides under a “/windowsapps/python” path and that, via a symbolic‑link resolution, points to the special `AppInstallerPythonRedirector.exe` target. If neither of those checks triggers, the method defers to the `FindBase->Validate` routine to decide on the file’s validity, returning that outcome.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::SetName@k_ZN19cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::SetName@k_ZN19cmF.body: The method takes a constant reference to a string, clears any previously stored names, and then invokes `AddName` to insert the supplied value. It performs no validation, so passing an empty string simply clears the list and adds an empty entry. If `AddName` throws, `SetName` will propagate that exception, leaving the object in an unchanged state.

@lcmFindProgramHelper::cmFindProgramHelp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindProgramHelper::cmFindProgramHelp.body:
The constructor stores the debug string, the supplied `cmMakefile` and `cmFindBase`, and records the policy status for CMP0109.  
On Windows‑style builds it pushes “.com” and “.exe” into an internal extensions list; otherwise it adds a blank‑extension entry. It then adds an empty‑extension entry to the list. This sets up the helper to search for programs with those extensions when resolving find‑program calls.

@lcmForEachCommand@k_Z16cmForEachCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmForEachCommand@k_Z16cmForEachCommand.body: The routine first verifies that the argument list is non‑empty, then checks for the special keyword “IN”. If found it delegates to a dedicated handler; otherwise it creates a function blocker. When a “RANGE” clause appears it parses optional start, stop and step values, validates the range, reserves the correct number of argument slots, and fills them with sequentially generated string values. On success it registers the blocker in the makefile and reports success; on any error it reports the failure via the status object.

@lcmFortranCompiler::cmFortranCompiler@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranCompiler::cmFortranCompiler@k.body: The `cmFortranCompiler()` function serves as the entry point for invoking the Fortran compiler pipeline. It sets up the necessary environment (e.g., paths, flags), triggers the compiler invocation, captures any build‑time diagnostics, and returns a status or artifact indicating the success or failure of the compilation step.

@lcmFortranLexer_GetCurrentBuffer@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranLexer_GetCurrentBuffer@k_Z31c.body: The function `cmFortranLexer_GetCurrentBuffer` extracts and returns the current input buffer that the Flex‑generated scanner is reading from. It casts the generic scanner pointer to the internal `yyguts_t` structure and uses the `YY_CURRENT_BUFFER` macro to expose the current buffer handle, which callers can then use to examine or modify the lexer’s input stream.

@lcmFortranParser_Error@k_Z21cmFortranPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_Error@k_Z21cmFortranPa.body: Sets the parser’s `Error` field to the supplied message; if the message pointer is null, it assigns the string “unknown error”.

@lcmFortranParser_FilePop@k_Z23cmFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_FilePop@k_Z23cmFortran.body: The function removes the most‑recently‑opened file from the parser’s internal stack, closes that file descriptor, and restores the lexer to the preceding input buffer so that further lexical analysis resumes with the previous file. It cleans up the buffer associated with the popped file and switches the scanner to the buffer of the file now at the top of the stack.

@lcmFortranParser_FilePush@k_Z24cmFortra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_FilePush@k_Z24cmFortra.body: The routine opens the supplied file, captures the current lexer buffer state, constructs a `cmFortranFile` object with that state and the file’s directory, creates a fresh lexer buffer, switches the lexer to it, and pushes the new file onto the parser’s file stack, returning `true` on success and `false` if the file cannot be opened.

@lcmFortranParser_GetInInterface@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_GetInInterface@k_Z30cm.body: This accessor simply exposes the parser’s current interface flag—indicating whether the parser is presently parsing an interface section. The function performs no side‑effects beyond reading the stored flag, and it assumes the parser object is valid.

@lcmFortranParser_GetInPPFalseBranch@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_GetInPPFalseBranch@k_Z.body: Checks whether the Fortran parser is currently inside an inactive pre‑processor branch.

@lcmFortranParser_GetOldStartcond@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_GetOldStartcond@k_Z31c.body: Retrieves the current value of `OldStartcond` stored in the `cmFortranParser` instance, returning it directly without side‑effects.

@lcmFortranParser_Input@k_Z21cmFortranPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_Input@k_Z21cmFortranPa.body: The function pulls up to `bufferSize` bytes from the file that is at the top of the parser’s file stack. It records whether the last byte read is a newline. If the file ends without a newline, it injects one into the buffer so the stream always terminates with a newline. Finally it returns how many bytes were actually read.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleDefine@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleDefine@k_Z26cmFort.body: If the current pre‑processor context is active (i.e. not inside a branch that evaluates to false), the routine records the supplied macro name in the parser’s collection of known macro definitions.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleElif@k_Z24cmFortra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleElif@k_Z24cmFortra.body: When a pending skip stack entry is active and we’re still in an otherwise‑true branch, it flips the parser into a false‑branch state.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleElse@k_Z24cmFortra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleElse@k_Z24cmFortra.body: The routine keeps the parser’s flag for “in a false‑branch” in sync with a helper stack that tracks whether a skipped block should be closed. If a false branch is already active it returns immediately; otherwise it looks at the top of the stack—setting the flag to 1 when that element is true, or to 0 when it is false.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleEndif@k_Z25cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleEndif@k_Z25cmFortr.body: When a pre‑processor #endif is encountered, the routine pops any pending “skip‑to‑end” entry that was queued, then decrements the counter that tracks nested false branches so that the parser’s state is correctly restored for the next source token.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleIf@k_Z22cmFortranP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleIf@k_Z22cmFortranP.body: The routine records the start of a new preprocessor branch by pushing a false flag onto the parser’s SkipToEnd stack, effectively marking that code following a `#if` (or `#elif`, `#ifdef`, etc.) must be skipped until the matching `#endif` is reached.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleIfdef@k_Z25cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleIfdef@k_Z25cmFortr.body: The routine pushes a flag onto the `SkipToEnd` stack and updates the `InPPFalseBranch` counter based on whether the current macro is already defined: if the parser is already in a false branch, it increments the counter; otherwise, if the macro hasn’t been seen before, it sets the counter to 1; otherwise it marks the top of the stack as true.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleIfndef@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleIfndef@k_Z26cmFort.body: When an `#ifndef` is encountered, the routine pushes a flag onto the `SkipToEnd` stack to remember that the current branch should be skipped. If the parser is already in a false branch it simply increments a counter; otherwise it checks whether the macro is already defined. If it is, it sets the flag to indicate the current block is false; if not, it marks that branch to be ignored.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleInclude@k_Z27cmFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleInclude@k_Z27cmFor.body: When the parser sees an `INCLUDE` directive it first verifies that it isn’t in a skipped pre‑processor branch. It then uses the current source directory (the top of the `FileStack`) as the first search location. A helper searches for a file matching the requested name; if found it records the file in the `Includes` set and immediately pushes that file onto the parsing stack so that file’s contents are parsed inline. If the file can’t be located, the routine simply exits without reporting an error.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleLineDirective@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleLineDirective@k_Z3.body: Parses “#line” directives that specify a source file, normalizes path separators to Unix style, skips built‑in references, and records the referenced file in the parser’s include set if the file exists.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleModule@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleModule@k_Z26cmFort.body: The function checks whether the parser is currently inside a pre‑processor false branch or an interface section. If neither condition applies, it normalizes the supplied module name to lower‑case, turns it into a `ModuleName` instance via `parser->ModName`, and inserts this name into the parser’s `Info.Provides` set so that the module becomes available for subsequent resolution.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleSubmodule@k_Z29cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleSubmodule@k_Z29cmF.body: The routine validates that the current parser state is not in a false‑branch of a pre‑processor conditional. It then normalises the supplied identifiers to lower‑case strings and records the fact that the module `module_name` is required and that the submodule `submodule_name` is provided. It relies on the helper `cmSystemTools::LowerCase` to perform the case conversion and finally updates the parser’s `Info.Requires` and `Info.Provides` sets with the corresponding names.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleSubmoduleNested@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleSubmoduleNested@k_.body: The routine first aborts if the current pre‑processor state is false. It then normalises the three supplied identifiers to lower‑case strings, constructs the corresponding module names and registers them in the parser’s requirement/availability sets: the supplied submodule becomes a required module, while the nested sub‑module becomes an available module for subsequent rules.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleUndef@k_Z25cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleUndef@k_Z25cmFortr.body: The function removes a macro definition from the parser’s internal set `PPDefinitions` when the parser is not inside a false‑branch of a preprocessor `#if` chain. It first checks that the parser is not currently in a false branch (`InPPFalseBranch` is false). If the macro exists in the set, the function erases the entry from the set.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleUse@k_Z23cmFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleUse@k_Z23cmFortran.body: When a Fortran module is used, this routine first verifies that the current parse state is not inside a false PP branch. It then normalises the module name to lower‑case and records the module as a required dependency by inserting it into the parser’s `Info.Requires` set.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleUseIntrinsic@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleUseIntrinsic@k_Z32.body: The function checks whether the current preprocessor context allows processing, converts the supplied intrinsic module name to lower‑case, and records that module in the parser’s intrinsic set for later resolution.

@lcmFortranParser_SetInInterface@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_SetInInterface@k_Z30cm.body: Checks whether the parser is in a false‑branch and, if not, writes the supplied value to its `InInterface` flag.

@lcmFortranParser_SetInPPFalseBranch@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_SetInPPFalseBranch@k_Z.body: The function records whether the parser is currently inside a false pre‑processor branch, updating an internal flag that later parsing steps consult to decide whether to ignore or skip tokens until the branch ends.

@lcmFortranParser_SetOldStartcond@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_SetOldStartcond@k_Z31c.body: The function assigns the supplied integer to the `OldStartcond` member of the `cmFortranParser` instance, thereby updating the parser’s stored start‑condition value.

@lcmFortranParser_StringAppend@k_Z28cmFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_StringAppend@k_Z28cmFo.body: Appends the given character to the parser's TokenString member.

@lcmFortranParser_StringEnd@k_Z25cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_StringEnd@k_Z25cmFortr.body: The function simply returns a pointer to the internal string buffer that holds the current token text. It dereferences the `TokenString` member of the parser and exposes its underlying C‑style string via `c_str()`. This gives callers direct access to the token data without copying or copying overhead.

@lcmFortranParser_StringStart@k_Z27cmFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_StringStart@k_Z27cmFor.body: The routine simply clears the internal string buffer that holds the current token being built, so that the parser starts fresh whenever a new string token is expected.

@lcmFortranParser_s::FindIncludeFile@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::FindIncludeFile@k_Z.body: The routine first checks whether the supplied name is already an absolute path; if so, it simply verifies that file exists and returns it. If not, it constructs a candidate path relative to the supplied directory and tests that path. Failing that, it walks through the parser’s include‑path list, appending each entry with the file name until it finds an existing file. If any of those attempts succeeds, the full path is assigned to `fileName` and the function returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmFortranParser_s::ModName@k_ZNK17cmFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::ModName@k_ZNK17cmFo.body: The member function simply concatenates the passed‑in string with the literal “.mod” and returns the result. It is marked `const`, so it promises not to modify the object’s state, and it returns a freshly‑created `std::string`.

@lcmFortranParser_s::SModName@k_ZNK17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::SModName@k_ZNK17cmF.body: The function produces a file‑style name by attaching the given `sub_name` to the base `mod_name` using the separator stored in the compiler. If the compiler’s separator string is empty, the returned string consists of `sub_name` followed by the extension (default “.mod”). Otherwise, it joins `mod_name`, the separator, and `sub_name`, then appends the extension. If the compiler has no explicit extension string, the default “.mod” is used.

@lcmFortranParser_s::cmFortranParser_s@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::cmFortranParser_s@k.body: Initializes member variables, sets flags, configures the lexical scanner, and creates a dummy buffer for fallback.

@lcmFortranParser_s::~cmFortranParser_s@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::~cmFortranParser_s@.body: The destructor frees the internal scanner by invoking cmFortran_yylex_destroy on this‑>Scanner.

@lcmFortranSourceInfo::cmFortranSourceIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranSourceInfo::cmFortranSourceIn.body: This public function retrieves metadata about Fortran source code—returning information such as the file path, line numbers, and optional context needed for diagnostics.

@lcmFortran_yy_create_buffer@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_create_buffer@k_Z26cmFort.body: Creates a new buffer structure, allocates the required memory for the buffer object and its character array (adding space for the two terminator bytes), initializes the buffer fields, and returns the populated object. It fails with a fatal error if any allocation or initialization step fails.

@lcmFortran_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z26cmFort.body: The routine first checks whether the supplied buffer pointer is non‑null, then, if this buffer is the one currently in use (`YY_CURRENT_BUFFER`), clears that global reference. It releases the buffer’s own data buffer when the flag `yy_is_our_buffer` is set, and finally frees the buffer structure itself. The logic assumes that only buffers owned by the scanner are freed, and that the current‑buffer flag is cleared before the final `yyfree`.

@lcmFortran_yy_flush_buffer@k_Z25cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_flush_buffer@k_Z25cmFortr.body: The routine clears a lexical buffer: it resets the character count to zero, writes two sentinel end‑of‑buffer markers into the buffer array, and resets internal pointers and flags (`yy_buf_pos`, `yy_at_bol`, and `yy_buffer_status`). If the buffer being flushed is the current active buffer, it re‑initialises the scan state by calling `yy_load_buffer_state`.

@lcmFortran_yy_init_buffer@k_ZL24cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_init_buffer@k_ZL24cmFortr.body: The function sets up a scan buffer: it receives a buffer state struct, a FILE pointer, and a scanner context; it copies the file descriptor into the buffer, zeroes its counters, assigns the stream, and marks the buffer as ready for token extraction.

@lcmFortran_yy_init_buffer@k_ZL24cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_init_buffer@k_ZL24cmFortr.body: The routine resets an existing buffer state for a new input source. It flushes any pending data, assigns the new FILE pointer, clears the fill‑flag, and resets line/column counters unless the buffer is already the current one. The routine also tags the buffer as interactive only if the associated file descriptor is a terminal. Finally, it preserves the caller’s errno value across the operation.

@lcmFortran_yy_load_buffer_state@k_ZL30c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_load_buffer_state@k_ZL30c.body: The function restores a `yyguts_t` instance from the current buffer context: it copies the buffer size (`yy_n_chars`), updates the text pointer chain (`yytext_ptr` and `yy_c_buf_p`), stores the active input stream, and caches the next character in `yy_hold_char`. This re‑establishes the scanner’s state after a buffer switch.

@lcmFortran_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z24cmFortra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z24cmFortra.body: The function checks that the supplied buffer has at least two EOB markers at the end; if that holds it allocates a `yy_buffer_state` struct, initializes its fields (size, position, flags such as “is_interactive” and “at_bol”), then calls `yy_switch_to_buffer` to make the scanner use this newly prepared buffer.

@lcmFortran_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z24cmFortra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z24cmFortra.body: The function wraps a raw memory area into a scanner‑ready buffer: it takes a base pointer and size, associates that memory with the supplied scanner context, and returns a `YY_BUFFER_STATE` structure that the lexer will use to read tokens from that region.

@lcmFortran_yy_scan_bytes@k_Z23cmFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_scan_bytes@k_Z23cmFortran.body: The routine allocates a temporary buffer sized for the supplied byte slice plus a pair of end‑of‑buffer markers, copies the data into it, appends the markers, then passes that buffer to the underlying scanner routine. After scanning, it tags the buffer as an internal one so it can be freed immediately after use and returns the scanning result.

@lcmFortran_yy_scan_string@k_Z24cmFortra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_scan_string@k_Z24cmFortra.body: The routine takes a C‑string and a scanner handle, computes the string’s byte count with `strlen`, and forwards that data to the generic `yy_scan_bytes` routine, returning the buffer state it produces.

@lcmFortran_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z29cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z29cmF.body: This routine updates the scanner’s active buffer. It first verifies that the buffer stack is initialized, then exits immediately if the requested buffer is already current. Otherwise, it flushes any buffered data from the old buffer, writes the pending position and character count back into the global state, switches the internal buffer pointer to the new buffer, restores the new buffer’s state, and finally marks that a buffer transition occurred for end‑of‑file handling.

@lcmFortran_yyalloc@k_Z17cmFortran_yyall.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyalloc@k_Z17cmFortran_yyall.body: The routine casts the supplied scanner handle to a `yyguts_t` pointer, ignores that pointer, and then simply returns a freshly allocated block of the requested size.

@lcmFortran_yyalloc@k_Z17cmFortran_yyall.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyalloc@k_Z17cmFortran_yyall.body: The function in `cmFortran_yyalloc` is a thin wrapper that takes a requested allocation size and a scanner context (`yyscan_t`) and returns a raw pointer (`void *`). Internally it performs the allocation (likely via `malloc` or a custom allocator) and sets up the returned memory according to the Fortran scanner’s expectations. It is used wherever a new chunk of memory is needed for the lexer/ parser to hold temporary tokens or symbol tables, ensuring the allocation is consistent with the scanner’s state and size bookkeeping.

@lcmFortran_yyensure_buffer_stack@k_ZL31.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyensure_buffer_stack@k_ZL31.body: The routine first checks whether the buffer stack has been allocated; if not, it allocates space for two entries, zeroes the memory and sets the maximum size to that value. When a push would exceed the current capacity, it expands the allocation by eight slots, zeroes the newly added region, and updates the maximum size. If any allocation fails, it aborts with a fatal error.

@lcmFortran_yyfree@k_Z16cmFortran_yyfree.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyfree@k_Z16cmFortran_yyfree.body: The function receives a pointer and a scanner context, casts the context to a `yyguts_t` structure (though the cast is unused), and then calls the standard `free` routine on the supplied pointer after converting it to a `char*`.

@lcmFortran_yyget_column@k_Z22cmFortran_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyget_column@k_Z22cmFortran_.body: The function `yyget_column` retrieves the current column index of the lexer’s internal buffer. It first casts the generic `yyscanner` pointer to the concrete lexer structure, then checks whether the global buffer pointer is valid; if not, it returns `0` as a sentinel. Otherwise it simply returns the stored `yycolumn` value, which tracks the column number of the next token.

@lcmFortran_yyget_debug@k_Z21cmFortran_y.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyget_debug@k_Z21cmFortran_y.body: The routine simply extracts the internal lexer structure from the opaque `yyscan_t` handle and returns the current debug‑enable flag (`yy_flex_debug`). In effect, it reports whether debugging mode is currently on for that particular scanner instance.

@lcmFortran_yyget_extra@k_Z21cmFortran_y.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyget_extra@k_Z21cmFortran_y.body: The function casts the generic `yyscanner` pointer to its concrete `yyguts_t` implementation and returns the stored `yyextra` field that holds any auxiliary data required by the parser.

@lcmFortran_yyget_in@k_Z18cmFortran_yyge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyget_in@k_Z18cmFortran_yyge.body: The function casts the `yyscanner` argument to a `struct yyguts_t *` and returns the `yyin` member of that structure, which is the `FILE*` associated with that scanner.

@lcmFortran_yyget_leng@k_Z20cmFortran_yy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyget_leng@k_Z20cmFortran_yy.body: The routine simply casts the supplied scanner pointer to its internal `ygut_t` type and returns the value stored in that structure’s `leng` member.

@lcmFortran_yyget_lineno@k_Z22cmFortran_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyget_lineno@k_Z22cmFortran_.body: The function retrieves the current line number from the scanner’s context. It first verifies that the current buffer exists; if it’s nil it returns 0. Otherwise it returns the global line counter (`yylineno`) that tracks the current line being scanned.

@lcmFortran_yyget_out@k_Z19cmFortran_yyg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyget_out@k_Z19cmFortran_yyg.body: Returns the `yyout` member of the internal `yyguts_t` structure that backs the scanner. It simply casts the opaque `yyscanner` argument to the concrete struct type and returns the stored `FILE*` that represents the current output stream.

@lcmFortran_yyget_text@k_Z20cmFortran_yy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyget_text@k_Z20cmFortran_yy.body: The routine casts the opaque `yyscanner` handle to its internal `yguts_t` structure and returns the `yytext` member, which holds the raw text for the current token.

@lcmFortran_yylex@k_Z15cmFortran_yylexP1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yylex@k_Z15cmFortran_yylexP1.body: The routine drives the Fortran lexer. It lazily initializes the scanner’s buffers, walks an FSM over the input stream, and, depending on the current state, emits one of several token kinds (e.g., string, CPP directive, or comment tokens). When it reaches a buffer boundary or end‑of‑file it performs a buffer‑switch or terminates scanning, handling special cases such as line‑continuations or fixed‑format blocks before returning the next token.

@lcmFortran_yylex_destroy@k_Z23cmFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yylex_destroy@k_Z23cmFortran.body: The function clears all scanner‑level resources: it unwinds the internal buffer stack, frees that stack and any start‑condition stack, resets global flags, re‑initializes shared globals, and finally releases the scanner structure itself.

@lcmFortran_yylex_init@k_Z20cmFortran_yy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yylex_init@k_Z20cmFortran_yy.body: The function validates a pointer, allocates memory for the global structure, zeroes that memory, and then delegates initialization to yy_init_globals(), reporting errors via errno.

@lcmFortran_yylex_init_extra@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yylex_init_extra@k_Z26cmFort.body: Allocates a yyguts_t instance, attaches it to the supplied globals pointer, performs zero‑initialization with a specific sentinel pattern, and finally invokes yy_init_globals to complete setup. It validates input pointer and cleans up on allocation failure.

@lcmFortran_yyparse@k_Z17cmFortran_yypar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyparse@k_Z17cmFortran_yypar.body: This routine drives the generated parser generated by Bison for the Fortran language. It repeatedly reads look‑ahead tokens, pushes them onto a state/value stack, and uses the tables (`yypact`, `yytable`, `yydefact`, `yydefgoto`) to decide whether to shift or reduce. When a rule matches it executes the corresponding semantic action (such as `RuleUse`, `RuleInclude`, etc.), then pops the needed symbols, updates the current state and pushes the semantic result back onto the stack. The code includes error‑recovery logic that discards offending tokens, resets the look‑ahead, and reports syntax errors. It also manages dynamic reallocation of the stacks and the error message buffer when memory runs low. The procedure returns 0 on success, 1 on abort, or 2 on memory exhaustion.

@lcmFortran_yypop_buffer_state@k_Z28cmFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yypop_buffer_state@k_Z28cmFo.body: The routine clears the current buffer in the `yyguts_t` context: it deletes the active buffer, resets the `YY_CURRENT_BUFFER` pointer, and if the buffer stack is non‑empty it decrements the stack pointer. If a buffer still exists after this cleanup, the function reloads its state and marks a buffer‑switch‑on‑EOF event in the context.

@lcmFortran_yypush_buffer_state@k_Z29cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yypush_buffer_state@k_Z29cmF.body: The function takes a buffer descriptor and a scanner instance, verifies the buffer is valid, ensures the internal buffer‑stack is initialized, then it stores the current buffer’s state (position and count) into the stack frame, replaces the current buffer with the new one, and finally loads the new buffer’s state into the scanner. This effectively pushes the new buffer onto the buffer stack, preserving the previous buffer’s context for later restoration.

@lcmFortran_yyrealloc@k_Z19cmFortran_yyr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyrealloc@k_Z19cmFortran_yyr.body: The routine simply forwards the request to the system allocator: it casts the supplied scanner to a local struct, then returns the result of `realloc(ptr, size)`. The cast to `char*` is a workaround that works with both char‑pointer and void‑pointer implementations of the pointer type; the function itself does nothing more than delegating the standard `realloc` call.

@lcmFortran_yyrealloc@k_Z19cmFortran_yyr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyrealloc@k_Z19cmFortran_yyr.body: The function `yyrealloc` is a thin wrapper around the standard reallocation routine used by the Fortran lexer. It accepts a pointer to an existing allocation, the desired new size (`yy_size_t`), and a scanner context (`yyscan_t`). The implementation typically performs a size‑checked `malloc` or `realloc` call, copies the old contents into the new block (often via `memcpy`), frees the old buffer, and returns the newly allocated pointer. The scanner parameter is used to propagate state or debugging info during the allocation. The function is a small, self‑contained helper for expanding buffers safely within the lexer’s memory‑management system.

@lcmFortran_yyrestart@k_Z19cmFortran_yyr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyrestart@k_Z19cmFortran_yyr.body: Re‑starts the lexer by ensuring a current buffer exists (creating one if needed), then re‑initialising that buffer with the supplied file and restoring the buffer state.

@lcmFortran_yyset_column@k_Z22cmFortran_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyset_column@k_Z22cmFortran_.body: Ensures that the scanner has a current input buffer; if one exists, it records the requested column number in the global column counter used for token position tracking.

@lcmFortran_yyset_debug@k_Z21cmFortran_y.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyset_debug@k_Z21cmFortran_y.body: The function assigns the provided `_bdebug` value to the global `yy_flex_debug` variable; the cast of the passed scanner to a `yyguts_t*` is performed but never used, so the local pointer `yyg` is effectively unused.

@lcmFortran_yyset_extra@k_Z21cmFortran_y.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyset_extra@k_Z21cmFortran_y.body: The routine simply assigns the supplied user‑defined extra data to the parser’s internal field. It receives the data type and a generic scanner handle, casts that handle to the concrete `yyguts_t` structure, and stores the value in the shared `yyextra` variable. This plumbing keeps the parser’s extra‐data accessible to the rest of the Fortran front‑end.

@lcmFortran_yyset_in@k_Z18cmFortran_yyse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyset_in@k_Z18cmFortran_yyse.body: The function simply assigns the supplied `FILE*` to the global `yyin` used by the scanner. It casts the opaque `yyscan_t` argument to the internal `yyguts_t` structure to reach the `yyin` field and writes the new file pointer into it.

@lcmFortran_yyset_lineno@k_Z22cmFortran_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyset_lineno@k_Z22cmFortran_.body: The function updates the scanner’s current‑line counter. It first verifies that an input buffer is active; if not, it aborts with a fatal error. Once verified, it stores the supplied line number in the global `yylineno` field for use by the lexer.

@lcmFortran_yyset_out@k_Z19cmFortran_yys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyset_out@k_Z19cmFortran_yys.body: The function `yyset_out` assigns the supplied `FILE*` to the global variable `yyout`. It casts the provided scanner to its internal struct type to access `yyg`. This effectively redirects all output of the lexer to the supplied stream.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch@k_ZN.body: The `ArgumentsMatch` method validates that the arguments supplied for a list‑file function match the expectations encoded in the internal state of the caller. It inspects the `cmListFileFunction` instance passed in (`lff`), comparing its constituent parameters—such as arguments, flags, or context identifiers—against the canonical configuration for that function type. If every element aligns, it returns `true`; otherwise, it returns `false`.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName@k_ZN.body: The function returns a `cm::string_view` that represents the name of the terminating command. It is pure virtual, so any derived implementation must supply the concrete string. The method is marked `const`, ensuring that the returned value does not modify any internal state.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::EndCommandSupportsA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::EndCommandSupportsA.body: This virtual function simply signals that an `EndCommand` instance can receive command‑line arguments. It returns `true` to allow any derived command‑processing logic to query this capability without further ado.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::GetStartingContext@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::GetStartingContext@.body: The `GetStartingContext()` member function is a simple accessor: it returns a constant reference to the `StartingContext` member stored in the object. It is marked `const` on both the function and the return type, guaranteeing that the caller cannot modify the returned context. The function body consists only of a single `return` statement that yields that reference.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::IsFunctionBlocked@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::IsFunctionBlocked@k.body: The method increments a depth counter when encountering a start marker, decrements it at a matching end marker, and when the counter reaches zero it validates that the start‑to‑end argument sets match the expectations. If they do not match, it emits a warning. In that case it replays any stored functions. If the function isn’t a block marker it simply queues the function and returns true to indicate that the block hasn’t been closed.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN17cmFunc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN17cmFunc.body: The `Replay` virtual method is expected to take a collection of `cmListFileFunction` objects—each of which represents an operation that was previously recorded—and replay those operations in the order supplied. A concrete implementation must iterate over the supplied vector, invoke the appropriate action for each element, and return `true` only when all operations complete successfully; otherwise `false`. The method is pure virtual, so every subclass that participates in the replay workflow is required to supply its own concrete logic for handling the specific function types in the vector.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::SetStartingContext@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::SetStartingContext@.body: The method assigns the supplied `cmListFileContext` instance to the object’s `StartingContext` member. It accepts the parameter by const reference and performs a direct assignment—no deep copying or validation logic is involved. Callers must ensure that the passed context is correctly initialized before invoking the setter.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::StartCommandName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::StartCommandName@k_.body: The function is a pure virtual accessor that must be implemented by each concrete subclass. It returns a lightweight view into the command‑name string owned by the class, allowing callers to inspect the identifier without incurring a copy. Since the method is `const`, it guarantees that the returned view does not modify internal state. Sub‑classes typically obtain the name from a member string or a static constant, returning a `cm::string_view` that refers to that storage. The contract ensures callers can safely read the name at any point in the object’s lifetime.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.body: The operator= overload performs a shallow copy of the internal block representation from the right‑hand side into the current object and returns a reference to *this so that the assignment can be chained.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::~cmFunctionBlocker@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::~cmFunctionBlocker@.body: This destructor is implicitly declared and will automatically be generated by the compiler unless you explicitly provide an implementation elsewhere. Because it is marked `virtual`, any derived class that implements its own destructor will be invoked correctly when a base‐pointer is deleted. The `= default` clause simply tells the compiler to use the compiler‑generated default implementation – in other words, no custom cleanup is required unless you override it in a derived class.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::addToCurrentP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::addToCurrentP.body: The function checks that there is an existing dependency in the content list, selects the appropriate list (rules or paths) based on the current helper state, and appends the supplied string to that last entry if it exists; otherwise it exits immediately.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::cmGccDepfileL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::cmGccDepfileL.body: The helper reads a GCC‑generated dependency file, pulls out the target and prerequisite paths (skipping comments and whitespace) and feeds them to the lexer so that downstream code can treat each path as a distinct token. It normalises quoting and escapes, and silently drops any malformed lines so that callers receive only clean include tokens.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newDependency.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newDependency.body: The function guards against a failed helper state, switches the helper to a “dependency” state, and then guarantees that the last entry in the content list has a non‑empty path element—creating one if the current list is empty or already ends with a non‑empty string.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newEntry@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newEntry@k_ZN.body: When invoked, `newEntry()` first checks whether the helper is already in the `Rule` state with a non‑empty rule set; if so, it marks the helper as `Failed` and exits immediately. Otherwise it switches to the `Rule` state, pushes a new default content element onto `Content`, and then calls `newRule()` to initialise the new rule.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newRule@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newRule@k_ZN2.body: It accesses the last `Content` element and appends a new rule when either no rules exist or the most‑recent rule is non‑empty, using `emplace_back()` to create a default‑constructed rule.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newRuleOrDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newRuleOrDepe.body: The function inspects the current state; if the helper is in the “Rule” state it invokes the rule‑creation routine, otherwise (and only in that case) it invokes the dependency routine. The logic simply routes to the appropriate helper method based on the current state flag.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::readFile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::readFile@k_ZN.body: Opens the file path given, feeding the stream through a lexer to build internal entries, sanitizes the parsed data, and returns true only if no parsing errors occurred.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::sanitizeConte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::sanitizeConte.body: The method walks through each entry in the internal `Content` container, first eliminating duplicate path strings by sorting and applying `unique`, then pruning any empty entries or normalising Windows‑style drive‑letters (removing an escaped colon). It subsequently discards empty rule strings and finally erases any content items that no longer contain rules.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_create_buffer@k_Z29cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_create_buffer@k_Z29cmG.body: Creates a new `yy_buffer_state` object: it allocates the struct, allocates its character buffer with `size+2` bytes (the extra two for end‑of‑buffer markers), sets the size field, marks the buffer as owned by this routine, calls `yy_init_buffer` to initialise the state, and finally returns the pointer. If any allocation fails it aborts with a fatal error.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z29cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z29cmG.body: The routine validates the buffer pointer, clears the global “current‑buffer” reference when the target buffer is the one in use, releases the character data held in the buffer’s internal buffer, and finally frees the buffer structure itself. It relies on a boolean flag to know whether the buffer belongs to the parser before deallocating the inner buffer, and uses yyfree to perform the actual memory deallocation.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_flush_buffer@k_Z28cmGc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_flush_buffer@k_Z28cmGc.body: The function resets a buffer’s state, clearing its character counter and inserting the two sentinel `YY_END_OF_BUFFER_CHAR` markers that signal the parser that the buffer has been exhausted. It then points the buffer pointers back to the start of this sentinel buffer, marks the buffer as “new”, and if the buffer in question is the current one, it triggers a re‑load via `yy_load_buffer_state`.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z27cmGcc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z27cmGcc.body: The routine prepares the lexer’s internal buffer state for a specific scanner instance. It receives a raw memory block (`base`), its length (`size`), and a scanner handle (`yyscanner`), and returns a `YY_BUFFER_STATE` describing how the lexer should read from that region during tokenization.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_bytes@k_Z26cmGccD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_bytes@k_Z26cmGccD.body: The routine allocates a buffer large enough to hold the supplied bytes plus two sentinel characters, copies the data into that buffer, appends the sentinel markers, and hands off the buffer to the scanner routine, marking the buffer as owned by the caller before returning the resulting scan state.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_string@k_Z27cmGcc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_string@k_Z27cmGcc.body: The routine simply forwards a null‑terminated C string to the underlying byte‑scanning routine. It receives a pointer to the string, computes its length with `strlen`, casts that length to an `int`, and invokes `yy_scan_bytes` with the string, that length, and the scanner context, returning whatever that helper returns.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z32.body: The routine pushes the current buffer to the stack, writes back any buffered characters and state to the previous buffer’s structure, then loads the new buffer’s configuration from the scanner’s context and flags that a buffer transition has occurred. This guarantees that any pending lexical material is flushed before the switch and that the internal flag tracking whether a buffer switch happened during an EOF routine is always set correctly.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyalloc@k_Z20cmGccDepfile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyalloc@k_Z20cmGccDepfile.body: The `yyalloc` function in `cmGccDepfile_yyalloc` is a lightweight allocator used by the lexer to obtain memory for token buffers. It receives a size (`yy_size_t`) and a scanner context (`yyscan_t`) and returns a `void*` pointing to a freshly allocated chunk. Internally it typically forwards to the scanner’s pool allocator, ensuring that the returned block is properly aligned and that the scanner’s bookkeeping is updated. This wrapper allows the lexer to request memory without interacting directly with the global new/delete mechanism, keeping allocation logic isolated from the rest of the lexer implementation.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyfree@k_Z19cmGccDepfile_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyfree@k_Z19cmGccDepfile_.body: The routine is a small helper used by the dependency‑file parsing code to drop a buffer that was allocated earlier. It accepts a raw pointer and a scanner context, casts the context to its internal struct type (though that struct is unused in the body), and then invokes `free` on the pointer after casting it to `char*`. The only non‑trivial aspect is that the function is intentionally thin so that callers simply pass the address of a buffer created by the scanner machinery and the routine cleans it up without any additional bookkeeping.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_column@k_Z25cmGccDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_column@k_Z25cmGccDe.body: The `yyget_column` function simply checks whether a buffer is available via `YY_CURRENT_BUFFER`; if not, it returns `0` immediately. When a buffer is present, it fetches the column index stored in the global `yycolumn` variable and returns that value. This gives callers the current column number for the scanner.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_debug@k_Z24cmGccDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_debug@k_Z24cmGccDep.body: The routine simply translates a scanner handle to its internal `yyguts_t` structure and returns the current value of the global `yy_flex_debug` flag.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_extra@k_Z24cmGccDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_extra@k_Z24cmGccDep.body: It pulls the `yyextra` field out of the private‑state struct that backs a scanner handle, after casting the generic `yyscanner` pointer to the concrete `struct yyguts_t` type.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_in@k_Z21cmGccDepfil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_in@k_Z21cmGccDepfil.body: The function casts the supplied scanner object to its internal structure type and simply returns the stored input `FILE*` field (i.e., `yyg->yyin`).

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_leng@k_Z23cmGccDepf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_leng@k_Z23cmGccDepf.body: It returns the stored length value from the supplied scanner object.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_lineno@k_Z25cmGccDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_lineno@k_Z25cmGccDe.body: This function casts the scanner pointer to its internal guts structure, checks whether a current buffer is active, and if so returns the stored line‑counter; otherwise it yields zero.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_out@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_out@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.body: Retrieves the output FILE* stored in the scanner’s guts structure; it simply casts the supplied scanner pointer to `yyguts_t` and returns the `yyout` member that holds the file where generated output is written.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_text@k_Z23cmGccDepf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_text@k_Z23cmGccDepf.body: The function pulls a pointer to the internal text buffer from a scanner context structure. It casts the generic scanner handle to the concrete `yyguts_t` type, then returns the `yytext` field stored within that structure.

@lcmGccDepfile_yylex@k_Z18cmGccDepfile_y.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yylex@k_Z18cmGccDepfile_y.body: The routine first establishes its internal state and reads characters from the current input buffer. As it reads, it walks a deterministic state machine: each character causes a transition until an accept state is reached. When the machine cannot advance, the routine rewinds to the last accept point and triggers the corresponding action via a switch statement. The actions cover building up the current file name, handling escape sequences, ending a rule or dependency, and signaling end‑of‑buffer or end‑of‑file conditions. When the buffer is exhausted, the routine swaps to the next buffer (or finishes if no further buffer exists) and repeats the state‑machine logic until the entire input stream is consumed.

@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_destroy@k_Z26cmGccD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_destroy@k_Z26cmGccD.body: Cleans up a yylex scanner instance by unwinding its buffer stack, freeing the two internal stacks, resetting the global state machine, and finally releasing the scanner structure itself.

@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_init@k_Z23cmGccDepf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_init@k_Z23cmGccDepf.body: The routine allocates a yyguts_t instance, clears the memory, and then hands the object to yy_init_globals to finish initializing the global scanner state. If the allocation fails or the globals initialization fails, it sets errno and returns 1.

@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_init_extra@k_Z29cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_init_extra@k_Z29cmG.body: The routine registers a user‑supplied “extra” type, allocates a fresh `yguts_t` block, zero‑initialises it, stores the pointer back into the caller’s globals structure, and finally forwards the success flag from `yy_init_globals`. It performs NULL‑pointer checks and returns error codes on allocation failure.

@lcmGccDepfile_yypop_buffer_state@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yypop_buffer_state@k_Z31c.body: The routine discards the active input buffer, erases it from the buffer table, decrements the stack pointer when a buffer remains, and if another buffer is still in the stack, it restores its state and marks that a buffer switch has occurred.

@lcmGccDepfile_yypush_buffer_state@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yypush_buffer_state@k_Z32.body: The routine records a new buffer state onto the current scanner’s stack of buffers. It first verifies the incoming buffer is valid, ensures the buffer stack has been initialized, and then stores the present buffer’s data (current position, character count, and hold‑char pointer) into the stack entry that will become the new “current” buffer. If no buffer was previously active, the stack pointer is left unchanged; otherwise the stack index is advanced and the new state copied in. Finally the routine restores the scanner to the new buffer’s context by re‑loading the buffer’s contents and marking that a switch has just occurred.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyrealloc@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyrealloc@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.body: The routine is a thin wrapper around the usual `realloc` semantics. It receives a raw pointer, a requested size (in bytes), and the current lexer‑context (`yyscan_t`). Internally it calls the underlying allocator to grow or shrink the memory block and returns the new address (or `NULL` on allocation failure). The function is invoked by the lexer during token‑buffer growth and when the parser needs to adjust the internal tables that hold the parsed dependency data.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyrestart@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyrestart@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.body: The routine initializes the scanner’s internal buffer stack. If no current buffer is present, it creates a new buffer of the configured size and pushes it onto the stack. Once the buffer is in place, it assigns it as the active buffer, then re‑establishes the scanner’s internal state from that buffer before returning.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_column@k_Z25cmGccDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_column@k_Z25cmGccDe.body: This helper validates that a buffer is present, then assigns the supplied column number to the scanner’s internal column counter used for diagnostic reporting.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_debug@k_Z24cmGccDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_debug@k_Z24cmGccDep.body: The routine simply stores the supplied flag value into the global debug switch. It casts the supplied scanner object to the internal structure type, fetches the field to write to, and updates `yy_flex_debug`. No further validation or side‑effects occur.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_extra@k_Z24cmGccDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_extra@k_Z24cmGccDep.body: The routine accepts a user‑supplied value of type `YY_EXTRA_TYPE` and a pointer to a scanner object. It casts that pointer to the internal `yyguts_t` structure and writes the supplied value into the global member `yyextra`, making it available for later stages of the processing.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_in@k_Z21cmGccDepfil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_in@k_Z21cmGccDepfil.body: The routine assigns the supplied FILE pointer to the scanner’s internal input handle after extracting the concrete `yuguts_t` structure from the opaque scanner argument.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_lineno@k_Z25cmGccDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_lineno@k_Z25cmGccDe.body: Sets the current line number in the scanner’s context. If no input buffer is active it aborts with a fatal error; otherwise the global `yylineno` variable is overwritten with the supplied value.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_out@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_out@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.body: It assigns the supplied `FILE*` to the global `yyout` variable, switching where future output is written. The scanner parameter is cast to its internal struct type but otherwise unused.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::Close@k_ZN21cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::Close@k_ZN21cmG.body: The `Close()` member turns the stream’s success flag (`Okay`) to true only if no failure is pending (`!fail()`), then shuts the underlying file descriptor, and finally invokes the base class’s cleanup routine to delete or promote the temporary file to its final location.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::Open@k_ZN21cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::Open@k_ZN21cmGe.body: Stores the requested filename, builds a temporary name, opens that file in binary or text mode per the flag, checks for failure (reporting an error unless quiet is requested), and returns a reference to the stream instance.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::SetCompression@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::SetCompression@.body: The `SetCompression` method simply assigns the `compression` flag to the internal `Compress` member of the `cmGeneratedFileStream` object. When invoked, the class’s state is altered so that subsequent read/write operations will honor the new flag. No validation or side‑effects are performed – the assignment is a single‑line state change that other code paths can query or rely on.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::SetCopyIfDiffer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::SetCopyIfDiffer.body: This method simply assigns the supplied boolean to the class’s internal `CopyIfDifferent` flag, toggling whether subsequent operations should perform a copy when a difference is detected.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::SetTempExt@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::SetTempExt@k_ZN.body: The method simply assigns the supplied string to the member variable `TempExt`. No validation or further processing is performed.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::WriteAltEncodin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::WriteAltEncodin.body: It temporarily sets the locale to the requested encoding with a `codecvt`, writes the string bytes, then restores the original locale—if `CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP` is defined it skips that locale machinery and writes directly after a dummy `static_cast`.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::cmGeneratedFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::cmGeneratedFile.body: The constructor sets up the stream’s locale to use a `codecvt` object only when the requested encoding is non‑`None`. If `CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP` is defined, the body is a no‑op stub.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::cmGeneratedFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::cmGeneratedFile.body: The constructor for `cmGeneratedFileStream` opens a temporary file with the supplied name and, if a locale is supplied, applies the appropriate codecvt encoding. If opening fails and the caller did not suppress errors (`quiet` is false), it emits a system‑level error. When the requested encoding is UTF‑8 with a BOM, it writes the standard BOM bytes (`EF BB BF`) before any other data is written.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::~cmGeneratedFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::~cmGeneratedFil.body: The destructor of `cmGeneratedFileStream` performs a cleanup sequence in a tightly‑scoped, single‑step manner: it first verifies the stream’s health, propagates the status to a private helper, flags the stream as closed by inverting its failure flag, and finally releases the underlying temporary file. This sequence guarantees that no residual file handles linger and that any base‑class resource finalisation occurs cleanly.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate@k_ZN21.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate@k_ZN21.body: If the input string contains the required marker it (optionally) creates a profiling record, constructs a `cmCompiledGeneratorExpression` with the input, and invokes its `Evaluate` method to obtain a transformed string; if the marker is absent, the original input is returned unchanged.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Find@k_ZN21cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Find@k_ZN21cmGe.body: The function scans a given string for the pattern `$<` and, only if that pattern is followed somewhere later by a `>` character, returns the index where the opening marker begins; if the pattern or closing marker is missing, it returns the sentinel value `npos`.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::IsValidTargetNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::IsValidTargetNa.body: The method declares a static regular‑expression validator that accepts strings comprising letters, digits, underscores, periods, plus signs, colons, hyphens and colons (used for namespaces). It then returns `true` when the supplied string matches this pattern and `false` otherwise.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Parse@k_ZNK21cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Parse@k_ZNK21cm.body: The function takes an input string, constructs a new cmCompiledGeneratorExpression using the current object’s `CMakeInstance` and `Backtrace`, and returns a `std::unique_ptr` to that newly created instance.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Preprocess@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Preprocess@k_ZN.body: The `Preprocess` function takes an input string and a processing context. According to the context type it either strips all generator expressions from the string, or removes export‑interface expressions (optionally resolving relative paths). If an unsupported context is supplied, the function triggers an assertion failure and returns an empty string.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::ReplaceInstallP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::ReplaceInstallP.body: The function scans a string for every occurrence of the literal `"$<INSTALL_PREFIX>"` and replaces each hit with the supplied replacement string. It iteratively moves past the last replacement point until no more matches exist, ensuring the original content is altered in-place without copying large buffers.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Split@k_ZN21cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Split@k_ZN21cmG.body: The routine scans the supplied string for the pattern “$<” and iteratively extracts each generator‑expression block, accounting for nested “$<…>” constructs. It identifies the boundaries of each block by matching the corresponding closing “>” (while tracking nesting level), stopping once the nesting level returns to zero), then appends the captured fragment (prefixed by any preceding text) to the output vector. The helper `cmExpandList` is invoked to further split any semicolon‑separated sub‑expressions that appear inside a block.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::StartsWithGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::StartsWithGener.body: This function checks if a C‑style string begins with the two‑character sequence “$<”. It first guards against a null pointer, then compares the first two characters for the exact pattern. If both conditions hold, it returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::StartsWithGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::StartsWithGener.body: It returns `true` only when the input string is at least two characters long and its first two characters are exactly `"$<"`.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::StripEmptyListE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::StripEmptyListE.body: The function trims a semicolon‑separated string by iterating through each character, appending only non‑empty segments, and finally removing a trailing semicolon if present. It uses `reserve` to avoid reallocation and skips consecutive semicolons to avoid empty tokens.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::cmGeneratorExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::cmGeneratorExpr.body: The constructor initializes a *cmGeneratorExpression* instance by storing the supplied `cmake` instance in the base class and copying the supplied back‑trace object into its own `Backtrace` member. It does nothing else—no additional logic is performed.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::cmGeneratorExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::cmGeneratorExpr.body: The deleted copy constructor prevents any copy‐instantiation of a `cmGeneratorExpression` object; attempts to copy will fail at compile time.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::operator=@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::operator=@k_ZN2.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents copying an existing `cmGeneratorExpression` into another instance. This guarantees that objects cannot be inadvertently reassigned, preserving the integrity of the expression objects.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::~cmGeneratorExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::~cmGeneratorExp.body: The destructor cleans up any resources owned by the `cmGeneratorExpression` instance, ensuring that allocated memory, file handles or intermediate expression objects are released before the object is destroyed.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Check.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Check.body: The function simply returns the value stored in the member variable `CheckResult`, leaving the object unchanged.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Check.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Check.body: The function walks up the parent chain of a DAG‑node, comparing the current node’s target and property against each ancestor’s. If it encounters an ancestor that matches the same target‑property pair, it returns either `SELF_REFERENCE` (if the matching ancestor is the immediate parent) or `CYCLIC_REFERENCE` otherwise.
