If no match is found, it returns `DAG`.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The function introspects properties flagged as transitive and, via the `CM_FOR_EACH_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY` macro, emits a compile‑time helper that registers a `DEFINE_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY_METHOD` implementation for each such property.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The function collects and normalizes the current UI‑config state into a lightweight options structure that the rest of the UI‑generation logic consumes, without mutating any mutable state.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: It declares a template‑style macro call that expands into a constexpr‑qualified member that defines a property‑like accessor. The macro `CM_FOR_EACH_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY` takes a property name and produces a `constexpr` function returning the corresponding value, essentially providing a compile‑time “getter” for the property.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: Returns true only when the property string retrieved from Top() exactly matches one of the three predefined identifiers.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The `EvaluatingCompileFeatures` routine simply iterates over every property that meets the transitive‑property macro and, for each such property, invokes the corresponding `DEFINE_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY_METHOD` block, aggregating the outcomes into a compile‑time flag set.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The method iterates over every transitive property in the class, invoking the macro `DEFINE_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY_METHOD` for each one; the macro expands into the implementation that registers the property as a read‑only field. It simply loops through the collection of properties and applies the macro, ensuring that all declared transitive properties are properly configured.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: This function simply verifies whether the current object's property string starts with either of the two predefined prefixes – “TARGET_GENEX_EVAL:” or “GENEX_EVAL:”. If it does, the function returns `true`; otherwise, it returns `false`.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: EvaluatingIncludeDirectories is a const utility that, when invoked, expands the macro `CM_FOR_EACH_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY` to invoke the supplied `DEFINE_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY_METHOD` macro for every transitive property in the current context, thereby producing the necessary include‑directory handling logic.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The function checks whether a given property transitively depends on another by traversing the dependency graph; it returns a boolean indicating the presence of such a dependency.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The `EvaluatingLinkDirectories` helper examines each registered link directory to collect transitive property definitions. It iterates over the internal list, applies the supplied macro `DEFINE_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY_METHOD` to each property, and aggregates the results into an internal map. This map is later used to resolve property lookups when building link graphs.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The `EvaluatingLinkExpression` method simply fetches the property string from the current top node and returns `true` if that string equals one of the four specific link‑related identifiers: `"LINK_DIRECTORIES"`, `"LINK_OPTIONS"`, `"LINK_DEPENDS"`, or `"LINK_LIBRARY_OVERRIDE"`.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body:
The function checks whether a target’s property string matches any of several predefined link‑library identifiers (e.g. “LINK_LIBRARIES”, “INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES”, “LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES”, etc.).  
If the supplied `ForGenex` value is `LINK_LIBRARY` or `LINK_GROUP`, it returns true when the property matches one of those identifiers (or when the property equals “INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES_DIRECT_EXCLUDE”). Otherwise it returns true only when the property matches the standard identifiers listed above.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: A public `EvaluatingLinkOptions` routine invokes the macro `CM_FOR_EACH_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY` to iterate over each transitive property, applying a supplied handler (via `DEFINE_TRANSITIVE_PROPERTY_METHOD`) and returning the aggregated result of the processed options.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: This routine simply checks if the current node’s property string is exactly “LINK_OPTIONS”. It reads the property from the top‑level node, wraps it in a string_view, and returns the result of that equality comparison.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The method obtains the current object's property string, then verifies that the string is longer than the literal "_LINKER_LAUNCHER" and that its final characters match that literal; it returns true only when both conditions hold.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The function simply compares the `Property` field of the top‑level object returned by `Top()` to the literal string `"INTERFACE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE"`. It returns `true` when that comparison succeeds and `false` otherwise.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The function scans a header list, checks that every required header has already been pre‑compiled, and returns a flag indicating whether the header set is valid or any headers are missing.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The EvaluatingSources method scans supplied source identifiers, applies a series of reliability metrics (e.g., historical accuracy, source provenance score, and recency checks), and emits a composite trust rating that is subsequently used to gate downstream ingestion or flag questionable entries.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Evalu.body: The macro expands into a compile‑time loop that registers each transitive property via the supplied macro.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::GetTr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::GetTr.body: It returns the value of the `TransitivePropertiesOnly` flag stored in the object returned by `Top()`.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::GetTr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::GetTr.body: The method simply reads the `CMP0131` flag stored on the top node of the internal DAG and returns that flag’s value.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Initi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Initi.body: Initializes internal state by retrieving the top‑level object, running the graph check, verifying that all transitive‑property methods succeed, and recording the target’s property in the seen map if it was not already present.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Repor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Repor.body: When an expression evaluation fails, the `ReportError` helper first checks whether the caller was already in a DAG‑error state and exits early if so. It then marks the current context as errored and respects a quiet mode that suppresses further reporting. If the offending node is the root of a self‑referencing chain, it produces a detailed error message identifying the target name and reports it as a fatal error. Otherwise, it emits a generic “dependency loop” message and walks up the parent chain, emitting a step‑by‑step trace of each expression in the cycle until the loop is resolved. The routine uses `IssueMessage` to surface each diagnostic with the appropriate back‑trace information.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::SetTr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::SetTr.body: The method simply flips a Boolean flag in the current object—when called, the `TransitivePropertiesOnly` flag is set to true, indicating that only transitive properties should be treated in subsequent logic.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::SetTr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::SetTr.body: The method simply flips the internal flag `CMP0131` to enabled, signaling that only transitive properties should be handled.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Top@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::Top@k.body: The function climbs up the parent chain until no further parent exists, then returns that top‑level instance.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::TopTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::TopTa.body: Retrieves the *Target* member of the object returned by the private Top() helper; it simply dereferences this->Top() and yields the pointer to that target, preserving const‑ness throughout.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::cmGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::cmGen.body: The constructor stores the supplied back‑trace, target, property string, and content pointer, sets default flag values, and then calls `Initialize()` to set up the internal DAG‑checker state.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::cmGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionDAGChecker::cmGen.body: Constructs an instance of the DAG‑checker, storing the supplied target, property string, and content pointer. It also keeps a reference to an optional parent, flags for transitive properties and CMP0131, and then calls Initialize() to finish setup.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::C.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::C.body: The routine gathers the list of languages that the current generator has enabled, then iterates over each one to build a file name specific to that language. For every language it obtains or creates a corresponding source file object, tags it as a “CMake‑generated” file, and registers a dependency so that the rest of the build system knows the file must be present before any targets that rely on it are considered built.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::F.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::F.body: The function turns a relative path into an absolute one by respecting the current policy. If the policy is `WARN`, it logs a warning but keeps the string unchanged; if it’s `OLD` it leaves the path as‑is; otherwise it collapses the string against either the current source or binary directory according to the role.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.body: The function reads the specified input (string or file), parses it into a generator expression, and then iterates over every enabled language and every generator configuration to produce the corresponding output files, handling any fatal errors and setting permissions along the way.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.body: The routine checks a condition expression; if it evaluates to true, it generates a file. It first evaluates the expression to obtain the content, then verifies whether a file with the same content already exists. If the file differs, it writes the new content, ensuring the file is registered in the build system and optionally applies a newline character. Permissions can be set after the write completes.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.body: Returns a copy of the internal `Files` vector.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.body: The method resolves the stored input path. If the stored value is already an absolute path it normalises it; otherwise it resolves the relative path against the current project source directory and returns the fully‑qualified filename.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::G.body: This routine evaluates a stored expression to derive the filename for an output file. It normalizes the path: if the result is a fully qualified path, it’s collapsed to a canonical form; otherwise it resolves the relative path against the current generator’s base location before returning it.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::c.body: The constructor simply stores the supplied data into its member fields, moving the input string, target string, the compiled‑expression pointers, the condition pointer, the flag indicating whether the input string is literal content, the newline character, the policy status, and the permission bits. Once the members are in place, the object is ready to perform its expression‑evaluation duties.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::c.body: The function essentially constructs a new cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile instance by taking an rvalue reference to an existing object (typically an unnamed temporary) and initializing the internal state of the new instance from that source.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::c.body: The constructor copies the internal configuration and expression‑evaluation tables from the supplied instance, creating a new `cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile` object that is ready to evaluate expressions in the same context as the original.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile::c.body: The `cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile` function acts as the central entry point for processing expression‑evaluation files in the cmGenerator subsystem. It orchestrates the loading, parsing, and evaluation of the expressions encoded in those files, triggering the downstream logic that consumes the resulting data.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::Evalua.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::Evalua.body: The `Evaluate` member is a pure‑virtual const function that derived expression‑evaluator classes must override. It receives a `cmGeneratorExpressionContext*` and produces a `std::string` describing the result of evaluating that expression. The function is invoked throughout the system whenever an expression context needs to be rendered into its string representation, ensuring all concrete evaluators supply a consistent implementation.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::GetTyp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::GetTyp.body: This pure‑virtual const member requires every concrete subclass to report the specific type it represents; callers use the returned value to decide how to treat the object at runtime without down‑casting, enabling type‑safe dispatch in polymorphic containers.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::cmGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::cmGene.body: It copies the internal state of an existing `cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator` instance – duplicating its expression mapping and any other member data into a new object.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::cmGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::cmGene.body: Creates a fresh evaluator instance and initializes its internal state, ensuring it’s ready to parse and evaluate generator expressions. It returns a default‑constructed object that will later be populated with the actual evaluation logic when invoked.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::operat.body: The `operator=` overload copies the internal expression‑tree and evaluation state from another `cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator`. It assigns all member fields (e.g., cached results, flags, and cached sub‑evaluators) and returns `*this` for chaining. The function is the canonical assignment operator used throughout the code to replace an evaluator’s contents with another instance’s contents.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::~cmGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionEvaluator::~cmGen.body:
It’s a virtual destructor that lets the compiler generate the default body automatically.  
Because it’s declared virtual, any derived implementation will be invoked correctly when an object is deleted through a base‑type pointer, ensuring all resources owned by the derived class are released in the right order.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::Eval.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::Eval.body: The method parses the supplied expression string into an internal representation, then creates a DAG‑checker instance based on the requested property (switching between “COMPILE_OPTIONS” and the given property when the flag is “COMPILE_FLAGS”). Finally it executes the compiled expression’s evaluation logic with the current generator, configuration, target, and language context, and returns the resulting string reference.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::cmGe.body: The constructor of `cmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter` initializes the instance by invoking the base `GeneratorExpression` constructor with the CMake instance from the supplied `cmLocalGenerator`. It then stores the supplied `cmLocalGenerator` pointer, copies the configuration string into `Config`, stores the supplied target pointer in `HeadTarget`, and assigns the optional language string to `Language`. No additional logic is performed in this constructor.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::cmGe.body: The constructor duplicates the state of an existing interpreter, copying its configuration data so the new object is independent of the source.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::oper.body: `operator=` is an overloaded assignment operator that sets the interpreter’s state from a given expression and returns a reference to the interpreter itself.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::AcceptsArbi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::AcceptsArbi.body: A virtual const member that, by default, always reports “false” – in other words, a hook that derived classes can override to signal whether they accept arbitrary content or not.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::EvaluateDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::EvaluateDep.body: The function constructs a `cmGeneratorExpression` from a property string, parses it into a compiled form, and evaluates it against the current build‑system context (configuration, language, and target hierarchy). While evaluating, it records whether any of the three sensitive‑condition flags (context‑sensitive, head‑sensitive, or link‑language‑sensitive) was triggered, marking the corresponding flags in the caller’s context. Finally, it returns the resolved string.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::GeneratesCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::GeneratesCo.body: The method is a virtual, const member that simply reports the presence of content. It returns `true`, so any call to this base implementation is interpreted as “content has been generated.” Derived classes can override it to provide more nuanced status while still preserving the const‑qualified contract.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::GetNode@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::GetNode@k_Z.body: Retrieves a global instance of a `cmGeneratorExpressionNode` associated with a string identifier. It performs a single lookup into a static map that holds the pre‑created node pointers; if the key exists, that pointer is returned, otherwise `nullptr` is returned.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::NumExpected.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::NumExpected.body: Returns the integer 1 to indicate that the class expects exactly one parameter.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::RequiresLit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::RequiresLit.body: Indicates whether the type demands a literal value as input; the base implementation returns false, but derived classes can override it to signal that literal input is mandatory.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::cmGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::cmGenerator.body: The `cmGeneratorExpressionNode()` function builds an AST node that represents a C++ expression. It parses a raw expression string, resolves its operands and operators, and packages the result into a `cmGeneratorExpressionNode` object for later code‑generation stages. This helper encapsulates the logic for turning a parsed expression into the internal representation used by the generator.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::~cmGenerato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionNode::~cmGenerato.body:
The destructor `~cmGeneratorExpressionNode()` is declared `virtual` and marked `= default;`.  
This means the compiler automatically generates a default destructor that simply destroys the object’s members, and that base‑class destructors are called in the usual order. Because the destructor is `virtual`, any subclass that derives from `cmGeneratorExpressionNode` can override it to perform custom cleanup while still invoking the base destructor chain. The defaulted declaration guarantees that no explicit resource‑release code is required unless a derived type introduces its own resources that need explicit release.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::Parse@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::Parse@k_Z.body: The function initializes an iterator to the beginning of the token list and then iterates through every token, calling `ParseContent` on each one until the iterator reaches the end of the list, thereby filling the provided `result` vector with parsed elements.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::ParseCont.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::ParseCont.body: The method iterates over the token stream, merging consecutive text fragments only when not nested, and otherwise creating new text nodes. When a begin‑expression token is encountered it hands off to the nested parser, while a comma or colon at the outer level triggers a helper to extend the current text block. Unexpected tokens trigger assertion failures.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::ParseGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::ParseGene.body: The routine walks through the token stream, collecting identifier tokens until it meets a colon or end token. It tracks nested levels so that nested expressions are parsed recursively, then builds a `GeneratorExpressionContent` object containing the gathered identifiers and any comma‑separated parameters, pushing that object into the result vector.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::cmGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::cmGenerat.body: The `cmGeneratorExpressionParser` constructor (or factory function) takes a forwarding reference to another `cmGeneratorExpressionParser` instance (itself) and moves its internal state into the newly created object. It performs no deep copying of the underlying expression tree; it merely swaps the parser’s internal buffers and any stored token streams so that the moved‑to instance can immediately resume parsing with the same context. This is used in the codebase to cheaply transfer ownership of a parser state between helper objects or temporary scopes without expensive re‑initialisation.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::cmGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::cmGenerat.body: The constructor simply clones the internal state of an existing parser: it copies the token stream, the current parsing position, and any cached flags so that a new `cmGeneratorExpressionParser` instance can be created with the same configuration as the source object. This shallow copy allows callers to preserve or restore a parser’s context without having to re‑parse the input.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::cmGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::cmGenerat.body: The constructor accepts a vector of `cmGeneratorExpressionToken`s and stores it in the member `Tokens` by moving the argument into that member variable.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::cmGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionParser::cmGenerat.body: `cmGeneratorExpressionParser` is a public entry point that takes a string or token stream and produces a parse tree or AST representation for the custom generator syntax. It performs lexical tokenization, grammar rule matching, and semantic validation before returning a structured `cmGeneratorExpressionParser` object that callers can query for expression details.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.body: The function inspects the target’s CUDA architecture setting. If the setting string is empty, it consults the generator’s policy mode: in non‑try‑compile builds it warns the user, otherwise it aborts with a fatal error. When the string is “false” it exits immediately, otherwise it forwards the parsed architectures string together with the compile/link context to a helper that actually emits the appropriate architecture flags.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.body: The function is a move‑constructor for the `CudaArchitecture` class. It takes an rvalue reference to another `CudaArchitecture` instance and initializes this object by transferring ownership of its internal resources, ensuring that any managed resources (such as device pointers or device memory handles) are properly moved rather than copied.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.body: The constructor takes an existing `CudaArchitecture` instance and replicates its internal configuration into the new object, copying device identifiers, stream settings, and any handles or context pointers it owns while preserving reference‑counting semantics for shared resources.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.body: The `CudaArchitecture()` function creates and returns a `CudaArchitecture` instance populated with device‑specific information (compute capability, available memory, stream‑queue limits, etc.) that is subsequently consumed by other parts of the build system.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAArchitecture.body: The function analyzes the requested CUDA architecture string (which may specify multiple GPU SMs optionally followed by a “real”/“virtual” specifier) and appends the appropriate `--generate-code=arch=` switches to the build‑flags string. It distinguishes between NVIDIA's NVCC and Clang’s CUDA compiler, adds I‑P‑O‑enabled options when requested, and emits a warning if Clang tries to disable virtual code that it does not support. The logic also covers special “all”/“all‑major” and “native” modes, and falls back to a default architecture list when needed.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAToolkitFlags.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddCUDAToolkitFlags.body: Adds a CUDA‑path flag to the flag string when the compiler is clang and a toolkit root is available.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddExplicitLanguage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddExplicitLanguage.body: The method inspects the source file for a language property. If none exists it exits immediately. It then consults the current policy status: for the “OLD” policy it simply returns; for the “NEW” or other enabled cases it proceeds. Finally it invokes `AppendFeatureOptions` to tack the detected language onto the flag string under the key “EXPLICIT_LANGUAGE”.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddExplicitObjectNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddExplicitObjectNa.body: Adds the supplied source‑file pointer to the internal set that tracks explicit object names.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddHIPArchitectureF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddHIPArchitectureF.body: The function collects the HIP architecture list from the target’s HIP_ARCHITECTURES property. It first validates that the property is present; if it’s disabled it exits. For a non‑NVIDIA target it iterates each architecture string and appends “ --offload‑arch=<arch>” to the supplied flag buffer, effectively enabling offloading for the selected GPU families.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddHeaderSetVerific.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddHeaderSetVerific.body: The function first checks whether interface‑header‑set verification is enabled for the current target. If not, it exits. Otherwise it collects the list of header sets to verify, building a set of file‑sets that actually belong to the target’s interface. It then constructs a special “verify” target library populated with the header‑set sources that need checking. For each such source it generates a temporary file that represents that header set; these files are added to the newly created target. After all sources are processed the verify target is registered with the local generator so that its build rules will be emitted during the makefile generation.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddISPCGeneratedHea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddISPCGeneratedHea.body: The function normalizes a given `config` string to upper‑case, then ensures the normalized key exists in the `ISPCGeneratedHeaders` map. If the key is new, it creates a new vector with the supplied header; otherwise it appends the header to the existing vector.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddISPCGeneratedObj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddISPCGeneratedObj.body: The function normalises the *config* string to upper‑case, then looks up that key in the internal map of generated‑object lists. If the key is missing it inserts a new entry keyed by the upper‑cased string; if the key already exists it appends the supplied vector of strings into the existing list. The routine therefore either creates a fresh collection of objects for a new configuration or extends an existing collection with new entries.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddIncludeDirectory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddIncludeDirectory.body:
Adds a source‑path to the build system’s include search list.  
If `before` is true, the directory is added at the front; otherwise it’s appended at the end.  
The function records the operation in the internal include directory set and records a property entry for later use.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddSource@k_ZN17cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddSource@k_ZN17cmG.body: The function forwards the given source string to its internal `Target` object, invoking that object's `AddSource` method with the same arguments, and subsequently calls a helper routine (`AddSourceCommon`) to perform any shared post‑processing.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddSourceCommon@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddSourceCommon@k_Z.body: The method inserts a new source entry into the `SourceEntries` collection. It creates a property entry using the current `CMakeInstance`, marks it as a source (`true`), attaches a back‑trace identifier, and then clears the internal source cache.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddSourceFileToUnit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddSourceFileToUnit.body: The method stores the given source file name in the internal collection of files that will be compiled together in a unity build. It simply inserts the string into the `UnityBatchedSourceFiles` container (a set or similar).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddSystemIncludeDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddSystemIncludeDir.body: The routine walks through every generator config string; for each one it substitutes a `$<CONFIG>` token in the supplied include path, builds a cache key from the config name (upper‑cased) and language, and records the resulting path in a per‑key vector. It then pushes that path into the target’s system‑include list and finally re‑sorts the vector to keep it in order for efficient binary look‑ups.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddTracedSources@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddTracedSources@k_.body: The routine forwards the supplied source list to its embedded Target’s AddTracedSources and, when the list isn’t empty, joins the entries with “;” and passes that string to AddSourceCommon.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AppendCustomCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AppendCustomCommand.body: The routine inserts the current target into a provided set when that target either hosts any non‑empty pre‑/post‑build commands or any configuration source that defines a custom command, effectively marking targets that affect custom command execution.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AppendLanguageSideE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AppendLanguageSideE.body: The function gathers the compile‑time languages that can generate side‑effects. It skips the known “no‑side‑effect” languages (C, CXX, OBJC, OBJCXX, ASM, CUDA, HIP) and, for every remaining language, records this target object in the supplied map under that language key.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::BuildBundleDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::BuildBundleDirector.body: BuildBundleDirectory builds a string by appending optional directories—derived from the bundle’s type (app, framework, or CF bundle)—to the provided base path.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::BuildFileSetInfoCac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::BuildFileSetInfoCac.body: The routine lazily builds a lookup table that maps every file path used by a target to the `FileSet` that supplied it. When invoked, it first checks a flag in the target’s configuration; if that cache has already been constructed it returns immediately. If the flag is unset it iterates over every declared file‑set of the current target. For each set it resolves the set object, emits an internal‑error message if the set is absent, then compiles the file and directory entries for that set, evaluates the directories against the current local generator context, and finally runs the set’s entry‑evaluation routine to populate a map from collapsed (canonical) file paths to the set that owns them. Once all sets have been processed, it flips the flag to indicate the cache is ready for subsequent queries.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::CanCompileSources@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::CanCompileSources@k.body: It simply forwards the check to its internal target component, returning that component’s `CanCompileSources` result.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::CanGenerateInstallN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::CanGenerateInstallN.body: The method checks the CMP0068 policy and any “skip” flags that might be set on the target. If the target is marked to be skipped, it may additionally issue a warning under the WARN policy. Finally, it returns true only when no skip condition is active.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckCMP0004@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckCMP0004@k_ZNK1.body: The function removes leading and trailing whitespace from the supplied string. If any trimming occurs it queries the current policy for CMP0004, which may be set to WARN, OLD, NEW, REQUIRED_IF_USED, or REQUIRED_ALWAYS. Depending on that setting it logs a warning or a fatal error via the `cmake` instance and attaches the current back‑trace. Finally it returns the cleaned string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckCxxModuleStatu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckCxxModuleStatu.body: The method verifies whether a target’s C++ sources can use CXX modules under the current generator. It first checks for any existing CXX module files; if none exist it scans the target’s source list for C++ files that require dynamic‑dependency resolution. If no module‑eligible sources remain, it returns silently. Otherwise, it confirms that the global generator actually supports modules—reporting fatal errors if the generator lacks module support, if the CXX language isn’t enabled, if the CXX20 standard isn’t requested, or if the compiler cannot provide dependency discovery. All errors are emitted via the Makefile’s issue‑message interface.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckLinkLibraries@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckLinkLibraries@.body: Checks which libraries must be linked for a target. If the property `LINK_LIBRARIES_ONLY_TARGETS` is set, it only inspects the libraries that belong to the current target; otherwise it checks both the implementation and interface libraries for every generated configuration. It walks the internal `LinkImplMap` and `LinkInterfaceMap` entries, calling `VerifyLinkItemColons` (and optionally `VerifyLinkItemIsTarget`) on each `cmLinkItem` to confirm that every required library is present and correctly classified.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckManagedType@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckManagedType@k_.body: The function inspects the `propval` string: if it is empty or the literal `"netcore"`, it designates the target as a mixed/unmanaged‑managed build and returns `ManagedType::Mixed`; otherwise it tags the target as fully managed and returns `ManagedType::Managed`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckPropertyCompat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::CheckPropertyCompat.body: This method collects the names of properties that the current target’s dependencies have emitted as boolean, string, minimum‑number, or maximum‑number values. It then verifies that each emitted property is associated with at most one of those interpretations; if a property appears in more than one category, it reports a fatal error noting that a property cannot serve simultaneously as a boolean, string, and numeric constraint.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ClearLinkInterfaceC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ClearLinkInterfaceC.body: The function empties the internal maps that hold link‑interface objects and their usage‑requirement data. By calling `LinkInterfaceMap.clear()` and `LinkInterfaceUsageRequirementsOnlyMap.clear()`, it resets the cached state for the current generation cycle.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ClearSourcesCache@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ClearSourcesCache@k.body: The method wipes all in‑memory caches that hold source‑level data – clearing configuration source lists, mapping of kind‑based sources, and every map or vector that tracks visited config objects, link implementation details, and pre‑compiled headers. All compile‑time options, include directories, and runtime binary paths are reset, leaving the generator in a clean state for the next round of processing.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::CompileInfo::Compil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::CompileInfo::Compil.body: `CompileInfo()` gathers and returns the current compilation context—such as compiler version, target architecture, build flags, and any user‑supplied metadata—encapsulated in a lightweight struct. It typically exposes a read‑only interface to other modules that need to query build‑time parameters at run‑time.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeAllConfigSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeAllConfigSou.body: The method scans each generator‑config, retrieves the associated sources, and records every distinct source file along with its kind. It builds a map from source pointers to their positions in the output vector so that each source’s config indices can be added without duplication.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeCompileFeatu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeCompileFeatu.body: The routine walks through every language enabled for the current target, resolves its C++ standard level from compile‑features data, updates the internal standard‑level mappings (including any required standard overrides), and reports success only if all features resolve cleanly; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeCompileFeatu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeCompileFeatu.body: Iterates through each language pair; for each language it ensures the target has an entry in `LanguageStandardMap`. If a standard isn’t already set, it first tries to copy the paired language’s value, then falls back to a default definition. For CUDA it rewrites a specific 98‑standard value to “03”. The routine always returns true.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeImportInfo@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeImportInfo@k.body: ComputeImportInfo walks through the exported target’s property set, pulling values for library names, SONAME flags, link dependencies, and language requirements, and then fills the supplied ImportInfo structure with that metadata. It first checks the mapped configuration for location and import library values, then proceeds to query optional suffix‑augmented properties for SONAME, no‑SONAME, and link‑related data, handling missing values by falling back to defaults in a graceful, conditional fashion.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeKindedSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeKindedSource.body: The function collects source‑file paths for the current build target, creates or re‑uses source objects for each path, classifies every file according to its extension, custom command flag, and target type, and appends the result (file, back‑trace, and its kind) into the supplied `KindedSources` structure. If the target is an object library and a file type that normally would not be linked (e.g. a def or idl file) is encountered, the function records the file and ultimately reports a fatal error.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkClosure@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkClosure@.body: The routine first parses the configuration string to populate a temporary `LinkClosure` object. It checks whether the target’s link‑er language is hard‑coded; if not, it runs a first pass to compute the closure. If a second pass is needed, it recomputes it and verifies the linker language hasn’t changed between passes, otherwise it reports an error.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkClosure@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkClosure@.body: The routine first collects every language that the target either builds itself or pulls from linked targets, merges them into a closure set, then selects the language whose linker should drive the build (using a preference scheme that honours explicit propagations). Finally it reports whether any of the involved languages had a link‑language‑sensitive condition.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkImplemen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkImplemen.body:
The method gathers the set of source‑language identifiers used by the target’s source files and then merges that set into the link‑implementation’s language list.

1. **Collect language set** – It starts with an empty `std::set<std::string> languages`.  
2. **Retrieve used languages** – Calls `GetLanguages(languages, config)` to inspect the target’s source files and populate the set with the languages that appear.  
3. **Propagate to the link implementation** – Finally inserts every element of this set into `impl.Languages` by invoking `insert` with the range `[languages.begin(), languages.end())`. This populates the link implementation with the languages the compiled output will require at link time.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkImplemen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkImplemen.body: The routine walks through each link‑entry of the target, evaluates it with the current configuration, resolves the dependency (including synthetic ones), and populates the target’s link‑library and object lists while tracking any head‑/context‑sensitive conditions or policy‑related warnings.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkImplemen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkImplemen.body: Iterates over the languages in the passed‑in implementation. For each language equal to “CUDA” or “HIP” that hasn’t been handled before, it calls `computeImplicitLanguageTargets<cmLinkImplItem>` with the config and the current object, and stores the resulting items in the implementation’s `LanguageRuntimeLibraries` map.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkInterfac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkInterfac.body: This overload simply forwards the request to the full‑signature version of ComputeLinkInterface, passing along the supplied configuration string, link‑interface object, and optional head target, and always supplies `false` for the final flag argument.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkInterfac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkInterfac.body: Populates the link‑interface data structure with the libraries that this target must link against at runtime. It walks the explicit library list in the interface, inserts any shared‑library dependencies that arise from the target’s own implementation, and, when the policy is in a warning or old state, records any “wrong‑config” libraries that were found. It also propagates language‑dependent libraries to dependents that use the archive, and, for static libraries, records the multiplicity suffix that may be needed for duplicate interfaces.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkInterfac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkInterfac.body: The routine determines the set of libraries that must be exported by a target’s link interface. It first resolves whether an explicit list was supplied via the new CMP0022 property or the legacy property and, based on the target’s type and policy state, builds the appropriate list from those values or from the target’s link‑implementation fallback. If an explicit list exists it is returned; otherwise the link‑implementation libraries are used.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkInterfac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeLinkInterfac.body: The method iterates through each language in `iface.Languages`. For every entry that is either “CUDA” or “HIP” and that does not already have a runtime‑library entry, it calls `computeImplicitLanguageTargets<cmLinkItem>` with the language, the supplied config string, and the current instance (`this`). The resulting vector of implicit link items is stored in `iface.LanguageRuntimeLibraries` under that language key.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeModuleDefini.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeModuleDefini.body: The function gathers information about a module’s sources and symbol‑export rules. It checks whether the build should emit a `.def` file (based on export settings or number of sources) and sets `info.DefFile` accordingly—either to a generated path or the first source file. This data is then used elsewhere to control the build system.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeObjectMappin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeObjectMappin.body: The function obtains generator‑specific configuration data from the Makefile, builds a set of those config keys, and if that set hasn’t already been processed (checked against VisitedConfigsForObjects) it exits. Otherwise it loops over each config name, calling GetObjectSources to collect the source files that belong to that configuration.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeOutputDir@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeOutputDir@k_.body: The method resolves the path that a build artifact should be written into. It first builds potential property names derived from the target type and the current build‑configuration name, then attempts to read those properties from the current generator’s property set. If a per‑configuration directory is found it evaluates that expression, otherwise a generic directory property is used. When neither property yields a value, the code falls back to standard output directories for executables, static/shared modules, or libraries. If none of these provide a path, the function defaults to the current output directory (".") and records that the default was used. Finally the chosen path is normalised to an absolute location relative to the generator’s binary directory, and the optional configuration suffix is appended if the system uses an effective‑platform name. The function returns whether a default path was used.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputePDBOutputDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputePDBOutputDir.body: The function resolves the directory that the generator should use when generating a particular product database (PDB). It first looks for a property specific to the requested kind (like `<Kind>_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`). If that property is present it evaluates any embedded generator expressions. If that fails, it falls back to a more generic property that may contain a per‑configuration override. Once a directory string is obtained it normalises it against the current binary directory: relative paths are collapsed to absolute paths. Finally, if the configuration string is non‑empty, it appends that string as an extra sub‑directory on the resulting path. The function returns success only when a usable directory was found.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeTargetManife.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeTargetManife.body: The function guards against re‑processing an already‑import target, then pulls in the shared global generator. Depending on the target’s type it fetches the proper set of names (output, shared object, real, PDB or import‑specific names). For each non‑empty name it constructs a full file path under the appropriate directory (runtime binary or import library artifacts) and adds that path to the global manifest via `AddToManifest`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeVersionedNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ComputeVersionedNam.body: The function sets `vName` to `prefix+base` if the target is Apple; otherwise it uses the supplied `name`. If a `cmValue` `version` is provided, it appends a period and that value to the name. Finally, if the target is Apple it appends the supplied `suffix`; otherwise it leaves the string unchanged.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ConstructSourceFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ConstructSourceFile.body: The routine walks through the build‑time properties that list public headers, private headers, and resources. For each file it fetches the corresponding source object, then records a flag entry that marks the file’s type and the folder name (“Headers”, “PrivateHeaders”, or “Resources” unless stripping is requested). If the flags have already been built it returns immediately, ensuring the mapping is generated only once.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::CreateFortranModule.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::CreateFortranModule.body: The function determines the directory for Fortran modules by first checking whether a property value is defined; if not, it uses the current binary directory unless it matches the working directory. It then examines a flag that indicates whether the module directory should be used; if that flag is set, the function resolves whether the target directory path is absolute or relative—prefixing the latter with the current binary directory. Finally, it creates the directory if it does not yet exist and returns the full path.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::DetermineHasMacOSXR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::DetermineHasMacOSXR.body: The method walks through a target’s install‑name configuration to determine whether it should use a special “@rpath” convention for a Mac OS X runtime. It first checks that the target is a shared library and that the property “INSTALL_NAME_DIR” is present and enabled. It then tests whether that value literally contains “@rpath” or otherwise falls back to a default “rpath” name derived from the import information. If neither condition is met and the required CMake flag (“CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_RUNTIME_C_FLAG”) is missing, it logs a fatal error. If all checks pass, the function returns true, signalling that the runtime can be installed using the rpath scheme.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::DeviceLinkSetter::D.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::DeviceLinkSetter::D.body: The constructor stores the reference to `target` and immediately calls `SetDeviceLink(true)`, saving its return value into `PreviousState`. This effectively turns the device link on for the lifetime of the `DeviceLinkSetter` instance and allows the link state to be restored when the object goes out of scope.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::DeviceLinkSetter::~.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::DeviceLinkSetter::~.body: The destructor re‑establishes the device link by invoking `Target.SetDeviceLink` with the stored `PreviousState`. This restores the original link configuration when the `DeviceLinkSetter` object is destroyed.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::DiscoverSyntheticTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::DiscoverSyntheticTa.body: The function scans the libraries found in the current module’s implementation. For each imported target that supplies C++20 sources, it builds a unique synthetic target name from a hash of that target’s directory and usage information. It checks the cache; if the synthetic target does not exist, it creates one, copies over policy statuses, file‑sets, and imported C++ module entries from the original target, applies the usage constraints, and then recurses into the newly created target. Finally, it records the synthetic target in the calling target’s synthetic‑dependency list.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::EvaluateInterfacePr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::EvaluateInterfacePr.body: The function checks whether a given property is defined for the target (recursively considering linked libraries). If it is, it uses a D‑Graph checker to detect self‑references or cycles, then evaluates the property using `cmGeneratorExpressionNode::EvaluateDependentExpression`. It walks through any linked libraries that contribute the property, merging their results (concatenated with “;”) and propagates any context‑sensitivity flags encountered along the way. The resulting string of all gathered values is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ExpandLinkItems@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ExpandLinkItems@k_Z.body: The function walks through each “link entry” supplied by the build system, parses it into a concrete expression, resolves that expression against the current target and configuration, and then collects the resulting link items into the appropriate buckets of the output interface object. It distinguishes header‑only entries versus library entries, and flags any that were built from “head‑sensitive” expressions. The result is a fully populated link interface ready for the rest of the build process.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GenerateHeaderSetVe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GenerateHeaderSetVe.body: The function creates a small “verification” file that lists the header file that should be included in a target build. It first checks that the source isn’t marked to skip linting and then determines which language (“C” or “CXX”) the source belongs to. If the language can’t be inferred from the source itself, it falls back on the global list of enabled languages; it prefers C++ over plain C. Once the language is settled, it picks the proper file extension (.c or .cxx), builds the full path for the verification file, creates the directory if needed, and writes a single line that includes the header file with an IWYU pragma comment. It finally returns the path to the created verification file.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAllConfigCompile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAllConfigCompile.body: The function walks through every configuration source, pulls the language string when present, and collects the distinct values in a set that is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAllConfigSources.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAllConfigSources.body: The function iterates over the collection returned by the class’s own `GetAllConfigSources()` method and appends only those entries whose `Kind` field matches the requested `SourceKind`. It builds a new vector containing the filtered results and returns it.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAllConfigSources.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAllConfigSources.body: The method lazily fills an internal vector on first use and then returns a reference to that vector. It checks `AllConfigSources.empty()`, calls `ComputeAllConfigSources()` if needed, and finally returns the member `AllConfigSources`. The function is marked `const`, yet it mutates the internal collection—so callers must not modify the returned vector unless they intend to modify the target’s state. Ensure that `ComputeAllConfigSources()` is thread‑safe if the class is accessed concurrently, and be mindful that the returned reference is lifetime‑bound to the object’s lifetime.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAppBundleDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAppBundleDirecto.body: The function builds a path string for an application bundle. It starts with the full name for the requested configuration, appends an extension (from a “BUNDLE_EXTENSION” property or “app” by default), and then optionally appends “/Contents” and “/MacOS” segments depending on the requested bundle‑directory level and whether the target platform is an Apple‑embedded build. The resulting string is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAppleArchs@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAppleArchs@k_ZNK.body:
The function returns a list of Apple‑specific architecture strings.  
It first checks that the current target is Apple; if not, it returns an empty vector.  
It then looks for a property named `OSX_ARCHITECTURES_` followed by an upper‑cased version of the supplied `config` string. If that property is missing, it falls back to the generic `OSX_ARCHITECTURES` property.  
If a property is found, its contents (a list of strings) are copied into the result vector.  
Finally, if the vector is still empty and no compiler‑target definition is defined for the current language, it loads a default list from the internal definition `_CMAKE_APPLE_ARCHS_DEFAULT`. The vector is then returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAutoUicOptions@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAutoUicOptions@k.body: The routine resolves the value of the “AUTOUIC_OPTIONS” property for the current configuration, halting early if the property isn’t present. When the property exists it feeds that string through a DAG‑based expression evaluator that records the evaluation graph. Finally the resulting list of strings is expanded and appended to the supplied result vector.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK1.body: The `GetBacktrace` function is a simple forwarding accessor: it retrieves a `cmListFileBacktrace` instance by delegating the call to the wrapped `Target` object and returns that result unchanged. It acts as a thin wrapper without additional state manipulation.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetBuildRPATH@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetBuildRPATH@k_ZNK.body: The method forwards the supplied configuration string to a common helper (GetRPATH) while supplying a fixed key – “BUILD_RPATH” – and returns the helper’s success flag, storing the resolved path in the output reference.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCFBundleDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCFBundleDirector.body: The function constructs a fully‑qualified bundle directory path by first calling the base name generator for the given configuration, then appending a file‑extension that is either taken from a configured property or, by default, selected based on whether the build is an Apple XCTest; if the caller requests a content‑level directory, it appends “/Contents” and, when a full directory is requested, appends “/MacOS” before returning the complete string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetClangTidyExportF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetClangTidyExportF.body:
The function queries a property named “<lang>\_CLANG_TIDY_EXPORT_FIXES_DIR” for the target.  
If the property is unset or empty it returns an empty string.  
Otherwise it interprets the value as a path; if that path is not absolute it prefixes the target’s current binary‑directory. Finally the path is normalised (collapses any “./”/“../” components) before returning it.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompatibleInterf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompatibleInterf.body: The function fetches a `CompatibleInterfaces` record for the supplied config key from a cached map. If the record hasn’t yet been fully populated (`Done` flag), it sets up a few default keys (`POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE`, `AUTOUIC_OPTIONS`) and then walks through the target’s dependency chain. For each linked generator it pulls out any property matching the pattern `COMPATIBLE_INTERFACE_…` (via the macro), extracts the list, and merges that list into the result’s property set. Finally the populated record is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileDefinitio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileDefinitio.body: The function retrieves the compile‑time definitions for a given configuration and language combination. It first looks up a cached vector of definitions keyed by the config‑string and language‑string; if present it returns that vector. When a cache miss occurs it constructs a new list by evaluating the target’s property entries, optionally appending interface entries for the given interface and handling any “COMPILE_DEFINITIONS_\<CONFIG\>” property according to the current policy. After processing the options via `processOptions`, the newly built list is stored in `CompileDefinitionsCache` before being returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileDefinitio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileDefinitio.body: The routine fetches a vector of `BT<std::string>` objects from the internal overload of `GetCompileDefinitions(config, language)`. It then reserves enough capacity in the output vector and transfers each string value into it via `emplace_back`, using move semantics to avoid unnecessary copies. The effect is that the caller receives a plain `std::vector<std::string>` populated with the compile‑time definitions.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileFeatures@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileFeatures@.body: The function collects a list of enabled compile‑time flags for the current build target. It builds a set of unique feature strings, invokes a DAG checker to validate the target‑property expressions, and conditionally adds debug‑specific options when the global “CMAKE_DEBUG_TARGET_PROPERTIES” list contains the keyword. After gathering the property entries it feeds them through `processOptions`, which expands them into the resulting vector of `BT<std::string>` objects that is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileFeatures@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileFeatures@.body: The method fills the supplied vector with strings produced by the class’s internal `GetCompileFeatures` helper. It first obtains a temporary vector of `BT<std::string>` objects, reserves space in `result`, then moves each `Value` into `result` using `emplace_back`. The operation is `const`, meaning it does not alter the object state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileInfo@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileInfo@k_ZN.body: Retrieves the compile configuration for the target. If the target is imported or of an unsupported type the call fails and returns nullptr. Otherwise it normalises the requested config string, looks up a cached CompileInfo in an internal map and, if absent, generates and stores a new entry before returning a reference to that information.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileOptions@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileOptions@k.body: This const member of cmGeneratorTarget produces a vector of compile‑option strings for a given configuration and language. It first consults a cache keyed on those parameters; if a cache entry is missing it evaluates target properties, builds up the necessary interface entries, runs the option‑parsing logic (including any debug‑specific flags), and finally stores the computed list in the cache before returning it.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileOptions@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompileOptions@k.body: The function retrieves a list of compile‑option strings via the internal `GetCompileOptions` helper, reserves space in the supplied `result` vector, and then moves each option into that vector using `emplace_back`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompilePDBDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompilePDBDirect.body: Retrieves the `CompilePdbDir` string stored in the `CompileInfo` object associated with the supplied `config`. If no matching `CompileInfo` is found, it yields an empty string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompilePDBName@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompilePDBName@k.body: The routine assembles the filename for a runtime‑generated PDB file. It first normalises the supplied configuration string to upper‑case, uses that to look up a property named `COMPILE_PDB_NAME_<config>`; if that property contains a value it prefixes the configured name with the current internal prefix and appends “.pdb”. If the per‑configuration property is missing, it falls back to a generic `COMPILE_PDB_NAME` property, applying the same prefix logic, and finally returns an empty string when no property is set.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompilePDBPath@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCompilePDBPath@k.body:
It constructs a file path by concatenating the directory and file name.  
If the primary directory is empty but the name is present and an output directory is defined, it falls back to an alternate directory.  
The result is the concatenated directory (with a trailing slash if non‑empty) plus the name.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetConfigCommonSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetConfigCommonSour.body: The routine collects the source files for every generator‑configuration pair, starting with the first one. It populates a vector with the files that belong to that configuration, compares the resulting list against the current canonical list, and if any discrepancy is detected it dumps both the canonical and offending lists in an error message and aborts the build. If all configurations match, the routine returns true.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCreateRuleVariab.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCreateRuleVariab.body: The function returns a CMake‑style variable name that describes how a target should be built. It examines the target’s type (static, shared, module, or executable). For static libraries it invokes a helper that builds a fully qualified name using the language, otherwise it just returns a hard‑coded string like `CMAKE_<lang>_CREATE_*`. If the target is an executable that exports symbols, it prefers the “LINK_EXECUTABLE_WITH_EXPORTS” variable if that definition already exists; otherwise it falls back to the generic “LINK_EXECUTABLE” variable. If the type doesn’t match any known case, the function returns an empty string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCustomCommands@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCustomCommands@k.body: In the `cmGeneratorTarget::GetCustomCommands` member, the method receives a vector of pointers to `cmSourceFile` objects (each pointing to a source file that may contain a custom command) and a configuration string. Inside the body, it invokes the macro `IMPLEMENT_VISIT(SourceKindCustomCommand)`, which expands to code that dispatches each file to a visitor handling `SourceKindCustomCommand` objects. The function itself is `const`, indicating that it does not modify the target object’s state, and its sole purpose is to trigger the handling logic for the custom command sources.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCustomObjectExte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCustomObjectExte.body: The function iterates over a static list of compiler‑mode names paired with file‑extension suffixes, checks the current build’s compiler ID, then scans the list for a matching “has_extension” flag; if found it returns the corresponding suffix string, otherwise it falls back to a null pointer.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCxxModuleSources.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetCxxModuleSources.body: The method adds C++ module source entries to the supplied vector. It does this by invoking the `IMPLEMENT_VISIT(SourceKindCxxModuleSource)` macro, which expands the logic that registers or enumerates the relevant source files according to the given configuration.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetDeprecation@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetDeprecation@k_ZN.body: Retrieves the `DEPRECATION` property from the object; if the property is set, it returns that value, otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetDirectory@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetDirectory@k_ZNK1.body:
It finds where a target artifact lives.  
If the target was imported it resolves the full import path, extracts the framework component when applicable, and returns that directory.  
Otherwise it looks up the target’s own output information, picking either the runtime binary output directory or the import‑library directory according to the artifact type, and falls back to an empty string if none applies.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetEffectiveFolderN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetEffectiveFolderN.body: The function checks whether folder‐property usage is enabled. If disabled, it returns an empty string. When enabled, it retrieves the configured folder value via `GetProperty("FOLDER")`; if that property is defined, the value is appended to `effectiveFolder` and returned. If the property is unset, the returned string remains empty.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExecutableNames@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExecutableNames@.body: The function checks that the target isn’t come from an imported dependency, gathers an optional version string (when the build system supports symbolic links), and then assembles a set of names for the executable artifact. It pulls the base name, adds prefixes and suffixes to form the output and “real” file names (appending the version where present), and also supplies the names for the import‑library and its associated “real” and “output” files as well as the program‑database file. Finally it returns a struct containing all those resolved name strings.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExplicitStandard.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExplicitStandard.body:
It normalizes the supplied configuration string (to upper‑case) and concatenates it with the requested language, forming a lookup key.  
The function then probes the `ExplicitStandardLevel` map; if an entry exists, it assigns that level to the result.  
Finally, it returns the optional wrapper—empty when no matching entry was found.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExportMacro@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExportMacro@k_ZN.body: The routine checks whether the current target is a shared‑, module‑, or export‑enabled executable. If so, it either fetches a custom export name from the DEFINE_SYMBOL property or synthesises one by appending “_EXPORTS” to the target’s identifier. It stores that identifier in the object’s `ExportMacro` member and returns a pointer to it; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExportName@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExportName@k_ZNK.body: The function returns the value of the *EXPORT_NAME* property if it exists and passes the validity check; otherwise it falls back to the object’s own name and reports an error when the property is present but invalid.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExternalObjects@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExternalObjects@.body: The method iterates over the supplied source files, invoking the visitor logic for any files flagged as external objects. The `IMPLEMENT_VISIT(SourceKindExternalObject)` macro hooks the appropriate visitor routine that records those objects into the generator’s internal registry, ensuring they are incorporated into the subsequent build steps.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExtraSources@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExtraSources@k_Z.body: The method collects every source file that falls under the “extra” category (as defined by the `SourceKindExtra` identifier) and appends each pointer to the supplied `data` vector. It uses the `IMPLEMENT_VISIT` helper to enumerate those files based on the supplied `config` string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFeature@k_ZNK17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFeature@k_ZNK17c.body: The function first checks whether a configuration string is supplied. If so, it concatenates the feature name with an underscore followed by the upper‑cased configuration string (e.g. “name_UB”) and looks that property up. If that lookup succeeds, it returns the value immediately. Failing that, it attempts to retrieve the property using only the feature name. If still not found, it forwards the request to its embedded generator.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFeatureSpecificL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFeatureSpecificL.body: The function checks whether IPO is enabled for the supplied language and configuration. If so, it appends “_IPO” to the variable name and returns that string only if that definition is set in the makefile; otherwise it simply returns the original variable name.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFilePostfix@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFilePostfix@k_ZN.body:
When called, the method builds a postfix string that will be appended to a file name.  
If the supplied `config` string is empty, it returns an empty string.  
Otherwise it converts the string to upper‑case, appends “\_POSTFIX”, and attempts to read that property from the instance.  
If the object is not an imported module and the property is present, but the object is a macOS bundle (application bundle or framework), the property value is discarded (set to null).  
Finally the method checks whether a framework‑specific postfix was supplied via `GetFrameworkMultiConfigPostfix`; if that is non‑empty, that value overrides any prior one.  
The function returns the resolved postfix string (or an empty string if none was found).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFilePrefix@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFilePrefix@k_ZNK.body:
The function returns a string prefix for the target.  
If the target is marked as “import‑only”, it retrieves an optional prefix via `GetFilePrefixInternal`; if that prefix is present it is returned, otherwise an empty string is returned.  
Otherwise, it falls back to the canonical full‑name prefix supplied by `GetFullNameInternalComponents`.  
The function does not perform any I/O or heavy computation; it simply conditionally selects between two pre‑computed strings.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFilePrefixIntern.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFilePrefixIntern.body: GetFilePrefixInternal returns the appropriate prefix string for a target when the target type supports it and the requested artifact type requires it; otherwise it returns nullptr.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFileSetForSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFileSetForSource.body: The method first triggers the cache‑build step for the supplied configuration and then queries the per‑config `FileSetCache` for the entry keyed by the source file’s full path. If the key is absent it returns `nullptr`; otherwise it returns a pointer to the cached file‑set object.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFileSuffix@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFileSuffix@k_ZNK.body: When the target is marked as imported, the method queries an internal helper to fetch the suffix string. If that helper returns a value, the suffix is returned; otherwise an empty string is supplied. If the target isn’t imported, the method simply extracts and returns the suffix component from the target’s full‑name components.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFileSuffixIntern.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFileSuffixIntern.body: The function checks the target type, determines if the artifact is an import library, and then retrieves the appropriate suffix property (IMPORT_SUFFIX or SUFFIX). If none is defined, it falls back to language‑specific and global definitions via the makefile. It returns a `cmValue` pointer to the resolved suffix or `nullptr` when no suffix applies.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFortranModuleDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFortranModuleDir.body: The function lazily creates and returns a cached path string: on the first call it invokes `CreateFortranModuleDirectory(working_dir)` to compute the directory and stores the result; subsequent calls simply return the stored string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFrameworkDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFrameworkDirecto.body: Combines the runtime artifact name (from GetOutputName) with a period‑separated extension or the literal “framework”; if the full‑level flag is true and the target isn’t Apple‑embedded, it appends a “/Versions/” folder followed by the framework version.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFrameworkMultiCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFrameworkMultiCo.body: The function checks if the supplied configuration string is non‑empty, builds a property name from it, and retrieves that property’s value. If the current generator is not an imported multi‑config build on Apple, it drops the postfix, otherwise it returns the property value (or an empty string when none).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFrameworkVersion.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFrameworkVersion.body: The method checks that the object isn’t an interface library, attempts to read the property `FRAMEWORK_VERSION`; if it’s not present it falls back to `VERSION`; if neither exists it simply returns the literal string “A”.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullName@k_ZNK17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullName@k_ZNK17.body: The function simply returns a string: if the object is marked as imported, it delegates to `GetFullNameImported(config, artifact)`; otherwise it falls back to `GetFullNameInternal(config, artifact)`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullNameComponen.author: AI Short Overview
