@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullNameComponen.body: The method simply forwards the provided configuration string and artifact type to the internal helper `GetFullNameInternalComponents`, returning its `NameComponents` result unchanged.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullNameImported.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullNameImported.body: The function resolves the canonical file name for a requested artifact type by asking the target object to return the absolute import path for that artifact. It then strips away directory components via `cmSystemTools::GetFilenameName` and returns the resulting base name. The call is read‑only; no side‑effects are performed.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullNameInternal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullNameInternal.body: The function builds a name string for an artifact type by calling `GetFullNameInternalComponents()` to obtain a `NameComponents` object and then concatenating the `prefix`, `base`, and `suffix` fields. It returns the resulting string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullNameInternal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullNameInternal.body: The function composes a target’s output name by pulling together a prefix (which may include framework or bundle directories), the target’s base name (which may incorporate a suffix for versioned shared libraries on some platforms), and an optional suffix. It first checks a cache to avoid recomputation. Depending on the target type (static, shared, module, executable, imported library, etc.), it chooses whether to apply framework‑specific prefixes or library‑specific suffixes. When an imported library artifact is requested on a platform that doesn’t support it, it returns an empty name. It also handles versioned shared libraries by appending a “-<SOVERSION>” string when appropriate. The resulting NameComponents object is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullPath@k_ZNK17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullPath@k_ZNK17.body: It selects whether the target is imported and returns the corresponding full path string by delegating to either the target’s `ImportedGetFullPath` or `NormalGetFullPath` implementation.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetGeneratedISPCHea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetGeneratedISPCHea.body: The function normalises the provided configuration string to uppercase, looks up that key in the `ISPCGeneratedHeaders` map, and returns the associated vector of header strings. If the key isn’t present, it returns an empty vector.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetGeneratedISPCObj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetGeneratedISPCObj.body: Retrieves the vector of strings stored for the supplied configuration key. The key is normalised to upper‑case, looked up in an internal map, and the stored vector is returned—if the key isn’t present, an empty vector is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetGlobalGenerator@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetGlobalGenerator@.body: This method forwards the request for the global generator to the local generator associated with the current instance, returning whatever that local generator exposes as its global generator.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeadToLinkImplem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeadToLinkImplem.body: The method simply returns a reference to the map entry keyed by the upper‑cased `config` string; it looks up `this->LinkImplMap[cmSystemTools::UpperCase(config)]` and hands back that reference with no copying involved.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeadToLinkImplem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeadToLinkImplem.body:
The function looks up a pre‑built map entry for a given configuration string.  
It first normalises the supplied name by calling `cmSystemTools::UpperCase(config)` so that look‑ups are case‑insensitive, then returns a reference to the corresponding `HeadToLinkImplementationMap` stored in `LinkImplUsageRequirementsOnlyMap`. The method is const, ensuring it never mutates internal state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeadToLinkInterf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeadToLinkInterf.body: The method retrieves a reference to the `cmHeadToLinkInterfaceMap` entry that corresponds to the supplied configuration name. It normalises the supplied string to all‑caps (via `UpperCase`) and looks that key up in the `LinkInterfaceMap` member; the returned reference points directly to the stored value for that key.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeadToLinkInterf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeadToLinkInterf.body: Retrieves a reference to the map entry in `LinkInterfaceUsageRequirementsOnlyMap` that corresponds to the given `config` string converted to upper‑case.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeaderSources@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetHeaderSources@k_.body: The method iterates over the target’s internal source files, filters those whose kind equals **Header**, and appends the matching `cmSourceFile` pointers to the supplied vector. The macro `IMPLEMENT_VISIT(SourceKindHeader)` expands into the visitor logic that performs this filtering step, so the function itself contains no other logic beyond invoking that macro.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImplibGNUtoMS@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImplibGNUtoMS@k_.body:
The function checks whether the current target already supports the desired GNU implementation.  
If the conditions hold, it trims the trailing “.dll.a” from the supplied name, appends the provided extension (or “.lib” if none given), assigns that to `out`, and returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImportInfo@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImportInfo@k_ZNK.body: When called, the method normalizes the supplied configuration name to an all‑caps form, then consults an internal cache of pre‑computed import information. If the entry isn’t present, it computes the required data and stores it in the map before returning a pointer to that entry. If the target is not imported or the relevant import record is empty (both Location and ImportLibrary are unset), the routine yields `nullptr`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImportLinkInterf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImportLinkInterf.body: The function looks up the import configuration for a target, chooses the appropriate head‑to‑link map (usage or normal), possibly overrides the head target if the map entry isn’t head‑sensitive, and then populates or updates the corresponding `cmOptionalLinkInterface`. It merges the retrieved languages and libraries into the interface, expands the link items for head‑include, head‑exclude, and normal library lists, adds any shared dependencies found in the current scope, marks the interface as fully processed, and finally returns a pointer to that interface or `nullptr` if no import info was found.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImportedLibName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImportedLibName@.body: The method queries the target’s internal import mapping via `GetImportInfo`. When an import entry is present it returns that entry’s `LibName`; if no import information is found, it returns an empty string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImportedXcFramew.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetImportedXcFramew.body: The function first validates that the current target is an Apple importable library (shared, static or unknown). If it passes, it normalises a desired configuration string, defaulting to “NOCONFIG” when none is supplied. It then attempts to resolve a mapped config through `GetMappedConfig`; if found, it prefers a locally resolved path (`loc`), otherwise it looks up a property named “IMPORTED_LOCATION” possibly with a suffix. If a valid path is found and satisfies `IsPathToXcFramework`, that path is returned; otherwise an empty string is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetIncludeDirectori.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetIncludeDirectori.body: The method retrieves the include‑directories for a target by first checking a cache; if absent it collects directories from property entries, language‑specific rules, implicit paths (including Swift, ISPC, and interface directories), and Apple framework handling, then stores and returns the accumulated list.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetInstallNameDirFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetInstallNameDirFo.body: Checks whether the build system has an install‑name flag set, and if so, it either returns the install tree path (when the OSX install‑name flag is active) or constructs a directory string based on whether a default path is used, appending a trailing “/”. If the conditions aren’t met it returns an empty string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetInstallNameDirFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetInstallNameDirFo.body: When the `CMAKE_PLATFORM_HAS_INSTALLNAME` option is enabled, the method retrieves the `INSTALL_NAME_DIR` property, substitutes the install‑prefix placeholder with the supplied `installPrefix`, evaluates the resulting expression in the current generator’s context, and if the result is non‑empty it appends a trailing slash. If no property is set it falls back to a default “@rpath/” value; otherwise it simply returns an empty string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetInstallRPATH@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetInstallRPATH@k_Z.body: This function forwards the supplied configuration string to the helper `GetRPATH`, supplying the constant key `"INSTALL_RPATH"`. It returns the helper’s boolean result while writing the resolved path into the referenced `rpath` parameter.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetKindedSources@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetKindedSources@k_.body:
The function returns the pre‑computed list of “kinded” source files for a given configuration string.  
If the object was built without any configuration‑dependent sources it simply returns the single cached entry.  
Otherwise it normalises the requested config name to upper‑case, looks it up in a map, and if an entry exists and is already initialised it returns that; if not, it creates a new entry, calls ComputeKindedSources to populate it, marks it initialised, and returns it.  
If an entry exists but is not yet initialised, the code logs a fatal error and returns an empty structure.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguageExtensio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguageExtensio.body: It fetches and returns the value of the “_EXTENSIONS” property that is associated with the requested language name by delegating to `GetPropertyWithPairedLanguageSupport`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguageStandard.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguageStandard.body: The function looks up a language‑specific standard via `GetLanguageStandardProperty`. If a matching property is found, it returns its value wrapped in a `cmValue`; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguageStandard.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguageStandard.body: The function builds a key from the supplied language and configuration name (upper‑casing the config string), looks it up in an internal map, and if a match is found returns a pointer to the corresponding string; otherwise it falls back to its target source using a key suffixed with “_STANDARD”.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguageStandard.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguageStandard.body: The method simply queries the internal property map for a language‑specific flag that indicates whether the current target requires the standard header for that language. It delegates to `GetPropertyWithPairedLanguageSupport`, passing the key `"_STANDARD_REQUIRED"`. If the property exists and evaluates to true, the function returns true; otherwise it returns false. The function returns a Boolean value that drives downstream code to decide whether the generated C++ sources should include the standard header for the requested language.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguages@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLanguages@k_ZNK1.body: The function gathers the set of programming languages used in the build. It first checks that the target can compile anything; if not, it returns immediately. Otherwise it queries all source files for the target, inserts any non‑empty language identifiers into the output set, and then recursively pulls the language sets from any object‑library targets that are linked to this target, whether those libraries were created via the newer “CMP0026” path or via the legacy approach. This recursive accumulation produces the final set of languages that the target depends on.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLibraryNames@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLibraryNames@k_Z.body: The function builds a collection of file‑name strings that describe all the different artifacts a target may produce. It first checks that the target is not an imported one, then pulls its VERSION and SOVERSION properties to decide whether a soname is required. Using the target’s prefix, base and suffix it fills out the base name, the plain output name, and the on‑disk real name (and, on Apple frameworks, the import variants). It calls helper functions to compute versioned names where needed, and finally returns a struct containing all those names.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkClosure@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkClosure@k_ZN.body: The method returns a pointer to a cached `LinkClosure`. It first checks whether the current target supports source compilation; if not, it returns a static empty instance. Otherwise it normalizes the provided configuration string to upper‑case, looks up the corresponding entry in `LinkClosureMap`, and if missing, builds a new `LinkClosure` by calling `ComputeLinkClosure`, inserts it into the map, and finally returns a pointer to the stored value.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkDepends@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkDepends@k_ZN.body: The method pulls the target’s declared “LINK_DEPENDS” values, builds target‑property entries for each of those items, feeds them through the DAG checker and interface‑registration logic, and finally packages the resolved dependency strings into a result vector that it returns.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkDepends@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkDepends@k_ZN.body:
It copies the dependency list returned by an internal call into a caller‑supplied vector.  
The method takes a reference to a vector of strings, a configuration string, and a language string.  
It first calls its own GetLinkDepends helper with the config and language arguments, obtains a vector of BT\<std::string\> values, reserves space in the result vector, and then emplaces each value’s string into the result by moving the underlying string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkDirectories@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkDirectories@.body: The method computes the list of directories that must be added to the link search path for a target. It first looks up a cached result keyed by the configuration string plus language (with an optional “‑device” suffix when appropriate). If a cache miss occurs, it evaluates the target’s properties—including debug flags and interface requirements—then collects the unique directories into a vector of `BT<std::string>`, stores that result in the cache, and returns it.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkDirectories@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkDirectories@.body: The function returns a list of link‑directories for a given build configuration. Internally it calls a private helper that produces a vector of helper objects (BT), each holding a string; it then reserves space in the supplied vector and copies (moves) each string into that vector. This effectively populates the output vector with the directories that must be used for linking.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.body: The member function returns a pointer to a link implementation that matches the supplied configuration string and the requested link interface. Internally it forwards the request to a second overload, passing `false` for an additional flag argument that controls an optional behavior.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.body: The function verifies the target can compile, selects the appropriate head‑to‑link‑implementation map (usage or normal), fetches the entry for the current object, optionally clears it on a second pass, lazily computes libraries, languages and runtime libraries the first time those flags are unset, and finally returns a pointer to that implementation.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.body: The routine returns a list of generator targets that constitute the closure for a given link‑config. If the current target cannot compile sources, it immediately returns an empty vector. Otherwise it looks up a cached result in `LinkImplClosureMap`. When the entry is not yet finished (`Done==false`), it marks the entry as finished, gathers the link‑implementation libraries via `GetLinkImplementationLibraries`, and for each library item invokes `processILibs` to build up the closure, recording which targets have already been emitted in a set to avoid duplication. Finally, the populated vector is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.body: The function simply forwards the request to a helper that resolves the appropriate libraries: it takes a configuration string and an implementation interface, then calls `GetLinkImplementationLibrariesInternal` with the current object as the target and returns the resulting collection.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.body: The function first resolves which head-to‑implementation map to use (usage or normal requirements). It then, if that map is populated and its first entry isn’t head‑sensitive, picks that head as the current target. It retrieves the corresponding implementation entry, lazily marking its libraries as “done” only when they haven’t been built yet, and triggers the actual library‑population routine. Finally, it returns a pointer to that entry.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInformation@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInformation@.body: The function caches and retrieves configuration‑specific link information. It normalises the configuration string to uppercase, checks an internal map for existing data, and if absent, constructs a new `cmComputeLinkInformation` instance that runs its own `Compute()` routine. After successful creation, it stores the object in the map, then verifies property compatibility before returning a reference to the stored information.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterface@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterface@k_.body: The method forwards the supplied `config` and `head` to an overloaded version of `GetLinkInterface`, passing `false` as a flag, and returns the resulting `cmLinkInterface` pointer.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterface@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterface@k_.body: The function first checks whether the target is an imported target and delegates to the import‑specific helper if so. If the target is not an “executable” that exports symbols, it returns `nullptr`. Otherwise it looks up a previously‑computed link interface in the per‑configuration map. If the map entry is head‑insensitive, the function re‑uses the interface belonging to the first head in the map. It lazily initializes or re‑computes the interface: if the library list is not yet built, it fills it; if the full interface has not yet been built, it builds the rest and the runtime‑specific libraries. Finally it returns a pointer to the interface if it exists, or `nullptr` otherwise.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.body: The method simply forwards the request to `checkInterfacePropertyCompatibility<bool>` with the current object, a property name, a config string, the literal string `"FALSE"`, the enum value `BoolType`, and a `nullptr` flag, and returns whatever boolean that helper returns.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.body: The function is a simple, const helper that forwards its arguments to a generic `checkInterfacePropertyCompatibility` routine. It supplies the current object, two string identifiers (`p` and `config`), a literal `"empty"` to indicate a default key, and the `NumberMaxType` marker, along with a null pointer argument. The result of that internal call – a `const char*` – is returned unchanged.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.body: The function forwards the supplied name‑ and configuration‑strings to `checkInterfacePropertyCompatibility`, supplying a default “empty” marker and a `NumberMinType` flag. It returns whatever that helper returns – a pointer to a character string if the property is found, otherwise `nullptr`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.body: The function receives two strings—`p` and `config`—then delegates to a helper template (`checkInterfacePropertyCompatibility`) that resolves a boolean‑style property value (defaulting to “FALSE”) under a specified property type (`BoolType`). It returns that value as a plain `std::string`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDep.body: The function calls a helper template that verifies whether the current object implements a requested interface string property. It returns the resulting C‑string pointer (or a default “empty” string) once the compatibility check succeeds.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceLib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceLib.body: The function retrieves the cached link‑interface library list for a target. It first checks if the current target is imported, delegating to the imported target’s own interface. For self‑contained executables that do not export any symbols it immediately returns `nullptr`. Otherwise it looks up the appropriate map (usage or normal) for the requested `config`. If the entry is found and is not head‑sensitive it falls back to the head target’s entry. It lazily builds the library list on first access by marking the entry as “done” and invoking `ComputeLinkInterfaceLibraries`. Finally it returns a pointer to the stored list if present, or `nullptr` otherwise.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkOptions::[la.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkOptions::[la.body: The lambda is an inline predicate that tests whether a `BT<std::string>` element’s `Value` equals the sentinel `DL_END`. It performs a simple comparison and returns that boolean result.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkOptions@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkOptions@k_ZN.body: GetLinkOptions looks up a cached list of link‑options for the current configuration and language. If not cached, it builds the list by evaluating the target’s properties, adding interface entries, parsing options, and, when creating a device link, wrapping host‑link options with a wrapper flag. It then replaces placeholder linker prefixes with the real wrapper, stores the result in the cache, and returns the prepared option vector.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkOptions@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkOptions@k_ZN.body: The routine first guards against propagating device‑link options that are inapplicable for an existing policy status. If that guard fails, it exits immediately without touching the output vector. Otherwise it calls an internal helper that returns a temporary list of option strings; it then reserves the destination vector to the exact size of that list and appends each value by move‑constructing them into the result container. The effect is to transfer the filtered list of options into the caller’s vector with minimal copying.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkPIEProperty@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkPIEProperty@.body: The function returns a pointer to a static string that contains a property value retrieved from the configuration. If the retrieved value is the literal “(unset)” or if the policy status is either WARN or OLD, the function returns `nullptr`; otherwise it returns the C‑string pointer to that value.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkerLanguage@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkerLanguage@k.body: The method resolves the current linker language configuration by delegating to its link‑closure; it simply fetches the `LinkerLanguage` value from the closure that corresponds to the supplied configuration string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocalGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocalGenerator@k.body: The function returns the `LocalGenerator` member held by the `cmGeneratorTarget` object. It exposes that member as a read‑only pointer without mutating any internal state, preserving the object's const‑ness. Callers receive the pointer and must account for the possibility that it could be `nullptr`; it is the only way to access the underlying local generator instance.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocation@k_ZNK17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocation@k_ZNK17.body: It returns the fully‑resolved path for the target binary, selecting either `ImportedGetFullPath` or `GetFullPath` based on whether the target is marked as imported, and caches that path in a static local string so the same string reference can be returned on each call.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocationForBuild.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocationForBuild.body: The function constructs the full file‑system path where the current build artifact will be written. If the target has already been imported, it simply pulls that pre‑computed path from the target’s imported path helper. Otherwise, it gathers the base directory from the target’s own directory resolution, optionally prefixes it with a configured “intermediate directory” string (if one is defined), and, on Apple platforms when the target is an app bundle, appends the bundle directory. Finally, it appends the artifact’s full name (including any runtime‑specific suffixes). The resulting string is returned by reference.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetMacContentDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetMacContentDirect.body: The method constructs and returns the full path for a Mac‑specific content bundle. It first obtains a base directory via `GetDirectory(config, artifact)`, appends a trailing slash, then selects whether the bundle should include a full‑level or content‑level subdirectory depending on whether the target framework is an Apple build (`IsFrameworkOnApple()`), and finally calls `BuildBundleDirectory` to assemble the final path string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetManagedType@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetManagedType@k_ZN.body: The function determines whether a generator target should be considered a managed target. It first checks that the target is not a shared library, then distinguishes static libraries as native. For imported targets it defers to the imported info if present. If the target has the `COMMON_LANGUAGE_RUNTIME` property set, that value is used directly. Finally, it defaults to managed only for C#‑only targets; otherwise it marks the target as native.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetManifests@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetManifests@k_ZNK1.body: Iterates over the supplied vector of source‑files, invoking the `IMPLEMENT_VISIT` macro for each entry whose kind matches `SourceKindManifest`, thereby processing and recording the manifest data.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetMaxLanguageStand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetMaxLanguageStand.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the internal `MaxLanguageStandards` map, so callers can inspect the stored language‑standard pairs without copying or mutating the underlying data.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetModuleDefinition.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetModuleDefinition.body: The routine verifies that the target can expose a module definition (shared‑ or module‑library, or an executable with exports). It normalizes the supplied config string to upper‑case, then searches an internal map keyed by that string. If the entry is missing, it constructs a fresh `ModuleDefinitionInfo` via `ComputeModuleDefinitionInfo`, inserts the freshly created object into the cache, and finally returns a pointer to the cached entry. If the target type check fails, it simply returns `nullptr`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetModuleDefinition.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetModuleDefinition.body: The function traverses the stored sources marked as module‑definition files, and appends each matching file to the supplied vector `data`. The macro `IMPLEMENT_VISIT(SourceKindModuleDefinition)` expands to the logic that performs this visit, so in practice the routine simply populates the vector with those source files.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetName@k_ZNK17cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetName@k_ZNK17cmGe.body: The function forwards the request to its contained `Target` object: it simply returns a const reference to the string returned by `Target::GetName()`. Because the method is marked `const`, it guarantees that calling it does not modify any state and that no copy of the string is made – the reference is only valid as long as the underlying `Target` instance remains alive.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetObjectDirectory@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetObjectDirectory@.body: The method builds the directory string for object files: it asks the global generator to expand the base object directory using the supplied config string, then on Apple systems replaces a placeholder token with the real “Objects‑normal” path so that build and export scripts receive the concrete directory. The function simply returns that computed path.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetObjectLibrariesC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetObjectLibrariesC.body: The routine walks the target’s source entries looking for strings that begin with the marker `$<TARGET_OBJECTS:` and end with a `>` character. For each such entry it pulls the embedded object‑library name, resolves it against the local generator’s available targets, and if a match is found appends the corresponding target to the supplied vector.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetObjectName@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetObjectName@k_ZN1.body: The function takes a pointer to a `cmSourceFile`, calls `ComputeObjectMapping()` to ensure its internal map is up‑to‑date, then returns a const reference to the string stored in `Objects` keyed by that file. This avoids copying the string; callers must keep the returned reference valid for the lifetime of the `cmGeneratorTarget` object.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetObjectSources@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetObjectSources@k_.body: The routine registers new source files for a specific build‑mode configuration. It first guards against repeated work by consulting a set of already‑visited configurations. For each file pointer in the provided list it inserts that pointer into an internal collection, then forwards that collection to a helper to resolve filenames. Finally, it marks the configuration as handled.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetOutputInfo@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetOutputInfo@k_ZNK.body: The function returns a pointer to the cached `OutputInfo` for a given configuration string. It first excludes imported or synthetic targets, returning `nullptr` for them. It verifies that the target has well‑defined output files, issuing an error if not. For a new configuration it inserts an empty entry in the cache map to guard against recursive calls, computes the output, import, and PDB directories, updates the map entry, and finally returns the populated `OutputInfo`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetOutputName@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetOutputName@k_ZNK.body: The function builds and caches a string that identifies the output artifact for a particular build target. It first checks a map keyed by the requested configuration and artifact type; if absent, it constructs a sequence of candidate property names (using the artifact type and the upper‑cased configuration string), then queries the generator’s property system to resolve the first available value. If none is found, it falls back to a default name. The result is stored in the map; if the map entry is already empty, the code treats this as a recursive call and logs a fatal error to avoid infinite recursion. The function finally returns the cached or newly computed output name.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetOutputTargetType.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetOutputTargetType.body:
The function maps an artifact type and generator type to a target‑string constant. It first normalises the artifact when the generator is Apple or Xcode, then branches on the current generator type:

* `SHARED_LIBRARY` – on DLL platforms it returns `"RUNTIME"` for a runtime artifact or `"ARCHIVE"` for an import library; on other platforms it returns `"LIBRARY"` or `"ARCHIVE"`.
* `STATIC_LIBRARY` always returns `"ARCHIVE"`.
* `MODULE_LIBRARY` returns `"LIBRARY"` for runtime artifacts and `"ARCHIVE"` for import libraries.
* `OBJECT_LIBRARY` returns `"OBJECT"`.
* `EXECUTABLE` returns `"RUNTIME"` for runtime artifacts and `"ARCHIVE"` for import libraries.

If no case matches, an empty string is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPDBDirectory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPDBDirectory@k_Z.body: It returns the path stored in the `OutputInfo` structure that the object knows about the current configuration. If the lookup succeeds, the string field `PdbDir` is returned; if the lookup fails, an empty string is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPDBName@k_ZNK17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPDBName@k_ZNK17c.body: This method assembles potential property keys from a supplied config string, attempts to resolve a matching property value, and returns a fully‑qualified path constructed from the resolved value (or a default base name) appended with “.pdb”. It simply queries a property bag for keys such as “PDB_NAME_<CONFIG>” and “PDB_NAME”, falling back to a default base if none are found.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPDBOutputName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPDBOutputName@k_.body: The `GetPDBOutputName` method constructs a fallback name for a runtime binary artifact. It starts with a base name derived from a generic output name routine, then optionally prepends a “PDB_NAME_” prefix tied to the supplied `config` string (converted to uppercase). Finally, it iterates over the potential property keys, using the first non‑empty property value found as the final name; if none of those properties exist, it keeps the original base name. This logic allows a configuration‑specific override of the default artifact name while preserving a sensible default when no override is supplied.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPackageReference.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPackageReference.body: Collects any VS‑package references defined in the current generator’s property system and returns them in a std::vector of strings.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchCreateCompile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchCreateCompile.body: The function builds a string of compiler‑options for creating a pre‑compiled header. It first checks a cache keyed by the language, configuration, and architecture; if the entry is new, it constructs the options list, optionally appending a warning flag or a template‑instantiation flag when the corresponding properties are set, and always appends the standard PCH‑creation option. After that, it performs a string replace on the placeholders `<PCH_HEADER>` and `<PCH_FILE>` with the resolved header and file paths, then returns the assembled option list.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchFile::[lambda.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchFile::[lambda.body: The lambda takes a string reference and an extension string. It searches for the last period in the input; if found, it removes the suffix after that dot, then appends the supplied extension and returns the new string. If no dot is present, it simply concatenates the extension to the original string. The code as written contains two omissions: the parameter name `str` is missing, and the lambda is not captured correctly (`std::string` misspelling as `std::string`). Once those are fixed, the logic behaves as described.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchFile@k_ZN17cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchFile@k_ZN17cm.body: The method inserts a new entry into the internal map keyed by `language + config + arch`. If the entry is new, it builds a pre‑compiled header filename: it first looks up the extension via `Makefile->GetSafeDefinition("CMAKE_PCH_EXTENSION")`; if the `CMAKE_LINK_PCH` option is enabled, it may replace the extension (or path) via the helper lambda. If the `PRECOMPILE_HEADERS_REUSE_FROM` property is set, it re‑queries the associated generator target to reuse an existing PCH. Finally, if no special extension is defined, it falls back to the default header name (`GetPchHeader`) and appends the extension. The computed path is stored in the map and returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchFileObject@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchFileObject@k_.body: It builds (or re‑uses) a PCH file name from the supplied config, language and arch combo. If the language string isn’t one of the supported tags or a file can’t be produced, it returns an empty string; otherwise it records the generated name in an internal map and returns the full filename.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchHeader@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchHeader@k_ZNK1.body: The function builds or re‑uses a pre‑compiled header for the requested language and architecture. It first checks that the language is supported (C, CXX, OBJC, OBJCXX) and that the build isn’t globally disabled. It then determines whether an existing PCH can be reused; if not, it gathers the list of headers that must be included, writes a new header file in the generator’s support directory (adding a language‑specific extension), optionally prefixed with the architecture name, and wraps the includes in optional prologue/epilogue definitions. The file is written to a temporary path and atomically moved to the final location if it changed, then the function returns the path of the generated PCH file (or an empty string if none was created).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchSource@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchSource@k_ZNK1.body: The routine first checks that the supplied language is one of the accepted C/Objective‑C variants; if not, it returns an empty string. When a language is accepted it records a unique key in a map (the key is the concatenated language‑config‑arch string) and, if this key did not exist yet, it creates the corresponding pre‑compiled header file. The filename is built by selecting an extension from a language‑to‑extension map that differs for GCC versus non‑GCC builds, and may include the architecture suffix. If a “reuse‑from” target is specified, the search for a common pre‑compiled header on that target is performed. When the header file is not yet present the function writes a minimal comment header, copies the header to the final path, and finally returns the path string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchUseCompileOpt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPchUseCompileOpt.body:
The function first looks up a cache entry keyed by the concatenated string (language+config+arch); if the entry does not exist it creates one with an empty string.  
If the entry is new, it builds a string of compiler options: it appends a definition that turns on PCH‑warning handling (if the *PCH_WARN_INVALID* property is true), appends a property‑defined option string that may come from the *<language>_COMPILE_OPTIONS_USE_PCH* property, and finally replaces the placeholders `<PCH_HEADER>` and `<PCH_FILE>` with the real header and file names produced by *GetPchHeader* and *GetPchFile*.  
The resulting string is stored in the cache and returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0003` function retrieves the current status for the policy identified by the “CMP0003” target identifier. It queries the internal policy table via the macro‑driven `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY(DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY)` routine, extracts the associated status flag, and returns it as an integer (1 for enabled, 0 for disabled) or an enumeration value depending on the internal implementation. The function performs validation of the supplied target code, looks up the corresponding entry in the policy repository, and propagates the result back to the caller.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function `GetPolicyStatusCMP0004` pulls a policy’s status by iterating over each target policy via the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY` macro. It constructs the appropriate target policy instance and returns the resulting status value without performing any heavy‑weight logic.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0008` function queries the current state of the CMP‑0008 policy and returns an enum (or integer) indicating whether it is enabled, disabled, or pending. It performs a simple lookup on the internal policy table, performs no side‑effects, and guarantees thread‑safety.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The routine simply interrogates the internal policy registry for the CMP0020 target and returns a status flag indicating whether that policy is currently enabled, disabled, or in an intermediate state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0021` routine is a read‑only accessor that, when invoked, returns the current state of the policy identified by the CMP0021 identifier. It performs a quick lookup of the internal policy registry, checks the `enabled` flag for that policy entry, and then translates that flag into a friendly status descriptor (e.g., “Active”/“Inactive”). No mutating side‑effects occur; the function simply queries and reports the status for the caller’s policy context.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The GetPolicyStatusCMP0022 function returns the current status of the CMP0022 target policy. It pulls the status from the system’s policy registry by using the DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY macro to register the target policy in the appropriate collection, then looks up the policy’s current state and returns that value.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0027` function performs a read‑only lookup for the CMP0027 policy entry in the internal policy repository. It accepts a policy identifier and returns a status flag indicating whether the policy is enabled, disabled, or in an error state. Internally it verifies that the target policy key exists, looks up the corresponding record in the cached policy map, and translates any error codes into a standardized status enum before returning it to the caller.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: GetPolicyStatusCMP0037 checks a target policy’s current state and returns the corresponding status value. It iterates over the installed policies via the CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY macro and produces the status for the matching target.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function `GetPolicyStatusCMP0038` is a read‑only routine that queries the current policy state for the CMP0038 target. It pulls the relevant flag bits from the internal policy table and translates them into a single status code (e.g., `ENABLED`, `DISABLED`, or `UNKNOWN`). It performs no side‑effects—only reads the policy data—and returns that status to the caller.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function checks the status of the CMP0041 policy for a given target, wrapping the logic in the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY(DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY)` macro to apply the check uniformly across all declared target policies.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: Retrieves the current status of the CMP0042 target policy from the internal policy store and exposes it through a const reference.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0046` function is a public const helper that uses the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY` macro to generate the logic for each declared policy. It returns the current status of the target policy in a single call.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The routine accepts a target policy identifier, performs a quick lookup in the internal policy registry, and returns the corresponding status object while leaving all state unchanged.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function `GetPolicyStatusCMP0060` is a const accessor that retrieves the current status of the CMP0060 target policy. It invokes the `DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY` macro to obtain the policy object, then checks whether the policy is valid and whether the caller has the required permissions. If the policy is missing or the caller lacks rights, it returns a predefined error status; otherwise it returns the policy’s active flag. The implementation relies on a read‑only lock to guarantee thread safety and uses a static cache to avoid repeated lookups.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: It’s a const member that, given a policy identifier, walks the pre‑generated list of target policies (via the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY(DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY)` macro) and returns the stored status for the matching policy. If no policy matches, it returns a sentinel value (e.g. “unknown”).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function retrieves the current status of the CMP0065 target policy. It validates the policy context, populates a status structure via the DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY macro, and returns an enum indicating whether the policy is enabled, disabled, or in an error state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: GetPolicyStatusCMP0068 declares a target policy via CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY and returns the current status flag for the CMP0068 policy.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function iterates over each target policy via the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY(DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY)` macro and returns a Boolean flag indicating whether the CMP0069 policy is enabled for that target.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function `GetPolicyStatusCMP0073` simply queries the current state of a specific policy identified by the constant `CMP0073`. It performs a quick lookup in the internal policy registry (using the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY` macro) and returns a status flag that indicates whether that policy is active, inactive, or in an intermediate state. The implementation relies on a single read‐only lookup operation, so it executes in O(1) time.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0076` function is a public, read‑only routine that inspects a target‑policy object (typically a global or context‑specific instance) and returns a status code indicating whether the requested policy is currently active, inactive, or in an error state. It pulls the relevant policy flag from the internal data store via the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY` macro, performs any required validation (e.g., checking that the policy object is initialized), and emits the final status as a simple enum or integer constant. The function itself is deliberately lightweight—no side‑effects beyond status reporting—and is intended for quick status checks in higher‑level decision‑making logic.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function `GetPolicyStatusCMP0081` iterates over each declared target policy (via the macro `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY(DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY)`) and returns the corresponding status. It essentially maps the policy identifier to its current state, returning a status value without mutating any internal state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function invokes the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY` macro with the policy name passed via `DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY`, retrieves the associated policy instance and returns its current status as a const reference.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: GetPolicyStatusCMP0095 returns the current compliance flag for the CMP‑0095 policy by inspecting the internal policy registry and translating the stored state into a status enum, without mutating any state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0099` routine fetches the status flag for the policy identified by the CMP0099 marker. It receives a single target identifier, looks it up in the internal policy table, and returns a status code indicating whether the policy is active, pending, or revoked. The routine relies on the macro `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY` to iterate over each declared target policy (via `DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY`), pulling the relevant status flag from the policy structure and returning it as an `int` (or enum) value for the caller to act upon.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: GetPolicyStatusCMP0104 retrieves the current activation state of a target policy by querying the policy registry. It accepts a policy identifier, performs an O(1) lookup into the in‑memory cache, and maps the retrieved flag to a well‑defined status enum (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, EXPIRED). If the record is missing, it throws a lightweight `PolicyNotFoundException`. The function is thread‑safe and avoids any external I/O beyond the cache lookup.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function `GetPolicyStatusCMP0105` is a read‑only accessor that returns the current status flag for the target policy identified by the constant `CMP0105`. Internally it uses the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY(DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY)` macro to register the policy with the system’s policy map at compile‑time. When invoked, the function simply looks up the policy’s entry in that map and returns a boolean (or an enum value) indicating whether the policy is enabled, pending, or blocked, without performing any mutable state changes.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function `GetPolicyStatusCMP0108` simply looks up the status flag for the “CMP0108” policy in the current context and returns that flag (or an error code if the lookup fails). It uses the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY(DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY)` macro to access the policy table, so no additional plumbing is required.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: GetPolicyStatusCMP0112 is a const member function that queries the current status of a target policy identified by the macro `DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY`. It takes a policy identifier (typically an enum value) and returns an enum or flag indicating whether the policy is active, inactive, or in transition. The function ultimately performs a read‑only lookup against the internal policy table without modifying any state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function `GetPolicyStatusCMP0113` is a const getter that checks whether the specified policy (identified by the macro `DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY`) is currently active. It invokes the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY` macro to instantiate the policy's runtime representation and returns the policy’s current status (active/inactive) as a simple boolean or enum value.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0119` function is a read‑only accessor that, given a target identifier, returns the current status code for that policy. It pulls the status from the in‑memory policy table and performs a quick bounds check before delivering the value.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: GetPolicyStatusCMP0131 retrieves the current status for the CMP0131 policy identifier. It accepts a target policy handle, validates its existence, and returns the corresponding status code from the internal policy store.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0142` member returns a status value indicating whether the policy identified by the caller’s policy‑id is in effect. Internally, it walks the collection of target‑policy objects that were registered via the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY(DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY)` macro, checks the corresponding policy instance (often a singleton), and returns its current operational state (enabled/disabled/unknown). The function itself is a const‑qualified accessor; it performs no side‑effects and simply forwards the internal state to the caller.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The function `GetPolicyStatusCMP0154` retrieves the current enforcement state for the CMP0154 policy. It examines the configured policy targets—those injected via the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY(DECLARE_TARGET_POLICY)` macro—and returns a status flag indicating whether the policy is enabled, disabled, or pending for each relevant target. The routine is purely const‑qualified, meaning it does not modify internal state and only reads the policy table; callers can safely invoke it from any context to query the policy’s operational state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0.body: The `GetPolicyStatusCMP0155` function queries the current state of a specific target policy—CMP0155—within the system. It validates whether the policy is enabled, disabled, or in a transitional state and returns that status via a dedicated enum. The function operates in constant‑time and simply forwards the status to the caller without mutating any internal state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPostBuildCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPostBuildCommand.body: The method simply forwards a request for the post‑build command list to the internal target object and returns the resulting vector unchanged; it is a read‑only accessor that passes through to `Target->GetPostBuildCommands()` and yields the stored `std::vector<cmCustomCommand>` reference.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPreBuildCommands.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPreBuildCommands.body: The function simply forwards a const reference to the internal vector of pre‑build custom commands held by the target object; it does not modify data and guarantees the caller sees the underlying command list unchanged.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPreLinkCommands@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPreLinkCommands@.body: It forwards the request to the underlying target and returns the const reference to the vector of custom commands that target holds.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPrecompileHeader.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPrecompileHeader.body: The function lazily builds and caches a list of pre‑compile headers for a specific configuration‑language pair. It first checks the `PrecompileHeadersCache`; if the entry exists, that cached vector is returned immediately. When no cache entry exists, it constructs a set of unique options, runs a DAG‑based evaluation of target properties (via `EvaluatedTargetPropertyEntries`), applies interface additions, and then processes all options (via `processOptions`). The resulting vector of `BT<std::string>` objects is stored in `PrecompileHeadersCache` keyed by a `ConfigAndLanguage` pair before being returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetProperty@k_ZNK17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetProperty@k_ZNK17.body: The method first queries a property via `cmTargetPropertyComputer`. If that lookup succeeds it returns the value; if a fatal error flag is set it returns `nullptr`; otherwise it falls back to the target’s own property lookup.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPropertyAsBool@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPropertyAsBool@k.body: The function simply forwards the call to the underlying target object and returns the boolean result that the target reports for the requested property.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPropertyKeys@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPropertyKeys@k_Z.body: Retrieves every key from the target’s property dictionary by delegating to the underlying property interface and returning the resulting list.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPropertyWithPair.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPropertyWithPair.body: The method attempts to fetch a property value by concatenating the requested language and suffix. If that lookup fails, it falls back to a predefined “paired” language mapping—e.g. using a C‑based key for “OBJC”, or a C++/GPU‑variant key for “OBJCXX”, “CUDA”, or “HIP”. Once a value is found, it is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetRPATH@k_ZNK17cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetRPATH@k_ZNK17cmG.body: The method attempts to resolve a property value for a generator target. It first retrieves the value via `GetProperty`. If the property is not found, it immediately returns `false`. Otherwise it feeds that value into `cmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate`, passing the local generator context and the supplied configuration string. The result of the evaluation is assigned to `rpath`, and the method returns `true` to signal success.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetRuntimeLinkLibra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetRuntimeLinkLibra.body: The function returns the runtime link library name for the current target, resolving it from a language‑specific default if present. It first fetches the default definition (`CMAKE_<lang>_RUNTIME_LIBRARY_DEFAULT`). If that is empty, it simply returns an empty string. Otherwise, it checks whether the target already has a `RUNTIME_LIBRARY` property for that language; if not, it uses the default. Finally, it evaluates any generator expressions in that value and normalises the result to upper‑case before returning it.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSOName@k_ZNK17cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSOName@k_ZNK17cm.body: The function resolves the file name for the shared‑object that a target will link against. It first checks whether the target was imported; if so, it looks up the import’s meta‑data. If the import declares no soname, it falls back to the file name of the library file. When the import comes from a framework on Apple it prefers a version‑tagged framework name; otherwise it strips a “@rpath/” prefix when present. If the target is not imported, it simply returns the name from the current build’s library map, selecting either the shared‑object name for a runtime binary or the import‑library name for other artifacts.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSafeProperty@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSafeProperty@k_Z.body: The GetSafeProperty method simply forwards the caller’s string key to GetProperty and returns the resulting string reference unchanged. It is a `const` member, so it guarantees it won’t modify the object state, but it performs no input validation or exception handling beyond what GetProperty does. The method’s name implies safety, yet the implementation itself contains no defensive checks, so callers must ensure that the supplied key is valid and that the underlying property is present; otherwise the call may throw or produce an invalid reference.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceDepends@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceDepends@k_.body: The function returns a pointer to the vector of source‑file pointers that the given file depends on. It looks up the file in the `SourceDepends` map; if the entry exists, the address of its `Depends` member is returned; otherwise `nullptr` is returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFilePaths@.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFiles@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFiles@k_ZN.body:
The function gathers a list of source‑file objects for a given configuration string.  
If the global generator has not yet completed its “configure‑done” phase, it walks through the file paths returned by `GetSourceFilePaths`, creates (or retrieves) a source‑file for each distinct path, and pushes it into a result vector.  
When configuration is finished, it simply returns the pre‑collected sources from `GetKindedSources`. The routine guarantees no duplicate entries by tracking already‑added files in a set.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFiles@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFiles@k_ZN.body: The function retrieves a list of source‑file pointers for a given configuration and appends them into the caller‑supplied vector. It first calls a private helper to get the data, then reserves enough space in the destination vector and copies each pointer in turn.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFilesWitho.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFilesWitho.body: It returns the list of source files whose `ObjectLibrary` string is empty, filtering the output of `GetKindedSources` by checking `GetObjectLibrary().empty()` before adding each source to the result vector.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFilesWitho.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFilesWitho.body: Retrieves all source‑file pointers that belong to the current generator but exclude those that are part of an object‑library. It obtains a temporary list from the helper `GetSourceFilesWithoutObjectLibraries(config)`, reserves the destination vector, and copies each pointer into `files`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceObjectLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceObjectLibr.body: Collects external source files specified in the configuration, resolves each file’s library to a matching generator target, and returns the set of those target objects.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourcesProperty@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourcesProperty@.body: The function collects the strings returned by each source entry, concatenates them into a single string using `cmList::to_string`, and returns that string wrapped in a `cmValue`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetStaticLibraryLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetStaticLibraryLin.body: The routine assembles a list of options for static‑library linking. It looks up the property named “STATIC_LIBRARY_OPTIONS”, turns each value into a `TargetPropertyEntry` via `CreateTargetPropertyEntry`, gathers them in `EvaluatedTargetPropertyEntries`, and feeds that collection into `processOptions` which deduplicates entries into `uniqueOptions` before appending the resulting `BT<std::string>` items into `result`. Finally it returns that vector.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetStaticLibraryLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetStaticLibraryLin.body: The function gathers link‑options for a static library by first invoking the class’s own `GetStaticLibraryLinkOptions(config, language)` helper, collecting the resulting strings into a temporary vector. It then reserves space in the output vector to avoid reallocations and copies each option into `result` via `emplace_back`, transferring ownership of the string value with `std::move`. The caller ends up with a vector populated with all the library’s link options.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSupportDirectory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSupportDirectory.body: It concatenates the binary directory with the generator’s name, appending either “_dir” on VMS or “.dir” otherwise.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetObjectName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetObjectName.body: The routine accepts a configuration string, collects every source file that belongs to the current target, and then resolves the corresponding object‑file names. It first gathers the sources, maps each to its intended object name via `ComputeObjectFilenames`, and finally appends every resulting name into the supplied vector. It also appends relative paths for any ISP‑generated outputs that belong under the target’s object directory.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetSourceFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetSourceFile.body:
The function `GetTargetSourceFileFlags` returns a `SourceFileFlags` structure for a given `cmSourceFile`.  
- It first attempts to find an existing entry in `SourceFlagsMap`.  
- If present, the stored flags are returned.  
- Otherwise, it examines the file’s `MACOSX_PACKAGE_LOCATION` property:  
  * If the property equals `"Resources"`, the file is classified as a resource; if resource stripping is enabled, the `MacFolder` is cleared.  
  * If the property begins with `"Resources/"`, the file is treated as a deep resource and the prefix is stripped.  
  * Otherwise the file is marked as a regular “MacContent”.  
- The resulting flags structure is then returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetVersion@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetVersion@k_.body: The routine pulls a property value, attempts to interpret it as a dotted‑three‑digit version string (major.minor.patch), and, if the parsing succeeds, writes the parsed numbers into the supplied references; otherwise the references stay at zero.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetVersion@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetVersion@k_.body: The function retrieves the target’s version numbers. It calls a private overload of `GetTargetVersion`, passing the string `"VERSION"` and three references. The caller passes `major` and `minor` by reference and receives a third value in a local variable `patch`. The function itself does not modify any class members because it is marked `const`; it only forwards the request to the internal helper. The local `patch` variable holds the patch component of the version but is not used further in the current implementation.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetVersionFal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetTargetVersionFal.body: Retrieves the major, minor and patch values by first trying the primary property and, if that property is unavailable, using the fallback property.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetType@k_ZNK17cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetType@k_ZNK17cmGe.body: The method forwards the request to the encapsulated target object and returns its `GetType()` result, which is an enum value of type `cmStateEnums::TargetType`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetUtilities@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetUtilities@k_ZNK1.body: Returns a constant reference to the set of <string, bool> pairs that the internal `Target` object exposes through its own `GetUtilities()` method. The function simply forwards that call, preserving const‑ness and avoiding any copying or modification of the underlying data.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetUtilityItems@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetUtilityItems@k_Z.body: The method lazily populates a set of cmLinkItem objects the first time it is called. It queries GetUtilities() to obtain a collection of string‑flag pairs, then for each pair it looks up an associated generator target via FindGeneratorTargetToUse. If a target exists, it inserts a link item referencing that target; otherwise it inserts a plain item constructed from the pair’s data. Subsequent calls simply return the already‑built set.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasContextDependent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasContextDependent.body: The method simply returns whether the internal flag `SourcesAreContextDependent` equals `Tribool::True`. If that flag is set, the function returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasExplicitObjectNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasExplicitObjectNa.body: The method calls `ComputeObjectMapping()` to ensure the internal map is populated, then checks whether the provided `cmSourceFile` key exists in the `ExplicitObjectName` map and returns `true` if found, otherwise `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasImplibGNUtoMS@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasImplibGNUtoMS@k_.body: The method simply returns true when both the current target has a named import library for the supplied configuration string and the property flag `"GNUtoMS"` is set to true. If either check fails, it returns false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasImportLibrary@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasImportLibrary@k_.body: The function decides whether an import library needs to be produced by checking that the target is a DLL‑style platform with exported symbols, that it is not a purely managed assembly, and that any necessary stub‑generation flags (both global and per‑makefile) allow it to be enabled. It also honors Apple text‑stub support when appropriate.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasKnownRuntimeArti.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasKnownRuntimeArti.body: Determines whether a generator target can resolve a location for a runtime artifact identified by a config string. It first confirms the target is a runtime binary; if the target isn’t, it returns false. If the target is imported, it fetches the corresponding import record; the method returns true only when that record exists and its `Location` field is not empty.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasLinkDependencyFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasLinkDependencyFi.body: The function returns true only when the target is a link‑able type (executable, shared, or module library), the “LINK_DEPENDS_NO_SHARED” property is not set, and both the generic and language‑specific dependency‑use flags (e.g. CMAKE_LINK_DEPENDS_USE_LINKER and CMAKE_<LANG>_LINK_DEPENDS_USE_LINKER) are defined and enabled in the makefile. If any of those conditions fails, it returns false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasMacOSXRpathInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasMacOSXRpathInsta.body: The function caches whether a specific target has the “MacOSXRpathInstallNameDir” property for a given configuration string. It first looks up the target in a per‑config cache; if present, it returns that stored result. Otherwise, it computes the value via `DetermineHasMacOSXRpathInstallNameDir`, saves it in the cache under the target key, and returns it.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasPackageReference.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasPackageReference.body: It checks whether the target is part of the build system and holds any package references.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasSOName@k_ZNK17cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HasSOName@k_ZNK17cm.body: The method confirms that the current target is a shared library that is permitted to use a soname, by ensuring it’s type is `SHARED_LIBRARY`, that the `NO_SONAME` flag isn’t override it, and that the makefile’s current linker language enables the soname flag.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveBuildTreeRPATH@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveBuildTreeRPATH@.body: The function first short‑circuits if the “SKIP_BUILD_RPATH” flag is set, in which case it returns `false`. It then attempts to resolve a build‑path string; if that succeeds it immediately returns `true`. If no path is found it falls back to the link‑implementation libraries lookup: it returns `true` only if that lookup yields a non‑empty library list. If neither source supplies a path or libraries, it finally returns `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveCxx20ModuleSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveCxx20ModuleSour.body: The method is a public, const member that returns a bool and takes a single `const std::string&` parameter. It’s intended to perform a simple truth test – for example, an equality or validity check – against the supplied string. The implementation details are omitted, so the exact condition it evaluates cannot be determined from the declaration alone.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveCxx20ModuleSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveCxx20ModuleSour.body: The lambda receives a file‑set name; it retrieves the corresponding file‑set from the target. If the set is missing, it reports an error via the supplied pointer (or internally) and returns `false`. Otherwise it checks whether the file‑set’s type string equals `"CXX_MODULES"` (the literal string) and returns that comparison result. This helper is used to confirm that a named file‑set actually represents a C++ module set.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveCxx20ModuleSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveCxx20ModuleSour.body: The function iterates over the target’s file‑set names; for each name it looks up the corresponding `FileSet`. If a lookup fails it records an explanatory message (via the optional `errorMessage` argument or by firing an internal‑error message). When a set is found it checks whether its type equals the special string `"CXX_MODULES"` and returns `true` only if at least one set matches that type, otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveCxxModuleSuppor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveCxxModuleSuppor.body: The function verifies that the C++ language is enabled, that a default C++ standard has been defined, that an explicit standard level of at least C++20 is requested, and that the requisite scan‑dependency rule is available. If all these conditions hold it returns **Supported**; otherwise it indicates the missing prerequisite with one of the four error flags (`MissingCxx`, `NoCxx20`, `MissingRule`).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.body: The `operator()` member simply takes a read‑only reference to a `BT<cmSourceFile*>` collection and returns a `bool`. In practice it’s used throughout the codebase as a lightweight helper that examines the supplied `BT` and reports whether a particular condition is satisfied (e.g., whether a certain file pointer appears in the container). Because it is marked `const`, it guarantees that the underlying object is not mutated while performing that check.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.body: The `operator()` function serves as a lightweight validator for the provided `AllConfigSource` object. It inspects the source’s fields, verifies required constraints, and returns a simple `true` or `false` flag indicating whether the configuration passes the internal checks.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.body: The lambda is a simple predicate that accepts a `BT<cmSourceFile*>` reference and returns `true` only when the contained `cmSourceFile` reports its language string equal to `"Fortran"`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.body: Returns true when the source’s language equals “Fortran”.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.body: operator() is a const member function that receives a pointer to a `cmGeneratorTarget`. It performs a check/validation based on that target and returns `true` or `false` to signal whether the operation succeeded.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources:.body: It captures the `config` object and returns true when the supplied `cmGeneratorTarget` reports having Fortran sources for that configuration.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources@.body: The function checks whether any source files for the current target or any of its linked source‑object libraries are written in Fortran. It first queries the target’s own source files; if none are Fortran, it walks the associated source‑object libraries and asks each of them if they contain Fortran sources, returning true as soon as one is found.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveFortranSources@.body:
The method walks the target’s source list, looking for a Fortran source.  
If none are found, it walks through each included generator configuration’s libraries, recursing into those targets until one reports a Fortran source or none remain.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveInstallTreeRPAT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveInstallTreeRPAT.body: This const member queries whether an install path has already been set up and is not deliberately ignored. It reads the current configuration via `GetInstallRPATH`, fills a string, and returns `true` only when that string is non‑empty and the global skip flag `"CMAKE_SKIP_INSTALL_RPATH"` is not asserted.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveWellDefinedOutp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::HaveWellDefinedOutp.body: The method simply verifies that the target’s state type belongs to one of the supported output categories (static, shared, module, object library, or executable).
