If the current type matches any of those enumerated values, it returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ImportInfo::ImportI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ImportInfo::ImportI.body: The `ImportInfo` function reads configuration or metadata from a predefined source (e.g., a file, database, or environment variables) and returns a structured object containing key attributes such as name, version, timestamps, and other relevant metadata. It performs validation checks on the retrieved data and populates the internal model used by other components.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ImportedGetLocation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ImportedGetLocation.body: This function retrieves the complete filesystem path for the target that was imported. It first ensures the current object is indeed an imported instance, then delegates to the target object’s `ImportedGetFullPath` method, passing along the supplied configuration string and specifying that the requested artifact type is a runtime‑binary. The returned string is the absolute path at which the imported runtime binary will reside.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsAIX@k_ZNK17cmGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsAIX@k_ZNK17cmGene.body: Delegates to the underlying `Target` object to determine whether it implements the AIX interface.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsAppBundleOnApple@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsAppBundleOnApple@.body: This const member simply forwards the query to its underlying `Target` object and returns the resulting boolean value.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsApple@k_ZNK17cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsApple@k_ZNK17cmGe.body: The function forwards the check to its internal target object and returns that result. It simply returns the value of `Target->IsApple()` without any additional processing.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsBundleOnApple@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsBundleOnApple@k_Z.body: The function reports whether the current build target is an Apple bundle by delegating three specific checks – framework, app bundle, and CF‑bundle – and returns true if any of them succeeds.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsCFBundleOnApple@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsCFBundleOnApple@k.body: The method reports whether the current object is a library module that runs on Apple platforms and has its “BUNDLE” property enabled. It returns true only when the type equals MODULE_LIBRARY, the instance is Apple‑specific, and the “BUNDLE” flag is set to true.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsCSharpOnly@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsCSharpOnly@k_ZNK1.body: The method checks whether the current build target can only be built with C# sources. It first confirms the target type is one of shared, static, or executable. Then it gathers all compile languages that the target can use; if a specific linker‑language property is present it is added. Finally, it returns true only when the resulting set contains exactly one language and that language is “CSharp”.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsChrpathUsed@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsChrpathUsed@k_ZNK.body: The function examines the target’s type, whether an install rule exists, and various CMake flags (e.g. CMAKE_SKIP_RPATH, BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH, CMAKE_NO_BUILTIN_CHRPATH). If the target is a shared/module/executable library that installs and the platform supports an install name, and the linker language uses a separator flag, the function returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsDLLPlatform@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsDLLPlatform@k_ZNK.body: It returns a boolean indicating whether the target platform is a DLL, delegating the check to the underlying `Target` object.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsDeprecated@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsDeprecated@k_ZNK1.body: The method returns true when the object’s “DEPRECATION” property contains any value (i.e. when the property is non‑empty); otherwise it returns false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsDeviceLink@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsDeviceLink@k_ZNK1.body: Returns the current state of the internal DeviceLink flag, indicating whether the device is considered linked.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsDotNetSdkTarget@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsDotNetSdkTarget@k.body: The function simply returns whether the `DOTNET_SDK` property is set on the current object—i.e., it checks that property is non‑empty and returns that boolean value.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsExecutableWithExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsExecutableWithExp.body: The method simply returns the result of the underlying target’s `IsExecutableWithExports()` call, exposing that information to callers of `cmGeneratorTarget`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsFortranBuildingIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsFortranBuildingIn.body: Checks whether the object’s Fortran intrinsic‑module flag is turned on and returns that value (defaulting false if the property isn’t set).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsFrameworkOnApple@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsFrameworkOnApple@.body: The method simply forwards the call to its `Target` object: it returns the boolean value returned by `Target->IsFrameworkOnApple()`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsIPOEnabled@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsIPOEnabled@k_ZNK1.body: The routine consults the target’s feature flag “INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION” and the current compiler‑specific flags to decide whether IPO should be enabled. It short‑circuits all but supported languages (C, C++, CUDA, Fortran) and, for CUDA, ensures the separate CUDA architecture and separate compilation flags are on. It then examines the policy status CMP0069: if the policy is old or warn and the legacy IPO option is enabled, the function can return true; otherwise it emits a warning or error and returns false. The function ultimately returns true only when all feature checks, language, policy, and CMake/compiler support tests pass; otherwise it returns false or reports a fatal error.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsImported@k_ZNK17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsImported@k_ZNK17c.body: Returns the result of the wrapped target’s IsImported() call. The method simply forwards the call to the underlying Target object and returns that value unchanged. It has no side‑effects and guarantees the returned boolean is identical to the target’s status.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsImportedFramework.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsImportedFramework.body: The method checks that the object is both Apple‑targeted and imported, and that its type is one of the library kinds. It then resolves the location using the supplied configuration string (defaulting to a pre‑configured value when empty), and finally calls a helper that determines whether the resolved path points into a framework directory.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsImportedGloballyV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsImportedGloballyV.body: It just forwards the check to the Target object: the const member returns the value of `Target->IsImportedGloballyVisible()`. No further logic is performed.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsImportedSharedLib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsImportedSharedLib.body: It returns true only when the current target is an imported shared‑library that lacks a specific SO name. If the target isn’t imported, isn’t a shared library, or has an SO name, the function falls back to `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsInBuildSystem@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsInBuildSystem@k_Z.body: The method reports whether a target is actively part of the build system. It immediately rejects imported targets, then inspects the target’s type: any normal executable, static, shared, module, or utility library returns true. Interface libraries only qualify if they actually contain source files or C++ modules. All other cases default to false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLanguageUsed@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLanguageUsed@k_ZN.body: It fills a set with the languages returned by `GetLanguages` for the supplied config and then returns `true` if the requested language string appears in that set.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkInterfaceDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkInterfaceDepe.body: The method returns true only when the target is not a library type and the requested property name is present in the interface‑specific boolean‑property list that `GetCompatibleInterfaces` builds for the supplied configuration string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkInterfaceDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkInterfaceDepe.body: The method returns true only when the object is not an OBJECT_LIBRARY or INTERFACE_LIBRARY and the named property appears in the `PropsNumberMax` collection of a compatible interface for the supplied configuration.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkInterfaceDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkInterfaceDepe.body: The function evaluates whether a given property name `p` has a minimum‑value constraint in the set of compatible interfaces for the current object. It first excludes objects that belong to the library (object or interface library), immediately returning `false`. For other objects it looks up the appropriate interface list via `GetCompatibleInterfaces(config)` and simply returns whether that list contains at least one instance of `p` (i.e. whether `PropsNumberMin.count(p)` is greater than zero).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkInterfaceDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkInterfaceDepe.body: The routine evaluates whether a named string property is supported by the current target’s set of compatible interfaces, skipping the “library” type classes. If the target’s type is `OBJECT_LIBRARY` or `INTERFACE_LIBRARY` it immediately returns `false`. Otherwise it queries the interface list supplied by `GetCompatibleInterfaces(config)` and reports `true` when the property appears in the resulting `PropsString` collection.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkLookupScope@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkLookupScope@k.body: The routine checks if a name string starts with the special “CMAKE_DIRECTORY_ID_SEP” prefix. When that prefix is present, it extracts the directory id that follows. If the id string is empty, the current instance’s local generator is returned; otherwise it looks up a matching local generator in the global registry. The function returns true when a scope has been successfully resolved, and false when the input does not represent a link‑lookup scope.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkable@k_ZNK17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsLinkable@k_ZNK17c.body: The function returns true if the current generator target’s type matches any of the library or executable‑with‑exports categories (static, shared, module, unknown, object, interface, or an executable that exports symbols). It simply checks the target’s type against those specific enum values.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsNormal@k_ZNK17cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsNormal@k_ZNK17cmG.body: The `IsNormal()` method simply forwards the call to the encapsulated `Target` object, returning whatever value that internal `Target->IsNormal()` reports.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsNullImpliedByLink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsNullImpliedByLink.body: The function checks whether the given string `p` appears in the `LinkImplicitNullProperties` collection held by the object; if it is found, the method returns `true`, otherwise `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsRuntimeBinary@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsRuntimeBinary@k_Z.body: Returns whether the current target is a runtime‑binary by delegating to its underlying `Target` object.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsSharedLibraryWith.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsSharedLibraryWith.body: The method simply forwards the check to its underlying Target object, returning that result without adding any extra logic. It exposes whether the current target is configured as a shared library that exposes exported symbols.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsSourceFilePartOfU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsSourceFilePartOfU.body: It returns **true** if `UNITY_BUILD` is enabled and the supplied file name exists in the `UnityBatchedSourceFiles` set; otherwise it returns **false**.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsSynthetic@k_ZNK17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsSynthetic@k_ZNK17.body: This member simply forwards the check to its `Target` instance, returning the boolean reported by `Target::IsSynthetic()`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsSystemIncludeDire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsSystemIncludeDire.body: The method lazily builds a cache of system‑include paths keyed by the given build‑config and language. It collects directories from the current target, its transitive dependencies, and language‑specific runtime libraries, normalises slashes, removes duplicates, sorts, and then performs a binary search to check whether the supplied directory string is present in that sorted list.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsWin32Executable@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsWin32Executable@k.body: This function returns whether the current target is marked as a 32‑bit executable. It does that by retrieving the internal “WIN32_EXECUTABLE” property for the target, evaluating it against the supplied configuration string in the current generator’s context, and then interpreting that evaluation with `cmIsOn` to decide if the property is considered “on”.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsXCTestOnApple@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsXCTestOnApple@k_Z.body: The function evaluates whether the current `cmGeneratorTarget` instance represents a CF bundle on an Apple platform and has the property `"XCTEST"` enabled. It returns `true` only when both conditions hold; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::KindedSources::Kind.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::KindedSources::Kind.body: The `KindedSources()` function gathers and returns a collection of source items that have been classified by their “kind”. It is used elsewhere in the code to supply those pre‑sorted sources to downstream processing steps.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::LinkClosure::LinkCl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::LinkClosure::LinkCl.body: The `LinkClosure` routine builds and returns a small helper that, when invoked, releases a previously‑acquired resource and triggers any registered cancel‑handlers. It captures the resource ID, a timeout period and a callback reference, then wires them into a lightweight λ‑object that guarantees the cleanup logic runs whenever the link is broken.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::LinkLanguagePropaga.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::LinkLanguagePropaga.body: Checks if the current instance’s type matches the `STATIC_LIBRARY` enum value. If it does, the method returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::LookupLinkItem@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::LookupLinkItem@k_ZN.body: The method performs a name‑based lookup: it first verifies the name is within the current lookup scope; if it is, an empty optional is returned. It normalizes the input string via `CheckCMP0004`; if the result is empty or equals the generator’s own name when a self‑lookup is disabled, the optional remains empty. Otherwise it resolves the link via `ResolveLinkItem` and returns the obtained optional.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::MacOSXRpathInstallN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::MacOSXRpathInstallN.body: The method checks whether the current target supports the CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_RUNTIME_C_FLAG flag; if not, it fails immediately. If the flag is present, it looks for a MACOSX_RPATH property: if that property exists it returns its value as a boolean. If the property is absent it consults the CMP0042 policy: if the policy is in warning mode it logs a warning for the target, and the function ultimately returns true only when the policy status is NEW.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::MacOSXUseInstallNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::MacOSXUseInstallNam.body: The function first checks if the target should use an install‑name directory by querying the `BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_NAME_DIR` property; if that property is set, it returns whether it is enabled. If the policy status for CMP0068 is `NEW`, the function immediately returns `false`. Otherwise, it checks the `BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH` property. If that property is true and the CMP0068 status is `WARN`, it logs a warning for the target. Finally, it returns the value of the `BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH` property to indicate whether the install‑name directory should be used.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::MaybeGetLocation@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::MaybeGetLocation@k_.body: The function attempts to resolve a location string for a given configuration. It first queries the target’s import data; if that contains a non‑empty location, it returns that value. If no import info is available, it falls back to resolving the path from the artifact’s default runtime location. The result is wrapped in an optional to indicate the presence or absence of a concrete location.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::MaybeHaveInterfaceP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::MaybeHaveInterfaceP.body: The method lazily determines whether the current target or any of its linked‑in‑library dependencies expose a given property. It first consults a cache (`MaybeInterfacePropertyExists`) keyed by the property name and the current configuration; if missing, it inserts a `false` entry and then evaluates the target’s own property. If that property is empty it recurses through the interface‑linked libraries attached to the current or head target, marking the property present when any linked target reports it. The result is cached and returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ModuleDefinitionInf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ModuleDefinitionInf.body: Returns a structured object that aggregates metadata about a compiled module—its name, symbol table, entry‑point signatures, and any auxiliary flags. It is used by the build system to pass that information down the compilation pipeline.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::NameComponents::Nam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::NameComponents::Nam.body: The `NameComponents` function takes a raw name string, breaks it into its constituent parts—such as given name(s), middle name(s), and family name(s)—and packages those pieces into a lightweight data structure for downstream use.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::Names::Names@k_ZN17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::Names::Names@k_ZN17.body: The `Names` constructor taking an rvalue reference (`Names(Names&&)`) is the move‑constructor: it creates a new `Names` object by stealing the resources of a temporary instance. In practice it usually copies internal pointers or handles into the new object, then zeroes or resets the source’s members to a safe‑empty state so that the source object can be safely destroyed or reassigned. This ensures the moved‑from instance remains in a valid, destructible state while the new instance now owns the original data.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::Names::Names@k_ZN17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::Names::Names@k_ZN17.body: `Names()` is a public helper that aggregates and returns a list of identifiers (e.g., a vector of strings). It is typically used in other parts of the code to provide a convenient, read‑only view of the available names.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::Names::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::Names::operator=@k_.body: The function implements move‑assignment: it accepts an rvalue reference (`Names&&`), assigns the internal state from the argument, and returns `*this`. It’s used wherever a `Names` instance needs to be rebound to another, e.g. `obj = other;` or `obj = std::move(other);`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::Names::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::Names::operator=@k_.body: The assignment operator copies the contents of a `Names` object into the current instance and returns a reference to the updated object, enabling chained assignments. It takes a single parameter `const Names &` and returns a `Names&`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedCxxModuleSuppor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedCxxModuleSuppor.body: The `NeedCxxModuleSupport` function first verifies the requested language string; only when the language matches the literal `"CXX"` does it evaluate further. It then asks whether the current context declares support for C++20 (`HaveCxxModuleSupport(config)` must return `Cxx20SupportLevel::Supported`). Finally, it consults the global generator via `CheckCxxModuleSupport` with an `Inspect` query, returning true only if that check succeeds. If any of these tests fails, the function returns `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedDyndep@k_ZNK17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedDyndep@k_ZNK17c.body: The method checks if the target language is Fortran or if the target requires C++ module support; if either condition holds, dynamic dependencies are needed.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedDyndepForSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedDyndepForSource.body: The function decides whether a source file must be scanned for dynamic dependencies. It first short‑circuits Fortran (always true) and non‑C++ code (always false). For C++ sources it queries the file set for module‑type, checks whether a C++20 rule or generator support is available, and finally consults the policy status (OLD, WARN, or NEW) to return true only when the required rule and generator support are present.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedImportLibraryNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedImportLibraryNa.body: The function returns true when either the current configuration already has an import library or when the target is a DLL platform and the type is either an executable or a module library.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedRelinkBeforeIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::NeedRelinkBeforeIns.body: It inspects whether a target that can be re‑linked (executables, shared or module libraries) actually needs a relink step before its install. The decision is based on whether the target has an install rule, whether rpath handling is enabled, whether the current build or install tree uses rpath, and if the platform’s linker supports rpath flags. If both a rpath is required and the Ninja generator is in use, it aborts with a fatal error to force the user to re‑link or disable rpath.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::NormalGetFullPath@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::NormalGetFullPath@k.body: The method builds the absolute file path for a target artifact. It starts by combining the output directory (obtained from `GetDirectory`) and, on Apple systems, appending the bundle directory via `BuildBundleDirectory`. It then appends the artifact‑specific name: if `realname` is true it uses `NormalGetRealName()`; otherwise it falls back to the generic full name. The result is a string path ready for file‑system use.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::NormalGetRealName@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::NormalGetRealName@k.body: The function first guards against being invoked on imported targets; if it is, it logs an internal‑error message. It then obtains the appropriate name set based on whether the target is an executable or a library. Finally, it returns either the real build name or the import name depending on whether the requested artifact is a runtime binary or an import‑time artifact.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::OutputInfo::OutputI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::OutputInfo::OutputI.body: OutputInfo gathers key state data and writes it to the console or log for diagnostic purposes.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::OutputInfo::empty@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::OutputInfo::empty@k.body: The function returns true only when all three internal directory members (`OutDir`, `ImpDir`, and `PdbDir`) are empty; if any of them contains a path, it returns false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ReportPropertyOrigi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ReportPropertyOrigi.body: The function checks whether a property name matches one of the target’s debug‑compatible properties, avoids re‑reporting the same property for the same target, and when it does, emits a single log entry that includes the property name, the result value, and the compatibility type.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkItem@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkItem@k_Z.body: This method simply forwards the request to an internal overload of `ResolveLinkItem`, passing along the object’s own `LocalGenerator`. It returns whatever that overload produces.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkItem@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkItem@k_Z.body: The function takes a string name and a generator context, then walks up the back‑trace chain to identify the target object that this name resolves to. It first tries to locate a matching target; if none is found it simply returns a link item holding the original string and marks it as unresolved. When a target is found it checks whether that target has been deprecated, emitting a warning that includes the back‑trace if so. It also skips targets that are plain executables lacking export symbols, treating them as non‑linkable. Finally, for a valid non‑depracted target it returns a link item wrapping the resolved target.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkerWrappe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkerWrappe.body: The lambda captures a string `LINKER` and, given a `BT<std::string>` object, returns `true` if that object's `Value` string begins with the `LINKER` sequence (using `compare(0, LINKER.length(), LINKER)`).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkerWrappe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkerWrappe.body: The lambda captures `SHELL` and returns `true` if the input string contains that substring, effectively serving as a predicate for a containment test.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkerWrappe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkerWrappe.body: It walks through the result list, finds every entry whose value starts with `LINKER:` (with or without an embedded `SHELL:` prefix), parses the trailing options string, and replaces the original entry with a series of wrapper‑flag entries. These new entries are built using the language‑specific wrapper flags derived from `Makefile`, and the resulting options are inserted back into the result vector either as a joined string or as separate entries depending on the `joinItems` flag. This produces a cleaned, wrapped list of linker options suitable for downstream use.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveTargetRefere.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveTargetRefere.body: For a given name, it simply forwards that name together with the current object’s `LocalGenerator` to the overload of `ResolveTargetReference`, returning the resulting `TargetOrString`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveTargetRefere.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveTargetRefere.body: This method takes a target name and a local generator context, attempts to locate a target that matches that name via `FindGeneratorTargetToUse`. If a match is found, the method returns a `TargetOrString` whose `Target` field points to that target; if no such target exists, it returns a `TargetOrString` containing the original name string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::SetDeviceLink@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::SetDeviceLink@k_ZN1.body: It updates the `DeviceLink` member and returns its former value.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::SourceFileFlags::So.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::SourceFileFlags::So.body: The move‑constructor copies the flag bit‑mask stored in the source object to the new one and clears the source’s mask, leaving the moved‑from instance in a valid but unspecified state. It typically performs a shallow copy of the internal flag fields and may be marked `noexcept`. No other side‑effects are expected.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::SourceFileFlags::So.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::SourceFileFlags::So.body: The `SourceFileFlags()` function returns a bitmask of flags that describe properties of a source file. These flags indicate whether the file is a header, a test source, or any other special markers needed by the compiler. The returned mask is used throughout the code to make decisions about parsing, symbol resolution, and code‑generation paths.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::SourceFileFlags::~S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::SourceFileFlags::~S.body: The `~SourceFileFlags()` routine returns a struct (or bitfield) that encodes various per‑file properties (e.g., whether a file is compiled, treated as a header, has inline symbols, etc.). It’s a helper used by the compiler to decide which source files participate in the build.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::StrictTargetCompari.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::StrictTargetCompari.body:
The operator compares two `cmGeneratorTarget` instances.  
It first orders them by the target’s name; if the names match it orders by the
current binary directory string.  
The function returns `true` only when the first argument should precede the second
in this ordering, otherwise `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetOrString::Tar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetOrString::Tar.body: The constructor accepts an rvalue reference of another `TargetOrString`, forwarding its data into the new instance. It enables an efficient move of the underlying target or string representation without copying.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetOrString::Tar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetOrString::Tar.body: This function returns the string representation of a target object (or the target itself if it is already a string).

@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.body: The `Evaluate` function is a pure virtual member that obliges every concrete subclass to produce an evaluation of the entity it represents. Implementations typically compute an expression’s value (often by traversing child nodes) and then return a reference to an internal string buffer that holds the textual representation of that result. Because the return type is a `const std::string&`, the implementation must guarantee the referenced string outlives the lifetime of the returned reference – usually by storing it in a member variable or static buffer – otherwise a dangling reference would be returned. The method is marked `const`, ensuring that the computation does not mutate the object’s internal state. The signature itself is intentionally minimal: the sole input is a string that may serve as a name or argument in the evaluation process, and the sole output is a string reference that callers can read without copying.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.body: GetBacktrace returns a cmListFileBacktrace object that encapsulates the backtrace of a file entry and is implemented by concrete subclasses.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.body: The method simply reports that no context‑sensitive condition was encountered—returning `false`.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.body:
The declaration declares a pure‑virtual member that, when overridden, must return a **const reference to `std::string`**.  
Because the function is marked `const`, the overriding implementation cannot modify the object on which it is called.  
The pure‑virtual (`=0`) form forces every concrete subclass to provide its own implementation of `GetInput()`.  
The return type `const std::string&` means callers receive a read‑only view of the string; they cannot change the underlying string via that reference.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.body: This constructor simply forwards the supplied `cmLinkImplItem` instance to its base class `LinkImplItem`, thereby initializing a `TargetPropertyEntry` object with the given item.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::TargetPropertyEntry.body: The destructor for `TargetPropertyEntry` performs the necessary cleanup of any resources owned by an instance of that class. It guarantees that when an object is destroyed, its internal state and any associated resources are correctly released, thereby preventing leaks or dangling references during runtime operation.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::TraceDependencies@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::TraceDependencies@k.body: The `TraceDependencies` member simply checks whether the target is a global target; if so, it exits early because global targets have no dependencies. Otherwise it creates a `cmTargetTraceDependencies` helper and invokes its `Trace()` method to walk through the target’s dependencies. This helper performs the actual dependency tracing.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::UpdateExplicitStand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::UpdateExplicitStand.body: The method inserts an entry into a map keyed by the combination of an upper‑cased configuration string and a language tag; if that key already exists, the stored level is replaced only when the new level is greater than the current one.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::UsesDefaultOutputDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::UsesDefaultOutputDi.body: The method delegates to `ComputeOutputDir`, passing `config` and `artifact`. It supplies an output string reference (`dir`) and returns the boolean result of that call, indicating whether the default directory was used.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::VerifyLinkItemColon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::VerifyLinkItemColon.body: It checks whether a link item refers to a known target. If the item’s target is missing, it builds an error message (choosing the message type according to the current policy), attaches the relevant back‑trace, reports the issue through the local generator, and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::VerifyLinkItemIsTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::VerifyLinkItemIsTar.body: The routine checks whether a `cmLinkItem` counts as a target. It first tests the item’s `Target` flag; if that is set it returns true. Otherwise it examines the item’s string representation for special characters or prefixes that signal a target (e.g., `-`, `$`, `\```, backslashes or specific library prefixes). If no such markers exist, it reports a fatal error showing the offending string and why the check failed, then returns false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::cmGeneratorTarget@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::cmGeneratorTarget@k.body: The constructor creates a target generator instance that ties a target to its CMake context. It grabs the makefile and global generator from the local generator, computes the object‑directory path, and then iteratively builds property expressions for include paths, compile options, features, definitions, link options, link directories, pre‑compiled headers, and source files. Finally it records the target’s policy map and determines whether the linker is a C++ one or falls back to the stored LINKER_LANGUAGE.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::cmGeneratorTarget@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::cmGeneratorTarget@k.body: `cmGeneratorTarget` is a constructor that cannot be used to copy an existing instance; the class marks its copy‑constructor as `delete`, so any attempt to copy an object of this type will be a compile‑time error. This pattern is typically employed to enforce unique ownership or to avoid accidental shallow copies of internal resources.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::operator=@k_ZN17cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::operator=@k_ZN17cmG.body: The deleted assignment operator disables copy‑assignment for `cmGeneratorTarget`, preventing inadvertent duplication of its internal state and forcing users to use move semantics or other explicit mechanisms instead.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::~cmGeneratorTarget@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::~cmGeneratorTarget@.body: The destructor cleans up any resources owned by a `cmGeneratorTarget` instance. When a `cmGeneratorTarget` object is destroyed—whether explicitly or via a smart‑pointer—the compiler-generated default destructor will release any internal buffers, close files, and free memory that the class holds. It guarantees that no dangling pointers or leaks remain after the object’s lifetime ends.

@lcmGetDirectoryPropertyCommand@k_Z29cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetDirectoryPropertyCommand@k_Z29cmG.body: The routine parses a command‑style argument list to locate a directory makefile (optionally overriding the default source directory when the explicit `"DIRECTORY"` flag is supplied), retrieves the requested property (or definition) from that makefile, and installs the result into the current makefile’s definitions. It reports failure via `cmExecutionStatus` when the argument list is malformed or the target makefile cannot be found.

@lcmGetPipes@k_Z10cmGetPipesPi@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetPipes@k_Z10cmGetPipesPi@f./Source.body: The routine creates a new pipe, then attempts to make each side close‑on‑exec. If any step fails it rolls back and returns the translated system error.

@lcmGetPropertyCommand@k_Z20cmGetPropert.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetPropertyCommand@k_Z20cmGetPropert.body: The routine parses a list of arguments to determine which make‑file scope (global, directory, target, source, test, variable, cache, install) and which form of information (brief doc, full doc, value, or definition flag) is requested. It validates the supplied directories, invokes the appropriate scope‑specific handler to retrieve the property, and stores the result in the target variable, reporting any errors via the status object.

@lcmGetSourceFilePropertyCommand@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetSourceFilePropertyCommand@k_Z30cm.body: The function validates the number of arguments, optionally processes a “DIRECTORY” or “TARGET_DIRECTORY” flag, resolves the source‑file path (making it absolute if needed), looks up the source file in the current Makefile, retrieves the requested property value, and finally adds a definition for the variable in the Makefile (or “NOTFOUND” if the property is absent).

@lcmGetTargetPropertyCommand@k_Z26cmGetT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetTargetPropertyCommand@k_Z26cmGetT.body: The function parses a three‑argument command that requests a property from a target. It verifies the target exists, resolves whether it is an alias, and attempts to read the requested property (either a computed property or a stored property). If the target or property is missing it emits a policy‑driven warning or fatal error; otherwise it defines a variable in the makefile with the property value (or a “‑NOTFOUND” marker if absent).

@lcmGetTestPropertyCommand@k_Z24cmGetTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetTestPropertyCommand@k_Z24cmGetTes.body: The function accepts a vector of strings and a status object. It first validates that the argument count is either 3 or 5; if the third argument is “DIRECTORY” it treats the following element as a test‑directory path. It then verifies the directory scopes with HandleAndValidateTestDirectoryScopes, locates the test by name, retrieves the requested property (if supplied), and finally adds a definition for the variable in the makefile, defaulting to “NOTFOUND” when the property is missing.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::AddCacheEnt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::AddCacheEnt.body: Adds an entry to the glob‑cache. If the key is new, it stores the supplied file list and back‑trace. If the entry already exists and the file list differs, it fires a fatal‑error with the old and new back‑trace information. If the entry exists unchanged, it simply records the new back‑trace.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body: The `CacheEntryKey` constructor simply initializes a key object from an existing one by moving its internal data (e.g., a string or ID). This allows a cache entry to be identified and looked‑up in collections that map keys to cached values. The constructor’s purpose is to enable efficient key construction without copying the underlying identifier, thereby keeping cache maps lightweight and fast.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body: The `CacheEntryKey` constructor simply creates a new key by copying all fields from an existing instance; it’s used wherever a new cache entry needs to be initialized with the same identifier data that another entry already holds.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body: Creates a CacheEntryKey object by assigning the five constructor arguments to the corresponding member variables: Recurse, ListDirectories, FollowSymlinks, Relative, and Expression.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body: The function serialises a glob pattern object to an output stream. It writes a header indicating whether recursion and symlink following are enabled, followed by the list of directories to search, an optional relative path, and finally the expression string that defines the glob. The output is a single string suitable for logging or debugging.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body: The function implements a strict weak ordering: it first checks the `Recurse` field, falling back to `ListDirectories`, `FollowSymlinks`, `Relative`, and finally `Expression`. If any field of the left‑hand side is less than the corresponding field of `r`, it returns `true`; otherwise, if any field is greater, it returns `false`. If all fields compare equal, it falls through to the final `return false`. The implementation contains a typo (`FollowSymlinks` instead of `FollowSymlinks`), but otherwise follows the standard pattern for chained comparisons.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::DoWriteVeri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::DoWriteVeri.body: Returns true only when both `VerifyScript` and `VerifyStamp` contain non‑empty strings; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::GetVerifySc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::GetVerifySc.body: The method simply returns a read‑only reference to the internal `VerifyScript` string. Because it returns a reference rather than a copy, no copying of the string is performed, and the caller cannot modify the returned value.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::GetVerifySt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::GetVerifySt.body: Returns a const reference to the internal `VerifyStamp` member, exposing its value without copying or allowing modification.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::Reset@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::Reset@k_ZN2.body: The method empties the internal data structures – it removes all entries from the three member containers (`Cache`, `VerifyScript`, and `VerifyStamp`), restoring the object to an initial, un‑initialised state.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::SaveVerific.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::SaveVerific.body:
The function writes a CMake script that will later verify that the global files have not changed.  
If the cache is empty it simply returns success.  
Otherwise it creates a directory for the script, writes a “VerifyGlobs.cmake” file that records each global command with its back‑trace and a list of expected files, and creates a stamp file to record the current state.  
On success it sets internal paths and returns `true`.

@lcmGlobalCommonGenerator::RemoveUnknown.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalCommonGenerator::RemoveUnknown.body: The routine walks each directory listed in `ClangTidyExportFixesDirs`, collects every file matching the `*.yaml` glob, and deletes those whose names are not already stored in `ClangTidyExportFixesFiles`. It uses a helper that checks file equality via `cmSystemTools::SameFile` before invoking `cmSystemTools::RemoveFile`.

@lcmGlobalCommonGenerator::SupportsDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalCommonGenerator::SupportsDirec.body: The `SupportsDirectConsole()` function is a virtual, protected member that simply returns `true`. In effect it signals that the class implementation declares support for a direct console interface, without performing any runtime logic or checks.

@lcmGlobalCommonGenerator::cmGlobalCommo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalCommonGenerator::cmGlobalCommo.body: A `cmGlobalCommonGenerator` is constructed by forwarding a `cmake*` instance to its base class, `cmGlobalGenerator`. No further logic is performed in the constructor body, so it relies on the base class to perform the necessary setup.

@lcmGlobalCommonGenerator::~cmGlobalComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalCommonGenerator::~cmGlobalComm.body: When an instance of cmGlobalCommonGenerator is destroyed, its virtual ~cmGlobalCommonGenerator runs, performing any necessary de‑allocation of owned resources. Because the destructor is marked override, any subclass that derives from this class can provide its own cleanup routine that will be invoked automatically when the object is destroyed. This guarantees a clean teardown across an inheritance hierarchy.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddBuildExportExpor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddBuildExportExpor.body: The function stores the supplied generator in the internal `BuildExportExportSets` map under its main export file name, and then forwards the instance to `AddBuildExportSet` for any additional processing.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddBuildExportSet@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddBuildExportSet@k.body: Registers the supplied generator under its main export‑file name in the internal map of export‑file generators.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddCMP0042WarnTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddCMP0042WarnTarge.body: The method simply registers the provided string as a new “warning” target by inserting it into the internal `CMP0042WarnTargets` collection.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddCMP0068WarnTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddCMP0068WarnTarge.body: The `AddCMP0068WarnTarget` method registers a new warning target by adding the supplied string to the `CMP0068WarnTargets` set maintained by the `cmGlobalGenerator` instance. This allows the system to remember which targets should trigger a specific warning (CMP‑0068) during later processing stages.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddExtraIDETargets@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddExtraIDETargets@.body: The method is a hook that derived classes can override to register additional IDE‑specific build targets—useful when a project needs to expose custom toolchains or build configurations to the IDE’s target list.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddInstallComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddInstallComponent.body: The function inserts a non‑empty component name into the `InstallComponents` collection. If the supplied string is empty, no action is taken; otherwise, the name is added to the set.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddToManifest@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddToManifest@k_ZN1.body: The routine pulls the path and base name from a supplied file path and records the name in both the Generated and All sets for the corresponding directory entry in DirectoryContentMap.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::AppendDirectoryForC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::AppendDirectoryForC.body: The method is intended to be overridden by derived generators that need to expose distinct configuration directories. When a subclass supports multiple build configurations, it implements this function to append the appropriate sub‑folder (for example, a configuration‑specific suffix such as “Debug” or “Release”) to the supplied output path. The base implementation does nothing.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::CheckALLOW_DUPLICAT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::CheckALLOW_DUPLICAT.body: The method verifies whether duplicate custom targets are permitted. If the global property `ALLOW_DUPLICATE_CUSTOM_TARGETS` is unset, it simply returns `true`. When the property is enabled, the function logs an error message indicating that the current generator does not support duplicate custom targets and returns `false`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::CheckCxxModuleSuppo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::CheckCxxModuleSuppo.body: The `CheckCxxModuleSupport` method is a hook that receives a query describing a Cxx module and is expected to indicate whether that module is supported. In the stub implementation shown, it simply returns `false`, meaning the current implementation reports that the queried module is not supported.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::ComputeTargetObject.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::ComputeTargetObject.body: The function belongs to the *cmGlobalGenerator* class and is meant to compute the directory in which a target’s object files should be stored. However, in the current source it contains no implementation – it simply has an empty body and therefore performs no action at all.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::Configure@k_ZN17cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::Configure@k_ZN17cmG.body: The function initializes the generator’s internal state, creates a snapshot of the current project layout, and constructs a new makefile instance. It then indexes that makefile, enforces directory‑level rules, registers global targets for each makefile, updates the cache with the current number of local generators, and finally emits progress information.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::CreateAnonymousRunt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::CreateAnonymousRunt.body: Creates a new runtime‑dependency set, pushes it onto the internal list, and returns a pointer to the freshly‑created instance.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::CreateGenerationObj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::CreateGenerationObj.body: The routine first calls CreateLocalGenerators, then—if configuration is already finished—runs CheckTargetProperties. Afterwards it creates generator targets for the requested type via CreateGeneratorTargets, and finally, when the target set equals AllTargets, it triggers ComputeBuildFileGenerators.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::DepfileFormat@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::DepfileFormat@k_ZNK.body: The `DepfileFormat()` member is a virtual, const member function that returns an `cm::optional<cmDepfileFormat>`. In its base implementation it simply returns `cm::nullopt`, signalling that no file‑format is set. Derived classes are expected to override it to provide a specific format value.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::EnableInstallTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::EnableInstallTarget.body: This public method simply flips the internal flag that controls whether an install target is enabled. Once called, `InstallTargetEnabled` is set to `true`, allowing the rest of the installation logic to proceed.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::EncodeLiteral@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::EncodeLiteral@k_ZN1.body: The `EncodeLiteral` function is a virtual method that takes a string reference (`std::string& lit`) and simply returns that reference unchanged. No additional processing or transformation is applied.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::EscapeJSON@k_ZN17cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::EscapeJSON@k_ZN17cm.body: Escapes double‑quotes, backslashes, and control characters such as newlines and tabs into their JSON escape sequences, leaving all other characters unchanged.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::ExpandCFGIntDir@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::ExpandCFGIntDir@k_Z.body: The method is a trivial identity pass‑through: it simply returns the supplied string unchanged. The second parameter is unused, so the method could be inlined or removed without affecting functionality. No state changes or side‑effects occur, making the implementation very lightweight and safe.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindGeneratorTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindGeneratorTarget.body: Finds a generator target by name: if an alias mapping exists for the name, forwards that value to the implementation routine; otherwise it simply queries with the original name.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindLocalGenerator@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindLocalGenerator@.body: FindLocalGenerator searches the internal map LocalGeneratorSearchIndex for a key matching id.String. If the key exists, it returns the associated cmLocalGenerator*; otherwise it returns nullptr. The method is const, so it guarantees no modification of the object’s state.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindMakeProgram@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindMakeProgram@k_Z.body:
The function first checks that the generator has supplied a file name via `FindMakeProgramFile`.  
If the macro **CMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM** is not defined in the current makefile, it reads a file named by that attribute.  
When the program path contains spaces, it shortens the directory part of the path (keeping the file name unchanged) and stores the cleaned path in the cache.  
If any step fails, it emits an error and returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindMakefile@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindMakefile@k_ZNK1.body: The method performs a lookup in the internal `MakefileSearchIndex` map: if an entry keyed by the supplied directory exists, it returns the associated `cmMakefile*`; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindTarget@k_ZNK17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindTarget@k_ZNK17c.body:
The function returns a pointer to a target by name.  
When `excludeAliases` is false, it first checks the `AliasTargets` map; if a matching alias exists, it delegates to `FindTargetImpl` with the alias’s value.  
If no alias matches or `excludeAliases` is true, it simply calls `FindTargetImpl` with the original name.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::ForceLinkerLanguage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::ForceLinkerLanguage.body: The `ForceLinkerLanguages` method is a private virtual hook that derived classes can override to enforce a specific linker strategy (e.g., choose a particular linker for a target language). Currently it is empty, so no behaviour is performed unless a subclass implements it.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::Generate@k_ZN17cmGl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::Generate@k_ZN17cmGl.body: The method orchestrates the generation pipeline: it records start time, initializes progress marks, processes evaluation files, configures custom targets, then iterates over each local generator—invoking each generator’s own generation, install‑rule, and test file generation while updating a running progress indicator. After all generators complete, it writes a summary, performs target‑link validation, issues any policy warnings, and finally logs the elapsed time before signalling completion.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GenerateImportFile@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GenerateImportFile@.body: The function attempts to find an export set for the given file. If it exists, it delegates the import generation to that set, cleans up any pending Makefile registrations if a particular configuration flag is unset, removes the set from the internal map, and returns the success status of the delegated operation. If no matching set is found, it simply returns false.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GeneratedMakeComman.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GeneratedMakeComman.body: It builds and returns the shell command string that will be executed by the Make tool.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetAllTargetName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetAllTargetName@k_.body: The function simply returns the literal string `"ALL_BUILD"` each time it is called; it is a `const` member that does not modify the object.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetBuildIgnoreError.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetBuildIgnoreError.body: The function is a virtual const member that returns a `const char*`. By default it returns `nullptr`; it’s intended to be overridden by derived classes to supply an actual ignore‑errors flag string.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCMakeCFGIntDir@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCMakeCFGIntDir@k.body: The `GetCMakeCFGIntDir` function simply returns a pointer to a string literal containing just a single dot (`"."`), indicating the current directory. It’s declared `virtual`, so derived classes can override it, and the `const` qualifier guarantees the caller can’t modify the returned pointer’s content.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCMakeInstance@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCMakeInstance@k_.body: The const member function simply returns the stored pointer `CMakeInstance`. It does not alter any state, but callers receive a raw pointer that could still modify the underlying instance, so use const‐qualified pointers or smart‐pointer wrappers when the instance should remain unchanged.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCleanTargetName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCleanTargetName@.body: The method is meant to provide a target‑name string to callers.  In a base class it returns a null pointer, while derived types override it to supply a specific, sanitized name. Because it’s const, callers cannot modify the returned data.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetConfigureDoneCMP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetConfigureDoneCMP.body: Returns the internal flag that indicates whether the CMP0026 (and CMP0024) configuration sequence has finished.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCurrentMakefile@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCurrentMakefile@.body: Returns a pointer to the current configuration’s makefile.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetDefaultBuildConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetDefaultBuildConf.body: The function is a virtual const member that simply returns the literal string `"Debug"`, serving as the default build‑configuration value that callers can rely on unless overridden.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetEditCacheTargetN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetEditCacheTargetN.body: It’s a virtual member that returns a pointer to a C‑style string (here it returns nullptr). The function is marked `const` so it guarantees no modification of the object state, and it’s declared `virtual` to allow overriding in derived classes. The `const` after the function (the return type `const char*`) indicates the returned pointer points to read‑only data. The body simply returns a null pointer, effectively signifying “no target” for an edit‑cache.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExportSets@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExportSets@k_ZN1.body: Returns a reference to the internal `ExportSets` map, letting callers inspect or modify the collection of export sets without copying it.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExportedTargetsF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExportedTargetsF.body: The method searches the internal map of export‑set definitions for the supplied file name; if a matching entry exists it returns a pointer to the corresponding generator object, otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExtraGeneratorNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExtraGeneratorNa.body: It returns the name of the associated extra generator when one is present; otherwise it yields an empty string.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetFileLockPool@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetForceUnixPaths@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetForceUnixPaths@k.body: Returns the current value of the ForceUnixPaths flag.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallLocalTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallLocalTarg.body: Returns a C‑string pointer that identifies the installation target; the base implementation returns `nullptr`, indicating that subclasses must override it to provide a valid name.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallStripTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallStripTarg.body: The function is a virtual const member that returns a pointer to a character array. Its implementation simply returns a null pointer, indicating that derived classes should provide an actual string name for the install‑strip target.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallTargetNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallTargetNam.body: The `GetInstallTargetName()` member simply supplies a fixed identifier for the installation target. When invoked, it returns the literal `"INSTALL"`—serving as a static tag that callers can use to distinguish the target name without any dynamic computation.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetJson@k_ZNK17cmGl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetJson@k_ZNK17cmGl.body: Creates a JSON object that holds the instance’s name and whether the instance is configured for multiple runs, then returns that object.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetLanguageEnabled@.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetLanguageOutputEx.author: AI Short Overview

If the language isn’t found, it falls back to the file’s own extension, but only if that extension is in the allowed set; otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetLinkerPreference.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetLinkerPreference.body: The method scans the internal language‑to‑preference map and returns the stored value; if the key is absent it falls back to zero.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetMakefileEncoding.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetMakefileEncoding.body: The function simply returns the enum value `codecvt_Encoding::None`. It indicates that, by default, no special encoding is applied to the makefile generation.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetName@k_ZNK17cmGl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetName@k_ZNK17cmGl.body: A `GetName()` member function is declared `virtual` and `const`, meaning it can be overridden in derived classes while guaranteeing it does not modify the object. @lcmGlobalGenerator::GetNamedRuntimeDepe.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetNeedSymbolicMark.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetNeedSymbolicMark.body: The function simply returns the value of the private member `NeedSymbolicMark`—i.e., a flag indicating whether the object requires a symbolic marker. The method is marked `const`, so it guarantees not modifying the object state.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPackageSourceTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPackageSourceTar.body: This member simply supplies a C‑string identifier for the package’s source‑target. It’s a virtual const accessor, currently returning a null pointer as a stub.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPackageTargetNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPackageTargetNam.body: The function simply returns a pointer to the literal string `"PACKAGE"`. @lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPreinstallTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPreinstallTarget.body: The member function is a virtual const accessor that is expected to be overridden in derived classes. @lcmGlobalGenerator::GetRealPath@k_ZN17c.author: AI Short Overview

If the key is not present—or the iterator returned by `lower_bound` points to a key that comes after the requested one—it inserts a new entry whose value is the real‑path returned by `cmSystemTools::GetRealPath`. Finally, it returns that stored value.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetRebuildCacheTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetRebuildCacheTarg.body: The function is a virtual const member that returns a pointer to a C‑style string. It’s meant to be overridden by derived classes to supply the name of the cache rebuild target.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetTargetDirectDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetTargetDirectDepe.body: It fetches the target’s dependency set from the internal `TargetDependencies` map and returns that set as a const reference.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetTestTargetName@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetTestTargetName@k.body:
It returns a pointer to the literal string “RUN_TESTS”.  
Being virtual lets subclasses override the returned target name.  
The const qualifier guarantees no mutation of the caller’s data.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetToolSupportsColo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetToolSupportsColo.body: The function returns a boolean flag indicating whether the current instance supports color operations. It simply returns the value of the member variable `ToolSupportsColor` without modifying any state.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetUseLinkScript@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetUseLinkScript@k_.body: This accessor simply yields the current state of the `UseLinkScript` flag that governs whether the link‑script feature is enabled for the instance.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GlobalSettingIsOn@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GlobalSettingIsOn@k.body: The function simply asks the first makefile in the generator’s list whether the named setting is on – after asserting the list isn’t empty, it forwards the query to that makefile’s `IsOn` method.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::HasKnownObjectFileL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::HasKnownObjectFileL.body: The method is intended to answer whether a specific target has an object‑file location known; as implemented it simply returns true, regardless of the passed target.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IndexGeneratorTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IndexGeneratorTarge.body: The method stores a pointer to a generator target in an internal map keyed by the target’s name, but only if the target is either not imported or has global visibility. This indexing facilitates quick lookup of targets during generation.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::InitializeProgressM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::InitializeProgressM.body: The function is an overridable hook that derived classes implement to set up or reset internal progress‐tracking markers. It’s invoked during initialization to ensure the subclass’s state is ready for subsequent progress reporting.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::InspectConfigTypeVa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::InspectConfigTypeVa.body: The function declares a virtual method that always returns `true`, effectively acting as a placeholder that can be overridden in derived classes.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsAlias@k_ZNK17cmGl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsAlias@k_ZNK17cmGl.body: The function returns whether a given string is in the generator’s internal list of alias targets, delegating the containment test to the `cm::contains` helper. It is marked `const` so it guarantees no mutation of the object state.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsExportedTargetsFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsExportedTargetsFi.body: The routine first checks that the supplied name exists inside the primary export set (`BuildExportSets`). If it does, the method then confirms the name is absent from the secondary set (`BuildExportExportSets`). Only in that case does the function report *true*; otherwise it returns *false*.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsGNUMakeJobServerA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsGNUMakeJobServerA.body: This virtual const method returns `false`, indicating that the class does **not** consider itself aware of a GNUMake job server.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsGeneratedFile@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsGeneratedFile@k_Z.body: The function receives a file path string and simply checks whether that path is present in the internal set (or map) of generated file names. If the lookup succeeds it returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`. The operation is a constant‑time hash lookup.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsIPOSupported@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsIPOSupported@k_ZN.body: The default implementation of IsIPOSupported() simply returns false, signifying that unless overridden, the class reports iPhone OS is not supported.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsMultiConfig@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsMultiConfig@k_ZNK.body: The base implementation simply reports that the object does not support multi‑configuration. Derived classes can override the function to return true when they handle multiple configuration instances.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsNinja@k_ZNK17cmGl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsNinja@k_ZNK17cmGl.body: The method `IsNinja` is a virtual const member function that returns a boolean value. In its base form it simply returns `false`, meaning that by default a class instance is not considered a ninja. Derived classes can override this function to provide a different return value.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsReservedTarget@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsReservedTarget@k_.body: This static helper examines the supplied target name against a compile‑time list of special‑keyword targets (e.g. “all”, “clean”, “install”, etc.) and returns true only when the name matches one of those reserved identifiers.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsVisualStudio@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsVisualStudio@k_ZN.body: The method simply reports whether the code is running under Visual Studio. In the base implementation it always returns false, so callers can override it in a derived class to signal a Visual Studio environment when appropriate.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsXcode@k_ZNK17cmGl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsXcode@k_ZNK17cmGl.body: The method is a const member that simply returns `false`. It is intended as a virtual hook that derived classes can override to indicate whether the current instance satisfies the condition represented by “Xcode”. By defaulting to `false`, it provides a safe base‑implementation that derived types can refine.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::Open@k_ZN17cmGlobal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::Open@k_ZN17cmGlobal.body: The `Open` function checks if an `ExtraGenerator` object is present; if so, it delegates the call to that object's `Open` method and returns whatever that call returns. If no `ExtraGenerator` exists, the function immediately returns `false`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::PrintBuildCommandAd.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::PrintBuildCommandAd.body: The method serves as a hook for derived generator classes to emit a warning or recommendation when a particular build‑command option is not supported. It receives a stream to write the message and the number of parallel jobs requested; the base implementation is empty, so subclasses override it to emit tailored advice.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::SelectMakeProgram@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::SelectMakeProgram@k.body: The routine resolves which make‑program name to use. It starts with the argument, checks it against the internal “off” logic, and if that test fails it pulls a cached value via `GetCacheDefinition`. When that fails it falls back to the supplied default. If after all this the chosen name is still empty, the method returns the constant string “CMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM‑NOTFOUND”.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::SetGeneratorToolset.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::SetGeneratorToolset.body: The function verifies whether a tool‑set string is supplied. If the string is non‑empty, it reports a fatal error via `mf->IssueMessage`, logs the message, and returns `false` to signal failure; otherwise it simply returns `true`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::SetSystemName@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::SetSystemName@k_ZN1.body: This virtual member accepts a constant string reference and a pointer to a `cmMakefile` object, performs an internal update (e.g., storing the name in the associated makefile context), and always reports success by returning `true`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::ShouldStripResource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::ShouldStripResource.body: The method simply asks the makefile whether it is targeting an Apple‑embedded platform; if that is true, it signals that any resource path should be removed.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::SplitFrameworkPath@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::SplitFrameworkPath@.body:
The function receives a path string and a `FrameworkFormat` flag.  
It first tests whether the path matches a regular‑expression pattern that describes a typical framework layout; if it does, it extracts the framework directory, the framework’s base name, and (optionally) a library suffix.  
If the format is `Strict`, it verifies that the extracted library suffix is present and conforms to the name; otherwise the function returns `nullopt`.  
For `Extended` format it simply returns a descriptor built from the parent directory and the base name of the path.  
If none of these conditions succeed, the function returns `nullopt`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsCrossConfig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsCrossConfig.body: The `SupportsCrossConfigs` method is a trivial flag that a derived type can override to signal that it supports cross‑configuration functionality. By defaulting to `false`, the base implementation conservatively denies that capability until a subclass explicitly reports otherwise.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsCustomComma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsCustomComma.body: Returns **false** – indicating that, by default, the class does not provide support for a custom command dependency file. Derived classes may override the method to change the behavior.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsDefaultBuil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsDefaultBuil.body: This function checks whether the current type supports the default build configuration. By default, it returns `false`, signalling that no default build type is provided unless a derived class overrides the behaviour to return `true`. The method is `const` and `virtual`, allowing subclasses to customize the support check while guaranteeing that the base implementation does not alter any internal state.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsDefaultConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsDefaultConf.body: This virtual member indicates whether the class is expected to handle any built‑in configuration values automatically. A derived implementation that returns `false` tells callers that they must explicitly provide the needed configuration; the base class itself does not supply any defaults.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsLinkerDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::SupportsLinkerDepen.body: This virtual method simply reports that the current implementation does **not** support a linker‑dependency file, because it returns `false` by default.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::UseEffectivePlatfor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::UseEffectivePlatfor.body: Returns false, indicating the default behavior is to ignore or disable using the effective platform name.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::UseFolderProperty@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::UseFolderProperty@k.body: The `UseFolderProperty` method checks whether the global `USE_FOLDERS` property is considered enabled. It first asks the current CMake instance for the property; if the property is defined it returns the property’s on/off status. If the property isn’t defined, the method falls back to a default that treats the property as enabled only when the first makefile’s policy status is `cmPolicies::NEW` for policy `CMP0143`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::cmGlobalGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::cmGlobalGenerator@k.body: The constructor initializes a new `cmGlobalGenerator` instance by configuring a set of internal flags and state settings that control how the generator behaves. It turns off symbolic‑dependency handling, enforces native path formats, disables colour output and link‑script usage, and turns off install‑target support. It also clears any timeout settings, assigns null outer‑make‑file pointers and resets tracking of the compiler‑run progress. Finally, it propagates these defaults into the global state manager to disable multi‑config generation, MinGWMake, MSYS shell, NMake, Watcom‑WMake, and Windows shell/VS‑IDE behaviour.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::~cmGlobalGenerator@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::~cmGlobalGenerator@.body: The destructor `~cmGlobalGenerator` is a public virtual cleanup routine that simply calls `ClearGeneratorMembers()` to release internal resources. It relies on the base class’s cleanup logic and expects derived classes to override the virtual function for any specific teardown.

@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::GetDefaultPl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::GetDefaultPl.body: The `GetDefaultPlatformName()` method is a pure virtual const member function that subclasses must override to provide the default name of the platform for which the generator factory is intended. It returns a `std::string` containing that name and does not modify any member data. Sub‑implementations typically query a configuration source or hard‑coded table of platform identifiers to produce the string. Because the method is const, it guarantees no state changes, and because it is pure virtual it enforces the contract that every concrete factory must provide this name.

@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::GetDocumenta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::GetDocumenta.body:
This function is a pure virtual const member that any concrete subclass must implement.  
It returns a `cmDocumentationEntry` object that presumably contains metadata (title, description, possibly tags or links) describing the component.  
Because it is declared `const`, the implementation must not modify any member data.  
As a pure virtual function, calling `GetDocumentation()` on a polymorphic type will dispatch to the concrete subclass implementation, allowing callers to query documentation uniformly across different generator types.

@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::SupportsPlat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::SupportsPlat.body: The `SupportsPlatform()` member is an abstract, const‑qualified predicate that concrete classes must implement to report whether the current platform (or configuration) is supported by the particular generator or factory. It returns a `bool` and is invoked by callers to gate logic that should only run on supported platforms.

@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::SupportsTool.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::SupportsTool.body: The `SupportsToolset` method is a pure virtual const member that derived classes must implement. It simply reports whether the current toolset is supported by the concrete implementation, returning a `bool` result.

@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::~cmGlobalGen.author: AI Short Overview
