@lcmGlobalGeneratorFactory::~cmGlobalGen.body: The destructor of `cmGlobalGeneratorFactory` is declared virtual and defaulted, ensuring that any derived implementation will be destructed correctly when a base‑pointer is deleted. It guarantees that resources allocated in subclasses are released in the proper order, preventing leaks in any context that uses a factory polymorphically.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddAdditionalC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddAdditionalC.body: Adds the supplied file name to the list of files that the generator will delete for the specified configuration.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddAssumedSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddAssumedSour.body: The function registers a list of assumed dependencies for a given source file. It merges the supplied collection into a set that tracks the required dependencies for that source, ensuring duplicates are ignored and the union of all appearances of the same source is stored.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddCXXCompileC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddCXXCompileC.body:
The method serialises a compiler invocation into the Ninja‑compatible `compile_commands.json` file.  
When the file’s first entry is written, it starts a JSON array (`[`) and then writes successive objects separated by commas.  
Each object contains the source‑file path (made relative to the output directory if necessary), the command line, the output object path, and the working‑directory.  
All values are JSON‑escaped via `cmGlobalGenerator::EscapeJSON`, and when `ComputingUnknownDependencies` is active, the path to the generated file is added to `CombinedBuildOutputs`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddCustomComma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddCustomComma.body: It registers a rule that triggers a custom command by creating a cmNinjaRule with the name “CUSTOM_COMMAND”, filling in the command string and description, and adding it to the generator’s rule set.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddMacOSXConte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddMacOSXConte.body: The method constructs a `cmNinjaRule` instance, populating its fields with a command string built by concatenating the base command from `CMakeCmd()` with a “‑E copy” directive that copies the input file to the desired output location. It then tags the rule with a brief description and comment before registering the rule through `AddRule()`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddPerConfigUt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddPerConfigUt.body: This method records a new per‑configuration target by inserting the supplied name into the internal `PerConfigUtilityTargets` set.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddRebuildMani.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddRebuildMani.body: Adds the path of the generated NINJA build file to the list of output files that will be emitted during the rebuild process.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddRule@k_ZN22.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddRule@k_ZN22.body: The function inserts a rule into the internal set if it isn’t already present, records the rule’s command length in a map, and then serializes the rule to the output stream. It guards against duplicate rules by short‑circuiting on the `insert()` result, and uses a simple integer cast for length storage.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddTargetAlias.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AddTargetAlias.body:
The method builds a target‑level alias for a given target and config.  
1. It computes the physical output path (NinjaOutputPath) and the logical alias name (BuildAlias).  
2. It collects the target’s artifacts via AppendTargetOutputs, unless the config is “all”.  
3. It then flags those artifacts as ambiguous so that no other target can claim them.  
4. Finally it inserts the alias into the global, config‑specific, and default alias maps, clearing any previous target if the new alias would clash.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendDirector.body: If a config string is present and the generator is in multi‑configuration mode, the function appends the concatenated string formed from the given prefix, config, and suffix into the `dir` string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendNinjaFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendNinjaFil.body: The function is a virtual, const‑qualified member that accepts a reference to a `GeneratedMakeCommand` object and a `std::string` argument. When implemented it should append the supplied string as a command argument—typically the path or flag—into the `GeneratedMakeCommand` instance. Because it’s marked `const`, it must not modify the state of the surrounding object; only the passed `command` may be altered. The body is currently empty, so the function merely serves as an override point for derived classes to provide the actual appending logic.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDe.body: The lambda checks if a dependency target can compile. If it can, it pulls that target’s generated ISPC headers and objects for the given configuration, normalizes their paths via `MapToNinjaPath`, and appends them to the `outputDeps` list.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDe.body:
The function walks the dependency graph of a target.  
If the target is of type GLOBAL_TARGET, it simply adds aliases for each utility from the target’s binary directory.  
Otherwise, it gathers all direct dependencies—appending outputs from each, collecting any ISPC headers/objects they provide, sorting the list, and appending the result to the `outputs` vector.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDe.body: The function recurses over a target’s direct dependencies, filters out targets that aren’t part of the build system or are disallowed by configuration settings, then collects the set of output files produced by those dependencies. It stores the result in a cache keyed by the target, configuration, and output‑generation flag, and finally merges that cached result into the caller’s output set, optionally adding the target’s own outputs.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetOu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetOu.body: The routine checks whether a target is a framework and then, based on its type and the requested dependency order, it appends the appropriate build‑artifact paths to the output list. For shared/static libraries it may order the dependency; executables get their import‑library and runtime binaries; object libraries follow the same ordering logic; other targets simply generate a path in the current binary directory (possibly wrapped in an alias if per‑config). The function ultimately populates the list of Ninja artifacts that will be linked into the final build.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::BuildAlias@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::BuildAlias@k_Z.body: The method receives two string references and simply returns the first argument unchanged.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ByConfig::Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ByConfig::Targ.body: The constructor simply moves the internal state of an existing `TargetDependsClosureKey` into a new instance. It accepts an unnamed rvalue reference of the same type and performs an efficient transfer of its data, preserving any flags or identifiers that represent a dependency closure key. This helper is used throughout the dependency graph machinery, notably in the generator routine referenced at line 623 of `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator.h`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ByConfig::Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ByConfig::Targ.body: The constructor creates a new `TargetDependsClosureKey` instance by copying the internal state from an existing key. It is employed in `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator` (around line 623) to materialize dependency‑closure keys that are later used to index or look‑up target dependency sets. The copy semantics preserve all members unchanged, ensuring callers receive an exact duplicate of the original key.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ByConfig::Targ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ByConfig::Targ.body: The `TargetDependsClosureKey` function produces a unique key that the build system uses to identify and manage the closure of target dependencies during target resolution.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CCOutputs::Add.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CCOutputs::Add.body: The `Add` method iterates over every supplied path, converting it to Ninja‑compatible form via `ConvertToNinjaPath`. If the resulting path is relative, it’s duplicated as an absolute path to satisfy Ninja 1251’s requirement; both representations are stored—`WorkDirOuts` for the relative form and `SeenCustomCommandOutput` is invoked for each form. Finally, every converted path is appended to the `ExplicitOuts` list, ensuring the generator is aware of all output files to be emitted.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CCOutputs::CCO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CCOutputs::CCO.body: The function is a move constructor that takes an rvalue reference to another `CCOutputs` instance and copies or moves its internal state into the new object, providing an efficient transfer of output data between objects without deep copying.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CCOutputs::CCO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CCOutputs::CCO.body: The constructor stores the supplied `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator*` in the member variable `GG`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CCOutputs::CCO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CCOutputs::CCO.body: Creates a new CCOutputs instance by copying all internal state (e.g., output buffers and metadata) from an existing object, so the new object starts in the same configuration as the source.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CMakeCmd@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CMakeCmd@k_ZNK.body: It pulls the first local generator and passes the CMake command to it, returning the result in shell format.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckALLOW_DUP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckALLOW_DUP.body: This method simply returns `true`, indicating that duplicate custom targets are always permitted without performing any further checks.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckCxxModule.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckCxxModule.body:
If Ninja supports C++20 modules the method immediately returns true.  
Otherwise it checks whether the requested query equals `Expected`, the instance isn’t already diagnosed, and the CMake instance isn’t in a try‑compile state. If those conditions hold, it constructs an error string explaining that the current Ninja version lacks the required features (and references the minimum required version) and reports it as a fatal error. Finally it returns false.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckFortran@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckFortran@k.body: The function checks if the Ninja generator supports Fortran dyndeps. If the feature is missing, it builds an error string with the required Ninja version, logs a fatal error through the makefile, records the fatal‑error flag, and returns false. If the feature is present, it simply returns true.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckISPC@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckISPC@k_ZN.body: The `CheckISPC` member verifies whether the current Ninja generator supports multiple‑output builds. It first checks the `NinjaSupportsMultipleOutputs` flag; if true, it simply returns `true`. When the flag is `false`, it constructs a detailed error string explaining that the present Ninja version (shown by `this->NinjaVersion`) does not meet the minimum required version (`RequiredNinjaVersionForMultipleOutputs()`), reports this as a fatal error through the supplied `cmMakefile` instance, sets the global fatal‑error flag, and finally returns `false`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckLanguages.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckLanguages.body: The function scans the supplied language list for specific language identifiers and delegates to the corresponding check routine. If the list contains "Swift" it additionally validates that only a single architecture is defined; encountering more than one architecture triggers a fatal error and causes the function to return false. In all other cases the function returns true when no problematic condition is detected.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckNinjaCode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckNinjaCode.body: Runs a `wincodepage` command to detect the encoding format Ninja reports. It parses the output line beginning with “Build file encoding:” and sets the internal `NinjaExpectedEncoding` flag accordingly (UTF‑8 for “UTF‑8”, ANSI for any other encoding). If the line is missing, it falls back to UTF‑8 with a warning. If the command fails, it logs a fatal error and marks a fatal‑error flag.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckNinjaFeat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CheckNinjaFeat.body: The function probes the current Ninja toolchain’s version string, compares it against a list of feature‑threshold constants, and stores the results in a set of Boolean flags (e.g. NinjaSupportsConsolePool, NinjaSupportsImplicitOuts, …). For the “dyndeps‑fortran” feature it has a legacy‑compatibility check: if the standard comparison fails, it parses a “.dyndep‑#” suffix in the version string; when the suffix equals “1” the flag is set. On Windows it also verifies “codepage” support, falling back to ANSI when absent.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CleanMetaData:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CleanMetaData:.body: The lambda builds a command vector starting with the Ninja executable and a “‑C” flag, then appends the CMake instance’s output directory, the “‑t” flag, and every element from the supplied `args`. It invokes `RunSingleCommand` with this vector; on failure it logs a fatal error containing the failed command and marks a fatal error occurred.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CleanMetaData@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CleanMetaData@.body: The routine builds a command vector starting with the Ninja executable and a "-C" flag pointing to the output directory, then appends any supplied arguments. It runs that command; on failure it logs a fatal error. Depending on whether the build is a single‑config build and whether the intermediate manifest file exists, it may invoke the `recompact` tool. Finally, if restats are supported and no custom output prefix is requested, it gathers the outputs that must be refreshed, builds the `restat` arguments, and runs that tool.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CloseBuildFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CloseBuildFile.body: The method safely disposes the internal file‑stream if it is present; otherwise it reports the unexpected missing state.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CloseCompileCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CloseCompileCo.body: The routine writes a newline and a closing bracket (`]`) to the output stream, then releases the stream handle by resetting its pointer.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CloseRulesFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CloseRulesFile.body: The routine guards against a dangling stream: if the internal pointer is set it is cleaned up; otherwise an error message is emitted.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ComputeTargetD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ComputeTargetD.body: The `ComputeTargetDependsClosure` routine gathers all transitive dependencies for a target in the Ninja build graph. It walks the dependency graph starting from a given target, following both normal and custom “depends on” edges, and records every reachable node so the build system knows exactly which files must be rebuilt when anything in that closure changes.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ComputeTargetO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ComputeTargetO.body: The function builds the full path that will hold the compiled object files for a target by concatenating the current binary directory, the target‑specific sub‑directory, and the internal CMake configuration directory. The resulting string is stored in `gt->ObjectDirectory`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConfigDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConfigDirector.body: The `ConfigDirectory` member simply returns a string (currently the empty string) that represents the directory path used for configuration. It’s `virtual` so subclasses can override it to provide the desired directory logic.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToNinja.body: The function normalizes a file‑path string by swapping “/” characters for backslashes on Windows (the `#ifdef _WIN32` block). It then returns the modified string unchanged on other platforms.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToNinja.body: The method turns an arbitrary file path into the form expected by the Ninja backend. It first looks up the path in a cache; if it’s already there it returns the stored value. If not, it asks the first local generator to resolve the path relative to its top‑build directory, then normalises it with the Ninja output helper. On Windows it swaps forward slashes for backslashes. The result is cached in `ConvertToNinjaPathCache` and finally returned.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CreateLinkLine.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CreateLinkLine.body: The function allocates a `cmLinkLineComputer` by calling `cm::make_unique<cmNinjaLinkLineComputer>` with the supplied `outputConverter`, the state snapshot directory of the first local generator, and the current object (`this`). It then returns this object wrapped in a `std::unique_ptr`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CreateLocalGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::CreateLocalGen.body: Creates a unique‑pointer to a new `cmLocalNinjaGenerator` instance, initialized with the current `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator` instance and the supplied `cmMakefile` pointer.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::DepfileFormat@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::DepfileFormat@.body: The function specifies that the current configuration uses the GCC depfile format for dependency files.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EnableCrossCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EnableCrossCon.body: The function checks whether any cross‑configuration is configured by returning `true` if the `CrossConfigs` container contains at least one entry; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EnableLanguage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EnableLanguage.body: The method registers requested languages with the Ninja build system. It first ensures that a multi‑configuration setup gets the appropriate CMake configuration types, then invokes the base generator’s enable routine. For each language it resolves the associated compiler unless the language is “NONE”. On Windows it also probes the compiler identity strings to detect a GCC‑on‑Windows scenario and marks that case if found.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EncodeLiteral@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EncodeLiteral@.body: The function normalizes a literal string by escaping `$` characters, escaping newline separators, and optionally replacing a configuration directory marker with the actual directory value when in a multi‑config build. It then returns the modified string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EncodePath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EncodePath@k_Z.body: The function normalises a file‑system path string: it converts backslashes to slashes (or vice‑versa) depending on the build environment, then runs an internal literal‑encoding step, and finally replaces spaces and colons with the “$ ” token sequence before returning the transformed string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EncodeRuleName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EncodeRuleName.body: The `EncodeRuleName` routine scans every character of an input string and builds a new string that contains only alphanumerics, underscores, and hyphens. Every character that falls outside that whitelist is converted into a dot‑prefixed two‑digit hexadecimal escape (e.g., the ASCII code `0x2E` becomes `.2e`). This guarantees that the resulting identifier matches the pattern `[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+` required for Ninja rule names.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::FindMakeProgra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::FindMakeProgra.body: The function first delegates to the base generator to locate a suitable make‑program; if that succeeds it reads the “CMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM” definition from the makefile, runs the command with a `--version` flag to capture the ninja version string, stores it, and then verifies that the detected version supports the required features. If running the command fails, it reports the failure as a fatal error.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::Generate@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::Generate@k_ZN2.body: The Generate function performs the core generation workflow: it first verifies that the current Ninja executable satisfies the minimum required version; if not, it logs a fatal error. It then opens the necessary output streams, clears per‑configuration dependency caches, and creates the top‑level targets such as “all” and the cache file. After setting internal flags (e.g., policy handling and unknown dependency tracking), it delegates to the base generator to actually emit the Makefile contents. Finally, it writes out all dependency information, handles any stream‑error states by marking the streams as failed, closes the file streams, and conditionally cleans stale metadata when it’s allowed to do so.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GenerateBuildC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GenerateBuildC.body: The function builds a Ninja build command by selecting the appropriate make program, adding optional flags (verbose, job count), appending the build‑config file, and finally inserting all supplied target names and user‑provided options. It returns a single `GeneratedMakeCommand` wrapped in a `std::vector`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetAdditionalC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetAdditionalC.body: The method is a `const` member function that simply returns the literal string `"CMakeFiles/clean.additional"`. It provides a fixed path string used elsewhere in the build system, typically to identify a clean‑up target or file that must be removed during a cleaning phase.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetAllTargetNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetAllTargetNa.body: This virtual const member simply returns a pointer to the string literal `"all"`; the literal remains valid for the life‑of‑program.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetByproductsF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetByproductsF.body: Retrieves the cached ByproductsForCleanTarget setting for a supplied configuration key from the internal Configs map.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetByproductsF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetByproductsF.body: Returns a reference to the internal ByproductsForCleanTarget member, exposing the dependency collection for the clean‑target context.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetByproductsF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetByproductsF.body: The function simply returns the relative path string `"CMakeFiles/cmake_byproducts_for_clean_target"`, which points to the CMake file used to generate the clean target.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetCleanTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetCleanTarget.body: This public const‑overridden member simply returns the literal string `"clean"`, which serves as the standard target name for cleanup operations.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetCommonFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetCommonFileS.body: The method simply returns the internally stored `cmGeneratedFileStream` instance via the `BuildFileStream` member; it forwards that pointer to callers without performing any additional logic.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetConfigFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetConfigFileS.body: This member simply hands back the already‑built stream object. It returns the pointer held in the `BuildFileStream` member, delegating all construction to that helper.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetCrossConfig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetCrossConfig.body: It returns a `std::set<std::string>` that contains every element already stored in `CrossConfigs` plus the `fileConfig` string passed to the function.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetDefaultConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetDefaultConf.body: `GetDefaultConfigs` returns a constant reference to the internal `DefaultConfigs` set. The method is marked `const`, ensuring the returned set is read‑only and that the function can be invoked on `const` instances of the class.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetDefaultFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetDefaultFile.body: The method returns the pointer stored in the `BuildFileStream` member; essentially it exposes the current default file stream to callers.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetDocumentati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetDocumentati.body: The method simply constructs and returns a `cmDocumentationEntry` that identifies the generator’s name and gives a short description that the generator creates the `build.ninja` file.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetEncodedLite.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetEncodedLite.body: GetEncodedLiteral forwards the supplied literal to EncodeLiteral and returns the resulting encoded string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetImplFileStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetImplFileStr.body: This const‑virtual member returns the pointer stored in the `BuildFileStream` member by calling its `get()` accessor.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetInstallStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetInstallStri.body: The function returns a static string literal, “install/strip”, identifying the name of the strip target used in the install process. It’s a const member function that simply returns that literal.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetInstallTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetInstallTarg.body: This const member function returns a pointer to the literal string `"install"`, which represents the name of the installation target.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetMakefileEnc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetMakefileEnc.body: It returns the current value of the `NinjaExpectedEncoding` member. As a `const` virtual function, it can be overridden in derived classes but otherwise simply provides read‑only access to the encoding that the generator expects for the generated Ninja makefile.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetName@k_ZNK2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetName@k_ZNK2.body: It forwards the call to the base class’s GetActualName() and returns the resulting string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetPackageSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetPackageSour.body: Returns a constant string literal identifying the package‑source target (“package_source”).

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetPackageTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetPackageTarg.body: This const member returns a C‑string literal `"package"`, signaling that the current instance is identified as a “package” target when queried via the `GetPackageTargetName` interface.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetPerConfigUt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetPerConfigUt.body: The function simply returns a constant reference to the internal set of strings that represent the utility targets for each configuration. No mutation or allocation occurs; it merely exposes the existing collection for read‑only inspection.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetRebuildCach.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetRebuildCach.body: The `GetRebuildCacheTargetName` method is a const member that overrides a virtual function, simply returning the constant C‑string literal `"rebuild_cache"`. This literal can be used directly as the name of a cache‑target object during rebuild operations.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetRuleCmdLeng.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetRuleCmdLeng.body: The function looks up the supplied rule name in a map (`RuleCmdLength`) and returns the stored integer length. If the key isn’t present, the code will throw a `std::out_of_range` exception because it attempts to access an absent element. It provides a direct read‑only lookup with no validation or bounds checking.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetRulesFileSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetRulesFileSt.body:
It returns a raw pointer to the internally stored `cmGeneratedFileStream`.  
The `get()` call retrieves that pointer from the internal container, so callers must keep the pointer valid for the stream’s lifetime.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetTestTargetN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::GetTestTargetN.body: It returns a pointer to a constant string literal that identifies the test target.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::HasCustomComma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::HasCustomComma.body: Checks whether the supplied string exists in the internal `CustomCommandOutputs` collection, returning `true` if it is found and `false` otherwise.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::HasOutputPathP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::HasOutputPathP.body: The method simply returns `true` when the internal string `OutputPathPrefix` contains any characters, otherwise `false`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::HasRule@k_ZN22.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::HasRule@k_ZN22.body: Checks whether the given rule name exists in the internal rule map and returns true if found, otherwise false.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::Indent@k_ZN22c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::Indent@k_ZN22c.body: The routine emits `count` copies of the predefined indent token (typically a tab or space sequence) into the supplied output stream, effectively producing a string of that many indentation units.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::InitOutputPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::InitOutputPath.body: The routine pulls the value of the CMake‑specific “CMAKE_NINJA_OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX” definition from the first local generator’s makefile and stores it in `OutputPathPrefix`, then guarantees the string ends with a trailing slash.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::IsGCCOnWindows.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::IsGCCOnWindows.body: Returns the value of the `UsingGCCOnWindows` member, indicating whether the current configuration is set to use GCC on Windows builds.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::IsIPOSupported.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::IsIPOSupported.body: The function simply reports that IP over Serial is supported by always returning `true`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::IsNinja@k_ZNK2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::IsNinja@k_ZNK2.body: The method simply reports that the object is a ninja by always returning `true`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::IsSingleConfig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::IsSingleConfig.body: The function checks whether a given target represents a single‑instance utility. It returns true only when the target’s type equals `cmStateEnums::UTILITY` and the target’s name is absent from the `PerConfigUtilityTargets` map, meaning no per‑configuration entry exists for it. The function itself is concise, but callers must ensure the target pointer is valid and that the map lookup uses the correct key (typically the target’s name).

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ListSubsetWith.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ListSubsetWith.body: The function examines each element of `items`. If any element is not found in the `all` set, it immediately returns an empty optional. If the vector contains only the string `"all"`, it returns the `defaults` set. Otherwise it builds a result set consisting of those items that are present in the `all` set and returns that set wrapped in an optional. If any of the above checks fails, the optional is null.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.body: It returns a helper object that captures the current instance, enabling further fluent mapping to a NinjaPath.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.body: The constructor takes a temporary MapToNinjaPathImpl object and transfers its internal state to the new instance, enabling efficient ownership transfer without copying data.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.body: Initializes internal state with the supplied global ninja generator pointer.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.body: The constructor `MapToNinjaPathImpl` simply copies an existing instance into a new one, preserving the internal mapping data; it initializes the new object with the same state as the source.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.body: The method simply forwards a given string to the `GG` helper’s `ConvertToNinjaPath` routine and returns the resulting string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.body: The function `~MapToNinjaPathImpl` is the core routine that translates a logical model path into a concrete Ninja path representation. It takes a *path* structure that describes a sequence of nodes and edges in the source graph and produces a `NinjaPath` object that can be serialized and stored in the Ninja intermediate representation. Internally it walks the input graph, gathers every node that must be emitted in the Ninja file (including any needed header or footer), then creates the corresponding `NinjaElement` objects and links them according to the original graph ordering. It returns a pair containing the `NinjaPath` and a list of any auxiliary data that the rest of the system needs to keep track of during code generation. The function is invoked by the global Ninja generator and by other parts that need to convert internal graph data into a format that Ninja can consume.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MarkAsGCCOnWin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MarkAsGCCOnWin.body: MarkAsGCCOnWindows() sets the UsingGCCOnWindows member to true, signaling that the instance should be treated as using GCC on a Windows platform.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::NewFactory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::NewFactory@k_Z.body: Creates and returns a `std::unique_ptr<cmGlobalGeneratorFactory>` that owns a freshly‑instantiated `cmGlobalGeneratorSimpleFactory<cmGlobalNinjaGenerator>`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::NinjaCmd@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::NinjaCmd@k_ZNK.body: The method retrieves the first local generator; if it’s available, it formats the stored Ninja command into shell syntax via `ConvertToOutputFormat`; otherwise it simply returns the literal string `"ninja"`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::NinjaOutputPat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::NinjaOutputPat.body: If the current instance has no output‑path prefix or the supplied path is already an absolute path, the function simply returns that path unchanged; otherwise it prepends the stored prefix to the path and returns the result.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OpenBuildFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OpenBuildFileS.body: The function first attempts to open a stream to the Ninja build file via `OpenFileStream`. If that fails it returns `false`. On success it writes a header comment into the stream and returns `true`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OpenFileStream.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OpenFileStream.body: This function attempts to create (or reuse) a `cmGeneratedFileStream` wrapped in a `std::unique_ptr`. It constructs the stream at the expected output directory, and if the stream is not already valid it writes a disclaimer header before signalling success. If the construction fails, it returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OpenRulesFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OpenRulesFileS.body: The function opens the rules file stream (via `OpenFileStream`) and writes a concise header comment that marks the file’s purpose and points to the main build file that includes it.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OrderDependsTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OrderDependsTa.body: It builds a string that uniquely identifies the order‑dependency rule for a given target – the name is just the target’s name prefixed with “cmake_object_order_depends_target_”.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OrderDependsTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::OrderDependsTa.body: It calls the base `OrderDependsTargetForTarget` routine, then appends the literal suffix “_private” to whatever string that routine returns, and returns that combined string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: The function is a simple accessor that returns the string literal `"1.3"`. It is declared static, so it can be invoked without an instance of the containing class, and because the return type is `std::string`, its value can be immediately used by client code to check or report the current Ninja build version.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: The function supplies the exact Ninja version string that the build system expects for the current code page. It is a hard‑coded constant used to enforce compatibility across different Ninja releases.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: This static helper simply returns the string `"1.5"`. Its purpose is to expose the minimum Ninja SDK version that a console pool requires, enabling callers to enforce compatibility without hard‑coding the value throughout the codebase. The return value is hard‑coded, so any change to the required version must be updated in this single location.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: The `RequiredNinjaVersionForDyndepsCxx` helper simply returns the hard‑coded string `"1.11"`. It is a static utility that callers can invoke to query the specific Ninja‑build‑system version that the Dyndeps C++ backend expects.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: The function simply returns the string `"1.10"`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: This helper simply provides the version string that the build system expects for implicit output handling. The returned constant `"1.7"` denotes the minimal Ninja version required for those features.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: The static helper simply returns the string literal `"1.8"`. This value represents the required Ninja build system version to be compatible with the manifest restoration logic. It has no parameters and performs no computation beyond returning the hard‑coded string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: It returns the literal string `"1.10.2"`, indicating the minimum Ninja version needed for metadata regeneration.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: The function returns the minimal Ninja build‑system version (“1.9”) required to support mult-line dependency files. It’s a simple helper that provides this static string for downstream checks.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: This function declares a static method that, when called, returns a hard‑coded string indicating the minimum Ninja version required for the “multiple‑output” build configuration. In the current implementation it simply returns the literal value `"1.10"`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: The function simply provides the specific Ninja version string that RestatTool expects to operate correctly.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::RequiredNinjaV.body: The function simply supplies the version string “1.10”, indicating the specific Ninja version that the unconditional recompact tool requires.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SeenCustomComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SeenCustomComm.body: Checks whether a `cmCustomCommand` pointer has already been inserted into the set of commands for the specified configuration. It returns `true` when the command was already present (i.e., the insertion would not add a new element) and `false` when it was newly inserted.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SeenCustomComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SeenCustomComm.body: The method simply records an output string in a collection and removes that string from a list of presumed source dependencies—essentially treating the output as a confirmed dependency that no longer needs tracking.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::StripNinjaOutp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::StripNinjaOutp.body: The function trims a trailing suffix from a given path string. It first guarantees the string ends in a slash, then invokes `cmStripSuffixIfExists` to remove the `OutputPathPrefix` value when it is present. If the string is empty or the suffix is absent, the path remains unchanged.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsCustom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsCustom.body: It returns `true`, indicating that custom command dependency files are supported.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsDirect.body: Returns whether the current `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator` instance is configured to support a direct console. The value is stored in its `NinjaSupportsConsolePool` member.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsImplic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsImplic.body: The member simply reports the internal flag that tracks whether the current generator instance is allowed to emit implicit output files. When queried, it just returns that flag value, which can be checked before attempting to emit any such outputs.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsLinker.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsLinker.body: The function always returns true, indicating that the linker dependency file feature is supported.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsManife.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsManife.body: The function simply returns the member flag `NinjaSupportsManifestRestat`, indicating whether the current instance supports the “manifest restat” capability.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsMultil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsMultil.body: This const method returns the value of the internal flag `NinjaSupportsMultilineDepfile`, indicating whether the Ninja generator currently supports multiline dependency files.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsPlatfo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsPlatfo.body: It always evaluates to `false`, signalling that the current platform is not supported.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsToolse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::SupportsToolse.body: This static function merely signals that no toolset is supported—it always returns `false` regardless of any context.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::TargetAlias::T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::TargetAlias::T.body: The function accepts an rvalue reference to an existing `TargetAlias` object and constructs a new instance by efficiently moving its internal state. It is primarily used to create a new alias from an existing one without copying data, typically in the global generator code (e.g., around line 575 in `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator.h`).

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::TargetAlias::T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::TargetAlias::T.body: The constructor simply copies the fields of another `TargetAlias` object, creating a new instance that duplicates the original’s data.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::TargetAlias::T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::TargetAlias::T.body: TargetAlias() returns a string identifier that represents a build‑target alias. The function consults the target definition storage and resolves the alias name that should be used in later stages of the build generator. It is invoked whenever a target name must be translated to its canonical alias before being emitted to the Ninja file.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteAssumedSo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteAssumedSo.body: The routine iterates through every pair in `AssumedSourceDependencies`. For each pair it constructs a `CCOutputs` instance containing the key, copies the associated dependency list into a `cmNinjaDeps` container, and finally invokes `WriteCustomCommandBuild` to emit a custom build step that declares those dependencies for the generated source file.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteBuild@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteBuild@k_Z.body: The function emits a single Ninja “build” statement: it starts by validating that the build rule and output list are non‑empty, then writes a comment line, lists the rule’s explicit and implicit outputs (including the special work‑dir form), followed by the command string and its explicit/implicit/order‑only dependencies. Finally it writes the variable assignments for that rule, optionally redirecting the command into a response‑file if the line length would exceed the supplied limit.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteBuiltinTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteBuiltinTa.body: It writes a divider, then emits the special “rebuild‑manifest,” “clean,” and “help” targets. Afterwards it emits a “default” target for each generator config file, and finally a default target if a default file is configured.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteComment@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteComment@k.body: The function writes a nicely formatted comment block to an output stream. It first checks for an empty comment, in which case it exits immediately. Then it prints a header line of hash characters, and iterates over each line of the supplied comment text. Each line is printed prefixed with “# ” and terminated with a newline, finishing with a blank line after the comment block.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomCom.body: The routine registers a custom command rule, aggregates any explicit dependencies it must track, constructs a `cmNinjaBuild` populated with the command text, description, and flags such as terminal usage, pool assignment, and depfile, and finally emits the resulting build stanza either into the common or implementation‑specific Ninja file.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDefault@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDefault@k.body: Writes a comment line, then prints a line that starts with “default” followed by each target in `targets` separated by spaces, ending with a newline.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDisclaime.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDisclaime.body: This method outputs a comment header that records the generator name and CMake version.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDivider@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDivider@k.body: The function writes a horizontal divider line comprised of hash marks and equal signs to the supplied output stream.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.body: The lambda takes a path string, normalises it with `ConvertToNinjaPath`, then (on Windows when GCC is in use) converts back‑slashes to forward‑slashes before returning the fixed path.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.body: The `operator()` function takes a `const std::string&` argument (likely a key or identifier) and returns a `CxxBmiLocation` object. Internally it probably looks up or constructs a location instance based on the supplied string—possibly invoking a lookup or factory. The function is used throughout the codebase wherever a `CxxBmiLocation` is required from a string key, providing a thin wrapper around whatever storage or mapping mechanism holds the actual location data.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.body:
The lambda captures the map `mod_files`. It receives a logical string, looks it up in the map, and returns a `CxxBmiLocation`:

- If an entry exists and the module is marked private, it returns `Private()`.
- Otherwise it returns `Known()` with the stored BMI path.
- If no entry is found, it returns `Unknown()`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.body: The operator() function is a public const member that returns a `cm::static_string_view`. Internally it uses the `LookupMethod` argument to produce the string view – essentially converting the lookup method information into a static view that the rest of the code expects.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.body:
The lambda turns a `LookupMethod` enum value into a compile‑time string view:  
- `ByName` → `"by-name"`  
- `IncludeAngle` → `"include-angle"`  
- `IncludeQuote` → `"include-quote"`  

If an unknown value is passed, it triggers a `false` assertion.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.body: This lambda takes a file name, looks it up in the global `mod_files` map, and if found returns the stored `BmiPath`. If the name isn’t present it returns an empty `optional`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteDyndepFil.body: The function sets up a local generator and writes out a Ninja dynamic‑dependency file that describes which modules a target needs. It parses the scanner output into `cmScanDepInfo` objects, builds a map of module names to their module files (including whether they’re private), and tracks module usage and reference lookup methods. The function checks for circular imports, writes a “Modules.json” file for downstream targets, and finally writes the metadata file used by the Ninja build system.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteFolderTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteFolderTar.body:
This routine iterates over all directory targets computed by `ComputeDirectoryTargets`.  
For each directory it creates a *phony* Ninja build rule that outputs the directory’s `all` file and adds a dependency for each supported configuration.  
It emits per‑configuration explicit dependencies and outputs, writing shortcut rules for multi‑config setups and an “all” target when cross‑config builds are enabled.  
Finally, it writes these rules to the appropriate configuration’s implementation file or the default file, ensuring every directory is buildable in the generated Ninja file.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteInclude@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteInclude@k.body: The function writes an include directive to the output stream: it first writes a comment (via WriteComment) and then appends `include ` followed by the given filename and a newline.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteMacOSXCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteMacOSXCon.body: The function registers a build rule that copies a content file into a target directory. It registers a “COPY_OSX_CONTENT” rule, associates the specified output and input files, and writes the rule to the Ninja build file.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteRule::[la.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteRule::[la.body: The lambda writes a key-value pair to the output stream, indenting the line first, but only when the supplied value string is non‑empty.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteRule@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteRule@k_ZN.body: The function validates that a rule has a name and a command (and rsp‑file content if an rsp‑file is used) and then emits a Ninja rule block to the stream: a comment, the rule declaration line, and a list of key/value pairs for the rule’s attributes (depfile, deps, command, description, and optional rspfile/rspfile_content, restat, and generator flag).

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetAli.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetAli.body: The function writes Ninja build rules for each target alias in the generator. For every alias it creates a build entry with the alias name as the output, clears any previous dependencies, and populates the explicit dependencies for the associated generator target. It skips aliases whose output already has a custom command. On multi‑config generators it emits separate rules for each config, writing them to the corresponding config files; otherwise it falls back to the default file. This produces the minimal set of alias rules needed for the generated Ninja build system.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetCle.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetCle.body: The function emits the Ninja rule that removes every file produced by the current generator: it writes a “CLEAN” rule that deletes the main build output and, for each configuration, the corresponding by‑product files, handling both single‑ and multi‑config cases as well as the optional additional‑clean target.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetCle.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetCle.body: The function first checks whether any generator configuration has files marked for additional clean‑up. If none exist, it cleans up the generated script file and returns. Otherwise it writes a CMake script that removes those files, registers that script as an output file, and then creates a Ninja rule named “CLEAN_ADDITIONAL”. That rule is used to generate a clean build for each configuration, including the multi‑config case.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetDef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetDef.body: The function checks whether the generator has an output‑path prefix. If not, it creates a dependency list containing the current target (`TargetAll`) and emits a Ninja “default” rule that makes that target the default.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetHel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetHel.body: The function registers a Ninja rule named “HELP” that outputs the list of primary targets. It writes that rule to the generated rules file, then creates a single‑step build targeting the “help” output path, which invokes the rule to emit the target list.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetReb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteTargetReb.body:
The routine adds a special “rerun‑CMake” rule to the Ninja build file. It first checks whether the global regeneration flag is suppressed; if not, it grabs the current CMake instance, pulls the first local generator to get source and build directories, and builds a command that invokes CMake with the appropriate command‑line switches (e.g. `--regenerate‑during‑build`, `--compile‑no‑warning‑as‑error`, `-S … -B …`). That rule is marked as a generator, and its outputs are recorded.  

The function then constructs a rebuild manifest object that lists all the files that must be considered implicit dependencies (including the CMake cache file and each local generator’s Makefile). It further integrates special handling for older Ninja versions that cannot use the “restat” feature: if the required feature is unavailable, it falls back to a phony target that triggers a glob‑verification script; otherwise it adds a “VERIFY_GLOBS” build that runs a CMake verification script and records the resulting stamp file. Finally, it writes this rebuild rule into the output stream, ensuring any missing inputs are handled gracefully.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteUnknownEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteUnknownEx.body: The routine first exits if there are no unresolved dependencies. It then builds a set of all outputs the system already knows about (generated files, implicit outputs, evaluation files, and any explicit files produced by custom commands). By taking the set difference between the full set of custom‑command outputs and the known ones it obtains the truly unknown explicit dependencies. For each such file it emits a phony build rule so Ninja can build it and records a warning message listing any leftover unknowns so the user can add proper BYPRODUCTS/OUTPUT entries.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteVariable@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::WriteVariable@.body: The function writes a variable declaration to a stream: it checks that the name is present, trims the value unless the name is one of a few exceptions, and if the value is non‑empty it emits an optional comment, the appropriate indentation, and the line `name = value`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::cmGlobalNinjaG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::cmGlobalNinjaG.body: The constructor initializes a new Ninja‑generator instance, taking ownership of the supplied state and wiring the generator into the common infrastructure defined by `cmGlobalCommonGenerator`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::cmGlobalNinjaG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::cmGlobalNinjaG.body: The constructor registers the Ninja generator with CMake, configures the command‑shell environment (falling back to `cmd.exe` if the `COMSPEC` path isn’t available), and flags that Ninja mode is active, pointing the generator to use `CMakeNinjaFindMake.cmake` for find‑make logic.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::cmGlobalNinjaG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::cmGlobalNinjaG.body: It creates a new `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator` instance from an existing one, copying its configuration and build settings.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.body: The assignment operator allows a temporary `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator` instance to be moved into an existing object: it takes an rvalue reference to the source, transfers internal state (typically by moving member variables), and returns a reference to the updated object.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.body: The `operator=` implementation simply performs a shallow copy of the internal state of a `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator` instance, returning `*this` so that the expression can be chained. It includes a guard against self‑assignment and preserves any base‑class state by invoking the base class’s copy logic.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::~cmGlobalNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::~cmGlobalNinja.body: The `~cmGlobalNinjaGenerator()` destructor cleans up resources allocated by the Global‑Ninja generator, ensuring any owned dynamic resources or handles are released before the object is destroyed.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::AddRebuil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::AddRebuil.body: Adds each generator configuration’s ninja implementation and config file paths to the output list, plus the general build file path when a default file configuration is present.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::AppendNin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::AppendNin.body: The method inspects a non‑empty configuration string; when present it injects the flag **‑f** followed by the full path returned by `GetNinjaConfigFilename(config)` into the supplied command object.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::BuildAlia.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::BuildAlia.body: It returns the input alias unchanged if the `config` argument is empty; otherwise it appends a colon‑separated `config` string to the alias.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::CloseBuil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::CloseBuil.body: The routine walks through the various file stream members that the generator keeps open. For each stream it checks whether the smart‑pointer is non‑null; if so, it calls `reset()` to close and drop the handle. If a stream that is expected to be open is missing, the helper emits an error message. The logic treats the “common” and “default” streams specially (no error if they weren’t open) and then iterates over each generator‑config instance, closing the corresponding implementation and configuration file streams and emitting diagnostics when any are unexpectedly missing.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::ConfigDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::ConfigDir.body: This function generates a directory string by prefixing the supplied `config` value with a leading slash only when `config` is non‑empty; otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::ExpandCFG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::ExpandCFG.body: The function returns a copy of the input string in which every occurrence of the placeholder returned by `GetCMakeCFGIntDir()` is replaced with the supplied `config` value. It performs the replacement via `cmSystemTools::ReplaceString` and returns the resulting string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetActual.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetActual.body: The function is a static accessor that simply returns the literal string `"Ninja Multi‑Config"`. It takes no arguments and produces no side effects.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetCMakeC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetCMakeC.body:
The function is a const member that simply returns a compile‑time string literal. In this implementation the body substitutes the pre‑defined macro `CONFIGURATION` into a C‑style string and returns it.  
It performs no side effects, merely produces a literal path for use elsewhere in the code.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetCommon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetCommon.body: The member function simply returns a pointer to the member `CommonFileStream` that the object owns. It is a `const override` that returns the stored stream via its `get()` accessor.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetConfig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetConfig.body: The method simply retrieves a stream pointer from an internal map: it looks up the `config` key in `ConfigFileStreams` and returns the stored pointer. If the key is absent, `std::map::at` throws an `std::out_of_range` exception, so callers must handle that or pre‑check existence. The returned pointer is a raw pointer to the internal object; its lifetime is tied to the owning container, so callers must not delete it. No additional safeguards (null checks, thread‑safety, etc.) are performed in this implementation.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetDefaul.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetDefaul.body: This `GetDefaultBuildConfig()` member simply returns an empty `std::string`. It’s a `const` method, meaning it doesn’t modify any member state, and it’s a placeholder that can later be filled with the logic needed to supply a default build configuration string for the global Ninja multi‑generator.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetDefaul.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetDefaul.body: Returns the internal `DefaultFileStream` instance by invoking its `get()` accessor, yielding a raw pointer to a `cmGeneratedFileStream`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetDocume.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetDocume.body: The `GetDocumentation` function is a static helper that packages a simple description of the generator. It constructs a `cmDocumentationEntry` whose first field is the actual name of the generator (as returned by `GetActualName()`) and whose second field is a short, fixed string that reads “Generates build‑<Config>.ninja files.” This single‑line description is used elsewhere in the build‑system tooling to expose the generator’s purpose in a concise documentation string.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetImplFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetImplFi.body: The method returns a pointer to a `cmGeneratedFileStream` associated with the given configuration string by looking it up in the `ImplFileStreams` map. Because it calls `std::map::at()`, it will throw `std::out_of_range` if the key is absent, and it returns whatever `std::unique_ptr` (or raw pointer) the map holds. The function is marked `const override`, so it cannot modify the object state and simply forwards the request to the underlying storage.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetName@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetName@k.body: It returns the real name of the object by delegating to the base implementation, guaranteeing the call is read‑only and that the returned string is constructed in a const context.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetNinjaC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetNinjaC.body: It builds a filename string by prefixing the supplied `config` name with `"build-"` and appending the predefined Ninja file extension. The result is returned as a `std::string`.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetNinjaI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetNinjaI.body: The function concatenates the string `"CMakeFiles/impl-"` with the supplied `config` value and appends the `NINJA_FILE_EXTENSION` suffix, returning the resulting path as the implementation file name.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetQtAuto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::GetQtAuto.body: Retrieves the list of generator configuration strings from the first makefile in the internal list, then appends all those strings to the vector supplied by the caller.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::InspectCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::InspectCo.body: The function first pulls the list of available configuration types from the first makefile; if that list is empty it inserts a default entry. It then builds a set of those types and stores the default build type in `DefaultFileConfig`, falling back to the first type if none is explicitly set. It validates that the default type is indeed in the set; if not, it logs a fatal error and aborts. Next it fetches the list of cross‑configurations, ensuring it is a subset of the available types; failure again produces a fatal error. The selected cross‑configs are stored in `CrossConfigs`. The function then reads the default‑configs string (falling back to the default type if unspecified), checks that it is only used when a default type or cross‑config list is already defined, and verifies that the parsed list of default configs is a subset of the cross‑config list. If any of these checks fails, it reports a fatal error and returns false; otherwise it sets `DefaultConfigs` accordingly and returns true.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::IsMultiCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::IsMultiCo.body: This virtual const function always reports that the implementing type supports a multi‑configuration arrangement, returning `true` to indicate that any instance of the class can be used in a multi‑configuration context.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::NewFactor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::NewFactor.body: The function allocates a new `cmGlobalGeneratorSimpleFactory` templated with `cmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator`, wraps that raw pointer in a `std::unique_ptr<cmGlobalGeneratorFactory>`, and returns the owning pointer. This yields a factory instance that owns its resources exclusively and will be released automatically when the pointer is destroyed.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::OpenBuild.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::OpenBuild.body: The lambda walks through every configuration name, opens the corresponding implementation and configuration file streams, writes a header comment into each stream, and inserts an include line to bring the implementation into the config file.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::OpenBuild.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::OpenBuild.body: The routine opens the common, default, and per‑configuration file streams, writes a brief header comment in each, and includes the corresponding implementation file for every configuration. It returns `true` only if all streams are successfully opened and populated.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::OrderDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::OrderDepe.body: The method builds a string by concatenating a fixed prefix with the name of the target and a normalized form of the supplied configuration, which it turns to upper‑case. The resulting identifier can then be used as a key in the ordering logic that drives which build target depends on which other targets.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::OrderDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::OrderDepe.body: The function invokes the core ordering routine `OrderDependsTargetForTarget`, then tags its result with a “_private” suffix before returning it.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::SupportsC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::SupportsC.body: The function simply returns `true`, signalling that the class supports cross‑configuration scenarios.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::SupportsD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::SupportsD.body: This override simply reports that the default build type is supported – it returns true whenever queried.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::SupportsD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::SupportsD.body: The function indicates that the class supports the use of its default configuration options. It is virtual so derived types can alter the behaviour, but in this implementation it simply returns `true`, meaning the default config path is always enabled for this type.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::cmGlobalN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::cmGlobalN.body: The constructor accepts an r‑value reference and efficiently moves all internal data from the source instance into the new object, initializing the inherited generator state and any local members without copying.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::cmGlobalN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::cmGlobalN.body: Creates an instance of a multi‑config generator by invoking the base constructor and turning on the “multi‑config” and “ninja‑multi” flags in the build state.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::cmGlobalN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::cmGlobalN.body: The constructor duplicates a `cmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator` instance, copying all its internal state—including configuration flags, generator lists, and any cached resources—so the new object behaves identically to the source.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::operator=.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::operator=.body: The move‑assignment operator copies the internal state of the right‑hand operand into the current object (shallowing any owned resources such as pointers or buffers) and returns a reference to *this to allow chaining.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::operator=.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::operator=.body: The assignment operator copies the data from the source `cmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator` into the target, updating its internal state (the underlying generator and any cached values) and then returns the target by reference to allow chaining of assignments.

@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::~cmGlobal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator::~cmGlobal.body: The `~cmGlobalNinjaMultiGenerator` override primarily orchestrates the creation of several Ninja objects in a single batch. In practice it hooks into the base class’s generation routine, injects any multi‑instance specific parameters (e.g., concurrency flags or dependency scopes), and aggregates the resulting instances into a container for downstream consumption.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AddCXX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AddCXX.body: The function records a compilation step. It takes a source file, its working‑directory, the actual compiler command string, and the resulting object path, then appends a JSON object containing those values to a persistent “compile_commands.json” file. If the file stream hasn’t yet been opened, it creates and starts the JSON array; otherwise it appends a comma separator before the new entry. The values are escaped for JSON syntax before being written.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AllowD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AllowD.body: The function simply signals that the implementation permits a delete operation even when an error occurs. It returns `true`, indicating that any error condition should not block the delete action.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AllowN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AllowN.body: `AllowNotParallel()` simply signals that the current object may safely execute its logic without needing parallel execution. The method is declared `virtual const`, so it can be overridden by derived classes and used as a hook for subclasses to indicate that they do not require or support parallel processing.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Append.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Append.body: Iterates over the target’s direct dependencies, skips any that aren’t part of the build system, and pushes the relative path for each eligible target’s “all” target into the supplied dependency vector.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CanEsc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CanEsc.body: The function returns a boolean that signals whether the generator forces UNIX‑style paths to be escaped as backslashes; in practice this means callers can rely on the system to escape backslashes in generated makefiles.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CheckA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CheckA.body: The overridden method simply returns `true`, indicating that duplicates for custom targets are always allowed.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Comput.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Comput.body: The function builds the full path to the directory where the target’s object files will be placed. It obtains the current binary directory and the target‑specific directory from the target’s local generator, concatenates those strings with a trailing slash, and stores the resulting path in the target’s `ObjectDirectory` member.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Config.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Config.body: Initializes the CMAKE_EDIT_COMMAND cache entry via GetEditCacheCommand(), then forwards to the base cmGlobalGenerator::Configure() to complete the standard global‑generator configuration.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Conver.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Conver.body: The function decides which helper routine to use. On Windows platforms it can either return a Windows‑style path or, if the internal flag is set, delegate to the Unix path routine; on non‑Windows systems it always falls back to the Unix helper.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CountP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CountP.body: The function tallies the number of progress marks that the current generator instance has emitted for every target belonging to the snapshot identified by `lg`. It walks the `DirectoryTargetsMap` for the snapshot, passing each target to `CountProgressMarksInTarget` while feeding an accumulating set of already‑emitted targets to avoid double‑counting. The resulting sum is returned as the total count.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CountP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CountP.body: Counts the number of progress marks for the target and all its build‑system dependencies, avoiding duplicate counts by tracking already‑processed targets in the `emitted` set.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Create.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Create.body: Creates a new `cmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3` instance tied to the current `cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3` object and returns it wrapped in a `std::unique_ptr<cmLocalGenerator>`.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Enable.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Enable.body: The function forwards the language list to the base class’s EnableLanguage, then iterates through each language in the list—skipping any entry named “NONE”—and for every other language it calls ResolveLanguageCompiler to set up that language’s compiler for the makefile.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Genera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Genera.body: Clears the export‑fix directories and files list, invokes the base‑class Generate(), tallies the overall action count, records per‑target progress counters, emits the progress‑mark files, writes the primary and CMake makefiles, drains the command‑db buffer, and finally drops any stray “Clang‑Tidy” export entries that were never used.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Genera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Genera.body: The function assembles a command line for invoking a make tool: it optionally turns on verbose mode, sets the makefile to use, applies the desired parallel‑job count, appends any global make options, and finally appends each target name (appending “/fast” when the Fast flag is set). This single `GeneratedMakeCommand` object is then returned.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetAct.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetAct.body: GetActualName is a static method that returns a string constant.
