@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetAll.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetAll.body: The function `GetAllTargetName` is a protected virtual member that returns a pointer to the literal string `"all"`. It provides a fixed identifier used by derived classes to represent a generic or “all‑targets” name.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetBui.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetBui.body: This member simply supplies the command‑line switch used when the build system is told to ignore error‑reporting. It returns a constant‑qualified C‑string literal (`"-i"`) and is marked `override` to satisfy the base class’s pure virtual contract. It is a straightforward, const‑qualified getter that always yields that flag value.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetCle.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetCle.body: A protected virtual method that returns the literal string “clean”; it’s intended to supply a standard identifier for subclasses.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetDoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetDoc.body: It returns a cmDocumentationEntry that pairs the generator’s actual name with a brief description of its purpose.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetEmp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetEmp.body: It returns the stored `EmptyRuleHackCommand` string, giving read‑only access to that value.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetEmp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetEmp.body: The function simply returns the string value held in the member variable `EmptyRuleHackDepends`.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetIns.body: This method simply returns the literal string `"install/local"` as the local installation target name.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetIns.body: The `GetInstallStripTargetName()` function is a protected, virtual const member that simply returns the literal path `"install/strip"`. It’s purpose is to supply a default target directory for strip‑related installation tasks, which subclasses can override to change the destination path while preserving const‑correctness and polymorphic behavior.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetIns.body: Returns the literal string `"install"`, which represents the name of the installation target.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetNam.body:
The function is a pure const override that simply forwards the request to a static helper, returning a freshly‑constructed `std::string`.  
Because it never mutates any member data it can safely be called from any thread without causing race conditions.  
The return value is copied out of the helper, so the caller receives an independent string; no aliasing or lifetime surprises occur.  
Note that if `GetActualName()` were to change internal state in future versions, that could break const‑ness, so keep that helper truly const‑safe.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetPac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetPac.body: This member function overrides a virtual base‑class method, is marked `protected` so subclasses can call it, and returns a compile‑time constant C‑string literal (`"package_source"`) that represents the name of the source target for a package.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetPac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetPac.body:
The `GetPackageTargetName()` member simply returns the literal string `"package"`.  
It’s declared `protected`, `virtual`, `const`, and marked `override`, indicating it implements an inherited virtual interface.  
At runtime it supplies the fixed target name to callers, with no side‑effects or dynamic calculation.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetPre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetPre.body: The function simply returns the literal string `"preinstall"`. It overrides a virtual function in a base class, providing the name of the target used during the pre‑installation phase of the installation workflow. The function is `const`, so it guarantees not to modify the object state, and the return type `const char*` indicates it returns a pointer to a null‑terminated string literal stored in static storage.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetReb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetReb.body: Returns a string literal identifying the cache target used in the rebuild process.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetTes.body: This member simply returns a constant string literal. It is a protected, virtual getter marked const, overridden in derived classes. It returns the literal `"test"` as a pointer to a C‑style string. It is intended to be overridden to provide the name of the specific test target.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Initia.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Initia.body: Clears the directory‑to‑target mapping. For every local generator it walks through each of its generator targets; if a target is not excluded, it inserts that target into the set for every ancestor directory up the build‑system hierarchy. It also adds that target’s direct dependents to the same directory set, building a map of directories to the targets that must be built.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::IsGNUM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::IsGNUM.body: The override simply signals that the object is prepared to work with the GNUMake job server by always returning true. This flag lets callers treat the instance as job‑server‑aware without needing to inspect any state‑specific details.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::IsIPOS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::IsIPOS.body: This override simply reports that the current platform supports iOS. When invoked, it immediately returns `true`, signalling that the surrounding code can safely assume that iOS‑specific logic is available.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::NewFac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::NewFac.body: The function creates and returns a `std::unique_ptr` to a `cmGlobalGeneratorFactory` that produces Unix‑makefile generators via a simple factory specialization. It simply allocates a new `cmGlobalGeneratorSimpleFactory<cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3>` object and wraps it in a `unique_ptr` for automatic memory management.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Record.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Record.body: This function stores the number of progress actions and the path of the variable file for a target.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.body: It returns the stored flag indicating whether the tool supports compiler‑dependency handling.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.body: Returns `true` to signal that the implementation always supports custom command dependency files.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.body: This member function declares that the current object supports the creation of linker‑dependency files by overriding a virtual interface. It simply returns `true`, signalling that downstream consumers can rely on the class to produce such files.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.body: Returns whether the tool indicates support for long‑line dependency handling.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.body: The `SupportsPlatform` method is a trivial static helper that simply returns `false`. It has no internal logic or runtime checks; it acts as a placeholder, signalling that the current platform is not supported.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.body: The function simply returns false, indicating that the toolset is not supported.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Target.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Target.body: The method opens the target variable file and loops over each action in the current target. For every action it writes a line of the form `CMAKE_PROGRESS_<index>=<percentage>` to that file, computing the percentage as either the incremental count (if the total is at most 100) or the cumulative percentage when the total exceeds 100. After writing each line it records that value in the internal `Marks` list. When the loop completes it appends a blank line and increments the supplied `current` counter by the number of actions just processed.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteC.body: The routine walks through every generator target and emits a set of make‑file rules that tie the target’s source directory to its build and install steps. It stitches together “build”, “clean” and “pre‑install” commands, attaches dependency markers, and inserts progress‑tracking calls where the build system is configured to report progress. The helper method `WriteMakeRule` is used to emit each rule into the supplied rule‑file stream.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteC.body: Iterate over each local generator and its targets, emitting distinct make rules for targets that belong in the build system while tracking emitted names to avoid duplicates. For each such target, it writes a normal build rule, a fast‑build rule, and if needed, a pre‑install relink rule, all formatted through helper methods that assemble the appropriate recursive make calls and dependency lists.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteD.body: The function gathers all non‑excluded targets in a directory, optionally filtering those that need relinking before install, and adds their relative paths to a dependency list for that directory’s make target. It also appends the sub‑directory targets unless excluded. If no dependencies result, a special “empty‑rule” entry is used. Finally the rule is written out via the root generator’s `WriteMakeRule`, marking it as a recursive target for that directory.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteD.body: The routine writes a header comment for the target directory, then generates the three directory‑level rules—“all”, “preinstall” and “clean”. The “clean” rule is supplied with the commands returned by AppendDirectoryCleanCommand. All three rules are emitted via calls to WriteDirectoryRule2 with the appropriate flag values.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteH.body: The routine writes a “help” rule to the Makefile that prints a list of valid targets. It first collects the names of global, utility, and project targets from all local generators, then appends each one to a command list using `AppendEcho`. Finally it calls `WriteMakeRule` to emit the rule that echoes the collected list.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteM.body: The routine writes the primary CMake file used by the build system. It first checks a flag that may suppress regeneration; if that flag is set it exits immediately. Otherwise it opens (or creates if necessary) the file “Makefile.cmake” in the output directory, writes a disclaimer header and records the generator name, then gathers the list of source files from all attached local generators. The list is sorted, uniquified, and written into the file as the list of makefile dependencies. It also records the output and product files for each generator. Finally, it delegates the writing of language‑specific rules to the helper function `WriteMainCMakefileLanguageRules`.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteM.body:
The function streams into the C‑Make file a single variable that lists every target’s *DependInfo* file that belongs to the current build.  
It iterates over each generator, then over each target generated by that generator. For every target that is part of the build system and is not a global target, it computes the path to that target’s *DependInfo.cmake* file, normalises the slashes, and writes an entry in the form `"  "file_path"` to the stream. Finally it closes the list with a `)` to terminate the variable assignment.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteM.body:
The routine writes the Unix‑style makefile for the current build.  
It opens the output file, writes the disclaimer via the root local generator, and then emits a rule that makes the “all” target the first target so that a plain `make` succeeds.  
After that it writes special top and bottom sections, iterates over the directory‑based targets to emit their specific rules, and finally emits convenience rules for each local generator. The function relies on the helper methods of `cmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3` and on the stored directory target data.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::cmGlob.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::cmGlob.body: Initialises a Unix‑style makefile generator, establishing path handling, program location, color support, and platform‑specific link‑script usage while configuring directives and flags.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::cmGlob.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::cmGlob.body: The public copy constructor of `cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3` creates a new instance that is an exact copy of an existing one, copying all internal members to preserve the state of the original object.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::operat.body: The overload copies the supplied `cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3` instance into the current object and returns a reference to the modified object, enabling assignment chaining.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::~cmGlo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::~cmGlo.body: The destructor for `cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3` ensures all resources used by this generator are released when an object of this type is destroyed. It performs the necessary cleanup—such as closing any open streams, removing temporary files it created, and releasing owned memory—so that derived objects can be safely de‑allocated without leaking resources.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::AllowDel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::AllowDel.body: The function returns `false`, meaning that delete operations should not be carried out when an error occurs.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::AllowNot.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::AllowNot.body: The function simply returns `false`, indicating that the operation is not permitted to run in parallel mode.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::EnableLa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::EnableLa.body: The function registers a set of default build‑time preprocessor definitions in the supplied makefile object, configuring the WATCOM toolchain, path handling, symbolic rule handling, and the compiler for both C and C++ sources. After establishing those defaults it forwards the language list and optional flag to the base class implementation, which applies the language settings further.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::Generate.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::Generate.body: It forwards a request to the underlying Unix‑Makefile generator: it calls `cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GenerateBuildCommand` with the supplied program, project name and directory, the list of targets, the build configuration, a fixed parallel‑level flag (`NO_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL`), the verbosity flag, and the provided build options and make options, and returns the resulting vector of `GeneratedMakeCommand` objects.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::GetActua.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::GetActua.body: The `GetActualName()` function is a static utility that simply returns the string literal `"Watcom WMake"`.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::GetDocum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::GetDocum.body: It returns a `cmDocumentationEntry` that pairs the generator’s actual name with the explanatory text “Generates Watcom WMake makefiles.”

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::GetName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::GetName@.body: The `GetName()` member simply forwards the request to `cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::GetActualName()`, returning that string as the name of this generator instance.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::IsGNUMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::IsGNUMak.body: The `IsGNUMakeJobServerAware` virtual function returns `false`, indicating that the current component does not participate in or recognize the GNUMakeJob server mechanism.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::NewFacto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::NewFacto.body: Creates a unique‑owned instance of `cmGlobalGeneratorSimpleFactory` parametrized with `cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator`. The returned pointer gives the calling code a factory capable of producing those generators.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::PrintBui.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::PrintBui.body: The protected virtual function checks the requested parallel‑build level; if a non‑default value is supplied it emits a warning about WMake’s lack of parallel support, then forwards the call to the base Unix‑Makefile generator for the standard advice output.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::SetSyste.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::SetSyste.body: The method checks the current makefile’s processor definition; if it equals “I86” it injects the Watcom wcl compiler definitions for both C and C++ sources, then defers the rest of the work to the base Unix‑makefile generator’s implementation.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::cmGlobal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::cmGlobal.body: The `cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator` function is a public constructor-like routine that initializes a make‑file generator object. It processes command‑line arguments, validates them, and creates the appropriate `cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator` instance (typically an instance of `cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator`). It then registers this generator with the CMake global registry so subsequent build steps can invoke it to produce a platform‑specific Unix‑style makefile.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::cmGlobal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::cmGlobal.body: The constructor installs the WatcomW settings: it turns on color output and symbolic marking, sets the include and line‑continuation directives, and applies Windows‑specific flags (e.g., silent mode and shell handling).

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::cmGlobal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::cmGlobal.body: The constructor creates a new `cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator` instance by copying the configuration and internal state from an existing instance. It preserves all generator settings, enabling the new object to generate the same type of makefiles as the original.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::operator.body: Assigns a `cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator` from an rvalue reference and returns a reference to the left‑hand side. It performs a move‑assignment style operation.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::operator.body: The `operator=` overload performs a member‑wise copy from the RHS object into the current instance. It first checks for self‑assignment, then copies each data member (including base‑class members via `cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3`), and finally returns `*this` so that chained assignments can be used. This operator ensures the object’s internal state is fully replicated, preserving invariants and avoiding leaks or double‑free issues.

@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::~cmGloba.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator::~cmGloba.body: The virtual destructor `~cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator()` is invoked whenever an instance of `cmGlobalWatcomWMakeGenerator` is destroyed. It performs cleanup of any resources that the generator has allocated—such as temporary files, opened streams, or internal data structures—ensuring that derived subclasses have a chance to release their own resources before the base destructor runs. The function simply orchestrates this orderly release; no further logic or side‑effects are expected.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddCommandsToB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddCommandsToB.body: The function creates a per‑configuration “make” script in `CMakeScripts`, writes a rule for each custom command, and then builds a command line that runs `make` in the build directory with that script. It attaches this command to the build phase’s `shellScript` attribute and disables environment‐var logging.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddConfigurati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddConfigurati.body: The routine builds a configuration list for a target object: it fetches the required configuration types, creates a list‑attribute container, and for each type builds a configuration object with its own settings group. Each configuration is appended to the list and marked with a comment; the first configuration in the list is flagged as the default visible configuration.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependAndLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependAndLi.body: It validates the supplied `Item` instance and reports success via a boolean.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependAndLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependAndLi.body: This lambda takes an `cmComputeLinkInformation::Item const*` and returns `true` if that pointer equals `libItemPtr`, otherwise `false`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependAndLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependAndLi.body: This lambda inserts `libItemPtr` into `configItemMap[configName]` only when it isn’t already present, using `std::find_if` to check for an existing pointer before appending.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependAndLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependAndLi.body: The routine validates the target, gathers its direct dependencies, and walks through the link‑information objects to decide whether a dependent library should be linked via the special “Link Binary With Libraries” phase or simply via standard linker flags. It builds per‑configuration maps of library items, collects framework and search paths (handling both standard and Xcode‑specific frameworks), and creates file references for any external libraries. For each library it records the appropriate search directories, attaches required search‑path attributes to the target, and registers the dependency in the build‑phase objects. The end result is a target populated with the correct list of library dependencies, search paths, and framework references for every configuration.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddDependTarge.body: Creates a proxy‐container object, links it to the source target via attributes, then creates a dependency record that points back to that proxy. The new dependency record is appended to the target’s existing dependency attribute.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedApp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedApp.body: Adds the specified “Embed App Extensions” objects to the given code object by calling `AddEmbeddedObjects` with the fixed target folder path (“13”) and the standard removal‑of‑headers flag.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedExt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedExt.body: The function pulls the pre‑declared sub‑folder spec string “16” and calls the helper `AddEmbeddedObjects` to embed a set of extension objects into the supplied `target` object. It tells the helper that the objects belong to the “Embed App Extensions” group, tags them with the macro name `XCODE_EMBED_EXTENSIONKIT_EXTENSIONS`, and directs the result into the `EXTENSIONS_FOLDER_PATH`. It also uses the default flag `RemoveHeadersOnCopyByDefault` so that any redundant headers are stripped during the copy step. This single call installs the extension kit into the target’s internal structure.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedFra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedFra.body: The `AddEmbeddedFrameworks` routine registers a framework‑level embedding step in the code‑generation pipeline. It invokes `AddEmbeddedObjects` with a hard‑coded identifier, a predefined destination sub‑folder string, and the flag `NoActionOnCopyByDefault`, thereby ensuring the selected framework objects are copied into the build output only when the target object requires them, without triggering any copy‑on‑copy side‑effects.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedObj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedObj.body: The routine collects the list of files to embed (frameworks, dylibs, or plain files) for a target that is a framework/bundle, creates a copy‑files phase with those references (applying any REMOVE_HEADERS/CodeSign flags), and finally inserts that phase just before the final post‑build step.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedPlu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedPlu.body: The routine calls the generic `AddEmbeddedObjects` helper, passing the supplied target object, a label string (“Embed PlugIns”), a constant key string (`“XCODE_EMBED_PLUGINS”`), the hard‑coded sub‑folder spec `"13"`, and a flag value that indicates no special action on copy. This effectively registers the embedded plug‑in objects for the given target.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedRes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddEmbeddedRes.body: The routine simply delegates to `AddEmbeddedObjects`, wiring the target with a sub‑folder “7” and a fixed tag (“XCODE_EMBED_RESOURCES”) while keeping the default copy‑action unchanged.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddExtraIDETar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddExtraIDETar.body: The method iterates over the internal project map, treating each entry’s first generator as the root for the current project. For each such root, it invokes `SetGenerationRoot` and subsequently calls `AddExtraTargets`, which in turn registers the standard IDE build targets such as ALL_BUILD, INSTALL, etc. This routine runs before any downstream generation logic to guarantee that those auxiliary targets are present in the generated build graph.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddExtraTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddExtraTarget.body:
The function creates an “ALL_BUILD” utility target that invokes `make` on all projects.  
It attaches any Xcode‑generated config files to that target, adds a zero‑check target that runs a re‑run CMake makefile when a rebuild is required, and hooks the generated targets into the build graph.  
For each generator target it registers the zero‑check as a dependency unless the target is excluded, and for object libraries it installs a post‑build depend‑check helper that runs the legacy depend‑helper makefile after the library is built.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddPositionInd.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddPositionInd.body: The function checks whether the target is executable, fetches its PIC configuration value, and if that value indicates position‑independent code, it adds an attribute “LD_NO_PIE” set to “NO” (otherwise “YES”) to the given code object.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddXCodeProjBu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AddXCodeProjBu.body: The method appends the *CMakeLists.txt* source file from the target’s current source directory to the supplied sources vector if it’s not already present.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendBuildSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendBuildSet.body: The routine searches the target’s configuration list for an entry whose name matches the supplied configName (or any entry if the name is empty). Once found, it fetches that entry’s existing build‑settings and hands off the new attribute/value pair to AppendOrAddBuildSetting, which inserts or updates the setting as appropriate.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendBuildSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendBuildSet.body: The function attaches a value to a settings object: it verifies that the value is a string or list, then depending on whether the attribute itself is a list or string, it either appends each element of the value list to the attribute list, or concatenates string values (separating with a space). If the types don’t match, it raises an error message.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendDefines@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendDefines@.body: The routine parses the supplied definition string into a list of individual items and then hands that list to a helper that appends each item to the internal collection, conditioned on the flag.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendDefines@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendDefines@.body: This routine iterates over a vector of raw define strings, normalises each entry to the appropriate `‑D` form (removing an existing `‑D` when `dflag` is false, or adding one when it is true), escapes any special characters via `AppendFlag`, and stores the escaped result into the supplied `BuildObjectListOrString` collection.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendDirector.body: The function simply concatenates the supplied `prefix`, `config`, and `suffix` strings onto the `dir` string, but only when a non‑empty `config` is supplied.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendFlag@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendFlag@k_Z.body: The routine appends a new flag string to the supplied flag list: it first tests whether the flag is non‑empty, then adds a space separator if the list already contains entries. If the flag contains any character that could interfere with downstream parsing (spaces, punctuation, backslashes, quotes, etc.), it is wrapped in single quotes and any internal single quotes or backslashes are escaped (single quotes become \'' and backslashes become \\). Once the escaped characters are inserted, the quoted flag is closed and the assembled string is appended to the list.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendOrAddBui.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::AppendOrAddBui.body: The routine ensures a particular attribute exists in a `cmXCodeObject` representing build settings: if the attribute is missing it adds the supplied value; otherwise it delegates to `AppendBuildSettingAttribute` to merge the new value into the existing attribute.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.body: It marks the instance as non‑empty and then either supplies the supplied text to a group‑attached generator (creating a string object) or, if no group is present, simply appends the text followed by a space to its internal string buffer.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.body: BuildObjectListOrString takes a collection of objects and, based on the context of the call, emits either a string representation of that collection or an actual list of object references that subsequent code can consume. It resolves object identities and orders them appropriately, then hands the result back to the caller.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.body: When `buildObjectList` is true, the constructor invokes the generator to create an `OBJECT_LIST` object and stores the resulting object in the member `Group`; otherwise it performs no further action.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.body: BuildObjectListOrString takes a structured description of objects (via a `BuildObjectListOrString` instance) and produces either a list of those objects or a single string representing them. It inspects the input to determine whether to assemble a collection of object representations or serialize them into a string form, returning the result for downstream code‑generation logic.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.body: The function returns a pointer to a `cmXCodeObject`. If the `Group` member is non‑null, the function immediately returns it; otherwise it falls back to creating a new object via the `Generator` using the stored `String`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.body: Returns a const reference to the internally stored string, letting callers read the value without copying or modifying it.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::BuildObjectLis.body: The `IsEmpty()` method returns the value of the internal `Empty` flag. It simply reads that member and returns it; it has no side‑effects and runs in constant time.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ClearXCodeObje.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ClearXCodeObje.body: The method wipes out all internal bookkeeping containers—sets, maps, and collections that track target sets, code objects, identifiers, and file reference mappings—resetting the generator’s state to a clean slate.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ComputeArchite.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ComputeArchite.body: The function clears any previously stored architectures, then attempts to populate the list from the `CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES` definition. If that definition is missing or empty, it falls back to the `_CMAKE_APPLE_ARCHS_DEFAULT` value. When neither is available, it falls back to the first architecture value supplied by `CMAKE_XCODE_ARCHS` (truncated at a semicolon if present). After establishing the default architecture, it calls `ComputeObjectDirArch` to finish the setup.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ComputeInfoPLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ComputeInfoPLi.body: The routine concatenates the target’s current binary directory with the subfolder “CMakeFiles/” and the target’s name, appending “.dir/Info.plist”, and returns that string.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ComputeObjectD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ComputeObjectD.body: When invoked, the method inspects how many architectures are present and whether an effective‑platform name is needed. If there are multiple architectures or an effective‑platform name is required, it assigns the special string `$(CURRENT_ARCH)`. If only one architecture exists, it assigns that single value. If no architectures are known, it falls back to a predefined default.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ComputeTargetO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ComputeTargetO.body: The function builds the `ObjectDirectory` string for a target: it first asks the helper that resolves the arch‑specific segment (`GetTargetObjectDirArch`), then concatenates the temporary directory prefix (from `GetTargetTempDir` and the config’s temp directory), a standard “$(OBJECT_FILE_DIR_normal:base)” marker, and that arch string, finally appending a trailing slash. This gives the full path that the code generator will use to place compiled objects for that target.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ConstructScrip.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ConstructScrip.body: This function builds a shell‑style script string that first changes into the appropriate working directory (falling back to the current binary directory if none is supplied) and then appends each non‑empty command from the supplied command generator after normalising its path separators and applying the generator’s output‑format conversion. It performs in‑place variable substitution on the directory and every command, and returns the assembled script.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ConvertToRelat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ConvertToRelat.body: The method forwards a given path to the helper `cmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputPath`, which resolves the path to a relative form appropriate for Make invocation. It simply returns that resolved string.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateBuildSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateBuildSet.body: It removes everything from the first occurrence of “=” onward, leaving the preceding part intact.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateBuildSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateBuildSet.body: Collects compile options per language, resolves include directories, builds framework and system search paths, handles architecture and versioning, and populates a build settings object with all these attributes (compiler flags, include paths, framework flags, and target‑specific flags such as library style, export macro, and pre‑compile headers).

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateCustomCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateCustomCo.body: The function collects the target’s pre‑, pre‑link, and post‑build commands, injects symlink helpers for shared libs, then constructs and registers run‑script phases (legacy‑ or standard‑build) in the order: pre‑build → custom rules → pre‑link → framework → post‑build, appending each phase to the build vector.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateCustomRu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateCustomRu.body: The function writes a makefile that registers every custom command for a target. It creates a rule file in the target’s binary directory, emits a top‑level “all” target that pulls in every output, adds include lines for generated depfiles, and emits a rule for each command with its dependencies and command line (including working‑dir handling and argument escaping). It also emits dummy rules for symbolic inputs that should not be built during a normal build.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateFlatClon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateFlatClon.body: Creates a new instance of the same type as the given object, copies all of its attributes into that instance, and returns the newly‑created clone.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateGlobalXC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateGlobalXC.body: The method evaluates a source path named “CMAKE_XCODE_XCCONFIG” for the current configuration. If the path is empty or the file cannot be found, it logs an error and aborts. Otherwise it creates an X‑code file reference for that source, validates success, and attaches the resulting reference to the supplied config object as its “baseConfigurationReference” attribute.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateGroups@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateGroups@k.body: The function walks through each generator’s source groups and assigns every source file to the appropriate group for that target. It skips targets that are not part of the build system, global targets, or the special check target. For each real source file it locates the corresponding source‑group, creates or fetches a PBX group object, and records it in a map keyed by the group’s path. It also drops in helper files such as CMakeLists.txt and Info.plist for targets that need them (e.g., a macOS bundle). The routine finishes with the map fully populated and returns `true`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateLegacyRu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateLegacyRu.body: Creates a build‑phase object for a legacy run‑script build step. If no commands are supplied and the phase name isn’t “CMake ReRun”, it returns null. Otherwise it instantiates a shell‑script build phase, tags it with a mask string, lists the files involved, names the phase, sets whether it runs only for deployment post‑processing, points to the shell interpreter, and attaches the supplied commands before returning the configured object.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateLocalGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateLocalGen.body: The function creates and returns a `cmLocalGenerator` wrapped in a `unique_ptr`. It constructs the generator with the current `cmGlobalXCodeGenerator` instance and the supplied `cmMakefile*`. If the current build system is “Twelve” or newer, it sets the generator to emit shell‑script link commands directly (via `SetLinkScriptShell(true)`). Finally it returns the constructed generator.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateObject@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateObject@k.body: Creates a unique cmXCodeObject of the requested type, registers it with the generator via addObject, and returns a raw pointer to that instance.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateObject@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateObject@k.body: The method builds a new cmXCode21Object, stores it in the generator’s internal collection via addObject, and hands back a raw pointer to that instance—leaving ownership of the object to the container that holds it.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateObjectRe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateObjectRe.body: The routine allocates a fresh `cmXCodeObject` marked as an object‑reference, links the supplied target object into that new node via `SetObject`, and hands the populated object back to the caller.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateOrGetPBX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateOrGetPBX.body: The method builds or retrieves a hierarchy of “PBX” groups that mirror a source group’s path. It first constructs a unique string key from the target folder, target name, and the source group’s full name. If that key already exists in `GroupNameMap`, it returns the cached group. Otherwise, it walks up the path components of the target folder, creating any missing intermediate groups with `CreatePBXGroup` and storing them in `TargetGroup`. When the source group itself isn’t the root (its full name differs from its simple name), the routine descends into deeper sub‑folders, creating nested groups accordingly. Finally, it creates a group for the current source group, adds it to `GroupNameMap`, and returns it. The function essentially guarantees a unique group object for every source group while maintaining a cached map of previously created groups.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreatePBXGroup.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreatePBXGroup.body: The function builds a new PBX group object, attaches it to the supplied parent’s child list if one exists, and returns the newly created group.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateReRunCMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateReRunCMa.body:
The routine assembles a list of all sub‑makefiles, deduplicates them, and emits a new `ReRunCMake.make` script under `CMakeScripts`.  
It writes a header block defining `TARGETS`, then appends each relative file path to that variable.  
When global verification is enabled it adds a “.NOTPARALLEL” rule that triggers a special `VERIFY_GLOBS` target invoking the CMake command with the appropriate source‑ and binary‑directories.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateRunScrip.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateRunScrip.body:
Creates a build‑phase object that will generate a shell script to run the custom command for every configuration type.  
For each configuration it builds a command block that checks the current configuration name, gathers the command’s real dependencies (resolving them via the local generator), and appends the resulting script to an accumulating string.  
The function records all dependency files and output files seen, attaches them as input and output paths, and creates (if necessary) empty dependency files under the `CMakeFiles/d/` directory.  
Finally it configures the phase with attributes such as the dependency file path, the `buildActionMask`, and flags controlling deployment‑only execution, before returning the populated phase object.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateRunScrip.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateRunScrip.body: Creates a build phase that runs the supplied custom commands in a shell script, conditioned on each configuration type. It collects all output files produced by those commands and returns an XCodeObject configured with the appropriate attributes (buildActionMask, files, outputPaths, etc.).

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateRunScrip.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateRunScrip.body: The function recursively adds build‑phase objects for source files that carry a custom command, using the visited set to avoid repeated work, storing each file‑command pair in the root map, and appending the created phase object to the supplied build‑phases container.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateRunScrip.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateRunScrip.body: Retrieves the list of source files for the target, then for each file calls the helper that creates a run‑script build‑phase for that file.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateString@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateString@k.body: The method creates a new `cmXCodeObject` of type `STRING`, sets its internal string value to the supplied `std::string`, and returns a pointer to this object.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateTargetXC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateTargetXC.body: Evaluates the target’s XCODE_XCCONFIG property; if absent it exits. Otherwise it fetches the corresponding source file, verifies it exists, creates a reference object for that file, and attaches it to the supplied configuration via the “baseConfigurationReference” attribute.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateUtilityT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateUtilityT.body:
The routine builds a shell‑script phase object, attaches lists for input and output files, and populates a set of attributes that describe the phase (such as the shell script itself and its execution flags).  
It then packages that phase into an aggregate target object, adds any necessary build‑rule references, records the target in an internal map for later lookup, and finally returns the created target object.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeBui.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeBui.body: It creates (or re‑uses) a build‑file XCode object for a given file path: it first obtains a unique file‑reference object, looks up that reference in a map, and if none exists it makes a new build‑file object, stores it in the map, and returns it.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeDep.body: The routine writes a makefile that forces Xcode to relink everything by emitting dummy rules for each target and its dependencies. It inserts a default target that simply echoes a warning, writes commands to delete stale binaries and linked objects for each configuration, and then outputs a list of relative‑path dependencies for each library and object library that Xcode must rebuild. This makes the build system re‑link everything whenever any of the recorded dependencies is newer than the target.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeFil.body: The routine first resolves the source file’s absolute path, obtains the language identifier from the current generator, and then delegates to CreateXCodeFileReferenceFromPath to construct and return the corresponding cmXCodeObject instance.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeFil.body: The routine parses a file path, infers its type from either a supplied source‑file property or by inspecting the extension, then creates or reuses a cmXCodeObject representing that file. It populates the object with attributes such as fileEncoding, the inferred file type (either explicit or last‑known), the file name, path and source tree classification, and finally attaches the object to the appropriate PBX group.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeObj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeObj.body: The function initializes the Xcode object tree by clearing any previous data, then constructs the root project object, a main group of child groups (products, frameworks, resources), and a list of build styles derived from the current configuration types. It sets up a global build‑settings object populated with SDK roots, architectures, deployment targets, and Swift language options, cloning this object per configuration and adding any custom‑command attributes. Finally, it generates target objects for each generator, attaches dependency and link information to them, and appends them to the root object's target list, returning success unless any group creation fails.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeSou.body: Creates an XCode build object for a source file, collecting language‑specific flags (fixed/free format), compile options, and per‑source definitions and attributes. It resolves include directories and appends them to the flag list, then constructs a settings object holding the compiler flags and attributes. Finally it attaches these settings to the build file object and returns it.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeTar.body: The method assembles a new XCode object for a target that is part of the build system. It creates a `PBXNativeTarget` instance, attaches the target’s build‑phase list, the corresponding build‑rules, and dependency list, then populates attributes for the target’s name, product name, and the file reference that points to the generated output file. The constructed object is stored in an internal map for quick lookup and returned.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeTar.body: The routine checks whether the target has already been emitted; if not, it gathers all source files from the target, splits them into source, header, resource, and content categories, creates appropriate build‑phase objects for each category (including framework‑specific copy phases), collects those phases into a list, and finally constructs and returns an Xcode target object that is appended to the output vector.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::CreateXCodeTar.body: The routine sets the current local generator, retrieves the list of its targets in the proper order, iterates over each target creating an X‑code representation, aborting with a false if any creation fails, and finally sorts the resulting collection before returning true.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::EnableLanguage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::EnableLanguage.body: The method injects a collection of build‑time definitions into the makefile (e.g. `XCODE` and a version string), declares the four standard CMake build types, turns off the compiler‑environment injection flag, hands control to the base language‑initializer, and finally triggers architecture discovery for the current build.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ExpandCFGIntDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ExpandCFGIntDi.body: The function scans the input text for two placeholder patterns—`$(CONFIGURATION)$(EFFECTIVE_PLATFORM_NAME)` and `$(CONFIGURATION)`—then substitutes each occurrence with the supplied configuration string, returning the fully‑expanded string.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ExtractFlag@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ExtractFlag@k_.body: The routine walks backwards through the supplied text, repeatedly locating the requested flag string with `rfind`. Whenever it finds an occurrence that is either at the start of the string or preceded by a space, it appends that occurrence to a result string and overwrites the original characters with spaces, effectively removing them from the source. It then continues searching from the preceding position until no further matches exist.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ExtractFlagReg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ExtractFlagReg.body: It scans the supplied text for the first occurrence of the pattern described by exp, pulls out that fragment (at the requested capture group), overwrites it with blanks in the original string, and hands the fragment back to the caller.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Creat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Creat.body:
The function verifies that the requested generator name matches the real one.  
If the name matches, it locates the Xcode version file by probing three standard paths.  
After parsing the “<major>.<minor>” version string it converts it into a numeric value (10×major + minor).  
If that numeric value is below 5.0 it emits a fatal error; otherwise it creates and returns a new `cmGlobalXCodeGenerator` instance initialized with the parsed version.  
If the build is bootstrapped (CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP defined) it skips the version checks and constructs a default‑version generator instead.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Facto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Facto.body: The `Factory` constructor accepts an rvalue reference (`Factory&&`) and copies the internal state of the passed‑in instance into the new object, effectively performing a move‑construction of the factory’s internal data. This allows a `Factory` instance to be constructed by taking ownership of resources from an existing instance without copying them, enabling efficient transfer of the factory’s internal configuration.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Facto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Facto.body: The `Factory` function is a constructor that takes a reference to another `Factory` object and initializes the new instance accordingly—typically copying or forwarding the internal state of the argument into the new object. It is used wherever a `cmGlobalXCodeGenerator` object needs to create or obtain a new factory instance that adheres to the `cmGlobalGeneratorFactory` interface.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Facto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Facto.body: Creates a new `cmGlobalXCodeGenerator` instance, registers it with the global generator registry, and returns a pointer to that instance so callers can use the generator in subsequent code‑generation calls.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetDe.body: The method returns the default platform name string—overriding a virtual const function.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetDo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetDo.body: Returns a `cmDocumentationEntry` by delegating to the base implementation (`cmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetDocumentation`).

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetGe.body: It returns a vector holding the single string supplied by cmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetActualName().

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetGe.body: It returns an empty vector of generator names.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetKn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::GetKn.body: This method is a const member that returns a `std::vector<std::string>`. Its current implementation simply returns an empty vector, effectively serving as a placeholder for the list of known platform strings.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Suppo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Suppo.body: This function simply reports that the current platform is unsupported by returning `false`. It overrides a virtual query in the base interface to signal that no specific support logic is available.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Suppo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::Suppo.body: The `SupportsToolset` member is a const virtual function that simply reports the class always supports the toolset by returning `true`. It overrides a base‑class interface, so any derived type will inherit this behavior unless overridden. The implementation is trivial, no state changes, and simply indicates that the toolset is enabled.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::opera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::opera.body: The operator is a public factory‑call that, when invoked, creates and returns a new instance by executing the stored factory callable.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::opera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::opera.body: The operator= copies the state of another Factory into the current object, member‑wise, and returns a reference to *this so that chained assignments can be performed.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::~Fact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Factory::~Fact.body: ~Factory() is a virtual destructor that guarantees proper cleanup of any resources allocated by a Factory instance. When an object of this type is destroyed, the function is invoked automatically to release memory, close connections, and perform any necessary de‑initialisation before the base class destructor runs. This enables derived factories to clean up their specific resources in a polymorphic context while ensuring that no dangling references remain.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::FilterConfigur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::FilterConfigur.body:
It scans an attribute string for a “[variant=…]” tag.  
If the tag exists and its value equals the passed configuration name, it strips that tag; otherwise it discards the attribute entirely.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::FindMakeProgra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::FindMakeProgra.body: The method checks whether the “CMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM” definition is disabled; if it is, it assigns the generator’s build command to that key in the makefile, and always returns true.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::FindXCodeTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::FindXCodeTarge.body: The `FindXCodeTarget` function returns the corresponding `cmXCodeObject` for a given target `t`. It first guards against a null pointer, then looks up the target in `XCodeObjectMap`. If the target isn’t present in the map it returns `nullptr`; otherwise it returns the stored object.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::FindXcodeBuild.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::FindXcodeBuild.body: The function probes the system for the executable named `xcodebuild`; if it can’t locate it, it defaults to the literal `"xcodebuild"`, and returns that path string.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ForceLinkerLan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ForceLinkerLan.body: The routine forces a particular link‑style language to be used when an Xcode target is built. It first verifies that the target is something that actually performs linking (executable, shared library, or module library). If the target already advertises the desired language in its link‑implementation list, the function exits. Otherwise it creates an empty source file in the target’s output tree, tags that file with the language property (e.g., “CXX”) and adds it to the source list. This dummy file tricks the build system into selecting the requested linker language for the target’s build step. The function also skips targets marked as iOS sticker‑packs, which are exempt from the linker‑language enforcement.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ForceLinkerLan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ForceLinkerLan.body: The routine iterates over every registered generator, retrieves the list of targets that the generator handles, and invokes `ForceLinkerLanguage` for each target to enforce the expected linker language for that target.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Generate@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Generate@k_ZN2.body:
It first calls the base generator, aborts if an error flag is set, then loops through each project in the project map.  
For projects marked to generate only at the top level it skips sub‑directories.  
It pre‑loads the enabled languages once, sets the current generation root, and finally writes out the xcode project.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GenerateBuildC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GenerateBuildC.body: The function builds a `GeneratedMakeCommand` for an Xcode‑based build. It selects the make program, attaches the project name (if supplied), sets the target(s) – defaulting to `ALL_BUILD` when no explicit targets are specified, or to `ALL_BUILD` when the target list contains “clean” – and adds flags for parallelization, job count, configuration, and any supplied extra options. The resulting command string is returned wrapped in a `std::vector`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetCMakeCFGInt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetCMakeCFGInt.body: The `GetCMakeCFGIntDir()` method provides the absolute path that the code generator uses to store its CMake build‑time configuration files. It’s a simple const member that concatenates two run‑time values—`CONFIGURATION` and `EFFECTIVE_PLATFORM_NAME`—into a single string and returns that string. In practice, callers use it to locate the directory where the generated CMake files (e.g., `.cmake/` or a platform‑specific subfolder) should be written or read from, ensuring that the config directory matches the current build target.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetDeploymentP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetDeploymentP.body: Returns a string identifying the target deployment environment for an Apple build. The string is chosen from a small lookup table based on `mf->GetAppleSDKType()`, mapping each SDK enumeration to a corresponding deployment‑target constant such as `TVOS`, `IPHONEOS`, `WATCHOS`, `XROS` or `MACOS`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetDocumentati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetDocumentati.body: The method constructs and returns a `cmDocumentationEntry` whose first element is the generator’s canonical name (via `GetActualName()`) and whose second element is the fixed description string “Generate Xcode project files.”. This entry is used by consumers that need metadata about the generator.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetLibraryOrFr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetLibraryOrFr.body: The method examines the supplied path for a framework component. It calls `SplitFrameworkPath`; if that returns an object, the method returns the framework‑specific path via `GetFrameworkPath()`. Otherwise, it returns the original path unchanged.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetObjectId@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetObjectId@k_.body:
The routine produces a 24‑character identifier.  
When a key is provided it hashes the type plus the key with SHA‑256, then truncates the hex digest to 24 characters.  
If no key is supplied it generates a UUID, strips hyphens and shortens it to 24 characters before returning the string.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetOrCreateId@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetOrCreateId@.body: The function checks whether a GUID value for a given name is already cached in the internal instance cache. If the value exists, it returns that stored value; otherwise it registers the supplied id in the cache and returns it.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetSymrootDir@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetSymrootDir@.body: It builds the path to the build sub‑directory inside the current instance’s home output directory by appending “/build” to that path.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetFileT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetFileT.body: The function examines a target’s declared type and any explicit file‑type override. It first looks for the property `"XCODE_EXPLICIT_FILE_TYPE"`; if present, that string is returned. Otherwise, it switches on the target’s state (library, library‑wrapper, bundle, executable, etc.) and maps each case to a hard‑coded suffix such as `"archive.ar"`, `"wrapper.framework"`, `"compiled.mach-o.dylib"`, etc., depending on the target’s properties (`FRAMEWORK`, Apple bundle flags). If none of the cases match, the function returns `nullptr`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetLinkF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetLinkF.body: The function returns a string identifier to be used for link flag configuration. When the Xcode version is ≥ 60 and the target is a static or object library it returns the flag string `"OTHER_LIBTOOLFLAGS"`, otherwise it returns `"OTHER_LDFLAGS"`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetProdu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetProdu.body: The function examines a target’s properties to decide which product‑type identifier string to return. It first looks for an explicit “XCODE_PRODUCT_TYPE” property and returns it if present; otherwise it inspects the target’s type and, when appropriate, checks for framework flags. Based on the type (library, module, shared, executable, etc.) it returns one of a handful of constant strings such as “com.apple.product‑type.framework”, “com.apple.product‑type.library.static”, “com.apple.product‑type.bundle”, “com.apple.product‑type.tool”, or “com.apple.product‑type.application”.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetTempD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetTempD.body: Combines the symroot directory with the target’s name and a “.build” suffix, then appends the supplied config name to form the full temporary path.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetXcodeBuildC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::GetXcodeBuildC.body: The routine lazily initializes the command string: on the first call it sets a flag, invokes `FindXcodeBuildCommand()` to compute the command, stores the result, and thereafter simply returns the cached string.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::HasKnownObject.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::HasKnownObject.body: This method checks whether the object‑file directory for the supplied target contains a valid architecture placeholder. It obtains the target’s object directory string, tests for a `$` marker; if found, it writes a descriptive message to the optional `reason` buffer and returns `false`, otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::InheritBuildSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::InheritBuildSe.body: The method walks through the target’s build‑configuration list, looks for a requested attribute in each configuration’s build‑settings, and when found it creates a list (via BuildObjectListOrString) that contains the value of “$(inherited)”, then appends that value to the target object via AppendBuildSettingAttribute.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::IsHeaderFile@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::IsHeaderFile@k.body: The function returns `true` when the source file’s extension is among the registered header extensions (e.g., `.h`, `.hpp`, etc.). It simply calls `cm::contains` against the list returned by `GetHeaderExtensions()` and the file’s extension. If the extension matches, the result is `true`; otherwise it is `false`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::IsMultiConfig@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::IsMultiConfig@.body: This function simply reports that the current Xcode setup supports multiple configurations. It always returns `true` regardless of any state or parameters, signifying that any invocation of the generator will work in a multi‑configuration environment.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::LookupFlags@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::LookupFlags@k_.body: Constructs a variable name from the supplied prefix, language code, and suffix, looks it up in the current makefile, and if a non‑empty definition exists it returns that value; otherwise it falls back to the supplied default string.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::NewFactory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::NewFactory@k_Z.body: Creates and returns a `std::unique_ptr<cmGlobalGeneratorFactory>` that owns a freshly allocated `Factory` instance.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Open@k_ZN22cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::Open@k_ZN22cmG.body: The Open method builds a path string for the requested project file and, unless in dry‑run mode, uses CoreFoundation APIs to open that file, returning whether the open succeeded.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::OutputXCodePro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::OutputXCodePro.body: The function builds an X‑code project bundle for the current target. It first verifies that there is at least one generator and that the X‑code objects can be created. Then it creates the output directory, writes the main project file (`project.pbxproj`) by invoking `WriteXCodePBXProj`, emits any shared schemes with `OutputXCodeSharedSchemes`, writes workspace settings via `OutputXCodeWorkspaceSettings`, clears internal state, and finally flushes the CMake cache for the current binary directory.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::OutputXCodeSha.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::OutputXCodeSha.body: The function first aggregates all `cmXCodeObject`s that represent Apple‑testable targets (i.e. `OBJECT` objects whose target has an `XCTEST_TESTEE` property and passes the `IsXCTestOnApple` flag). These objects are grouped by their testee in a map. Afterwards, if the internal Xcode version is at least 6.4, the method iterates through the same objects again, and for each that meets the target‑type (native or aggregate) and the build‑flag (`IsInTryCompile` or `XCODE_GENERATE_SCHEME` property) tests, it emits a shared‑scheme file using the `cmXCodeScheme` helper. The function returns true if at least one scheme was written.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::OutputXCodeWor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::OutputXCodeWor.body: Creates the directory `project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata`, then writes a `WorkspaceSettings.xcsettings` file in Property‑List XML. The file records the current Xcode build system; if the engine version is ≥ 1.0 it records the system type (`"Original"` or `"Latest"`) and, depending on the Xcode version, the corresponding deprecation‑diagnostic flag. If scheme files were generated, it also records an explicit flag to skip auto‑creating contexts. The function stops when the output file cannot be opened.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ParseGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ParseGenerator.body: The function tokenizes a comma‑separated string of toolset definitions, treating the first token optionally as the toolset name. It then iterates over the remaining tokens, ensuring each has a ‘=’ separator. For each key/value pair it checks for duplicate keys and delegates handling to `ProcessGeneratorToolsetField`; if any token is malformed or duplicated, it reports a fatal error via the makefile’s message system and aborts parsing. If all tokens succeed, the function returns `true`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::PostBuildMakeT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::PostBuildMakeT.body: It builds a string in the form `PostBuild.<name>.<config>` by replacing any spaces in the supplied name with underscores before concatenating the parts.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ProcessGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ProcessGenerat.body: The function validates the toolset field “buildsystem”. It accepts only the string values “1” or “12” (mapping to the two supported build systems), sets the internal `XcodeBuildSystem` flag, and rejects any other value with a fatal error. It also checks that the chosen system is compatible with the current Xcode version; if the combination is invalid it emits another fatal error and returns `false`. If all checks succeed, the function returns `true`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::RelativeToBina.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::RelativeToBina.body: The method forwards the supplied path string to the current root generator’s `MaybeRelativeToCurBinDir` routine and returns whatever string that routine produces.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::RelativeToSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::RelativeToSour.body: The routine takes a file path, checks whether it lies under the current source tree, and if so, rewrites it to a relative form; otherwise it passes the path unchanged.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SetCurrentLoca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SetCurrentLoca.body: The function assigns a supplied local generator to the `CurrentLocalGenerator` member, pulls its associated makefile into `CurrentMakefile`, and refreshes the `CurrentConfigurationTypes` list by querying that makefile for its generator configurations (including empty ones).

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SetGenerationR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SetGenerationR.body: The method stores the supplied generator as the current root, records its project name, creates the output directory if needed, and builds the path to the helper makefile that will be used during code generation.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SetGeneratorTo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SetGeneratorTo.body: The `SetGeneratorToolset` method parses a string of tool‑set identifiers into the internal `GeneratorToolset` list. It first calls `ParseGeneratorToolset`; if that fails the call returns `false`. If parsing succeeded and the caller requested a build (`build == true`), the method returns `true` immediately. Otherwise, if the list is non‑empty it registers the toolset with the makefile via `AddDefinition`. Finally it records the build system string and always returns `true` on successful completion.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SetSystemName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SetSystemName@.body: The method records the supplied string in its internal `SystemName` member and then forwards the operation to the base class’s `SetSystemName`, returning whatever value the base implementation produces.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ShouldStripRes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::ShouldStripRes.body: The function flags that a resource path should be removed—returning `true` irrespective of the input.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SortXCodeObjec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SortXCodeObjec.body: Applies the C++ standard `std::sort` to the internal vector `XCodeObjects`, using the `objectIdLessThan` comparator to order the elements by their identifiers. This rearranges the collection in place, ensuring subsequent code that relies on a deterministic order accesses the objects in that sequence.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SpecialTargetE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::SpecialTargetE.body: The function is a guard that records whether one of a handful of special build‑targets has already been processed. It compares the supplied name against a hard‑coded list of target identifiers. If the name matches and that target is already in `TargetDoneSet`, it reports success (returns `true`). If the target has not yet been recorded, it inserts the name into the set and signals that it has not yet been emitted by returning `false`. For any other name it simply returns `false`.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::UseEffectivePl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::UseEffectivePl.body: It pulls the global “XCODE_EMIT_EFFECTIVE_PLATFORM_NAME” flag; if that flag isn’t set it defers to the makefile’s built‑in Apple‑Embedded check, otherwise it simply reports whether the flag value evaluates to true.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::WriteXCodePBXP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::WriteXCodePBXP.body: The `WriteXCodePBXProj` routine serialises a project’s data into a stream: it sorts the internal code objects, emits a fixed file header, writes key metadata fields (`archiveVersion`, `classes`, `objectVersion`), dumps the list of objects via `PrintList`, and finally records the root object’s identifier for the current project.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::XCodeEscapePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::XCodeEscapePat.body: The function scans the input for a space or brackets. If any are present it returns the text wrapped in single quotes; otherwise it returns the original string unchanged.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::addObject@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::addObject@k_ZN.body: The function receives a unique‑pointer to a code object, verifies that if the object is of type OBJECT it has not already been registered (by checking the internal ID set), and on success adds its identifier to that set before appending the object to the internal collection.

@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::cmGlobalXCodeG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalXCodeGenerator::cmGlobalXCodeG.body: The constructor initializes a new code‑generator instance for a specific code‑generation target. It stores the supplied version string and numeric code, then selects the appropriate build‑system (either “Twelve” or “One”) based on that version. All internal pointers are cleared, and flags are reset to default values. It also assigns the default object‑directory pattern based on the current architecture macro, and finally flags the underlying engine that it will generate a multi‑configuration generator.

@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::cmGraphAdjacency.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::cmGraphAdjacency.body: This constructor moves the underlying adjacency list vector from the source instance into the new instance, leaving the source empty.

@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::cmGraphAdjacency.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::cmGraphAdjacency.body: The constructor copies every entry from the supplied adjacency list, initializing the new instance with the same edge entries.

@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::cmGraphAdjacency.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::cmGraphAdjacency.body: The function builds an adjacency‑list representation of a graph from its edge list, populating a data structure that other modules consume to traverse the graph efficiently.

@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
