@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::operator=@k_ZN20.body: It assigns another adjacency list to the current one, copying the underlying vector of `cmGraphEdgeList` elements so that the new graph has the same edges as the source.

@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::operator=@k_ZN20.body: The assignment operator copies the underlying adjacency vector from the right‑hand operand into the current graph list, returning `*this` for chaining.

@lcmGraphEdge::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK11cmGra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK11cmGra.body: It returns a const reference to the `Backtrace` member without altering any internal state.

@lcmGraphEdge::IsCross@k_ZNK11cmGraphEdg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::IsCross@k_ZNK11cmGraphEdg.body: This method is a simple, read‑only accessor that returns the value of the internal `Cross` member. It does not alter any state and guarantees no observable side‑effects, simply reporting whether the object’s cross state is true or false.

@lcmGraphEdge::IsStrong@k_ZNK11cmGraphEd.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::IsStrong@k_ZNK11cmGraphEd.body: The function simply returns the current value of the internal `Strong` flag; it does not modify any state.

@lcmGraphEdge::cmGraphEdge@k_ZN11cmGraph.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::cmGraphEdge@k_ZN11cmGraph.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied arguments to the member variables—assigning `Dest` to the size `n`, `Strong` to `s`, `Cross` to `c`, and moving the `cmListFileBacktrace` into `Backtrace`. No additional logic is performed inside the body.

@lcmGraphEdge::operator unsigned long@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::operator unsigned long@k_.body: Returns the internal `Dest` value as a `size_t`, enabling implicit conversion of the object to that integral type.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::Connection::Connecti.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::Connection::Connecti.body: Initialises the member variables src, dst, and scopeType with the provided arguments.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::CreateTargetFile@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::CreateTargetFile@k_Z.body: Creates a new file stream named from the internal base name plus a sanitized item string and a supplied suffix, writes a header for that item and the node data into the stream, and returns the stream object.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::EscapeForDotFile@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::EscapeForDotFile@k_Z.body: The function returns a new string with all double‑quote characters in the input replaced by backslash‑escaped quotes. It does this by calling `cmSystemTools::EscapeChars` on the raw data buffer with a single‑quote escape sequence.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::FindAllConnections@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::FindAllConnections@k.body: Function seeds a set containing the root item and hands the traversal work off to a helper that walks the graph, populating the supplied connections container with every reachable link.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::FindAllConnections@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::FindAllConnections@k.body: The function performs a depth‑first traversal of a dependency graph: starting from a `rootItem`, it retrieves its outgoing connections from the supplied map, copies them into the supplied `extendedCons` list, and then recursively descends into each destination item that has not yet been visited. It stops when an item has no outgoing links in the map or when every reachable item has already been visited.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::GetEdgeStyle@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::GetEdgeStyle@k_ZN16c.body: Returns a style string for an edge. It sets a string containing the constant for private or interface links. If the dependency type is not handled, it returns an empty string.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::ItemExcluded@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::ItemExcluded@k_ZN16c.body: The function determines whether a given link item should be omitted from the graph output. It first checks if the item's name matches any user‑supplied filter list; if so, it returns true. A `null` target causes exclusion when external generation is disabled. Utility‑type items whose names begin with “Nightly”, “Continuous”, or “Experimental” are filtered out as well. Any imported item is suppressed unless external generation is turned on. If none of these rules apply, it defers to the generic type‑enablement logic, returning the negated result of `TargetTypeEnabled`.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::ItemNameFilteredOut@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::ItemNameFilteredOut@.body: The routine simply decides whether an item name should be excluded from further processing. It first treats the literal “>” as a hard‑wired marker that always triggers exclusion. Next it checks whether the name is listed in a global set of reserved targets and filters those out. Finally, it iterates through a collection of regular‑expression filters; if any of those matches the incoming name, the function signals exclusion. If none of these conditions apply, the function returns false, meaning the name is acceptable for further handling.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::ItemNameWithAliases@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::ItemNameWithAliases@.body: The method collects every alias that maps to the supplied `itemName` across all local generators. It then removes duplicates, sorts the aliases, and appends them—each wrapped in parentheses and separated by a newline—to the original item name, producing a composite string that lists the item and its aliases.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::OnDirectLink@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::OnDirectLink@k_ZN16c.body: It forwards the caller’s dependency information to `VisitLink`, passing the two link items, a hard‑coded `true` flag to indicate a direct link, and a style object retrieved via `GetEdgeStyle(dt)`.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::OnIndirectLink@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::OnIndirectLink@k_ZN1.body: When an indirect link is encountered, the OnIndirectLink routine forwards that relationship to VisitLink, passing the two link items and a flag of false to signal that the link is indirect.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::OnItem@k_ZN16cmGraph.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::OnItem@k_ZN16cmGraph.body: The method first filters out items deemed excluded. For any remaining item it builds a unique node identifier by concatenating a fixed prefix with an ever‑incrementing integer, records that mapping, and then delegates to a helper that serialises the node to the global output stream.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::PathSafeString@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::PathSafeString@k_ZN1.body: Filters the input string, keeping only alphanumeric characters plus the safe set of “.”, “-”, and “_”, and returns the cleaned string.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::ReadSettings@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::ReadSettings@k_ZN16c.body: The function attempts to load a configuration file for the GraphViz tool. It first checks whether the supplied file exists, falling back to a default name if not. It then parses that file using a local generator; any definitions found update the instance’s settings such as graph name, header, and node prefix. Several boolean flags are set based on whether particular Make definitions are present, enabling or disabling generation for various target types. Finally, if a list of ignore‑target regexes is provided, each is compiled and stored for later filtering.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::TargetTypeEnabled@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::TargetTypeEnabled@k_.body: This private const method maps a target type to the corresponding flag that controls whether a graph should be generated for that type. When called, it evaluates the supplied `TargetType` value and returns the member variable that indicates if that particular target class should be included in the output; for the built‑in “global” target it always returns `false`.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::VisitGraph@k_ZN16cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::VisitGraph@k_ZN16cmG.body: The `VisitGraph` method writes the graph header and legend to the output stream. It simply forwards the global stream to the `WriteHeader` and `WriteLegend` helpers, completing the rendering of the current graph.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::VisitLink@k_ZN16cmGr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::VisitLink@k_ZN16cmGr.body: The routine first filters out any items that should not be emitted (either of the two items or because the link is not a direct one). If the link qualifies, it writes the dependency record to the global output stream. When the “per‑target” or “per‑depender” tables are enabled, it appends the connection entry to the corresponding in‑memory list for later use.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::Write@k_ZN16cmGraphV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::Write@k_ZN16cmGraphV.body: The `Write` function serialises a global graph by first traversing the graph’s nodes, then sorting the generator‑targets to guarantee deterministic output. It records each target’s link item in a stable order and finally emits per‑target and depend‑er connections when the corresponding flags are enabled.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteConnection@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteConnection@k_ZN.body:
The `WriteConnection` routine emits a single edge line in a GraphViz‐style output. It pulls the textual names of the two link items (`depender` and `dependee`), resolves them to internal node identifiers via the `NodeNames` map, and writes a line in the format

```
"    "<node1>" -> "<node2>" <edgeStyle> // <dependerName> -> <dependeeName>
```

to the supplied `cmGeneratedFileStream`. This produces the visual representation of the dependency between the two items.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteFooter@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteFooter@k_ZN16cm.body: The `WriteFooter` method appends a closing brace followed by a newline to the output stream. It simply flushes `"}\n"` into the `cmGeneratedFileStream` passed in.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteHeader@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteHeader@k_ZN16cm.body: The function writes a GraphViz header to a stream. It escapes the supplied graph name to be dot‑safe, then emits a `digraph “<escaped‑name>” {` line followed by the stored header text and a closing newline. It ends the block with the corresponding `}` (not shown in the snippet).

@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteLegend@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteLegend@k_ZN16cm.body:
The routine writes a subgraph named **clusterLegend** into the output stream.  
It emits a series of node definitions—`legendNode0`‑`legendNode7`—each labeled with a library type (“Executable”, “Static Library”, etc.) and assigned a shape constant (`GRAPHVIZ_NODE_SHAPE_*`).  
After the nodes, the function appends directed edges that use the predefined edge‑style constants (`GRAPHVIZ_EDGE_STYLE_*`) and, when needed, a plain edge to keep the graph layout together. The edges include invisible ones that simply force the Graphviz layout engine to keep the legend nodes aligned.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteNode@k_ZN16cmGr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::WriteNode@k_ZN16cmGr.body: The method resolves the internal name for the link item, looks up the node’s alias string, escapes that string for dot syntax, and emits a single line to the output stream that declares the node with its label and shape. The call sequence is: obtain `itemName`, look up `nodeName` in the `NodeNames` map, build an alias‑augmented name with `ItemNameWithAliases`, escape it with `EscapeForDotFile`, finally write the formatted line to `fs`.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::WritePerTargetConnec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::WritePerTargetConnec.body: Collects indirect dependencies for each target, skips excluded items, and writes each discovered connection to its dedicated output file by invoking the supplied source/destination extraction logic.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::cmGraphVizWriter@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::cmGraphVizWriter@k_Z.body: `cmGraphVizWriter` is a constructor that stores the output file name and opens a stream to write into it. It pulls the project name from the supplied `cmGlobalGenerator` to initialise the graph’s title, and seeds the dot‑syntax header with a default node style. It also keeps a reference to the `cmGlobalGenerator` for later use.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::cmGraphVizWriter@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::cmGraphVizWriter@k_Z.body: Creates a fresh `cmGraphVizWriter` instance that inherits the graph layout and link items from the supplied source object, copying the internal state needed for graph traversal and emitting of visual elements. The constructor performs the necessary initialization of its base visitor class and any internal helpers used to generate the visual representation.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::operator=@k_ZN16cmGr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::operator=@k_ZN16cmGr.body: The assignment operator for **`cmGraphVizWriter`** performs a deep copy of the source object into the current instance. It copies all internal state—such as graph data, rendering options, and any cached metadata—while ensuring that the destination is left in a valid, consistent state. After copying, it returns `*this`, enabling fluent chaining. This operator is the canonical way to duplicate a `cmGraphVizWriter` object while preserving its internal consistency.

@lcmGraphVizWriter::~cmGraphVizWriter@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphVizWriter::~cmGraphVizWriter@k_.body: The destructor of `cmGraphVizWriter` invokes `WriteFooter` on its `GlobalFileStream`. This guarantees the writer’s output stream is closed and the footer is emitted before the object is destroyed, ensuring a clean termination of the generated file.

@lcmHasLiteralPrefix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasLiteralPrefix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralPr.body: Returns true if the given string starts with the literal array supplied (ignoring its terminating null).

@lcmHasLiteralPrefix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasLiteralPrefix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralPr.body: The template `cmHasLiteralPrefix(cm::string_view, const char (&)[N])` evaluates whether the provided `string_view` starts with the literal character sequence held in the `char[N]` array. It performs a compile‑time comparison of the first `N` characters of the view against the literal and returns `true` when they match and `false` otherwise.

@lcmHasLiteralSuffix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasLiteralSuffix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralSu.body: Takes a `cm::string_view` and a literal C‑string (passed by reference), constructs a `string_view` that skips the trailing null byte (`N‑1` length), and forwards the check to `cmHasSuffix`. It returns `true` only if the original string ends with that literal suffix.

@lcmHasLiteralSuffix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasLiteralSuffix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralSu.body: The template returns true when the supplied `cm::string_view` ends with the literal suffix given by the `const char (&)[N]` array; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixNSt3__117b.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixNSt3__117b.body: Checks whether a `cm::string_view` starts with a provided `cmValue` and returns `true` if the prefix matches the beginning of the string, otherwise `false`.

@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixNSt3__117b.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixNSt3__117b.body: The function checks whether a `string_view` begins with a supplied prefix by invoking `compare` over the first `prefix.size()` characters and comparing the result to zero. It returns `true` only when that comparison succeeds.

@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixNSt3__117b.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixNSt3__117b.body: Checks whether a non‑empty string view begins with a specific character.

@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixi7cmValue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixi7cmValue.body: The `cmHasPrefix` helper inspects a supplied string view against a prefix value (represented by a `cmValue` type) and simply returns a `bool` that tells whether the view begins with that prefix. It is used throughout the code base wherever a string needs to be checked for a particular prefix.

@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixic.body: Checks whether a given string view begins with the supplied single character, returning true only if the first character of the view matches that character.

@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixii.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixii.body: The routine simply returns whether the first string argument begins with the second string argument, yielding `true` for a match and `false` otherwise.

@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixNSt3__117b.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixNSt3__117b.body: The function determines whether a given string view ends with a specified suffix. It first guards against a null suffix, then checks that the view is at least as long as the suffix. Finally, it compares the final characters of the view with the suffix content, returning true only if they match exactly.

@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixNSt3__117b.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixNSt3__117b.body: Checks whether `str` ends with the characters in `suffix` by verifying length fit and performing a `compare` on the trailing segment. It returns `true` only if the suffix matches exactly.

@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixNSt3__117b.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixNSt3__117b.body: Checks whether the last character of the given string matches the supplied suffix character, returning true only when the string is non‑empty and its final character equals that suffix.

@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixi7cmValue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixi7cmValue.body: The function `cmHasSuffix` takes a `cm::string_view` and a `cmValue` (typically a string or string‑view) and returns `true` if the view ends with the supplied suffix value, otherwise `false`. It performs a simple suffix comparison without allocating new strings, just iterating over the tail of the input.

@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixic.body: cmHasSuffix checks whether a string ends with a specific character. It takes a string_view and a character, returning true if the string’s last character matches the supplied char and false otherwise. The function is used throughout the codebase to determine suffix presence in various string parsing scenarios.

@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixii.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixii.body: Checks whether the first string view ends with the second string view, returning true only when the suffix matches exactly. It performs the comparison in‑place without allocating temporary buffers.

@lcmHexFileConverter::DetermineFileType@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHexFileConverter::DetermineFileType@.body: The routine opens the specified file, reads its first line into a buffer, and examines the leading character and the length of the line. If the line starts with a colon and its length lies between the defined Intel‑HEX bounds, it reports an Intel‑HEX file; if it starts with an “S” and its length fits the Motorola S‑record bounds, it reports a Motorola S‑record file. In every other case—or if the line is too short, too long, or contains non‑hex characters—it returns Binary.

@lcmHexFileConverter::TryConvert@k_ZN18c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHexFileConverter::TryConvert@k_ZN18c.body: Converts a source file of Motorola‑S or Intel‑HEX format into a binary output, returning `true` only when every line is successfully converted; it aborts on type mismatch, file‑open failure, or conversion error, ensuring both streams are closed before exit.

@lcmIfCommand@k_Z11cmIfCommandRKiR17cmEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfCommand@k_Z11cmIfCommandRKiR17cmEx.body: The routine expands the supplied arguments, runs the condition evaluator on them, and if the condition fails it creates a blocker object that will prevent the following commands from executing. It reports any errors with the proper message type (fatal or regular) and records a fatal error flag when the condition cannot be satisfied.

@lcmImplicitDependsList::cmImplicitDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmImplicitDependsList::cmImplicitDepen.body: The `cmImplicitDependsList` function returns a list of implicit dependency descriptions for the current context. It collects and aggregates any internal dependencies that are required but not explicitly declared, providing a flattened view of all such implicit links for downstream processing.

@lcmImplicitDependsList::operator=@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmImplicitDependsList::operator=@k_ZN2.body: The assignment operator copies the contents of a `cmImplicitDependsList` into the current instance, performing any necessary internal state updates. After the copy, it returns a reference to `*this` so that callers can chain assignments or use the object immediately.

@lcmIncludeCommand@k_Z16cmIncludeCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIncludeCommand@k_Z16cmIncludeCommand.body: Handles an `include` call: validates the arguments, resolves module or file paths (including deprecated module handling), applies policy checks, reads the dependent file (setting a result variable if requested), and reports success or any errors.

@lcmIncludeDirectoryCommand@k_Z25cmInclu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIncludeDirectoryCommand@k_Z25cmInclu.body: The routine parses a list of include‑directory arguments, detects whether each should be added before or after the current includes (via the “BEFORE”/“AFTER” flag), distinguishes system‑style paths, normalises them with `GetIncludes`, and then registers the resulting directories in the makefile’s include lists, handling any empty‑string errors along the way.

@lcmIncludeExternalMSProjectCommand@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIncludeExternalMSProjectCommand@k_Z3.body: The `cmIncludeExternalMSProjectCommand` function validates that at least two arguments are supplied. It parses optional keyword arguments (`TYPE`, `GUID`, `PLATFORM`) and collects remaining items as dependencies. For a Win32 build it creates a new utility target, optionally storing a GUID in the cache, attaches provided type and platform mapping, and registers any dependencies. The target is marked to be excluded from “all” builds if the corresponding property is set. The function returns `true` on success.

@lcmIncludeGuardCommand@k_Z21cmIncludeGu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIncludeGuardCommand@k_Z21cmIncludeGu.body: cmIncludeGuardCommand examines an optional argument to determine whether the include guard should be applied at the current list file, a directory, or globally. It checks if that guard is already defined in the chosen scope; if not, it sets the guard and returns success.

@lcmIncludeRegularExpressionCommand@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIncludeRegularExpressionCommand@k_Z3.body: The function checks that the caller supplied 1–2 arguments; it stores the first argument as the include‑regex pattern in the current makefile and, if a second argument is supplied, stores that as the complain‑regex pattern. It returns true on success or reports an error if the argument count is wrong.

@lcmInstallCommand@k_Z16cmInstallCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommand@k_Z16cmInstallCommand.body: The function checks for an empty argument list and returns success immediately. If arguments are supplied, it turns on the install target in the makefile and then dispatches the first argument to the corresponding handler from a table that maps sub‑commands to functions. The dispatch is performed by the helper `subcommand` object, which looks up the handler for the given key and invokes it with the remaining arguments and status object. The function simply returns whether that dispatch succeeded.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::CheckPermis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::CheckPermis.body: The routine scans a static list of allowed permission strings; if the supplied permission string matches one of those entries, it appends that string to the output buffer and returns true, otherwise it returns false.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::CheckPermis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::CheckPermis.body: The routine first resets the internal string buffer, then iterates over every entry in the `Permissions` collection, invoking a helper that appends any matching authority to that buffer. It returns `true` only if every individual check succeeds.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::Finalize@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::Finalize@k_.body: Checks that the caller has permission; if allowed it copies the destination into a string field, normalises path separators, and returns true (otherwise returns false).

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetComponen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetComponen.body: It returns the name of the component that was set in the current object, falling back in that order: first the value stored in `Component`, then the component supplied by a `GenericArguments` instance, then a predefined default string. If all those sources are empty, it returns a single static string literal `"Unspecified"`. The function is `const` and operates purely on internal state, never mutating any member fields.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetConfigur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetConfigur.body: Returns the member vector if it contains elements; otherwise, if a fallback argument object exists, forwards the call to that object's `GetConfigurations`; if neither is available, returns the (empty) member vector.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetDefaultC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetDefaultC.body: It returns the string stored in `DefaultComponentName` as a const reference.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetDestinat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetDestinat.body: It checks whether the object’s own destination string is set; if so, it returns that string, otherwise it falls back to a generic argument’s destination, and finally it returns an empty string if none of those are present.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetExcludeF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetExcludeF.body:
If the current object has its own *ExcludeFromAll* flag set, the method returns `true`.  
Otherwise, it falls back to its `GenericArguments` member (if present) and returns whatever that object's `GetExcludeFromAll()` reports; if that yields `false` (or no member), the method returns `false`.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.body: The method returns a reference to the internal string stored in `NamelinkComponent` if it is non‑empty; otherwise it simply forwards to the `GetComponent()` helper and returns that result.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.body: It returns true when the current object’s `NamelinkOnly` flag is set; if that flag is not set, it defers to its `GenericArguments` object (if present) to determine the value, otherwise it returns false.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.body: This method returns whether a name‑link skip flag is set. It first checks its own flag (`NamelinkSkip`); if that flag is true, it immediately returns `true`. If not, it looks for a `GenericArguments` object and delegates the check to that object via `GetNamelinkSkip()`. If neither source provides a set flag, the method returns `false`. The logic is a simple delegation pattern that propagates the skip indication through a chain of argument holders.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetOptional.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetOptional.body: The function reports whether the command arguments are marked optional. If the current object’s `Optional` flag is set, it returns `true`; otherwise it forwards the check to an optional `GenericArguments` instance, falling back to `false` if none is present.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetPermissi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetPermissi.body: The method returns a string reference that holds the effective permission set: if the current object has a non‑empty `PermissionsString`, that value is returned; otherwise the method defers to a `GenericArguments` instance (if present); if neither is available it falls back to an empty string.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetRename@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetRename@k.body: The method first checks whether the `Rename` member holds a non‑empty string; if so, it returns that string by reference. If not, it checks a non‑null `GenericArguments` pointer and, if present, delegates to that object's `GetRename()` call. When neither source supplies a non‑empty string, it falls back to a static empty string constant.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetType@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetType@k_Z.body: It simply returns a const reference to the `Type` string stored in the object, allowing callers to inspect the value without copying it.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::HasNamelink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::HasNamelink.body: This function returns `true` when the current instance holds any entries in its `NamelinkComponent` container. If that container is empty, it defers to the wrapped `GenericArguments` object (if present) to see whether it, in turn, contains a component. If neither holds components, it resolves to `false`.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::SetGenericA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::SetGenericA.body: Sets the internal `GenericArguments` member to the supplied pointer.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::cmInstallCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::cmInstallCo.body: The constructor stores the supplied default component name and registers a series of command‑argument keys (destination, component, name‑link flags, exclusions, renames, permissions, configurations, optional flags, etc.) by calling Bind on each member.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::cmInstallCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::cmInstallCo.body:
The `cmInstallCommandArguments` helper registers the command‑line options used by the installer.  
When invoked, it receives an `cmInstallCommandArguments` rvalue reference and forwards the contained options to the base `cmArgumentParser<void>` machinery, which records each flag, its default value, and any constraints (e.g., required values). This allows the install command to parse and validate its arguments before dispatching the actual installation logic.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::cmInstallCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::cmInstallCo.body: Populates internal state with parsed install command arguments and invokes the base‐class validation logic.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::GetF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::GetF.body: This member function simply returns a const reference to the internal `FileSet` string, guaranteeing that callers cannot modify the object while still avoiding a copy of the string. It is marked `const`, so it can be invoked on const instances, and because the return type is a reference it avoids unnecessary copying overhead.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::Pars.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::Pars.body: The routine first prepends the literal “FILE_SET” to the supplied argument list and then hands the augmented list over to the base class’s parsing routine, storing the resulting un‑consumed arguments in the supplied vector.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::cmIn.body: Initialises the base with the supplied component string and registers the “FILE_SET” command to the internal FileSet handler.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::cmIn.body: The function initializes a collection of arguments for a file‑based install command. It accepts a temporary instance (the rvalue reference), parses the supplied data, and stores the resulting argument set in the internal container that the command file handling code later consults.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::cmIn.body: cmInstallCommandFileSetArguments copies the supplied argument object into the internal configuration used by the command‑file installer, filling fields such as source path, destination, permissions, and any relevant flags so that the install routine can later apply them when executing the command file.

@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::GetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::GetI.body: It returns a const reference to the `IncludeDirs` vector stored in the object, exposing the list of include directories without copying or modifying the underlying data.

@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::Pars.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::Pars.body: The function reads a list of directory strings, normalises them to Unix‑style paths, and pushes each into the `IncludeDirs` vector. It skips the first argument (the command itself) and exits early if no arguments are supplied.

@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::cmIn.body: The function checks whether a particular argument is present in the arguments list for an install command.

@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::cmIn.body: Checks whether a given install‑command line contains a specific argument. It takes a reference to a cmInstallCommandIncludesArgument instance and returns a bool indicating presence.

@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::cmIn.body: The `cmInstallCommandIncludesArgument` routine checks whether a given argument string is present in the current command’s argument list and returns a boolean flag indicating presence or absence. It’s called during the command‑parsing workflow (e.g., at line 209 of `cmInstallCommandArguments.cxx` and line 68 of the corresponding header).

@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::Comput.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::Comput.body: The function assigns the provided `cmLocalGenerator` to its `LocalGenerator` member. It then looks up a generator target by name: first in the current local scope, and if that fails, in the global generator. Finally it returns `true` regardless of the lookup result.

@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::Genera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::Genera.body: Generates an optional include directive for a CMake script by looking up the script location; if found, it writes an include line with proper escaping to the stream.

@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::GetDes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::GetDes.body: It evaluates the stored `Destination` expression by passing the current `LocalGenerator` and the supplied configuration string to `cmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate`, then returns the resulting string.

@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::GetOpt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::GetOpt.body: Returns the value of the member variable `Optional` for the current object instance without changing any state or side‑effects. The method is `const`, guaranteeing that it can be called safely on `const` objects and that its call cannot modify the object’s internal state.

@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::GetScr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::GetScr.body: It builds a path string by concatenating a support‑directory prefix with an optional config string: if the input string is empty it uses “noconfig”, otherwise it appends the provided name, producing a path like `…/install‑cxx‑module‑bmi‑<name>.cmake`.

@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::GetTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::GetTar.body: Returns a pointer to the internally stored `cmGeneratorTarget` instance.

@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::cmInst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::cmInst.body: Sets up the B‑module generator with the supplied target name, file‑permission string, and optional flag, while enabling per‑config actions.

@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::~cmIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::~cmIns.body: The destructor of `cmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator` is a virtual cleanup routine that releases any resources owned by the module and guarantees that derived classes can extend the de‑allocation logic. It simply invokes the base destructor and frees any dynamically allocated state before the object is discarded.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::AddDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::AddDirect.body: The function `AddDirectoryInstallRule` registers a new installation rule for a set of directories. It takes a stream reference, a configuration string, an indentation helper, and a vector of directory paths. Internally it resolves the target location via `GetDestination(config)`, then invokes the helper `AddInstallRule` supplying that destination, a type flag indicating a directory install, the list of directories, and various optional parameters such as file/ directory permissions, literal arguments and indentation. The call to `AddInstallRule` is the sole operative step that records the rule into the installer’s rule‑set.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::Compute@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::Compute@k.body: The function assigns the supplied `cmLocalGenerator` pointer to the member `LocalGenerator` and immediately returns `true`.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GenerateS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GenerateS.body:
The routine checks the `ActionsPerConfig` flag.  
If the flag is true, it simply forwards to the base‑class `GenerateScriptActions`; otherwise it emits a default add‑directory rule via `AddDirectoryInstallRule` using the stored directory list.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GenerateS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GenerateS.body: The method gathers the directories from the given configuration, resolves any relative paths to absolute ones based on the current source directory, and finally registers an install rule for those directories.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GetDestin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GetDestin.body: The function returns a string by invoking `cmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate` with the instance’s `Destination` and `LocalGenerator` fields and the supplied `config` argument, yielding the resolved directory path.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GetDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GetDirect.body:
The function returns a vector of directory‑names.  
If the `ActionsPerConfig` flag is set, it evaluates each stored directory string in the current configuration context; otherwise it returns the raw list. The result is returned by moving the internal vector.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GetOption.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::GetOption.body: It returns the value of the member variable `Optional`; the method is `const`, so it guarantees not modifying the object. The function simply returns that boolean field.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::cmInstall.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::cmInstall.body: The constructor creates a directory‑install generator. It stores the directory list, destination, permissions, literal arguments, and whether the operation is optional. It calls the base installer with the configuration data, then determines whether each configuration requires a separate action by examining if the destination or any supplied directory contains a generator expression (i.e. a placeholder that will be resolved per‑configuration). If such an expression is found, it flags that actions must be performed per configuration.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::~cmInstal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::~cmInstal.body: The `~cmInstallDirectoryGenerator` destructor is a trivial, compiler‑generated default. It simply releases the automatic cleanup for all member data; no manual resource release logic is required.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::Compute@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::Compute@k_ZN.body: Assigns the provided local generator to the internal member and then forwards that same pointer to the ExportSet’s `Compute` routine, returning its boolean result.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::ComputeTempD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::ComputeTempD.body: The method simply assigns the class’s temporary directory member by calling its own internal helper, ensuring the current value is refreshed with a freshly computed path.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateImpo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateImpo.body: `GenerateImportFile` is a protected member that receives a pointer to a `cmExportSet`. It iterates over the export entries in that set and emits the corresponding import directives into a file that will be used by the installation process to wire the exported symbols into the build.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateImpo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateImpo.body: GenerateImportFile consumes a configuration string and a pointer to a collection of export data, producing an import file that encapsulates the specified exports.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateScri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateScri.body: The function first verifies that the export set contains at least one target export; if none are present it aborts by reporting an error. It then ensures a temporary directory exists and sets up the path to the main import file. The export generator is configured with the namespace, old export flag, and any configuration types (or a default if none are supplied). It produces the import file and delegates the remainder of the script generation to the base installer implementation.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateScri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateScri.body: The function emits a small CMake script that first checks if the previously installed export file differs from the current one; if it does, the old file(s) are removed and the new export file is installed. It then calls AddInstallRule to register the installation of the main export file with the generated script.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateScri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GenerateScri.body: The function first delegates to the base generator to create the generic installation rules. Then it iterates over the configuration‑specific import files: for each configuration it emits a CMake `if()` block that checks a per‑configuration test macro, installs the associated file list, and ends the block. It similarly processes the C++‑module import files: it constructs a path for the module directory, checks whether any per‑configuration export file is already present and writes a CMake sequence that replaces outdated files, printing a status message. Finally, it handles any additional module‑target files in the same conditional‑install pattern. The routine therefore produces the configuration‑aware install rules and manages cleanup of old export files.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetCxxModule.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetCxxModule.body: Returns the string held in the `CxxModulesDirectory` member, representing the directory path for Cxx modules.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetDestinati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetDestinati.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the internal `Destination` string.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetDestinati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetDestinati.body: Returns the full path string by concatenating the `Destination` member with a slash and the `FileName` member.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetExportSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetExportSet.body: The method simply returns the internal pointer to the export set stored in the object. If the member has never been initialized, callers will receive a `nullptr`.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetFileName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetFileName@.body: The function simply returns the member string that stores the file’s name. Because it is marked `const`, it guarantees it does not modify the object’s state and can be called on const instances. Returning by value copies the string; if performance under tight memory constraints is a concern, returning a const reference or moving the string might be considered, but only if callers expect a mutable copy.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetLocalGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetLocalGene.body: Returns a pointer to the internal `LocalGenerator` member without modifying the object.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetMainImpor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetMainImpor.body: The method returns a reference to the string stored in the object (`MainImportFile`). It guarantees that the returned reference cannot be used to modify that member because the function is `const`. Callers must keep the object alive while using the reference; otherwise the reference would dangle.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetNamespace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetNamespace.body: The method simply returns a const reference to the stored `Namespace` string, allowing callers to read the namespace without triggering a copy while guaranteeing that the string can’t be altered.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetTempDir@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::GetTempDir@k.body: The `GetTempDir` member lazily initializes and caches a temporary‑directory string. On the first call, if `TempDir` is still empty, it calls the internal `TempDirCalculate()` helper to compute a path and returns that value. Subsequent calls simply return the already‑stored string without recomputing it.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::TempDirCalcu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::TempDirCalcu.body: The function builds a temporary directory path by concatenating the current binary directory with `"/CMakeFiles/Export"`. If no explicit destination is set, it simply returns that path. When a destination is present, it appends a forward‑slash and an MD5 hash of the destination string (to keep the path short) before returning the full path.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::cmInstallExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::cmInstallExp.body: The constructor creates a new export‑generator instance: it stores the supplied export set, file‑name and namespace information, and records whether the exported configuration should be treated as an old‑style export or a new Android‑specific one. It then decides at runtime whether to instantiate a cmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator (for Android builds) or a cmExportInstallFileGenerator (for normal builds). Finally, it registers itself with the export set so that generator will be invoked during the installation phase.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::cmInstallExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::cmInstallExp.body: The `cmInstallExportGenerator` function initializes an export generator module, wires up the necessary resources, and performs any required configuration steps before the generator is used. It also guards against unintended copying by deleting the copy constructor.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::operator=@k_.body: The operator= function performs a deep copy of another cmInstallExportGenerator instance into the current one. It copies all internal state members from the right‑hand side operand into the left‑hand side object, then returns a reference to the updated object so that the assignment can be chained. It guarantees that after the call the object holds an identical state to the source instance.

@lcmInstallExportGenerator::~cmInstallEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallExportGenerator::~cmInstallEx.body: `~cmInstallExportGenerator()` triggers the cleanup of any resources associated with an export‑generator instance. It guarantees that internal data structures are released, any pending callbacks are cancelled, and that the object is left in a safe state before being reclaimed by the runtime. It protects against leaks, double‑destructing, and dangling references in the surrounding code.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::CalculateFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::CalculateFi.body: The method uses the file‑set helper to gather directory entries, turns those entries into concrete directory objects, and then populates a map that associates each directory name with the list of file names belonging to that directory.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::Compute@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::Compute@k_Z.body: The function stores the supplied `cmLocalGenerator` in `LocalGenerator` and then resolves the target name first against the local generator’s non‑alias targets. If that lookup yields nothing, it falls back to the global generator’s target lookup. In either case it finally returns `true`, signalling that the resolution succeeded (although it never reports failure).

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GenerateScr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GenerateScr.body: The routine extracts a set of files per directory from the supplied configuration string, builds the target sub‑path (appending a slash‑prefixed sub‑directory when present), and registers an install rule for that file group via `AddInstallRule`. This rule carries the configured optional flag and the file‑permission string supplied in the `cmInstallFileSetGenerator`.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetDestinat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetDestinat.body: The function returns a string by evaluating the `Destination` expression with the current `LocalGenerator` and the supplied `config`. It simply forwards those values to `cmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate` and returns the resulting string.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetDestinat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetDestinat.body: Returns the stored value of the `Destination` member string.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetFileSet@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetFileSet@.body: The method simply returns the stored `FileSet` pointer; it is declared `const` so callers cannot modify the returned pointer through the caller.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetOptional.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetOptional.body: Returns the value of the `Optional` member without modifying the object; the method is `const`, so it promises no state change, and simply returns the stored boolean flag.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetTarget@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetTarget@k.body: This const method simply returns the stored target pointer, allowing callers to read the target without modifying the object.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::cmInstallFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::cmInstallFi.body: This constructor creates an installer for a file set. It stores the target name, the file‑set pointer, the destination path, the desired file permissions, and whether the operation is optional. It forwards the configuration list and message level to the base generator and sets `ActionsPerConfig` to true to enable per‑config actions.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::cmInstallFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::cmInstallFi.body: The constructor copies an existing generator’s configuration—preserving its file‑set and any installation flags—so the new instance can be used interchangeably in the same install pipeline.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::operator=@k.body: The assignment operator takes a const reference to another `cmInstallFileSetGenerator` and copies its internal data (file set collections and any configuration flags) into the current instance, returning a reference to that instance.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::~cmInstallF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::~cmInstallF.body: This destructor is declared `override` in the class definition and defined as `= default;` in the implementation file. The compiler-generated destructor performs member‑wise destruction, so each data member of `cmInstallFileSetGenerator` is automatically destroyed in the order they were declared. No manual clean‑up logic is required. It simply ensures that any resources owned by the class (e.g., file handles, pointers, or other RAII objects) are released correctly when an instance goes out of scope.

@lcmInstallFilesCommand@k_Z21cmInstallFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesCommand@k_Z21cmInstallFi.body:
The function first checks that at least two arguments were supplied. It then enables the “install” target in the global generator.  
If the second argument is the keyword `FILES`, it gathers the requested file names, resolves each to a source path via `FindInstallSource`, and creates an install generator for those files at the destination path.  
Otherwise it treats the remaining arguments as a generic install action, packaging them into a lambda that will be invoked later. Finally it registers the default component name with the global generator and returns success.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::AddFilesInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::AddFilesInsta.body: The method writes a rule that installs a list of files into the target directory for a given configuration. It resolves the destination path using `GetDestination`, decides whether the files are to be treated as programs or normal files based on `Programs`, then calls the internal helper `AddInstallRule` with the file list, optional settings, file permissions and any rename mapping. No directory‑permission string is supplied, so the helper uses defaults for the destination directories.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::Compute@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::Compute@k_ZN2.body: It assigns the supplied `cmLocalGenerator` instance to the internal `LocalGenerator` member so that the object can use it later.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GenerateScrip.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GenerateScrip.body: The method emits the script‑generation logic for a file‑install generator. When the instance’s `ActionsPerConfig` flag is set, it simply forwards the request to the parent `cmInstallGenerator::GenerateScriptActions`, letting the base class emit the appropriate actions. If that flag is unset, it instead invokes its own `AddFilesInstallRule`, passing the current file list so the script rule is emitted for those files.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GenerateScrip.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GenerateScrip.body: The function first retrieves the list of files associated with the supplied configuration string by calling `GetFiles`, then passes that list together with the configuration name and indentation level to `AddFilesInstallRule` to produce the corresponding installation rule.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GetDestinatio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GetDestinatio.body: It evaluates the stored `Destination` expression by applying the current local generator to the supplied configuration string and returns the resulting string.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GetFiles@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GetFiles@k_ZN.body: The function returns a vector of strings. If `ActionsPerConfig` is true it builds a list of evaluated file expressions (using `config`) and returns that list; otherwise it returns the stored file list unchanged.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GetOptional@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GetOptional@k.body: Returns the current value of the `Optional` flag, indicating whether the optional feature is enabled.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GetRename@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::GetRename@k_Z.body: The method evaluates the `Rename` expression with the current generator context and a supplied configuration string, returning the resulting string.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::cmInstallFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::cmInstallFile.body: The function creates a new `cmInstallFilesGenerator` instance by copying the internal state from an existing object, ensuring that all file‑generation settings—such as source paths, destination targets, and file‑type filters—are preserved for the new instance.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::cmInstallFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::cmInstallFile.body: This constructor builds an installer that copies a list of files to a target directory, optionally renames and applies permissions. It stores the source file list, destination path, any rename expression, and whether installation actions should be performed once per configuration or for each configuration. The constructor also records whether the installation is optional and whether any of the inputs contain generator expressions that require special handling.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::operator=@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::operator=@k_Z.body: The `operator=` overload copies all the internal state from the right‑hand side instance into the current object and returns a reference to `*this`, enabling fluent chaining of assignments.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::~cmInstallFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::~cmInstallFil.body: The destructor is virtual and defaulted, ensuring any derived class cleans up its own resources automatically without custom logic.

@lcmInstallGenerator::AddInstallRule@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::AddInstallRule@k_Z.body: The method writes a CMake install rule to an output stream. It maps the internal install type to its string keyword (e.g., “DIRECTORY”, “PROGRAM”, “EXECUTABLE”, etc.), emits warnings if the destination is an absolute path, and emits the actual `file(INSTALL DESTINATION …)` command. The rule can mark the install optional, set file‑ and directory‑level permissions, rename files if required, and append literal arguments when provided.

@lcmInstallGenerator::AddTweak@k_ZN18cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::AddTweak@k_ZN18cmI.body: The `AddTweak` routine inserts a conditional block into the output stream: it writes an `if` statement that checks whether the supplied file exists and is not a symlink, then emits the tweak string produced by the provided `TweakMethod`, and finally closes the block with an `endif`.

@lcmInstallGenerator::AddTweak@k_ZN18cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::AddTweak@k_ZN18cmI.body: The method builds a tweak entry. If there’s only one file it just writes the tweak command for that file. If many files are passed it emits a `foreach` block: it first writes a single‑file tweak for a placeholder `${file}`, then emits a `foreach(file)` loop listing each target file in quotes, and finally writes the body of the loop. The helper writes the loop body by calling the same routine recursively with the file placeholder. All indentation and quoting is handled via the `Indent` helper.

@lcmInstallGenerator::CheckCMP0082@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::CheckCMP0082@k_ZN1.body: The method receives two boolean references; when the first flag is true, it assigns true to the second flag, otherwise it leaves the second flag unchanged.

@lcmInstallGenerator::Compute@k_ZN18cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::Compute@k_ZN18cmIn.body: The overridden `Compute` method performs no custom logic—it simply returns `true` immediately.

@lcmInstallGenerator::ConvertToAbsoluteD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::ConvertToAbsoluteD.body: The function prefixes a predefined installation path to a relative destination string, leaving absolute paths unchanged.

@lcmInstallGenerator::CreateComponentTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::CreateComponentTes.body: The function produces a string that represents a condition for a CMake install component test. When the flag `all_components` is true, it returns “CMAKE_INSTALL_COMPONENT” if `exclude_from_all` is also true, otherwise it returns an empty string. If `all_components` is false, it returns a string composed of “CMAKE_INSTALL_COMPONENT STREQUAL ” followed by the given component name. If `exclude_from_all` is false, an additional “ OR NOT CMAKE_INSTALL_COMPONENT” is appended. This logic effectively builds a textual predicate that can be used in a CMake test for checking whether a specific component is installed.

@lcmInstallGenerator::GenerateScript@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::GenerateScript@k_Z.body: The method first builds a test string for the component using `CreateComponentTest`. If that string is non‑empty it emits an `if(` test string `)` line to the output stream. It then calls `GenerateScriptConfigs` (passing the current indentation or its successor depending on `AllComponents`) to write the actual configuration blocks, and finally writes a matching `endif()` line to close the conditional block. All indentation is handled by the `Indent` helper.

@lcmInstallGenerator::GetAllComponentsFl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::GetAllComponentsFl.body: The `GetAllComponentsFlag` accessor simply returns the value of the private member `AllComponents`. Because it is marked `const`, it guarantees not to modify any state, and callers can safely call it on temporary or const instances. However, callers must guard against the possibility that the flag is not yet initialized; if this flag is changed elsewhere, the returned value may become stale. The function itself is trivial and incurs no runtime overhead beyond the direct read of the boolean field.

@lcmInstallGenerator::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK.body: Retrieves a constant reference to the internal `Backtrace` member without copying it, allowing callers to inspect the trace while preserving immutability.

@lcmInstallGenerator::GetComponent@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::GetComponent@k_ZNK.body: Returns a constant reference to the internal string member. Because the method is marked const, it guarantees no modification of the object. The returned reference is read‑only, so callers cannot alter the underlying string. The function is trivial, simply forwarding the stored value.

@lcmInstallGenerator::GetDestDirPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::GetDestDirPath@k_Z.body: The function concatenates the value of the `DESTDIR` environment variable with the supplied `file` string, inserting a slash only when needed (i.e., when the file name is not already prefixed with one). It returns the resulting absolute path string that represents where the file will be installed on disk.

@lcmInstallGenerator::GetExcludeFromAll@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::GetExcludeFromAll@.body: The method reads the `ExcludeFromAll` flag of the object and returns it. It is a pure accessor that never changes state. It simply provides read‑only visibility into that internal setting.

@lcmInstallGenerator::HaveInstall@k_ZN18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::HaveInstall@k_ZN18.body: The virtual `HaveInstall()` simply returns `true` unconditionally. In practice this acts as a hook that subclasses can override to signal whether an install step is required or completed, but the base implementation assumes an install is always present and performs no additional checks or side‑effects.

@lcmInstallGenerator::InstallsForConfig@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::InstallsForConfig@.body: The method `InstallsForConfig` simply forwards the supplied configuration string to the private helper `GeneratesForConfig` and returns its Boolean outcome. It does not perform any additional logic or validation itself, acting merely as a thin wrapper around the underlying generation routine.

@lcmInstallGenerator::SelectMessageLevel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::SelectMessageLevel.body: When called, the function returns a `MessageLevel` value: it first checks the `never` flag, then queries the `CMAKE_INSTALL_MESSAGE` definition from the supplied `cmMakefile`; if the definition matches one of the known string literals (`"ALWAYS"`, `"LAZY"`, or `"NEVER"`), it returns the matching enum value, otherwise it falls back to `MessageDefault`.

@lcmInstallGenerator::cmInstallGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::cmInstallGenerator.body: Creates a script‑generator instance that stores the target destination, component name, message verbosity, flags for excluding from all components and whether all components should be installed, and keeps the supplied back‑trace data for later use.

@lcmInstallGenerator::cmInstallGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::cmInstallGenerator.body: Prevents accidental copying by marking the copy constructor as deleted, ensuring instance uniqueness and preventing inadvertent state duplication.

@lcmInstallGenerator::operator=@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::operator=@k_ZN18cm.body: The `operator=` in `cmInstallGenerator` is deleted, meaning that any attempt to copy‑assign a `cmInstallGenerator` object will be a compile‑time error. This prevents accidental reuse or modification of an existing instance and enforces that the class is only movable or constructible in controlled ways.

@lcmInstallGenerator::~cmInstallGenerato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::~cmInstallGenerato.body: The function `~cmInstallGenerator()` is the destructor for the `cmInstallGenerator` class. It overrides a virtual destructor to guarantee proper cleanup of any resources allocated by this type when an instance is destroyed.

@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.body: Assigns the supplied `cmLocalGenerator` pointer to its `LocalGenerator` member and returns `true` to indicate success.

@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.body: The function writes a conditional block to an output stream. It first emits an `if` line that checks whether a component is empty or matches another; if that test passes, it emits the corresponding test call(s), otherwise it emits an alternative test. After that, it appends any per‑configuration script blocks and finally closes the block with an `endif()` line.

@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.body: The protected function serialises a `cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet` into a CMake‑style script. It emits a call to `file(GET_RUNTIME_DEPENDENCIES …)` with arguments for the resolved dependency variable, lists of executables, libraries and modules, and a bundle executable when present. It then writes generic evaluator arguments for directory matches and inclusion/exclusion regexes, followed by the list of post‑exclude files. Finally, if a path prefix is defined, it writes that as `RPATH_PREFIX`. This script is what the generator consumes to materialise the runtime dependency information for a particular build configuration.

@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.body: The function **cmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerator** is a core helper that scans the current install context to build a runtime‑dependency graph. It walks the in‑memory representation of modules, resolves each module’s declared runtime requirements, and aggregates them into a `cmRuntimeDependencies` object that the `cmInstallGenerator` uses to emit the final install script. Internally it leverages a cached map of module names to dependency lists, performs a depth‑first traversal of the dependency DAG, and eliminates duplicates before returning the populated dependency set to the caller.

@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.body: The constructor creates a runtime‑dependency generator, storing the supplied dependency set and the lists of directories, regexes, and files that control inclusion/exclusion. It also records flags for path handling and whether to skip installing runtime paths, and keeps the names of the library and framework components for later use.

@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.body: The function implements the generator that collects runtime dependency information for a CMake install target. It walks the build graph, inspects declared dependencies, and emits a list of modules or libraries that must be present at runtime. Its output feeds the install‑script generator to embed necessary runtime packages into the final installation payload.

@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.body: The `operator=` function is a copy‑assignment operator for `cmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerator`. It accepts an rvalue reference to another generator instance, copies the internal `RuntimeDependenciesGenerator` data members (including any cached dependency lists and flags), and finally returns the current object by reference to support chaining. This operator allows the object to be updated in place with another instance’s state in a way that preserves the generator’s internal configuration and avoids unnecessary re‑initialization.

@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.body: Assigns the internal state of a `cmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerator` instance from another instance, effectively performing a deep copy of its configuration and data.

@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerat.body: The `~cmInstallGetRuntimeDependenciesGenerator()` function is the entry point that scans the current project’s installation metadata and produces the set of runtime dependencies that need to be pulled in for a successful install. It walks the dependency graph, resolves version constraints, and emits a list of packages (or paths) that the installer should fetch. The result is typically consumed by downstream installers to prepare the runtime environment before launching the application.

@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.body: The routine resolves a generator target named in `TargetName`. It first queries the current local generator; if that search fails or the found target is not marked as imported, it falls back to the global generator. In either case the found target is stored in `Target` and the function returns true.

@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.body: The function generates a CMake install script snippet for a specific target type. It determines the target’s path, matches it against platform‑specific regexes (bundle, framework, CF bundle), and emits an `install()` command with the appropriate `cmInstallType_*` flag and permissions. In the Apple bundle case it emits a directory rule for the bundle’s sub‑directory; otherwise it emits the standard executable, shared library or module library rule using the file list and permissions. The output is written to the supplied output stream with the chosen indentation.

@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.body: The method evaluates the stored destination expression using the current local generator and the supplied configuration string and returns that computed value as a `std::string`.

@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.body: The method simply returns the value of the member variable `Optional`. It is a `const` member function, so it cannot modify the object, and it returns a `bool` indicating whether the option is present. This is a straightforward getter that provides read‑only access to the internal state.

@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.body: Returns a pointer to the internal `Target` member without altering the object’s state.

@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.body: The constructor configures the installation generator for an imported runtime component. It forwards the destination, configuration list, component name and message level to the base generator, stores the target name and file‑permission string, records whether the artifact is optional, and guarantees that actions are applied per‑configuration by setting `ActionsPerConfig = true`.

@lcmInstallProgramsCommand@k_Z24cmInstal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallProgramsCommand@k_Z24cmInstal.body: The function activates the install target, registers a default install component, and queues a generator action that will invoke the internal `FinalAction` routine with the destination path and the remaining arguments supplied by the caller.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.body: The function creates a `std::unique_ptr<TargetItem>` from the supplied `bundleExecutable` pointer via `cm::make_unique` and then forwards that unique‑owned item to another overload of `AddBundleExecutable`. The return value is whatever that overload returns—a `bool` indicating success or failure of adding the executable.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.body: This function forwards the supplied bundle executable to an internal routine that expects a unique pointer to an `ImportedTargetItem`. It creates that unique object from the input and returns the boolean result of that underlying addition.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.body: The function checks whether the internal pointer already holds a value; if it does, it returns false. Otherwise it stores the passed pointer, forwards it to the helper AddExecutable, and returns true. It effectively flags success only on the first successful insertion.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.body: The function wraps the supplied executable into a unique‑owned `TargetItem` instance and forwards that pointer to the internal `AddExecutable` helper, effectively registering the executable for later installation.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.body: The method accepts a pointer to a `cmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGenerator`, wraps it in a `cm::ImportedTargetItem` via `cm::make_unique`, and hands that unique pointer to the underlying `AddExecutable` implementation that stores the item for later use.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.body: The method moves the supplied `unique_ptr<Item>` into the internal container, appending it to the `Executables` list via a standard `push_back` operation.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.body: The function registers a new install target by wrapping the supplied `cmInstallTargetGenerator` into a `TargetItem` and inserting it into the class’s internal collection of targets.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.body: Creates a unique‑wrapped `ImportedTargetItem` from the supplied generator and enqueues it into the internal library registry.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.body: It takes ownership of the passed `std::unique_ptr<Item>` and appends it to the internal `Libraries` vector by moving the pointer into the collection.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.body: The function accepts a module instance, wraps it in a `cm::make_unique<TargetItem>` to produce a uniquely‑owned `TargItem`, and forwards that unique pointer to the underlying `AddModule` implementation. It effectively transfers ownership of the supplied module into the internal collection.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.body: The `AddModule` method registers a new module by wrapping the supplied pointer in an `ImportedTargetItem` via `cm::make_unique` and passing that unique pointer to an overload of `AddModule` that handles the actual storage.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.body: The function appends a module to an internal list. It takes ownership of a `std::unique_ptr<Item>` and forwards it into the `Modules` container via `std::move`, thereby transferring responsibility and ensuring the module is no longer owned by the caller.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Empty@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Empty@k.body: When you call this function, it inspects three internal containers (`Executables`, `Libraries`, and `Modules`). If every one of those containers has no elements, the function returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetBund.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetBund.body: Returns the pointer to the bundle’s executable instance stored in the object.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetDisp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetDisp.body: Returns a `cm::string_view` of either the stored name or the sentinel `"<anonymous>"` when the name is empty.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetExec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetExec.body: Returns a const reference to the internal `Executables` vector, giving callers read‑only access to the stored objects without copying them.
