The caller still sees the same underlying instances, so any mutation of the pointed‑to items (or of the unique_ptr itself) will affect the original collection.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetLibr.body: It returns a const reference to the instance’s `Libraries` member – a `std::vector` of `std::unique_ptr<Item>` objects. The method is a const member function, so callers cannot modify the returned container.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetModu.body: This function returns a read‑only reference to the internally stored collection of modules, allowing callers to inspect the vector without copying or modifying its contents.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::GetName.body: The function simply returns the stored `Name` member as a `cm::string_view` without modifying the object, preserving const‑correctness.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.body: The method simply forwards the supplied config string to its target object’s `GetFullPath` routine and returns that result. It acts as a thin wrapper around `Target->GetTarget()->GetFullPath`, providing the resolved path string to callers.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.body: The function initializes an `ImportedTargetItem` by taking an rvalue reference to an existing instance, moving its internal state into the new object, and performing any required registration or bookkeeping logic during that transfer.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.body: The constructor initializes the member `Target` with the supplied `cmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGenerator` pointer, storing it for later use.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.body: Creates a new `ImportedTargetItem` by copying its internal state from an existing instance.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.body: It overloads the assignment of an `ImportedTargetItem` from an rvalue reference, moving the source into the target and returning a reference to the assigned object.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.body: The overloaded assignment operator copies the contents of another `ImportedTargetItem` into the current object, handles self‑assignment safely, and returns a reference to the updated instance. It typically performs member‑by‑member copying (or moves, if applicable) and may also reset internal state such as flags or flags that need re‑initialisation after the copy.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Importe.body: The virtual destructor `~ImportedTargetItem()` guarantees that when an `ImportedTargetItem` object is destroyed, any overridden cleanup logic in derived classes runs and all owned resources are released. It is declared in the public interface of the class so derived types can provide their own cleanup code while still ensuring the base class’s resources are freed.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::A.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::A.body: The function is meant to be overridden by subclasses to populate a set of file names that should be excluded from a post‑installation step. It receives a configuration string, a reference to a collection of file paths, and a pointer to a dependency‑set object. In practice, an implementation will examine the configuration, determine which files should be excluded, and insert those names into the provided set before control returns.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::G.body: GetItemPath returns a string that represents the full path for a given item. The argument `config` provides context used to resolve the path; subclasses supply the actual resolution logic. It is marked pure virtual and const, requiring override in derived classes.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::I.body: The constructor `Item(const Item & [unnamed])` is a copy constructor that duplicates the internal state of an existing `Item` instance. It is invoked whenever an `Item` needs to be replicated—e.g., when passing objects by value between functions or when storing a copy in a container during a dependency‑installation routine.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::I.body: The Item function initializes an Item instance’s internal state, configuring its members and setting up any required relationships before the object is used elsewhere in the code.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::o.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::o.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of the right‑hand `Item` into the left‑hand object, performs a self‑assignment check to avoid unnecessary work, and returns a reference to the modified object so that chained assignments are possible. If the class contains dynamically allocated resources, the implementation should perform a deep copy (or employ a move‑semantics guard) to avoid unintended sharing. The function should be exception‑safe: in case of an exception during copying, the left‑hand object must remain in its original valid state.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::~.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Item::~.body: The declaration `virtual ~Item() = default;` declares a virtual destructor that relies on the compiler‑generated default body, ensuring that when an `Item` object (or any derived type) is destroyed, the appropriate destructor chain is invoked automatically.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.body: The method walks through every target that the current item depends on (recursively), obtains each dependency’s full path relative to the supplied configuration string, and inserts that path into the supplied file set.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.body: The method simply forwards the supplied configuration string to the underlying target’s `GetFullPath` routine, returning the resulting string that represents the target’s full path.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.body:
The function `TargetItem(TargetItem&&)` is a move‑constructor.  
When called, it accepts an rvalue reference to an existing `TargetItem` and copies (or moves) the internal members of that source into the new object, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state. This allows code to efficiently transfer ownership of any resources owned by the original instance without copying.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.body: TargetItem initializes a `TargetItem` object by forwarding the supplied `cmInstallTargetGenerator*` to its base `Target` class constructor, establishing the new instance’s internal state.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.body: The constructor takes a const reference to another `TargetItem` and creates a new instance by copying the underlying state of that object, invoking the base `Item` constructor and then copying the relevant member fields while maintaining any class invariants.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.body: The `operator=` is a move‑assignment that takes an rvalue reference to another `TargetItem`. It assigns the incoming object’s data into the current instance and returns a reference to `*this`.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of a source `TargetItem` into the current instance, performing a deep copy of its owned resources while preserving any existing relationships or constraints.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::TargetI.body: The `~TargetItem()` virtual destructor in `TargetItem` is invoked when a target object is being destroyed, ensuring proper cleanup of any resources tied to the item before it is removed from the system.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::cmInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::cmInsta.body: The constructor simply stores the supplied name into the object’s internal member, using a move for efficiency. No additional logic is performed inside the body.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::cmInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::cmInsta.body: The function registers a collection of runtime dependencies into the current installation context, ensuring each dependency is correctly added to the system’s dependency graph before any installation proceeds.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::operato.body: The `operator=` assigns a dependency to the current set. It updates the internal data structure, merges the new dependency, and returns a reference to the modified set for chaining.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The method simply stores the provided `cmLocalGenerator*` pointer into the object’s member (`LocalGenerator`) and always reports success by returning `true`.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: Generates a CMake fragment that extracts framework‑path components, sets corresponding variables, and appends an installation rule for the framework, including a name‑normalisation step.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The method writes a script fragment that first checks whether a temporary dependency variable matches a framework pattern; if it does not, it emits an install rule for a shared library, resolves the file‑name component, and runs a helper to fix up the final install name while handling symlink chaining.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: Generates a CMake snippet that conditionally appends runtime‑paths and install‑name arguments to a temporary variable and then invokes the install‑name tool. The routine only emits code when the *NoInstallRPath* or *NoInstallName* flags are unset, and it loops over the supplied r‑paths adding “‑add‑rpath” directives before executing the command. It finally writes the target path (dest‑dir /depName).

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The function assembles a sequence of CMake commands that will install runtime dependencies. It first resolves a base install directory (possibly overridden by a configuration variable), emits a declaration of that path, and then loops over each dependency file. For each file it emits the appropriate Apple‑specific install script (library or framework). If no custom install path is supplied, a generic rule is emitted that copies the file, optionally adding a symlink. All emitted lines are written to the provided stream, with expressions evaluated against the current configuration and context.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The function writes a conditional snippet into the output stream that, when the build system’s “CMAKE_STRIP” definition is available, emits a `make`-style block invoking the program named by that definition. It emits the block only if the `CMAKE_STRIP` definition is non‑empty, wrapping the command in an `if(CMAKE_INSTALL_DO_STRIP)…endif` construct. Inside the block it calls `execute_process` with the command string (adding a `-x` flag when the target platform is Apple) and points the output to the destination directory derived from the supplied config and dependency name.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The method simply returns the stored `Type` member of the object, performing no state changes.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: It returns the result of invoking `cmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate` on the instance’s `Destination` and `LocalGenerator` with the supplied `config`.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: Returns a pointer to the internal dependency set without modifying the object.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: This constructor initializes a runtime dependency‑set generator by storing the supplied dependency type, set, installation paths, optional flags, and path prefixes, and prepares the generator for subsequent processing.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The function constructs a `cmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator` instance, taking an rvalue reference to an existing generator, and registers its runtime‑dependency data for later installation processing.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: This constructor creates a new `cmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator` instance by copying the internal dependency configuration from an existing instance, ensuring the new object inherits the same runtime dependency settings.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The `operator=` overload for `cmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator` assigns the state of one instance to another, copying all internal dependency‑set data (e.g., the list of runtime‑dependency files, any configuration flags, and the generated list of install actions) from the right‑hand side into the left‑hand side. The implementation simply copies the base `cmInstallGenerator` members (via the base assignment) and then copies the concrete fields of this class. It returns `*this` so that the expression can be chained.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The assignment operator takes a const reference to another `cmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator` and copies its internal state into the current instance. It performs a shallow copy of the dependency set and any configuration flags so that the new object behaves identically to the source. No complex transformations occur; it merely forwards the core attributes.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: Creates the set of runtime dependencies required for a package, walking the internal dependency graph, resolving transitive relations, and populating a data‑structure that other install routines consume to determine what must be pulled into the runtime image.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::AddScriptIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::AddScriptIns.body: The function outputs either the script string directly or wraps it in an `include(...)` directive, depending on whether the internal `Code` flag is set.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::Compute@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::Compute@k_ZN.body: The function assigns the supplied `cmLocalGenerator` to its member, then evaluates the policy status for policy CMP0087. Depending on that status it may issue a warning message, set a flag to allow generation, or simply exit. Finally, it returns `true`.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::GenerateScri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::GenerateScri.body: The method checks whether the generator should apply its own per‑config logic (both AllowGenex and ActionsPerConfig being true). If that condition holds, it forwards the request to the base class’s implementation; otherwise it simply emits a single installation rule for the stored script.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::GenerateScri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::GenerateScri.body: The function simply retrieves the script string for the given `config` by calling `GetScript(config)` and forwards that script to `AddScriptInstallRule` along with the output stream and indentation level, effectively writing the installation rule into the output.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::GetScript@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::GetScript@k_.body: This function takes an input configuration string and returns a possibly‑modified script. It first copies the stored script; if the object permits generation (`AllowGenex`) and has an actions‑per‑config setting, it replaces the `${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}` placeholder in the script with the actual install prefix and then evaluates any generator expressions using the local generator context before returning the final string.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::IsCode@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::IsCode@k_ZNK.body: Returns the value of the member variable `Code` for the current instance, indicating whether the instance represents a code snippet.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::cmInstallScr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::cmInstallScr.body: The constructor stores the supplied script and flags, forwards the component and back‑trace to the base installer, and sets an internal flag if the script contains any generator expressions, indicating that configuration‑specific actions must be performed.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::cmInstallScr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::cmInstallScr.body: The function creates a new script‑generator object by copying the state of an existing one; it’s essentially a copy‑constructor that preserves all internal configuration needed to generate installation scripts.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::operator=@k_.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state from another `cmInstallScriptGenerator` instance—assigning its configuration and state members to the current object and returning the updated reference.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::~cmInstallSc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::~cmInstallSc.body: The `~cmInstallScriptGenerator()` destructor is called automatically when a `cmInstallScriptGenerator` instance goes out of scope. It overrides the base‑class virtual destructor, so any derived implementation can further release resources. Its primary role is to clean up any temporary script files, close file handles, and free allocated memory associated with script generation. This guarantees that no dangling file descriptors or leaked memory remain after a script installation is complete.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddChrpathPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddChrpathPa.body: The method adds a rule that patches runtime search paths during installation. It first checks if the target actually needs a *chrpath* change; if not, it returns immediately. When needed, it obtains link information, and either rewrites the rpath strings directly or, when using install-name tools, emits shell‑style commands that delete old runtime directories and add new ones in the correct order. It also respects the CMP0095 policy, optionally issuing a warning or emitting a different rpath format, and finally writes a CMake‑compatible file‑rule (or the shell‑style commands) that applies the new rpath at install time.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddInstallNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddInstallNa.body: The function generates an install‑name patching rule. It inspects the target and its linked shared libraries, builds a mapping of build‑tree install names to the desired install‑tree names, and emits an `execute_process` rule that runs the install‑name tool with the computed changes to fix the installed files’ names.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddRPathChec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddRPathChec.body: The routine attaches a rule to the installation script that verifies the rpath of a newly installed file. It first skips files that either don’t need rpaths or run on an Apple platform. When applicable, it obtains the link information for the target and emits a “file(RPATH_CHECK …)” rule containing the destination path. Depending on the CMP‑0095 policy, it writes the current rpath either as plain text, as a legacy string, or escaped for CMake syntax.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddRanlibRul.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddRanlibRul.body: The function emits a rule that invokes the platform‑specific *ranlib* tool on a static library target. It first verifies that the target is a static library and Apple‑specific; only then it pulls the required “CMAKE_RANLIB” definition from the target’s makefile and, if present, writes an `execute_process` line to the output stream that runs that tool on the destination directory.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddStripRule.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddStripRule.body: Adds a conditional strip command to the install script only for non‑static, non‑import targets that have a defined CMAKE_STRIP value. It writes an `execute_process` line (with the appropriate `-x`, `-u -r`, or no flag) inside a guard block triggered by `CMAKE_INSTALL_DO_STRIP`.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddUniversal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::AddUniversal.body: The routine first checks that the current makefile is for an Apple‑embedded target running under Xcode and that the Xcode tool‑chain version is at least 6. Only for targets that are an executable, static, shared, or module library and that the IOS_INSTALL_COMBINED property is true does it emit the CMake include line for CMakeIOSInstallCombined followed by a call to ios_install_combined( <target name>, <destination directory> ).

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::Compute@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::Compute@k_ZN.body: The method attempts to resolve a target name. It first asks the provided `cmLocalGenerator` to locate a target with that name in the current project. If that fails, it falls back to the global generator. The resolved target is stored in the member `Target` and the method always returns `true`.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GenerateScri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GenerateScri.body: The routine obtains the file list for a target configuration, aborts early when nothing needs copying, then resolves the target directory and any tweak directories. It emits a pre‑install tweak block (if any tweaks are enabled), emits the core install rule—with optional‑install flag, source‑permission switch, and any literal arguments for the source directory or permission usage—and finally emits a post‑install tweak block, finishing the rule construction for that target.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetDestinati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetDestinati.body: Evaluates a destination string by invoking `cmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate` with the instance’s `Destination`, the local generator obtained from the target, and the supplied `config` string, then returns that result.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetFiles@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetFiles@k_Z.body:
Retrieves a set of file‑paths that must be copied from the build tree to the final install location.  
The function examines the target’s type (executable, static, shared, module, framework, bundle, framework‑like objects etc.) and, according to that type, it builds the list of source‑to‑destination paths.  
It sets a `Type` value (e.g. executable, static lib, directory) and a flag `NoTweak` when the target is a library of object files.  
Finally it verifies that every source has a matching destination and returns the `Files` container filled with `From`/`To` entries.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetInstallFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetInstallFi.body:
The routine checks whether the target is an executable or a library.  
For executables it pulls the suitable name (import library, import‑real, real, or canonical) from `GetExecutableNames`, normalizing import names with `GetImplibGNUtoMS` and falling back to the canonical name if the conversion fails.  
For libraries it does the same but pulls names from `GetLibraryNames`, handling the import‑lib, import‑real, real, or shared‑object cases, again defaulting to the canonical name when needed.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetInstallFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetInstallFi.body: Returns a string computed by the static overload of `GetInstallFilename`, passing the object’s current target, the supplied configuration string, and a flag that reflects whether the library is an import or a normal type.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetInstallOb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetInstallOb.body: The routine gathers the target’s object names into the supplied vector and then prefixes each entry with the directory returned by `computeInstallObjectDir`, effectively producing fully-qualified paths for the install objects.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetOptional@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetOptional@.body: Returns the value of the member `Optional` for the current instance.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetTarget@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::GetTarget@k_.body: The method returns the `Target` member pointer of the current object; it provides read‑only access to the target pointer stored in the class.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::IsImportLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::IsImportLibr.body: The method just reports the current value of the `ImportLibrary` member—returning the stored flag without altering any state. It is a read‑only accessor that merely yields the boolean held in the object.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::IssueCMP0095.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::IssueCMP0095.body: The function examines an input path string for the substring “${” to detect a pattern that may trigger the CMP0095 escaping rule. If that pattern is present, it emits an author‑warning via the target’s CMake instance, indicating that the corresponding path entry will not be escaped in the intermediate `cmake_install.cmake` script.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::PostReplacem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::PostReplacem.body: The routine orchestrates the registration of several installation patch rules by sequentially invoking dedicated helpers for install‑name patching, charpath patching, universal install rule, ranlib rule, and strip rule.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::PreReplaceme.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::PreReplaceme.body: The method performs a single operation: it forwards the supplied parameters—output stream, indentation level, configuration string, and target file path—to an internal routine that registers a rule for checking relative path correctness in the replacement process.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::SetImportlin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::SetImportlin.body: This function receives a `NamelinkModeType` value and assigns it to the `ImportlinkMode` member, effectively updating the internal mode setting.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::SetNamelinkM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::SetNamelinkM.body: Assigns the supplied `NamelinkModeType` value to the class’s internal `NamelinkMode` member, changing the object’s mode.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::cmInstallTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::cmInstallTar.body: The constructor creates an install‑generator instance that records the target name, destination directory, permissions string, and whether the target should be treated as an optional or library‑import item. It forwards the provided configurations and component name to the base `cmInstallGenerator` constructor, and then sets internal flags indicating that the generator should act per‑configuration (`ActionsPerConfig = true`) and that no special name‑linking is requested (`NamelinkMode = ImportlinkMode = NamelinkModeNone`).

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::cmInstallTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::cmInstallTar.body: The `cmInstallTargetGenerator` constructor creates a new generator instance from an existing one, copying its configuration so the new object can immediately generate install targets with the same settings. This constructor typically receives a reference to another `cmInstallTargetGenerator` and uses its internal state (e.g., mappings, flags, and generator options) to initialize the new instance.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::operator=@k_.body: The operator performs a straightforward deep copy: it copies each data member from the supplied object into the current instance and then returns *this for chaining.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::~cmInstallTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::~cmInstallTa.body: The virtual destructor `~cmInstallTargetGenerator()` guarantees that when a `cmInstallTargetGenerator` instance goes out of scope, all its internal resources are released—e.g., de‑allocating any owned buffers, closing file handles, and resetting internal state before the object is reclaimed by the runtime.

@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::cmInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::cmInsta.body: Creates a local‑install generator object, moves an existing generator into it, and registers that instance so it can be used to schedule the install of targets within the current build.

@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::cmInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::cmInsta.body: Initializes a local install target generator by invoking the base constructor with the target name, destination path, implementation flag, and other defaults, then triggers Compute to populate its state.

@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::cmInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::cmInsta.body: The function is a copy‑constructor for `cmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal`. It takes an existing generator object and creates a new instance that re‑inherits its internal configuration so that the new generator can immediately participate in the same local‑installation workflow as the original.

@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::operato.body: The operator= in `cmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal` performs a shallow copy of the source object into the current instance. It copies the internal state that the generator holds—such as the list of targets, any configured options, and any internal flags. No special resource handling or ownership transfer is performed; the assignment simply mirrors the contents of the right‑hand side into the left‑hand side.

@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::operato.body: The assignment operator copies the configuration state from the source object into the current instance—copying all internal members (install options, target data, etc.) and returns a reference to the modified object.

@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::~cmInst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGeneratorLocal::~cmInst.body: The function implements the local‑target installation routine. When invoked it builds and registers the target objects specific to the local generator, wiring them into the internal data structures that drive the overall installation flow. It performs any target‑specific setup required before signalling that the local target list is ready for further processing.

@lcmInstallTargetsCommand@k_Z23cmInstall.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetsCommand@k_Z23cmInstall.body: cmInstallTargetsCommand processes a list of target names (or a special `RUNTIME_DIRECTORY` keyword) and configures the Makefile to install them under the given runtime directory, marking each target as having an install rule. It returns false if arguments are missing or a target cannot be found.

@lcmInstalledFile::AppendProperty@k_ZN15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::AppendProperty@k_ZN15.body: The function adds a property to the file’s internal property map. It creates a generator expression by parsing the supplied value string and appends that expression to the property’s value list. If the property didn’t exist, it is implicitly created in the map.

@lcmInstalledFile::GetName@k_ZNK15cmInst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::GetName@k_ZNK15cmInst.body: The GetName() method simply returns a const reference to the internal `Name` string, exposing the stored value for read‑only access while avoiding any copying of the string data.

@lcmInstalledFile::GetNameExpression@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::GetNameExpression@k_Z.body: It returns a read‑only reference to the internal `NameExpression` object, exposing the underlying compiled expression that represents the file’s name. Because the method is `const`, the caller cannot modify the returned expression. The implementation simply dereferences the internal pointer, so callers should ensure that pointer is valid before invoking the function.

@lcmInstalledFile::GetProperties@k_ZNK15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::GetProperties@k_ZNK15.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the internal property map, allowing callers to inspect the stored properties without the ability to modify them.

@lcmInstalledFile::GetProperty@k_ZNK15cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::GetProperty@k_ZNK15cm.body: The `GetProperty` method checks whether the requested property key exists in the internal `Properties` map. If the key is missing, it returns `false`. When the key is found, it builds a single string by concatenating each `ValueExpression`’s input string, separated by semicolons, and assigns that concatenated string to the `value` out‑parameter, finally returning `true`.

@lcmInstalledFile::GetPropertyAsBool@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::GetPropertyAsBool@k_Z.body: The function retrieves the value of a named property into a local string, then returns `true` only if the property was found and its string value evaluates as an “on” indicator (via `cmIsOn`).

@lcmInstalledFile::GetPropertyAsList@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::GetPropertyAsList@k_Z.body: The method retrieves a property value, turns that string into a list of tokens via a helper, and returns the resulting vector by move‑ing it out. If the value is empty, the function simply yields an empty vector.

@lcmInstalledFile::HasProperty@k_ZNK15cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::HasProperty@k_ZNK15cm.body: It returns `true` when the supplied string is present as a key in the internal `Properties` collection; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmInstalledFile::Property::Property@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::Property::Property@k_.body: Property’s copy constructor is explicitly deleted, which forces any attempt to copy a Property instance to be a compile‑time error. This design choice guarantees that Property objects cannot be duplicated unintentionally, thereby preserving uniqueness of resources tied to each instance and preventing accidental sharing of internal state.

@lcmInstalledFile::Property::Property@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::Property::Property@k_.body: This constructor initializes a `Property` instance with the default state required by the surrounding library. It performs any necessary internal setup so that the object is ready for use in subsequent code sections.

@lcmInstalledFile::Property::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::Property::operator=@k.body: It forbids copying an existing `Property` object by marking the copy‑assignment operator as `delete`.

@lcmInstalledFile::Property::~Property@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::Property::~Property@k.body: The `~Property()` destructor is a defaulted, compiler‑generated destructor for the `cmInstalledFile::Property` class. It simply performs the standard clean‑up of any member data—destroying member objects and freeing any owned resources. Because it is marked `= default`, the compiler generates the body; if the class contains only plain‑old or standard‑library types, no explicit code is required, and the destructor does nothing beyond the normal automatic destruction of those members.

@lcmInstalledFile::RemoveProperty@k_ZN15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::RemoveProperty@k_ZN15.body: The method deletes an entry identified by the supplied key from the internal property map by invoking the underlying container’s `erase` routine with that key. This clears the corresponding mapping without altering any other state.

@lcmInstalledFile::SetName@k_ZN15cmInsta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::SetName@k_ZN15cmInsta.body: The function records the supplied name string and builds a parsed expression from it by creating a generator expression with the current back‑trace context before assigning both the raw name and the parsed expression to the object’s members.

@lcmInstalledFile::SetProperty@k_ZN15cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::SetProperty@k_ZN15cmI.body: Removes any existing property entry for the given name and then appends the new key/value pair to the file’s property list.

@lcmInstalledFile::cmInstalledFile@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::cmInstalledFile@k_ZN1.body: The declaration `cmInstalledFile(const cmInstalledFile&) = delete;` defines the copy‑constructor of the `cmInstalledFile` class and marks it as deleted. This means that attempts to copy‑construct an instance (e.g. `cmInstalledFile a = b;` or passing an object by value) will be a compile‑time error. The class therefore cannot be duplicated; only moving or creating fresh objects is allowed.

@lcmInstalledFile::cmInstalledFile@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::cmInstalledFile@k_ZN1.body: The constructor initializes a new instance, setting up the internal state needed for tracking an installed file’s status.

@lcmInstalledFile::~cmInstalledFile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstalledFile::~cmInstalledFile@k_ZN.body: The destructor simply cleans up a `cmInstalledFile` instance when it goes out of scope: it automatically destroys any member objects and releases any owned resources, with no extra custom logic.

@lcmIsInternallyOn@k_Z16cmIsInternallyOn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsInternallyOn@k_Z16cmIsInternallyOn.body: This function simply forwards the check to the `IsInternallyOn` member of `cmValue` and returns that result.

@lcmIsInternallyOn@k_Z16cmIsInternallyOn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsInternallyOn@k_Z16cmIsInternallyOn.body: cmIsInternallyOn forwards a C‑string pointer to the static helper `cmValue::IsInternallyOn` and returns that boolean result.

@lcmIsInternallyOn@k_Z16cmIsInternallyOn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsInternallyOn@k_Z16cmIsInternallyOn.body: A thin wrapper that forwards the check to the `cmValue` helper – it simply queries whether the supplied string view denotes an internally‑enabled state.

@lcmIsNOTFOUND@k_Z12cmIsNOTFOUND7cmValue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsNOTFOUND@k_Z12cmIsNOTFOUND7cmValue.body: Returns `true` when the supplied `cmValue` instance indicates a “not‑found” state; otherwise returns `false`.

@lcmIsNOTFOUND@k_Z12cmIsNOTFOUNDNSt3__11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsNOTFOUND@k_Z12cmIsNOTFOUNDNSt3__11.body: The function returns `true` when the supplied string view does **not** match any entry in the internal lookup; otherwise it returns `false`. It acts as a quick “is‑missing” check used by the surrounding code to gate subsequent logic.

@lcmIsNOTFOUND@k_Z12cmIsNOTFOUNDi@f./Sou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsNOTFOUND@k_Z12cmIsNOTFOUNDi@f./Sou.body: The function simply forwards the check to `cmValue::IsNOTFOUND`. It returns `true` when the supplied `cm::string_view` represents a value that should be treated as “not found.”

@lcmIsOff@k_Z7cmIsOff7cmValue@f./Source/.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsOff@k_Z7cmIsOff7cmValue@f./Source/.body: A lightweight wrapper that forwards a boolean check to the underlying `cmValue::IsOff()` method, effectively exposing a quick inline test to determine if a value represents an “off” state.

@lcmIsOff@k_Z7cmIsOffNSt3__117basic_stri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsOff@k_Z7cmIsOffNSt3__117basic_stri.body: This function evaluates a `cm::string_view` and returns `true` when its contents are effectively empty (e.g., no characters or only whitespace). It’s a lightweight helper used across the code base to guard against accidental “on” states where a string appears non‑empty but contains only ignorable text.

@lcmIsOff@k_Z7cmIsOffPKc@f./Source/cmVal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsOff@k_Z7cmIsOffPKc@f./Source/cmVal.body: The `cmIsOff` function is a tiny inline helper that forwards a raw C‑string to the `cmValue::IsOff` routine, returning the resulting boolean. It’s purpose is to give callers a lightweight, type‑safe way to test whether a string represents an “off” value without exposing the underlying `cmValue` details.

@lcmIsOff@k_Z7cmIsOffi@f./Source/cmValue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsOff@k_Z7cmIsOffi@f./Source/cmValue.body: The function `cmIsOff` accepts a `cm::string_view` and simply forwards the call to `cmValue::IsOff`, returning the resulting boolean value. It’s an inline wrapper that keeps the public API concise while delegating the actual check to the underlying `cmValue` implementation.

@lcmIsOn@k_Z6cmIsOn7cmValue@f./Source/cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsOn@k_Z6cmIsOn7cmValue@f./Source/cm.body: Returns whether the supplied `cmValue` reports itself as on.

@lcmIsOn@k_Z6cmIsOnNSt3__117basic_string.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsOn@k_Z6cmIsOnNSt3__117basic_string.body: cmIsOn examines a supplied string view to determine whether it represents an enabled state. It simply checks whether the view contains a value that is interpreted as “on”—typically the literal `"on"` or `"true"` (case‑insensitive). If the string matches one of those values, the function returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`. If the view is empty or only whitespace, it returns `false`.

@lcmIsOn@k_Z6cmIsOnPKc@f./Source/cmValue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsOn@k_Z6cmIsOnPKc@f./Source/cmValue.body: cmIsOn forwards the supplied C‑string to `cmValue::IsOn` and returns that function’s boolean result.

@lcmIsOn@k_Z6cmIsOni@f./Source/cmValue.h.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsOn@k_Z6cmIsOni@f./Source/cmValue.h.body: Returns true when the passed string view represents an “on” state, delegating the check to `cmValue::IsOn`. It’s a tiny, inline wrapper that simply forwards the call and returns the resulting boolean.

@lcmIsSpace@k_Z9cmIsSpacec@f./Source/cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsSpace@k_Z9cmIsSpacec@f./Source/cmS.body: The function returns `true` only when the byte has its most‑significant bit clear (i.e., it is a plain ASCII character) and `std::isspace` reports it as a whitespace.

@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Map@k_ZN19cmJSONH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Map@k_ZN19cmJSONH.body: The function creates a map of string keys to values of type T by applying a filtering step that accepts all entries, effectively delegating the work to `MapFilter`.

@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Optional@k_ZN19cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Optional@k_ZN19cm.body: The `Optional` template produces a callable that attempts to parse a JSON value into an `std::optional`. If the value is `nullptr`, the optional is reset and the function reports success; otherwise it constructs a new value and forwards the parsing logic to the supplied function.

@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Required@k_ZN19cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Required@k_ZN19cm.body: The `Required` helper creates a wrapper that first verifies a JSON value is present. It returns a lambda that takes an output reference, a `const Json::Value*`, and a `cmJSONState*`. If the value pointer is `nullptr`, it invokes the supplied `error` functor and returns `false`; otherwise it forwards the call to the supplied `func`. This pattern is typically used to embed presence‑checks in custom JSON deserialization routines.

@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Vector@k_ZN19cmJS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Vector@k_ZN19cmJS.body: The function creates a helper that filters a `std::vector<T>` using the supplied callable `func`. It forwards the supplied `error` generator and attaches a trivial predicate that accepts every element (`return true`). The resulting object can be used to iterate over the vector while applying `func` to each element.

@lcmJSONState::AddError@k_ZN11cmJSONStat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONState::AddError@k_ZN11cmJSONStat.body: Adds an error message to the internal error list—creating a new `Error` instance with the supplied string and pushing it onto the `errors` collection.

@lcmJSONState::AddErrorAtValue@k_ZN11cmJ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONState::AddErrorAtValue@k_ZN11cmJ.body: The method records an error condition. When supplied with a JSON value that is non‑null, it writes the error at that value’s offset; if no such location is present, it logs the error generically.

@lcmJSONState::cmJSONState@k_ZN11cmJSONS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONState::cmJSONState@k_ZN11cmJSONS.body: The constructor loads a JSON file, strips any leading BOM, stores the file’s raw text in `doc`, and attempts to parse it into the supplied `root` node while logging any parsing or file‑access errors.

@lcmJSONState::cmJSONState@k_ZN11cmJSONS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONState::cmJSONState@k_ZN11cmJSONS.body: The `cmJSONState` function is a simple default constructor that initializes a new instance of the `cmJSONState` type. It runs with no arguments, leaving the object in its default‑constructed state.

@lcmJoin@k_Z6cmJoinRKT_NSt3__117basic_st.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJoin@k_Z6cmJoinRKT_NSt3__117basic_st.body: This template converts a sequence of elements into a single string by sequentially appending each element to an output stream, inserting the supplied separator between successive items, and returns the accumulated string.

@lcmJoin@k_Z6cmJoinRKT_i.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJoin@k_Z6cmJoinRKT_i.body: The template `cmJoin` takes a range of elements and a `cm::string_view` separator. It constructs and returns a single `std::string` by concatenating each element in the range using the supplied separator.

@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::GetLDConfigPat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::GetLDConfigPat.body: Retrieves the system’s library search paths by running the ldconfig utility with flags that list the current paths. It parses each line of the output, extracts the path token before the colon, and appends those paths to the supplied vector. On failure it logs an error in the archive and returns false; on success it returns true.

@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::cmLDConfigLDCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::cmLDConfigLDCo.body: The constructor takes an rvalue reference of `cmLDConfigLDConfigTool` and forwards the initialization to the base `cmLDConfigTool`. It then moves the internal configuration data from the source object into the new instance, guaranteeing that the moved‑from object is left in a safe, destructible state without leaking resources.

@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::cmLDConfigLDCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::cmLDConfigLDCo.body: The constructor simply forwards the provided `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` pointer to its base class (`cmLDConfigTool`). It performs no other initialization.

@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::cmLDConfigLDCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::cmLDConfigLDCo.body: The constructor simply copies an existing `cmLDConfigLDConfigTool` instance into a new one, duplicating all internal state so the new object behaves identically to the source.

@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::operator=@k_ZN.body: The move‑assignment operator takes an rvalue of the same type, copies or moves the internal configuration data into the current instance, and returns a reference to that instance so chaining of assignments is possible.

@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::operator=@k_ZN.body: The assignment operator copies the entire internal state from the right‑hand operand into the current object, ensuring that after the call the target instance holds exactly the same configuration values. It performs a deep copy of all member fields (including any base‑class parts) and returns a reference to the left‑hand object so that chained assignments can be used. The implementation usually guards against self‑assignment and forwards to the base class’s assignment when appropriate.

@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::~cmLDConfigLDC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLDConfigLDConfigTool::~cmLDConfigLDC.body: When a `cmLDConfigLDConfigTool` object is destroyed, its destructor releases any configuration‑related resources that were allocated during its lifetime. It calls the base `cmLDConfigTool` destructor to perform the standard clean‑up tasks, then clears out any internal state—such as resetting flags, detaching observers, and freeing buffers that were used to hold temporary configuration data.

@lcmLDConfigTool::cmLDConfigTool@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLDConfigTool::cmLDConfigTool@k_ZN14c.body: The constructor accepts a pointer to a `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` and assigns it to the member variable `Archive`, effectively recording the archive instance for later use.

@lcmLDConfigTool::~cmLDConfigTool@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLDConfigTool::~cmLDConfigTool@k_ZN14.body: The destructor is declared virtual and defaulted, guaranteeing that any subclass will have its own destructor invoked automatically when an object of the base type is destroyed. It relies on the compiler‑generated body, so no explicit cleanup code is needed in the header.

@lcmLGInfoProp@k_ZL12cmLGInfoPropP10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLGInfoProp@k_ZL12cmLGInfoPropP10cmMa.body: Retrieves the value of the named property from the supplied target; if the property exists it is inserted into the supplied `cmMakefile` via `AddDefinition`.

@lcmLibDirsLinked@k_ZL15cmLibDirsLinkedR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLibDirsLinked@k_ZL15cmLibDirsLinkedR.body: The function returns `true` when the two directory strings resolve to the same real path; it first checks whether at least one of them is a symlink and then compares the results of `cmSystemTools::GetRealPath` for both paths.

@lcmLinkDirectoriesCommand@k_Z24cmLinkDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkDirectoriesCommand@k_Z24cmLinkDi.body: It parses the supplied arguments to determine if the directories should be added before or after existing ones, collects the directory paths, and registers them with the makefile.

@lcmLinkImplItem::cmLinkImplItem@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkImplItem::cmLinkImplItem@k_ZN14c.body: The constructor takes a `cmLinkItem` instance and a boolean flag. It forwards the item to the base class via `std::move` and stores the flag in the member `CheckCMP0027`.

@lcmLinkImplItem::cmLinkImplItem@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkImplItem::cmLinkImplItem@k_ZN14c.body: The constructor simply forwards initialization to the base class `cmLinkItem`, invoking its default constructor. No additional state is set in this derived type.

@lcmLinkInterface::cmLinkInterface@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkInterface::cmLinkInterface@k_ZN1.body: cmLinkInterface() orchestrates the setup and teardown of external link interfaces by registering callbacks, validating protocol compliance, and routing message traffic through the appropriate channel handlers.

@lcmLinkItem::AsStr@k_ZNK10cmLinkItem5As.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItem::AsStr@k_ZNK10cmLinkItem5As.body: It returns the name of the target when available; otherwise it returns a stored string.

@lcmLinkItem::cmLinkItem@k_ZN10cmLinkIte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItem::cmLinkItem@k_ZN10cmLinkIte.body: Constructs a `cmLinkItem` by storing the supplied name, whether it should be cross‑linked, and the back‑trace information that will later be used to reference the corresponding files.

@lcmLinkItem::cmLinkItem@k_ZN10cmLinkIte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItem::cmLinkItem@k_ZN10cmLinkIte.body: A cmLinkItem object is created by storing the supplied target pointer, the cross‑flag value, and moving the supplied back‑trace list into its own member variables.

@lcmLinkItem::cmLinkItem@k_ZN10cmLinkIte.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItem::cmLinkItem@k_ZN10cmLinkIte.body: The `cmLinkItem` constructor is a default constructor that simply initializes a new `cmLinkItem` instance. It ensures all member fields are set to their default values before the object is used elsewhere in the code.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::GetDependencie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::GetDependencie.body: Aggregates all library and utility references required for a target: first it pulls private implementation libraries and marks them as `LinkPrivate`; then it pulls interface libraries, overlaying any existing entries as `LinkPublic` or `LinkInterface`; after that it collects object libraries that are not yet mapped and tags them as `Object`; finally it enumerates any utility items that remain unreferenced and tags them as `Utility`. The resulting map contains a key‑to‑dependency entry for every referenced library or item.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::ItemVisited@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::ItemVisited@k_.body: The method returns whether an item’s string identifier is already in the `VisitedItems` collection; if it’s absent, the string is inserted before returning the original “visited” flag.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::LinkVisited@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::LinkVisited@k_.body: The `LinkVisited` function records and queries whether a specific link between two `cmLinkItem` objects has already been processed. It builds a string pair from the two items, checks the `VisitedLinks` set for that pair, inserts it if absent, and returns `true` only when the pair was previously present.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::OnDirectLink@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::OnDirectLink@k.body: A protected pure virtual member that must be overridden in derived visitors. It receives a `cmLinkItem const&` that identifies the link being processed and lets the implementation decide how to react when a direct link event occurs.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::OnIndirectLink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::OnIndirectLink.body: When a traversal encounters an indirect link it calls this hook; a concrete visitor implements it to perform whatever handling is needed for that situation (e.g., updating state, firing callbacks, or triggering side‑effects).

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::OnItem@k_ZN22c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::OnItem@k_ZN22c.body: The `OnItem` method is a protected pure virtual function that subclasses must implement to process individual `cmLinkItem` instances. It is intended as a callback for derived visitor classes to react to each item as it is traversed or modified, ensuring consistent handling across the system.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::VisitGraph@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::VisitGraph@k_Z.body: The `VisitGraph` function is a pure virtual member of a graph‑visitor interface. It is called whenever the traversal reaches a graph element identified by a string name. Implementations must provide the concrete logic for processing that element – for example, collecting statistics, transforming nodes, or performing validations. Because it is declared `= 0`, any subclass of this visitor must override the method; otherwise the compiler will reject the subclass. This function acts as the single entry point for every concrete visitor that wishes to plug its processing logic into the graph‑visiting framework.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::VisitItem@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::VisitItem@k_ZN.body: This method first skips any item that has already been processed (via `ItemVisited`); if it’s a new item it fires the visitor’s `OnItem` hook and then recursively processes all links tied to that item by invoking `VisitLinks`.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::VisitLinks@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::VisitLinks@k_Z.body: VisitLinks first verifies that the supplied link item actually has an associated target; if the target is null it simply returns. Otherwise it fetches the target’s generator configuration list (including the special “empty config” flag) and iterates over that list, recursively calling the same visitor helper for each config to walk the sub‑links from that point.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::VisitLinks@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::VisitLinks@k_Z.body: The function walks the dependency graph for a given link item: it fetches the item’s target, gathers its direct dependencies, and for each one it ensures the dependee is processed only once, fires the direct‑link event, then fires an indirect‑link event when the current item isn’t the root. After handling a link it recurses into each dependee with the same root, allowing the graph to be fully traversed.

@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::~cmLinkItemGra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemGraphVisitor::~cmLinkItemGra.body: The destructor for `cmLinkItemGraphVisitor` is virtual, allowing derived visitors to override it if necessary. Marked as `= default`, it relies on the compiler to synthesize a trivial destructor that performs no custom cleanup beyond the base class’s own destructors. This ensures that when a derived class’s object is destroyed, all resources are released correctly without manual boiler‑plate code.

@lcmLinkItemValidForDevice@k_ZL24cmLinkI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkItemValidForDevice@k_ZL24cmLinkI.body: The function checks whether a link‑item string is permitted for a device by verifying that it either has no leading hyphen or matches one of the accepted prefixes (‑l, ‑L or —library). If the test succeeds, it returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeFrameworkPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeFrameworkPa.body: When fwSearchFlag is true the function appends each path returned by cli.GetFrameworkPaths() into a single string; otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkLibrari.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkLibrari.body: Collects library strings into a vector, then calls `cli.AppendValues` to merge that list into the final output string.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkLibrari.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkLibrari.body: ComputeLinkLibraries computes a runtime path string via ComputeRPath and appends it to the linkLibraries vector when non‑empty. It then calls ComputeLinkLibs to populate the vector with library entries. Afterwards it appends any rpath_link flags escaped for shell syntax and, if present, the stdLibString, and finally inserts the resulting string into linkLibraries.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkLibs@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkLibs@k_.body: This function assembles a string of linked‑library paths by first collecting them into a vector via a helper overload, then calling `cli.AppendValues` to serialize the list into a single string that is returned.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkLibs@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkLibs@k_.body: The routine iterates over the `cmComputeLinkInformation`’s items, filters out the ones whose target type is an interface or object library, and for each remaining item builds a formatted string. If the item is marked as a path, it converts the path value to a link‑style reference and then to the desired output format; otherwise it uses the raw value. Finally it appends a trailing space to the string and pushes the result into the output vector.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkPath@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkPath@k_.body: The method collects link‑path fragments into a list, passes that list to the private `ComputeLinkPath` overload to populate it, then appends those fragments to the `cli` accumulator and finally returns the resulting string.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkPath@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeLinkPath@k_.body: The method builds a list of linker arguments by iterating over the target items supplied in the `cmComputeLinkInformation` object. For each static or shared library target it appends a string prefixed by the supplied flag and suffixed by a terminator, optionally switching the artifact type to an import‑library form when that library is present. After completing the list it appends any directories returned by `GetDirectoriesWithBacktraces`, again prefixing/terminating them with the same flag. The resulting vector of `BT<std::string>` objects is returned through the output `linkPath` argument.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeRPath@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ComputeRPath@k_ZN1.body:
Creates a string of runtime‑library options for the link command.  
If no separator is set, it emits a separate `-R…` flag for each directory; otherwise it combines all directories into one option, escaping the path string for shell safety. The resulting string is returned.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ConvertToLinkRefer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ConvertToLinkRefer.body: This method simply forwards the supplied library path to the `OutputConverter` instance and returns the string produced by `MaybeRelativeToCurBinDir`. The function is const‑qualified, does not alter any internal state, and relies on the converter to compute a relative path when appropriate.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ConvertToOutputFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ConvertToOutputFor.body: The method determines which output format to request based on two flags (`ForResponse` and `UseNinjaMulti`) and forwards the original string together with the chosen format flag and a quote‑handling toggle to an injected `OutputConverter`. The returned string is the fully formatted result.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::ConvertToOutputFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::ConvertToOutputFor.body: The method determines which output format to target by examining the object’s flags (`ForResponse`, `UseNinjaMulti`) and then forwards the request to its `OutputConverter` instance, supplying the chosen format together with the `UseWatcomQuote` flag. The result of that conversion is returned to the caller.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::GetLinkerLanguage@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::GetLinkerLanguage@.body: The routine forwards a request for a linker language string to the supplied target object, returning whatever string the target’s own `GetLinkerLanguage` implementation produces.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::SetForResponse@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::SetForResponse@k_Z.body: The method simply stores the supplied Boolean in the object’s internal flag, which downstream logic consults to decide whether to produce a response.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::SetRelink@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::SetRelink@k_ZN18cm.body: Assigns the supplied flag to the internal member, altering the object’s internal state used by downstream logic.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::SetUseNinjaMulti@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::SetUseNinjaMulti@k.body: It updates the internal flag that determines whether the linker uses the Ninja‑based multi‑link pass.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::SetUseWatcomQuote@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::SetUseWatcomQuote@.body: Assigns the supplied boolean to the internal flag indicating whether Watcom quoting should be used.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::cmLinkLineComputer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::cmLinkLineComputer.body: Initializes the internal references for the state directory and output converter.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::cmLinkLineComputer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::cmLinkLineComputer.body: The deleted copy constructor prevents unintended duplication of `cmLinkLineComputer` instances, ensuring each object remains a unique, non‑copyable entity.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::operator=@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::operator=@k_ZN18cm.body: Disabling assignment prevents accidental modification of an existing `cmLinkLineComputer` instance, ensuring each instance remains independent and its state cannot be inadvertently overwritten.

@lcmLinkLineComputer::~cmLinkLineCompute.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineComputer::~cmLinkLineCompute.body: The destructor `~cmLinkLineComputer()` is declared virtual and defaulted. This means that when an object of any derived type is destroyed, the compiler will automatically generate the destructor, and the base class’s destructor will be called implicitly. It relies on the standard language rules to invoke any derived destructor before the base one, ensuring resources are freed correctly without the need for explicit cleanup code. The virtual nature allows subclasses to provide specialized cleanup logic while still being invoked automatically during destruction.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeLinkL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeLinkL.body: The function collects unique link‑library references from a list of items supplied in a `cmComputeLinkInformation` object. It skips any library that is a shared, module, object, or interface library, and skips static libraries that have the `CUDA_RESOLVE_DEVICE_SYMBOLS` property set. For each remaining item it normalises the path (removing unsupported suffixes or converting relative paths) and appends a trailing space to separate entries. It then looks up the link‑implementation data to find a matching library record and, if found, copies the back‑trace information for that library. Each processed library is inserted into the result vector only once (duplicates are discarded by the `emitted` set). Finally, if a standard‑library string is supplied, it is appended to the list as a final entry.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.body: The operator() function takes a const reference to a cmComputeLinkInformation::Item and returns a bool value.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.body: Checks that the item’s target is a static library that must be linked in device mode.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.body: The function scans the list of link targets for any static‑library item that does not have the “CUDA_RESOLVE_DEVICE_SYMBOLS” flag but does have the “CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION” flag. If at least one such item is found, it returns true, signalling that device‑linking is required.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.body: The method performs a single‑step check on a `cmComputeLinkInformation::Item`, returning `true` when the item meets the internal consistency criteria and `false` otherwise. It is intended to be invoked in contexts that require a quick validation before proceeding with further link‑information processing.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.body: The lambda returns true only when the target library is a static library that has device‑symbol resolution disabled, separable compilation turned on, and IPO enabled for the CUDA configuration.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::ComputeRequi.body: The routine scans the list of link‑targets in the supplied compute‑link information. It returns `true` if any target is a static library that does not have CUDA‑device‑symbol resolution enabled, is marked separable for CUDA, and has IPO turned on for the current CUDA configuration.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::GetLinkerLan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::GetLinkerLan.body: The `GetLinkerLanguage` method is a virtual member that returns a `std::string` indicating the linker language used by the target. In this implementation it simply returns the literal string `"CUDA"`.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::cmLinkLineDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::cmLinkLineDe.body: The constructor of `cmLinkLineDeviceComputer` simply forwards the provided `cmOutputConverter*` and `cmStateDirectory const&` to its base class `cmLinkLineComputer`. No additional initialization logic is performed in the body.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::cmLinkLineDe.author: AI Short Overview

Copying an instance of this class is explicitly forbidden, as its copy constructor is declared `delete`, preventing accidental or unintended duplication of the internal state.

@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
