@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::~cmLinkLineD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkLineDeviceComputer::~cmLinkLineD.body: The `~cmLinkLineDeviceComputer` function is a virtual destructor. It is marked with `override` to guarantee that derived types will invoke the correct cleanup logic. The implementation in the source file simply delegates to the compiler‑generated default destructor (`= default;`), ensuring that all member resources are properly released when a `cmLinkLineDeviceComputer` object goes out of scope.

@lcmLinkedTree::Clear@k_ZN12cmLinkedTree.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::Clear@k_ZN12cmLinkedTree.body: This member function empties the internal collections `UpPositions` and `Data`. It simply invokes their `clear()` methods, removing all stored elements from both containers.

@lcmLinkedTree::GetPointer@k_ZN12cmLinke.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::GetPointer@k_ZN12cmLinke.body: The function returns the address of the element at the specified index in the internal array. It does no bounds checking, so callers must guarantee that `pos` is a valid index before calling `GetPointer`.

@lcmLinkedTree::GetReference@k_ZN12cmLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::GetReference@k_ZN12cmLin.body: `GetReference` is a templated member that returns a reference to the element stored at the supplied index in the container’s data array. It simply indexes the underlying array (or vector‐like container) using `pos` and returns the element. The function relies on `PositionType` being a valid index (in bounds) and `Data` being a storage holding the elements. It performs no copying, just a reference fetch.

@lcmLinkedTree::IsLast@k_ZN12cmLinkedTre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::IsLast@k_ZN12cmLinkedTre.body: The function returns `true` when the iterator’s internal position equals the number of elements in the container, effectively checking whether the iterator is positioned at the end of the sequence.

@lcmLinkedTree::Pop@k_ZN12cmLinkedTree3P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::Pop@k_ZN12cmLinkedTree3P.body: The `Pop` method removes the element referenced by the passed iterator. It first verifies that the container is non‑empty, then checks if the iterator points to the last element. If so, it pops the trailing entries in both the data and position lists. Finally it returns an iterator that now points to the element that followed the removed one (or the end if there was none).

@lcmLinkedTree::Push@k_ZN12cmLinkedTree4.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::Push@k_ZN12cmLinkedTree4.body: The function `Push` takes an `iterator` argument and forwards it to a private implementation helper, passing a default-constructed value of type `T`. It inserts the new element at the position specified by the iterator and returns an iterator that refers to the newly inserted element.

@lcmLinkedTree::Push@k_ZN12cmLinkedTree4.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::Push@k_ZN12cmLinkedTree4.body: The function forwards the insertion of `t` to the underlying implementation by moving the element into the container and returns an iterator that refers to the inserted element.

@lcmLinkedTree::Push_impl@k_ZN12cmLinked.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::Push_impl@k_ZN12cmLinked.body: The routine first verifies that the internal position and data vectors are still in sync. It records the iterator’s position in the auxiliary position vector, appends the moved element into the data vector, and finally returns an iterator that refers to the newly inserted element at the end of the container.

@lcmLinkedTree::Root@k_ZNK12cmLinkedTree.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::Root@k_ZNK12cmLinkedTree.body: Returns an iterator positioned at the first node of the tree by casting the current object to a non‑const `cmLinkedTree` and constructing an iterator with index 0.

@lcmLinkedTree::Truncate@k_ZN12cmLinkedT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::Truncate@k_ZN12cmLinkedT.body: Removes all elements after the first element in both `UpPositions` and `Data`, then returns an iterator pointing at the second element.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::IsValid@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::IsValid@k_ZNK1.body: The function `IsValid` verifies that the object is attached to a tree and that the stored index (`Position`) refers to an element that actually exists in that tree’s data vector. It first guards against a null tree pointer; if the tree is missing, the function immediately reports `false`. If a tree is present, it compares `Position` against the size of the tree’s data vector, returning `true` only when the index is within the valid range (`0 ≤ Position < size`). If `Position` falls outside that range, the function reports `false`.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::StrictWeakOrde.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::StrictWeakOrde.body: Checks that the two iterators belong to the same tree and returns true when the current iterator’s position precedes the other’s position.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::iterator@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::iterator@k_ZN1.body: Initializes a newly‑created iterator instance by storing a pointer to the supplied tree and the starting position. It performs no other logic beyond these member assignments.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::iterator@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::iterator@k_ZN1.body: This constructor sets the iterator’s internal state to an empty tree and zero position, preparing it for traversal.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator!=@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator!=@k_Z.body: The function first validates that both iterators belong to a consistent tree structure (ensuring the backing vectors are the same size). It then simply inverts the result of the equality comparison, delegating that logic to the already‑implemented `operator==`. This keeps the implementation minimal while ensuring the comparison is performed safely on the internal data structures.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator*@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator*@k_ZN.body: It validates the internal tree state and returns the element that precedes the current position, i.e. the reference stored at `Position‑1`.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator*@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator*@k_ZN.body: Returns a reference to the element at the current position in the underlying tree.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator++@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator++@k_Z.body: The method moves the iterator to the next node: it validates the tree and position, then sets `Position` to the value stored in `Tree->UpPositions` at the index `Position‑1`. It effectively performs a pre‑increment for a tree‑based iterator.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator->@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator->@k_Z.body: The function returns a pointer to the node immediately preceding the current `Position` in the tree. It first verifies that the tree and the indices are consistent via a series of assertions, then retrieves the pointer stored at the index `Position‑1` (the element just before the current position). If any assertion fails or the index is out of range, the function will trigger an assertion failure.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator->@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator->@k_Z.body: Retrieves the pointer for the current node in the tree, after verifying that the tree exists, that its internal position vectors are consistent, and that the position index is valid.

@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator==@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLinkedTree::iterator::operator==@k_Z.body: Compares two iterator instances from the same tree and returns true only if their internal positions match. The method asserts that the tree pointers are non‑null, that the tree’s internal size invariants hold, and that both iterators belong to the same tree before performing the equality check on the position field.

@lcmList::ComputeIndex@k_ZNK6cmList12Com.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmList::ComputeIndex@k_ZNK6cmList12Com.body:
The `ComputeIndex` method maps a logical position `pos` into an actual list index while optionally enforcing bounds.  
When `boundCheck` is `true`, it first verifies that the container isn’t empty; if it is, an `std::out_of_range` exception is thrown.  
For a non‑empty list, the method normalises a negative `pos` by adding the list length, effectively performing a circular wrap‑around. It then verifies that the resulting index lies within `[0, size‑1]`; any violation triggers another `std::out_of_range`.  

If `boundCheck` is `false`, the method simply converts a possibly negative position into the equivalent positive index by adding the list size when the position is negative, without performing any range checks.  

In short, the function returns the effective zero‑based index corresponding to an arbitrary signed index, optionally throwing an exception when the index is out of bounds.

@lcmList::ComputeInsertIndex@k_ZNK6cmLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmList::ComputeInsertIndex@k_ZNK6cmLis.body:
The function validates and normalises an insertion position.  
When *boundCheck* is true it verifies that the supplied `pos` falls inside the current list bounds – throwing an exception if the list is empty and `pos` isn’t zero or if `pos` (after normalising negative values relative to the list length) lies outside the inclusive range `[0, length]`.  
If *boundCheck* is false, it simply returns the supplied position, interpreting negative indices as offsets from the list’s end. The routine therefore guarantees that any returned index will be a legal slot inside the container for a subsequent insert operation.

The function returns an iterator pointing at the first element inserted.

@lcmListFileFunction::LowerCaseName@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileFunction::LowerCaseName@k_ZN.body: The `LowerCaseName` member simply returns a stored string value – it’s a read‑only accessor that guarantees no exceptions (the `noexcept` qualifier) and returns a const reference to preserve the string’s immutability.

@lcmListFileFunction::OriginalName@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileFunction::OriginalName@k_ZNK.body: It returns a const reference to the internal string member without modifying state or throwing exceptions.

@lcmListFileFunction::cmListFileFunction.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileFunction::cmListFileFunction.body: Creates an Implementation instance with the given name, source‑file line range, and argument list, storing it in the internal Impl member.

@lcmListFileLexerAppend@p@l./Source/Lexe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexerAppend@p@l./Source/Lexe.body: The function concatenates a provided text string onto the lexer’s current token buffer. It first checks whether the existing buffer has enough space; if not, it allocates a larger buffer (newSize = current length + appended length + 1 for the NUL), copies the current token data, frees the old buffer, appends the new text, terminates with a NUL, and updates the token length and buffer size. The routine omits all null‑pointer checks (e.g., lexer or text being NULL) and relies on plain `strcpy`/`memcpy`, so a misuse can lead to undefined behaviour or a memory leak. The implementation also re‑allocates the buffer on every append that exceeds the current size, which can be expensive for many small appends – using `realloc` or incremental growth would be more efficient.

@lcmListFileLexerDestroy@p@l./Source/Lex.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexerDestroy@p@l./Source/Lex.body: The function resets the lexer’s state by clearing the current token, releasing the YACC-generated lexer scanner, and then closing any open file handle and freeing the allocated string buffer. It also clears the buffer indices so that subsequent calls start from a clean state.

@lcmListFileLexerInit@p@l./Source/LexerP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexerInit@p@l./Source/LexerP.body: The function checks whether the lexer has a source to read (a file or a string buffer). If so, it calls the lexer‑specific YACC‑generated initialization routine to create the scanning context and then stores the lexer instance in that context so subsequent token fetches can retrieve the owning lexer. If neither source is present, the function simply exits without performing any work.

@lcmListFileLexerInput@p@l./Source/Lexer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexerInput@p@l./Source/Lexer.body: The routine reads input data into the supplied buffer, translating any CR‑LF pairs into single LF characters and preserving any trailing carriage‑return that could belong to the next read. It keeps a “cr” offset field to remember that leftover CR, and updates this field after each read. When no file remains it simply copies any remaining characters from an internal string buffer. The function returns the number of bytes actually filled, or 0 if there is nothing more to read.

@lcmListFileLexerSetToken@p@l./Source/Le.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexerSetToken@p@l./Source/Le.body: Sets the current token’s line/column numbers from the lexer’s current line/column and then stores the supplied text into the token buffer. It first checks if an existing buffer can be reused; if the new text fits in the current buffer it simply copies it and records its length. Otherwise it frees the old buffer, allocates a new one (or leaves it empty if no text is supplied) and updates the token’s length field.

@lcmListFileLexer_Delete@kcmListFileLexe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_Delete@kcmListFileLexe.body: This routine first clears the internal file‑name buffer (by resetting it to zero) and then releases the memory occupied by the lexer instance itself, ensuring that any resources it holds are properly released before the object is discarded.

@lcmListFileLexer_GetCurrentColumn@kcmLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_GetCurrentColumn@kcmLi.body: The function simply returns the current column number stored in the lexer structure. It reads the `column` field of a `cmListFileLexer` instance and returns it as a `long`. The function assumes the pointer passed is valid; passing a `NULL` pointer would result in undefined behavior. The returned value is the number of columns parsed so far in the current line, useful for error reporting or syntax highlighting.

@lcmListFileLexer_GetCurrentLine@kcmList.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_GetCurrentLine@kcmList.body: It returns the value stored in the lexer’s internal line counter, giving the current line number being processed.

@lcmListFileLexer_GetTypeAsString@kcmLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_GetTypeAsString@kcmLis.body: Converts each enum value in the lexer’s token type to a readable string literal; when the input token doesn’t match any explicit case, it falls through to return “unknown token”.

@lcmListFileLexer_New@kcmListFileLexer_N.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_New@kcmListFileLexer_N.body: Allocates a `cmListFileLexer` structure, zero‑initialises it, sets its `line` and `column` fields to 1, and returns the newly created object—or `NULL` if allocation fails.

@lcmListFileLexer_ReadBOM@p@l./Source/Le.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_ReadBOM@p@l./Source/Le.body: It examines the first few bytes of the file: reading 0‑4 bytes in sequence, matching them against the standard BOM patterns for UTF‑8, UTF‑16 BE/LE, UTF‑32 BE/LE. If a known pattern is seen it returns the corresponding enum; otherwise it resets the file position to the start of the file and signals no BOM (or a broken state if the stream cannot be rewound).

@lcmListFileLexer_Scan@kcmListFileLexer_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_Scan@kcmListFileLexer_.body: The function checks whether there is any input to process—if both the file stream and the string buffer are empty it returns `NULL`. If input is available it invokes the internal lexer (`cmListFileLexer_yylex`). On success it returns the address of the current token; on failure it clears the current filename by calling `cmListFileLexer_SetFileName` with zeros and then returns `NULL`.

@lcmListFileLexer_SetFileName@kcmListFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_SetFileName@kcmListFil.body: The function closes any previously opened file for the lexer, clears its internal state, then opens the file specified by `name` in binary‑read mode. If a BOM pointer is supplied, it reads and stores the file’s BOM. The function returns 1 on success and 0 if the file fails to open.

@lcmListFileLexer_SetString@kcmListFileL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_SetString@kcmListFileL.body: The `cmListFileLexer_SetString` routine replaces the lexer’s internal string buffer with a copy of the supplied text. It first clears any existing buffer by destroying the lexer, then allocates space for the new string (including a null terminator), copies it, and resets internal indices (`string_position` to the start and `string_left` to the string length). After copying, it re‑initialises the lexer for scanning the fresh content. The function returns a success flag (`1`) unless the allocation fails, in which case it returns `0`.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_create_buffer@kcmLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_create_buffer@kcmLi.body: The routine allocates a new buffer structure, records the requested size, and allocates a character buffer that is two bytes larger (for the end‑of‑buffer markers). It sets the buffer‑ownership flag, calls an initializer that ties the buffer to a file stream, and returns the populated buffer structure. If any allocation fails it logs a fatal error and aborts.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_delete_buffer@kcmLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_delete_buffer@kcmLi.body: The routine releases a scanning buffer: it first verifies the buffer pointer is non‑null, clears the current‑buffer slot if the buffer being deleted is the active one, then frees the buffer’s internal data (if it was allocated by the scanner) and finally frees the buffer structure itself. It guards against double frees by checking the ownership flag and avoids dereferencing a nil pointer; on unlikely edge cases (e.g. the buffer is already in use elsewhere) it simply exits without action.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_flush_buffer@kcmLis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_flush_buffer@kcmLis.body: The function clears a buffer’s contents, zeroing its character count and inserting the required sentinel end‑of‑buffer markers at the start of the buffer. It resets internal pointers and flags so the scanner knows the buffer is now empty and in the “new” state. If the buffer being flushed is the one currently active (`YY_CURRENT_BUFFER`), it triggers a fresh state load for the scanner.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_init_buffer@kc3cmLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_init_buffer@kc3cmLi.body: This routine prepares the lexer’s internal buffer for a new input source. It assigns the provided `FILE*` to the buffer’s file pointer, zeroes the read‑and‑write positions, and sets the buffer’s state flags (e.g. `YY_BUF_STATE_NORMAL`). It also allocates or re‑uses a temporary scratch space for the scanner’s use, ensuring that the `yyscanner` structure now points to a clean, freshly‑initialized buffer ready for tokenisation.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_init_buffer@p@l./So.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_init_buffer@p@l./So.body: The routine flushes the buffer, assigns the new input file, resets line and column counters if the buffer isn’t the current one, marks whether the input is interactive, and restores the original errno value.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_load_buffer_state@p.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_load_buffer_state@p.body: The routine copies the current buffer’s meta‑data into the lexer’s global structure: it records the number of characters read, the pointer to the current position in that buffer, the file handle it’s reading from, and the next character that will be consumed.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_scan_buffer@kcmList.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_scan_buffer@kcmList.body: Creates a new `YY_BUFFER_STATE` structure that tracks a buffer of characters read from a source. It verifies that the caller supplied enough space for the two end‑of‑buffer characters required by the lexer, allocates the buffer struct, populates fields (size, position, flags indicating whether it’s an owned buffer, etc.), points the lexer’s current buffer pointers to this new buffer, and returns the new buffer handle for further scanning operations.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_scan_bytes@kcmListF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_scan_bytes@kcmListF.body: Creates a buffer just large enough to hold the input bytes plus two sentinel characters. It copies the supplied data into that buffer, places two end‑of‑buffer markers at the end, and then forwards the buffer to the core scanner routine. Once the scan completes, it marks the buffer as owned so it can be freed later, and finally returns the buffer handle.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_scan_string@kcmList.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_scan_string@kcmList.body: The function creates a scan buffer from a C‑string: it simply passes the string pointer and its length (obtained with strlen) to `yy_scan_bytes` and returns the resulting buffer state.

@lcmListFileLexer_yy_switch_to_buffer@kc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yy_switch_to_buffer@kc.body: The routine switches the lexer’s current input buffer to a new one: it first guarantees the buffer stack is initialized, then if the requested buffer is already active it exits immediately. Otherwise it writes back the current buffer’s position and character count into its saved state, assigns the new buffer as active, reloads that buffer’s state into the scanner, and finally flags that a buffer switch has happened so that any pending end‑of‑file handling will treat it correctly.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyalloc@kcmListFileLex.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyalloc@kcmListFileLex.body: The `cmListFileLexer_yyalloc` routine is a thin wrapper around `malloc`. It takes a requested size and a scanner handle, casts the scanner to a `struct yyguts_t *` (though the casted pointer isn’t used), and then simply returns the result of `malloc(size)`. No extra bookkeeping, alignment or zero‑initialisation is performed.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyensure_buffer_stack@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyensure_buffer_stack@.body: This routine guarantees that the scanner’s internal stack of buffer‑state pointers is allocated and adequately sized. On first call it allocates an array (initially one slot, though the comment says two) and zeroes it; on subsequent calls it checks whether the current top index has reached the allocated limit and, if so, grows the array by a fixed growth factor (8). The routine is responsible for maintaining the stack’s dynamic size and for detecting allocation failures.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyfree@kcmListFileLexe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyfree@kcmListFileLexe.body: The function receives a pointer and a scanner object, casts the scanner to a `yyguts_t` struct (though the resulting pointer is unused), and finally calls `free()` on the provided pointer. It’s a thin wrapper used by the lexer to release memory that was allocated during tokenization.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_column@kcmListFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_column@kcmListFi.body: The function simply returns the current column number for the scanner. It casts the generic scanner handle to the internal context structure, verifies that the current buffer is valid, and then returns the stored column value. The only point to watch is that the `yycolumn` field must have been set by the lexer’s token‑reading logic; if the buffer is null the routine returns 0.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_debug@kcmListFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_debug@kcmListFil.body: The function casts the supplied scanner pointer to its internal `yyguts_t` structure and returns the global `yy_flex_debug` flag, effectively exposing the current debug state.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_extra@kcmListFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_extra@kcmListFil.body: The routine simply casts the generic scanner handle to its internal structure type and returns the stored `yyextra` member, exposing the auxiliary data that accompanies the scanner instance.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_in@kcmListFileLe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_in@kcmListFileLe.body: This function takes a scanner context (`yyscan_t`) and is intended to return the file descriptor that the lexer uses as its input stream. Internally it casts the generic scanner pointer to the concrete `yyguts_t` structure and then returns the global `yyin` variable, which is presumed to hold the `FILE*` opened for the source file.  The snippet, however, contains a couple of typical pitfalls: `yyin` is never defined or assigned in this fragment, and the local variable `yyg` remains unused, so a compiler would flag unused warnings or errors unless the surrounding context supplies additional code.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_leng@kcmListFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_leng@kcmListFile.body: It casts the scanner handle to a `ygyguts_t` pointer and returns the value stored in its `yyleng` field.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_lineno@kcmListFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_lineno@kcmListFi.body: Returns the scanner’s current line number, or zero when no active buffer is present.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_out@kcmListFileL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_out@kcmListFileL.body: The routine simply casts the opaque scanner token to its internal structure and returns the `yyout` member, which is the `FILE *` that the lexer writes its output to.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_text@kcmListFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyget_text@kcmListFile.body: The function casts the scanner handle to its internal `yyguts_t` structure and simply returns the `yytext` member (a pointer to the current token text).

@lcmListFileLexer_yylex@kcmListFileLexer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yylex@kcmListFileLexer.body: The function `cmListFileLexer_yylex` is the core scanning routine for the `cmListFile` lexer. It initializes the scanner state the first time, then repeatedly reads characters from the current input buffer. On each character it walks a deterministic automaton, updating the current state until a transition fails. Once a transition fails, the routine records the accept state and emits the corresponding token: new‑line, comment, bracket, identifier, string, space, or error tokens. It handles special cases such as end‑of‑buffer transitions and nested buffers, and it also rolls back to the last accept point when no rule matches. When EOF is reached it performs the final buffer‑switch handling and returns a NULL token.

@lcmListFileLexer_yylex_destroy@kcmListF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yylex_destroy@kcmListF.body: During cleanup the routine walks the internal buffer stack, deletes each buffer in turn, clears the stack pointer, then frees the heap‑allocated buffer and start‑stack arrays, re‑initialises global flags, and finally releases the scanner itself.

@lcmListFileLexer_yylex_init@kcmListFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yylex_init@kcmListFile.body: The routine takes a pointer to a global‐context structure, validates it, allocates a zero‑initialised `yyguts_t` instance, and finally hands off to `yy_init_globals` to complete the lexer setup. If allocation or the final init fails, the function reports an error.

@lcmListFileLexer_yylex_init_extra@kcmLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yylex_init_extra@kcmLi.body: The routine registers the supplied `yy_user_defined` type with the lexical engine, then verifies that the global‑pointer argument is non‑NULL. If the check passes it allocates a new `yyguts_t` structure, zero‑initialises it, re‑assigns the extra pointer to the freshly allocated block, and finally delegates to `yy_init_globals` to finish the global initialisation.

@lcmListFileLexer_yypop_buffer_state@kcm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yypop_buffer_state@kcm.body: The helper simply resets the lexer’s current buffer, popping it off the internal stack, and restores the previous buffer state so that the scanner can resume processing the next file or buffer after an EOF is reached.

@lcmListFileLexer_yypush_buffer_state@kc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yypush_buffer_state@kc.body: The routine saves the current buffer state onto an internal stack and then switches the scanner to the supplied buffer. It first checks that the new buffer is not NULL, pushes the previous buffer onto the stack if one exists, copies the current position and character data into the new buffer’s fields, and finally updates the active‑buffer pointer so the lexer starts reading from that buffer.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyrealloc@kcmListFileL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyrealloc@kcmListFileL.body: The routine accepts a generic pointer, the desired new size, and a scanner handle. It casts the scanner to its private `struct yyguts_t*` representation, but otherwise ignores it. Finally, it forwards the request to the standard `realloc` routine and returns whatever the underlying allocator yields.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyrestart@kcmListFileL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyrestart@kcmListFileL.body: The function re‑initialises the lexer state for a new input stream. It checks whether the current buffer exists; if not, it makes sure the buffer stack is ready, creates a new buffer for the supplied file, then attaches that buffer to the scanner and restores the scanner’s internal state from the buffer.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_column@kcmListFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_column@kcmListFi.body: Sets the column number used by the lexer to the supplied value after confirming an active input buffer exists; if no buffer is present, it aborts with a fatal error. The function simply updates the internal yycolumn field of the scanner state.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_debug@kcmListFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_debug@kcmListFil.body: The function assigns the supplied debug flag to the global flag used by the lexer and associates it with the scanner instance passed in. It casts the opaque scanner pointer to the internal `yyscanner` structure (`yyguts_t`) before updating the flag.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_extra@kcmListFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_extra@kcmListFil.body: The routine stores the supplied extra‐data pointer in the scanner’s context structure. It casts the opaque scanner handle to the internal `yyguts_t` structure and assigns `yyextra` to the passed `user_defined` value.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_in@kcmListFileLe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_in@kcmListFileLe.body: It stores the supplied `FILE*` into the lexer’s internal data structure—casting the opaque scanner pointer to its concrete `yyguts_t` type and writing the pointer into the global (or static) variable that the generated lexer functions reference for reading input.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_lineno@kcmListFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_lineno@kcmListFi.body: The function validates that an input buffer is present; if so, it assigns the supplied line number to the lexer’s internal line counter (`yylineno`). If no buffer is available, it aborts with a fatal error.

@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_out@kcmListFileL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileLexer_yyset_out@kcmListFileL.body: The routine assigns the supplied `FILE*` to the global `yyout` variable after extracting the internal context from the scanner handle.

@lcmListFileParser::AddArgument@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::AddArgument@k_ZN16cm.body: Adds a new argument token to the internal list, validates the separation rules (ensuring whitespace separates arguments), and reports any violation as an error or warning through the messenger. If a separation error occurs it returns false; otherwise it records the event and returns true.

@lcmListFileParser::CheckNesting@k_ZNK16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::CheckNesting@k_ZNK16.body: The routine walks the function list for a file, keeping a stack of the most recent “block‑type” encountered. Whenever it sees a closing token (e.g. `endif`, `endwhile`, `endforeach`…), it verifies that the corresponding opening token is on top of the stack; if it isn’t, the routine immediately returns the context of the offending function. When the loop ends, any remaining unmatched blocks are reported by returning the top of the stack. If the stack is empty, it returns a null option.

@lcmListFileParser::IssueError@k_ZNK16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::IssueError@k_ZNK16cm.body: The `IssueError` method records the file path and line number where the error occurred, enriches the current back‑trace with this information, logs the error via the messenger as a fatal message, and marks that a fatal error has happened in the system.

@lcmListFileParser::IssueFileOpenError@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::IssueFileOpenError@k.body: The function forwards the supplied text to the messenger as a fatal‑error message, attaching the current back‑trace. It uses the messenger to report the issue and relies on the stored back‑trace for context.

@lcmListFileParser::Parse@k_ZN16cmListFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::Parse@k_ZN16cmListFi.body: The routine walks through the token stream, treating spaces, newlines, and comment brackets as separators. When it sees an identifier after a newline it parses a function header, pushes the constructed function into the list, and reports any token‑type mismatch as an error. Finally it verifies that all flow‑control blocks are properly nested before returning success.

@lcmListFileParser::ParseFile@k_ZN16cmLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::ParseFile@k_ZN16cmLi.body: The function assigns the supplied file name, expands it to a Windows‑compatible path on 32‑bit builds, attempts to open the file via the lexer while validating the BOM, and if any check fails reports an error and aborts; otherwise it hands off control to the internal Parse routine which processes the file contents.

@lcmListFileParser::ParseFunction@k_ZN16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::ParseFunction@k_ZN16.body: Parses the lexer stream after a function name, collecting arguments inside matching parentheses, supporting nested parentheses, quoted, and bracketed arguments, and flagging any separation issues; errors are reported and false returned if the invocation is malformed.

@lcmListFileParser::ParseString@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::ParseString@k_ZN16cm.body: Stores the supplied file name, feeds the string into the lexer, and if that succeeds calls the internal parsing routine, returning its boolean result (otherwise reporting a buffer‑allocation error).

@lcmListFileParser::cmListFileParser@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::cmListFileParser@k_Z.body: The constructor wires together the parser with its data sources: it forwards the supplied `cmListFile` to the `ListFile` base class, stores a moved‑in back‑trace object, keeps a messenger reference, and creates a lexer instance by calling `cmListFileLexer_New()`.

@lcmListFileParser::cmListFileParser@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::cmListFileParser@k_Z.body: The `cmListFileParser` function reads a text file containing a comma‑separated list of items, tokenizes each line, and fills a container with the extracted strings. It validates line format, skips blank or comment lines, and throws an exception if any line fails the expected pattern.

@lcmListFileParser::operator=@k_ZN16cmLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::operator=@k_ZN16cmLi.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents any form of copy‑assignment. It guarantees that a `cmListFileParser` instance can only be constructed or moved, never reassigned to another instance after construction.

@lcmListFileParser::~cmListFileParser@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileParser::~cmListFileParser@k_.body: The destructor releases the lexer instance owned by the parser, calling `cmListFileLexer_Delete(this->Lexer)` to clean up the lexical resources.

@lcmLoadCacheCommand@k_Z18cmLoadCacheCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLoadCacheCommand@k_Z18cmLoadCacheCom.body: The function parses the arguments for a `load_cache` command, first handling a special `READ_WITH_PREFIX` case, then enforcing that only that form may be used in script‑mode. It builds exclusion and inclusion sets based on the `EXCLUDE`/`INCLUDE_INTERNALS` markers found in the argument list, and finally iterates over each directory argument calling `LoadCache` on the current makefile instance.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::ComputeObjectF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::ComputeObjectF.body: Iterates over the supplied map of source files, calling GetObjectFileNameWithoutTarget for each entry to compute the corresponding object‑file name (respecting any custom extension) and stores the result back into the map.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetConfigNames.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetConfigNames.body: The function `GetConfigNames` simply returns a constant reference to the internal `ConfigNames` vector. Because it is declared `const`, it promises not to modify the object’s state and guarantees that callers receive a read‑only view of the stored names. This preserves encapsulation while avoiding an unnecessary copy of potentially large data.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetTargetFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetTargetFortr.body: The routine builds a string of command‑line options to pass to a Fortran compiler. It adds the flag that turns on module‑output, optionally sets the directory that will receive the compiled modules, and, if a separate module‑path flag is defined, it emits the same directory in the include search path. The resulting flag string is returned.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetWorkingDire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetWorkingDire.body: This member simply returns the current binary directory stored in the snapshot: it calls `GetDirectory()` on `StateSnapshot`, then `GetCurrentBinary()` on that result, and returns the string reference.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::cmLocalCommonG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::cmLocalCommonG.body: Creates an instance of cmLocalCommonGenerator by first invoking the base‑class constructor with the supplied `cmGlobalGenerator` and `cmMakefile`. It then populates its internal list of configuration names with the set of names returned by the makefile’s `GetGeneratorConfigs` call (passing the flag that allows empty configurations). The constructor therefore establishes the generator’s configuration catalogue from the provided makefile.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::cmLocalCommonG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::cmLocalCommonG.body: The copy‑constructor initializes a new instance by duplicating every internal member of an existing `cmLocalCommonGenerator` object—including the base‑class state in `cmLocalGenerator`—so that the new instance behaves as an exact replica of the source, preserving configuration flags, data sources, and any runtime state that the generator maintains.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.body: Copies the internal data of a source `cmLocalCommonGenerator` into the current instance, performing any base‑class copying and guarding against self‑assignment before returning a reference to the assigned object.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::~cmLocalCommon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::~cmLocalCommon.body: The destructor is virtual and defaulted, meaning no explicit cleanup code is provided. It allows derived classes to override if they need custom de‑allocation while still ensuring the base class resources are released automatically. The compiler synthesizes the body, so when an instance of `cmLocalCommonGenerator` (or any subclass) goes out of scope, its destructor will be invoked automatically, freeing any owned resources in a safe and predictable way.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddArchitectureFlags.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddArchitectureFlags.body: Adds Apple‑specific architecture flags to a compiler options string when compiling for Apple targets. It queries the target for supported architectures given the current language and config, optionally filters them, and appends “‑arch <arch>” entries. It also merges optional sysroot and deployment‑target flags by pulling definitions from the makefile, handling placeholder replacements and per‑arch sysroot variations, thus building the final flag string that the compiler will consume.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCMP0018Flags@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCMP0018Flags@k_ZN.body:
The method appends the appropriate compiler flags for a CMP0018 target.  
It first determines whether the target is a shared‑ or module‑library; this flag influences whether the “old” flag set should be used.  
If the legacy flag‑set is chosen, it delegates to `AddSharedFlags` to add the common flags for that language.  
Otherwise, it checks whether the target’s configuration enables position‑independent code; if so, `AddPositionIndependentFlags` is invoked.  
Finally, for shared targets it appends the `"DLL"` feature option via `AppendFeatureOptions`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddColorDiagnosticsF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddColorDiagnosticsF.body: It fetches whether colored diagnostics are enabled for the current language, builds the appropriate CMake option name, and appends those options to the supplied flag string. If diagnostics are disabled or unset, no flags are added.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCompileOptions@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCompileOptions@k_.body: The function gathers a list of compiler‑flags from the target, language, and configuration data. It first creates a temporary vector, delegates to a second overload that fills that vector, and then appends the resulting flags to the supplied string. This pattern keeps the public interface simple while delegating the heavy‑lifting logic to a helper that returns a vector of flags ready to be merged.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCompileOptions@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCompileOptions@k_.body: The function collects compile‑time flags for a target by inspecting its `COMPILE_FLAGS` and `COMPILE_OPTIONS` properties, then conditionally appends any language‑specific or standard‑specific modifiers (e.g. `/JMC`, warning‑as‑error flags). It normalises any already‑escaped flag strings, escapes new options, and finally pushes the resulting option strings into the supplied `flags` vector.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddConfigVariableFla.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddConfigVariableFla.body: The routine fetches two flag definitions from the makefile and appends them to the supplied flag string. First it pulls the general variable definition, then, if a config name is supplied, it constructs a config‑specific identifier (variable\_config in uppercase) and appends that definition as well.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCustomCommandToOu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCustomCommandToOu.body: The method verifies the command has at least one output, attaches the current back‑trace to the command, and forwards it to an internal helper that actually registers the command under the generator origin. If the command lacks outputs, it reports an error and returns `nullptr`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCustomCommandToTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddCustomCommandToTa.body: The routine looks up a target by name, aborting with a null pointer if the lookup fails. It then stamps the new custom command with the current back‑trace level and forwards the call to a helper that wires the command into the target’s command list. Finally it returns the target object that now owns the added command.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddGeneratorSpecific.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddGeneratorSpecific.body: The function acts as an extension point where derived classes can override it to inject generator‑specific installation logic into the install‑time pipeline, typically using the supplied `ostream` for logging or configuration output.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddGeneratorTarget@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddGeneratorTarget@k.body: The routine stores a new generator‑target instance in the local generator’s collection, adds an entry in the local name‑lookup map for fast retrieval, and propagates the target into the global index.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddHelperCommands@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddHelperCommands@k_.body: The AddHelperCommands method is called during a class’s initialization to enqueue a set of helper commands—typically custom callbacks or shortcuts—into the object’s internal command registry, ensuring those commands become available to consumers of the class.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddISPCDependencies@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddISPCDependencies@.body:
The routine first verifies that the “ISPC” language is enabled for the current generator; if it isn’t it exits early.  
When enabled, it fetches the header‑suffix property, computes the suffixes for the current architecture, and determines whether extra auxiliary objects are required.  
For every generator configuration it resolves the object and header directories, collects the source files belonging to that configuration, and for each ISPC‑source file it derives the corresponding output object name. It then removes the file extensions to build a header file path, registers that header with the target, and if extra objects are needed, it generates and adds those objects to the target’s dependency list.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddImportedGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddImportedGenerator.body: Adds a new generator target to the internal map of imported targets and then registers it with the global generator so it can be looked‑up‑by name. The method simply inserts the target into the map keyed by its name and forwards it to the global indexer.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddLanguageFlags@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddLanguageFlags@k_Z.body: Adds a collection of language‑specific compiler options to a flag string: it pulls the appropriate CMAKE_<lang>_FLAGS values for the given target and configuration, appends any language‑standard switch when needed, and then applies compiler‑specific tweaks (Swift version switches, CUDA/HIP arch flags, RC fallback handling, Clang overlay, MSVC/Watcom runtime‑library choices, and MSVC debug‑info format).

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddLanguageFlagsForL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddLanguageFlagsForL.body: The routine enriches the flag string for a link step by invoking `AddLanguageFlags` with the link step and, when IPO is enabled for the given language and configuration, appending the IPO flag via `AppendFeatureOptions`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddOwnedImportedGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddOwnedImportedGene.body: The routine simply records a newly created target object by moving its `std::unique_ptr` into the `OwnedImportedGeneratorTargets` container, thereby transferring ownership so that the `cmLocalGenerator` instance will eventually own and be responsible for that target’s lifetime.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddPchDependencies@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddPchDependencies@k.body: The function walks through each build configuration for a target, gathers the source files that need pre‑compiled headers, and for each language that has a PCH it creates or re‑uses the corresponding PCH source. It sets appropriate scan‑and‑link flags, attaches the PCH file to the target as a dependency, and handles multi‑architecture and reuse scenarios so that the resulting build will use the proper pre‑compiled headers without re‑compilation.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddPositionIndepende.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddPositionIndepende.body:
The routine probes the *Makefile* for the appropriate compiler‑flags string for the requested language.  
If the target type indicates an executable, it first tries the “…_PIE” definition; if that yields nothing it falls back to “…_PIC”.  
When a non‑empty string is retrieved, the function splits that string into individual flag tokens and appends each to the supplied *flags* buffer after escaping any special characters. The net effect is that *flags* ends up containing the position‑independent compiler options that should be applied when building the target.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddSharedFlags@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddSharedFlags@k_ZN1.body: The function checks if a shared‑library build is requested (`shared` true). If so, it retrieves the language‑specific shared‑flag string from the Makefile via `GetSafeDefinition("CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_\<lang>_FLAGS")` and appends that string to the existing flag list via `AppendFlags`. The local `flagsVar` variable is unused.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddSourceOutputs@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddSourceOutputs@k_Z.body: The routine loops through each declared output string. For those that contain no generator expression it simply records the mapping between that output file and the source file in the internal bookkeeping. When an output contains a generator expression it invokes a helper that expands the expression into concrete file names (potentially for multiple configurations) and registers each of those expanded names in the same mapping. This keeps the internal state in sync with the set of generated files for the source.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddTargetByproducts@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddTargetByproducts@.body: The routine walks through the supplied by‑product list. For each entry it first determines whether the string contains a generator expression; if not, it registers the by‑product against the target via `UpdateOutputToSourceMap`. When a generator expression is detected it expands the generated‑output paths (via `ExpandCustomCommandOutputGenex`) and registers each resulting output path in the same map. This keeps the by‑product mapping current for every configuration.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddUnityBuild@k_ZN16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddUnityBuild@k_ZN16.body: If the target is marked for unity build, the routine scans each configuration’s source list, omitting files that cannot participate (e.g., C++ files requiring module scanning or marked to skip). It then filters those eligible sources per language, builds either a batched or grouped set of unity source files according to the mode property, and finally attaches the generated unity sources to the target, flagging them to skip further unity processing and recording their source path and any configuration‑specific definitions.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddUnityFilesModeAut.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddUnityFilesModeAut.body: The routine partitions a list of sources into batches and writes each batch to a single “unity” file. It accepts a target generator, language flag, configuration list, and a set of filtered sources, plus text to prepend/append around each file. The routine iterates over the source list in chunks of `batchSize` (defaulting to the whole list if zero) and produces a file name derived from `filename_base` with an index suffix. For each batch it calls `WriteUnitySource` with the current slice of sources and the before/after fragments, collecting the resulting `UnitySource` objects into a vector that is returned.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddUnityFilesModeGro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddUnityFilesModeGro.body: Groups UnityBatchedSource objects by their UNITY_GROUP property, creates a Unity source file for each group using the provided base filename and language suffix, and returns the list of UnitySource objects.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddUtilityCommand@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddUtilityCommand@k_.body: Creates a new utility target in the current makefile, records it as generator‑provided, and, if the supplied command contains any lines or dependencies, attaches that command to the target via `detail::AddUtilityCommand`. The function returns the constructed target object.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddVisibilityPresetF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddVisibilityPresetF.body: The function examines the language string; if it’s empty it exits immediately. It then checks whether the target is a shared or module library or has exported executables, and if the CMP0063 policy is not OLD or WARN it may apply a warning flag. Based on the policy status it may set a warning string. It calls helper routines to add the appropriate compiler options for the language and for inline visibility handling. Finally, if a warning string was generated and this is a new warning for the target, it emits a warning message about the visibility settings that CMake is not applying.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AddXCConfigSources@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AddXCConfigSources@k.body: The `AddXCConfigSources` virtual method is a hook that derived classes implement to register the appropriate XC configuration sources onto the supplied `cmGeneratorTarget`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AllAppleArchSysroots.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AllAppleArchSysroots.body: The `operator()` method accepts a constant string reference and returns a boolean flag that indicates whether a particular condition (e.g., a validation or a comparison) is satisfied.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AllAppleArchSysroots.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AllAppleArchSysroots.body: Returns `true` when the architecture’s system‑root is either disabled (via `cmIsOff`) or matches the supplied `sysroot` pointer.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AllAppleArchSysroots.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AllAppleArchSysroots.body: The function iterates over every architecture string in the supplied vector and verifies that each one’s system‑root entry in the internal `AppleArchSysroots` map either equals the supplied `sysroot` value or is marked “off”. If any map entry differs, the function immediately returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendCompileOptions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendCompileOptions.body: The method reads a comma‑separated string of options, splits it into individual values, and appends those values to an existing options string. It returns early if the input list is empty, otherwise it constructs a helper list and delegates the actual appending to a private overload that receives the expanded list and an optional regex filter.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendCompileOptions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendCompileOptions.body: The function builds a string of compiler flags. When a regex is supplied it filters the vector of options for matches; each match is escaped and appended to the options string via `AppendFlagEscape`. If no regex is given, it simply appends every flag in the vector. The logic uses `cmsys::RegularExpression` for matching and keeps the operation const‑safe.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendCompileOptions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendCompileOptions.body:
The function appends each flag from the supplied vector into the `options` vector.  
If a regex is supplied it filters the flags against that expression using `RegularExpression::find`; otherwise all flags are added.  
During the append it escapes the flag value via `AppendFlagEscape` before moving it into the destination vector.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendDefines@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendDefines@k_ZNK1.body: The method receives a set of definitions and a string containing a comma‑separated list. If the list is non‑empty it expands that list into individual definition strings (via cmExpandListWithBacktrace) and then recursively invokes AppendDefines to merge those new definitions into the supplied set.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendDefines@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendDefines@k_ZNK1.body:
The routine walks through the supplied vector of definitions.  
For each entry it first verifies the definition via `CheckDefinition`; if the check fails the definition is ignored.  
Valid definitions are then trimmed of an optional “-D” literal prefix (if present) and inserted into the output set, otherwise they’re inserted unchanged.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendDependencyInfo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendDependencyInfo.body: The function checks whether the current generator supports linker‑dependency files and whether the target has one; if both are true it resolves the flag template, expands any placeholders into the actual dependency file path, resolves the wrapped linker flags for the target’s link language, and finally appends those flags into the provided flag list.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFeatureOptions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFeatureOptions.body: The function looks up a list of compiler‑options for the requested language/feature pair in the Makefile and, if such options exist, appends each one to the supplied flag string (escaping them as needed).

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFlagEscape@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFlagEscape@k_Z.body: The function appends a flag to a string of flags. It takes the raw flag, escapes it for shell usage via `EscapeForShell`, and forwards the resulting escaped string to `AppendFlags`. The call to `IsNinjaMulti()` determines whether multi‑mode handling is applied during the escape.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFlags@k_ZNK16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFlags@k_ZNK16c.body: Appends `newFlags` to the existing string `flags`, inserting a single space between them only when `flags` already contains text, and only if `newFlags` is non‑empty and not composed solely of whitespace.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFlags@k_ZNK16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFlags@k_ZNK16c.body: The routine walks through the supplied vector of flag values and, for each element, delegates to a second‑level AppendFlags to merge that individual flag string into the accumulating `flags` string. The work is simply a one‑by‑one concatenation loop that forwards each flag’s value to the underlying helper responsible for actually appending the flag text.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendIPOLinkerFlags.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendIPOLinkerFlags.body: The function first verifies that IPO is enabled for the given language and configuration; if not, it exits early. It then confirms the target type is one of the executable, shared library, or module library variants; other types abort. Afterward, it retrieves the macro‑defined list of IPO flags via the Makefile, and appends each entry to the passed flag string after escaping.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendIncludeDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendIncludeDirecto.body: The function takes a vector of strings and a string containing a comma‑separated list of include paths. It first checks whether the list string is empty; if it is, it exits immediately. Otherwise it parses the string into a list object (`cmList`) and delegates the actual work to another overload of `AppendIncludeDirectories`, passing that list along with the source file information.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendIncludeDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendIncludeDirecto.body: The routine walks through the supplied vector of include paths. For each path it checks that it is an absolute path; if it isn’t, it emits a fatal error and exits. Otherwise, the path is normalised to a Unix‑style slash format, then inserted into the output vector only if it hasn’t already appeared before. This guarantees that the final include list contains only distinct, canonicalised directories.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendLWYUFlags@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendLWYUFlags@k_ZN.body: Determines whether a target wants the LWYU flag. It queries the target’s properties, pulls the matching flag definition from the makefile if present, and if that flag is non‑empty, appends it to the current flags via `AppendFlags`. The function returns whether the flag was applied.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendModuleDefiniti.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendModuleDefiniti.body: The function checks whether the target has a module definition file for the supplied config; if present, it resolves the flag that controls the linker to read that file (via `CMAKE_LINK_DEF_FILE_FLAG`), converts the file path into a link‑reference format using `linkLineComputer` and the output converter, then appends the resulting flag string to the `flags` buffer. If any lookup fails, the function exits without altering the flag string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendPositionIndepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendPositionIndepe.body: The function gathers the compile‑time PIC options for a target that is an executable, checks that the chosen language and PIC support are enabled in the makefile, and appends those flags to the `flags` string, escaping each flag as needed.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CheckDefinition@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CheckDefinition@k_ZN.body:
The function inspects a macro‑definition string to see if it uses “function‑style” syntax or contains a ‘#’ character, both of which most compilers cannot pass on a command line.  
If either pattern is detected it logs a warning, suggests moving the macro to a header file, and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ClearDependencies@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ClearDependencies@k_.body: Clears the dependency structures stored in the supplied `cmMakefile` instance—resetting any internal tables, lists or maps that track required files or targets, and optionally prints diagnostic output when the `verbose` flag is true.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeHomeRelativeO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeHomeRelativeO.body: This method resolves a destination file path relative to the current user’s home directory. It accepts a target file name, normalises any path components, guards against directory‑traversal escapes, and produces a canonical relative path string that callers can safely use for file generation or output placement.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeObjectFilenam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeObjectFilenam.body: The routine walks the supplied map of source‑file pointers and produces the object‑file name that should be emitted for each source. It builds that name by applying the target’s naming conventions (output directory, extension, and any target‑specific suffix), and stores the result back into the map for later use during linking.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeObjectMaxPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeObjectMaxPath.body:
The routine determines the maximum permissible length for an object file path.  
On Windows it hard‑codes 250; on other systems it defaults to 1000.  
If the build defines the variable `CMAKE_OBJECT_PATH_MAX`, the routine attempts to parse that value. If parsing succeeds and the value is at least 128, that value replaces the default; otherwise the value is ignored and a warning is issued.  
Finally it clears the list of any previously recorded violations.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeTargetCompile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeTargetCompile.body: Collects the set of configuration names, determines which language pairs are enabled in the current Makefile, and then iterates over every target in the generator. For each target, it computes the compile features for every configuration name; if any of those steps fails, the function returns false. If the target can compile sources, it runs the additional compile‑feature computation that takes into account the inferred enabled languages. When all targets have been processed successfully, the function returns true.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeTargetManifes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeTargetManifes.body: The routine gathers the available configuration names, then iterates over each target that belongs to the build system. For every such target, it calls that target’s ComputeTargetManifest for every configuration name. This populates the manifest with the target’s details for each configuration.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ConstructComment@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ConstructComment@k_Z.body:
The function first checks if the supplied command already carries a comment via `GetComment`.  
If that optional value is present, it returns it immediately.  
Otherwise, if the command has output file names, it builds a comment string by concatenating the relative path of each output, prefixed by “Generating ”, separating them with commas.  
If neither case applies, it simply returns the supplied `default_comment`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ConvertToIncludeRefe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ConvertToIncludeRefe.body: This method forwards the supplied file path and output format to `ConvertToOutputForExisting`, returning whatever string that helper produces.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CopyPchCompilePdb::[.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CopyPchCompilePdb::[.body: The function transforms a supplied `cm::string_view` into an owning `std::string`, usually by copying or composing it for downstream use.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CopyPchCompilePdb::[.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CopyPchCompilePdb::[.body: The lambda builds a string: if the global generator is in multi‑config mode it prefixes the passed expression with a `$<CONFIG:…>` tag; otherwise it simply returns the expression verbatim.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CopyPchCompilePdb@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CopyPchCompilePdb@k_.body: The routine writes a CMake‑generated script that loops over the supplied extensions, verifies that a compiled PDB file from a “reuse‑from” target exists and is newer than the destination, then copies it (retrying up to 30 times if necessary). It then creates a custom command that runs this script, adds the new file as a by‑product (for VS) or output (for other tools), and records the resulting file path in the target’s properties.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateEvaluationFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateEvaluationFile.body: Iterates through every evaluation file attached to the current generator and tells each file to produce its output using the supplied configuration string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateEvaluationFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateEvaluationFile.body: The routine pulls the current generator’s configuration list and then iterates over each config string, invoking the overload that accepts a single string. This produces a separate output file for every configuration entry.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateRulePlaceholde.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateRulePlaceholde.body: The method builds and returns a new `cmRulePlaceholderExpander` instance, passing the current generator’s compiler list, variable‑mapping table, and the system‑roots for compiler and linker into its constructor.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateSafeUniqueObje.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateSafeUniqueObje.body: Creates a new file name by normalising a supplied string: it removes leading slashes, replaces colons, spaces and “../” with safe characters, optionally prefixes a “_p” mangling string if the build flag is set, and appends an incrementing suffix until no other entry in its map uses the same value. If the resulting name would produce a path longer than the configured limit, it logs a warning once. The unique name is stored in an internal map and the mapped value is returned.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateUtilityOutput@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateUtilityOutput@.body: The function builds a path string by combining the current binary directory with a “/CMakeFiles/” suffix and the target name, then looks up or creates a source file entry for that path. If the entry exists it marks the file as symbolic (setting the “SYMBOLIC” property), otherwise it logs an error. Finally, it returns the constructed path string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ExpandCustomCommandO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ExpandCustomCommandO.body: The function collects and deduplicates paths produced by custom commands. It parses the command output string into a generator expression, then iterates over all generator configurations, expanding each command’s output paths into a list of strings. After gathering all of them it removes duplicates via `cmRemoveDuplicates` before returning the cleaned list.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ExpandCustomCommandO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ExpandCustomCommandO.body: The method takes a compiled generator expression and a configuration string, evaluates the expression to produce a list of output paths, normalizes each path relative to the current binary directory using `CollapseFullPath`, and finally returns that list.

@lcmLocalGenerator::FindGeneratorTargetT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::FindGeneratorTargetT.body: Finds a generator target with the given name. It first looks in `ImportedGeneratorTargets`; if not found it checks an alias map (`AliasTargets`) to resolve a name that refers to another target, and then again looks up that target in the imported map. If still not found it tries to locate a local non‑alias target. When nothing matches it delegates the lookup to the global generator. This helper therefore resolves local, aliased and imported targets in that order before falling back to a global lookup.

@lcmLocalGenerator::FindLocalNonAliasGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::FindLocalNonAliasGen.body: If the requested name exists in the generator’s internal lookup table, the function returns the corresponding target pointer; otherwise it returns a null pointer.

@lcmLocalGenerator::Generate@k_ZN16cmLoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::Generate@k_ZN16cmLoc.body: The `Generate` member is a virtual hook that derived classes can override. Its body is empty, so the base implementation performs no action.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateAppleInfoPLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateAppleInfoPLi.body:
The function locates the template file that describes a macOS X bundle’s `Info.plist`.  
If the template path isn’t absolute, it resolves it via the module‑file lookup.  
When the file is missing, it emits an error and aborts the operation.  

Inside a temporary makefile scope it injects the target’s metadata—such as executable name, icon, identifiers, version strings, bundle name, and copyright—into predefined variable definitions.  
Finally, it runs the configuration pass that substitutes those variables into the template, producing the final plist for the target.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateFrameworkInf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateFrameworkInf.body: The routine locates the framework‑info plist template (falling back to a default when none is supplied), verifies that file can be accessed, and if missing emits a clear error. It then injects the target’s properties into the makefile’s variable scope—overriding any pre‑existing values—so that the configuration file is rendered with the correct framework name, icon, identifier, version strings and bundle version. Once the variables are set, it invokes the makefile engine to copy the rendered output to the supplied file name.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateInstallRules.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateInstallRules.body: The function computes the installation prefix from environment or project definitions, emits a CMake script that sets up install‑specific variables, emits rules for each install generator (including sub‑directory handling), and finally records a manifest file listing the installed files.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateTargetInstal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateTargetInstal.body: The function walks over each generator target, skipping interface libraries. For each remaining target it writes any pre‑install script, emits the appropriate install command for the target type (executables, static/module libs, and shared libs with special Windows handling), and finally writes any post‑install script.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateTestFiles@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GenerateTestFiles@k_.body: The routine first aborts if testing is disabled via the CMAKE_TESTING_ENABLED flag. It then builds the path for the generated test file, creates a writer stream, and emits a header block that records the source and build directories. It writes any test‑specific spec file, include files, and the test generators’ own code blocks. Finally, it lists the sub‑directories and any directory‑label properties that should be applied to the generated test configuration.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetBackwardsCompatib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetBackwardsCompatib.body: The routine lazily initializes the backward‑compatibility field on first use. It reads a string definition from the project’s makefile, parses the three‑component version number, and stores the encoded result in `BackwardsCompatibility`. Subsequent calls simply return the cached value.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetBinaryDirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetBinaryDirectory@k.body: This method forwards a request to the internal CMake instance and hands back the string that represents the path of the binary output directory.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCMakeInstance@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCMakeInstance@k_Z.body: The `GetCMakeInstance` method on `cmLocalGenerator` simply forwards the request to its `GlobalGenerator` and returns the pointer it provides. In effect, it gives callers access to the globally‑shared “CMake” instance that the local generator relies on.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCurrentBinaryDire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCurrentBinaryDire.body: It forwards the request to the stored snapshot: it returns a reference to the string that represents the current binary‑directory path stored in `StateSnapshot`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCurrentSourceDire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCurrentSourceDire.body: Returns a const reference to the string that represents the current source path held inside the generator’s state snapshot. The method simply forwards that reference by calling `GetDirectory().GetCurrentSource()` on the snapshot object. No copying or mutation occurs; the caller receives the directory string directly.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetDeviceLinkFlags@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetDeviceLinkFlags@k.body: The routine configures device‑linking flags for a target: it checks whether IPO is required for the target’s language, appends the corresponding flag, then gathers the libraries that must be linked (including framework paths) via the link‑line computer. After that it injects visibility flags and encodes them, finally collecting any compile‑options that need to be passed to the link script before returning the assembled flag string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetFeature@k_ZN16cmL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetFeature@k_ZN16cmL.body: The `GetFeature` routine builds a feature key by appending an upper‑cased suffix from `config` (if provided), then walks up through the snapshot chain of directories until it finds a property matching that key and returns it; if no match is found it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetFrameworkFlags@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetFrameworkFlags@k_.body: The function assembles the compiler‑search flags that enable the linker to locate system‑frameworks on an Apple build. It first checks that the target is an Apple host; if not, it returns an empty string. It then fetches two definitions from the makefile—one for normal framework searching and one for system‑framework searching. If both are unset, no flags are needed. It collects the include paths (both from the target and the local generator) and identifies those that actually point to framework directories. Each unique framework directory found is added to a set of emitted directories. For each framework path recorded in the target’s link information, it appends the appropriate flag (system‑search or normal‑search) followed by the path itself in shell‑escaped form, ensuring duplicates are skipped. The resulting string of flags is then returned.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGeneratorTargets@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGeneratorTargets@.body: Returns a const reference to the internal vector of generator targets.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGlobalGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGlobalGenerator@k.body: A subtle point is that `GetGlobalGenerator()` simply returns the `GlobalGenerator` member of the current object. In multithreaded contexts, callers must assume that the returned pointer is still valid—i.e., the underlying object hasn’t been destroyed or moved. Also consider that the pointer is returned by value, so the caller must not modify the pointed‑to object unless it is explicitly designed for mutation. The method itself imposes no copying or allocation overhead, but callers should guard against dereferencing a `nullptr` if the object wasn’t properly constructed.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGlobalGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGlobalGenerator@k.body: The method simply returns a pointer to the `GlobalGenerator` member held by the object. Because it is declared `const`, the function guarantees that no member data will be altered during the call. The returned pointer can be `nullptr` if the internal member hasn’t been initialized, so callers should guard against that. No side‑effects occur, and no additional state is changed.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body: The method simply forwards its parameters (`target`, `lang`, and `config`) to the internal helper `GetIncludeDirectoriesImplicit` and returns whatever that helper returns—a vector of `BT<std::string>` values representing the include‑path set for the requested target and language.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body: The function simply delegates to `GetIncludeDirectoriesImplicit`, passing along the supplied vector, target, language, and configuration string so that the implicit implementation populates the include‑directory list.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body:
