The lambda captures references to `result` (a vector) and `emitted` (a set).  
When called with a directory name, it inserts the name into `emitted`; if that insertion succeeds (meaning the name was not already present), it appends the name to `result`. Thus it adds each directory only once, preserving uniqueness.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body:
`emitBT` captures `result` and `emitted`.  
When called with a `BT<std::string>`, it inserts the string value into `emitted`; if that value was not already present, the `BT` is added to `result`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body: It examines a string argument and returns true if that string ends with the literal suffix \"/usr/include".

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body: The public member `operator()` is a const member that returns a Boolean value and takes a single `const std::string&` argument. It is typically invoked to perform a Boolean test or comparison based on the supplied string, and is referenced in several places throughout the code.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body: This lambda checks whether a directory should be treated as a system include path. It first resolves the real path of the supplied directory. It then returns **true** when the directory is *not* in the `implicitSet` or `implicitExclude` collections, *or* when the global flag `isCorCxx` is set and the directory appears in the `resolvedEnvCPATH`. This logic lets the calling code decide whether to skip, reorder, or treat a directory as an implicit search location.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body: It builds a deduplicated list of include directories for a target: it collects user‑specified paths, merges compiler‑provided implicit paths (filtered by language and explicit exclusions), and appends system standard include paths. Dirs are emitted only once, in an order that respects project‑requested priority and language‑specific rules.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body: The function calls the internal helper that returns a vector of include‑path strings for the specified target, language, and build‑config, then appends those strings to the supplied vector, reserving space in advance to avoid reallocations.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeFlags@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeFlags@k_ZN.body: The function builds a string of compiler include‑flags from a list of directories. It consults the current language and project settings to decide whether to quote paths, whether to use the system flag, and whether to prepend framework‑search flags. In the loop it emits each directory once, optionally repeating the system flag per entry, and finally removes trailing separators before returning the trimmed flag string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIndividualFileTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIndividualFileTar.body: The function scans an environment (e.g., a build system or project directory) and, for each file that matches a specific target pattern, pushes its path into the supplied vector reference. It effectively enumerates the individual file‑level targets that downstream processing (for example, an incremental build or dependency resolution) can act upon.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetLinkDependencyFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetLinkDependencyFil.body: The function simply returns the hard‑coded file name `"link.d"`. It ignores its parameters – the `target` and `config` arguments are unused – and provides the name of the file that will hold dependency information for linking.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetLinkLibsCMP0065@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetLinkLibsCMP0065@k.body: GetLinkLibsCMP0065 evaluates whether a given target is an executable that should be linked with shared libraries. It examines the policy state for CMP0065 (WARN, OLD, NEW, etc.) together with the target’s ENABLE_EXPORTS property. If the policy dictates that shared‑library flags should be added, it pulls the flag definition from the makefile under the key “CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_LINK_<language>_FLAGS”. If none of the conditions apply, it returns an empty string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetMSVCDebugFormatNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetMSVCDebugFormatNa.body: The function retrieves the MSVC debug format string for a given target: it first reads the default value, then checks whether the target supplies an override; if an override exists, that value is evaluated as an expression and returned (or left empty if evaluation fails).

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetMakefile@k_ZNK16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetMakefile@k_ZNK16c.body: Returns a pointer to the internal Makefile instance (without modifying it).

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetObjectFileNameWit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetObjectFileNameWit.body: The function builds an object‑file path for a source file. It first picks a relative path to the source (or to the binary tree), picks the shorter of the two, then removes a leading “CMakeFiles/.../” prefix when the source is a unity or pre‑compiled‑header file. It strips or replaces the source extension with the language‑specific object extension unless the source file is marked to keep its extension. Finally, it normalises the resulting path to guarantee a unique, safe file name under the supplied max‑path directory.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetOwnedImportedGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetOwnedImportedGene.body: The method simply returns a const reference to the `OwnedImportedGeneratorTargets` member, allowing callers to read (not modify) the vector of owned imported generator targets.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZN.body: Retrieves and returns the status of a policy by forwarding the supplied policy ID to the underlying `Makefile` object’s `GetPolicyStatus` method, returning whatever status that call yields.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetProjectName@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetProjectName@k_ZNK.body: It simply returns the project name that is stored in the `StateSnapshot` object.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetRealDependency@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetRealDependency@k_.body: The function resolves a dependency name to an actual path. It first checks whether a target with that name exists; if so, it returns the target’s full path (or a target‑level dependency for object/interface libraries). If no such target exists, it treats the name as a file path, looking first in the source tree, then in the binary tree, collapsing relative paths as needed. If the file still cannot be found, it falls back to the current binary directory.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetRuleLauncher@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetRuleLauncher@k_ZN.body: The function obtains a property value (from its own Makefile or an optional target), evaluates that value as a generator expression using the current generator and the supplied config string, and returns the resulting string (or an empty string if the property was unset).

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetShouldUseOldFlags.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetShouldUseOldFlags.body:
The routine first retrieves the default flag string for the requested language.  
If the caller requests a shared library and the current flag variable differs from that default, the function consults the CMP0018 policy: if the policy is in its old‑behaviour mode it returns true; otherwise it falls back to the new behaviour and returns false.  If the flag variable hasn’t changed or the library isn’t shared, it simply returns false.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourceDirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourceDirectory@k.body: The `GetSourceDirectory` member simply forwards a request to the `CMake` instance associated with the current generator and returns the string returned by that instance’s `GetHomeDirectory()` call. In other words, it exposes the directory that the internal CMake instance considers the project’s “home” or source base. It does not perform any validation or transformation; it just retrieves and returns the stored string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourceFileLanguag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourceFileLanguag.body: This member simply forwards the language information held by a `cmSourceFile`. It accepts a `cmSourceFile` reference and returns the result of its `GetLanguage()` call—typically a string identifier such as `"C++"`, `"Python"`, or whatever language tag the source file uses.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourceFileWithOut.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourceFileWithOut.body: The routine returns a pointer to a source file that matches a requested output name. If the supplied path isn’t absolute, it falls back to a legacy linear search that can handle by‑product files. When the name is absolute it looks it up in the internal map; if a matching entry exists and the requested kind isn’t conflict with a by‑product restriction, the stored source is returned. If no match is found, the function returns `nullptr`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourcesWithOutput.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourcesWithOutput.body: The function retrieves the set of source files that produce a requested output file. If the output name isn’t a full path, it performs a linear lookup that returns the target source and the associated source file; otherwise it consults the cached mapping of output names to source sets and returns the stored result, or an empty set when no match is found.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetState@k_ZNK16cmLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetState@k_ZNK16cmLo.body: The `GetState` member simply forwards a request to the underlying global generator: it calls `GetCMakeInstance()` on the `GlobalGenerator` object and returns the state pointer that the returned instance provides. The function is const‑qualified and returns a `cmState*`. Its behavior is a thin wrapper—no state mutation, just dereferencing and delegating to the global generator’s state provider.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetStateSnapshot@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetStateSnapshot@k_Z.body: The function simply forwards a request to the `Makefile` member. It calls `GetStateSnapshot()` on that object and returns the resulting `cmStateSnapshot` value, effectively providing a snapshot of the current state.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetStaticLibraryFlag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetStaticLibraryFlag.body: The function builds a list of compile‑time flags used when linking a static library. It first pulls general static‑linker flags from the Makefile, optionally appends a configuration‑specific flag if one exists. It then collects any static‑library flags defined for the given target, again adding a configuration‑specific variant if defined. Finally it adds any additional options returned by `GetStaticLibraryLinkOptions` and returns the full vector of flags.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetStaticLibraryFlag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetStaticLibraryFlag.body: The routine gathers the static‑library flags for the current target (based on the supplied configuration and link language) and merges those flags into the string passed in `flags`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetCompileFlag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetCompileFlag.body: The function obtains a list of compile‑time options for a specific target by calling a lower‑level helper that returns a vector of strings, and then merges those options into the supplied output string by appending them.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetCompileFlag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetCompileFlag.body: The function assembles the compiler switches needed to build a target, pulling in language‑specific switches, target‑specific architecture options, and any extra flags (Fortran, IPCO, visibility, diagnostics) before finally appending the global define flags and framework flags. Once all pieces are collected it returns the flag vector for the caller.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDefines@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDefines@k_Z.body: The function collects the export‑macro definition for a target and merges it with the target’s own compile definitions, returning the combined set of defines.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDefines@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDefines@k_Z.body: The function asks the local generator to provide its set of defines for the given target, configuration and language. It obtains the result as a set of wrapped strings (`BT<std::string>`), then copies the contained string values into the supplied `defines` set.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDirectory@k.body: The `GetTargetDirectory` method in `cmLocalGenerator` simply reports that the operation is unsupported in the current generator context. When invoked, it triggers an error message indicating the call is inappropriate for a local generator and immediately returns an empty string, effectively signaling that no target directory can be provided.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetFlags@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetFlags@k_ZN1.body: It gathers the lists of library names, link flags and paths for a target by delegating to a helper overload, then concatenates each collected list into the corresponding output strings.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetFlags@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetFlags@k_ZN1.body: The function gathers all linker‑flags for a target. It first normalises the configuration name, obtains the target’s link information, and then branches on target type. For static libraries it calls GetStaticLibraryFlags; for shared modules it builds the shared‑library flag string (adding any config‑specific definitions, export flags, and linker‑options). For executables it similarly assembles the flag string, appending config‑specific settings, export flags, and any extra options. After the type‑specific flags are collected it appends position‑independent, dependency‑info, and module‑definition flags, encodes them for the makefile, and finally pushes the resulting flag string onto the output vector.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetFortranFlag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetFortranFlag.body: The function supplies a string containing the compiler‑specific “fortran” flags that a particular generator must provide—returning an empty string by default and allowing derived generators to override it.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetXcFrameworkFlags@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetXcFrameworkFlags@.body: The function assembles a string of include‑search flags for Apple‑specific frameworks by retrieving the corresponding flag definitions from the makefile and then iterating over each framework header path returned by the link information, prefixing each path with the system flag if the directory is a system include directory otherwise with the ordinary flag.

@lcmLocalGenerator::IsMinGWMake@k_ZNK16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::IsMinGWMake@k_ZNK16c.body: The `IsMinGWMake` method simply returns the value of the `UseMinGWMake` flag stored in the generator’s internal state. It is a `const` member that performs no mutation and relies solely on `GetState()` to obtain the result.

@lcmLocalGenerator::IsNMake@k_ZNK16cmLoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::IsNMake@k_ZNK16cmLoc.body: It returns the current UseNMake flag from the object’s state.

@lcmLocalGenerator::IsNinjaMulti@k_ZNK16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::IsNinjaMulti@k_ZNK16.body: Returns whether the current generator state indicates that “Ninja‑multi” should be used. It simply forwards the request to the state object: `GetState()` returns a pointer to a state instance that exposes a `UseNinjaMulti()` member, and the function returns that value.

@lcmLocalGenerator::IsRootMakefile@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::IsRootMakefile@k_ZNK.body: The function returns true when the current instance’s build‑system parent directory is missing/invalid—i.e., the object represents the top‑level makefile. It performs a single check on the internal snapshot state, returning the negated validity of the parent directory.

@lcmLocalGenerator::IsWatcomWMake@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::IsWatcomWMake@k_ZNK1.body: The `IsWatcomWMake` member simply reports whether the current local‑generation context has enabled the *WatcomWMake* feature. It reads the current `State` object via `GetState()` and returns the value of its `UseWatcomWMake()` flag. No additional logic is performed; the function merely forwards the stored flag.

@lcmLocalGenerator::IsWindowsShell@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::IsWindowsShell@k_ZNK.body: Returns a Boolean flag indicating whether the generator’s current state has chosen to use a Windows‑style shell – it simply forwards the query to `GetState()->UseWindowsShell()`.

@lcmLocalGenerator::IssueMessage@k_ZNK16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::IssueMessage@k_ZNK16.body: The method forwards a log‑style message of the supplied type and text to the underlying CMake instance, attaching the object’s DirectoryBacktrace for contextual tracing.

@lcmLocalGenerator::JoinDefines@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::JoinDefines@k_ZN16cm.body: The `JoinDefines` routine composes a single space‑delimited string of compiler‑define switches. It first determines the prefix to use (`-D` or a language‑specific flag from the makefile), then iterates over the supplied set of definition tokens. For each token it escapes special characters (`$`, `#`) when the Watcom compiler is active, otherwise it formats the token as either a flag only or a flag with an equals‑separated value (using `EscapeForShell` for quoting). Each processed token is appended to the output string with a leading space when necessary, resulting in a ready‑to‑use command‑line fragment.

@lcmLocalGenerator::LinearGetSourceFileW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::LinearGetSourceFileW.body: The method scans the project’s source files in order, looking for a custom command whose output list contains the requested filename. If such a match is found it returns that file and signals that it is not a by‑product; otherwise it falls back to by‑product outputs only when the caller requested that kind, returning the first matching by‑product file (or null).

@lcmLocalGenerator::LinearGetTargetWithO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::LinearGetTargetWithO.body: The function iterates through the repository’s ordered list of targets, inspecting each target’s pre‑build, pre‑link, and post‑build commands for an output that matches the supplied name. When a match is found it returns the corresponding target; if none match, it returns a null pointer.

@lcmLocalGenerator::MakeCustomCommandGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::MakeCustomCommandGen.body: Creates a single `cmCustomCommandGenerator` instance configured with the given `cmCustomCommand` and configuration string, stores it in a `std::vector`, and returns that vector.

@lcmLocalGenerator::NeedBackwardsCompati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::NeedBackwardsCompati.body: The function evaluates the current policy status (WARN, OLD, NEW, or required‑type) and then compares the runtime compatibility value against the encoded 2.4 threshold, returning true only when the current compatibility level meets or falls below that threshold; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmLocalGenerator::OutputLinkLibraries@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::OutputLinkLibraries@.body: The function creates two vectors of strings, delegates to another overload to populate them, and then appends the resulting values into the supplied output strings.

@lcmLocalGenerator::OutputLinkLibraries@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::OutputLinkLibraries@.body: The routine pulls the library‑path flag and terminator from the makefile for the current link language, fetches the language‑specific list of standard libraries, appends the framework search flag, and finally fills the supplied vectors with the computed link paths and libraries.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ProcessEvaluationFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ProcessEvaluationFil.body: The routine walks through the evaluation‑file list, invokes each file’s own generator, stops if a fatal error is flagged, then collates and sorts the file names it produced. It checks the new list against the already‑generated set to catch any overlap; if duplicates surface, it emits an error and aborts. Finally it appends the unique set of file names into the caller’s vector, keeping the list ordered and deduplicated.

@lcmLocalGenerator::SourceEntry::SourceE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::SourceEntry::SourceE.body: SourceEntry is the public entry point that initializes and registers a new source instance. It pulls in the necessary data structures, validates the incoming request, and hands off control to the underlying handler that actually stores the source metadata in the repository. The function orchestrates the transition from user‑supplied input to a fully‑formed source object, ensuring all required invariants are satisfied before it persists the entry.

@lcmLocalGenerator::TraceDependencies@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::TraceDependencies@k_.body: The method walks the generator’s internal collection of targets; for each target that reports itself as part of the current build system it forwards a single call to that target’s own tracing routine. No other state‑changes occur, and the function merely propagates the tracing activity downstream to every relevant target.

@lcmLocalGenerator::UnityBatchedSource::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::UnityBatchedSource::.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied `cmSourceFile*` to the base class `Source` via an initializer list. No additional initialization occurs – the body of the constructor is empty, so the object ends up holding whatever state the base class sets up from that pointer.

@lcmLocalGenerator::UnitySource::UnitySo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::UnitySource::UnitySo.body: UnitySource stores a file path and a flag indicating whether to use per‑configuration data.

@lcmLocalGenerator::UpdateDependencies@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::UpdateDependencies@k.body: The method accepts a target‑info string and two Boolean flags (verbose and color) and always returns `true`. It’s a virtual hook intended for subclasses to override in order to adjust dependency handling logic.

@lcmLocalGenerator::UpdateOutputToSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::UpdateOutputToSource.body: The routine keeps a map from output file names to the source that produced them, inserting a new entry only when one isn’t already present or when a new primary output should replace an existing by‑product mapping. When a fresh mapping is added it calls a helper to materialise the generated source. If an entry already exists it preserves the first producer unless the new information represents a higher‑priority primary output, in which case it updates the entry.

@lcmLocalGenerator::UpdateOutputToSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::UpdateOutputToSource.body: The routine registers an output’s origin. When the supplied key is absent, it creates a new entry, populates the target and emits a generated source entry. If the key already exists, it attaches the target only if that slot was empty; otherwise it flags that more than one command claimed the same output, potentially triggering a warning.

@lcmLocalGenerator::WriteUnitySource@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::WriteUnitySource@k_Z.body: It creates a Unity‑mode source file: the function opens a file stream, writes a standard header comment, then iterates over the supplied UnityBatchedSource items. For each item it may record a per‑configuration guard if the number of config strings differs from the supplied list, constructing a guard macro string (“defined(CMAKE_UNITY_CONFIG_…)”). It then registers the source file with the target, writes an include statement with optional before/after snippets and a unique ID marker, and finally returns a UnitySource object indicating the file name and whether per‑configuration processing was used.

@lcmLocalGenerator::WriteUnitySourceIncl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::WriteUnitySourceIncl.body: Accepts two immutable string references and returns a Boolean value that signals whether the second string satisfies a particular relation with the first (for example equality, pattern matching or a custom condition defined elsewhere). The routine uses standard library string operations, and includes defensive checks to avoid null‑dereferencing or accidental modification of the inputs, thus keeping the call safe and predictable even when invoked with atypical or empty arguments.

@lcmLocalGenerator::WriteUnitySourceIncl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::WriteUnitySourceIncl.body: A lambda that returns true when the two string paths are equal or when the first path is a sub‑directory of the second one.

@lcmLocalGenerator::WriteUnitySourceIncl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::WriteUnitySourceIncl.body:
The function writes a conditional include block into a Unity build file.  
If a condition is supplied it emits `#if …` and `#endif`.  
When a unique‑ID string is given it emits a macro that expands to a hash of the source file path (using either a relative or absolute form) and tags the include with a comment.  
Optionally it writes any supplied preceding or following text before and after the `#include` line. The code blocks the header with undef/define to avoid re‑definition clashes.

@lcmLocalGenerator::cmLocalGenerator@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::cmLocalGenerator@k_Z.body: The constructor prepares the local generator by initializing internal state from the supplied global generator and makefile, caching compiler and tool‑chain options for each enabled language, and mapping environment‑specific variables (such as CPATH entries and system‑root directories) into its own variable mapping for later use in rule generation. It also sets flags for output handling (e.g., universal binary flags) and establishes compatibility settings based on the detected environment.

@lcmLocalGenerator::cmLocalGenerator@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::cmLocalGenerator@k_Z.body: Creates a new `cmLocalGenerator` instance by copying the internal state from the supplied object. The constructor copies all configuration parameters and prepared data structures so that the new instance behaves identically to the source until further modifications.

@lcmLocalGenerator::operator=@k_ZN16cmLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::operator=@k_ZN16cmLo.body: The assignment operator copies every member of the source `cmLocalGenerator` into the target object, returns a reference to `*this`, and handles self‑assignment safely. It preserves the semantics of a normal copy‑assignment: state after the call is identical to the argument, with no side‑effects beyond the member assignments.

@lcmLocalGenerator::~cmLocalGenerator@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::~cmLocalGenerator@k_.body: The virtual destructor is defaulted, so it performs no custom cleanup but guarantees that all resources owned by derived classes are released automatically.

@lcmLocalGeneratorCheckObjectName@k_ZN12.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGeneratorCheckObjectName@k_ZN12.body: This function verifies that the generated object‑file name does not exceed the allowed maximum length after accounting for the depth of the build‑directory path. It first computes the maximum allowable length for the object name (`max_obj_len`). If the current object name exceeds that limit, it calls `cmLocalGeneratorShortenObjectName` to truncate the name. When the name is within limits it simply returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false` to indicate the path is too deep or the name too long.

@lcmLocalGeneratorShortenObjectName@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGeneratorShortenObjectName@k_ZN.body: The routine trims a path‑style string to fit a given maximum length. It first computes how many characters exceed the limit, locates a directory separator near that point, and if a separator is found it replaces the leading part of the string with an MD5 hash of that prefix. The replaced string then replaces the original name. The function returns whether the new name is at least as short as requested.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AddCustomComman.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AddCustomComman.body: The function registers a custom command in the internal map and keeps a set of targets that reference it, adding the command to the list only when it appears for the first time.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AdditionalClean.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AdditionalClean.body: The routine inspects the Makefile for an `ADDITIONAL_CLEAN_FILES` property, evaluates the expression list into actual filenames, then registers each of those names—after normalising them against the current binary directory—as files to be removed during a clean build. This bridges the project‑specific clean list into the global Ninja‑style clean map.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendCustomCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendCustomCom.body:
The function iterates over the list of dependency names returned by `ccg.GetDepends()`.  
For each name it calls `GetRealDependency`, which resolves the name against the current configuration to produce an actual path.  
When that resolution succeeds, the resolved path is converted to a Ninja‑compatible form and appended to the `ninjaDeps` vector.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendCustomCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendCustomCom.body: The routine adds any custom commands to the list of lines to be emitted by the Ninja file. It first ensures that a working‑directory change line (“cd …”) is added if the command set is non‑empty, and then creates a launcher string from the current generator. It then iterates over every custom command: converts it to the appropriate shell quoting, appends it to the output list, and finally calls the custom generator’s AppendArguments to tack on any per‑command arguments. The function quietly skips any empty commands and handles multi‑configuration conversions when necessary.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDep.body: The function forwards the supplied target, output list, configuration paths, and dependency descriptor to the global Ninja generator by calling `AppendTargetDepends` on the global instance; effectively registering that target’s build‑time dependencies should be tracked by the Ninja build system.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetOut.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetOut.body: The function forwards the call to the globally shared ninja generator, passing the target, the collection of output dependencies, the configuration string, and a flag (`DependOnTargetArtifact`). This effectively records the target’s outputs in the global dependency graph.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::BuildCommandLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::BuildCommandLin.body:
The method assembles a single shell command string for Ninja from a vector of individual command fragments.  
If no fragments are provided it returns the predefined no‑op sentinel.  
When a custom step is requested it may spool the fragments into a temporary script file; the resulting command string then includes the script path, a hash of the script for change detection, and the appropriate Ninja specifiers.  
On Windows builds, it prefixes the command with “/C /” to invoke the Ninja command separator, and otherwise it stitches the fragments with “&&” to preserve the logical order.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToInclud.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToInclud.body: It forwards a path and format to the internal `ConvertToOutputFormat` routine and returns the resulting string, effectively translating the given path into the requested output format.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateRulePlace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateRulePlace.body: The method calls the base implementation of the expander, assigns the special `$TARGET_IMPLIB` marker as the target implementation library, and returns the freshly configured expander wrapped in a `std::unique_ptr`.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateUtilityOu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateUtilityOu.body: The method checks whether the global generator supports multi‑config and whether the list of by‑products is unique for all configurations. If either condition fails it falls back to the base implementation. When both conditions hold it builds a base path in the output‑directory for the target, creates a source entry for each configuration marked as symbolic, registers the target as a per‑config utility target, and finally returns the path string containing a `<CONFIG>` placeholder for the specific configuration.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::Generate@k_ZN21.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::Generate@k_ZN21.body: The `Generate` routine orchestrates the creation of Ninja build files for all targets in a CMake‑based project. It first resolves the output directory relative to the current binary folder, then writes the global and per‑configuration makefiles (the main build rules, the common header, and optionally the verbose rules file). For each target that is part of the build graph it constructs a `cmNinjaTargetGenerator`, generating the per‑configuration rule blocks and handling phony alias targets for multi‑config projects. Finally it emits custom command fragments and performs per‑config clean‑up cleanups.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCMakeInstanc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCMakeInstanc.body: The function simply forwards the request to the global generator and returns whatever `GetCMakeInstance()` it provides. It does not perform any logic on its own behalf—just acts as a thin wrapper around the global generator’s method.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCMakeInstanc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCMakeInstanc.body: The function is a simple forwarder: in a const context it calls `GetGlobalGenerator()` and returns whatever that object’s `GetCMakeInstance()` returns—i.e. a constant pointer to the CMake instance that the global generator owns.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCommonFileSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCommonFileSt.body: It forwards a reference to the shared file stream maintained by the global generator. The local generator simply returns the stream reference obtained from its `GetGlobalNinjaGenerator()` instance.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetGlobalNinjaG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetGlobalNinjaG.body: The method simply returns the global ninja generator for the current instance by casting the base‑class pointer returned by `GetGlobalGenerator()` to `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator*`.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetGlobalNinjaG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetGlobalNinjaG.body: The method returns a pointer to the global `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator` associated with the current instance. It does this by calling the inherited `GetGlobalGenerator()` (which yields a `cmGlobalGenerator*`) and then converting that pointer to the more specific `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator` type with `static_cast`. Since the method is `const`, it promises not to modify the object and guarantees that the returned pointer refers to a const object.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetImplFileStre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetImplFileStre.body: The function merely forwards the request for an implementation‑file stream to the global Ninja generator. It calls `GetGlobalNinjaGenerator()->GetImplFileStream(config)` and dereferences the returned pointer, returning that reference unchanged. No additional logic or side‑effects occur.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetLinkDependen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetLinkDependen.body: The method constructs a file path for the link‑dependency file for a given target: it concatenates the target’s support directory with the global “ConfigDirectory” for the supplied config string, appending “/link.d”. This path is used downstream to locate or generate that dependency file.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetRulesFileStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetRulesFileStr.body: It forwards the request to the global Ninja generator and hands back a reference to the stream that holds the rules file. It exposes that stream without copying it, keeping the call fast and side‑effect‑free.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetTargetDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetTargetDirect.body: Constructs a path string by concatenating the literal `"CMakeFiles/"` with the supplied target’s name, then appends either `"_dir"` (when compiled with `__VMS`) or `".dir"` (otherwise). The resulting string is returned.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetWorkingDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetWorkingDirec.body: The `GetWorkingDirectory` function is an accessor that returns a reference to the string containing the directory path in which the binary that the generator writes resides. It does this by delegating to the internal state object, calling its `GetBinaryDirectory()` method, and returning the result. The implementation assumes that the underlying state object remains valid for the lifetime of the caller and that `GetBinaryDirectory()` returns a valid reference; if either of those conditions fails, the returned reference would be dangling. It also relies on the const‑qualified qualifier of the method, ensuring that callers cannot modify the returned path.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::HasUniqueByprod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::HasUniqueByprod.body: The function iterates over each by‑product name, parses it into a generator expression, and then expands every custom‑command output path for each generator‑config. It records each expanded path in a set; if any path is seen twice, the function returns false. If all paths remain unique, it returns true.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MakeCustomComma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MakeCustomComma.body: The function builds a list of command‑generator objects for a given custom command. It creates a standard generator for the current configuration, and, when a cross‑configuration build is enabled, it adds extra generators for each other configuration that differs from the current one. If any of the command’s outputs or by‑products use a generator expression that is shared among configurations, the function removes the cross‑configuration generators so that only a single generator remains.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MakeCustomLaunc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MakeCustomLaunc.body: The function fetches the custom‑launcher string from the makefile, expands any rule‑placeholder variables it contains (such as the output file name), and returns that expanded command line; if the property isn’t defined, it simply returns an empty string.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MaybeRelativeTo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MaybeRelativeTo.body: The method resolves a path that may be relative to the top‑level binary directory by first normalising it with `MaybeRelativeToTopBinDir` and then converting that to an absolute output path via the global ninja generator’s `NinjaOutputPath`. It simply forwards the string it receives and returns the resolved path string.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteBuildFileT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteBuildFileT.body: The function writes the header section of the generated Ninja files. It writes the common header first, then for each configuration (in a multi‑config project) writes a separate header, the required Ninja version line, a configuration variable line, and the “include” directives for that configuration. For single‑config projects it writes those lines once. Finally it writes the common include list and the work‑directory line, and then emits the header for the rule file.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCommandScr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCommandScr.body: The function generates a shell or batch script from a list of command strings. It first resolves a destination path – if a target is supplied it uses that target’s support directory; otherwise it falls back to a default build‑output directory. It then creates the directory, appends the custom step name, and appends a “‑” suffix plus the command‑config if the generator is multi‑configuration. The file extension is chosen according to the OS (”.bat” on Windows, “.sh” elsewhere). After opening the file it writes a command‑header that disables echo on Windows or enables exit on errors on POSIX, and then iterates over the command lines, writing each. For Windows each line is wrapped in a failure test that jumps to an error label and reports the line number and exit status. Finally, on Windows it appends a return‑to‑success label. The constructed path is returned.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomComm.body: The function registers a custom command in the Ninja build file. It first skips any command that has already been emitted for the current configuration. It then creates one or more custom‑command generators for the command, and for each generator it gathers the outputs, by‑products and dependency information. If a generator has no outputs or by‑products, it is ignored. It collects order‑only dependencies by walking through the target set and intersecting their declared dependencies. It figures out whether any output is marked symbolic (which forces a “phony” target). It then builds a list of explicit dependencies, sorts any order‑only dependencies, and finally writes either a phony build rule (if no command lines exist) or a real command rule with a unique step name, optional depfile handling, and appropriate comment. The produced rule is written out through the global Ninja generator.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomComm.body:
The routine emits the Ninja‑language build instructions for each user‑declared custom command.  
It walks the list of custom commands stored in the generator, looks up the target that a command is supposed to populate, and calls WriteCustomCommandBuildStatement to serialize that command‑to‑target pair using the supplied configuration file name.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaConfi.body: The function simply forwards the supplied `config` string to the global helper to emit a Ninja variable named `CONFIGURATION`, adding a comment that the variable holds the configuration used for custom commands.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaFiles.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaFiles.body: The routine first emits a divider line, then writes a comment noting that the auxiliary rules file will be included. It obtains a reference to the global generator, retrieves the path to the rules file, encodes that path, and finally emits a `include` statement accompanied by a comment.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaFiles.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaFiles.body: The method writes a comment block that includes a shared “common” ninja file. It first prints a divider, then a header comment, obtains a path from the global generator, encodes the path to a safe form, and finally emits an `include` statement with a brief description.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaRequi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaRequi.body: The routine selects the minimal Ninja version string that the current generator supports. It first picks the default version, then overwrites it if the console pool is supported, and finally switches to the manifest‑restart version when that feature is enabled and re‑generation is not suppressed. The chosen string is emitted as a comment and assigned to `ninja_required_version`.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaWorkD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaWorkD.body: The routine writes a comment and divider to the Ninja build file, then retrieves the binary directory of the current generator, strips the output‑path prefix from it, and finally emits a line assigning that cleaned path to the `cmake_ninja_workdir` variable.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WritePools@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WritePools@k_ZN.body: The function writes a divider, then pulls the pool list from the global JOB_POOLS property (or the Makefile definition if the property is unset). It iterates over each “name=depth” entry, parses the numeric depth, and emits a “pool <name> depth = <depth>” line; malformed entries trigger an error.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteProcessedM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteProcessedM.body: The function writes a header divider into the output stream, then emits a comment block that lists the CMakeLists‑declared statements for the current list file. It pulls the safe definition of the current list file name, and if the generator is operating on the root makefile it flags that fact. Finally, it writes another divider and ends with a blank line.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteProjectHea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteProjectHea.body: The function writes a header block to the output stream: it first writes a divider line, then prints a comment line containing the current project name followed by a list of configuration names joined with commas, and finally writes another divider line.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::cmLocalNinjaGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::cmLocalNinjaGen.body: The constructor creates a `cmLocalNinjaGenerator` object, forwarding the supplied `cmGlobalGenerator` and `cmMakefile` to its base class `cmLocalCommonGenerator`. It performs no additional initialization beyond that base‑class setup.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::~cmLocalNinjaGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::~cmLocalNinjaGe.body: The destructor is a defaulted, virtual override that simply invokes the compiler‑generated cleanup for all member variables; no additional code is executed.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AddImpl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AddImpl.body: It records a source file as an implicit dependency of a target. The method indexes a nested map by target name, scanner kind, language, and object name, then appends the source string to the corresponding list.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.body: The function creates a small helper script in the target’s build directory that lists all files to delete. It emits a “file(REMOVE_RECURSE …)” block for each file, then adds a single command that invokes `$(CMAKE_COMMAND) -P` on that script. If no specific file is supplied, it also emits per‑language clean rules for the target.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.body: The lambda takes a `const std::string&` argument named `cmd` and returns a new string that prefixes a `+` character to the argument by calling `cmStrCat`. It effectively produces a string in the form `"+" + cmd`.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.body: This routine iterates over a supplied custom‑command generator, constructs each command line (expanding any rule placeholders, converting relative paths, and handling Windows‑specific .bat/.cmd prefixes), optionally prepends a launcher and prefixes with a job‑server marker, then appends the resulting string(s) to the supplied command list.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.body: It iterates over each custom command in the vector, constructs a cmCustomCommandGenerator using the current configuration name, then calls AppendCustomCommand to add that command to the target’s command list, supplying the relative path and a flag set to true.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.body: The function iterates over the list of dependencies returned by `ccg.GetDepends()`. For each dependency string, it calls `GetRealDependency` with the current configuration name to obtain the actual target name. If that lookup succeeds, the resolved name is appended to the `depends` vector via `push_back`. The routine simply enriches the dependency list; it produces no return value.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendC.body: The function iterates through each `cmCustomCommand` in the supplied list, instantiates a `cmCustomCommandGenerator` with the current command, the generator’s configuration name, and itself as the parent context, then forwards that generator to the internal helper `AppendCustomDepend` to add the resulting dependency information into the accumulating dependency list.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendD.body: The function collects any extra files marked for cleaning, writes a small CMake script that removes them, and finally appends a clean‑command to the list of commands that will be invoked when the build is cleaned.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendE.body: The routine parses the supplied text line‑by‑line, building a shell command that will emit each line. It detects whether colored output is supported; if so, it maps the echo type (normal, depend, build, link, generate, global) to a `cmake_echo_color` flag. For each line it emits either a plain `@echo …` command or a `cmake_echo_color` invocation that may include progress‑related options. The constructed command strings are appended to the `commands` vector, one per logical line.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendF.body: When invoked on a Watcom W‑make generator, the method checks if the incoming flag text contains an escaped quote (`\\\"`). If so, it swaps that sequence with a literal quote and then delegates the modified string to the base `AppendFlags` routine; otherwise it passes the original string unchanged.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendR.body: Appends the rule file to the dependency vector unless the project sets the `CMAKE_SKIP_RULE_DEPENDENCY` option to true.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::AppendR.body: If the skip flag isn’t set, it pulls every rule‑file in the second argument into the dependency vector, otherwise it leaves the vector untouched.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CheckMu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CheckMu.body: The routine walks the list of declared output pairs from the `CMAKE_MULTIPLE_OUTPUT_PAIRS` definition and removes any dependent file that exists while its corresponding primary file does not. It prints a message when the verbose flag is set.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::ClearDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::ClearDe.body: The routine walks through each target listed in the CMAKE_DEPEND_INFO_FILES definition. For each target it loads its dependency list file, clears any implicit dependencies via a cmDepends clearer (optionally verbose), removes the internal‑check file, and if compiler‑generated dependency files exist it clears those as well and touches a timestamp file to force a fresh regeneration of the dependency information.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Compute.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Compute.body: The function assigns `HomeRelativeOutputPath` to the result of `MaybeRelativeToTopBinDir(GetCurrentBinaryDirectory())`. If the resulting path equals `"."`, it clears it. Finally, if the path is non‑empty, it appends a trailing slash.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Convert.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Convert.body: It takes a relative file path, prefixes it with the current binary directory and a slash, and returns that combined string.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Convert.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Convert.body: The function simply forwards the supplied path string to the `ConvertToMakefilePath` implementation of the global generator object. It performs a `static_cast` to obtain a `cmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3*` and then returns the result of invoking that method.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Convert.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Convert.body: The function normalises a file‑system path by first tokenising it into individual components, then rebuilds the string with the appropriate path separator for the current platform. It optionally prefixes and suffixes the result with either a straight quote or the Watcom‑style quote (`’`/`'`), depending on the `useWatcomQuote` flag. During the rebuild it treats the leading component specially so that a root or drive letter is preserved correctly and any trailing slash is suppressed to avoid duplicate separators. The output is a correctly quoted, platform‑aware path ready for use in a makefile.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CreateC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CreateC.body: This lambda captures a `prefix` string and returns a new string formed by concatenating that prefix with any string argument supplied to the caller.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CreateC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CreateC.body:
The function inserts a change‑directory command into the command list.  
It first checks whether the target path already matches the relative
path; if it does, no action is taken.  
Depending on the generator type it either prefixes a single `cd` (or
`cd /d` on MinGW) to every command in the vector or inserts a
stand‑alone `cd` command before and after the command sequence, so
that the process runs in the desired directory.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CreateM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::CreateM.body: Creates a make‑file variable name by concatenating the two input strings, stripping any dots, pluses, or dashes that would break a make‑file parser, and then normalising the result (dots→\_, pluses→___, minuses→\_\_). If the shortened name collides with one already in the map, it appends a numeric suffix until a unique key is produced. The function keeps a map of the original names to their cleaned versions so repeated calls can return the same string without recomputing it.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::EchoPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::EchoPro.body: EchoProgress reports the current progress of an operation—typically printing or logging a status message that reflects how much of the task has been completed.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Generat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Generat.body: The method configures whether color output and diagnostic options are enabled, then walks through every target in the local generator’s build order. For each eligible target it merges dependencies’ command lists, generates a rule file via a target‑generator, and records the progress in the global generator. Finally it writes the local makefile and stores per‑directory information in a helper file.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetColo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetColo.body: Returns the current state of the internal “ColorMakefile” flag.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetComm.body: The method returns the stored set of source‑file pointers that have been marked visited for the supplied target.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetConf.body: The function retrieves the sole configuration name from the internal list returned by `GetConfigNames()` and returns that string, asserting that the list contains exactly one element.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetCrea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetCrea.body: The function simply returns the inverse of the internal `SkipAssemblySourceRules` flag: it yields `true` whenever that flag is `false` (indicating that assembly‑source rules should be generated) and `false` otherwise.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetCrea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetCrea.body: The function returns the inverse of the member flag `SkipPreprocessedSourceRules`. When `SkipPreprocessedSourceRules` is true, the function yields `false`, signalling that pre‑processed source rules should not be created; when the flag is false, it yields `true` and the creation path is enabled. This simple boolean gate is used by callers to decide whether to generate or skip the rule set that operates on pre‑processed sources.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetHome.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetHome.body: Returns a reference to the internally stored string that represents the relative path used for output files, exposing it without copying or modifying the underlying value.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetImpl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetImpl.body: The function returns a reference to an `ImplicitDependLanguageMap` that maps implicit dependencies for the given target `tgt`. It looks up the target’s name in the map `this->ImplicitDepends` and indexes it by the requested scanner type, returning the stored map for that target‑scanner combination.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetIndi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetIndi.body:
This method collects the names of all local object files produced by the generator.  
It first obtains the map of object‑file names to their info, then iterates that map, appending each file name to the supplied vector.  
If a file has a pre‑processing rule, it also appends a corresponding “.i” target; if it has an assembly rule, it appends a “.s” target.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetLink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetLink.body: The function constructs and returns the absolute path to the link‑dependency file for the specified target by appending `"link.d"` to the target’s support directory.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetLoca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetLoca.body: Returns a reference to the internal `LocalHelp` vector so callers can read the help strings without copying the container. The reference is const‑qualified, guaranteeing the caller cannot modify the data. The function itself performs no logic beyond exposing the stored data.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetLoca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetLoca.body: The function walks through every compile‑ready target in the current generator. For each target it enumerates the source files that will produce object files, builds the full path for each resulting object file (including the target’s directory component), and inserts an entry in the supplied map. Each entry records whether the original source file had an extension and records the source’s language and the target that produced it.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetRecu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetRecu.body: The function builds a shell command string that runs make on a nested Makefile. It prepends the global make command with any global silent flag that the global generator has set, optionally prefixes the inherited MAKEFLAGS if the target environment requires it, then appends the target name resolved relative to the top‑level build tree and escaped properly for the current shell. Finally, it returns that complete command string.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetRela.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetRela.body: This const method builds a path string by concatenating the stored `HomeRelativeOutputPath` with the directory derived from `GetTargetDirectory(target)`. It simply returns that combined string.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::GetTarg.body: The method builds a directory string by concatenating `"CMakeFiles/"` with the target’s name and appending either `"_dir"` (on VMS) or `".dir"` otherwise, then returns that string.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::LocalOb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::LocalOb.body: It constructs a `LocalObjectEntry` instance, storing the provided `cmGeneratorTarget*` in the member `Target` and moving the given language string into the member `Language`. No additional logic is performed in the body.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::LocalOb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::LocalOb.body: LocalObjectEntry() provides a default‑initialised representation of a local object entry that is used during the generation of the makefile in the Unix build system.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::MaybeCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::MaybeCo.body: The method checks whether the current build target is the Watcom WMake environment and whether the passed‑in command string refers to a full file path that contains spaces or parentheses. If both tests succeed, it resolves that path to its 8.3‑style short form and returns the command string in the shell‑output format; otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::ScanDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::ScanDep.body: The routine pulls in stored directory settings, adjusts path handling (including forced Unix paths and relative top directories), opens the main and internal dependency rule files, writes a disclaimer into each, and then iterates over the languages defined in the directory list, creating a language‑specific dependency scanner that emits the appropriate rule fragments into the streams. It exits false if any step fails.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::SetBorl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::SetBorl.body: Sets the internal flag `BorlandMakeCurlyHack` to the supplied boolean value.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::SetMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::SetMake.body: Updates the internal flag that governs whether make commands should be escaped twice.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::SetMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::SetMake.body: This function assigns the provided integer `s` to the member field `MakefileVariableSize`. It updates the internal state of the object to reflect the new size value.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::UpdateD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::UpdateD.body: The function reads the target’s “DependInfo” file, compares the timestamps of dependency files (both internal and external), and, if any are newer than the current dependency records, it rescans the target’s source files to regenerate the dependency listings. It then writes the fresh dependency data back to the relevant make‑dependency files, ensuring the build system has the latest dependency information.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteCM.body: The function writes a string literal that can be safely re‑parsed by CMake: it wraps the argument in quotes and escapes any internal backslashes or double‑quotes, writing the escaped sequence to the provided output stream.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteCo.body: The function is invoked to emit a make‑file rule that gives the helper target a convenient name. It first verifies that the real target and the helper target differ; only when they differ does it create a dependency list containing the real target and construct an empty list of commands. Finally, it forwards the helper target, the dependency list, and other metadata to `WriteMakeRule` to generate the rule.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteDe.body: The function writes the dependency‑scanning configuration for a build target. It first writes a flag to enable project‑only dependency filtering. Then it enumerates the languages that need implicit dependency checks, emits the file lists per language, and emits compiler‑specific settings (compiler ID, Fortran sub‑module handling, preprocessor definitions, and include paths). Finally it records any include‑transform rules and emits the set of dependency files needed by the compiler.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteDi.body:
Creates a *CMakeDirectoryInformation.cmake* file in the current binary directory.  
The routine first opens the target file, aborting if the stream cannot be opened.  
It writes a header disclaimer, then emits a small CMake configuration section that defines the top‑source and top‑binary relative paths for that build tree.  
If the global flag to force Unix‑style paths is set, a corresponding flag is written to the file.  
Finally, it records the include‑file regular‑expression strings for C and C++ scans and complaints, emitting them as CMake cache entries.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteDi.body: The function writes a comment header to an output stream that marks the file as auto‑generated by CMake, including the generator name and CMake version numbers, so downstream tools can ignore or treat it as read‑only.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteDi.body: The method writes a long separator line—specifically a line of “#” and “=” characters—into the supplied output stream. It’s used to visually break sections in a generated Makefile.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteLo.body: The `WriteLocalAllRules` routine generates a makefile that drives the entire build system. It first writes a “default” rule that runs the `all` target, emits a special rule for a single‑process build when parallelism is disabled, and then emits rules for all globally‑declared targets. Each target’s pre‑ and post‑build commands are appended, and a “fast” shortcut target is created for the special “install” targets. Finally it writes the top‑level “all”, “clean”, and pre‑install rules, adding any required consistency checks or rebuild hooks when the system is set to recompute dependencies.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteLo.body: The method writes the local Makefile: it emits the common rules, emits the target rules for this generator (or convenience rules per object file), adds preprocessing/assembly convenience rules when enabled, emits a “help” rule if missing, and finishes with the special‑bottom directives.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteLo.body: The method iterates over every build target produced by the generator. For each target that is an executable, static/shared/library, utility, or object library it writes a make rule that changes to the target’s directory, invokes a recursive make on a dedicated helper makefile (“CMakeFiles/Makefile2”), and writes that rule to the output stream. It then emits a second convenience rule that points the target’s canonical name to the same build rule. Finally, for each target that needs a pre‑install relink it emits a “preinstall” rule that runs the same helper makefile in the target’s sub‑directory. The method tracks emitted names in the supplied set.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteMa.body: The function writes a single rule into a makefile stream. It first validates that a target is supplied, then emits a comment line (splitting multi‑line comments on “\n”). The target is converted to a relative makefile path and, if flagged, prefixed with a symbolic flag retrieved from the Makefile object. Dependencies are emitted either as a single line or split into separate lines when the list is long, and the associated commands are wrapped with a tab and a trailing newline. When the rule is not a Watcom‑WMake rule it adds a “.PHONY” declaration and finally appends the target to a local help list if requested.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteMa.body: Writes the standard environment and utility variable definitions into the generated makefile. It emits the current shell target (`SHELL`), the path to the CMake executable, and standard helper commands such as `RM`. It also writes any escape sequences required for the build system, e.g., mapping an `=` character for use in recipe lines. The output adapts to the current platform (Windows vs. Unix) and emits the source‑ and binary‑directory paths in the chosen format.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteOb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteOb.body:
The function writes a convenience rule to the makefile.  
It first checks if the object’s source has an extension and, if so, produces a target name without that extension for the help section.  
Then it builds a command list by iterating over each target entry, generating a recursive make call for that target and appending the resulting command.  
Finally it writes the rule to the stream using `WriteMakeRule`, supplying the constructed dependencies and command list.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteSp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteSp.body: Writes a divider line, inserts a comment noting a special rule to run CMake with the --check‑build‑system flag, and, unless suppression is enabled, emits a make rule named `cmake_check_build_system`. The rule runs the CMake executable (optionally changing to the binary directory) and contains no dependencies, ensuring that any target that depends on it will not trigger regeneration.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteSp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::WriteSp.body: The function writes the top‑level header of the generated makefile. It outputs a divider, a comment line, then declares a special rule that disables implicit rules, followed by a series of rules that strip VCS‑style suffixes, add a dummy suffix for compatibility, and finally emit a handful of special targets that silence verbose output, switch verbose mode, and force a bogus target to keep dependent rules from being discarded.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::cmLocal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::cmLocal.body: Initializes a Unix Makefile generator with default settings: disables color output, skips preprocessed and assembly source rules, disables special escape handling and the Borland hack, and starts the makefile variable size at zero.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::cmLocal.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::cmLocal.body: The function is a copy‑constructor that creates a new `cmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3` instance by copying the internal state from the supplied reference.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::operato.body: The assignment operator creates a new `cmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3` instance by copying the internal state from the source object. It copies any configuration data—such as file‑paths, build flags, and internal state flags—into the target object, ensuring that all dependencies and resource handles are correctly duplicated. The method guards against self‑assignment, and it performs the copy in a try‑catch block to keep the object in a valid state even if an exception is thrown during copying. Because the implementation relies on shallow copies of many member objects, it typically performs a simple assignment of primitive members, while delegating deeper object copying to their own copy constructors. Overall, the operator keeps the object in sync with its source while avoiding leaks or dangling pointers.

@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::~cmLoca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3::~cmLoca.body: The virtual destructor of `cmLocalUnixMakefileGenerator3` is defaulted, ensuring that when an object of this type is destroyed the compiler-generated clean‑up code runs automatically, correctly releasing any resources that the class may allocate.

@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::AddGeneratorSpe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::AddGeneratorSpe.body:
The function walks over every generator target, verifies that each has an install‑name path set up, then emits a CMake‑style declaration of the project’s binary directory.  
If the build is for an Apple‑embedded platform it inspects the SDK type to determine a short‐form platform token (e.g., `iphoneos`, `appletvsimulator`, etc.) and writes a small block of conditional CMake logic that sets `PLATFORM_NAME`/`EFFECTIVE_PLATFORM_NAME` variables based on that token. The emitted CMake code is tiny, just enough for the build system to pick the right platform string at configure time.

@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::AddXCConfigSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::AddXCConfigSour.body:
The method pulls the **“XCODE_XCCONFIG”** property from a *cmGeneratorTarget*.  
If the property is missing it exits.  
Otherwise it pulls the list of generator‑specific configuration files (`Makefile::IncludeEmptyConfig`).  
For every entry it evaluates the expression defined in the property (using the current target and configuration) and, when the evaluation yields a non‑empty path, registers that file as a source for the target.

@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::AppendFlagEscap.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::AppendFlagEscap.body: The function forwards a flag string to the global code generator, delegating the actual flag handling to that component.

@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::ComputeObjectFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::ComputeObjectFi.body: The function maps each `cmSourceFile` to an object‑file name derived by stripping the source file’s extension, appending “.o”, normalising the result to lower‑case for case‑insensitive platforms, and tracks how many times each lower‑case name appears. When a name appears twice, the implementation is designed to emit a diagnostic warning about the duplicate.

@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::Generate@k_ZN21.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::Generate@k_ZN21.body: The `Generate` method first invokes its base class’s `Generate` implementation, then iterates over each generator target returned by `GetGeneratorTargets()`. For each target it calls `HasMacOSXRpathInstallNameDir("")`, presumably to register or flag an empty installation‑name directory for that target.

@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::GetTargetDirect.body: The function simply returns an empty string, signaling that this generator currently has no per‑target directory to provide.

@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::cmLocalXCodeGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::cmLocalXCodeGen.body: Creates a new code‑generation instance by forwarding the global generator and makefile objects to its base class, then disables the flag that would otherwise add binary‑generation options to the language‑specific flag list.

@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::~cmLocalXCodeGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalXCodeGenerator::~cmLocalXCodeGe.body: The destructor is declared virtual and defaulted (`= default`). It simply invokes the compiler‑generated cleanup for all member objects, ensuring that any resources owned by a concrete `cmLocalXCodeGenerator` instance are released correctly when the object is destroyed, even when deleted polymorphically through a base‑class pointer.

@lcmLocaleRAII::cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocaleRAII::cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLoc.body: The deletion of the copy‑constructor means instances of `cmLocaleRAII` cannot be copied; any attempt to invoke a copy will fail at compile time, guaranteeing that objects of this type remain unique and preventing accidental duplication.

@lcmLocaleRAII::cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocaleRAII::cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLoc.body: This constructor captures the current locale, then forces the C locale for its scope. The RAII idiom guarantees the original locale is restored when the object is destroyed.

@lcmLocaleRAII::operator=@k_ZN12cmLocale.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocaleRAII::operator=@k_ZN12cmLocale.body:
`operator=` is the copy‑assignment operator that has been explicitly deleted.  
Attempting to assign a `cmLocaleRAII` to another instance will fail at compile time, preventing accidental copying of the object.

@lcmLocaleRAII::~cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocaleRAII::~cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLo.body: The destructor restores the locale that was saved in `OldLocale` by calling `setlocale(LC_CTYPE, this->OldLocale.c_str());`.

@lcmMachO::GetErrorMessage@k_ZNK7cmMachO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMachO::GetErrorMessage@k_ZNK7cmMachO.body: It returns a reference to the internal error message string without making a copy, so callers can inspect the message but cannot modify it. The function never mutates state, and no exception is thrown. It simply forwards the stored string reference, ensuring zero‑allocation overhead.

@lcmMachO::GetInstallName@k_ZN7cmMachO14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMachO::GetInstallName@k_ZN7cmMachO14.body: The `GetInstallName` member scans the first Mach‑O header in the object’s internal list for a `LC_LOAD_DYLIB`, `LC_LOAD_WEAK_DYLIB`, or `LC_ID_DYLIB` load command.
