When it encounters such a command, it pulls the string that follows the command’s fixed header and copies it into the supplied string reference. If no suitable command is found, the function returns false; otherwise it returns true with the extracted name.

@lcmMachO::PrintInfo@k_ZNK7cmMachO9Print.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMachO::PrintInfo@k_ZNK7cmMachO9Print.body: The function is a const member that accepts an output stream, but its body is currently empty—acting as a placeholder for future diagnostic output.

@lcmMachO::Valid@k_ZNK7cmMachO5ValidEv@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMachO::Valid@k_ZNK7cmMachO5ValidEv@f.body: The method simply returns the negation of the internal list’s `empty()` state, indicating whether any `MachO` objects are stored.

@lcmMachO::cmMachO@k_ZN7cmMachOC1EPKc@f..author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMachO::cmMachO@k_ZN7cmMachOC1EPKc@f..body: Creates an internal instance of cmMachOInternal using the supplied file name, storing it in the `Internal` member via `make_unique`.

@lcmMachO::cmMachO@k_ZN7cmMachOC1ERKS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMachO::cmMachO@k_ZN7cmMachOC1ERKS_.body: This function performs a shallow copy of the object’s internal state: it takes a const reference to another `cmMachO` instance and initializes the new instance’s members from that source. It avoids deep copying of any owned resources, assuming all members are trivially copy‑constructible.

@lcmMachO::operator bool@k_ZNK7cmMachOcv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMachO::operator bool@k_ZNK7cmMachOcv.body: This operator lets a const instance be checked in a Boolean context by delegating to its `Valid()` member. Because it’s marked `explicit`, it won’t trigger accidental implicit conversions; callers must expressly test the object’s validity before treating it as a `bool`.

@lcmMachO::~cmMachO@k_ZN7cmMachOD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMachO::~cmMachO@k_ZN7cmMachOD1Ev.body: The destructor `~cmMachO()` cleans up all internal resources when a `cmMachO` instance is destroyed, releasing any allocated memory, closing handles, and performing any necessary finalization logic before the object is removed from memory.

@lcmMacroCommand@k_Z14cmMacroCommandRKiR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroCommand@k_Z14cmMacroCommandRKiR.body: The function validates that an argument list is supplied, flags an error if the list is empty, otherwise it creates a `cmMacroFunctionBlocker`, stores the supplied arguments in that blocker, and registers the blocker in the current makefile’s function‑blocker list, finally returning `true`.

@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch.body: The function expands the argument list from the list‑file entry and then checks whether the first expanded argument matches the first argument stored in the current macro function blocker. If there are no arguments after expansion, the match succeeds by default.

@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName.body: The method supplies the literal name that represents the termination instruction for a macro; when invoked it simply yields a `string_view` containing `"endmacro"`.

@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN12_.body: The `Replay` function records a macro command into the makefile: it creates a `cmMacroHelperCommand` populated with the macro’s arguments, moves the supplied list of functions into that command, records the current file path and policy information, and finally registers the command in the current makefile state via `AddScriptedCommand`.

@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::StartCommandNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::StartCommandNa.body: The member function overrides a base virtual that returns a `string_view` pointing at the literal `"macro"`. It is `const`, so it guarantees no mutation of the object and simply returns that string view each time it is called.

@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::cmMacroFunctio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::cmMacroFunctio.body: The constructor `cmMacroFunctionBlocker(cmMacroFunctionBlocker&&)` efficiently initializes a new `cmMacroFunctionBlocker` by moving an existing instance into it. It forwards the move‑constructed state to its base `cmFunctionBlocker` and performs any needed internal bookkeeping during that transfer.

@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::cmMacroFunctio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::cmMacroFunctio.body: The constructor accepts a reference to another `cmMacroFunctionBlocker` and copies its internal data into the new instance. It is used to duplicate a macro function blocker when a copy of an existing blocker is required.

@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference, moves the internal state of the temporary `cmMacroFunctionBlocker` into the current instance, and returns a reference to the modified object.

@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN.body: This overload allows a `cmMacroFunctionBlocker` instance to be assigned from another instance. It copies all internal state (like the stored function block and any flags) from the source object into the target, ensuring both objects represent the same macro function block after the operation.

@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::~cmMacroFuncti.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroFunctionBlocker::~cmMacroFuncti.body: The virtual destructor `~cmMacroFunctionBlocker()` is invoked automatically when an instance of `cmMacroFunctionBlocker` is destroyed. It guarantees that any resources allocated by the object—such as internal macro blocks, reference‐counted buffers, or temporary flags—are properly released and that any pending macro‑specific state is reset before the object’s memory is reclaimed. Its implementation typically calls the base class destructor to unwind the inheritance chain and then performs any class‑specific cleanup required for the macro handling logic.

@lcmMacroHelperCommand::cmMacroHelperCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroHelperCommand::cmMacroHelperCom.body: The constructor accepts an rvalue reference to another `cmMacroHelperCommand` instance and initializes the new object by moving the internal state from that source, ensuring all member data is transferred efficiently while maintaining class invariants.

@lcmMacroHelperCommand::cmMacroHelperCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroHelperCommand::cmMacroHelperCom.body: The constructor initializes a `cmMacroHelperCommand` instance from an existing one, copying its internal state so the new helper can be used in subsequent command processing.

@lcmMacroHelperCommand::cmMacroHelperCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroHelperCommand::cmMacroHelperCom.body: The function `cmMacroHelperCommand` bundles macro arguments into a command‑ready structure, handling parsing, validation, and dispatching to the appropriate macro handler before returning the parsed command object for further execution.

@lcmMacroHelperCommand::operator()@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMacroHelperCommand::operator()@k_ZNK.body: The function expands the macro’s argument list, verifies that enough arguments were supplied, then enters the macro’s local scope. It substitutes formal parameter placeholders in each stored function argument with the actual values (including the special “argc”, “argn”, and “argv” tokens), invokes every function collected in the macro body, and propagates any “return”, “break”, or nested‑error statuses back to the caller. If any sub‑command fails it returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmMakeCommandLine@k_Z17cmMakeCommandLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakeCommandLine@k_Z17cmMakeCommandLi.body: Creates and populates a cmCustomCommandLine instance with the supplied options and arguments so that the resulting object can be used in a CMake custom command.

@lcmMakeDirectoryCommand@k_Z22cmMakeDire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakeDirectoryCommand@k_Z22cmMakeDire.body: The command receives one path argument, validates that the caller has write permission for that path in the current makefile, and if allowed it calls `cmSystemTools::MakeDirectory` to create the directory, reporting success via the return value and setting an error message in `status` if the check fails.

@lcmMakeRange@k_Z11cmMakeRangeRKT_@f./So.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakeRange@k_Z11cmMakeRangeRKT_@f./So.body: Creates a `cmRange` by capturing the `begin()` and `end()` iterators of the supplied range; the return type is `cmRange<decltype(range.begin())>` and it simply returns `{range.begin(), range.end()}`.

@lcmMakeRange@k_Z11cmMakeRangeT_T0_@f./S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakeRange@k_Z11cmMakeRangeT_T0_@f./S.body: Creates a cmRange object that holds the supplied begin iterator and the supplied end iterator, with its type parameter inferred from the first iterator. This convenience wrapper forwards the two iterator arguments to the cmRange constructor, allowing callers to construct a range without explicitly specifying the template argument.

@lcmMakeSingleCommandLine@k_Z23cmMakeSin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakeSingleCommandLine@k_Z23cmMakeSin.body: It builds a single‑line custom command string by joining the command name, arguments, and any required environment variables into the format expected by CMake’s internal processing.

@lcmMakefile::AddAlias@k_ZN10cmMakefile8.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddAlias@k_ZN10cmMakefile8.body: It stores an alias in the class’s internal map and, if requested, registers that alias with the global generator.

@lcmMakefile::AddCMakeDependFile@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCMakeDependFile@k_ZN10c.body: Adds the file string to the internal `ListFiles` vector, updating the collection of dependency files.

@lcmMakefile::AddCMakeDependFilesFromUse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCMakeDependFilesFromUse.body: The method reads the property `CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS`, splits the string into a list, and for each entry it checks whether the path is absolute. Absolute paths are added directly; relative ones are prefixed with the current source directory before being added.

@lcmMakefile::AddCMakeOutputFile@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCMakeOutputFile@k_ZN10c.body: The method simply appends the supplied file name to the `OutputFiles` collection, storing it for later use.

@lcmMakefile::AddCacheDefinition@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCacheDefinition@k_ZN10c.body: This overload forwards the supplied parameters to the internal overload that accepts a `cmValue` constructed from the documentation string. It allows callers to pass a raw string for the documentation field, with an optional `force` flag that defaults to `false`.

@lcmMakefile::AddCacheDefinition@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCacheDefinition@k_ZN10c.body: AddCacheDefinition checks whether a cache entry already exists and, unless the caller forces an override, re‑uses that value. If the entry is a path or file‑path type, it normalizes the paths before storing them. After normalizing, the entry is added to the internal cache and, if applicable, any legacy‑policy handling is performed.

@lcmMakefile::AddCacheDefinition@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCacheDefinition@k_ZN10c.body: The function registers a cache entry by packaging the supplied strings into cmValue objects and then calling the internal implementation. It accepts the name, the value string, optional documentation text, the cache‑entry type, and a flag that, when true, forces an overwrite of an existing entry. The call simply forwards these arguments to the underlying `AddCacheDefinition(name, cmValue{value}, cmValue{doc}, type, force)` routine.

@lcmMakefile::AddCompileDefinition@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCompileDefinition@k_ZN1.body: The method simply forwards the supplied string to the internal `AppendProperty` helper, adding it under the key “COMPILE_DEFINITIONS” so that subsequent make‑file construction stages know that this compile definition should be emitted.

@lcmMakefile::AddCompileOption@k_ZN10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCompileOption@k_ZN10cmM.body: Adds the supplied option to the internal list of compiler flags by storing it via `AppendProperty` under the key `"COMPILE_OPTIONS"`. This allows subsequent build steps to pull the accumulated flags for a makefile.

@lcmMakefile::AddCustomCommandOldStyle@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCustomCommandOldStyle@k.body: The method converts an old‑style custom‑command description into the current internal format. It creates a `cmCustomCommand`, fills in its dependencies, command lines, and comment, and then either attaches that command to the target itself (if the source and target are identical, meaning a post‑build rule) or hooks it up to each output file. For each output it clones the command, assigns the appropriate output, and registers it. It also checks whether the source is a real source file (via the extension regex) and, if so, uses it as the main dependency; otherwise the command simply depends on the source file. If the target isn’t already present, it reports an error.

@lcmMakefile::AddCustomCommandToOutput@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCustomCommandToOutput@k.body: The method attaches a new custom command to the current generator, first ensuring that the command has at least one output and that its command lines are valid. It then marks those outputs and by‑products as generated, records the current policy snapshot for the command, and finally hands off the command to the generator action queue. When the command is executed, the callback (if supplied) is invoked with the resulting source file.

@lcmMakefile::AddCustomCommandToTarget@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCustomCommandToTarget@k.body: The method attaches a custom command to a build target. It resolves the target object, validates the command lines, creates any required by‑product sources, records policy values, then queues a generator action that records the command with back‑trace information and finally returns the target (or null if validation fails).

@lcmMakefile::AddDefineFlag@k_ZN10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddDefineFlag@k_ZN10cmMake.body: The method checks whether the supplied flag string is empty. If not, it appends the flag to the internal list of original define‑flags (`DefineFlagsOrig`). It then calls `ParseDefineFlag()`; if that call returns `true`, indicating the flag is a definition that should be processed by the compile‑definitions code path, the method returns immediately. If not, it appends the flag to the general `DefineFlags` list for non‑definition flags. The function performs no other processing or side‑effects.

@lcmMakefile::AddDefinition@k_ZN10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddDefinition@k_ZN10cmMake.body: The method forwards a named value to another overload by dereferencing the provided value. If `value` is null or not dereferenceable, the call will trigger a crash or undefined behavior.

@lcmMakefile::AddDefinition@k_ZN10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddDefinition@k_ZN10cmMake.body: Adds a new definition to the internal state. It records the name/value pair in the snapshot and, if a watcher is installed, emits a notification that the variable was modified and accessed by passing the raw data pointer to the watcher.

@lcmMakefile::AddDefinition@k_ZN10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddDefinition@k_ZN10cmMake.body: Adds a named definition to the internal make‑file registry – essentially registering a string value under the given key so it can later be expanded or referenced by other build‑time components.

@lcmMakefile::AddDefinitionBool@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddDefinitionBool@k_ZN10cm.body: The method takes a name and a boolean flag, then forwards the name with the string “ON” if the flag is true or “OFF” otherwise, delegating to the generic AddDefinition implementation.

@lcmMakefile::AddEvaluationFile@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddEvaluationFile@k_ZN10cm.body: The function creates a new `cmGeneratorExpressionEvaluationFile` with the supplied parameters and appends it to the `EvaluationFiles` collection held by the `cmMakefile` instance, preserving the original file content flag and configuration values for later use.

@lcmMakefile::AddExecutable@k_ZN10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddExecutable@k_ZN10cmMake.body: Creates a new executable target using the given name and source list, optionally tags it to be omitted from the global “all” target list, registers its sources and links it into the project’s global link information, and returns the constructed target object.

@lcmMakefile::AddExportBuildFileGenerato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddExportBuildFileGenerato.body: Adds a newly created export‑build‑file generator into the makefile’s internal list, transferring ownership of the supplied `unique_ptr` into the collection via `emplace_back`.

@lcmMakefile::AddFunctionBlocker@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddFunctionBlocker@k_ZN10c.body: Adds a newly‑created blocker to the internal stack, attaching the current back‑trace context if any active execution frames exist.

@lcmMakefile::AddGeneratorAction@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddGeneratorAction@k_ZN10c.body: Creates a `GeneratorAction` from the forwarded parameters and forwards that object to the overload that accepts a single `GeneratorAction`.

@lcmMakefile::AddGeneratorAction@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddGeneratorAction@k_ZN10c.body: The method moves an incoming `GeneratorAction` into the `GeneratorActions` container after verifying that no actions have been invoked yet, storing the current back‑trace so the action can be replayed later.

@lcmMakefile::AddGlobalLinkInformation@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddGlobalLinkInformation@k.body: This function inspects a target’s LINK_LIBRARIES property, skipping utility‑style targets, and iterates over the list of library names. For each name it determines whether the library is marked “optimized” or “debug”, setting the corresponding library type flag. It then adds the library to the target’s link list and records the debug‑generation expression under the INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES property.

@lcmMakefile::AddImportedTarget@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddImportedTarget@k_ZN10cm.body: Creates a new `cmTarget`, registers it in the imported‑target maps, records the name in the state snapshot, and returns a raw pointer to the newly owned target. The function simply wires together those bookkeeping structures and hands back the target for further use.

@lcmMakefile::AddIncludeDirectories@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddIncludeDirectories@k_ZN.body: The method updates the internal directory list with a new include‑path entry. It first skips any work when the supplied vector is empty. A string representation of the entire path list is generated, then it is added either at the front or back of the current entry list depending on the *before* flag. Finally every target in the makefile receives the same entry string through its own InsertInclude call.

@lcmMakefile::AddInstallGenerator@k_ZN10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddInstallGenerator@k_ZN10.body: Adds a non‑null `cmInstallGenerator` instance into the object’s internal list, transferring ownership of the pointer via `std::move`.

@lcmMakefile::AddLibrary@k_ZN10cmMakefil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddLibrary@k_ZN10cmMakefil.body: The routine creates a new target of the specified library type, clears any stale dependency metadata, optionally tags the target to be omitted from global “all” listings, registers the supplied source files with the target, and finally records the target in the global link‑info registry before returning the constructed target object.

@lcmMakefile::AddLinkDirectory@k_ZN10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddLinkDirectory@k_ZN10cmM.body:
The method adds a directory to the current snapshot’s list of link‑directories.  
If the `before` flag is true it inserts the new entry at the start of the list; otherwise it appends it to the end. The directory string is wrapped in a `BT<std::string>` instance that also records the current back‑trace for provenance.

@lcmMakefile::AddLinkOption@k_ZN10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddLinkOption@k_ZN10cmMake.body: Adds the supplied string to the internal list of link‑options stored under the “LINK_OPTIONS” key by delegating to `AppendProperty`.

@lcmMakefile::AddNewTarget@k_ZN10cmMakef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddNewTarget@k_ZN10cmMakef.body: Creates a new target of the requested type with the supplied name by calling CreateNewTarget, then returns a pointer to that freshly created target.

@lcmMakefile::AddNewUtilityTarget@k_ZN10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddNewUtilityTarget@k_ZN10.body: Creates a target of type UTILITY and, if requested, tags it with EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL so it isn’t pulled in by the generic “all” target.

@lcmMakefile::AddSourceGroup@k_ZN10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddSourceGroup@k_ZN10cmMak.body: Creates a vector holding the supplied name and forwards that vector, together with the regex string, to the internal overload of AddSourceGroup.

@lcmMakefile::AddSourceGroup@k_ZN10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddSourceGroup@k_ZN10cmMak.body: The method scans a vector of component names from the end toward the start to locate an existing group that matches the provided hierarchy. If such a group exists it updates its regex; otherwise it creates a new group hierarchy by adding a top‑level group and then iteratively adding child groups for each remaining component, linking each new group to its parent. If any step fails, an error is reported.

@lcmMakefile::AddSubDirectory@k_ZN10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddSubDirectory@k_ZN10cmMa.body: AddSubDirectory integrates a new sub‑directory into the current build system. It first validates that the system is not in a deferred‑execution state and that the target binary directory is unique. It then captures a snapshot of the current state, sets the source and binary paths for the new directory, creates a sub‑Makefile instance, and registers it with the global generator. Finally it may configure the sub‑directory immediately or defer that step, and registers an install generator for the new sub‑makefile.

@lcmMakefile::AddSynthesizedTarget@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddSynthesizedTarget@k_ZN1.body: Creates a new synthesized target of the given type and name, adding it as a generated target in the system.

@lcmMakefile::AddSystemIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddSystemIncludeDirectorie.body: Adds the supplied directories to the global system‑include set, then propagates that list to every target so they all search the same paths.

@lcmMakefile::AddTargetObject@k_ZN10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddTargetObject@k_ZN10cmMa.body: The method creates or re‑uses a `cmSourceFile` for the given object file, flags that file as the object library for the specified target name, records it as an external object, and finally inserts the file into the internal source‑group collection (unless the build is bootstrapped). It also leaves a placeholder for determining the object’s language policy.

@lcmMakefile::AddTestGenerator@k_ZN10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddTestGenerator@k_ZN10cmM.body: Adds the supplied `std::unique_ptr<cmTestGenerator>` to the internal list of generators when it is non‑null, transferring ownership with `std::move`.

@lcmMakefile::AddUtilityCommand@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddUtilityCommand@k_ZN10cm.body: Creates a new utility target in the makefile, validates the custom command’s input lines and dependencies, records policy values, creates generated output sources, and registers the command as a generator action so that it can be executed later in the build graph.

@lcmMakefile::AppendCustomCommandToOutpu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AppendCustomCommandToOutpu.body: Validates custom commands, then records a generator action that, during later back‑trace processing, appends the supplied command lines to the specified output file.

@lcmMakefile::AppendProperty@k_ZN10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AppendProperty@k_ZN10cmMak.body: The method forwards a property/value pair to the current directory snapshot. It calls `StateSnapshot.GetDirectory().AppendProperty()` with the supplied property name, value, the `asString` flag, and the instance’s `Backtrace` for tracking.

@lcmMakefile::CanIWriteThisFile@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::CanIWriteThisFile@k_ZNK10c.body: It evaluates whether a file name is permitted to be written in the current source tree by checking build‑mode flags and directory relationships. If source‑changes are enabled, it always returns true. Otherwise, in an in‑source build it permits writing only when the file is in the output directory (or a sub‑directory thereof) and not a sub‑directory of the source tree. If the file is outside the source tree or inside the output tree, it is considered writable.

@lcmMakefile::CheckCMP0037@k_ZNK10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::CheckCMP0037@k_ZNK10cmMake.body: The function verifies that a given target name and type comply with the CMP0037 policy. It examines the current policy status; if the policy is *WARN* and the target is not an interface library, it emits a warning message. If the policy is *REQUIRED_* (either if used or always), the function treats the condition as fatal, returning `false`. In all other cases it simply returns `true`.

@lcmMakefile::ClearMatches@k_ZN10cmMakef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ClearMatches@k_ZN10cmMakef.body: The routine reads the current number of match slots, iterates over that many variables, clears any that are defined, and finally writes back a zero counter while marking every touched variable as used.

@lcmMakefile::Configure@k_ZN10cmMakefile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::Configure@k_ZN10cmMakefile.body: The Configure() routine drives an initial build‑system bootstrap: it records the current source file, ensures the CMakeFiles directory exists, parses the CMakeLists.txt file into a function list, applies policy checks (requiring the cmake_minimum_required() command and injecting a default project() if missing), runs the parsed functions (deferred via DeferCommands), and then recursively configures any sub‑directories that were registered as “UnConfiguredDirectories”. Once all sub‑directories are configured it finalises dependency files from the user.

@lcmMakefile::ConfigureFile@k_ZN10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ConfigureFile@k_ZN10cmMake.body: The routine checks that the target file can be written and that the source file exists; it then either copies the file unchanged or opens it for reading, expands variables and optionally escapes quotes in each line, normalises line endings according to the requested style, writes the result to a temporary file, and finally replaces the original file (restoring the original permissions).

@lcmMakefile::ConfigureString@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ConfigureString@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The routine walks the source string line‑by‑line, rewrites any embedded #cmakedefine or #cmakedefine01 tokens by looking up their definitions, emits the result to the output string, and finally performs a variable expansion pass that may escape quotes depending on the flags.

@lcmMakefile::ConfigureSubDirectory@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ConfigureSubDirectory@k_ZN.body: The function initializes a child `cmMakefile` from its parent, verifies that the child’s source directory contains a `CMakeLists.txt` file, and then—depending on the current policy setting for CMP0014—issues either a warning, normal or fatal message. If the file is present, it calls the child’s `Configure()` routine and logs debug output on entry and exit. If the file is missing, the routine exits early after reporting the appropriate policy‑based issue.

@lcmMakefile::CreateGeneratedOutputs@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::CreateGeneratedOutputs@k_Z.body: The method iterates over the supplied `outputs` vector. For each entry, it checks whether the string already exists in the internal registry (via `cmGeneratorExpression::Find`). If the entry is not found, the method invokes `GetOrCreateGeneratedSource` to ensure a generated source object is created (or retrieved if already present). This routine essentially guarantees that every requested output has an associated source object, creating new ones only when necessary.

@lcmMakefile::CreateNewTarget@k_ZN10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::CreateNewTarget@k_ZN10cmMa.body: The method inserts a new target into the file’s internal map. It creates a `cmTarget` with the supplied name, type, visibility, and configuration, inserts it into `Targets`, and if the insertion succeeded it updates the internal ordered list, indexes the target in the global generator, and registers the target name in the state snapshot. It then returns a pair: a reference to the newly‑created target and a boolean flag that is `true` when the target was newly created (or `false` if an entry already existed).

@lcmMakefile::CreateSource@k_ZN10cmMakef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::CreateSource@k_ZN10cmMakef.body: CreateSource registers a new source file instance. It first allocates a unique cmSourceFile object, computes a normalised file‑name (lower‑casing on Windows/Apple for case‑insensitive lookup), and appends the file to two lookup tables: SourceFileSearchIndex for general lookup and, if the file is of type Known, to KnownFileSearchIndex for fast “known‑path” queries. The newly created file is then stored in SourceFiles and a pointer to this object is returned.

@lcmMakefile::CreateTest@k_ZN10cmMakefil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::CreateTest@k_ZN10cmMakefil.body: The function first asks the current object whether a test with the supplied name already exists. If `GetTest` finds an existing instance, it is returned immediately. When no such test is found, the code creates a new `cmTest` instance via the helper `cm::make_unique`. It sets the test’s name, inserts the newly‑created instance into the internal `Tests` map (moving the unique pointer into that container), and finally returns a raw pointer to the newly inserted test.

@lcmMakefile::DebugFindPkgRAII::DebugFin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::DebugFindPkgRAII::DebugFin.body: The constructor stores the current value of `DebugFindPkg` from the `cmMakefile` instance, then assigns the result of `GetCMakeInstance()->GetDebugFindPkgOutput(pkg)` to that member. This effectively updates the makefile’s debug‑find‑pkg flag to the value returned for the specified package.

@lcmMakefile::DebugFindPkgRAII::~DebugFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::DebugFindPkgRAII::~DebugFi.body: Restores the Makefile’s debug flag to the value stored in OldValue, effectively reverting any temporary changes made during the debug find operation.

@lcmMakefile::DeferCall@k_ZN10cmMakefile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::DeferCall@k_ZN10cmMakefile.body: The routine validates that the internal `Defer` member is set; if it isn’t, it fails immediately. When `Defer` is present, it appends a new `DeferCommand` constructed from the supplied id, file path and list function into that member’s `Commands` container and reports success.

@lcmMakefile::DeferCancelCall@k_ZN10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::DeferCancelCall@k_ZN10cmMa.body: When the internal `Defer` object exists, the routine walks through its `Commands` list and empties the `Id` field of any entry whose `Id` matches the supplied string. If no such entry is found or the `Defer` object is absent, it returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmMakefile::DeferGetCall@k_ZNK10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::DeferGetCall@k_ZNK10cmMake.body: The method searches the stored “deferred” commands for the supplied identifier, concatenates the original command name with each of its arguments (separated by semicolons), and returns that string wrapped in an optional; if no match is found or the defer list is empty, it returns an empty optional.

@lcmMakefile::DeferGetCallIds@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::DeferGetCallIds@k_ZNK10cmM.body: Returns an optional string containing the concatenated Id values of every `DeferCommand` in the `Defer` list that has a non‑empty Id. If the `Defer` pointer is null or no commands satisfy the filter, the optional is empty.

@lcmMakefile::DisplayStatus@k_ZNK10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::DisplayStatus@k_ZNK10cmMak.body: The function first checks if the current CMake instance is in FIND_PACKAGE_MODE; if so, it exits immediately. Otherwise it updates the build progress with the supplied message and completion percentage. If compiled with debugging support and a debug adapter is present, it forwards that message to the adapter for debugging output.

@lcmMakefile::DoGenerate@k_ZN10cmMakefil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::DoGenerate@k_ZN10cmMakefil.body: The `DoGenerate` routine expands all variables, executes every registered generator action once, marks the action phase as completed, and then prunes any output or list‑file entries that refer to files that are not persisted (i.e., were created only transiently during the run).

@lcmMakefile::EnableLanguage@k_ZN10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::EnableLanguage@k_ZN10cmMak.body: It validates that no deferred build is in progress, registers the internal configuration directory, removes duplicate language entries while warning about repeated requests, and finally enables the languages in two phases: first the non‑RC ones, then the RC‑specific language if present.

@lcmMakefile::EnforceDirectoryLevelRules.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::EnforceDirectoryLevelRules.body: The routine checks that the current Makefile contains a `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION …)` directive. If that line is missing, it builds a diagnostic message and, depending on the project’s policy setting for CMP0000, it either issues a warning, silently continues (for older policy), or aborts with a fatal error, marking that a fatal error has occurred.

@lcmMakefile::EnforceUniqueDir@k_ZNK10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::EnforceUniqueDir@k_ZNK10cm.body: The routine verifies that the chosen binary directory is not already in use for a different source tree. If the directory is already employed, it emits an appropriate diagnostic (a warning or fatal error depending on the current policy) and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmMakefile::EnforceUniqueName@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::EnforceUniqueName@k_ZNK10c.body: EnforceUniqueName checks whether a requested target name conflicts with an existing alias or target. If the name already exists, it reports a message explaining the conflict and returns false. It respects policy CMP0002: in the WARN case it emits a warning; in OLD it allows the conflict; in REQUIRED cases it triggers a fatal error; in NEW it accepts the name. Custom targets may override the conflict if the user has enabled the global ALLOW_DUPLICATE_CUSTOM_TARGETS flag. If none of those apply, it returns true only when the name is unique and no conflict remains.

@lcmMakefile::ExecuteCommand@k_ZN10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ExecuteCommand@k_ZN10cmMak.body:
The function first checks whether the specified command is blocked, returning immediately if so.  
If a callback is set, it triggers that callback.  
It then registers the command in a call‑stack manager (the stack manager is simply constructed and discarded, which has the side‑effect of registering the call).  
Next it guards against excessive recursion: if the current depth exceeds the configured limit, it logs a fatal error and aborts the operation.  
If a suitable command prototype is found, the function optionally prints trace information (if tracing is enabled) and then invokes the command with the supplied arguments. The command’s return value and any nested error state are inspected; if invocation fails or a nested error is present, the function reports a fatal error, optionally sets a fatal‑error flag, and marks the operation as failed.  
If no matching command is found, it reports an unknown command fatal error and flags a fatal‑error state.  
Finally, it returns the success flag (`result`).

@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesCMP0019@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesCMP0019@k_Z.body:
The routine scans the current policy setting for CMP0019.  
If the policy is either OLD or WARN it expands any %-style variables that appear in the `INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES` value of the project and of each target.  
During expansion it records any actual changes of the value and, when the policy is WARN, reports them via a warning message.  
The same logic applies to the `LINK_DIRECTORIES` and `LINK_LIBRARIES` properties.

@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesInString@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesInString@k_.body: The method expands environment‑style tokens in the supplied string. It simply forwards the call to the full‑argument overload, supplying `false` for both optional flags, and then returns the resulting string by reference.

@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesInString@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesInString@k_.body: The function expands variables in a string according to the current policy setting. It first validates that the “at‑only” mode isn’t conflict with escape options, then dispatches to one of three internal implementations: the old algorithm, a new algorithm, or a warning‑mode that keeps the original string and logs a difference if the new algorithm changes the result. Errors or fatal conditions trigger a fatal error flag. The function performs string substitutions, handles quoting and back‑slash escapes, and, when the new policy differs from the old one, emits a warning about the change. Finally it returns the (possibly modified) source string.

@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesInStringNew.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesInStringNew.body: The routine scans the input string, detects variable tokens in the forms `${VAR}`, `@VAR@`, `$ENV{VAR}`, and `$CACHE{VAR}`, looks up each token in the appropriate source (internal map, environment, or cache), and substitutes it with the resolved value. It handles nested braces, escape sequences, and tracks unmatched variables to report an error, finally returning a message type to indicate success or failure.

@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesInStringOld.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ExpandVariablesInStringOld.body: The function expands $‑style and @‑style placeholders in a string, using a regex‑based scan for @VAR@ when the `atOnly` flag is set, otherwise delegating parsing to a helper that supports ${VAR} and $ENV{VAR} syntax and handles quoting/escaping and error reporting.

@lcmMakefile::FindLocalNonAliasTarget@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FindLocalNonAliasTarget@k_.body: The `FindLocalNonAliasTarget` function looks up a target by name in the internal map `Targets`. If the key exists it returns a pointer to the stored `cmTarget` object; otherwise it returns `nullptr`. The lookup is a single‑hash‑table (or red‑black tree) find operation, so it runs in expected O(1) time. It does not modify the map and thus preserves const‑correctness.

@lcmMakefile::FindSourceGroup@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FindSourceGroup@k_ZNK10cmM.body: FindSourceGroup searches through a list of source‑group objects for a match to a given file name. It first checks each group’s explicit file list, then falls back to checking any regular‑expression patterns that group declares. If neither applies, it falls back to a default “catch‑all” group.

@lcmMakefile::FindTargetToUse@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FindTargetToUse@k_ZNK10cmM.body: This function resolves a target name to an actual `cmTarget` instance by following a priority chain: first it checks for a local alias (unless `excludeAliases` is true), then looks up an imported target, otherwise falls back to a locally defined target, and finally to a globally defined target via the project’s global generator.

@lcmMakefile::FormatListFileStack@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FormatListFileStack@k_ZNK1.body: The function walks up the call‑stack snapshots, collects each `GetExecutionListFile()` into a vector, reverses it, then builds a string that lists each file prefixed by its depth level in the stack, each line indented appropriately, and finally returns that string.

@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::FunctionP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::FunctionP.body: The constructor registers a new function scope in the `Makefile` instance – it forwards the supplied `fileName` and policy map to `PushFunctionScope`, which records the function’s definition and associated policy information for later processing.

@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::FunctionP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::FunctionP.body: The `FunctionPushPop` helper encapsulates a “push‑on‑construction, pop‑on‑destruction” guard pattern. When you instantiate it inside a block, the constructor records the current state (often a stack or map entry) and the destructor restores that state automatically, ensuring the original context is reinstated even if exceptions are thrown. The copy constructor is intentionally deleted to enforce unique ownership semantics and prevent accidental copying of the guard object.

@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::Quiet@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::Quiet@k_Z.body: The method clears the `ReportError` flag on the current object, effectively turning off any error‑reporting that would normally be triggered.

@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::operator=.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::operator=.body:
`operator=` returns a reference to the object but is explicitly deleted.  
This means instances of `FunctionPushPop` cannot be copy‑assigned; attempting to assign one object to another will be a compile‑time error, preventing accidental or unintended copying.

@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::~Function.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FunctionPushPop::~Function.body: When a `FunctionPushPop` instance is destroyed, its destructor removes the corresponding function scope from the owning `Makefile` by calling `PopFunctionScope` with the previously stored `ReportError` object.

@lcmMakefile::Generate@k_ZN10cmMakefile8.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::Generate@k_ZN10cmMakefile8.body: The `Generate` routine invokes the generator’s internal generation logic (`DoGenerate`), then interrogates the current `CMAKE_BACKWARDS_COMPATIBILITY` definition. If that definition is present and indicates a CMake version older than 2.4, it triggers a fatal error message explaining that only CMake 2.4 or newer is supported—and advises using a 2.8.x release for older‑compatible setups.

@lcmMakefile::GeneratorAction::Generator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GeneratorAction::Generator.body: Initializes an instance of the base `Action` class by forwarding the supplied action object via `std::move`. The constructor simply delegates construction to the base class without performing any additional logic.

@lcmMakefile::GeneratorAction::Generator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GeneratorAction::Generator.body: The constructor takes a `std::unique_ptr` to a `cmCustomCommand` and an rvalue reference of type `CCActionT`. It forwards the second argument to the base class `CCAction` and stores the pointer in the member `cc`, transferring ownership with `std::move`.

@lcmMakefile::GeneratorAction::operator(.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GeneratorAction::operator(.body: When the internal condition `cc` is true, the operator forwards the current generator and back‑trace to `CCAction`, moving `cc` into it; if not, it asserts a valid `Action` exists and then calls that action with the same arguments.

@lcmMakefile::GetAliasTargets@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetAliasTargets@k_ZNK10cmM.body: Returns a copy of the internal map that links alias identifiers to their concrete target strings, letting callers query which target string corresponds to any given alias.

@lcmMakefile::GetAppleSDKType@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetAppleSDKType@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The function obtains the CMake system’s current OSX SDK root directory, lower‑cases it, and then iterates over a hard‑coded map of known SDK names. If the root string starts with or contains one of those names (or a slash‑separated form of it), the corresponding AppleSDK enumeration value is returned; otherwise it falls back to `AppleSDK::MacOS`.

@lcmMakefile::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK10cmMake.body: The function simply returns the `Backtrace` member of the current `cmMakefile` instance.

@lcmMakefile::GetCMakeInstance@k_ZNK10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCMakeInstance@k_ZNK10cm.body: The member function simply forwards a call to the `GlobalGenerator` object: it returns the `CMake*` instance that the generator holds. It performs no additional logic; it merely returns the pointer stored in `GlobalGenerator`.

@lcmMakefile::GetCompileDefinitionsEntri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCompileDefinitionsEntri.body: This member fetches the compile‑definition entries from the current snapshot’s directory, delegating the call straight to the `StateSnapshot` instance.

@lcmMakefile::GetCompileOptionsEntries@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCompileOptionsEntries@k.body: It pulls the compile‑options string list from the current snapshot’s directory and returns that list.

@lcmMakefile::GetComplainRegularExpressi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetComplainRegularExpressi.body: Returns a const reference to the stored regex string used to locate complaint‑file paths.

@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentBinaryDirectory@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentBinaryDirectory@.body: The method returns a reference to the string that represents the current binary directory stored in the state snapshot. It simply forwards the reference from `StateSnapshot.GetDirectory().GetCurrentBinary()` without copying.

@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentLogLevel@k_ZNK10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentLogLevel@k_ZNK10.body: It grabs the CMake instance, pulls the CLI‑specified log level, and if that is unset it falls back to the value stored in the CMAKE_MESSAGE_LOG_LEVEL variable before returning that level.

@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentSourceDirectory@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentSourceDirectory@.body: This member simply forwards a const reference to the current source‑directory string stored in the object’s state snapshot.

@lcmMakefile::GetCustomCommandTarget@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCustomCommandTarget@k_Z.body: The function looks up a target in the internal map of targets. If the target is missing it emits a warning or error message based on the current policy setting; for object‑library or interface‑library targets it additionally rejects them with a fatal error and returns `nullptr`. If the target exists and passes these checks, the function simply returns a pointer to that target.

@lcmMakefile::GetDebugFindPkgMode@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDebugFindPkgMode@k_ZNK1.body: This member function simply returns the current value of the `DebugFindPkg` flag. It is a read‑only accessor that tells callers whether the debug‑find‑package mode is enabled for the `cmMakefile` instance.

@lcmMakefile::GetDefaultConfiguration@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDefaultConfiguration@k_.body: The function first checks whether the current generator is multi‑configuration. If that is true, it returns an empty string; otherwise it queries the safe definition of the key `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` and returns that value.

@lcmMakefile::GetDefineFlags@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDefineFlags@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: Retrieves the value stored in the member variable `DefineFlags`.  The function is marked `const`, guaranteeing it does not modify the object, simply exposing the current flag string.

@lcmMakefile::GetDefineFlagsCMP0059@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDefineFlagsCMP0059@k_ZN.body: It’s a trivial accessor that returns the raw string stored in the object. The function is marked `const` so it guarantees no state changes, and it simply returns the internal `DefineFlagsOrig` member’s C‑style string via `c_str()`. The returned pointer points to that string’s data and is valid until the object is destroyed or the string is modified.

@lcmMakefile::GetDefinition@k_ZNK10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDefinition@k_ZNK10cmMak.body: GetDefinition first queries the current state snapshot for a definition by name. If that lookup fails, it falls back to an initialized‑cache lookup. When variable‑watching is active, the function reports the access to the watcher; if that callback mutates the storage, GetDefinition re‑retrieves the value to reflect any change. The returned cmValue is the resolved definition (or null).

@lcmMakefile::GetDefinitions@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDefinitions@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: The method gathers all unique definition keys currently present in the build‑state: it first extracts the keys from the snapshot’s closure collection, then appends the keys of every cached entry, finally sorting the combined list before returning it.

@lcmMakefile::GetDirectoryId@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDirectoryId@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: The function creates a string containing the memory address of the current instance, formatted as “(address)”. It simply returns that value as an identifier for the directory.

@lcmMakefile::GetEvaluationFiles@k_ZNK10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetEvaluationFiles@k_ZNK10.body: Provides read‑only access to the stored vector of evaluation files.

@lcmMakefile::GetExportBuildFileGenerato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetExportBuildFileGenerato.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the internal collection of export‑build‑file generators so callers can enumerate the generators without modifying the underlying vector.

@lcmMakefile::GetGeneratorConfigs@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetGeneratorConfigs@k_ZNK1.body: The `GetGeneratorConfigs` member collects the configuration identifiers that the current generator should expose. It first checks whether the global generator supports multiple configurations. If it does, it pulls the list of available configuration types from the “CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES” definition. When the generator isn’t multi‑config, and the requested mode isn’t request only that case, the function looks up the single “CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE” definition and, if present, appends that single value to the list. If the caller asked for an empty configuration slot (`IncludeEmptyConfig`) and no configurations have been collected yet, it inserts a single empty string to represent that slot. Finally, it returns the built list (moving the vector to avoid copying).

@lcmMakefile::GetGlobalGenerator@k_ZNK10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetGlobalGenerator@k_ZNK10.body: The method simply returns the pointer stored in the `GlobalGenerator` member; because the method is `const`, it promises not to modify any member variables. The returned pointer is a direct reference to that internal object, so callers should not modify it unless they intentionally do so. This function doesn’t perform any checks or allocate new objects—it just hands off the stored pointer as is.

@lcmMakefile::GetHomeDirectory@k_ZNK10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetHomeDirectory@k_ZNK10cm.body: Retrieves the home‑directory string stored in the underlying CMake instance and returns it as a const reference.

@lcmMakefile::GetHomeOutputDirectory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetHomeOutputDirectory@k_Z.body: Returns the current build‑output directory by delegating to the underlying `CMake` instance—essentially a thin wrapper that forwards the request to `GetCMakeInstance()->GetHomeOutputDirectory()`.

@lcmMakefile::GetImportedTargets@k_ZNK10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetImportedTargets@k_ZNK10.body: The function returns a freshly‑allocated vector that contains the pointers stored in the internal `ImportedTargets` collection. It iterates over that collection, copies each target pointer into a local vector, and finally returns that vector to the caller.

@lcmMakefile::GetIncludeDirectoriesEntri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetIncludeDirectoriesEntri.body: This method fetches the include‑directory list stored in the current snapshot by delegating to the underlying directory object and returns that list.

@lcmMakefile::GetIncludeRegularExpressio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetIncludeRegularExpressio.body: The method simply returns a constant reference to the “INCLUDE_REGULAR_EXPRESSION” property string stored in the object, delegating the lookup to `GetProperty`.

@lcmMakefile::GetInstallGenerators@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetInstallGenerators@k_ZN1.body: The `GetInstallGenerators` function returns a (read‑only) reference to the internal `InstallGenerators` vector – a vector of `unique_ptr` objects that point to `cmInstallGenerator` instances. It exposes the current set of install generators without allowing external modification of the vector itself, though the pointed‑to objects can still be altered.

@lcmMakefile::GetInstallGenerators@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetInstallGenerators@k_ZNK.body: The function returns a read‑only reference to the internal collection of `cmInstallGenerator` objects stored in `InstallGenerators`, guaranteeing callers cannot modify the underlying vector.

@lcmMakefile::GetIsSourceFileTryCompile@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetIsSourceFileTryCompile@.body: Returns the value of the `IsSourceFileTryCompile` flag, indicating whether the source file should be attempted for compilation.

@lcmMakefile::GetLinkDirectoriesEntries@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetLinkDirectoriesEntries@.body: Retrieves the collection of link‑directory entries stored in the current state snapshot by delegating to the directory helper and returns that cmBTStringRange.

@lcmMakefile::GetLinkOptionsEntries@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetLinkOptionsEntries@k_ZN.body: Retrieves the link‑options entries stored in the current snapshot’s directory object, returning that string range.

@lcmMakefile::GetListFiles@k_ZNK10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetListFiles@k_ZNK10cmMake.body: Returns a const reference to the internal vector that holds the file names, letting callers read the list without copying or altering the stored data.

@lcmMakefile::GetMessenger@k_ZNK10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetMessenger@k_ZNK10cmMake.body: The method simply fetches the messenger that belongs to the `CMake` instance that owns this `cmMakefile`. It does this by delegating to the `GetCMakeInstance()` accessor (which itself already guarantees the instance exists) and then returns the messenger returned by that instance. No new object is created; it’s a direct forwarder that keeps the class opaque to any caller.

@lcmMakefile::GetModulesFile@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetModulesFile@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: The method forwards the request to another overload, passing an uninitialised boolean flag and a debug buffer string that it leaves unchanged, returning whatever string the underlying implementation produces.

@lcmMakefile::GetModulesFile@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetModulesFile@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: The function simply forwards its arguments to the more detailed overload by creating an empty `debugBuffer` string and passing it along. It returns whatever string that overload produces, taking the caller’s `system` flag by reference.

@lcmMakefile::GetModulesFile@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetModulesFile@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: The function searches for a module file with the supplied name first in the directories listed by the CMAKE_MODULE_PATH variable; if none is found, it falls back to the standard “Modules” directory under the CMake root. It returns the first matching path it discovers, sets the `system` flag to true if that path came from the module‑path search (indicating a system module), otherwise leaves it false, and, when debug is enabled, appends each attempted path to the supplied `debugBuffer` while optionally issuing a warning if both paths exist according to policy CMP0017.

@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateGeneratedSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateGeneratedSource.body: This routine fetches or creates a source file under the known‑location kind, tags the resulting object as generated via MarkAsGenerated(), and hands it back to the caller.

@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSource@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSource@k_ZN10cm.body: The function checks if a source file already exists for the given name and kind; if found, it returns that existing `cmSourceFile` instance, otherwise it creates a new source via `CreateSource` and returns it.

@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSourceGroup@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSourceGroup@k_Z.body: `GetOrCreateSourceGroup` takes a name string, looks up the special delimiter definition (defaulting to “/\\” if absent), tokenizes the input using that delimiter, and then hands the resulting token list to the internal `GetOrCreateSourceGroup` routine that actually creates or fetches the matching `cmSourceGroup`.

@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSourceGroup@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSourceGroup@k_Z.body:
This routine checks whether a source‑group object already exists for a particular list of folder names.  
If it cannot be found (`GetSourceGroup` returns `nullptr`), it creates a new group via `AddSourceGroup` and then fetches the fresh entry again. Finally, it returns the pointer to the located or newly created group.

@lcmMakefile::GetOrderedTargets@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOrderedTargets@k_ZNK10c.body: It returns a read‑only reference to the internally stored list of targets that have already been sorted and ordered.

@lcmMakefile::GetOutputFiles@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOutputFiles@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: The function returns a const reference to the internal `OutputFiles` member, providing read‑only access without copying the vector’s contents.

@lcmMakefile::GetOwnedImportedTargets@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOwnedImportedTargets@k_.body: The function simply returns a reference to the internal vector that holds the imported targets owned by the instance.

@lcmMakefile::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZNK10cmM.body: Retrieves the current status for a policy identified by `id`, optionally constrained to the parent scope, delegating the work to the internal `StateSnapshot` member.

@lcmMakefile::GetProperty@k_ZNK10cmMakef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetProperty@k_ZNK10cmMakef.body: The `GetProperty` member of `cmMakefile` retrieves the value for a named property. When the requested name is `"TESTS"`, it returns a string containing the names of all test entries in the internal `Tests` map; otherwise it forwards the query to the `StateSnapshot` directory. The routine constructs the key list by copying the first element from each pair in the map, joins them into a comma‑separated string via `cmList::to_string`, and wraps that string in a `cmValue` to return.

@lcmMakefile::GetProperty@k_ZNK10cmMakef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetProperty@k_ZNK10cmMakef.body: It forwards the property query to the stored state snapshot’s directory and returns the result as a `cmValue`.

@lcmMakefile::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK10c.body: The function simply checks whether a named property evaluates to an “on” value by delegating to `GetProperty` and feeding the returned string into `cmIsOn`. It returns true when that helper deems the property string truthy (e.g. “1”, “yes”, “on”), and false otherwise. If `GetProperty` fails or returns an empty string, the call to `cmIsOn` will return false.

@lcmMakefile::GetPropertyKeys@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetPropertyKeys@k_ZNK10cmM.body: It pulls the list of property keys from the current snapshot’s directory by delegating the call to the `GetDirectory()` helper and returns that vector.

@lcmMakefile::GetRecursionDepth@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetRecursionDepth@k_ZNK10c.body: Returns the value stored in the `RecursionDepth` member, exposing the current recursion depth as a `size_t`.

@lcmMakefile::GetRecursionDepthLimit@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetRecursionDepthLimit@k_Z.body: The function reads the maximum recursion depth setting from the project’s definition; if that’s missing it falls back to an environment variable, and if parsing succeeds it replaces the default value. The resolved value is then returned as a `size_t`.

@lcmMakefile::GetRequiredDefinition@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetRequiredDefinition@k_ZN.body: The function tries to fetch a definition by name; if it isn’t found it logs an error via cmSystemTools::Error and returns an empty string, otherwise it returns the retrieved definition.

@lcmMakefile::GetSONameFlag@k_ZNK10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSONameFlag@k_ZNK10cmMak.body: This method builds a macro key by appending an underscore‑separated language tag to the base string `CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_SONAME`, then appending `"_FLAG"`. It then retrieves the corresponding string definition via `GetDefinition`, returning a C‑style pointer to that string.

@lcmMakefile::GetSafeDefinition@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSafeDefinition@k_ZNK10c.body: Returns a const reference to the string obtained from `GetDefinition(name)` – it simply forwards the call and returns the result unchanged.

@lcmMakefile::GetSource@k_ZNK10cmMakefil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSource@k_ZNK10cmMakefil.body: The `GetSource` function searches for a source file registered under a given name and location kind. If the file is already known, it returns the stored instance immediately. If not, it constructs a `cmSourceFileLocation` for the requested name, normalises the name (including stripping extensions and, on Windows/Apple, lower‑casing it), and then probes the internal search index. When a matching `cmSourceFile` is found in that index, the function returns it; otherwise, it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmMakefile::GetSourceFiles@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSourceFiles@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: This const member returns a reference to the internal `SourceFiles` vector, exposing it as a read‑only container of `std::unique_ptr<cmSourceFile>` objects. The function merely provides access to the existing collection without copying or modifying it.

@lcmMakefile::GetSourceGroup@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSourceGroup@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: The routine walks the stored source‑group collection in order, first matching the first name component; on success it descends through the matched group’s children via `LookupChild` until the entire name path is consumed, returning the located group or `nullptr` if any segment fails to match.

@lcmMakefile::GetSourceGroups@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSourceGroups@k_ZNK10cmM.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the internal `SourceGroups` member (a `std::vector<cmSourceGroup>`). The method is `const` so callers cannot modify the underlying vector.

@lcmMakefile::GetState@k_ZNK10cmMakefile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetState@k_ZNK10cmMakefile.body: Returns a pointer to the current cmState by delegating the call to the underlying CMake instance; it simply forwards the request and returns whatever pointer that instance returns.

@lcmMakefile::GetStateSnapshot@k_ZNK10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetStateSnapshot@k_ZNK10cm.body: Returns the current StateSnapshot held by the object. The const accessor simply returns that member value—no mutation occurs.

@lcmMakefile::GetSystemIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSystemIncludeDirectorie.body: The function returns a constant reference to the internal `SystemIncludeDirectories` set, providing read‑only access to the stored include directories without copying the container.

@lcmMakefile::GetTargets@k_ZN10cmMakefil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetTargets@k_ZN10cmMakefil.body: It returns a reference to the internal `cmTargetMap` member so callers can inspect or modify the stored target mappings directly.

@lcmMakefile::GetTargets@k_ZNK10cmMakefi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetTargets@k_ZNK10cmMakefi.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the internal map that associates each target with its configuration data, allowing callers to inspect the current target set without permitting modification.

@lcmMakefile::GetTest@k_ZNK10cmMakefile7.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetTest@k_ZNK10cmMakefile7.body: The function looks up a test name in the internal map `Tests`. If an entry exists it returns the raw pointer stored in that map entry; otherwise it returns `nullptr`. The method is read‑only (`const`), so the caller receives a non‑const pointer that may be used to modify the test object.

@lcmMakefile::GetTestGenerators@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetTestGenerators@k_ZNK10c.body: Returns the internal collection of test generators stored in the object. The method simply provides read‑only access to that vector, exposing each element as a `unique_ptr` that cannot be modified through the returned reference.

@lcmMakefile::GetTests@k_ZNK10cmMakefile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetTests@k_ZNK10cmMakefile.body: The function iterates through all test generators owned by the instance. For each generator that reports it can produce tests for the supplied configuration string, it pushes that generator’s test onto the vector passed in. The resulting vector contains only the tests that match the provided configuration.

@lcmMakefile::GetVariableWatch@k_ZNK10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetVariableWatch@k_ZNK10cm.body: It returns a pointer to the `VariableWatch` owned by the current CMake instance—if that instance exists and has a watch, otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmMakefile::HasCMP0054AlreadyBeenRepor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::HasCMP0054AlreadyBeenRepor.body:
The function inserts the supplied `context` into the member `CMP0054ReportedIds`.  
If the insertion succeeds (`second` is true), the context was not reported before, and the function returns `false`.  
If the insertion fails (`second` is false because the key already exists), the function returns `true`, indicating the context was previously reported.

@lcmMakefile::IgnoreErrorsCMP0061@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IgnoreErrorsCMP0061@k_ZNK1.body: The function checks the current policy status for the CMP0061 policy. It sets `ignoreErrors` to false only when the status is `cmPolicies::NEW`; in all other cases it keeps the default value of true (or simply returns the current value). The function finally returns that flag.

@lcmMakefile::InitCMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TY.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::InitCMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TY.body: The method guarantees that the CMake cache entry **CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES** exists; if the entry is absent, it assigns the supplied default string and registers it in the cache as a semicolon‑separated list of supported configuration types.

@lcmMakefile::InitializeFromParent@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::InitializeFromParent@k_ZN1.body: The function copies the parent cmMakefile’s entire configuration into the current instance: it re‑sets the system‑include directories, propagates the flag sets, propagates the implicit‑include‑transform property, propagates compile‑definition properties (including per‑config overrides when the CMP0043 policy is in WARN/OLD mode), copies the label list, link‑library list, and projects the project name and file‑regex settings, and finally transfers the imported target lists and recursion depth counter. The result is a child makefile whose settings mirror those of its parent.

@lcmMakefile::IsAlias@k_ZNK10cmMakefile7.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsAlias@k_ZNK10cmMakefile7.body: The function reports whether a given name is an alias: it first checks the instance’s own `AliasTargets` list, and if not found, defers to the global generator’s alias lookup. It returns `true` only when the name is present in either of those two checks.

@lcmMakefile::IsDefinitionSet@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsDefinitionSet@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The function checks whether a named definition exists in the internal state. It first asks the current snapshot for the definition; if it’s missing, it falls back to the cache of initialized values. When compiled with the variable‑watching flag, it records an access event for unknown variables so they can be traced later. The function finally returns true if any of those look‑ups yields a non‑null value, otherwise false.

@lcmMakefile::IsFunctionBlocked@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsFunctionBlocked@k_ZN10cm.body: The function checks whether any blockers exist; if the blocker stack is empty it immediately reports “not blocked” (returns false). Otherwise it forwards the check to the top blocker by calling its IsFunctionBlocked with the same arguments, returning that blocker’s result.

@lcmMakefile::IsImportedTargetGlobalScop.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsImportedTargetGlobalScop.body: The function returns true when the instance’s `CurrentImportedTargetScope` member equals the `ImportedTargetScope::Global` enumeration value.

@lcmMakefile::IsLoopBlock@k_ZNK10cmMakef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsLoopBlock@k_ZNK10cmMakef.body: The function asserts that the loop‐counter stack is non‑empty and then returns true only when the current top value of that stack is greater than zero, signalling that the current context is inside a loop block.

@lcmMakefile::IsNormalDefinitionSet@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsNormalDefinitionSet@k_ZN.body: The function fetches the definition from the snapshot, notifies any variable‑watcher that a previously‑unknown variable has been defined, and then simply returns whether the definition pointer is non‑null.

@lcmMakefile::IsOn@k_ZNK10cmMakefile4IsO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsOn@k_ZNK10cmMakefile4IsO.body: It forwards the name to `GetDefinition`, then hands the resulting definition object to `cmIsOn` and returns that status.

@lcmMakefile::IsProjectFile@k_ZNK10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsProjectFile@k_ZNK10cmMak.body: This function returns `true` when a file path is located in the project’s home directory or in the output directory, except if the path falls inside the `CMakeFiles` sub‑directory.

@lcmMakefile::IsRootMakefile@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsRootMakefile@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: The function returns true when the current makefile has no valid parent directory (i.e., it sits at the root of the build‑system tree).

@lcmMakefile::IsSet@k_ZNK10cmMakefile5Is.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsSet@k_ZNK10cmMakefile5Is.body: The function retrieves a value for the given name; if the lookup fails, the string is empty, or the value is flagged as *NOTFOUND*, it returns false; otherwise it reports true.

@lcmMakefile::IssueMessage@k_ZNK10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IssueMessage@k_ZNK10cmMake.body: The function checks whether an error‑level message should mark the current execution context as nested, then forwards the message along with back‑trace information to the CMake instance for handling.

@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::MacroPushPop.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::MacroPushPop.body: Creates a new macro scope in the current makefile by forwarding the supplied file name and policy map to the underlying Makefile’s PushMacroScope routine.

@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::MacroPushPop.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::MacroPushPop.body: MacroPushPop temporarily pushes a macro onto the current context and automatically restores the previous macro when the object is destroyed, ensuring that macro state changes are confined to the object's lifetime.

@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::Quiet@k_ZN10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::Quiet@k_ZN10.body: The `Quiet()` function simply disables error reporting by setting the `ReportError` flag to `false`.

@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::operator=@k_.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents copying or assigning a `MacroPushPop` instance, enforcing that objects of this type must be constructed or moved only via explicit moves, and cannot be implicitly reassigned.

@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::~MacroPushPo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::MacroPushPop::~MacroPushPo.body: This destructor calls `Makefile->PopMacroScope(ReportError)`, releasing the macro scope that was pushed earlier.

@lcmMakefile::MarkVariableAsUsed@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::MarkVariableAsUsed@k_ZN10c.body: Records a variable name in the internal state snapshot to note that the variable has been referenced.

@lcmMakefile::MaybeWarnCMP0074@k_ZN10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::MaybeWarnCMP0074@k_ZN10cmM.body: The method checks whether a root variable was defined either in the project file or in the environment. If it has been defined and this variable has not yet triggered a warning, it writes a compatibility warning that CMake will ignore the variable and reports the current value(s) to the user.

@lcmMakefile::MaybeWarnCMP0144@k_ZN10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::MaybeWarnCMP0144@k_ZN10cmM.body: When a package‑root variable is present—either as a defined value or an environment override—and a warning for that variable has not already been emitted, the routine logs a single notice. The notice lists the supplied definition and/or environment value (if any) and points out that the standard find_package routine will ignore that variable, though a custom CMake module could still reference it.

@lcmMakefile::MaybeWarnUninitialized@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::MaybeWarnUninitialized@k_Z.body:
The method checks whether a variable was previously initialized.  
If the “warn‑on‑uninit” flag is enabled and the variable hasn’t been marked as initialized, it generates a warning message—only when the source file belongs to the current project or is a system variable.

@lcmMakefile::NewDeferId@k_ZNK10cmMakefi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::NewDeferId@k_ZNK10cmMakefi.body: The function `NewDeferId` simply forwards a request for a fresh defer‑identifier to the global generator by calling `GetGlobalGenerator()->NewDeferId()`, and returns that identifier string.

@lcmMakefile::OnExecuteCommand@k_ZN10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::OnExecuteCommand@k_ZN10cmM.body: Assigns the supplied `std::function<void()>` to the internal `ExecuteCommandCallback` member by moving it, thus preserving the callable for later execution.

@lcmMakefile::ParseDefineFlag@k_ZN10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ParseDefineFlag@k_ZN10cmMa.body: The function receives a `-D`/`/D` flag string, validates its syntax against simple regexes, and then applies the CMP0005 policy to decide whether a non‑trivial definition is acceptable. If the policy allows it, the flag is either added to or removed from the `COMPILE_DEFINITIONS` property; otherwise a warning or fatal error is emitted and the flag is rejected.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformIs32Bit@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformIs32Bit@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The routine first checks whether the “CMAKE_INTERNAL_PLATFORM_ABI” definition is defined; if its value equals the string “ELF X32”, it immediately returns false (indicating a 32‑bit ABI is not in use). Otherwise it falls back to the standard 64‑bit test: it asks for “CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P” and returns true only if that value parses to the integer 4 (the size of a pointer on a 32‑bit system). In every other circumstance it yields false.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformIs64Bit@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformIs64Bit@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The function `PlatformIs64Bit` returns `true` when the macro `CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P` expands to the string representation of the value `8`, implying a 64‑bit pointer size; otherwise it returns `false`. If the macro is not defined or the expansion is not a numeric string, the comparison will fail and the function will fall back to `false`.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsAppleEmbedded@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsAppleEmbedded@k_.body: The method simply checks whether the current Apple SDK is not the regular macOS SDK; if it isn’t, the function returns true, indicating an embedded Apple platform is in use.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsAppleSimulator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsAppleSimulator@k.body: Returns true if the current `AppleSDK` value is one of the four simulator kinds (AppleTVSimulator, IPhoneSimulator, WatchSimulator, XRSimulator). If it matches none of those, it returns false.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsx32@k_ZNK10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsx32@k_ZNK10cmMak.body: This method examines the current build context for the special definition `CMAKE_INTERNAL_PLATFORM_ABI`. When that value is present and matches the literal `"ELF X32"` (using the `_s` suffix to form a `std::string_view`), the function returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`. The logic is a single‑branch check of a string against a specific constant.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformSupportsAppleTextS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformSupportsAppleTextS.body: It returns true only when the build system is on the APPLE platform and the CMAKE_TAPI flag is set.

@lcmMakefile::PolicyOptionalWarningEnabl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PolicyOptionalWarningEnabl.body: The function checks whether an optional policy warning is enabled for a given variable.
