It checks the target type via `GetGeneratorTarget()->GetType()` and assigns the appropriate CUDA linking definition—`CMAKE_CUDA_DEVICE_LINK_LIBRARY` for static, shared, or module libraries, and `CMAKE_CUDA_DEVICE_LINK_EXECUTABLE` for executables—to a temporary list. Finally, it moves the list’s data out as the return value.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::ComputeL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::ComputeL.body: The function constructs a sequence of shell commands for Ninja to build the current target. It pulls pre‑defined linker rules from the makefile, substitutes the current configuration’s values, and, for static libraries, it also injects special run‑time steps such as removing old archives, invoking the archive tool, and touching the result to keep timestamps correct. The resulting vector of commands is returned for execution.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Generate.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Generate.body: The routine first validates the target’s type and determines the appropriate linker language. It then emits the language‑specific rules and iterates over each configuration name: for each file it outputs the corresponding build statements, branching on whether the target is an object library, an interface library (requiring C++ module sources), or a normal library (emitting device‑link and link statements). After generating per‑config rules, it adds an alias if cross‑config builds are enabled and finally registers any extra clean files.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::GetVisib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::GetVisib.body: The function inspects the generator target’s type and returns a string literal that names the corresponding artifact type: “static library”, “shared library”, “shared module” (with a special “CFBundle shared module” when the CF‑bundle flag is set) or “executable”; it returns `nullptr` when the type is unknown.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.body: The method builds the rule name string: it concatenates the language‑specific link target string, the constant tag “_DEVICE_LINK_COMPILE__”, the encoded name of the current generator target, and finally the supplied config string.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.body: The method constructs a target‑name string for a C++ build rule by concatenating the language‑specific prefix returned by `TargetLinkLanguage(config)`, a fixed suffix `"_DEVICE_LINK__"`, the URL‑encoded rule name of the current generator target, and the original `config` string, returning that composite string.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.body: The function builds a rule‑identifier string by concatenating the target‑language name, a fixed token (“_FATBINARY__”), the encoded generator name, and a trailing underscore‑separated config fragment. It returns this composite string for use as a unique key in the C++ build system.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.body: It builds and returns a composite rule string by concatenating the target language, target‑type name, an encoded rule name and the supplied config string (using `cmStrCat`).

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::Language.body: The function builds a rule‑identifier string by concatenating the target’s link language, its type‑name, a “LINKER__” token, the encoded rule name, and the supplied config string—all joined with underscores.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::TargetLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::TargetLi.body: The function simply forwards a configuration string to the underlying generator target and returns the resulting language string.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::TargetNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::TargetNa.body: The routine checks the target’s type: if the target is an executable it returns the list produced by `GetExecutableNames(config)`; otherwise it yields the list produced by `GetLibraryNames(config)`. The returned value is of type `cmGeneratorTarget::Names`.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::TextStub.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::TextStub.body: Generates a string that blends a static prefix with the encoded rule name of the generator’s target and the supplied configuration, returning the combined result.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteCxx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteCxx.body:
The routine creates a phony build target that represents the C++ module library.  
It constructs a `cmNinjaBuild` with the target name, sets a comment that includes the target name, and then appends the appropriate output files from both the local and, if it’s the first config, the global generator’s by‑products.  
A dependency on the “CXX” file is added, the build is written to the common file stream, and finally an alias for the target name is registered.  
(The `fileConfig` argument is currently unused – the TODO comment indicates that it should be incorporated in future revisions.)

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteDev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteDev.body: It creates three distinct build rules for a CUDA device target. For each rule it pulls the appropriate tool definitions from the current makefile, builds a command line by concatenating the tool path with the required options and placeholders, and uses a RulePlaceholderExpander to substitute target‑specific variables (target name, type, output file, fat‑binary name, etc.). After configuring the rule’s name, command, comment, and description, it registers the rule with the global rule generator so the build system will invoke those steps during a normal build.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteDev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteDev.body: The function checks if CUDA build support is enabled; if not, it aborts. It then evaluates whether the current target needs device‑linking via a helper that inspects the target, local generator, and the configuration. When linking is required, it prepares a unique output path in the build‑output tree and registers that file in the clean‑target list. Finally it emits the associated Ninja rules—writing a comment header, choosing the proper compiler‑specific branch (Clang or NVIDIA) and delegating to helper writers that emit the actual build rules for the device link object.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteDev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteDev.body: The routine builds the Ninja build rules needed to link device kernels for each CUDA GPU architecture in the target. It deduplicates object and link‑dependency files, emits a per‑architecture .cubin, aggregates them into a fat‑binary, and then creates the register and stub files that expose the kernels. The generated rules are written to the global and local Ninja generators for the final executable.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteLan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteLan.body: The private `WriteLanguagesRules` helper orchestrates the generation of language‑specific build rules. It pulls the set of languages required by a target’s source files (normal object sources and, separately, BMI‑only sources), and for each distinct language it delegates to `WriteLanguageRules` to emit the corresponding rule sections. The function only performs this collection‑and‑delegate work; no additional logic is mixed in.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteLin.body: This function creates and registers the link rule for a target. It constructs the rule name, expands placeholders for target type, language, and flags (including Swift‑specific handling), decides whether to use a response file, builds the command list, and finally adds any necessary symlink or stub rules before registering the rule with the global generator.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteLin.body: The function writes the Ninja‑build rule that links the output binary for a target. It gathers the target’s files, flags, and dependencies, builds the appropriate command line (respecting response files, Swift modules, and platform quirks), and emits the corresponding `build` statement and any necessary symlink/alias entries. It also handles pre/post‑link commands and cleans up temporary files.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteNvi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteNvi.body: The method builds a linker rule for CUDA‑device builds. It checks if the rule already exists; if not, it prepares a set of variables (target name, type, language, output locations, flags, etc.) and expands these into a command string. Depending on whether a response file should be used, it either injects the command into a response file or keeps it on‑line. The rule is then added to the global rule set for later invocation.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteNvi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteNvi.body: The function prepares and emits a Ninja build rule that links an NVIDIA‑device target. It resolves the target’s import‑library path, checks whether a rebuild is necessary, constructs the link command with device‑specific flags and dependencies, handles platform quirks (e.g. back‑slash conversion on Windows), and finally writes the rule to the Ninja file stream.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteObj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::WriteObj.body: The function builds a phony build target named after the generator’s target name, attaches a comment describing the object library, and appends outputs that represent the object files and clean‑up artefacts. It registers the explicit dependencies for those outputs, writes the corresponding build rule to the global generator’s output stream, and finally registers an alias for the target so it can be referenced by its original name.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::cmNinjaN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::cmNinjaN.body: The constructor of `cmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator` initializes the generator by first verifying that the target is not an object‑library; if it is a real build target it iterates through each configuration name returned by `GetConfigNames()` and ensures the corresponding output directory exists (creating it if necessary). It then creates an instance of `cmOSXBundleGenerator`, assigns it to `OSXBundleGenerator`, and registers the generator’s `MacContentFolders` as the bundle’s content folders.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::cmNinjaN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::cmNinjaN.body: Copies the configuration from an existing cmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator instance. The constructor initializes all member data members—typically flags, configuration options, and internal resource collections—so that the new object behaves identically to the source. It performs a deep copy of any owned data structures to avoid shared mutable state between the two instances.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::operator.body: Copies all internal state from the source object into the current instance, updating member values so that the target object ends up in the same state as the source, and returns a reference to the assigned object.

@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::~cmNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator::~cmNinja.body: The `~cmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator()` is the class‑level destructor; it’s declared `virtual` (`override`) so that when an instance is destroyed the base‑class destructor is invoked, and any owned resources are released. The implementation is marked `=default;` in the source file, letting the compiler generate the default destruction logic.

@lcmNinjaRule::cmNinjaRule@k_ZN11cmNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaRule::cmNinjaRule@k_ZN11cmNinja.body: This constructor initializes a rule object by taking a string identifier and storing it in a member called `Name`. The constructor simply moves the supplied string into that member; no additional logic is executed.

@lcmNinjaRule::cmNinjaRule@k_ZN11cmNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaRule::cmNinjaRule@k_ZN11cmNinja.body: A move‑constructor that takes an rvalue reference to another `cmNinjaRule` and moves its internal state into the new instance. It’s the canonical way to transfer ownership of a rule without deep copying, typically used when building or re‑using rule objects across different parts of the build system.

@lcmNinjaRule::cmNinjaRule@k_ZN11cmNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaRule::cmNinjaRule@k_ZN11cmNinja.body: The function `cmNinjaRule(const cmNinjaRule& [unnamed])` is a copy constructor for the `cmNinjaRule` type. It accepts an already‑constructed `cmNinjaRule` instance (passed by const reference) and initializes the new object as an exact copy of that instance. Internally, it copies the rule’s configuration data (e.g. its name, pattern, target‑type flags, and any nested rule relationships) into the new object’s member variables. It is typically invoked when rules are duplicated during parsing or rule‑merging steps—such as when a rule is reused in a different build configuration or when an intermediate representation of a rule is created from an existing one.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AddIncludeFlag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AddIncludeFlag.body: Adds include‑path compiler flags for a target. It gathers directories via `GetIncludeDirectories`, builds the flags with `GetIncludeFlags`, normalizes backslashes to slashes for GCC on Windows, and appends the result to the supplied `languageFlags` string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AdditionalClea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AdditionalClea.body: The function reads the *ADDITIONAL_CLEAN_FILES* target property, evaluates that list in the current build context, and registers each resolved path with the global Ninja generator as an extra file to delete during a clean.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::CompileWithDef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::CompileWithDef.body: The function checks whether the build system is configured to compile with user‑defined flags for the supplied language by looking up the corresponding “CMAKE_<lang>_COMPILE_WITH_DEFINES” option in the current Makefile. It simply returns the result of that lookup.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeDefines.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeDefines.body: The `ComputeDefines` method gathers compile‑time pre‑processor definitions from a source file and from the current configuration. It evaluates any expressions in those definitions using the expression interpreter, merges them with any existing defines in the local generator, and finally returns a single string containing all the accumulated `-D` flags that should be passed to the compiler.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeFlagsFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeFlagsFo.body: The method builds a compiler flag string for a particular source file. It first gathers the architectures relevant to the requested language and config, then identifies which architecture’s pre‑compiled header (PCH) source matches the file. It prepends an explicit language flag, appends language‑specific and source‑specific flags, and finally attaches any module‑specific options (e.g. C++ modules). The resulting string contains only the flags that must be passed to the compiler for that object.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeInclude.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeInclude.body: The function assembles the compiler‑flag string for a given source file: it pulls any include directories defined on that file, uses an expression interpreter to resolve them, then asks the local generator to format those directories into a compiler‑flag string, finally appending any additional language‑specific include flags before returning the combined string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeLinkDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeLinkDep.body: ComputeLinkDeps produces a list of Ninja‑style dependencies for a target’s link step. It skips static‑or‑object‑library targets, then pulls direct link dependencies, any module‑definition sources, manifest‑defined sources, and any user‑supplied link‑depends, mapping all collected paths through the generator’s path‑mapper.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeOrderDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeOrderDe.body: The function builds and returns a string that represents the dependency ordering chain for a given target.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ConvertToNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ConvertToNinja.body: The method simply forwards the supplied path string to the global generator’s conversion routine and returns the resulting Ninja‑style absolute path string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ConvertToNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ConvertToNinja.body: The method forwards the input path string to the global generator’s `ConvertToNinjaPath` routine and returns the resulting string reference unchanged.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EmitSwiftDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EmitSwiftDepen.body: The function gathers the real‑world file names for a Swift‑compiled source: it resolves the compiled‑source path, the object file path, and then figures out the Swift dependency, diagnostics, and make‑dependency files—falling back to defaults (.swiftdeps, .dia, .d) when explicit names aren’t supplied. It packages those paths into a small JSON object and stores that mapping in the target‑generator’s SwiftOutputMap for the given configuration.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EnsureDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EnsureDirector.body: If the supplied path is an absolute path, the method calls cmSystemTools::MakeDirectory to create that directory; otherwise it resolves the path relative to the current Ninja generator’s home‑output directory and creates the resulting location.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EnsureParentDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EnsureParentDi.body: Ensures that the directory containing a given file path is present by delegating the task of creating any missing intermediate directories to the internal helper `EnsureDirectoryExists`. The method obtains the parent directory of the supplied path via `cmSystemTools::GetParentDirectory` and passes that result to the directory‑creation routine, guaranteeing that any subsequent file operations have a valid location to target.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ExportObjectCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ExportObjectCo.body: The function first checks whether compile‑export commands should be emitted. If so, it builds a set of placeholder variables describing language, source path (escaped to shell format), object name, directories, and compiler flags (including any CUDA‑specific flags if the target language is CUDA). It then expands a rule placeholder string using those variables, builds the final command line from the expanded rule and output configuration, and finally registers that command with the global generator so the object file will be built during the Ninja build.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ForceResponseF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ForceResponseF.body: Checks whether the build‑time flag `CMAKE_NINJA_FORCE_RESPONSE_FILE` has been set by either the makefile’s own definitions or an environment variable, and returns true if either source reports the flag is present.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::Generate@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::Generate@k_ZN2.body: The `Generate` function is a pure virtual member that derived classes must implement. It accepts a configuration string (passed by const reference) and is expected to perform some generation logic—typically building or configuring internal state—based on that string. Derived types provide the concrete behavior, while the base class provides the interface.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GenerateSwiftO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GenerateSwiftO.body: The routine first checks whether any Swift dependencies are configured; if none it returns immediately. Otherwise it determines the path to the dependencies file (using a target property if present, otherwise a default location). It then creates a JSON object embedding that path, writes it to the output‑file‑map JSON, and finally appends the appropriate flag containing that file path to the command line.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetBmiFilePath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetBmiFilePath.body:
The function assembles a filesystem path to the binary‑module‑info (BMI) file for a given source file and build‑configuration.  
It first obtains the base output directory from the local generator, appending a trailing slash when needed.  
If the imported‑C++‑module information for the supplied config has not yet been initialized, it pulls the corresponding generator property (“IMPORTED_CXX_MODULES_\<CONFIG>”) and caches that data.  
Using that cached info, it derives the BMI filename that belongs to the source file (via `BmiNameForSource`).  
Finally, it stitches together the target directory, the config‑specific sub‑directory, and that BMI name to yield the full path, which the caller then uses for later processing.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetClangTidyRe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetClangTidyRe.body: This method builds the relative file path for a Clang‑tidy replacement file by concatenating the given directory, the current generator’s home‑relative output path, the target and config directories, and the source’s object name, appending a “.yaml” suffix.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetCommonFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetCommonFileS.body: This accessor forwards the request to the global generator and hands back the shared `cmGeneratedFileStream` instance it manages. The call chain ends with a dereference of the pointer returned by the global generator, ensuring the caller receives a reference to the same stream object that underpins the build system’s file‑output logic.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetCompiledSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetCompiledSou.body: The function takes a source‑file object, pulls its absolute path, and converts that path into the Ninja‑style absolute form via `ConvertToNinjaAbsPath`, returning the resulting string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetDyndepFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetDyndepFileP.body: The method builds a full file path by joining the output directory, the target directory for the current generator target, the configuration directory for the requested config, and a language‑specific suffix ending in “.dd”. It then returns this constructed path.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetGeneratorTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetGeneratorTa.body: This member function simply returns the stored `GeneratorTarget` pointer. Because the method is marked `const`, it guarantees it won’t modify the object and can be called on immutable instances. The returned pointer should be treated as read‑only by callers; if it may be `nullptr`, callers should guard against dereferencing. The function itself performs no additional logic beyond the direct member access, so its thread‑safety and performance characteristics are essentially trivial.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetGlobalGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetGlobalGener.body: The `GetGlobalGenerator` member function returns the global ninja generator associated with the current target. In a const context it forwards the request to its internal `LocalGenerator`, invoking `GetGlobalNinjaGenerator()` and returning that result.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetImplFileStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetImplFileStr.body: The method simply forwards the request for an implementation file stream to the global generator and returns the stream that the generator provides.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetLocalGenera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetLocalGenera.body: Returns a pointer to the object’s internal local generator for read‑only access.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetMakefile@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetMakefile@k_.body: It returns the instance’s `Makefile` member pointer, guaranteeing no modification by declaring itself `const`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjectFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjectFileP.body: The function constructs the full filesystem path for an object file by pulling the target directory from the current generator, appending the configuration‑specific sub‑directory, then adding the object name derived from the source file, and finally returning that composite string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjects@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjects@k_Z.body: Searches the internal `Configs` map for the supplied `config` key and, if present, hands back the associated `Objects` collection; otherwise it yields an empty container.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetPreprocesse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetPreprocesse.body: The function generates the full path for an already‑preprocessed source file. It first picks the proper extension to use for the preprocessed file (handling special cases for Fortran‑style extensions such as “F”, “fpp”, etc.), then constructs the new object‑file name by appending “‑pp.” before that extension. Finally it prefixes the result with the configured output directory (the local generator’s home‑relative path plus the target‑specific target directory and configuration directory) to form the absolute path returned.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetRulesFileSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetRulesFileSt.body: Returns a reference to the global *rules‑file* stream by delegating to the associated global generator.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetDepen.body: It concatenates the current binary directory with the target‑specific directory, the config‑specific subdirectory, and the language name, appending “DependInfo.json” to form the full path.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetFileP.body:
Constructs a path for the target file by appending the given file name to the output directory obtained from `GetTargetOutputDir`.  
If the output directory is empty or simply “.”, the function returns the original file name unchanged; otherwise it prefixes that name with the directory path and a separating slash.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetName@.body: The `GetTargetName` method is a simple accessor that returns the name of the generator’s target object. It is marked `const`, so it guarantees not modifying the state of `cmNinjaTargetGenerator`. Inside, it simply forwards the call to the encapsulated `GeneratorTarget` member, invoking its `GetName()` method and returning that string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetOutpu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetOutpu.body: This function returns the Ninja‑compatible path for the target’s output directory by asking the associated generator target for its directory and then normalizing the result with `ConvertToNinjaPath`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageCompil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageCompil.body: The function concatenates the supplied language identifier, a fixed “_COMPILER__” token, the encoded target name, a suffix indicating whether scanning is enabled (“_scanned_” or “_unscanned_”), and finally the config string, producing the unique compiler‑rule name string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageDyndep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageDyndep.body: The method builds a unique rule‑identifier string for dynamic‑dependency rules. It concatenates the given language name, a fixed marker (`"_DYNDEP__"`), the encoded generator target name via `EncodeRuleName`, and the supplied config string, returning the composed string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguagePrepro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguagePrepro.body: It concatenates the language tag, a fixed marker string, the encoded target name, and a configuration string into a single identifier used for rule‑generation.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageScanRu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageScanRu.body: The function builds a rule‑identifier string that combines the language name, a fixed “_SCAN__” marker, the encoded target name, and a configuration suffix. It simply concatenates these pieces via `cmStrCat`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The function constructs a new instance of `MacOSXContentGeneratorType`, initializing it with the supplied arguments (which include any necessary configuration or context) and then returns that instance for subsequent use.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The constructor stores the provided generator pointer and moves the configuration string into an internal member for later use.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The constructor creates a new `MacOSXContentGeneratorType` instance by copying the internal state of an existing instance, ensuring that all of its member data and any shared resources are duplicated correctly before the new object is used for subsequent content‑generation operations.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The operator checks whether the current build target is an Apple bundle; if not, it returns immediately. If it is, it creates the appropriate content directory for the current configuration and, when the config differs from the default file‑config, it skips directories that would collide with the native‑config files. It then resolves the source file’s path, produces the corresponding output path inside the bundle, writes a build rule to copy that file into the bundle, and records the output as an extra file for the target’s configuration.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The operator assigns a temporary `MacOSXContentGeneratorType` to an existing one by moving its contents; it returns a reference to the left‑hand side after the move.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The assignment operator copies all internal state from the right‑hand side into the current object, producing a new instance that mirrors the source’s configuration and content.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: This function is the destructor for the MacOSXContentGeneratorType class; when an instance of that type is destroyed, it releases any resources or memory that the content generator has allocated during its lifetime.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.body: The method simply forwards the call: it invokes `MapToNinjaPath()` on the object returned by `GetGlobalGenerator()` and returns that value unchanged.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::NeedExplicitPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::NeedExplicitPr.body: The function returns `true` only when the supplied language string is exactly `"Fortran"`, otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::New@k_ZN22cmNi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::New@k_ZN22cmNi.body: The static factory produces a unique pointer to the proper generator subclass. It switches on the target’s enum type: normal targets, shared, static, module, and object libraries all yield a `cmNinjaNormalTargetGenerator`; interface libraries create one only if the target has C++20 sources; otherwise the switch falls through. Utility and global targets produce a `cmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator`. The default case simply returns an empty unique_ptr.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::OrderDependsTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::OrderDependsTa.body: The method simply forwards the ordering request to the global generator: it passes the current target and the supplied config string to `GetGlobalGenerator()->OrderDependsTargetForTarget()` and returns whatever string that call produces.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::OrderDependsTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::OrderDependsTa.body: The function simply forwards its call to the global generator: it passes the current `GeneratorTarget` along with the supplied `config` string to `OrderDependsTargetForTargetPrivate` on the global generator instance and returns the resulting string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ScanningFiles:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ScanningFiles:.body: Returns true when both internal containers contain no elements; otherwise returns false.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::SetMsvcTargetP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::SetMsvcTargetP.body: The function checks whether the makefile has any of three MSVC architecture identifiers. If so, it builds the PDB path for the target, fills `TARGET_PDB` and `TARGET_COMPILE_PDB` entries in the variable map, makes sure the target directories exist, and returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteCompileRu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteCompileRu.body: The routine first queries whether the target requires dynamic dependency scanning by calling `NeedDyndep`. If that flag is true, it emits a compile rule with scanning enabled; afterward it always writes a compile rule with scanning disabled.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteCompileRu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteCompileRu.body: The function prepares a Ninja build rule for compiling a source file in a specific language. It configures compilation flags, handles preprocessing and dependency scanning, adds optional response file handling, and registers the resulting rule in the global rule list.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteCxxModule.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteCxxModule.body: The routine validates that the source file is a C++ file, then assembles a Ninja build rule that produces a BMI file. It prepares all needed variables (flags, defines, includes, dependency files, scan outputs), records the resulting object and response‑file paths, and registers that rule with the Ninja generator. It also handles any special output‑file handling (e.g., Msvc or module‑map formats) and ensures the target’s supporting directories exist before emitting the final build entry.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteLanguageR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteLanguageR.body: This protected member writes a brief header for the target language (only when `NINJA_GEN_VERBOSE_FILES` is defined) and then delegates to `WriteCompileRule` to record the actual rule for that language.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteObjectBui.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteObjectBui.body: The `WriteObjectBuildStatement` routine builds a Ninja build rule for a single source file: it figures the language, generates the compiled‑output path, computes the compiler flags, includes, and system‑includes, and assembles a command line that may include a custom compiler launcher. It then records the rule’s explicit and implicit dependencies (including pre‑processing, dynamic dependency files, and any generated headers), and finally writes the rule to the Ninja file along with any additional outputs or clean‑up files.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteObjectBui.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteObjectBui.body: This routine writes Ninja build rules for a target’s object files. It gathers custom commands, headers, and external objects, then creates order‑only phony targets with the required dependencies. It also handles private generated sources, incorporates Fortran‑scanning logic, and emits language‑specific compile rules to the target’s implementation file.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteTargetDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteTargetDep.body: The routine builds a JSON object that records the compiler identifiers for the target language, the directories that hold the compiled modules (including any special sub‑module paths for Fortran), the include directories, and the directories of linked targets that feed into the build. It also registers callbacks for resolving object and BMI file paths and, when the bootstrap flag is absent, injects dynamic‑dependency data. Finally it writes the collected information to the target‑depend info file for the requested language/configuration.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::addPoolNinjaVa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::addPoolNinjaVa.body: It pulls a pool property from a target and stores the value in the variable map when that property exists.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::cmNinjaTargetG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::cmNinjaTargetG.body: The constructor initializes the base target generator and the OS‑X content generator for each generator configuration found in the target’s Makefile, storing each created generator in the internal map keyed by the configuration name.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::cmNinjaTargetG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::cmNinjaTargetG.body: A copy constructor that creates a new `cmNinjaTargetGenerator` instance by duplicating the internal state of an existing one.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.body: The operator simply performs a deep copy of a given `cmNinjaTargetGenerator` instance into the current object and returns a reference to the object that was assigned to.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::~cmNinjaTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::~cmNinjaTarget.body: When a `cmNinjaTargetGenerator` instance goes out of scope, the destructor runs to tidy up any internal state—freeing caches, resetting shared pointers, and generally ensuring that any dynamically allocated data associated with target generation is properly released before the object is discarded.

@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::Generat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::Generat.body:
If the current target is not per‑config, it simply writes a pair of build statements for the supplied config and exits.  
Otherwise it loops over the generator’s known config names; for each that matches the requested config in the cross‑config table, and that satisfies any target‑type constraints, it writes the corresponding build statements.

@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::WriteUt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::WriteUt.body: Generates Ninja build rules for a utility target: it gathers the target’s custom commands and source files, resolves per‑config directories, collates their outputs and dependencies, writes the resulting build steps to the appropriate Ninja file, and registers an alias for the logical target name.

@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::cmNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::cmNinja.body: The constructor simply forwards its argument to the base class `cmNinjaTargetGenerator` and performs no additional initialization—currently it contains an empty body.

@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::cmNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::cmNinja.body: The constructor initializes a new instance by copying the internal state from an existing `cmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator`. It copies any configuration data, target lists, and internal flags from the source object, ensuring that the new object is in the same state as the original. The copy constructor is used whenever a separate generator instance needs to be created that preserves the same target‑generation logic without re‑reading or recomputing the configuration data.

@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::operato.body: The operator= overload copies the contents of another cmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator into the current instance, performing any necessary self‑check and member assignments, and finally returns a reference to the left‑hand object for chaining.

@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::~cmNinj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator::~cmNinj.body: The destructor runs automatically when an object of `cmNinjaUtilityTargetGenerator` goes out of scope. Because it is declared `= default`, it merely triggers the normal destruction of its data members and base classes—no extra custom logic is executed.

@lcmNonempty@k_Z10cmNonempty7cmValue@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNonempty@k_Z10cmNonempty7cmValue@f./.body: Checks whether a `cmValue` instance holds any data by simply negating its `IsEmpty()` flag—returning `true` only when the value is not empty.

@lcmNonempty@k_Z10cmNonemptyNSt3__117bas.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNonempty@k_Z10cmNonemptyNSt3__117bas.body: It returns `true` when the provided `cm::string_view` contains at least one character and `false` when the view is empty.

@lcmNonempty@k_Z10cmNonemptyPKc@f./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNonempty@k_Z10cmNonemptyPKc@f./Sourc.body: Checks if a C‑style string pointer points to a non‑empty string by negating the result of the `cmValue::IsEmpty` check.

@lcmNonempty@k_Z10cmNonemptyi@f./Source/.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmOrderDirectories::AddLanguageDirecto.body: Adds a list of directory paths to the object’s internal collection of language‑specific directories. The call passes a vector of strings and uses a helper `cm::append` to copy the entries into the `LanguageDirectories` member.

@lcmOrderDirectories::AddLinkLibrary@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::AddLinkLibrary@k_Z.body: The routine adds a new link‑library path to the internal constraint set, ensuring it is only recorded once. If the path belongs to an implicit directory it creates a special‑handled entry; otherwise it simply appends a standard constraint record.

@lcmOrderDirectories::AddOriginalDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::AddOriginalDirecto.body: The routine walks through each string in the supplied list, ignoring any entry that is considered an implicit directory or that is an empty string. For every remaining path it delegates to the helper that actually records the directory in the internal data structure.

@lcmOrderDirectories::AddOriginalDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::AddOriginalDirecto.body: Adds a directory string to the internal collection if it isn’t already present, storing the directory in a vector and mapping its name to the corresponding index in a hash map, and then returns that index.

@lcmOrderDirectories::AddRuntimeLibrary@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::AddRuntimeLibrary@.body: The method registers a runtime shared‑object by inserting its path into a set that tracks emitted libraries. If the path hasn’t been seen before, the code checks whether it belongs to an implicit directory; if so, it creates a special constraint entry for that directory. Otherwise it appends a standard constraint entry. Duplicate paths are silently ignored to avoid re‑processing the same library.

@lcmOrderDirectories::AddUserDirectories.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::AddUserDirectories.body: The function accepts a const reference to a vector of strings and appends those strings into the member vector `UserDirectories`. It uses the helper `cm::append` to perform the insertion.

@lcmOrderDirectories::CollectOriginalDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::CollectOriginalDir.body: The routine assembles the directory list in three passes: it first enqueues the user‑specified directories, then walks the constraint entries calling each entry’s `AddDirectory`, and finally appends the language‑runtime directories. The ordering is preserved in the order of insertion, so the original sequence of user entries is maintained as much as possible.

@lcmOrderDirectories::DiagnoseCycle@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::DiagnoseCycle@k_ZN.body: The routine checks whether a cycle has already been reported; if not, it marks the cycle as diagnosed, builds a warning message that a safe configuration cannot be produced because a cycle exists in the dependency graph, enumerates every conflicting directory with its required predecessors, and finally logs the warning through the global CMake instance.

@lcmOrderDirectories::FindConflicts@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::FindConflicts@k_ZN.body: The routine builds a conflict graph by allocating space, collecting conflict edges from each constraint entry, then tidying the adjacency lists by sorting and removing duplicates before handing off to the implicit‑conflict logic.

@lcmOrderDirectories::FindImplicitConfli.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::FindImplicitConfli.body: The routine walks the list of implicit‑directory entries, invokes each entry’s own conflict‑checker, collects any conflict messages, and if any are found emits a warning diagnostic describing that the requested purpose for the target cannot be safely generated because some files in those directories clash with libraries in implicit directories.

@lcmOrderDirectories::GetOrderedDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::GetOrderedDirector.body: The function lazily computes a sorted list of directories: on first call it collects the original directories, resolves any name conflicts, orders them according to the defined criteria, and then caches the result. Subsequent calls return the cached `OrderedDirectories` vector without recomputing.

@lcmOrderDirectories::GetRealPath@k_ZN18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::GetRealPath@k_ZN18.body: The function keeps a cache of resolved paths in a map. When asked for a directory string, it first looks up that string; if the entry doesn’t exist (or the key is after any equal‑key entry) it creates the real path by calling `GetRealPath`, inserts the key‑value pair into the map, and finally returns the cached value. In short: it performs a lookup‑in‑insert pattern that stores and re‑uses resolved paths.

@lcmOrderDirectories::IsImplicitDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::IsImplicitDirector.body: It resolves the given path to its canonical form and tests whether that canonical path is stored in the `ImplicitDirectories` map.

@lcmOrderDirectories::IsSameDirectory@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::IsSameDirectory@k_.body: Compares the canonical forms of two directory paths: it resolves each path via `GetRealPath` (which normalizes and resolves symlinks or relative components) and then checks for byte‑wise equality. The method returns true only when the resolved absolute paths match exactly, thereby ignoring superficial differences such as “./” or differing case on case‑insensitive filesystems.

@lcmOrderDirectories::OrderDirectories@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::OrderDirectories@k.body: The routine clears any previous cycle flag and resets the walk identifier, then iterates over every entry in `OriginalDirectories`. For each directory it bumps the walk id and calls `VisitDirectory`, which performs the depth‑first traversal from that node.

@lcmOrderDirectories::SetImplicitDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::SetImplicitDirecto.body: The function replaces the current implicit directory set with a new collection: it first clears the internal set, then iterates over the supplied collection, converting each path via `GetRealPath` (to resolve any relative or alias components) before inserting it into the internal `ImplicitDirectories` set.

@lcmOrderDirectories::SetLinkExtensionIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::SetLinkExtensionIn.body: This function assigns the supplied list of link‑extension strings to the class member `LinkExtensions` and compiles the supplied regular expression into a pattern object stored in `RemoveLibraryExtension`.

@lcmOrderDirectories::VisitDirectory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::VisitDirectory@k_Z.body: The routine performs a depth‑first traversal over the conflict graph, marking a node as visited with the current walk id, recursing on each neighbor, and when a previously‑visited node in the current walk is hit, it reports a cycle. Once all predecessors have been emitted, the directory is appended to the output list.

@lcmOrderDirectories::cmOrderDirectories.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectories::cmOrderDirectories.body: The constructor initializes internal members: it stores the passed global generator pointer, target pointer, and purpose string; it also marks that no directory ordering has yet been computed.

@lcmOrderDirectories::cmOrderDirectories.author: AI Short Overview

It guarantees that no orphaned resources remain after the object is destroyed.

@lcmOrderDirectoriesCompare::cmOrderDire.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmOrderDirectoriesCompare::cmOrderDire.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmOrderDirectoriesCompare::cmOrderDire.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmOrderDirectoriesCompare::operator()@.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmOrderDirectoriesCompare::~cmOrderDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectoriesCompare::~cmOrderDir.body: The function `~cmOrderDirectoriesCompare` is a comparison routine used in the directory‑listing logic. When two directory entries are passed in, it examines their metadata (such as timestamps, names, or other priority flags) and returns an ordering value suitable for `qsort`‑style sorting (negative if first comes before second, zero if equal, positive if after). It is the core comparison used by the `cmOrderDirectories` sorting logic to arrange directories in the desired sequence.

@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::AddDirec.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::FileMayC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::FileMayC.body: The function first checks whether a file with the given name already exists in the directory. If it does, it reports a conflict only when that existing file is not the same as the one that would be written (checked via `SameFile`). If the file does not exist, it queries the generator for the set of files that will be built in that directory; if the name appears there, it again reports a conflict. Otherwise the function returns false.

@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::FindConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::FindConf.body: `FindConflict` is a pure virtual member that obliges derived classes to implement a directory‑level conflict check. When called with a directory string, the implementation should scan that directory’s contents (or metadata) and return true if any conflicting entries are detected; otherwise it returns false. The function is declared `protected` to allow subclasses to access internal state while keeping the interface hidden from external callers.

@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::FindConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::FindConf.body: The function iterates over every entry in the `OriginalDirectories` list, and for each entry checks whether that directory has a conflict with the current object’s directory. If a conflict is detected, it records a `ConflictPair` (consisting of the current directory’s index and the supplied `index`) in the `ConflictGraph` vector so that subsequent logic can enforce the proper ordering of conflicting directories.

@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::FindImpl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::FindImpl.body: The routine scans the list of known search paths and, for each path that differs from the current one, checks whether that path hides a required library. If a conflict is detected, it records the offending directory in the supplied stream, noting that the conflict originates from files in that directory.

@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::Report@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::Report@k.body: The `Report` pure virtual member declares an interface for writing a diagnostic or status report into an output stream. @lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::cmOrderD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::cmOrderD.body: The function parses a file path string and stores the directory and file name parts. It first stores the full path, then checks whether the path contains “.framework”. If it does, a regular‑expression matcher splits the path into three capture groups: the part before “.framework”, the part inside the framework directory, and the part after. When a match is found, the part before the framework directory is assigned to `Directory` and the remainder of the path after that segment becomes `FileName`. If the pattern doesn’t match, the routine falls back to simple extraction of the path’s directory and base name via `GetFilenamePath` and `GetFilenameName`.

@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraint::cmOrderD.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraintLibrary::F.author: AI Short Overview

The operator is employed in places that need to duplicate a constraint library object—typically when a new instance must mirror an existing one without invoking the constructor again.

@lcmOrderDirectoriesConstraintSOName::Fi.author: AI Short Overview

It first checks whether a soname is already recorded; if so, it asks the helper routine FileMayConflict to see if any file in that directory matches that soname. @lcmOutputConverter::ConvertDirectorySep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmOutputConverter::ConvertDirectorySep.body: When invoked in an MSYS‑style shell, the routine rewrites a path that begins with a drive letter so that a path like `c:/foo` becomes `/c/foo`. @lcmOutputConverter::ConvertToOutputForE.author: AI Short Overview

If the path exists on disk and contains a space, it looks up a cached short‑form version of that path; if it isn’t in the cache it obtains one via `GetShortPath`. For each such line it extracts the routine name, function name, line number and hit count, and attempts to resolve the routine to an actual source file. When that file is found it looks up the line offset for the routine in that file, and then updates an internal coverage vector that maps absolute line numbers to hit counts. It skips routine “RSEL”, re‑uses the previous entry when the same routine and function are repeated, and logs an error if the required source file cannot be located. It returns false immediately if the file cannot be opened, otherwise it returns true after processing all entries.

@lcmParseGTMCoverage::cmParseGTMCoverage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseGTMCoverage::cmParseGTMCoverage.body: Accepts an rvalue reference to a cmParseGTMCoverage instance and an unnamed argument, moving the internal state into a newly constructed object (effectively performing a move‑constructor).

@lcmParseGTMCoverage::cmParseGTMCoverage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseGTMCoverage::cmParseGTMCoverage.body: The constructor simply forwards the provided coverage‑handler container and test instance to its base class `cmParseMumpsCoverage`, initializing the new GTM‑coverage parser with those parameters.

@lcmParseGTMCoverage::cmParseGTMCoverage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseGTMCoverage::cmParseGTMCoverage.body: The `cmParseGTMCoverage` routine takes a `cmParseGTMCoverage` instance, validates its fields, and extracts the GTM coverage metrics into a lightweight data structure for downstream reporting. It centralizes data‑extraction logic for any component needing coverage insight, ensuring defensive checks on malformed input and efficient re‑use of shared parsing utilities.

@lcmParseGTMCoverage::operator=@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview

This allows an efficient transfer of resources instead of copying, enabling fast reassignment of the object’s contents.

@lcmParseGTMCoverage::operator=@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseGTMCoverage::operator=@k_ZN18cm.body: The assignment operator creates a copy of a `cmParseGTMCoverage` instance by copying all of its internal members—including any state inherited from `cmParseMumpsCoverage`—into the current object and returns `*this` so that the assignment can be chained or used as an lvalue.

@lcmParseGTMCoverage::~cmParseGTMCoverag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseGTMCoverage::~cmParseGTMCoverag.body: ~cmParseGTMCoverage() is a virtual destructor that performs cleanup specific to the GTM‑coverage component. It first invokes the base class destructor to release shared resources, then deallocates any GTM‑specific data structures created during parsing.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::FindJavaFile@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::FindJavaFile@k_.body: FindJavaFile searches a directory tree for a file matching the specified routine name, assigns the discovered file path to the provided string reference, and returns true when a matching file is found (false otherwise).

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::InitializeJavaF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::InitializeJavaF.body: The function creates a new Java source file from a given file path. It writes a standard Java header, imports, and a skeleton class skeleton into that file. It is used to set up a fresh Java file that other parts of the code can populate with specific content.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::LoadCoverageDat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::LoadCoverageDat.body: The function iterates over the supplied file list, logging each attempt and verifying that the target ends with a “.xml” extension before invoking `ReadJacocoXML`. If that helper fails for any file, the routine aborts immediately and reports failure; otherwise it continues until all entries have been processed, ultimately returning success.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::LoadSource@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::LoadSource@k_ZN.body: Attempts to read the source file specified by the string argument and load its contents into the internal data structures, returning true on success and false on failure.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::ReadJacocoXML@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::ReadJacocoXML@k.body: The function creates an XMLParser for the current test and coverage objects, calls its ParseFile routine on the supplied file path, and then returns true unconditionally—so it never reports failures or propagates parsing errors.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::RemoveUnCovered.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::RemoveUnCovered.body: It scans the internal map of files tracked during the Jacoco parsing pass and prunes any entry whose coverage map indicates that the file never received any executable statement hit. The result is a trimmed collection that contains only those source files that actually contributed to a coverage report.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::SplitString@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::SplitString@k_Z.body: The function tokenizes the input line by whitespace, pushes each token into the supplied vector, and returns true if any token was produced (false otherwise).

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::EndE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::EndE.body: Handles the termination of an element. It is a protected override that receives the element’s name but currently performs no operation.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::Find.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::Find.body: Checks whether the specified file exists in either the source or binary directories via the helper routine; it returns true if found in either location and false otherwise.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::Pack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::Pack.body: The `PackagePathFound` virtual method scans a supplied `baseDir` for a file named `fileName`. It constructs a glob pattern, then uses a recursive globber that follows symbolic links to collect all matching files. If any matches exist, it iterates over them, extracts the parent directory, and compares that directory’s suffix against the current object’s `PackageName`. On a match, it logs the discovery, sets the internal `PackagePath` member to the directory path, and returns `true`. If no matches are found, the method returns `false`.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::Star.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::Star.body: On a package element the routine stores the package name and clears any previously cached path. When a sourcefile element is seen it resolves the file path, logs the event, opens the file and pushes a placeholder entry for every line read into the internal coverage map. For a line element it parses the “ci” and “nr” attributes from the attributes list and records the ci value at the corresponding line index in the current file’s coverage vector.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::XMLP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::XMLP.body: XMLParser is a concrete implementation that inherits from cmXMLParser; it reads Jacoco‑style XML coverage reports, extracts the relevant metrics, and populates the internal data structures used by cmParseJacocoCoverage.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::XMLP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::XMLP.body: The constructor initializes an XMLParser instance by passing the supplied `cmCTest*` to its base class `CTest` and storing the provided `cmCTestCoverageHandlerContainer&` as a member reference for later use.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::XMLP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::XMLP.body: It constructs an XMLParser instance by duplicating the internal state from an existing object. No new resources are allocated beyond what the base parser already sets up.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::oper.body: The operator= function implements a move‑assignment for XMLParser: it takes an rvalue reference to another XMLParser, moves its internal state into *this, and returns a reference to the current object.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::oper.body: The assignment operator copies the internal parsing state and configuration from the source `XMLParser`, ensuring that any owned resources (e.g., buffers, node trees) are duplicated or transferred correctly. It returns a reference to the current object to allow chaining.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::~XML.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser::~XML.body: ~XMLParser is the virtual destructor of `cmParseJacocoCoverage::XMLParser`. It runs automatically when an instance of this parser is destroyed, freeing any internal buffers, parser state, or file handles that the parser may have acquired during its lifetime. The destructor ensures that the XML parsing context is cleaned up cleanly before the object goes out of scope.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::cmParseJacocoCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::cmParseJacocoCo.body: The constructor consumes a temporary `cmParseJacocoCoverage` object, initializing a new instance by parsing a Jacoco JSON coverage report and building the internal data structures required for later processing.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::cmParseJacocoCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::cmParseJacocoCo.body: Creates a `cmParseJacocoCoverage` object by delegating to the base `Coverage` constructor with the supplied container and storing the supplied `cmCTest` pointer in its `CTest` member for later use.

@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::cmParseJacocoCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseJacocoCoverage::cmParseJacocoCo.body: cmParseJacocoCoverage is a public member that takes a Jacoco coverage report and builds an internal representation of the executed branches and lines for later use by other modules.

@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::FindMumpsFile@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::FindMumpsFile@k_.body: The routine checks the map for an exact match, then falls back to three common prefixes (“GUX”, “GTM”, “ONT”). If a match is found it writes the directory path into `filepath` and returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::InitializeMumpsF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::InitializeMumpsF.body: The routine opens the specified MUMPS file, reads each line in turn, and populates the coverage vector with –1 for non‑executable lines and 0 otherwise. It scans a line for the first non‑whitespace, non‑semicolon character; if that character is a period it skips the label token, then marks the line as executable only when the next character is not a semicolon. The result is a vector of flags representing each line’s executability.

@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::LoadCoverageData.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::LoadCoverageData.body: The `LoadCoverageData` method receives a string reference (typically a file path or raw data blob) and returns a `bool` indicating success. Implementations in derived classes should parse the supplied data, populate the internal coverage structures, and signal whether the load succeeded.

@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::LoadPackages@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::LoadPackages@k_Z.body: The function takes a directory path, uses a glob helper to locate all `*.m` files there, stores each file in a map keyed by the file’s base name (minus its extension), and then calls `InitializeMumpsFile` on each one. It then returns `true` to signal success.

@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::ReadCoverageFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::ReadCoverageFile.body: The function opens the specified file and line‑by‑line reads its contents. For every line it splits the string at the first “:”. If the prefix is “packages” it calls `LoadPackages` with the following path; if it’s “coverage_dir” it calls `LoadCoverageData`. Any other prefix triggers an error log. If the file stream cannot be opened, the function returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true` after processing all lines.

@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::cmParseMumpsCove.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::cmParseMumpsCove.body: Initializes a coverage‑parsing helper by wiring the test container and test into the base classes that drive the parsing logic.

@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::~cmParseMumpsCov.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseMumpsCoverage::~cmParseMumpsCov.body: It’s the destructor that cleans up the parser’s internal state. It guarantees that any allocated resources or temporary data structures used during coverage parsing are released before the object is discarded.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::PrintCoverage@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::PrintCoverage@k_ZN.body: PrintCoverage traverses internal coverage data structures and outputs a formatted summary of the current coverage state (e.g., hit counts, uncovered branches, and metrics) to the console or log stream.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadArraySize@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadArraySize@k_ZN.body: The function consumes a stream expecting the literal “a:” followed by an integer. If the stream contains that pattern, it assigns the parsed integer to `size` and returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadCoverageArray@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadCoverageArray@.body: The function parses a coverage‑list file: it first checks for the expected “;a:” header, reads the declared number of entries, then iteratively reads each “line:value” pair. For each pair it normalizes the line index (0‑based, treating negatives as zero) and stores the value in a vector that is extended as needed, using –1 as an “unset” marker; if a line already has a value the read count is added to the existing value. It returns true on success or false if any format error occurs.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadFileInformatio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadFileInformatio.body: The routine checks for a leading “s:” token, then reads an integer length, extracts the quoted file‑name string that follows, and finally invokes ReadCoverageArray to parse the associated coverage data, returning success status accordingly.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadInt@k_ZN18cmPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadInt@k_ZN18cmPa.body: The function reads characters from the provided input stream until it encounters a colon `:` or semicolon `;`. All read characters are appended into a temporary string buffer `s`. Once the delimiter is reached, the accumulated string is converted to an integer using `atoi` and stored in the output parameter `v`. The function always returns `true`, regardless of whether parsing actually succeeded or if the input stream failed before a delimiter was found.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadPHPCoverageDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadPHPCoverageDir.body: The method loads a directory, iterates its files, and for each non‑directory file invokes a helper to parse the file; if any parse fails it aborts and returns false, otherwise it returns true.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadPHPData@k_ZN18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadPHPData@k_ZN18.body: The function opens a file stream, validates that the file begins and ends with the expected curly‑bracket delimiters, and in a loop repeatedly calls `ReadFileInformation()` for each element in the declared array size. It returns `false` immediately on any I/O error or format mismatch, otherwise returns `true` after successfully consuming the entire array.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadUntil@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::ReadUntil@k_ZN18cm.body: The function reads characters from the supplied stream until either the specified terminator character is encountered or the stream ends. It returns true when the terminator was found, otherwise false. No characters read are retained, and no explicit error handling is performed; if the terminator never appears before EOF, the loop will exit via the stream failure condition.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::cmParsePHPCoverage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::cmParsePHPCoverage.body: The function `cmParsePHPCoverage` accepts an instance of itself (by reference) and a second unnamed parameter, then proceeds to analyze and update internal state based on PHPCoverage data. It returns an integer representing the number of elements processed or a status code indicating success/failure of the parsing operation.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::cmParsePHPCoverage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::cmParsePHPCoverage.body: This constructor simply forwards the supplied container and test pointer to its base classes (`Coverage` and `CTest`) and performs no further initialization.

@lcmParsePHPCoverage::cmParsePHPCoverage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePHPCoverage::cmParsePHPCoverage.body: The `cmParsePHPCoverage` routine parses a PHPCoverage object (or input buffer) and populates internal data structures with the parsed information. It performs validation checks on the input, fills in the relevant fields, and returns a success indicator (or a parse‑result object) to signal whether the operation succeeded.

@lcmParsePlist@k_Z12cmParsePlistRKNSt3__.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParsePlist@k_Z12cmParsePlistRKNSt3__.body: Runs plutil on the supplied file, captures its stdout via a pipe, parses that output as JSON into a Json::Value, and returns an optional containing that value; returns nullopt if the conversion fails or the JSON parsing fails.

@lcmParseXcFrameworkPlist@k_Z23cmParseXc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmParseXcFrameworkPlist@k_Z23cmParseXc.body: It builds the full path to the framework’s `Info.plist` file, parses that file, checks that its metadata matches the expected bundle type and format version, builds a `cmXcFrameworkPlist` instance from the parsed data, and returns an optional containing that object (or an empty optional if any step fails).

@lcmPathLabel::GetHash@k_ZNK11cmPathLabe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPathLabel::GetHash@k_ZNK11cmPathLabe.body: The `GetHash` member simply returns the stored hash value. It exposes a reference to that internal member, which is fine as long as the object outlives that reference. It offers a quick read‑only access to the hash without copying. The function is marked `const`, ensuring callers cannot modify the object through the reference.

@lcmPathLabel::GetLabel@k_ZNK11cmPathLab.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPathLabel::GetLabel@k_ZNK11cmPathLab.body: Returns a const reference to the stored label, guaranteeing no copy is made and no mutation of the object. It preserves const‑ness by returning `this->Label` unchanged.

@lcmPathLabel::cmPathLabel@k_ZN11cmPathL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPathLabel::cmPathLabel@k_ZN11cmPathL.body: Initializes its internal state and computes a Jenkins‑style hash of the supplied label string.

@lcmPathLabel::cmPathLabel@k_ZN11cmPathL.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmPathLabel::cmPathLabel@k_ZN11cmPathL.author: AI Short Overview
