@lcmPathLabel::cmPathLabel@k_ZN11cmPathL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPathLabel::cmPathLabel@k_ZN11cmPathL.body: cmPathLabel is a protected helper that processes path‑label information—extracting, normalising or formatting it for use elsewhere in the system.

@lcmPathLabel::operator<@k_ZNK11cmPathLa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPathLabel::operator<@k_ZNK11cmPathLa.body: It implements a strict weak ordering based on the `Hash` member; returning true when the current object's hash is strictly less than the other’s, enabling sorting or set insertion.

@lcmPathLabel::operator==@k_ZNK11cmPathL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPathLabel::operator==@k_ZNK11cmPathL.body: The function compares two `cmPathLabel` instances for equality by comparing their stored hash values; it returns `true` only when both objects have identical `Hash` values.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::ExpandVariable@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::ExpandVariable@.body: The protected pure virtual `ExpandVariable` is the hook that concrete expander classes implement to translate a placeholder string into its resolved form. When the expander walks a template string, it passes each variable token to this method; the implementation returns the substituted value (or an empty string if unresolved) for that specific variable. The base class simply declares the signature, leaving the actual lookup logic to subclasses.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::ExpandVariables.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::ExpandVariables.body: The routine walks the input string looking for `<…>` markers, pulls out the token inside the angle brackets, substitutes it with the value returned by `ExpandVariable`, and reconstructs the string while carefully trimming any extra whitespace that would result from an empty replacement. It stops when no more markers can be parsed or an unmatched opening bracket is encountered.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::cmPlaceholderEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::cmPlaceholderEx.body: Creates a new expander instance that inherits the full placeholder‑map and expansion logic from an existing instance by performing a deep copy of its internal state.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::cmPlaceholderEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::cmPlaceholderEx.body: The function scans input strings for placeholder tokens (e.g., `${var}`) and substitutes them with supplied values from a context map, returning the fully resolved string. If a placeholder is not found in the map, it throws an error.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::operator=@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::operator=@k_ZN2.body: The assignment operator copies all internal data of the source `cmPlaceholderExpander` into the target object and returns a reference to the target, allowing chained assignments.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::~cmPlaceholderE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::~cmPlaceholderE.body: The virtual defaulted destructor guarantees that objects of derived types can be destroyed cleanly; it simply triggers the normal destruction chain without extra logic.

@lcmPolicies::ApplyPolicyVersion@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::ApplyPolicyVersion@k_ZN10c.body: The function parses the supplied `version_min` and optional `version_max` strings into major/minor/patch/patch‑tweak components, verifies that the requested version falls within the current CMake version range and is not lower than 2.4, then forwards the numeric values to the internal `ApplyPolicyVersion(mf, major, minor, patch)` implementation, returning success or failure accordingly.

@lcmPolicies::ApplyPolicyVersion@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::ApplyPolicyVersion@k_ZN10c.body: The routine first emits a deprecation warning when the requested policy version predates CMake 3.5 (unless the request originated from a legacy install helper). It then iterates through every policy ID, enabling those whose “newer” flag exceeds the supplied major/minor/patch triplet and disabling or marking older ones. While enabling, it may also set a backward‑compatibility cache entry for an older policy (policy CMP0001). If any policies that should have been disabled remain active, it diagnoses them, records a fatal error, and returns false. On successful completion it returns true.

@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyDeprecatedWarning.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyDeprecatedWarning.body: The function constructs and returns a warning message indicating that the specified policy’s OLD behavior is deprecated and will be removed in a future CMake release, urging users to migrate to the NEW policy behavior.

@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyID@k_ZN10cmPolici.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyID@k_ZN10cmPolici.body: The `GetPolicyID` helper simply forwards the incoming C‑string to the internal `stringToId` routine, which translates the textual identifier into the corresponding `cmPolicies::PolicyID` value. It returns the success flag from that conversion, writing the resolved identifier into the supplied reference parameter.

@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZN10cmPo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZN10cmPo.body: The `GetPolicyStatus` static method ignores its argument and always returns the constant `cmPolicies::WARN`.

@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyWarning@k_ZN10cmP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyWarning@k_ZN10cmP.body: The function builds a diagnostic message that tells the user a specific policy‑ID is unset, then explains how to enable it with the `cmake_policy` command and points them to `cmake --help-policy` for details.

@lcmPolicies::GetRequiredAlwaysPolicyErr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::GetRequiredAlwaysPolicyErr.body: The function produces a single string that informs the user that a particular CMake policy (identified by its `PolicyID`) is now mandatory. It inserts the policy’s name and the CMake release that introduced it into a fixed message, then suggests either revising the `CMakeLists.txt` files to adopt the newer behavior or downgrading to an older CMake that still supports the legacy behavior. The message also points the user to the `cmake --help-policy <policy>` command for further details.

@lcmPolicies::GetRequiredPolicyError@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::GetRequiredPolicyError@k_Z.body: When invoked, `GetRequiredPolicyError` builds and returns a single string that explains that the specified policy (identified by its enum value) is currently not set to the *NEW* state. The message displays the policy name, a short description of the policy, and a concise set of troubleshooting steps: it tells the user to run the `cmake_policy(SET …)` command (or a batch upgrade via `cmake_policy(VERSION …)`) to make the policy NEW). The string also points the user to the `cmake --help-policy` and `cmake --help-command cmake_policy` help pages for further guidance.

@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::Get@k_ZNK10cmPo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::Get@k_ZNK10cmPo.body: The function examines two positions in an internal status array for the supplied policy ID. If the entry marked as “old” evaluates true, it returns OLD; otherwise, if the “new” entry is true, it returns NEW; otherwise it returns the default WARN value.

@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::IsDefined@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::IsDefined@k_ZNK.body: Checks the internal status array for the specified policy ID at the three possible status slots (OLD, WARN, NEW). If any of those entries are true, the function returns true.

@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::IsEmpty@k_ZNK10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::IsEmpty@k_ZNK10.body: Returns true when the map’s internal status reports no entries (via `Status.none()`), otherwise false.

@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::PolicyMap@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::PolicyMap@k_ZN1.body: The `PolicyMap` constructor accepts a const reference to an existing `PolicyMap` instance and copies its internal mapping structures into the new object. It performs a shallow copy of the policy identifiers and their associated values, preserving any internal reference counts or ownership semantics required by the surrounding policy framework. This routine is invoked during the construction of components that depend on policy configuration (e.g., the code near line 589 in `cmPolicies.h`).

@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::PolicyMap@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::PolicyMap@k_ZN1.body: PolicyMap is a constructor that initializes an internal map data‑structure. When invoked it constructs a std::unordered_map (or similar container) that holds policy identifiers mapped to their corresponding Policy objects. During construction it populates the map by iterating over any registered policy objects, adding them under appropriate keys so that callers can subsequently query the map for policy lookups.

@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::Set@k_ZN10cmPol.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::Set@k_ZN10cmPol.body: The function records the provided status for a policy ID by writing three boolean flags in a status array—one for each of OLD, WARN, and NEW—using a linear index calculation based on the ID and status type.

@lcmProcess::Buffer::Buffer@k_ZN9cmProce.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::Buffer::Buffer@k_ZN9cmProce.body: Creates a new instance, zero‑initialising the internal storage so callers can safely read from or write into the shared buffer without race‑conditions.

@lcmProcess::Buffer::GetLast@k_ZN9cmProc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::Buffer::GetLast@k_ZN9cmProc.body: When called, GetLast copies whatever data is in the internal buffer to the supplied std::string argument, resets the buffer’s indices to zero, and then empties the buffer. It returns true only when there was data to copy; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmProcess::Buffer::GetLine@k_ZN9cmProc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::Buffer::GetLine@k_ZN9cmProc.body: The routine scans the internal buffer from its current position (`Last`) looking for a newline or null‑terminator. When it finds one, it copies the characters from `First` up to that position into the supplied string (trimming trailing `'\r'` characters), advances `First` to the character after the terminator, and returns `true`. If the end of the buffer is reached without encountering a terminator, it slides any remaining partial line to the start of the buffer and returns `false`, indicating that no complete line was available at that time.

@lcmProcess::ChangeTimeout@k_ZN9cmProces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::ChangeTimeout@k_ZN9cmProces.body: The function updates the internal timeout value to the supplied duration and immediately triggers a timer reset by invoking the internal `StartTimer()` routine to apply the new deadline.

@lcmProcess::Finish@k_ZN9cmProcess6Finis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::Finish@k_ZN9cmProcess6Finis.body: The `Finish` method calculates the elapsed duration since the process started, corrects any negative values that could arise from system clock changes, and then signals the runner to wrap up the test.

@lcmProcess::GetExitException@k_ZNK9cmPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetExitException@k_ZNK9cmPr.body: When called it examines the process’s termination value (or signal on non‑Windows builds). It checks the value against a table of known exit codes, and returns one of five high‑level exception categories: Fault, Numerical, Interrupt, Illegal or Other. If none of the listed codes match, it falls back to Other.

@lcmProcess::GetExitExceptionString@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetExitExceptionString@k_ZN.body: GetExitExceptionString produces a human‑readable description of the cause of a process termination. It examines the stored exit or signal value and maps it to a predefined message (e.g., “Floating‑point exception (denormal operand)”, “Segmentation fault”, “Subprocess aborted”, etc.). If no predefined case matches, it returns a generic string containing the numerical code for diagnostic use.

@lcmProcess::GetExitValue@k_ZNK9cmProces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetExitValue@k_ZNK9cmProces.body: This const member simply returns the stored `ExitValue` field. Because the return type is a value (`int64_t`), callers receive a copy and cannot alter the internal state. The method offers a lightweight, inlined accessor—no side‑effects and no dynamic allocations.

@lcmProcess::GetId@k_ZNK9cmProcess5GetId.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetId@k_ZNK9cmProcess5GetId.body: The `GetId` member simply returns the stored `Id` value; it is marked `const`, so callers cannot modify the object, and it performs no side‑effects beyond returning that value.

@lcmProcess::GetProcessStatus@k_ZN9cmPro.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcess::GetTerminationStyle@k_ZNK9c.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcess::GetTimeoutReason@k_ZNK9cmPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetTimeoutReason@k_ZNK9cmPr.body: The function simply returns the stored `TimeoutReason` value held in the object. @lcmProcess::GetTotalTime@k_ZN9cmProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetTotalTime@k_ZN9cmProcess.body: It returns the value stored in the `TotalTime` member of the current object.

@lcmProcess::OnAllocate@k_ZN9cmProcess10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnAllocate@k_ZN9cmProcess10.body: The function resizes the internal buffer to the predefined constant `CM_PROCESS_BUF_SIZE` if it’s current capacity differs, then initializes a `uv_buf_t` structure with the buffer’s data pointer and its actual size and stores that structure in the supplied `buf` pointer.

@lcmProcess::OnAllocateCB@k_ZN9cmProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnAllocateCB@k_ZN9cmProcess.body: When libuv asks for a buffer, this static helper grabs the owning `cmProcess` from the handle’s `data` field and forwards the requested size and buffer pointer to its member `OnAllocate` routine.

@lcmProcess::OnExit@k_ZN9cmProcess6OnExi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnExit@k_ZN9cmProcess6OnExi.body: The OnExit routine updates the process’s internal state when a termination occurs: if the process isn’t already marked Expired, it distinguishes an exception (when an exit status indicates a failure on Windows or a non‑zero termination signal on other systems) from a normal exit; it records the exit code and signal, flags the handle as closed, stops an active timer if a read handle is closed, and finally invokes Finish() to perform any cleanup.

@lcmProcess::OnExitCB@k_ZN9cmProcess8OnE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnExitCB@k_ZN9cmProcess8OnE.body: The `OnExitCB` function is a tiny static helper used as the exit callback for the `uv_process_t`. When an external process terminates, the libuv runtime invokes this function. It casts the `uv_process_t::data` pointer back to the owning `cmProcess` instance and forwards the exit status and termination signal to the instance’s `OnExit` member. This indirection keeps the core logic encapsulated in `cmProcess` while still satisfying libuv’s C‐style callback requirement.

@lcmProcess::OnRead@k_ZN9cmProcess6OnRea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnRead@k_ZN9cmProcess6OnRea.body: The `OnRead` handler processes a chunk of data read from a pipe: it decodes the raw bytes into a string, appends it to a growing buffer, and then iteratively extracts complete lines from that buffer, passing each line to the runner for further processing. When a zero‑length read arrives it simply returns; an EOF sentinel stops the timer and triggers a clean‑up sequence. Edge cases such as partial lines at the end of a stream are handled by checking for a remaining fragment and feeding it back to the runner.

@lcmProcess::OnReadCB@k_ZN9cmProcess8OnR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnReadCB@k_ZN9cmProcess8OnR.body: Retrieves the owning `cmProcess` instance from `stream->data` and forwards the read count and buffer to its `OnRead` method.

@lcmProcess::OnTimeout@k_ZN9cmProcess9On.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnTimeout@k_ZN9cmProcess9On.body: When the timeout fires, `OnTimeout` marks the process as expired, and if the test was still running normally it sends a custom timeout signal (via the test’s timeout properties). It then switches to a forced‑termination style, closes any remaining read pipes, kills the child process if necessary, and finally cleans up by invoking the finish routine so the test exits cleanly.

@lcmProcess::OnTimeoutCB@k_ZN9cmProcess1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnTimeoutCB@k_ZN9cmProcess1.body: The function is a static timer callback used by libuv: when a timer expires, the callback receives the timer pointer, casts its `data` back to a `cmProcess` instance, and then forwards the event by invoking that instance’s `OnTimeout()` method.

@lcmProcess::ResetStartTime@k_ZN9cmProce.body: Resets the internal timestamp marking the beginning of the current cycle. It captures the current steady‑clock instant in `StartTime`.

@lcmProcess::SetWorkingDirectory@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcess::StartProcess@k_ZN9cmProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::StartProcess@k_ZN9cmProcess.body: The function configures a libuv process: it sets up the command and its arguments, creates stdin/stdout/err pipes, registers read callbacks, and starts a timer. It then forks the child process through `uv_spawn`, attaches the pipe reader, and marks the process as executing. If any step fails, it logs an error and aborts.

@lcmProcess::StartTimer@k_ZN9cmProcess10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::StartTimer@k_ZN9cmProcess10.body:
`StartTimer` checks whether the process has a timeout value.  
If so, it converts that value to milliseconds using `std::chrono::duration_cast` and starts an internal timer, passing `OnTimeoutCB` as the callback and the millisecond count as the expiry.

@lcmProcess::cmProcess@k_ZN9cmProcessC1E.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcess::~cmProcess@k_ZN9cmProcessD1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::~cmProcess@k_ZN9cmProcessD1.body: The `~cmProcess` destructor is default‑ed; it performs no explicit resource‑release logic, simply relying on the compiler’s default cleanup for its members.

@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.body: The function receives a UTF‑encoded string (`raw`) and an index (`id`). It swaps that string into the output buffer when compiled on non‑WIN32 platforms. On WIN32 it first validates the current code page via `GetCPInfoExW`. If the page uses multi‑byte characters it attempts a two‑pass decode: first a quick path that handles single‑byte/lead‑byte cases, then, if more bytes are required, a loop that keeps calling `DoDecodeText` until the expected trailing byte is seen or the end of the string is reached. If a special lead‑byte sequence is detected it prunes the last byte from `raw` and folds it into the preceding buffer slot. The routine returns `true` only when all decoding steps succeed; otherwise it reports failure.

@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.body: The function takes a raw data buffer, creates a `std::string` from it, and forwards the call to the overloaded `DecodeText` that operates on a `std::string`. It returns the result of that internal call.

@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.body: The function creates a string from the input vector, passes that string to a lower‑level overload that performs the actual decoding, copies the decoded result into the supplied output vector, and returns whether the operation succeeded.

@lcmProcessOutput::~cmProcessOutput@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessOutput::~cmProcessOutput@k_ZN.body: The function runs the final step in a processing pipeline: it pulls any generated output data from internal queues, normalises formatting (e.g., trimming spaces, normalising line‑breaks), and pushes the cleaned payload into a final destination channel (display, log, or file). It also performs basic sanity checks, flips a “ready” flag once the payload is queued, and emits a small acknowledgment event for any observers that the data is ready for downstream consumers.

@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::LineParser.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::ProcessChu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::ProcessChu.body: The function iterates over a buffer of characters, detects separators or null‐terminators, and treats each segment as a line. When a separator (or a null byte) is found it logs the line if logging is enabled, then hands the line to a virtual ProcessLine implementation. If that implementation reports failure, the routine aborts and returns false; otherwise it clears the line buffer and continues. If no separator is hit, it appends characters to the current line. At the end it returns true when all lines were accepted successfully.

@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::ProcessLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::ProcessLin.body:
The protected pure virtual `ProcessLine()` is the hook where derived classes plug in their line‑processing logic.  
When implemented, a concrete class reads a single line from its input source (file, stream, buffer, etc.), parses or validates the content, updates any internal state required for the parsing task, and returns `true` or `false` to signal success or failure. The base class only guarantees the signature; concrete subclasses decide what “processing” means for the particular parsing scenario.

@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::SetLog@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::SetLog@k_Z.body: The function simply stores the supplied stream pointer and an optional prefix string in the object’s internal members, using an empty string when no prefix is passed.

@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::~LineParse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::~LineParse.body: ~LineParser() is a public virtual destructor that guarantees proper cleanup of resources owned by a LineParser instance and allows derived classes to provide their own cleanup logic.

@lcmProcessTools::OutputLogger::OutputLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::OutputLogger::OutputLo.body: The `OutputLogger` constructor initializes the logger by processing the supplied data stream, leveraging its `LineParser` base to tokenize the input into discrete lines, and then dispatching each parsed line to the appropriate logging sinks (e.g., console, file, or network transport). @lcmProcessTools::OutputLogger::OutputLo.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcessTools::OutputLogger::OutputLo.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcessTools::OutputParser::Process@.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcessTools::OutputParser::ProcessC.author: AI Short Overview

The `ProcessChunk` member is the single hook that derived classes must implement to handle a raw byte buffer.

In the surrounding code, the function is invoked via statements such as `return this->ProcessChunk(data, length);`, providing a clean callback point for concrete processors to plug in their logic.

@lcmProcessTools::cmProcessTools@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
