@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::Fin.body: It clears any previously‑searched locations, then probes the includer’s directory first, iterating over each allowed header extension to form a candidate path and test if the file exists. When a match is found it stores that file’s handle; otherwise the directory is queued for later search. The function returns true only if a header file was successfully located.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::Mes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::Mes.body: The method creates a header string by concatenating the supplied base string with “.{…}” syntax that encloses a comma‑separated list of the class’s `HeaderExtensions`. It forwards that string to `MessagePath` and returns the resulting string.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::Pro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::Pro.body: It walks through the headers returned by `BaseEval()`, calling `EvalHeader` on each; if any call fails it exits immediately. It then does the same for the sources via `EvalSource`, again returning early on failure.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::Reg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::Reg.body:
The method validates that a particular include string is only ever generated by one source file.  
When it finds an existing mapping it logs a collision error and returns false; otherwise it creates a new mapping (or updates an existing one) and returns true.  
In short: it keeps the include‑to‑file mapping consistent, and reports any duplicate‑string conflicts.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::Reg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::Reg.body: The function inserts a supplied mapping handle into the internal mapping table. If the source file is a header, the handle is stored in the header‑mapping table; otherwise it goes into the source‑mapping table. It first checks whether a mapping for that file name already exists; if not, the new handle is stored. If one exists and the incoming mapping specifies an include string, that new mapping replaces the old one, otherwise it is ignored.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::ope.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::ope.body: The operator= overload implements a move‑assignment for `JobEvalCacheMocT`. It takes an rvalue reference to a temporary of the same type, transfers ownership of its internal state into the current object (typically via member‑wise `std::move` or similar semantics), and returns a reference to the updated object. It ensures that after the assignment the source temporary is left in a valid, “moved‑from” state and that the destination holds the new data.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::ope.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::ope.body: The assignment operator copies the internal cache state from the supplied `JobEvalCacheMocT` instance into the current object, returning a reference to the updated instance. It performs a deep copy of the underlying cache contents while preserving any necessary invariants.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::~Jo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheMocT::~Jo.body: When a `JobEvalCacheMocT` object is destroyed, its virtual destructor `~JobEvalCacheMocT()` is invoked. This routine cleans up the internal cache structures that were populated during a job’s evaluation phase. In practice it iterates over the cached entries, releases associated resources (memory, locks, or file handles), and ensures the surrounding cache manager is left in a consistent state. This guarantees that no stale or dangling data persists after the job’s evaluation cycle finishes.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::JobEva.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::JobEva.body: Creates a new instance by stealing its internal state from an existing object, so that the source object is left empty and the new instance takes ownership of the cached data.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::JobEva.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::JobEva.body: The constructor creates a new `JobEvalCacheT` by copying the internal state of an existing instance—duplicating its cached evaluation results, job status, and any associated metadata so that the new object behaves identically to the source.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::Messag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::Messag.body: The function builds a single string by iterating over each entry in the `SearchLocations` container, appending a formatted line for each path. It pre‑allocates a buffer of 512 bytes, then for each path it appends a two‑space prefix, the result of `MessagePath(path)` and a newline, returning the concatenated string.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::operat.body: Moves data from a temporary `JobEvalCacheT` into the current instance, updating its internal state (typically by moving or swapping members) and finally returns a reference to the object that was assigned to.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::operat.body: The assignment operator copies the contents of one `JobEvalCacheT` instance into another, returning a reference to the updated object. It handles the copy semantics for the cache type, ensuring the target reflects the source’s state after the call.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::~JobEv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheT::~JobEv.body: The destructor of `JobEvalCacheT` performs the necessary cleanup of any cache structures it owns and guarantees that the base class `JobT` is properly torn down. It releases resources tied to the job evaluation cache and makes sure that any internal bookkeeping is correctly disposed before the object is reclaimed.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Eva.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Eva.body: operator() takes a const reference to an IncludeKeyT and returns true only when that key passes its internal validation logic; otherwise it returns false, enabling callers to gate logic based on the key’s validity.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Eva.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Eva.body: It searches for the specified UI file, logs an error if the file can’t be found, skips processing for files marked to be ignored, and otherwise registers the file‑to‑key mapping.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Eva.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Eva.body: The function examines the UIC data of a source file: for every include entry it builds the expected “.ui” name, searches the listed directories for that file, logs a missing‑file error if not found, skips files marked as “skipped”, and upon success registers a mapping for the found UI file.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Fin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Fin.body: It expands the supplied path, attempts to load the corresponding .ui file, and if found it caches that file’s handle for later use, signaling success.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Fin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Fin.body:
The function clears `SearchLocations` and then scans the current and configured directories for a `.ui` file named after `UiName`.  
A captured lambda `findUi` resolves a full path, checks the file’s timestamp, and if found, stores the handle in `UiFileHandle`.  
If an `includePrefix` is supplied, it first tries that path; otherwise it falls back to the directory list and then to the search‑paths list.  
The routine returns `true` as soon as a matching file is located, otherwise `false`.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Pro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Pro.body: The routine first reserves enough space in `SearchLocations` to avoid reallocations while collecting search paths. It then walks through the headers defined in `BaseEval()`, invoking `EvalFile` on each; if any evaluation fails the function exits immediately. Afterwards it proceeds similarly over the source files, again calling `EvalFile` and returning early on failure.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Reg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::Reg.body: The function checks whether the include string is already registered. If it is, the code verifies that the existing mapping comes from the same UI file; otherwise it logs a conflict and returns false. If the include string is not found, a new handle is created with the new source file, stored in the mapping, and the function returns true.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::ope.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::ope.body: The move‑assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to another `JobEvalCacheUicT`, transfers its internal data into the current instance using move semantics, and returns a reference to *this so the assignment can be chained.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::ope.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::ope.body: The `operator=` function implements assignment for `JobEvalCacheUicT`. It takes a const reference to another `JobEvalCacheUicT` instance, copies its internal state into the current object, and returns a reference to `*this`. This enables statements such as `obj1 = obj2;` to overwrite `obj1` with the contents of `obj2`.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::~Jo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobEvalCacheUicT::~Jo.body: ~JobEvalCacheUicT() is a virtual destructor that cleans up the resources allocated by a job‑evaluation cache instance. It overrides the base class’s destructor, ensuring that any UIC‑specific allocations are properly released and that the cache’s internal state is reset before the object is discarded.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFenceT::JobFenceT@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFenceT::JobFenceT@.body: JobFenceT’s constructor simply delegates to its base class `JobT`, passing `true`. This signals that the job instance should be treated as a fence type—effectively marking it with the “fenced” flag that downstream logic relies on when scheduling or executing jobs.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFenceT::Process@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFenceT::Process@k_.body: The overridden `Process` method orchestrates the core business logic: it pulls in data, runs the necessary computations, and then flushes the results back to the calling context, wrapping up any required cleanup automatically.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFenceT::~JobFenceT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFenceT::~JobFenceT.body: The virtual destructor `~JobFenceT()` cleans up a job‑fence instance: it deregisters the fence from any global manager, releases any held locks or semaphores, and signals any waiting observers that the fence is gone. This guarantees that resources tied to the job fence are released in a well‑ordered way before the object is finally reclaimed.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFinishT::Process@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFinishT::Process@k.body: When the scheduler reaches this point it simply tells the job‑generator to abort, treating the job as a successfully finished task.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFinishT::~JobFinis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobFinishT::~JobFinis.body: Finalizes a job by cleaning up allocated resources, updating status, and notifying listeners that the job has completed.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocPredefsT::Proce.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocPredefsT::Proce.body: The method regenerates the `moc_predefs.h` file: it runs the pre‑defs generation command, compares the resulting text with the current file, and if they differ it rewrites the file and updates its timestamp; otherwise it merely refreshes the file’s modification time. Errors during any step are logged and abort the routine.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocPredefsT::Updat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocPredefsT::Updat.body:
This const member decides whether a predefinition file needs to be regenerated.  
It first tests whether the file already exists; if not, it notes that it must generate it because it doesn’t exist.  
If the configuration settings have changed, it records that a regeneration is required.  
Otherwise it compares timestamps: if the generated file is older than the executable that produces it, it signals that the file must be regenerated.  
When any of those situations applies, it writes a concise explanatory message into the supplied string pointer and returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocPredefsT::~JobM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocPredefsT::~JobM.body: The `~JobMocPredefsT()` virtual destructor runs automatically when a `JobMocPredefsT` object is destroyed. It guarantees the base `JobFenceT` destructor is invoked and allows derived classes to perform any custom cleanup—such as deallocating resources or detaching observers—by overriding this method. It must be defined (typically in a `.cpp` file) so that each concrete subclass can release its own resources while still preserving the base‑class cleanup.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocsCompilationT::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocsCompilationT::.body: The Process() routine collects the set of moc‑eligible headers, constructs a tiny autogenerated‑header block, and then either writes a fresh moc‑compilation file or simply touches it if unchanged. If no headers were found it emits a short placeholder comment; otherwise it writes the file only when the content differs from the existing file, otherwise it just updates the timestamp to keep the build system aware of a change.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocsCompilationT::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobMocsCompilationT::.body: ~JobMocsCompilationT is a destructor for the `JobMocsCompilationT` class. It runs cleanup logic when an object of this type is destroyed, typically releasing resources allocated during the compilation job, signalling job completion to dependent components, and ensuring any pending I/O or thread‑level locks are properly torn down.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::JobP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::JobP.body: The function creates a new `JobParseHeaderT` instance from an existing one by transferring the internal state of the temporary object. It copies (or moves) the header‑specific attributes—such as parsed fields, flags, and any auxiliary data—into the freshly constructed instance. The operation is performed during the construction phase to ensure the new object starts with a coherent header state derived from the source.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::JobP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::JobP.body: JobParseHeaderT is a copy constructor for the JobParseHeaderT type. It receives a const reference to another instance of the same type and copies the internal state from that source object, ensuring the new instance is an identical duplicate of the original.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::JobP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::JobP.body: JobParseHeaderT reads a job’s header information, extracts relevant metadata into the internal parse structure, and then signals success or failure to the caller.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::Proc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::Proc.body: Process first attempts to read the file; on failure it returns immediately. If the file contains a MOC section, it processes that section with MocMacro() and MocDependecies(). If a UIC section is present, it processes includes via UicIncludes().

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::oper.body: The overload moves the internal state of a temporary `JobParseHeaderT` into the current instance—effectively transferring its members without copying—while returning a reference to the modified object so callers can chain assignments.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::oper.body: The operator overload copies the fields of the source `JobParseHeaderT` into the current object, performing a shallow assignment. It returns a reference to the updated object (`*this`). This enables idiomatic `a = b;` semantics for the header type.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::~Job.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseHeaderT::~Job.body: `~JobParseHeaderT()` is the class destructor. When a `JobParseHeaderT` object is destroyed, this virtual destructor runs, performs any necessary cleanup (e.g., freeing buffers, closing streams) and then invokes the base class destructor to release any inherited resources.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::JobP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::JobP.body: The constructor takes a temporary `JobParseSourceT` by rvalue reference and initializes the new instance by stealing its internal state (e.g., buffers, flags, and any owned resources). It essentially implements a move‑constructor: the temporary’s members are transferred to the new object, and the source is left in a valid but unspecified state, preventing deep copies and preserving resource ownership.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::JobP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::JobP.body: The constructor copies the contents of an existing `JobParseSourceT` instance into a new object, initializing all internal fields from the source object. It provides a shallow copy of the parse source state so that the new instance behaves identically to the original.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::JobP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::JobP.body: The function `JobParseSourceT()` is a public member that returns a job‑parse object populated from a raw source. It extracts the source string, tokenizes it, and builds a `JobParseT` instance that encapsulates the parsed data for downstream processing.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::Proc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::Proc.body: The `Process` function first attempts to read a file via `ReadFile()`. If the read fails, it exits early. When the file is successfully loaded, it checks whether the file is a MOC or UIC file. For MOC files it invokes the three helper routines to handle the macro, dependency, and include sections. For UIC files it only processes the include section.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::oper.body: Accepts a temporary JobParseSourceT and transfers its data into the current instance, returning *this for further usage.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::oper.body: The `operator=` overload copies all members from the source object into the current instance and returns `*this` so that chained assignments are possible. It simply performs a deep copy of the relevant state held in `JobParseSourceT`.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::~Job.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseSourceT::~Job.body: The destructor (~JobParseSourceT()) cleans up resources allocated by JobParseSourceT, ensuring that any internal buffers, file handles, or other dynamically allocated objects are properly released before the object is destroyed.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::CreateKeys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::CreateKeys.body: Add each string from **source** to **container** as a new `IncludeKeyT` object, using the supplied prefix length as the constructor argument. The routine exits immediately when **source** is empty, and reserves the vector’s capacity first to avoid repeated reallocations.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::JobParseT@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::JobParseT@.body: It moves the supplied `SourceFileHandleT` into the member `FileHandle` when the object is created.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::JobParseT@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::JobParseT@.body: `JobParseT` is a constructor that inherits the base `JobT` constructors and initializes a job instance. It pulls in the necessary job data (typically identifiers, parameters, and state) from the arguments supplied at construction time, setting up the object for subsequent job‑processing steps.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::JobParseT@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::JobParseT@.body: JobParseT constructs a job‑parsing object, initializing its internal data structures and setting up the necessary state for subsequent job‑handling operations.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::MocDepende.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::MocDepende.body: The routine first exits early if no dependency filters are configured or output generation is disabled. It then scans the current content for any of the configured filter keys, performing a quick string‑search before invoking a regular‑expression matcher for each matching filter. When a match is found, the captured substring is added to a set of dependency strings. Finally the set of discovered dependencies is copied into the internal `ParseData` structure, normalising line endings in the stored paths.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::MocInclude.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::MocInclude.body: The routine scans the job‑specific content for “moc” occurrences, harvests each match from a regex match, and splits the found include names into two sets: ones whose file names start with the prefix “moc_” (stored in `underscore`) and the others (stored in `dot`). After collecting them, it calls `CreateKeys` to register the two groups.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::MocMacro@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::MocMacro@k.body: The function walks through each macro‑filter defined in the current object. For every filter it first checks whether the source text contains that filter’s key string. If the key is present, it runs a regex match using the filter’s expression. When a match succeeds it records the filter key as the macro name in the current parse data and returns immediately, otherwise it continues with the next filter.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::ReadFile@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::ReadFile@k.body: The routine first clears any stale parse data and logs the start of a parse operation. It then calls `cmQtAutoGenerator::FileRead` to load the file contents into the internal string buffer. If the read fails, an error message containing the file path and the underlying error is logged and the function returns `false`. If the file is read but turns out empty, a warning is logged and the function again returns `false`. On successful, non‑empty read the function returns `true`.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::UicInclude.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::UicInclude.body: The `UicIncludes` routine first verifies that the parsing context contains a `ui_` token; if not, it exits early. Otherwise it scans the source string with a pre‑compiled regular‑expression (`RegExpInclude`), pulls out every include name, inserts the matches into a `std::set<std::string>`, and finally forwards that set to `CreateKeys` along with the current file handle data.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::operator=@.body: The `operator=` implementation performs a move‑assignment for `JobParseT`. It swaps the internal state of the target object with that of a temporary `JobParseT` passed by rvalue‑reference, taking ownership of any owned resources while guaranteeing strong‑exception safety. It takes care to deallocate or reset any existing resources in the target before adopting the new state, ensuring no resource leaks or double‑destructions.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::operator=@.body: The operator copies every member from the source object into the current instance and returns the current object by reference, enabling fluent chaining.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::~JobParseT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobParseT::~JobParseT.body: When an object of the derived `JobParseT` is destroyed, the compiler invokes this virtual destructor, which performs any necessary cleanup for resources allocated during job parsing. It ensures that any memory, file handles, or network connections allocated in the derived parsing logic are correctly released before the base class destructor runs.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsFinishT::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsFinishT::.body: The lambda iterates over every name in `dirSet`, attempts to create the directory with `cmSystemTools::MakeDirectory`, and logs an error via `LogError` whenever the creation fails.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsFinishT::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsFinishT::.body: Creates the required output directories when MOC or UIC generation is enabled, then submits jobs for MOC compilation, merges dependency files if a dep file is present, and finally queues a finish job.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsFinishT::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsFinishT::.body: The `~JobProbeDepsFinishT` routine is called when a job’s dependency‑probe phase has finished. It marks the job as completed, performs any necessary cleanup (e.g., clearing temporary flags or buffers), and propagates the finished status to the surrounding system.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::Fin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::Fin.body: The function walks a set of candidate directories in a specific order—first checking a pre‑generated dependency file for an absolute path, then looking in the source directory, and finally iterating over a list of include paths—returning the first pair of path and timestamp for which the file exists; if none are found it returns an empty pair.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::Gen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::Gen.body: The `Generate` member creates a moc job for a given mapping. When logging is enabled it records a reason string. It probes the mapping; upon success it registers the parent output directory, fetches the source‑file cache entry, and submits a `JobCompileMocT` job to the worker pool. If the `compFile` flag is set, it marks the compilation as updated. The function always returns `true`.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::Pro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::Pro.body: The function determines whether a moc‑generated file needs to be regenerated. It first checks whether the output file exists, then whether the moc settings have changed, or whether the source, pre‑definition file, moc executable, or any of its parsed dependencies are newer than the current output. If any of those conditions hold, it reports the corresponding reason and returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::Pro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::Pro.body: The function iterates over the header and source mapping collections in the `MocEval` object, registering new “include‑only” compilation targets when an entry’s `IncludeString` is empty. For each mapping it invokes a private `Generate` helper; if that helper reports failure it aborts the whole routine, otherwise it continues until all mappings are processed.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::~Jo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsMocT::~Jo.body: ~JobProbeDepsMocT() finalizes a JobProbeDepsMocT instance by releasing associated resources and resetting its internal state during the job dependency‑management routine.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsT::~JobPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsT::~JobPr.body: The destructor of `JobProbeDepsT` releases the resources that were acquired during a job‑probe’s dependency tracking, ensuring that any registered probes, dependency maps, or temporary data structures are properly cleared before the object is destroyed.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsUicT::Pro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::JobProbeDepsUicT::Pro.body: The function probes whether the output file needs to be rebuilt. It first checks that the file exists and is up‑to‑date; if the file is missing or any of the following conditions holds it returns `true` – that the settings changed, the source file is newer than the output, or the uic executable is newer – and records a reason string if requested; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::ParseCacheT::ReadFrom.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmQtAutoMocUicT::SettingsFileRead@k_ZN.body:
It builds a hash of the current configuration.

@lcmQtAutoRccT::SettingsFileWrite@k_ZN12.body: The method first checks whether any settings have changed. If so, it writes the new settings string to the file, logging the operation in verbose mode. If the write fails, it logs an error, deletes the stale settings file to force a full rebuild on next run, and returns false. Finally, regardless of success, it releases the lock file and returns true if everything succeeded.

@lcmQtAutoRccT::TestInfoFile@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoRccT::TestInfoFile@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The method checks whether the RCC output file is older than the associated info file. If it is, it attempts to “touch” (update timestamp) the output file while logging this action. If the touch fails, it records an error and returns false; otherwise it marks that the build file changed and returns true.

@lcmQtAutoRccT::TestQrcRccFiles@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoRccT::TestQrcRccFiles@k_ZN12_G.body: The `TestQrcRccFiles` helper verifies whether the QRC resource file needs regeneration. It first ensures the input `.qrc` file is present; if missing it logs an error and aborts. It then checks whether the already‑generated `.rcc` file exists. If not, it sets `generate` to true and records the reason. If the settings have changed, or if the current `.rcc` file is older than either the source `.qrc` file or the rcc executable, it again flags regeneration, optionally logging the rationale when verbosity is enabled. If none of these conditions trigger, the function simply returns true, indicating no regeneration is necessary.

@lcmQtAutoRccT::TestResources@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoRccT::TestResources@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The function reads a QRC‑file’s resource list, verifies that each listed file exists and is newer than the current rcc output; if any file is newer it logs a reason and sets `generate` to true to trigger a rebuild.

@lcmQtAutoRccT::cmQtAutoRccT@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoRccT::cmQtAutoRccT@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: `cmQtAutoRccT` is a class whose copy constructor is explicitly deleted (`cmQtAutoRccT(cmQtAutoRccT const&) = delete;`). This guarantees that instances of the type cannot be copied, enforcing that each object must be constructed anew or moved, and preventing accidental duplication of internal state.

@lcmQtAutoRccT::cmQtAutoRccT@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoRccT::cmQtAutoRccT@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: It forwards the `GenT::RCC` value to the `cmQtAutoGenerator` base class, configuring the object to generate RCC‑specific output.

@lcmQtAutoRccT::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoRccT::operator=@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: This operator= is deleted, so attempting to assign one cmQtAutoRccT instance to another will trigger a compile‑time error. It effectively prevents accidental copying or moving of objects that manage internal resources, enforcing that instances must remain distinct after construction.

@lcmQtAutoRccT::~cmQtAutoRccT@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoRccT::~cmQtAutoRccT@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The destructor of `cmQtAutoRccT` is overridden to perform cleanup when an object of this type is destroyed; it relies on the compiler‑generated default destructor to release any owned resources.

@lcmRST::NormalLine@k_ZN5cmRST10NormalLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::NormalLine@k_ZN5cmRST10NormalLi.body: NormalLine clears any prior formatting state and forwards the supplied string to OutputLine with the normal‑line flag set to true.

@lcmRST::OutputLine@k_ZN5cmRST10OutputLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::OutputLine@k_ZN5cmRST10OutputLi.body: The routine flushes any pending newline first, then either writes the supplied text verbatim or, if inline markup is requested, it substitutes placeholders and scans the string for role, literal, and link markers. When a marker is found it emits the surrounding text plus a formatted token (back‑ticks around role/text, escaped link text, or literal back‑ticks) until the whole line is processed.

@lcmRST::OutputMarkupLines@k_ZN5cmRST17O.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::OutputMarkupLines@k_ZN5cmRST17O.body: The function walks through `MarkupLines`. For each non‑empty line it prepends a single space and then hands the string to `OutputLine`, passing along the `inlineMarkup` flag. After the loop it sets `OutputLinePending` to `true`, signalling that the output buffer should be flushed before any further output.

@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveCodeBlock@k_ZN5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveCodeBlock@k_ZN5.body: This method simply calls `OutputMarkupLines(false)`, signaling the rendering engine to emit the current directive block’s markup lines without any special formatting.

@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveLiteralBlock@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveLiteralBlock@k_.body: It runs the helper routine that emits the pending markup lines. After the output helper finishes, the function returns, leaving the internal state unchanged.

@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveParsedLiteral@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveParsedLiteral@k.body: The routine simply invokes `OutputMarkupLines(true)`—triggering the markup‑generation logic with the flag that signals the output phase.

@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveReplace@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveReplace@k_ZN5cm.body: Records the current markup lines into the replacement string identified by `ReplaceName`, concatenates them with spaces, and clears the stored name after copying.

@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveTocTree@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessDirectiveTocTree@k_ZN5cm.body: Iterates over each non‑empty markup line that does not start with “:”, looks up an optional mapping in TocTreeLink, and calls ProcessInclude with the resolved path plus “.rst” and the TocTree flag.

@lcmRST::ProcessFile@k_ZN5cmRST11Process.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessFile@k_ZN5cmRST11Process.body: The function opens the file named `fname`. If the file opens it sets the document’s base path, invokes either `ProcessModule` or `ProcessRST` according to `isModule`, sets the pending‑output flag, and returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmRST::ProcessInclude@k_ZN5cmRST14Proc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessInclude@k_ZN5cmRST14Proc.body: The routine guards against deep recursion by capping at ten includes, spawns a new cmRST with an incremented depth, adjusts the replace flag when appropriate, resolves the file path relative to the document root or current directory, calls ProcessFile to process the file, and returns whether the file was successfully located.

@lcmRST::ProcessLine@k_ZN5cmRST11Process.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessLine@k_ZN5cmRST11Process.body: When a line starts with “..”, `ProcessLine` clears the current markup state, determines whether the line matches a known directive pattern (module, literal, replace, include, toctree, etc.), records the line for later output, and sets the appropriate `DirectiveType` flag. Lines that do not match any directive are treated as normal text and simply added to the output stream.

@lcmRST::ProcessModule@k_ZN5cmRST13Proce.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessModule@k_ZN5cmRST13Proce.body: The routine consumes a line‑based stream, keeps a marker string that marks the start of a section, and when that marker appears in a line it processes the preceding part of that line, clears the marker, flags a pending output, and resets its internal state to prepare for a new section.

@lcmRST::ProcessRST@k_ZN5cmRST10ProcessR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ProcessRST@k_ZN5cmRST10ProcessR.body: The routine reads lines from the supplied stream one by one, hands each line to the instance’s ProcessLine() routine, and once the stream is exhausted it calls Reset() to restore the object to a clean state.

@lcmRST::ReplaceSubstitutions@k_ZN5cmRST.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::ReplaceSubstitutions@k_ZN5cmRST.body: The routine scans the supplied line for tokens that match entries in a substitution table. When a token is found it checks a set of already‑used substitutions to avoid repeating the same replacement twice. If the token is eligible, the function looks up the real replacement string in a lookup container and appends that string in place of the original token, building the output string piece by piece. Once the whole input has been processed, the accumulated string is returned.

@lcmRST::Reset@k_ZN5cmRST5ResetEv@f./Sou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::Reset@k_ZN5cmRST5ResetEv@f./Sou.body: This method clears the current state of a directive instance by clearing its stored markup lines and resetting the directive and markup type fields to their defaults, after optionally processing any pending directive logic through the appropriate handler for the current directive type.

@lcmRST::UnindentLines@k_ZN5cmRST13Unind.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::UnindentLines@k_ZN5cmRST13Unind.body: The routine first scans for the indentation common to all non‑empty lines after the first one. It records that prefix, then removes it from each following line. Afterward it prunes any leading or trailing blank lines, shrinking the vector so at least one line stays. The net result is a compacted block of text with uniform indentation stripped.

@lcmRST::cmRST@k_ZN5cmRSTC1ERNSt3__113ba.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRST::cmRST@k_ZN5cmRSTC1ERNSt3__113ba.body: The constructor stores the output stream and the document‑root, then builds a collection of regular‑expression patterns that match the various directive keywords used in the markup. Finally, it inserts an entry into a replacement map for the special token “release”, which pulls the current CMake version via cmVersion::GetCMakeVersion().

@lcmReadGccDepfile@k_Z16cmReadGccDepfile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmReadGccDepfile@k_Z16cmReadGccDepfile.body: The function opens a dependency file at the given path, parses it into a `cmGccDepfileContent` object, then normalises all referenced paths. For each rule and path, it optionally prefixes a supplied string when the path is relative and `prependPaths` is `All`. It also collapses any full‑path references and converts every path to a long‑form canonical representation before returning the optional result.

@lcmRemoveCommand@k_Z15cmRemoveCommandRK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRemoveCommand@k_Z15cmRemoveCommandRK.body:
The function `cmRemoveCommand` removes a set of values from a makefile variable.  
It first obtains the variable’s current value, expands any sub‑variables it contains, then iterates over the supplied argument list: if an expanded value is **not** in that list, it is appended to a new value string. Finally, the function writes this new list back as the variable’s definition. The function always returns `true` to indicate success.

@lcmRemoveDefinitionsCommand@k_Z26cmRemo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRemoveDefinitionsCommand@k_Z26cmRemo.body: The function iterates over a list of flag identifiers, asking the current `Makefile` instance to drop each definition via `RemoveDefineFlag`. It returns `true` after processing all supplied names.

@lcmRemoveDirectory@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRemoveDirectory@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function attempts to delete a directory specified by `dir`. It first checks whether the path is a symlink; if so, it delegates to `RemoveFile`. If not a symlink, it verifies that the recursive flag is enabled when the caller intends a non‑recursive removal; otherwise it aborts with an error message. If the path is an ordinary directory, it calls `RemoveADirectory` to perform the actual deletion. On any failure, an error is printed and the function returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmRemoveDuplicates@k_Z18cmRemoveDuplic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRemoveDuplicates@k_Z18cmRemoveDuplic.body: This template forwards the call to another overload that operates on iterators, returning a `const_iterator` that points to the new logical end.

@lcmRemoveDuplicates@k_Z18cmRemoveDuplic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRemoveDuplicates@k_Z18cmRemoveDuplic.body: The function removes duplicate elements from the provided range and returns an iterator that points just past the last element that remains after the removal.

@lcmRemoveDuplicates@k_Z18cmRemoveDuplic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRemoveDuplicates@k_Z18cmRemoveDuplic.body: Iterates through the range, keeping only the first occurrence of each value; each new element is copied to the front of the sequence, and the function returns an iterator marking the new logical end of the container.

@lcmRemoveMatching@kc3cmRemoveMatching@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRemoveMatching@kc3cmRemoveMatching@f.body: The template removes elements from the supplied container that satisfy the matching predicate defined by the provided `MatchRange`. It returns an iterator pointing to the new logical end of the container after the removal.

@lcmReturnCommand@k_Z15cmReturnCommandRK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmReturnCommand@k_Z15cmReturnCommandRK.body: The function validates that a `return` command is invoked with the correct arguments. It first checks the current policy status; if the policy is `WARN` it logs a warning and proceeds with old behaviour, if `OLD` it simply returns success. When the policy requires an error (`REQUIRED_IF_USED` or `REQUIRED_ALWAYS`) it emits a fatal error message, marks the system as errored, and returns `false`. If the first argument is not the literal `"PROPAGATE"`, the function records an error in `status` and flags a fatal error. In all other cases it records the invocation arguments in `status` and ultimately returns `true`.

@lcmReverseRange@k_Z14cmReverseRangeRKT_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmReverseRange@k_Z14cmReverseRangeRKT_.body: Creates a `cmRange` that iterates over the supplied range in reverse order by using its `rbegin()` and `rend()` members, returning a range whose element type is that of the reverse iterator.

@lcmRotate@k_Z8cmRotateT_S_S_@f./Source/.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRotate@k_Z8cmRotateT_S_S_@f./Source/.body: The function performs a forward‑only rotation: it moves the element at `middle` to the front of the range `[first,last)` and returns the iterator that now points to that element. The returned iterator is the original `first` advanced by the number of elements that were rotated. The code requires that the template argument satisfy the `ForwardIterator` concept.

@lcmRt2CtSelector::eval@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRt2CtSelector::eval@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The `eval` template dispatches on the integer `r`. When `r` is 0 it simply returns `false`. When `r` is 1 it forwards the comparison to `Comp<T>()(lhs,rhs)`. For any other value it delegates to the nested `cmRt2CtSelector<Ops…>::eval`, passing `r‑1` along with the operands. This creates a compile‑time chain that resolves to the appropriate operation for each `r`.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::ExpandRuleV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::ExpandRuleV.body: The function stores the supplied `outputConverter` and the rule‑variable map in its member fields, then delegates the actual placeholder‑expansion work to `ExpandVariables`, which scans the string and replaces any variable references using the stored data.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::ExpandVaria.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::ExpandVaria.body: The method looks up the supplied variable name in a series of known substitutions. It first checks a set of pre‑defined keys—such as “LINK_FLAGS”, “MANIFESTS”, “FLAGS”, etc.—against a `ReplaceValues` structure; when a match is found it returns the stored string. For variables that map to compiler or tool‑chain directives it consults the `Compilers` map and assembles a command string by concatenating the relevant parts from `VariableMappings`, inserting optional arguments and sysroot settings. When the variable is not found in any map it simply returns the original name unchanged.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::RuleVariabl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::RuleVariabl.body: The function `RuleVariables` accepts an rvalue reference to a `RuleVariables` instance and constructs a new `RuleVariables` object by moving its contents. The returned object is typically used to establish the variable bindings required for subsequent rule evaluation.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::RuleVariabl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::RuleVariabl.body: `RuleVariables` is a copy constructor that initializes a new `RuleVariables` object by copying the internal state from another instance passed as a const reference.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::RuleVariabl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::RuleVariabl.body: It aggregates rule variables for internal rule processing.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::SetTargetIm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::SetTargetIm.body: The function assigns the supplied string to the class member `TargetImpLib`.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::cmRulePlace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::cmRulePlace.body: The constructor simply transfers ownership of the internal expander state from a temporary instance into a fresh `cmRulePlaceholderExpander` object, ensuring all internal pointers and buffers are moved rather than copied.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::cmRulePlace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::cmRulePlace.body: The constructor takes an existing cmRulePlaceholderExpander instance and creates a new expander that inherits the same placeholder‑expansion behavior. It copies the internal state (e.g., registered placeholder tokens, replacement rules) so that the new object behaves identically in transforming rule strings.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::cmRulePlace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::cmRulePlace.body: The constructor simply stores the provided compiler‑to‑path and variable‑to‑path mappings, along with the system‑root directories, so that instance can later perform placeholder expansion using that information.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::operator=@k.body: `operator=` overloads the assignment operator to allow moving a `cmRulePlaceholderExpander` from another instance. The function assigns the contents of the right‑hand side to the current object (effectively performing a move) and then returns a reference to the object itself for chaining.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::operator=@k.body: The `operator=` overload copies the internal state of another `cmRulePlaceholderExpander` into the current instance, effectively replicating its placeholder mapping and any configuration flags, and then returns a reference to the instance itself.

@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::~cmRulePlac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRulePlaceholderExpander::~cmRulePlac.body: The function walks a rule’s token stream, locating `~`‑prefixed placeholders, and replaces each with its evaluated value (often a string or ID). It does this inside a rule‑specific expander, inheriting from `cmPlaceholderExpander`, so it only needs to supply the concrete mapping logic for rule‑level placeholders.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::AddResolve.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::AddResolve.body: The routine records the supplied name in an internal map, flags whether this entry is truly new (by comparing the new path against previously‑stored entries via `SameFile`), and finally associates the supplied vector of resolved paths with the corresponding key in the `RPaths` lookup.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::AddUnresol.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::AddUnresol.body: The method simply records a new unresolved dependency name by inserting it into the `UnresolvedPaths` set maintained by the `cmRuntimeDependencyArchive` instance. It accepts the path name as a `std::string` reference and adds it to the internal set, ensuring that subsequent resolution logic can track that this path remains unresolved until processed.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetBundleE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetBundleE.body: Returns a const reference to the internal string storing the executable path.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetGetRunt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetGetRunt.body: It looks up‑to‑date for a tool named by the caller, expands that tool’s command list and reports whether the tool was found. If the caller supplied a custom definition (or a fallback “objdump”), that definition is expanded and returned. When no definition is supplied, the routine builds a list of common MSVC‑style directories (from both registry entries and environment variables), then runs a helper to resolve the actual executable path. If the helper finds a path, the function emits the single‑argument command and signals success; otherwise it reports failure.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetGetRunt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetGetRunt.body:
The function is a simple accessor that returns a reference to the string value stored in the `Makefile` object under the key `"CMAKE_GET_RUNTIME_DEPENDENCIES_TOOL"`. It is declared `const`, so it guarantees no modification of the object’s state. The call chain is:

1. `GetMakefile()` retrieves the `Makefile` instance associated with the archive.
2. `GetSafeDefinition(key)` looks up the string value for that key, returning a reference to the stored string.  
The returned reference is the tool name used at runtime to locate the CMake‑generated dependency‑resolution tool.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetMakefil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetMakefil.body: The function `GetMakefile()` is a const member that simply returns a pointer to the `cmMakefile` instance held inside `this->Status`. It forwards the underlying object without copying or modification, and guarantees no side‑effects because the return value is a raw pointer to an internal resource.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetRPaths@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetRPaths@.body: It returns a reference to the class’s internal `RPaths` map (mapping `std::string` keys to `std::vector<std::string>` values) without copying the data.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetResolve.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetResolve.body: The member simply returns the internal map of string keys to sets of strings—an immutable reference that lets callers inspect the resolved‑paths mapping without modifying it.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetRuntime.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetRuntime.body: The method iterates over the three supplied lists, invoking the linker’s `ScanDependencies` routine for each entry. If any scan fails it returns `false` immediately. Only when every item succeeds does the function return `true`.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetSearchD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetSearchD.body: The `GetSearchDirectories()` method simply returns a constant reference to the internal `SearchDirectories` member. Because it returns a reference, no copy of the vector is performed, and callers can inspect the list of directories without being able to modify them. The function itself is straightforward and incurs no additional runtime cost beyond the reference return.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetUnresol.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::GetUnresol.body: Returns a const reference to the internal set of unresolved path strings so callers can inspect the current unresolved paths without modifying the set.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::IsPostExcl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::IsPostExcl.body: The function evaluates whether a given name satisfies any of the “exclude” rules while not being overridden by the “include” rules. It uses small helper lambdas that scan the stored regexes and file lists with `std::any_of`, and returns `true` when the name matches an exclude pattern or file that isn’t overridden by an include match.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::IsPreExclu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::IsPreExclu.body: The method scans the stored regexes: it returns true only when the supplied name matches a pattern in the *pre‑exclude* list and does **not** match any pattern in the *pre‑include* list; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::PlatformSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::PlatformSu.body: The function returns `true` when the supplied platform string matches one of the hard‑coded entries ("Windows", "Linux", or "Darwin") in the static set; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::Prepare@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::Prepare@k_.body: The method selects the appropriate runtime linker by reading the platform identifier; it creates a platform‑specific linker instance and invokes that instance’s Prepare() routine, returning the result. If the identifier isn’t recognized, it records an error and returns false.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::SetError@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::SetError@k.body: The method accepts a string reference and simply forwards that string to the internal Status object's `SetError` method, marking the runtime as failed with the supplied error message.

@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::cmRuntimeD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmRuntimeDependencyArchive::cmRuntimeD.body: The constructor stores the supplied search paths, bundle executable, and the include/exclude pattern vectors, moving each list into internal fields and compiling the regex strings into usable patterns for later dependency‑resolution passes.

@lcmScanDepFormat_P1689_Parse@k_Z27cmSca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScanDepFormat_P1689_Parse@k_Z27cmSca.body: The function reads a JSON dependency file, validates its structure (ensuring only one source rule and a supported version), extracts rule data (work‑directory, outputs, provides, and requires), populates the provided `cmScanDepInfo` object, and returns true only if no parsing errors occurred.

@lcmScanDepFormat_P1689_Write@k_Z27cmSca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScanDepFormat_P1689_Write@k_Z27cmSca.body: The routine assembles a JSON description of a scan‑dependency rule: it records the primary output, its extra outputs, any provided modules (with optional compiled‑module paths, source paths, lookup methods) and required modules (again with optional paths and lookup methods), serialises this structure, and writes it to the supplied file path, returning a boolean status for the write operation.

@lcmScriptGenerator::CreateComponentTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::CreateComponentTest.body: Creates a ready‑to‑use test stub for the named component—injecting the proper namespace, handling includes, and ensuring the generated code snippet compiles without conflicts.

@lcmScriptGenerator::CreateConfigTest@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::CreateConfigTest@k_.body: This method builds a regular‑expression string that matches the supplied configuration string exactly. It starts with a literal prefix stored in `RuntimeConfigVariable`, appends the literal anchor `^(`, then appends the escaped/encoded representation of `config` (via `cmScriptGeneratorEncodeConfig`) if the string is non‑empty, and finally closes the pattern with `)$`. The result is returned.

@lcmScriptGenerator::CreateConfigTest@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::CreateConfigTest@k_.body: Creates a regular‑expression string that matches any of the supplied configuration strings. It starts with a runtime variable, then joins the inputs separated by “|” inside a capture group, escaping each element through `cmScriptGeneratorEncodeConfig`. The final pattern is wrapped in `^…$` anchors.

@lcmScriptGenerator::Generate@k_ZN17cmSc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::Generate@k_ZN17cmSc.body:
The method assigns the supplied configuration name and a pointer to the caller‑supplied vector of types, invokes the internal script‑generation routine, and then clears the stored data. It simply performs the following steps:

1. `ConfigurationName` is set to the passed `config`.  
2. `ConfigurationTypes` stores the address of the supplied vector.  
3. Calls `GenerateScript(os)` to render the script into the stream.  
4. Clears `ConfigurationName` and null‑sets `ConfigurationTypes`.  

(End)

@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScript@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScript@k_ZN.body: The `GenerateScript` function is a protected, virtual entry point that writes script code to the supplied stream. It first creates an `Indent` object (presumably to manage indentation levels) and then delegates the actual emission to `GenerateScriptConfigs`, passing both the stream and the indentation context so that any per‑configuration code can be correctly formatted.

@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptActio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptActio.body: The function checks whether per‑configuration actions are enabled and, if so, it forwards the stream and current indentation level to GenerateScriptForConfig, thereby emitting the script snippet for the current configuration.

@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptActio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptActio.body: Checks whether any configuration criteria exist. If the configuration list is empty, it emits a single unconditional block of script actions. When the list contains entries, it builds a test string using `CreateConfigTest`, emits an `if` line with that test, generates the associated actions inside the block, and closes with an `endif`. The function relies on `GenerateScriptActions` and uses the `indent` helper to format the output.

@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptActio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptActio.body: The routine first checks whether the generator has multiple configuration types. If only one is present, it simply delegates to a helper that emits the single rule. When several types exist, it iterates over each configured type, emits a test string for that type, and writes an `if/elseif` chain that encloses the specific code for that configuration. It may add a final `else` block when no matching configuration is available, and always closes the chain with an `endif`.

@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptConfi.body: The protected virtual function `GenerateScriptConfigs` decides which generation routine to invoke based on the `ActionsPerConfig` flag. If the flag is true, it calls `GenerateScriptActionsPerConfig`; otherwise it falls back to `GenerateScriptActionsOnce`. No other actions are performed.

@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptForCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptForCo.body: The function is a protected virtual hook that derived classes can override to emit script code. By default it performs no action – the body is intentionally empty, so any concrete implementation must provide its own logic.

@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptNoCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptNoCon.body: The `GenerateScriptNoConfig` function is intended to emit a serialized representation of the object’s state into a provided output stream. When invoked, the method writes a textual script to the supplied `std::ostream`, using the supplied `Indent` value to format the output appropriately. The implementation is left empty, serving as a hook that derived classes can override to provide their own serialization logic without needing a configuration phase.

@lcmScriptGenerator::GeneratesForConfig:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GeneratesForConfig:.body:
It returns `true` or `false` after inspecting the supplied string.  
The function is marked `const`, so the body cannot modify any class members.  
It takes a single `const std::string&` argument, meaning the caller cannot alter the passed‑in string.  
The implementation likely performs a quick check (e.g., a pattern match, validity test, or flag extraction) and emits the result as the boolean return value.

@lcmScriptGenerator::GeneratesForConfig:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GeneratesForConfig:.body: The lambda captures `config_upper` by reference and, given an input string `cfg`, returns `true` if and only if the string converted to upper‑case matches the captured value. It effectively checks whether the supplied configuration string is exactly the expected value.

@lcmScriptGenerator::GeneratesForConfig@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::GeneratesForConfig@.body: The method normalizes the supplied configuration string to upper‑case and checks whether it matches any stored configuration string (case‑insensitively). If the instance holds no configurations it simply returns true; otherwise it returns true only when an exact (case‑insensitive) match is found, false otherwise.

@lcmScriptGenerator::NeedsScriptNoConfig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::NeedsScriptNoConfig.body: A protected, virtual const method that derived classes can override. By default it simply returns false, signalling that a script‑based configuration is not required in this context.

@lcmScriptGenerator::cmScriptGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::cmScriptGenerator@k.body: The constructor simply moves the supplied configuration name and list of options into its member variables, establishing the internal state that later drives the script‑generation logic.

@lcmScriptGenerator::cmScriptGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::cmScriptGenerator@k.body: The `cmScriptGenerator` constructor is declared as deleted to forbid copying a generator instance; it ensures the class is non‑copyable at compile time.

@lcmScriptGenerator::operator=@k_ZN17cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::operator=@k_ZN17cmS.body: The deleted assignment operator blocks copying of cmScriptGenerator instances, preventing any assignment from one instance to another.

@lcmScriptGenerator::~cmScriptGenerator@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGenerator::~cmScriptGenerator@.body: The `~cmScriptGenerator` is a virtual destructor that will be automatically invoked when a `cmScriptGenerator` object is destroyed. It is declared with the `= default` specifier, meaning the compiler generates the default destructor body; no custom cleanup logic is needed, and derived classes can override it if necessary.

@lcmScriptGeneratorEncodeConfig@k_ZL29cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGeneratorEncodeConfig@k_ZL29cm.body:
Iterates over each character in `config`.  
– If the character is a lower‑case alphabet, it appends a bracketed pair: `[` + upper‑case version + original + `]`.  
– If it’s an upper‑case alphabet, it appends `[` + original + lower‑case version + `]`.  
– All other characters are copied verbatim.

@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::Next@k_ZNK23c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::Next@k_ZNK23c.body: When invoked, it returns a new `cmScriptGeneratorIndent` whose `Level` field is the current object's level plus the supplied step (defaulting to 2). The call does not alter the existing instance.

@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::Write@k_ZNK23.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::Write@k_ZNK23.body: The `Write` member simply outputs a number of space characters equal to the object’s `Level` value. It loops from `0` to `Level‑1` and inserts a single space into the supplied stream each iteration, providing indentation when the object is serialized.

@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::cmScriptGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::cmScriptGener.body: The function takes a temporary `cmScriptGeneratorIndent` instance and transfers its internal indentation configuration into the new object, ensuring that any subsequently‑generated scripts adhere to the correct indentation rules.

@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::cmScriptGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::cmScriptGener.body: Accepts a const reference to a cmScriptGeneratorIndent object and performs an operation on that instance.

@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::cmScriptGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::cmScriptGener.body: The constructor sets the internal indentation level used by the script‑generation logic. It receives a depth value and records it for later formatting work.

@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::cmScriptGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::cmScriptGener.body: cmScriptGeneratorIndent() is a simple helper that configures the indentation level used by the script generator. It takes no arguments and simply returns the current indentation value (or applies a default if none is set). The function is invoked wherever the code needs to adjust or query the current indentation state before emitting new script lines.

@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::operator=@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::operator=@k_Z.body: Assigns a temporary `cmScriptGeneratorIndent` to the current instance by moving its internal state, then returns a reference to the modified object.

@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::~cmScriptGene.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmScriptGeneratorIndent::~cmScriptGene.body: This public function `~cmScriptGeneratorIndent` is a utility that, given a desired indentation level, returns a string consisting of that many tab characters (or spaces), which is then used by the script‑generation routines to format generated JavaScript code consistently.

@lcmSearchPath::AddCMakePath@k_ZN12cmSea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::AddCMakePath@k_ZN12cmSea.body: The routine retrieves a CMake variable’s value from the current FC makefile; if the variable is defined, it expands that value into a list of paths and for each entry calls `AddPathInternal`, thereby appending the path to the internal path list.

@lcmSearchPath::AddCMakePrefixPath@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::AddCMakePrefixPath@k_ZN1.body: The routine expands a CMake variable’s definition into a list of path strings and registers that list as prefix paths relative to the current source directory of the makefile. It first ensures the internal `FC` pointer is valid, then queries the makefile for a definition of the supplied variable name. If a value is found, the value’s string list is expanded into a `cmList` and passed to `AddPrefixPaths`, anchored at the makefile’s current source directory.

@lcmSearchPath::AddEnvPath@k_ZN12cmSearc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::AddEnvPath@k_ZN12cmSearc.body: The `AddEnvPath` routine expands a single environment variable into its constituent directories. It first calls `cmSystemTools::GetPath` to split the value of the supplied variable into a vector of path strings. It then iterates over this vector, invoking `AddPathInternal` for each path element. The method therefore appends all directories defined by the environment variable to the internal search path list.

@lcmSearchPath::AddEnvPrefixPath@k_ZN12c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::AddEnvPrefixPath@k_ZN12c.body: Retrieves the value of the named environment variable, expands it into a list of separate path components, optionally removes any trailing “/bin” segment from each component, and registers the resulting paths as new search‑prefixes.

@lcmSearchPath::AddPath@k_ZN12cmSearchPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::AddPath@k_ZN12cmSearchPa.body: The method simply forwards the supplied path to the internal routine `AddPathInternal`, supplying an empty string for the namespace argument. This keeps the public API minimal while delegating the real work to the helper.

@lcmSearchPath::AddPathInternal@k_ZN12cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::AddPathInternal@k_ZN12cm.body: The routine normalises a supplied path relative to an optional base directory, optionally normalises a prefix string, and then adds the resulting pair to the internal collection only if that pair hasn’t already been registered. It relies on a lookup set to avoid duplicates, and uses move semantics to keep copies minimal. The function is protected, ensuring its logic stays confined to the class hierarchy while guaranteeing that only distinct paths are stored.

@lcmSearchPath::AddPrefixPaths@k_ZN12cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::AddPrefixPaths@k_ZN12cmS.body: The function iterates over a list of directory strings and appends one or more suffixes—`bin`, `include`, `lib`, or framework‑style paths—to each entry based on the `CMakePathName` field of the internal `FC` object and on various makefile definitions. It also inserts architecture‑specific parts (e.g. “‑unknown‑” or a custom arch name) when the `CMAKE_LIBRARY_ARCHITECTURE` definition is present, and finally registers the composed paths with `AddPathInternal`. The routine therefore constructs a set of full search paths that can later be used when looking for files.

@lcmSearchPath::AddSuffixes@k_ZN12cmSear.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::AddSuffixes@k_ZN12cmSear.body: The function `AddSuffixes` expands the existing path list by appending each supplied suffix to every stored path. It first temporarily swaps the current list out of `this->Paths`, reserves enough capacity for the new expanded entries, then normalizes path and prefix slashes. For each original path it appends a trailing slash when missing, combines every suffix into a new path entry, and finally reinserts the unchanged original path. This yields a list containing every suffix‑appended version plus the original paths.

@lcmSearchPath::AddUserPath@k_ZN12cmSear.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::AddUserPath@k_ZN12cmSear.body: The method first verifies that the caller’s `FC` object is valid. It then expands any registry variables in the supplied path string by querying the Windows registry. For each resolved expansion it performs a directory glob, collecting matching directories into a list. Finally, each directory in that list is passed to the internal path‑adding routine, which records the path relative to the current source directory.

@lcmSearchPath::ExtractWithout@k_ZNK12cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::ExtractWithout@k_ZNK12cm.body: The routine iterates over the internal `Paths` collection, discarding any entry whose `Path` key is present in the `ignorePaths` set or whose `Prefix` matches an entry in `ignorePrefixes`. It optionally empties the supplied output vector first, then appends the remaining `Path` strings to it.

@lcmSearchPath::GetPaths@k_ZNK12cmSearch.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::GetPaths@k_ZNK12cmSearch.body: The function simply hands back a read‑only view of the instance’s internal collection of `PathWithPrefix` objects. Because it’s marked `const`, callers can read the vector but cannot modify the owning object.

@lcmSearchPath::PathWithPrefix::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::PathWithPrefix::operator.body: The function implements a strict weak ordering: it first compares the underlying `Path` members; if they differ, that determines the ordering. If the paths are identical, it defers to the `Prefix` values. This two‑step comparison is essential for using `PathWithPrefix` in ordered containers (e.g., `std::set` or `std::map` keys). It relies on the `operator<` of the contained `Path` and `Prefix` types; any unexpected ordering in those types will propagate here. A subtle point is the typo in the call `other.Prefix`—this should be `other.Prefix`.

@lcmSearchPath::cmSearchPath@k_ZN12cmSea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::cmSearchPath@k_ZN12cmSea.body: The constructor forwards the supplied `cmFindCommon*` argument to the base class `FC` and stores it in the member `FC`. This completes the initialization of a `cmSearchPath` instance.

@lcmSearchPath::cmSearchPath@k_ZN12cmSea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::cmSearchPath@k_ZN12cmSea.body: cmSearchPath is a utility that implements the logic needed to locate a file or resource by walking through a collection of search directories, returning the first match it finds.

@lcmSearchPath::operator=@k_ZN12cmSearch.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::operator=@k_ZN12cmSearch.body: The `operator=` member is the class’s copy‑assignment operator. It is compiler‑generated (defaulted), so it simply copies all data members from the right‑hand `cmSearchPath` argument and returns a reference to the left‑hand instance for chaining.

@lcmSearchPath::size@k_ZNK12cmSearchPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::size@k_ZNK12cmSearchPath.body: Returns the current number of entries stored in the `Paths` collection – a constant‑qualified accessor that simply forwards the underlying container’s size.

@lcmSearchPath::~cmSearchPath@k_ZN12cmSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPath::~cmSearchPath@k_ZN12cmSe.body: The function creates a search context that locates and validates configuration search paths.

@lcmSearchPathStripBin@k_ZL20cmSearchPat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSearchPathStripBin@k_ZL20cmSearchPat.body: The function removes a trailing “/bin” or “/sbin” component: if the input string ends with one of those suffixes, it calls `cmSystemTools::GetFilenamePath` to return the path stripped of that suffix; otherwise it returns the input unchanged.

@lcmSeparateArgumentsCommand@k_Z26cmSepa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSeparateArgumentsCommand@k_Z26cmSepa.body: The routine interprets a vector of strings as a command definition. It checks that exactly one of the command‑type flags (UNIX_COMMAND / WINDOWS_COMMAND / NATIVE_COMMAND) is set, verifies that the required options (PROGRAM or SEPARATE_ARGS) are coherent, and ensures no extraneous arguments remain. Depending on the flags it parses the supplied command string either as a Unix or Windows command line, optionally separates a program name from its arguments, escapes semicolons, and finally stores the resulting command string in the makefile’s definition table. If any validation fails it reports an error through the status object and aborts the operation.

@lcmSetCommand@k_Z12cmSetCommandRKiR17cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSetCommand@k_Z12cmSetCommandRKiR17cm.body: cmSetCommand interprets the supplied arguments to either set, clear, or cache a make‑file variable. It parses the first argument as the variable name, applies any special “ENV{…}” syntax for environment‑style assignments, handles optional CACHE, FORCE, and PARENT_SCOPE modifiers, and finally updates or removes the definition in the current or parent scope while reporting any misuse or conflicts.

@lcmSetDirectoryPropertiesCommand@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSetDirectoryPropertiesCommand@k_Z31c.body: The command receives a list of property/value pairs; it verifies the list is well‑formed, rejects properties that are reserved for other mechanisms (e.g., cache variables or user‑defined commands), and then applies each accepted pair to the current makefile context by invoking `SetProperty` on the makefile instance.

@lcmSetPropertyCommand@k_Z20cmSetPropert.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSetPropertyCommand@k_Z20cmSetPropert.body: The `cmSetPropertyCommand` routine parses a list of arguments that specify a property‑setting operation, validates the target scope (global, directory, target, etc.), and then dispatches to a specialized handler for that scope. It supports appending values, string concatenation or removal of entries, and can work with source‑file or test‑directory scopes, handling path validation and absolute‑path requirements before invoking the appropriate handler.

@lcmSetSourceFilesPropertiesCommand@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSetSourceFilesPropertiesCommand@k_Z3.body: The function parses a list of arguments that describe one or more source‑file scopes followed by property assignments. It first checks that at least two arguments were supplied, then it separates the directory options (DIRECTORY/TARGET_DIRECTORY) and the property keyword list. It validates the scopes, converts relative paths to absolute if required, and finally iterates over each resolved scope calling the helper that actually applies the property changes. If any step fails it reports an error and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmSetTargetPropertiesCommand@k_Z28cmSe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSetTargetPropertiesCommand@k_Z28cmSe.body: The function parses a list of arguments, checks that a mandatory “PROPERTIES” keyword and an odd number of following items are present, and then iterates over each target name preceding that keyword. For each target it verifies that it isn’t an alias and that the target exists in the makefile; if so, it applies each property/value pair (taken in sequence after the keyword) to the target via `SetProperty` and subsequently verifies the property via `CheckProperty`. If any step fails, an appropriate error is recorded in `status`.

@lcmSetTestsPropertiesCommand@k_Z27cmSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSetTestsPropertiesCommand@k_Z27cmSet.body: The routine first validates that the caller supplied an argument list containing at least one test name and a “PROPERTIES” marker followed by an even‑numbered list of property/value pairs. It then locates the target makefile (optionally within a user‑supplied directory) and, for each identified test, applies the supplied property assignments. If any test name cannot be resolved or if parsing fails, an error is recorded in the supplied status object and the function returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmSourceFile::AddDepend@k_ZN12cmSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::AddDepend@k_ZN12cmSource.body: This method stores a given dependency string into the object’s internal list of dependencies.

@lcmSourceFile::AppendProperty@k_ZN12cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::AppendProperty@k_ZN12cmS.body: The method checks the property name and, if it matches a known key, stores the value together with a back‑trace record in the corresponding internal list (include directories, compile options, or compile definitions). If the property name isn’t one of those special keys, it forwards the request to the generic `Properties` handler.

@lcmSourceFile::CheckExtension@k_ZN12cmS.author: AI Short Overview
