@lcmSourceFile::CheckExtension@k_ZN12cmS.body: It extracts the file extension (removing the leading dot), assigns that value to the object’s extension field, flags the file as an external object for common object‑file extensions, and falls back to a language guess if the language has not already been set.

@lcmSourceFile::CheckLanguage@k_ZN12cmSo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::CheckLanguage@k_ZN12cmSo.body: The `CheckLanguage` function inspects a file extension string to determine the programming language of the source file. It retrieves the current `Makefile` through the `Location` object, then asks the global generator for the language associated with that extension. If a language is returned (i.e., the string is non‑empty), it assigns that value to the `Language` member of the object. If no match is found, the member remains unchanged. This routine performs no other side‑effects and does not return a value.

@lcmSourceFile::FindFullPath::[lambda_0].author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::FindFullPath::[lambda_0].body: It builds a full path from the supplied directory, then checks whether that file (or a variant with an extra extension) was already produced or physically present. If either test passes, the path is stored and the routine returns true; otherwise it reports failure.

@lcmSourceFile::FindFullPath@k_ZN12cmSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::FindFullPath@k_ZN12cmSou.body: The routine resolves a source file’s absolute location. It first tests whether the file has already been marked as generated; if so it records the path and returns success. If the file is not generated, the routine searches the current source and binary directories, optionally appending known extensions, to find an existing file. When found, it stores the resolved path and sets a flag; when the search fails it records an error (and may issue a warning) and returns failure.

@lcmSourceFile::GetCompileDefinitions@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetCompileDefinitions@k_.body: It returns a read‑only reference to the internal `CompileDefinitions` container, letting callers inspect the stored definitions without copying or mutating them. The function is marked `const`, so it guarantees that calling code cannot alter the object’s state; callers only receive a reference that must not be used to modify the vector. The implementation simply forwards the stored vector, ensuring callers see the exact collection that the object holds.

@lcmSourceFile::GetCompileOptions@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetCompileOptions@k_ZNK1.body: This function simply returns a constant reference to the internal `CompileOptions` vector, allowing callers to inspect the options without modifying them.

@lcmSourceFile::GetCustomCommand@k_ZNK12.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetCustomCommand@k_ZNK12.body: Retrieves a read‑only pointer to the internal command object, exposing it for inspection or execution while keeping the instance immutable.

@lcmSourceFile::GetDepends@k_ZNK12cmSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetDepends@k_ZNK12cmSour.body: It returns a const reference to the internal `Depends` vector, giving callers read‑only access to the list of dependency strings without copying the data.

@lcmSourceFile::GetExtension@k_ZNK12cmSo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetExtension@k_ZNK12cmSo.body: `GetExtension` is a simple const accessor that returns a const reference to the `Extension` member. Because it returns a reference, callers receive the actual string stored in the object—no copy is performed. The const qualifier guarantees that invoking this method cannot modify any member data, preserving the object’s invariants. This function is typically used when the caller needs read‑only access to the file extension without copying the underlying string, and it should be safe to call on any `cmSourceFile` instance as long as the `Extension` string has been properly initialized.

@lcmSourceFile::GetFullPath@k_ZNK12cmSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetFullPath@k_ZNK12cmSou.body: Returns a reference to the stored `FullPath` string.

@lcmSourceFile::GetIncludeDirectories@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetIncludeDirectories@k_.body: The `GetIncludeDirectories()` member simply returns a const reference to the internal `IncludeDirectories` vector, allowing callers to inspect the list of include paths without incurring a copy and guaranteeing the returned sequence cannot be modified.

@lcmSourceFile::GetIsGenerated@k_ZNK12cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetIsGenerated@k_ZNK12cm.body:
The function returns whether the source file is marked as “generated”.  
* If `IsGenerated` is already set, the method returns `true` immediately.  
* Otherwise, for a `GlobalAndLocal` check, it retrieves the `propGENERATED` value from the file’s local property store.  
* In all other cases the function returns `false`.

@lcmSourceFile::GetLanguage@k_ZNK12cmSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetLanguage@k_ZNK12cmSou.body: It checks if a language value has already been set via `GetProperty`. If that property is present, it returns that value; otherwise it falls back to the member‑level `Language` field.

@lcmSourceFile::GetLocation@k_ZNK12cmSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetLocation@k_ZNK12cmSou.body: It returns a const reference to the `Location` member stored in the `cmSourceFile` instance.

@lcmSourceFile::GetObjectLibrary@k_ZNK12.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetObjectLibrary@k_ZNK12.body: Returns the stored library name (a copy of the member variable). It is a `const` member so the caller cannot modify the object. It simply returns the value of `ObjectLibrary`.

@lcmSourceFile::GetOrDetermineLanguage@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetOrDetermineLanguage@k.body: The method first examines whether the user has explicitly set a language value; if so, it caches that value in its `Language` member and returns it. If the language is still unset, it checks whether the file’s location is fully resolved or merely has an extension. In the ambiguous‑location case it invokes `ResolveFullPath()` to discover the extension; otherwise it extracts the extension from the file name and derives the language from it. In either case it updates the internal `Language` member before returning it.

@lcmSourceFile::GetProperties@k_ZNK12cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetProperties@k_ZNK12cmS.body: The method returns a constant reference to the internal `Properties` map, guaranteeing no modification of the map or object state and avoiding unnecessary copying.

@lcmSourceFile::GetProperty@k_ZNK12cmSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetProperty@k_ZNK12cmSou.body: The `GetProperty` routine first inspects the requested property name. It contains a series of hard‑coded checks for the following identifiers: `LOCATION`, `INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES`, `COMPILE_OPTIONS`, and `COMPILE_DEFINITIONS`. For each match it verifies that the associated member collection is non‑empty; if empty it returns `nullptr`. When non‑empty it converts the collection to a single comma‑separated string via `cmList::to_string` and returns that string wrapped in a `cmValue`. If none of those special cases applies, the method looks up the property in a generic properties map. Should that lookup fail, it attempts a chained lookup via the owning makefile’s state, falling back to a `nullptr` if the property cannot be resolved. The method returns a `cmValue` instance or `nullptr` to indicate absence.

@lcmSourceFile::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK1.body: The method simply returns the boolean value of a named property. It fetches the property string via `GetProperty(prop)` and forwards that string to the helper `cmIsOn`, which interprets any non‑empty, non‑zero‑value string as true. If `GetProperty` yields an empty string or a value that parses to zero, the result will be `false`.

@lcmSourceFile::GetPropertyForUser@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetPropertyForUser@k_ZN1.body: Handles requested property values from a source file, handling special cases for LOCATION, LANGUAGE and GENERATED properties with policy checks; otherwise it falls back to the standard property map lookup.

@lcmSourceFile::GetSafeProperty@k_ZNK12c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::GetSafeProperty@k_ZNK12c.body:
The function returns a reference to a string that represents the requested property.  
If the internal lookup yields a value, that string is returned; otherwise a static empty string is returned. The return type guarantees that callers never receive a dangling reference.

@lcmSourceFile::MarkAsGenerated@k_ZN12cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::MarkAsGenerated@k_ZN12cm.body: The routine flags the current source file as generated and propagates that status to the global generator by resolving the file’s absolute path and invoking the generator’s bookkeeping routine.

@lcmSourceFile::Matches@k_ZN12cmSourceFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::Matches@k_ZN12cmSourceFi.body: `Matches` simply forwards the check to the underlying `Location` object, returning the result of that comparison.

@lcmSourceFile::RemoveProperty@k_ZN12cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::RemoveProperty@k_ZN12cmS.body: The method simply delegates the removal of a property to the internal `SetProperty` routine by passing the property name and a null value (`cmValue{ nullptr }`).

@lcmSourceFile::ResolveFullPath@k_ZN12cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::ResolveFullPath@k_ZN12cm.body:
The function returns a reference to `FullPath`.  
If that member is still empty it runs `FindFullPath`; when that succeeds it runs `CheckExtension`.  
Finally it returns the (possibly updated) `FullPath`.

@lcmSourceFile::SetCustomCommand@k_ZN12c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::SetCustomCommand@k_ZN12c.body: The function accepts an owning pointer to a `cmCustomCommand` instance and stores that pointer in the object’s `CustomCommand` member. It simply transfers ownership of the passed command to the class, replacing any previously stored command with the new one.

@lcmSourceFile::SetObjectLibrary@k_ZN12c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::SetObjectLibrary@k_ZN12c.body: The method simply assigns the supplied string to the `ObjectLibrary` member of the current instance.

@lcmSourceFile::SetProperties@k_ZN12cmSo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::SetProperties@k_ZN12cmSo.body: The `SetProperties` method replaces the object’s internal `Properties` map with a new `cmPropertyMap` instance. It takes ownership of the supplied map via `std::move`, ensuring the old contents are transferred efficiently without copying the key‑value pairs. This effectively updates the source file’s property set to the new values provided.

@lcmSourceFile::SetProperty@k_ZN12cmSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::SetProperty@k_ZN12cmSour.body: The function clears any existing entries for the specified property and, if a non‑empty value is supplied, adds that value—paired with the current back‑trace—to the corresponding list. For properties that do not match the three special cases, it simply forwards the call to the generic property store.

@lcmSourceFile::SetProperty@k_ZN12cmSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::SetProperty@k_ZN12cmSour.body: The method forwards the supplied property name and string value to the internal `SetProperty` overload after converting the value via `cmValue`.

@lcmSourceFile::StoreProperty@k_ZN12cmSo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::StoreProperty@k_ZN12cmSo.body: The method accepts a property name and its value and records the pair in the class’s internal mapping of properties. It’s invoked to persist configuration changes or updates, typically after a property has been modified by client code.

@lcmSourceFile::cmSourceFile@k_ZN12cmSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFile::cmSourceFile@k_ZN12cmSou.body: Constructs a source‑file instance, feeding the given file name, its makefile context, and whether it’s generated. If marked generated, the object records that status; otherwise it is treated as a normal known source.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::DirectoryIsAmbig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::DirectoryIsAmbig.body:
Returns the value stored in the `AmbiguousDirectory` member.  
The method is a simple accessor; it has no side‑effects, no parameters, and guarantees it does not alter the object’s state.  
Because it merely returns a flag, it is safe to call from any context without risking race‑conditions or exceptions.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::DirectoryUseBina.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::DirectoryUseBina.body: When an ambiguous directory flag is set, the method resolves the real directory by collapsing the stored path with the current binary directory from the associated Makefile and then clears the ambiguity flag.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::DirectoryUseSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::DirectoryUseSour.body: The method asserts that a makefile is present; if the directory is flagged as ambiguous, it resolves the stored directory path by collapsing it relative to the current source directory (via `CollapseFullPath`) and then clears the ambiguity flag.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::ExtensionIsAmbig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::ExtensionIsAmbig.body: The method simply returns the current value of the internal flag that indicates whether the extension is ambiguous. It reads the member variable `AmbiguousExtension` and returns its value.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::GetDirectory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::GetDirectory@k_Z.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the `Directory` string stored in the object, exposing it without allowing modification.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::GetFullPath@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::GetFullPath@k_ZN.body: This const member builds a single string by calling the two helper methods: it takes the directory string returned by `GetDirectory()`, appends a slash when that string is non‑empty, and finally concatenates the file name returned by `GetName()`. The result is a path string that combines the directory and name parts with a slash separator.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::GetMakefile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::GetMakefile@k_ZN.body: Returns a pointer to the internal `Makefile` member for read‑only access.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::GetName@k_ZNK20c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::GetName@k_ZNK20c.body: The function simply returns a const reference to the stored string member, allowing callers to read the value without copying or modifying it.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::Matches@k_ZN20cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::Matches@k_ZN20cm.body: The `Matches` function checks whether two `cmSourceFileLocation` instances refer to the same file. It first verifies that file names match when both extensions are considered ambiguous. When only one side has an ambiguous extension, it delegates the check to `MatchesAmbiguousExtension`. Afterwards, it compares absolute or relative directories: if both sides have absolute directories they must be identical; if both are relative, they must refer to the same source or binary directory; otherwise it rejects the match. If all checks succeed it updates the current instance with the matched location and returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::MatchesAmbiguous.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::MatchesAmbiguous.body: The function first verifies that the current object’s Makefile is valid, then performs a quick name comparison. If the names differ, it attempts to see whether the current name could be formed by appending a known extension to the other name: it checks that the current name starts with the other name followed by a dot and that the remaining suffix is one of the recognised extensions via the CMake instance. If both conditions hold, it returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::Update@k_ZN20cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::Update@k_ZN20cmS.body: The `Update` routine examines the current instance’s ambiguity flags. If the existing object is marked as ambiguous for the directory (or extension) and the incoming `loc` object reports a concrete value, it copies that value into the target’s member and clears the corresponding ambiguity flag. Thus it propagates a resolved location only when the new data is non‑ambiguous.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::UpdateExtension@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::UpdateExtension@.body: The `UpdateExtension` helper inspects a supplied file name, strips its extension, and uses the global language‑generator to decide whether the extension is recognized. If the extension matches a known language or a known file type, it keeps the original name and marks the extension as unambiguous. Otherwise, it attempts to resolve the path against the current source tree; if a file with that name exists on disk it adopts that name and clears the ambiguous directory flag. If no match is found the internal name and extension remain unchanged.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::cmSourceFileLoca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::cmSourceFileLoca.body: The constructor creates a source file location object from a makefile, file name, and a kind flag. It determines whether the path is absolute, extracts the directory and file name, normalizes the directory if needed, and then either marks the directory as known (setting ambiguity flags accordingly) or updates the file extension based on the given kind.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::cmSourceFileLoca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::cmSourceFileLoca.body: The constructor copies the provided `cmSourceFileLocation` instance into a new object: it copies the `Makefile` member via the member‑initializer list and assigns the remaining fields (`AmbiguousDirectory`, `AmbiguousExtension`, `Directory`, and `Name`) from the source instance.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::cmSourceFileLoca.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::cmSourceFileLoca.body: The function `cmSourceFileLocation` resolves the full path of the source file that a `cm` object is associated with, typically using the internal file‑tracking metadata of the compilation unit. It returns this path as a string (or equivalent type) so that downstream code can reference the original source file for diagnostics or debugging purposes.

@lcmSourceFileLocation::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFileLocation::operator=@k_ZN20.body: By marking the assignment operator as deleted, the class forbids any implicit or explicit copy‑assignment. The compiler will reject any statement that attempts to assign one `cmSourceFileLocation` object to another, ensuring that the internal state of a source‑file location instance cannot be altered after it has been constructed.

@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::cmSourceFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::cmSourceFileP.body:
The `cmSourceFilePathCompare` function supplies a comparator for source‑file path objects.  
It returns a boolean indicating whether the first path comes before the second in the desired ordering (typically alphabetic‑lexicographic or case‑insensitive).  
The function is invoked in places such as the sorting logic in `cmGlobalXCodeGenerator.cxx` (e.g., around line 1330) and wherever the project needs to order or hash source‑file paths consistently.

@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::cmSourceFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::cmSourceFileP.body: The helper implements a comparison operation on *cmSourceFilePath* objects, enabling the code to order and lookup source file paths—often inside sorted containers or lookup tables that rely on an ordering relationship.

@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::cmSourceFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::cmSourceFileP.body: The function implements the logic used by the comparison operator for `cmSourceFilePathCompare`. It accepts two `SourceFilePath` objects, extracts their underlying file‑path strings, and performs a lexicographic comparison that is consistent with the ordering expected by the surrounding code. The return value follows the standard pattern: negative if the first argument precedes the second, zero if equal, and positive otherwise. This comparison is employed by `cmGlobalXCodeGenerator` when sorting or deduplicating source‑file lists to guarantee deterministic ordering across builds.

@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::operator()@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::operator()@k_.body: This operator returns true when the full‑path string of the left file is lexicographically smaller than the right file’s – it simply compares the resolved paths of two `cmSourceFile` instances.

@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::~cmSourceFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceFilePathCompare::~cmSourceFile.body: The function performs a normalized lexical comparison of two source‑file paths: it normalises path separators, splits each path into components, and compares the components in sequence. It returns a signed integer that is < 0 if the first path precedes, > 0 if it follows, and 0 if the paths are equal. The result is used to order files consistently in global code generation and in hash‑based look‑ups.

@lcmSourceGroup::AddChild@k_ZN13cmSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::AddChild@k_ZN13cmSource.body: The function appends the passed `cmSourceGroup` instance to the internal vector of children, effectively registering the child group as a member of the current group.

@lcmSourceGroup::AddGroupFile@k_ZN13cmSo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::AddGroupFile@k_ZN13cmSo.body: The method registers a new group file by inserting the supplied name into the internal collection, which automatically guarantees uniqueness because the underlying container is a set.

@lcmSourceGroup::AssignSource@k_ZN13cmSo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::AssignSource@k_ZN13cmSo.body: Adds a source file to the group’s internal list.

@lcmSourceGroup::GetFullName@k_ZNK13cmSo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::GetFullName@k_ZNK13cmSo.body: The method is a const accessor that simply returns a const reference to the stored `FullName` member. It does not modify any state, and because it returns a reference it avoids unnecessary copying of the string.

@lcmSourceGroup::GetGroupChildren@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::GetGroupChildren@k_ZNK1.body: It returns a const reference to the internal vector that holds the child groups, exposing that collection without copying or modifying it.

@lcmSourceGroup::GetName@k_ZNK13cmSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::GetName@k_ZNK13cmSource.body: Returns a const reference to the stored `Name` string, letting callers read the value without copying or modifying it. The method is marked `const`, ensuring the call cannot change the object’s state.

@lcmSourceGroup::GetSourceFiles@k_ZNK13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::GetSourceFiles@k_ZNK13c.body: The method returns a **const reference** to the `SourceFiles` member, guaranteeing callers cannot modify the vector or the objects it points to while still avoiding a copy of the collection.

@lcmSourceGroup::LookupChild@k_ZN13cmSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::LookupChild@k_ZN13cmSou.body: The `LookupChild` routine iterates over the internal vector of child groups, comparing each child’s name to the supplied string. When a match is found it immediately returns a pointer to that child; otherwise, after exhausting the list, it yields `nullptr`.

@lcmSourceGroup::MatchChildrenFiles@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::MatchChildrenFiles@k_ZN.body: It walks through the current group and its children, returning the first `cmSourceGroup` that reports a file match for the supplied name (or `nullptr` if none is found).

@lcmSourceGroup::MatchChildrenFiles@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::MatchChildrenFiles@k_ZN.body: The function performs a depth‑first search: it first tests the current group for a file match; if none, it recurses into each child group, returning the first matching child or nullptr.

@lcmSourceGroup::MatchChildrenRegex@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::MatchChildrenRegex@k_ZN.body: It walks through the current group’s children in depth‑first order, calling the same helper on each child. If any child (or a descendant) reports a match, that child is returned immediately. If none of the children match, the function checks the current group itself and returns it when the name matches; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmSourceGroup::MatchesFiles@k_ZNK13cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::MatchesFiles@k_ZNK13cmS.body: The function simply checks whether the supplied file name exists in the object’s internal set `GroupFiles`. It returns `true` when the name is found (i.e., the find iterator is not `cend()`), otherwise `false`.

@lcmSourceGroup::MatchesRegex@k_ZN13cmSo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::MatchesRegex@k_ZN13cmSo.body: The `MatchesRegex` function returns `true` when the supplied `name` string matches the regex stored in the `cmSourceGroup` instance; otherwise it returns `false`. It simply forwards the check to the internal `GroupRegex` object's `find` method.

@lcmSourceGroup::SetGroupRegex@k_ZN13cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::SetGroupRegex@k_ZN13cmS.body: It compiles the supplied pattern into the internal regex object. If the pointer is null, it falls back to a pattern that matches nothing (`"^$"`).

@lcmSourceGroup::cmSourceGroup@k_ZN13cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::cmSourceGroup@k_ZN13cmS.body: The constructor initializes a source‑group object by storing the supplied name, allocating an internal data structure, and configuring the group’s match pattern. If a parent name is supplied, it prefixes the new group’s name with the parent path, building the fully qualified name for later use.

@lcmSourceGroup::cmSourceGroup@k_ZN13cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::cmSourceGroup@k_ZN13cmS.body: Copies every field from the given instance—including the internal data object (cloned via `cm::make_unique`)—so the new `cmSourceGroup` holds a full, independent copy of the source’s configuration.

@lcmSourceGroup::operator=@k_ZN13cmSourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::operator=@k_ZN13cmSourc.body: The assignment operator copies every data member from the supplied source object into the current instance—overwriting Name, GroupRegex, GroupFiles, SourceFiles, and the internal data—and then returns a reference to the updated instance.

@lcmSourceGroup::~cmSourceGroup@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroup::~cmSourceGroup@k_ZN13cm.body: When a `cmSourceGroup` object is reclaimed, its destructor takes care of any allocated resources—closing file descriptors, tearing down network sockets, and freeing internal buffers—so that the surrounding system is left in a clean state.

@lcmSourceGroupCommand@k_Z20cmSourceGrou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceGroupCommand@k_Z20cmSourceGrou.body: Handles command arguments to create or modify a source‑group entry in a makefile: parses the arguments vector, validates required options (e.g., group name, source‑group flag, regex, file list), fetches or creates the corresponding `cmSourceGroup` object from the current makefile, sets its regex when supplied, and appends the listed files (after normalising their paths) to that group. The function returns `true` only if all required options were present and applied without error.

@lcmSourceInfo::cmSourceInfo@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceInfo::cmSourceInfo@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: The constructor takes an rvalue reference to another `cmSourceInfo` instance and initializes the new object by moving its internal data members (such as source paths, file lists, or parsed metadata) into the newly‑constructed instance, avoiding any deep copies.

@lcmSourceInfo::cmSourceInfo@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceInfo::cmSourceInfo@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: Constructs a new instance by copying the data members from the provided `cmSourceInfo` object.

@lcmSourceInfo::cmSourceInfo@k_ZN12_GLOB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourceInfo::cmSourceInfo@k_ZN12_GLOB.body: cmSourceInfo returns a populated cmSourceInfo structure that groups key metadata for a particular source file—typically including the file’s full path, timestamps, and any associated dependency information.

@lcmSourcesWithOutput::cmSourcesWithOutp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourcesWithOutput::cmSourcesWithOutp.body: Moves an instance of cmSourcesWithOutput into a new object, transferring all of its internal data (such as source collections, flags, and any owned resources) without performing expensive copies. The function is intended to be invoked when an existing cmSourcesWithOutput object must be moved into another context while preserving its state.

@lcmSourcesWithOutput::cmSourcesWithOutp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourcesWithOutput::cmSourcesWithOutp.body: This routine gathers and returns a list of source objects enriched with their corresponding output metadata.

@lcmSourcesWithOutput::~cmSourcesWithOut.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSourcesWithOutput::~cmSourcesWithOut.body: The function walks the internal graph of source‑to‑output relationships, pulling together every source that has an explicit output value for the current context. It filters out any sources that do not expose an output, then packages the remaining pairs into a lightweight list that downstream modules can consume.

@lcmSplitExtension@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSplitExtension@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116c.body: The function parses a file‑name string, splits off the last dot‑separated suffix into the returned string, and writes the remaining leading part into the supplied reference; if no dot is present, the reference is set to the whole input and an empty string is returned.

@lcmStandardLevel::Index@k_ZNK15cmStanda.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStandardLevel::Index@k_ZNK15cmStanda.body: Returns the value stored in the private member `index_`.

@lcmStandardLevel::cmStandardLevel@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStandardLevel::cmStandardLevel@k_ZN1.body: It constructs an object that stores the provided `index` in the member `index_`, which is then used to determine the standard level.

@lcmStandardLevelResolver::GetCompileOpt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStandardLevelResolver::GetCompileOpt.body: The method first checks whether a compiler mapping for the requested language exists in the static `StandardComputerMapping`. If no entry is found it simply returns an empty string; otherwise it forwards the call to the stored `GetCompileOptionDef` implementation of that entry, passing along the current makefile context, the target and the supplied configuration string.

@lcmStandardLevelResolver::GetEffectiveS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStandardLevelResolver::GetEffectiveS.body: The routine searches the language‑specific mapping; if the key isn’t present it returns an empty string. When a match exists, it forwards the call to that mapping entry’s GetEffectiveStandard(), passing along the Makefile pointer, the target and the supplied config string.

@lcmStandardLevelResolver::LanguageStand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStandardLevelResolver::LanguageStand.body: The method takes a language code and a string that represents a specific standard. It looks up the language in the `StandardComputerMapping`; if the language is not found it returns an empty optional. Otherwise it forwards the standard string to the stored `LanguageStandardLevel` object for that language and returns the resulting optional value.

@lcmStandardLevelResolver::cmStandardLev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStandardLevelResolver::cmStandardLev.body: The `cmStandardLevelResolver` constructor stores the supplied `cmMakefile` pointer in the member `Makefile`, enabling the resolver to query the makefile’s data during level resolution.

@lcmState::AddBuiltinCommand@k_ZN7cmStat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::AddBuiltinCommand@k_ZN7cmStat.body: Adds a new builtin command under a lowercase key, checking that no duplicate exists and then inserting it into the internal command map.

@lcmState::AddBuiltinCommand@k_ZN7cmStat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::AddBuiltinCommand@k_ZN7cmStat.body: The function registers a built‑in command under the given name by storing a lambda that forwards the supplied arguments to `InvokeBuiltinCommand`.

@lcmState::AddDisallowedCommand@k_ZN7cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::AddDisallowedCommand@k_ZN7cmS.body: The function registers a built‑in command that is disallowed under a certain policy. It creates a lambda that, when invoked, checks the current policy status in the makefile. If the policy is at WARN level it issues a warning (optionally appending an extra warning string); if the policy is at NEW or REQUIRED levels it emits a fatal error and aborts the command; otherwise it falls through to the default behavior. Finally it delegates to the underlying `InvokeBuiltinCommand` implementation to execute the command.

@lcmState::AddFlowControlCommand@k_ZN7cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::AddFlowControlCommand@k_ZN7cm.body: It inserts the supplied command name into the internal set of flow‑control command names, then forwards the command itself to the standard built‑in command registration routine so it becomes available for execution.

@lcmState::AddFlowControlCommand@k_ZN7cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::AddFlowControlCommand@k_ZN7cm.body: The method stores the provided name in the `FlowControlCommands` container and then delegates to `AddBuiltinCommand` to register the command for later use.

@lcmState::AddScriptedCommand@k_ZN7cmSta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::AddScriptedCommand@k_ZN7cmSta.body: The function normalizes the provided command name, checks whether a flow‑control command with that name already exists in the internal map, and if so reports a fatal error. If a command of that name already exists, it archives the old one under a prefixed underscore name before inserting the new command into the map. If the operation succeeds it returns true; otherwise it signals failure.

@lcmState::AddUnexpectedCommand@k_ZN7cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::AddUnexpectedCommand@k_ZN7cmS.body: The `AddUnexpectedCommand` helper registers a built‑in command that signals a syntax error whenever a command is unrecognised or appears in an inappropriate context. The handler receives the command name and an error message; it queries the current CMake version via `GetDefinition("CMAKE_MINIMUM_REQUIRED_VERSION")`. If the name is `endif` and the version is older than 1.4, it accepts the command as if the `endif` was expected; otherwise it records the supplied error in the execution status and indicates the command was not handled. This allows the system to gracefully report unexpected syntax and maintain backward‑compatibility for older versions.

@lcmState::AddUnexpectedFlowControlComma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::AddUnexpectedFlowControlComma.body: The method records a flow‑control command name in the internal set (`FlowControlCommands`) and then delegates to `AddUnexpectedCommand`, passing along the same name and the supplied error message.

@lcmState::CacheEntryTypeToString@k_ZN7c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::CacheEntryTypeToString@k_ZN7c.body: The routine clamps an enum value to a defined range and returns a reference to the corresponding string in a static lookup table.

@lcmState::ClearDependencyProvider@k_ZN7.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::ClearDependencyProvider@k_ZN7.body: The function simply resets the `DependencyProvider` member, typically a `std::unique_ptr`, clearing the internal dependency cache and preventing further use of the old instance. It must guard against dereferencing a null pointer—calling `reset()` on a `nullptr` is a no‑op, but subsequently accessing the provider would fail. This clean reset pattern avoids lingering state but requires callers to reacquire a valid provider before next use.

@lcmState::DefineProperty@k_ZN7cmState14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::DefineProperty@k_ZN7cmState14.body: The method registers a property definition in the internal property registry by forwarding the supplied name, scope, descriptions, chained flag, and initialization source to the PropertyDefinitions object.

@lcmState::GetBinaryDirectory@k_ZNK7cmSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetBinaryDirectory@k_ZNK7cmSt.body: The method simply hands back the stored path to the caller. It returns a read‑only reference to the internal string that holds the directory name, so callers can read the value but cannot alter it.

@lcmState::GetCacheEntryProperty@k_ZN7cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetCacheEntryProperty@k_ZN7cm.body: The method receives a cache key and a property name, forwards the lookup to the underlying `CacheManager`, and returns the value that corresponds to that property for the given key.

@lcmState::GetCacheEntryType@k_ZNK7cmSta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetCacheEntryType@k_ZNK7cmSta.body: The function simply forwards the request to the cache manager: it asks the manager what type of cache entry the supplied key corresponds to and returns that `CacheEntryType` enum value.

@lcmState::GetCacheEntryValue@k_ZNK7cmSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetCacheEntryValue@k_ZNK7cmSt.body: The method delegates a key lookup to the internal cache manager, returning whatever `GetCacheEntryValue` supplies. It’s a straightforward, read‑only pass‑through that preserves the current state unchanged.

@lcmState::GetCommand@k_ZNK7cmState10Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetCommand@k_ZNK7cmState10Get.body: It looks up a command by first normalising the supplied name to lower‑case and then hands the lookup off to the internal helper that performs an exact name match.

@lcmState::GetGlobalProperty@k_ZN7cmStat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetGlobalProperty@k_ZN7cmStat.body: The function examines the supplied property name. Depending on the exact string it either pulls a list of internal values (cache keys, command names, enabled languages, known C/C++ features, etc.), converts that list to a string, and stores it in the global property map, or it returns that string directly as a `cmValue`. For the special “CMAKE_…_KNOWN_FEATURES” names it uses a pre‑defined macro list of feature identifiers to build a semi‑colon separated string at compile‑time. If none of the specific names match, the function falls back to the generic property store and returns the requested property’s value.

@lcmState::GetGlobalPropertyAsBool@k_ZN7.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetGlobalPropertyAsBool@k_ZN7.body: Retrieves the value for a given property name from the global configuration store and returns the result of converting that value to a boolean via cmIsOn.

@lcmState::GetInitializedCacheValue@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetInitializedCacheValue@k_ZN.body: Delegates a read‑only lookup to the `CacheManager`, returning the cached value (or `cmValue()`) for the supplied key without mutating the `cmState` instance.

@lcmState::GetLanguageEnabled@k_ZNK7cmSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetLanguageEnabled@k_ZNK7cmSt.body: The `GetLanguageEnabled` member checks whether a language string is present in the `EnabledLanguages` container. It performs a binary search over that container—so the container must be sorted—and returns `true` if the string exists, otherwise `false`. The function is declared `const`, ensuring it does not modify the object.

@lcmState::GetMode@k_ZNK7cmState7GetMode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetMode@k_ZNK7cmState7GetMode.body: The `GetMode` function returns the current `StateMode` stored in the object. Because the method is `const`, callers may safely invoke it on a `const` instance without affecting internal state. It performs a shallow copy of the enum value and should be inlined in production code for minimal overhead. The function is trivial but serves as the canonical accessor; ensure that `StateMode` is an enum or POD type to avoid unnecessary copying. It also guarantees the returned value cannot be modified, protecting encapsulation.

@lcmState::GetPropertyDefinition@k_ZNK7c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetPropertyDefinition@k_ZNK7c.body: The method forwards a lookup request for a property definition identified by its name and scope to the internal `PropertyDefinitions` collection, returning a pointer to the matching definition or `nullptr` if none is found.

@lcmState::GetSourceDirectory@k_ZNK7cmSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetSourceDirectory@k_ZNK7cmSt.body: The method simply returns a const reference to the `SourceDirectory` string stored in the `cmState` object. It guarantees no copy or modification of the string and preserves const‑ness of the caller.

@lcmState::GetTargetTypeName@k_ZN7cmStat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::GetTargetTypeName@k_ZN7cmStat.body: The function takes a target‑type enum value and returns the corresponding string literal. It declares a series of static string constants (generated via a macro) for each possible target, then uses a `switch` to match the incoming enum to the right constant and returns it. If none of the cases matches, an assertion is triggered and an empty string is returned.

@lcmState::InTopLevelIncludes@k_ZNK7cmSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::InTopLevelIncludes@k_ZNK7cmSt.body: This method simply returns the current value of the `ProcessingTopLevelIncludes` flag, indicating whether the instance is presently handling top‑level includes.

@lcmState::IsPropertyChained@k_ZNK7cmSta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::IsPropertyChained@k_ZNK7cmSta.body: The member returns `true` if a property definition with the given name and scope exists and that definition reports itself as chained; otherwise it yields `false`.

@lcmState::ParseCacheEntry@k_ZN7cmState1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::ParseCacheEntry@k_ZN7cmState1.body: The function attempts to parse a string of the form “key:type=value”. It uses two static regexes – one that matches quoted keys and one that matches plain keys – to capture the key, the type token and the value. When a match succeeds it converts the type string to an enum value and trims a surrounding pair of single‑quote marks from the value. If the entry doesn’t match either regex it falls back to a helper that parses an entry without an explicit type. The function returns a boolean indicating whether parsing succeeded.

@lcmState::RemoveBuiltinCommand@k_ZN7cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::RemoveBuiltinCommand@k_ZN7cmS.body: The method removes an entry from the internal map of built‑in commands after verifying that the supplied name is already in lower‑case format, then performs an erase operation on the container.

@lcmState::SetCacheEntryProperty@k_ZN7cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::SetCacheEntryProperty@k_ZN7cm.body: This method simply forwards the supplied key, property name, and value to the underlying `CacheManager`, invoking its `SetCacheEntryProperty` routine with the same parameters.

@lcmState::SetDependencyProvider@k_ZN7cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::SetDependencyProvider@k_ZN7cm.body: It stores the supplied provider into the class’s internal member by moving the argument into `DependencyProvider`. This avoids a copy of the provider object while ensuring the member holds the newly‑provided instance.

@lcmState::SetGlobalProperty@k_ZN7cmStat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::SetGlobalProperty@k_ZN7cmStat.body: The method simply forwards the supplied property name and value to the `GlobalProperties` helper, updating the global configuration accordingly.

@lcmState::SetGlobalProperty@k_ZN7cmStat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::SetGlobalProperty@k_ZN7cmStat.body: The function simply forwards the supplied name‑value pair to the `GlobalProperties` helper, invoking its `SetProperty` method. It accepts two `const std::string&` parameters, so the caller must ensure that the strings are correctly encoded and that the global property collection is already constructed; otherwise a crash or race condition may occur. The routine itself performs no validation or error handling, so callers should validate the property name/value beforehand and consider synchronisation if `GlobalProperties` is accessed from multiple threads.

@lcmState::SetIsGeneratorMultiConfig@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::SetIsGeneratorMultiConfig@k_Z.body: Assigns the `IsGeneratorMultiConfig` member to the supplied boolean value, thereby toggling the internal flag that indicates whether the generator operates in multi‑configuration mode.

@lcmState::SetNinja@k_ZN7cmState8SetNinj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::SetNinja@k_ZN7cmState8SetNinj.body: The function simply stores the supplied boolean in the internal `Ninja` field of the calling object. It performs a direct assignment with no validation, error handling, or side‑effects beyond that single state change.

@lcmState::SetNinjaMulti@k_ZN7cmState13S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::SetNinjaMulti@k_ZN7cmState13S.body: The method simply assigns the incoming Boolean flag to the instance’s `NinjaMulti` member. No additional logic or validation is performed.

@lcmState::SetWatcomWMake@k_ZN7cmState14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::SetWatcomWMake@k_ZN7cmState14.body: Sets the internal flag `WatcomWMake` to the value supplied in the argument.

@lcmState::StringToCacheEntryType@k_ZN7c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::StringToCacheEntryType@k_ZN7c.body: The function maps an input string to a `cmStateEnums::CacheEntryType` enum value. It starts with a default of `STRING`, forwards the string and a reference to that enum to a helper routine that performs the actual conversion, and finally returns the resolved type.

@lcmState::StringToCacheEntryType@k_ZN7c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::StringToCacheEntryType@k_ZN7c.body: This static helper translates a string identifier into its corresponding `cmStateEnums::CacheEntryType` enum value. It searches the global list `cmCacheEntryTypes`; if the string matches an entry, it assigns the enum value derived from the entry’s position and returns `true`. If no match is found, the function leaves the out‑parameter unchanged and returns `false`.

@lcmState::UseGhsMultiIDE@k_ZNK7cmState1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::UseGhsMultiIDE@k_ZNK7cmState1.body: Retrieves the current value of the `GhsMultiIDE` flag stored in the `cmState` instance.

@lcmState::UseMSYSShell@k_ZNK7cmState12U.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::UseMSYSShell@k_ZNK7cmState12U.body: Returns the read‑only flag that tracks whether the MSYS shell is enabled.

@lcmState::UseMinGWMake@k_ZNK7cmState12U.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::UseMinGWMake@k_ZNK7cmState12U.body: Returns the value of the internal `MinGWMake` flag, exposing whether the “min GW make” option is active. The method is `const`, so it guarantees no modification of the object’s state.

@lcmState::UseNMake@k_ZNK7cmState8UseNMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::UseNMake@k_ZNK7cmState8UseNMa.body: The member simply returns the value stored in the member variable `NMake`.

@lcmState::UseNinja@k_ZNK7cmState8UseNin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::UseNinja@k_ZNK7cmState8UseNin.body: The `UseNinja` member simply returns the current value of the `Ninja` flag stored in the instance. It provides a read‑only view of whether the ninja mode is enabled.

@lcmState::UseNinjaMulti@k_ZNK7cmState13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::UseNinjaMulti@k_ZNK7cmState13.body: It returns the current value of the object’s `NinjaMulti` flag, indicating whether that mode is enabled.

@lcmState::UseWatcomWMake@k_ZNK7cmState1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::UseWatcomWMake@k_ZNK7cmState1.body: It returns the current value of the `WatcomWMake` flag stored in the `cmState` object.

@lcmState::UseWindowsShell@k_ZNK7cmState.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::UseWindowsShell@k_ZNK7cmState.body: It returns the value of the member flag that indicates whether the system should use a Windows shell.

@lcmState::UseWindowsVSIDE@k_ZNK7cmState.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmState::UseWindowsVSIDE@k_ZNK7cmState.body: The method simply exposes the current setting that indicates whether the Windows Visual Studio IDE is enabled. It returns the value stored in the `WindowsVSIDE` member without mutating any state.

@lcmStateDetail::PolicyStackEntry::Polic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateDetail::PolicyStackEntry::Polic.body: The constructor builds a PolicyStackEntry by assigning the supplied `derived` reference to its `derived` member and storing the supplied boolean in its `Weak` member; no additional processing occurs in the body.

@lcmStateDetail::PolicyStackEntry::Polic.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateDetail::PolicyStackEntry::Polic.body: Constructs a PolicyStackEntry instance, storing the supplied bool in Weak. The constructor accepts an optional flag (default false) and forwards it to the member Weak via an initializer‑list.

@lcmStateDirectory::GetCurrentBinary@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateDirectory::GetCurrentBinary@k_Z.body: It simply returns the `OutputLocation` string stored in the `DirectoryState` instance, without changing any state.

@lcmStateDirectory::GetCurrentSource@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateDirectory::GetCurrentSource@k_Z.body: The `GetCurrentSource` method simply returns a reference to the `Location` string stored in the `DirectoryState` object. It’s a const accessor that never modifies state and guarantees read‑only access to the current directory path.

@lcmStateDirectory::GetProperty@k_ZNK16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateDirectory::GetProperty@k_ZNK16c.body: The function receives a property name, queries whether that property is “chained” (i.e. whether it’s value depends on another property) via the `IsPropertyChained` call, and then forwards the request to a helper that accepts the property and a boolean flag indicating whether chaining should be honoured. The helper then performs the actual lookup.

@lcmStateDirectory::GetProperty@k_ZNK16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateDirectory::GetProperty@k_ZNK16c.body: The function checks the requested property name against a set of predefined keys. For common keys such as “PARENT_DIRECTORY”, “BINARY_DIR”, “SOURCE_DIR”, and various list‑type properties (sub‑directories, targets, cache entries, compile/link options, etc.), it constructs a string (often a comma‑separated list) from the current directory or snapshot state and returns it wrapped in a `cmValue`. If the property is not one of those known keys, the function queries the directory’s internal property map; if that returns nothing and the caller requested a chained lookup, it recursively consults the parent directory snapshot and ultimately falls back to the global snapshot state.

@lcmStateDirectory::SetCurrentBinary@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateDirectory::SetCurrentBinary@k_Z.body: The function updates the internal output location path by storing the supplied directory string, normalizing path separators to Unix format, resolving any redundant path components, and finally registering the resolved path as the current binary directory definition for the build system.

@lcmStateDirectory::SetCurrentSource@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateDirectory::SetCurrentSource@k_Z.body: Assigns the supplied path to the internal state string, normalizes the slash format to Unix style, removes any redundant “/./” components, and records the resolved path in the snapshot under the key for the current source directory.

@lcmStateSnapshot::CanPopPolicyScope@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::CanPopPolicyScope@k_Z.body: It returns true when the current position’s `Policies` pointer differs from its `PolicyScope` pointer, indicating that a policy scope can be popped; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmStateSnapshot::GetBuildsystemDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::GetBuildsystemDirecto.body: The function creates and returns a `cmStateSnapshot` that captures the current internal state and the current build‑system directory scope. It pulls `State` and `Position->BuildSystemDirectory->CurrentScope` from the instance and packages them into the snapshot struct.

@lcmStateSnapshot::GetBuildsystemDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::GetBuildsystemDirecto.body:
The method returns a snapshot of the directory that contains the current snapshot’s position.  
If the instance has no state or the current position is at the root, it returns an empty snapshot. Otherwise it resolves the parent directory and, when that parent is not root, it builds a snapshot pointing to that parent’s current build‑system scope.

@lcmStateSnapshot::GetDefinition@k_ZNK15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::GetDefinition@k_ZNK15.body: The method retrieves the value associated with a given definition name from the current snapshot’s context. It first asserts that the snapshot’s variable store is valid, then delegates to the global `cmDefinitions` lookup passing the requested name, the snapshot’s variable set, and the root context to obtain the appropriate `cmValue`.

@lcmStateSnapshot::GetDirectory@k_ZNK15c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::GetDirectory@k_ZNK15c.body: The function returns a `cmStateDirectory` instance that bundles the current object’s `Position->BuildSystemDirectory` reference with the snapshot itself. It simply packages those two pieces into the returned structure.

@lcmStateSnapshot::GetPolicy@k_ZNK15cmSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::GetPolicy@k_ZNK15cmSt.body: Retrieves the effective policy for a given policy ID by walking up the build‑system directory tree from the current scope and returning the first defined policy found. If no explicit policy exists along the chain it returns the default status.

@lcmStateSnapshot::GetProjectName@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::GetProjectName@k_ZNK1.body: Returns a copy of the stored project name from the snapshot’s build‑system directory. It assumes the internal pointers are valid; if they’re null a dereference exception would be thrown.

@lcmStateSnapshot::GetState@k_ZNK15cmSta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::GetState@k_ZNK15cmSta.body: The `GetState()` member simply returns a raw pointer to the `cmState` instance stored inside the snapshot object. Because it’s marked `const`, the method guarantees not to modify the snapshot’s state; it merely hands back the stored pointer. Callers receive this pointer directly and must treat it as read‑only unless they explicitly copy or clone the underlying state. The function performs no copy or cloning—it just forwards the internal `State` member, so the returned pointer reflects the lifetime of the snapshot object itself.

@lcmStateSnapshot::IsValid@k_ZNK15cmStat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::IsValid@k_ZNK15cmStat.body: The method returns `true` only when the snapshot’s internal `State` pointer is non‑null, its `Position` object reports itself as valid, and that position is not the root of the snapshot’s underlying data. Otherwise it yields `false`.

@lcmStateSnapshot::RemoveDefinition@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::RemoveDefinition@k_ZN.body: Internally, the method clears the variable identified by *name* from the current position’s map of variables.

@lcmStateSnapshot::SetDefaultDefinitions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::SetDefaultDefinitions.body: The method populates internal definitions that describe the current build environment. It queries the host system name, then sets flags such as WIN32, UNIX, APPLE, BSD variants, and Linux, all of which map to the platform’s identifier strings. It records CMake version components (major, minor, patch, tweak, full string) and the files directory path. Finally, it establishes the default include‑file regex to match any file path.

@lcmStateSnapshot::cmStateSnapshot@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::cmStateSnapshot@k_ZN1.body: A `cmStateSnapshot` instance captures a point‑in‑time view of an object’s state. Its public constructor takes another snapshot by reference and performs a shallow copy of the internal state data. This allows a lightweight, read‑only view of the current state that can be inspected without mutating the original object.

@lcmStateSnapshot::operator=@k_ZN15cmSta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::operator=@k_ZN15cmSta.body: The operator overload implements a move‑assignment: it replaces the contents of the left‑hand object with those of the right‑hand rvalue and returns a reference to the updated object. This allows efficient assignment of temporary snapshots while enabling chained assignments.

@lcmStateSnapshot::operator=@k_ZN15cmSta.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStateSnapshot::operator=@k_ZN15cmSta.body: The assignment operator copies all internal state from the supplied snapshot into the current instance, updating every relevant member and finally returns a reference to *this for chaining.

@lcmStrCat@k_Z8cmStrCatOT_OT0_DpOT1_@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrCat@k_Z8cmStrCatOT_OT0_DpOT1_@f./.body: The `cmStrCat` template takes one or more arguments, turns each into a pair consisting of a view of the string‑like value and a pointer to its owning string, and forwards those pairs to `cmCatViews`. The resulting `std::string` is the concatenated result of all supplied arguments.

@lcmStrLen@k_Z8cmStrLenRAT__Kc@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrLen@k_Z8cmStrLenRAT__Kc@f./Source.body: Template accepts a reference to a character array; at compile time it returns the array’s size minus one, effectively giving the length of a null‑terminated string literal.

@lcmStrToLong@k_Z11cmStrToLongPKcPl@f./S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrToLong@k_Z11cmStrToLongPKcPl@f./S.body: It wraps `strtol` for you: it clears `errno`, calls `strtol` with base 10, stores the result in the supplied pointer, and returns true only when the conversion consumed the whole string (the returned pointer points to a terminating NUL), the original pointer was advanced, and no errno flag was set—i.e. no overflow, under‑flow, or syntax error occurred.

@lcmStrToLong@k_Z11cmStrToLongRKNSt3__11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrToLong@k_Z11cmStrToLongRKNSt3__11.body: Delegates conversion of a `std::string` to a raw C‑string, but the call is syntactically incorrect and never writes the resulting `long` value to `*value`.

@lcmStrToLongLong@k_Z15cmStrToLongLongPK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrToLongLong@k_Z15cmStrToLongLongPK.body: The function converts a C‑string into a 64‑bit integer using the standard `strtoll` routine. It places the result in the supplied `value` pointer and returns `true` only when the conversion succeeds without leftover characters and no error flag was raised. It returns `false` if the string contains non‑numeric characters, is empty, or the conversion overflows.

@lcmStrToLongLong@k_Z15cmStrToLongLongRK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrToLongLong@k_Z15cmStrToLongLongRK.body:
The helper simply forwards the call to an overload that accepts a C‑style string, so the code is only a thin wrapper. The only concerns are the usual pitfalls:  
• the header `<string>` must be included, otherwise `std::string` is unresolved;  
• the member should be `c_str()` (no `c_str`).  
• It returns whatever the underlying overload returns.

@lcmStrToULong@k_Z12cmStrToULongPKcPm@f..author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrToULong@k_Z12cmStrToULongPKcPm@f..body: The routine trims leading whitespace, disallows a leading minus sign, then calls `strtoul` (base‑10). It succeeds only when the conversion consumes the entire input string (i.e. `endp == str` is false and the final character is the null terminator) and no error flag (`errno`) is set during the conversion. It returns true on a successful parse and false otherwise.

@lcmStrToULong@k_Z12cmStrToULongRKNSt3__.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrToULong@k_Z12cmStrToULongRKNSt3__.body: Converts a `std::string` into an unsigned long by delegating to the overload that takes a C‑string pointer, returning `true` only when the conversion succeeds.

@lcmStrToULongLong@k_Z16cmStrToULongLong.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrToULongLong@k_Z16cmStrToULongLong.body: The function converts a C‑string into an unsigned 64‑bit integer. It first skips leading whitespace; if the first non‑space character is ‘‑’, parsing fails. It then calls the helper `strtoull` to perform the base‑10 conversion and succeeds only when the entire string was consumed (next char is `'\0'`) and no parsing error (`errno==0`). The returned value is stored in the supplied pointer.

@lcmStrToULongLong@k_Z16cmStrToULongLong.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStrToULongLong@k_Z16cmStrToULongLong.body: The function takes a `std::string` and a pointer to an unsigned long long variable, then forwards those arguments to another overload that accepts a C‑style string. It returns the result of that call. Its job is to parse the string into an unsigned 64‑bit integer and store it in the supplied pointer.

@lcmStringCommand@k_Z15cmStringCommandRK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStringCommand@k_Z15cmStringCommandRK.body: Handles a collection of string‑based subcommands by mapping each subcommand name to a corresponding handler function. It first verifies that at least one argument is supplied, then looks up the first argument in a static map of subcommand strings to handler functions, and finally invokes the matched handler with the remaining arguments and a status reference.

@lcmStringReplaceHelper::GetError@k_ZN21.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStringReplaceHelper::GetError@k_ZN21.body: This function returns a const reference to the internal string member `ErrorString`. It returns the string unchanged, allowing callers to read the error message without copying the string. The method should be marked `const` to emphasize that it does not modify the object.

@lcmStringReplaceHelper::IsRegularExpres.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStringReplaceHelper::IsRegularExpres.body: Returns the internal `RegularExpression` object's validity state.

@lcmStringReplaceHelper::IsReplaceExpres.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStringReplaceHelper::IsReplaceExpres.body: Returns true if the internal flag `ValidReplaceExpression` is set, otherwise false.

@lcmStringReplaceHelper::ParseReplaceExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStringReplaceHelper::ParseReplaceExp.body: The routine scans the internal replace‑expression string character by character, splitting it into literal fragments and escape sequences. When it encounters a backslash, it determines whether the following character is a digit (interpreted as a placeholder index), ‘n’ (interpreted as a newline) or a literal backslash, and appends the resolved value to the internal replacement buffer. If an unknown escape or a trailing backslash appears, it flags the expression as invalid and records an error message.

@lcmStringReplaceHelper::Replace@k_ZN21c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStringReplaceHelper::Replace@k_ZN21c.body: The Replace function clears the output string, scans the input string for matches to a pre‑compiled regular expression, and sequentially builds the output by appending non‑matched fragments and the replacement text (plain text or captured groups) for each match. If a match has zero length it reports an error. The function returns true on success or false when an error (empty match or out‑of‑range back‑reference) occurs.

@lcmStringReplaceHelper::cmStringReplace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStringReplaceHelper::cmStringReplace.body: The constructor assigns the supplied regex and replacement string to internal members, stores a reference to the supplied makefile, and immediately invokes ParseReplaceExpression() to process the replace pattern.

@lcmStripSuffixIfExists@k_Z21cmStripSuff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStripSuffixIfExists@k_Z21cmStripSuff.body: The function removes the last character from a string if that character matches the supplied suffix; it relies on a helper that checks whether the string ends with that suffix before calling `pop_back`.

@lcmStripSuffixIfExists@k_Z21cmStripSuff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmStripSuffixIfExists@k_Z21cmStripSuff.body: The `cmStripSuffixIfExists` helper scans a given string and, if that string ends with the supplied suffix, truncates the suffix out of the string in‑place. It uses a `string_view` for the suffix to avoid copies and only mutates the original string when the suffix is actually present; otherwise the string remains unchanged.

@lcmSubcommandTable::cmSubcommandTable::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSubcommandTable::cmSubcommandTable::.body: This lambda returns a boolean that is true when the first element of `left` is strictly less than the first element of `right`. It is typically used as a comparison function for sorting containers that store elements with a `first` member.

@lcmSubcommandTable::cmSubcommandTable@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSubcommandTable::cmSubcommandTable@k.body: Creates an instance from a list of elements, copies them into its internal storage, and then sorts that storage by each element’s first member so that subsequent lookups can be performed efficiently.

@lcmSubcommandTable::operator()::[lambda.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSubcommandTable::operator()::[lambda.body: It evaluates whether an element’s first field precedes a supplied key string, returning true if that field is lexicographically smaller.

@lcmSubcommandTable::operator()@k_ZNK17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSubcommandTable::operator()@k_ZNK17c.body: The function performs a binary search in the table’s internal container to locate a sub‑command matching the supplied key. If a matching entry is found, it invokes the associated handler with the provided arguments and status object, propagating any status changes and returning the handler’s success flag. If no entry matches, it records an error message in *status* and returns `false`.

@lcmSubdirCommand@k_Z15cmSubdirCommandRK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSubdirCommand@k_Z15cmSubdirCommandRK.body: The routine parses the arguments supplied to a SUBDIRS command. It validates the argument list, then iterates over each entry. For a relative path it resolves the source and binary locations and registers the sub‑directory via `AddSubDirectory`; for an absolute path it uses the last path component to compute the binary location. If a path does not exist an error is recorded and the overall result flag is set to false. The `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` token simply turns on an exclusion flag used when adding the directory. The function returns true only when every supplied directory exists and was successfully added.

@lcmSystemTools::AppendEnv@k_ZN13cmSyste.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::AppendEnv@k_ZN13cmSyste.body: The function iterates over the supplied vector of strings and invokes the helper routine PutEnv once per entry, thereby adding each string as a new environment variable. It performs a straightforward linear pass (O(n)) over the input, with no error handling; any failure in PutEnv would propagate back to the caller.

@lcmSystemTools::CalculateCommandLineLen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CalculateCommandLineLen.body: The function determines the maximum size in bytes for a command‑line argument string. It first sets a hard‑coded limit (8191 bytes on Windows, or PAGE_SIZE × 32 on Linux). It then queries the system via `sysconf(_SC_ARG_MAX)` to get the runtime‑defined `ARG_MAX` value and reduces it slightly to leave space for environment data. The final limit is the smaller of the two values (or the raw value on other platforms).

@lcmSystemTools::ChangeRPath@k_ZN13cmSys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ChangeRPath@k_ZN13cmSys.body: The function is a small, static helper that opens a given file, searches its contents for any instance of the supplied “old” path string, and rewrites the file with that string replaced by the current working‑directory path. It returns `true` on success and `false` if the file cannot be read, the old string isn’t appear, or the write operation fails. It assumes the caller will supply the new path via the current program directory and that the file is text‑based so string replacement is straightforward.

@lcmSystemTools::ChangeRPath@k_ZN13cmSys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ChangeRPath@k_ZN13cmSys.body: The function tries to update an RPATH entry in a given file. It first calls a helper routine specific to “ELF” format; if that succeeds it returns its result. If not, it falls back to a routine for “XCOFF” format. If neither helper can handle the file format, it sets an error message (unless one is already supplied) and returns false, otherwise returns true.

@lcmSystemTools::CheckRPath@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CheckRPath@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: CheckRPath verifies that the supplied file can be located within the directory described by newRPath and returns true only when that file is accessible and no security constraints are violated.

@lcmSystemTools::CheckRPath@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CheckRPath@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: The function opens the file, attempts to parse it as an ELF executable and, if successful, checks whether the ELF’s RPATH or RUNPATH entries already contain the supplied new path. If the new path string is empty, the function succeeds only when those entries are present; otherwise, it searches the entry’s value for the new path as a substring. If the file is an XCOFF executable, it performs the same test on the binary’s lib‑path entry. The function returns true only when the new path is already represented in the appropriate RPATH‑type entry; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToLongPath@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToLongPath@k_ZN1.body: Converts a string in‑place by normalizing separators, stripping redundant components (``.```, ``..``) and expanding any environment or shortcut tokens so that the resulting buffer contains a fully qualified path.

@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToLongPath@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToLongPath@k_ZN1.body: The routine scans a Windows‑only path for a tilde character; if found it calls the Win32 API to resolve the path to its fully‑qualified form, overwriting the original string with the wide‑to‑narrow conversion of that long form. On non‑Windows builds the body is a no‑op.

@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputPath@k_Z.body: `ConvertToOutputPath` normalises a file system path so that it can be safely used as a target directory or file name. It converts back‑slashes to forward slashes, removes redundant path components, and guarantees the resulting string ends with a directory separator if it represents a directory. The function returns this cleaned‑up string for use in file‑generation helpers.

@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputPath@k_Z.body: Converts a supplied path string to the appropriate file‑system form for the current target: on Windows it returns a Windows‑style path unless a global flag forces Unix‑style paths; on non‑Windows targets it always produces a Unix style path.

@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputSlashes@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputSlashes@.body: The function normalises a file‑path string by ensuring the directory separators match the current output convention (e.g. converting “\” to “/” on POSIX or the inverse on Windows). It mutates the `path` argument in‑place, so callers receive a ready‑to‑use string without allocating a new buffer.

@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputSlashes@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToOutputSlashes@.body: The routine scans the supplied string; when building a Windows build that is not forced to use Unix‐style slashes, it walks the string replacing every ‘/’ character with ‘\’. If those compile conditions aren’t met, the code simply does nothing (the static_cast line is a no‑op).

@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToRunCommandPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToRunCommandPath.body: The function takes a file‑path string and returns a normalized, “run‑ready” path string. It resolves any relative path components, cleans up path separators to match the current OS, and removes trailing slashes so that the resulting string can be inserted directly into a command line.

@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToRunCommandPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ConvertToRunCommandPath.body: Converts a given file system path to the format suitable for the current operating‑system. At compile‑time it checks if the target platform is a Windows build (using the _WIN32 flag) and not a Cygwin target; if so, it forwards the string to a Windows‑specific conversion routine, otherwise it uses the Unix‑specific routine. The function simply returns that result.

@lcmSystemTools::CopySingleFile@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CopySingleFile@k_ZN13cm.body: Copies a single file from a given source path, returning a `CopyResult` that signals success or failure of the copy operation.

@lcmSystemTools::CopySingleFile@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CopySingleFile@k_ZN13cm.body: CopySingleFile performs a conditional copy of a file from oldname to newname, checking whether the files differ, falling back to a blockwise copy on failure, handling Windows‑specific locking retries, setting file permissions on the target, and reporting errors via an optional string pointer.

@lcmSystemTools::CreateLink@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateLink@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: CreateLink is a static helper that attempts to establish a link from a supplied source path. It performs the necessary file operations, returns a cmsys::Status indicating success or failure, and propagates any I/O errors back to the caller.

@lcmSystemTools::CreateLink@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateLink@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: The function invokes a quiet variant of the link‑creation routine, examines the returned status, and if the operation fails it emits a detailed error message composed with `cmStrCat` and `status.GetString()`. Finally it propagates the status value back to the caller.

@lcmSystemTools::CreateLinkQuietly@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateLinkQuietly@k_ZN1.body: The function is a public static helper that attempts to create a hard or symbolic link from a source file to a target path and returns a `cmsys::Status` indicating success or failure. It performs the operation without emitting diagnostic messages, relying on the caller to handle any errors.

@lcmSystemTools::CreateLinkQuietly@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateLinkQuietly@k_ZN1.body: Creates a hard link by calling uv_fs_link, capturing any error and converting the returned errno into a cmsys::Status object that distinguishes Windows and POSIX cases (with a special path for older libuv builds). If the link operation fails, the function maps the libuv system error into a proper status code and returns it; otherwise it returns a default‑constructed status (implying success).

@lcmSystemTools::CreateSymlink@k_ZN13cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateSymlink@k_ZN13cmS.body: Creates a symlink from the given source path to the specified target and returns a cmsys::Status indicating success or failure.

@lcmSystemTools::CreateSymlink@k_ZN13cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateSymlink@k_ZN13cmS.body: Creates a symbolic link by delegating to a quiet helper. If the helper reports failure, the routine logs the error message. The operation status is then returned.

@lcmSystemTools::CreateSymlinkQuietly@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateSymlinkQuietly@k_.body: The function **CreateSymlinkQuietly** attempts to create a symbolic link from the source path (`origName`) to the destination path (`toFile`/`newFileName`). It returns a `cmsys::Status` indicating success or failure and internally suppresses any diagnostic messages so the caller receives only the final status.

@lcmSystemTools::CreateSymlinkQuietly@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateSymlinkQuietly@k_.body:
Creates a symbolic link from the supplied source path to the target path.  
The routine prepares a `uv_fs_req_t` request, optionally sets the `UV_FS_SYMLINK_DIR` flag when the source is a directory (on Windows), calls `uv_fs_symlink`, and translates any libuv error into a `cmsys::Status` value. It returns that status, which callers can inspect to determine whether the link was created successfully or why it failed.

@lcmSystemTools::CreateTar@k_ZN13cmSyste.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateTar@k_ZN13cmSyste.body: Creates a tar archive named *outFileName*, packing the supplied files into a single file. It opens the target file for writing, iterates over each file path, writes the proper header entries, copies the file data, and finalizes the stream. The routine returns *true* on success or *false* if any step fails.

@lcmSystemTools::CreateTar@k_ZN13cmSyste.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::CreateTar@k_ZN13cmSyste.body: The routine opens the target file and feeds a list of file paths into a tar‑writer object. It selects the requested compression mode (none, gzip, bzip2, xz, or zstd), configures the archive’s format string and log verbosity, then iterates over each supplied path adding the file to the archive. If any add fails it reports the error and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmSystemTools::DisableRunCommandOutput.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::DisableRunCommandOutput.body: Disables command‑output by setting a global flag to true.

@lcmSystemTools::DoNotInheritStdPipes@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::DoNotInheritStdPipes@k_.body: The routine checks whether the current process is attached to a console screen buffer. If it is, it simply returns without touching anything. If it isn’t, it duplicates the current process’s standard output and error handles and re‑sets them, ensuring that the process’s stdout and stderr are not inherited by subsequent console processes.

@lcmSystemTools::DoesFileExistWithExtens.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::DoesFileExistWithExtens.body: The static helper iterates through a supplied list of extensions, appending each to a base path and checking for existence (typically via `std::filesystem::exists`). If any constructed path exists, it returns true; otherwise false. It is used in several parts of the code to verify that a file can be located under a set of alternative suffixes, simplifying downstream path‑resolution logic.

@lcmSystemTools::DoesFileExistWithExtens.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::DoesFileExistWithExtens.body: The routine iterates over the supplied extensions list, concatenating each extension to the supplied base name, and invokes the underlying file‑existence query. If any of the generated names resolves to an existing file, it returns true; otherwise it falls through and returns false.

@lcmSystemTools::EnableRunCommandOutput@.author: AI Short Overview
