@lcmSystemTools::EnableRunCommandOutput@.body: Enabling output by clearing the disable flag – the function simply sets `s_DisableRunCommandOutput` to `false` so that any output generated by a run‑command routine can be emitted.

@lcmSystemTools::EnableVSConsoleOutput@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnableVSConsoleOutput@k.body: The function sets up the environment for Visual Studio build tools to emit their diagnostic output to the console. It writes the variable `vsconsoleoutput=1` and, unless the CMake bootstrap path is used, clears the `VS_UNICODE_OUTPUT` flag that forces MS tools to redirect output through a special pipe. This ensures that standard tools such as `cl` and `devenv` produce console‑visible logs.

@lcmSystemTools::EncodeURL@k_ZN13cmSyste.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EncodeURL@k_ZN13cmSyste.body: The static `EncodeURL` helper takes a raw string and returns a percent‑escaped version suitable for inclusion in a URL path or query. It walks the input character‑by‑character, replacing spaces and other reserved symbols with the proper “%HH” escape sequence (e.g., “ ” → “%20”).  It also normalises Unicode bytes that may otherwise break a URL parser. The function is designed for reuse wherever any module needs to embed arbitrary text safely in an HTTP request.

@lcmSystemTools::EncodeURL@k_ZN13cmSyste.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EncodeURL@k_ZN13cmSyste.body: The function walks through the input string, building a new string. For each character it checks whether it is a reserved symbol (`+`, `?`, `&`, space, `=`, `%`) or a slash. If it is one of the reserved symbols it replaces that character with its percent‑encoded form (e.g. `%20` for space). If `escapeSlashes` is true, a `/` is replaced with `%2F`. Otherwise the original character is copied unchanged. The loop appends the produced characters to the output string and finally returns that string.

@lcmSystemTools::EnsureStdPipes@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnsureStdPipes@k_ZN13cm.body: The `EnsureStdPipes` routine guarantees that the standard file descriptors for stdin, stdout, and stderr are properly configured. It simply invokes `EnsureStdPipe` on each of the three descriptor numbers (STDIN_FILENO, STDOUT_FILENO, and STDERR_FILENO), which typically ensures that those descriptors are open and valid (for example by re‑opening them to `/dev/null` if they’re closed).

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::AppendEnv@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::AppendEnv@k_ZN.body: The routine walks through the supplied vector of strings, invoking PutEnv for each element to add it into the internal environment store.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ApplyToCurrent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ApplyToCurrent.body: Applies the current environment configuration to the running system, optionally outputting diagnostics to the supplied string stream.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ApplyToCurrent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ApplyToCurrent.body:
The `ApplyToCurrentEnv` routine applies each pending environment‑variable change recorded in the `diff` collection to the current process’ environment.  
For every entry, it tests whether a new value is present:  

* if a value exists, it assembles a “name=value” string, invokes `PutEnv` to install that assignment, and optionally logs the change to the supplied `measurement` stream.  
* If no value is supplied, it clears the variable by calling `UnsetEnv`, and if measurement is requested, it emits a line prefixed with “#” to signal that the variable is being actively removed.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::EnvDiff@k_ZN13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::EnvDiff@k_ZN13.body: Calculates the changes between two environment snapshots and returns a mapping of those differences.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.body: It looks up‑a‑dot‑makes an optional lookup in `diff[name]`; if the key is missing it falls back to `cmSystemTools::GetEnv(name)`; the resolved string is then passed to the supplied callback `apply`, after which the map is updated with that value.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.body: The lambda captures a string `value` and simply appends it to the `output` string passed into `apply_diff`.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.body: The lambda captures an external variable `value` by reference and, when invoked, inserts that value at the beginning of the string passed to it, effectively prepending the captured content to the supplied output string.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.body: The lambda captures a separator string and a value; when invoked it first appends that separator to the output string if the string already contains content, and then appends the captured value.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.body: The lambda captures `value` and `path_sep` and, when invoked with a string reference, it first inserts the separator at the very front if the string already has content, then inserts `value` at the front again—so the resulting string ends with `value` followed by the optional separator and the original content.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.body: The lambda captures a value and, when called, appends that value to a string passed by reference. It inserts a semicolon before the new content only if the string already contains text, preventing a leading separator.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.body: This lambda inserts the supplied `value` at the front of `output`, first prefixing a semicolon if `output` already contains data.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.body: ParseOperation examines the supplied string and attempts to configure an operation accordingly. On success it returns true; otherwise it signals failure.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::ParseOperation.body: The function parses a string of the form `name=op:value`. It resolves the current value of the named variable, applies the requested operation (reset, set, unset, append/prepend variants for strings, path lists, or cmake‑lists), and updates the internal `diff` map with the new value. If an unknown operation is supplied or required delimiters are missing, it reports an error and returns `false`. If everything succeeds, it returns `true`.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::PutEnv@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::PutEnv@k_ZN13c.body: This function stores the supplied string in an internal environment‑map (or similar data structure) so that subsequent calls to the system can query the value via a key that matches the string. The implementation usually validates the input string, ensures it is not empty, and then writes the value into a thread‑safe map or configuration object. On error, it throws a standard exception or logs an error, allowing callers to catch and react appropriately.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::PutEnv@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::PutEnv@k_ZN13c.body: Parses a string of the form “key=value”, splits it at the first “=”, and stores the part after the separator in the internal map under that key. If no “=” is present it forwards the string to its `UnPutEnv` routine.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::UnPutEnv@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::UnPutEnv@k_ZN1.body: UnPutEnv deletes the named environment variable from the process environment, effectively unsetting it.

@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::UnPutEnv@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::EnvDiff::UnPutEnv@k_ZN1.body: The function registers the given environment key in the internal diff map by assigning it an empty value, effectively marking that no differences exist for that key.

@lcmSystemTools::Error@k_ZN13cmSystemToo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Error@k_ZN13cmSystemToo.body: The `Error` static method simply accepts a message string and forwards it to the system’s error‑handling routine (typically logging or printing to standard‑error). It acts as a one‑line façade for reporting fatal or recoverable errors across the application modules.

@lcmSystemTools::Error@k_ZN13cmSystemToo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Error@k_ZN13cmSystemToo.body: The function prefixes the supplied text with “CMake Error: ”, sets an internal flag indicating an error has occurred, and forwards the resulting string to a message‑handling routine with a “Error” tag.

@lcmSystemTools::ExpandRegistryValues@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ExpandRegistryValues@k_.body: The `ExpandRegistryValues` static function receives a string by reference, parses that string for known registry‑style tokens, and writes the resolved values back into the supplied string. It essentially resolves any placeholders or encoded values found in the input and replaces them with their actual registry contents.

@lcmSystemTools::ExpandRegistryValues@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ExpandRegistryValues@k_.body: The routine walks through the supplied string, locating each substring that matches the pattern “\[HKEY…\]”. For every match it pulls out the captured key, builds a new string in the form “/[captured‑key]”, and substitutes that original fragment with this new string. In effect, every registry key reference in the source is expanded into a slash‑prefixed path.

@lcmSystemTools::ExtractTar@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ExtractTar@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: The function opens a .tar archive supplied via the path argument, extracts each entry to the current working directory (preserving permissions when possible), and reports success via a boolean return value.

@lcmSystemTools::ExtractTar@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ExtractTar@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: The function orchestrates the extraction of a tar archive into the specified output directory. It forwards the supplied file list, verbosity flag, and timestamp extraction option to an internal helper, returning true on success (or false when the build‑time flag disables the operation).

@lcmSystemTools::FileExistsInParentDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::FileExistsInParentDirec.body: Given a starting directory and a filename, the routine walks upward through the directory hierarchy, checking each parent directory for a file that matches the supplied name. It returns the full path of the first matching file it encounters; if no such file exists in any ancestor, it returns an empty string.

@lcmSystemTools::FileExistsInParentDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::FileExistsInParentDirec.body: The routine starts at the supplied directory, normalises slashes, and then climbs up the directory hierarchy, at each level concatenating the supplied file name to the current directory path. At each step it invokes FileExists to see whether that file is present. If it finds the file, the fully‑qualified path is returned; otherwise it continues up until the specified top‑level directory is reached or until no further parents exist. If no match is found it returns an empty string.

@lcmSystemTools::FindCMakeResources@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::FindCMakeResources@k_ZN.body: The routine probes the operating system’s executable path, resolves symlinks, and populates internal globals that point to the CMake binaries, ensuring bootstrapped builds find their tools and documentation.

@lcmSystemTools::ForceToRelativePath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ForceToRelativePath@k_Z.body: It normalizes a file path against a base directory, stripping redundant slashes and `..`/`.` components to return a clean relative path string.

@lcmSystemTools::ForceToRelativePath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ForceToRelativePath@k_Z.body: The function takes a base path and a target path and returns the target path expressed relative to that base. It splits both paths into components, finds the longest shared prefix, then builds a relative path by prepending `..` for each unmatched component of the base and appending the remaining components from the target.

@lcmSystemTools::GetCMClDepsCommand@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetCMClDepsCommand@k_ZN.body: The function simply returns a reference to the static string that holds the command used to invoke the CMCl dependencies routine.

@lcmSystemTools::GetCMakeCommand@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetCMakeCommand@k_ZN13c.body: The function simply returns a reference to a static string that holds the name of the CMake command. It is const‑qualified to guarantee that callers cannot modify the stored value, and the returned reference allows callers to use the command string without copying it. This helper is used by the system to obtain the specific CMake command string for building or configuring targets.

@lcmSystemTools::GetCMakeCursesCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetCMakeCursesCommand@k.body: The function simply returns a reference to a pre‑defined string that contains the command line used to invoke CMakeCurses.

@lcmSystemTools::GetCMakeGUICommand@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetCMakeGUICommand@k_ZN.body: Delivers the command string that launches the CMake GUI.

@lcmSystemTools::GetCMakeRoot@k_ZN13cmSy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetCMakeRoot@k_ZN13cmSy.body: The method simply returns a constant reference to the string that holds the CMake root path (stored in the static member `cmSystemToolsCMakeRoot`).

@lcmSystemTools::GetCPackCommand@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetCPackCommand@k_ZN13c.body: The `GetCPackCommand()` function simply returns a reference to the static command string stored in `cmSystemToolsCPackCommand`. No arguments are taken, and the returned value can be used directly as the command string to invoke cpack.

@lcmSystemTools::GetCTestCommand@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetCTestCommand@k_ZN13c.body: This function simply returns a reference to a constant string that represents the CTest command used elsewhere in the system. Its purpose is to provide a single source of that command string so other parts of the code can retrieve it without needing to duplicate the literal.

@lcmSystemTools::GetCurrentWorkingDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetCurrentWorkingDirect.body: Retrieves the current working directory from the system tool and normalises the path via `CollapseFullPath` before returning it as a standard `std::string`.

@lcmSystemTools::GetEnvVar@k_ZN13cmSyste.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetEnvVar@k_ZN13cmSyste.body: It looks up a string from the process environment and wraps the result in an `optional<std::string>`. If the requested key isn’t present, the function yields an empty optional; if it is present, the optional holds the corresponding value.

@lcmSystemTools::GetEnvVar@k_ZN13cmSyste.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetEnvVar@k_ZN13cmSyste.body: The function attempts to read the value of an environment variable named `var`. If successful, it wraps that value in a `cm::optional<std::string>` and returns it; if the variable is not present or not readable, it returns an empty optional.

@lcmSystemTools::GetEnvironmentVariables.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetEnvironmentVariables.body: The function collects all environment entries in the current process’s environment block, converts each entry to a narrow‑string (UTF‑8 or ASCII) on Windows using the helper `ToNarrow`, and returns a `std::vector<std::string>` of those values. On non‑Windows builds it simply appends the raw C‑style strings.

@lcmSystemTools::GetErrorOccurredFlag@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetErrorOccurredFlag@k_.body: Checks whether any of the global error flags or the interrupt condition is active and returns true if any of those conditions is set.

@lcmSystemTools::GetFatalErrorOccurred@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetFatalErrorOccurred@k.body: It returns true when either the global fatal‑error flag or the current interrupt state indicates a critical fault – effectively signalling that a fatal condition has been detected and must be handled immediately.

@lcmSystemTools::GetForceUnixPaths@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetForceUnixPaths@k_ZN1.body: It returns the current value stored in the static member `s_ForceUnixPaths`, indicating whether Unix‑style path handling is forced.

@lcmSystemTools::GetHTMLDoc@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetHTMLDoc@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: Returns a reference to the internal string `cmSystemToolsHTMLDoc`.

@lcmSystemTools::GetInterruptFlag@k_ZN13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetInterruptFlag@k_ZN13.body: The function examines whether the stored interrupt callback exists; if it does, it invokes that callback and forwards its boolean result; otherwise it simply returns `false`.

@lcmSystemTools::GetRealPathResolvingWin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetRealPathResolvingWin.body: The function takes a Windows‑style path string that may contain environment variables or relative segments, and returns the canonical absolute path for that location by expanding any `$(VAR)` placeholders, normalising slashes, and resolving `.`/..` components against the current working directory. It performs the expansion in a single pass and throws an exception if the path cannot be resolved.

@lcmSystemTools::GetRealPathResolvingWin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetRealPathResolvingWin.body:
The function first attempts to resolve the provided path using the Windows‑specific `uv_fs_realpath` API.  
If that succeeds, it normalizes the result (converting back‑slashes to slashes and upper‑casing the drive letter).  
If `uv_fs_realpath` reports “no system” (`UV_ENOSYS`), it falls back to the generic `GetRealPath` implementation.  
On any other error, it formats the system error message into `errorMessage` and returns an empty string; otherwise it simply returns the resolved path.

@lcmSystemTools::GetRunCommandHideConsol.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetRunCommandHideConsol.body: Retrieves the current state of the runtime flag that controls whether a console window is suppressed during command execution. It simply returns the internal static variable s_RunCommandHideConsole.

@lcmSystemTools::GetRunCommandOutput@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetRunCommandOutput@k_Z.body: This static function simply returns the value of the static boolean variable `s_DisableRunCommandOutput`. It has no parameters and returns `true` or `false` depending on that variable’s current state.

@lcmSystemTools::GetSystemName@k_ZN13cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetSystemName@k_ZN13cmS.body: The function checks compile‑time macros to return hard‑coded names for Win32 and Android. On other platforms it lazily queries `uname`, caches the result in a static string, then post‑processes the returned sysname to map various Unix flavors (BSD, kFreeBSD, CYGWIN, MSYS) to friendly identifiers. If the `uname` call fails or returns an empty string, it returns an empty string.

@lcmSystemTools::GetSystemPathlistSepara.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GetSystemPathlistSepara.body: The function returns the appropriate path‑separator character: a semicolon when compiled for Windows (_WIN32 defined) and a colon otherwise, matching the standard file‑path conventions of those platforms.

@lcmSystemTools::Glob@k_ZN13cmSystemTool.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Glob@k_ZN13cmSystemTool.body: The `Glob` helper simply scans the supplied directory for filenames that satisfy the given regular‑expression filter, gathering the matches into a result list that other parts of the system can use.

@lcmSystemTools::Glob@k_ZN13cmSystemTool.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Glob@k_ZN13cmSystemTool.body: The function opens the supplied directory, walks through each file it finds, and pushes any file whose name matches the supplied regular‑expression pattern into the supplied vector.

@lcmSystemTools::GlobDirs@k_ZN13cmSystem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GlobDirs@k_ZN13cmSystem.body: The `GlobDirs` static helper expands a given path pattern, scans the file system under that pattern, and records every directory entry it finds. It’s a thin wrapper that resolves wild‑cards in `fullPath` into concrete directory names and stores the results in the caller’s data structure, facilitating later lookup or processing.

@lcmSystemTools::GlobDirs@k_ZN13cmSystem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GlobDirs@k_ZN13cmSystem.body: GlobDirs walks a directory tree that may contain a “/*” glob pattern. It splits the path into a base part and a suffix, loads the base directory, and for each entry that is a directory (excluding “.” and “..”), it appends the suffix and recurses. Paths that do not contain a glob are simply added to the result list.

@lcmSystemTools::GuessLibraryInstallName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GuessLibraryInstallName.body: The `GuessLibraryInstallName` helper scans a supplied filesystem path to infer what the library’s install‑time name should be. It typically examines the path string for known suffixes (`.so`, `.dll`, `.dylib`, etc.), strips off build‑specific directories (e.g. `cmake‑build` or `lib/` prefixes) and normalises the result into a canonical “install‑name” string that other components can use when resolving library search paths. When called, it returns `true` if it successfully parsed a name, or `false` if the input does not match any recognised pattern. This logic is invoked in `cmSystemTools.h` around line 534 for runtime resolution of library locations during project configuration.

@lcmSystemTools::GuessLibraryInstallName.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GuessLibraryInstallName.body: The function tries to determine a library’s install name from a Mach‑O file. If compiled with the Mach parser, it parses the file at `fullPath`, retrieves the name via `GetInstallName`, stores it in `soname`, and returns true on success; otherwise it simply returns false.

@lcmSystemTools::GuessLibrarySOName@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GuessLibrarySOName@k_ZN.body: static bool GuessLibrarySOName(std::string const& fullPath) analyzes a file‑path string to decide whether it denotes a shared‑object library file. It inspects the string for typical library naming patterns (e.g., suffixes such as “.so”, “lib*.so”, or known prefixes) and returns true when a match is found, otherwise false.

@lcmSystemTools::GuessLibrarySOName@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::GuessLibrarySOName@k_ZN.body: Attempts to infer the SONAME for a given file. It first parses the file as an ELF object; if that fails, it checks whether the file is a symbolic link and resolves the target. When the target’s name matches the original file name and contains no path components, that name is returned as the SONAME; otherwise the function fails and returns false.

@lcmSystemTools::HandleResponseFile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::HandleResponseFile@k_ZN.body: The routine walks a range of string arguments, expands any that start with “@” by reading the referenced file and tokenising its content (using a platform‑specific parser), and finally returns the flattened argument list.

@lcmSystemTools::HelpFileName@k_ZN13cmSy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::HelpFileName@k_ZN13cmSy.body: The function takes a string view, copies it into a string, removes any “\<” and “\>” characters by calling a string‑replacement routine, and returns the cleaned string.

@lcmSystemTools::InitializeLibUV@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::InitializeLibUV@k_ZN13c.body: The routine performs a one‑time bootstrap of libuv only on Windows. It first obtains the default libuv loop via `uv_default_loop()`; if a loop is returned it immediately closes it (`uv_loop_close()`), which forces libuv to re‑initialize the internal loop data on the next call. The function then forces libuv to operate in text‑mode by setting `_fmode` (or calling `_set_fmode()` when the MSVC macro is available). Finally it installs an application‑supplied report handler (`EnableMSVCDebugHook()`), which suppresses libuv‑generated pop‑ups. No other actions occur outside the `#if defined(_WIN32)` guard.

@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToFramework@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToFramework@k_ZN1.body: The function examines a supplied path string and determines whether it points to a framework directory. It returns true when the path matches the expected framework pattern; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToFramework@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToFramework@k_ZN1.body: The function returns true if the supplied `path` string is a fully qualified path (i.e., not a relative path) and ends with the literal suffix “.framework”. It does this by calling `cmSystemTools::FileIsFullPath` to verify the path is absolute and then checking the suffix via the helper `cmHasLiteralSuffix`. If either test fails, the function returns false.

@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToMacOSSharedLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToMacOSSharedLibr.body: The function `IsPathToMacOSSharedLibrary` is a static helper that accepts a `std::string` reference and returns a `bool`. Its purpose is to determine whether the supplied path points to a macOS shared library (typically a “.dylib” file in the system library tree). Internally it usually normalises the path, checks that the suffix is “.dylib”, and verifies that the path lies under the standard system library directories (e.g., `/System/Library/` or equivalent framework paths). If the string satisfies those conditions it returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToMacOSSharedLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToMacOSSharedLibr.body: The routine returns true when the supplied string satisfies two criteria: the string is a complete file system path (checked via `FileIsFullPath`) and it ends with the literal suffix “.dylib”. If either check fails, the function returns false.

@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToXcFramework@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToXcFramework@k_Z.body: The function verifies that a supplied path points to the expected XcFramework layout, ensuring that the required directory structure and key components are present so that the path is indeed an XcFramework location.

@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToXcFramework@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::IsPathToXcFramework@k_Z.body: The function returns true only when the supplied string is a fully-qualified path that ends with “.xcframework”. It does this by first confirming the path string represents a full path (via `FileIsFullPath`) and then checking that the string literally ends with the exact suffix “.xcframework”. If either test fails, the function returns false.

@lcmSystemTools::ListTar@k_ZN13cmSystemT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ListTar@k_ZN13cmSystemT.body: The `ListTar` routine is a static helper that receives a single filename (the destination path) and writes a tar‑archive file containing all the files that belong to the current run‑time installation. It opens the target file, writes a tar header for each member (usually a `.tar` entry), and streams the actual file contents in a streamed fashion. The routine returns `true` when the archive was created successfully, otherwise `false`. The method contains only the bare essentials for building the archive, and relies on standard I/O error handling to report failures.

@lcmSystemTools::ListTar@k_ZN13cmSystemT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ListTar@k_ZN13cmSystemT.body:
The function `ListTar` delegates the extraction of a tar archive to `extract_tar`.  
When the `CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP` flag is defined it immediately returns `false`, otherwise it forwards the provided filename, file list, and verbosity flag to `extract_tar`, returning that call’s result.

@lcmSystemTools::MakeTempDirectory@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::MakeTempDirectory@k_ZN1.body: The function verifies that the supplied path string ends with the literal suffix `"XXXXXX"`, then it creates any missing parent directories along that path. On Windows it repeatedly generates a random 6‑character suffix from a predefined alphabet until `Mkdir` succeeds, otherwise it falls back to the POSIX `mkdtemp()` routine. On success it returns a `cmsys::Status::Success()`; on failure it reports the underlying errno via a `cmsys::Status::POSIX_errno()` status.

@lcmSystemTools::MakeTempDirectory@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::MakeTempDirectory@k_ZN1.body: The function generates a uniquely named temporary directory. It accepts a reference to a string that will receive the full path of the created directory. Internally it uses the appropriate platform‑specific system calls (for example mkdir with S_IRWX for POSIX, or CreateDirectory with security flags on Windows), ensuring the directory has the proper permissions. On success it returns a success‑status; on failure it returns an error status that can be inspected by the caller. If the directory already exists the function typically appends a numeric suffix until an unused name is found, and it performs any necessary cleanup on partial failures.

@lcmSystemTools::MakeTempDirectory@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::MakeTempDirectory@k_ZN1.body: Checks whether the requested path is non‑empty. If the string is empty, it immediately returns an `EINVAL` status; otherwise it delegates to the internal helper that actually creates the temporary directory.

@lcmSystemTools::MakefileColorEcho@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::MakefileColorEcho@k_ZN1.body: The function writes a message to stdout, optionally wrapped in ANSI colour codes when the global flag is enabled. It checks special test‑mode environment variables (“DART_TEST_FROM_DART”, “DASHBOARD_TEST_FROM_CTEST”, “CTEST_INTERACTIVE_DEBUG_MODE”) to skip colour escapes during dashboard builds, and respects a `newline` flag to decide whether to terminate the line. When colour is disabled or set to normal, it prints the string plainly; otherwise it emits the colour prefix via `cmsysTerminal_cfprintf` before the text and then writes a final newline if requested.

@lcmSystemTools::Message@k_ZN13cmSystemT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Message@k_ZN13cmSystemT.body: The Message function displays a user‑supplied string, optionally prefixed with a title when provided. It is a utility that centralizes the application’s message output logic.

@lcmSystemTools::Message@k_ZN13cmSystemT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Message@k_ZN13cmSystemT.body: The `Message` function simply forwards a string and its accompanying metadata to the system’s internal messaging subsystem – typically resulting in the message being queued for display, logging, or further handling by the application.

@lcmSystemTools::Message@k_ZN13cmSystemT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Message@k_ZN13cmSystemT.body: The function simply creates a cmMessageMetadata instance, assigns its title field from the supplied C‑string, and forwards the text and this metadata to the internal Message overload that accepts both a string and a metadata object.

@lcmSystemTools::Message@k_ZN13cmSystemT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Message@k_ZN13cmSystemT.body: The routine forwards the supplied message to a registered callback; if none is present it falls back to outputting the string to the standard error stream.

@lcmSystemTools::MoveFileIfDifferent@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::MoveFileIfDifferent@k_Z.body: The function compares the contents (or a checksum) of the file at `source` with the existing target file. If the files differ—or the target is missing—it copies the file from `source` to the destination, effectively “moving” it only when a change is detected. This avoids unnecessary copy‑overwrites when the data is already identical, ensuring the destination always reflects the latest content without redundant I/O.

@lcmSystemTools::MoveFileIfDifferent@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::MoveFileIfDifferent@k_Z.body: The routine checks whether the source and destination files differ; if they do, it first attempts to rename the source to the destination path, falling back to copying the file if the rename fails, and finally deletes the original.

@lcmSystemTools::ParseArguments@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ParseArguments@k_ZN13cm.body: The function splits a command string into individual arguments and returns them as a vector of strings.

@lcmSystemTools::ParseArguments@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ParseArguments@k_ZN13cm.body: It tokenizes a command string into separate arguments, correctly interpreting spaces, quoted fragments, and escape sequences—especially handling backslashes in a special way for Windows‑style paths.

@lcmSystemTools::ParseUnixCommandLine@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ParseUnixCommandLine@k_.body: The function takes a C‑style command string, splits it into individual arguments using the internal parsing routine `cmsysSystem_Parse_CommandForUnix`, and pushes the resulting tokens into the supplied `std::vector<std::string>` container.

@lcmSystemTools::ParseWindowsCommandLine.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ParseWindowsCommandLine.body: The routine walks a raw command‐line string and extracts individual arguments as they would appear when a Windows program receives them via `GetCommandLine`. It keeps track of whether it is inside a quoted sequence, counts preceding backslashes to determine whether a quote is escaped, and pushes each completed argument into the supplied vector. The logic follows the MSDN rules: backslashes before a quote are interpreted as escapes, an odd number of them escapes the quote, and an even number ends the quoted section. When a space is encountered outside quotes, the current argument is finished and stored; otherwise it is treated as a literal space. Backslashes that are not part of an escape are appended as literal `\` characters. After the loop, any pending argument is flushed to the vector.

@lcmSystemTools::PrintSingleCommand@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::PrintSingleCommand@k_ZN.body: The function receives a list of command tokens and produces a single quoted string. If the vector is empty it simply returns an empty string. Otherwise it wraps each token in double‑quotes and joins them with a trailing space using the `cmWrap` helper.

@lcmSystemTools::RandomSeed::[unnamed]::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RandomSeed::[unnamed]::.body: The public function merges two pieces of data—likely two “seed” objects—into a single result; it is called from several other locations in the code, typically after processing that ends with the closing brace at line 2444.

@lcmSystemTools::RandomSeed@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RandomSeed@k_ZN13cmSyst.body:
The function generates a 32‑bit seed value.  
It first tries to obtain a truly random value from the system’s entropy source.  
If that fails, it falls back to combining the current system time with the process ID (using XOR on the high‑ and low‑order bits of the time and the PID), producing a value that is fairly unpredictable.

@lcmSystemTools::RelativeIfUnder@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RelativeIfUnder@k_ZN13c.body: The function checks whether the given path is a sub‑path of a predefined base directory. If it is, it returns that relative path; otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lcmSystemTools::RelativeIfUnder@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RelativeIfUnder@k_ZN13c.body: The function takes two path strings – a “top” directory and a full path “in”. It returns “.” if the two strings match, otherwise if in is a sub‑directory of top it strips the top part and returns the remaining relative path. If neither case applies, it simply returns the original path unchanged.

@lcmSystemTools::RelativePath@k_ZN13cmSy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RelativePath@k_ZN13cmSy.body: The `RelativePath` helper normalises a file system path, stripping any `.` or `..` components and collapsing duplicate separators, then returns the cleaned path relative to the current working directory. It simply accepts a string, validates that the path isn’t absolute (unless explicitly allowed), and then resolves the relative path string for use elsewhere in the code.

@lcmSystemTools::RelativePath@k_ZN13cmSy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RelativePath@k_ZN13cmSy.body: It checks that both `local` and `remote` are absolute paths, logs an error if either isn’t, and then returns the relative path computed by the underlying `cmsys::SystemTools::RelativePath` function.

@lcmSystemTools::RemoveRPath@k_ZN13cmSys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RemoveRPath@k_ZN13cmSys.body: RemoveRPath is a static helper that attempts to delete a file or directory specified by its path. It returns true on success, otherwise false and can optionally populate an error string via the supplied pointer.

@lcmSystemTools::RemoveRPath@k_ZN13cmSys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RemoveRPath@k_ZN13cmSys.body: The routine first attempts to strip the target path using a dedicated “ELF” handler; if that fails it falls back to an “XCOFF” routine. When neither helper succeeds it simply concludes that the file contains no recognizable R‑path data and reports success.

@lcmSystemTools::RenameFile@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RenameFile@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: Accepts two string references —one for the current filename and one for the target name—then attempts to invoke the operating‑system’s rename operation, returning true on success or false if any step fails.

@lcmSystemTools::RenameFile@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RenameFile@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: The static `RenameFile` function attempts to rename a file identified by `oldname`. It performs the rename operation, returning a `RenameResult` that indicates whether the operation succeeded, failed, or encountered an error such as permission issues or missing source file. It encapsulates the rename logic so callers don’t need to manage low‑level file‑system calls directly.

@lcmSystemTools::RenameFile@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RenameFile@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: The function forwards the old and new filenames to an internal overload that performs the actual rename, always requesting a replacement when the target exists, and returns `true` only if that internal call reports a `RenameResult::Success`.

@lcmSystemTools::RenameFile@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RenameFile@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: RenameFile moves the file named oldname to newname, optionally overwriting an existing file if the Replace flag allows it. On Windows it keeps retrying until the move succeeds, clearing read‑only bits if necessary and handling anti‑virus or explorer locks; on UNIX it falls back to the atomic link or rename system calls. It reports the last failure code via the err parameter and returns a status enum that distinguishes success, no‑replace, or generic failure.

@lcmSystemTools::RepeatedRemoveDirectory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RepeatedRemoveDirectory.body: The function attempts to delete the specified directory and returns true when the operation succeeds and false otherwise. It gracefully handles failure conditions, ensuring that any exception or permission issue is caught and reported via the returned flag.

@lcmSystemTools::RepeatedRemoveDirectory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RepeatedRemoveDirectory.body: The function attempts to delete a directory, retrying on Windows until the helper succeeds or the retry count is exhausted; on other platforms it simply returns the removal result.

@lcmSystemTools::ReportLastSystemError@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ReportLastSystemError@k.body: The function builds a single error string by appending the supplied message to the prefix “: System Error: ” and the last system‑error string supplied by the superclass. It then passes that fully‑assembled string to the class‑specific error routine `Error()`.

@lcmSystemTools::ResetErrorOccurredFlag@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::ResetErrorOccurredFlag@.body: This function clears the global error flags `s_FatalErrorOccurred` and `s_ErrorOccurred` by setting them to `false`. It is intended to be called when a reset of the error state is required—such as after handling an error condition or before a new operation cycle. It performs a simple assignment; no side‑effects or external interactions.

@lcmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand@k_ZN13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand@k_ZN13.body: The function runs the supplied command string on the system shell and returns `true` if the execution succeeded; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand@k_ZN13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand@k_ZN13.body: The static `RunSingleCommand` takes a vector of strings that represent a command and its arguments, executes that command (typically via a system call or process spawn), and returns `true` if the command succeeded (exit status 0) and `false` otherwise. It’s a thin wrapper that abstracts process launch and error handling for the rest of the system.

@lcmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand@k_ZN13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand@k_ZN13.body: The function checks whether the global “disable output” flag is set; if so it forces the output option to `OUTPUT_NONE`. It then tokenises the supplied command string into a vector of arguments. If no arguments result from parsing, the function immediately returns `false`. Otherwise it forwards the parsed arguments and the original arguments pointers to the overloaded `RunSingleCommand` that accepts a vector, returning that result.

@lcmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand@k_ZN13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::RunSingleCommand@k_ZN13.body: Runs a command line‑by‑line process, capturing stdout/stderr as requested, respecting a timeout and output‑flag. It builds the argument list, configures a `cmsysProcess`, executes it, streams back any output or error, interprets exit status, reports exceptions/timeouts, and finally cleans up and returns success/failure.

@lcmSystemTools::SaveRestoreEnvironment:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SaveRestoreEnvironment:.body: This function establishes a guard object that, when constructed, captures the current environment (e.g., thread‑local data, configurations) and pushes a restoration point onto a stack. On destruction it restores the previously captured state. Because the copy constructor is deleted, the guard cannot be inadvertently copied, preventing multiple concurrent restorations that would otherwise corrupt the stack.

@lcmSystemTools::SaveRestoreEnvironment:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SaveRestoreEnvironment:.body: This constructor captures the current environment variables into the `Env` member by calling `cmSystemTools::GetEnvironmentVariables()`.

@lcmSystemTools::SaveRestoreEnvironment:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SaveRestoreEnvironment:.body: The declaration prevents any form of copy‑assignment – attempting to assign one `SaveRestoreEnvironment` object to another will be a compile‑time error. This enforces that instances are immutable after construction, ensuring the cleanup logic tied to the object is preserved without accidental copying.

@lcmSystemTools::SaveRestoreEnvironment:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SaveRestoreEnvironment:.body: The function clears the current process environment by iterating over every key in the current environment map, unsetting each key, and then re‑appends all stored key/value pairs that were captured earlier. It achieves this by first retrieving all current variables via `GetEnvironmentVariables()`, removing each entry from the environment via `cmSystemTools::UnsetEnv`, and finally restoring the original set by calling `cmSystemTools::AppendEnv` on the saved `Env` vector that was captured at construction time.

@lcmSystemTools::SetErrorOccurred@k_ZN13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetErrorOccurred@k_ZN13.body: This function toggles a global error indicator to true, signalling that a failure has been registered.

@lcmSystemTools::SetFatalErrorOccurred@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetFatalErrorOccurred@k.body: When invoked, the method flips an internal sentinel flag to true, signaling that a fatal error has been registered. It performs no other actions beyond updating that single static boolean.

@lcmSystemTools::SetForceUnixPaths@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetForceUnixPaths@k_ZN1.body: Sets the internal flag that determines whether Unix‑style paths are enforced.

@lcmSystemTools::SetInterruptCallback@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetInterruptCallback@k_.body: The method stores the supplied callback into the internal callback holder, enabling subsequent interrupt events to invoke it.

@lcmSystemTools::SetMessageCallback@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetMessageCallback@k_ZN.body: The function registers a user‑supplied callback to be invoked whenever the system dispatches a message. By calling `SetMessageCallback`, you replace the current handler with the supplied function; future message events will trigger that callback.

@lcmSystemTools::SetMessageCallback@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetMessageCallback@k_ZN.body: The function stores the supplied callback in the static member `s_MessageCallback` by moving the argument into it; this allows the program to invoke the callback later without copying the callable.

@lcmSystemTools::SetRPath@k_ZN13cmSystem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetRPath@k_ZN13cmSystem.body: The function `SetRPath` accepts a file name and a relative‑path string. It writes the supplied relative path into the file’s internal data (e.g., updates a configuration entry or in‑memory record) and returns `true` on success or `false` if the operation fails.

@lcmSystemTools::SetRPath@k_ZN13cmSystem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetRPath@k_ZN13cmSystem.body: The function tries to apply a new RPATH value to a file. It first attempts an ELF‑style update; if that fails it falls back to an XCOFF update. If neither succeeds and the file lacks an RPATH entry, it treats an empty new path as a no‑change request and returns success. Otherwise it reports failure and can write an error message.

@lcmSystemTools::SetRunCommandHideConsol.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetRunCommandHideConsol.body: Updates the internal flag that controls whether console output is hidden.

@lcmSystemTools::SetStderrCallback@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetStderrCallback@k_ZN1.body: SetStderrCallback registers a callable that will be invoked whenever a diagnostic string needs to be emitted to the standard‑error stream. The supplied callback is stored internally and used by the system’s error‑printing helpers to forward messages instead of writing them directly to std‑err.

@lcmSystemTools::SetStderrCallback@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetStderrCallback@k_ZN1.body: The function stores a supplied callback in the `s_StderrCallback` member by moving it into the class. It simply assigns the parameter to the internal member without any additional processing.

@lcmSystemTools::SetStdoutCallback@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetStdoutCallback@k_ZN1.body: `SetStdoutCallback` registers a callback that the system will invoke whenever something writes to standard output. The supplied function object receives the string to be sent and lets the caller decide what to do with it – for instance, appending to a buffer or forwarding to another stream. The function is called in the test harness to capture test‑output and to reset it to a default no‑op when testing is finished.

@lcmSystemTools::SetStdoutCallback@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SetStdoutCallback@k_ZN1.body: It stores the supplied callback in the internal member `s_StdoutCallback`. This lets the system invoke that callback whenever standard‑output messages need handling.

@lcmSystemTools::SimpleGlob@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SimpleGlob@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: The function `SimpleGlob` is a public static helper that takes a string pattern and returns `true` when the supplied string satisfies the globbing rules (e.g., wildcard matching), and `false` otherwise.

@lcmSystemTools::SimpleGlob@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SimpleGlob@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: The `SimpleGlob` routine scans a directory (derived from the supplied glob) and populates the supplied `files` vector with entries whose filenames begin with the prefix part of the glob (the part before the trailing '*'). It returns `true` only when at least one match is found; the `type` argument (positive = directories only, negative = files only, zero = both) is used to filter the results. It skips the special entries `.` and `..` and ignores matches that do not satisfy the prefix test.

@lcmSystemTools::SplitEnvPath@k_ZN13cmSy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SplitEnvPath@k_ZN13cmSy.body: The function parses a single string containing a colon‑separated list of directory paths (the format used by environment variables such as `PATH`). It tokenises that string into individual elements and returns the collection as a `std::vector<std::string>`. No additional context or explanatory header is provided.

@lcmSystemTools::SplitEnvPath@k_ZN13cmSy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SplitEnvPath@k_ZN13cmSy.body: Splits a PATH‑style string into separate path components, normalizing any backslashes to forward slashes, and returns the resulting fragments as a vector of strings.

@lcmSystemTools::SplitProgramFromArgs@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SplitProgramFromArgs@k_.body: The function parses a command line string into a program path and its arguments, storing each token in a supplied container, and returns true on success (false on parse failure).

@lcmSystemTools::SplitProgramFromArgs@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::SplitProgramFromArgs@k_.body: Parses a command line into two parts: the first token, taken as the program name, and the remainder, taken as the argument string. While scanning it respects single‑ and double‑quoted substrings, and handles back‑slash escapes, stopping at the first unescaped whitespace that is outside any quote. It returns true only when all quotes are correctly closed, ensuring no dangling escape remains.

@lcmSystemTools::Stderr@k_ZN13cmSystemTo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Stderr@k_ZN13cmSystemTo.body: The `Stderr` static helper simply writes the supplied string to the standard error output stream (e.g., `std::cerr`) and optionally flushes it, providing a consistent way to emit diagnostic messages across the codebase.

@lcmSystemTools::Stderr@k_ZN13cmSystemTo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Stderr@k_ZN13cmSystemTo.body: The `Stderr` function writes the supplied string to the standard error stream. If a callback has been registered (`s_StderrCallback`), the callback is invoked with the string; otherwise `std::cerr` is used directly. This allows callers to substitute their own error‑handling logic while falling back to the default console output when no handler is set.

@lcmSystemTools::Stdout@k_ZN13cmSystemTo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Stdout@k_ZN13cmSystemTo.body: The Stdout function simply takes a string reference and writes that text to the console (via std::cout). It serves as a lightweight, reusable logger invoked throughout the project to emit diagnostic or informational messages.

@lcmSystemTools::Stdout@k_ZN13cmSystemTo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::Stdout@k_ZN13cmSystemTo.body: If a callback is registered it forwards the string; otherwise it writes the string to `std::cout` and flushes the stream.

@lcmSystemTools::UnsetEnv@k_ZN13cmSystem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::UnsetEnv@k_ZN13cmSystem.body: `UnsetEnv` checks whether the macro `HAVE_UNSETENV` is defined. If not, it delegates to `UnPutEnv`; otherwise it calls the system function `unsetenv` and returns `true`. If the macro is undefined, it simply returns the result of `UnPutEnv`.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompare@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompare@k_ZN13cm.body: It takes a comparison operator and two version strings, and returns whether the first string satisfies the specified relation relative to the second. The implementation parses each string into its numeric components, compares the parts in sequence, and reports the result according to the supplied operator.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompare@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompare@k_ZN13cm.body: The function takes a comparison operator and two version strings and returns whether the first satisfies the operator relative to the second, according to the usual semantic‑version rules. It parses each component (major/minor/patch and pre‑release tags) and applies the requested operator (equal, greater‑than, etc.) to decide the boolean result.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompare@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompare@k_ZN13cm.body: The `VersionCompare` function forwards the comparison operation to a global helper that works on C‑style strings. It takes the requested operation (`op`), the left‑hand side as a `std::string`, and the right‑hand side as a C‑style string literal or pointer. It simply converts the `std::string` to a C string (via `c_str()`/`c_str()` in actual code) and calls the underlying `::VersionCompare` implementation, returning its boolean result.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompare@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompare@k_ZN13cm.body: The function accepts two version strings and a comparison operator, then delegates to the global `::VersionCompare` overload that operates on C‑style strings, returning the comparison result.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareEqual@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareEqual@k_Z.body: The function evaluates whether two version strings represent the same version, returning true only when all numeric components and suffix markers match exactly.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareEqual@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareEqual@k_Z.body: The `VersionCompareEqual` helper simply delegates to the general `VersionCompare` routine, passing the `OP_EQUAL` flag. It returns `true` only when the two version strings are parsed to the same semantic version; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareGreater@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareGreater@k.body: The function `VersionCompareGreater` is a public static helper that receives two version strings (`lhs` and a second parameter—presumably `rhs`). It parses each string into numeric components (major/minor/patch) and performs an ordinal comparison: it returns `true` when the first argument represents a higher version number than the second, otherwise `false`. This helper is invoked in places such as the `cmInstallTargetGenerator` code at line 893 and defined in `cmSystemTools.h` at line 317 to provide a consistent, reusable comparison across the project.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareGreater@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareGreater@k.body: Returns whether two version strings compare as “greater”. The function forwards the call to the internal `VersionCompare` routine, passing the `OP_GREATER` flag (which represents the “greater‑than” comparison). The result is a `bool` indicating if the left‑hand string is strictly newer (or higher) than the right‑hand string.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareGreaterEq.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareGreaterEq.body: The function takes two version‑string arguments and returns `true` if the first string represents a version that is **not lower** than the second one (i.e., it is the same or higher). It’s used throughout the build tools to guard feature activation or API compatibility by comparing version tags encoded in plain text.

@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareGreaterEq.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::VersionCompareGreaterEq.body: The method simply delegates the comparison to the internal `VersionCompare` routine, passing `OP_GREATER_EQUAL` so that it returns true when the first string is greater‑than or equal to the second.

@lcmSystemTools::WaitForLine@k_ZN13cmSys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::WaitForLine@k_ZN13cmSys.body: The function connects to a running `cmsysProcess`, continuously polls its output stream until the exact string passed in `line` appears in the output buffer. When the match is found it returns an `int` status value (typically `0` for success, non‑zero for timeout or error). The call blocks until the line appears or a timeout/exit condition occurs, making the routine suitable for synchronizing test harnesses with externally spawned processes.

@lcmSystemTools::WaitForLine@k_ZN13cmSys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::WaitForLine@k_ZN13cmSys.body: The `WaitForLine` routine blocks until the target process writes a newline‑delimited line to its stdout or stderr streams. It repeatedly polls both pipes via `cmsysProcess_WaitForData`, decoding any received bytes with `DecodeText`, and appends them to the corresponding buffer (`out` or `err`). When a newline is detected it extracts the line content, clears the consumed buffer segment, and returns either `cmsysProcess_Pipe_STDOUT` or `cmsysProcess_Pipe_STDERR` to signal which pipe produced the line. If a timeout occurs it returns `cmsysProcess_Pipe_Timeout`; if both pipes close with remaining data it returns the leftover contents. The routine therefore streams raw output, handles carriage‑return trimming, and delivers a single line of text or an end‑of‑stream signal.

@lcmSystemTools::strverscmp@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::strverscmp@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: `strverscmp` is a utility that parses two version‑style strings, compares each numeric component in order, and returns a negative value if the first string is earlier, a positive value if it is newer, or zero if the versions are identical. It’s employed in the list code to order entries alphabetically by version.

@lcmSystemTools::strverscmp@k_ZN13cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemTools::strverscmp@k_ZN13cmSyst.body: This function performs a string comparison by delegating to the C‑style helper `cm_strverscmp`. It accepts two `std::string` arguments by constant reference, extracts their underlying C‑strings with `c_str()`, and returns the integer value produced by `cm_strverscmp`. The returned integer typically indicates whether the first string is less than, equal to, or greater than the second (e.g., negative, zero, or positive).

@lcmSystemToolsArgV::Store@k_ZNK17cmSyst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsArgV::Store@k_ZNK17cmSyst.body: The `Store` method appends the strings in `ArgV` to the supplied vector. It iterates over the null‑terminated array, copying each C‑string into the vector passed by reference.

@lcmSystemToolsArgV::cmSystemToolsArgV@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsArgV::cmSystemToolsArgV@k.body: This constructor forwards the supplied `argv` pointer array to the `ArgV` base class, enabling the derived object to access the command‑line arguments that were passed to the program.

@lcmSystemToolsArgV::cmSystemToolsArgV@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsArgV::cmSystemToolsArgV@k.body: cmSystemToolsArgV(const cmSystemToolsArgV&) = delete; // Disallows copying of the cmSystemToolsArgV type.

@lcmSystemToolsArgV::operator=@k_ZN17cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsArgV::operator=@k_ZN17cmS.body: A deleted copy‑assignment operator is defined for `cmSystemToolsArgV`, preventing any code from using the `=` operator to copy‑assign one instance to another. This design choice enforces immutability of the type.

@lcmSystemToolsArgV::~cmSystemToolsArgV@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsArgV::~cmSystemToolsArgV@.body: This destructor iterates over the NUL terminated array `ArgV`, frees each allocated string, and finally frees the array itself. It cleans up the dynamic memory associated with the command‑line arguments stored in the object.

@lcmSystemToolsFindRPath@k_ZL22cmSystemT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsFindRPath@k_ZL22cmSystemT.body: The routine scans a colon‑delimited string for a desired token, verifying that the match is bounded by colons before and after it, and returns the index or npos if the token is absent.

@lcmSystemToolsRPathInfo::cmSystemToolsR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsRPathInfo::cmSystemToolsR.body: The function implements a move constructor for the `cmSystemToolsRPathInfo` struct: it accepts an rvalue reference to an existing instance and efficiently transfers ownership of its internal members to the new object, avoiding costly deep copies and ensuring no residual resources are left behind.

@lcmSystemToolsRPathInfo::cmSystemToolsR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsRPathInfo::cmSystemToolsR.body: Copies the supplied instance’s path metadata into a new `cmSystemToolsRPathInfo` object, propagating all relevant attributes so the new instance mirrors the original.

@lcmSystemToolsRPathInfo::cmSystemToolsR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsRPathInfo::cmSystemToolsR.body: cmSystemToolsRPathInfo returns a populated cmSystemToolsRPathInfo struct that contains metadata for a given path—such as existence, type (file/directory), size, permissions, and any associated tool‑specific flags. It is used by other components to query the status of a system‑tool path before attempting operations on it.

@lcmSystemToolsRPathInfo::~cmSystemTools.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmSystemToolsRPathInfo::~cmSystemTools.body: The function `~cmSystemToolsRPathInfo()` collects and returns a `cmSystemToolsRPathInfo` structure that holds the resolved file‑system path string along with auxiliary metadata (such as whether the path is relative or absolute, existence flags, and any error state that arose while normalising the path). It’s mainly invoked by other modules to standardise path handling and to expose a uniform result object that callers can inspect for validity and diagnostic information.

@lcmTarFilesFrom@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarFilesFrom@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114cmT.body: The function reads a plain‑text list file. For each non‑empty line it pushes the line into the output vector unless the line starts with `"--add-file="`, in which case only the following path is stored. A line beginning with a single hyphen is treated as an error and causes the function to return `false`. The function returns `true` only when all lines are processed without encountering an invalid line.

@lcmTarget::AddInstallGenerator@k_ZN8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddInstallGenerator@k_ZN8cmT.body: The method simply appends the supplied generator pointer to the target’s internal list of generator objects.

@lcmTarget::AddLinkLibrary@k_ZN8cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddLinkLibrary@k_ZN8cmTarget.body: Adds a library to the target’s link list, generating an appropriate name (using the target’s name if the library is a non‑import target and not a general library) and appending the resulting generator expression to the target’s “LINK_LIBRARIES” property. It avoids re‑adding duplicates, conditionally records explicit dependencies in a cache for later dependency resolution, and honors the current policy flags when adding the library to the internal list.

@lcmTarget::AddPostBuildCommand@k_ZN8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddPostBuildCommand@k_ZN8cmT.body: Adds a custom build command to the internal list of commands that will run after the target is built, moving the supplied command into the `PostBuildCommands` vector.

@lcmTarget::AddPostBuildCommand@k_ZN8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddPostBuildCommand@k_ZN8cmT.body: Adds a custom command to the internal list that will be executed after the target finishes building.

@lcmTarget::AddPreBuildCommand@k_ZN8cmTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddPreBuildCommand@k_ZN8cmTa.body: Adds a new custom command to the target’s list of pre‑build commands. It accepts an rvalue reference to the command object, moves it into the internal `PreBuildCommands` vector, and leaves the caller with no returned value.

@lcmTarget::AddPreBuildCommand@k_ZN8cmTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddPreBuildCommand@k_ZN8cmTa.body: Adds the supplied custom command to the target’s internal pre‑build command list.

@lcmTarget::AddPreLinkCommand@k_ZN8cmTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddPreLinkCommand@k_ZN8cmTar.body: Adds the given command to the target’s internal list of pre‑link commands.

@lcmTarget::AddPreLinkCommand@k_ZN8cmTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddPreLinkCommand@k_ZN8cmTar.body: Adds a pre‑link command to the target's internal list. The function simply takes a constant reference to a `cmCustomCommand` and appends it to the `PreLinkCommands` vector.

@lcmTarget::AddSource@k_ZN8cmTarget9AddS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddSource@k_ZN8cmTarget9AddS.body: The function registers a source file into the target’s internal collection. It creates a `cmSourceFileLocation` for the supplied path, verifies whether an entry with that location already exists in the source list, and if not, inserts a new entry either at the beginning or end of the list depending on the `before` flag. After ensuring the entry is unique, it checks for any generator expressions that might conflict with the same name; if such an expression is found it returns `nullptr`. Otherwise it creates or retrieves the source representation via `Makefile->GetOrCreateSource` and returns the resulting `cmSourceFile` pointer.

@lcmTarget::AddUtility@k_ZN8cmTarget10Ad.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddUtility@k_ZN8cmTarget10Ad.body: The method moves the supplied pair of a string and a bool into the internal utilities list, appending it to the collection.

@lcmTarget::AddUtility@k_ZN8cmTarget10Ad.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AddUtility@k_ZN8cmTarget10Ad.body: Adds the named utility to the target’s `Utilities` map, storing a pair of the utility name and its cross‑flag. It uses the supplied `cmMakefile` to get a back‑trace; if none is provided, a default back‑trace is used.

@lcmTarget::AppendProperty@k_ZN8cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::AppendProperty@k_ZN8cmTarget.body: The `AppendProperty` member checks for reserved and mutually‑exclusive property names; if the property is one of those it emits a fatal error. Otherwise it walks a list of usage‑requirement objects and a list of file‑set objects, delegating the write operation to whichever object can handle the property. When none of them consumes the property it falls back to the generic `Properties.AppendProperty` implementation, which either appends or sets the property value depending on the `asString` flag.

@lcmTarget::CanCompileSources@k_ZNK8cmTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::CanCompileSources@k_ZNK8cmTa.body: The function returns true only when the target is synthetic or its type falls into one of the executable, static‑library, shared‑library, module‑library, or object‑library categories; otherwise it returns false, except when the target is imported, which immediately yields false.

@lcmTarget::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK8cmTarget1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK8cmTarget1.body: The `GetBacktrace` member simply returns a reference to the `Backtrace` data stored in the implementation object. It is declared `const` to guarantee that callers cannot modify the returned object, and the return type (`cmListFileBacktrace const&`) is a reference so no copy is performed. This function therefore provides read‑only access to whatever internal back‑trace information is kept inside the underlying implementation of the target.

@lcmTarget::GetComputedProperty@k_ZNK8cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetComputedProperty@k_ZNK8cm.body: The method passes the request to `cmTargetPropertyComputer::GetProperty`, which looks up and returns the value of the named property for this target using the supplied makefile context.

@lcmTarget::GetDebugGeneratorExpressions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetDebugGeneratorExpressions.body: The function wraps the supplied value in a CMake‑style expression that tags it with the current debug configurations. If the link‑library type is “GENERAL”, it simply returns the original value. Otherwise it constructs a string that lists all debug configurations (separated by commas and wrapped with `$<CONFIG:…>` markers). If there’s more than one configuration, it encloses them in `$<OR: …>` tags. When the type is “OPTIMIZED”, it further wraps the string in `$<NOT: …>` tags. The final string is returned in the form `"$<…:value>"`.

@lcmTarget::GetFileSet@k_ZN8cmTarget10Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetFileSet@k_ZN8cmTarget10Ge.body:
Returns a pointer to the `cmFileSet` object stored under the given key in the internal map.  
If the key isn’t present, it returns `nullptr`.  
The returned pointer refers directly to the element in the container—no copy is made.

@lcmTarget::GetHaveInstallRule@k_ZNK8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetHaveInstallRule@k_ZNK8cmT.body: The method simply returns the value of the `HaveInstallRule` flag stored in the underlying implementation object (`impl`). If the flag is set, it indicates that an install rule is present; otherwise the function reports that no rule has been installed.

@lcmTarget::GetIsGeneratorProvided@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetIsGeneratorProvided@k_ZNK.body: The accessor returns the internal flag that indicates whether the generator is currently provided. It retrieves this value without modifying any state.

@lcmTarget::GetLanguageStandardProperty@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetLanguageStandardProperty@.body: Retrieves a pointer to the stored string value for a given key; if the key is absent the function returns nullptr.

@lcmTarget::GetMakefile@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetMakefile@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.body: Retrieves the pointer stored in the target’s implementation, exposing the internal make‑file for downstream consumers without modifying state.

@lcmTarget::GetMappedConfig@k_ZNK8cmTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetMappedConfig@k_ZNK8cmTarg.body: The function resolves the location and import‑library strings for a requested build configuration. It searches the target’s property map for a config‑specific entry (e.g. “MAP_IMPORTED_CONFIG_<CONFIG>”), falls back to the generic names if that fails, and finally fills in `loc`, `imp`, and `suffix` with the appropriate property values; it returns `true` only when a matching configuration (or an interface library) is found, otherwise `false`.

@lcmTarget::GetName@k_ZNK8cmTarget7GetNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetName@k_ZNK8cmTarget7GetNa.body: Returns a reference to the internal string stored in the implementation object, keeping the call constant‑safe and avoiding any copying.

@lcmTarget::GetPolicyMap@k_ZNK8cmTarget1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetPolicyMap@k_ZNK8cmTarget1.body: The `GetPolicyMap` member simply returns a constant reference to the internal `PolicyMap` stored in the `impl` object, allowing callers to read the map without modifying it while keeping the function itself `const`.

@lcmTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0022@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetPolicyStatusCMP0022@k_ZNK.body: The function invokes the `CM_FOR_EACH_TARGET_POLICY` macro to iterate over each registered policy target. During expansion, it fetches the current status of that target’s policy and returns it as part of the `GetPolicyStatusCMP0022` result set.

@lcmTarget::GetPrefixVariableInternal@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetPrefixVariableInternal@k_.body: The method inspects the object's build‑state type and the requested artifact form. Based on those values it picks one of a handful of static CMake prefix strings and returns it. If the state falls outside any explicit branch it falls through to the final `return ""`, yielding an empty string. The branch paths include small platform‑specific checks (e.g., `IsApple()`, `IsAndroidGuiExecutable()`, and `impl->IsAIX`) that adjust which string is returned for import‑library cases.

@lcmTarget::GetProperties@k_ZNK8cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetProperties@k_ZNK8cmTarget.body: It returns a read‑only reference to the target’s internal property map (`cmPropertyMap`), allowing callers to inspect the target’s properties without modifying them.

@lcmTarget::GetProperty@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetProperty@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.body: The function receives a property name and returns a corresponding cmValue or nullptr. It first checks whether the name belongs to a predefined set of “special” properties; if the property is a language‑standard flag it looks it up in a map and returns its value. For the remaining known properties it sequentially queries a list of internal “usage‑requirement” objects (sources, compile options, includes, etc.) and returns the first non‑empty result. If the request is for the target’s type, name, binary or source directory, it fetches that data from the stored state. For the “manually added dependencies” property it concatenates the list of utilities into a comma‑separated string. If no internal property matched, the function falls back to a generic property table and, when appropriate, may forward the request through the makefile state hierarchy before giving up with a null value.

@lcmTarget::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK8cmTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK8cmTa.body: The method fetches the value for the named property from the target object and forwards that raw value to the helper `cmIsOn` which interprets it as a Boolean flag. Because the method is marked `const`, it guarantees no mutation of the object state. Note that `GetProperty` must return a type that `cmIsOn` can sensibly coerce (typically a string or numeric token such as `"true"`, `"1"`, `"0"`, etc. If the property is missing, the behaviour of `GetProperty` (return value or throw) will dictate whether `cmIsOn` evaluates as `false` or propagates an exception. The code as shown uses `std::string` which is a typo for `std::string`; correcting that avoids a compile‑time error.

@lcmTarget::GetSafeProperty@k_ZNK8cmTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetSafeProperty@k_ZNK8cmTarg.body: The function retrieves a property value via `GetProperty`. If the returned `cmValue` is truthy, it returns a const reference to that string; otherwise it returns a reference to a static empty string, guaranteeing the caller never receives a dangling reference. The function is `const`, so it doesn’t modify object state, and uses a static const string to avoid allocating a new string each call when the property is absent.

@lcmTarget::GetSuffixVariableInternal@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetSuffixVariableInternal@k_.body: The function examines the target’s type and the requested artifact type, then returns the corresponding CMake suffix string. It uses nested switch statements: the outer switch distinguishes between static, shared, module, and executable targets; the inner switch selects the specific suffix for runtime binaries versus import libraries. The returned string reflects the library or executable file’s suffix convention defined in CMake.

@lcmTarget::GetTllSignatureTraces@k_ZNK8.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetTllSignatureTraces@k_ZNK8.body: The function iterates over the internal `TLLCommands` map and writes every entry whose key equals the supplied `sig` to the supplied output stream. It converts the file paths to relative paths before printing them, and produces each trace prefixed with a standard bullet string. The function performs no other side‑effects; it simply formats and emits the matching command records.

@lcmTarget::GetType@k_ZNK8cmTarget7GetTy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetType@k_ZNK8cmTarget7GetTy.body: This member returns the stored `cmStateEnums::TargetType` value held in the object’s implementation. The call simply forwards the value from `impl->TargetType` without performing any additional logic.

@lcmTarget::HasKnownObjectFileLocation@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::HasKnownObjectFileLocation@k.body: The method simply asks the global generator whether this target already has a known object‑file location, returning that result. It passes the target itself and a pointer for an explanatory message to the generator, then returns the generator’s boolean answer.

@lcmTarget::ImportedGetFullPath@k_ZNK8cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::ImportedGetFullPath@k_ZNK8cm.body: The function searches for the runtime location of an imported target. It first resolves a desired configuration name (defaulting to “NOCONFIG” when none is given), then checks the target’s mapped configuration information. Depending on the artifact type (runtime binary or import library) it pulls the location from cached properties or falls back to default properties, handling Apple Xcode frameworks specially by parsing the `plist` file. If no location is found it emits a warning or fatal error according to the policy status and returns a sentinel string `"<name>-NOTFOUND"`.

@lcmTarget::InsertInclude@k_ZN8cmTarget1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::InsertInclude@k_ZN8cmTarget1.body: The function registers an include directory entry in the target’s internal include list. If the `before` flag is true, the new path is added to the front of the list; otherwise it is appended to the end. It simply forwards this request to the underlying `IncludeDirectories` helper, which performs the actual insertion.

@lcmTarget::InsertLinkOption@k_ZN8cmTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::InsertLinkOption@k_ZN8cmTarg.body: Receives an entry and a flag and forwards the entry to the underlying LinkOptions object using the corresponding action enumeration to either prepend or append the option.

@lcmTarget::IsAIX@k_ZNK8cmTarget5IsAIXEv.author: AI Short Overview
