@lcmTarget::IsAIX@k_ZNK8cmTarget5IsAIXEv.body: This method forwards the internal “IsAIX” flag stored in the implementation object to callers, letting code query whether the current target instance supports the AIX interface.

@lcmTarget::IsAppBundleOnApple@k_ZNK8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsAppBundleOnApple@k_ZNK8cmT.body: Checks whether the current object is an executable Apple‑specific bundle by verifying that its type is EXECUTABLE, its Apple flag is true, and that the property “MACOSX_BUNDLE” is set.

@lcmTarget::IsApple@k_ZNK8cmTarget7IsApp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsApple@k_ZNK8cmTarget7IsApp.body: The `IsApple()` member simply returns the value of the `IsApple` flag stored in the `impl` sub‑object; it expects that `impl` is non‑null and that the flag was initialized appropriately elsewhere.

@lcmTarget::IsDLLPlatform@k_ZNK8cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsDLLPlatform@k_ZNK8cmTarget.body: This const member simply returns the internal flag that indicates whether the current target is a DLL platform.

@lcmTarget::IsExecutableWithExports@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsExecutableWithExports@k_ZN.body: Checks whether the object is in the executable state and the “ENABLE_EXPORTS” flag is set. It returns `true` only if the type equals `cmStateEnums::EXECUTABLE` and the `ENABLE_EXPORTS` property evaluates to true; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmTarget::IsFrameworkOnApple@k_ZNK8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsFrameworkOnApple@k_ZNK8cmT.body: It returns true only when the target is either a shared or static library, the host is Apple, and the `FRAMEWORK` property is present.

@lcmTarget::IsImported@k_ZNK8cmTarget10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsImported@k_ZNK8cmTarget10I.body: Returns `true` if the underlying implementation reports the object as imported, otherwise `false`.

@lcmTarget::IsImportedGloballyVisible@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsImportedGloballyVisible@k_.body: It checks the target’s `TargetVisibility` flag and returns `true` only when the value is `ImportedGlobally`; for all other visibility states it returns `false`, asserting if an unexpected value is encountered.

@lcmTarget::IsNormal@k_ZNK8cmTarget8IsNo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsNormal@k_ZNK8cmTarget8IsNo.body: The function examines the target’s visibility flag. If the flag equals `Visibility::Normal`, it returns `true`; for any other visibility enumeration it returns `false`. If an unexpected value is encountered, an assertion is triggered and the function falls back to returning `false`.

@lcmTarget::IsPerConfig@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsPerConfig@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.body: It returns the value of the `PerConfig` member in the implementation object, effectively reporting whether the current target is in the “per‑config” state.

@lcmTarget::IsRuntimeBinary@k_ZNK8cmTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsRuntimeBinary@k_ZNK8cmTarg.body: Checks the target’s type against a handful of enum values. If the type matches EXECUTABLE, SHARED_LIBRARY, or MODULE_LIBRARY, it returns true; any other value falls through the switch and yields false.

@lcmTarget::IsSharedLibraryWithExports@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsSharedLibraryWithExports@k.body: Returns true only when the target is a shared library that has the “ENABLE_EXPORTS” property enabled; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmTarget::IsSynthetic@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsSynthetic@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.body: The function evaluates the target’s visibility state. It returns `true` when the `TargetVisibility` value equals `Generated`; for all other defined visibility values (`Normal`, `Imported`, `ImportedGlobally`) it returns `false`. If an unrecognized visibility value is encountered, the function triggers an assertion failure to surface the unexpected state.

@lcmTarget::PushTLLCommandTrace@k_ZN8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::PushTLLCommandTrace@k_ZN8cmT.body: The method logs a new command only if it differs from the last one recorded; it returns false when the signature matches the previous entry, otherwise it adds the pair (signature, context) to the internal list and returns true.

@lcmTarget::SetHaveInstallRule@k_ZN8cmTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::SetHaveInstallRule@k_ZN8cmTa.body: Updates the internal flag that governs whether the install‑time rule is enabled during later processing.

@lcmTarget::SetIsGeneratorProvided@k_ZN8.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::SetIsGeneratorProvided@k_ZN8.body: Updates the internal flag that tracks whether a generator has been provided.

@lcmTarget::SetProperty@k_ZN8cmTarget11S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::SetProperty@k_ZN8cmTarget11S.body:
`SetProperty` updates a target’s property value while enforcing all restrictions.  
*Read‑only properties* (`MANUALLY_ADDED_DEPENDENCIES`, `NAME`, `TYPE`) trigger a fatal error.  
If the target is imported, attempts to change `EXPORT_NAME`, `SOURCES`, `IMPORTED_GLOBAL` or `IMPORTED_LIBNAME` are rejected.  
The method walks through several *usage‑requirement* objects; if any accepts the write it returns.  
File‑set objects are handled similarly.  
Special cases:  
‑ CUDA flags require the target to be an object library and the compiler flag must be present.  
‑ `PRECOMPILE_HEADERS_REUSE_FROM` re‑binds a target’s headers from another target.  
Language standard properties are stored in a map.  
If none of the above match, the property is stored in the internal property map.

@lcmTarget::SetProperty@k_ZN8cmTarget11S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::SetProperty@k_ZN8cmTarget11S.body: This overload simply forwards the call to the main `SetProperty` overload, passing a `cmValue{nullptr}` that represents a null value, thereby setting the specified property to null.

@lcmTarget::SetProperty@k_ZN8cmTarget11S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::SetProperty@k_ZN8cmTarget11S.body: SetProperty forwards the supplied property name and value to another overload, passing a `cmValue` constructed from the string value.

@lcmTarget::~cmTarget@k_ZN8cmTargetD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview

No custom cleanup logic runs; the normal RAII semantics clean up any allocated resources as the object goes out of scope or is deleted.

@lcmTargetCollectLinkLanguages::GetHadLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetCollectLinkLanguages::GetHadLi.body: It simply returns the stored boolean flag that indicates whether the current link condition is language‑sensitive.

@lcmTargetCollectLinkLanguages::Visit@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetCollectLinkLanguages::Visit@k_.body: The `Visit` function walks a dependency graph: it first guards against null targets and avoids revisiting already‑seen items. For a new target it fetches the corresponding link interface, sets a flag if the interface is language‑sensitive, records each language it exposes, and then recurses over all linked libraries, thereby building a complete set of languages while preventing infinite loops.

@lcmTargetCollectLinkLanguages::cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetCollectLinkLanguages::cmTarget.body: The constructor stores the supplied `config` string, keeps a reference to the supplied language set, records the supplied head target and whether this is a second pass, and finally records the target in a `Visited` set so the caller knows this target has been processed.

@lcmTargetCompileDefinitionsCommand@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetCompileDefinitionsCommand@k_Z3.body: cmTargetCompileDefinitionsCommand forwards the supplied arguments to a `TargetCompileDefinitionsImpl` instance, invoking its `HandleArguments` method with the arguments and a predefined command identifier, and returns the boolean result of that call.

@lcmTargetCompileFeaturesCommand@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetCompileFeaturesCommand@k_Z30cm.body: The function forwards the given arguments to a `TargetCompileFeaturesImpl` instance, invoking its `HandleArguments` method with the command string `"COMPILE_FEATURES"`. The return value of `cmTargetCompileFeaturesCommand` is simply the boolean result produced by that `HandleArguments` call.

@lcmTargetDepend::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK14cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK14cm.body: The member function simply returns a reference to the stored back‑trace data. It is declared `const`, so the returned reference is itself `const`, guaranteeing callers cannot alter the underlying object. Because it returns a reference, the caller receives the original data without copying it, but must keep the owning object alive while using the reference.

@lcmTargetDepend::IsCross@k_ZNK14cmTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::IsCross@k_ZNK14cmTarge.body: This method simply exposes the internal cross flag—returning the current value of `Cross` so callers can inspect whether the object is marked as cross without altering state.

@lcmTargetDepend::IsLink@k_ZNK14cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::IsLink@k_ZNK14cmTarget.body: The `IsLink()` member simply returns the value of the member flag `Link`. It’s a const getter that yields a `bool`, allowing read‑only inspection of the link status.

@lcmTargetDepend::IsUtil@k_ZNK14cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::IsUtil@k_ZNK14cmTarget.body: Returns the current value of the `Util` member field.

@lcmTargetDepend::SetBacktrace@k_ZNK14cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::SetBacktrace@k_ZNK14cm.body: This method simply assigns the supplied `cmListFileBacktrace` instance to the `Backtrace` member of the object.

@lcmTargetDepend::SetCross@k_ZNK14cmTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::SetCross@k_ZNK14cmTarg.body: When called, `SetCross` assigns the supplied value to the member `Cross` even though the method is marked `const`. This violates C++ const‑semantics, because the method promises not to modify the object but actually does. The compiler will issue an error unless `Cross` is declared `mutable`, or the function isn’t truly `const`. The function also ignores exception safety and thread‑safety: concurrent calls could race on `Cross`.

@lcmTargetDepend::SetType@k_ZNK14cmTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::SetType@k_ZNK14cmTarge.body: When called, the method simply toggles a single flag: if the argument `strong` is true it turns on the member named `Util`; otherwise it turns on the member named `Link`.

@lcmTargetDepend::cmTargetDepend@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::cmTargetDepend@k_ZN14c.body: The constructor forwards the supplied `cmGeneratorTarget` pointer to the base class’s constructor, storing it in the `Target` member. This establishes the new object as a dependent target for the given generator target.

@lcmTargetDepend::operator const cmGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::operator const cmGener.body: It returns a const‑qualified pointer to the internal `Target` member, so callers can read‑only the target object without allowing any mutation. The function is marked `const`, guaranteeing that invoking it cannot alter the state of the calling instance.

@lcmTargetDepend::operator*@k_ZNK14cmTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::operator*@k_ZNK14cmTar.body: Enables dereferencing an instance to expose its underlying Target object as a read‑only const reference, letting callers use the Target without modifying the wrapper.

@lcmTargetDepend::operator->@k_ZNK14cmTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::operator->@k_ZNK14cmTa.body: The function overloads `operator->` to return the class member `Target`, so callers can use the `->` syntax to access members of that underlying object.

@lcmTargetIncludeDirectoriesCommand@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetIncludeDirectoriesCommand@k_Z3.body: The function forwards the argument list and execution status to a helper that registers include directories. It passes a keyword identifier and a bit‑or of flags indicating that include directories should be processed before, after, and for system‑level headers. The helper returns a boolean indicating whether the operation succeeded.

@lcmTargetLinkDirectoriesCommand@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetLinkDirectoriesCommand@k_Z30cm.body: The function delegates parsing of link‑directory arguments to the `TargetLinkDirectoriesImpl` helper, invoking its `HandleArguments` routine with a “LINK_DIRECTORIES” flag and a preprocessing stage (`PROCESS_BEFORE`). It returns the helper’s success indicator.

@lcmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand::[lambda_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand::[lambda_.body: This lambda resets the nesting counter, verifies that no library‑level dependency is pending (`haveLLT` must be false), then delegates to `tll.HandleLibrary`. If the handling fails it returns `false`; otherwise it clears the current entry and returns `true`. It also emits a FIXME comment about warning when a partial `genex` nesting is detected.

@lcmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand::[lambda_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand::[lambda_.body: Captures `currentEntry` by reference and appends a new argument to it—if `currentEntry` already holds a string it adds a semicolon before the new part; otherwise it simply assigns the argument as the first entry.

@lcmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand@k_Z28cmTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetLinkLibrariesCommand@k_Z28cmTa.body: The routine registers link libraries for a target. It first validates that the target exists and is not an alias or utility, then parses the list of arguments, interpreting keywords such as `LINK_INTERFACE_LIBRARIES`, `INTERFACE`, `PUBLIC`, `PRIVATE`, and library‑type specifiers (`debug`, `optimized`, `general`). It accumulates arguments that may contain generator expressions, handling nested generator delimiters. For each library argument it invokes the `TLL` helper to add the library to the target’s link configuration. It also enforces policy‑controlled rules (CMP0016, CMP0039, CMP0022) and emits errors or warnings when invalid usage is detected. The function returns `true` on success and `false` on error.

@lcmTargetLinkOptionsCommand@k_Z26cmTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetLinkOptionsCommand@k_Z26cmTarg.body: The function `cmTargetLinkOptionsCommand` simply forwards the supplied arguments to a `TargetLinkOptionsImpl` instance, invoking its `HandleArguments` method with the `"LINK_OPTIONS"` flag and a `PROCESS_BEFORE` mode. It returns whatever boolean value that call yields.

@lcmTargetPrecompileHeadersCommand@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPrecompileHeadersCommand@k_Z32.body: This routine prepares a pre‑compile headers request by forwarding the supplied argument list to the `TargetPrecompileHeadersImpl` instance. It simply runs `HandleArguments` with the literal `"PRECOMPILE_HEADERS"` and the reuse‑processing mode and returns the resulting status.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleArgumen.body: The function first verifies that enough arguments were supplied and that the specified target is not an alias, then resolves the target via the makefile. It checks whether the target type permits the requested property (e.g., source handling) and processes optional flags such as SYSTEM, prepend/append modes, and a REUSE_FROM directive, before delegating the remaining arguments to ProcessContentArgs for final handling.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleDirectC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleDirectC.body: The `HandleDirectContent` function is a pure virtual member that derived classes must override. It receives a pointer to a `cmTarget` object (representing a target resource) and is expected to process the content supplied to that target. Implementations should perform any necessary validation, extraction or transformation of the content, and return `true` to signal successful handling or `false` to indicate a failure. Because it is pure virtual, the base class provides no default implementation; each concrete subclass must provide its own handling logic.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleInterfa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleInterfa.body: The routine builds a property name prefixed by “INTERFACE_”, fetches the current value for that property from the target, then writes a new value that is the joined content optionally concatenated with the existing value separated by a semicolon. When prepend is false it simply appends the joined content to the property instead.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleMissing.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleMissing.body: The base class defines an abstract hook for subclasses to provide concrete handling logic when a requested target cannot be located. Sub‑implementations receive the target’s identifier as a string and decide how to react—whether by throwing an exception, logging, or attempting a fallback resolution.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::Join@k_ZN23cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::Join@k_ZN23cm.body:
It is a pure‑virtual hook that subclasses must implement.  
When invoked it is expected to take a `std::vector<std::string>` and produce a single concatenated string—effectively joining the supplied fragments into one output string.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::PopulateTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::PopulateTarge.body: The function first guards against an empty content vector, then routes the vector to one of two handlers depending on the scope string. If the scope is “PRIVATE” or “PUBLIC”, it invokes `HandleDirectContent`; failure of that call aborts with `false`. For “INTERFACE” or “PUBLIC”, it calls `HandleInterfaceContent`. In all other cases it simply returns `true`.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::ProcessConten.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::ProcessConten.body:
The method first validates the requested scope string against the allowed values ("PUBLIC", "PRIVATE", "INTERFACE") and fails with an error if it’s not one of those.  
When the scope is valid, it consumes the following arguments until the next scope keyword, collects them, and then checks that the scope is permitted for the current target type (e.g., INTERFACE libraries may only set INTERFACE properties, imported targets may only set INTERFACE, and utility targets must be PRIVATE).  
If all checks pass, it hands off the collected content and scope to `PopulateTargetProperties` to apply the new property values.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::SetError@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::SetError@k_ZN.body: The `SetError` method simply forwards the supplied error string to the internal `Status` object, marking the current command instance as having an error.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::cmTargetPropC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::cmTargetPropC.body: This constructor stores a reference to the makefile supplied by the surrounding execution status and keeps that reference in its own `Status` member for later use. It simply forwards the `cmMakefile` pointer from the status object into the object’s internal state.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::cmTargetPropC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::cmTargetPropC.body: The function applies a named property value to the target’s internal metadata, ensuring that any subsequent target‑related commands see the updated setting.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::operator=@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::operator=@k_Z.body: The `operator=` function is a copy‑assignment operator that takes a `const` reference to another `cmTargetPropCommandBase` instance and copies its internal state into the current object, returning a reference to the assigned instance for chaining. It performs a member‑wise copy of all relevant fields, ensuring proper handling of resources (e.g., copying dynamically allocated data and resetting any internal caches).

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::~cmTargetProp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::~cmTargetProp.body: When an instance of a derived command is deleted through a pointer to `cmTargetPropCommandBase`, the compiler‑generated virtual destructor automatically runs, triggering any overridden cleanup in the derived class before deallocating the base part. This guarantees that resources owned by subclasses are released correctly without extra boilerplate in each derived type.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::ComputeLocat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::ComputeLocat.body: ComputeLocation returns the location string of a given target by delegating to the target’s GetLocation method, passing along the provided config string.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::ComputeLocat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::ComputeLocat.body: The function fetches a target’s location string, returning a const reference to that string.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::ComputeLocat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::ComputeLocat.body: The function simply forwards a location query to the target object. It accepts a pointer to a target, calls the target’s `GetLocation` method with an empty string argument, and returns whatever string that method produces.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::ComputeLocat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::ComputeLocat.body: The function `ComputeLocationForBuild` receives a pointer to a `Target` object and returns a reference to a `std::string` that represents the file‑system path or unique identifier where the specified target should be built. Internally it performs necessary validation of the target’s properties and resolves any relative components to an absolute path, ensuring that the returned string is reusable without copying. The function is invoked from `cmTargetPropertyComputer.h` (line 40) to provide the correct build location for downstream build‑execution logic.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::GetLocation@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::GetLocation@.body: The function checks whether the target is a library or executable and, if the requested property is “LOCATION” (optionally prefixed or suffixed by a configuration name), it computes and returns the location using the appropriate helper. If the property does not match any supported pattern, it returns a null‑value.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::GetProperty@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::GetProperty@.body: The function takes a target object and a property name, checks if a location for that property exists (via `GetLocation`), returning it if found; if a fatal system error has already been recorded it yields `nullptr`; otherwise, if the requested property string is `"SOURCES"`, it returns whatever `GetSources` produces for the target; if none of those cases match, it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::GetSources@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::GetSources@k.body: The method is a thin wrapper: it accepts a `cmGeneratorTarget` instance and, without inspecting any other state, simply returns the value produced by that target’s `GetSourcesProperty()` member function.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::GetSources@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::GetSources@k.body: The function extracts and aggregates the source files for a given target by traversing the target’s recorded entries in the provided `cmMakefile` and packages them into a `cmValue` to be consumed by the property‑computing machinery.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::HandleLocati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::HandleLocati.body: The function queries the policy status for CMP0026 in the supplied makefile. Depending on that status it selects a hint string (“should” or “may”), sets an associated message type, and if a hint is chosen it builds a diagnostic string explaining that the LOCATION property can’t be read for the given target and sends that through the makefile’s messaging system. It finally returns whether a fatal error was triggered.

@lcmTargetSelectLinker::Choose@k_ZN20cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetSelectLinker::Choose@k_ZN20cmT.body: The function returns the single language in the preferred list, or aborts the build when that list contains more than one entry. If the list is empty it simply returns an empty string. If the list contains exactly one language it returns that language. If the list contains more than one language it reports a fatal error indicating that a target contains several languages with the same highest preference.

@lcmTargetSelectLinker::Consider@k_ZN20c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetSelectLinker::Consider@k_ZN20c.body: The function updates the current preference value for a language: it fetches the integer preference via `GG->GetLinkerPreference(lang)`, compares it to the stored `Preference`, and if higher it replaces it (clearing the `Preferred` set). If the new value equals the current one, it adds the language to the `Preferred` collection.

@lcmTargetSelectLinker::cmTargetSelectLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetSelectLinker::cmTargetSelectLi.body: The `cmTargetSelectLinker` member simply accepts an rvalue reference to another `cmTargetSelectLinker` object—effectively acting as a move‑constructor or a move‑assignment helper. It copies or swaps the internal linkage state from the source instance into the current one, enabling fluent chaining of link‑selection operations in the generator component.

@lcmTargetSelectLinker::cmTargetSelectLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetSelectLinker::cmTargetSelectLi.body: The constructor stores the supplied `cmGeneratorTarget` pointer in its `Target` member and then resolves the global generator instance by chaining through the local generator: `Target->GetLocalGenerator()->GetGlobalGenerator()`, storing the result in `GG`. This establishes the object’s reference to the global generator for subsequent operations.

@lcmTargetSelectLinker::cmTargetSelectLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetSelectLinker::cmTargetSelectLi.body: This constructor creates a new `cmTargetSelectLinker` instance by copying the internal state from an existing one. It performs a shallow copy of the member fields that represent a target selection linker and does not modify the source instance. It’s employed in various parts of the code, such as in `cmGeneratorTarget.cxx` around line 2734, to duplicate a linker before passing it to other modules.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::CheckCustom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::CheckCustom.body: The `CheckCustomCommand` routine walks through every generator configuration that may reference custom commands. For each applicable custom‑command generator it pulls out the utilities used in that generator’s command line and registers them with the target’s utility list, while also pulling the file‑level dependencies listed in the generator’s “DEPENDS” section and adding them to a set. After building that set, it iterates over the collected file names, and any that are not recognized as built‑in utilities are enqueued via `FollowName` for later processing.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::CheckCustom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::CheckCustom.body: It takes a vector of `cmCustomCommand` objects and simply hands each one over to the class’s own `CheckCustomCommand` helper, letting that helper deal with the command’s specifics in the context of the current target.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::FollowName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::FollowName@.body: It looks up the supplied name in the internal map. If the entry is missing, it queries the local generator for a source with that output, possibly converting a relative name to a full path. When a matching target or source is found, the function registers the dependency (pushing it onto the current entry’s dependency list and queuing the source for processing).

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::FollowNames.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::FollowNames.body: The `FollowNames` routine iterates over a vector of string identifiers, invoking the per‑item handler `FollowName` for each entry in sequence order. It performs no validation beyond the loop, simply delegating the work to the existing `FollowName` logic.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::IsUtility@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::IsUtility@k.body: The function extracts the base name from the supplied dependency path, removes a trailing “.exe” if present, and then searches the current generator for a target matching that name. If it finds such a target and the dependency path resolves to the same output location, it registers that target as a utility dependency and returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::QueueSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::QueueSource.body: The method adds a source file to two internal queues only when that file hasn’t already been queued: it inserts the pointer into a set to track queued items, pushes the pointer into the main queue, and appends its resolved path to a list of newly added sources.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::Trace@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::Trace@k_ZN2.body: It walks the queue of source files, pulling each one in turn. For each file it gathers its declared dependencies (both explicit and those added by custom commands), normalises any full‑path names, and feeds them into the target’s dependency graph. Once the queue is drained it registers the collected sources with the generator target.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::cmTargetTra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::cmTargetTra.body: The `cmTargetTraceDependencies` function aggregates and registers the dependency relationships for a generated target trace. It walks the trace’s constituent elements, resolves any referenced targets, and records the resulting dependency links in the target’s dependency set, ensuring that downstream consumers can resolve the full dependency chain when the target is built.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::cmTargetTra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::cmTargetTra.body: This constructor walks a target’s source tree: it collects every source file added to the target, enqueues it for dependency analysis, and ensures that none of those sources in turn pulls in the target again (i.e. no circular dependency). It also registers any custom pre‑/post‑build commands that may participate in the dependency graph.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::cmTargetTra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::cmTargetTra.body: The `cmTargetTraceDependencies` function walks the dependency graph for a target, pulling trace‑information from the supplied dependency object and normalising it into the target’s internal dependency set. It then updates the target’s trace tables so subsequent queries can resolve which objects a given target depends upon.

@lcmTest::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK6cmTest12Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK6cmTest12Get.body: The `GetBacktrace` member function simply returns a const reference to the `Backtrace` member held by a `cmTest` instance; it does not alter the object’s state.

@lcmTest::GetCommandExpandLists@k_ZNK6cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetCommandExpandLists@k_ZNK6cm.body: Returns the value of the `CommandExpandLists` member flag, indicating whether command‑expansion is enabled for the current instance.

@lcmTest::GetMakefile@k_ZN6cmTest11GetMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetMakefile@k_ZN6cmTest11GetMa.body: GetMakefile provides direct access to the internal Makefile object by returning a pointer to it, enabling callers to use the Makefile without copying or altering its state.

@lcmTest::GetOldStyle@k_ZNK6cmTest11GetO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetOldStyle@k_ZNK6cmTest11GetO.body: It provides read‑only access to the OldStyle flag.

@lcmTest::GetProperties@k_ZN6cmTest13Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetProperties@k_ZN6cmTest13Get.body: Returns a non‑const reference to the internal property map, giving direct read/write access.

@lcmTest::GetProperty@k_ZNK6cmTest11GetP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetProperty@k_ZNK6cmTest11GetP.body: The method first queries the local property map; if the key isn’t present it checks whether the property is “chained” via the make‑file state. If it is, it recursively asks the make‑file for a value; otherwise it returns null. If a value is found, that value is returned unchanged.

@lcmTest::SetCommandExpandLists@k_ZN6cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::SetCommandExpandLists@k_ZN6cmT.body: This method flips the internal flag that governs whether command lists are expanded during the test run.

@lcmTest::SetOldStyle@k_ZN6cmTest11SetOl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::SetOldStyle@k_ZN6cmTest11SetOl.body: The method simply assigns the supplied boolean to the member field `OldStyle`. It performs no checks, validations, or side‑effects, so callers should ensure the context (e.g., object state or thread‑safety) is appropriate before invoking it.

@lcmTest::SetProperty@k_ZN6cmTest11SetPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::SetProperty@k_ZN6cmTest11SetPr.body: The method simply delegates the property name and value to the internal properties manager; it performs no additional processing and returns nothing.

@lcmTest::SetProperty@k_ZN6cmTest11SetPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::SetProperty@k_ZN6cmTest11SetPr.body: This overload simply forwards the call to the main `SetProperty` implementation, passing a `cmValue` constructed from a null pointer. In effect it assigns the specified property a null value.

@lcmTest::SetProperty@k_ZN6cmTest11SetPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::SetProperty@k_ZN6cmTest11SetPr.body: The function forwards a property/value pair to the underlying `SetProperty` implementation by wrapping the string value in a `cmValue` object before delegating.

@lcmTestGenerator::Compute@k_ZN15cmTestG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::Compute@k_ZN15cmTestG.body: The function accepts a pointer to a `cmLocalGenerator` instance and stores it in the `LG` member of `cmTestGenerator`. No additional logic is performed.

@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.body: The lambda receives a `std::string` argument, parses it with `ge.Parse`, and then evaluates the resulting object using the current context (`this->LG`) and a provided configuration (`config`).

@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.body: The function takes the raw command‑line argument list, parses each token with the supplied generator expression object, and then evaluates that parsed value in the current context (using the internal logic and the provided configuration string). It finally returns a vector containing all of the resulting evaluated strings.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateInternalPrope.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateInternalPrope.body: The function collects the current test’s back‑trace information and writes it out as a single quoted string. It first writes a marker ("_BACKTRACE_TRIPLES") and then appends each back‑trace entry in the form `FilePath;Line;Name`, separating successive entries with semicolons. If the back‑trace list is empty, the routine simply returns without emitting anything.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateOldStyle@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateOldStyle@k_ZN.body: Marks the test as generated, checks whether the test name must be quoted, emits the corresponding CMake `add_test` call (with or without the “[==]” wrapper), escapes and quotes each argument, writes the test properties list, and finally adds any internal properties.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptActions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptActions.body: The function decides between per‑configuration and legacy test handling. If `ActionsPerConfig` is true, it forwards to the base class `cmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptActions`, which emits actions for each configuration. Otherwise it falls back to the legacy path, calling `GenerateOldStyle` after asserting the test is old‑style. This keeps old tests compatible while reusing the new generator for multi‑config cases.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptConfigs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptConfigs.body: The protected override simply forwards the call to the base `cmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptConfigs` – it doesn’t alter the stream or indentation, just delegates the work of creating the script‐level configurations to the inherited implementation.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptForConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptForConf.body: The function flags the test as generated, prepares a generator‑expression context, decides whether the test name needs quoting, and then emits the CMake `add_test` command: it expands and escapes the command line arguments (including any emulator wrapper for cross‑compiled executables), writes the test name and properties, and finally outputs the test’s properties list.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptNoConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptNoConfi.body:
The `GenerateScriptNoConfig` helper writes a test‑add command to the output stream. It first checks whether the test name must be quoted based on the current policy and on how many `=` signs are needed to delimit the quoted name. Depending on that decision it emits either a quoted form

```
add_test([==[test_name]==] NOT_AVAILABLE)
```

or the plain form

```
add_test(test_name NOT_AVAILABLE)
```

to the provided stream.

@lcmTestGenerator::GetTest@k_ZNK15cmTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GetTest@k_ZNK15cmTest.body: It returns the pointer to the internally stored `cmTest` object, exposing this member in a read‑only (const) context.

@lcmTestGenerator::NeedsScriptNoConfig@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::NeedsScriptNoConfig@k.body: The function returns true when the test has already been generated, is aware of per‑configuration actions, has no specific configuration entries (i.e., the set of configurations is empty), yet still declares a configuration type dependency. In short, it checks whether a script is still required in the absence of explicit configurations.

@lcmTestGenerator::TestsForConfig@k_ZN15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::TestsForConfig@k_ZN15.body: The method simply forwards the supplied configuration string to an internal generator routine and returns that routine’s Boolean outcome—indicating whether test generation succeeded for the given configuration.

@lcmTestGenerator::cmTestGenerator@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::cmTestGenerator@k_ZN1.body: The constructor stores a pointer to the supplied `cmTest` instance, forwards the “CTEST_CONFIGURATION_TYPE” and configuration list to the base `cmScriptGenerator`, and records whether the test uses the old (one‑action‑per‑config) style by inspecting `test->GetOldStyle()`. It also flags that the test has not yet been generated (`TestGenerated = false`) and clears any per‑test data (`LG = nullptr`). No additional state is initialized.

@lcmTestGenerator::cmTestGenerator@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::cmTestGenerator@k_ZN1.body: The public constructor `cmTestGenerator(cmTestGenerator const&)` is deleted, meaning the class cannot be copied; attempting to instantiate it this way will result in a compile‑time error.

@lcmTestGenerator::operator=@k_ZN15cmTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::operator=@k_ZN15cmTes.body: Deletes the copy‑assignment operator for `cmTestGenerator`, so attempts to assign one instance to another are prohibited.

@lcmTestGenerator::~cmTestGenerator@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::~cmTestGenerator@k_ZN.body: The `~cmTestGenerator` function is a virtual destructor that overrides a base‑class destructor. It runs automatically when an instance of `cmTestGenerator` (or a class derived from it) goes out of scope, allowing the class to release any owned resources before the object is reclaimed by the allocator.

@lcmTimestamp::AddTimestampComponent@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::AddTimestampComponent@k_Z.body: The function builds the string representation of a timestamp component specified by a single‑character flag. It selects the appropriate format—year, month, day, hour, minute, second, offset, or epoch‑seconds—formats the value, and for certain flags it applies special handling (e.g. UTC “Z”/“z” or epoch‑seconds “s”). The result is returned as a std::string.

@lcmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT@.body: The member simply forwards its arguments to an overload that accepts an additional offset argument, passing `0` for that offset and returning the resulting timestamp string.

@lcmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT@.body: The method assembles a timestamp string by first ensuring a format mask (defaulting to a UTC‑aware ISO‑8601 form when omitted), then retrieving a broken‑down `tm` representation via either `gmtime` or `localtime` depending on `utcFlag`. It walks the format mask, replacing each `%`‑specifier with the corresponding value from the time structure (day, month, hour, etc.) by calling the helper `AddTimestampComponent`. If `gmtime`/`localtime` fails it simply returns an empty string. The final string is returned.

@lcmTimestamp::CreateUtcTimeTFromTm@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::CreateUtcTimeTFromTm@k_ZN.body: Creates a UTC epoch timestamp from a tm structure. It temporarily sets the TZ environment variable to UTC, invokes tzset() and mktime(), then restores the original TZ; on MSC_VER≥1400 it shortcuts to the _mkgmtime implementation.

@lcmTimestamp::CurrentTime@k_ZNK11cmTime.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::CurrentTime@k_ZNK11cmTime.body: The method returns a formatted time string. It fetches the current epoch time via libuv’s `uv_gettimeofday`, optionally overrides that value if the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable is set (in which case micro‑seconds are cleared to zero), and formats the resulting timestamp according to the supplied format string. If the epoch cannot be obtained it simply returns an empty string.

@lcmTimestamp::FileModificationTime@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::FileModificationTime@k_ZN.body: The routine turns a supplied file‑path into an absolute path, checks that the target exists, then pulls its last‑modified time with libuv’s `uv_fs_stat`. It converts the resulting `time_t` and nanosecond value into a `time_t` + microsecond pair, normalising the nanoseconds to microseconds for consistency with `cmTimestamp::CurrentTime()`. Finally, it formats the value into the requested string representation, honouring the UTC flag, or returns an empty string when the file is absent.

@lcmTimestamp::cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTimes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTimes.body: The constructor moves the internal state of an existing `cmTimestamp` object into a new instance, transferring ownership of its timestamp data without copying.

@lcmTimestamp::cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTimes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTimes.body: `cmTimestamp` is a copy‑constructor for the `cmTimestamp` class. When invoked it receives a const reference to another `cmTimestamp` object and copies that object’s internal timestamp data into the newly created instance, ensuring the new object starts with the exact state of the source.

@lcmTimestamp::cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTimes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTimes.body: The `cmTimestamp()` function obtains the current time in UTC, formats it as a compact string (e.g., `"YYYYMMDDhhmmss"`), and returns that string to callers. It is used throughout the codebase wherever a stable, sortable time tag is required.

@lcmTimestamp::~cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTime.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::~cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTime.body: The `~cmTimestamp()` function is a convenience interface that formats and returns the current system time as a string (typically RFC‑3339 or ISO‑8601 compliant). It gathers the system clock, normalises the value to UTC, and emits the result in a single call, making timestamp creation straightforward for callers.

@lcmTransformDepfile@k_Z18cmTransformDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTransformDepfile@k_Z18cmTransformDep.body: The routine reads a dependency‑file (optionally re‑reading it if it already exists), parses it into an in‑memory representation, and then serialises that representation in the requested output format (GCC, Makefile or MSBuild additional inputs). It performs file‑system checks and directory creation as needed, and returns a Boolean indicating success.

@lcmTrimWhitespace@k_Z16cmTrimWhitespace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTrimWhitespace@k_Z16cmTrimWhitespace.body: Trims leading and trailing whitespace characters from a `cm::string_view` and returns a new `std::string`. It uses the view’s bounds to copy only the non‑whitespace range, so callers get a freshly allocated string without modifying the original view.

@lcmTrimWhitespace@k_Z16cmTrimWhitespace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTrimWhitespace@k_Z16cmTrimWhitespace.body: The `cmTrimWhitespace` routine receives a string view, scans from the beginning until the first non‑space character, then scans backward to the last non‑space, and finally constructs a new `std::string` with that slice. If the view contains only whitespace, it returns an empty string. The algorithm is linear in the length of the input, and uses only a few pointer comparisons, so it is fast and uses minimal extra memory.

@lcmTryCompileResult::cmTryCompileResult.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTryCompileResult::cmTryCompileResult.body:
The `cmTryCompileResult()` function performs the compilation test for a given code fragment. It parses the input, attempts to compile it using the configured compiler, and then populates a `cmTryCompileResult` structure with three key pieces of information:  

* **Success flag** – `true` if the compiler accepted the fragment, `false` otherwise.  
* **Diagnostic list** – a vector of `cmTryCompileError` entries describing any failures or warnings that occurred.  
* **Result code** – an integer encoding the outcome (e.g., 0 = success, non‑zero = error type).  

The struct is returned to the caller, which can then examine the diagnostics and decide whether the code snippet is usable.

@lcmTryRunCommand@k_Z15cmTryRunCommandRK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTryRunCommand@k_Z15cmTryRunCommandRK.body: The function validates the arguments supplied to a `try_run()` invocation, ensures that it isn’t being executed in the special “find‑package” build mode, and finally delegates the actual invocation logic to a `TryRunCommandImpl` helper. It returns `true` only when that helper reports success; otherwise it signals failure and emits an error message.

@lcmTryRunResult::cmTryRunResult@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTryRunResult::cmTryRunResult@k_ZN12_.body: Creates a new `cmTryRunResult` by taking a temporary of the same type and transferring its contents into the new instance. The unnamed rvalue reference indicates that the original object is left in a valid but unspecified state after the move, avoiding any deep copy of internal state or resources.

@lcmTryRunResult::cmTryRunResult@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTryRunResult::cmTryRunResult@k_ZN12_.body: The function takes a const reference to a `cmTryRunResult` instance (passed as an unnamed temporary) and returns a freshly constructed `cmTryRunResult` object—effectively copying or re‑initializing the supplied state.

@lcmTryRunResult::cmTryRunResult@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTryRunResult::cmTryRunResult@k_ZN12_.body: The cmTryRunResult() routine attempts to execute a command and returns a simple result structure that signals whether the operation succeeded, along with any error details that may have been produced.

@lcmUVProcessChain::ErrorStream@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::ErrorStream@k_ZN16cm.body: This function simply returns the integer value stored in the `BuiltinStream` field of the `ErrorStreamData` structure pointed to by the `Data` member of the current object.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Finished@k_ZNK16cmUV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Finished@k_ZNK16cmUV.body: Returns true when every process in the chain has been marked as completed; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmUVProcessChain::GetLoop@k_ZN16cmUVPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::GetLoop@k_ZN16cmUVPr.body: The method simply returns a reference to the `uv_loop_t` object stored in the internal `Data` structure, allowing callers to use the event loop without copying the object.

@lcmUVProcessChain::GetStatus@k_ZNK16cmU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::GetStatus@k_ZNK16cmU.body: Returns a reference to the `ProcessStatus` of the process at the given index. If the index is out of bounds this function will invoke undefined behaviour.

@lcmUVProcessChain::GetStatus@k_ZNK16cmU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::GetStatus@k_ZNK16cmU.body: The routine builds a vector sized to the current chain, fills it with pointers to the individual process statuses obtained via `GetStatus(i)`, and finally returns that collection.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Finish.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Finish.body: The `Finish` method clears any temporary output and error streams and then marks the data object as valid.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Prepar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Prepar.body: The method configures the three standard streams (input, error, output) for the process chain. Depending on each stream’s type (None, Builtin, External) it sets the appropriate flags and file descriptors, creating pipes where necessary (error stream built‑in pipe, output built‑in pipe). It then wires each process in the chain together by creating a new pipe between every consecutive pair of processes, storing the resulting pipe objects in each process’s `InputPipe` and `OutputPipe`. If any allocation or `uv_pipe_open` call fails, the function returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.body: The `Finish` method simply marks the current process as finished by setting the `Finished` flag to `true` and increments the global counter of completed processes. It performs no further logic beyond those two assignments.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::SpawnP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::SpawnP.body: The lambda assigns the provided exit and termination signals to the `ProcessData` object's status fields and then triggers its `Finish()` routine to complete the processing.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::SpawnP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::SpawnP.body: The function launches a child process: it builds a `uv_process_options_t` from the supplied `ProcessConfiguration`, wires stdin/stdout/stderr according to whether the process is the first or last in the chain, registers an exit callback that records exit status and signals completion, and finally invokes `uv_spawn`, falling back to `Finish()` if spawning fails.

@lcmUVProcessChain::OutputStream@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::OutputStream@k_ZN16c.body: Returns the built‑in stream identifier stored in the process chain’s internal data structure.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Status::GetException.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Status::GetException.body: The function inspects a child process exit. If a spawn‑failure is detected it returns a *Spawn* exception with the OS error string. Otherwise it tests whether the child finished; on Windows it decodes the returned exit code into a known status (e.g. interrupt, floating‑point, illegal instruction, etc.) and returns that exception code and a short message. On non‑Windows builds it translates the termination signal into an exception code (mostly “Other”) and gives the signal number in a message. If no match is found it returns *None* with an empty message.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Valid@k_ZNK16cmUVPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Valid@k_ZNK16cmUVPro.body: This function simply returns the value of the `Valid` flag stored inside the `Data` object, indicating whether the chain’s internal data is in a valid state.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Wait::[lambda_0]@kcm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Wait::[lambda_0]@kcm.body: The lambda receives a `uv_timer_t` pointer, casts its `data` member to a `bool*`, and writes `true` into that location – effectively flagging the timer’s expiration.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Wait@k_ZN16cmUVProce.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Wait@k_ZN16cmUVProce.body: The Wait method installs a one‑shot timer that sets a flag after the requested time. It then blocks in a loop that repeatedly calls uv_run until either the timer fires or all pending processes in the chain finish. The method returns true if the timeout flag never fires (i.e. completion before the deadline), otherwise false.

@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.body: Moves the `Data` member from the temporary `other` instance into the new object using `std::move`, ensuring the operation does not throw exceptions.

@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.body: The deleted copy constructor prevents any attempt to copy a cmUVProcessChain instance. Any code that tries to construct a new object from an existing one will be rejected at compile‑time, ensuring that instances cannot be duplicated inadvertently and that resources managed by the class remain uniquely owned.

@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.body: The constructor creates a unique‐owned `InternalData` object and immediately calls `Loop.init()` to prepare the internal looping structure.

@lcmUVProcessChain::operator=@k_ZN16cmUV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::operator=@k_ZN16cmUV.body: This function implements the move‐assignment operator for `cmUVProcessChain`. It takes an rvalue reference to another `cmUVProcessChain`, moves that object’s `Data` member into the current instance using `std::move`, and then returns a reference to `*this`.

@lcmUVProcessChain::operator=@k_ZN16cmUV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::operator=@k_ZN16cmUV.body: This operator overload marks the assignment operator as deleted, preventing any copy‑assignment of a `cmUVProcessChain` instance. It guarantees that objects of this type cannot be assigned after construction, enforcing immutability and preventing accidental copying of internal state.

@lcmUVProcessChain::~cmUVProcessChain@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::~cmUVProcessChain@k_.body: The `~cmUVProcessChain()` function is the destructor for the `cmUVProcessChain` class. It is invoked automatically when an object of this class is destroyed, and its default implementation (specified by `= default`) ensures that any resources held by the instance are released cleanly.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::AddCommand@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::AddCommand@k_.body: Adds a new process to the internal list only when the supplied `arguments` vector is non‑empty. It pushes a default‑constructed entry onto `Processes`, assigns the provided vector to that entry’s `Arguments` field, and returns a reference to the builder so callers can chain further calls.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetBuiltinStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetBuiltinStr.body: The function configures a *stream* in the builder. It matches the passed value against `Stream_INPUT`, `Stream_OUTPUT`, and `Stream_ERROR`. In the output/error branches it fetches the appropriate slot in `Stdio` and tags its `Type` as `BuiltIn`. The input case currently has a placeholder. Finally, the builder instance is returned for fluent chaining.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalSt.body: The method checks whether the supplied FILE pointer exposes a valid descriptor. If it does, it forwards the request to the overload that accepts a descriptor; otherwise it delegates to the no‑stream variant. The returned reference allows the caller to chain further configuration calls.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalSt.body: The function updates the internal stream metadata for the specified standard‑IO stream. Depending on whether the stream is an INPUT, OUTPUT, or ERROR stream, it locates the corresponding `Stdio` entry, marks its type as External, and records the supplied file descriptor. Finally, it returns a reference to the builder for fluent chaining.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetMergedBuil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetMergedBuil.body: It flips the internal flag that the process chain now merges the built‑in output and error streams and then calls the chain‑builder helper to register those two streams in order. This call returns the same builder object so calls can be chained fluently.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetNoStream@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetNoStream@k.body: The method clears the stream type for the specified standard stream (input, output or error) by setting its `Type` field to `None`, and returns the builder instance for fluent chaining.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetWorkingDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetWorkingDir.body: The function assigns the given string to the internal `WorkingDirectory` member and returns a reference to the builder itself, enabling method chaining. It does not perform any validation or error handling; callers should ensure the path is valid before invoking it.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::Start@k_ZNK23.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::Start@k_ZNK23.body: The `Start` member builds a `cmUVProcessChain` object: it prepares the chain data; if preparation fails it returns immediately; otherwise it iterates over the stored processes, spawning each one into the chain—marking the first and last elements accordingly—then finalises the data before returning the finished chain.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::cmUVProcessCh.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::cmUVProcessCh.body: The constructor initializes a `cmUVProcessChainBuilder` instance by moving an existing builder’s internal state—copying any accumulated chain‑building steps and configuration flags into the new instance—so that the new builder continues with the exact sequence and settings that the source object already prepared.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::cmUVProcessCh.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::cmUVProcessCh.body: The constructor takes an existing `cmUVProcessChainBuilder` instance and copies its internal state into a new object, enabling the creation of fresh builders that share the same configuration as the original.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::cmUVProcessCh.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::cmUVProcessCh.body: Creates and returns a builder object that wires together UV‑processing steps so callers can configure and chain them together.

@lcmUVStreamRead::[lambda_0]@kcmUVStream.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVStreamRead::[lambda_0]@kcmUVStream.body: The lambda is a read‑callback used by the libuv read machinery. When invoked it casts the handle’s data pointer to a `cmUVStreamReadHandle`, resizes that handle’s internal buffer to the suggested size, and then writes the address and length of that buffer into the supplied `uv_buf_t` structure so that libuv can copy incoming data into it.

@lcmUVStreamRead::[lambda_1]@kcmUVStream.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVStreamRead::[lambda_1]@kcmUVStream.body: The lambda acts as a read‑callback: when bytes are read it moves the buffer into the stream’s internal buffer, resizes it to the amount read, and invokes the `OnRead` handler. If no bytes are returned (or an EOF condition) it invokes `OnFinish` and stops the stream.

@lcmUVStreamRead@k_Z14cmUVStreamReadP11u.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVStreamRead@k_Z14cmUVStreamReadP11u.body: Creates a read‑handle that stores two callbacks, attaches that handle to the stream’s `data` field, and calls `uv_read_start` with two lambdas: the first allocates a buffer and the second forwards the read data to `onRead`. When `nread` ≤ 0 it invokes `onFinish` and stops the read. This setup lets the caller receive data chunks via the supplied callbacks while the handle stays alive through the returned `unique_ptr`.

@lcmUnsetCommand@k_Z14cmUnsetCommandRKiR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUnsetCommand@k_Z14cmUnsetCommandRKiR.body: The `cmUnsetCommand` routine removes a variable from a CMake session. It first validates the argument count, then examines the first argument to decide whether to unset an environment variable (prefixed with `ENV{}`) or a Makefile variable. It supports three scopes – the current scope, the cache, and the parent scope – by calling the appropriate removal helper in `Makefile`. If the arguments don’t match any supported pattern, it reports an error and returns `false`.

@lcmUuid::BinaryToString@k_ZNK6cmUuid14B.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::BinaryToString@k_ZNK6cmUuid14B.body: The function converts a binary buffer into a dash‑separated hexadecimal string. It walks through a predefined group layout, appends a hyphen before each group except the first, and for each byte in the group, appends the two‑digit hex representation returned by `ByteToHex`. Finally, it returns the assembled string.

@lcmUuid::ByteToHex@k_ZNK6cmUuid9ByteToH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::ByteToHex@k_ZNK6cmUuid9ByteToH.body: The routine takes a single byte and produces a two‑character string containing its hexadecimal digits in lowercase. It constructs a string initialized with two spaces, then fills the positions 0 and 1 in reverse order by computing the low‑order nibble first and writing the corresponding hex digit. The code currently uses `static_cast<char>` (which is actually `static_cast<char>`) and accesses the string via `at(1‑i)`—both of which can trigger out‑of‑bounds or type‑casting issues. The function returns the string directly, so callers receive a 2‑character string that represents the byte.

@lcmUuid::CreateHashInput@k_ZNK6cmUuid15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::CreateHashInput@k_ZNK6cmUuid15.body: The function first assigns the provided `uuidNamespace` vector to `output`. If `name` is non‑empty, it appends the raw bytes of `name` to that vector by resizing `output` and copying the bytes with `memcpy`.

@lcmUuid::FromDigest@k_ZNK6cmUuid10FromD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::FromDigest@k_ZNK6cmUuid10FromD.body: Copies the first 16 bytes of the supplied digest into a 16‑byte buffer, masks and sets the UUID version and variant fields by bit‑wise operations, and returns the binary buffer converted to a standard UUID string via `BinaryToString`.

@lcmUuid::FromMd5@k_ZNK6cmUuid7FromMd5ER.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::FromMd5@k_ZNK6cmUuid7FromMd5ER.body: The method builds a byte vector from the supplied namespace and name, hashes that data with an MD5 algorithm, then converts the resulting digest into a string representation (via `FromDigest`) and returns it.

@lcmUuid::FromSha1@k_ZNK6cmUuid8FromSha1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::FromSha1@k_ZNK6cmUuid8FromSha1.body: It builds the SHA‑1 input from the supplied namespace and name, hashes it, and returns the resulting 128‑bit digest formatted as a RFC 4122 version‑5 UUID string.

@lcmUuid::IntFromHexDigit@k_ZNK6cmUuid15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::IntFromHexDigit@k_ZNK6cmUuid15.body:
`IntFromHexDigit` reads a single hexadecimal character and writes its numeric value into the `output` reference.  
If the character is `'0'`–`'9'`, `'a'`–`'f'`, or `'A'`–`'F'`, the function converts it to the corresponding integer (0‑15) and returns `true`. Any other character causes a `false` return. The function relies on simple range checks and plain arithmetic (`input‑'0'`, `input‑'a'+0xA`, etc.).

@lcmUuid::StringToBinary@k_ZNK6cmUuid14S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::StringToBinary@k_ZNK6cmUuid14S.body: Converts a 36‑character UUID string into a 16‑byte binary vector. It first verifies the string length, then sequentially parses each hexadecimal group defined by the internal `kUuidGroups` table. For each group it checks that a hyphen is present (except before the first group), consumes the required number of hex characters, and delegates the actual hex‑to‑byte conversion to `StringToBinaryImpl`. If any group fails validation or conversion, the function aborts and returns `false`; otherwise, on success it returns `true` after filling `output` with the parsed bytes.

@lcmUuid::StringToBinaryImpl@k_ZNK6cmUui.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::StringToBinaryImpl@k_ZNK6cmUui.body:
This `StringToBinaryImpl` method validates that the input string’s length is even (since each byte is represented by two hex digits), then iterates over each pair of characters, converting them from hex to a single byte via the helper `IntFromHexDigit`. It accumulates the resulting byte into the `output` vector and returns `true` if all conversions succeed, or `false` on encountering an odd length or a non‑hex digit.  
Key points to watch:  
- The parameter type `std::vector<unsigned char>` should be `std::vector<unsigned char>` (the current code may compile only if such a typedef exists).  
- `push_back` is non‑standard; usually `push_back` → `push_back` or simply `push_back`.  
- The cast to `char` and shift‑or‑bitwise combination must produce a `unsigned char` byte (`static_cast<unsigned char>(c1 << 4 | c2)`).  
- The function returns a bool indicating success and leaves `output` untouched when false.

@lcmUuid::cmUuid@k_ZN6cmUuidC1EOS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::cmUuid@k_ZN6cmUuidC1EOS_.body: The constructor `cmUuid(cmUuid&&)` performs a move‑construction: it takes an rvalue reference to another `cmUuid` instance, copies its internal identifier state into the new object, and leaves the source in a valid but unspecified state. It typically performs a shallow copy of the underlying UUID representation without allocating new resources, ensuring a noexcept guarantee and efficient transfer of ownership.

@lcmUuid::cmUuid@k_ZN6cmUuidC1ERKS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::cmUuid@k_ZN6cmUuidC1ERKS_.body: Creates a new `cmUuid` instance by copying the internal state of the supplied object. The parameter is an unnamed const reference, so the function performs a shallow copy of the internal data members, leaving the source object untouched. It performs no additional side‑effects or dynamic allocation beyond copying the existing fields into the new instance.

@lcmUuid::cmUuid@k_ZN6cmUuidC1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUuid::cmUuid@k_ZN6cmUuidC1Ev.body: The `cmUuid()` function generates a unique identifier string (typically a UUID/GUID) and returns it. It is used wherever a distinct identifier is needed.

@lcmVSLink::Link@k_ZN8cmVSLink4LinkEv@f..author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVSLink::Link@k_ZN8cmVSLink4LinkEv@f..body: The routine first checks whether an incremental link should be performed (only when the Incremental flag is set and at least one manifest is available). If verbose output is enabled, it emits an informative message. In that case it hands off to LinkIncremental(); otherwise it prints a different status message and calls LinkNonIncremental().

@lcmVSLink::LinkIncremental@k_ZN8cmVSLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVSLink::LinkIncremental@k_ZN8cmVSLin.body: The routine orchestrates an incremental link pass: it creates a temporary manifest resource, runs the resource compiler on it, invokes the manifest tool to produce a final manifest when needed, and finally performs a second link so the updated manifest is embedded—all while avoiding a full rebuild.

@lcmVSLink::LinkNonIncremental@k_ZN8cmVS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVSLink::LinkNonIncremental@k_ZN8cmVS.body: The method prepares and runs a link operation: it first guarantees the resource‑compiler path is present in the PATH environment, appends any specified manifest options to the command, then invokes the linker; it returns 0 on success and –1 if the link command fails.

@lcmVSLink::Parse@k_ZN8cmVSLink5ParseEii.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVSLink::Parse@k_ZN8cmVSLink5ParseEii.body: Parse consumes a list of command‑line arguments, extracts options such as `--intdir`, `--rc`, and `--mt`, configures internal state flags (e.g. `Incremental`, `LinkGeneratesManifest`), establishes target‑file and manifest paths, and appends any required manifest flags to the link command before returning success or failure.

@lcmVSLink::RunMT@k_ZN8cmVSLink5RunMTERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVSLink::RunMT@k_ZN8cmVSLink5RunMTERK.body: The function assembles the argument vector for the **MT** tool: it inserts the tool path (or default “mt”), the “/nologo” flag, optional “/manifest” entries for a linker‑generated manifest file and any user‑supplied manifests, the output file name, and, if requested, the “/notify_update” flag. It then invokes `RunCommand` with the constructed vector and propagates the resulting exit status, returning that status (or –1 on failure).

@lcmVSLink::cmVSLink@k_ZN8cmVSLinkC1EOS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVSLink::cmVSLink@k_ZN8cmVSLinkC1EOS_.body: The cmVSLink routine establishes a connection between a newly created link object and an existing view‑state instance. It consumes the link instance (via an rvalue reference) and forwards the necessary state data to the target view, updating internal references so that subsequent operations can resolve the link’s target without additional lookups. The function is invoked in the command dispatch code around line 2150 to wire up command‑handling infrastructure.

@lcmVSLink::cmVSLink@k_ZN8cmVSLinkC1ERKS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVSLink::cmVSLink@k_ZN8cmVSLinkC1ERKS.body: `cmVSLink` is a constructor that creates a new link between two `cmVS` objects by storing the target reference in the source’s internal linkage table. It returns the new link instance, allowing callers to manipulate the relation further.

@lcmVSLink::cmVSLink@k_ZN8cmVSLinkC1Eib@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVSLink::cmVSLink@k_ZN8cmVSLinkC1Eib@.body: Sets the internal type and verbosity flag for a cmVSLink instance.

@lcmValue::Compare@k_ZNK7cmValue7Compare.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::Compare@k_ZNK7cmValue7Compare.body: The method checks for null pointers and returns 0 when both operands are null, −1 if the stored value is null, 1 if the argument is null. Otherwise it forwards the comparison to the underlying string view’s compare function.

@lcmValue::Compare@k_ZNK7cmValue7Compare.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::Compare@k_ZNK7cmValue7Compare.body: This member compares the current `cmValue` to another by first dealing with null pointers: if both values are null it returns 0, if only the current object is null it returns –1, if only the argument is null it returns 1, otherwise it delegates the comparison to the stored `Value` object's own `compare` method.

@lcmValue::Compare@k_ZNK7cmValue7Compare.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::Compare@k_ZNK7cmValue7Compare.body: The `Compare` member performs an element‑wise lexical comparison of the stored value against another `cm::string_view`. It returns an `int` that follows the convention used throughout the code: a value less than zero indicates the left side is smaller, zero indicates equality, and a value greater than zero indicates the left side is larger. The function is marked `noexcept` to guarantee it cannot throw, and its `const` qualifier means it does not modify the object. This return value is subsequently employed by the logical comparison helpers that map the result to the various relational operators used in the library.

@lcmValue::Get@k_ZNK7cmValue3GetEv@f./So.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::Get@k_ZNK7cmValue3GetEv@f./So.body: It returns a pointer to the internally stored string. The method is noexcept and cannot modify the object.

@lcmValue::GetCStr@k_ZNK7cmValue7GetCStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::GetCStr@k_ZNK7cmValue7GetCStr.body: Returns a pointer to the underlying C string – or `nullptr` if the internal value is empty.

@lcmValue::IsEmpty@k_ZN7cmValue7IsEmptyE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsEmpty@k_ZN7cmValue7IsEmptyE.body: The function returns true when the passed pointer is null or the first character is the null terminator, effectively testing for an empty C‑string. It performs no allocation or bounds checking, so callers should guarantee the pointer points to valid memory before invoking it.

@lcmValue::IsEmpty@k_ZN7cmValue7IsEmptyE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsEmpty@k_ZN7cmValue7IsEmptyE.body: The `IsEmpty` static function simply returns `true` when the supplied `string_view` contains no characters, and `false` otherwise; it performs this check with no copy or allocation, thanks to the `empty()` member of `std::string_view`.

@lcmValue::IsEmpty@k_ZNK7cmValue7IsEmpty.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsEmpty@k_ZNK7cmValue7IsEmpty.body: The `IsEmpty` method checks whether the internal `Value` pointer is `nullptr` or points to an empty container (via its `empty()` method). It returns `true` only in those cases; otherwise it returns `false`. The function is marked `noexcept`, guaranteeing no exception will be thrown during evaluation.

@lcmValue::IsInternallyOn@k_ZN7cmValue14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsInternallyOn@k_ZN7cmValue14.body: The function returns `true` only when the passed string view is exactly four characters long and matches the pattern **“i_on”** (case‑insensitive first and third letters). If any of the checks fails, it returns `false`.

@lcmValue::IsInternallyOn@k_ZN7cmValue14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsInternallyOn@k_ZN7cmValue14.body: The function returns `true` only when the passed C‑string pointer is non‑null and the secondary overload (which works on `cm::string_view`) reports the value as “internally on”. It simply forwards the check to that overload after guarding against a null pointer.

@lcmValue::IsInternallyOn@k_ZN7cmValue14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsInternallyOn@k_ZN7cmValue14.body: The `IsInternallyOn` function is a small, static helper that determines whether a given `cm::string_view` identifies an “internal‑on” state. It performs a quick, constant‑time check on the supplied string view and returns a plain `bool`. The code is used in several places (e.g., `cmValue::IsInternallyOn` calls and the `cmValue` constructor logic) to gate logic that only runs when the value string matches a particular internal‑on pattern. No side‑effects or allocations occur.

@lcmValue::IsInternallyOn@k_ZNK7cmValue1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsInternallyOn@k_ZNK7cmValue1.body: It returns `true` only when both the stored pointer is non‑null **and** the underlying string view satisfies the internal‑on check performed by `cmValue::IsInternallyOn`.

@lcmValue::IsNOTFOUND@k_ZN7cmValue10IsNO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsNOTFOUND@k_ZN7cmValue10IsNO.body: Checks if a supplied string view is exactly `"NOTFOUND"` or ends with the suffix `"-NOTFOUND"`.

@lcmValue::IsNOTFOUND@k_ZN7cmValue10IsNO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsNOTFOUND@k_ZN7cmValue10IsNO.body: The function returns true when the pointer is nullptr or when the same logic applied to a string_view representation of the value indicates “not found”. It simply forwards the check to an overload that takes a string_view (and is marked noexcept).

@lcmValue::IsNOTFOUND@k_ZN7cmValue10IsNO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsNOTFOUND@k_ZN7cmValue10IsNO.body: The function evaluates a string view and returns `true` iff the view is either empty or matches the internal sentinel that marks a value as “not found”.

@lcmValue::IsNOTFOUND@k_ZNK7cmValue10IsN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsNOTFOUND@k_ZNK7cmValue10IsN.body: The function returns true when the stored pointer is non‑null and the associated static predicate `cmValue::IsNOTFOUND` also reports true for the pointed‑to string view.

@lcmValue::IsOff@k_ZN7cmValue5IsOffENSt3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsOff@k_ZN7cmValue5IsOffENSt3.body: The function examines the length of the input string and performs a case‑by‑case comparison against known “off” literals: an empty string, single‑character forms (‘0’, ‘N’, ‘n’), the two‑letter “NO”, the three‑letter “OFF”, the five‑letter “FALSE” and the six‑letter “IGNORE”. If none of those patterns match, it falls back to `IsNOTFOUND(value)` to handle unrecognised values.

@lcmValue::IsOff@k_ZN7cmValue5IsOffEPKc@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsOff@k_ZN7cmValue5IsOffEPKc@.body: The static helper simply returns **true** if the input pointer is `nullptr` or if the single‑argument overload that operates on a `string_view` deems the value "off". It forwards the check to the other overload, passing the raw C‑string to a `string_view` constructed from it. This allows the function to be safely called with a possibly null pointer without propagating a null dereference.

@lcmValue::IsOff@k_ZN7cmValue5IsOffEi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsOff@k_ZN7cmValue5IsOffEi.body:
The `IsOff` static helper simply decides whether a supplied `cm::string_view` represents an “off” value.  
In practice it treats a string view as “off” when that view contains no characters (i.e., an empty string). The function therefore returns `true` only when the view is empty; otherwise it returns `false`. This behavior is used throughout the code to treat a missing or empty string as an “off” state, such as in the various checks shown in `cmValue.h`.

@lcmValue::IsOff@k_ZNK7cmValue5IsOffEv@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsOff@k_ZNK7cmValue5IsOffEv@f.body: The `IsOff` member simply reports whether the wrapped value is logically “off”. It returns true when the internal pointer is null, and otherwise defers to the helper `cmValue::IsOff`, feeding it with a view of the pointed‑to string.

@lcmValue::IsOn@k_ZN7cmValue4IsOnENSt3__.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsOn@k_ZN7cmValue4IsOnENSt3__.body: The function examines the length of the supplied string view and returns true if the view matches any of the common textual truth indicators: a single‑character “1”, “Y”/“y”; a two‑character “ON”/“on”; a three‑character “YES”/“yes”; or a four‑character “TRUE”/“true” (case‑insensitive). If the string length is anything else, it falls through to the final return of false.

@lcmValue::IsOn@k_ZN7cmValue4IsOnEPKc@f..author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsOn@k_ZN7cmValue4IsOnEPKc@f..body: The method safely tests a C‑string pointer: if the pointer is non‑null it forwards the string to the string‑view overload; if the pointer is null it immediately returns false. It never allocates or throws, and guarantees no exception because it’s marked `noexcept`.

@lcmValue::IsOn@k_ZN7cmValue4IsOnEi.author: AI Short Overview
