@lcmValue::IsOn@k_ZN7cmValue4IsOnEi.body: The function checks whether a given string represents an “on” state – e.g., the literal “on”, “true”, or a non‑zero numeric value – and returns true only if that condition holds.

@lcmValue::IsOn@k_ZNK7cmValue4IsOnEv@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsOn@k_ZNK7cmValue4IsOnEv@f./.body: This function returns true when the internal pointer `Value` is non‑null and the string it points to satisfies the `cmValue::IsOn` condition. If either the pointer is null or the string fails the check, it returns false.

@lcmValue::IsSet@k_ZNK7cmValue5IsSetEv@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::IsSet@k_ZNK7cmValue5IsSetEv@f.body: Returns `true` only when the container is neither empty nor in a special “NOT‑FOUND” state – effectively a quick boolean test that the element set contains an item.

@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1EDn@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1EDn@f./.body: The constructor initializes the object directly from a `std::nullptr_t` marker, setting its internal state to represent a null or empty value without throwing exceptions.

@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1EPKNSt3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1EPKNSt3.body: This constructor initializes the member `Value` with the pointer passed in `value`. Because it is declared `explicit`, it prevents accidental implicit conversions from a `std::string*` to this type, and the `noexcept` qualifier guarantees that it does not throw exceptions during initialization.

@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1ERKNSt3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1ERKNSt3.body: The constructor initializes the member `Value` with a pointer to the supplied string reference (`Value(&value)`). It is marked `explicit` to forbid implicit conversions and `noexcept` to guarantee it throws no exceptions during construction.

@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1ERKS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1ERKS_.body: The `cmValue` copy constructor is an implicitly‑generated, noexcept‑safe copy that simply performs a member‑wise copy of the object’s data, relying on the compiler to generate the efficient default implementation.

@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1Ev.body: The `cmValue` public constructor is a defaulted, noexcept constructor that simply creates an instance of the type. It is typically used when a default‑constructed value is required, such as in the comparison snippets (`l.Compare(cmValue{})`).

@lcmValue::operator bool@k_ZNK7cmValuecv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::operator bool@k_ZNK7cmValuecv.body: The overload allows an instance to be implicitly convertible to a bool: it returns `true` only when the internal pointer (`Value`) is non‑null, otherwise `false`. The `noexcept` qualifier guarantees that the conversion cannot throw, and the `const` qualifier ensures it can be invoked on a const object.

@lcmValue::operator const std::basic_str.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::operator const std::basic_str.body: The function declares an implicit conversion operator that allows an instance of the class to be used where a `const std::basic_string<char>&` is expected. It is marked `noexcept` and `const`, indicating it does not modify the object and guarantees no exceptions. Inside the body it simply forwards to another member function (`operator*()`), presumably returning the desired string reference.

@lcmValue::operator int@k_ZNK7cmValuecvi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::operator int@k_ZNK7cmValuecvi.body:
This member function performs an implicit conversion of the object into a `cm::string_view`.  
Because it’s marked `explicit`, the conversion only applies in direct conversions and doesn’t participate in implicit overload resolution.  
The `noexcept` qualifier guarantees no exceptions are thrown during the conversion, so callers can safely assume the call is noexcept.  
At run‑time the body simply forwards to the internal implementation – `this->operator*()` – which yields the underlying view representation (typically a `string_view` instance backed by the object’s internal storage).

@lcmValue::operator*@k_ZNK7cmValuedeEv@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::operator*@k_ZNK7cmValuedeEv@f.body: The `operator*` overload returns a reference to the string stored in the object. It checks whether the internal pointer is null; if so, it returns a shared sentinel (`cmValue::Empty`), otherwise it dereferences the pointer and returns the pointed‑to string. The method is `const`, marked `noexcept`, and avoids copying by returning a reference.

@lcmValue::operator->@k_ZNK7cmValueptEv@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::operator->@k_ZNK7cmValueptEv@.body: Returns a pointer to the internal string value – if the stored value is null it hands back the address of a static empty string instance.

@lcmValue::operator=@k_ZN7cmValueaSEDn@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::operator=@k_ZN7cmValueaSEDn@f.body: This operator overload clears the internal pointer when a `nullptr` is assigned. It simply sets `Value` to `nullptr` and returns the current object reference.

@lcmValue::operator=@k_ZN7cmValueaSERKS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::operator=@k_ZN7cmValueaSERKS_.body: Assigns the contents of another cmValue to the current instance and returns a reference to that instance.

@lcmValue::~cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::~cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueD1Ev.body: The `~cmValue()` routine constructs and returns an instance of `cmValue`, initializing its internal fields with the supplied arguments and then making that instance available for subsequent use across the code base.

@lcmVariableWatch::AddWatch@k_ZN15cmVari.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatch::AddWatch@k_ZN15cmVari.body:
Adds a watch entry for the named variable.  
If an entry with the same callback and client‐data pointer already exists, it returns false; otherwise it inserts a new pair (containing the callback, client data, and optional delete hook) into the internal vector for that variable and returns true.

@lcmVariableWatch::GetAccessAsString@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatch::GetAccessAsString@k_Z.body: The routine maps an integer to a predefined string by indexing a single static array of six literals. It first normalizes the index by resetting any out‑of‑range value to the sentinel “NO_ACCESS”, then returns a const reference to the stored entry, avoiding any allocation or copying.

@lcmVariableWatch::RemoveWatch@k_ZN15cmV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatch::RemoveWatch@k_ZN15cmV.body: The routine removes a specific watch entry from an internal map. It checks if a watch for the given variable exists; if not, it exits. It then iterates through the stored list for that variable, looking for an entry whose method matches the supplied `WatchMethod`. If a `client_data` pointer is supplied, only an entry whose client data matches that pointer is removed; otherwise any matching method will be detached. Upon removal it erases the element and returns immediately.

@lcmVariableWatch::VariableAccessed@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatch::VariableAccessed@k_ZN.body: The method looks up the variable in the watch map, copies the list of weak‑pointer callbacks, invokes each that can still be locked, and returns true if any callbacks were found and run, otherwise false.

@lcmVariableWatch::cmVariableWatch@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatch::cmVariableWatch@k_ZN1.body: The default constructor initializes the watcher’s internal state and registers the instance with the monitoring framework. It performs only the minimal setup required for the object to begin observing variable changes.

@lcmVariableWatch::~cmVariableWatch@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatch::~cmVariableWatch@k_ZN.body: ~cmVariableWatch performs the necessary cleanup of any resources owned by the object when it is destroyed, ensuring that no internal state is left in an invalid state.

@lcmVariableWatchCallbackData::cmVariabl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatchCallbackData::cmVariabl.body: The `cmVariableWatchCallbackData` public constructor takes an rvalue reference to another `cmVariableWatchCallbackData` instance and initializes the new object by moving its internal state (e.g., member variables) from the source instance. This provides an efficient way to transfer callback data without copying.

@lcmVariableWatchCallbackData::cmVariabl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatchCallbackData::cmVariabl.body: The constructor simply copies the contents of another cmVariableWatchCallbackData instance into the new object, copying every internal field so that the new instance holds the same state as the source. It performs a shallow copy of the data members while preserving any invariants required for proper callback handling.

@lcmVariableWatchCallbackData::cmVariabl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatchCallbackData::cmVariabl.body: Creates a new `cmVariableWatchCallbackData` instance, initializes its members with the required defaults, and returns the pointer for use in subsequent variable‑watch callback handling.

@lcmVariableWatchCallbackData::~cmVariab.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatchCallbackData::~cmVariab.body: The function `~cmVariableWatchCallbackData()` is a public entry point that receives a `cmVariableWatchCallbackData` structure containing the state information needed to process a variable‑watch callback. It extracts the relevant fields (such as the variable name, watch mask, and callback context) from that structure, performs any required validation, and then triggers the corresponding callback routine, forwarding the extracted data to the caller.

@lcmVariableWatchCommand@k_Z22cmVariable.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatchCommand@k_Z22cmVariable.body: The function registers a watch on a named variable, creating a callback object that will be invoked when that variable is accessed. It requires at least one argument (the variable name) and optionally a second argument that becomes the command string. It refuses to watch `CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_FILE`, allocates a `cmVariableWatchCallbackData` instance, registers the watch through `GetVariableWatch()->AddWatch`, and finally schedules a generator action to run after the watch has been triggered.

@lcmVariableWatchCommandVariableAccessed.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVariableWatchCommandVariableAccessed.body:
When a variable is accessed, the callback first blocks re‑entrancy by using the `InCallback` flag, then turns the numeric access type into a human‑readable string.  
If a custom command is configured, it constructs a list of arguments (the variable name, the access type string, the new value, the current list file and the stack trace) and executes that command; otherwise it simply logs the access event.

@lcmVersion::GetCMakeVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVersion::GetCMakeVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.body: The function simply returns a string literal that holds the current CMake version identifier. It exposes this value as a read‑only C‑style string for external code.

@lcmVersion::GetMajorVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVersion::GetMajorVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.body: The function simply returns the value of the macro `CMake_VERSION_MAJOR` as an unsigned integer. It gives callers the major component of the current version without any additional logic.

@lcmVersion::GetMinorVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVersion::GetMinorVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.body: The function simply returns the pre‑defined `CMake_VERSION_MINOR` macro, exposing that value as the library’s minor version number.

@lcmVersion::GetPatchVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVersion::GetPatchVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.body: The function simply returns the value of the macro `CMake_VERSION_PATCH`, which represents the patch component of the project’s version number. It’s a static accessor that exposes the patch level for callers.

@lcmVersion::GetTweakVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmVersion::GetTweakVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.body: The function simply returns the constant value 0 as an unsigned integer.

@lcmWarnUnusedCliWarning@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWarnUnusedCliWarning@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The routine receives a variable name and a pointer to a `cmake` instance (passed as void‑pointer). It casts that pointer back to its real type and tells the `cmake` object that the named CLI variable has now been “touched” or referenced. The other parameters are unused and serve only to satisfy the expected signature.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::ExpandExpression@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::ExpandExpression@k_.body: ExpandExpression takes an expression string, a view, and a separator; it clears the previous error, obtains the registry views for the view, and for each view it parses the expression, substitutes registry placeholders with actual values read via KeyHandler. If a key cannot be resolved, the placeholder is replaced with the sentinel string. It returns the vector of resolved expressions or nullopt if the expression is unsupported on non‑Win32 targets.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::FromView@k_ZN17cmWi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::FromView@k_ZN17cmWi.body: The function translates a `View` enum value into a string view by looking up the value in a static unordered map that pairs each enum member with its string literal. If the lookup succeeds, it returns that string view; if the value isn’t in the map, it falls back to an empty string view.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetLastError@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetLastError@k_ZNK1.body: This const member function simply returns the value stored in the `LastError` member variable.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetSubKeys@k_ZN17cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetSubKeys@k_ZN17cm.body: GetSubKeys opens a registry key in each view specified by the `view` argument, collects all sub‑key names returned by each successful handler, removes duplicates, sorts them, and returns the resulting list wrapped in an `optional` container. If no valid view produces a result, or if compiled for non‑Windows targets, the function returns `nullopt`. It records any encountered error message in `LastError`, clearing it only after a successful query.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetValueNames@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetValueNames@k_ZN1.body: The function queries the Windows registry for value names under a supplied key across all relevant registry views. It aggregates the results into a vector, removes duplicates, sorts them, and returns the vector wrapped in an optional if at least one query succeeded; otherwise it returns an empty optional.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::ReadValue@k_ZN17cmW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::ReadValue@k_ZN17cmW.body: Reads a named value from the Windows registry under a specified view hierarchy, using a default‑separator if none is supplied, and returns the value wrapped in an `optional<std::string>` (or `nullopt` if the key/value is missing).

@lcmWindowsRegistry::ToView@k_ZN17cmWind.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::ToView@k_ZN17cmWind.body: The function looks up the supplied name in a compile‑time, static `unordered_map` of known view identifiers. If a match is found, it returns an `optional` containing the corresponding `cmWindowsRegistry::View` value; otherwise it returns an empty optional (`nullopt`).

@lcmWindowsRegistry::cmWindowsRegistry@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::cmWindowsRegistry@k.body: The constructor initializes a Windows‑specific registry: it stores the supplied supported‑type set and, when on a real Windows build, queries the makefile for the target architecture’s void size, storing the resulting bit‑width (32‑ or 64‑bit) for later use; on non‑Windows systems it simply records an error message.

@lcmWorkerPool::EmplaceJob@k_ZN12cmWorke.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkerPool::EmplaceJob@k_ZN12cmWorke.body: Creates an instance of type T with the supplied arguments and immediately forwards it to `PushJob`, returning the success flag from that call.

@lcmWorkerPool::JobT::JobT@k_ZN12cmWorke.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkerPool::JobT::JobT@k_ZN12cmWorke.body: A constructor that accepts an optional boolean flag (defaulting to false) and initializes the member `Fence_` with that flag; the body of the constructor is empty.

@lcmWorkerPool::JobT::Process@k_ZN12cmWo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkerPool::JobT::Process@k_ZN12cmWo.body: It declares an abstract, protected member that any subclass must provide an implementation for. The class that contains this declaration is forced to be abstract; only derived types can instantiate it. The pure‑virtual form (`=0`) guarantees that the compiler will issue an error if a derived class forgets to override `Process()`. The function itself is a hook that derived classes use to inject custom behaviour—often used in a polymorphic worker‑pool pattern where different worker types implement their own processing logic while the base class supplies shared infrastructure.

@lcmWorkerPool::JobT::UserData@k_ZNK12cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkerPool::JobT::UserData@k_ZNK12cm.body: This protected method returns a `void*` pointing to the user‑supplied data stored in the pool instance (`Pool_`). It simply forwards the call to the pool’s own `UserData()` accessor, allowing derived classes to obtain the raw user data in a const‑safe way.

@lcmWorkerPool::JobT::~JobT@k_ZN12cmWork.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkerPool::JobT::~JobT@k_ZN12cmWork.body: A virtual destructor guarantees that objects of derived types in the `cmWorkerPool` hierarchy are cleaned up correctly when deleted through a base‐class pointer. By marking the destructor `virtual`, the compiler will invoke the appropriate destructor for the dynamic type of the object at runtime. Because it is defined with `= default`, the compiler generates a trivial destructor that simply calls the destructors of its base classes and member members; no custom deallocation logic is required. This makes the destructor lightweight while still enabling polymorphic deallocation in a polymorphic class hierarchy.

@lcmWorkerPool::ProcessResultT::ProcessR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkerPool::ProcessResultT::ProcessR.body: ProcessResultT aggregates per‑task results from the worker pool into a single struct instance. It packages status codes, timestamps, and any returned data so callers can inspect the outcome of a particular processing round without inspecting individual worker traces.

@lcmWorkerPool::~cmWorkerPool@k_ZN12cmWo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkerPool::~cmWorkerPool@k_ZN12cmWo.body: Upon destruction of a `cmWorkerPool` object, the compiler-generated default destructor cleans up all internal bookkeeping: it releases any owned worker threads, frees associated thread‑local storage, and deallocates any internal buffers or queues. No manual resource handling code is needed; the default implementation relies on the compiler to invoke the destructors of member objects, guaranteeing that the pool’s internal state is correctly released before the object is reclaimed.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::Failed@k_ZNK18cmWo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::Failed@k_ZNK18cmWo.body: It returns true when the internal `ResultCode` is non‑zero, signalling that the operation failed.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::GetLastResult@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::GetLastResult@k_ZN.body: Returns the stored value of the member variable `ResultCode`; the call has no side‑effects.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::GetOldDirectory@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::GetOldDirectory@k_.body: Returns an immutable reference to the stored directory path held in the `OldDir` member.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::Pop@k_ZN18cmWorkin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::Pop@k_ZN18cmWorkin.body: The `Pop` routine restores the previous working directory by swapping in the stored path from the `OldDir` member and then discarding that history entry. If `OldDir` is empty, the method exits silently.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::SetDirectory@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::SetDirectory@k_ZN1.body: The function attempts to change the current working directory using `cmSystemTools::ChangeDirectory`. If that call succeeds, it clears `ResultCode` (sets it to 0) and returns `true`; otherwise it records the system error via `errno` and returns `false`.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::cmWorkingDirectory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::cmWorkingDirectory.body: It records the current working directory, then calls `SetDirectory` to change to the supplied path. This change is stored in `OldDir` for later restoration.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::cmWorkingDirectory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::cmWorkingDirectory.body:
The `cmWorkingDirectory` constructor initializes a single‑instance object that represents a temporary working directory.  
Because the copy constructor is explicitly deleted, the object cannot be copied; any attempt to do so will fail at compile time.  
Use it by creating a new instance with the desired path and interacting only through its public member functions.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::operator=@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::operator=@k_ZN18cm.body: The assignment operator is explicitly deleted, preventing any copy‑assignment of a cmWorkingDirectory instance. This keeps the object immutable after construction, ensuring that a new instance can’t be inadvertently copied or reassigned to an existing one.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::~cmWorkingDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::~cmWorkingDirector.body: When a `cmWorkingDirectory` object is destroyed, its destructor invokes `Pop()` on the current instance to clean up whatever internal state `Pop()` handles.

@lcmWrap@k_Z6cmWrapNSt3__117basic_string.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWrap@k_Z6cmWrapNSt3__117basic_string.body: Returns a single string composed of a prefix, the items in `rng` joined by the supplied separator, and a suffix. The helper functions `cmCatViews`, `cmJoin`, and `cmCatViews` are used internally to stitch the views together efficiently, avoiding unnecessary copies. The template works with any range that implements `empty()` and `begin()/end()` for its elements.

@lcmWrap@k_Z6cmWrapcRKT_cNSt3__117basic_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWrap@k_Z6cmWrapcRKT_cNSt3__117basic_.body: This overload of `cmWrap` takes a single‑character prefix and suffix, wraps them as one‑character `string_view`s, and forwards the arguments to a more general overload that operates on `string_view` arguments.

@lcmWrap@k_Z6cmWrapcRKT_ci.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWrap@k_Z6cmWrapcRKT_ci.body: The `cmWrap` helper constructs a lightweight `std::string` by taking a starting delimiter (`char`), a `Range` that supplies a contiguous sub‑range of characters, an ending delimiter (`char`), and a `cm::string_view` that may represent an existing string segment. It simply concatenates the two delimiters with the content of the supplied `Range` and `string_view`, producing a new string. This is useful for building formatted string fragments in a single step without allocating intermediate temporaries.

@lcmWrap@k_Z6cmWrapiRKT_ii.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWrap@k_Z6cmWrapiRKT_ii.body: The `cmWrap` template builds a string by stitching together a string‑view prefix, a range of values, and two additional string‑views that supply separators or suffixes. It is typically used to format a line of text that needs a header‑like prefix, a list of items (the `Range` argument), and trailing text fragments. The function simply concatenates the components in order, returning the resulting `std::string`.

@lcmWriteFileCommand@k_Z18cmWriteFileCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWriteFileCommand@k_Z18cmWriteFileCom.body: The routine accepts a vector of tokens expected to be: file name followed by optional text segments, optionally terminated by the keyword “APPEND” to indicate that the file should be appended rather than overwritten. It first checks argument count, extracts the target file name, then concatenates any remaining tokens into a single message string. The function verifies that the current build‑environment is permitted to create the file in the requested location, creating parent directories as necessary and temporarily granting write permission if needed. It opens the file in either “out” or “app” mode depending on the append flag, writes the assembled message followed by a newline, restores permissions if it had to change them, and reports success/failure through the supplied status object.

@lcmWriteToFileCallback@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWriteToFileCallback@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The routine serves as the write‑callback for a generic copy operation. It casts the incoming buffer to a `char*`, multiplies the element size by the element count to obtain the total byte count, and feeds that many bytes into the `cmsys::ofstream` supplied via the `data` pointer. Finally, it returns that byte count.

@lcmWriteToMemoryCallback@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWriteToMemoryCallback@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The function takes a raw memory block (given by `ptr` and a size expressed as `size` × `nmemb`), casts that block to a `char*`, and appends the bytes into a `cmFileCommandVectorOfChar` instance supplied via `data`. It returns the number of bytes that were written (the product of `size` and `nmemb`).

@lcmXCode21Object::PrintComment@k_ZN15cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCode21Object::PrintComment@k_ZN15cm.body: The method writes a C‑style comment to the supplied stream. If the object’s own comment string is empty, it first looks up an attribute named “name” in the object hierarchy; if that attribute exists, its string value is copied (quotes stripped) into the comment buffer. The comment is then emitted as `/* … */`.

@lcmXCode21Object::PrintList@k_ZN15cmXCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCode21Object::PrintList@k_ZN15cmXCo.body: The method formats a collection of `cmXCodeObject` instances. It prefixes the output stream with an opening brace, then streams each sub‑category of objects (targets, files, build phases, references, etc.) through a helper overload that knows how to render that particular subtype, and finally closes the list with a brace.

@lcmXCode21Object::PrintList@k_ZN15cmXCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCode21Object::PrintList@k_ZN15cmXCo.body: The routine scans a vector of `cmXCodeObject` pointers, and when at least one object has the requested type flag, it emits a start‑tag, prints the matching objects, and finally emits an end‑tag.

@lcmXCode21Object::cmXCode21Object@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCode21Object::cmXCode21Object@k_ZN1.body: Constructs a new object by forwarding the supplied type and identifier to its base class and then records the fixed value 21 in the internal Version field.

@lcmXCode21Object::cmXCode21Object@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCode21Object::cmXCode21Object@k_ZN1.body: The function is a move‑constructor for the `cmXCode21Object` class, taking an rvalue reference to another instance and initializing the new object by transferring its internal resources. This allows efficient construction without copying the entire object state.

@lcmXCode21Object::cmXCode21Object@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCode21Object::cmXCode21Object@k_ZN1.body: Creates a new instance from an existing one, duplicating its internal state so that the new object behaves exactly like the original.

@lcmXCode21Object::operator=@k_ZN15cmXCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCode21Object::operator=@k_ZN15cmXCo.body: The move‑assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to another `cmXCode21Object`, transfers its internal state into `*this`, leaves the source in a valid but unspecified state, and returns a reference to the target object.

@lcmXCode21Object::operator=@k_ZN15cmXCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCode21Object::operator=@k_ZN15cmXCo.body: The assignment operator takes a const reference to another `cmXCode21Object`, copies all of its internal state into the current instance (properly handling self‑assignment), and returns a reference to `*this` so that calls can be chained. It performs a deep copy of the underlying resources, so any mutable members must themselves be safely copy‑assigned.

@lcmXCode21Object::~cmXCode21Object@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCode21Object::~cmXCode21Object@k_ZN.body: The destructor for `cmXCode21Object` releases any resources owned by the instance and guarantees that its internal state is correctly deregistered when the object is disposed.

@lcmXCodeObject::AddAttribute@k_ZN13cmXC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::AddAttribute@k_ZN13cmXC.body: Adds the supplied value into the `ObjectAttributes` map under the given key. If the key already exists, the stored pointer is replaced. No checks or error handling are performed.

@lcmXCodeObject::AddAttributeIfNotEmpty@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::AddAttributeIfNotEmpty@.body: The method verifies that the supplied `value` is non‑null and reports that it actually contains data (via `IsEmpty()`); only when both conditions are satisfied does it invoke `AddAttribute`, thereby attaching the value to the current object.

@lcmXCodeObject::AddDependLibrary@k_ZN13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::AddDependLibrary@k_ZN13.body: The function adds a dependency library name to the internal `DependLibraries` mapping for the supplied configuration key. It simply pushes the new string onto the vector that is stored under that key. The implementation should use `std::string` and `push_back`.

@lcmXCodeObject::AddDependTarget@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::AddDependTarget@k_ZN13c.body: Adds the given `tName` string to the vector stored under `configName` in the `DependTargets` map.

@lcmXCodeObject::AddObject@k_ZN13cmXCode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::AddObject@k_ZN13cmXCode.body: The method appends the supplied object pointer to the internal list container, marking the object for subsequent handling.

@lcmXCodeObject::AddUniqueObject@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::AddUniqueObject@k_ZN13c.body: Adds the given object to the internal list only if it isn’t already stored—checking the list first with `cm::contains` and then pushing the pointer back if it’s unique.

@lcmXCodeObject::CopyAttributes@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::CopyAttributes@k_ZN13cm.body:
`CopyAttributes` performs a shallow copy of member fields from the supplied `copy` object into the current instance.  
- The code simply assigns each pointer‑typed member (`ObjectAttributes`, `List`, `String`, `Object`) to the same addresses held by the source object.  
- As a result, the destination and source now share the same underlying objects; modifications to any of those members in one instance affect the other.  
- Because no deep copy or reference counting is performed, callers must ensure that the lifetime of those pointed‑to objects outlives both instances, or explicitly manage ownership semantics to avoid dangling references.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetAttribute@k_ZNK13cmX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetAttribute@k_ZNK13cmX.body: The function searches the object’s attribute map by name, returning the matching attribute value if found or `nullptr` when the key is absent.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetComment@k_ZNK13cmXCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetComment@k_ZNK13cmXCo.body: It returns a const reference to the stored string member, allowing callers to read the comment without copying or modifying it. The method is marked `const`, so it guarantees no state change and can be called on const instances. The reference returned remains valid as long as the owning object outlives.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetDependLibraries@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetDependLibraries@k_ZN.body: The function simply returns a reference to the internal `DependLibraries` map that holds each library’s list of dependencies, allowing callers to inspect which libraries a given library pulls in. Because the return type is a reference to the map itself, callers can read the current mappings without copying the entire structure; however, the returned reference is not read‑only, so any external code that obtains it could, in principle, modify the map unless it’s protected elsewhere.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetDependTargets@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetDependTargets@k_ZNK1.body: The method simply returns a const reference to the internal `DependTargets` map, exposing its contents to callers for inspection while preventing any modification.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetId@k_ZNK13cmXCodeObj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetId@k_ZNK13cmXCodeObj.body: The `GetId` member returns a constant reference to the internal `Id` member, giving callers read‑only access without copying the string. It does not modify state, so callers cannot change the underlying value.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetIsA@k_ZNK13cmXCodeOb.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetIsA@k_ZNK13cmXCodeOb.body: Returns the value of the member variable `IsA`, guaranteeing that the object remains unchanged.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetObject@k_ZN13cmXCode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetObject@k_ZN13cmXCode.body: GetObject simply returns the internal `cmXCodeObject*` stored in the instance, giving callers read‑only access to that object without altering any state.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetObject@k_ZNK13cmXCod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetObject@k_ZNK13cmXCod.body: The function scans the member `List` of the current object for an entry whose `IsA` field matches the requested type `t`. If it finds a match, it returns that pointer; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetObjectCount@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetObjectCount@k_ZN13cm.body: The `GetObjectCount()` member simply returns the current number of elements stored in the internal list. It accesses the underlying container’s `size()` method, which is a constant‑time operation, so the call is O(1). If the list is empty, the function returns `0`; otherwise it returns the actual count of objects held.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetObjectList@k_ZNK13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetObjectList@k_ZNK13cm.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the internally stored list of objects.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetString@k_ZNK13cmXCod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetString@k_ZNK13cmXCod.body:
The function simply returns an internal string member by reference.  
It’s a const accessor that allows read‑only read access to the stored string without copying it.  
The `const` qualifier on the member function guarantees callers can’t modify the object through the returned reference.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetTarget@k_ZNK13cmXCod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetTarget@k_ZNK13cmXCod.body: Returns a pointer to the internal `Target` member. Because the function is marked `const`, it guarantees that calling code cannot modify the object, only read its state.

@lcmXCodeObject::GetType@k_ZNK13cmXCodeO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::GetType@k_ZNK13cmXCodeO.body: The function simply returns the value stored in the member variable `TypeValue` without modifying any state. Because it is marked `const`, it guarantees that the function cannot alter the object, so it can be safely called from constant contexts. This allows read‑only access to the type information that the class keeps internally.

@lcmXCodeObject::HasComment@k_ZNK13cmXCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::HasComment@k_ZNK13cmXCo.body: The function is a const member that simply tests whether the `Comment` member holds any text; it returns true when the string isn’t empty.

@lcmXCodeObject::HasObject@k_ZNK13cmXCod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::HasObject@k_ZNK13cmXCod.body: The method simply forwards the query to a helper routine – it checks whether the supplied `cmXCodeObject` pointer appears in the internal list. If it is found, it returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmXCodeObject::Indent@k_ZN13cmXCodeObj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::Indent@k_ZN13cmXCodeObj.body: The function writes the specified number of tab characters to the supplied output stream, decrementing the level counter until it reaches zero. It assumes `level` is non‑negative; no bounds checking is performed, so passing a negative value results in no output. No error handling or early‑exit logic is present.

@lcmXCodeObject::InsertObject@k_ZN13cmXC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::InsertObject@k_ZN13cmXC.body: The method inserts a `cmXCodeObject*` into the internal list at the given index only if that index is smaller than the current number of objects; otherwise it performs no action.

@lcmXCodeObject::IsEmpty@k_ZNK13cmXCodeO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::IsEmpty@k_ZNK13cmXCodeO.body: The function inspects the object’s type and returns true only when the corresponding member container is empty. For a list, it queries List.empty(); for a string it checks String.empty(); for an attribute group it checks ObjectAttributes.empty(); and for plain objects or object references it verifies that the underlying pointer is nullptr. If no case matches, the function falls back to a final return true to silence any compiler warning, though that path is unreachable in normal use.

@lcmXCodeObject::PrependObject@k_ZN13cmX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::PrependObject@k_ZN13cmX.body: The method takes a pointer to a `cmXCodeObject` and inserts it at the very front of the internal list by calling `insert` with `List.begin()`. This effectively places the new object as the first element in the list.

@lcmXCodeObject::Print@k_ZN13cmXCodeObje.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::Print@k_ZN13cmXCodeObje.body: The method writes a human‑readable representation of the current object to a supplied stream: it emits the object’s identifier, its comment, and a block of key/value pairs. It applies indentation based on the object’s version flag and format flags, and formats the attribute list with consistent separators and line breaks.

@lcmXCodeObject::PrintAttribute@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::PrintAttribute@k_ZN13cm.body: The function renders an attribute of a `cmXCodeObject` to a stream. Depending on the object’s `TypeValue`, it formats lists, attribute groups, references, or strings. It indents each level, writes commas or braces as needed, prints comments when present, and recursively traverses nested attributes. It terminates each attribute with a semicolon and newline (or separator) for a clean output.

@lcmXCodeObject::PrintComment@k_ZN13cmXC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::PrintComment@k_ZN13cmXC.body: PrintComment writes a comment string to a supplied std::ostream, and can be overridden by derived classes to alter the output format.

@lcmXCodeObject::PrintList@k_ZN13cmXCode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::PrintList@k_ZN13cmXCode.body: The function writes a collection of `cmXCodeObject` instances to the supplied output stream in a simple, indented list format. It first emits an opening brace, then iterates over the passed vector calling each object’s own `Print()` routine when its `TypeValue` matches the `OBJECT` flag, and finally writes a closing brace. The output is wrapped in a single indentation level for each element.

@lcmXCodeObject::PrintString@k_ZN13cmXCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::PrintString@k_ZN13cmXCo.body: The function writes the supplied string to the given output stream. It surrounds the string with double‑quotes if the string is empty or contains non‑alphanumeric characters or a comment start, and escapes internal quotes and backslashes so the text can be parsed safely.

@lcmXCodeObject::PrintString@k_ZNK13cmXC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::PrintString@k_ZNK13cmXC.body: The function forwards the current object’s `String` member to a static helper that writes that string to the given output stream.

@lcmXCodeObject::SetComment@k_ZN13cmXCod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::SetComment@k_ZN13cmXCod.body:
The method copies the supplied string into the object's internal `Comment` member.  
It accepts the argument by const reference, so no temporary copy is made.  
No additional validation, error handling, or side‑effects occur.

@lcmXCodeObject::SetId@k_ZN13cmXCodeObje.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::SetId@k_ZN13cmXCodeObje.body: The function assigns the provided string to the member variable `Id` of the current object.

@lcmXCodeObject::SetObject@k_ZN13cmXCode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::SetObject@k_ZN13cmXCode.body: The setter simply replaces the internal `Object` pointer with the supplied pointer, taking ownership of the new reference and overwriting the previous value.

@lcmXCodeObject::SetString@k_ZN13cmXCode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::SetString@k_ZN13cmXCode.body: The `SetString` member simply assigns the provided string to the internal `String` field. It takes a `const std::string&` (though the standard type is `std::string`) and copies that value into the object’s member, effectively replacing any previous content.

@lcmXCodeObject::SetTarget@k_ZN13cmXCode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::SetTarget@k_ZN13cmXCode.body: Assigns the incoming pointer to the internal member so the object now points to that target.

@lcmXCodeObject::cmXCodeObject@k_ZN13cmX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::cmXCodeObject@k_ZN13cmX.body: The constructor sets default values (version 15, null target/object), stores the supplied type and id, and if the type flag equals OBJECT, it adds an attribute named “isa” with a null value.

@lcmXCodeObject::cmXCodeObject@k_ZN13cmX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::cmXCodeObject@k_ZN13cmX.body: The constructor takes an existing cmXCodeObject by const reference and performs a shallow copy of the entire internal state into the new instance, preserving the exact configuration of all members without altering any external state.

@lcmXCodeObject::operator=@k_ZN13cmXCode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::operator=@k_ZN13cmXCode.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of the source `cmXCodeObject` into the target, handling self‑assignment safely and returning a reference to the updated instance.

@lcmXCodeObject::~cmXCodeObject@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeObject::~cmXCodeObject@k_ZN13cm.body: The destructor simply assigns the member `Version` the value 15.

@lcmXCodeScheme::FindConfiguration@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::FindConfiguration@k_ZN1.body: FindConfiguration looks up the requested configuration in the internal list; if it can’t find it and the list isn’t empty, it falls back to the first entry, otherwise it simply echoes back the supplied name.

@lcmXCodeScheme::IsExecutable@k_ZN13cmXC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::IsExecutable@k_ZN13cmXC.body: The function examines the generator target of a code object; if the target is missing it reports an error and yields false, otherwise it reports true when the target’s type enum matches EXECUTABLE.

@lcmXCodeScheme::IsTestable@k_ZNK13cmXCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::IsTestable@k_ZNK13cmXCo.body: The function returns true when the object has test entries or its target is executable; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteAnalyzeAction@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteAnalyzeAction@k_ZN.body: It writes an XML element named AnalyzeAction, setting a single attribute buildConfiguration to the supplied configuration string.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteArchiveAction@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteArchiveAction@k_ZN.body: The function serializes an `<ArchiveAction>` element, emitting the current build configuration and a flag to indicate that the archive should be revealed in the organizer.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteBuildAction@k_ZN13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteBuildAction@k_ZN13.body: The routine writes an XML snippet that declares a build‑action node, assigns a handful of flags (parallelizeBuildables, buildImplicitDependencies, and various build‑for flags) and embeds a single buildable reference before closing all tags.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteBuildableReference.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteBuildableReference.body: The function emits an XML element named **BuildableReference**. It first starts the element, then breaks out any preceding attributes. Three attributes are added to describe the object: the primary identifier, the blueprint id (via `GetId()`), and the name of the target object (`GetTarget()->GetFullName(noConfig)`). Finally it records the blueprint’s own name and the container string prefixed with “container:”, then closes the element. The `noConfig` placeholder hints at a missing configuration value that should be supplied before calling `GetFullName()`.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteCustomWorkingDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteCustomWorkingDirec.body:
The `WriteCustomWorkingDirectory` routine inspects a configuration property named “XCODE_SCHEME_WORKING_DIRECTORY”.  
If that property is unset it writes an XML attribute `useCustomWorkingDirectory="NO"`.  
Otherwise it writes `useCustomWorkingDirectory="YES"` and resolves the property string via `cmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate`, emitting the resulting path as the `customWorkingDirectory` attribute.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteLaunchAction@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteLaunchAction@k_ZN1.body: It writes a single XML element that describes the complete launch configuration for a target, serializing all the settings that the target’s properties expose. It emits attributes for debugger, launcher, launch style, and a host of diagnostic flags (address‑, thread‑, and UB sanitizers). In addition it outputs nested elements for arguments, environment variables, and a list of executable options, optionally adding options for memory‑sanitizers or GPU frame capture when the relevant flags are set.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteLaunchActionAdditi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteLaunchActionAdditi.body: The function checks whether a named property (`varName`) is true for the target; if so, it writes an XML `<AdditionalOption>` element containing the supplied key/value pair and marks it enabled, then returns true. If the property isn’t set, it returns false and writes nothing.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteLaunchActionAttrib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteLaunchActionAttrib.body: The function queries a boolean property on the target; if that property is true it writes an XML attribute named `attrName` with the value `"YES"` and returns `true`, otherwise it simply returns `false`.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteLaunchActionBoolea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteLaunchActionBoolea.body: The routine fetches the property named by varName from the current target, decides whether that property is “on” (either it is present or the supplied default true is used), writes the corresponding “YES” or “NO” value into the XML writer under attrName, and returns the resulting on‑state.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteProfileAction@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteProfileAction@k_ZN.body: The routine serialises an XML `<ProfileAction>` element: it writes the supplied build‑configuration string, sets a flag indicating the launch‑scheme arguments environment should be used, writes a (blank) tool identifier, and then emits the current working‑directory path and a debug‑document‑versioning attribute (set to true).

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteTestAction@k_ZN13c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteTestAction@k_ZN13c.body: The function writes a TestAction element into an XML stream. It adds the build‑configuration and debugger/launcher identifiers, then iterates over the Tests collection to emit each testable reference via WriteBuildableReference. If the object is testable, it also emits a MacroExpansion block referencing the target. Finally, it writes an empty AdditionalOptions section before closing the TestAction element.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteVersionString@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteVersionString@k_ZN.body: The function converts the internal version number into a fixed‑width string: it writes the value of `XcodeVersion * 10` into a four‑character buffer padded with leading zeros (e.g., `0003` for `XcodeVersion = 0.3`). It relies on `std::setw(4)` and `std::setfill('0')` to ensure the string always has four digits, even for single‑digit values.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteXCodeSharedScheme@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteXCodeSharedScheme@.body: Creates the shared‑scheme sub‑directory (if it doesn’t exist), builds the path to the scheme file, opens that file with a stream that only writes when the contents differ, and finally writes the scheme data by invoking WriteXCodeXCScheme.

@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteXCodeXCScheme@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::WriteXCodeXCScheme@k_ZN.body: The method simply emits an XML fragment that records the upgrade version and a hard‑coded version tag, then emits a handful of action elements (build, test, launch, profile, analyze, archive). Each action element is created by a helper that pulls a configuration name from a property or a default (“Debug”), and then writes the corresponding configuration data to the output stream using the same writer instance.

@lcmXCodeScheme::cmXCodeScheme@k_ZN13cmX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXCodeScheme::cmXCodeScheme@k_ZN13cmX.body: The constructor stores the supplied generator and target object, copies the test set into the member `Tests`, pulls the target’s name into `TargetName`, and records the provided configuration list and Xcode version in the new instance.

@lcmXMLElement::Attribute@k_ZN12cmXMLEle.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLElement::Attribute@k_ZN12cmXMLEle.body: The `Attribute` template creates an XML attribute by forwarding the supplied name and value to the underlying XML writer (`xmlwr`). It then returns a reference to the current element (`*this`) to allow fluent chaining of further attribute or element calls.

@lcmXMLElement::Comment@k_ZN12cmXMLEleme.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLElement::Comment@k_ZN12cmXMLEleme.body: The `Comment` method forwards a C‑string to an internal XML writer. When called, it simply passes the supplied comment text to the wrapped `xmlwr` object's `Comment` function, which inserts it into the resulting XML output.

@lcmXMLElement::Content@k_ZN12cmXMLEleme.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLElement::Content@k_ZN12cmXMLEleme.body: This template forwards the argument to the underlying XML writer. It accepts any type by reference and passes it unchanged to `xmlwr.Content`.

@lcmXMLElement::Element@k_ZN12cmXMLEleme.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLElement::Element@k_ZN12cmXMLEleme.body: The function accepts an element name and a value of any type and forwards them to the internal XML writer.

@lcmXMLElement::cmXMLElement@k_ZN12cmXML.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLElement::cmXMLElement@k_ZN12cmXML.body: It creates an `cmXMLElement` instance that immediately starts a new XML element by invoking `StartElement(tag)` on the supplied writer. When the object goes out of scope its destructor will finish the element (typically by calling `EndElement`). This pattern guarantees proper pairing of start‑/end‑tags without the caller needing to remember to close the element manually.

@lcmXMLElement::cmXMLElement@k_ZN12cmXML.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLElement::cmXMLElement@k_ZN12cmXML.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied tag to the internal XML writer, invoking `StartElement(tag)` so that element is emitted as the next output element.

@lcmXMLElement::~cmXMLElement@k_ZN12cmXM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLElement::~cmXMLElement@k_ZN12cmXM.body: When an instance of cmXMLElement is destroyed, its destructor calls xmlwr.EndElement(), signalling the underlying XML writer that the current element’s opening tag has been closed and that the writer should output the corresponding closing tag.

@lcmXMLParser::CharacterDataHandler@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::CharacterDataHandler@k_ZN.body: The function is a protected virtual entry point meant to be overridden by derived XML‑parser implementations. It receives a raw buffer of character data and its length, allowing subclasses to process or transform the data as part of an XML parsing workflow.

@lcmXMLParser::CleanupParser@k_ZN11cmXML.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::CleanupParser@k_ZN11cmXML.body: The `CleanupParser` routine checks whether the parser object is present; if it’s missing it reports an initialization issue and aborts the cleanup. When a parse error flag is clear it calls the underlying XML library to signal the end of input. On failure it logs an error via `ReportXmlParseError`. Finally it deallocates the parser instance and returns a status flag indicating whether the operation succeeded.

@lcmXMLParser::EndElement@k_ZN11cmXMLPar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::EndElement@k_ZN11cmXMLPar.body:
The `EndElement` hook is invoked when the parser reaches the end of an XML element. It simply writes a line to standard output in the form

```
End element: <name>
```

so that anyone tracing the parse flow can see that the named element has closed. Derived parsers can override this virtual method to perform custom cleanup or state updates when an element finishes.

@lcmXMLParser::FindAttribute@k_ZN11cmXML.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::FindAttribute@k_ZN11cmXML.body: The function scans an array of name/value string pairs (null‑terminated) and returns the value whose name matches the supplied attribute string; if no match it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmXMLParser::InitializeParser@k_ZN11cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::InitializeParser@k_ZN11cm.body: The method first verifies whether a parser instance already exists; if so, it logs an error flag and aborts. Otherwise it creates a new XML parser, registers element‑, character‑data handlers, and links the parser to the current object. Finally, it clears any previous parse error and reports success.

@lcmXMLParser::Parse@k_ZN11cmXMLParser5P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::Parse@k_ZN11cmXMLParser5P.body: This method runs the parser in a single, linear flow: it first sets up the parser, then feeds the whole input string to the chunk‑processing routine, and finally tears down any allocated resources before returning the combined success flag.

@lcmXMLParser::ParseFile@k_ZN11cmXMLPars.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::ParseFile@k_ZN11cmXMLPars.body: The function opens the specified file, streams its contents into a string, and then hands that string to the `Parse` routine for XML parsing.

@lcmXMLParser::ReportError@k_ZN11cmXMLPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::ReportError@k_ZN11cmXMLPa.body: The `ReportError` routine is a helper that forwards an error message: when a callback is registered it calls that function with the line number, the message, and the callback’s context; if no callback is set, it writes the error to standard error output.

@lcmXMLParser::StartElement@k_ZN11cmXMLP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::StartElement@k_ZN11cmXMLP.body: When the XML parser encounters the start of an element it calls `StartElement`. The method receives the element’s name and a pointer to its attributes, and it simply logs the element name for debugging. This function is marked `protected` and `virtual`, allowing derived parsers to override its behaviour while keeping the interface hidden from external callers.

@lcmXMLParser::cmXMLParser@k_ZN11cmXMLPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::cmXMLParser@k_ZN11cmXMLPa.body: The constructor initializes internal state: it clears the parser pointer, sets the parse‑error counter to zero, and initializes the callback pointer and its associated data pointer to null.

@lcmXMLParser::~cmXMLParser@k_ZN11cmXMLP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::~cmXMLParser@k_ZN11cmXMLP.body: The destructor checks whether the internal parser object exists; if so, it triggers a dedicated cleanup routine that safely releases resources allocated during parsing.

@lcmXMLSafe::Quotes@k_ZN9cmXMLSafe6Quote.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLSafe::Quotes@k_ZN9cmXMLSafe6Quote.body: The method simply assigns the supplied boolean to the internal `DoQuotes` flag of the current object and returns the object itself, enabling fluent chaining of calls. It performs no complex logic; the only thing to watch is that `this` must not be null before invoking the method.

@lcmXMLSafe::cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLSafe::cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeC1E.body: cmXMLSafe is a move‑constructor that takes an rvalue reference to another instance of the same type. It transfers ownership of all internal members (typically pointers, buffers, and flags) to the new object, ensuring that the source is left in a valid, empty state. This guarantees that no deep copying of large XML structures is performed and that resources are not duplicated, thereby keeping the operation lightweight and exception‑safe.

@lcmXMLSafe::cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLSafe::cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeC1E.body: A constructor for `cmXMLSafe` stores the supplied C‑string in the member `Data` (a pointer to the original buffer), records its length in `Size` (converted to an unsigned long with `static_cast`), and sets a flag `DoQuotes` to `true` by default. No other logic is performed in the body.

@lcmXMLSafe::cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLSafe::cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeC1E.body: The constructor stores the supplied string in `Data` (a pointer to the string’s internal buffer), records its length in `Size`, and defaults the flag `DoQuotes` to `true`.

@lcmXMLSafe::cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLSafe::cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeC1E.body: Creates a `cmXMLSafe` instance from a supplied value, initializing its internal state so the object can safely produce an XML‑escaped string (e.g., for use in `cmXMLWriter::Quotes(false)` calls).

@lcmXMLSafe::str@k_ZNK9cmXMLSafe3strEv@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLSafe::str@k_ZNK9cmXMLSafe3strEv@f.body: The member simply writes the object to an std::ostringstream and returns the resulting string, giving a stringified view of the instance.

@lcmXMLSafe::~cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeD1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLSafe::~cmXMLSafe@k_ZN9cmXMLSafeD1.body: On object destruction, the function frees all internal XML buffers and restores the internal state so that no stray pointers or allocated memory remain in the object.

@lcmXMLWriter::Attribute@k_ZN11cmXMLWrit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::Attribute@k_ZN11cmXMLWrit.body: The function renders a name/value pair to an output stream. It first runs `PreAttribute()`, then writes `name="…"` where the value is escaped by `SafeAttribute(value)` before being streamed. This guarantees proper encoding of attribute values.

@lcmXMLWriter::BreakAttributes@k_ZN11cmX.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::BreakAttributes@k_ZN11cmX.body: The method simply turns on a flag that indicates attributes should be processed in a broken‑up mode. This flag is later checked by the writer logic to decide whether to emit attributes in separate lines or keep them inline.

@lcmXMLWriter::Comment@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::Comment@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.body: The routine finalises an opened tag, optionally inserts a line break when no content follows, and emits a comment node—flushed as `<!-- comment -->`—appending the stream’s current output buffer.

@lcmXMLWriter::Content@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::Content@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.body: The function template `Content` receives a const reference to any type `T`. It first calls `PreContent()`, then writes the provided value to an internal output stream after processing it through `SafeContent`.

@lcmXMLWriter::Doctype@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::Doctype@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.body: This method writes a DOCTYPE declaration to the XML output. It first closes any pending start tag, optionally inserts a line break when no content follows, then emits the string `< !DOCTYPE …>` with the supplied argument.

@lcmXMLWriter::Element@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::Element@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.body: This routine finalizes any pending start tag, inserts a line break if required, and emits a self‑closing XML tag for the supplied element name.

@lcmXMLWriter::Element@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::Element@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.body: This template writes a single element: it invokes `StartElement` with the provided name, passes the value to `Content`, then calls `EndElement` to close the tag.

@lcmXMLWriter::EndDocument@k_ZN11cmXMLWr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::EndDocument@k_ZN11cmXMLWr.body: The function finalises the XML output: it first verifies that the current indentation depth is zero (ensuring no further nested tags remain) and then writes a single newline to the output stream.

@lcmXMLWriter::EndElement@k_ZN11cmXMLWri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::EndElement@k_ZN11cmXMLWri.body: When called, `EndElement()` decreases the current indentation level, writes a closing tag for the current element (either `/>` for a self‑closing element or `</tag>` for a normal element), optionally inserts a line break if the element wasn't just content, then pops that element from the internal stack and clears the flag indicating the current element is no longer open.

@lcmXMLWriter::ProcessingInstruction@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::ProcessingInstruction@k_Z.body: The function finalizes any pending start‑element marker, optionally inserts a line break if the current output context isn’t already in text form, and then writes out a standard XML processing‑instruction fragment (`<?target data?>`) to the writer’s internal stream.

@lcmXMLWriter::StartDocument@k_ZN11cmXML.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::StartDocument@k_ZN11cmXML.body: The function writes the XML declaration to the `Output` stream, inserting the supplied encoding string inside the `encoding="…"` attribute of the `<?xml …?>` header.

@lcmXMLWriter::StartElement@k_ZN11cmXMLW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::StartElement@k_ZN11cmXMLW.body: Creates a new XML element by closing any pending start, writing a `<name>` tag, pushing the name onto the internal element stack, incrementing the nesting level and marking the element as open.

@lcmXMLWriter::~cmXMLWriter@k_ZN11cmXMLW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::~cmXMLWriter@k_ZN11cmXMLW.body: The destructor guarantees the `cmXMLWriter` instance has finished its work by asserting that the internal indentation counter is zero before the object is destroyed.

@lcmXcFrameworkPlist::SelectSuitableLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcFrameworkPlist::SelectSuitableLibr.body: The function iterates through `AvailableLibraries`, matching the current system name and platform‑variant against each library’s supported values; on a match it returns that library, otherwise it logs a fatal error and returns `nullptr`.

@lcmXcFrameworkPlist::cmXcFrameworkPlist.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcFrameworkPlist::cmXcFrameworkPlist.body: The function `cmXcFrameworkPlist()` registers and returns the list of available plug‑ins for the Xc framework. It queries the internal registry, gathers all registered plug‑in identifiers, and returns them in a standard list structure so the rest of the system can enumerate the current plug‑ins.

@lcmXcodeBuildSystemString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeBuildSystemString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The routine translates a `BuildSystem` enumeration value into its textual representation. It matches on `One` (yielding `"1"`) or `Twelve` (yielding `"12"`). If none of those values is supplied, it falls through and yields an empty `cm::string_view`.

@lcmXcodeVersionParser::CharacterDataHan.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeVersionParser::CharacterDataHan.body: The override takes a raw data buffer and its length, then pushes that block into the internal buffer. It’s a virtual extension of a base handler, so any subclass can swap the append logic while preserving the basic contract of feeding raw bytes into the stored stream.

@lcmXcodeVersionParser::EndElement@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeVersionParser::EndElement@k_ZN2.body: When the XML parser hits an element named “key”, it stores the element’s content into the member `Key`. If it then hits a “string” element whose name matches `CFBundleShortVersionString`, it saves the content into the member `Version`.

@lcmXcodeVersionParser::StartElement@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeVersionParser::StartElement@k_Z.body: The overridden `StartElement` implementation simply resets the internal `Data` string to empty. Whenever an element begins, the function clears any previously stored content, ignoring the passed `name` and `attributes` parameters.

@lcmXcodeVersionParser::cmXcodeVersionPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeVersionParser::cmXcodeVersionPa.body: The move‑constructor of `cmXcodeVersionParser` efficiently transfers ownership of a pre‑parsed version object into a new instance. Internally, it swaps out‑of‑box buffers and re‑initializes member pointers so that the new instance inherits the original state without deep copying. This technique keeps construction lightweight and avoids unnecessary copy‑construction while preserving the parser’s internal context across object boundaries.

@lcmXcodeVersionParser::cmXcodeVersionPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeVersionParser::cmXcodeVersionPa.body: The constructor takes an existing parser instance and clones its configuration and state, creating a fresh parser ready to read the same Xcode‑version XML fragments that the source parser handled. It’s invoked when a new parser is needed with identical parsing options in the global X‑code generation module.

@lcmXcodeVersionParser::cmXcodeVersionPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeVersionParser::cmXcodeVersionPa.body: Sets the instance’s version identifier to **1.5**, establishing that the object carries that specific version tag.

@lcmXcodeVersionParser::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeVersionParser::operator=@k_ZN20.body: This operator overload allows a `cmXcodeVersionParser` to be assigned from another instance via an rvalue reference. It moves the internal state of the right‑hand side into the current object and returns a reference to the object that performed the assignment.

@lcmXcodeVersionParser::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeVersionParser::operator=@k_ZN20.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of the source parser into the current instance. It copies all member variables that represent the parsing context—such as the current XML node, buffer pointers, and any flags that indicate whether parsing succeeded—while resetting any transient state in the target object. It returns a reference to the target instance (*this) to allow chaining. The function guards against self‑assignment and ensures that no dangling pointers or memory leaks arise during the copy.

@lcmXcodeVersionParser::~cmXcodeVersionP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXcodeVersionParser::~cmXcodeVersionP.body: The `~cmXcodeVersionParser()` virtual function is responsible for parsing the **Xcode** version metadata from an XML document. It extracts the `major` and `minor` version components, validates the format against known constraints, and stores the result in the internal `cmXcodeVersion` representation for later validation and compatibility checks.

@lcm_archive_entry_pathname@k_ZL25cm_arc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_archive_entry_pathname@k_ZL25cm_arc.body: The function returns a narrow‑encoded string representation of the entry’s path name. If the build has wide‑string support (`cmsys_STL_HAS_WSTRING`), it calls `archive_entry_pathname_w()` and passes the result through `cmsys::Encoding::ToNarrow` to produce a narrow `std::string`. If wide‑string support is absent, it simply forwards the result of `archive_entry_pathname()`. This conditional path ensures the function works correctly regardless of whether wide‑string handling is compiled in.

@lcm_archive_read_open_file@k_ZL25cm_arc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_archive_read_open_file@k_ZL25cm_arc.body: The function wraps a call to the appropriate internal file‑opening routine: if the build defines `cmsys_STL_HAS_WSTRING`, the passed‑in file name is converted to a wide string and `archive_read_open_filename_w` is invoked; otherwise it falls back to `archive_read_open_filename`. The return value is simply forwarded from that underlying routine.

@lcm_fileno@k_Z9cm_filenoPi@f./Source/cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_fileno@k_Z9cm_filenoPi@f./Source/cm.body: The function returns the operating‑system file descriptor for the `FILE*` passed in—essentially a thin wrapper around the (non‑standard) `fileno()` call.

@lcm_get_date@kcm_get_date.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_get_date@kcm_get_date.body: cm_get_date parses a date string supplied in `str` and returns the corresponding time_t value, optionally using the supplied `now` value for calculations.

@lcm_strverscmp@k_ZL13cm_strverscmpPKcS0.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_strverscmp@k_ZL13cm_strverscmpPKcS0.body: It finds the first differing byte, checks if that byte begins a digit run, and if so compares the numeric substrings by leading‑zero count and length. If the numeric parts are equal it resolves the order by the raw byte values.

@lcm_strverscmp_count_leading_zeros@k_ZL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_strverscmp_count_leading_zeros@k_ZL.body: This function scans a character array beginning at index b and walks forward while the current character is the digit ‘0’ and the following character is also a digit. It returns the number of such consecutive ‘0’ characters found, effectively reporting how many leading zeros precede a non‑zero digit in the string.

@lcm_strverscmp_find_digits_begin@k_ZL31.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_strverscmp_find_digits_begin@k_ZL31.body: This function walks backward from the given index `i` until it reaches a character that is not a digit, then returns that index.

@lcm_strverscmp_find_digits_end@k_ZL29cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_strverscmp_find_digits_end@k_ZL29cm.body: Advances the index until a non‑digit is encountered and returns that position.

@lcm_strverscmp_find_first_difference_or.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_strverscmp_find_first_difference_or.body: The routine walks forward through two null‑terminated strings until it encounters a mismatch or a string terminator. When it reaches the first differing byte (or the end of one string), it returns that offset, effectively indicating the first point of divergence or that the strings are identical up to the shorter string’s length.

@lcm_utf8_decode_character@kcm_utf8_deco.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_utf8_decode_character@kcm_utf8_deco.body: The routine reads a byte sequence from the supplied buffer, uses the first byte to determine how many continuation bytes follow, validates each byte, then stitches the bit fragments together to form the Unicode code‑point, writes that value into the supplied integer, and returns a pointer to the byte after the decoded character (or null if the sequence is malformed).

@lcm_utf8_is_valid@kcm_utf8_is_valid@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_utf8_is_valid@kcm_utf8_is_valid@f./.body: The function walks through a C string, decoding it byte by byte with `cm_utf8_decode_character`. It stops when either the end of the string is reached or a decoding error occurs. If the walk finishes exactly at the string’s null terminator, it reports the string as a valid UTF‑8 sequence; otherwise, it deems the string invalid.

@lcmake::ActualConfigure@k_ZN5cmake15Act.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ActualConfigure@k_ZN5cmake15Act.body: The ActualConfigure method performs the full CMake initialization. It starts by cleaning up and rebuilding the scratch directories, runs a pre‑configuration sanity check, and then selects or creates the appropriate generator instance, verifying that the generator, instance, platform, and toolset match any cached values. It writes the necessary cache entries (including emulators for cross‑compiling), clears old state, records the configuration in the log, and finally persists the cache. On success it returns 0; on failure it returns negative error codes.

@lcmake::AddCMakePaths@k_ZN5cmake13AddCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::AddCMakePaths@k_ZN5cmake13AddCM.body: The function records the paths to the CMake tools in the internal cache: it stores the main CMake executable, and – if the build is not in bootstrap mode – the auxiliary ctest and cpack utilities. After adding those entries it verifies that the CMake modules directory exists under the installation root; if the check fails it logs an error and aborts the initialization, signalling a failure with a return value of 0, otherwise it reports success with 1.

@lcmake::AddCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake13AddCa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::AddCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake13AddCa.body: The method forwards the supplied key, value, help‑string, and type to an internal overload that accepts a `cmValue` constructed from the help string, effectively adding a cache entry.

@lcmake::AddCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake13AddCa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::AddCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake13AddCa.body: Adds a cache entry with the supplied key, value, help string and type. It updates internal messenger settings according to specific warning keys and removes any unused client watchers.

@lcmake::AddCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake13AddCa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::AddCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake13AddCa.body: The public `AddCacheEntry` method simply forwards the supplied key, value, help string, and type to an internal implementation that wraps the string arguments in a `cmValue` container before storing them in the cache. This wrapper likely handles the underlying storage logic for the cache entry.

@lcmake::AddDefaultExtraGenerators@k_ZN5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::AddDefaultExtraGenerators@k_ZN5.body: The method appends a set of predefined generator factories into the `ExtraGenerators` collection, but only if the macro `CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP` is not defined. It pulls in factories for standard code‑block types such as Eclipse, Kate, Sublime, and other lightweight generators, adding them automatically at construction time.

@lcmake::AddDefaultGenerators@k_ZN5cmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::AddDefaultGenerators@k_ZN5cmake.body: The function populates the internal generator registry with a set of pre‑defined generator factories. Depending on build‑time macros it adds Visual Studio‑compatible factories (15/16/17 VS, 14, 12, 9), Borland‑Make, NMake, JOM, MSYS, MinGW, GHS, Unix, Ninja, and optional WMake/XCode. @lcmake::GetSystemInformation@k_ZN5cmake.body: The function sets up a temporary working area, interprets command‑line options to decide whether to generate a specific generator or write results to a file, runs an internal CMake invocation that writes its output to a results file, and finally streams that file to stdout (if requested) before tearing the temporary directory down.

@lcmake::GetTopCheckInProgressMessage@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetTopCheckInProgressMessage@k_.body: The method removes and returns the most recent message stored in the `CheckInProgressMessages` collection, effectively giving callers the latest in‑progress check‑message and clearing it from the list.

@lcmake::GetTrace@k_ZNK5cmake8GetTraceEv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetTrace@k_ZNK5cmake8GetTraceEv.body: Returns the current trace flag value stored in the object.

@lcmake::GetTraceExpand@k_ZNK5cmake14Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetTraceExpand@k_ZNK5cmake14Get.body: It returns the current value stored in the private member `TraceExpand`.

@lcmake::GetTraceFile@k_ZN5cmake12GetTra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetTraceFile@k_ZN5cmake12GetTra.body: The method simply returns the current trace file: if a redirect has been installed, it forwards the request to that instance; otherwise it returns the default trace file that belongs to the object.

@lcmake::GetTraceFormat@k_ZNK5cmake14Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetTraceFormat@k_ZNK5cmake14Get.body:
The member function returns the stored trace‑format value.  
It is a `const` accessor that simply returns the value held in `TraceFormatVar` without modifying the object.

@lcmake::GetTraceSources@k_ZNK5cmake15Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetTraceSources@k_ZNK5cmake15Ge.body: Returns a const reference to the internal vector of trace‑source strings, so callers see the original collection without copying. Because the method is const, the returned vector itself cannot be modified, though the strings it contains could still be altered if held elsewhere.

@lcmake::GetVariableWatch@k_ZN5cmake16Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetVariableWatch@k_ZN5cmake16Ge.body: The method simply returns a pointer to the internally stored `cmVariableWatch` instance (`VariableWatch`). It invokes `VariableWatch.get()` to obtain the pointer and returns it unchanged.

@lcmake::GetWarnUninitialized@k_ZNK5cmak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetWarnUninitialized@k_ZNK5cmak.body: Retrieves and returns the current value of the flag that tracks whether the class should warn about uninitialized state. The method never mutates the object; it simply exposes that internal boolean.

@lcmake::GetWarnUnusedCli@k_ZNK5cmake16G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetWarnUnusedCli@k_ZNK5cmake16G.body: Returns the current value of the private `WarnUnusedCli` flag, indicating whether unused‑CLI‑argument warnings are enabled.

@lcmake::GetWorkingMode@k_ZN5cmake14GetW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetWorkingMode@k_ZN5cmake14GetW.body: Returns the value stored in the `CurrentWorkingMode` member of the object.

@lcmake::HandleDeleteCacheVariables@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::HandleDeleteCacheVariables@k_ZN.body: When invoked with a variable name, the function first clears a global flag so that subsequent cache handling won’t recurse. It then records the current values of each named cache entry (plus any help strings), reports those that changed, wipes the cache directory, loads the empty cache, re‑adds the recorded entries, and finally warns the user that the cache has been reset. If no errors were flagged during the process, the function triggers a fresh run of the configuration step before returning.

@lcmake::HasCheckInProgress@k_ZNK5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::HasCheckInProgress@k_ZNK5cmake1.body: The `HasCheckInProgress` method simply reports whether any check‑in‑messages are pending by checking if the internal container is non‑empty. It operates in constant time, returning `true` when at least one message exists, otherwise `false`.

@lcmake::IsACLikeSourceExtension@k_ZNK5c.author: AI Short Overview
