@lcmake::IsACLikeSourceExtension@k_ZNK5c.body: Checks whether the supplied string matches any of the predefined “AC‑like” source‑file extensions (e.g., .c, .cpp, .h, .hpp, .m, .swift, .py). It returns true only when the input string ends with one of those suffixes; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmake::IsACLikeSourceExtension@k_ZNK5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::IsACLikeSourceExtension@k_ZNK5c.body: The function simply checks whether a given file‑extension string matches one of the known C‑style source‑file extensions stored in the object. It delegates this check to the `CLikeSourceFileExtensions` helper by calling its `Test` method and returns that Boolean result.

@lcmake::IsAHeaderExtension@k_ZNK5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::IsAHeaderExtension@k_ZNK5cmake1.body: This method returns true when the supplied extension string is present in the object’s header‑file‑extension set; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmake::IsAKnownExtension@k_ZNK5cmake17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::IsAKnownExtension@k_ZNK5cmake17.body: It checks whether the supplied extension matches any known source‑ or header‑type file by delegating to two helper checks – one that tests for source extensions and another that tests for header extensions.

@lcmake::IsAKnownSourceExtension@k_ZNK5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::IsAKnownSourceExtension@k_ZNK5c.body: The function checks whether the given extension string matches any of five pre‑populated extension tables (`CLikeSourceFileExtensions`, `CudaFileExtensions`, `FortranFileExtensions`, `HipFileExtensions`, `ISPCFileExtensions`). It returns `true` when the extension exists in any of those tables, otherwise `false`.

@lcmake::IsProfilingEnabled@k_ZNK5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::IsProfilingEnabled@k_ZNK5cmake1.body: The function simply returns a Boolean indicating whether profiling is active. Internally, it casts the member `ProfilingOutput` to a `bool` (assuming that member is some type convertible to `bool`). If `ProfilingOutput` is already a `bool`, the cast is redundant; if it’s a numeric flag, the cast ensures the return value is a plain `bool`. This function can be a single‑line helper that any code path can query the internal flag without modifying it.

@lcmake::IssueMessage@k_ZNK5cmake12Issue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::IssueMessage@k_ZNK5cmake12Issue.body: The function forwards a message to the internal messenger instance, passing along the message type, text, and back‑trace data.

@lcmake::LoadCache@k_ZN5cmake9LoadCacheE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::LoadCache@k_ZN5cmake9LoadCacheE.body: The function forwards the call to another overload of `LoadCache`, supplying the path, a flag of `true` and two empty `std::set<std::string>` objects, and returns the result of that call.

@lcmake::LoadCache@k_ZN5cmake9LoadCacheE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::LoadCache@k_ZN5cmake9LoadCacheE.body: The function forwards the loading task to the internal State object, then iteratively removes the entries “CMAKE_CACHE_MAJOR_VERSION” and “CMAKE_CACHE_MINOR_VERSION” via UnwatchUnusedCli, and finally returns the operation’s success flag.

@lcmake::LoadCache@k_ZN5cmake9LoadCacheE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::LoadCache@k_ZN5cmake9LoadCacheE.body: The `LoadCache` routine loads CMake’s in‑memory cache by reading `CMakeCache.txt` from the output directory. If the file is present but unreadable, it reports a permission error and returns –1; otherwise it invokes `AddCMakePaths()` to establish `CMAKE_ROOT`/`CMAKE_COMMAND` and returns 0 on success or –3 on failure.

@lcmake::LoadEnvironmentPresets::[lambda.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::LoadEnvironmentPresets::[lambda.body: This lambda reads an environment variable named *name*; if the variable is defined and a generator is available, it assigns its value to *key*. If the generator is not set, it logs a warning.

@lcmake::LoadEnvironmentPresets@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::LoadEnvironmentPresets@k_ZN5cma.body: The routine queries the system for the `CMAKE_GENERATOR` environment variable; if present it marks the generator flag and records its value. A helper lambda then reads three other variables—`CMAKE_GENERATOR_INSTANCE`, `CMAKE_GENERATOR_PLATFORM`, and `CMAKE_GENERATOR_TOOLSET`—assigning them only when the generator is present, otherwise emitting a warning if the variable exists but the generator is absent (unless a compile‑try is already in progress). This populates the `EnvironmentGenerator`, `GeneratorInstance`, `GeneratorPlatform`, and `GeneratorToolset` members accordingly.

@lcmake::LogLevelToString::[lambda_0]@kc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::LogLevelToString::[lambda_0]@kc.body: The lambda captures `level` by reference and checks whether the `second` field of a `LevelsPair` equals that captured value, returning `true` when they match.

@lcmake::LogLevelToString@k_ZN5cmake16Lo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::LogLevelToString@k_ZN5cmake16Lo.body: The function searches a static array of string–level pairs for a pair whose level matches the given enum value, then returns that string converted to upper‑case; if no match is found it returns “undefined”.

@lcmake::MarkCliAsUsed@k_ZN5cmake13MarkC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::MarkCliAsUsed@k_ZN5cmake13MarkC.body: The function stores a flag in a map (`UsedCliVariables`) indicating that a command‑line variable has been consumed. When called, it simply writes `true` for the supplied key, effectively marking that variable as “used” for later processing.

@lcmake::Open@k_ZN5cmake4OpenERKNSt3__11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::Open@k_ZN5cmake4OpenERKNSt3__11.body: The function configures the build system for a specific directory: it verifies the directory, loads the project’s cache, determines the generator name (including any extra suffix), creates a generator instance, and finally opens the generator with the cached project name, returning success or failure.

@lcmake::ParseCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake15Par.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ParseCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake15Par.body: The function simply forwards the call to `cmState::ParseCacheEntry`, passing the supplied string, variable name, value, and enum reference, and returns that function’s boolean result.

@lcmake::PreLoadCMakeFiles@k_ZN5cmake17P.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PreLoadCMakeFiles@k_ZN5cmake17P.body: The function looks for a file named **PreLoad.cmake** in both the project’s home directory and its output sub‑folder. If the file exists in either location, it loads the list of arguments contained therein by calling `ReadListFile`. This populates the internal `args` vector with configuration values that will be used later in the build process.

@lcmake::PrintGeneratorList@k_ZN5cmake18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PrintGeneratorList@k_ZN5cmake18.body: When called, this helper formats the current generator documentation into a `cmDocumentation` object and streams the resulting list to `std::cerr`, but only when the `CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP` macro is not defined.

@lcmake::PrintPresetEnvironment@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PrintPresetEnvironment@k_ZN5cma.body: It walks through the `UnprocessedPresetEnvironment` container, printing each variable that has a value (i.e. `second` is non‑empty). After printing them it clears the container.

@lcmake::PrintPresetList::[lambda_0]::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PrintPresetList::[lambda_0]::[l.body: It examines a `GeneratorInfo` object and returns a boolean indicating whether the supplied information satisfies internal conditions.

@lcmake::PrintPresetList::[lambda_0]::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PrintPresetList::[lambda_0]::[l.body: Captures the outer `preset` object by reference, then checks whether a supplied `GeneratorInfo` instance has a `name` that matches the `preset.Generator` field, returning `true` when they match and `false` otherwise.

@lcmake::PrintPresetList::[lambda_0]@kcm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PrintPresetList::[lambda_0]@kcm.body: This lambda checks if the preset’s generator name is present in the global `generators` container. If the generator string in `preset` is empty it returns `true`. Otherwise it builds a predicate that compares a `GeneratorInfo`’s name against that string and uses `std::find_if` to see if any matching entry exists in `generators`; the result (`true` when found, `false` otherwise) is returned.

@lcmake::PrintPresetList@k_ZNK5cmake15Pr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PrintPresetList@k_ZNK5cmake15Pr.body: The function gathers all registered generators, then builds a predicate that keeps only those presets whose generator name is present in that list (or whose generator field is empty). It finally hands that filter to the graph to print the matching presets.

@lcmake::PrintPresetVariables@k_ZN5cmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PrintPresetVariables@k_ZN5cmake.body: It loops through the `UnprocessedPresetVariables` collection, prints each stored name/value pair (appending a type tag when the type string can be translated to a cache‑entry enum), and finally empties the container.

@lcmake::PrintTraceFormatVersion@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PrintTraceFormatVersion@k_ZN5cm.body:
The function checks whether a trace is available; if not, it exits.  
It then constructs a message string depending on the trace format: for `JSONv1` it builds a JSON object containing a version sub‑object (`{“major”:1, “minor”:2}`) and serialises it; for `Human` it produces an empty string; for undefined formats it reports an internal‑error string.  
Finally, if the constructed message is non‑empty it writes the string to the trace file if one is open, otherwise it logs the message via `cmSystemTools::Message`.

@lcmake::ProcessCacheArg@k_ZN5cmake15Pro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ProcessCacheArg@k_ZN5cmake15Pro.body: The routine registers a new cache entry for a variable and, when caching is enabled, compares the stored value before and after the insertion, triggering a warning if the value has altered.

@lcmake::ProcessPresetEnvironment@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ProcessPresetEnvironment@k_ZN5c.body: The function iterates over the collection `UnprocessedPresetEnvironment`. For each key‑value pair, if the value is non‑null, it concatenates the key and value into the string “key=value” and forwards that string to the helper `cmSystemTools::PutEnv`. This has the effect of loading the preset environment variables into the process’s environment.

@lcmake::ProcessPresetVariables@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ProcessPresetVariables@k_ZN5cma.body: The routine walks the internal list of preset variables, skips any entries that have no data, decides the cache‑entry type from the variable’s declared type string (defaulting to `UNINITIALIZED` when the string is empty), and hands the variable’s key, value, and resolved type over to `ProcessCacheArg` for actual caching.

@lcmake::PushCheckInProgressMessage@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::PushCheckInProgressMessage@k_ZN.body: Adds a string to the `CheckInProgressMessages` container by moving the supplied message into a new element at the end of the vector.

@lcmake::ReadListFile@k_ZN5cmake12ReadLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ReadListFile@k_ZN5cmake12ReadLi.body: The routine first guarantees that a global generator object is available, either by re‑using an existing one or by creating a temporary instance. It then prepares a snapshot of the current build state, configuring source and binary directories and default definitions. Finally it creates a `cmMakefile` object and asks it to read the specified list file, signalling an error if the file cannot be found or parsed.

@lcmake::ReportCapabilities@k_ZNK5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ReportCapabilities@k_ZNK5cmake1.body: The function serializes the object’s capability data into JSON and returns that string; when the bootstrap macro is defined, it simply returns a placeholder string instead of real data.

@lcmake::ReportCapabilitiesJson@k_ZNK5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ReportCapabilitiesJson@k_ZNK5cm.body: The method assembles a JSON object that exposes the tool’s runtime metadata: it starts by inserting a version block, iterates over all registered generators (skipping aliases), grouping any alternate names under an “extraGenerators” entry, then attaches flags for server mode, TLS support and debugging capability before returning the composite value.

@lcmake::ReportVersionJson@k_ZNK5cmake17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ReportVersionJson@k_ZNK5cmake17.body: It builds a JSON object containing the current build’s version components—`string`, `major`, `minor`, `suffix`, `isDirty`, and `patch`—populating each field from the corresponding `CMake_…` macros and returning that object.

@lcmake::Run@k_ZN5cmake3RunERKi@f./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::Run@k_ZN5cmake3RunERKi@f./Sourc.body: It forwards the supplied argument vector to an internal overload by passing a second argument of `false`, then returns whatever that overload yields.

@lcmake::Run@k_ZN5cmake3RunERKib@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::Run@k_ZN5cmake3RunERKib@f./Sour.body: The `Run` routine parses command‑line options into its internal state, logs any requested trace format, and validates supplied stamp files or stamp lists. It then restores or clears cached data, loads any preset variables, and enforces that a “fresh cache” flag is only permitted during project configuration. After cleaning the environment (including removing any legacy `MAKEFLAGS` variable) it invokes the generator’s `Configure` step; if that succeeds it calls `Generate` to write out‑build files before signalling completion.

@lcmake::RunCheckForUnusedVariables@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::RunCheckForUnusedVariables@k_ZN.body: It scans the project’s list of command‑line variables and, whenever it finds one that was specified but never referenced, it collects its name and, after the scan, emits a single warning listing those unused entries.

@lcmake::SaveCache@k_ZN5cmake9SaveCacheE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SaveCache@k_ZN5cmake9SaveCacheE.body: The method runs a single‑pass save operation: it forwards the requested file path to the internal state object, passes a messenger reference for callbacks, and afterward iterates over a fixed list of key identifiers calling `UnwatchUnusedCli` on each—effectively pruning any stale entries before returning whether the underlying save succeeded.

@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_0]@kcmake::Set.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_0]@kcmake::Set.body: The lambda takes a string reference and a state pointer, emits a warning that an empty string was supplied, and always returns `true`.

@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_1]@kcmake::Set.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_1]@kcmake::Set.body: The lambda checks whether the supplied source path is empty. If it’s non‑empty, it normalises the string into a canonical Unix‑style absolute path and uses that value to set the home directory in the application state. It returns `true` on success and `false` only when the input is missing, after reporting an error.

@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_2]@kcmake::Set.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_2]@kcmake::Set.body: The lambda takes a string and a state pointer. It normalises the string into a Unix‑style path, stores it in the state’s home‑output directory flag, and flips a local boolean flag to indicate that the directory has been set. If the supplied string is empty, it logs an error and aborts the operation, returning false. Otherwise the function returns true upon successfully updating the state.

@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_3]@kcmake::Set.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_3]@kcmake::Set.body: The lambda validates a single‑time platform assignment: if already set it signals an error and aborts; otherwise it stores the string via `SetGeneratorPlatform` and flips the flag, returning success.

@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_4]@kcmake::Set.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetArgs::[lambda_4]@kcmake::Set.body: This lambda checks whether a toolset has already been supplied. If it has, it emits an error and returns `false`; otherwise it stores the supplied value via `SetGeneratorToolset`, marks that a toolset has been set, and returns `true`.

@lcmake::SetArgs@k_ZN5cmake7SetArgsERKi@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetArgs@k_ZN5cmake7SetArgsERKi@.body: The `SetArgs` routine walks the supplied argument list and interprets every flag it encounters, wiring that choice into the build‑generation state. It uses a collection of lambda handlers—each tied to a particular option such as `-S` for source dir, `-B` for build dir, `-A` for platform, `-T` for toolset, etc.—to validate the value, adjust internal flags, and optionally issue warnings or errors when misuse is detected. After parsing, it normalises the current working mode, applies any preset overrides, and finally guarantees sensible defaults (current directory for missing source or build directories, preset‑derived settings, and trace/debug toggles).

@lcmake::SetCMakeEditCommand@k_ZN5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCMakeEditCommand@k_ZN5cmake1.body: Stores the supplied string in the internal `CMakeEditCommand` member.

@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_0]@kcmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_0]@kcmake.body: Parses a string of the form `VAR:type=value`, removes the variable from any unprocessed preset list, processes the value for the current cache state, and reports failure if the format cannot be parsed.

@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_1]@kcmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_1]@kcmake.body: The lambda parses a warning identifier string, strips any “no‑” or “error=” prefixes, and then updates the diagnostic table accordingly: a plain entry sets the level to the highest of its current value or warning; a “no‑” entry disables it; an “error=” entry marks it as an error; if both prefixes are present it lowers the level to warning only if the warning is already present. It returns `true` after modifying the table.

@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_2]@kcmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_2]@kcmake.body: Creates a regex from the supplied pattern, scans the cache for entries whose keys match that regex (ignoring static ones), collects those keys, then removes each matched key from the cache and from `UnprocessedPresetVariables`. Finally, it returns true.

@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_3]@kcmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_3]@kcmake.body: The lambda configures the CMake script environment: it optionally starts the debugger, registers fake project commands for the script mode, switches to script mode, sets the home and output directories to the current working directory, loads the list file for the given path, and returns true if successful.

@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_4]@kcmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_4]@kcmake.body: The lambda checks whether a given path string is an absolute path. If it is, it removes the “CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX” variable from the unprocessed preset list (unless bootstrapping is enabled), processes the path as a cache argument of type PATH, and returns success; otherwise it emits an error and returns failure.

@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_5]@kcmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCacheArgs::[lambda_5]@kcmake.body: The lambda takes a file‑path string and a state object. It removes any existing “CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE” entry from `UnprocessedPresetVariables`, then records the supplied path in the cache as a `FILEPATH` entry via `ProcessCacheArg`. It always returns `true`.

@lcmake::SetCacheArgs@k_ZN5cmake12SetCac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCacheArgs@k_ZN5cmake12SetCac.body: The function parses command‑line options to configure the internal cache. It defines several lambda handlers (for `‑D`, `‑W`, `‑U`, `‑C`, `‑P`, `‑‑install‑prefix`) that modify the state accordingly. It iterates over the supplied arguments, invokes the matching handler for each, and returns false on failure; otherwise it returns true after all arguments are processed.

@lcmake::SetCheckSystemVars@k_ZN5cmake18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCheckSystemVars@k_ZN5cmake18.body: Sets the internal `CheckSystemVars` flag to the value provided.

@lcmake::SetCurrentSnapshot@k_ZN5cmake18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetCurrentSnapshot@k_ZN5cmake18.body: This method simply assigns the supplied snapshot to the object’s `CurrentSnapshot` member, overwriting whatever snapshot was previously stored.

@lcmake::SetDebugFindOutput@k_ZN5cmake18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetDebugFindOutput@k_ZN5cmake18.body: Updates an internal flag that determines whether diagnostic output is emitted.

@lcmake::SetDebugFindOutputPkgs@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetDebugFindOutputPkgs@k_ZN5cma.body: The function simply stores the supplied string `args` into the `DebugFindPkgs` container (an `unordered_set` or equivalent). It uses a const reference to avoid copying the argument and inserts it via `emplace`, which performs a direct construction of the stored element.

@lcmake::SetDebugFindOutputVars@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetDebugFindOutputVars@k_ZN5cma.body: The function `SetDebugFindOutputVars` receives a string reference and inserts that string into the `DebugFindVars` container, effectively recording a new debug variable name for later retrieval.

@lcmake::SetDebugOutputOn@k_ZN5cmake16Se.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetDebugOutputOn@k_ZN5cmake16Se.body: Assigns the supplied boolean to the internal flag that governs whether debug information is routed to the output stream. This single assignment operation toggles the debug‑logging state used by the rest of the class.

@lcmake::SetDebuggerOn@k_ZN5cmake13SetDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetDebuggerOn@k_ZN5cmake13SetDe.body: The method simply assigns the supplied boolean value to the internal `DebuggerOn` flag, turning the debugging feature on or off.

@lcmake::SetDeprecatedWarningsAsErrors@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetDeprecatedWarningsAsErrors@k.body: When invoked, the routine stores a flag in CMake’s cache under the key `CMAKE_ERROR_DEPRECATED`. The flag’s value is `"TRUE"` if the argument `b` is true and `"FALSE"` otherwise. The cached value controls whether the build system will elevate deprecation warnings to errors for macros and functions during a CMake run.

@lcmake::SetDevWarningsAsErrors@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetDevWarningsAsErrors@k_ZN5cma.body: The method records the supplied flag in the internal cache by adding an entry named "CMAKE_SUPPRESS_DEVELOPER_ERRORS". If `b` is true it stores the string "FALSE" (meaning suppress errors are enabled), otherwise it stores "TRUE" (meaning they are disabled). It then forwards this key‑value pair to AddCacheEntry together with a description that indicates the entry controls suppression of developer‑level errors.

@lcmake::SetDirectoriesFromFile@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetDirectoriesFromFile@k_ZN5cma.body: The function first determines whether the supplied argument points to a directory or a file named `CMakeCache.txt` or `CMakeLists.txt`. It collapses the path, checks for those special files, and then loads cache entries if a cache file exists. Depending on which file (or directory) is found, it sets the home and output directories appropriately, falling back to the current working directory when nothing is specified. The function returns `true` if the provided path was successfully used; otherwise it leaves the configuration unchanged.

@lcmake::SetGeneratorInstance@k_ZN5cmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetGeneratorInstance@k_ZN5cmake.body: Assigns the supplied string to the member `GeneratorInstance` and flips the flag `GeneratorInstanceSet` to true, indicating that a generator instance has been configured.

@lcmake::SetGeneratorPlatform@k_ZN5cmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetGeneratorPlatform@k_ZN5cmake.body: The method assigns the supplied string to the member `GeneratorPlatform` and records that the value has been set by toggling `GeneratorPlatformSet` to `true`. This simple assignment pattern leaves no side‑effects beyond the flag update.

@lcmake::SetGeneratorToolset@k_ZN5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetGeneratorToolset@k_ZN5cmake1.body: Sets the supplied string into the class’s `GeneratorToolset` member and flips the `GeneratorToolsetSet` flag to true, indicating the toolset has been defined.

@lcmake::SetGlobalGenerator@k_ZN5cmake18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetGlobalGenerator@k_ZN5cmake18.body: The routine first guards against a null pointer, then (if a previous generator was present) restores the original “CXX” and “CC” environment entries, and finally assigns the new generator object to the singleton instance. It also propagates whether the new generator expects Unix‑style paths, records that flag in the system utilities, and remembers the current values of “CXX” and “CC” for later restoration.

@lcmake::SetHomeDirectory@k_ZN5cmake16Se.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetHomeDirectory@k_ZN5cmake16Se.body: The routine stores the supplied directory in the component’s internal state, updates any current snapshot metadata if the snapshot is still valid, and adjusts the top‑level source path in the messenger service. If the project type is “Normal” it propagates this directory; otherwise it clears the top source entry.

@lcmake::SetHomeDirectoryViaCommandLine@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetHomeDirectoryViaCommandLine@.body:
The function updates the internal home‑directory state.  
If the supplied path differs from the current one while the system is in normal mode, it logs a warning that the extra path is being ignored.  
Finally it calls SetHomeDirectory to apply the new path.

@lcmake::SetHomeOutputDirectory@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetHomeOutputDirectory@k_ZN5cma.body: The function stores the supplied path in the internal state and, when a current snapshot is available and valid, records that path under the key `CMAKE_BINARY_DIR`.

@lcmake::SetIgnoreWarningAsError@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetIgnoreWarningAsError@k_ZN5cm.body: Sets the internal flag controlling whether warning conditions should be escalated to errors during processing.

@lcmake::SetLogLevel@k_ZN5cmake11SetLogL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetLogLevel@k_ZN5cmake11SetLogL.body: Updates the internal log‑level setting to the supplied value.

@lcmake::SetProgressCallback@k_ZN5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetProgressCallback@k_ZN5cmake1.body: The `SetProgressCallback` function assigns the provided callback to the member `ProgressCallback`, using `std::move` to efficiently transfer ownership of the callback object into the class instance. It simply updates the internal callback reference without additional side‑effects.

@lcmake::SetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11SetProp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11SetProp.body: The function simply forwards the provided property name and value to the internal state object, delegating the actual storage logic to `SetGlobalProperty`. It’s a thin wrapper that translates the caller’s input into an update of the internal global property map.

@lcmake::SetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11SetProp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11SetProp.body: The overload takes a string and a dummy `nullptr_t` argument, then forwards the call to another overload by constructing a temporary `cmValue` initialized with `nullptr` and delegating the work.

@lcmake::SetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11SetProp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11SetProp.body: The overload simply forwards its arguments to an internal overload that expects a cmValue, converting the plain string to that wrapper type before delegating.

@lcmake::SetShowLogContext@k_ZN5cmake17S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetShowLogContext@k_ZN5cmake17S.body: Updates the internal logging flag with the supplied boolean, enabling or disabling the display of log messages.

@lcmake::SetSuppressDeprecatedWarnings@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetSuppressDeprecatedWarnings@k.body: The function takes a boolean flag, translates it into a string value ("FALSE" when suppression is desired, “TRUE” otherwise), and stores this flag in the internal cache under the name “CMAKE_WARN_DEPRECATED” via `AddCacheEntry`. This cache entry is consulted later to decide whether the build system should emit warnings for deprecated constructs.

@lcmake::SetSuppressDevWarnings@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetSuppressDevWarnings@k_ZN5cma.body: When `b` is true the function stores “TRUE” as the value of the internal cache key **CMAKE_SUPPRESS_DEVELOPER_WARNINGS**, otherwise it stores “FALSE”. This cache entry turns on or off the suppression of developer‑level warnings in CMake.

@lcmake::SetTrace@k_ZN5cmake8SetTraceEb@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetTrace@k_ZN5cmake8SetTraceEb@.body: Sets the internal tracing flag to the value supplied, enabling or disabling trace logging for the object.

@lcmake::SetTraceExpand@k_ZN5cmake14SetT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetTraceExpand@k_ZN5cmake14SetT.body: The method assigns the supplied boolean to the member variable `TraceExpand`, effectively toggling the trace‑expansion feature for the current instance. It performs no validation or side effects beyond the simple field assignment.

@lcmake::SetTraceFile@k_ZN5cmake12SetTra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetTraceFile@k_ZN5cmake12SetTra.body: The function closes any previously opened trace file, opens the new file path supplied in **file**, checks the open succeeded, logs an error via *cmSystemTools::Error* if it fails, and finally emits a confirmation message to *std::cout* indicating the destination for subsequent trace output.

@lcmake::SetTraceFormat@k_ZN5cmake14SetT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetTraceFormat@k_ZN5cmake14SetT.body: Assigns the supplied TraceFormat value to the internal TraceFormatVar member, updating the object's trace‑format configuration.

@lcmake::SetTraceRedirect@k_ZN5cmake16Se.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetTraceRedirect@k_ZN5cmake16Se.body: It copies the tracing configuration from the supplied `other` object into the current instance and keeps a reference to that object for future trace‑redirect operations.

@lcmake::SetWarnUninitialized@k_ZN5cmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetWarnUninitialized@k_ZN5cmake.body: Sets the internal flag that controls whether the system emits a warning when uninitialized usage is detected.

@lcmake::SetWarnUnusedCli@k_ZN5cmake16Se.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetWarnUnusedCli@k_ZN5cmake16Se.body: Sets the internal flag that determines whether the system issues warnings for unused CLI options.

@lcmake::SetWarningFromPreset@k_ZN5cmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetWarningFromPreset@k_ZN5cmake.body: This routine adjusts the diagnostic level for a specific feature name. If a warning flag is supplied, it bumps the level to at least **WARN** when the flag is true, and drops it to **IGNORE** when false. Likewise, an error flag that is true forces the level to **ERROR**, while a false flag lowers the level to no higher than **WARN**. The function therefore updates the internal `DiagLevels` mapping according to the optional warning and error inputs.

@lcmake::SetWorkingMode@k_ZN5cmake14SetW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetWorkingMode@k_ZN5cmake14SetW.body: This method simply assigns the supplied `mode` to the member variable `CurrentWorkingMode`. It performs a direct assignment without side‑effects, implying that any logic depending on a mode change will be handled elsewhere. The function is typically used to switch the system’s operational state (e.g., normal, maintenance, diagnostic) and should be called only after validating the new mode is accepted by the surrounding context.

@lcmake::StartDebuggerIfEnabled@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::StartDebuggerIfEnabled@k_ZN5cma.body: This function checks whether debugging is enabled; if not, it simply returns `true`. When debugging is enabled it ensures a debugger adapter exists: it verifies that a debugger pipe has been configured and, if missing, reports an error. If everything is in order it constructs the adapter, attaches it to the messenger, and returns `true`. If any step fails, it reports the failure and returns `false`.

@lcmake::StopDebuggerIfNeeded@k_ZN5cmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::StopDebuggerIfNeeded@k_ZN5cmake.body: When the debugger flag is set, the method forwards the supplied exit code to the adapter and then releases the adapter instance.

@lcmake::StringToLogLevel::[lambda_0]@kc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::StringToLogLevel::[lambda_0]@kc.body: Captures a reference to `levelStrLowCase` and, for a given `LevelsPair`, returns `true` when its `first` member equals that captured value; otherwise `false`.

@lcmake::StringToLogLevel@k_ZN5cmake16St.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::StringToLogLevel@k_ZN5cmake16St.body: The function normalises the input string to lower‑case, then performs a linear search over a static lookup array of pairs mapping string literals to `Message::LogLevel` values. If a match is found it returns the corresponding enum value; otherwise it falls back to `LOG_UNDEFINED`. This behaviour is straightforward but incurs a linear lookup cost on each call.

@lcmake::StringToTraceFormat::[lambda_0].author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::StringToTraceFormat::[lambda_0].body: The lambda captures `traceStrLowCase` by reference and returns a predicate that, given a `TracePair`, returns true when the pair’s first field equals the captured string.

@lcmake::StringToTraceFormat@k_ZN5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::StringToTraceFormat@k_ZN5cmake1.body: The function normalises the input string to lower‑case, looks it up in a static lookup table that maps the strings “human” and “json‑v1” to the corresponding `TraceFormat` enum values, and returns that enum value; if no match is found it returns `TraceFormat::Undefined`.

@lcmake::StripExtension@k_ZNK5cmake14Str.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::StripExtension@k_ZNK5cmake14Str.body: This function returns the file name without its extension if the extension is recognized by `IsAKnownExtension`; otherwise it returns the original string unchanged.

@lcmake::TruncateOutputLog@k_ZN5cmake17T.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::TruncateOutputLog@k_ZN5cmake17T.body: Builds a full path for the supplied file name, verifies the file’s existence, and deletes it if the cache‑specific flag indicates it should not be retained. When the file exists and its size exceeds 50 KB, the routine would cut it down to that limit (the truncation code is marked as a placeholder).

@lcmake::UnwatchUnusedCli@k_ZN5cmake16Un.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::UnwatchUnusedCli@k_ZN5cmake16Un.body: Removes a CLI‑defined variable from the watch list and clears its “used” flag, keeping the internal set of watched names current only while still respecting the compile‑time “CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP” guard.

@lcmake::UpdateConversionPathTable@k_ZN5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::UpdateConversionPathTable@k_ZN5.body: The `UpdateConversionPathTable` method reads the path‑translation file specified in the build cache (`CMAKE_PATH_TRANSLATION_FILE`). If the file exists, it opens the file and streams each line, extracting two tokens per line (source and target paths) and registers them via `cmSystemTools::AddTranslationPath`. If the file cannot be opened, a specific error message is emitted and the system error is logged. This function keeps the translation table in sync with the cache entry.

@lcmake::UpdateProgress@k_ZN5cmake14Upda.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::UpdateProgress@k_ZN5cmake14Upda.body: The function verifies that a progress‑callback exists and that the system isn’t already in a “try‑compile” state; if both conditions are met, it forwards the supplied message and progress fraction to the callback.

@lcmake::WasLogLevelSetViaCLI@k_ZNK5cmak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::WasLogLevelSetViaCLI@k_ZNK5cmak.body: Returns the internal flag indicating whether the log level was configured via the command‑line interface.

@lcmake::WatchUnusedCli@k_ZN5cmake14Watc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::WatchUnusedCli@k_ZN5cmake14Watc.body: The function registers a watch for the supplied CLI variable name. It records the variable in the watch list and, if the variable hasn’t yet appeared in the “used” map, inserts an entry initialized to `false` so it can later be flagged as unused.

@lcmake::Workflow::CalculatedStep::Calcu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::Workflow::CalculatedStep::Calcu.body: Creates a `CalculatedStep` instance by storing the supplied step number, type identifier, name, and a callable action in its member fields.

@lcmake::Workflow@k_ZN5cmake8WorkflowERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::Workflow@k_ZN5cmake8WorkflowERK.body: The `Workflow` routine loads preset configurations from the current directory, validates that the requested preset exists and is enabled, then iteratively constructs a sequence of build/configure/test/package steps based on the preset’s type. Each step is wrapped in a `CalculatedStep` that holds a callable action; the action is invoked sequentially, printing progress and halting immediately on any non‑zero return code. If any step fails, the function propagates that error code. If all steps succeed, the function returns zero.

@lcmake::cmake::[lambda_0]@kcmake::cmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::cmake::[lambda_0]@kcmake::cmake.body: The lambda accepts an initializer‑list of `cm::string_view` objects, copies them into a vector `exts.ordered` (pre‑reserved for the list size), and then populates `exts.unordered` with the same sequence by inserting the whole vector range into the set.

@lcmake::cmake@k_ZN5cmakeC1ENS_4RoleEN7c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::cmake@k_ZN5cmakeC1ENS_4RoleEN7c.body: The constructor creates a fully‑configured “cmake” instance: it records the current working directory, allocates its caches and watchers, builds a snapshot of the current state, and registers default and extra generators. It sets up the lists of file extensions for source, header, CUDA, Fortran, HIP, and ISPC files, applies a stack‑size limit on Apple systems, loads any preset environment settings, and turns on console output for the build tools.

@lcmake::cmake@k_ZN5cmakeC1ERKS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::cmake@k_ZN5cmakeC1ERKS_.body: `cmake` is a constructor that takes a const reference to a `cmake` instance. It is marked `delete`, meaning the type cannot be copy‑constructed. The class provides no implicit copy constructor; attempting to copy a `cmake` object will trigger a compile‑time error.

@lcmake::operator=@k_ZN5cmakeaSERKS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::operator=@k_ZN5cmakeaSERKS_.body: The deleted overload of the assignment operator in `cmake` blocks any attempt to assign one instance to another—any code like `a = b;` will be rejected by the compiler.

@lcmake::~cmake@k_ZN5cmakeD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::~cmake@k_ZN5cmakeD1Ev.body: The destructor `cmake::~cmake()` is the default compiler‑generated implementation. It performs no custom logic; it simply lets the compiler handle the cleanup of any members.

@lcmakeCheckStampFile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmakeCheckStampFile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine reads the stamp‑dependency file for the given stamp name. If the file can’t be read or any listed dependency is newer than the stamp, it reports the stamp is stale and returns *false*. If all dependencies are older, it creates a temporary stamp file, atomically renames it over the original stamp, and returns *true* indicating the stamp is current and no rebuild is required.

@lcmakeCheckStampList@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmakeCheckStampList@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: Checks that a stamp‑list file exists and that each entry in it passes its individual stamp check—returning false (and reporting that CMake must rerun) if the file is missing or any stamp fails.

@lcmakemainGetMakefile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmakemainGetMakefile@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The routine first checks that the supplied `cmake` object and its debug‑output flag are non‑null; if so, it fetches the global generator via `GetGlobalGenerator()`, and returns that generator’s current makefile through `GetCurrentMakefile()`. If any of those prerequisites fail, it simply returns `nullptr`.

@lcmakemainGetStack@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmakemainGetStack@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function `cmakemainGetStack` takes a `cmake` object, obtains its associated `cmMakefile` via `cmakemainGetMakefile`. If a valid `cmMakefile` is returned, it calls `FormatListFileStack()` to get a string representation of the stack of files. If the resulting string is non‑empty, it prefixes the string with a newline and the literal “Called from: ” before returning it. If no `cmMakefile` is found, an empty string is returned.

@lcmakemainMessageCallback@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmakemainMessageCallback@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body:
The function logs a diagnostic message.  
It receives a message string, metadata describing the desired color, and a `cmake` context.  
On Windows it sends the text directly to `stderr`, prefixing it with the requested color code before flushing. On non‑Windows builds it writes the text to the standard error stream and appends a call‑stack trace from `cmakemainGetStack`.  
In either case the output is immediately flushed so it appears promptly in the console.

@lcmakemainProgressCallback@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmakemainProgressCallback@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The callback gathers the current build context and emits a single‑line status message only when the progress value is negative or when a directory name has been determined from the message prefix. It formats the output with a “-- ” prefix, the message, the directory (if any), and the current stack depth before writing it to `std::cout`.

@lcmcmd::ExecuteCMakeCommand@k_ZN5cmcmd1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::ExecuteCMakeCommand@k_ZN5cmcmd1.body: This routine interprets an array of command‑line tokens and dispatches to a large set of built‑in file‑system utilities. It handles operations such as copying, renaming, touching, creating directories, managing environment variables, running arbitrary shell commands, manipulating symbolic and hard links, invoking various hash checks, and packing/unpacking archives. The function consolidates all these actions into a single command interpreter, reporting errors and returning status codes for each sub‑operation.

@lcmcmd::ExecuteEchoColor@k_ZN5cmcmd16Ex.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::ExecuteEchoColor@k_ZN5cmcmd16Ex.body: The routine parses the argument list after the executable name, uses the `--switch=` flag to turn colour‑output on or off, and matches any of the recognised colour switches (`--black`, `--red`, …, `--white`, `--bold`) to set the current foreground colour. It also recognises `--no-newline`/`--newline` to control trailing newlines and a `--progress‑dir=` option that, if supplied together with a following `--progress‑num=` argument, triggers an intermediate progress report. Every argument that does not match a recognised flag is passed unchanged to `cmSystemTools::MakefileColorEcho`, which emits the string in the selected colour (or uncoloured if disabled). The function always returns 0.

@lcmcmd::ExecuteLinkScript@k_ZN5cmcmd17E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::ExecuteLinkScript@k_ZN5cmcmd17E.body:
The routine parses a “--verbose” switch from its argument list, opens the requested link‑script file, and then executes each non‑blank line in that file one by one.  
For every command it creates a temporary child process (with its stdout/stderr piped to the caller), runs the command, waits for completion, and propagates any non‑zero exit code or child‑level errors back as its own return value.  The function returns 0 on full success or a positive error code corresponding to the first failing command it encounters.

@lcmcmd::HandleCoCompileCommands@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::HandleCoCompileCommands@k_ZN5cm.body: The function parses a command‑line argument list, identifies any “--source=…”, “--launcher=…”, or compiler‑specific options (defined in the global `CoCompilers` list), collects the respective handlers, and then executes each handler in turn. After those handlers finish, if the `--` marker was found and a normal compiler command is still pending, it prefixes any requested launchers and invokes the real compiler with the remaining arguments, returning the compiler’s exit status. If no compiler commands are supplied or parsing fails, an error message is written and a non‑zero return code is produced.

@lcmcmd::HashSumFile@k_ZN5cmcmd11HashSum.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::HashSumFile@k_ZN5cmcmd11HashSum.body: The routine walks through the filenames supplied after the first two command‑line arguments, attempts to hash each one with the requested algorithm, emits an error message when a target cannot be processed (either a directory or a non‑existent file), and finally returns the number of such failures.

@lcmcmd::RunLLVMRC@k_ZN5cmcmd9RunLLVMRCE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::RunLLVMRC@k_ZN5cmcmd9RunLLVMRCE.body: The function parses its argument list into a preprocessing command and a compiler command, runs the preprocessor to produce an intermediate file, then runs the compiler on that file, handling any errors and finally cleaning up temporary files.

@lcmcmd::RunPreprocessor@k_ZN5cmcmd15Run.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::RunPreprocessor@k_ZN5cmcmd15Run.body: The `RunPreprocessor` function launches an external preprocessor by constructing a `cmUVProcessChainBuilder` pipeline. It opens the destination file, configures that file descriptor as the process’s output stream, attaches a built‑in error stream, and adds the supplied command sequence. After starting the process, it waits synchronously for completion, checks the exit code, prints any error stream to `std::cerr`, and returns `0` on success or `1` on any failure.

@lcmcmd::SymlinkExecutable@k_ZN5cmcmd17S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::SymlinkExecutable@k_ZN5cmcmd17S.body: The routine inspects two arguments—`realName` (the target path) and `name` (the link name)—and, only when they differ, attempts to create a symlink via `SymlinkInternal`. If that internal call reports failure, it logs an error string and returns `1`; otherwise it returns `0`.

@lcmcmd::SymlinkInternal@k_ZN5cmcmd15Sym.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::SymlinkInternal@k_ZN5cmcmd15Sym.body: Checks whether the target path already exists and removes it if so, then attempts to create a symlink pointing to the supplied source file. On Windows, if the user lacks the required privilege, it falls back to copying the file; otherwise it reports any creation error. The function returns the status code that indicates success or failure.

@lcmcmd::SymlinkLibrary@k_ZN5cmcmd14Syml.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::SymlinkLibrary@k_ZN5cmcmd14Syml.body: The `SymlinkLibrary` function takes a vector of string arguments, extracts three path names from positions 2–4, normalizes them to Unix‑style slashes, and attempts to create symbolic links: first, a link from the real library file to the target name if the names differ, and second, a link from that target name to the provided alias `name` when needed. It reports any failure via `cmSystemTools::Error` and returns 0 for success or 1 for failure.

@lcmcmd::VisualStudioLink@k_ZN5cmcmd16Vi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::VisualStudioLink@k_ZN5cmcmd16Vi.body: The routine re‑routes standard output to the system code page before invoking the Visual Studio linker. It first validates that at least two arguments are supplied, expands any “@”‑prefixed temporary‑file arguments by parsing the file contents, and then feeds the resulting list of command‑line tokens to a `cmVSLink` instance that parses and executes the link operation for the specified tool‑chain type.

@lcmcmd::WindowsCEEnvironment@k_ZN5cmcmd.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd::WindowsCEEnvironment@k_ZN5cmcmd.body: The function sets up and prints the environment variables (PATH, INCLUDE, LIB) for the requested version of the Windows CE compiler; if the requested compiler can be found it returns success (0), otherwise it signals failure with –1.

@lcmcmdProgressReport@k_ZL19cmcmdProgres.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmdProgressReport@k_ZL19cmcmdProgres.body: The routine reads the current count from `count.txt`, then walks through the comma‑separated list in *num*, creating a file inside the `Progress` subfolder for each token and writing “empty” into it. Finally, it prints the completion percentage based on how many of those files have been created versus the original count.

@lcmcmd_cmake_ninja_depends@k_Z25cmcmd_c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd_cmake_ninja_depends@k_Z25cmcmd_c.body: The routine parses a set of command‑line options (‑‑tdi, ‑‑‑src, etc.), validates that all required values are supplied, and then dispatches to a language‑specific helper (currently only Fortran is supported). It gathers the include paths from that helper, emits a dependency file listing the primary output followed by each include path, and finally writes a dep‑info file in the P1689 format. It returns 0 on success and a non‑zero error code when validation or file output fails.

@lcmcmd_cmake_ninja_depends_fortran@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd_cmake_ninja_depends_fortran@k_ZN.body: This routine reads a JSON descriptor that lists include directories, a module directory and compiler settings, then parses a Fortran source file. While parsing it records every module it provides, each module it requires, and any include directives it contains. It finally returns a structured object that lists those provided modules (with optional paths relative to the top‑build directory), the required modules, and the include files found during the scan.

@lcmcmd_cmake_ninja_dyndep@k_Z24cmcmd_cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmcmd_cmake_ninja_dyndep@k_Z24cmcmd_cm.body: The routine collects command‑line options (the “--” prefixed flags and .ddi files), reads a JSON configuration file supplied by the `--tdi` argument, extracts values such as build directories and module paths, initializes a `cmake` instance configured for a “Ninja” generator, and finally writes a dyn‑dependency (dyndep) file in the target build tree.

@lcmsys::CollapseFullPathImpl@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CollapseFullPathImpl@k_ZN5cmsys.body: The function normalises a file path by splitting its components, optionally prepending a base directory when the path is relative, then re‑joining the parts, normalising slashes and case (on Windows), and finally updating the translation table if required before returning the resulting path.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.body: Adds a new command‑line argument record to the internal registry by populating a callback structure with the argument name, type information, any variable pointer and help text, then stores it in the internal map and forces a refresh of the usage help.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.body: AddArgument registers a new command‑line argument in the parser’s internal registry. It records the argument’s name, help text, expected type, and any default value, ensuring that each argument is unique before being processed at runtime.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.body: The macro registers a named option by storing the provided string key together with a pointer that will receive the parsed value. It performs minimal validation and inserts the pair into the global argument table for use during later argument‑parsing.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.body: The macro registers a Boolean flag into the command‑line parser, wiring it to a `bool` variable that is automatically parsed from a supplied flag value.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.body: Adds a double‑valued argument named “DOUBLE” to the command‑line argument list, making it available for later parsing and lookup.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddArgume.body: The `AddArgument` function appends a string to the internal vector of command‑line arguments. It accepts a string‑like value and pushes it onto the end of the vector that holds all supplied arguments. The macro simply forwards that call to the underlying implementation.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.body: The macro expands to a member function that registers a command‑line flag whose presence turns a stored Boolean value to true. The function takes a flag name and a description string, registers the flag with the parser, and returns the current value (true/false) of that flag after parsing.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.body: The macro registers a flag key with the command‑line parser, storing the supplied string in a static buffer and wiring the flag’s value pointer so that when the flag appears on the command line its value is automatically set to true/false.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.body: Adds a Boolean flag to the command‑line parser: when the flag appears on the command line it sets the associated variable to true; if absent, the variable remains false.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.body: Adds a named boolean flag to the command‑line argument table, binding the flag to a `bool` variable that will be set to `true` when the flag is present and `false` otherwise. It registers the flag’s short help text, default, and expected usage so the argument‑parser can validate and populate the variable during parsing.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddBoolea.body: AddBooleanArgument registers a boolean flag by expanding the macro CommandLineArgumentsAddBooleanArgumentMacro(INT, int), yielding a function that takes the flag’s integer identifier and a default integer value, storing that flag as a true/false argument for the command‑line parser.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddCallba.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::AddCallba.body: It registers a new argument handler by building a callback record from the supplied parameters and inserting that record into the internal map keyed on the argument string. After the record is stored, it refreshes the help text by regenerating the help list.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::CommandLi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::CommandLi.body: The constructor creates a fresh internal data structure, then assigns default values: an empty help string, a line‑length limit of 80 characters, and disables the flag that would otherwise preserve unused arguments.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::DeleteRem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::DeleteRem.body: The routine walks the supplied argument array and frees each element before freeing the array itself. It uses `delete[]` (not `delete`) for each element and finally deletes the array pointer, assuming each element was allocated with `new[]`.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GenerateH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GenerateH.body: The routine scans the registered callbacks, groups any duplicate argument names together, determines the longest token length for column alignment, and then appends each option and its description to an internal string buffer. It wraps long descriptions to the preset line length and emits a neatly‑formatted help text.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetArgv0@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetArgv0@.body: Retrieves the stored argument string from the internal container and exposes it as a C‑style string (`const char*`). This accessor simply returns the raw pointer to the underlying `std::string` data; callers obtain a read‑only view of the value that was stored in `Internals->Argv0`.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetHelp@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetHelp@k.body: GetHelp walks a mapping of callbacks to resolve an argument to its ultimate help text. It returns the help string of the final callback in the chain, or null if the argument has no entry. It follows any internal help redirects until no further mapping is found.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetLastAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetLastAr.body: The method returns the next ordinal after the internal marker of the last argument—essentially the count of arguments, cast to `unsigned int`.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetMatche.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetMatche.body: The method clears the supplied vector, scans the internal callback map, and adds each key string to the vector whenever the supplied argument string matches the key exactly or starts with it. It returns `true` if at least one match was found; otherwise `false`.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetRemain.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetRemain.body: The function builds a new array of C‑style strings that contains the arguments starting with the stored `Argv0` and then every argument beyond the internally tracked `LastArgument`. It allocates space for each string, copies them with `strcpy`, and finally assigns the resulting count to `*argc` and the array pointer to `*argv`.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetUnused.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::GetUnused.body: The routine gathers the stored “unused” command‑line tokens that were skipped during parsing. It allocates an array big enough for the first stored token and every element in the `UnusedArguments` list, copies each string into a newly‑allocated `char*` buffer, and finally returns the count (`argc`) and pointer array (`argv`).

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::Initializ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::Initializ.body: The `Initialize` member constructs the command‑line parsing infrastructure: it stores the executable’s own name in `Internals->Argv0`, then iterates over every supplied argument (from index 1 to `argc‑1` inclusive) and feeds each into `ProcessArgument`. The call to `this->Initialize()` likely wires up internal state (possibly resetting flags, counters, or allocating buffers). All arguments are processed in order, ensuring that the internal state reflects the complete argument list once the loop completes.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::Initializ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::Initializ.body: The function forwards the raw argument array to an overload that expects a `const char* const*`. In effect, it casts the `argv` array to a pointer‑to‑const‑char pointer and invokes the other `Initialize` that takes that type. The cast is syntactically correct, but it is an unusual form; a more conventional approach would simply pass the array without an explicit cast, or use `const char* const*` directly.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::Initializ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::Initializ.body: Resets the internal argument vector to an empty state and zero‑indexes the last argument counter.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::Parse@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::Parse@k_Z.body: The `Parse` routine walks through the stored argument vector, matches each token against the registered argument descriptors via `GetMatchedArguments`, then dispatches the match to the proper handler: if the argument expects no value it simply records it; if a space‑separated value follows, or a value attached with `=`, it grabs the succeeding token or the part after the `=`; for multi‑argument syntax it consumes all following tokens until a new argument begins. Successful matches invoke the registered callback to populate the associated variable. Unknown tokens are either reported as errors or, if enabled, collected into the unused‑arguments buffer. The method returns a success flag when all arguments are processed.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.body: The `PopulateVariable` method receives a callback structure and a string value. It runs the registered callback; on failure it rolls back the argument count and returns `false`. If successful, it logs the assignment then uses a type‑switch to convert the string into the correct native type (int, double, string, bool, or vectors thereof), assigning the result via the corresponding overload. If the type is unrecognized it prints an error, decrements the counter, and returns `false`. Otherwise the method returns `true` after storing the value.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.body: Assigns `value` to the string pointed to by `variable`; the function dereferences the pointer and copies the argument into the referenced string.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.body: The function frees any previously allocated storage, allocates a new buffer sized to the supplied string plus a null terminator, and copies the string into that buffer. It assumes the caller has already allocated the double pointer and that the string argument is valid.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.body: Sets the Boolean pointer to true when the supplied string matches any of the common truth tokens (“1”, “ON”, “on”, “On”, “TRUE”, “true”, “True”, “yes”, “Yes”, “YES”). Otherwise it assigns false.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.body: The function reads a string argument, converts that string to a double using `strtod`, and writes the result back to the supplied `variable`. It does no validation of the conversion result and leaves the returned pointer (`res`) unused. The code relies on a non‑standard function (`strtod`) and uses `value.c_str()` instead of the usual `c_str()` or `c_str` method; both can cause compile‑time or runtime issues. It also ignores the commented‑out error handling that would have inspected `res` before dereferencing it.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::PopulateV.body: Accepts a pointer to a string vector and a string; it appends the string to the vector and leaves the vector modified.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::ProcessAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::ProcessAr.body: Appends the supplied argument string to the internal argument vector (`Internals->Argv`), effectively recording it for later use.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::SetClient.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::SetClient.body: The `SetClientData` member simply assigns the supplied pointer to the internal `ClientData` member of the `Internals` structure. No additional validation, copying, or reference‑counting logic is performed; the raw pointer is stored as‑is.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::SetLineLe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::SetLineLe.body: Checks that the supplied length falls between 9 and 1000, stores it in LineLength, and then triggers help‑text generation.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::SetUnknow.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::SetUnknow.body: Assigns the supplied callback to Internals‑>UnknownArgumentCallback.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::~CommandL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArguments::~CommandL.body: The destructor releases any memory owned by the `Internals` member, preventing leaks.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsCallbackStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsCallbackStr.body: CommandLineArgumentsCallbackStructure is a move constructor that accepts an rvalue reference to an unnamed instance of its own type and moves the internal state into the newly created instance.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsCallbackStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsCallbackStr.body: The function clones a supplied callback‑structure into a new instance and then returns that instance so it can be used wherever a fresh command‑line arguments handler is required.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsCallbackStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsCallbackStr.body: The `CommandLineArgumentsCallbackStructure` struct bundles the functions and state used when a command‑line parsing routine processes an argument. It holds the function pointers that are invoked for validation and handling, plus any context data that must be carried through the callback chain. This structure is passed around by the parsing code to keep the argument‑processing logic modular and easily testable.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsInternal::C.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsInternal::C.body: This constructor creates a new `CommandLineArgumentsInternal` instance by taking ownership of all arguments from an existing instance (passed as an rvalue reference). It essentially performs a move‑style transfer, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state while the new object inherits the original arguments.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsInternal::C.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsInternal::C.body: The constructor simply creates a new `CommandLineArgumentsInternal` instance by copying all of its internal state from the given source object. It duplicates the list of arguments and any metadata so that the new instance behaves exactly like the source.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsInternal::C.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsInternal::C.body: Creates a default‐initialised internal argument container that is stored in the object’s internal state. This helper is invoked to populate the internal arguments structure when a CommandLineArguments instance is constructed.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsInternal::~.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsInternal::~.body: The function parses raw command‑line tokens, normalises them (e.g., handles quoted strings and escapes), maps each token to a defined option or flag, and populates the resulting argument object that downstream components consume. It also validates mandatory arguments and reports parsing errors via the framework’s error‑handling path.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsMapOfStrucs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsMapOfStrucs.body: Moves an existing map of command‑line arguments into a new instance by taking an rvalue reference to the source. It avoids expensive copying and is used throughout the code to initialise fresh map objects from existing ones.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsMapOfStrucs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsMapOfStrucs.body: The constructor copies an existing `CommandLineArgumentsMapOfStrucs` instance—duplicating its internal string‑to‑struct map so the new object starts out‑of‑the‑box with the same argument data.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsVectorOfStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsVectorOfStr.body: The constructor efficiently transfers an existing vector of strings into the new instance, delegating the move to the base `std::vector<std::string>` constructor so that the internal storage is simply re‑used rather than rebuilt.

@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsVectorOfStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::CommandLineArgumentsVectorOfStr.body: Creates a new instance of the vector‑like class by taking an existing `CommandLineArgumentsVectorOfStrings` object and copying its string elements into the new instance.

@lcmsys::Directory::Clear@k_ZN5cmsys9Dir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::Clear@k_ZN5cmsys9Dir.body: The function empties the internal path string and drops all entries from the file list, resetting the directory’s state to an empty directory.

@lcmsys::Directory::Directory@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::Directory@k_ZN5cmsys.body: Moves the internal pointer from the source object into the new instance, then clears the source’s pointer so its resources are released safely.

@lcmsys::Directory::Directory@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::Directory@k_ZN5cmsys.body: The declaration makes the copy constructor of `Directory` unavailable by marking it `= delete;`. It forces any use of a `Directory` instance to employ move semantics or direct construction and prevents accidental shallow copies that could leave shared resources in an inconsistent state.

@lcmsys::Directory::Directory@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::Directory@k_ZN5cmsys.body:
The constructor simply allocates a new instance of `DirectoryInternals` and assigns the returned pointer to the member `Internal`.  
If you rely on raw pointers, remember to release the memory in the destructor or switch to a smart‑pointer (e.g., `std::unique_ptr<DirectoryInternals>`) to avoid leaks.

@lcmsys::Directory::FileIsDirectory@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::FileIsDirectory@k_ZN.body: The routine checks a stored file entry at position `i`. On a build that defines `_WIN32` but not `__CYGWIN__`, it inspects that entry’s attribute flags to decide if the record represents a directory; otherwise it queries the OS via `kwsys::SystemTools::FileIsDirectory` on the file path.

@lcmsys::Directory::FileIsSymlink@k_ZNK5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::FileIsSymlink@k_ZNK5.body: The function retrieves the file’s path from the directory entry at index *i* and then uses the platform‑specific `kwsys::SystemTools::FileIsSymlink` helper to test whether the file’s attributes indicate a symbolic link. On Windows it queries the stored file attributes via `FindData.dwFileAttributes`; on other platforms it simply passes the path to the general helper.

@lcmsys::Directory::GetFile@k_ZNK5cmsys9.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::GetFile@k_ZNK5cmsys9.body: The function returns a pointer to the C‑string of the file name at the given index. It performs no bounds checking—if the index is out of range or if the container is destroyed, the returned pointer may dangle. The const qualifier guarantees that the object itself is not modified, but callers must still ensure that the returned pointer is not used beyond the lifetime of the underlying string.

@lcmsys::Directory::GetFileName@k_ZNK5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::GetFileName@k_ZNK5cm.body: Returns a const reference to the file name string stored in `Internal->Files` at index `i`.

@lcmsys::Directory::GetFilePath@k_ZNK5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::GetFilePath@k_ZNK5cm.body: The `GetFilePath` method returns the absolute path of the file at position `i` in the internal file list. It starts with the base directory stored in `this->Internal->Path`, appends a trailing slash if one is missing, then appends the file’s name at `Files[i]`. The resulting string is returned as the full path string.

@lcmsys::Directory::GetNumberOfFiles@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::GetNumberOfFiles@k_Z.body: Returns the number of files stored in the `Files` collection, cast to an unsigned long. It accesses the internal `Files` member through `this->Internal` and casts the result of `size()` to the desired return type. This simple accessor relies on the internal pointer being valid and the `size()` value fitting in an unsigned long without overflow.

@lcmsys::Directory::GetNumberOfFilesInDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::GetNumberOfFilesInDi.body: The function opens a directory named by the supplied string, iterates through every entry returned by `readdir`, increments a counter for each file encountered, and finally returns that counter. If opening fails it writes the system error into the optional `errorMessage` buffer and returns zero. It resets `errno` to zero before the call to `readdir` and checks for subsequent errors after the loop. It uses the C‑style `DIR*` and `readdir` loop instead of the C++ directory iterators. The implementation returns a `bool`‑type value (`false`) in an otherwise `unsigned long` return‑type context, which is a type‑inconsistency bug. It also fails to close the directory in the error branch, potentially leaking the file descriptor if `errorMessage` is non‑null. The implementation ignores the usual `<dirent.h>` safety checks and does not handle memory‑leak in case of `readdir` returning null before the loop terminates.

@lcmsys::Directory::GetPath@k_ZNK5cmsys9.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::GetPath@k_ZNK5cmsys9.body: It returns a pointer to the internal string’s underlying C‑style buffer—no copy is made, so the caller must keep the Directory instance alive while using the returned pointer.

@lcmsys::Directory::Load@k_ZN5cmsys9Dire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::Load@k_ZN5cmsys9Dire.body: The function clears its current data, attempts to open the named directory, and on success enumerates each entry until the end of the stream, pushing each file name into an internal container. If opening fails or an iteration error occurs, it records the corresponding error string in the supplied message buffer and returns a failure status; otherwise it records the path and returns success.

@lcmsys::Directory::operator==@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::operator==@k_ZN5cmsy.body: The deleted operator== prevents any implicit or accidental equality comparison of Directory objects, forcing callers to use a custom comparison function instead.

@lcmsys::Directory::operator=@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::operator=@k_ZN5cmsys.body: This move‑assignment operator takes an rvalue reference, swaps the internal data of the current object with that of the source, and returns a reference to the updated object (`*this`). It effectively implements a move assignment that preserves exception safety by using `std::swap`.

@lcmsys::Directory::operator=@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::operator=@k_ZN5cmsys.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents copying or reassigning a Directory instance, ensuring the object cannot be altered through assignment.

@lcmsys::Directory::~Directory@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::~Directory@k_ZN5cmsy.body: The destructor releases the internal resource by calling `delete` on the `Internal` pointer. It assumes that the pointer is valid and that no other part of the program will later use it; no null‑check or ownership‑verification is performed. If another object still holds that pointer or the pointer is already freed elsewhere, a double‑delete or use‑after‑free would ensue. The `delete` itself is noexcept, so the destructor will not throw, but any exception safety must be handled by the surrounding code. Using a smart pointer (e.g., `std::unique_ptr`) is recommended to avoid such pitfalls.

@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::DirectoryIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::DirectoryIn.body: The function initializes and returns an instance of the `DirectoryInternals` class. It takes an optional parameter (here passed as an unnamed argument) that allows caller code to influence the construction details. Once called, it constructs the internal directory representation, sets up its state, and hands the fully‑initialized object back to the caller.

@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::DirectoryIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::DirectoryIn.body: The function is a copy‑constructor that creates a new `DirectoryInternals` object from an existing one. It copies the internal data structures (e.g., directory tables, metadata) into the new instance and re‑establishes any internal invariants required for correct operation.

@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::DirectoryIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::DirectoryIn.body: The `DirectoryInternals` constructor initializes the internal data‑storage structure for a `Directory` instance, allocating a fresh `DirectoryInternals` object and linking it to the owning `Directory` via its `Internal` member.

@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::FileData::F.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::FileData::F.body:
The `FileData` constructor stores the supplied file name in a member called `Name`.  
When compiled on a 32‑bit Windows target it also stores the supplied `WIN32_FIND_DATAW` structure in a member called `FindData`; otherwise that member is omitted.  
Both members are initialized via move semantics (`std::move`) to avoid copies.

@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::~DirectoryI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DirectoryInternals::~DirectoryI.body: This public helper aggregates and returns the internal representation of a directory: it collects the name, size, permissions, timestamps, and child entries from the underlying storage layer, packaging them into a lightweight DTO that callers can use to introspect or serialize the directory contents without exposing internal state.

@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::CloseLibrary@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::CloseLibrary@k_Z.body: The `CloseLibrary` function closes a dynamically loaded module by calling `NSUnLinkModule` with the `NSUNLINKMODULE_OPTION_NONE` flag. It returns a boolean indicating whether the un‑link succeeded, but the return type is declared as `int`. The function does not free the module’s mapped memory, because the `NSUNLINKMODULE_OPTION_KEEP_MEMORY_MAPPED` flag is omitted.

@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::GetSymbolAddress.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::GetSymbolAddress.body: The routine looks up a symbol in the specified library, optionally prepending an underscore on Apple‑GCC builds, obtains its address via `NSAddressOfSymbol`, and returns that address cast to the `SymbolPointer` type (i.e. a function‑pointer).

@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::LastError@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::LastError@k_ZN5c.body: The `LastError` method simply returns a null pointer (`0`) to indicate that no error message is available.

@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::LibExtension@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::LibExtension@k_Z.body: The `LibExtension` function is a public static helper that simply returns the string literal “`.so`”. It’s typically used wherever a codebase needs to supply the appropriate file‑extension value when assembling a library file name (e.g., `myLib` + LibExtension() = `myLib.so`).

@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::LibPrefix@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
