@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::LibPrefix@k_ZN5c.body: It simply returns a `const char*` pointing to the string literal `"lib"`.

@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::OpenLibrary@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::OpenLibrary@k_ZN.body: The function is a public static member that opens a dynamic library by name, delegating the work to an overload that supplies a default flag value of 0. It returns the resulting `LibraryHandle` instance that callers can use to interact with the loaded library.

@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::OpenLibrary@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::DynamicLoader::OpenLibrary@k_ZN.body: The function verifies that no special flags are set, creates an object‑file image for the requested library, and if that succeeds it links the module with immediate binding and returns the handle (or null if creation fails).

@lcmsys::Encoding::CommandLineArguments:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Encoding::CommandLineArguments:.body:
The `Main` function turns the raw command‑line buffer supplied to a program into a normal `CommandLineArguments` object.  
On Windows it first obtains the wide‑character representation of the whole command line with `CommandLineToArgvW`, then copies each wide argument into a narrow‑character `std::string` stored in a `std::vector`, frees the temporary buffer, and finally constructs a `CommandLineArguments` instance from that vector.  
On non‑Windows builds it simply forwards the original `argc`/`argv` pair to the constructor.

@lcmsys::Encoding::CommandLineArguments:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Encoding::CommandLineArguments:.body: The function returns the number of command‑line arguments supplied to the program, excluding the program name itself. It does this by casting the size of the internal `argv_` vector to `int` and subtracting one, and it guarantees that callers cannot modify its state because it is marked `const`.

@lcmsys::Encoding::CommandLineArguments:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Encoding::CommandLineArguments:.body: The `argv()` member simply returns a pointer to the first element of the internal `argv_` array that holds the command‑line arguments.

@lcmsys::Encoding::CommandLineArguments:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Encoding::CommandLineArguments:.body: The destructor iterates through the internal `argv_` container, calling `free` on each stored C‑string pointer. It assumes every entry in the vector was allocated with `malloc`/`calloc` and that no element is `nullptr`. After freeing all entries the vector’s own memory is released automatically. This routine is responsible for cleaning up the raw string buffers supplied to the `CommandLineArguments` instance.

@lcmsys::FStream::ReadBOM@k_ZN5cmsys7FSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::FStream::ReadBOM@k_ZN5cmsys7FSt.body: Detects up to four leading bytes in the stream and compares them against the canonical BOM byte‑sequences for UTF‑8, UTF‑16 (big‑/little‑endian) and UTF‑32 (big‑/little‑endian). If a match is found it returns the corresponding enum; otherwise it restores the stream’s read position and reports that no BOM is present.

@lcmsys::FileInDir@k_ZN5cmsysL9FileInDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::FileInDir@k_ZN5cmsysL9FileInDir.body: Creates a new path by normalising `dir` to Unix‑style slashes and appending the file‑name extracted from `source`. The function returns this concatenated string.

@lcmsys::Glob::FindFiles@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::FindFiles@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob.body: It parses a path string, normalises it into an absolute path (handling relative paths, Windows drive letters, and UNC‑style network shares), tokenises the path into components separated by '/', collects those components into an internal list of expressions, and then walks the resulting path hierarchy, calling a directory‑processing routine on each level until the whole path is resolved.

@lcmsys::Glob::GetFollowedSymlinkCount@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::GetFollowedSymlinkCount@k.body: Returns the current value of the internal `FollowedSymlinkCount` field.

@lcmsys::Glob::GetListDirs@k_ZNK5cmsys4G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::GetListDirs@k_ZNK5cmsys4G.body: The `GetListDirs` member simply returns the current value of the private flag `ListDirs`. It is a const function, so it does not modify any state and merely reports whether the directory list is active.

@lcmsys::Glob::GetRecurseListDirs@k_ZNK5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::GetRecurseListDirs@k_ZNK5.body: The method simply returns the current value of the private member flag that controls whether recursive directory enumeration is enabled.

@lcmsys::Glob::GetRecurseThroughSymlinks.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::GetRecurseThroughSymlinks.body: It returns the current value of the `RecurseThroughSymlinks` flag—i.e., whether the logic should follow symlinks recursively or stop at the first link.

@lcmsys::Glob::GetRelative@k_ZN5cmsys4Gl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::GetRelative@k_ZN5cmsys4Gl.body: This function returns a pointer to the internal C‑style string stored in `Relative`. If the string is empty, it returns `nullptr`; otherwise it returns the address of the underlying character array via `c_str()`.

@lcmsys::Glob::Glob@k_ZN5cmsys4GlobC1Ev@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::Glob@k_ZN5cmsys4GlobC1Ev@.body: The constructor simply wires up the object’s internal state: it allocates a new `GlobInternals` instance, clears the relative‑path string, and sets a handful of flags that govern how searches recurse. The flags include `Recurse` (whether recursive traversal is enabled), `RecurseThroughSymlinks` (defaulting to true for backward‑compatibility), `RecurseListDirs` (controls whether directories are listed recursively), and `FollowedSymlinkCount` (tracks symlink depth). The `ListDirs` flag indicates whether directory entries should be enumerated at all. The constructor does no heavy work beyond these field initialisations.

@lcmsys::Glob::PatternToRegex@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::PatternToRegex@k_ZN5cmsys.body: Converts a Unix‑style glob expression into a POSIX regular‑expression: it expands `*` and `?` into non‑slash matches, parses bracket expressions (including negation), escapes metacharacters, and optionally anchors the pattern to the full input while optionally enforcing case‑insensitivity.

@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseOff@k_ZN5cmsys4Glo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseOff@k_ZN5cmsys4Glo.body: Disables recursion on the current instance by invoking the internal `SetRecurse(false)` method.

@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseOn@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseOn@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob.body: This method turns on the internal recursion flag by invoking `SetRecurse(true)`.

@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseThroughSymlinksOff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseThroughSymlinksOff.body: Disables recursive traversal of symbolic links by setting the internal flag to false, so subsequent path resolution stops at the first symlink rather than following its target.

@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseThroughSymlinksOn@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseThroughSymlinksOn@.body: Enables symlink recursion by invoking `SetRecurseThroughSymlinks(true)` to turn on the internal flag.

@lcmsys::Glob::SetListDirs@k_ZN5cmsys4Gl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::SetListDirs@k_ZN5cmsys4Gl.body: Sets the internal `ListDirs` flag to the supplied boolean value.

@lcmsys::Glob::SetRecurse@k_ZN5cmsys4Glo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::SetRecurse@k_ZN5cmsys4Glo.body: This method assigns the value of its boolean argument to the class’s internal `Recurse` flag, effectively enabling or disabling recursion for the object.

@lcmsys::Glob::SetRecurseListDirs@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::SetRecurseListDirs@k_ZN5c.body: Updates the internal flag that determines whether directory listings recurse into subdirectories. When the flag is set to true, subsequent listings include nested directories; when false, only top‑level directories are returned.

@lcmsys::Glob::SetRecurseThroughSymlinks.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::SetRecurseThroughSymlinks.body: Sets the member flag that controls whether directory traversal recurses through symbolic links to the supplied boolean value.

@lcmsys::Glob::SetRelative@k_ZN5cmsys4Gl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::SetRelative@k_ZN5cmsys4Gl.body: This function updates the `Relative` member: if the supplied pointer is `nullptr`, it resets `Relative` to an empty string; otherwise it stores the provided string in `Relative`.

@lcmsys::Glob::~Glob@k_ZN5cmsys4GlobD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::~Glob@k_ZN5cmsys4GlobD1Ev.body: The destructor simply frees the internal data owned by the object. It assumes that the `Internals` member was allocated earlier and that no other object still holds a dangling reference to that heap block. It will delete that memory, so callers must ensure the object’s lifetime ends before any such references are used again.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::RegExpCompile@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::RegExpCompile@k_.body: The `RegExpCompile` public function is the entry point for turning a regular‑expression source into a usable compiled form. It accepts the raw specification (typically a pattern string, possibly with flags), processes the pattern into an internal representation, and produces a `RegExpCompile` instance that can be used for matching. The function encapsulates the parsing, tokenization, and optimization steps required to transform a textual pattern into the runtime structures that drive pattern matching.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::RegExpCompile@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::RegExpCompile@k_.body: The function parses a pattern string into an internal representation, initializing the matcher’s internal nodes and queues so a compiled regular expression can be used for matching.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::RegExpCompile@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::RegExpCompile@k_.body: RegExpCompile parses a regex pattern string into an internal parse tree, resolving anchors, escapes, groups and quantifiers while tracking syntax errors and flag state. It builds a compact representation that other modules use for matching and optimisation, handling edge cases such as nested alternations or empty‑match patterns.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::reg@k_ZN5cmsys13.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::reg@k_ZN5cmsys13.body: The function parses a regular‑expression string (via the global `regparse` pointer) and builds a tree of nodes representing that expression. It handles parentheses by creating an OPEN/​CLOSE pair, processes branches separated by ‘|’, and sets flags for width and start conditions. On failure (e.g. malformed parentheses or missing terminators) it reports an error and returns `nullptr`; otherwise it returns a pointer to the root node of the constructed tree.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regatom@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regatom@k_ZN5cms.body: The function reads the next character from a regex pattern, determines whether it represents a literal, special metacharacter (like `^`, `$`, or `.`), a character class or a grouped sub‑expression, and constructs the corresponding syntax‑tree node. It updates the supplied flag word to indicate properties such as “has width” or “simple” and returns a pointer to the newly created node, or `nullptr` if a malformed construct is detected.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regbranch@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regbranch@k_ZN5c.body: The function parses a branch of a regular‑expression pattern. It creates a node for the branch (regnode(BRANCH)), walks the input stream until it hits the end of the branch (a ‘|’, a closing parenthesis, or end‑of‑string), and for each sub‑piece it calls `regpiece` to build the sub‑node. Flags returned from each sub‑node are accumulated in `*flagp`. The pieces are linked together with `regtail`. If no sub‑pieces are found, a “nothing” node is created. The function finally returns the node that represents the whole branch.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regc@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regc@k_ZN5cmsys1.body: When invoked, `regc` copies the supplied byte `b` into the array pointed to by `regcode` if that array is active; if the code buffer is in the dummy state, it simply bumps `regsize` instead of writing.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::reginsert@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::reginsert@k_ZN5c.body: The routine copies the current buffer contents after the desired insertion point, places the new operator byte at that position, and then updates the internal buffer pointers and terminators to maintain proper termination.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regnode@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regnode@k_ZN5cms.body:
The function appends a new instruction node into the compiled‐code buffer.  
It first checks whether the buffer pointer (`regcode`) is still at the dummy sentinel; if so, it simply bumps the buffer size counter (`regsize`) by three bytes to make room for the new node and returns that sentinel pointer.  
Otherwise, it writes the operation byte (`op`) at the current `regcode` position, then writes a zero byte to represent a null “next” link and a second zero byte as padding, advances the `regcode` pointer past these three bytes, and finally returns the original start pointer of the newly written node.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regoptail@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regoptail@k_ZN5c.body: When called with a valid non‑dummy pointer whose opcode is BRANCH, the method forwards the operand and value to `regtail`. If the pointer is null, a dummy pointer, or the opcode is not BRANCH, it exits immediately.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regpiece@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regpiece@k_ZN5cm.body: regpiece parses the next chunk of a regular‑expression pattern after an atom has been read by regatom. It inspects the following operator, sets the flag bits that describe the produced node (e.g. whether a loop or a branch will be present), and builds the transition graph for the quantifier (*, +, ? and ordinary repetition). If the operator is a repetition operator and the atom was non‑empty, it attaches the appropriate node types (STAR, PLUS, BRANCH, etc.), wiring the main path and back‑branching for loops or optional branches. If the operator would produce an empty operand it emits an error and returns null. The function advances the parse pointer and returns a pointer to the created node.

@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regtail@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpCompile::regtail@k_ZN5cms.body: The routine scans a linked‑list of regex nodes to reach the last node. Once found, it computes the distance between that node and the supplied `val` pointer. Depending on the node’s opcode it writes this distance as a 16‑bit value immediately after the node’s opcode byte. This effectively tags the node with a “tail” pointer that later resolves back‑references.

@lcmsys::RegExpFind::RegExpFind@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpFind::RegExpFind@k_ZN5cms.body: The `RegExpFind` function performs pattern matching against a string, returning a `bool` to indicate whether the supplied regex succeeds. It accepts a pattern string and an input string, and optionally a `const char*` flag that toggles case‑sensitivity. Internally it uses the standard POSIX‑compatible regex engine to compile the pattern on‑the‑fly, then performs a single scan over the target string; on a match it sets an internal match flag and records the start and end positions of the match. If the pattern is invalid or no match is found, it returns `false` and leaves the match position fields unset. The routine is exposed publicly so higher‑level modules can use it to test for the presence of a token or delimiter without pulling in the full regex parsing logic.

@lcmsys::RegExpFind::RegExpFind@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpFind::RegExpFind@k_ZN5cms.body: `RegExpFind` is a constructor that creates a new instance by copying the state of an existing `RegExpFind` object. The constructor takes a reference to an unnamed source object and copies its internal search configuration—such as pattern lists, matching flags, and any pre‑computed state—so that the new instance behaves identically to the original. The function does not perform any additional logic beyond this shallow copy; it simply assigns internal members from the source to the new object.

@lcmsys::RegExpFind::RegExpFind@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpFind::RegExpFind@k_ZN5cms.body: RegExpFind returns the index of the first match of a specified regular expression pattern in a given string (or –1 if no match is found).

@lcmsys::RegExpFind::regmatch@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpFind::regmatch@k_ZN5cmsys.body: The method scans a pre‑compiled regular‑expression program against a given input string. It walks the program node by node, handling anchors (BOL/EOL), literal matches, wildcards, and branching for alternation. When a full match reaches the END token it returns 1; otherwise it returns 0.

@lcmsys::RegExpFind::regrepeat@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpFind::regrepeat@k_ZN5cmsy.body: The function consumes a pattern token `p`, examines the current input buffer (`reginput`), and walks through that buffer until the pattern stops matching. It keeps a running tally (`count`) of how many characters were consumed. Depending on the operand type (`OP(p)`), it either counts all characters (`ANY`), matches a fixed string exactly (`EXACTLY`), matches any of a set of characters (`ANYOF`), or matches any but a set (`ANYBUT`). In each case it advances the input pointer (`scan`) accordingly and finally returns the number of characters that matched. The global `reginput` is updated to the new position after the match.

@lcmsys::RegExpFind::regtry@k_ZN5cmsys10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegExpFind::regtry@k_ZN5cmsys10.body: The `regtry` function attempts to match a substring against a regular‑expression pattern. It initializes internal pointers (`reginput`, `regstartp`, `regendp`), clears the buffer for sub‑expression tracking, and then calls `regmatch` with the pattern offset by one. If `regmatch` succeeds, it records the start and end positions of the match in the provided `start`/`end` pointers and returns success (1); otherwise it returns failure (0).

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.body: Constructs a `RegularExpression` from a C‑style string, initializing its internal state and invoking `compile` to parse the pattern when the argument is non‑null.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.body: The constructor initializes the new object’s internal data members with default values and then invokes the `compile` routine on the supplied pattern string.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.body: The copy constructor duplicates a `RegularExpression` instance by allocating a fresh buffer sized `rxp.progsize`, copying the existing program bytes into it, and then re‑pointing any internal pointers (`regmust`, `regstart`, `reganch`, `regmlen`) so that they reference the new buffer rather than the old one. It also propagates the current match state (`regmatch`) and the last match index (`regstart`) from the source object.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.body: The constructor sets all member fields to their default empty or zero states, ensuring the new object starts with no compiled regex data and zero parameter count.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::compile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::compile@k_ZN.body: The `compile` function validates the supplied expression, performs a two‑pass parse to compute the compiled size, allocates the program buffer, emits the compiled bytecode, and then analyzes the resulting bytecode to fill in optimisation hints (`regstart`, `reganch`, `regmust`, `regmlen`). If any stage fails it returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true` and the object is ready for matching.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::compile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::compile@k_ZN.body: The `compile` function is a thin wrapper that accepts a `std::string` and forwards its C‑string representation to the underlying compile routine, returning the boolean result of that call.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::deep_equal@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::deep_equal@k.body: The method performs a thorough comparison of two regular‑expression objects: it first checks that both have the same size, then iterates through the internal program array comparing every element, and finally verifies that the iterator ranges (`start`/`end`) are identical in both objects. If any of these checks fails, it returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::end@k_ZNK5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::end@k_ZNK5cm.body: Returns the ending offset of a matched substring by delegating to the underlying `regmatch` object’s `end` method, taking an integer argument and returning the result as a `std::string::size_type`.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZN5cm.body: The wrapper forwards the call to the internal find routine, passing the string pointer, match context, offset, and options, and returns the result of that invocation.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZN5cm.body: The `find` function performs a quick string search on the current regular‑expression object. It takes a `std::string` reference and an offset and forwards the search request to the underlying `find` implementation that expects a raw C‑string. The function returns `true` when a match is found at or after the given offset (according to the options supplied); otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZNK5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZNK5c.body:
The function walks through an input string trying to match it against a previously‑compiled regular‑expression program. It first clears and records the search string. If no program exists, it fails. It verifies that the program’s header byte matches the expected magic value; if that check fails, it prints an error and returns false. If the expression contains a “must‑appear” substring (`regmust`), the routine scans the input for that literal sequence; absence of the sequence also aborts with false.

If the expression is anchored at the beginning (`reganch`), the engine runs a single “try” once. Otherwise, the routine either exploits a known starting character (`regstart`) by jumping to each occurrence of that character in the input and attempting a match from there, or, if no such hint is available, scans every character sequentially. On any successful try, it returns true; otherwise, after exhausting all positions, it returns false.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZNK5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZNK5c.body:
The `find` function scans a C‑style string for a match against a pre‑compiled regular expression.  
When called, it attempts to locate the first substring that satisfies the pattern; if one is found it fills the supplied `RegularExpressionMatch` instance with the match’s start position, length, and any captured groups. It returns `true` when a match is successfully located, otherwise `false`.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::is_valid@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::is_valid@k_Z.body: The function simply checks whether the `program` member of the `RegularExpression` object is non‑null, returning `true` if it exists (meaning the expression is considered valid) and `false` otherwise.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::match@k_ZNK5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::match@k_ZNK5.body: The `match` member merely forwards the supplied integer to the `regmatch` member’s `match` routine and returns whatever string that routine yields.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::num_groups@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::num_groups@k.body: It returns the total number of capturing groups in the regex pattern, which is stored in the `regnpar` field (the pre‑computed count of groups).

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::operator!=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::operator!=@k.body: Returns `true` when the current expression differs from `r`; otherwise returns `false`. It simply negates the result of `operator==`.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::operator==@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::operator==@k.body: The `operator==` member simply checks whether two `RegularExpression` objects describe identical regular expressions by comparing their size fields and the contents of their underlying program arrays. It first verifies that both objects are the same size; if they are, it then iterates over the program array comparing each entry. If any entry differs, it immediately returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::operator=@k_.body: The assignment operator performs a deep copy of a `RegularExpression`: it first protects against self‑assignment, then frees the current program buffer, allocates a new buffer sized to the source, copies the raw program bytes into it, and finally updates all internal pointer members (such as `regmatch`, `regmust`, `regstart`, `reganch`, and `regmlen`) to point into the newly copied data so the target object exactly mirrors the source’s state.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::regMatch@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::regMatch@k_Z.body: The function simply returns a const reference to the `regmatch` member, giving read‑only access to the stored match result without copying or modifying the object.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::set_invalid@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::set_invalid@.body: This method clears the current regex program by deleting the dynamic array and resetting the pointer to `nullptr`. It’s a straightforward cleanup routine that ensures the internal program buffer is released before reuse.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::start@k_ZNK5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::start@k_ZNK5.body: It returns the start index of the nth match reported by the underlying matcher.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::~RegularExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::~RegularExpr.body: This destructor releases the memory allocated for the `program` array inside a `RegularExpression` object. It uses `delete[]` to free the array and is surrounded by a conditional compilation guard (`#ifndef _WIN32`).

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::Regular.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::Regular.body: The move constructor for `RegularExpressionMatch` efficiently transfers the internal state of a temporary instance into a new object, avoiding deep copies of any owned resources. It guarantees that the moved‑from object is left in a valid, empty state while the new instance takes ownership of the original data.

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::Regular.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::Regular.body: The constructor creates a new `RegularExpressionMatch` by copying the internal state (e.g. matched span, flags, and captured groups) from an existing instance. It performs a shallow copy of the object’s data, enabling safe duplication of match objects without re‑parsing the expression.

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::Regular.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::Regular.body: The constructor simply initializes `startp`, `endp`, and `searchstring` to their default values—null pointers or an empty string—without performing any further logic.

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::clear@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::clear@k.body: Resets the internal state – it nulls the first elements of the `startp` and `endp` arrays and clears the `searchstring` pointer.

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::end@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::end@k_Z.body: Returns the offset of the capture‑n terminus relative to the original string, or string::npos if that capture never occurred.

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::isValid.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::isValid.body: It returns the first element of the `startp` array.

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::match@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::match@k.body: The function returns a substring of the internal buffer using the `n`‑th range. If `startp[n]` is zero (or otherwise false), it returns an empty string; otherwise it constructs a `std::string` from the range defined by `startp[n]` and `endp[n]`.

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::operato.body: The assignment operator makes a new instance a copy of an existing `RegularExpressionMatch` by copying its internal data members. It returns a reference to the left‑hand side so the result can be chained. It performs a self‑assignment check to avoid unnecessary work when the two operands are the same. The operator does not perform any dynamic allocation; it just copies the fields into the current object.

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::start@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::start@k.body: The function checks whether a match exists at position n; if it does not, it returns `std::string::npos`. Otherwise it returns the zero‑based offset of that match relative to the original search string, computed as the stored start pointer minus the base pointer of the search string.

@lcmsys::RemoveTrailingSlashes@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RemoveTrailingSlashes@k_ZN5cmsy.body: Trims a trailing “/” or “\” from a path string. It skips removal when the slash follows a drive letter or if the string equals “/”. If the truncated string fits in the supplied buffer, it copies it there; otherwise it copies into an auxiliary string buffer. The function returns a pointer to the cleaned string.

@lcmsys::Status::GetString@k_ZNK5cmsys6S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::GetString@k_ZNK5cmsys6S.body: The function returns a textual description of the current status. It examines the `Kind_` member: if the kind is `Success`, it simply returns the literal “Success”; otherwise it fetches the string for a POSIX error via `strerror` or, on Windows builds, formats the system‑error message using `FormatMessageA`. After the message has been retrieved, it is freed with `LocalFree` before being copied into the return value. The function therefore translates an internal error enumeration into a human‑readable string.

@lcmsys::Status::IsSuccess@k_ZNK5cmsys6S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::IsSuccess@k_ZNK5cmsys6S.body: This accessor simply checks whether the stored enum value matches the `Success` variant, returning the result immediately without side effects.

@lcmsys::Status::POSIX@k_ZN5cmsys6Status.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::POSIX@k_ZN5cmsys6Status.body: Creates a `Status` object whose kind is `POSIX` and assigns the supplied integer to its `POSIX_` member, then returns that object.

@lcmsys::Status::POSIX_errno@k_ZN5cmsys6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::POSIX_errno@k_ZN5cmsys6.body: The function constructs and returns a `Status` object that maps the current value of the global `errno` variable to the corresponding POSIX error code via the `Status::POSIX` factory.

@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.body: The function constructs a `Status` instance by taking ownership of an existing `Status` object through a move‑semantics constructor, transferring its internal state to the new instance.

@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.body: Creates a new `Status` instance by copying the data from the supplied reference, allowing the new object to represent the same state as the original.

@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.body: Creates a `Status` object with the default internal state. The static helper `Success()` simply returns a new `Status()` instance that represents a successful state.

@lcmsys::Status::Success@k_ZN5cmsys6Stat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::Success@k_ZN5cmsys6Stat.body: The `Success` function is a static helper that simply constructs and returns a default‑initialised `Status` object—effectively signalling that an operation completed without error. It wraps the creation of a default status value and provides a concise API for callers to use.

@lcmsys::Status::operator bool@k_ZNK5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::operator bool@k_ZNK5cms.body: Implicitly casting the object to a Boolean simply forwards the internal *IsSuccess* check, so an instance can be used in a boolean context (e.g. `if(obj) …`). The implementation is a single line that returns the result of that private helper, letting callers treat the type as a “truthy” indicator of the internal state.

@lcmsys::Status::operator=@k_ZN5cmsys6St.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::operator=@k_ZN5cmsys6St.body: `operator=` is a move‑assignment operator that takes an rvalue reference to another `Status` object, copies or moves its internal data into the current instance, and returns a reference to the updated object.

@lcmsys::Status::~Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Stat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::~Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Stat.body: When a `Status` object is destroyed, this routine releases its internally held resources and resets all internal flags back to their default values, ensuring no lingering state or memory leaks remain.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetCPUDescri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetCPUDescri.body: It builds a string containing the number of cores followed by the processor’s name or, if that name is empty, a fallback string of clock‑speed, vendor and extended name, then trims any double‑spaces before returning the string.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetFamilyID@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetFamilyID@.body: Delegates to the underlying implementation object and returns the resulting string identifier.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetHostname@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetHostname@.body: The `GetHostname` function simply forwards the call to its internal implementation object and returns the hostname string it provides.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetLoadAvera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetLoadAvera.body: The function forwards the request to its underlying implementation and returns the resulting double value.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetLogicalPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetLogicalPr.body: The `GetLogicalProcessorsPerPhysical` function is a thin public façade that forwards the query to the underlying `Implementation` object and returns the value it reports. It simply returns the count of logical processors that belong to each physical core (i.e., the number of logical processors that can run concurrently on a single physical core).

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetModelID@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetModelID@k.body: The method returns a string obtained from the internal `Implementation` object. It simply forwards the call to `Implementation->GetModelID()` and returns that value.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetNumberOfL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetNumberOfL.body: The method simply forwards the query for the number of logical CPUs to the encapsulated implementation object, returning that count.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetNumberOfP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetNumberOfP.body: The function is a thin wrapper around the underlying implementation. When called, it simply returns whatever value the `Implementation` object reports for the number of physical CPUs. It accepts no arguments, returns an `unsigned int`, and forwards the call to `Implementation->GetNumberOfPhysicalCPU()`. The wrapper adds no logic of its own, so any errors or special cases would be dictated by the implementation layer.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetOSName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetOSName@k_.body: Returns the operating‑system name string obtained from the underlying implementation component. It simply forwards the request to `Implementation->GetOSName()` and returns that value.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetOSPlatfor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetOSPlatfor.body: GetOSPlatform() simply forwards to the underlying Implementation object and returns a C‑string pointer that identifies the operating‑system platform. The method itself performs no additional logic; it relies on the implementation to provide the string and may return a nullptr if the implementation is not initialized.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetOSRelease.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetOSRelease.body: The function delegates to the underlying `Implementation` object and returns the pointer it provides. It simply forwards the request for the operating‑system release string.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetOSVersion.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetOSVersion.body: The member function `GetOSVersion` simply forwards a request for the operating‑system version to the concrete implementation stored in the `Implementation` member. It returns whatever string the implementation supplies, encoded as a `const char*`.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetProcessId.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetProcessId.body: GetProcessId retrieves the current process identifier as a 64‑bit integer by delegating to its Implementation object and returns that value.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetProcessor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetProcessor.body: The method simply forwards a call to the underlying implementation object and returns the integer reported by `Implementation::GetProcessorCacheSize()`.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetProcessor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetProcessor.body: Retrieves the current processor clock speed in GHz by delegating to the underlying implementation object. It simply forwards the call and returns the float result.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetTotalPhys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetTotalPhys.body: Retrieves and returns the total amount of physical memory available to the system, delegating the actual query to the Implementation object.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetTotalVirt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetTotalVirt.body: Returns the total virtual‑memory size by delegating the call to its underlying implementation object.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetVendorID@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetVendorID@.body: The function returns a pointer to the vendor identifier string stored in the underlying implementation. It simply forwards the request to the `Implementation` object and returns the value it supplies.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetVendorStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::GetVendorStr.body: The function hands off the vendor string to the underlying implementation and returns that C‑style string pointer unchanged.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::Is64Bits@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::Is64Bits@k_Z.body: Returns the value reported by the underlying implementation, indicating whether the current system uses a 64‑bit architecture.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::RunCPUCheck@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::RunCPUCheck@.body: Runs the CPU‑health check routine by delegating to the internal `Implementation` object.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::RunMemoryChe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::RunMemoryChe.body: It delegates the system’s memory‑diagnostics to the underlying implementation—invoking `Implementation->RunMemoryCheck()` to perform the check.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::RunOSCheck@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::RunOSCheck@k.body: The method simply forwards the OS‑check request to the internal implementation object, invoking its `RunOSCheck()` routine.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::SystemInform.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::SystemInform.body: Creates a new `SystemInformationImplementation` instance and stores the pointer in the `Implementation` member of the `SystemInformation` object.

@lcmsys::SystemInformation::~SystemInfor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemInformation::~SystemInfor.body: The destructor simply releases the owned `Implementation` instance to avoid memory leaks.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::AddSpaceBetweenCap.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::AddSpaceBetweenCap.body: Iterates over the input string, appending each character to a new string and inserting a space whenever an uppercase character follows a non‑space, non‑uppercase character. The logic inspects each character in turn; when the current character is an uppercase letter and the previous character is neither a space nor an uppercase letter, a space is appended before the current character. The resultant string is returned.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::AppendStrings@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::AppendStrings@k_ZN.body: The function allocates a new buffer large enough for the two strings plus the terminator, copies the first string into it, appends the second string, and returns the new buffer. If either argument is null it simply returns a duplicate of the non‑null string (via `DuplicateString`). It performs no bounds checks beyond the size calculation, and the caller must remember to free the returned pointer.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::AppendStrings@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::AppendStrings@k_ZN.body: The routine recursively skips any null argument, allocating just enough space for the remaining strings, copies them in sequence, and returns the new buffer (or nullptr on allocation failure).

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Capitalized@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Capitalized@k_ZN5c.body: The function returns a new string where the first character is upper‑cased and every subsequent character is lower‑cased; an empty input yields an empty string. It constructs the result by resizing a temporary buffer and copying converted characters one‑by‑one.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CapitalizedWords@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CapitalizedWords@k.body: The function walks through each character of the input string and turns any alphabetic character that either starts the string or follows a space into its uppercase form, returning the modified string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ChangeDirectory@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ChangeDirectory@k_.body: Attempts to change the current working directory to the supplied path. If the underlying system call fails, it returns a Status object reflecting the error via `POSIX_errno()`; otherwise it signals success.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ClassFinalize@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ClassFinalize@k_ZN.body: The function simply releases the singleton instance that `SystemTools` retains in its static member. When invoked, it calls `delete` on that pointer, deallocating the object and freeing its memory. If the pointer is already null or has been freed earlier, the call will trigger undefined behaviour—potentially a crash—so the function must be called exactly once during program shutdown or guarded by a null‑check.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ClassInitialize@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ClassInitialize@k_.body: The function initializes SystemTools by enabling a VMS feature when compiled under VMS, creates the global SystemToolsStatic singleton, and optionally registers special translation paths: it preserves “/tmp/”, and if the current working directory is a logical path, it discovers the shortest logical alias that still resolves to the same physical path and adds that alias to the translation map.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CloneFileContent@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CloneFileContent@k.body:
The method opens the source file read‑only, removes any existing destination file, and then creates a new destination file with the appropriate permissions.  
On Linux it uses the `ioctl` `FICLONE` ioctl to clone the underlying inode; on macOS it falls back to `copyfile` (bypassing the metadata‑cloning option when running as root).  If the platform supports `utimensat`, it updates timestamps with that, otherwise it falls back to `utimes`.  On failure it returns a `CopyStatus` indicating the error type and the problematic path.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.body: The function simply forwards the input string to `CollapseFullPathImpl`, passing `nullptr` for the options parameter. It relies on the implementation to perform the actual path collapsing logic and returns the resulting string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.body: The function forwards the path and base (or `nullptr` if no base) to `CollapseFullPathImpl`, creating a temporary string only when a base string is supplied.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.body: The function forwards the supplied `in_path` and `in_base` to `CollapseFullPathImpl` and returns whatever that helper returns.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ComparePath@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ComparePath@k_ZN5c.body: The function performs a case‑insensitive string comparison. On Windows/Apple it uses the platform‑specific helper (`_stricmp`, `strcasecmp` or `Strucmp`). If none of those compile‑time flags are set, it falls back to a plain `==` comparison. The implementation relies on preprocessor directives to pick the right comparison routine at build time.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToOutputPat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToOutputPat.body: It normalises a file‑path string, delegating to the platform‑specific helper that actually performs the conversion.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToUnixOutpu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToUnixOutpu.body: The routine normalises a file‑system path so it can safely be used on a Unix‑style system. It strips back‑to‑back‑slashes that would otherwise be parsed as an escape sequence, collapses consecutive “//” occurrences, and escapes spaces and parentheses by prefixing them with a backslash. In short, it “flattens” a Windows‑style path into a single‑slash‑separated form that can be passed to a Unix tool without mis‑interpretation.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToUnixSlash.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToUnixSlash.body: The routine normalises a file‑system path string. It first exits on an empty argument, then, on non‑VMS builds, walks the string replacing back‑slashes with forward slashes, coalescing any double slashes into a single one. When the path begins with a tilde it expands that to the current user’s home directory (either via an environment variable or the passwd entry). Finally, it strips a trailing slash unless the string is a root or a single‑character path such as “c:”.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToWindowsOu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToWindowsOu.body: Replaces ‘/’ with ‘\\’, collapses duplicate backslashes, and if the path contains spaces (or is already quoted) it encloses the string in double quotes—returning the cleaned‑up Windows‑style path.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyADirectory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyADirectory@k_Z.body: Copies a directory tree from the source path to the destination by iterating over the entries in a loaded Directory object, recursively calling itself for sub‑directories and delegating single file copies to CopyAFile, while propagating any failure status back to the caller.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyAFile@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyAFile@k_ZN5cms.body: The function delegates the copy operation to either `CopyFileAlways` or `CopyFileIfDifferent` based on the `always` flag, returning the resulting status.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyFileAlways@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyFileAlways@k_Z.body: The routine takes two path strings. It first ensures the destination directory exists—creating it if the source is a directory or if the target path points into one. If the destination points to a directory, it appends the source file name to form a full path. When the source and target refer to the same file, it short‑circuits and returns. Otherwise it attempts to clone the file’s bytes; on failure it falls back to a block‑wise copy. Finally, if permissions were requested, it applies them to the new file before returning a status object that indicates success or the specific failure reason.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyFileContentBlo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyFileContentBlo.body: The function opens the source file, removes any existing destination file, then streams the source in 4096‑byte blocks to the destination while checking `gcount()` after each read. It flushes the output stream, closes both files, and returns a status object indicating success or the specific source/destination path that caused the failure.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyFileIfDifferen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyFileIfDifferen.body: The function first checks if the destination path is a directory; if it is, it builds a new target path inside that directory and recurses into the same function for that new path. If the source and destination are the same file, it simply returns a success status; otherwise, when they differ, it performs a copy operation.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::CopySt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::CopySt.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied arguments to its base‑class and member variable. It takes a `Status` value `s` and a `WhichPath` value `p`, uses the member‑initializer list to initialize the inherited `Status` sub‑object with `s` and assigns the member variable `Path` to `p`. No additional logic occurs in the body.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::CopySt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::CopySt.body: CopyStatus efficiently transfers the internal state of a temporary CopyStatus instance into the current object by moving its resources rather than performing a deep copy.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::CopySt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::CopySt.body: CopyStatus performs a shallow copy of the status object's internal fields, simply copying member values without performing any deep copy or side‑effects.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::operat.body: The move‑assignment overload takes a temporary `CopyStatus` by rvalue reference and copies or moves its internal state into the target object, then returns a reference to the target so calls can be chained. It typically performs a self‑assignment guard, moves the owning resources, and updates any relevant flags to reflect the new state.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::~CopyS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyStatus::~CopyS.body: The ~CopyStatus routine performs a shallow copy of the status fields from one object to another, ensuring that the destination instance ends up with identical flag values and any pending flags set in the source. It returns a success flag indicating whether the copy succeeded, and performs sanity checks on the source’s state before copying.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CountChar@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CountChar@k_ZN5cms.body: `CountChar` returns the number of times a given character appears in a C‑style null‑terminated string. It scans the string until the terminating `'\0'`, incrementing a counter each time the current character matches the target character. The routine operates in linear time relative to the string length and uses no dynamic memory. It performs a null‑pointer check before entering the loop. The function is thread‑safe and performs no side effects.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CreateSymlink@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CreateSymlink@k_ZN.body:
Establishes a symbolic link from the target path to the source path.  
On Windows it invokes `CreateSymbolicLinkW`, passing a flag that indicates directory‑ness when applicable and a privilege flag that allows unprivileged creation.  
If the call fails, the returned error is wrapped in a `Status` value.  
On POSIX‑style systems it simply calls `symlink`; a failure sets the status to the current `errno`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CreationTime@k_ZN5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CreationTime@k_ZN5.body: The function `SystemTools::CreationTime` returns the file creation timestamp in seconds since the Unix epoch. It normalises platform specifics: on Windows it pulls the `ftCreationTime` field via `GetFileAttributesExW` and converts it to POSIX time; on POSIX it reads the `st_ctime` field from `stat`. If the file cannot be read or the API call fails, the function returns 0.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CropString@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CropString@k_ZN5cm.body: The function trims a string to a maximum length by keeping the first half, then the last part, and inserting dots in the middle to show omitted text. It resizes the output to exactly `max_len` characters and replaces the central characters with periods when the length exceeds two. This truncation logic can produce an out‑of‑range access if `max_len` is 1 or 2 because the code still attempts to write `n[middle]` (or `n[middle±1]`) even when the string is too short, potentially causing a buffer violation.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::DecodeURL@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::DecodeURL@k_ZN5cms.body: The function scans a URL string for percent‑encoded byte sequences. When it finds a % followed by two hex digits, it converts those two hex digits into a single byte and appends that byte to the result. Characters that are not percent‑encoded are copied unchanged. The result is a string in which all percent‑encodings have been replaced by their decoded byte values.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Delay@k_ZN5cmsys11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Delay@k_ZN5cmsys11.body: The routine blocks the current thread for roughly the requested number of milliseconds. On Windows it calls the OS‑provided `Sleep` which accepts a millisecond value, while on other platforms it falls back to a custom `usleep` routine. The implementation splits any delay longer than one second into whole‑second chunks (via `sleep`) and the remaining fractional part in microseconds (via `usleep`). It simply performs the timing call and returns without side effects.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::DeleteRegistryValu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::DeleteRegistryValu.body: The `DeleteRegistryValue` function is a stub that takes a registry key name and a WOW64 flag but immediately returns `false`, effectively performing no deletion logic.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::DetectFileType@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::DetectFileType@k_Z.body: DetectFileType opens the specified file in binary mode, reads up to the requested length, and iterates through the buffer counting bytes that look like printable ASCII (including space, tab, newline, carriage‑return). The function then computes the fraction of non‑printable bytes; if that fraction exceeds the supplied threshold it declares the file “binary”, otherwise “text”. It returns “unknown” if the filename is null, points to a directory, the file can’t be opened, or reading fails.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::DuplicateString@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::DuplicateString@k_.body: The function allocates a new buffer with the exact length needed (including the terminating null), copies the source string into it using `strcpy`, and returns a pointer to the newly‑allocated copy. If the input pointer is `nullptr`, the routine simply returns `nullptr`. It never frees the allocated memory, so callers must remember to delete the result when done. It also depends on `strlen` (presumably `strlen`) to be safe; no bounds checking is performed during the copy, so a malformed source string could overflow the destination buffer.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::EnableMSVCDebugHoo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::EnableMSVCDebugHoo.body: Enabling this hook typically injects a callback into the MSVC debugging stack so that any debug‑time events (breakpoints, exceptions, or log output) are intercepted and routed to the application’s own logging or monitoring system. The routine often performs a one‑time registration of the hook and may adjust internal flags to enable or disable the debug‑capture mode.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::EscapeChars@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::EscapeChars@k_ZN5c.body: The function scans the input string and inserts the given escape character before every character that appears in the `chars_to_escape` list. If that list is empty or null, the original string is returned unchanged.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::EstimateFormatLeng.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::EstimateFormatLeng.body: This routine walks the format string character by character, adding the length of the format itself and incrementally adding the size of each supplied argument. For a string argument it takes the actual string length, while for numeric or other unspecified types it adds a fixed 64‑byte upper bound. It stops on a null‑terminator and returns the accumulated total.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.body: The function first guards against a null pointer and then forwards the check to the overload that accepts a `std::string` instance.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.body: The function verifies the pointer is non‑null; if the pointer is null it returns `false`. Otherwise it converts the C‑string to a `std::string` and delegates the existence check to the string‑based overload.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.body: The function first checks that the supplied string is non‑empty, then on Windows it converts the path to a wide string and calls GetFileAttributesW. If the file is a reparse point, it opens the file with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT to query the reparse data and treats a reparse tag of IO_REPARSE_TAG_APPEXECLINK as an existing file. On non‑Windows platforms it simply calls access() with either R_OK or F_OK depending on a compile‑time flag.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.body: The function returns true only when the supplied path actually exists and, if the caller requested a file, the path isn’t point to a directory; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileHasSignature@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileHasSignature@k.body: The routine opens the file, seeks to the supplied offset, reads a block equal to the length of the supplied signature string, and returns true when the read bytes exactly match the signature; otherwise it returns false. It uses a raw buffer read and a simple string comparison to determine the match.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsDirectory@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsDirectory@k_.body: The function checks whether a given path refers to a directory by first normalising the path (trailing slashes are removed) and then calling the platform‑specific API to retrieve the file’s attributes. On Windows it calls `GetFileAttributesW` on an extended‑path string; on POSIX it calls `stat()` and tests the mode bits with `S_ISDIR`. If the attribute retrieval fails or the path is empty, the function returns `false`; otherwise it returns true when the directory flag is set.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsExecutable@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsExecutable@k.body: The function resolves whether a given path points to an executable file. On Windows it normalises the path, queries the file attributes via `GetFileAttributesW`, and treats any non‑directory file as executable. On other platforms it simply verifies the file is not a directory and that execute permission is granted.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFIFO@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFIFO@k_ZN5cm.body: The function examines a file path to decide if the target is a FIFO. On Windows it opens the file with `CreateFileW`, obtains its type via `GetFileType`, and compares that type to `FILE_TYPE_PIPE`; on POSIX it performs an `lstat` on the path and uses `S_ISFIFO` on the mode bits. If either check fails, it returns false; otherwise true.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFullPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFullPath@k_Z.body: The function forwards the supplied path string to a static helper, passing along a numeric hint derived from the string’s first two characters. That hint is `0` if the string is empty, `1` if only the first character is non‑null, and `2` if both the first and second characters exist. The helper then uses that value to determine whether the path is a fully-qualified absolute path.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFullPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFullPath@k_Z.body: Accepted string is read as a C‑style buffer: the wrapper simply passes the pointer and length to a lower‑level routine that returns true when the buffer represents a full path, otherwise false.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsSymlink@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsSymlink@k_ZN.body: The function returns a `bool` indicating whether a path points to a symbolic link. On Windows it converts the supplied UTF‑8 string to a wide string, fetches the file’s attributes with `GetFileAttributesW` and forwards the attribute flag to `FileIsSymlinkWithAttr`. On POSIX it calls `lstat`, inspecting the mode field for the symbolic‑link bit via the macro `S_ISLNK`. If the filesystem call fails, the function simply returns `false`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileLength@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileLength@k_ZN5cm.body: The function returns the size of the specified file in bytes. On Windows it calls `GetFileAttributesExW` and reads the 32‑bit size fields, but only the lower 32 bits are currently used; larger files would be truncated. On non‑Windows systems it falls back to a `stat` call, casting the `st_size` field to `unsigned long`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileTimeCompare@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileTimeCompare@k_.body: Fetches the modification timestamps of the two files. It stores the comparison result in *result: –1 if the first file is older, 1 if it’s newer, 0 if the times match. It returns a status code signalling success or a specific error that occurred during the operation.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FilesDiffer@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FilesDiffer@k_ZN5c.body: The function checks whether two file paths point to identical content. It first verifies existence and size via system‐specific attribute queries (Windows‑style `GetFileAttributesExW` or POSIX `stat`), short‑circuiting a zero‑length file as equal. Then it opens both files in binary mode, reads each in fixed‑size buffers, and byte‑wise compares the buffers with `memcmp`. As soon as any block differs, it returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false` after exhausting the entire file size.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindDirectory@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindDirectory@k_ZN.body: The routine searches the supplied list of paths for a sub‑directory named `name`. It first calls `SystemToolsStatic::FindName` to resolve a candidate path. If that call returns a non‑empty string and the returned path points to a directory, the function normalises the path with `CollapseFullPath` and returns it; otherwise it returns an empty string to indicate that no matching directory was found.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindFile@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindFile@k_ZN5cmsy.body: The function searches for a file named `name` in the paths supplied via `userPaths`. It first invokes `FindName` to locate a matching path, then checks that the result is not a directory. If a valid file path is found, it normalises that path (using `CollapseFullPath`) and returns it; otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindLastString@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindLastString@k_Z.body: The routine walks the first string backward, comparing successive blocks of length `len2` against the second string. When a full match is found it returns the pointer into the first string where the match begins; otherwise it yields `nullptr`. It uses `strlen` and a simple backward loop, so it will scan roughly `O(n⋅m)` characters and may be noticeably slower on long inputs. An empty‑second‑string special case is also noteworthy: the routine will treat it as a match and return the terminating NUL pointer, which may not be the intended behaviour.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindLibrary@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindLibrary@k_ZN5c.body: The function searches for a named library in the current executable’s directory, then in a combined list of system‑wide and user‑supplied paths. It first checks if the library already exists as a plain file; if not, it iterates through each path, appending expected suffixes (.framework, .lib, .so, .a, .sl, .dyld, .dll) depending on the operating‑system macros, and returns the resolved absolute path when a match is found. If no match appears, it returns an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.body: The wrapper first verifies that the supplied name is non‑empty; if it isn’t, it immediately returns an empty string. Otherwise, it forwards the call to an overload that takes a std::string, passing along the supplied paths and the system‑path flag.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.body: The routine searches for an executable named `name` by scanning first a system path (unless suppressed) and then any supplied `userPaths`. On Windows it appends `.com` and `.exe` extensions when appropriate, trims quotes, and normalises slashes before checking file existence; if found it returns the fully‑resolved path, otherwise an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.body: It checks each supplied name in order, calling the helper overload for that name. On finding a non‑empty path, it immediately returns that path; otherwise it falls back to an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgramPath@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgramPath@k_.body: The routine accepts a program name (argv0), attempts to resolve its full filesystem path, populates `pathOut` with that path if found, and returns a boolean status; on failure it returns `false` and fills `errorMsg` with the list of candidate paths that were unsuccessfully checked.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Fopen@k_ZN5cmsys11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Fopen@k_ZN5cmsys11.body: The function opens a file. On Windows it first strips any ‘e’ characters from the mode string, converts the filename to a wide string, and passes that wide path and trimmed mode to `_wfopen`. On non‑Windows systems it simply delegates to the standard `fopen` call.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetActualCaseForPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetActualCaseForPa.body: The function normalizes a file‑system path into its real‑case form. On Windows it calls a helper that queries the file system for the exact mixed‑case name; on other systems it simply returns the input unchanged.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetCurrentDateTime.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetCurrentDateTime.body: The `GetCurrentDateTime` function captures the current system time, formats it according to the supplied `format` string using `strftime`, and returns the formatted timestamp as a `std::string`. It uses a 1024‑byte buffer for the formatted result and converts the `time_t` value into a local `tm` struct before returning the string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetCurrentWorkingD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetCurrentWorkingD.body: The routine attempts to read the current working directory into a fixed‑size buffer, copies the returned C‑string into a `std::string`, normalises the path separators to Unix form, and returns the resulting string. If the helper fails to provide a working‑directory string, the function simply returns an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.body: The static method retrieves the value of a requested environment variable. On Windows it delegates to a buffered helper that internally caches the string; otherwise it simply forwards to the standard `getenv`. If the key is not set, it returns a null pointer.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.body: Returns true only when the requested key is present in the environment; on Windows the key is first converted to a wide string, _getenviron is invoked, and the resulting wide string is converted back to narrow form before being stored in `result`. If the key isn’t found, the function returns false.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.body: The function returns a C‑style string that contains the value of the environment variable whose name is supplied in `key`. On Windows (`_WIN32`) it forwards the lookup to `SystemToolsStatic::GetEnvBuffered`, otherwise it simply calls the standard `getenv` routine. If the variable is unset, the returned pointer is `nullptr`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.body: This method forwards the string argument to the overload that accepts a C‑string and returns the result in the supplied output parameter.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetExecutableExten.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetExecutableExten.body: This function returns a string literal that represents the executable file extension for the current platform. On Windows‑style systems (detected via the `_WIN32`, `__CYGWIN__`, or `__VMS` macros) it yields the literal `".exe"`, otherwise it yields an empty string. The literal is stored in read‑only memory, so the pointer is safe to use after the function returns.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameExtensi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameExtensi.body: The function strips everything before the last dot in a file name, returning the trailing part as the extension; if no dot is found it yields an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameLastExt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameLastExt.body:
The function extracts and returns the part of a filename that follows the last dot. It does so by:

1. Obtaining the file‑name portion of the full path via `GetFilenameName`.  
2. Finding the index of the final period with `rfind('.')`.  
3. If a period exists, it removes everything before that period (including the period itself) with `erase(0, dot_pos)`.  
4. The remaining string is then returned. If no period appears, an empty string is returned.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameName@k_.body: The routine scans the supplied path for the last path‑separator (either ‘/’ or ‘\\’) and returns the substring that follows it; if no separator is found it returns the original string unchanged.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenamePath@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenamePath@k_.body: Normalizes the supplied path to use forward slashes, then strips everything after the last slash and returns the remaining directory portion (or an empty string if no directory part exists). It handles the root‐path case and preserves the trailing slash after a Windows drive letter.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameWithout.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameWithout.body: The function receives a file path, uses `GetFilenameName` to isolate the file component, then trims the string at the first dot it finds. If no dot is present, the original string is returned unchanged.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameWithout.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameWithout.body: The routine trims the string returned by GetFilenameName to the last dot: it locates the final period in the file‑name; if one exists, the string is shrunk to that position, otherwise the original string is kept.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetLastSystemError.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetLastSystemError.body: The function simply captures the current value of `errno` into a local variable and returns the human‑readable message that `strerror` produces for that value, converted into a `std::string`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetLineFromStream@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetLineFromStream@.body: The routine reads the next line from the supplied stream. It trims a trailing carriage‑return if present, optionally truncates the string to a caller‑supplied limit, and then reports whether any data was read. It returns false only when the stream is bad or empty; otherwise it supplies the line and an indicator of whether there is more data left in the stream.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetMaximumFilePath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetMaximumFilePath.body: The function simply returns the predefined maximum file‑path length constant (`KWSYS_SYSTEMTOOLS_MAXPATH`). This value is used by the application to validate that a path string does not exceed the system’s maximum path length.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetOperatingSystem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetOperatingSystem.body: The routine calls GetVersionExA to obtain a OSVERSIONINFOEXA structure, inspects the platform ID, major/minor version and product type, then maps those numeric values to human‑readable names (e.g. “Microsoft Windows 10”, “Microsoft Windows Server 2016 family”, “Microsoft Windows Server 2008 R2 family”, etc.). For legacy releases it may read registry values to determine the exact edition. Finally it concatenates the OS name, edition and build number into a string that is returned.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetParentDirectory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetParentDirectory.body: Returns the directory portion of the supplied path by delegating to `GetFilenamePath`. The function simply forwards the input string to `GetFilenamePath` and returns that value, effectively stripping off the final path component.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetPath@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetPath@k_ZN5cmsys.body: The function parses the value of an environment variable (defaulting to “PATH”) into individual directories and stores them in the supplied vector. It selects the separator character based on the target platform (`;` for Win32, `:` otherwise), then splits the retrieved string on that separator. Each component is appended to the vector and finally converted to Unix‑style forward slashes before returning.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetPermissions@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetPermissions@k_Z.body: The function validates that the input C‑string is non‑null and, on success, delegates the permission lookup to an overload that accepts a `std::string`. It simply returns the status from that internal call after constructing the string from the raw pointer.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetPermissions@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetPermissions@k_Z.body: The `GetPermissions` function probes a file’s attributes (Windows or POSIX) and translates them into a Unix‑style mode mask. It sets read/write flags based on read‑only and directory status and adds execute bits for .exe/.com/.cmd/.bat extensions, returning a `Success` status or the relevant failure code.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetProgramPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetProgramPath@k_Z.body: The function receives a path string, runs `SplitProgramPath` to divide it into directory and file parts, and simply returns the directory portion.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetRealPath@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetRealPath@k_ZN5c.body: The function resolves a supplied path string into its absolute form. It calls the helper `Realpath`, passing the input path, a string reference to receive the resolved path, and an output pointer for an error message. The resolved string is then returned to the caller.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetRegistrySubKeys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetRegistrySubKeys.body: The function receives a registry key path and a vector to be filled with that key’s sub‑keys, then returns a Boolean indicating whether the operation succeeded (currently always false).

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetShortPath@k_ZN5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetShortPath@k_ZN5.body: The routine trims leading/trailing quotes from an input path, converts the trimmed string to a wide string, and invokes `GetShortPathNameW` to obtain the short‑form path. On success it copies the result into `shortPath`; on failure it returns the last Win32 error status. In non‑Windows builds it simply echoes the original path.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetTerminalWidth@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetTerminalWidth@k.body: The function returns the width of the current terminal in columns. It first queries the terminal size via ioctl; if that fails it falls back to the COLUMNS environment variable; if the value is < 9 it yields –1, otherwise it returns the detected width.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetTime@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
