@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetTime@k_ZN5cmsys.body: The `GetTime` function returns the current timestamp as a `double` in seconds. On Windows it queries the system’s `FILETIME`, scales the high/low 64‑bit parts into a fractional epoch value and subtracts the 1970‑epoch offset to produce a Unix‑style epoch value. On other platforms it falls back to `gettimeofday`, combining the seconds and microseconds fields into a double. It’s a straightforward wrapper that normalises the platform‑specific time APIs into a single, portable `double` representation.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::HasEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::HasEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.body: The function tests whether an environment variable is defined. On Windows it first converts the ANSI key to a wide string via a helper that converts the key, then pulls the value using a platform‐specific wide API. On non‑Windows it simply calls the standard `getenv`. It returns `true` when a non‑null pointer is returned, otherwise `false`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::HasEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::HasEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.body: The function forwards a `std::string` key to an overload that accepts a C‑style string. It therefore relies on the string’s `c_str()` method (note the typo in the code should be `c_str()`), and on the presence of a matching overload of `HasEnv(const char*)`. No other logic is performed; the function merely returns the result of that call.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::IsSubDirectory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::IsSubDirectory@k_Z.body: The function normalises both paths to Unix‑style slashes, then checks that the `subdir` string is longer than `dir` and that the character at the position where the directory ends is a slash. If those conditions hold, it resizes `subdir` to the same length as `dir` and finally compares the two strings with `ComparePath` to decide whether `subdir` is a descendant of `dir`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Join@k_ZN5cmsys11S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Join@k_ZN5cmsys11S.body: The function builds a single string by concatenating every element in the supplied vector, inserting the supplied separator only after the first element. It first calculates the required buffer size (total length of all strings plus the length of every separator that will actually appear), reserves that capacity on the result string, and then appends each part while conditionally adding the separator. The algorithm runs in linear time in the number of input elements and performs no more than one allocation for the final string. It gracefully handles an empty list by returning an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::JoinPath@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::JoinPath@k_ZN5cmsy.body: The function forwards the vector of path components to the overload that accepts iterators, returning the joined path string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::JoinPath@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::JoinPath@k_ZN5cmsy.body: The function walks a vector of strings between two iterators, reserves enough capacity, appends each component with a preceding '/' except for the first two elements (which are appended directly). It returns the joined path string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::LocateFileInDir@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::LocateFileInDir@k_.body: The routine scans a directory tree for a given file name. It first normalises the input paths, handling Windows‑style drive letters, and then checks whether the file exists directly under the supplied directory. If it’s not found, it iteratively walks up the file’s own path components—adding them as sub‑folders—to the base directory and recurses until the file is located or the search space is exhausted. When found, it returns the full path and a success flag.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::LowerCase@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::LowerCase@k_ZN5cms.body: The function allocates a new string of identical length, copies each character into it after converting the character to its lowercase form with `tolower`, and returns that new string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeCidentifier@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeCidentifier@k_.body: The MakeCidentifier routine trims a supplied string into a valid C‑identifier: it prefixes an underscore when the first character is a digit and then walks the string, turning any character that isn’t a letter, digit, or underscore into an underscore. It returns the cleaned string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeDirectory@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeDirectory@k_ZN.body:
The function creates a directory at the supplied path.  
If the path argument is null it returns a POSIX‑style error.  
Otherwise, it forwards the call to the string‑based overload.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeDirectory@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeDirectory@k_ZN.body: The routine first checks whether the supplied path string is empty, returning a POSIX error if so. It then verifies whether the target already exists: if it is a directory it reports success; if it exists but isn’t a directory it returns an existence error. If the path does not exist, the function walks through each directory component in the path string, temporarily terminating the string at each slash, calling Mkdir to create that sub‑directory, then restoring the slash before proceeding. After all components are created it attempts to create the final directory, returning the corresponding status (success or a POSIX error).

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ModifiedTime@k_ZN5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ModifiedTime@k_ZN5.body:
The function returns the last‑modified timestamp for the specified file.  
It normalises the platform: on Windows it uses `GetFileAttributesExW` (converted to a Windows path), otherwise it calls `stat`.  
On success it returns the epoch‑based value; on failure it yields zero.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ParseURL@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ParseURL@k_ZN5cmsy.body: The function applies a regular‑expression pattern to the supplied URL string, extracts the nine capture groups (protocol, user, password, host, port, path) into the corresponding output parameters, and finally returns `true` when the pattern matches or `false` otherwise. If the `decode` flag is set, each extracted token is passed through a URL‑percent‑decoding routine before being returned.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ParseURLProtocol@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ParseURLProtocol@k.body: Parses the supplied URL string with a regular‑expression that captures a protocol and the following path component. It returns a bool indicating success; on success the protocol and dataglom output strings are populated, with an optional URL‑decoding step controlled by the `decode` flag. The function simply returns false if the regex fails to match, otherwise true after extracting and optionally decoding.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::PathExists@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::PathExists@k_ZN5cm.body: Checks if the supplied path string is non‑empty and, depending on the build target, queries the file system (using `GetFileAttributesW` on Windows or `lstat` elsewhere) to see whether an entry at that path can be found, returning `true` only when the lookup succeeds.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::PutEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::PutEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.body:
Parses a string of the form “name=value”.  
If an ‘=’ is present it extracts the key and value and invokes `setenv(name, value, 1)`.  
If the key is absent it calls `kwsysUnPutEnv`.  
Returns `true` when the underlying call returns zero, otherwise `false`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReadRegistryValue@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReadRegistryValue@.body: The static `ReadRegistryValue` returns a boolean indicating success; it accepts a key string, a reference to a string to receive the value, and a `KeyWOW64` type (presumably a wrapper around the registry key). It should attempt to read a registry entry and, if successful, populate the output string; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReadSymlink@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReadSymlink@k_ZN5c.body: The function opens the supplied path, checks for a reparse point, reads the reparse buffer, extracts the target path depending on whether it’s a symlink, mount‑point, or app‑exec link, and assigns that resolved path to `origName`, returning a status indicating success or any failure.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::RelativePath@k_ZN5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::RelativePath@k_ZN5.body: The function computes a relative path from a base directory to a target by first normalising both paths, detecting the longest shared prefix, then prefixing the remaining parts of the source with “..” segments and appending the differing suffix of the destination; if no common prefix exists (e.g. on different drive letters on Windows) it simply returns the destination path as‑is.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveADirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveADirectory@k.body: The routine traverses a directory tree, temporarily granting write rights to the target so it can delete every entry it encounters. It skips the special entries “.” and “..”, descends into sub‑directories unless they are symlinks, and deletes each file or leaf it finds. Once the tree is empty, it calls the underlying POSIX rmdir to unlink the directory itself, propagating any failure status back to the caller.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveChars@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveChars@k_ZN5c.body: The function allocates a new buffer, copies the original string into it while skipping any character that appears in the second argument, and returns a pointer to the newly created null‑terminated string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveCharsButUppe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveCharsButUppe.body: The routine allocates a new buffer, copies only the characters that are digits 0‑9 or the capital letters A‑F, null‑terminates the result, and returns that freshly allocated string (or nullptr if the input was null).

@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveFile@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveFile@k_ZN5cm.body:
This static function attempts to delete a file or directory.  
On Windows it first calls `DeleteFileW`; if the file is missing or already gone it reports success.  
When access is denied it clears the read‑only bit, retries the delete, and if the target is a reparse point or a directory it removes the corresponding entry.  
The function restores any temporarily changed permissions before returning a `Status` that contains the final error code (or success).  
On POSIX it simply calls `unlink` and returns the appropriate `Status` based on `errno`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReplaceChars@k_ZN5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReplaceChars@k_ZN5.body: The function scans the input string `str`; for each character it compares against every character in the `toreplace` list, and whenever it finds a match it writes the `replacement` character into that position. It then returns the original string pointer.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReplaceString@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReplaceString@k_ZN.body: The routine walks through a mutable string and substitutes every occurrence of a specified pattern with a new token, falling back to a helper that receives the pattern length. It exits immediately when the search token is empty, avoiding any search. Once the guard passes, it delegates the actual search‑and‑replace logic to an internal helper that performs the string traversal and substitution in‑place.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReplaceString@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReplaceString@k_ZN.body: The function performs a string‑replacement operation: it checks whether the substring to replace is empty, and if not, forwards the operation to an overloaded helper that works on C‑style strings and sizes. It effectively replaces every occurrence of the supplied pattern with the new string in the supplied buffer.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SameFile@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SameFile@k_ZN5cmsy.body: Checks two paths and returns true if the underlying file system reports them as the same object – on Windows it pulls the volume‑serial and file‑index fields from the file‑information buffer; on other platforms it compares the device, inode and size values obtained from a stat call. If any comparison fails or either file fails to open, the function returns false.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SetPermissions@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SetPermissions@k_Z.body: Validates the provided path pointer, then forwards the call to the string‑based overload, returning whatever status that routine produces.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SetPermissions@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SetPermissions@k_Z.body: The `SetPermissions` function changes a file’s permission bits. It first verifies the file exists; if not, it returns a POSIX error for `ENOENT`. If `honor_umask` is true, it temporarily applies the current umask to the requested mode by masking the mode bits. It then attempts to set the permissions using the platform‑specific API (`_wchmod` on Windows, `chmod` elsewhere). If the system call fails, it returns the corresponding POSIX error status; otherwise it reports success.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Split@k_ZN5cmsys11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Split@k_ZN5cmsys11.body: The routine walks through the supplied text, extracts substrings terminated by a newline (removing a preceding carriage‑return if present), and appends each fragment to the supplied vector. On encountering the final line it pushes the remaining tail and returns false; otherwise it continues until the string is exhausted and returns true.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Split@k_ZN5cmsys11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Split@k_ZN5cmsys11.body: Iterates over the input string, splits at each occurrence of the separator, appends each fragment to the `lines` vector, and returns true unless the string ends with the separator (in which case the last fragment is empty and the function returns false).

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitPath@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitPath@k_ZN5cms.body: The routine clears a supplied component vector, extracts the first component of a pathname (handling a leading “/” or “\”) and, if requested, expands a leading “~” to the current user’s home directory. It then iterates over the remaining characters, breaking the string at directory separators (both ‘/’ and ‘\’), storing each sub‑path in the vector. The function relies on helper calls such as `SplitPathRootComponent` for the root extraction and `GetEnv` for environment variable lookup, and finally pushes the trailing component if one remains.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitPathRootCompo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitPathRootCompo.body: The function inspects a path string to identify and isolate its leading component—whether a network share (e.g. `\\server\share`), a root directory (`/` or `C:\`), a home‑path (`~`), or a relative path. It copies the root part into the supplied output string (if non‑null) and returns a pointer to the remaining suffix of the original string. If no root is found, it returns an empty string and leaves the output empty.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitProgramPath@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitProgramPath@k.body:
The routine normalises a path string, then probes whether the supplied string denotes a directory.  
If it does **not** describe a directory, the routine locates the last ‘/’, separates that suffix as the filename and truncates the remainder to the directory component.  
A single‑character return of `true/false` signals whether the original path pointed to an existing directory; any failure to recognise a directory results in the function returning `false`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitString@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitString@k_ZN5c.body: The function splits an input string on a specified separator character, returning a vector of the resulting substrings. When invoked with the `isPath` flag set to true, it treats a leading slash specially—preserving it as a separate element before performing the split. It iterates through the string, locating separator positions, and copies the intervening substrings into the output vector.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Stat@k_ZN5cmsys11S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Stat@k_ZN5cmsys11S.body: It validates the provided path and forwards the call to the string‑based overload, returning that call’s result.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Stat@k_ZN5cmsys11S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Stat@k_ZN5cmsys11S.body: Stat is a static routine that first validates its argument, sets errno when the supplied path is empty, and then forwards the request to the platform‑specific stat implementation—on Windows it converts the path to a wide string and invokes _wstat64, otherwise it calls the POSIX stat. It returns the integer status from that call (‑1 on error).

@lcmsys::SystemTools::StringEndsWith@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::StringEndsWith@k_Z.body: The function checks whether the second string is a suffix of the first: it verifies pointers, compares lengths, and uses `strncmp` on the tail of the first string; it returns `true` when the suffix matches and `false` otherwise.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::StringEndsWith@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::StringEndsWith@k_Z.body:
The function checks whether `str1` ends with the C‑string `str2`. It first guards against a null suffix pointer, then uses the length of `str1` and the length of the C‑string (via `strlen`).  
If the suffix is longer than the original string, it immediately returns `false`. Otherwise it performs a `strncmp` on the portion of `str1` that should match `str2`. If the comparison returns zero (equal), the expression returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`. The ternary operator is unnecessary – returning the result of the comparison directly would be simpler.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::StringStartsWith@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::StringStartsWith@k.body: Checks whether the first string begins with the second one by first ensuring neither pointer is null, then verifying that the first string’s length is at least that of the second and that the first *len2* characters match exactly.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::StringStartsWith@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::StringStartsWith@k.body: The function returns `true` only when the first argument (`str1`) begins with the C‑string supplied in the second argument (`str2`). It first guards against a null pointer, then compares lengths and finally uses `strncmp` on the underlying character arrays to decide whether the prefix matches. If any of these checks fail, the function returns `false`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Strucmp@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Strucmp@k_ZN5cmsys.body: The function walks two strings in tandem, lower‑casing each character with a (presumed) `tolower` helper, and stops when a mismatch occurs or a null terminator is reached. It then returns the signed difference of the differing characters, effectively yielding a non‑zero value if the strings differ and zero otherwise. The code, however, has a few caveats: it assumes `tolower` exists, leaks a local pointer by using `*l++` without bounds checking, and the `while` condition `lc == rc && lc` will keep looping while the two characters match **and** the current character is non‑null, but stops only on mismatch or null; it also fails to handle null‑pointer inputs or mis‑aligned string ends.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::TestFileAccess@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::TestFileAccess@k_Z.body: The function merely checks for a null pointer and then forwards the call to an overload that accepts a `std::string`. It returns false immediately when `filename` is null, otherwise it returns whatever the inner `TestFileAccess` overload returns. The implementation relies on converting the C‑string to a `std::string` and delegating the actual permission test to the other helper.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::TestFileAccess@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::TestFileAccess@k_Z.body: The function verifies that the supplied file name is non‑empty and then calls the platform‑specific access routine (_waccess on Windows, access otherwise) to test whether the requested permissions (read, write, execute) are granted. It returns true only if the system call reports success (returns zero); otherwise it returns false.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::TextFilesDiffer@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::TextFilesDiffer@k_.body: The routine opens the two paths and walks through them simultaneously, pulling one line at a time. If any line differs, or one stream ends earlier than the other, it reports a difference; otherwise it reports no difference.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Touch@k_ZN5cmsys11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Touch@k_ZN5cmsys11.body: The routine checks for the existence of the specified path. If the file is absent and the caller requested creation, it creates an empty file (creating it if needed) and then updates the timestamp to the current system time. The implementation uses the native API for the platform—CreateFileW/SetFileTime on Windows and utimensat/utimes on POSIX—returning a status object that reports success or the underlying error code.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::UnCapitalizedWords.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::UnCapitalizedWords.body: Converts the first character of each word in a string to lower‑case, leaving the rest of the word unchanged. It scans the string, and whenever a character is alphabetic and either at the start of the string or follows a space, it replaces that character with its lower‑case form. The function returns the modified string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::UnPutEnv@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::UnPutEnv@k_ZN5cmsy.body: The function delegates to the underlying system API `kwsysUnPutEnv`, passing the supplied string and returns `true` only when that call succeeds (i.e., when the API returns 0).

@lcmsys::SystemTools::UpperCase@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::UpperCase@k_ZN5cms.body: The function copies the input string into a new string, converting every character to upper‑case using `toupper`. It allocates the destination string to the same length as the source, then iterates over each character, assigns the upper‑case result to the corresponding position in the new string, and finally returns that string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::WriteRegistryValue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::WriteRegistryValue.body: The `WriteRegistryValue` method is a static helper that receives a registry key path, a string value, and a `KeyWOW64` enumeration value and is expected to write that value into the Windows registry. In its current form it performs no actual registry operation and immediately returns `false`, indicating that the function is a stub awaiting full implementation.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsAppendComponents@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsAppendComponents@k_Z.body: The routine walks a range of path fragments and appends them to a target vector while normalising relative components. It treats a lone “..” as a back‑step: if there is a previous component it pops it, otherwise it preserves the fragment only when it sits at the start of a relative path. Any “.” components are ignored. The function uses simple vector operations (checking size and resizing) to perform the normalisation, ensuring that a path never “escapes” above the root.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsManager::SystemTools.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsManager::SystemTools.body: When the first instance of **SystemToolsManager** is created, the constructor increments a global counter. If that counter equals one, it triggers the one‑time class‑wide initialization routine `SystemTools::ClassInitialize()`. Subsequent instances skip this call because the condition no longer holds.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsManager::~SystemTool.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsManager::~SystemTool.body: When an instance of `SystemToolsManager` is destroyed, this destructor decrements a global reference counter. Once that counter reaches zero, it invokes `SystemTools::ClassFinalize()` to clean up shared resources.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::FileIsFullPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::FileIsFullPa.body: The function examines a C‑string to decide whether it represents an absolute path. On Windows it requires at least two characters and accepts a drive letter or a backslash start; on non‑Windows it allows a single character or a tilde start, and otherwise requires a leading slash. The routine returns true when the string satisfies the platform‑specific absolute‑path pattern and false otherwise.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::FindName@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::FindName@k_Z.body: The `FindName` routine builds a list of candidate directories by first adding the system’s standard search directory (unless the `no_system_path` flag disables it) and then appending any custom paths supplied via `userPaths`. It then iterates over this list, appending the given file name to each directory (ensuring a trailing slash when needed) and checks for the file’s existence. When found it returns the fully‑qualified path; otherwise it returns an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::ReplaceStrin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::ReplaceStrin.body: The method scans the supplied string for every occurrence of the target pattern, terminates that segment, and stitches the replacement string in its place, rebuilding the overall string until no more matches exist.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::SystemToolsS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::SystemToolsS.body: `SystemToolsStatic` is a static factory‑style helper that accepts an rvalue reference to an existing `SystemToolsStatic` instance and returns a new instance that owns the same resources (typically moved). It’s typically used to create a fresh instance that takes ownership of whatever data the original held.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::SystemToolsS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::SystemToolsS.body: Creates a new SystemToolsStatic instance by copying the internal state from an existing instance, enabling duplication of the tools configuration.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::SystemToolsS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::SystemToolsS.body: SystemToolsStatic is a static helper class that centralizes common system‑level utilities—state‑checking, configuration parsing, and thread‑safe logging—providing a single point of access for the rest of the code base.  It encapsulates the low‑level plumbing required by several subsystems, and its constructor is guarded against re‑initialisation to preserve global consistency.  The class exposes only static methods, keeping its own state immutable, which in turn eliminates race conditions and simplifies unit‑testing.  Because the class is invoked from multiple modules, the API remains lightweight to avoid unnecessary allocations.

@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::~SystemTools.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemToolsStatic::~SystemTools.body: The destructor `~SystemToolsStatic()` cleans up the static resources used by the `SystemToolsStatic` class, releasing any allocated memory, closing open file handles, and resetting static flags or handles so that subsequent use of the system tools starts from a clean state.

@lcmsys::kwsysEnvCompare::operator()@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::kwsysEnvCompare::operator()@k_Z.body: It’s a comparison operator: it returns true when the first string is lexicographically less than the second, trimming any trailing part after the first ‘=’ in each string before doing the comparison.

@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Free::Free@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Free::Free@k_ZN5cm.body: The constructor simply assigns the supplied environment pointer to its `Env` member via an initializer list, doing no further processing.

@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Free::Free@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Free::Free@k_ZN5cm.body: The class `Free` is explicitly non‑copyable: its copy‑constructor is declared as deleted. This prevents accidental copying of `Free` objects, ensuring that instances cannot be implicitly copied or moved, which is important for maintaining ownership semantics in the surrounding code.

@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Free::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Free::operator=@k_.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents copying an existing `Free` instance, ensuring that objects of the class cannot be inadvertently reassigned after construction. This enforces immutability of the internal state and safeguards against unintended side‑effects during assignments.

@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Free::~Free@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Free::~Free@k_ZN5c.body: The function deallocates the memory that `Env` holds by casting it to a `const envchar*` and passing it to `free`. This effectively releases the buffer the object previously owned.

@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Release@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::kwsysEnvSet::Release@k_ZN5cmsys.body: Finds the key in the container; if it exists, removes that element and returns the old pointer (or `nullptr` if the key isn’t present).

@lcmsys::kwsysUnPutEnv@k_ZN5cmsysL13kwsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::kwsysUnPutEnv@k_ZN5cmsysL13kwsy.body: The function parses a “name=value” string. It locates the first ‘=’, extracts the part before it, and passes that name to `unsetenv`. If no ‘=’ is found, it just passes the entire string. The routine always returns 0, so callers never learn whether the unset succeeded.

@lcmsys::regnext@k_ZN5cmsysL7regnextEPKc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::regnext@k_ZN5cmsysL7regnextEPKc.body: The function checks whether the input pointer points to the sentinel `regdummyptr`; if so, it signals the end of a list by returning `nullptr`. Otherwise, it fetches a relative offset through the `NEXT` macro. If that offset is zero, it also returns `nullptr`. Depending on the operation code (`OP`) found at the current node, it either steps backward (when the operation equals `BACK`) by subtracting the offset from the current pointer or steps forward by adding the offset. The result is the address of the following or preceding element in the underlying data structure.

@lcmsys::regnext@k_ZN5cmsysL7regnextEPc@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::regnext@k_ZN5cmsysL7regnextEPc@.body: regnext computes the address of the next opcode in a compiled regex stream. It first checks for a dummy pointer and returns `nullptr` if encountered. It then retrieves an offset value via the `NEXT` macro; if that value is zero, it again returns `nullptr`. Finally, depending on whether the current opcode is a back‑reference (`BACK`), it either subtracts or adds the offset to the current pointer to locate the next instruction.

@lcmsysBase64_Decode3@kcmsysBase64_Decod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysBase64_Decode3@kcmsysBase64_Decod.body: The routine decodes a four‑character Base‑64 block: each character is mapped to its 6‑bit value, the four values are stitched back into up to three raw bytes (using bit‑shifts and masks), and if the block ends in one or two ‘=’ paddings it returns the corresponding byte count; otherwise it returns 3. If any character isn’t a valid Base‑64 symbol it returns 0.

@lcmsysBase64_Decode@kcmsysBase64_Decode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysBase64_Decode@kcmsysBase64_Decode.body: It loops over 4‑byte blocks, calling kwsysBase64_Decode3 to turn each block into up to 3 bytes written to the output buffer, and stops when the buffer can’t accept another full triplet, with a tail‑case handling for the final 1–2 bytes.

@lcmsysBase64_Encode1@kcmsysBase64_Encod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysBase64_Encode1@kcmsysBase64_Encod.body: The routine takes a single byte, maps the high‑6 bits to the first Base64 character and the low‑2 bits (shifted into a 6‑bit slot) to the second, then appends two ‘=’ pads. It relies on a helper that converts a 6‑bit value into the Base64 alphabet and does not guard against over‑runs or varying input lengths.

@lcmsysBase64_Encode2@kcmsysBase64_Encod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysBase64_Encode2@kcmsysBase64_Encod.body: Encodes a 3‑byte block into four 6‑bit base64 symbols: it splits the incoming 24‑bit stream into four 6‑bit groups, feeds each group to kwsysBase64EncodeChar, and pads the output with “=”.

@lcmsysBase64_Encode3@kcmsysBase64_Encod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysBase64_Encode3@kcmsysBase64_Encod.body: This routine encodes a 3‑byte block of binary data into the four‑character Base‑64 string that a decoding routine can reverse. It pulls each byte of the source buffer and, by successive shifts and masks, stitches together the appropriate 6‑bit values that correspond to the Base‑64 alphabet. The algorithm is straightforward but must be used only on three‑byte slices that are properly aligned; passing an incomplete chunk or a buffer shorter than three bytes will result in reading beyond the buffer bounds. The function performs no bounds checks, so callers must guarantee that `src` points to at least three bytes of valid data and that `dest` has space for four output bytes.

@lcmsysBase64_Encode@kcmsysBase64_Encode.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysBase64_Encode@kcmsysBase64_Encode.body: The routine copies the source data to a Base‑64 representation in the supplied output buffer, handling the tail of the input in the usual 3‑byte grouping scheme: a full 3‑byte block writes 4 encoded bytes; a 2‑byte tail writes 3 encoded bytes plus one padding byte; a 1‑byte tail writes 2 encoded bytes plus two padding bytes. If the caller requests a padding marker, the routine appends “====” after the final block. The return value is the number of output bytes written.

@lcmsysProcess_AddCommand@kcmsysProcess_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_AddCommand@kcmsysProcess_.body: The routine expands a process's command list: it allocates a new array, copies the existing command pointers, and appends a newly‑parsed or tokenized command entry (depending on the `Verbatim` flag). It cleans up the previous array, updates the count, and returns success (1) or failure (0) on allocation errors.

@lcmsysProcess_Delete@kcmsysProcess_Dele.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_Delete@kcmsysProcess_Dele.body: Deletes a process instance: if it’s still running it detaches or waits for it to finish, then clears its command, working directory, pipe descriptors, releases any exit‐code and result buffers, and finally frees the process structure itself.

@lcmsysProcess_Disown@kcmsysProcess_Diso.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_Disown@kcmsysProcess_Diso.body: This routine verifies that the process is still running and detached; if so, it closes its pipes, frees its resources, and finally marks the process state as “disowned”.

@lcmsysProcess_Execute@kcmsysProcess_Exe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_Execute@kcmsysProcess_Exe.body: The routine creates the pipeline of processes described in the process object. It first validates the object, sets up its pipes (stdin/stdout/stderr) via files, shared or native descriptors, and then sequentially spawns each command in a forked child while wiring the streams between them. After all children are launched it restores the original working directory, cleans up unneeded file descriptors and marks the process as executing.

@lcmsysProcess_GetErrorString@kcmsysProc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetErrorString@kcmsysProc.body: The function returns a string that describes the status of a process object: if the passed pointer is NULL it reports that the process structure is missing, otherwise it reports the error message stored in the structure or, if no error is flagged, simply returns “Success”.

@lcmsysProcess_GetExceptionString@kcmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetExceptionString@kcmsys.body: The function checks that the supplied `kwProcess` object is non‑null, has a valid result buffer, and contains at least one command. If any of those conditions fails, it simply returns a static error message. When the process is in the *exception* state, it pulls the exit‑exception string from the last command in the result array and returns that. Otherwise, it indicates that no exception occurred by returning a “No exception” string.

@lcmsysProcess_GetExceptionStringByIndex.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetExceptionStringByIndex.body: The function checks that the requested index is within bounds, then returns the stored exception string only when the result state equals kwsysProcess_StateByIndex_Exception; if not, it returns the string “No exception”.

@lcmsysProcess_GetExitCode@kcmsysProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetExitCode@kcmsysProcess.body: It returns the exit code of the last command in the process if that command exists; otherwise it returns 0.

@lcmsysProcess_GetExitCodeByIndex@kcmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetExitCodeByIndex@kcmsys.body: The function retrieves the exit‑code stored at the given array index in a process object after ensuring the index is within bounds (the check macro does that), then returns the value from the CommandExitCodes table.

@lcmsysProcess_GetExitException@kcmsysPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetExitException@kcmsysPr.body: The function returns the exit‑exception value recorded for the most‑recent command in the process. If the process structure is nil, has no recorded results, or contains no commands, it falls back to a generic “other” exception constant.

@lcmsysProcess_GetExitExceptionByIndex@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetExitExceptionByIndex@k.body: It retrieves the exit‑exception value stored for the process at a specific slot. The function first verifies that the requested `idx` is within the valid range of exception indices (via the `KWSYSPE_IDX_CHK` macro) and then fetches the `ExitException` field from the `ProcessResults` array in the supplied `kwsysProcess` structure.

@lcmsysProcess_GetExitValue@kcmsysProces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetExitValue@kcmsysProces.body: The function `cmsysProcess_GetExitValue` safely retrieves the exit code of the most recent command in a `kwsysProcess` instance. It first verifies that the `kwsysProcess` pointer, its `ProcessResults` array, and the command count are all valid; if any of those checks fail, it returns `-1` to signal an error or “no command” condition. If valid, it returns the `ExitValue` field of the last command structure in the array.

@lcmsysProcess_GetExitValueByIndex@kcmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetExitValueByIndex@kcmsy.body: The function retrieves the exit value stored in the `ProcessResults` array at the supplied index. It first verifies the index is within bounds via the `KWSYSPE_IDX_CHK(-1)` macro, then returns that value.

@lcmsysProcess_GetOption@kcmsysProcess_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetOption@kcmsysProcess_G.body: The routine inspects a `kwProcess` instance and returns a corresponding flag value based on an enumerated option id. It first guards against a `NULL` handle, then discriminates over the supplied identifier to fetch the relevant field (`OptionDetach`, `MergeOutput`, `Verbatim`, or `CreateProcessGroup`). If the identifier is unrecognized, it yields zero.

@lcmsysProcess_GetState@kcmsysProcess_Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetState@kcmsysProcess_Ge.body: The routine examines the supplied pointer; if the pointer is non‑null it returns the stored state value, otherwise it falls back to a predefined “error” value.

@lcmsysProcess_GetStateByIndex@kcmsysPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_GetStateByIndex@kcmsysPro.body: Retrieves the state value stored at index `idx` in the process result array after a bounds check, and returns that integer.

@lcmsysProcess_Interrupt@kcmsysProcess_I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_Interrupt@kcmsysProcess_I.body: The routine first confirms the target process is still in the executing state and not already timed‑out or killed. Then, depending on whether a separate process group was created, it delivers an interrupt signal either to each child PID individually or to the whole group (via kill (0,…)), thus terminating the process and all of its descendants.

@lcmsysProcess_Kill@kcmsysProcess_Kill@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_Kill@kcmsysProcess_Kill@f.body:
The routine first verifies that the process is actually in the executing state; if not, it exits immediately. It then closes the write side of the signal‑pipe to prevent a SIGPIPE that might otherwise be raised when the child exits.  

On non‑Apple systems it calls a helper to close all the child‑side pipe read ends before any kill action is taken, guarding against Cygwin’s peculiar blocking behaviour when a child is waiting to write to a pipe.  

The core loop marks the process as “killed” and walks through every stored child PID: each one is sent a terminate signal and then repeatedly `waitpid()` until the wait is not interrupted by a signal.  

After all children are reaped, on Apple platforms the routine performs one final pass of the pipe‑closure helper (to avoid the “full pipe, write end still open” quirk). Finally it clears the count of commands left, signalling that no child commands remain.

@lcmsysProcess_KillPID@kcmsysProcess_Kil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_KillPID@kcmsysProcess_Kil.body: The routine forwards a numeric identifier to the lower‑level routine that terminates a process: it casts the supplied `unsigned long` value to a `pid_t` and invokes `kwsysProcessKill`.

@lcmsysProcess_New@kcmsysProcess_New@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_New@kcmsysProcess_New@f./.body: The function allocates a new `kwsysProcess` structure, zero‑initialises all its fields, and sets up its default state: the standard input is marked as shared with the parent process, no native pipes are opened (their file descriptors are set to `-1`), and the process state is marked as *Starting*. It returns the freshly‑constructed pointer (or `NULL` if the allocation fails).

@lcmsysProcess_ResetStartTime@kcmsysProc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_ResetStartTime@kcmsysProc.body: If the pointer is valid, the routine overwrites the process’s `StartTime` field with the current timestamp retrieved from `kwsysProcessTimeGetCurrent()`. If the pointer is `NULL`, it simply returns without making any changes.

@lcmsysProcess_SetCommand@kcmsysProcess_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_SetCommand@kcmsysProcess_.body: The routine first checks for a NULL handle and aborts early. It then iterates over every existing command in the process’s internal table, freeing each string and the array entries themselves, resetting the count of commands to zero. After de‑allocating the old command list it releases the array of command pointers. Finally, if a new command string is supplied it installs it via the helper routine and returns the result; otherwise it signals success with a 1.

@lcmsysProcess_SetOption@kcmsysProcess_S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_SetOption@kcmsysProcess_S.body: This routine updates a `kwsysProcess` instance by writing the supplied `value` into the field that matches the supplied `optionId`. It first guards against a nil pointer, then uses a `switch` over the identifier and assigns the corresponding member (`OptionDetach`, `MergeOutput`, `Verbatim`, or `CreateProcessGroup`) to the value. Any unrecognized `optionId` is ignored.

@lcmsysProcess_SetPipeFile@kcmsysProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_SetPipeFile@kcmsysProcess.body: The routine assigns a custom file path to one of the three standard‑pipe descriptors (stdin, stdout, or stderr) of a `kwsysProcess` object. It first checks that the process structure is non‑NULL, selects the appropriate member pointer based on the `prPipe` selector, frees any previously‑allocated string, and duplicates the supplied `file` path into that member. After setting the string it invokes the internal helpers to configure the native and shared‑memory pipes accordingly. If any allocation fails or an invalid pipe identifier is supplied, the function returns 0; otherwise it returns 1.

@lcmsysProcess_SetPipeNative@kcmsysProce.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_SetPipeNative@kcmsysProce.body: The routine assigns the supplied pair of file‑descriptor values to the struct member corresponding to the requested standard‑io channel (STDIN, STDOUT, or STDERR). If the pointer argument is null, the function clears the member entries to –1 and, in that case, it invokes the generic “file” and “shared” configuration helpers to ensure the internal state reflects that the native descriptors are no longer in use.

@lcmsysProcess_SetPipeShared@kcmsysProce.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_SetPipeShared@kcmsysProce.body: The function configures a `kwsysProcess` instance to treat a specified standard‑stream pipe (`STDIN`, `STDOUT`, or `STDERR`) as shared or not. It flips the corresponding `PipeShared…` flag to 1 or 0, then, if the pipe is marked shared, it explicitly disables any file‑based or native pipe redirection by invoking the helper setters with a zero argument.

@lcmsysProcess_SetTimeout@kcmsysProcess_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_SetTimeout@kcmsysProcess_.body: The function assigns a requested timeout to the `kwProcess` structure, clamps negative values to zero, and marks the cached `TimeoutTime` as stale by setting its second component to –1 so any dependent logic will recompute it on next use.

@lcmsysProcess_SetWorkingDirectory@kcmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_SetWorkingDirectory@kcmsy.body: This function updates the `WorkingDirectory` field of a `kwsysProcess` instance. It first checks for a valid pointer, returns `0` if the process pointer is null, and returns `1` immediately if the new directory string is identical to the current one (by pointer or string comparison). If the directory differs, it frees the existing string (if any), duplicates the new path with `strdup`, and returns `1` on success or `0` if memory allocation fails.

@lcmsysProcess_WaitForData@kcmsysProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_WaitForData@kcmsysProcess.body: The routine blocks until data appears on any of the process’s pipes or until the user‑specified timeout expires. It walks through the available pipes, returns the ID of the pipe that provided data, updates the remaining timeout in the caller‑supplied `userTimeout` pointer, and if no data arrives before the timeout, it reports a timeout condition (or, if the process itself timed out, it aborts the child processes and returns a “none” indicator).

@lcmsysProcess_WaitForExit@kcmsysProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_WaitForExit@kcmsysProcess.body: The routine blocks until all child processes finish or a timeout occurs, then iterates over each command’s termination status. It translates wait‑pid return codes into the internal state machine, recording exit codes, exceptions, and any signal‑based abnormal exit. Finally it records the overall process state and performs a uniform cleanup.

@lcmsysString_strcasecmp@kcmsysString_st.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysString_strcasecmp@kcmsysString_st.body: The routine performs a case‑insensitive string comparison. It dispatches to a platform‑specific helper (e.g. `_stricmp` or `strcasecmp`) when available; otherwise it falls back to a fast table‑lookup loop that normalizes both operands to lower case before performing a byte‑wise difference. The function returns the lexical difference value in the same convention as standard `strcmp`.

@lcmsysString_strncasecmp@kcmsysString_s.author: AI Short Overview

@lcompatibilityAgree@k_ZL18compatibility.author: AI Short Overview

@lcompatibilityType@k_ZL17compatibilityT.author: AI Short Overview

@lconsistentNumberProperty@k_ZL24consist.author: AI Short Overview
@lconsistentNumberProperty@k_ZL24consist.body: The function parses two strings as signed integers. If either string fails to parse, it returns {false,nullptr}. @lconsistentProperty@k_Z18consistentProp.author: AI Short Overview

@ldo_build@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_18do_buildEi.body: The routine parses command‑line options for a cmake build, sets up the requested preset, target list, parallel job level, and clean/resolve flags, configures progress callbacks, and finally invokes the internal build engine with those parameters.

@ldo_cmake::[lambda_4]@kdo_cmake::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_cmake::[lambda_4]@kdo_cmake::[lambd.body: The lambda captures the variable `cm` by reference and, when invoked, forwards its two arguments (`msg` and `md`) along with a pointer to `cm` to the function `cmakemainMessageCallback`.

@ldo_cmake::[lambda_5]@kdo_cmake::[lambd.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_cmake::[lambda_5]@kdo_cmake::[lambd.body: The call registers a callback that captures the current `cm` instance by reference. When invoked, it forwards the supplied message and progress value to `cmakemainProgressCallback`, passing a pointer to the originating `cm` object.

@ldo_cmake@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_18do_cmakeEi.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_cmake@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_18do_cmakeEi.body: Parses command‑line arguments for CMake, configuring options such as –‑i, –‑system-information, and cache‑listing flags. It then creates a cmake instance, sets callbacks, and executes the selected mode (project, script, or package‑search). Finally it returns an error code indicating success or failure.

@ldo_command@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110do_comm.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_command@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110do_comm.body: The function builds a vector of argument strings from the supplied `ac`/`av` array, then passes that vector along with the console buffer to `cmcmd::ExecuteCMakeCommand`, returning the command’s result.

@ldo_install::[lambda_0]@kdo_install::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_install::[lambda_0]@kdo_install::[l.body: This lambda ignores its string argument, sets an external flag `verbose` to `true`, and always returns `true`.

@ldo_install::[lambda_1]@kdo_install::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_install::[lambda_1]@kdo_install::[l.body: Captures a reference `cm` and, upon being invoked with a message string and accompanying metadata, forwards these arguments to `cmakemainMessageCallback`.

@ldo_install::[lambda_2]@kdo_install::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_install::[lambda_2]@kdo_install::[l.body: Sets a progress‑listener that forwards the message, progress value and a pointer to the current `cm` object to the `cmakemainProgressCallback` routine.

@ldo_install@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110do_inst.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_install@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110do_inst.body: The `do_install` routine sets up a `cmake` script to perform a project install. It first parses the command‑line arguments (`--config`, `--component`, `--default-directory-permissions`, `--prefix`, `--strip`, and verbosity flags) and validates that a target directory has been supplied. It then configures a `cmake` instance with appropriate callbacks and options derived from those arguments, builds a vector of `cmake`‑style switches (including the `-DCMAKE_INSTALL_*` options), and finally invokes `cm.Run` with those arguments, returning `0` on success or `1` on failure.

@ldo_open::[lambda_0]@kdo_open::[lambda_.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_open::[lambda_0]@kdo_open::[lambda_.body: This lambda captures a reference to `cm` and simply forwards the supplied `msg` and `md` arguments to `cmakemainMessageCallback`, passing along a pointer to the captured `cm`.

@ldo_open::[lambda_1]@kdo_open::[lambda_.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_open::[lambda_1]@kdo_open::[lambda_.body: The lambda captures the current `cm` object by reference and forwards the two parameters (`msg` and `prog`) to the helper `cmakemainProgressCallback` together with a pointer to the same `cm` instance. It effectively hooks the `cm` object's own progress‑callback mechanism into the external callback routine.

@ldo_open@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17do_openEiPK.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_open@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17do_openEiPK.body: The routine receives a directory path as its first user‑supplied argument, validates that it is non‑empty, hooks up message and progress callbacks on a `cmake` instance, and then calls `cm.Open(dir, false)`, returning 0 on success or 1 on failure.

@ldo_workflow::[lambda_2]@kdo_workflow::.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_workflow::[lambda_2]@kdo_workflow::.body: The lambda captures a reference to `cm` and immediately forwards the supplied message and its metadata to `cmakemainMessageCallback`, passing along a pointer to the captured `cm` instance.

@ldo_workflow::[lambda_3]@kdo_workflow::.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_workflow::[lambda_3]@kdo_workflow::.body: The call registers a progress‑reporting handler that forwards the received message and progress value to cmakemainProgressCallback, passing along a pointer to the current cm instance for use inside that routine.

@ldo_workflow@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111do_wor.author: AI Short Overview
@ldo_workflow@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111do_wor.body: The routine parses the supplied options (preset name, whether to list presets, or request a fresh build), displays a help message if none of the required arguments are given, installs internal callbacks for messaging and progress reporting, and finally invokes cmake’s Workflow routine with the resolved parameters.

@ldup_field@kdup_field@f./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@ldup_field@kdup_field@f./Source/CursesD.body: Creates a copy of an existing FIELD structure at a specified row/col. It allocates space for a new FIELD, copies all of the original’s attributes (including buffer contents), and returns the new instance; if allocation fails, it frees any partially‑created structure and reports an error.

@ldynamic_field_info@kdynamic_field_info.author: AI Short Overview
@ldynamic_field_info@kdynamic_field_info.body: When called, the routine verifies that the supplied `FIELD` structure is non‑null and, if the caller provided non‑null pointers for the output arguments, copies `field->drows`, `field->dcols`, and `field->maxgrow` into them. It then returns `E_OK`; otherwise it returns `E_BAD_ARGUMENT`.

@lentry_to_remove::entry_to_remove@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lentry_to_remove::entry_to_remove@k_ZN1.body: The function `entry_to_remove` takes a temporary `entry_to_remove` instance (passed as an rvalue reference) and removes the corresponding entry from its owning data structure, typically returning a status or updating container state.

@lentry_to_remove::entry_to_remove@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lentry_to_remove::entry_to_remove@k_ZN1.body: The function pulls optional prefix‑related entries from the supplied makefile and stores them as its internal state.

@lentry_to_remove::entry_to_remove@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lentry_to_remove::entry_to_remove@k_ZN1.body: The `entry_to_remove` function accepts an object of type `entry_to_remove`, copies the data from that object into a new instance of the same type, and then performs any cleanup or deletion logic required for the entry. It is used in various parts of the code, for instance cleanup at line 339 of `cmFindBase.cxx` and elsewhere where an `entry_to_remove` instance must be dropped or destroyed.

@lentry_to_remove::remove_self@k_ZNK12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lentry_to_remove::remove_self@k_ZNK12_G.body: If the object is considered valid, remove_self looks through the vector for a string equal to its stored value. Once that element is located (after skipping count entries), the function erases it from the vector, effectively deleting that entry.

@lentry_to_remove::valid@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lentry_to_remove::valid@k_ZNK12_GLOBAL_.body: Returns true only when the stored string is non‑empty and the internal counter is greater than zero.

@lescapeDependencyPath@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lescapeDependencyPath@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The routine walks the input path character‑by‑character, inserting escape sequences for `$`, `#`, and spaces while preserving the original content, then returns the transformed string.

@lescapeForShellOldStyle@k_ZL22escapeFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lescapeForShellOldStyle@k_ZL22escapeFor.body: The function examines whether the input contains spaces. On Windows, if the string contains spaces but no internal quotation marks it is returned surrounded by double‑quotes; otherwise the string is returned unchanged. On non‑Windows systems it escapes each space by prefixing it with a backslash before returning the transformed string.

@lexit@kexit.author: AI Short Overview
@lexit@kexit.body: The `exit(int)` routine is a thin wrapper around the standard termination call that accepts a status code. It’s used throughout the code base to signal shutdown—e.g., `exit(YY_EXIT_FAILURE)` signals a failure condition. The wrapper typically performs any pre‑exit bookkeeping such as flushing diagnostics, releasing resources, or logging a message before delegating to the underlying termination primitive.

@lextract_job_number@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lextract_job_number@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: extract_job_number parses a job‑count string, validates that it’s a positive integer that fits into an int, and falls back to a predefined parallel‑level if the string is empty. If the string fails validation it writes an error message and returns –1.

@lextract_tar@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111extrac.author: AI Short Overview
@lextract_tar@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111extrac.body: The function opens the specified tar archive, iterates over its entries, and extracts only those files that match a supplied inclusion list. It optionally preserves timestamps, outputs progress when verbose, and cleans up all resources before returning a success flag.

@lfclose@kfclose.author: AI Short Overview
@lfclose@kfclose.body: `fclose()` closes a file stream. It flushes any buffered output, releases file‑descriptor resources, and returns **0** on success or **EOF** (typically ‑‑1) on failure. In the code base it’s invoked with `fclose(lexer->file);` to shut down the lexer’s input file. The function assumes a valid `FILE*`; passing `NULL` or an already‑closed stream can trigger undefined behavior or a return value indicating error.

@lfgetpos@kfgetpos.author: AI Short Overview
@lfgetpos@kfgetpos.body:
`fgetpos` reads the current file offset of a file descriptor.  
When called as `fgetpos(f, &p)`, it writes that offset into the supplied pointer `p` and returns an `int` status code.

@lfield_arg@kfield_arg@f./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_arg@kfield_arg@f./Source/CursesD.body: The function takes a pointer to a `FIELD`, normalises that structure and returns its `arg` member as a `void *` pointer.

@lfield_back@kfield_back@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_back@kfield_back@f./Source/Curse.body: Retrieves the `back` attribute of a field instance.

@lfield_buffer@kfield_buffer@f./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_buffer@kfield_buffer@f./Source/C.body: It returns the address of the requested buffer when the index lies within the field’s valid range; otherwise it yields a NULL pointer.

@lfield_fore@kfield_fore@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_fore@kfield_fore@f./Source/Curse.body: The macro `GEN_FIELD_ATTR_GET_FCT(fore)` expands to a small inline function that retrieves the value of the `fore` member of a struct. It typically accepts a pointer to the containing instance and returns the member’s value, usually performing a simple dereference of the member field. This getter is designed to be efficient and type‑safe, often inlined by the compiler for zero‑overhead access.

@lfield_index@kfield_index@f./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_index@kfield_index@f./Source/Cur.body: The `field_index` helper safely extracts the `index` value from a `FIELD` instance: if the supplied pointer and its `form` member are valid, it returns that member; otherwise it yields –1 to signal an absent or invalid field.

@lfield_info@kfield_info@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_info@kfield_info@f./Source/Curse.body: The routine returns the dimensions and buffer parameters of a `FIELD` object: it copies the field’s row, column, and buffer counts into the caller‑supplied integers, after validating the input pointer.

@lfield_init@kfield_init@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_init@kfield_init@f./Source/Curse.body: The function `field_init` sets up a new field instance: it allocates its storage, zeros out essential members, and assigns the supplied initial values to the field’s members. It also checks arguments for validity and returns a status flag indicating success or failure.

@lfield_just@kfield_just@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_just@kfield_just@f./Source/Curse.body: The routine normalizes the supplied `FIELD` instance and returns the value stored in its `just` member.

@lfield_opts_off@kfield_opts_off@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_opts_off@kfield_opts_off@f./Sour.body: Disables the selected flags in a field’s options bit‑mask. It first validates that the supplied mask is a subset of the defined options mask (`ALL_FIELD_OPTS`). If the mask is valid, the function normalises the field (presumably to keep invariants) and then clears those bits in `field->opts` by calling `_nc_Synchronize_Options`. The routine returns the status of that operation (typically `0` on success or an error code).

@lfield_status@kfield_status@f./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_status@kfield_status@f./Source/C.body: Checks if a field’s status flag indicates a change—by normalising the field and testing the `_CHANGED` bit, it returns true when that bit is set, otherwise false.

@lfield_term@kfield_term@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_term@kfield_term@f./Source/Curse.body: The `field_term` routine (invoked via `GEN_HOOK_GET_FUNCTION(field,term)`) fetches the specific “term” value for a field in a hook context. It locates the field descriptor, reads its associated term metadata, and returns that term (typically as a string or structured token) to the caller.

@lfield_type@kfield_type@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_type@kfield_type@f./Source/Curse.body: `field_type` receives a constant `FIELD` pointer and returns a pointer to the `type` member of the normalized `FIELD` instance (`Normalize_Field(field)->type`).

@lfield_userptr@kfield_userptr@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_userptr@kfield_userptr@f./Source.body: The function normalises the supplied `FIELD` structure and returns its `usrptr` member, which points to the user‑supplied data stored in that field.

@lfileno@kfileno.author: AI Short Overview
@lfileno@kfileno.body: `fileno()` returns the underlying file‑descriptor integer for a `File*`. It’s a thin wrapper that extracts the native `int fd` field from a file object (or otherwise returns –1 for a null/invalid file) so callers can pass that value to functions like `isatty()` to test whether the descriptor is connected to a terminal.

@lfindFilesIn@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111findFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lfindFilesIn@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111findFi.body: The function creates a `Glob` instance to search recursively under the given path (without following symlinks), collects the found file names, throws a runtime_error if the search yields none, sorts the list for deterministic ordering, and returns the vector of file paths.

@lfopen@kfopen.author: AI Short Overview
@lfopen@kfopen.body: fopen is a thin wrapper that opens a file with a given mode and returns a handle (or NULL on failure) that callers use for subsequent I/O.

@lform_driver@kform_driver@f./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_driver@kform_driver@f./Source/Cur.body: The routine first checks that the supplied form is properly linked and in a valid state, then matches the command code to an entry in a dispatch table of handlers. If a match is found, the corresponding handler is invoked; otherwise it falls back to a generic field‑edit routine. Finally, the current field is refreshed and the routine returns a status code.

@lform_init@kform_init@f./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_init@kform_init@f./Source/CursesD.body: `GEN_HOOK_GET_FUNCTION(form,init)` expands to a function named `form_init` that performs the initial setup for a form component. The function typically registers the form with the system, registers its fields, sets up default values and validation callbacks, and hooks any custom event handlers required for the form’s lifecycle.

@lform_opts@kform_opts@f./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_opts@kform_opts@f./Source/CursesD.body: It normalizes the incoming `FORM`, masks its option flags with `ALL_FORM_OPTS`, and returns that filtered set.

@lform_opts_off@kform_opts_off@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_opts_off@kform_opts_off@f./Source.body: Disables any of the bits in `opts` that are defined in `ALL_FORM_OPTS`; if any flag outside that mask is supplied it returns an error, otherwise it clears those bits from the form’s options.

@lform_opts_on@kform_opts_on@f./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_opts_on@kform_opts_on@f./Source/C.body: The function takes a form and an options mask, validates that the mask contains only allowed bits, normalizes the form if needed, applies the option bits to the form’s options field, and returns `E_OK` or an error code.

@lform_sub@kform_sub@f./Source/CursesDia.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_sub@kform_sub@f./Source/CursesDia.body: The `form_sub` routine simply normalizes the supplied `FORM` instance and then fetches the window object that corresponds to that normalized form. In short, it normalizes the form and returns the window associated with the normalized form.

@lform_term@kform_term@f./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_term@kform_term@f./Source/CursesD.body: The routine constructs a term entity from supplied components, normalising values and enforcing consistency constraints defined by the domain model.

@lform_win@kform_win@f./Source/CursesDia.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_win@kform_win@f./Source/CursesDia.body: Returns the window stored in the form; if none is set, it falls back to the default screen (stdscr).

@lfprintf@kfprintf.author: AI Short Overview
@lfprintf@kfprintf.body: fprintf is a standard I/O routine that writes formatted text to a specified output stream. It receives a FILE* pointer (the destination stream) followed by a format string and optional arguments that fill in format specifiers. The function processes the format string, substitutes the provided arguments, and writes the resulting output to the stream; it returns the number of bytes written or a negative value if an error occurs.

@lfread@kfread.author: AI Short Overview
@lfread@kfread.body: The `fread` routine copies a specified block of data from a file into a supplied buffer, returning the number of bytes that were actually read. In the lexer’s parsing loop it is called to fill a segment of the buffer just before the next token extraction step.

@lfree@kfree.author: AI Short Overview
@lfree@kfree.body: The `free` routine simply releases a dynamically‑allocated block pointed to by its argument; it deallocates the memory, clears the pointer reference in the caller, and performs no further side‑effects. It expects a valid address (or `nullptr`) and returns nothing.

@lfree_field@kfree_field@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfree_field@kfree_field@f./Source/Curse.body: The `free_field` function deallocates a `FIELD` structure safely. It first validates the pointer, checks whether the field is still linked or in use, and then either frees a lone field or detaches it from a circular chain before releasing its type information. Finally, it frees the field itself and signals success.

@lfree_fieldtype@kfree_fieldtype@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lfree_fieldtype@kfree_fieldtype@f./Sour.body: The routine verifies that the supplied `FIELDTYPE` pointer is non‑null, then checks that it is not currently referenced elsewhere (`ref` is zero) or marked as in‑use (`_RESIDENT` bit). If the type has left/right links, it decrements their reference counters before finally freeing the structure with `free()`. On success it returns `E_OK`; otherwise it returns an error code (`E_BAD_ARGUMENT` or `E_CONNECTED`).

@lfree_form@kfree_form@f./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lfree_form@kfree_form@f./Source/CursesD.body: The routine first guards against a NULL pointer and a “posted” flag. If the form is still editable, it calls Disconnect_Fields to drop any field links, frees the inner page buffer if present, and finally releases the form structure itself, signalling success with E_OK or an error code for bad arguments or an already‑posted form.

@lfseek@kfseek.author: AI Short Overview
@lfseek@kfseek.body:
`fseek` is a thin wrapper around the standard `fseek` operation.  
It takes a file pointer, an offset, and a mode (e.g., `SEEK_SET`, `SEEK_CUR`, `SEEK_END`) and moves the file’s current read/write position accordingly.  
The function returns `0` on success and `-1` on failure, propagating the same semantics as the underlying POSIX `fseek`.  
Use it just before any file I/O that depends on an explicit file position, like the error‑checking in `cmListFileLexer.c` where the call to `fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET)` validates that the file descriptor `f` can be reset to the beginning for subsequent parsing.

@lfsetpos@kfsetpos.author: AI Short Overview
@lfsetpos@kfsetpos.body: fsetpos likely receives a file descriptor and a pointer to an integer that will receive the new file offset. It attempts to move the file pointer to the specified position and returns 0 on success, a non‑zero error code otherwise. The call in cmListFileLexer.c checks this return value to decide whether the seek succeeded.

@lgetExpectedOptions@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetExpectedOptions@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: Creates a small list containing the four predefined option names – kTreeOptionName, kPrefixOptionName, kFilesOptionName, and kRegexOptionName – and returns that list.

@lgetInputPath@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112getIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetInputPath@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112getIn.body: The function `getInputPath` looks up a definition in the current makefile for the supplied argument string. If no definition is found, it records an error in the status object and returns `false`; otherwise it copies the definition’s string value into `path` and returns `true`.

@lgetLinkInterfaceDependentProperty@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetLinkInterfaceDependentProperty@k_Z3.body: The function dispatches on the type of a property value and forwards the request to the target object’s corresponding getter. For `StringType` it returns the string property; for numeric bounds it returns the min or max string; for boolean it asserts failure and returns `nullptr`. If an unknown type is supplied the function asserts and returns `nullptr`.

@lgetLinkInterfaceDependentProperty@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetLinkInterfaceDependentProperty@k_Z3.body:
The function retrieves a property value that is specific to the link‑interface type associated with a given target.  
It accepts a pointer to a `cmGeneratorTarget`, inspects its internal link‑interface identifier (e.g., a value from an enum or a string key), and then queries the property store or lookup table that maps interface identifiers to concrete `PropertyType` values. The returned `PropertyType` is the one that is meant to be used for that particular link interface.

@lgetLinkInterfaceDependentProperty@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetLinkInterfaceDependentProperty@k_Z3.body: The helper template forwards a request to the target’s GetLinkInterfaceDependentBoolProperty method, passing along the property name and configuration string, and returns the resulting boolean value. The CompatibleType and bool‑pointer parameters are unused and can be ignored.

@lgetLinkedTargetsContent@k_ZL23getLinke.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetLinkedTargetsContent@k_ZL23getLinke.body:
The function walks through each linked library of a target.  
For each library that has a target it creates a temporary evaluation context, calls that target’s `EvaluateInterfaceProperty` for the requested property, and, if a non‑empty string is returned, appends it to a string that is returned, separating values with semicolons.

@lgetMessageColor@k_ZL15getMessageColor1.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetMessageColor@k_ZL15getMessageColor1.body: The function maps a `MessageType` to a terminal foreground color code: internal, fatal, and author errors yield red, author warnings and general warnings yield yellow, and all other cases return the normal color.

@lgetNumWidth@k_Z11getNumWidthm@f./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetNumWidth@k_Z11getNumWidthm@f./Sourc.body: The function computes how many decimal digits an integer contains. It starts with a width of 1 and repeatedly divides the value by 10, incrementing the width counter until the value drops below 10, then returns that count.

@lgetSourceGroupFilesPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetSourceGroupFilesPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function returns a set of file paths with the given root directory stripped from each path.

@lgetStringToLogLevelPairs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetStringToLogLevelPairs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function declares a static const array of `LevelsPair` objects that pair each string identifier ("error", "warning", etc.) with the corresponding `Message::LogLevel` enum value, then returns a reference to this array. This allows callers to look up a log‑level value by its string name without constructing a new array each time.

@lgetTypedProperty@k_Z16getTypedProperty.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetTypedProperty@k_Z16getTypedProperty.body: The function retrieves a property value from the given target, optionally passing that value through a supplied interpreter; if no interpreter is supplied it simply returns the property value converted to a string, otherwise the interpreter processes and evaluates it before returning the result.

@lget_prefixes@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112get_p.author: AI Short Overview
@lget_prefixes@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112get_p.body: Retrieves the defined prefix list from a `cmMakefile`; if that definition exists it returns it, otherwise it supplies a compile‑time default (`";lib"` on Windows, `"lib"` otherwise).

@lget_suffixes@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112get_s.author: AI Short Overview
@lget_suffixes@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112get_s.body: The function returns a string of library‑file suffixes: it first selects a compile‑time default list of suffixes (“.so;.a” for generic POSIX, “.tbd;.dylib;.so;.a” on Apple, “.sl;.so;.a” on HP‑UX, and “.lib;.dll.a;.a” on Windows) and then overrides that value if the current CMakefile contains a definition for “CMAKE_FIND_LIBRARY_SUFFIXES”. If that property is defined, the function returns its value; otherwise it falls back to the default list compiled into the static string.

@lgetattrs@kgetattrs.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetattrs@kgetattrs.body: The function `getattrs()` queries the current window’s attribute bits and returns a bitmask of those attributes. It’s called from the terminal‑driver to populate the attribute fields when the window’s state is restored or redrawn.

@lgetmaxyx@kgetmaxyx.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetmaxyx@kgetmaxyx.body: It determines the largest y‑axis and x‑axis extents a window can occupy and writes those values back to the caller.

@lgmtime@kgmtime.author: AI Short Overview
@lgmtime@kgmtime.body:
`gmtime` converts a `time_t` value into a `struct tm` representation for use in the rest of the code.  
It returns a pointer to a static buffer that is overwritten on each call, so no heap allocation is required.  
The function performs a standard conversion to GMT (or the host’s local time, depending on the system’s definition of `time_t`) and stores the result in that buffer before returning it.  
The implementation guards against null‑pointers and avoids copying large temporaries, providing fast, side‑effect‑free behaviour that callers can invoke repeatedly without worrying about memory management.

@lhandleQueryCommand::[lambda_0]@khandle.author: AI Short Overview
@lhandleQueryCommand::[lambda_0]@khandle.body: A lambda that takes a `const std::string&` and returns `true` when the string contains no characters.

@lkwsysSystem__AppendArgument@p@l./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lkwsysSystem__AppendArgument@p@l./Sourc.body: The routine appends a null‑terminated argument string to a dynamic array of argument pointers. It first ensures the string ends with a `'\0'` byte via a helper; if that fails it aborts. It then checks whether the backing array has room; if not, it reallocates a larger block (doubling the current size), copies the old pointers over, frees the old block, and updates the bounds pointers. After that, it allocates space for the new string itself, copies the string into that space, advances the end pointer, and finally clears the temporary buffer (`arg_begin`/`arg_end` are reset to the start). On success it returns 1, otherwise 0.

@lkwsysSystem__AppendByte@p@l./Source/kw.author: AI Short Overview

Finally it writes the supplied byte into the new buffer at the current end position and bumps that end pointer, returning 1 to signal success (or 0 when a malloc fails).

@lmemcpy@kmemcpy.author: AI Short Overview
@lmemcpy@kmemcpy.body:
The routine copies a specified byte‑count from a source buffer into a destination buffer and returns the destination pointer.  
Key points for use:

* **Signature** – `void* memcpy(void* dest, const void* src, unsigned long n);`  
* **Behavior** – Copies `n` bytes from `src` to `dest`. The caller must guarantee that `dest` has at least `n` bytes allocated.  
* **Overlap** – Overlapping regions produce undefined behaviour; use `memmove` if overlap is possible.  
* **Return value** – The returned pointer is the original `dest`, allowing call‑chaining.  

The function is employed in several modules (`ProcessUNIX.c`, `cmListFileLexer.c`, `fld_dup.c`, `frm_driver.c`, `System.c`) to transfer buffers without allocation overhead.

@lmemset@kmemset.author: AI Short Overview
@lmemset@kmemset.body: The `memset` routine is a low‑level, standard library primitive that writes a single byte value repeatedly into a contiguous block of memory and returns a pointer to that block. It is typically used to zero‑initialize or otherwise scrub buffers before they are reused, as in the examples shown. In practice it is essentially a thin wrapper around `memset` in the system C library that fills `n` bytes of the destination area with the byte value supplied in the third argument and then returns the address passed in the first argument.
