@lneedToQuoteTestName@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body:
The function inspects the policy status for CMP0110 in the makefile.  
* If the policy is set to **WARN** and the test name contains any forbidden character (`$[] #;\t\n"\\`), it emits a warning and returns **true** (the name must be quoted).  
* If the policy is **OLD** it never quotes the name and returns **false**.  
* For any other policy (`REQUIRED_*` or `NEW`) it simply returns **true**.  

Thus the routine decides whether the test name needs quoting based on the current CMP0110 policy.

@lphrase@p@l./Utilities/cmlibarchive/lib.body: The function consumes a token stream that represents a time‑or‑date phrase. It first tests whether the token sequence matches any of the predefined phrase handlers (time, zone, date, day) and, if matched, returns success immediately. If the token sequence begins with an “ago” token, it interprets it as a relative time unit and flips the sign of any existing relative offset. When the token is a bare number it interprets it in several contexts: a lone year, a full YYYYMMDD integer, or a simple hour or hour:minute encoding (e.g., 513 → 5:13). If any of these conditions is satisfied it updates the state fields (year, month, day, hour, minutes, seconds, relative offsets) and advances the token pointer, returning true. If no pattern matches it returns false.

@lpolicyForString@k_ZL15policyForStringP.author: AI Short Overview
@lpolicyForString@k_ZL15policyForStringP.body: The function converts a string name into its corresponding policy enum value. It defines a helper macro that compares the input string against each policy literal using `strcmp`, returning the matching `cmPolicies` enum when a match is found. It then expands a list macro that iterates over every known policy, invoking the helper macro for each. If none match, an assertion triggers and a default policy value is returned.

@lpost_form@kpost_form@f./Source/CursesD.author: AI Short Overview
@lpost_form@kpost_form@f./Source/CursesD.body: The routine validates the supplied form structure, refuses to run if it’s already posted or malformed, then checks that the form can fit into its target window. It forces a page re‑initialisation, sets the internal posted flag, runs the form‑ and field‑initialisation hooks, and finally refreshes the current field to make the form visible.

@lprepareFilesPathsForTree@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lprepareFilesPathsForTree@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: The function takes a list of input paths and a base directory, expands each path to an absolute path, drops entries that resolve to directories (or paths ending in a slash), and returns the remaining file paths in a new vector. It pre‑allocates the result vector for efficiency and uses the helper `CollapseFullPath` to perform the path resolution.

@lprintMessagePreamble@k_ZL20printMessag.author: AI Short Overview
@lprintMessagePreamble@k_ZL20printMessag.body: The function writes a header string into the supplied stream depending on the MessageType value and always returns true.

@lprintMessageText@k_ZL16printMessageTex.author: AI Short Overview
@lprintMessageText@k_ZL16printMessageTex.body: The function writes a prefix (a colon followed by a newline) into the supplied stream and then formats the given text with a fixed indentation of two spaces before sending it to the stream.

@lprocessILibs@k_ZL12processILibsRKNSt3_.author: AI Short Overview
@lprocessILibs@k_ZL12processILibsRKNSt3_.body: processILibs walks a target’s link‑interface libraries tree. It first checks whether the current link item’s target has already been recorded in the emitted set; if not, it records the target in tgts. Then, if the target supports the interface, it retrieves its linked libraries via GetLinkInterfaceLibraries and recurses into processILibs for each of those libraries, accumulating them while ensuring each target is processed only once by the emitted guard. This simple recursion propagates all indirect dependencies for a target.

@lprocessIncludeDirectories@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lprocessIncludeDirectories@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The function iterates over the include‑directory entries for a target, validating each path. It checks for missing files when the target was imported, issuing a fatal or warning message according to the CMP0027 policy. Relative paths are caught as errors (CMP0021), again depending on the policy status. Valid entries are normalised to Unix slashes, inserted into a set to avoid duplicates, and stored in the result vector; if debugging is enabled it accumulates the used paths for logging. The routine reports used includes at the end of each target’s evaluation.

@lprocessLinkDirectories@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lprocessLinkDirectories@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The routine walks through the target’s evaluated link‑directory entries, checks each path for absoluteness, reports any relative path according to the current policy, normalises slashes, and stores each unique directory in the supplied vector while keeping a set of already‑seen paths. If debugging is on, it also records and logs the directories that were actually used.

@lprocessObjectKindVersions@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lprocessObjectKindVersions@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The routine walks through the supplied version strings, parses each into major/minor numbers, and tries to register the first acceptable pair with the API. On first success it returns empty; otherwise it returns an error indicating none of the requested versions is supported.

@lprocessOptions@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114pro.author: AI Short Overview
@lprocessOptions@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114pro.body: The function iterates over each property entry in `entries`. For each option value it checks if the value is a device‑specific marker (`DL_BEGIN`/`DL_END`). When device options are enabled it inserts them separately and may split a `DL_BEGIN`‑prefixed option into its constituent arguments. Non‑duplicate options are stored in the `options` vector together with the entry’s back‑trace. When `debugOptions` is true, it records the option string in a debug log. After processing each entry it emits a log entry listing all options applied to the current target.

@lprocessSources@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114pro.author: AI Short Overview
@lprocessSources@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114pro.body: processSources iterates over the target’s evaluated property entries, resolves each source file’s full path (issuing warnings if any part is relative), records the resolved path in srcs (and in uniqueSrcs when new), optionally logs the source list when debugSources is true, and finally returns a flag indicating whether any of the processed entries was context‑dependent.

@lprocessTree@k_ZL11processTreeR10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lprocessTree@k_ZL11processTreeR10cmMake.body: The routine walks the internal tree of makefile nodes, applying any necessary transformations or updates, and reports whether the processing succeeded.

@lprocessTree@k_ZL11processTreeR10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lprocessTree@k_ZL11processTreeR10cmMake.body: The `processTree` function collects the target directory and optional prefix from the parsed arguments, gathers the list of source files (either from a supplied list or from the makefile’s non‑generated sources), normalises their paths relative to the current source directory, verifies that the target directory is a common prefix for all files, and finally registers those files in the corresponding source‑group entries. It returns `true` on success or `false` if the prefix check fails.

@lrealloc@krealloc.author: AI Short Overview
@lrealloc@krealloc.body: realloc performs a dynamic reallocation of a memory block: it allocates a new region of the requested size, copies existing contents up to the smaller of the old and new sizes, frees the old region if reallocation is necessary, and returns a pointer to the new block—or `nullptr` if the allocation cannot be satisfied.

@lrelativeIfUnder@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115re.author: AI Short Overview
@lrelativeIfUnder@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115re.body: The function checks whether the supplied `path` can be expressed relative to the directory `cur` without escaping the ancestor `top`. If it is a sub‑directory of `cur` (or of `cur` under `top`) it calls `ForceToRelativePath` to convert it to a relative form; otherwise it returns the original path unchanged.

@lrelunitphrase@p@l./Utilities/cmlibarch.author: AI Short Overview
@lrelunitphrase@p@l./Utilities/cmlibarch.body: The function examines the next few tokens in the input stream to see if they form a relative‑time phrase such as “‑3 hours”, “+1 minute”, “1 day”, “‑3 months”, etc. When a match is found it adjusts the running counters (`HaveRel`, `RelSeconds`, `RelMonth`) by the appropriate quantity and consumes the tokens, returning `1`. If no pattern matches, it returns `0`.

@lreportError@k_Z11reportErrorP28cmGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lreportError@k_Z11reportErrorP28cmGener.body: Marks the error flag in the passed context, optionally aborts early if the quiet flag is set, formats the diagnostic message with the expression and its result, and forwards it to the logger as a fatal error.

@lrequireDeviceLinking@k_Z20requireDevic.author: AI Short Overview
@lrequireDeviceLinking@k_Z20requireDevic.body: It checks whether the build configuration requires a device‑link step for a target. It first confirms CUDA is enabled, that the target isn’t just an object library, and that the makefile has the device‑link flag. It then examines the target’s CUDA properties (e.g. CUDA_RESOLVE_DEVICE_SYMBOLS, CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION) and its link dependencies. If any of these indicate that device code must be linked (for shared, module, or executable targets), it returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lrhash_final@krhash_final.author: AI Short Overview
@lrhash_final@krhash_final.body: The function finalises an ongoing hash computation: it writes the hash value into the supplied buffer and returns a status indicator.

@lrhash_free@krhash_free.author: AI Short Overview
@lrhash_free@krhash_free.body: The function `rhash_free` releases all dynamic memory owned by the `rhash` instance: it iterates over each bucket, frees any allocated entries and their keys/values, then deallocates the bucket array itself and finally clears the hash structure. It performs a guard‑check for a null pointer before any deallocation.

@lrhash_get_digest_size@krhash_get_diges.author: AI Short Overview
@lrhash_get_digest_size@krhash_get_diges.body: The function `rhash_get_digest_size` receives a hash‑algorithm identifier and returns the number of bytes that the corresponding digest occupies. It is typically used to allocate buffers of the correct length (as in the `std::vector` example). If the identifier is unknown, the function will return a non‑positive value (often 0) indicating that the digest length is not defined.

@lrhash_init@krhash_init.author: AI Short Overview
@lrhash_init@krhash_init.body: Creates an internal hashing context keyed by the supplied identifier and wires the internal tables and buffers needed for the subsequent cryptographic hash operations.

@lrhash_library_init@krhash_library_init.author: AI Short Overview
@lrhash_library_init@krhash_library_init.body: The `rhash_library_init` routine performs the one‑time bootstrap of the hashing subsystem: it builds the internal hash‑function registry, allocates the core data‑structures (like the hash‑state pool), and hooks in the platform’s memory‑allocation hooks. Once this work is completed, all other components can safely request hash operations without needing to re‑initialize the library.

@lrhash_reset@krhash_reset.author: AI Short Overview
@lrhash_reset@krhash_reset.body: The `rhash_reset` routine re‑initialises the supplied hash context to a clean state: it zeroes out the internal buffer, resets all counters (e.g., length, digest offset), and restores any required constants to their default values so the instance can be reused for a fresh hash computation.

@lrhash_update@krhash_update.author: AI Short Overview
@lrhash_update@krhash_update.body: The `rhash_update` routine consumes a pre‑initialised hash context, a raw data buffer and its length, and it mutates the internal state to incorporate that chunk of input. It returns an `int` status code – typically zero on success or a negative error value if the input was invalid or the context corrupted.

@lrootIsPrefix@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112rootI.author: AI Short Overview
@lrootIsPrefix@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_112rootI.body: The function iterates over each string in the supplied vector. If any entry does not start with the supplied `root` prefix, it writes a diagnostic message into the `error` string and returns `false`. If all entries match the prefix, it returns `true`.

@lset_current_field@kset_current_field@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_current_field@kset_current_field@f.body: The routine validates the supplied form and field, verifies that the field belongs to the form and is selectable, and if the form is not yet posted it simply assigns the field as the current one. For a posted form it first performs an internal validation; if the field differs from the current one it runs the necessary hooks (field‑term, form‑term, field‑init, form‑init) and possibly changes the page using `_nc_Set_Form_Page`). Finally it refreshes the form’s visual state and returns an error code that indicates success or the type of failure that occurred.

@lset_field_back@kset_field_back@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_field_back@kset_field_back@f./Sour.body: The `set_field_back` function is a small helper generated by the `GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT( back )` macro. It receives a pointer to a context/structure and a value, then writes that value into the corresponding field inside the context (usually after validating the pointer and possibly performing bounds checks). The macro also arranges the function to return an error code (often `0` on success or a negative value on failure).

@lset_field_buffer@kset_field_buffer@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_field_buffer@kset_field_buffer@f./.body: The routine copies a C‑style string into a specific buffer of a `FIELD` object. It validates the pointers and buffer index, optionally verifies that all characters are printable (for buffer 0), then, if the field is growable and the incoming string is longer than the current buffer, it expands the field’s storage first. After that, it copies the string into the target buffer using either a fast `memccpy` or a manual loop, pads the remainder of the buffer with blanks if the source string is shorter than the buffer, and finally synchronises any dependent fields or linked buffers before returning the status code.

@lset_field_fore@kset_field_fore@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_field_fore@kset_field_fore@f./Sour.body: The macro expands to a small inline function that assigns the supplied value to the target structure’s `fore` field, performing any type‑specific checks or side‑effects that the surrounding attribute system requires (e.g., validating ranges or updating dependent flags).

@lset_field_init@kset_field_init@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_field_init@kset_field_init@f./Sour.body: set_field_init assigns a specified field the provided initial value, using the GEN_HOOK_SET_FUNCTION macro to generate the appropriate setter logic for that field.

@lset_field_just@kset_field_just@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_field_just@kset_field_just@f./Sour.body: set_field_just validates a requested justification value against the acceptable values (NO_JUSTIFICATION, JUSTIFY_LEFT, JUSTIFY_CENTER, JUSTIFY_RIGHT). If the value is valid and differs from the current field justification, it normalizes the field and calls `_nc_Synchronize_Attributes` to apply the change, returning the status from that synchronization (or E_OK if no change is needed). If the value is invalid, it returns E_BAD_ARGUMENT.

@lset_field_status@kset_field_status@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_field_status@kset_field_status@f./.body: The function first calls `Normalize_Field` on the supplied field structure. It then toggles the `_CHANGED` bit in the field’s `status` member: if `status` is true, that bit is set; if false, the bit is cleared. Finally it returns the constant `E_OK` indicating success.

@lset_field_term@kset_field_term@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_field_term@kset_field_term@f./Sour.body: The macro expands to a lightweight setter that assigns the supplied value to the indicated field, handling pointer indirections safely and guarding against null‑value assignments.

@lset_field_userptr@kset_field_userptr@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_field_userptr@kset_field_userptr@f.body: The routine normalizes the target field structure, stores the supplied user pointer in its internal `usrptr` slot, and returns success (`E_OK`).

@lset_fieldtype_arg@kset_fieldtype_arg@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_fieldtype_arg@kset_fieldtype_arg@f.body: Assigns three function pointers (make, copy, free) to a field‑type descriptor and marks the descriptor as having argument support. It validates the inputs and returns an error code if either pointer is null.

@lset_form_init@kset_form_init@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_form_init@kset_form_init@f./Source.body: The `set_form_init` routine registers the form‑specific initialization routine via the `GEN_HOOK_SET_FUNCTION` macro, effectively wiring the form’s own `init` function into the hook system.

@lset_form_opts@kset_form_opts@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_form_opts@kset_form_opts@f./Source.body: The routine validates the supplied option mask against the predefined set of acceptable flags. It clears any bits outside that set by masking `opts` with `ALL_FORM_OPTS`. If any bits remain after masking, the function returns an error (`E_BAD_ARGUMENT`). Otherwise, it assigns the sanitized mask to the form’s options field via `Normalize_Form(form)` and reports success (`E_OK`).

@lset_form_sub@kset_form_sub@f./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_form_sub@kset_form_sub@f./Source/C.body: The routine assigns the supplied window to the form’s `sub` member after ensuring the form hasn’t already been submitted. If the form is flagged as posted, it returns the `E_POSTED` error code; otherwise it writes the new window reference into `form->sub` and returns `E_OK`.

@lset_form_term@kset_form_term@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_form_term@kset_form_term@f./Source.body: The `set_form_term` function (generated by the `GEN_HOOK_SET_FUNCTION(form,term)` macro) assigns the supplied `term` value to the form’s internal term field and updates any dependent state accordingly.

@lset_form_win@kset_form_win@f./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_form_win@kset_form_win@f./Source/C.body: When called with a non‑NULL form that has not yet been posted, the routine normalises the form structure and stores the supplied WINDOW pointer in the form’s internal win field, then returns success (E_OK). If the form is already posted, it aborts and returns the error code E_POSTED.

@lset_max_field@kset_max_field@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_max_field@kset_max_field@f./Source.body: If the input pointers are valid and the requested grow limit is non‑negative, the routine checks whether the field is a single‑line field. For a single‑line field it ensures the new maximum grows does not exceed the column count; for a multi‑line field it ensures it does not exceed the row count. If the new limit is zero or the current dimensions fall below that limit it marks the field as growable, otherwise it clears the grow flag. The function finally returns success unless the pre‑checks fail.

@lset_new_page@kset_new_page@f./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lset_new_page@kset_new_page@f./Source/C.body:
The routine normalises the supplied field structure and then checks whether the field’s form is already connected; if so it aborts with `E_CONNECTED`.  
If the `new_page_flag` is true, it sets the `_NEWPAGE` bit in `field->status`; otherwise it clears that bit.  
Finally it returns `E_OK` on success.

@lshouldAddContentLevel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lshouldAddContentLevel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: It returns true when the supplied level equals `ContentLevel` or when the helper `shouldAddFullLevel(level)` signals that a full level should be added.

@lshouldAddFullLevel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lshouldAddFullLevel@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: Checks whether the supplied `level` equals the `FullLevel` enumerator, returning that Boolean result.

@lsnprintf@ksnprintf.author: AI Short Overview
@lsnprintf@ksnprintf.body: snprintf writes a formatted string into a supplied buffer, ensuring not to overrun the buffer. It takes the target buffer, the buffer size, a format string and a variable argument list. The function returns the number of characters written (excluding the terminating NUL) or a negative value on failure. The buffer size argument protects against over‑write, making it a safer replacement for the standard snprintf.

@lsscanf@ksscanf.author: AI Short Overview
@lsscanf@ksscanf.body: The `sscanf` function behaves like the standard C `sscanf` routine: it parses a null‑terminated source string according to a format string and writes the resulting values into the provided addresses. The first argument is a pointer to the input string; the second argument is a format string that may contain conversion specifiers such as `%u` for unsigned integers and `%n` for recording the number of characters consumed. The `restrict` qualifier indicates that the two pointers cannot alias each other. The function returns an `int` that contains the number of input items successfully converted; it returns `EOF` (usually ‑1) on error. In the example shown, `sscanf` is used to parse an IPv4 dotted‑decimal address string into four `unsigned int` variables (`d1`‑`d4`) and records the length of the parsed string in `len`.

@lstatusForTarget@k_ZL15statusForTargetP.author: AI Short Overview
@lstatusForTarget@k_ZL15statusForTargetP.body: The function checks whether the supplied policy string matches one of the known policy names. It expands a macro that, for each policy, compares the string with that policy’s literal and, when it matches, returns the corresponding `GetPolicyStatusX` result from the target object. If no known policy string matches, it triggers an assertion failure and falls back to a warning status.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::hash_value.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::hash_value.body: Computes a hash of a filesystem path and returns it as a size_t value, which is used for quick equality checks or look‑ups elsewhere in the code.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::operator==.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::operator==.body: Compares two `path::iterator` instances by checking that both refer to the same `path` object and that the internal indices (or node pointers) are identical, returning `true` only when the two iterators represent the same position in the same sequence.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::begi.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::begi.body: The `begin()` member returns an iterator positioned at the very first element of the internal `Path` container. It creates this iterator by passing `this` and the underlying container’s `begin()` to the iterator’s constructor, enabling callers to iterate from the start of the path in a type‑safe way.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::clea.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::clea.body: The `clear()` method resets the class’s internal state: it clears all cached data structures, resets flags, and restores any default configuration values. In other parts of the system, calls to `clear()` are used to explicitly reset the engine’s working context before processing a new batch of input or after a termination event.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::comp.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::comp.body: The function returns an integer that indicates whether the current path object comes before, after, or is equal to the supplied `path` argument. It invokes the underlying `compare` routine on the two path instances and returns that result unchanged.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::empt.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::empt.body: The `empty()` member simply returns whether the wrapped path collection contains any elements. It is a `const` and `noexcept` helper used to guard against further mutation and to provide a quick boolean test for callers such as the `cmCMakePath` checks shown in the code.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::end@.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::end@.body: It returns an iterator that points to the end of the internal path container, allowing callers to traverse the path’s elements without modifying the container.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::exte.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::exte.body:
The function `extension()` is a public, `const` member that returns the part of the path after the last period (the file‑extension). It operates on the internal representation of the path (likely a `std::string` or similar) and simply forwards the call to the underlying `Path` object’s `extension()` method. Because it is marked `const`, callers can invoke it without modifying the path instance. Typical edge cases to be aware of are:

* The path contains no dot – in that case the function returns an empty string.
* The path ends with a dot (e.g., “file.”) – the returned extension will be an empty string as well.
* Paths that contain multiple periods (“archive.tar.gz”) – the function will return the substring after the last dot (“gz”).
* Hidden security concerns are minimal; however, ensure that the underlying `Path` implementation does not expose any private pointers or rely on mutable static state.

In practice, the method is usually used in helper wrappers like `cmCMakePath::GetExtension()`, which simply forwards the call and lets callers obtain the extension of a path in a type‑safe way.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::file.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::file.body: Returns the file‑name component of the internally stored path by delegating to the underlying Path object's `filename()` method.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::gene.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::gene.body: The template returns a `basic_string` constructed with the supplied allocator, using the allocator’s traits to forward the character type. It behaves like a normal string constructor but accepts an allocator parameter, ensuring the correct character traits are applied at compile‑time.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.body: `has_extension()` is a public const member that simply reports whether the underlying `Path` object contains a file extension. It forwards the query to the internal `Path` implementation and returns a `bool` reflecting the presence (or absence) of an extension segment.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.body: The function returns true when the underlying `Path` object contains a file‑name component. It’s used by `HasFileName()` to expose that check, returning whether the path ends with a non‑empty file name.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.body: The function checks whether the current path object contains a non‑root component, returning `true` when a valid parent segment is present and `false` otherwise.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.body: The function returns true when the current `Path` instance contains any relative components (e.g., “../”), otherwise it returns false; it simply forwards the query to the underlying `Path::has_relative_path()` implementation.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.body: The `has_root_directory()` function examines the internal `Path` object and returns `true` when that path contains a non‑empty root component (for example `C:\` on Windows or `/` on POSIX), and `false` otherwise. It is invoked by `cmCMakePath::HasRootDirectory()`, which simply forwards the result of this underlying check.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.body: Returns `true` if the underlying `Path` object holds a non‑empty root name; otherwise `false`. It simply forwards the check to `Path::has_root_name()` and returns that value.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.body: The function simply forwards the call to the underlying path object and returns whether that path contains a root component (e.g., “/” on POSIX or a drive‑letter and colon on Windows). It reports true only when the stored path string begins with a root indicator, otherwise false.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::has_.body: `has_stem` returns a `bool` indicating whether the current `Path` object contains a stem component, delegating the check to the underlying `Path` implementation. It is invoked elsewhere (e.g., `cmCMakePath.h` line 606) to query this state.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::is_a.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::is_a.body: The `is_absolute()` member simply tells you whether the wrapped `Path` object represents an absolute path. It forwards the check to `Path.is_absolute()` and returns that result. When the function returns `true`, the path begins with a root component (e.g., a leading “/” on Unix or a drive letter on Windows); otherwise it is a relative path. This boolean is used throughout the code wherever downstream logic must know whether a path is absolute before performing operations that assume that property.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::is_r.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::is_r.body: The `is_relative()` member simply forwards to the underlying `Path` representation to indicate whether the stored path string is relative (i.e., doesn’t start with a root component). It returns `true` when the path has no leading slash (or equivalent root marker on Windows), otherwise `false`. The function is a const accessor, so it has no side‑effects and can be safely called from any context. Its contract assumes the `Path` object is already constructed; callers should not invoke it on a default‑constructed or otherwise‑invalidated instance.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::iter.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::iter.body: Creates a new iterator instance that points to the same position in the same underlying data structure as the provided iterator, copying over any internal references and state. No dynamic allocation beyond simple member copying is performed.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::iter.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::iter.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::iter.body: The function increments the iterator to point to the next element in the underlying container and returns a reference to the iterator itself (after the increment). It updates any internal state (such as current position) and may check for end‑sentinel conditions, potentially throwing an exception if incrementing past the last element. @lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::lexi.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::lexi.body: The `lexically_normal` function returns a canonical representation of the stored path string. It trims any leading or trailing whitespace, collapses consecutive slashes, and normalises back‑references (`..`) and current‑directory markers (`.`). No filesystem resolution is performed; the output is purely a string that respects the lexical rules expected by other parts of the code.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::lexi.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::lexi.body: The function returns a canonical or “closest‑in‑lexical‑order” copy of the supplied path, used internally for path resolution and matching within the system’s path hierarchy.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::lexi.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::lexi.body: The `lexically_relative` function computes a relative path by stripping the common prefix of the current `path` object from a supplied base path. It normalizes path separators, resolves “.” and “..” segments, and returns a new path that preserves the original object’s const‑ness, ensuring no side‑effects. It performs minimal checks—returning the input unchanged if the base is empty or identical, and throws a clear exception only when the base cannot be resolved relative to the current path.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::oper.body: The function takes a pointer to a `value_type` and appends the pointed‑to object to the current instance, returning *this. @lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::oper.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::path.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::repl.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::repl.body: The function takes a `path` reference as input and produces a new `path` reference that contains the same base path but with the extension part replaced by whatever new extension the implementation supplies. @lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::repl.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::root.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::root.author: AI Short Overview

It simply returns the stored `root` member (or computes it from the current path if stored) without side‑effects, enabling callers to retrieve the base location for further path construction.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::stem.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::stem.body: The `stem()` member simply extracts and returns the final path component – the file name without any extension – from the stored path string. It typically walks backwards to the last path separator (supporting both `/` and `\\` on the relevant platform) and returns the substring that follows it. If the path ends with a separator or contains no separator at all, the function returns the original string unchanged. It performs this operation in‑place without altering the internal `Path` state.

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::stri.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::swap.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::__fs::filesystem::path::swap.body: The `swap` routine exchanges the internal state of two `path` instances in place‑for‑the‑runtime, typically by invoking the move semantics of `std::swap` or a member‑swap on the underlying path representation. It guarantees strong exception safety—no observable state change if the underlying operation throws—and leaves each caller’s path unchanged except for their new identities, making it a drop‑in replacement for normal `std::swap`.

@lstd::__1::all_of@k_ZNSt3__16all_ofB7v1.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::all_of@k_ZNSt3__16all_ofB7v1.body: This template evaluates a range: given two iterators delineating a range and a predicate, it returns `true` if the predicate holds for every element in that range and `false` otherwise.

@lstd::__1::back_inserter@k_ZNSt3__113ba.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::basic_string::~basic_string@.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::basic_str.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::basic_str.body: `basic_string_view` is a small helper that accepts a `const _CharT*` (typically a C‑style string) and returns a lightweight view type (`cm::string_view`) that can be passed to formatting helpers like `FormatPath`. It’s used, for example, in `cmCMakePath.h` where a `Path` is constructed from a `string_view` of a source string.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::basic_str.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::basic_str.body: The `basic_string_view` function creates and returns a non‑owning view of a string‑like container, optionally parameterized by character traits. It can be invoked on existing strings or string‑view objects to obtain a lightweight handle that supports sub‑range access and efficient copying of the underlying sequence without allocating new memory.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::basic_str.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::basic_str.body: `basic_string_view` creates a lightweight string-view object that simply holds a pointer to the supplied text and its length, avoiding any allocation or copying. It is used throughout the build system to pass string data around efficiently—e.g., in `cmSeparateArgumentsCommand` when adding a definition and in `cmWindowsRegistry` for root, subkey, and value names—so callers can share the same underlying buffer without incurring copy overhead.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::begin@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::begin@k_Z.body: The `begin()` member returns a read‑only iterator that points to the first character of the underlying string view. The iterator is const‑qualified, so dereferencing yields a `char` that may not be modified. It can be used directly in a range‑based `for` loop to scan the entire view without copying the string data. The iterator remains valid until the `string_view` object is destroyed or its internal buffer is invalidated; any mutation to the source string may invalidate the iterator.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::compare@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::compare@k.body: The function performs a lexicographic comparison between the internal string view of the current object and another string view that is passed in as an argument. It returns a negative integer if the current view is lexicographically less than the argument, zero if they are equal, and a positive integer if it is greater. The comparison uses the supplied character traits for ordering and optionally for case‑insensitivity.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::copy@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::copy@k_ZN.body: Copies the requested number of elements of a character buffer into a target buffer, returning the number of elements actually written. The call in *cmString.cxx* simply forwards the request to the underlying view’s copy implementation, using the provided destination pointer, count of items to copy, and the source position offset.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::data@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::data@k_ZN.body: The `data()` function is a public const accessor that returns a pointer to the object’s internal data buffer. It does not modify the object; it merely yields a read‑only view of the underlying storage so callers can read the contents without changing state.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::empty@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::empty@k_Z.body: Checks whether a string contains any characters, returning true when it has no elements. It is used in the code to guard against null‑front accesses by verifying the string’s length before further processing.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::end@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::end@k_ZNK.body: The `end()` function returns the iterator that represents the logical end of the string view; it points just past the last character so that any loop or algorithm that scans the view can stop when that iterator is reached.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::find@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::find@k_ZN.body: The function performs a substring search on a string view: it returns the zero‑based index where the searched sequence first occurs, or the special npos value when it is absent.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::find@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::find@k_ZN.body: find scans a buffer for a pattern and returns the offset where the pattern occurs (or a special sentinel value if not found).

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::find@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::find@k_ZN.body: The `find` method scans a sequence of type `CharT` starting from a specified index and returns the position where the target value occurs; if the value is not present it returns the sequence length (the sentinel value `size_type` indicates “not found”). If `start` is past the end it simply returns `size_type{}`.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::front@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::front@k_Z.body: The `front()` member simply returns a (const) reference to the very first element of the underlying container. It is guaranteed not to modify the object and requires that the container contains at least one element; otherwise the call is undefined. This allows callers (as shown in the `cmStringAlgorithms` usage) to inspect or compare the leading character of a string without extracting it.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::length@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::length@k_.body: The `length` member simply reports how many elements the object holds. In practice it’s called on a string‐like view to obtain the substring size before trimming the leading prefix. It guarantees no side‑effects and never mutates the internal state.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::operator=.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::operator=.body: Assigns the source view’s data pointer and length to the target, effectively copying the string view’s state. @lstd::__1::basic_string_view::operator[.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::operator[.body: The `operator[]` overload returns a `const_reference` to the element at the supplied `size_type` index. Use it when you need const‑access to an element, and invoke the bounds‑checking overload for safety in production code.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::size@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::size@k_ZN.body: The `size()` function returns the number of elements in the underlying container, enabling callers to perform size checks, arithmetic, and bounds calculations across the codebase.

@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::substr@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::basic_string_view::substr@k_.body: The `substr` member produces a new string‑view that refers to the requested slice of the original buffer; no copying of characters occurs. The first argument indicates the offset from the beginning of the view, and an optional second argument limits the number of characters taken. If the length argument is omitted, the view extends to the end of the underlying string. Bounds checks are performed: if the offset or requested range would exceed the original view’s size, the call falls back to the maximum valid extent.

@lstd::__1::chrono::steady_clock::now@k_.body: A single call to this static helper yields an instantaneous time‑point object that callers can store and later compare against other points to gauge elapsed periods. @lstd::__1::chrono::system_clock::from_t.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::chrono::system_clock::from_t.body: Creates a `time_point` value from a raw integer, interpreting the number as a timestamp (typically seconds since the Unix epoch) and returning the corresponding time‑point object.

@lstd::__1::chrono::system_clock::now@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::chrono::system_clock::now@k_.body: The function `now()` supplies a single point in time that represents the current moment according to the system clock. It produces a value of type `time_point` (essentially an alias for `std::chrono::system_clock::time_point`) and is invoked throughout the codebase whenever an exact timestamp is needed—whether to mark the beginning of a test run, to compute elapsed duration, or to embed a timestamp into XML output.

@lstd::__1::chrono::system_clock::to_tim.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::chrono::system_clock::to_tim.body: The function `to_time_t` is a helper that converts a `time_point` object into a `time_t` value. Internally it usually performs a simple conversion such as `return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::seconds>(tp.time_since_epoch()).count();`. This routine is invoked in several places: during test submissions to stamp the current instant, when recording test start times, and when serialising timestamps for XML output.

@lstd::__1::chrono::time_point::time_sin.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__1::count_if@k_ZNSt3__18count_if.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::count_if@k_ZNSt3__18count_if.body:
`count_if` is a utility that scans a range defined by two iterators and tallies how many elements satisfy a supplied predicate.  
The function accepts:

* an **input iterator type** (`_InputIterator`);
* a **predicate type** (`_Predicate`), usually a function object or lambda that returns `true` when the element should be counted.

The return type is the `difference_type` associated with that iterator (via `iterator_traits`), meaning an integer capable of representing the distance between the two iterators.

Typical use‑cases in the code base include:

* Counting elements that meet a certain condition (e.g., number of even numbers, number of string tokens that contain a substring, etc.);
* Filtering a container to compute statistics without allocating intermediate containers.

In practice, you would invoke it like:

```cpp
auto n = count_if(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x){ return x%2==0; });  // count evens
```

The function simply iterates from `first` to `last`, applies `pred` to each element, and increments a counter whenever the predicate returns `true`. No material is stored; only a numeric count is returned.

@lstd::__1::dec@k_ZNSt3__13decB7v160000E.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__1::dec@k_ZNSt3__13decB7v160000E.body: `dec` is an I/O manipulator that, when inserted into a stream, switches the stream’s formatting flag to use decimal base for subsequent integer output. It effectively resets any previous base manipulator (e.g., `hex` or `oct`) back to decimal, ensuring that values printed after it are shown in decimal form.

@lstrchr@k_Z6strchrB7v160000Ua9enable_if.author: AI Short Overview
@lstrchr@k_Z6strchrB7v160000Ua9enable_if.body:
`strchr` is a small helper that mimics the standard library’s `strchr`.  
It walks through the supplied string until it encounters the target character and returns a pointer to that character in the original buffer; if the character is absent, it returns `nullptr`.  

Typical usage patterns in the code base:

* **Search in a loop** – In *cmSystemTools.cxx* the routine is employed inside a `while` that keeps retrieving the next slash (`'/'`) separator:  
  ```cpp
  while ((sep = strchr(sep, '/'))) { … }
  ```
  The loop terminates when no more slashes can be found; the returned pointer is used as the boundary for subsequent parsing steps.

* **Skip the matched character** – In *cmFortranLexer.cxx* the function is combined with a pointer addition to advance past a marker:  
  ```cpp
  yylvalp->string = strdup(strchr(yytext, '<')+1);
  ```
  Here the returned address is immediately incremented by one, yielding a string that starts just after the first `<` that appears in `yytext`.

**Key implementation notes**

| Aspect | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| Return semantics | `NULL` if the character is not present; otherwise pointer to the matched byte in the original buffer. |
| Safety | Caller must guarantee the input string is non‑NULL and null‑terminated. |
| Performance | Linear scan; no extra allocations. |

**Edge considerations for developers**

* Passing a `nullptr` as the input string – will crash. Guard against this before calling.  
* Expecting the returned pointer to be non‑modified: the caller must not alter the string content before using the pointer.  
* When used with `strdup` or `strdup`, the returned pointer may point into a buffer that will be freed – ensure lifetime extends as needed.

These points summarize the function’s purpose and typical application in the surrounding code.

@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringDn@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringDn@f./.body: This template specialization implements a generic `valueAsString` helper that accepts a `std::nullptr_t` argument (representing an unset value) and simply returns the literal string `"(unset)"`. The function is marked with `template <>` and is a specialization for the type `std::nullptr_t`; it ignores its argument and always produces the same string. This helper can be used wherever a string representation of an “unset” or `nullptr`‑like value is required.

@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringNSt3__.author: AI Short Overview
@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringNSt3__.body: This template simply forwards a `std::string` argument unchanged, returning the same string instance. It is a no‑op placeholder that satisfies a generic string‑to‑string conversion signature.

@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringPKc@f..author: AI Short Overview
@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringPKc@f..body: The function takes a `const char*` argument and returns a `std::string`. If the input pointer is non‑null it copies the pointed‑to C‑string into a `std::string`; otherwise it substitutes the literal `"(unset)"`. The template parameter is unused in the snippet, so the call simply returns the string representation of the pointer or the placeholder.

@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringT_.author: AI Short Overview
@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringT_.body: The `valueAsString` template takes a `PropertyType` instance and returns a `std::string` that represents the value in a readable form. It is used throughout the codebase to serialize property values—for example, converting a numeric or boolean property to its string representation for logging, display, or serialization. The function performs the inverse of any parsing routine that reads a string back into a `PropertyType`.

@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringb@f./S.author: AI Short Overview
@lvalueAsString@k_Z13valueAsStringb@f./S.body: Converts a boolean value into the literal strings “TRUE” or “FALSE” based on its truth value.

@lwaddch@kwaddch.author: AI Short Overview
@lwaddch@kwaddch.body: The `waddch` routine inserts a character into the current form buffer at the current cursor position and shifts the remaining content accordingly. It returns a status flag (0 for success, non‑zero for error).

@lwaddnstr@kwaddnstr.author: AI Short Overview
@lwaddnstr@kwaddnstr.body: waddnstr writes a string into a window’s internal buffer at the current cursor position. It copies `len` bytes from the supplied buffer into the window’s data area, updates cursor and line information accordingly, and returns an integer status code indicating success or failure.

@lwattrset@kwattrset.author: AI Short Overview
@lwattrset@kwattrset.body: The `wattrset` routine is a small utility used by the form‑handling driver to apply the attribute settings stored in a field descriptor to a specific `WINDOW`. It simply copies the values from the field’s internal attribute cache into the `WINDOW`’s attribute state (setting color, boldness, reverse video, etc.) and pushes that change through `wattrset()` before the form is redisplayed. This helper keeps the rest of the form‑handling code free of repetitive attribute‑management logic.

@lwbkgdset@kwbkgdset.author: AI Short Overview
@lwbkgdset@kwbkgdset.body: The `wbkgdset()` routine is a helper that applies the configured background and gradient attributes to a form field—initializing or updating the field’s visual background before rendering. It returns an integer status code to signal success or failure.

@lwclrtobot@kwclrtobot.author: AI Short Overview
@lwclrtobot@kwclrtobot.body: The function `wclrtobot` processes the `w` field of a form structure (as seen in `frm_driver.c` line 2501) and returns an integer value that the driver routine consumes for subsequent calculations.

@lwclrtoeol@kwclrtoeol.author: AI Short Overview
@lwclrtoeol@kwclrtoeol.body: The `wclrtoeol()` routine clears a form field widget from the current cursor position to the end of its line. It is invoked after user input has been removed or when the form needs to be refreshed, ensuring the visual field is blank from that point onward. It works by iterating over the form’s internal buffer and updating the display buffer accordingly.

@lwcursyncup@kwcursyncup.author: AI Short Overview
@lwcursyncup@kwcursyncup.body: The `wcursyncup` routine updates the form‑window’s internal cursor state to match the current visual cursor position. When called (e.g., in `frm_driver.c` line 604), it reads the current input cursor coordinates, writes them to the form window structure, and triggers any pending redraw or state‑flag updates needed so that subsequent input events see the correct cursor position.

@lwdelch@kwdelch.author: AI Short Overview
@lwdelch@kwdelch.body: `wdelch()` removes a single character from the current position in a form, updating internal buffers and returning a status code.

@lwdeleteln@kwdeleteln.author: AI Short Overview
@lwdeleteln@kwdeleteln.body: The wdeleteln function deallocates a form’s `w` resource, freeing its memory and cleaning up any internal state associated with that window.

@lwerase@kwerase.author: AI Short Overview
@lwerase@kwerase.body: The `werase` routine clears the in‑memory state of a form object, flushing any buffered fields and resetting internal flags before the form is disposed or reused. It accepts a single `Form` pointer, checks for a valid handle, and then writes a zeroed byte‑array over the form’s data area, ensuring the form is blank for the next operation.

@lwinch@kwinch.author: AI Short Overview
@lwinch@kwinch.body: winch returns an integer that represents a character value (after any required masking) used when rendering a line. It supplies the needed data for the line‑ending logic in frm_driver.c.

@lwinnstr@kwinnstr.author: AI Short Overview
@lwinnstr@kwinnstr.body: The function writes a string to a UI window. It takes a pointer to a `WINDOW` structure, a C‑string to print, and an integer that typically represents the string length or a desired width. It returns an `int` status code (usually zero on success). The call sites in `frm_driver.c` and `frm_data.c` use it to display text in various UI components.

@lwinsch@kwinsch.author: AI Short Overview
@lwinsch@kwinsch.body: The `winsch` routine is a tiny helper that performs a quick check and returns a single status code. It examines the current form context (via its parameters) to see whether a particular “channel” value is acceptable – usually confirming that the channel is neither empty nor already set. If the condition passes, it returns `0`; otherwise it returns a negative error code to indicate failure. This helper is used in places where a form’s window or channel must be validated before proceeding further.

@lwinsertln@kwinsertln.author: AI Short Overview
@lwinsertln@kwinsertln.body: The `winsertln()` routine inserts a new line into the current form’s buffer—appending a newline to the form’s internal data structures and updating any necessary cursors or viewport information that relies on that line count.

@lwinsnstr@kwinsnstr.author: AI Short Overview
@lwinsnstr@kwinsnstr.body: The function writes a null‑terminated string into a form buffer. It takes a form pointer, a pointer to the text to write, and the length of that text, then copies the bytes into the form’s internal buffer and returns the number of bytes written (or –1 on error).

@lwmove@kwmove.author: AI Short Overview
@lwmove@kwmove.body: wmove is a utility that repositions a form’s window within its parent frame. It updates the internal coordinates for the window and triggers the required redraw logic so that the visual layout reflects the new placement.

@lwrapOptions::[lambda_0]::operator()@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lwrapOptions::[lambda_0]::operator()@k_.body: This public const member simply returns a `std::string` constructed from the supplied argument. It’s used wherever a string representation of the current object is required.

@lwrapOptions::[lambda_0]@kwrapOptions::.author: AI Short Overview
@lwrapOptions::[lambda_0]@kwrapOptions::.body: This lambda captures a reference to a `std::string` named `wrapperFlag`. When invoked with a `std::string` argument `o`, it concatenates the *last character* of `wrapperFlag` with `o` and returns the resulting string.

@lwrapOptions@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111wrapOp.author: AI Short Overview
@lwrapOptions@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111wrapOp.body: WrapOptions scans a list of option strings and rewrites any that carry the “‑Wl” or “‑Xlinker” prefixes into the canonical “LINKER:” form. It then groups consecutive non‑LINKER options into a sub‑list and emits each element prefixed (or concatenated when a separator is supplied) with the supplied wrapper flags. The resulting set of wrapped strings is packaged into a vector of BT\<std::string> and returned.

@lwsyncup@kwsyncup.author: AI Short Overview
@lwsyncup@kwsyncup.body: The function `wsyncup` synchronizes the state of a form window with the system’s window‑manager. It updates the window’s layout, refreshes its contents, and ensures that any pending UI changes are committed before the window is displayed again.

@lyy_fatal_error@k_ZL14yy_fatal_errorPKc.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_fatal_error@k_ZL14yy_fatal_errorPKc.body: The function `yy_fatal_error` is a static helper that receives an error message and a scanner context pointer. It simply writes the supplied message to `stderr` and aborts the process with a failure exit code (`YY_EXIT_FAILURE`). The cast to `struct yyguts_t` is unused; the routine’s purpose is purely to surface a fatal condition and terminate the program.

@lyy_fatal_error@k_ZL14yy_fatal_errorPKc.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_fatal_error@k_ZL14yy_fatal_errorPKc.body: The routine is a private helper used by the scanner code to abort execution when a fatal error is detected. It accepts a message string and the current scanner object, prints the supplied message to the standard error stream, and then terminates the process with a predefined failure exit code. The passed‑in `yyscanner` value is only cast to an internal structure and otherwise ignored.

@lyy_fatal_error@p@l./Source/LexerParser.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_fatal_error@p@l./Source/LexerParser.body: The function accepts a message string and a scanner object, casts the scanner to an internal structure (though it’s unused), writes the supplied message to standard error, and then terminates the process with the predefined failure exit code. It performs no parameter validation and will terminate unconditionally whenever invoked.

@lyy_get_next_buffer@k_ZL18yy_get_next_b.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_get_next_buffer@k_ZL18yy_get_next_b.body: The function moves existing input characters into the scanner’s buffer, reads more characters from the underlying stream (handling end‑of‑file markers), reallocates the buffer when it runs out of space, and updates the pointers that track how many characters have been read so that scanning can continue.

@lyy_get_next_buffer@k_ZL18yy_get_next_b.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_get_next_buffer@k_ZL18yy_get_next_b.body: The routine prepares the next input buffer for the scanner. It first checks whether the current buffer is exhausted; if so, it moves any unconsumed characters to the start of the buffer, then reads more data from the input stream into the buffer. If the buffer runs out of space it reallocates a larger array (doubling its size or adding more space). It also handles special end‑of‑buffer and end‑of‑file markers, signalling to the caller whether the scan can continue, should restart, or if the file has ended.

@lyy_get_next_buffer@p@l./Source/LexerPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_get_next_buffer@p@l./Source/LexerPa.body: The routine re‑buffers the current scanner buffer before the next read: it copies any trailing text after a previous scan boundary back to the start, then pulls more input from the underlying source into the unused part of the buffer. It handles end‑of‑file conditions by returning a sentinel value, and grows the buffer on‑the‑fly if there isn’t enough room. The function finally updates pointers so the scanner can continue consuming characters from the refreshed buffer.

@lyy_get_previous_state@k_ZL21yy_get_pre.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_get_previous_state@k_ZL21yy_get_pre.body: The function walks backward through the input buffer from the current read position, following the automaton tables (yy_base, yy_chk, yy_def, yy_meta, yy_nxt). As it steps each character, it updates the scanner’s last‑accepted state and position whenever an accepting state is reached. When the transition table signals no further move (chk mismatch) it stops and returns that state, representing the previous lexer state just before the current point.

@lyy_get_previous_state@k_ZL21yy_get_pre.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_get_previous_state@k_ZL21yy_get_pre.body: The function walks through the input buffer from the scanner’s start position (with an initial offset for the beginning‑of‑line marker) until the current buffer limit, following the transition tables. Whenever the current state is an accepting state it records that state and the position where it was seen. After processing all input, it returns the final state reached.

@lyy_get_previous_state@p@l./Source/Lexe.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_get_previous_state@p@l./Source/Lexe.body: Iterates through the scanner’s buffer, following the transition tables (yy_chk, yy_def, yy_nxt, yy_meta, yy_accept) to compute the state machine’s next state; it records the last accepted state and position whenever a transition is accepted and finally returns the state reached after processing the input stream.

@lyy_init_globals@k_ZL15yy_init_globalsP.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_init_globals@k_ZL15yy_init_globalsP.body: The routine simply zeroes all fields of the shared `yyguts_t` structure and sets the default input/output streams (to `stdin/stdout` if `YY_STDINIT` is defined, otherwise to `NULL`). No dynamic allocation occurs; the function merely clears state and returns success.

@lyy_init_globals@k_ZL15yy_init_globalsP.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_init_globals@k_ZL15yy_init_globalsP.body: The routine resets the internal state of the scanner: it zero‑initializes all internal pointers and counters, sets the input and output streams to either standard I/O or NULL depending on the `YY_STDINIT` flag, and finally returns 0 to indicate success.

@lyy_init_globals@p@l./Source/LexerParse.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_init_globals@p@l./Source/LexerParse.body: Reinitializes the scanner’s context structure, clearing all buffer pointers, stack counters, and stream handles before a parse begins. It also establishes the default input/output streams when YY_STDINIT is defined, and returns zero to signal success.

@lyy_reduce_print@k_ZL15yy_reduce_printP.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_reduce_print@k_ZL15yy_reduce_printP.body: The routine emits a concise trace of a parse‑time reduction: it announces the rule being applied (reporting its rule index and source‑line number) and then iterates over the right‑hand side symbols, printing each token’s symbolic name and value via the helper `yy_symbol_print`.

@lyy_stack_print@k_ZL14yy_stack_printPaS.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_stack_print@k_ZL14yy_stack_printPaS.body: The routine walks the array of state slots from the supplied bottom pointer up to the top pointer, printing each integer value in turn. It writes a header line (“Stack now”) followed by the sequence of values separated by spaces, and finishes with a newline.

@lyy_symbol_print@k_ZL15yy_symbol_printP.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_symbol_print@k_ZL15yy_symbol_printP.body: Prints a symbol’s name and value to a file—prefixing with “token” or “nterm” based on its kind.

@lyy_symbol_value_print@k_ZL21yy_symbol_.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_symbol_value_print@k_ZL21yy_symbol_.body: The routine emits the value of a symbol to the supplied stream. It takes the symbol kind, a pointer to the value, and a scanner context, and performs a lightweight guard against null values while suppressing unused‑parameter diagnostics through the helper macros.

@lyy_syntax_error_arguments@k_ZL25yy_syn.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_syntax_error_arguments@k_ZL25yy_syn.body: This helper counts and returns the number of expected tokens that should be reported after a syntax error. It checks whether the parser has a look‑ahead token; if so, it first adds that token to the array, then calls `yypcontext_expected_tokens` to collect any additional expected tokens from the current context, accounting for default actions and state‑merging nuances. The function returns the total count (or `YYENOMEM` on allocation failure).

@lyy_syntax_error_arguments@k_ZL25yy_syn.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_syntax_error_arguments@k_ZL25yy_syn.body: The routine fills a supplied array with the token that caused the syntax error (if any) and then appends the set of tokens that would have been accepted in that state. It uses the parser‑context to query the lookahead token and, if it is present, first writes that token into the array and then calls yypcontext_expected_tokens to obtain the list of expected tokens. The return value is the total count of arguments written; a return of YYENOMEM indicates the helper could not obtain the expected token list.

@lyy_try_NUL_trans@k_ZL16yy_try_NUL_tran.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_try_NUL_trans@k_ZL16yy_try_NUL_tran.body: The function walks a transition table: it records the last accepting state, follows transition links via the auxiliary arrays, and returns zero if the traversal ends in the special “jam” state (28); otherwise it yields the new state value.

@lyy_try_NUL_trans@k_ZL16yy_try_NUL_tran.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_try_NUL_trans@k_ZL16yy_try_NUL_tran.body: The function takes a current state and a scanner object, records the state when it is an accepting one, then walks the transition table until it finds a matching transition. If the transition leads to the special jam state (215) it returns 0; otherwise it returns the new state.

@lyy_try_NUL_trans@p@l./Source/LexerPars.author: AI Short Overview
@lyy_try_NUL_trans@p@l./Source/LexerPars.body: The routine uses the scanner’s transition tables to walk from the current state until a transition matches the character code 16. While stepping, it records the most recent accepting state and its buffer position. When the loop ends, it returns 0 if the new state is the special jam state (78), otherwise it returns the new state value.

@lyydestruct@k_ZL10yydestructPKc15yysymb.author: AI Short Overview
@lyydestruct@k_ZL10yydestructPKc15yysymb.body: The routine prints a symbol record with a supplied message, then invokes the YY_IGNORE_MAYBE_UNINITIALIZED_BEGIN / END macros to silence potential warnings about unused or uninitialized values.

@lyydestruct@k_ZL10yydestructPKc15yysymb.author: AI Short Overview
@lyydestruct@k_ZL10yydestructPKc15yysymb.body: The function serves as a helper that logs the removal of a scanner symbol. It accepts a message string and symbol kind, then invokes a macro to output the symbol’s information while deliberately swallowing unused parameters with a pair of ignore‑macros so that the compiler sees no warnings.

@lyyguts_t::yyguts_t@k_ZN8yyguts_tC1EOS_.author: AI Short Overview
@lyyguts_t::yyguts_t@k_ZN8yyguts_tC1EOS_.body: The `yyguts_t` constructor accepts an rvalue reference to an existing `yyguts_t` object and constructs a new instance by moving the internal state of that source object. It uses move semantics to transfer ownership of any internal resources without copying, allowing the new instance to take over the contents of the argument efficiently.

@lyyguts_t::yyguts_t@k_ZN8yyguts_tC1ERKS.author: AI Short Overview
@lyyguts_t::yyguts_t@k_ZN8yyguts_tC1ERKS.body: Creates a new `yyguts_t` instance by duplicating the internal state of an existing `yyguts_t` object.

@lyyguts_t::yyguts_t@k_ZN8yyguts_tC1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lyyguts_t::yyguts_t@k_ZN8yyguts_tC1Ev.body:
`yyguts_t()` is a public factory function that returns a `yyguts_t` instance.  
This struct aggregates shared state (token tables, error flags, and helper data) that the lexer modules consume during parsing.  
The function initializes this container—typically zero‑filling flags, allocating any required buffers, and setting up pointers to the lexer’s shared tables—so each lexer can operate with a consistent global context.

@lyypcontext_expected_tokens@k_ZL26yypco.author: AI Short Overview
@lyypcontext_expected_tokens@k_ZL26yypco.body: The routine walks the parsing tables for the current state to enumerate the token kinds that are acceptable as the next input token. It starts with the state index from the context, checks whether that state has a default action, and if not, loops over the range of possible token indices. For each token that matches the look‑ahead table and is not an error token, it appends the token kind to the supplied array (or increments a count if no array). If no tokens were found, the array is filled with `YYEMPTY`. The function finally returns the number of expected tokens that were collected.

@lyypcontext_expected_tokens@k_ZL26yypco.author: AI Short Overview
@lyypcontext_expected_tokens@k_ZL26yypco.body: The routine walks the action table for the current parser state, collects every valid look‑ahead token that would trigger a non‑error rule, and returns how many such tokens exist. If a buffer pointer is supplied, it fills that buffer with the token kinds in order; otherwise it merely counts them. If no token is admissible it falls back to the single `YYEMPTY` token.

@lyystpcpy@k_ZL8yystpcpyPcPKc@p@l./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lyystpcpy@k_ZL8yystpcpyPcPKc@p@l./Sourc.body: The routine walks through the source string, copying each byte into the destination buffer until it hits a `'\0'` terminator. After the copy, it returns a pointer to the last character written (i.e. the null byte at the end).

@lyystpcpy@k_ZL8yystpcpyPcPKc@p@l./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lyystpcpy@k_ZL8yystpcpyPcPKc@p@l./Sourc.body: The routine copies a null‑terminated character array from `yysrc` into the buffer pointed to by `yydest`, advancing both pointers until the terminating zero is written, and then returns a pointer to the final character of the copy.

@lyystrlen@k_ZL8yystrlenPKc@p@l./Source/.author: AI Short Overview
@lyystrlen@k_ZL8yystrlenPKc@p@l./Source/.body: The function traverses a C‑style string character‑by‑character until it encounters a null terminator, increments a counter, and returns that counter as the string’s length. It’s a naïve implementation of `strlen` that assumes the input is non‑null and contains no bounds checking.

@lyystrlen@k_ZL8yystrlenPKc@p@l./Source/.author: AI Short Overview
@lyystrlen@k_ZL8yystrlenPKc@p@l./Source/.body: The function walks a null‑terminated C‑string, incrementing a counter until it meets the terminator, then returns that counter as the string length. It assumes the passed pointer is valid; passing a null pointer would lead to undefined behaviour.

@lyysymbol_name@k_ZL13yysymbol_name15yys.author: AI Short Overview
@lyysymbol_name@k_ZL13yysymbol_name15yys.body: Returns the corresponding name string for a given `yysymbol_kind_t` value by indexing into the `yytname` array.

@lyysymbol_name@k_ZL13yysymbol_name15yys.author: AI Short Overview
@lyysymbol_name@k_ZL13yysymbol_name15yys.body: The function indexes a pre‑populated lookup table (`yytname`) with the supplied enum value and returns the corresponding C‑string pointer.

@lyysyntax_error@k_ZL14yysyntax_errorPlP.author: AI Short Overview
@lyysyntax_error@k_ZL14yysyntax_errorPlP.body:
The routine creates a human‑readable syntax‑error message for the parser.  
It examines the parsing context to determine which token was seen and which tokens were expected, selects an appropriate template string that may list up to five expected symbols, and fills in the token names.  
If the supplied buffer is too small it signals that the caller must grow the buffer (returning ‑1 and setting the required size).  
The function returns a status code: 0 for success, −1 if the buffer was too small, or YYENOMEM if it could not allocate the needed space.

@lyysyntax_error@k_ZL14yysyntax_errorPlP.author: AI Short Overview
@lyysyntax_error@k_ZL14yysyntax_errorPlP.body: The routine builds a diagnostic string that describes a syntax error. It examines the parsing context to learn which token was seen and which tokens would have been expected, picks an appropriate format string (with the right number of “%s” slots), and writes the final message into the caller‑supplied buffer if that buffer is large enough. If the buffer is too small it signals the caller to grow the buffer and retry.

@lyytnamerr@k_ZL9yytnamerrPcPKc@p@l./Sou.author: AI Short Overview
@lyytnamerr@k_ZL9yytnamerrPcPKc@p@l./Sou.body: The routine scans a string for quoted text. When the source begins with a double‑quote it walks forward until the matching closing quote, copying each character (except the delimiters) into the destination buffer if supplied. Escaped backslashes (`\\`) are collapsed to a single backslash in the output. Once the terminating quote is found, the function returns the number of characters written (or the length of the source if no buffer was given). If the input does not start with a quote, the routine simply copies the whole string unchanged.

@lyytnamerr@k_ZL9yytnamerrPcPKc@p@l./Sou.author: AI Short Overview
@lyytnamerr@k_ZL9yytnamerrPcPKc@p@l./Sou.body: The routine removes surrounding double‑quotes from a literal, copies the interior into a supplied buffer (or merely counts the characters), and then returns the length of that unquoted string. If the supplied buffer pointer is null, it simply measures the string’s size. It walks the source string one character at a time, recognizing an escaped backslash only when followed by another backslash; a single backslash that isn’t doubled terminates the operation. When a closing double‑quote is found, the buffer is zero‑terminated and the final count is returned. In other cases it writes each ordinary character to the destination until the end quote is reached. The function therefore acts as a lightweight parser that strips optional outer quotes and any simple escape sequences from a quoted string literal.

@lyyunput@k_ZL7yyunputiPcPv@p@l./Source/.author: AI Short Overview
@lyyunput@k_ZL7yyunputiPcPv@p@l./Source/.body: The function restores a character to the scanner’s input buffer. It first places the character `c` back at the current read position (`yy_cp`), then updates the scanner’s internal pointers—`yytext_ptr`, `yy_hold_char`, and `yy_c_buf_p`—so the next read will see this character. If the buffer is almost full, it shifts the contents upward to make room for two end‑of‑buffer markers before inserting the character. The routine ensures the buffer state remains consistent for the next scan.

@lzonephrase@p@l./Utilities/cmlibarchive.author: AI Short Overview
@lzonephrase@p@l./Utilities/cmlibarchive.body:
The function consumes the next token in the input stream.  
When the token is a zone identifier it increments the zone counter, records the zone value, sets the DST flag (on if a DST token follows, off otherwise) and advances the token pointer. If no zone token is seen it returns zero.
